Zacheus certainly was rich, and chosen by Christ: but by bestowing half his goods on the poor, and restoring also fourfold what he had taken by fraud (for the one is not enough, nor hath liberality any grace if the injury remaineth, because not spoils but gifts are sought), he received a more abundant reward than he bestowed.
discantdivitesnoninfacultatibuscrimenher.la: Discant dívites non in facultátibus crimen hærere, sed in iis, qui uti nesciant facultátibus. Nam divítiæ ut impedimenta improbis, ita bonis sunt adjumenta virtútis. Dives certe Zachǽus, et eléctus a Christo: sed dimidium bonórum suórum paupéribus largiendo, reddendo étiam in quadruplum, quæ fraude sustúlerat, (álterum enim non sat est, nec habet grátiam liberalitas, si injúria persevérat, quia non spólia, sed dona quærúntur) uberiorem mercédem quam conferebat, accépit.

etbeneprincepsinduciturpublicanorumquisi.en: And well is a chief of the publicans brought in. Who now would despair of himself, when even this man, whose wealth was from fraud, came to salvation? And he, saith he, was rich: that thou mayest know that not all the rich are covetous. Because he was low of stature. What meaneth it, that the Scripture hath expressed the stature of no other but this man? See lest perchance he was little in malice, or as yet little in faith. For he had not yet promised to restore: he had not yet seen Christ: rightly was he still little. But John was great, because he both saw Christ, and the Spirit as a dove abiding upon Christ, as he himself saith: I saw the Spirit coming down as a dove, and remaining upon him.
etbeneprincepsinduciturpublicanorumquisi.la: Et bene princeps indúcitur publicanorum. Quis jam de se desperet, quando et iste, cui census ex fraude, ad salútem pervénit? Et ipse, inquit, dives. Ut scias non omnes dívites, avaros. Quia statúra pusíllus erat. Quid sibi vult, quod nullius altérius staturam Scriptúra, nisi hujus expressit? Vide ne forte malítia pusíllus, aut adhuc pusíllus fide. Nondum enim reddere promiserat: nondum viderat Christum: mérito adhuc pusíllus. Joánnes autem magnus, quia et Christum vidit, et Spíritum sicut columbam super Christum manentem, sicut ipse ait: Vidi Spíritum descendentem sicut colúmbam, et manentem super eum.

celebritashuiuscongregationisdedicatiest.en: The festival of this assembly is the dedication of a house of prayer. This then is the house of our prayers; but the house of God are we ourselves. If we ourselves are the house of God, we are built in this world, that we may be dedicated at the end of the world. The building, nay rather the building up, hath labour; the dedication, exultation. That which was done here when these walls were rising, the same is done now, when believers in Christ are gathered together. For by believing, as it were, timber and stones are hewn from the woods and mountains: but when they are catechized, baptized, formed, they are as it were hewn, levelled, and smoothed between the hands of the workmen and builders. Yet they make not a house of the Lord, but when they are joined together by charity.
celebritashuiuscongregationisdedicatiest.la: Celebritas hujus congregatiónis, dedicatio est domus oratiónis. Domus ergo nostrárum oratiónum ista, domus autem Dei nos ipsi. Si domus Dei nos ipsi, nos in hoc sǽculo ædificamur, ut in fine sǽculi dedicemur. ædificium, imo ædificatio habet labórem; dedicatio exsultationem. Quod hic fiebat, quando ista surgebant, hoc fit modo, cum congregantur credéntes in Christum. Credéndo enim, quasi de silvis et móntibus ligna et lápides præciduntur: cum vero catechizantur, baptizantur, formantur, tamquam inter manus fabrorum et opificum dolantur, collineentur, complanantur. Verúmtamen domum Dómini non fáciunt, nisi quando caritáte compaginantur.

lignaistetlapidessinonsibicertoordinecoh.en: If these timbers and stones did not hold together in a certain order, if they did not peaceably interlock, if they did not, by holding together, in a manner love one another, no man would enter here. Lastly, when thou seest in any building the stones and timbers holding well together, thou enterest secure, thou fearest not its fall. The Lord Christ, therefore, willing to enter and to dwell in us, said, as it were in building: A new commandment I give unto you: That you love one another. A new commandment, saith he, I give unto you. For ye were old, ye were not yet making a house for me, ye lay in your ruin. Therefore, that ye may be raised out of the oldness of your ruin, love one another.
lignaistetlapidessinonsibicertoordinecoh.la: Ligna ista et lápides si non sibi certo órdine cohærerent, si non se pacífice innecterent, si non se invicem, cohærendo sibi, quodámmodo amarent, nemo huc intraret. Dénique quando vides in áliqua fabrica lápides et ligna bene sibi cohærere, secúrus intras, ruinam non times. Volens ergo Dóminus Christus intrare, et in nobis habitáre, tamquam ædificando dicébat: Mandátum novum do vobis: Ut vos invicem diligatis. Mandátum, inquit, novum do vobis. Veteres enim eratis, domum mihi nondum faciebatis, in vestra ruína jacebatis. Ergo ut eruamini a vestræ ruinæ vetustáte,vos invicem amate.

consideretergocaritasvestraedificariadhu.en: Let your charity therefore consider that this house is still being built throughout the whole world, as was foretold and promised. For when the house is built after the captivity, as another Psalm hath it, it is said: Sing ye to the Lord a new canticle: sing to the Lord, all the earth. What he said there, A new canticle, that the Lord said, A new commandment. For what hath a new canticle, but a new love? To sing is the part of a lover. The voice of this singer is the fervour of holy love. Let us love, let us love freely: for we love the Lord, than whom we find nothing better: let us love him for his own sake, and ourselves in him, yet for his sake.
consideretergocaritasvestraedificariadhu.la: Consideret ergo cáritas vestra, ædificari adhuc istam domum toto, sicut prædictum est et promíssum, orbe terrárum. Cum enim ædificátur domus post captivitátem, sicut habet álius Psalmus, dícitur: Cantáte Dómino cánticum novum: cantáte Dómino omnis terra. Quod ibi dixit, Cánticum novum; hoc Dóminus dixit, Mandátum novum. Quid enim habet cánticum novum, nisi amórem novum? Cantare amantis est. Vox hujus cantoris, fervor est sancti amóris. Amémus, gratis amémus: D(3minum enim amámus, quo nihil mélius invenimus: ipsum amémus propter ipsum, et nos in ipso, tamen propter ipsum.

exlibinlucpropefinem.en: From Book 8 on Luke, near the end
exlibinlucpropefinem.la: Ex Lib. 8 in Luc., prope finem

queautemturbanisiimperiteconfusiomultitu.en: But what is the crowd, but the confusion of the unskilled multitude, which cannot see the summit of wisdom? Therefore Zacheus, as long as he is in the crowd, seeth not Christ: he climbeth above the crowd, and seeth: that is, having now passed beyond the ignorance of the people, he merited to behold him whom he desired. And beautifully he added: Because the Lord was to pass that way: either where the sycamore was, or where he was that should believe; that he might both keep the mystery and sow grace. For he had so come, that through the Jews he might pass to the Gentiles.
queautemturbanisiimperiteconfusiomultitu.la: Quæ autem turba, nisi imperitæ confúsio multitúdinis, quæ vérticem nequit vidére sapiéntiæ? Ergo Zachǽus quámdiu in turba est, non videt Christum: supra turbam ascéndit, et vidit: hoc est, plebis jam transgressus inscítiam, méruit quem desiderabat, aspicere. Pulchre autem addidit: Quia illa parte erat transiturus Dóminus: vel ubi sycomorus, vel ubi creditúrus: ut et mystérium serváret, et grátiam seminaret Sic enim venerat, ut per Judǽos transiret ad Gentes.

vidititaquezacheumsursumiamenimsublimita.en: He saw therefore Zacheus above. For already, by the loftiness of his faith, he stood out among the fruits of new works, as by the height of a fruitful tree. And since we have turned from the figure to morals, it delighteth us, among so many delights of the believers, to relax the mind on the Lord's day, and to mingle festivity. Zacheus in the sycamore, namely the new fruit of a new time, that in this also might be fulfilled that saying: The fig tree hath put forth her green figs.
vidititaquezacheumsursumiamenimsublimita.la: Vidit ítaque Zachǽum sursum. Jam enim sublimitáte fídei inter fructus novarum óperum, velut fœcúndæ altitúdine árboris eminebat Et quóniam de typo ad moralia defleximus, inter tot credéntium voluptates Domínica die relaxare ánimum, festivitátem admiscere deléctat. Zachǽus in sycomoro, novum vidélicet novi témporis pomum, ut in hoc quoque compleretur illud: Arbor fici prodúxit grossos suos.

adhocenimchristusadvenitutexlignisnonpom.en: For to this end Christ came, that from trees not fruits but men might be born. We read elsewhere: When thou wast under the fig tree, I saw thee. Nathanael, therefore, under the tree, that is, upon the root, because he was just. For the root is holy. Yet Nathanael was under the tree, because he was under the law: Zacheus above the tree, because above the law. The one was the hidden defender of the Lord, the other his public preacher. The one was still seeking Christ from the law: the other, now above the law, was leaving his own things, and following the Lord.
adhocenimchristusadvenitutexlignisnonpom.la: Ad hoc enim Christus advenit, ut ex lignis non poma, sed hómines nascerentur. Legimus álibi: Cum esses sub árbore fici, vidi te. Ergo Nathánæl sub árbore, hoc est, supra radícem, quia justus. Radix enim sancta. Sub árbore tamen Nathanæl, quia sub lege: Zachǽus supra árborem, quia supra legem. Ille Dómini occúltus defensor, hic públicus prædicator. Ille adhuc Christum ex lege quærebat: iste jam supra legem relinquebat sua, et Ddminum sequebatur.

attenditeinpsalmodedicationisquemmodocan.en: Give heed, in the psalm of the dedication which we have just sung, to the building out of the ruin. Thou hast cut my sackcloth: this pertaineth to the ruin. What then to the building? And hast compassed me with gladness. The voice of the dedication: To the end that my glory may sing to thee, and I may not be pierced. Who is it that speaketh? Know him in his words. If I expound, it is obscure. Therefore I will say his words, and straightway ye know him that speaketh, that ye may love him that speaketh to you. Who is it that could say: Thou hast brought forth, O Lord, my soul from hell?
attenditeinpsalmodedicationisquemmodocan.la: Atténdite in psalmo dedicationis, quem modo cantavimus, ex ruína ædificiorum. Conscidísti saccum meum: hoc pértinet ad ruinam. Quid ergo ad ædificium? Et accinxisti me lætítia. Vox dedicationis: Ut cantet tibi glória mea, et non compúngar. Quis est, qui lóquitur? In verbis ejus agnoscite. Si expono, obscúrum est. Ergo verba ejus dicam, contínuo agnoscitis loquéntem, ut ametis alloquentem. Quis est, qui dícere pótuit: Eruísti Dómine ab inferis ánimam meam?

cuiusanimaiamabinferiserutestnisidequadi.en: Whose soul hath now been brought forth from hell, but his of whom it is said in another place: Thou wilt not leave my soul in hell? A dedication is set forth, and a deliverance is sung; the canticle of the dedication of the house, and it is said: I will extol thee, O Lord, for thou hast upheld me: and hast not made my enemies to rejoice over me. Give heed to the Jews, his enemies, who thought that they had slain Christ, had conquered him as an enemy, had destroyed him as a man like the rest and mortal.
cuiusanimaiamabinferiserutestnisidequadi.la: Cujus ánima jam ab inferis eruta est, nisi de qua dictum est álio loco: Non derelínques ánimam meam in inférno? Proponitur dedicatio, et cantatur liberátio, cánticum dedicationis domus, et dícitur: Exaltábo te Dómine, quóniam suscepísti me: et non jucundasti inimícos meos super me. Atténdite Judǽos inimícos, qui se putabant occidisse Christum, vicisse tamquam inimícum, perdidisse quasi hóminem céteris similem atque mortalem.

resurrexittertiadieeteiusvoxestexaltabot.en: He rose again the third day, and his is the voice: I will extol thee, O Lord, for thou hast upheld me. Give heed to the Apostle saying: For which cause God also hath exalted him. And hast not made my enemies to rejoice over me. They indeed rejoiced in the death of Christ; but at his resurrection, ascension, and preaching some were pricked to the heart. In his preaching therefore, and through the fame of the constancy of the Apostles, some were pricked and converted; some were hardened and confounded; yet none rejoiced.
resurrexittertiadieeteiusvoxestexaltabot.la: Resurréxit tértia die, et ejus vox est: Exaltábo te Dómine, quóniam suscepísti me. Atténdite Apóstolum dicéntem: Propter quod eum exaltávit. Et non jucundasti inimícos meos super me. Ipsi quidem in Christi morte jucundabantur, sed in ejus resurrectióne, ascensione, prædicatióne aliqui compungebantur, In ejus ergo prædicatióne, et per Apostolórum constantiæ diffamatiónem aliqui compungebantur, et convertebantur: aliqui obdurabantur, et confundebantur, nulli tamen jucundabantur.

libinmoraliumcappostmedium.en: Book 27 of the Morals, ch. 27, after the middle
libinmoraliumcappostmedium.la: Lib. 27 in Moralium, cap. 27 post medium

pusillusitaquezacheussycomorumsubiitetdo.en: Little Zacheus therefore climbed into the sycamore, and saw the Lord: because they who humbly choose the foolishness of the world, themselves contemplate the wisdom of God with keen insight. For the crowd hindereth our littleness from seeing the Lord: because the tumult of worldly cares presseth upon the weakness of the human mind, that it may not look upon the light of truth. But we wisely climb the sycamore, if with foresight we hold in mind that foolishness which is commanded by God. For what is more foolish in this world than not to seek what is lost, to yield up our possessions to them that seize them, to return no injury for injuries received, nay rather, when others are added, to show patience?
pusillusitaquezacheussycomorumsubiitetdo.la: Pusíllus ítaque Zachǽus sycomorum súbiit, et Dóminum vidit: quia qui mundi stultítiam humíliter eligunt, ipsi Dei sapiéntiam subtíliter contemplantur. Pusillitatem namque nostram ad vidéndum Dóminum turba præpedit: quia infirmitátem humánæ mentis, ne lucem veritátis intendat, curarum sæculárium tumúltus premit. Sed prudénter sycomorum ascendimus, si provide eam quæ divínitus præcipitur, stultítiam mente tenemus. Quid enim in hoc mundo stúltius quam amíssa non quærére, possessa rapientibus relaxare, nullam pro accéptis injúriis injúriam reddere, imo adjúnctis áliis patientiam præbere?

modoquandoimplenturecclesieputamusiucund.en: Now, when the churches are filled, think we that the Jews rejoice? Churches are built, dedicated, filled: how do they rejoice? Not only do they not rejoice, but they are even confounded, and the voice of him that exulteth is fulfilled: I will extol thee, O Lord, for thou hast upheld me: and hast not made my enemies to rejoice over me. Thou hast not made them rejoice over me: if they believe in me, thou wilt make them rejoice in me. That we may not say much, let us at length come to those things which we have sung. How doth Christ say: Thou hast cut my sackcloth, and hast compassed me with gladness? His sackcloth was the likeness of sinful flesh.
modoquandoimplenturecclesieputamusiucund.la: Modo, quando implentur ecclésiæ, putamus jucundari Judǽos? Ecclésiæ ædificantur, dedicantur, implentur: quómodo illi jucundantur? Non solum non jucundantur, sed étiam confundúntur, et implétur vox exsultantis: Exaltábo te Dómine, quóniam suscepísti me: et non jucundasti inimícos meos super me. Non jucundasti super me: si mihi credant, jucundabis in me. Ne multa dicamus, ad illa, quæ cantavimus, aliquándo veniamus. Quómodo dicit Christus: Conscidísti saccum meum, et accinxisti me lætítia? Saccus ejus erat similitúdo carnis peccáti.

nontibivilescatquodaitsaccummeumibierati.en: Let it not seem vile to thee that he saith, My sackcloth: therein was enclosed thy price. Thou hast cut my sackcloth. We have escaped through that sackcloth. Thou hast cut my sackcloth. In the passion it was cut. How then is it said to God the Father: Thou hast cut my sackcloth? Wilt thou hear how it is said to the Father: Thou hast cut my sackcloth? Because he spared not his own Son, but delivered him up for us all. For he did it by means of the Jews, who knew it not, that they who knew might be redeemed, and they who denied might be confounded. For they know not what good they have wrought for us by their evil. The sackcloth was hung up, and the wicked one as it were rejoiced. The persecutor cut the sackcloth with the lance, and the Redeemer poured forth our price.
nontibivilescatquodaitsaccummeumibierati.la: Non tibi vilescat, quod ait, Saccum meum: ibi erat inclúsum prétium tuum. Conscidísti saccum meum. Evasimus ad saccum istum. Conscidísti saccum meum. In passióne conscissus est. Quómodo ergo Deo Patri dícitur: Conscidísti saccum meum? Quómodo Patri dicatur, vis audíre: Conscidísti saccum meum? Quia próprio Fílio non pepércit, sed pro nobis ómnibus trádidit illum. Fecit enim per Judǽos nescientes, unde redimerentur sciéntes, et confunderentur negantes. Nesciunt enim quid boni nobis operati sunt malo suo. Suspensus est saccus, et quasi lætátus est ímpius. Conscidit saccum láncea persecútor, et fudit prétium nostrum Redémptor.

cantetchristusredemptorgematiudasvendito.en: Let Christ the Redeemer sing, let Judas the seller groan, let the Jew the buyer blush. Behold, Judas sold, the Jew bought; they did an evil business; both are condemned; seller and buyer have destroyed themselves. Let therefore our Head speak, let him speak for the body slain, for the body dedicated. Let him speak, let us hear: Thou hast cut my sackcloth, and hast compassed me with gladness: that is, thou hast cut my mortality, and hast compassed me with immortality and incorruption. To the end that my glory may sing to thee, and I may not be pierced. What is: I may not be pierced? Let the persecutor no more bear the lance against me, that I may not be pierced. For Christ, rising again from the dead, dieth now no more; death shall no more have dominion over him.
cantetchristusredemptorgematiudasvendito.la: Cantet Christus Redémptor, gemat Judas venditor, erubescat Judæus emptor. Ecce Judas véndidit, Judæus emit, malum negotium egérunt, ambo damnáti sunt, seípsos perdiderunt venditor et emptor. Dicat ergo caput nostrum, dicat pro córpore occiso, pro córpore dedicato. Dicat, audiamus: Conscidísti saccum meum, et accinxisti me lætítia: id est, conscidísti mortalitatem meam, et accinxisti me immortalitate et incorruptióne. Ut cantet tibi glória mea, et non compúngar. Quid est, Non compúngar? Jam contra me non ferat lanceam persecútor, Ut non compúngar. Christus enim surgens a mórtuis, jam non móritur, et mors illi ultra non dominábitur.

homiliavenerabilisbedepresbyteri.en: Homily by the Venerable Bede, Priest.

queimpossibiliasuntapudhominespossibilia.en: The things that are impossible with men are possible with God. For behold, the camel, laying down the burden of his hump, passeth through the eye of the needle; that is, the rich man and publican, leaving the load of riches and despising the wealth gotten by fraud, goeth up by the narrow gate and the strait way that leadeth to life. Who with wonderful devotion of faith, to see the Saviour, made up by climbing a tree what he lacked by nature: and therefore justly, though he himself dared not ask it, he received the blessing he desired, of receiving the Lord as his guest.
queimpossibiliasuntapudhominespossibilia.la: Quæ impossibilia sunt apud hómines, possibilia sunt apud Deum. Ecce enim camélus, deposita gibbi sárcina, per forámen acus transit, hoc est, dives et publicanus, relícto ónere divitiárum, contempto censu fraudum, angústam portam, arctamque viam, quæ ad vitam ducit, ascéndit. Qui mira devotióne fídei ad vidéndum Salvatórem, quod natúra minus habúerat, ascensu supplet árboris: atque ídeo juste, quamvis ipse rogare non aúdeat, benedictiónem Domínicæ susceptionis, quam desiderabat, accépit.

mysticeautemzacheusquiinterpretaturiusti.en: Mystically, Zacheus, which is interpreted justified, signifieth the people believing from among the Gentiles; who, the more he was occupied with worldly cares, the lower he had been brought by crimes that weighed him down. But he was washed, he was sanctified, he was justified in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, and in the Spirit of our God. He sought to see the Saviour entering Jericho, but could not for the crowd: because he longed to share in the grace of faith which the Saviour brought to the world; but the ingrown habit of vices had hindered him from attaining his desire.
mysticeautemzacheusquiinterpretaturiusti.la: Mystice autem Zachǽus, qui interpretátur justificatus, credentem ex Géntibus pópulum significat. Qui quanto curis sæculáribus occupatior, tanto flagítiis deprimentibus erat factus humilior. Sed ablútus est, sed sanctificátus, sed justificatus in nómine Dómini nostri Jesu Christi, et in spíritu Dei nostri. Qui intrántem Jericho Salvatórem vidére quærebat, sed præ turba non póterat: quia grátiæ fídei, quam mundo Salvátor áttulit, participare cupiebat: sed inolita vitiórum consuetúdo, ne ad votum perveniret, obstiterat.

eademnamqueturbanoxieconsuetudinisquesup.en: For the same crowd of hurtful habit, which rebuked the blind man crying out lest he should ask for light, hindereth also the publican looking up, lest he see Jesus. But as the blind man overcame the voices of the crowds by crying out more and more, so the little man must needs surmount the obstacle of the hurtful crowd by seeking higher things, must leave earthly things, and climb the tree of the cross. For the sycamore (which is a tree like the mulberry in its leaves, but surpassing it in height, whence also it is called by the Latins the lofty one) is called the foolish fig. And the same cross of the Lord, which nourisheth believers as a fig, is mocked by unbelievers as foolish.
eademnamqueturbanoxieconsuetudinisquesup.la: Eádem namque turba noxiæ consuetúdinis, quæ supra cæcum clamántem, ne lumen peteret, increpabat; étiam suspicientem publicanum, ne Jesum vídeat, tardat. Sed sicut cæcus turbarum voces magis ac magis clamando devícit: ita pusíllus necésse est turbæ nocentis obstaculum altióra petendo transcendat, terréna relinquat, árborem crucis ascendat. Sycomorus namque (quæ est arbor fóliis moro símilis, sed altitúdine præstans, unde et a Latinis celsa nuncupátur), ficus fatua dícitur. Et eádem domínica crux, quæ credéntes alit ut ficus, ab incredulis irridetur ut fatua.

ergodumnovamconstructionemsanctehuiusecc.en: While therefore we gladly behold the new building of this holy church, which we dedicate this day to the divine name, we find that there is owed by us both the greatest praise to our God, and to your holiness a discourse befitting the building of the divine house. And our discourse will then be fitting, if it have in itself somewhat of edification which may profit to the good of your souls, God building you up within. What we see done here bodily in the walls, let it be done spiritually in your minds: and what we behold finished here in stones and timbers, let it, the grace of God building, be perfected in your bodies.
ergodumnovamconstructionemsanctehuiusecc.la: Ergo, dum novam constructionem sanctæ hujus ecclésiæ libénter attendimus, quam divíno nómini hódie dedicamus, invenimus a nobis deberi et Deo nostro máximam laudem, et sanctitati vestræ congruum de divínæ domus ædificatione sermónem. Tunc autem sermo noster congruus erit, si in se áliquid ædificationis hábeat, quod utilitati animárum vestrarum, Deo vos interius ædíficánte, proficiat. Quod hic factum corporaliter videmus in parietibus, spiritaliter fiat in mentibus: et quod hic perféctum cernimus in lapídibus et lignis, hoc ædíficánte grátia Dei, perficiatur in corpóribus vestris.

principaliterergogratiasagamusdominodeon.en: First of all, therefore, let us give thanks to the Lord our God, from whom is every best gift, and every perfect gift; and let us praise his goodness with all the eagerness of our heart, for that, to build this house of prayer, he visited the mind of his faithful, stirred up their affection, supplied help, inspired them that were not yet willing to will it, and helped the endeavours of their good will to do it: and thereby God, who worketh in his own both to will and to accomplish according to his good will, himself began all these things, himself perfected them.
principaliterergogratiasagamusdominodeon.la: Principaliter ergo grátias agamus Dómino Deo nostro, a quo est omne datum optimum, et omne donum perféctum; et ejus bonitátem tota cordis alacritate laudémus, quóniam ad construendam istam domum oratiónis, fidélium suórum visitávit ánimum, excitávit afféctum, surrogavit auxílium, inspiravit necdum volentibus ut vellent, adjúvit bonæ voluntátis conátus ut fácerent: ac per hoc Deus, qui operátur in suis et velle et perfícere pro bona voluntáte, hæc ómnia ipse coépit, ipse perfécit.

etquiaoperabonainconspectusuonumquamesse.en: And because he never suffereth good works to be vain in his sight, he will give to his faithful, to whom while they wrought he granted the favour of his power, a worthy reward for so great a work. Still further thanks are to be given to our God. For this church, which he caused to be built to his name, he hath caused also to be honoured the more with the relics of the holy Martyrs.
etquiaoperabonainconspectusuonumquamesse.la: Et quia ópera bona in conspéctu suo numquam esse permittit inánia, fidélibus suis, quibus operántibus præbuit virtútis suæ favórem, tríbuet condignam pro tanta operatióne mercédem. Adhuc ámplius agendæ sunt grátiæ Deo nostro. Hanc enim ecclésiam, quam fecit nómini suo construi, fecit étiam sanctórum Mártyrum relíquiis ámplius honorari.

etcumvenissetadlocumsuspiciensiesusvidit.en: And when he was come to the place, Jesus looking up saw him. The Saviour, walking through Jericho, came to the place where Zacheus, running before, had climbed up into the sycamore: because, having sent through the world the heralds of his word, in whom he himself in truth both spoke and went, he came to the people of the nations, who, being already lifted up by faith in his passion, burned also to be made blessed by the known face of his Godhead. Looking up he saw him, because he chose him, lifted up by the grace of faith from earthly desires, and standing out above the unbelieving crowds. For with God to see is to choose or to love. Whence is that saying: The eyes of the Lord are upon the just. For we also see the things we love; from those which we abhor we hasten to turn away our gaze.
etcumvenissetadlocumsuspiciensiesusvidit.la: Et cum venísset ad locum, suspiciens Jesus vidit illum. Perambulans Jericho Salvátor, venit ad locum, ubi præcúrrens Zachǽus sycomorum conscenderat: quia missis per mundum sui verbi præconibus, in quibus ipse nimírum et loquebátur et ibat, venit ad pópulum natiónum, qui passiónis ejus fide jam sublimis exsistens, étiam divinitátis ejus ardébat agnita fácie beari. Suspiciens vidit illum, quia per grátiam fídei a terrenis cupiditatibus elevátum, turbisque infidélibus præeminentem elégit. Vidére enim Dei, elígere vel amáre est. Unde est illud: Óculi Dómini super justos. Nam et nos quæ amámus, vidére; ab his, quæ exsecramur, intúitum festinamus avértere.

viditergoiesusvidentemsequielegiteligent.en: Jesus therefore saw him that saw him, because he chose him that chose him, and loved him that loved him. This order of advancing, to wit, of coming through faith in the Lord's Incarnation to the knowledge of his Godhead, as it were of beholding the face of Jesus through the sycamore, the excellent Doctor showeth, when he saith: For I judged not myself to know anything among you, but Jesus Christ, and him crucified. And likewise reproaching others: You are become, saith he, such as have need of milk, and not of strong meat; calling milk the weak things of the temporal dispensation, strong meat the high things of the eternal majesty.
viditergoiesusvidentemsequielegiteligent.la: Vidit ergo Jesus videntem se, quia elégit eligentem se, et amávit amántem. Hunc sane órdinem proficiendi, hoc est, per fidem domínicæ Incarnationis ad cognitionem divinitátis perveniendi, quasi per sycomorumJesu fáciem speculandi Doctor egrégius osténdit. cum ait: Non enim judicavi scire me áliquid inter vos, nisi Christum Jesum, et hunc crucifíxum. Itémque áliis exprobrans: Facti estis, inquit, quibus lacte opus sit, non solido cibo. Lac infirma temporariæ dispensatiónis, solidum cibum árdua perpetuæ majestátis appellans.

etdixitadeumzacheefestinansdescendequiah.en: And he said to him: Zacheus, make haste and come down; for this day I must abide in thy house. And he made haste and came down, and received him with joy. The Lord abode once in the house of the prince of the pharisees, that is, he taught in the synagogue of the Jews: but because with venomous tongue they carped at him for not being washed before dinner, for healing on the sabbath, for receiving publicans and sinners, for disputing against avarice, and for doing the other things worthy of God; wearied with their crimes, he departed and fled away, saying: Your house shall be left to you desolate. But this day he must abide in the house of little Zacheus; that is, the grace of the new light shining forth, he must rest in the humble heart of the believing nations.
etdixitadeumzacheefestinansdescendequiah.la: Et dixit ad eum: Zachǽe, festinans descénde, quia hódie in domo tua opórtet me manére. Et festinans descéndit, et excépit illum gaudens. Manébat aliquándo Dóminus in domo príncipis pharisæorum, hoc est, in Judæórum synagóga docebat: sed quia non baptizátum ante prandium, sábbato curantem, publicanos et peccatóres recipientem, contra avarítiam disputantem, et cétera digna Deo gerentem, lingua venenata carpebant: pertæsus eórum facinora, discéssit et aufugit, dicens: Relinquetur vobis domus vestra desérta. Hódie autem in domo pusilli Zachæi opórtet illum manére: hoc est, novæ lucis grátia coruscante, in húmili credéntium natiónum corde quiéscere.

communisomniumdomusestecclesiainquamvobi.en: The Church is the common house of all, into which, you having entered first, we enter, keeping the form of the disciples: and therefore, as soon as we have entered, we offer peace to all in common, that we may follow the law given to them. Let none therefore be torpid with sloth: let none have his mind hanging upon worldly things, when the priests have now entered to preach. For no small punishment hangeth over this thing. Truly I would a thousand times rather, having entered the house of any one of you, be repulsed, than, preaching here, not be heard. This would be more grievous to me than that, since indeed this house is more my own than that.
communisomniumdomusestecclesiainquamvobi.la: Commúnis ómnium domus est Ecclésia, in quam, vobis prius ingressis, nos intramus, discipulórum formam retinentes: ideóque commúniter ómnibus statim atque ingressi fuerimus, ut illis datam legem sequámur, pacem offerimus. Nemo ígitur socórdia torpeat: nemo sæculáribus rebus suspénsum ánimum hábeat, cum jam ad prædicándum sacerdótes intraverint Non enim parva huic rei imminet pœna. Equidem millies pótius malim in domum alicújus vestrum ingréssus destitui, quam hic prǽdicans non audiri. Hoc mihi molestius esset, quam illud, quando quidem magis própria hæc est, quam illa.

namhicmagneillenostreopespositesunthicsp.en: For here those great riches of ours are laid up, here all our hope. For what in this place is not great and wonderful? For this table is far more precious and more pleasant; and this lamp than that, as they know who, anointed with oil in faith, have been freed from sicknesses. This chest also is much better, and more necessary. For it containeth not garments, but mercy shut up within: although they be few that possess it. Here also is a couch far more excellent than that: for the rest of the divine Scriptures is sweeter than any bed.
namhicmagneillenostreopespositesunthicsp.la: Nam hic magnæ illæ nostræ opes pósitæ sunt, hic spes nostra omnis. Quid enim hoc loco non magnum est et admirándum? Nam hæc mensa longe pretiosior est atque jucúndior: et lucérna hæc, quam illa, ut norunt qui cum fide óleo perúncti, a morbis liberáti sunt. Arca étiam hæc multo mélior, magísque necessaria. Non enim vestes, sed misericórdiam inclúsam cóntinet: quamvis pauci sint, qui eam possideant. Hic et lectulus est valde illo præstantior: divinárum enim Scripturárum réquies quovis lecto suavior est.

etquidemsiconcordiaperfecteservareturano.en: And indeed, if concord were perfectly kept by us, we should have no other house besides this. And that what I have said is not hard, those three thousand and five thousand men bear witness, who had one house, and one table, and one soul. For the multitude of believers, he saith, had but one heart and one soul. But because we are far from their virtue, and are divided by our houses, at least when we come together here, let us do this with all zeal. For although in other things we be poor and needy, in this place at least, when we come in here to you, receive us with charity: and when I say, Peace be to you, answer, And with thy spirit, not with the voice only, but with the mind also.
etquidemsiconcordiaperfecteservareturano.la: Et quidem si concórdia perfecte servarétur a nobis, nullam áliam domum præter hanc haberemus. Hoc autem quod dixi, non esse durum, testantur illa tria míllia, et quinque míllia hóminum, quibus et domus una, et mensa una, et ánima una erat. Multitúdinis enim credéntium, inquit, unum erat cor, et ánima una. Sed quia longe ab illórum virtúte absumus, et per domos disjúncti sumus, saltem quando huc convenimus, id omni stúdio faciámus. Nam etsi in áliis rebus páuperes, et ínopes sumus, hoc loco saltem, cum huc ad vos intramus, cum caritáte nos suscipite: cumque, Pax vobis, dico: Et cum spíritu tuo, non voce solum, sed ánimo quoque respondete.

etcumviderentomnesmurmurabantdicentesquo.en: And when all saw it, they murmured, saying, that he was gone to be a guest with a man that was a sinner. It is manifest that the Jews ever hated the salvation of the Gentiles. For it is written: But the next sabbath day, the whole city almost came together to hear the word of God. And the Jews seeing the multitudes, were filled with envy, and contradicted those things which were said by Paul. And elsewhere the faithful brethren also disputed against the prince of the Apostles, saying: Why didst thou go in to men uncircumcised, and didst eat with them?
etcumviderentomnesmurmurabantdicentesquo.la: Et cum vidérent omnes, murmurabant, dicéntes, quod ad hóminem peccatórem divertisset. Maniféstum est, Judǽos semper Géntium odisse salútem. Scriptum est enim: Sequénti vero sábbato pene univérsa cívitas convénit audíre verbum Dei. Vidéntes autem turbas Judǽi repléti sunt zelo, et contradicebant iis, quæ a Paulo dicebántur. Et álibi, fidéles étiam fratres advérsus Apostolórum príncipem disceptabant, dicéntes: Quare introisti ad viros præpútium habéntes, et manducasti cum illis?

stansautemzacheusdixitaddominumeccedimid.en: But Zacheus standing, said to the Lord: Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor; and if I have wronged any man of any thing, I restore him fourfold. While others calumniated him as a sinner, Zacheus himself standing, that is, persisting in the truth of the faith which he had begun, proveth that he was not only converted from being a sinner, but also had his conversation among the perfect. For the Lord saying: If thou wilt be perfect, go, sell all that thou hast, and give to the poor; whosoever lived innocently before his conversion may, being converted, give all to the poor.
stansautemzacheusdixitaddominumeccedimid.la: Stans autem Zachæus, dixit ad Dóminum: Ecce dimidium bonórum meórum Dómine do paupéribus: et si quid áliquem defraudavi, reddo quadruplum. Áliis calumniántibus hóminem peccatórem, ipse Zachǽus stans, id est, in ea quam coéperat fídei veritáte persistens, non solum se ex peccatore conversum, sed étiam inter perfectos probat esse conversatum. Dicénte enim Dómino: Si vis perféctus esse, vade, vende ómnia quæ habes, et da paupéribus: quisquis ante convérsiónem innocenter vixit, ómnia convérsus potest dare paupéribus.

atquialiquafraudesustulitprimoheciuxtale.en: But he that hath taken anything by fraud ought first to restore it according to the law, then to give what remaineth to him to the poor. And so he also, because he keepeth nothing for himself, hath dispersed all his goods, hath given to the poor; his justice remaineth for ever and ever. And this is that wise foolishness which the publican had gathered from the sycamore as the fruit of life: to wit, to restore what was seized, to leave one's own, to despise the visible, to desire even to die for the invisible, to deny oneself, and to long to follow the footsteps of the Lord who is not yet seen.
atquialiquafraudesustulitprimoheciuxtale.la: At qui áliqua fraude sústulit, primo hæc juxta legem reddere, deínde quod sibi remanserit, debet dare paupéribus. Ac sic et ipse, quia sibi nil retinet, ómnia sua dispergit, dat paupéribus, justítia ejus manet in sǽculum sǽculi. Et hæc est sápiens illa stultitia quam de sycomoro publicanus quasi fructum vitæ legerat: rapta vidélicet reddere, própria relínquere, visibilia contemnere, pro invisibilibus étiam mori desideráre, seípsum abnegare, et ejus, qui necdum videátur, Dómini vestígia sequi concupíscere.

exepistolaprimasanctifelicispapequarti.en: From the first Epistle of St. Felix the Fourth, Pope.
exepistolaprimasanctifelicispapequarti.la: Ex Epístola prima sancti Felícis Papæ quarti.

tabernaculummoysendominoprecipientefecis.en: We read that Moses, at the Lord's command, made and hallowed the tabernacle, with its table and altar, and the other vessels and utensils for fulfilling the divine worship: and we know that he not only hallowed them with divine prayers, but also, at the Lord's bidding, anointed them with the unction of holy oil. And in what manner these things were done, and how none other than the priests, anointed with the holy unction and consecrated to the Lord with holy vestments, and the Levites, handled these sacred things, carried them, set them up and took them down, is found in the law of the Lord, in those very institutions which at the Lord's command were written by Moses.
tabernaculummoysendominoprecipientefecis.la: Tabernáculum Móysen, Dómino præcipiente, fecísse et sacrasse, cum mensa et altári ejus, et céteris vasis et utensilibus ad divínum cultum explendum, legimus: et non solum divínis précibus ea sacrasse, sed étiam sancti ólei unctióne, Dómino jubente, perlinisse novimus. Qualiter autem hæc facta sint, et quómodo ipsa sacra non álii, quam sacerdótes sacra unctióne delibuti, Dominoque cum véstibus sanctis sacrati, et Levitæ tractabant, ferebant, erigebant et deponebant: in ipsis institutionibus, quæ jubente Dómino conscriptæ sunt per Móysen, in lege Dómini reperitur.

qualiterergodavidregumpiissimusamplifica.en: In what manner therefore David, the most pious of kings, enlarged the worship of God, and would have built a temple to the Lord, but was forbidden because of the much blood which he had shed, and himself had gathered the expenses; and how Solomon also, his son, by the command and with the help of God, accomplished that very thing which he had desired to do, and consecrated the temple with the altar and the rest for performing the divine worship: is read in the book of Kings. Solomon therefore made at that time a solemn feast, and all Israel with him, a great multitude, from the entrance of Emath to the river of Egypt, before the Lord our God seven days and seven days, that is, fourteen days, and on the eighth day he sent away the people.
qualiterergodavidregumpiissimusamplifica.la: Qualiter ergo David, regum piíssimus, amplificaverit cultum Dei, et templumDomino ædificare volúerit, sed propter multum sánguinem quem effuderat, prohibitus est, et ipse collegerat expensas: Salomon quoque, fílius ejus idípsum, quod ipse fácere optaverat, jubente et auxiliante Deo perfécit, et templum cum altári, et réliqua ad divínum cultum peragéndum consecrávit: in libro Regum légitur. Fecit ergo Salomon in témpore illo festivitátem celebrem, et omnis Israël cum eo, multitúdo magna ab introitu Emath usque ad rivum Ægýpti, coram Dómino Deo nostro septem diébus, et septem diébus, id est, quatuórdecim diébus, et in die octáva dimísit pópulos.

solemnitatesdedicationumecclesiarumetsac.en: The solemnities of the dedications of churches and of priests are to be solemnly celebrated every year, the Lord himself giving the example, who came to the feast of the dedication of the temple, to celebrate the same festival with the rest of the people, giving to all the pattern of doing so; as it is written: And it was the feast of the dedication at Jerusalem: and it was winter. And Jesus walked in the temple, in Solomon's porch. And that the dedication is to be celebrated for eight days, ye will find in the book of Kings, when the dedication of the temple was ended.
solemnitatesdedicationumecclesiarumetsac.la: Solemnitates dedicationum ecclesiárum et sacerdótum, per síngulos annos solémniter sunt celebrandæ, ipso Dómino exémplum dante, qui ad festum dedicationis templi, ómnibus id faciéndi dans formam, cum réliquis pópulis eámdem festivitátem celebratúrus venit, sicut scriptum est: Facta sunt encænia in Jerosólymis, et hiems erat, et ambulabat Jesus in templo in pórticu Salomonis. Quod autem octo diébus encænia sint celebranda, in libro Regum, perácta dedicatione templi, reperietis.

inhomiliaryhiemdetempdomipostepiph.en: In the Winter Homilies, on the Season, the First Sunday after the Epiphany
inhomiliaryhiemdetempdomipostepiph.la: In Homiliary Hiem de Temp. dom. I post Epiph.

materiesuinquitevangelistaconservabatomn.en: His mother, saith the Evangelist, kept all these words in her heart. Let us also, my brethren, imitate the loving Mother of the Lord, by keeping ourselves also all the words and deeds of our Lord and Saviour fixed in our heart. By meditation day and night on these words and deeds of the Lord let us drive back the troublesome assaults of vain and hurtful thoughts: by frequent converse upon them let us take care both to restrain ourselves and our neighbours from idle fables and from the ill-sweetened talk of detraction, and to come to the frequent praise of God. Let us learn therefore the chastity of the holy Virgin in all things, who, no less modest in mouth than in body, kept the arguments of faith in her heart.
materiesuinquitevangelistaconservabatomn.la: Mater Jesu, inquit Evangelísta, conservábat ómnia verba hæc in corde suo. Imitémur et nos, fratres mei, piam Dómini Matrem, ipsi quoque ómnia verba et facta Dómini ac Salvatóris nostri fixo in corde conservándo. Horum Dómini verbórum et actórum meditatióne diúrna et noctúrna importúnos inánium nocentiúmque cogitatiónum repellámus incúrsus: horum crebra collatióne et nos et próximos nostros a fábulis supervácuis et male dulcorátis detractiónum collóquiis castigáre, atque ad divínæ frequéntiam laudis accédere curémus. Discámus ergo sanctæ Vírginis in ómnibus castitátem, quæ non minus ore pudíca, quam córpore, arguménta fidei conservábat in corde.

delaudibusvirgmatrishomiln.en: On the praises of the Virgin Mother, Homily 2, n. 3
delaudibusvirgmatrishomiln.la: De laudibus Virg. Matris Homil. 2, n. 3

letarepateradamsedmagistuohevamaterexsul.en: Rejoice, O father Adam, but more do thou, O mother Eve, exult; both, I say, be comforted over your daughter, and such a daughter. For the time is at hand when the reproach shall be taken away, and the man shall have no cause against the woman: who indeed, while he was imprudently trying to excuse himself, hesitated not cruelly to accuse her, saying: The woman, whom thou gavest me, gave me of the tree, and I did eat. Wherefore run, O Eve, to Mary; run, O mother, to thy daughter; let the daughter answer for the mother; let her make satisfaction for the mother: for behold, if the man fell through a woman, now he is not raised up save through a woman.
letarepateradamsedmagistuohevamaterexsul.la: Lætáre pater Adam, sed magis tu, o Heva, mater, exsúlta; ambo, inquam consolámini super fília, et tali fília. Instat namque tempus, quam jam tollátur oppróbrium, nec hábeat vir qui causétur advérsus féminam: qui útique, dum se imprudénter exsuráre conarétur, crudéliter illam accusáre non cunctátus est, dicens: Múlier quam dedísti mihi, dedit mihi de ligno, et comédi. Proptérea curre, Heva, ad Maríam; curre, mater, ad fíliam; fília pro matre respóndeat; ipsa pro matre satisfáciat: quia ecce si vir cécedit per féminam, jam non erígitur nisi per féminam.

indormitbmariehomilia.en: On the Falling-asleep of the B. Mary, homily 2

tutelatuaimmortalisestmarietintercessiov.en: Thy protection is immortal, O Mary; and thy intercession is life; and thy patronage perpetual. For unless thou didst go before, none would become spiritual; none would adore God in the Spirit. For then was man made spiritual, when thou, O Mother of God, wast made the dwelling of the Holy Ghost: none is filled with the knowledge of God save through thee, O most holy one. None is saved save through thee, O Mother of God; none is free from dangers save through thee, O Virgin Mother; none is redeemed save through thee, O Mother of God; none hath obtained the gift of mercy save through thee, O thou who wast worthy to contain God. For who so defendeth sinners? But thou, who art mighty with God by a mother's authority, obtainest the excellent grace of forgiveness even for them that sin grievously. For thou canst not but be heard, since God, as to his true and spotless Mother, in all things, and through all things, and in all things, doeth thy will. Hence rightly every afflicted one fleeth to thee; the weak cleaveth to thee; he that is assailed by war setteth thee against his enemies.
tutelatuaimmortalisestmarietintercessiov.la: Tutéla tua immortális est, María; et intercéssio, vita; et protéctio perpétua. Nisi enim, tu præíres, nemo spiritális eváderet; nemo in Spíritu Deum adoráret. Tunc enim spiritális factus est homo, cum tu, Deípara Spíritus Sancti habitáculum effécta es: nemo Dei cognitióne replétus est nisi per te, o sanctíssima. Nemo salvus nisi per te, o Deípara; nemo periculórum expers nisi per te, Virgo parens; nemo redémptus nisi per te Dei Mater; nemo domum per misericórdiam consecútus, nisi per te, o digna, quæ Deum cáperes. Quis enim tantópere peccatóres deféndit? Tu autem, quæ matérna auctoritáte in Deum pólleas, étiam iis qui enórmiter peccant, exímian remissiónis gratiam concílias. Non enim potes non exaudíri, cum Deus, ut veræ ac intemerátæ Matri suæ, quoad ómnia, et per ómnia, et in ómnibus, morem gerat. Hinc mérito, afflíctus quisque ad te cónfugit; infírmus tibi adhaéret; bello petítus te hóstibus oppónit.

quidadmariamaccederetrepidethumanafragil.en: Why should human frailty fear to approach to Mary? There is nothing harsh in her, nothing terrible; she is all sweet. Turn over more diligently the whole course of the Gospel history: and if perchance thou find in Mary anything of rebuke, anything hard, in fine any sign even of slight indignation, hold her henceforth suspect, and fear to approach her. But if thou find, as indeed they are, that all things that pertain to her are rather full of goodness and grace, full of meekness and mercy, give thanks to him who in his most kind compassion hath provided for thee such a mediatrix, in whom there can be nothing to suspect. Lastly, she hath been made all things to all; with most abundant charity she hath made herself a debtor to the wise and to the unwise. To all she openeth the bosom of her mercy, that all may receive of her fulness: the captive redemption, the sick healing, the sorrowful consolation, the sinner pardon, the just grace, the Angel joy. She discusseth not past merits, but showeth herself easy to be entreated by all, most merciful to all; lastly, she compassionateth the necessities of all with a most ample affection.
quidadmariamaccederetrepidethumanafragil.la: Quid ad Maríam accédere trépidet humána fragílitas? Nihil austérum in ea, nihil terríbile; tota suávis est. Revólve diligéntius evangélicæ históriæ sériem univérsam: et si quid forte increpatórium, si quid durum, si quod dénique signum vel ténuis indignatiónis occúrrerit in María, de cétero suspéctam hábeas, et accédere vereáris. Quod si, ut vere sunt, plena magis ómnia pietátis et grátiæ, plena mansuetúdinis et misericórdiæ, quæ ad eam pértinent, invéneris, age grátias ei, qui talem tibi mediatrícem benigníssima miseratione provídit, in qua nihil possit esse suspéctum. Dénique ómnibus ómnia facta est, sapiéntibus et insipiéntibus copiosíssima caritáte debitrícem se fecit. Omnibus misericórdiæ sinum ejus áperit, ut de plenitúdine ejus accípiant univérsi, captívus redemptiónem, æger curatiónem, tristis consolatiónem, peccátor véniam, justus grátiam, Angelus lætítiam. Ipsa prætérita non díscutit mérita, sed ómnibus sese exorábilem, ómnibus clementíssimam præbet, ómnium dénique necessitátes amplíssimo quodam miserátur afféctu.

sitperteexcusabilequodperteingerimusfiat.en: Through thee may that be excused which through thee we bring before him; may that be granted which with faithful mind we ask. Receive what we offer, grant in return what we ask, excuse what we fear, for thou art the only hope of sinners. Through thee we hope for the pardon of our offences, and in thee, most blessed one, is the expectation of our rewards. Holy Mary, succour the wretched; help the faint-hearted; comfort the sorrowful; pray for the people; plead for the clergy; intercede for the devout female sex: let all feel thy help, whosoever celebrate thy holy commemoration.
sitperteexcusabilequodperteingerimusfiat.la: Sit per te excusábile quod per te ingérimus; fiat impetrábile quod fida mente póscimus. Accípe quod offérimus, redóna quod rogámus, excúsa quod timémus, quia tu es spes única peccatórum. Per te sperámus véniam delictórum et in te, beatíssima, nostrórum est expectátio præmiórum. Sancta María, succúrre míseris; juva pusillánimes; réfove flébiles; ora pro pópulo; intérveni pro clero; intercéde pro devóto femíneo sexu: séntiant omnes tuum juvámen, quicúmque célebrant tuam sanctam commemoratiónem.

infestovisitbmvhom.en: On the feast of the Visitation of the B.V.M., Homily 2

magnificatanimameadominumetexultavitspir.en: My soul doth magnify the Lord: and my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour. Which words, though they rightly befit all the perfect, yet it most became the blessed Mother of God to utter them, who, singular by the privilege of her merit, burned with spiritual love of him in whose bodily conception she rejoiced. Who rightly could exult with a special joy above the other saints in Jesus, that is, in her Saviour; because him whom she knew to be the everlasting author of salvation, she knew was to be born of her flesh by a temporal birth, so that in one and the same person he was truly both her son and her Lord.
magnificatanimameadominumetexultavitspir.la: Magníficat ánima mea Dóminum; et exultávit spíritus meus in Deo salutári meo. Quæ cum ómnibus perféctis verba recte convéniant, máxime tamen ea beátam Dei Genitrícem proférre decébat, quæ mériti privilégio singuláris spirituáli ipsíus dilectióne flagrábat, cujus corporáli conceptióne gaudébat. Quæ jure in Jesu, id est, in salutári suo speciáli præ céteris sanctis gáudio pótuit exultáre, quia quem perpétuum salútis auctórem nóverat, hunc ipsum temporáli ortu de carne sua nascitúrum esse sciébat quátenus in una eadémque persóna veráciter suus et filius esset et Dóminus.

quamviliadeseipsasenseritedocetetquodomn.en: She teacheth how lowly she thought of herself, and that whatever good of merit she had, she received it by the bounty of heavenly grace, saying: Because he hath regarded the humility of his handmaid: for behold from henceforth all generations shall call me blessed. For she showeth that in her own judgment she had been a lowly handmaid of Christ, but declareth that by the regard of heavenly grace she was suddenly exalted, and so greatly glorified, that her pre-eminent blessedness is rightly wondered at by the voice of all nations. She added also the gifts of the divine goodness, which she had wondrously received, praising them with worthy thanksgiving: Because he that is mighty hath done great things to me; and holy is his name. She attributeth nothing therefore to her own merits, who referreth all her greatness to the gift of him who, being essentially mighty and great, is wont to make his faithful, from little and weak, strong and great.
quamviliadeseipsasenseritedocetetquodomn.la: Quam vília de seípsa sénserit édocet, et quod omne quidquid boni mériti hábuit, hoc supérna grátia largiénte percéperit, dicens: Quia respéxit humilitátem ancíllæ suæ: ecce enim ex hoc beátam me dicent omnes generatiónes. Húmilem quippe Christi ancíllam suo judício se fuisse demónstrat, sed respéctu se grátiæ celéstis repénte sublimátam pronúntiat, atque in tantum glorificátam, ut sua beatitúdo præcípua mérito cunctárum géntium voce mirétur. Addidit étiam adhuc divínæ pietátis múnera, quæ mirabíliter accépit, digna gratiárum actióne colláudans. Quia fecit mihi magna qui potens est, et sanctum nomen ejus. Nihil ergo suis méritis tríbuit, quæ totam magnitúdinem ad illíus donum refert, qui essentiáliter potens et magnus exístens, fidéles suos de parvis atque infírmis fortes fácere consuévit, et magnos.

beatamariavirgointerhominesaudiresolamer.en: The blessed Virgin Mary alone among men merited to hear before all: Thou hast found grace. How much? As much as he had said: full. And truly full, which should pour itself upon and into the whole creation with a bountiful shower: for thou hast found grace with God. When he saith these things, the Angel himself also marvelleth, either that a woman alone, or that all men had merited life through a woman: the Angel is astonished that the whole God should come within the narrow confines of a virgin's womb, for whom the whole creation together is narrow. Hence it is that the Angel tarrieth, hence it is that he calleth the virgin by her merit, addresseth her by grace, scarcely revealeth the cause to her as she heareth, that he may raise her understanding, and scarcely calmeth her after her long trembling.
beatamariavirgointerhominesaudiresolamer.la: Beáta María Virgo, inter hómines audíre sola méruit præ ómnibus: invenísti grátiam. Quantam? Quantam díxerat: plenam. Et vere plenam, quæ largo imbre totam fúnderet et infúnderet creatúram: invenísti enim grátiam apud Deum. Hæc cum dicit, et ipse Angelus mirátur, aut féminam tantum, aut omnes hómines vitam meruísse per féminam: stupet Angelus, totum Deum veníre intra virginális úteri angústias, cui tota simul angústa est creatúra. Hinc est, quod remorátur Angelus, hinc est, quod vírginem vocat de mérito, de grátia compéllat, vix causam prodit audiénti, sane ut sensum promóveat, vix longa trepidatióne compónit.

cuminsuaestimationetamhumilisessetmarian.en: Though Mary was so lowly in her own esteem, she was nevertheless also great-souled in believing the promise; so that she who reckoned herself nothing else but a little handmaid doubted not in any wise that she was chosen for this incomprehensible mystery, and believed that she would presently be the true Mother of God and man. This truly doth the privilege of divine grace work in the hearts of the elect, that neither doth humility make them faint-hearted, nor greatness of soul arrogant: but rather they work together, so that not only doth no exaltation creep in from greatness of soul, but thence chiefly is humility advanced: that they may be found the more God-fearing, and not ungrateful to the giver of gifts; and in turn, that no faint-heartedness may steal in on the occasion of humility; but the less each one is wont to presume of himself even in the least things, the more may they trust in the divine power even in all great things.
cuminsuaestimationetamhumilisessetmarian.la: Cum in sua æstimatióne tam húmilis esset María, nihilóminus et in promissiónis credulitáte magnánimis, ut quæ nihil áliud quam exíguam sese reputábat ancíllam, ad incomprehensíbile hoc mystérium nullátenus se dubitáret eléctam, et veram Dei et hóminis Genetrícem créderet mox futúram. Agit hoc nimírum in córdibus electórum grátiæ prærogatíva divínæ, ut eos nec humílitas pusillánimes fáciat, nec magnanímitas arrogántes: magis autem cooperéntur sibi, ut non solum nulla ex magnanimitáte subíntret elátio, sed hinc máxime provehátur humílitas: ut inveniántur eo ámplius timoráti, et largitóri múnerum non ingráte, ac vicíssim ex occasióne humilitátis pusillanímitas nulla subrépat; sed quo minus de sua quisque vel in mínimis præsúmere consuévit, eo ámplius étiam in magnis quibúsque de divína virtúte confídant.

obsecrovosfilioliemulaminimansuetudinems.en: I beseech you, my little children, emulate her meekness, if ye love Mary; if ye strive to please her, emulate her modesty. For nothing is so fitting for man, nothing so becoming to a Christian, and nothing so beseemeth above all a monk. And indeed the virtue of humility shineth forth clearly enough in the Virgin from this very meekness. Truly humility and meekness are foster-sisters. For as pride is the mother of presumption, so true meekness proceedeth only from true humility.
obsecrovosfilioliemulaminimansuetudinems.la: Obsecro vos, filíoli, æmulámini mansuetúdinem, si Maríam dilígitis; si conténditis ei placére, æmulámini modéstiam ejus. Nihil enim tam idóneum hómini, nihil tam cóngruum christiáno, maximésque mónachum nihil adeo decet. Et quidem manifésta satis in Vírgine ex hac ipsa manuetúdine virtus humilitátis elúcet. Nimírum collactáneæ sunt humílitas et manuetúdo. Sicut enim mater præsumptiónis elátio, sic manuetúdo vera nonnísi ex vera humilitáte procédit.

cuiservatestvictorianisimarieipsaproculd.en: For whom was the victory reserved, but for Mary? She without doubt crushed the venomous head, who brought to nothing every suggestion of the wicked one, as well from the allurement of the flesh as from the pride of the mind. And what other woman was Solomon seeking, when he said: Who shall find a valiant woman? For the wise man knew the weakness of this sex, its frail body, its slippery mind. Yet because he had read that God had promised, and saw that it was fitting, that he who had conquered through a woman should be conquered through her, he said, greatly marvelling: Who shall find a valiant woman? That is to say: If thus both the salvation of us all, and the restoration of innocence, and the victory over the enemy hang upon the hand of a woman; it is altogether necessary that a valiant one be provided, who may be fit for so great a work.
cuiservatestvictorianisimarieipsaproculd.la: Cui serváta est victória, nisi Maríæ? Ipsa procul dúbio caput contrívit venenátum, quæ omnímodam malígni suggestiónem tam de carnis illécebra, quam de mentis supérbia dedúxit ad níhilum. Quam vero áliam Sálomon requirébat, cum dicébat: Mulíerem fortem quis invéniet? Nóverat quippe vir sápiens hujus sexus infirmitátem, frágile corpus, lúbricam mentem. Quia tamen et Deum légerat promisísse, et ita vidébat congrúere, ut qui vícerat per féminam, vincerétur per ipsam, veheménter admírans ajébat: Mulíerem fortem quis invéniet? Quod est dícere: Si ita de manu féminæ pendet et nostra ómnium salus, et innocéntiæ restitútio, et de hoste victória; fortis omníno necésse est ut provideátur, quæ ad tantum opus possit esse idónea.

totisergomedulliscordiumtotisprecordioru.en: With all the marrow of our hearts therefore, with all the affections of our breasts, and with all our desires, let us venerate this Mary; for such is the will of him who willed that we should have all through Mary. This, I say, is his will, but for our sakes. My little children, she is the sinners' ladder, she is my greatest confidence, she is the whole ground of my hope. For what? Can the Son either repel her, or suffer a repulse? Can the Son not hear, or not be heard? Neither, plainly. Thou hast found, saith the Angel, grace with God. Happily so. She will ever find grace, and it is grace alone that we need; truly it is grace alone whereby we are saved. Why do we desire other things, brethren? Let us seek grace, and let us seek it through Mary, for what she seeketh she findeth, and cannot be disappointed. Let us seek grace, but grace with God: for with men favour is deceitful. Let others seek merit; let us study to find grace. For what? Is it not of grace that we are here? Truly it is of the mercies of the Lord that we are not consumed.
totisergomedulliscordiumtotisprecordioru.la: Totis ergo medúllis córdium, totis præcordiórum afféctibus, et votis ómnibus Maríam hanc venerémur; quia sic est volúntas ejus, qui totum nos habére vóluit per Maríam. Hæc, inquam, volúntas ejus est, sed pro nobis. Filíoli, hæc peccatórum scala, hæc mea máxima fidúcia est, hæc tota rátio spei meæ. Quid enim? Potéstne Fílius aut repéllere, aut sustinére repúlsam? Non audíre, aut non audíri Fílius potest? Neutrum plane. Invenísti, ait Angelus, grátiam apud Deum. Felíciter. Semper hæc invéniet grátiam, et sola est grátia qua egémus; nimírum sola est grátia, qua salvámur. Quid nos ália concupíscimus, fratres? Quærámus grátiam, et per Maríam quærámus, quia quod quærit, ínvenit, et frustrári non potest. Quærámus grátiam, sed grátiam apud Deum: nam apud hómines grátia fallax. Quærant álii méritum, nos inveníre grátiam studeámus. Quid enim? Num grátiæ est quod hic sumus? Profécto misericórdiæ Dómini est, quod non sumus consúmpti nos.

quiddicebasoadammulierquamdedistimihided.en: What didst thou say, O Adam? The woman, whom thou gavest me, gave me of the tree, and I did eat. These are words of malice, whereby thou rather increasest than blottest out thy fault. Yet Wisdom hath conquered malice. For a woman is given for a woman, a wise one for a foolish, a humble one for a proud; who, instead of the tree of death, may offer thee the taste of life, and instead of that poisonous food of bitterness, may bring forth the sweetness of the eternal fruit. Change therefore the word of wicked excuse into the voice of thanksgiving, and say: Lord, the woman whom thou gavest me, gave me of the tree of life, and I did eat; and it is become sweeter than honey to my mouth, because in it thou hast quickened me. For behold, to this end was the Angel sent to the Virgin. O Virgin to be admired and most worthy of all honour! O woman to be venerated, wonderful above all women, the restorer of our parents, the quickener of their posterity!
quiddicebasoadammulierquamdedistimihided.la: Quid dicébas, o Adam? Múlier quam dedísti mihi, dedit mihi de ligno, et comédi. Verba malítiæ sunt hæc, quibus magis áugeas quam déleas culpam. Verúmtamen Sapiéntia vicit malítiam. Rédditur nempe fémina pro fémina, prudens pro fátua, húmilis pro supérba; quæ pro lingo mortis gustum tibi pórrigat vitæ, et pro venenóso cibo illo amaritúdinis, dulcédinem páriat fructus ætérni. Muta ergo iníque excusatiónis verbum in vocem gratiárum actiónis, et dic: Dómine, múlier quam dedísti mihi, dedit me de ligno vitæ, et comédi; et dulce factum est super mel ori meo, quia in ipso vivificásti me. Ecce enim ad hoc missus est Angelus ad Vírginem. O admirándam et omni honóre digníssimam Vírginem! O féminam venerándam, super omnes féminas admirábilem, paréntum reparatrícem, posterórum vivificatrícem!

missusestangelusadvirginemvirginemcarnev.en: The Angel was sent to the Virgin; a virgin in flesh, a virgin in mind, a virgin by profession, a virgin in fine such as the Apostle describeth, holy in mind and body; not newly nor by chance found, but chosen from the beginning, foreknown by the Most High and prepared for himself, kept by the Angels, foreshadowed by the Fathers, promised by the Prophets. To say a few things out of many, what other woman doth God seem to thee to have foretold, when he saith to the serpent: I will put enmities between thee and the woman? And if thou still doubtest whether he spoke of Mary, hear what followeth: She shall crush thy head. For whom was this victory reserved, but for Mary?
missusestangelusadvirginemvirginemcarnev.la: Missus est Angelus ad Vírginem; vírginem carne, vírginem mente, vírginem professióne, vírginem dénique, qualem descríbit Apóstolus, mente et córpore sanctam; nec nóviter, nec fortuíto invéntam, sed a sǽculo eléctam, ab Altíssimo præcógnitam, et sibi præparátam, ab Angelis servátam, a Pátribus præsignátam, a Prophétis promíssam. Ut pauca loquar de plúribus, quam tibi áliam prædixísse Deus vidétur, quando ad serpéntem ait: Inimicítias ponam inter te et mulíerem? Et si adhuc dúbitas an de María díxerit, audi quod séquitur: Ipsa cónteret caput tuum. Cui hæc serváta victória est, nisi Maríæ?

beataprogeniesundechristusnatusest.en: Blessed is the stock from which Christ was born.
beataprogeniesundechristusnatusest.la: Beáta progénies, unde Christus natus est.

oquamgloriosestvirgoqueceliregemgenuit.en: O how glorious is the Virgin, who brought forth the King of heaven!
oquamgloriosestvirgoqueceliregemgenuit.la: O quam gloriósa est Virgo, quæ cæli Regem génuit!

felixnamquesessacravirgomarietomnilauded.en: For happy art thou, O holy Virgin Mary, and most worthy of all praise.
felixnamquesessacravirgomarietomnilauded.la: Felix namques es, sacra Virgo Mária, et omni laude digníssima.

myrrhetguttetcasiaavestimentistuisagradi.en: Myrrh and stacte and cassia perfume thy garments, from the ivory steps: out of which the daughters of kings have delighted thee in thy honour.
myrrhetguttetcasiaavestimentistuisagradi.la: Myrrha et gutta et cásia a vestiméntis tuis, a grádibus ebúrneis, ex quibus delectavérunt te fíliæ regum in honóre tuo.

benedictetvenerabilisesvirgomaria.en: Blessed and venerable art thou, O Virgin Mary,
benedictetvenerabilisesvirgomaria.la: Benedícta et venerábilis es, Virgo María,

cuiusvisceramerueruntportaredominumchris.en: Whose womb merited to bear Christ the Lord.
cuiusvisceramerueruntportaredominumchris.la: Cujus víscera meruérunt portáre Dóminum Christum.

canutusquartussuenonisesthritiidanorumre.en: Canute the Fourth, son of Sweyn Estridsen, king of the Danes, conspicuous for faith, piety, and uprightness of manners, gave from his tender years a pattern of excellent holiness. Having obtained his father's sceptre with the highest acclamation of all, he began to apply himself diligently to the furthering of religion, to increase the churches with revenues, and to adorn them with precious furniture. Then, burning with zeal for spreading the faith, he attacked barbarous kingdoms in just warfare, and brought the conquered and subject nations under the Christian law. And being glorious with very many victories, and increased in riches, he cast down his royal diadem at the feet of Christ crucified, subjecting himself and his kingdom to him who is King of kings and Lord of lords. He chastised his body with fasts, hair-shirts and scourges. He was ever constant in prayer and contemplation, lavish toward the poor, beneficent toward all: nor did he ever turn aside from the path of justice and of the divine law.
canutusquartussuenonisesthritiidanorumre.la: Canutus quartus, Suenonis Esthritii Danorum regis filius, fide, pietate et morum honestate conspicuus, eximiæ sanctitatis a teneris annis specimen dedit. Paternum sceptrum summa omnium acclamatione adeptus, religioni promovendæ sedulo incumbere, ecclesias reditibus augere, et pretiosa supellectili ornare cœpit. Tum zelo propagandæ fidei succensus, barbara regna justo certamine aggressus, devictas subditasque nationes christianæ legi subjugavit. Victoriis autem plurimis gloriosus, et divitiis auctus, regale diadema ad Christi crucifixi pedes abjecit, se et regnum illi subjiciens, qui Rex regum est, et Dominus dominantium. Corpus suum jejuniis, ciliciis et flagellis castigavit. In oratione et contemplatione assiduus, erga pauperes profusus, erga omnes beneficus semper fuit: nec umquam a justitiæ divinæque legis semita deflexit.

hisaliisquevirtutibusimbutusadsupremumpe.en: Endowed with these and other virtues, the holy king was hastening to the highest summit of perfection. Now it happened that the kingdom of England was invaded by William, duke of the Normans, with a formidable army. And when the English implored the help of the Danes, and the king had resolved to succour them, he committed the conduct of the war to Olaf his brother. Who, enticed by the desire of reigning, turned his arms to the king's destruction, stirring up the soldiers and the people against him. Nor were incitements to the rebellion lacking. For when the king, by laws put forth, had ordained that tithes should be paid to the churches, that the precepts of God and of the Church should be observed, and that transgressors should be punished, very many perverse and wicked men, being embittered, began first to make tumult, then to stir up the common people, and at length to plot the death of the most holy king.
hisaliisquevirtutibusimbutusadsupremumpe.la: His aliisque virtutibus imbutus, ad supremum perfectionis apicem sanctus rex properabat. Accidit autem ut Angliæ regnum a Wilhelmo Normandorum duce, formidabili exercitu invaderetur. Anglis vero, Danorum opem implorantibus, cum succurrere rex decrevisset, belli expeditionem Olao fratri commisit. Qui regnandi cupiditate illectus, arma vertit in regis perniciem, militibus et populo contra illum concitatis. Nec defuerunt rebellioni fomenta. Cum enim rex, editis legibus, decimas ecclesiis solvi, Dei et Ecclesiæ præcepta servari, transgressores puniri sanxisset, plerique perversi ac scelerati homines exacerbati, primum quidem tumultuari, tum plebem commovere, ac tandem sanctissimo regi necem moliri cœperunt.

sciensigiturrexfuturorumpresciusmortemsi.en: The king therefore, foreknowing the things to come, and knowing that death was at hand for him for justice' sake, having foretold it, went to the church of St. Alban the Martyr at Odense, as to the place of combat: and being fortified with the sacraments, he commended his agony to the Lord. Soon the multitude of the conspirators, coming thither, tried to set fire to the church, to break down the doors and to burst in. And when they could not accomplish this, approaching the windows, they ceased not to hurl with great violence stones and arrows at the holy king, who was praying on bended knees for his enemies: until, pierced by the blows of stones and darts, and at length by a lance, falling down before the altar with outstretched arms, he was crowned with a glorious martyrdom, Gregory the Seventh then sitting on the apostolic throne. God afterwards made his Martyr illustrious by many miracles. For Denmark, oppressed by grievous famine and divers calamities, paid the penalty of the sacrilege committed. Many also, afflicted with divers sicknesses, obtained remedy and health at his tomb. And when the queen tried secretly to carry off his sacred body by night and to translate it elsewhere, she was terrified by a great brightness sent from heaven, and desisted from her purpose.
sciensigiturrexfuturorumpresciusmortemsi.la: Sciens igitur rex, futurorum præscius, mortem sibi propter justitiam imminere; ea prænuntiata, ad ecclesiam sancti Albani Martyris Othoniæ, tamquam ad locum certaminis, profectus est: et sacramentis munitus, agonem suum Domino commendabat. Mox ibi adveniens conjuratorum multitudo, ecclesiæ ignem admovere, fores confringere et in eam irrumpere tentarunt. Quod cum perficere non possent, ad fenestras accedentes, saxa et sagittas in sanctum regem, flexis genibus pro inimicis orantem, magno impetu jaculari non cessarunt: donec lapidum et telorum ictibus, ac tandem lancea confossus, glorioso martyrio, ante altare extensis brachiis procumbens, coronatus est, sedente in apostolico throno Gregorio septimo. Multis postea miraculis Martyrem suum illustravit Deus. Nam gravi penuria et diversis calamitatibus oppressa Dania, patrati sacrilegii pœnas luit. Plures étiam variis languoribus afflicti, ad ejus tumulum remedium et incolumitatem consecuti sunt. Cumque regina sacrum ejus corpus noctu clam surripere, et alio transferre conaretur, emisso cælitus ingenti splendore perterrita, a proposito cessavit.

anicetussyrusimperatoremarcoaurelioanton.en: Anicetus, a Syrian, ruled the Church in the time of the emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus. He decreed that clerics should not let their hair grow long. Five times in the month of December he ordained seventeen priests, four deacons, and nine bishops for divers places. He lived in the pontificate eight years, eight months, and twenty-four days. Crowned with martyrdom for the faith of Christ, he was buried on the Appian Way in the cemetery which was afterwards called that of Callistus, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of May.
anicetussyrusimperatoremarcoaurelioanton.la: Anicetus Syrus, imperatore Marco Aurelio Antonino, praefuit Ecclesiae. Decrevit ne clerici comam nutrirent. Quinquies mense Decembri ordinavit presbyteros decem et septem, diaconos quatuor, episcopos per diversa loca novem. Vixit in pontificatu annos octo, menses octo, dies viginti quatuor. Propter Christi fidem martyrio coronatus, sepultus est via Appia in ccemeterio, quod postea Callisti appellatum est, decimo quinto Kalendas Majas.

deusquisancteritetantamgratiamconferredi.en: O God, who didst vouchsafe to bestow upon Saint Rita so great grace that she loved her enemies, and bore in her heart and on her brow the marks of thy charity and passion: grant us, we beseech thee, by her intercession and merits, so to spare our enemies and to contemplate the sorrows of thy passion, that we may attain the rewards promised to the meek and to them that mourn:
deusquisancteritetantamgratiamconferredi.la: Deus, qui sanctæ Ritæ tantam grátiam conférre dignátus es, ut inimícos dilígeret et in corde ac fronte caritátis et passiónis tuæ signa portáret: da nobis, quǽsumus, ejus intercessióne et méritis; inimícis nostris sic párcere et passiónis tuæ dolóres contemplári, ut promíssa mítibus ac lugéntibus prǽmia consequámur:

petronillasanctipetrifiliavirgoformacorp.en: Petronilla, the daughter of St. Peter, was a virgin of excellent beauty of body, but much more excellent in beauty of soul: when she was sick, blessed Peter was asked why he, who healed others, did not restore health to his own daughter; he answered: Because it is expedient for her. Yet, that he might leave to none room to doubt of his power, he bade her rise from her bed and serve the guests. A little after she fell back into the same sickness; and when at length she had recovered from it, Count Flaccus, moved by her fame, loved her without even having seen her, and earnestly strove that she should be given him in marriage.
petronillasanctipetrifiliavirgoformacorp.la: Petronilla, sancti Petri filia, virgo forma corporis eximia, sed animi pulchritudine multo præstantior fuit: quæ ægrota cum esset, à beato Petro quæsitum est, cur, qui alienos sanaret, filiæ suæ sanitatem non restitueret? respondit: quia sic expedit ei. Veruntamen, ut nemini de sua potestate dubitandi locum relinqueret, eam furgere jussit è lecto, et conuiuis ministrare. Quæ paulo post in eundem morbum recides, ex eo cum aliquando conualuisset, ejus fama cómotus, ne visam quidem Flaccus Comes adamauit, enixeq. contendit, ut sibi daretur in matrimonium.

petronillaautemintelligensvirginitatisue.en: But Petronilla, perceiving that snares were being laid for her virginity, which she had dedicated to Jesus Christ, by the most bitter enemy of mankind, took a space of three days to deliberate, and spent all that time in fasting and prayer, constantly asking of her heavenly spouse that he would not suffer violence to be done to her holy purpose: and so on the third day God came to the help of the virgin: for, burning with the love of her divine spouse, when she had received the Eucharist, he called her to the heavenly nuptials. Her body, buried on the Ardeatine Way, was afterwards translated by Paul the First, Pontiff, into the Basilica of the prince of the Apostles.
petronillaautemintelligensvirginitatisue.la: Petronilla autem intelligens virginitati sue, quam Jesu Christo dicarat, ab acerrimo humani gene ris hoste parari insidias; sumpto sibi tridui spatio ad deliberandum, totum illud tepus in jejuniis, et oratione consumpsit, alliduè petens à cælesti sponso, ne sancto proposito suo vim afferri pateretur: itaque subuenic die tercio virgini Deus: nam eam diuini sponsi amore flagrantem, ubi Eucharistiam sumpsisset, ad cælestes nuptias euocauit. Cujus corpus in via Ardeatina sepultum, postea à Paulo primo pontifice in Basilicam principis Apostolorum translatum est.

brevepiixdieisept.en: Brief of Pius X of 18 Sept. 1908

sermoaliasepistoladegazophylacio.en: Sermon, otherwise Epistle 34, on the Treasury

libadversusheresescapaliasnum.en: Book 3 against Heresies, ch. 18, otherwise 20, nn. 5-6
libadversusheresescapaliasnum.la: Lib. 3 adversus Haereses cap. 18, alias 20, num. 5-6

sanctamariasuccurremiserisiuvapusillanim.en: Holy Mary, succour the wretched, help the faint-hearted, comfort the sorrowful, pray for the people, plead for the clergy, intercede for the devout female sex: let all feel thy help, whosoever celebrate thy solemn Commemoration.
sanctamariasuccurremiserisiuvapusillanim.la: Sancta María, succurre míseris, juva pusillánimes, réfove flébiles, ora pro pópulo, intérveni pro clero, intercéde pro devóto femíneo sexu: séntiant omnes tuum juvámen, quicúmque célebrant tuam solémnem Commemoratiónem.

exiissocietatisiesusodalibusquiecclesiei.en: Of those members of the Society of Jesus who most adorned the beginnings of the Church in North America about the middle of the seventeenth century, God chose eight most pure victims for himself, that the seeds of faith, watered with their blood, might thereafter grow up into more abundant harvests. All these Martyrs, born in France and, except two laymen, raised to the priesthood, were sent by their Superiors into the Canadian Mission, which was then called New France; and after innumerable apostolic journeys from the city of Quebec through those various immense regions, and most severe labours for one and the same cause of religion, though not at one and the same time nor place, they were most cruelly put to death. As the leaders and masters of these are rightly reckoned John de Brebeuf, born of a noble family at Condé in the diocese formerly of Bayeux, now of Coutances, and Isaac Jogues, of Orleans, men burning with a strenuous and apostolic zeal, greatly given to mortification, most closely united to God in prayer, and sometimes enlightened also by heavenly visions. Not unlike them were their four companions, priests: Anthony Daniel, of Dieppe, Gabriel Lalemant and Charles Garnier, of Paris, and Noel Chabanel, of Mende; who all faithfully discharged the sacred ministry in various villages, chiefly among the Hurons.
exiissocietatisiesusodalibusquiecclesiei.la: Ex iis Societatis Jesu sodalibus, qui Ecclesiæ in America boreali exordia medio sæculo septimo maxime illustrarunt, octo purissimas hostias sibi elegit Deus, ut fidei semina earum sanguine irrigata in uberiores segetes deínde succrescerent.
