Omnes hi Martyres, in Gallia nati et, præter duos laicos, sacerdotio aucti, in Missionem Canadensem, quæ Novæ Galliæ tunc vocabatur, a Superioribus missi, post innumeros ex urbe Quebecensi per varias illas immensas regiones apostolicos excursus, asperrimosque labores ob unam eamdemque religionis causam, etsi non uno eodemque tempore nec loco, crudelissime necati sunt. Horum veluti duces ac magistri merito censentur Joannes de Brebeuf, Condæi in diocesi olim Baiocensi nunc Constantiensi nobili genere ortus, et Isaacus Jogues, aurelianensis, viri strenuo et apostolico zelo incensi, mortificationi maxime dediti, cum Deo in oratione conjunctissimi, cælestibus étiam visionibus quandoque illustrati. Ab iis haud absimiles erant quatuor socii sacerdotes Antonius Daniel, dieppensis, Gabriel Lalemant et Carolus Garnier, parisienses, Natalis Chabanel, mimatensis; qui omnes variis in pagis potissimum inter Hurones sacris muneribus fideliter fungebantur.

sanctituidominemirabileconsecutisuntiter.en: Thy Saints, O Lord, have followed a wonderful way, serving thy commandments, that they might be found unhurt in the mighty waters:
sanctituidominemirabileconsecutisuntiter.la: Sancti tui, Domine, mirabile consecuti sunt iter, servientes præceptis tuis, ut invirentur illæsi in aquis validis:

frequentesfinitimorumiroquensiumincursio.en: The frequent inroads of the neighbouring Iroquois, often laying waste the Huron mission, not seldom brought the life of the Fathers into the utmost peril. In the year one thousand six hundred and forty-two, Isaac Jogues, with René Goupil, a temporal coadjutor of the Society of Jesus, while journeying from the city of Quebec to the Hurons, fell into the hands of the Iroquois, who tortured him and his companion most cruelly and reduced them to slavery. In the same year, on the twenty-ninth day of September, René, being ordered by a barbarous old man to be slain in hatred of the saving cross, breathed forth his most pure soul near Auriesville, in the present State of New York. Isaac, the next year, having found an occasion of escape, returned into France; but after a year, seeking America again, and going once and again to the same barbarians, formerly his executioners, with John de la Lande, likewise a coadjutor of the Society of Jesus, on the eighteenth day of October in the year one thousand six hundred and forty-six, in the present diocese of Albany, being struck with a hatchet, he obtained the palm of martyrdom. And on the following day his companion John, crowned with the same crown, flew away to heaven.
frequentesfinitimorumiroquensiumincursio.la: Frequentes finitimorum Iroquensium incursiones, Huronicam missionem sæpe vastantes, haud raro in supremum discrimen Patrum vitam vocabant. Anno millesimo sexcentesimo quadragesimo secundo, Isaacus Jogues, cum Renato Goupil, Societatis Jesu coadjutore temporali, ex urbe Quebecensi ad Hurones iter faciens, in Iroquenses incidit, qui eum ejusque socium dirissime torquent et in servitutem redigunt. Eodem anno die vigesima nona Septembris, Renatus, in odium salutiferæ crucis a barbaro sene interfici jussus, prope Auriesville, in hodierno Neo-Eboracensi Statu, candidissimam animam efflavit. Isaacus anno proximo, aufugiendi occasionem nactus, in Galliam revertit; sed post annum Americam repetens et semel atque iterum ad eosdem barbaros, suos olim carnifices, cum Joanne de la Lande, Societatis Jesu item coadjutore, progressus, die decima octava Octobris anno millesimo sexcentesimo quadragesimo sexto, in hodierna diocesi Albanensi, acinace percussus martyrii palmam consecutus est. Postero vero die ejus socius Joannes, eadem redimitus corona, ad cælum evolavit.

annomillesimosexcentesimoquadragesimooct.en: In the year one thousand six hundred and forty-eight, on the fourth day of July, Anthony Daniel, who had the care of the village of St. Joseph among the Hurons, fearlessly defending his flock against the invading Iroquois, pierced with arrows and with fiery bullets, laid down his life at the doors of the church, a good shepherd for his sheep. In the following year, on the sixteenth day of March, John de Brebeuf, rightly called the apostle of the Hurons, being taken by the Iroquois together with Gabriel Lalemant, after long and most cruel tortures, the barbarians themselves marvelling at the unconquered fortitude of the champion of Christ, died gloriously in the village of St. Ignatius, in the region of Canada now called Ontario; whom on the morrow Gabriel Lalemant followed by the same bloody way and with the same virtue. And in the month of December of the same year one thousand six hundred and forty-nine, on the eve of the Immaculate Conception of the blessed Virgin Mary, Charles Garnier, pierced with wounds and struck with an axe, ended a most innocent life by a glorious death. Lastly, on the following day, Noel Chabanel, treacherously set upon by an apostate Huron and cast into a river, obtained the longed-for palm of martyrdom in the Mission so dear to him, to whose service, nature resisting in vain, he had bound himself for ever by a heroic vow. These eight first Martyrs of North America the Supreme Pontiff Pius the Eleventh, in the holy year one thousand nine hundred and twenty-five, enrolled among the Blessed, and five years later inscribed in the calendar of the Saints.
annomillesimosexcentesimoquadragesimooct.la: Anno millesimo sexcentesimo quadragesimo octavo, die quarta Julii Antonius Daniel, qui pagi Sancti Joseph inter Hurones curam gerebat, contra invasores Iroquenses gregem suum impavidus defendens, sagittis et ignitis glandibus confossus, ad templi fores bonus pastor pro ovibus animam posuit. Anno proximo, die decima sexta Martii, Joannes de Brebeuf, Huronum apostolus merito nuncupatus, una cum Gabriele Lalemant, ab Iroquensibus comprehensus, post diuturnos sævissimosque cruciatus, ipsis barbaris invictam Christi pugilis fortitudinem demirantibus, in pago Sancti Ignatii in hodierna Canadensi regione Ontario nuncupata, gloriosus occubuit; quem postridie Gabriel Lalemant eadem cruenta via eademque virtute secutus est. Mense autem Decembri ejusdem anni millesimi sexcentesimi quadragesimi noni, in pervigilio Immaculatæ Conceptionis beatæ Mariæ Virginis, Carolus Garnier, vulneribus confossus et securi percussus, innocentissimam vitam glorioso exitu conclusit. Postero demum die, Natalis Chabanel, ab Hurone apostata dolose invasus et in profluentem dejectus, in dilecta sibi Missione, cui perpetuo colendæ, natura frustra obsistente, heroico voto se obstrinxerat, optatam martyrii palmam adeptus est. Hos octo Americæ borealis primores Martyres Pius Undecimus Pontifex Maximus, anno sacro millesimo nongentesimo vigesimo quinto, Beatorum numero, eosque quinque post annis Sanctorum fastis ascripsit.

quiconfiduntinillumintellegentveritateme.en: They that trust in him shall understand the truth: and they that are faithful in love shall rest in him.
quiconfiduntinillumintellegentveritateme.la: Qui confidunt in illum, intellegent veritatem: et fideles in dilectione acquiescent illi.

noteinevangelicaslectionesindiefestoomni.en: Notes on the Gospel lessons: on the feast of All Saints, after the beginning
noteinevangelicaslectionesindiefestoomni.la: Notæ in evangelicas lectiones: in die festo Omnium Sanctorum, post initium

notabochristumlongealiterquamhuncmundumd.en: I shall note that Christ teacheth and declareth concerning blessedness far otherwise than this world. For it is proper to the world falsely to place man's happiness in perishable and fleeting things, which must be left here; just as if it were said: Happy is the people that hath these things. Nay rather, those whom Christ here declareth blessed, the foolish world accounteth only as wretched and unhappy, and is wont to despise and turn away from them; so that hence also Christ himself testifieth to the Apostles: Amen, amen I say to you, that you shall lament and weep, but the world shall rejoice: and you shall be made sorrowful. And rightly said Solomon: He that walketh in the right way, and feareth God, is despised by him that goeth by an infamous way.
notabochristumlongealiterquamhuncmundumd.la: Notabo Christum longe aliter quam hunc mundum, de beatitudine docere atque pronuntiare. Mundi etenim est proprium rebus caducis et fluxis, quæ hic relinquendæ sunt, mentiri hominis felicitatem, perinde ac si dicatur: Beatus populus, cui hæc sunt. Immo vero quos Christus beatos hic pronuntiat, eos insipiens mundus tantum pro miseris et infelicibus ducit, eosdem de more contemnit atque aversatur, ut hinc étiam Christus ipse testetur Apostolis: Amen, amen dico vobis, quia plorabitis et flebitis vos; mundus autem gaudebit, vos autem contristabimini. Recteque dixit Salomon: Ambulans recto itinere et timens Deum, despicitur ab eo qui infami graditur via.

beatidemumsuntquipersecutionempropterius.en: Blessed lastly are they that suffer persecution for justice' sake, and by their unconquered patience obtain the eternal kingdom of Christ. To this kind of blessedness none are more to be referred than Stephen the protomartyr and the other most valiant soldiers and martyrs of Christ: since, being dragged as sheep to the slaughter, they strove even unto blood for Christian justice, so that no force or savagery of enemies, no bitterness of tribulation or temptation, could lead them away and separate them from the confession of the faith, the charity of Christ, the doctrine of the Church, and the path of justice. O happy they, who could testify with a good conscience: Who then shall separate us from the love of Christ? Shall tribulation? or distress? or famine? or nakedness? or danger? or persecution? or the sword? But in all these things we overcome, because of him that hath loved us. We have passed through fire and water, and thou hast brought us out into a refreshment.
beatidemumsuntquipersecutionempropterius.la: Beati demum sunt qui persecutionem propter justitiam patiuntur, suaque invicta patientia Christi regnum æternum obtinent. Ad hoc genus beatitudinis, nulli magis quam protomartyr Stephanus aliique fortissimi Christi milites ac martyres referendi sunt: quoniam velut oves ad occisionem pertractæ, ad sanguinem usque pro justitia christiana certarunt, nulla ut hostium vis atque barbaries, nulla tribulationis vel tentationis acerbitas eos a fidei confessione, Christi caritate, doctrina Ecclesiæ et justitiæ tramite potuerit abducere ac separare. O felices illi qui bona testari conscientia potuerunt: Quis nos separabit a caritate Christi? Tribulatio? an angustia? an fames? an nuditas? an periculum? an persecutio? an gladius? In his omnibus superamus propter eum qui dilexit nos. Transivimus per ignem et aquam, et eduxisti nos in refrigerium.

pretereafelicesomnesquihancscalamiacobsu.en: Moreover, happy are all they who to this day ascend this ladder of Jacob, marked by the eight steps above, leaving all hindrances behind, so that daily they overcome their deadly enemies, the world, the flesh and Satan, and by the pursuit of virtues make for themselves a step to blessed immortality. But far happier still are they who have made an end of fighting and conquering, and, the very labour of ascending being finished, have come to the crown of the contest; and now, like soldiers that have received their discharge and served their time, enjoy the highest rest, and dwell in the heavenly tabernacle, laden with a most ample reward. Nor is there any doubt that the holy Martyrs and godly Doctors flourish above the other elect unto everlasting ages, since for their heroic virtues they obtain by a special privilege the aureole, as the Theologians call it, and an excellent laurel.
pretereafelicesomnesquihancscalamiacobsu.la: Præterea felices omnes qui hanc scalam Jacob, superioribus gradibus octo distinctam, in hunc usque diem ascendunt, relictis omnibus impedimentis, ita ut capitales hostes, mundum, carnem ac satanam, cotidie vincant sibique virtutum studio gradum faciant ad beatam immortalitatem. Verum longe feliciores et illi, qui pugnandi et vincendi fecere finem et, ipso ascendendi labore confecto, ad certaminis coronam pervenerunt jamque, veluti rude donati et emeriti milites, quiete summa potiuntur, et in cælesti tabernaculo habitant, mercede amplissima cumulati. Nec dubium quin sancti Martyres piique Doctores præ ceteris florescant electis in perpetuas æternitates, quoniam ob virtutes heroicas aureolam, sicut Theologi vocant, et excellentem lauream peculiari privilegio consequentur.

daquesumusomnipotensdeusutquibeatinmarty.en: Grant, we beseech thee, almighty God, that we who keep the solemnity of blessed N., thy Martyr, may be helped by his intercession with thee.
daquesumusomnipotensdeusutquibeatinmarty.la: Da, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, qui beáti N., Mártyris tui, solémnia cólimus, ejus apud te intercessiónibus adjuvémur.

uteniminfirmaturpeccatoradversisitaiustu.en: For as the sinner is weakened by adversity, so the just man is strengthened by temptations. Thus did the Saints fight against sin; thus were they made both stronger by labouring and victors by dying. No athlete can be called stronger without a contest, none can be crowned without a victory. No soldier hath subdued the enemy without battle; none without war hath deserved well of his commander. Thou hast, O Christian, fit arms wherewith to overcome the foe; thou hast most strong weapons wherewith to vanquish the enemy.
uteniminfirmaturpeccatoradversisitaiustu.la: Ut enim infirmátur peccátor advérsis, ita justus tentatiónibus roborátur. Sic dimicárunt advérsus peccátum Sancti; sic, et laborándo fortióres, et moriéndo victóres effécti sunt. Nullus athlétes sine certámine fórtior dici, nullus sine victória póterit coronári. Nemo miles sine prœlio hostem subjécit; nemo sine bello imperatórem proméruit. Habes, christiáne, competéntia arma, quibus hostem expúgnes; habes fortíssima tela, quibus inimícum debelles.

beatipatrisnmeritaiamintutopositasecurim.en: Let us without fear magnify the merits of the blessed Father N., now placed in safety; who, holding manfully the helm of faith, hath now cast the anchor of hope in a calm haven, and hath brought the ship, full of heavenly riches and eternal merchandise, to the longed-for shore; who held the shield of the fear of God unwearyingly against all adversaries, until he came to the victory. For what was the whole course of his life, but one conflict with a watchful enemy?
beatipatrisnmeritaiamintutopositasecurim.la: Beáti Patris N. mérita, jam in tuto pósita, secúri magnificémus; qui, gubernáculum fídei viríliter tenens, ánchoram spei tranquílla jam in statióne compósuit, et plenam cæléstibus divítiis et ætérnis mércibus navem, optáto in líttore, collocávit; qui contra omnes adversários scutum timóris Dei támdiu infatigabíliter ténuit, donec ad victóriam perveníret. Quid enim fuit totus vitæ illíus cursus, nisi uníus cum vígili hoste conflíctus?

quantishiccecisaviaveritatiserrantibuset.en: To how many blind, wandering from the way of truth and already hanging from the highest crag over the abyss, did he restore their lost sight, and repair that vision whereby Christ might be seen? Into the deaf ears of how many, condemned by the stopping of unbelief, did he pour the precious hearing to receive the voice of the heavenly commandments; that, when God called them to mercy, they might answer by obedience? How many wounded inwardly did he cure of their infirmity by the art of his angelic mouth and of his prayers?
quantishiccecisaviaveritatiserrantibuset.la: Quantis hic cæcis, a via veritátis errántibus et de summa jam in profúndum rupe pendéntibus, amíssum réddidit visum; et illum, quo Christus viderétur, reparávit intúitum? Quantórum áuribus surdis et infidelitátis obturatióne damnátis, ad percipiéndam vocem cæléstium mandatórum, pretiósum infúdit audítum; ut, vocánti Deo ad misericórdiam, respondérent per obediéntiam? Quantos intrínsecus vulnerátos, angélici oris arte et oratiónum, ab infirmitáte curávit?

necimmeritodoctoressanctihyadumnuncupati.en: And not without reason are the holy Doctors signified by the name of the Hyades. For in the Greek tongue rain is called hyetos, and the Hyades took their name from rains, because when they rise they without doubt bring showers. Well therefore are they expressed by the name of the Hyades, who, brought to the state of the universal Church as it were to the face of heaven, have poured the showers of holy preaching upon the dry earth of the human breast. For if the word of preaching were not rain, Moses would by no means have said: Let my speech be expected as the rain; and the Truth would in no wise have said by Isaias: I will command my clouds to rain no rain upon it; and that which we brought forward a little before: Therefore the stars of rain have been withheld.
necimmeritodoctoressanctihyadumnuncupati.la: Nec immérito Doctóres sancti Hýadum nuncupatióne signántur. Græco quippe elóquio hýetos plúvia vocátur, et Hýades nomen a plúviis accepérunt, quia ortæ procul dúbio imbres ferunt. Bene ergo Hýadum appellatióne expréssi sunt, qui, ad statum universális Ecclésiæ quasi in cæli fáciem dedúcti, super aréntem terram humáni péctoris, sanctæ prædicatiónis imbres fudérunt. Si enim prædicatiónis sermo plúvia non esset, Móyses mínime dixísset: Exspectétur sicut plúvia elóquium meum; et nequáquam per Isaíam Véritas díceret: Mandábo núbibus meis, ne pluant super eam imbrem; atque hoc, quod paulo ante protúlimus: Quam ob rem prohíbitæ sunt stellæ pluviárum.

deusquinosbeatorumnetnconfessorumtuoruma.en: O God, who gladdenest us by the yearly solemnity of thy blessed Confessors N. and N.: mercifully grant, that we who keep their heavenly birthday may also imitate their deeds.
deusquinosbeatorumnetnconfessorumtuoruma.la: Deus, qui nos beatórum N. et N. Confessórum tuórum ánnua solemnitáte lætíficas: concéde propítius; ut quórum natalítiæ cólimus, étiam actiónes imitémur.

nequeeniminanisheccautiestetvanaformidoq.en: For neither is this caution empty, nor this fear vain, which taketh thought for the way of salvation, which keepeth the life-giving commandments of the Lord; that they who have dedicated themselves to Christ, and, withdrawing from carnal concupiscence, have vowed themselves to God both in flesh and in mind, may finish their work, destined for a great reward, and may study no longer to be adorned or to please any one but their Lord, from whom they also await the reward of virginity, as he himself saith: All men take not this word, but they to whom it is given. For there are eunuchs, who were born so from their mother's womb: and there are eunuchs, who were made so by men: and there are eunuchs, who have made themselves eunuchs for the kingdom of heaven.
nequeeniminanisheccautiestetvanaformidoq.la: Neque enim inánis hæc cáutio est, et vana formído, quæ ad salútis viam cónsulit, quæ domínica et vitália præcépta custódit, ut quæ se Christo dicáverint, et a carnáli concupiscéntia recedéntes tam carne, quam mente se Deo vóverint, consúmment opus suum magno prǽmio destinátum, nec ornári jam, aut placére cuíquam, nisi Dómino suo, stúdeant, a quo et mercédem virginitátis expéctant, dicénte ipso: Non omnes cápiunt verbum, sed illi quibus datum est. Sunt enim spadónes, qui ex útero matris sic nati sunt: et sunt spadónes, qui coácti sunt ab homínibus; et sunt spadónes, qui seípsos castravérunt propter regnum cœlórum.

denuoquoqueperhancangelivocemcontinentie.en: Again also, by this voice of the Angel, the gift of continence is shown, virginity is proclaimed: These are they who were not defiled with women: for they are virgins: these follow the Lamb whithersoever he goeth. For neither doth the Lord promise the grace of continence to men only, and pass over women: but since the woman is a portion of the man, and was taken and formed from him, in almost all the Scriptures God speaketh to the first-formed, because they are two in one flesh, and in the male the female also is signified. But if continence followeth Christ, and virginity is destined for the kingdom of God, what have they to do with earthly dress and with ornaments, whereby, while they long to please men, they offend God?
denuoquoqueperhancangelivocemcontinentie.la: Dénuo quoque per hanc Angeli vocem continéntiæ munus osténditur, virgínitas prædicátur. Hi sunt, qui cum muliéribus se non coinquinavérunt: vírgines enim permansérunt: hi sunt qui sequúntur Agnum quocúmque íerit. Neque enim tantum másculis continéntiæ grátiam Dóminus repromíttit, et féminas prǽterit: sed quóniam fémina viri pórtio est, et ex eo sumpta atque formáta est, in Scriptúris fere ómnibus ad protoplástum Deus lóquitur, quia sunt duo in carne una, et in másculo simul significátur et fémina. Quod si Christum continéntia séquitur, et regno Dei virgínitas destinátur: quid est illis cum terréno cultu, et cum ornaméntis, quibus dum homínibus placére géstiunt, Deum offéndunt?

permulieremvicitpermulieremsuperatusesth.en: By a woman he conquered, by a woman he was overcome. This was formerly his weapon: this hath now become the instrument of his slaughter; this vessel hath appeared invincible. She of old sinned first, and died: this one died, that she might not sin. She of old, puffed up with the hope of a vain promise, violated the laws of God: this one despised the present life, that she might not forswear her faith in her benefactor. What excuse then can men hereafter hope for, if they be soft and slothful; what pardon indeed, when women bear themselves bravely and manfully, when they gird themselves so nobly for the contests of godliness?
permulieremvicitpermulieremsuperatusesth.la: Per mulíerem vicit, per mulíerem superátus est. Hoc illíus ántea telum erat: hoc illíus nunc cædis factum est instruméntum, hoc vas appáruit insuperábile. Peccávit illa prior, et mórtua est: ista mórtua est, ne peccáret. Illa tum fútilis promíssi spe infláta, Dei leges violávit: hæc vitam præséntem contémpsit, ne fidem in suum benefactórem ejuráret. Quam ígitur deínceps speráre póterunt excusatiónem viri, si molles sint, et ignávi; quam vero véniam, cum fórtiter ac viríliter se gerant mulíeres, cum ádeo se generose ad certámina pietátis accíngant?

fuitilicorpusimbecillumetobnoxiussexusin.en: She had a weak body, and a sex liable to injury; but grace coming upon her hid the weakness of all these. For there is nothing, nothing at all, more powerful than he who with great zeal hath the fear of God fixed in his mind; but though the enemies threaten fire, though the sword, though wild beasts, though anything else, he despiseth all without difficulty; which assuredly this blessed woman also did.
fuitilicorpusimbecillumetobnoxiussexusin.la: Fuit ili corpus imbecíllum, et obnóxius sexus injúriæ; verúmtamen ómnium horum imbecillitátem advéniens grátia occultávit. Nihil enim est, nihil plane poténtius est co, qui magno cum stúdio Dei timórem hábeat in mente defíxum; sed quamvis ignes, quamvis ferrum, quamvis béstias, quamvis áliud quidvis minêntur hostes, ómnia nullo negótio contémnit; quod útique Beáta ista étiam fecit.

sobriiestoteetvigilatequiaadversariusves.en: Be sober and watch: because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, goeth about seeking whom he may devour: whom resist ye, strong in faith: knowing that the same affliction befalls your brethren who are in the world.
sobriiestoteetvigilatequiaadversariusves.la: Sóbrii estóte, et vigiláte: quia adversárius vester diábolus tamquam leo rúgiens círcuit, quærens quem dévoret: cui resístite fortes in fide, sciéntes eámdem passiónem ei, quæ in mundo est, vestræ fraternitáti fíeri.

inevangdominicaipostpascha.la: In Evang. Dominica I post Pascha

natalemsanctiioannisfratrescarissimihodi.en: We celebrate this day, dearly beloved brethren, the birthday of St. John: which we read was granted to none of the Saints before. For the birthday of the Lord alone and of blessed John is celebrated and kept throughout the whole world. For this one a barren woman brought forth, that one a virgin conceived: in Elizabeth barrenness is overcome, in blessed Mary the wont of conception is changed. Elizabeth, by knowing a husband, bore a son: Mary believed the Angel, and conceived. Elizabeth conceived a man, and Mary a man: but Elizabeth a man only, Mary God and man.
natalemsanctiioannisfratrescarissimihodi.la: Natálem sancti Joánnis, fratres caríssimi, hódie celebrámus: quod nulli umqua Sanctórum légimus fuísse concéssum. Solíus enim Dómini, et beáti Joánnis dies nativitátis in univérso mundo celebrátur et cólitur. Hunc enim stérilis péperit, illum virgo concépit: in Elísabeth sterílitas víncitur, in beáta María conceptiónis consuetúdo mutátur. Elísabeth virum cognoscéndo, fílium génuit: María Angelo crédidit, et concépit. Hóminem concépit Elísabeth, hóminem et María: sed Elísabeth solum hóminem, María Deum et hóminem.

magnusigiturioannescuiusmagnitudinietiam.en: Great therefore is John, to whose greatness even the Saviour beareth witness, saying: There hath not risen among them that are born of women a greater than John the Baptist. He excelleth the rest, he standeth out above all: he surpasseth the Prophets, he goeth beyond the Patriarchs: and whosoever is born of woman is less than John. Perchance someone will say: If among them that are born of women John is the greater, is he greater than the Saviour? God forbid. For John was born of a woman, but Christ was born of a virgin. The one came forth from the recesses of a corruptible womb, the other was brought forth from the flower of a spotless virgin.
magnusigiturioannescuiusmagnitudinietiam.la: Magnus ígitur Joánnes, cujus magnitúdini étiam Salvátor testimónium perhibet, dicens: Non surréxit inter natos mulíerum major Joánne Baptísta. Præcéllit céteros, éminet univérsis: antecéllit Prophétas, supergréditur Patriárchas: et quisquis de mulíere natus est, inférior est Joánne. Dicet fortásse áliquis: Si inter natos mulíerum Joánnes major est, major est Salvatóre? Absit. Joánnes enim natus mulíeris, Christus autem vírginis natus est. Ille corruptíbilis úteri sínibus effúsus est, iste impollútæ vírginis flore progénitus.

dehomiliasanctiambrosiiepicopi.en: From the Homily of St. Ambrose, Bishop.

ioannesestinquitnomeneiusnonpoteratelisa.en: John, saith she, is his name. Elizabeth could not be ignorant of the Lord's forerunner, she who had prophesied Christ. And well is it added: Because there was none of his kindred that was called by this name: that thou mayest understand that the name was not of the family, but of the prophet. Zachary also is asked by signs: but because unbelief had taken from him speech and hearing, what he could not with the voice, he spake with his hand and with letters.
ioannesestinquitnomeneiusnonpoteratelisa.la: Joánnes est, inquit, nomen ejus. Non póterat Elísabeth Dómini ignoráre prænúntium, quæ prophetáuerat Christum. Et bene ádditur: Quia nemo in cognatióne ejus vocabátur hoc nómine: ut intélligas nomen non géneris esse, sed vatis. Zacharías quoque nutu interrogátor: sed quia incredúlitas ei affátum eripúerat et audítum, quod voce non póterat, manu et lítteris est locútus.

scripsitautemdicensioannesestnomeneiuset.en: And he wrote, saying: John is his name. And here the name is not imposed, but confirmed. And rightly his tongue was forthwith loosed: because that which unbelief had bound, faith loosed. Let us also therefore believe, that we may speak; that our tongue, which is bound with the bonds of unbelief, may be loosed by the voice of reason.
scripsitautemdicensioannesestnomeneiuset.la: Scripsit autem dicens: Joánnes est nomen ejus. Et hic nomen non impónitur, sed astrúitur. Meritóque contínuo resolúta est lingua ejus: quia quam vínxerat incredúlitas, fides solvit. Credámus et nos ígitur, ut loquámur; ut lingua nostra, quæ incredulitátis vínculis est ligáta, ratiónis voce solvátur.

scribamusspiritumysteriasivolumusloquisc.en: Let us write the mysteries in spirit, if we would speak: let us write the forerunner of Christ, not on tables of stone, but on the fleshly tables of the heart. For he that speaketh John prophesieth Christ. Let us speak John, let us speak Christ also: that our mouth too may be opened, which, as in so great a priest, after the manner of a dumb beast, the reins of a wavering faith were restraining.
scribamusspiritumysteriasivolumusloquisc.la: Scribámus spíritu mystéria, si vólumus loqui: scribámus prænúntium Christi, non in tábulis lapidéis, sed in tábulis cordis carnálibus. Etenim qui Joánem lóquitur, Christum prophétat. Loquámur Joánnem, loquámur et Christum: ut nostrum quoque os possit aperíri, quod in sacerdóte tanto, irrationális modo pécudis, fræna nutántis fídei coërcebant.

nonsinecausafactumputemusfratrescarissim.en: Let us not think it came to pass without reason, dearly beloved brethren, that the most glorious princes of the Christian faith, Peter and Paul, on one day, in one place, suffered the sentence of one tyrant. They suffered on one day, that they might come to Christ together: in one place, that Rome might not lack either of them: under one persecutor, that an equal cruelty might bind both. The day therefore, I think, was appointed for their merit, the place for their glory, the persecutor for their virtue. And in what place, then, did they endure martyrdom? In the city of Rome, which holdeth the princedom and headship of the nations; to wit, that where the head of superstition was, there the head of holiness might rest; and where the princes of the Gentiles dwelt, there the princes of the churches might abide.
nonsinecausafactumputemusfratrescarissim.la: Non sine causa factum putemus, fratres carissimi, quod gloriosissimi Christianæ fidei principes Petrus et Paulus, una die, uno loco, unius tyranni toleravere sententiam. Una die passi sunt, ut ad Christum pariter pervenirent: uno in loco, ne lateri Roma deesset: sub uno persecutore, ut æqualis crudelitas utrumque constringeret. Dies ergo, puto, pro merito, locus pro gloria, persecutor decretus est pro virtute. Et in quo tandem loco martyrium pertulerunt? In urbe Roma, quæ principatum et caput obtinet nationum; scilicet ut ubi caput superstitionis erat, illic caput quiesceret sanctitatis; et ubi gentilium principes habitabant, illic ecclesiarum principes morarentur.

cuiusautemmeritisintbeatissimipetrusetpa.en: But of what merit are the most blessed Peter and Paul we may understand from this, that whereas the Lord enlightened the region of the East by his own passion, he vouchsafed, that it might be nothing less, to enlighten the quarter of the West in his stead with the blood of the apostles. And although his passion sufficeth us for salvation, yet their martyrdom also hath been given us for an example. On this day therefore the blessed apostles shed their blood: but let us see the cause why they suffered; to wit, that among other wonders they also by their prayers cast down that magician Simon from the void of the air in a headlong fall.
cuiusautemmeritisintbeatissimipetrusetpa.la: Cujus autem meriti sint beatissimi Petrus et Paulus, hinc possumus intelligere, quod cum Dominus Orientis regionem propria illustraverit passione; Occidentis plagam, ne quid minus esset, vice sui apostolorum sanguine illuminare dignatus est. Et licet illius passio nobis sufficiat ad salutem, tamen étiam horum martyrium nobis contulit ad exemplum. Hodierna igitur die beati apostoli sanguinem profuderunt: sed videamus causam quare isti perpessi sunt, scilicet quod inter cetera mirabilia étiam magum illum Simonem orationibus suis de aëris vacuo præcipiti ruina prostraverunt.

cumenimidemsimonsechristumdiceretettamqu.en: For when the same Simon said that he was Christ, and asserted that he could ascend by flying, as a son to his father, and, lifted up by magic arts, had suddenly begun to fly: then Peter, kneeling down, prayed to the Lord, and by holy prayer overcame the magic lightness. For the prayer ascended to the Lord before the flight, and the just petition arrived before the wicked presumption; Peter, set upon earth, obtained what he asked before Simon reached the heavenly places whither he was making. Then therefore Peter brought him down from the high air as one bound, and, dashing him headlong upon a rock, broke his legs: and this in reproach of that deed, that he who a little before had tried to fly suddenly could not walk, and he who had taken to himself wings lost his feet.
cumenimidemsimonsechristumdiceretettamqu.la: Cum enim idem Simon se Christum diceret, et tamquam filium ad patrem asseret volando se posse conscendere, atque elatus subito magicis artibus volare cæpisset: tunc Petrus fixis genibus precatus est Dominum, et precatione sancta vicit magicam levitatem. Prior enim ascendit ad Dominum oratio, quam volatus, et ante pervenit justa petitio, quam iniqua præsumptio; ante Petrus in terris positus obtinuit quod petebat quam Simon perveniret in cælestibus, quo tendebat. Tunc igitur Petrus velut vinctum illum de sublimi ære deposuit, et quodam præcipitio in saxo elidens ejus crura confregit: et hoc in opprobrio facti illius, ut qui paulo ante volare tentaverat, subito ambulare non posset, et qui pennas assumpserat, plantas amitteret.

oratdedormdeipare.en: Oration 2 on the Falling-asleep of the Mother of God

iubilemusinarcadominideitotoanimetmurica.en: Let us rejoice with all our soul in the ark of the Lord God, and the walls of Jericho shall fall, the hostile fortresses, I say, of the adverse powers. Let us exult in spirit with David. For the ark of the Lord hath this day come to rest. Let us cry out with Gabriel, who holdeth the first place among the angels: Hail, full of grace: the Lord is with thee. Hail, inexhaustible sea of joy. Hail, only relief of troubles. Hail, remedy of all the sorrows of the heart. Hail, holy virgin, through whom death was cast out, and life brought in.
iubilemusinarcadominideitotoanimetmurica.la: Jubilemus in arca Domini Dei toto animo, et muri cadent Hiericontini, contrariarum, inquam potestatum infestæ munitiones. Cum David exsultemus spiritu. Arca enim Domini hodie requievit. Clamemus cum Gabriele, qui primum locum obtinet inter angelos: Ave gratia plena: dominus tecum. Ave gaudii pelagus inexhaustum. Ave unicum molestiarum levamen. Aue omnium cordis dolorum medicamentum. Ave sancta virgo per quam mors quidem fuit expulsa, vita autem introducta.

desermonesanctiioannisdamasceni.en: From the Sermon of St. John Damascene

oratdedormitionedeiparesubfinem.en: Oration 2 on the Falling-asleep of the Mother of God, near the end
oratdedormitionedeiparesubfinem.la: Orat. 2 de Dormitione Deiparæ, sub finem

exantiquaaccepimustraditionequodtemporeg.en: We have received from ancient tradition, that at the time of the glorious falling-asleep of the blessed Virgin, all the holy Apostles, who were journeying through the world for the salvation of the Gentiles, being borne aloft in a moment of time, came together at Jerusalem. And when they were there, there appeared to them a vision of angels, and the psalmody of the heavenly Powers was heard; and so with divine glory she gave up her holy soul into the hands of God. But her body, which had in an unspeakable manner received God, being borne forth with the hymnody of angels and apostles, was laid in a tomb at Gethsemane; in which place the song of the Angels continued for three days together.
exantiquaaccepimustraditionequodtemporeg.la: Ex antíqua accépimus traditióne, quod témpore gloriósæ dormitiónis beátæ Virginis, univérsi quidem sancti Apóstoli, qui orbem terræ ad salútem Géntium peragrábant, moménto témporis in sublíme eláti, convenérunt Jerosólymis. Cumque illic essent, eis vísio appáruit angélica, et audíta est psalmodía cæléstium Potestátum; et sic cum divína glória in manus Dei sanctam trádidit ánimam. Ejus autem corpus, quod Deum ineffábili quadam ratióne suscépit, cum angélica et apostólica hymnodía elátum, in lóculo fuit depósitum Gethsemane; quo in loco Angelórum cantus mansit tres dies contínuos.

tuveroosacrorumsepulcrorumsacratissimump.en: But thou, O most sacred of sacred sepulchres, after the sepulchre of the Lord, which gave the beginning of life, which was the fountain of resurrection (for I will speak with thee as with a living thing), where is that pure gold which the hands of the apostles laid up in thee? Where are the riches which cannot be consumed? Where is the new volume, in which God the Word was unspeakably written without hand? Where is the abyss of grace? Where is the sea of healings? Where is that desirable body of the virgin Mother of God?
tuveroosacrorumsepulcrorumsacratissimump.la: Tu vero o sacrorum sepulcrorum sacratissimum, post domini quidem sepulcrum, quod uitæ dedit principium, quod fuit fons resurrectionis, (tecum enim loquar tamquam cum animato) ubinam est aurum illud purum, quod manus apostolorum in te condiderunt! Ubi divitiæ, quæ consumi nequeunt! Ubi novum uolumen, in quo ineffabiliter deus uerbum sine manu inscriptum fuit! Ubi abyssus gratiæ? Ubi pelagus curationum? Ubi est desiderabile illud deiparæ uirginis corpus?

posttresautemdiesangelicocantucessantequ.en: But after three days, the song of the Angels ceasing, the Apostles that were present opened the tomb (since Thomas alone, who had been absent, came after the third day, and desired to venerate the body that had received God); but in no part could they find her sacred body. And when they had found only the things in which she had been laid, and were filled with an unspeakable fragrance which came forth from them, they closed the tomb. Astonished at the wonder of this mystery, they could think only this, that he who was pleased to take flesh of the Virgin Mary, and to be made man and to be born, though he was God the Word and the Lord of glory, and who after the birth kept her virginity incorrupt; the same was pleased also, after she had departed, to honour her immaculate body, kept incorrupt, by translating it before the common and universal resurrection.
posttresautemdiesangelicocantucessantequ.la: Post tres autem dies angélico cantu cessante, qui áderant Apóstoli (cum unus Thomas, qui abfúerat, post tértium diem venísset, et, quod Deum suscéperat, corpus adoráre voluísset), túmulum aperuérunt; sed omni ex parte sacrum ejus corpus nequáquam inveníre potuérunt. Cum ea autem tantum inveníssent, in quibus fúerat compósitum, et ineffabili, qui ex iis proficiscebátur, essent odóre repléti, lóculum clausérunt. Ejus mystérii obstupefácti miráculo, hoc solum cogitáre potuerunt, quod, cui plácuit ex María Vírgine carnem súmere, et hóminem fíeri et nasci, cum esset Deus Verbum, et Dóminus glóriæ, quique post partum incorrúptam servávit ejus virginitátem; eídem étiam plácuit, et ipsíus, postquam migrávit, immaculátum corpus, incorrúptum servátum, translatióne honoráre ante commúnem et universálem resurrectiónem.

quidqueritisinsepulcreamqueadcelestiatra.en: Why seek ye in the sepulchre her who hath been translated to the heavenly tabernacles? why demand ye of me an account of my keeping? I cannot resist the divine commands. The most sacred body imparted holiness to me also, for it filled me with the fragrance of a most precious ointment, and made me a divine temple; leaving the linen cloths, it went away, caught up on high, angels, archangels, and all the heavenly powers accompanying it. Now angels surround me; now divine grace dwelleth in me. Therefore I am become a house of healing for the sick. I am a perpetual fountain of healings: I am a remedy against devils: I am a city of refuge for all that flee unto me.
quidqueritisinsepulcreamqueadcelestiatra.la: Quid quæritis in sepulcro eam, quæ ad cælestia translata est tabernacula? cur a me custodiæ rationem exposcitis? Non possum ego divinis jussis resistere. Sacrosanctum corpus mihi quoque sanctitatem impertivit quod me pretiosissimi unguenti fragrantia replevit, et divinum templum effecit relictis sindonibus, abiit raptum sublime, comitantibus angelis, archangelis, et omnibus cælestibus potentiis. Nunc me circumdant angeli; nunc divina in me habitat gratia. Ergo evasi officina medicinæ ægrotantibus. Ego sum fons perennis curationum: Ego remedium aduersus dæmones: Ego civitas refugii omnibus ad me confugientibus.

aderanttunccumapostolissanctissimustimot.en: There were present then with the Apostles the most holy Timothy, the first bishop of the Ephesians, and Dionysius the Areopagite, as he himself testifieth in those things which he wrote to the aforesaid Timothy concerning blessed Hierotheus, who himself also was then present, speaking thus: For even among the inspired Prelates themselves, when we also, as thou knowest, and many of our holy brethren, had come together to behold the body that gave the beginning of Life and received God (and there were present also James the brother of the Lord, and Peter, the supreme and most ancient summit of theologians): the sacred body having been seen, it pleased all, as each was able, to celebrate in hymns the infinite goodness of the divine power.
aderanttunccumapostolissanctissimustimot.la: Aderant tunc cum Apóstolis sanctíssimus Timotheus, primus epíscopus Ephesiórum, et Dionysius Areopagíta, sicut ipse testátur in iis, quæ de beáto Hierótheo, qui ipse quoque tunc áderat, scripsit ad prædíctum Timótheum, sic dicens: Nam étiam apud ipsos a Deo afflátos Sacrórum antístites, quando nos quoque, ut nosti, et multi ex sanctis nostris frátribus, ad contuéndum corpus, quod Vitæ princípium dedit, et Deum suscépit, convenissémus (áderat autem et Dómini frater Jacóbus, et Petrus, supréma et antiquíssima theologórum súmmitas): et viso sacro córpore, plácuit ómnibus, prout quisque póterat, hymnis celebráre infínitam bonitátem divínæ poténtiæ.

innativitatebmv.en: On the Nativity of the B. V. M.

remanseruntergoinilladomodebetotiosa.en: They remained therefore in that house ... ought to be idle.
remanseruntergoinilladomodebetotiosa.la: Remanserunt ergo in illa domo... debet otiosa.

erantergoinillastatisauditis.en: There were therefore in that ... having been heard.
erantergoinillastatisauditis.la: Erant ergo in illa ... statis auditis.

inquantumautemhocdatdeus.en: But in so far as this ... God giveth.
inquantumautemhocdatdeus.la: In quantum autem hoc ... dat deus.

itaquedominuslibenteringredituretineiusq.en: And therefore the Lord willingly entereth, and reclineth in the affection of him that hath believed. But again the envy of the faithless is kindled, and a figure of the punishment to come is foreshown. For while the faithful feast and recline in that kingdom of heaven, faithlessness shall be tormented with fasting. At the same time it is shown how great a difference there is between the zealots of the Law and those of grace; that they who follow the law suffer the eternal hunger of a fasting mind: but they who have received the word into the inward parts of the soul, being refreshed by the abundance of heavenly food and of the fountain, cannot hunger and thirst.
itaquedominuslibenteringredituretineiusq.la: Itaque Dominus libenter ingreditur, et in ejus qui crediderit, recumbit affectu. Sed rursus accenditur invidia perfidorum, et futuræ pœnæ species præfiguratur. Epulantibus enim fidelibus, et in illo cœlorum recumbentibus regno, perfidia jejuna torquebitur. Simul ostenditur quantum intersit inter æmulos Legis et gratiæ, quod illi qui legem sequuntur, jejunæ mentis famem patiantur æternam: qui vero verbum in interioribus animæ receperunt, alimenti cœlestis et fontis ubertate recreati esurire et sitire non possunt.

etideoquianimoieiunabantmurmurabantdicen.en: And therefore they that fasted in mind murmured, saying: Why doth he eat and drink with publicans and sinners? This is the serpent's voice. For the serpent uttered this as his first word, saying to Eve: Why hath God commanded you, that you should not eat of every tree? They therefore pour forth the venom of their father, who say: Why doth he eat and drink with publicans and sinners? Whence the Lord, by eating with sinners, forbiddeth us not to enter into a feast even with Gentiles, saying: They that are in health need not a physician, but they that are ill.
etideoquianimoieiunabantmurmurabantdicen.la: Et ideo qui animo jejunabant, murmurabant dicentes: Quare cum publicanis et peccatoribus manducat et bibit? Serpentina vox ista est. Denique hanc primam vocem serpens emisit, dicens Evæ: Quid utique dixit Deus: Nolite manducare ex omni ligno? Ergo patris sui venena diffundunt, qui dicunt: Quid utique cum publicanis et peccatoribus manducat et bibit? Unde Dominus cum peccatoribus manducando, etiam cum gentilibus non prohibet nos inire convivium, dicens: Non egent qui sani sunt, medico, sed qui male habent.

indominfraoctassumptbmarievirg.en: On the Sunday within the Octave of the Assumption of the B. Virgin Mary
indominfraoctassumptbmarievirg.la: In Dom. infra Oct. Assumpt. B. Mariae Virg.

eiuscorpuspostearomamnicolaoprimopontifi.en: These things moved Trajan to send a messenger to the Crimea, who tied an anchor about Clement's neck, and cast him into the deep of the sea. After it had been done, while the Christians were praying on the shore, the sea went back three miles, and when they followed it, they found a grotto of marble, in form like a temple, and therein a stone coffin wherein was laid the body of the Martyr, and, hard by, the anchor wherewith he had been sunk. Then were the country people moved to receive the faith of Christ. The body of Clement was afterwards brought to Rome, in the time of Pope Nicholas I, and buried in his own Church. A Church was also built in the Crimea, in the place where God had made the water to break forth. Clement lived as Pope nine years, six months, and six days. He held two Ordinations in the month of December, wherein he made ten Priests, two Deacons, and fifteen Bishops for diverse places.
eiuscorpuspostearomamnicolaoprimopontifi.la: (English data with its first sentence left in Latin) Ejus corpus postea Romam Nicolao Primo Pontifice translatum, in Ecclesia ipsius

inillotemporedixitiesusphariseisparabola.en: At that time, Jesus spoke to the Pharisees this parable: A certain man gave a great supper, and he invited many. And he sent his servant at supper time to tell those invited to come, for everything is now ready. And they all with one accord began to excuse themselves. The first said to him, ‘I have bought a farm, and I must go out and see it; I pray you hold me excused.’ And another said, ‘I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I am on my way to try them; I pray you hold me excused.’ And another said, ‘I have married a wife, and therefore I cannot come.’ And the servant returned, and reported these things to his master. Then the master of the house was angry and said to his servant, ‘Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in here the poor, and the crippled, and the blind, and the lame.’ And the servant said, ‘Sir, your order has been carried out, and still there is room.’ Then the master said to the servant, ‘Go out into the highways and hedges, and make them come in, so that my house may be filled. For I tell you that none of those who were invited shall taste of my supper.’
inillotemporedixitiesusphariseisparabola.la: In illo témpore: Dixit Iesus pharisǽis parábolam hanc: Homo quidam fecit cœnam magnam, et vocávit multos. Et misit servum suum hora cœnæ dícere invitátis, ut venírent, quia iam paráta sunt ómnia. Et cœpérunt simul omnes excusáre. Primus dixit ei: Villam emi, et necésse hábeo exíre et vidére illam: rogo te, habe me excusátum. Et alter dixit: Iuga boum emi quinque et eo probáre illa: rogo te, habe me excusátum. Et álius dixit: Uxórem duxi, et ídeo non possum veníre. Et revérsus servus nuntiávit hæc dómino suo. Tunc irátus paterfamílias, dixit servo suo: Exi cito in pláteas et vicos civitátis: et páuperes ac débiles et cæcos et claudos íntroduc huc. Et ait servus: Dómine, factum est, ut imperásti, et adhuc locus est. Et ait dóminus servo: Exi in vias et sepes: et compélle intrare, ut impleátur domus mea. Dico autem vobis, quod nemo virórum illórum, qui vocáti sunt, gustábit cœnam meam.

sequentiasanctievangeliisecundumlucam.en: Continuation + of the Holy Gospel according to Luke

cumergouniversavitiapercontinentiamdestr.en: Since then all vices are destroyed by continence, and whatsoever avarice thirsteth for, whatsoever pride striveth after, whatsoever lust coveteth, is overcome by the firmness of this virtue; who doth not understand how great a help is given us through fasting? wherein it is enjoined that we abstain not only from food, but also from all carnal desires. Otherwise it is superfluous to undergo hunger, and not to lay aside an evil will; to be afflicted by cutting off food, and not to draw back from sin once conceived. Carnal, not spiritual, is that fast wherein the body alone is not spared, and one continueth in those things which are more hurtful than all delights.
cumergouniversavitiapercontinentiamdestr.la: Cum ergo universa vitia per continentiam destruantur, et quidquid avaritia sitit, quidquid superbia ambit, quidquid luxuria concupiscit, hujus virtutis soliditate superetur; quis non intelligat quantum nobis praesidii per jejunia conferatur? in quibus indicitur, ut non solum a cibis, sed etiam ab omnibus carnalibus desideriis temperetur. Alioqui superfluum est suscipere esuriem, et iniquam non deponere voluntatem; reciso affligi cibo, et a concepto non resilire peccato. Carnale est, non spiritale jejunium, ubi soli corpori non parcitur, et in iis quae omnibus deliciis nocentiora sunt, permanetur.

hecnosfratrescharissimiidcircodicimusuta.en: These things, dearly beloved brethren, we say to this end, that your minds may awake to the zeal of watchfulness, that they grow not torpid with security, nor languish in ignorance, but that fear may ever stir them, and carefulness confirm them in good works, weighing that which is added by the voice of our Redeemer: Men withering away for fear and expectation of what shall come upon the whole world. For the powers of heaven shall be moved. For what doth the Lord call the powers of heaven but the Angels, Archangels, Thrones, Dominations, Principalities and Powers, which at the coming of the strict Judge shall then appear visibly to our eyes, that they may then strictly exact of us that which now our invisible Maker patiently beareth? Where it is also added: And then they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds with great power and majesty. As if it were openly said: In power and majesty shall they see him whom, set in lowliness, they would not hear, that they may feel his might so much the more strictly then, as now they bow not the neck of their heart to his patience.
hecnosfratrescharissimiidcircodicimusuta.la: Haec nos, fratres charissimi, idcirco dicimus, ut ad cautelae studium vestrae mentes evigilent, ne securitate torpeant, ne ignorantia languescant, sed semper eas et timor sollicitet, et in bono opere sollicitudo confirmet, pensantes hoc quod Redemptoris nostri voce subjungitur: Arescentibus hominibus prae timore et exspectatione quae supervenient universo orbi. Nam virtutes coelorum movebuntur. Quid etenim Dominus virtutes coelorum nisi angelos, archangelos, thronos, dominationes, principatus et potestates appellat, quae in adventu districti judicis nostris tunc oculis visibiliter apparebunt, ut districte tunc a nobis exigant hoc, quod nos modo invisibilis conditor aequanimiter portat? Ubi et subditur: Et tunc videbunt Filium hominis venientem in nubibus cum potestate magna et majestate. Ac si aperte diceretur: In potestate et majestate visuri sunt quem in humilitate positum audire noluerunt, ut virtutem ejus tanto tunc districtius sentiant, quanto nunc cervicem cordis ad ejus patientiam non inclinant.

nonsecundumvisionemoculorumiudicabithecn.en: He shall not judge according to the sight of the eyes. These things we refer to the first coming of the Saviour: the Jews contend that they shall come to pass at the end of the world. For he accepteth no man's person in judgment: but he speaketh to the Scribes and Pharisees and rulers: Woe to you, hypocrites: and, The kingdom of God shall be taken from you, and shall be given to a nation yielding the fruits thereof. Nor did he reprove according to the hearing of the ears. For when they said: Master, we know that thou art a true speaker, and teachest the way of God in truth, neither carest thou for any man: for thou dost not regard the person: knowing their wickedness, he answered: Why do you tempt me, ye hypocrites? and other things like these. But he judged with justice the poor in spirit, whose is the kingdom of God: and he reproved with equity the meek and humble of the earth, saying to the Apostles: Are you also yet without understanding? And again: Do you not yet know nor understand?
nonsecundumvisionemoculorumiudicabithecn.la: Non secundum visionem oculorum judicabit. Haec nos ad primum adventum referimus Salvatoris: Judaei in fine mundi contendunt futura. Nullius enim personam accipit in judicio: sed Scribis et Pharisaeis ac principibus loquitur: Vae vobis, hypocritae: Et, Auferetur a vobis regnum Dei, et dabitur genti facienti fructus ejus. Nec secundum sermonem et auditum aurium corripuit. Illis enim dicentibus: Magister, scimus quia verax es, et viam Dei in veritate doces, et non ad te pertinet de aliquo: neque enim vides in faciem: sciens malitiam eorum, respondebat: Quid me tentatis, hypocritae? et caetera his similia. Judicabat autem in justitia pauperes spiritu, quorum est regnum Dei: et arguebat in aequitate mansuetos et humiles terrae, dicens ad Apostolos: Adhuc et vos insipientes estis? Et iterum: Necdum scitis neque intelligitis?

discamusergofratrescharissimiarundinemve.en: Let us learn therefore, dearly beloved brethren, not to be a reed shaken by the wind; let us make firm our soul set amid the breezes of tongues; let the state of our mind stand unbending. Let no detraction provoke us to anger, and let no favour incline us to the slackness of a useless graciousness. Let not prosperity lift us up, nor adversity trouble us, that we who are fixed in the firmness of faith may in no wise be moved by the changeableness of passing things. Moreover there is added concerning his manner of life: But what went you out into the desert to see? A man clothed in soft garments? Behold they that are clothed in soft garments are in the houses of kings. For John is described as having been clothed with a garment woven of camels' hair. And what is it to say: Behold they that are clothed in soft garments are in the houses of kings, but to show by an open sentence that they fight not for a heavenly but for an earthly king, who flee from suffering hard things for God, but, given over to outward things alone, seek the softness and delight of the present life? Let no man therefore think that there is no sin in the luxury and study of garments; for if this were not a fault, the Lord would in no wise have praised John for the roughness of his clothing.
discamusergofratrescharissimiarundinemve.la: Discamus ergo, fratres charissimi, arundinem vento agitatam non esse; solidemus animum inter auras linguarum positum, stet inflexibilis status mentis. Nulla nos detractio ad iram provocet, atque ad remissionem inutilis gratiae nullus favor inclinet. Non nos prospera elevent, non adversa perturbent, ut qui in soliditate fidei figimur, nequáquam rerum transeuntium mutabilitate moveamur. Adhuc autem de ejus expressione subjungitur: Sed quid existis in desertum videre? Hominem mollibus vestitum? Ecce qui mollibus vestiuntur in domibus regum sunt. Camelorum etenim pilis contextis vestitus Joannes fuisse describitur. Et quid est dicere: Ecce qui mollibus vestiuntur in domibus regum sunt, nisi aperta sententia demonstrare quia non coelesti, sed terreno regi militant hi qui pro Deo perpeti aspera fugiunt, sed, solis exterioribus dediti, praesentis vitae mollitiem et delectationem quaerunt? Nemo ergo existimet in fluxu atque studio vestium peccatum deesse, quia si hoc culpa non esset, nullo modo Joannem Dominus de vestimenti sui asperitate laudasset.

indominicoagrodilectissimicuiusoperariis.en: In the Lord's field, dearly beloved, whereof we are the labourers, it behoveth us to exercise a spiritual husbandry prudently and watchfully, that, with persevering diligence, taking care of the things that are to be done in their due seasons, we may rejoice in the fruit of holy works. Which things if they be neglected through slothful idleness and sluggish indolence, our ground will bring forth no generous shoot, and, overgrown with thorns and thistles, it will yield not that which is to be laid up in barns, but that which is to be burned in the flames. But this field, dearly beloved, while the grace of God watereth it as dew from above, is fenced by faith, tilled by fasting, sown by almsgiving, made fruitful by prayer, that among our plantings and waterings no root of bitterness may spring up, nor the growths of any harmful stock lift themselves up; but that, the seed of all vices being destroyed, a joyful harvest of virtues may grow together.
indominicoagrodilectissimicuiusoperariis.la: In Dominico agro, dilectissimi, cujus operarii sumus, oportet nos prudenter atque vigilanter spiritalem exercere culturam, ut perseveranti industria, quae legitimis temporibus sunt exsequenda, curantes, de sanctorum operum fruge laetemur. Quae si pigro otio et inerti desidia negligantur, terra nostra nihil generosi germinis pariet, et spinis ac tribulis obsita, non producet quae condenda sint horreis, sed quae urenda sint flammis. Ager autem iste, dilectissimi, rorante desuper gratia Dei, fide munitur, jejuniis exercetur, eleemosynis seritur, orationibus fecundatur, ut inter plantationes rigationesque nostras nullius amaritudinis radix pullulet, nec se incrementa cujusque noxiae stirpis attollant; sed enecate omnium semine vitiorum, coalescat seges laeta virtutum.

quomodofietistudquoniamvirumnoncognoviin.en: How shall this be done, because I know not man? A generation incredible and unheard of had first to be heard, that it might be believed. That a virgin should bring forth is the sign of a divine mystery, not of a human one. In short, Take thee, he saith, a sign: Behold a virgin shall conceive in her womb, and shall bear a son. Mary had read this, therefore she believed that it would come to pass: but how it should come to pass she had not read before; for how it should come to pass had not been revealed even to so great a prophet. For the mystery of so great a message was to be uttered not by the mouth of man, but of an angel. Today for the first time it is heard: The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee. And it is heard, and it is believed. In short: Behold, she saith, the handmaid of the Lord; be it done to me according to thy word. See her humility, see her devotion: she calleth herself the handmaid of the Lord, who is chosen to be his mother: nor was she lifted up by the sudden promise; by calling herself at once a handmaid, she claimed for herself no privilege of so great a grace, being one who would do what she was bidden.
quomodofietistudquoniamvirumnoncognoviin.la: Quo modo fiet istud; quoniam virum non cognovi? Incredibilis et inaudita generatio ante audiri debuit, ut crederetur. Virginem parere, divini est signum mysterii, non humani. Denique, accipe, inquit, tibi signum: Ecce virgo in utero accipiet, et pariet filium. Legerat hoc Maria, ideo credidit futurum: sed quomodo fieret, ante non legerat; non enim quemadmodum fieret, vel tanto prophetae fuerat revelatum. Tanti namque mandati mysterium non hominis fuit, sed angeli ore promendum. Hodie primum auditur: Spiritus sanctus superveniet in te. Et auditur, et creditur. Denique: Ecce, inquit, ancilla Domini, contingat mihi secundum verbum tuum. Vide humilitatem, vide devotionem, ancillam se dicit Domini, quae mater eligitur: nec repentino exaltata promisso est, simul ancillam dicendo, nullam sibi praerogativam tantae gratiae vindicavit, quae faceret quod juberetur.

inthisactofthevirginthenweseethegreaterg.en: In this act of the Virgin then we see the greater going to visit and to succour the lesser: Mary to Elizabeth, Christ to John. And so afterwards also, that he might sanctify the baptism of John, the Lord came to baptism. Speedily too are the benefits of the coming of Mary and of the presence of the Lord declared. For as soon as Elizabeth heard the salutation of Mary, the infant leaped in her womb. And she was filled with the Holy Ghost. Mark the distinction, and the proper meaning of each word. Elizabeth first heard the voice, but John first felt the grace: she heard by the order of nature, he leaped by reason of the mystery: she felt the coming of Mary, he the coming of the Lord: the woman the coming of the woman, the babe the coming of the babe. These speak of grace, those work it within, and they set about the mystery of loving-kindness by the advancing of their mothers; and by a twofold miracle the mothers prophesy by the spirit of their little ones. The infant leaped, the mother was filled. The mother was not filled before the son: but when the son had been filled with the Holy Ghost, he filled his mother also. John leaped, and the spirit of Mary leaped also. When John leaped, Elizabeth is filled: yet we know that Mary is not filled with the Spirit, but that her spirit leaped; for the Incomprehensible was working incomprehensibly in the mother. And the one is filled after conceiving, the other before conceiving.
inthisactofthevirginthenweseethegreaterg.la: In this act of the Virgin then we see the greater going to visit and to succour the lesser: Mary to Elizabeth, Christ to John. Denique etiam postea, ut sanctificaret baptismum Ioannis, Dominus venit ad baptismum. Cito quoque adventus Mariae, et praesensentiae dominicae beneficia declarantur. Simul enim ut audivit salutationem Mariae Elizabeth, exsultavit infans in utero eius. Et repleta est Spiritu sancto. Vide distinctionem, singulorumque verborum proprietates. Vocem prior Elizabeth audivit, sed Ioannes prior gratiam sensit: illa naturae ordine audivit, iste exsultavit ratione mysterii: illa Mariae, iste Domini sensit adventum: femina mulieris, et pignus pignoris. Istae gratiam loquuntur, illi intus operantur, pietatisque mysterium maternis adoriuntur profectibus; duplicique miraculo prophetant matres spiritu parvulorum. Exsultavit infans, repleta est mater. Non prius mater repleta, quam filius: sed cum filius esset repletus Spiritu sancto, replevit et matrem. Exsultavit Ioannes, exsultavit et Mariae spiritus. Exsultante Ioanne, repletur Elizabeth: Mariam tamen non repleri Spiritu, sed spiritum eius exsultare cognovimus; incomprehensibilis enim incomprehensibiliter operabatur in matre. Et illa post conceptum repletur, ista ante conceptum.

namsiinterhomineseademumfirmaamicitiestq.en: For if among men that friendship at length is firm which likeness of character hath joined, though yet sameness of wills often tendeth to wicked affections, how much ought we to desire and strive that in nothing we differ from those things which are pleasing to God! Of whom the prophet saith: For wrath is in his indignation; and life in his good will: because the dignity of the divine majesty will not otherwise be in us, unless there be imitation of his will.
namsiinterhomineseademumfirmaamicitiestq.la: Nam si inter homines ea demum firma amicitia est, quam morum similitudo sociarit, cum tamen parilitas voluntatum saepe in reprobos tendat affectus, quantum nobis optandum atque nitendum est ut in nullo ab iis quae Deo sunt placita, discrepemus! De quo dicit propheta: Quoniam ira in indignatione ejus, et vita in voluntate ejus: quia non aliter in nobis erit dignitas divinae majestatis, nisi imitatio fuerit voluntatis.

dicenteitaquedominodiligesdominumdeumtuu.en: Since therefore the Lord saith: Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with thy whole heart, and with thy whole mind; and thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself: let the faithful soul take up the unfading charity of its Author and Ruler, and subject itself wholly also to his will, in whose works and judgments nothing is void of the truth of justice, nothing of the compassion of mercy. For though one be wearied with great labours and many hardships, he hath good cause for bearing them who understandeth that by adversities he is either corrected or proved. But the loving-kindness of this charity cannot be perfect unless our neighbour also be loved. By which name are to be understood not those only who are joined to us by friendship or kinship, but all men whatsoever, with whom we have a common nature, whether they be enemies or allies, whether free or bond.
dicenteitaquedominodiligesdominumdeumtuu.la: Dicente itaque Domino: Diliges Dominum Deum tuum ex toto corde tuo, et ex tota mente tua; et diliges proximum tuum sicut teipsum: suscipiat fidelis anima auctoris sui atque rectoris immarcescibilem charitatem, totamque se etiam ejus subjiciat voluntati, in cujus operibus atque judiciis nihil vacat a veritate justitiae, nihil a miseratione clementiae. Quoniam etsi magnis quis laboribus et multis fatigetur incommodis, bona est illi causa tolerandi, qui se adversis vel corrigi intelligit, vel probari. Charitatis vero istius pietas perfecta esse non poterit, nisi diligatur et proximus. Quo nomine non ii tantum intelligendi sunt qui nobis amicitia aut propinquitate junguntur, sed omnes prorsus homines, cum quibus nobis natura communis est, sive illi hostes sint, sive socii; sive liberi, sive servi.

adprecesnostrasdeitatisaures.en: To our prayers the ears of thy Godhead,

deusinclinapietatesola.en: O God, incline of thy mercy alone,

supplicumvotasuscipeprecamur.en: Receive the vows of thy suppliants, we pray,

respiceclemenssoliodesancto.en: Look down in mercy from thy holy throne,

vultuserenolampadesillustra.en: With serene countenance enlighten our lamps,

luminetuotenebrasdepelle.en: With thy light drive out the darkness,

criminalaxapietatemulta.en: Loose our crimes in thy great mercy,

abluesordesvinculadisrumpe.en: Wash away our filth, break our chains,

parcepeccatisrelevaiacentes.en: Spare our sins, raise up the fallen,

tesinetetromergimurprofundo.en: Without thee we are plunged in the foul deep,

labimuraltascelerissubunda.en: We sink beneath the high wave of wickedness,

brachiotuotrahimuradclara.en: By thine arm we are drawn to the light,

christeluxverabonitasetvita.en: O Christ, true light, goodness and life.
christeluxverabonitasetvita.la: Christe, lux vera, bónitas et vita.

gaudiummundipietasimmensa.en: Joy of the world, mercy immeasurable,

quinosamorteroseosalvasti.en: Who hast saved us from death by thy rosy
quinosamorteroseosalvasti.la: Qui nos a morte róseo salvasti

inseretuumpetimusamorem.en: Implant, we beseech thee, thy love

mentibusnostrisfideirefunde.en: In our minds, of faith pour forth again

lumeneternumcharitatisauge.en: The eternal light, of charity increase

tunobisdonafontemlacrimarum.en: Grant thou to us a fount of tears,

vitiacarnismilliaretunde.en: Beat back the thousand vices of the flesh

proculanobisperfidusabsistat.en: Far from us let the faithless one depart,

sanctusassistatspiritusatua.en: Let the Holy Ghost stand by us, from thy

gloriadeositeternopatri.en: Glory be to God the eternal Father,

sittibisempergenitorisnate.en: Be to thee ever, Son of the Begetter,

cumquequalisspirituspercuncta.en: With whom the equal Spirit through all
cumquequalisspirituspercuncta.la: Cum quo æquális Spíritus per cuncta,

commemoratiodominicaipostpentecostem.en: Commemoration of the 1st Sunday after Pentecost

delibroprimoregum.en: From the First Book of Kings.

etfactumestindiebusillisconveneruntphili.en: And it came to pass in those days, that the Philistines gathered themselves together to fight: and Israel went out to war against the Philistines, and camped by the Stone of help. And the Philistines came to Aphec,
etfactumestindiebusillisconveneruntphili.la: Et factum est in diebus illis, convenerunt Philisthiim in pugnam: et egressus est Israël obviam Philisthiim in prælium, et castrametatus est juxta Lapidem adjutorii. Porro Philisthiim venerunt in Aphec,

etinstruxeruntaciemcontraisrelinitoautem.en: And put their army in array against Israel. And when they had joined battle, Israel turned their backs to the Philistines, and there was slain in that fight here and there in the fields about four thousand men.
etinstruxeruntaciemcontraisrelinitoautem.la: et instruxerunt aciem contra Israël. Inito autem certamine, terga vertit Israël Philisthæis: et cæsa sunt in illo certamine passim per agros, quasi quatuor millia virorum.

etreversusestpopulusadcastradixeruntquem.en: And the people returned to the camp: and the ancients of Israel said: Why hath the Lord defeated us today before the Philistines? Let us fetch unto us the ark of the covenant of the Lord from Silo, and let it come in the midst of us, that it may save us from the hand of our enemies.
etreversusestpopulusadcastradixeruntquem.la: Et reversus est populus ad castra: dixeruntque majores natu de Israël: Quare percussit nos Dominus hodie coram Philisthiim? Afferamus ad nos de Silo arcam fœderis Domini, et veniat in medium nostri, ut salvet nos de manu inimicorum nostrorum.

misitergopopulusinsilettuleruntindearcam.en: So the people sent to Silo, and they brought from thence the ark of the covenant of the Lord of hosts sitting upon the cherubims: and the two sons of Heli, Ophni and Phinees, were with the ark of the covenant of God.
misitergopopulusinsilettuleruntindearcam.la: Misit ergo populus in Silo, et tulerunt inde arcam fœderis Domini exercituum sedentis super Cherubim: erantque duo filii Heli cum arca fœderis Dei, Ophni et Phinees.

cumquevenissetarcafederisdominiincastrav.en: And when the ark of the covenant of the Lord was come into the camp, all Israel shouted with a great shout, and the earth rang again.
cumquevenissetarcafederisdominiincastrav.la: Cumque venisset arca fœderis Domini in castra, vociferatus est omnis Israël clamore grandi, et personuit terra.

etaudieruntphilisthiimvocemclamorisdixer.en: And the Philistines heard the noise of the shout, and they said: What is this noise of a great shout in the camp of the Hebrews? And they understood that the ark of the Lord was come into the camp.
etaudieruntphilisthiimvocemclamorisdixer.la: Et audierunt Philisthiim vocem clamoris, dixeruntque: Quænam est hæc vox clamoris magni in castris Hebræorum? Et cognoverunt quod arca Domini venisset in castra.

timueruntquephilisthiimdicentesvenitdeus.en: And the Philistines were afraid, saying: God is come into the camp. And sighing, they said:
timueruntquephilisthiimdicentesvenitdeus.la: Timueruntque Philisthiim, dicentes: Venit Deus in castra, et ingemuerunt, dicentes:

confortaminietestoteviriphilisthiimneser.en: Take courage and behave like men, ye Philistines: lest you come to be servants to the Hebrews, as they have served you: take courage and fight.
confortaminietestoteviriphilisthiimneser.la: Confortamini, et estote viri, Philisthiim, ne serviatis Hebræis, sicut et illi servierunt vobis: confortamini, et bellate.

pugnaveruntergophilisthiimetcesusestisre.en: So the Philistines fought, and Israel was overthrown, and every man fled to his own dwelling: and there was an exceeding great slaughter; for there fell of Israel thirty thousand footmen.
pugnaveruntergophilisthiimetcesusestisre.la: Pugnaverunt ergo Philisthiim, et cæsus est Israël, et fugit unusquisque in tabernaculum suum: et facta est plaga magna nimis, et ceciderunt de Israël triginta millia peditum.

etarcadeicaptestduoquoquefiliihelimortui.en: And the ark of God was taken: and the two sons of Heli, Ophni and Phinees, were slain.
etarcadeicaptestduoquoquefiliihelimortui.la: et arca Dei capta est: duo quoque filii Heli mortui sunt, Ophni et Phinees.

cumqueillenominassetarcamdeiceciditdesel.en: And when he had named the ark of God, he fell from his stool backwards by the door, and broke his neck and died.
cumqueillenominassetarcamdeiceciditdesel.la: Cumque ille nominasset arcam Dei, cecidit de sella retrorsum juxta ostium, et fractis cervicibus mortuus est.

exhomadpopantioch.en: 60th Homily to the people of Antioch.

quoniamverbumdicithocestcorpusmeumetasse.en: Since the Word saith: This is my body, let us both assent and believe, and behold it with the eyes of the understanding. For Christ hath delivered to us nothing sensible: but, though in things sensible, yet all things intelligible. So also in baptism: by a sensible thing, namely water, the gift is bestowed; but that which is wrought, the birth and the renewal, is intelligible. For if thou wert incorporeal, he would have given thee these gifts bare and incorporeal: but because the soul is joined to the body, he giveth thee things intelligible in things sensible. How many now say: I would fain see his form, his figure, his clothes, his shoes? Behold, thou seest him, thou touchest him, thou eatest him. And thou indeed desirest to see his clothes: but he granteth thee not only to see him, but also to eat him, and to touch him, and to take him within thee. Let no one therefore approach with loathing, no one slackly, but all on fire, all fervent and roused. For if the Jews, standing, and having shoes on their feet, and holding staves in their hands, ate the lamb in haste: much more oughtest thou to be watchful. For they indeed were about to set out for Palestine, and therefore had the guise of wayfarers: but thou must pass into heaven. Wherefore thou oughtest to watch in all things: for no small punishment is set forth for them that receive unworthily.
quoniamverbumdicithocestcorpusmeumetasse.la: Quoniam Verbum dicit: Hoc est corpus meum: et assentiamur, et credamus, et intellectualibus ipsum oculis intueamur. Nihil enim sensibile nobis Christus tradidit: sed sensibilibus quidem rebus, at omnia intelligibilia. Itidem et in baptismate: per rem nempe sensibilem aquam, donum confertur: intelligibile vero quod perficitur, generatio et renovatio. Si enim incorporeus esses, nuda et incorporea tibi dedisset ipse dona: sed quoniam anima corpori conserta est, in sensibilibus intelligibilia tibi præbet. Quot nunc dicunt: Vellem ipsius formam aspicere, figuram, vestimenta, calceamenta? Ecce eum vides, ipsum tangis, ipsum manducas. Et tu quidem vestimenta cupis videre: ipse vero tibi concedit non tantum videre, verum et manducare, et tangere, et intra te sumere. Igitur accedat nemo cum nausea, nemo resolutus, omnes accensi, omnes ferventes et excitati. Nam si Judæi stantes, et calceamenta in pedibus habentes, et baculos manibus gestantes, agnum cum festinatione comedebant: te multo magis oportet esse solertem. Nam illi quidem in Palæstinam erant profecturi, et propterea viatorum figuram habebant: tu vero debes in cælum migrare. Quapropter in omnibus oportet te vigilare: nec enim parva pœna proponitur indigne sumentibus.

consideraquarumadversusproditoremindigna.en: Consider how thou art indignant against the traitor, and against them that crucified him: and so consider lest thou also be guilty of the body and blood of Christ. They slew the most holy body, but thou receivest it with a defiled soul, after so many benefits. For it was not enough for him to be made man, to be smitten with buffets, and to be crucified: but he also mingleth himself with us; and not by faith only, but in very deed he maketh us his body. How much purer then ought he to be who enjoyeth such a sacrifice? than what sunbeam ought not the hand to be more resplendent that divideth this flesh? the mouth that is filled with spiritual fire, the tongue that is reddened with that most awful blood? Think with what honour thou art distinguished, of what table thou partakest. That which the Angels beholding tremble, and dare not look upon freely because of the brightness that flasheth therefrom; with this are we fed, with this are we united, and we are made one body of Christ, and one flesh.
consideraquarumadversusproditoremindigna.la: Considera quarum adversus proditorem indignaris, contra eos, qui illum crucifixerunt: ítaque considera, ne tu quoque sis reus corporis et sanguinis Christi. Illi sanctissimum corpus occiderunt, tu vero polluta suscipis anima, post tot beneficia. Neque enim illi satis fuit, hominem fieri, colaphis cædi, et crucifigi: verum et semetipsum nobis commiscet; et non fide tantum, verum et ipsa re nos suum efficit corpus. Quo non oportet igitur esse puriorem, tali fruentem sacrificio? quo solari radio non splendidiorem manum, carnem hanc dividentem? os quod igni spiritali repletur, linguam quæ tremendo nimis sanguine rubescit? Cogita quali sis insignitus honore, quali mensa fruaris. Quod Angeli videntes horrescunt, neque libere audent intueri propter emicantem inde splendorem; hoc nos pascimur, huic nos unimur, et facti sumus unum Christi corpus, et una caro.

quisloqueturpotentiasdominiauditasfaciet.en: Who shall declare the powers of the Lord? who shall set forth all his praises? What shepherd feedeth his sheep with his own blood? And why say I, a shepherd? There are many mothers who, after the pains of childbirth, give their children to other nurses. But this he hath not endured: but he himself feedeth us with his own blood, and in all ways joineth us closely to himself. To each of the faithful he uniteth himself through the mystery, and those whom he hath begotten he nourisheth by himself, and giveth them not to another: by this again persuading thee that he took thy flesh. Let us not then be slothful, being counted worthy of such charity and honour. See ye not with what eagerness infants take the breast, and with what force they fasten their lips upon the paps? Let us too approach this table with like alacrity, nay rather with far greater, let us draw, as infants at the breast, the grace of the Spirit, and let our one sorrow be to be deprived of this food. The works set before us are not of human power. He that then did these things at that supper, the same doeth them now also. We hold the place of ministers: but he that sanctifieth them and changeth them is he himself.
quisloqueturpotentiasdominiauditasfaciet.la: Quis loquetur potentias Domini, auditas faciet omnes laudes ejus? Quis pastor oves proprio pascit cruore? Et quid dico, pastor? Matres multæ sunt, quæ post partus dolores, filios aliis tradunt nutricibus. Hoc autem ipse non est passus: sed ipse nos proprio sanguine pascit, et per omnia nos sibi coagmentat. Unicuique fidelium semet ipsum per mysterium commiscet, et quos genuit per semet ipsum enutrit, nec alteri tradit: et hoc tibi rursum persuadens quod carnem tuam assumpsit. Ne torpeamus igitur tanta digni charitate, et honore putati. Nonne uidetis quanta promptitudine paruuli papillas capiunt, et quanto impetu labia uberibus infigunt? Accedamus cum tanta nos quoque alacritate ad hanc mensam, quinimmo cum longe majori trahamus tamquam infantes lactentes spiritus gratiam, et unus sit nobis dolor hac esca privari. Non sunt humanæ uirtutis opera proposita. qui tunc ista fecit in illa cena, idem ea nunc quoque facit. Nos ministrorum tenemus locum: qui uero sanctificat ea, et immutat, ipse est.

inillotemporedixitiesusphariseisparabola.en: At that time: Jesus spake unto the Pharisees this parable: A certain man made a great supper, and bade many. And so on.
inillotemporedixitiesusphariseisparabola.la: In illo témpore: Dixit Jesus pharisæis parabolam hanc: Homo quidam fecit cœnam magnam, et vocavit multos. Et réliqua.

hocdistarefratrescarissimiinterdeliciasc.en: Between the delights of the body and of the heart, dearly beloved brethren, there is wont to be this difference: that bodily delights, when they are not possessed, kindle a strong desire for themselves; but when they are greedily eaten, they forthwith turn the eater to loathing through satiety.
