But, on the contrary, spiritual delights, when they are not possessed, are held in loathing; but when they are possessed, in desire: and they are hungered after the more by him that eateth, the more they are eaten by him that hungereth. In the former the appetite pleaseth, the experience displeaseth: in the latter the appetite is of little worth, and the experience pleaseth the more. In the former appetite begetteth satiety, satiety loathing: but in the latter appetite bringeth forth satiety, satiety appetite. For spiritual delights increase desire in the mind, while they satisfy it: because the more their savour is perceived, the more is that known which is to be loved the more eagerly: and therefore when they are not possessed they cannot be loved, because their savour is unknown. For who can love that which he knoweth not?
hocdistarefratrescarissimiinterdeliciasc.la: Hoc distare, fratres carissimi, inter delicias corporis et cordis solet: quod corporales deliciæ, cum non habentur, grave in se desiderium accendunt: cum vero avide eduntur, comedentem protinus in fastidium per satietatem vertunt. At contra, spiritales deliciæ, cum non habentur, in fastidio sunt; cum vero habentur, in desiderio: tantoque a comedente amplius esuriuntur, quanto et ab esuriente amplius comeduntur. In illis appetitus placet, experientia displicet: in istis appetitus vilis est, et experientia magis placet. In illis appetitus saturitatem, saturitas fastidium generat: in istis autem appetitus saturitatem, saturitas appetitum parit. Augent enim spiritales deliciæ desiderium in mente, dum satiant: quia quanto magis earum sapor percipitur, eo amplius cognoscitur quod avidius ametur: et idcirco non habitæ amari non possunt, quia earum sapor ignoratur. Quis enim amare valeat quod ignorat?

proindepsalmistanosadmonetdicensgustatee.en: Hence the Psalmist admonisheth us, saying: O taste, and see that the Lord is sweet. As if he said openly: Ye know not his sweetness, if ye taste it not at all: but touch the food of life with the palate of the heart, that, proving its sweetness, ye may be able to love it. But man lost these delights when he sinned in paradise: he went forth outside, when he closed his mouth to the food of eternal sweetness. Whence we also, born in the misery of this pilgrimage, come hither already loathing, and know not what we ought to desire. And the disease of our loathing groweth the more, the more the soul withdraweth itself from eating of that sweetness; and it desireth not the inward delights, for this very reason, that it hath long and far grown unused to eating them. Therefore we waste away with our loathing, and are wearied with the long plague of starvation. And because we will not taste within the sweetness prepared for us, we wretched ones love our hunger without.
proindepsalmistanosadmonetdicensgustatee.la: Proinde Psalmista nos admonet, dicens: Gustate et videte, quoniam suavis est Dominus. Ac si aperte dicat: Suavitatem ejus non cognoscitis, si hanc minime gustatis: sed cibum vitæ ex palato cordis tangite, ut probantes ejus dulcedinem, amare valeatis. Has autem homo delicias tunc amisit, cum in paradiso peccavit: extra exiit, cum os a cibo æternæ dulcedinis clausit. Unde nos quoque nati in hujus peregrinationis ærumna, huc fastidiosi jam venimus, nescimus quid desiderare debeamus. Tantoque se amplius fastidii nostri morbus exaggerat, quanto se magis ab esu illius dulcedinis animus elongat, et eo jam internas delicias non appetit, quo eas comedere, diu longeque desuevit. Fastidio ergo nostro tabescimus, et longa inediæ peste fatigamur. Et quia gustare intus nolumus paratam dulcedinem, amamus foris miseri famem nostram.

sermdetempcircamed.en: Sermon 197, on the Season, about the middle.

sermdeieiuniomensis.en: Sermon 9, on the fast of the seventh month.

crucemsanctamsubiitquiinfernumconfregita.en: He underwent the holy cross, who broke hell asunder; he is girded with power, he rose again the third day, alleluia.
crucemsanctamsubiitquiinfernumconfregita.la: Crucem sanctam súbiit, qui inférnum confrégit; accínctus est poténtia, surréxit die tértia, allelúja.

inillotemporedixitiesusdiscipulissuisvos.en: At that time: Jesus said unto His disciples: Ye are the salt of the earth. But if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be salted? And so on.
inillotemporedixitiesusdiscipulissuisvos.la: In illo témpore: Dixit Jesus discípulis suis: Vos estis sal terræ. Quod si sal evanúerit, in quo saliétur? Et réliqua.

exhomiliainluceantemed.en: From Homily 17 on Luke 10, before the middle.
exhomiliainluceantemed.la: Ex Homilía 17 in Lucæ 10 ante med.

considerandumnobisestutquiuneademqueexho.en: We must consider that he who sufficeth not to admonish all together by one and the same voice of exhortation, should strive to instruct each one, as far as he is able, and to edify them by private discourse. For we ought continually to weigh what is said to the holy Apostles, and through the Apostles to us: You are the salt of the earth. If then we are salt, we ought to season the minds of the faithful. Ye therefore who are shepherds, consider that ye feed the animals of God; of which animals indeed it is said to God by the Psalmist: In it shall thy animals dwell. And often we see that a rock of salt is set before brute animals, that they may lick from that same rock of salt and be bettered. As a rock of salt therefore among brute animals, so ought the priest to be among the peoples. For the priest must needs take care what he saith to each, how he admonisheth every one: that whosoever is joined to the priest may be seasoned, as by the touch of salt, with the savour of eternal life.
considerandumnobisestutquiuneademqueexho.la: Considerándum nobis est, ut, qui una eadémque exhortatiónis voce non súfficit simul cunctos admonére, stúdeat síngulos, in quantum valet, instrúere, privátis locutiónibus ædificáre. Debémus namque pensáre contínuo, quod sanctis Apóstolis dícitur, et per Apóstolos nobis: Vos estis sal terræ. Si ergo sal sumus, condíre mentes fidélium debémus. Vos ígitur, qui pastóres estis, pensáte, quia Dei animália páscitis; de quibus profécto animálibus Deo per Psalmístam dícitur: Animália tua habitábunt in ea. Et sæpe vidémus, quod petra salis brutis animálibus antepónitur, ut ex éadem salis petra lámbere débeant, et meliorári. Quasi ergo inter bruta animália petra salis, debet esse sacérdos in pópulis. Curáre namque sacerdótem necésse est, quæ síngulis dicat, unumquémque quáliter admóneat: ut quisquis sacerdóti júngitur, quasi ex salis tactu ætérnæ vitæ sapóre condiátur.

cumergocohortationesnostrasauribusvestre.en: When therefore we bring our exhortations to the ears of your holiness, believe that he himself speaketh to you whose office we discharge: because we both admonish you with his affection, and preach to you no other thing than what he taught; beseeching you that, having the loins of your mind girt up, you lead a chaste and sober life in the fear of God. You are my crown, as the Apostle saith, and my joy, if your faith, which from the beginning of the Gospel hath been preached in the whole world, shall have continued in love and holiness. For although it behoveth the whole Church, which is throughout all the world, to flourish in all virtues; yet it especially becometh you, among other peoples, to excel in the merits of piety, whom, founded upon the very citadel of the apostolic Rock, both our Lord Jesus Christ redeemed together with all men, and the blessed Apostle Peter taught above all men.
cumergocohortationesnostrasauribusvestre.la: Cum ergo cohortatiónes nostras áuribus vestræ sanctitátis adhibémus, ipsum vobis, cujus vice fúngimur, loqui crédite: quia et illíus vos afféctu monémus, et non áliud vobis, quam quod dócuit, prædicámus; obsecrántes, ut succíncti lumbos mentis vestræ, castam et sóbriam vitam in Dei timóre ducátis. Coróna mea, sicut Apóstolus ait, et gáudium vos estis, si fides vestra, quæ ab inítio Evangélii in univérso mundo prædicáta est, in dilectióne et sanctitáte permánserit. Nam licet omnem Ecclésiam, quæ in toto est orbe terrárum, cunctis opórteat florére virtútibus; vos tamen præcípue inter céteros pópulos decet méritis pietátis excéllere, quos in ipsa apostólicæ petræ arce fundátos, et Dóminus noster Jesus Christus cum ómnibus redémit, et beátus Apóstolus Petrus præ ómnibus erudívit.

prorsusinquamfiliusdavidnontantumcarnese.en: Truly, I say, a son of David, not only in the flesh, but in faith, in holiness, in devotion: whom the Lord found, as another David, according to his own heart, to whom he might safely commit the most secret and most sacred mystery of his heart: to whom, as to another David, he made manifest the uncertain and hidden things of his wisdom; and gave him not to be ignorant of the mystery which none of the princes of this world knew: to whom, finally, it was given, that which many kings and prophets, though they desired to see, saw not; to hear, and heard not; not only to see and to hear, but also to carry, to lead, to embrace, to kiss, and to nourish and to guard.
prorsusinquamfiliusdavidnontantumcarnese.la: Prorsus, inquam, filius David non tantum carne, sed fide, sed sanctitate, sed devotione: quem tamquam alterum David Dominus inuenit secundum cor suum, cui tuto committere secretissimum atque sacratissimum sui cordis arcanum: cui tamquam alteri David incerta & occulta sapientiæ suæ manifestavit; et dedit illi non ignarum esse mysterii, quod nemo principum hujus sæculi agnovit: cui denique datum est, quod multi reges et prophetæ, cum vellent videre, non viderunt; audire & non audierunt; non solum videre et audire, sed étiam portare, deducere, amplecti, deosculari, & nutrire & custodire.

propterquodsuccinctilumbosmentisvestreso.en: Wherefore having the loins of your mind girt up, being sober, trust perfectly in the grace which is offered you in the revelation of Jesus Christ,
propterquodsuccinctilumbosmentisvestreso.la: Propter quod succincti lumbos mentis vestræ, sobrii, perfecte sperate in eam, quæ offertur vobis, gratiam, in revelationem Jesu Christi:

quasifiliiobedientienonconfiguratipriori.en: As children of obedience, not fashioned according to the former desires of your ignorance:
quasifiliiobedientienonconfiguratipriori.la: quasi filii obedientiæ, non configurati prioribus ignorantiæ vestræ desideriis:

sedsecundumeumquivocavitvossanctumetipsi.en: But according to him that hath called you, who is holy, be you also in all manner of conversation holy:
sedsecundumeumquivocavitvossanctumetipsi.la: sed secundum eum qui vocavit vos, Sanctum: et ipsi in omni conversatione sancti sitis:

quoniamscriptumestsanctieritisquoniamego.en: Because it is written: You shall be holy, for I am holy.
quoniamscriptumestsanctieritisquoniamego.la: quoniam scriptum est: Sancti eritis, quoniam ego sanctus sum.

etsipatreminvocatiseumquisineacceptionep.en: And if you invoke as Father him who, without respect of persons, judgeth according to every one's work: converse in fear during the time of your sojourning here.
etsipatreminvocatiseumquisineacceptionep.la: Et si Patrem invocatis eum, qui sine acceptione personarum judicat secundum uniuscujusque opus, in timore incolatus vestri tempore conversamini.

scientesquodnoncorruptibilibusaurovelarg.en: Knowing that you were not redeemed with corruptible things as gold or silver, from your vain conversation of the tradition of your fathers:
scientesquodnoncorruptibilibusaurovelarg.la: Scientes quod non corruptibilibus, auro vel argento, redempti estis de vana vestra conversatione paternæ traditionis:

sedpretiososanguinequasiagniimmaculatich.en: But with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb unspotted and undefiled,
sedpretiososanguinequasiagniimmaculatich.la: sed pretioso sanguine quasi agni immaculati Christi, et incontaminati:

precognitiquidemantemundiconstitutionemm.en: Foreknown indeed before the foundation of the world, but manifested in the last times for you,
precognitiquidemantemundiconstitutionemm.la: præcogniti quidem ante mundi constitutionem, manifestati autem novissimis temporibus propter vos,

quiperipsumfidelesestisindeoquisuscitavi.en: Who through him are faithful in God, who raised him up from the dead, and hath given him glory, that your faith and hope might be in God.
quiperipsumfidelesestisindeoquisuscitavi.la: qui per ipsum fideles estis in Deo, qui suscitavit eum a mortuis, et dedit ei gloriam, ut fides vestra et spes esset in Deo:

helenaconstantinimaterierusalempetiitall.en: Helena, the mother of Constantine, went to Jerusalem, alleluia.
helenaconstantinimaterierusalempetiitall.la: Helena Constantini mater Jerusalem petiit, alleluja.

tuncprecepiteosomnesignecremariatillitim.en: Then she commanded that they all be burned with fire; but they, being afraid, delivered up Judas, alleluia.
tuncprecepiteosomnesignecremariatillitim.la: Tunc praecepit eos omnes igne cremari at illi timentes tradiderunt Judam, alleluja.

morsetvitaappositasunttibisinonostendasm.en: Death and life are set before thee, if thou show me not the cross of Christ, alleluia.
morsetvitaappositasunttibisinonostendasm.la: Mors et vita apposita sunt tibi si non ostendas mihi crucem Christi, alleluja.

cumqueascendissetiudasdelacuperrexitadlo.en: And when Judas had come up out of the pit, he went to the place where the holy cross lay, alleluia.
cumqueascendissetiudasdelacuperrexitadlo.la: Cumque ascendisset Judas de lacu perrexit ad locum ubi jacebat sancta crux, alleluja.

orabatiudasdeusdeusmeusostendemihilignum.en: Judas prayed: O God, my God, show me the wood of the holy cross, alleluia.
orabatiudasdeusdeusmeusostendemihilignum.la: Orabat Judas deus deus meus ostende mihi lignum sanctae crucis, alleluja.

nequesecundumlucernametponunteamsubmodoq.en: Neither do men light a candle and put it under a bushel. What think we, that it is so said, under a bushel, that only the hiding of the candle is to be understood? as though he said: No man lighteth a candle and hideth it. Or doth the bushel also signify something? so that to put a candle under a bushel is to set the comforts of the body above the preaching of the truth, so that a man therefore preacheth not the truth, while he feareth lest he suffer some trouble in bodily things. And well is it called a bushel, whether because of the retribution of measure, whereby each shall receive the things he hath done in the body; that there, saith the Apostle, every one may receive the things done in the body: and as though of this bushel of the body it is said in another place: With what measure you mete, it shall be measured to you again. Or because temporal goods, which are accomplished by the body, are both begun and pass away within a fixed measure of days.
nequesecundumlucernametponunteamsubmodoq.la: Neque secundum lucernam, et ponunt eam sub modo. Quid putamus, ita esse dictum sub modo, ut occultatio tantum lucernæ accipienda sit? tanquam si diceret. Nemo accendit lucernam, et occultat illam. An aliquid étiam modus significat? ut hoc sit ponere lucernam sub modo, superiora facere corporis commoda, quam prædicationem ueritatis, ut ideo quisque ueritatem non prædicet, dum timet ne aliquid in rebus corporalibus molestiæ patiatur. Et bene modius dicitur, sive propter retributionem mensuræ, qua quisque recipiet quæ gessit in corpore; ut illic, inquit Apostolus, recipiat unusquisque quæ gessit in corpore: et tamquam de hoc modio corporis alio loco dicant, In qua mensura mensi fueritis, in ea remetietur uobis. Sine quoniam temporalia bona, quæ corpore peraguntur, certa dierum mensura et inchoantur, et transeunt.

commemoratiooctavespetri.en: Commemoration of the Octave of St. Peter

tuespastoroviumprincepsapostolorumtibitr.en: Thou art the Shepherd of the sheep, * the Prince of the Apostles; unto thee are given the keys of the kingdom of heaven.
tuespastoroviumprincepsapostolorumtibitr.la: Tu es Pastor óvium * Princeps Apostolorum, tibi traditæ sunt claves regni cælorum.

etsuperhancpetramedificabecclesiammeam.en: And upon this rock I will build my Church.
etsuperhancpetramedificabecclesiammeam.la: Et super hanc petram ædificabo Ecclésiam meam.

deusquihodiernamdiemapostolorumtuorumpet.en: O God, who didst hallow this day by the martyrdom of thine Apostles Peter and Paul: grant to thy Church in all things to follow the precept of those through whom she received the beginning of religion.
deusquihodiernamdiemapostolorumtuorumpet.la: Deus, qui hodiérnam diem Apostolórum tuórum Petri et Pauli martýrio consecrásti: da Ecclésiæ tuæ, eórum in ómnibus sequi præcéptum; per quos religiónis sumpsit exórdium.

sermovenerabilisbedepresbyteri.en: Sermon of the Venerable Bede, Priest

inlucevangcapi.en: On the Gospel of Luke, chap. 1

acceptovirginisconsensumoxangeluscelesti.en: Having received the Virgin's consent, the angel forthwith returneth to heaven; she goeth to the hill country, she hasteneth to visit Elizabeth, not as one unbelieving of the oracle, or doubtful of the example, but as one joyful in her desire, devout in her duty, giving likewise a figurative example, that every soul which hath conceived the Word of God in its mind should forthwith climb with the step of love the lofty summits of the virtues, that it may be able to enter the city of Juda, that is, the citadel of confession and praise, and to abide therein, as it were for three months, unto the perfection of faith, hope and charity.
acceptovirginisconsensumoxangeluscelesti.la: Accepto virginis consensu, mox angelus cælestia repetit, illa petit montana, festinat invisere Elisabeth, non quasi incredula de oraculo, vel dubia de exemplo, sed ut læta de voto, religiosa pro officio, typicum pariter exemplum tribuens, quod omnis anima, quæ Verbum Dei mente conceperit, virtutum statim celsa cacumina gressu conscendat amoris, quatenus civitatem Juda, id est confessionis, et laudis arcem penetrare, et usque ad perfectionem fidei, spei, et caritatis, quasi tribus in ea mensibus valeat commorari.

discevirgohumilitatemmarieutetcorporecas.en: Learn, O virgin, the humility of Mary, that thou mayest be both chaste in body and devout in heart. The younger visiteth the elder, the virgin greeteth the wife. For it is fitting that the more chaste a virgin is, the more humble she be, and that, deferring to her elders, she commend the habit of chastity by the praise of humility. In another sense, Mary cometh to Elizabeth, the Lord cometh to John: the one that she may be filled with the Holy Ghost, the other that his baptism may be consecrated: and the humbling of the greater is surely the exaltation of the lesser.
discevirgohumilitatemmarieutetcorporecas.la: Disce virgo humilitatem Mariæ, ut et corpore casta, et pectore possis esse devota. Visitat junior seniorem, salutat virgo uxorem. Decet enim, ut quo castior virgo, eo sit humilior, et senioribus deferens, habitum castitatis præconio commendet humilitatis. Aliter Maria ad Elisabeth, Dominus venit ad Joánnem, hæc ut Spiritu Sancto repleatur, illius ut baptisma consacretur: majorumque humiliatio minorum est utique exaltatio.

vocempriorelisabethaudivitsedioannesprio.en: Elizabeth first heard the voice, but John first felt the grace. She heard by the order of nature, he leaped by reason of the mystery. She felt the coming of Mary, he the coming of the Lord. These speak of grace, those work it within, and they set about the mystery of loving-kindness by the advancing of their mothers, and by a twofold miracle the mothers prophesy by the spirit of their little ones. The infant leaped, and the mother was filled; the mother was not filled before the son, but when the son had been filled with the Holy Ghost, he filled his mother also.
vocempriorelisabethaudivitsedioannesprio.la: Vocem prior Elisabeth audivit, sed Joannes prior gratiam sensit. Illa naturæ ordine audivit, iste exaltavit ratione mysterii. Illa Mariæ, iste Domini sensit adventum. Istæ gratiam loquuntur, illi intus operantur, pietatisque mysterium maternis adoriuntur profectibus, duplicique miraculo prophetant matres spiritu paruulorum. Exultavit infans, et repleta mater est; non prius mater repleta quam filius, sed cum filius esset repletus Spiritu Sancto, replevit et matrem.

piusaquiliensisimperatoremantoninoveropo.en: Pius of Aquileia, created Pontiff under the Emperor M. Antoninus Verus, appointed a penalty for the priest through whose negligence any of the blood of the Lord should have been spilt. Let them do penance, he saith, forty days, if aught have fallen upon the ground; if upon the altar, three days; if upon the upper cloth, four; if it have flowed down upon the lower, nine days; if as far as the fourth, twenty days: wheresoever it hath fallen, if it can be taken up, let it be licked up; if otherwise, let it be either washed or scraped: whatsoever hath been washed or scraped, let it be burned, and the ashes laid up in the sacrarium. Having moreover made many useful decrees, he was crowned with martyrdom, and was buried in the Vatican on the fifth of the Ides of July; having sat eleven years, two months, twenty-one days: and in five ordinations in the month of December he had created ten bishops, nine priests, twenty-one deacons.
piusaquiliensisimperatoremantoninoveropo.la: Pius Aquiliensis, Imperatore M. Antonino Vero, Pontifex creatus, pœnam statuit in sacerdotem cujus negligentia de sanguine domini aliquid stillaverit. Pænitentiam enim, inquit, agant quadraginta diebus, si in terram aliquid deciderit, si super altare, tribus diebus: si super linteum superius, quattuor: si in inferius defluxerit, novem diebus: si usque ad quartum, uiginti diebus: ubi cumque ceciderit, si recipi potest, lambatur; sin aliter, aut lavetur, aut radatur: quidquid lotum, aut rasum est, comburatur, et cinis in sacrarium reponatur. Multis præterea utiliter decretis martyrio coronatur, et sepelitur in Vaticano quinto idus Julii; cum sedisset annos undecim, menses duos, dies uiginti unum: et episcopos decem, presbyteros novem, diaconos uigintiunum, mense Decembri quinque ordinationibus creasset.

inillotemporedixitiesusturbissiquisvenit.en: At that time, Jesus said unto the multitudes: If any man come to Me, and hate not his father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brethren, and sisters, yea, and his own life also, he cannot be My disciple. And so on.
inillotemporedixitiesusturbissiquisvenit.la: In illo témpore: Dixit Jesus turbis: Si quis venit ad me, et non odit patrem suum, et matrem, et uxorem, et filios, et fratres, et sorores, adhuc autem et animam suam, non potest meus esse discipulus. Et réliqua.

siconsideremusfratrescarissimiqueetquant.en: If we consider, dearly beloved brethren, what and how great are the things that are promised us in heaven, all things that are possessed on earth grow vile in the mind. For earthly substance, compared with heavenly felicity, is a burden, not a help. Temporal life, compared with eternal life, is rather to be called death than life. For what else is the very daily decay of corruption but a certain prolonging of death? But what tongue sufficeth to tell, or what understanding to grasp, how great are those joys of the city above: to be among the choirs of Angels, to stand with the most blessed spirits before the glory of the Creator, to behold the present face of God, to see the light that hath no bounds, to be touched by no fear of death, to rejoice in the gift of everlasting incorruption? But at the hearing of these things the soul is inflamed, and already longeth to stand there where it hopeth to rejoice without end. But to great rewards one cannot come except through great labours. Whence also Paul the excellent preacher saith: He shall not be crowned, except he strive lawfully.
siconsideremusfratrescarissimiqueetquant.la: Si consideremus fratres carissimi, quæ et quanta sunt, quæ nobis promittuntur in cælis, vilescunt animo omnia quæ habentur in terris. Terrena namque substantia supernæ felicitati comparata, pondus est, non subsidium. Temporalis vita æternæ vitæ comparata, mors est potius dicenda quam vita, Ipse enim quotidianus defectus corruptionis quid est aliud, quam quædam prolixitas mortis? Quæ autem lingua dicere, vel quis intellectus capere sufficit, illa supernæ civitatis quanta sint gaudia; Angelorum choris interesse, cum beatissimis spiritibus gloriæ Conditoris assistere, præsentem Dei vultum cernere, incircumscriptum lumen videre, nullo mortis metu affici, incorruptionis perpetuæ munere lætari? Sed ad hæc audita inardescit animus, jamque illic cupit assistere, ubi se sperat sine fine gaudere. Sed ad magna præmia perveniri non potest, nisi per magnos labores. Unde et Paulus egregius prædicator dicit: Non coronabitur, nisi qui legitime certaverit.

delectetergomentemmagnitudopremiorumsedn.en: Let the greatness of the rewards therefore delight the mind, but let not the struggle of the labours deter it. Whence the Truth saith to them that come to him: If any man come to me, and hate not his father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brethren, and sisters, yea and his own life also, he cannot be my disciple. But it is fitting to ask how we are commanded to hate our parents and kindred according to the flesh, who are bidden to love even our enemies? And surely the Truth saith of the wife: What God hath joined together, let no man put asunder. And Paul saith: Husbands, love your wives, as Christ also the Church. Behold, the disciple preacheth that the wife is to be loved, whereas the Master saith: He that hateth not his wife cannot be my disciple. Doth the judge announce one thing, and the herald cry another? Or can we at once both hate and love? But if we weigh the force of the precept, we are able to do both by discernment: so that we love our wife, and them that are joined to us by kinship of the flesh, and whom we know to be our neighbours; and those whom we suffer as adversaries in the way of God, we disown by hating and fleeing them.
delectetergomentemmagnitudopremiorumsedn.la: Delectet ergo mentem magnitudo præmiorum, sed non deterreat certamen laborum. Unde ad se venientibus Veritas dicit: Si quis venit ad me, et non odit patrem suum, et matrem, et uxorem, et filios, et fratres, et sorores, adhuc autem et animam suam, non potest meus esse discipulus. Sed percontari libet, quomodo parentes et carnaliter propinquos præcipimur odisse, qui jubemur et inimicos diligere? Et certe Veritas de uxore dicit: Quod Deus conjunxit, homo non separet. Et Paulus ait: Viri, diligite uxores vestras, sicut et Christus Ecclesiam. Ecce, discipulus uxorem diligendam prædicat, cum magister dicat: Qui uxorem non odit, non potest meus esse discipulus. Numquid aliud judex nuntiat, aliud præco clamat? An simul et odisse possumus, et diligere? Sed si vim præcepti perpendimus, utrumque agere per discretionem valemus: ut uxorem, et eos, qui nobis carnis cognatione conjuncti sunt, et quos proximos novimus, diligamus; et quos adversarios in via Dei patimur, odiendo et fugiendo nesciamus.

quasienimperodiumdiligiturquicarnaliters.en: For he is loved, as it were, through hatred, who, being carnally minded, is not hearkened to when he urgeth wicked things upon us. But that the Lord might show that this hatred toward our neighbours proceedeth not from passion but from charity, he added forthwith that we must hate our own life also. It is plain therefore that he ought to hate his neighbour by loving him, who hateth him even as himself. For then do we well hate our own soul, when we yield not to its carnal desires, when we break its appetite, when we strive against its pleasures. That which therefore, being despised, is led to better things, is loved as it were through hatred. Thus doubtless ought we to show to our neighbours the discernment of this hatred, that we both love in them what they are, and hold in hatred that wherein they withstand us in the way of God.
quasienimperodiumdiligiturquicarnaliters.la: Quasi enim per odium diligitur, qui carnaliter sapiens, dum prava nobis ingerit, non auditur. Ut autem dominus demonstraret hoc erga proximos odio non de affectione procedere, sed de charitate, addidit protinus, odisse et animam nostram. Constat ergo, quia amando debet odisse proximum, qui sic eum odit sicut semet ipsum. tunc etenim nostram animam bene odimus, cum ejus carnalibus desiderijs non acquiescimus, cum ejus appetitum frangimus, ejus uoluptatibus reluctamur. Quæ ergo contempta ad melius ducitur, quasi per odium amatur. Sic nimirum exhibere proximis nostria odij discretionem debemus, ut in eis et diligamus quod sunt, et habeamus odio quod in dei nobis itinere obsistunt.

hodiereginaassistesadextrisfiliiubiquere.en: Today the Queen, standing at the right hand of her Son who reigneth everywhere, in gilded clothing, surrounded with the variety of incorruption and immortality, is celebrated in sacred and solemn words; not that she standeth there according to the spirit only, as it were without body and flesh: but that she is clothed, as regardeth her most holy flesh, with incorruptibility and immortality. And again she is surrounded with variety, as regardeth the most holy bones which uphold her flesh. For from her flesh and from her bones, as from the old Adam, this new Adam, that he might fulfil his part, fashioned for himself a rib, namely this incarnation, and having once put it on, he beareth it for ever. And hence this new Eve is called the mother of life, and remaineth surrounded with variety unto the firstfruits of the immortal life of all the living.
hodiereginaassistesadextrisfiliiubiquere.la: Hodie regina assistes a dextris filii ubique regnantis, quasi in vestitu deaurato, incorruptionis, et immortalitatis circumamicta varietate, sacris et sollemnibus verbis celebratur, non quod secundum spiritum tantum, quasi sine corpore, et carne assistat: sed quod induta sit quantum spectat ad sanctissimam ejus carnem incorruptibilitate, et immortalitate. Circumamicta varietate rursus est, quantum attinet ad ossa sanctissima, quæ ejus carnem suffulciunt. Nam ex carne ejus, et ex ossibus ejus, veluti ex veteri Adamo novus iste Adam, ut vicem ejus expleret, costam sibi finxit, nimirum istam incarnationem, eaque semel indutam perpetuo gestat. Ac proinde nova ista Eva mater vitæ appelatur, circumamictaque varietate permanet ad primitias vitæ immortalis omnium viventium.

beatamtepredicantomnesangelorumetterrest.en: All the hierarchies of angels and of earthly beings proclaim thee blessed: thou who art both blessed in the heavens, and on earth proclaimed blessed: Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb. For with blessings of this kind doth the first rank, which consisteth of the Thrones, Cherubim and Seraphim, celebrate: Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is thy womb which bore God, and the breasts which he, while yet a little infant, sucked. And the second hierarchy, which embraceth within itself the Dominations, Virtues and Powers, learning from the higher hierarchy, looketh upon thee and crieth: Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is thy womb which conceived God, and the paps which nourished God when he was made a child.
beatamtepredicantomnesangelorumetterrest.la: Beatam te prædicant omnes angelorum, et terrestrium hierarchiæ: quæ et in cœlis benediceris, et in terris beata prædicaris: Benedicta tu in mulieribus, et benedictus fructus ventris tui, Hujusmodi enim benedictionibus celebrat prima acies quæ ex Thronis, Cherubinis, et Seraphinis constat: Beata tu in mulieribus, et beatus uterus tuus, qui portavit Deum: et ubera, quæ ille adhuc infantulus suxit. Secunda vero hierarchia, quæ in se Dominationes, Virtutes, Potestatesque complectitur, a sublimiori hierarchia ediscens, ad te respiciens clamat, Benedicta tu in mulieribus, et benedictus venter tuus, qui Deum concepit: et mammillæ, quæ Deum educaverunt puerum factum.

iamtertiexprincipibusangelisetarchangeli.en: And now the third rank, of the Principalities, Angels and Archangels, to whom it was commanded by God who sent them that through Gabriel the Archangel alone it should put forth a most splendid and most capacious hymn in these words: Hail, full of grace, the Lord is with thee. From these, then, we the earthly hierarchies, bearing the exaltations of God hereafter, whether because we have learned it, or because we have borrowed these words, exalt thee with a great and tuneful voice, saying: Hail, full of grace, the Lord is with thee: intercede, O Mistress and Lady, and Queen, and Mother of God, for us; and he who was brought forth of thee is our God incarnate; to whom belongeth glory and magnificence, and all honour and adoration and thanksgiving, with the Father who is without beginning, and with the holy, good and lifegiving Spirit, both now and ever, and world without end. Amen.
iamtertiexprincipibusangelisetarchangeli.la: Jam tertia ex principibus, angelis, et archangelis acies, quibus mandatum fuit a Deo mittente, ut per unum Gabrielem archangelum ederet splendidissimum, et capacissimum hymnum in hæc verba: Ave gratia plena, Dominus tecum: Ab istis deinde nos hierarchiæ terrestres, exaltationes Dei in future ferentes, sive quod didicimus, sive quod mutuo hæc verba sumpserimus, exaltamus te magna et canora voce dicentes: Ave gratia plena: dominus tecum: intercede hera, et Domina, et regina, et mater dei pro nobis et qui editus est ex te, incarnatus Deus poster est; quem decet gloria, et magnificentia: omnisque honor, et adoratio, et gratiatum actio: cum patre initii experte, et cum santo, bono, vivifico spiritu, et nunc et semper, et in sæcula sæculorum. Amen.

inillotemporeintravitiesusinquoddamcaste.en: At that time: Jesus entered into a certain village, and a certain woman, named Martha, received Him into her house. And so on.
inillotemporeintravitiesusinquoddamcaste.la: In illo témpore: Intravit Jesus in quoddam castellum: et mulier quædam, Martha nomine, excepit illum in domum suam. Et réliqua.

quidautemputamusnosreprebensumesseminist.en: But what do we think, that the ministry of Martha was reproved ... should press on to the one knowledge.
quidautemputamusnosreprebensumesseminist.la: Quid autem putamus nos reprebensum esse ministerium Marthæ ... uni instet scientiæ.

simeliorparsestcurnonomnessedmultaabuno.en: If it is the better part, why do not all ... but many things from one.
simeliorparsestcurnonomnessedmultaabuno.la: Si melior pars est, cur non omnes … sed multa ab uno.

multasuntquefactusuntergonecistaminister.en: Many are the things that have been made: ... therefore neither these ministries.
multasuntquefactusuntergonecistaminister.la: Multa sunt quæ factu sunt: … ergo nec ista ministeria.

exsermdeverbisdompauloantemedium.en: From Sermon 27 on the Words of the Lord, a little before the middle
exsermdeverbisdompauloantemedium.la: Ex Serm. 27. de Verbis Dom., paulo ante medium

benemarthacircacorporalemdominiquiddicam.en: Well did Martha minister to the bodily, what shall I say, need or will, of the Lord? She ministered to mortal flesh. But who was in the mortal flesh? In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. Behold what Mary was hearing. The Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us. Behold him to whom Martha ministered. Therefore Mary hath chosen the better part, which shall not be taken away from her. For she chose that which shall abide for ever; therefore it shall not be taken away from her.
benemarthacircacorporalemdominiquiddicam.la: Bene Martha circa corporalem Domini, quid dicam, necessitatem, an voluntatem? ministrebat carni mortali. Sed quis erat in carne mortali? In principio erat Verbum, et Verbum erat apud Deum, et Deus erat Verbum. Ecce quod Maria audiebat. Verbum caro factum est, et habitavit in nobis. Ecce Martha cui ministrabat. Ergo Maria meliorem partem elegit, quae non auferetur ab ea. Hoc enim elegit, quod semper manebit, ideo non auferetur ab ea.

circaunummariasevoluitoccupariiamtenebat.en: Mary wished to be busied about one thing. Already she held fast: But it is good for me to adhere to God. She sat at the feet of our Head. The more humbly she sat, the more did she receive. For water floweth together into the lowliness of the valley, it runneth down from the swellings of the hill. The Lord therefore did not rebuke the work, but distinguished the service. Thou art busy about many things: but one thing is necessary. This Mary hath already chosen for herself.
circaunummariasevoluitoccupariiamtenebat.la: Circa unum Maria se voluit occupari. Jam tenebat: Mihi autem adhærere Deo bonum est. Sedebat ad pedes capitis nostri. Quanto humilius sedebat, tanto amplius capiebat. Confluit enim aqua ad humilitatem convallis, denotat de tumoribus collis. Non ergo Dominus opus reprehendit, sed munus distinxit. Circa multa es occupata: porro unum est necessarium. Jam hoc sibi Maria elegit.

exantiquaaccepimustraditionequodtemporeg.en: We have received from ancient tradition, that at the time of the glorious falling-asleep of the blessed Virgin, all the holy Apostles, who were journeying through the world for the salvation of the Gentiles, being borne aloft in a moment of time, came together at Jerusalem. And when they were there, there appeared to them a vision of angels, and the psalmody of the heavenly Powers was heard; and so with divine glory she gave up her holy soul into the hands of God. But her body, which had in an unspeakable manner received God, being borne forth by the care of the angels and with the hymnody of the apostles, was laid in a tomb at Gethsemane; in which place the song of the Angels continued for three days together.
exantiquaaccepimustraditionequodtemporeg.la: Ex antiqua accepimus traditione, quod tempore gloriosae dormitionis beatae Virginis, universi quidem sancti Apostoli, qui orbem terrae ad salutem Gentium peragrabant, momento tomporis in sublime elati, convenerunt Jerosolymis: cumque illic essent, eis visio apparuit angelica, et audita est psalmodia coelestium Potestatum; et sic cum divina gloria in manus Dei sanctam tradidit animam. Ejus autem corpus, quod Deum ineffabili quadam ratione suscepit, cura angelica et apostolica hymnodia elatum, in loculo fuit depositum Gethsemane: quo in loco Angelorum cantus mansit tres dies continuos.

posttresautemdiesangelicocantucessantequ.en: But after three days, the song of the Angels ceasing, the Apostles that were present opened the tomb (since Thomas alone, who had been absent, came after the third day, and desired to venerate the body that had received God); but in no part could they find her sacred body. And when they had found only the things in which she had been laid, and were filled with an unspeakable fragrance which came forth from them, they closed the tomb. Astonished at the wonder of this mystery, they could think only this, that he who was pleased to take flesh of the Virgin Mary, and to be made man and to be born, though he was God the Word and the Lord of glory, and who after the birth kept her virginity incorrupt; the same was pleased also, after she had departed, to honour her immaculate body, kept incorrupt, by translating it before the common and universal resurrection.
posttresautemdiesangelicocantucessantequ.la: Post tres autem dies angelico cantu cessante, qui aderant Apostoli cum unus Thomas, qui abfuerat, post tertiura diera venisset, et quod Deum susceperat, corpus adorare voluisset, tumulum aperuerunt; sed orani ex parte sacrum ejus corpus nequáquam invenire potuerunt. Cum ea autem tantum invenissent, in quibus fuerat compositura, et ineffabili, qui ex iis proficiscebatur, essent odore repleti, loculum clauserunt. Ejus mysterii obstupefacti miraculo hoc solum cogitare potuerunt, quod cui placuit ex Maria Virgine carnem suniere, et hominera fieri et nasci, cura esset Deus Verbum, et Dominus gloriae: quique post partura incoruptam servavit ejus virginitatem, eidem etiam placuit et ipsius, postquara migravit, iramaculatum corpus, incorruptum servatum, translatione honorare ante communem et universalem resurrectionem.

aderanttunccumapostolissanctissimustimot.en: There were present then with the Apostles the most holy Timothy, the first bishop of the Ephesians, and Dionysius the Areopagite, as he himself testifieth in those things which he wrote to the aforesaid Timothy concerning blessed Hierotheus, who himself also was then present, speaking thus: For even among the inspired Prelates themselves, when we also, as thou knowest, and many of our holy brethren, had come together to behold the body that gave the beginning of Life and received God (and there were present also James the brother of the Lord, and Peter, the supreme and most ancient summit of theologians): the sacred body having been seen, it pleased all, as each was able, to celebrate in hymns the infinite goodness of the divine power.
aderanttunccumapostolissanctissimustimot.la: Aderant tunc cum Apostolis sanctissimus Timotheus, primus episcopus Ephesiorum, et Dionysius Areopagita, sicut ipse testatur in iis, quae de beato Hierotheo, qui ipse quoque tunc aderat, scripsit ad praedictum Timotheum, sic dicens: Nam etiam apud ipsos a Deo afflatos sacrorum antistites, quando nos quoque, ut nosti, et multi ex sanctis nostris fratribus, ad contuendum corpus, quod vitae principium dedit, et Deum suscepit, convenissemus (aderat autem et Domini frater Jacobus, et Petrus, suprema et antiquissima theologdrum summitas): et viso sacro corpore, placuit omnibus, prout quisque poterat, hymnis celebrare infinitam bonitatem divinae potentiae.

libergenerationisiesuchristifiliidavidfi.en: The Book of the generation of Jesus Christ, the Son of David, the son of Abraham. Abraham begat Isaac, and Isaac begat Jacob. And so on.
libergenerationisiesuchristifiliidavidfi.la: Liber generationis Jesu Christi filii David, filii Abraham. Abraham genuit Isaac. Isaac autem genuit Jacob. Et reliqua.

etposttransmigrationembabylonisiechonias.en: And after the transmigration of Babylon, Jechonias begot Salathiel. If we wish to put Jechonias at the end of the first fourteen, in the following there will not be fourteen, but thirteen. Let us know therefore that the former Jechonias is the same as Joakim, and the second the son, not the father. Of whom the former is described; which, through the fault of scribes and the length of time, hath been confused among the Greeks and Latins.
etposttransmigrationembabylonisiechonias.la: Et post transmigrationem Babylonis Iechonias genuit Salathiel. Si uoluerimus Iechoniam in fine primæ tessaradecadis ponere, in sequenti non erunt quattuordecim, sed tredecim. Sciamus igitur Iechoniam priorem ipsum esse quem et Ioacim, secundum autem filium non patrem. Quorum prior describitur; quod scriptorum uitio et longitudine temporum apud Græcos Latinosque confusus est.

iacobautemgenuitiosephhunclocumobiecitno.en: And Jacob begot Joseph. This passage the Emperor Julian cast up against us as a disagreement of the Evangelists: why the Evangelist Matthew called Joseph the son of Jacob, and Luke called him the son of Heli; not understanding the custom of the Scriptures, that the one is his father according to nature, the other according to the law. For we know that this was commanded through Moses at the bidding of God, that if a brother or a kinsman should die without children, another his brother should take his wife to raise up seed to his brother or his kinsman. Joseph the husband of Mary: when thou hearest husband, let not a suspicion of marriage steal upon thee, but remember the custom of the Scriptures, that the betrothed are called husbands, and the betrothed women wives.
iacobautemgenuitiosephhunclocumobiecitno.la: Iacob autem genuit Ioseph. Hunc locum obiecit nobis Iulianus Augustus dissonantiæ evangelistarum, cur euangelista Matthæus Ioseph dixerit filium Iacob, et Lucas eum filium appellarit Heli, non intelligens consuetudinem scripturarum, quod alter secundum naturam, alter secundum legem ei pater sit. Scimus enim hoc per Moysem deo iubente præceptum, ut si frater aut propinquus absque liberis mortuus fuerit, alius ejus frater accipiat uxorem ad suscitandum semen fratris, uel propinqui sui. Ioseph uirum Mariæ, cum utrum audieris, suspitio tibi non subeat nuptiarum, sed recordare consuetudinis scripturarum, quod sponsi uiri, et sponsæ uocentur uxores.

etatransmigrationebabylonisusqueadchrist.en: And from the transmigration of Babylon to Christ are fourteen generations. Count from Jechonias to Joseph, and thou wilt find thirteen generations. The fourteenth generation therefore will be reckoned in Christ himself. Now the generation of Christ was in this wise. Let the diligent reader inquire and say: Since Joseph is not the father of the Lord Saviour, what doth the order of the generation, brought down to Joseph, pertain to the Lord? To whom we shall answer, first, that it is not the custom of the Scriptures that the order of women be woven into the generations; then, that Joseph and Mary were of one tribe, whence by the law he was bound to take her as a kinswoman:
etatransmigrationebabylonisusqueadchrist.la: Et a transmigratione Babylonis usque ad Christum generationes quattuordecim. Numera a Iechonia usque ad Ioseph, et inuenies generationes tredecim. Quartadecima ergo generatio in ipsum Christum reputabitur. Christi autem generatio sic erit. Quærat diligens lector, et dicat: Cum Ioseph non sit pater domini salvatoris, quid pertinet ad dominum generationis ordo deductus usque ad Ioseph? Cui respondebimus primum, non esse consuetudinis scripturarum, ut mulierum in generationis ordo texatur: deinde, ex una tribu fuisse Ioseph et Mariam, unde ex lege eam accipere cogebatur ut propinquam:

deifiliusnondiuitemautlocupletemaliquamf.en: The Son of God chose for his mother not a rich or wealthy woman, but that blessed Virgin whose soul was adorned with virtues. For since blessed Mary kept chastity above all human nature, therefore she conceived Christ the Lord in her womb. Running therefore to this most holy Virgin and Mother of God, let us obtain the profit of her patronage. Therefore all ye who are virgins, whosoever ye be, flee to the Mother of the Lord. For she by her patronage will keep for you your most beautiful, most precious and incorruptible possession.
deifiliusnondiuitemautlocupletemaliquamf.la: Dei Fílius non díuitem, aut locuplétem áliquam féminam sibi matrem elégit, sed beátam vírginem illa, cujus ánima virtútibus ornáta erat. Cum enim beáta María supra omnem humánam natúram castitátem seruáret, proptérea Christum Dóminum in ventre concépit. Ad hanc ígitur sanctíssimam vírginem et Dei matrem accurréntes, ejus patrocíniis utilitátem assequámur. Ítaque quacúmque estis vírgines, ad matrem Dómini confúgite. Illa enim pulchérrimam, pretiosíssimam, et incorruptíbilem possessiónem patrocínio suo vobis conservábit.

magnumreueramiraculumfratresdilectissimi.en: A great miracle indeed, dearly beloved brethren, was the blessed ever-Virgin Mary. For what greater or more illustrious than she hath at any time been found, or can at any time be found? She alone hath surpassed heaven and earth in greatness. What is holier than she? Not Prophets, not Apostles, not Martyrs, not Patriarchs, not Angels, not Thrones, not Dominations, not Seraphim, not Cherubim, nor finally any other thing among created things visible or invisible, can be found greater or more excellent. She is at once the handmaid and the mother of God: at once virgin and parent.
magnumreueramiraculumfratresdilectissimi.la: Magnum reuéra miráculum, fratres dilectíssimi, fuit beáta semper virgo María. Quid namque illa majus aut illústrius ullo umquam témpore inuéntum est, seu aliquándo inveníri póterit? Hæc sola cælum ac terram amplitúdine superávit. Quidnam illa sánctius? Non Prophétæ, non Apóstoli, non Mártyres, non Patriárchæ, non Ángeli, non Throni, non Dominatiónes, no Séraphim, non Chérubim, non dénique áliud quídpiam inter creátas res visíbiles aut inuisíbiles, majus aut excelléntius inveníri potest. Eadem ancílla Dei est et mater: éadem virgo et génitrix.

haceiusmaterestquiapatreanteomneprincipi.en: She is his mother, who was begotten of the Father before all beginning, whom Angels and men acknowledge as the Lord of all things. Wouldst thou know how much more excellent this Virgin is than the heavenly powers? They stand by with fear and trembling, veiling their faces: she offereth the human race to him whom she bore. Through her also we obtain pardon of sins. Hail therefore, Mother, heaven, maiden, virgin, throne, the adornment, glory and stay of our Church; pray assiduously for us to Jesus thy Son and our Lord, that through thee we may find mercy in the day of judgement, and may obtain the good things which are laid up for them that love God, by the grace and loving-kindness of our Lord Jesus Christ: with whom to the Father together and to the Holy Ghost be glory, honour and dominion, now and ever, world without end. Amen.
haceiusmaterestquiapatreanteomneprincipi.la: Hac ejus mater est, qui a Patre ante omne princípium génitus suit, que Ángeli et hómines agnóscunt Dóminum rerum ómnium. Vis ne cognóscere, quanto virgo hæc præstántior fit cæléstibus poténtis? Illæ cum timóre et tremóre assistunt, fáciem velántes suam: hæc humánum genus illi offert quem génuit. Per hanc et peccatórum véniam conséquimur. Ave ígitur mater, cælum, puélla, virgo, thronus, Ecclésiæ nostræ decus, glória et firmaméntum, assídue pro nobis precáre Jesum fílium tuum et Dóminum nostrum: ut per te misericórdiam inveníre in die judícij, et quæ repósita sunt iis qui díligunt Deum, bona cónsequi possímus, grátia et benignitáte Dómini nostri Jesu Christi: cum quo Patri simul et sancto Spirítui glória, honor, et impérium nunc et semper in sǽcula sæculórum, Amen.

sermosancticyrilliepiscopialexandrini.en: Sermon of St. Cyril, Bishop of Alexandria.

hilaremvideohodiecetumfideliumomniumquic.en: I see today a joyful assembly of all the faithful, who have come together with ready hearts, called together by holy Mary, the Mother of God, ever Virgin. Praise and glory be to thee, O holy Trinity, that thou hast called us all together to this feast. Praise be also to thee, O holy Mother of God. For thou art the precious pearl of the world: thou the lamp of unquenchable light, the crown of virginity, the sceptre of the orthodox faith, the indissoluble temple containing him who can nowhere be contained, Mother and Virgin: thou art blessed among women, the parent of him who cometh blessed in the name of the Lord.
hilaremvideohodiecetumfideliumomniumquic.la: Hilarem video hodie cœtum fidelium omnium, qui convenerunt promptis animis, a sancta et Dei Matre Maria semper Virgine convocati. Laus et gloria sit tibi sancta Trinitas, quod omnes nos ad hanc celebritatem convocaris. Sit étiam tibi sancta Dei Mater laus. Tu enim es pretiosa margarita orbis terrarum: tu lucerna inextincti luminis, corona virginitatis, sceptrum orthodoxæ fidei, templum indissolubile continens eum qui nusquam contineri potest, Mater et Virgo: tu benedicta inter inter mulieres, ejus parens qui benedictus venit in nomine domini.

pertetrinitassanctificaturpertecruxpreti.en: Through thee the Trinity is hallowed: through thee the precious Cross is named and adored in all the world. Through thee heaven exulteth, Angels and Archangels rejoice, devils are put to flight, and man himself is called back to heaven. Every creature held fast by the error of idols hath been turned to the knowledge of the truth, and faithful men have come to holy Baptism, and churches have been built in all the world.
pertetrinitassanctificaturpertecruxpreti.la: Per te Trinitas sanctificatur: per te crux pretiosa dicitur, et adoratur in toto orbe terrarum. Per te exsultat cælum, lætantur Angeli et Archangeli, fugantur dæmones, et homo ipse ad cælum revocatur. Omnis creatura idolorum errore detenta, conversa est ad notitiam veritatis, et fideles homines ad sanctum baptisma pervenerunt, atque in toto orbe terrarum constructæ sunt ecclesiæ.

teadiutricegentesveniuntadpenitentiamqui.en: By thy help the nations come to repentance. What more? Through thee the only-begotten Son of God, that true light, hath shone upon them that sat in darkness and in the shadow of death. Thee the Prophets foretold, thee the Apostles celebrated with the highest praises. Who shall be able to set forth the proclamation of thy praises, O Mary, Mother and Virgin? Her, dearly beloved brethren, let us celebrate, adoring her Son, the spotless Bridegroom of the Church: to whom be honour and glory world without end. Amen.
teadiutricegentesveniuntadpenitentiamqui.la: Te adjutrice gentes veniunt ad pœnitentiam. Quid plura? Per te unigenitus Dei Filius vera illa lux effulsit sedentibus in tenebris et umbra mortis. Te Prophetæ prænuntiarunt, te apostoli summis laudibus celebrarut.. Quisnam poterit tuarum laudum præconia explicare, Maria Mater et Virgo? Hanc, fratres dilectissimi, celebremus, ejus Filium Ecclesiæ sponsum immaculatum adorantes: cui honor et gloria in sæcula sæculorum. Amen.

exaudidomineprecesnostrasetinterveniente.en: Graciously hear our prayers, O Lord: and, blessed Damasus thy Confessor and Bishop interceding, be appeased and grant us pardon and peace.
exaudidomineprecesnostrasetinterveniente.la: Exáudi, Dómine, preces nostras: et interveniénte beáto Dámaso Confessóre tuo atque Pontífice, indulgéntiam nobis tríbue placátus et pacem.

quiexteortusestsoliustitie.en: For out of thee rose the Sun of righteousness.
quiexteortusestsoliustitie.la: Quia ex te ortus est sol justítiæ

commemoratiodominicatertiapostpascha.en: Commemoration of the Third Sunday after Easter

decusparentietfilio.en: Honour to the Father and to the Son,

sanctoquesitspiritui.en: And to the Holy Ghost be it,

regnumqueinomneestseculum.en: And kingdom is unto every age.

hocchristenobishocpater.en: This to us, O Christ, this, O Father,

liberdelignovite.en: Book of the Tree of Life.

porroutdelaterechristidormientisformaret.en: Moreover, that the Church might be formed out of the side of Christ sleeping, it was granted by divine ordinance that one of the soldiers should pierce that sacred side with a spear, opening it, so that, as blood with water flowed forth, the price of our salvation might be poured out; which, shed forth from the hidden fountain of the Heart, should give power to the sacraments of the Church to confer the life of grace, and should be for those already living in Christ a cup of the living fountain, springing up unto life everlasting. Arise therefore, O soul, friend of Christ, cease not to watch, there put thy mouth, that thou mayest draw waters out of the Saviour's fountains.
porroutdelaterechristidormientisformaret.la: Porro ut de latere Christi dormientis formaretur Ecclesia, divina est ordinatione indultum, ut unus militum lancea latus sacrum illud aperiendo perfoderet, quatenus sanguine cum aqua manente pretium effunderetur nostrae salutis, quod a fonte scilicet Cordis arcano profusum, vim daret sacramentis Ecclesiae ad vitam gratiae conferendam, essetque jam in Christo viventibus poculum fontis vivi, salientis in vitam aeternam. Surge igitur anima amica Christi, vigilare non cesses, ibi os appone, ut haurias aquas de fontibus Salvatoris.

mortuenimaitiesuetadhucincrucependenteap.en: For when Jesus was dead, he saith, and still hanging on the cross, a soldier cometh near, pierceth his side with a spear, and thence flowed water and blood. The one is the symbol of baptism, the other of the sacrament. Therefore he saith not: There came out blood and water; but there came out first water, and blood, because first we are washed by baptism, and afterwards are consecrated by the mystery.
mortuenimaitiesuetadhucincrucependenteap.la: Mortuo enim, ait, Jesu, et adhuc in cruce pendente, approximat miles, latus lancea perciissit, et exinde aqua fluxit, et sanguis. Unum baptismatis symbolum, aliud sacramenti. Ideo non ait: Exiit sanguis et aqua; sed exiit aqua primum et sanguis, quia primum baptismate diliiimur, et postea mysterio dedicamur.

audifilietvideetinclinaauremtuametoblivi.en: Hearken, O daughter, and see, and incline thy ear, and forget thy people and thy father's house:
audifilietvideetinclinaauremtuametoblivi.la: Audi, fília, et vide, et inclína aurem tuam, et oblivíscere pópulum tuum, et domum Patris tui:

etconcupiscetrexdecoremtuum.en: And the King shall greatly desire thy beauty.

manumsuammisitadfortia.en: She hath put out her hand to strong things:

manumsuamaperuitinopietpalmassuasextendi.en: She hath opened her hand to the needy, and stretched out her hands to the poor.
manumsuamaperuitinopietpalmassuasextendi.la: Manum suam apéruit ínopi, et palmas suas exténdit ad páuperem.

invocavietvenitinmespiritussapientieetpr.en: I called, and the spirit of wisdom came upon me, and I preferred her before kingdoms and thrones:
invocavietvenitinmespiritussapientieetpr.la: Invocávi, et venit in me spíritus sapiéntiæ, et præpósui illam regnis et sédibus:

etdivitiasnihilesseduxiincomparationeill.en: And esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her.
etdivitiasnihilesseduxiincomparationeill.la: Et divitias nihil esse duxi in comparatióne illíus.

meliorestenimsapientiacunctisopibuspreti.en: For wisdom is better than all the most precious riches.
meliorestenimsapientiacunctisopibuspreti.la: Mélior est enim sapiéntia cunctis ópibus pretiosíssimis.

homiliadelaudvirgmatris.en: Homily 1 on the Praises of the Virgin Mother

littencyclquasprimasdieidecembris.en: Encyclical Letter Quas primas, of the 11th day of December 1925
littencyclquasprimasdieidecembris.la: Litt. Encycl. Quas primas diei 11 Decembris 1925

tractinioanntractinioann.en: Treatise 51 on John, 12-13; Treatise 117 on John, 19-21
tractinioanntractinioann.la: Tract. 51 in Joann. 12-13; Tract 117 in Joann. 19-21

adcelireginamdieioctobris.en: Ad caeli Reginam, of the 11th day of October 1954

deepistolaprimabeatipauliapostoliadcorin.en: Lesson from the first letter of St. Paul the Apostle to the Corinthians
deepistolaprimabeatipauliapostoliadcorin.la: De Epístola prima beáti Pauli Apóstoli ad Corínthios

siautemresurrectiomortuorumnonestnequech.en: But if there be no resurrection of the dead, then Christ is not risen again.
siautemresurrectiomortuorumnonestnequech.la: Si autem resurréctio mortuórum non est: neque Christus resurréxit.

siautemchristusnonresurrexitinanisesterg.en: And if Christ be not risen again, then is our preaching vain, and your faith is also vain.
siautemchristusnonresurrexitinanisesterg.la: Si autem Christus non resurréxit, inánis est ergo prædicátio nostra, inánis est et fides vestra:

invenimurautemetfalsitestesdeiquoniamtes.en: Yea, and we are found false witnesses of God: because we have given testimony against God, that he hath raised up Christ; whom he hath not raised up, if the dead rise not again.
invenimurautemetfalsitestesdeiquoniamtes.la: invenímur autem et falsi testes Dei: quóniam testimónium díximus advérsus Deum quod suscitáverit Christum, quem non suscitávit, si mórtui non resúrgunt.

namsimortuinonresurguntnequechristusresu.en: For if the dead rise not again, neither is Christ risen again.
namsimortuinonresurguntnequechristusresu.la: Nam si mórtui non resúrgunt, neque Christus resurréxit.

deactibusapostolorum.en: Lesson from the Acts of the Apostles

deielepropheta.en: Lesson from the book of Joel

etfiliisionexsultateetletaminiindominode.en: And you, O children of Sion, rejoice, and be joyful in the Lord your God: because he hath given you a teacher of justice, and he will make the early and the latter rain to come down to you as in the beginning.
etfiliisionexsultateetletaminiindominode.la: Et fílii Sion exsultáte, et lætámini in Dómino Deo vestro: quia dedit vobis doctórem justítiæ, et descéndere fáciet ad vos imbrem matutínum et serótinum, sicut in princípio.

etimplebunturareefrumentetredundabunttor.en: And the floors shall be filled with wheat, and the presses shall overflow with wine and oil.
etimplebunturareefrumentetredundabunttor.la: Et implebúntur áreæ fruménto, et redundábunt torculária vino et óleo.

etreddamvobisannosquoscomeditlocustabruc.en: And I will restore to you the years, which the locust, and the bruchus, and the mildew, and the palmerworm hath eaten: my great host which I sent upon you.
etreddamvobisannosquoscomeditlocustabruc.la: Et reddam vobis annos, quos comédit locústa, bruchus, et rubígo, et erúca: fortitúdo mea magna quam misi in vos.

etcomedetisvescentesetsaturabiminietlaud.en: And you shall eat in plenty, and shall be filled: and you shall praise the name of the Lord your God, who hath done wonders with you: and my people shall not be confounded for ever.
etcomedetisvescentesetsaturabiminietlaud.la: Et comedétis vescéntes, et saturabímini: et laudábitis nomen Dómini Dei vestri, qui fecit mirabília vobíscum: et non confundétur pópulus meus in sempitérnum.

etscietisquiainmedioisrelegosumetegodomi.en: And you shall know that I am in the midst of Israel: and I am the Lord your God, and there is none besides: and my people shall not be confounded for ever.
etscietisquiainmedioisrelegosumetegodomi.la: Et sciétis quia in médio Israël ego sum, et ego Dóminus Deus vester, et non est ámplius: et non confundétur pópulus meus in ætérnum.

eteritpostheceffundamspiritummeumsuperom.en: And it shall come to pass after this, that I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh: and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy: your old men shall dream dreams, and your young men shall see visions.
eteritpostheceffundamspiritummeumsuperom.la: Et erit post hæc: effúndam spíritum meum super omnem carnem, et prophetábunt fílii vestri et fíliæ vestræ: senes vestri sómnia somniábunt, et júvenes vestri visiónes vidébunt.

possumusetaliterdicerequodetiameisdemver.en: We can also say otherwise: that it is written in the same words, according to the Hebrew truth, in Isaias: There shall come forth a rod out of the root of Jesse, and a Nazarene shall go up out of his root.
possumusetaliterdicerequodetiameisdemver.la: Possumus et aliter dicere: quod etiam eisdem verbis, juxta Hebraicam veritatem, in Isaia scriptum sit: Exiet virga de radice Jesse, et Nazaræus de radice ejus conscendet.

maurusnobilisromanuspuerapatreeutychiode.en: Maurus, a noble Roman, offered to God as a boy by his father Eutychius under the discipline of St. Benedict, in a short time made such progress by divine grace that he was a wonder to his master himself; who often set him before the other disciples to imitate, as a pattern of regular observance and of all virtues.
maurusnobilisromanuspuerapatreeutychiode.la: Maurus nobilis Romanus, puer a patre Eutychio Deo sub sancti Benedicti disciplína oblatus, brevi tantum divina grátia profecit, ut ipsi magistro admiratióni esset; qui illum sæpe, véluti regularis observantiæ et virtútum ómnium specimen, ceteris discípulis ad imitándum proponebat.

cuiusadhucadolescentisilludadmirabilisob.en: Of him, while yet a youth, that example of wonderful obedience is recorded by Pope St. Gregory. For when Placidus the monk, having fallen into the lake, was being carried away by the force of the waters, Maurus, running up at the command of the holy Father, and walking upon the waters, seized his companion by the hair and drew him to land.
cuiusadhucadolescentisilludadmirabilisob.la: Cujus adhuc adolescentis illud admirábilis obediéntiæ exemplum a sancto Gregório Papa commemorátur. Nam, cum Placidus mónachus in lacum prolapsus, aquárum ímpetu raperétur, sancti Patris jussu accurrens Maurus, et super aquas incédens, socium capíllis apprehensum, ad terram attraxit.

continentietantafuitutperquadragesimambi.en: So great was his abstinence, that through Lent he took food only twice in the week, and that most sparingly. He took his sleep standing, or, when excessive weariness compelled him, sitting, upon a heap of lime and sand spread with haircloth.
continentietantafuitutperquadragesimambi.la: Continentiæ tantá fuit, ut per Quadragesimam bis tantum in hebdomada, et quidem parcissime cibum sumeter. Somnum stando, vel cum nimia, eum lassitudo compulisset, sededo, super aggestum calcis et fabuli strato cilicio capiebat.

missusingalliamabeodemsanctobenedictocel.en: Sent into Gaul by the same St. Benedict, having built a famous monastery, over which he presided forty years, he wonderfully spread the monastic discipline. At length, renowned for holiness and miracles, being more than seventy years of age, he passed to heaven, in the year of salvation five hundred and sixty-five.
missusingalliamabeodemsanctobenedictocel.la: Missus in Gálliam ab eodem sancto Benedicto, célebri monasterio exstructo, cui annos quadragínta præfuit, monasticam disciplínam mirifice propagávit. Denique sanctitáte et miraculis clarus, septuagenario major migrávit in cælum, anno salútis quingentésimo sexagésimo quinto.

tervirgiscesussumsemellapidatussumternau.en: Thrice was I beaten with rods, * once was I stoned, thrice I suffered shipwreck, for Christ the Lord.
tervirgiscesussumsemellapidatussumternau.la: Ter virgis cæsus sum, * semel lapidátus sum, ter naufrágium pértuli pro Christo Dómino. Ps. 97

gratiadeisumidquodsumetgratieiusinmevacu.en: By the grace of God * I am what I am: and his grace in me hath not been void.
gratiadeisumidquodsumetgratieiusinmevacu.la: Grátia Dei * sum id quod sum: et grátia ejus in me vácua non fuit. Ps. 98

sufficittibipaulegratiameanamvirtusmeain.en: Sufficient for thee, * O Paul, is my grace: for my power is made perfect in infirmity.
sufficittibipaulegratiameanamvirtusmeain.la: Súfficit tibi, * Paule, grátia mea: nam virtus mea in infirmitáte perfícitur. Ps. 100

ecceegomittovossicutovesinmedioluporumdi.en: Behold I † send you as sheep in the midst of wolves, saith the Lord: be ye therefore wise as serpents, and simple as doves.
ecceegomittovossicutovesinmedioluporumdi.la: Ecce ego † mitto vos sicut oves in médio lupórum, dicit Dóminus: estóte ergo prudéntes sicut serpéntes, et símplices sicut colúmbæ. Ps. 253, 254, 255

robertusincampanianobilibusortusparentib.en: Robert, born in Champagne of noble parents (when, while his mother was with child of him, the Mother of God appeared to her, and espoused her finger with a ring, saying that she willed that the son whom she bore in her womb should be her spouse; which was the cause that all his monasteries were consecrated to the name of the Mother of God), in his eleventh year received the regular habit at St. Peter de la Celle. There, giving himself night and day to fastings and prayers, he rendered to God a pleasing service, subjecting the flesh to the spirit, and the spirit to the Creator. By God's disposing, having been elected Prior by the monks of that monastery, he was chosen Abbot by the monks of Tonnerre.
robertusincampanianobilibusortusparentib.la: Robertus in Campania, nobilibus ortus parentibus, cum matri su@ de illo prægnanti, Dei Mater apparuisset, et digitum ejus annulo subarrasset dicens, velle, ut suus esset sponsus filius, quem in utero prtabat: quod fuit causa, ut omnia sua Monasteria ipsius Dei Matris nomini consecrarentur: annum agens undecimum apud sanctum Petrum de Cella suscepit habitum regularem. Ubi jejuniis, et orationibus vacans nocte, et die gratum Deo exhibebat obsequium, carnem spiritui, spiritum Creatori subjiciens. Ipso sic disponente, ad Monachis illius Monasterii electus in Priorem, ad Tornodorensibus in Abbatem cooptatur.

posteaadquibusdameremitisfuitrogatusutid.en: Afterwards he was asked by certain hermits to take upon him the same office over them; and he would have satisfied their wishes, had not the monks of Tonnerre protested. Dismissing the messengers, he gave them sure hope that, as soon as the opportunity should be granted him by the Lord, he would go to them. Afterwards, taking two companions, he went to a wood whose name was Molesme, where, labouring with their own hands, they built dwellings and an oratory of the branches of trees, and therein offered to the Lord saving victims and the sacrifice of a contrite heart. But since he greatly desired that, wherever the servants of God were found, he also should be found, he came to the place Hauz, and being devoutly received by those monks, a little after they elected him Abbot.
posteaadquibusdameremitisfuitrogatusutid.la: Postea ad quibusdam Eremitis fuit rogatus, ut idem munus super eis admitteret; quorum votis satisfecisset, nisi Tornodorenses Monachi reclamassent. Dimittens nuntios spem illis certam dedit se quam cito facultas tribueretur ei à Domino, ad eos profecturum. Assumptis posteà duobus sociis, juit ad nemus, cujus nomen Molismus erat, ubi propriis manibus laborantes, ex ramis arborum domicilia, et oratorium construxerunt, in eqoque Domino salutares hostias, et sacrificium contriti cordis offerebant. Sed cum maxime desideraret ubicumque serui Dei reperiebantur, ipse quoque reperiti, venit ad locum Hauz, et devote ab istis Monachis susceptus, paulo post Abbatem illum elegerunt.

desuotamensecessumolismensescontristatis.en: The monks of Molesme, however, being saddened at his withdrawal, went to the Supreme Pontiff; and relying on his authority they recalled the man of God to Molesme; where certain monks, as Alberic and Stephen and two others, since they desired the eremitic life, set out to a place called Vivicus; but being driven thence, they came to a forest called Cîteaux, where, having built an oratory in honour of the Blessed Mary, they persevered. Now blessed Robert, hearing of their holy manner of life, took with him twenty-two monks and went to them, that he might be a sharer and helper of their holy purpose; and being received by them with the greatest devotion, he presided over them for some time with fatherly care.
desuotamensecessumolismensescontristatis.la: De suo tamen secessu Molismenses contristati Summum Pontificem adjerunt; ejusque auctoritate freti virum Dei revocavere Molismum, in quo aliqui, ut Albericus, et Stephanus, et alii duo, cum Eremiticam vitam appeterent, ad locum, Vivicus dictum profecti sunt; sed ab illo pulsi, ad syluam Cisttertium vocatam, devenerunt, ubi ædificato Oratorio in honorem Beatæ Mariæ, perseveratunt. Audiens autem beatus Robertus sanctam ipsorum conversationem, assumptis secum vigintiduobus monachis perrexit ad eos, ut sancti eorum propositi esset particeps, et adjutor, a quibuscum summa devotione susceptus, eisdem aliquandiu paterna solicitudine præfuit.

tantopastoredestituiegreferentesmonachim.en: The monks of Molesme, bearing it ill to be deprived of so great a shepherd, went to the Supreme Pontiff, that he might compel blessed Robert to return to Molesme. The Pontiff, assenting to them, wrote to the Bishop of Chalon, that, another Abbot having been appointed for the Cistercians, he should compel Robert to return to Molesme. Having therefore set in order the things that pertained to observance according to the Rule of St. Benedict, he set Alberic over them as Abbot in his place, and, when he was dead, put Stephen in his stead. And thus blessed Robert, being the founder of that new plantation, since he had the government of both monasteries, namely of Molesme and of Cîteaux, returned a second time to Molesme. At length, when his death was now drawing near, the Lord revealed to him its hour, and in the ninety-third year of his age, renowned for miracles, he sent forth his spirit to heaven, on the third day before the Kalends of May, in the year of the Lord one thousand and ninety-eight.
tantopastoredestituiegreferentesmonachim.la: Tanto pastore destitui ægre ferentes Monachi Molismi, Summum Pontificem adjerunt, ut beatum Robertum Molismum regredi cogeret. Annuens eis pontifex Cabilonensi Episcopo scripsit, quatenus alio Abbate Cisterciensibus ordinato, Robertum cogeret reverti Molismum. Dispositis ergo quæ ad observantiam, secundum regulam sancti Benedicti pertinebant, Abbatem eis loco sui præfecit Albericum, et eo mortuo Stephanum subrogavit. Sicque novellæ illius plantationis institutor existens beatus Robertus, cum utriusque Monasterii Molismensis scilicet, et Cisterciensis regimen haberet, Molismum secundo rediit. Tandem cum jam suum obitum appeteret, ejus horam illi Dominus revelavit, et anno ætatis suæ nonagesimotertio, clarus marculis spiritum transmisit ad cælos, tertio Kalendas Majii, Anno Domini millesimo nonagesimo octavo.

quidicitseinipsomaneredebetsicutilleambu.en: He that saith he abideth in him, ought himself also to walk, even as he walked.
quidicitseinipsomaneredebetsicutilleambu.la: Qui dicit se in ipso manére, debet, sicut ille ambulávit, et ipse ambuláre.

quodauteminterrogatdominusetillapetenter.en: Now that the Lord asketh, and, when she asked, answered: What wilt thou? cometh not of ignorance; but it is said in the person of him who was to be scourged and crucified. As also in the case of the woman with the issue of blood: Who touched me? And of Lazarus: Where have you laid him? In the Old Testament also: Adam, where art thou? And: I will go down and see whether they have done according to the cry that is come to me; or whether it be not so, that I may know. Now the mother of the sons of Zebedee maketh her request through a woman's error and from the affection of love, not knowing what she asked. Nor is it any wonder if she be charged with unskilfulness, since it is said of Peter, when he would make three tabernacles, that he knew not what he said.
quodauteminterrogatdominusetillapetenter.la: Quod autem intérrogat Dóminus, et, illa peténte, respóndit: Quid vis? non venit de ignorántia: sed ex ejus persóna dícitur, qui flagellándus et crucifigéndus erat. Quómodo et in hæmorrhoísa: Quis me tétigit? Et de Lázaro: Ubi posuístis eum? In véteri quoque testaménto: Adam, ubi es? Et: Descéndens vidébo si juxta clamórem, qui venit ad me, perfíciant: sin autem non est, ut sciam. Póstulat autem mater filiórum Zebedæi erróre mulíebri et pietátis afféctu, nésciens quid péteret. Nec mirum si ista arguátur imperétiæ, cum de Petro dicátur, quando tria vult fácere tabernácula, nésciens quid díceret.

gulielmusnobilibusparentibusversellisini.en: William, born of noble parents at Vercelli in Insubria, had scarcely completed the fourteenth year of his age, when, burning with a wonderful ardour of piety, he undertook a pilgrimage to that most famous church of St. James in the farthest part of Spain, whither men come together in very great numbers from the whole Christian world for the sake of fulfilling a vow. This journey he pursued barefoot, clad in a single tunic only, and girded with a double iron ring; and on it he suffered innumerable and grievous hardships of hunger, thirst, cold and heat, with the greatest peril of his life.
gulielmusnobilibusparentibusversellisini.la: Guliélmus nobílibus paréntibus Verséllis in Insúbria natus, vix quartum décimum ætátis suæ annum expléverat, eum miro quodam pietátis ardóre flagrans peregrinatiónem aggréssus est ad celebérrimum illud sancti Jacóbi templum in extréma Hispánia‚ quo ex univérso orbe Christiáno voti persolvéndi causa, frequentíssimi hómines convéniunt. Quod iter nudis pédibus, única tantum amíctus túnica, ac dúplici férreo círculo præcínctus prosecútus est; innumeráque in eo et immánia famis, sitis, frígoris, et æstus summo cum vitæ discrímine est perpéssus incómmoda.

reversusinitaliamnovamadsanctumdominisep.en: Having returned into Italy, he planned a new pilgrimage to the holy Sepulchre of the Lord, which is venerated at Jerusalem: but various and most grievous hindrances arose to prevent his carrying out his purpose, the divine Power drawing back the religious disposition of the youth to higher and holier things. Then, while he dwelt for two years on Monte Solicoli, and meanwhile wore himself down with fasting, watchings, sleeping on the ground, and continual prayers, upheld by divine help he restored sight to a blind man. When this miracle was made known and the fame of it spread abroad, William could no longer lie hidden: wherefore he thought again to go to Jerusalem, and eagerly set out upon the journey.
reversusinitaliamnovamadsanctumdominisep.la: Revérsus in Itáliam, novam ad sanctum Dómini Sepúlchrum, quod Jerosólymis cólitur, peregrinatiónem molítur: sed quóminus propósitum exequátur, vária atque gravíssima intercédunt impediménta, divíno Númine, ad altióra et sanctióra religiósam júvenis índolem retrahénte. Porro dum in solículo Monte biénnium commorátur, interímque inédia‚ vigíliis, chameúniis, atque assíduis oratiónibus macerátur, divína subníxus ope, cæco lumen restítuit. Quo édito miráculo fama percrebrescénte jam Guliélmus latére non póterat: quare íterum Jerosólymam adíre cógitat et álacris se itíneri commíttit.

deiautemmonituquieidemapparuitaproposito.en: But by the warning of God, who appeared to him, he was called back from his purpose, being destined to be more useful and more fruitful as well among the Italians as among foreign nations. Then on the summit of Monte Vergiliano, which was afterwards called the Virgin's, in a rough and inaccessible place, he built a monastery with wonderful speed. Then he gathered to himself men as his companions, and religious men, and formed them to a fixed rule of life most closely fitted to the precepts and counsels of the Gospel, both by certain laws taken in great part from the institutes of blessed Benedict, and by word and the examples of a most holy life.
deiautemmonituquieidemapparuitaproposito.la: Dei autem mónitu‚ qui eídem appáruit, a propósito revocátur, utílior ac fructuósior tam apud Italos‚ quam apud éxteras natiónes futúrus. Tum Monastérium in Virgiliáni Montis cacúmine, quod deínde Vírginis est appellátum, loco áspero et inaccésso miránda exædíficat celeritáte. Sócios deínde viros et religiósos adscíscit, eósque ad certam vivéndi normam Evangélicis præcéptis et consíliis summópere accommodátam, tum certis légibus ex beáti Benedícti institútis magna ex parte desúmptis, tum verbo et sanctissimæ vitæ exemplis infórmat.

aliisdeindemonasteriiserectisclariorindi.en: Then, other monasteries having been raised, the holiness of William, becoming more famous day by day, brought to him from all sides many men, drawn by the fragrance of his holy life and the fame of his miracles. For the dumb received speech, the deaf hearing, the withered strength, and those suffering from various and incurable diseases health, through his intercession. He turned water into wine, and wrought very many other wonders. Among which this must not be passed over in silence, that, when a wretched woman was sent to tempt his chastity, he rolled himself unhurt upon burning coals spread upon the ground. Roger, King of Naples, being informed of this, was brought to the highest admiration of the man of God. At length, having foretold the time of his death to the king and to others, renowned for countless virtues and miracles he fell asleep in the Lord, in the year of salvation one thousand one hundred and forty-two.
aliisdeindemonasteriiserectisclariorindi.la: Aliis deinde Monastériis eréctis, clárior in dies facta Guliélmi sánctitas, multos ad eum úndique viros perdúcit, sanctæ vitæ odóre, ac miraculórum fama alléctos. Nam muti loquélam, surdi audítum, áridi vigórem‚ varióque et immedicábili morbo laborántes sanitátem ipsíus intercessióne recepérunt. Aquam in vinum convértit, aliáque complúra mirabília patrávit. Inter quæ illud non siléndum, quod muliércula ad ejus castitatem tentándam missa, in ardentibus prunis humi stratis illæsum se volutávit. De qua re cértior factus Rogérius Neápolis rex, in summam viri Dei admiratiónem addúcitur. Demum témpore sui óbitus regi aliísque prænuntiáto, innúmeris virtútibus et miráculis clarus obdormívit in Dómino‚ anno salútis millésimo centésimo quadragésimo secúndo.

homlxviinnativsioanbapt.en: Homily 66; On the Nativity of St. John the Baptist 2

cunctorumquidemprophetarumfratrescarissi.en: The memory of all the prophets, dearest brethren, is indeed to be venerated.
