Blessed John the Baptist, whose very birthday is honoured today, hath so far surpassed the glory of them all, that he revealed by the truth of present witness the Lord Jesus our Saviour, not only as to come, but as already come and dwelling among men; whom, when he had seen him hastening to his baptism among the mingled crowds, pointing him out as it were with his finger, he said: Behold the Lamb of God, behold him who taketh away the sins of the world. How innocent is his life, or with what devotion can we requite his merits, who both first knew and alone showed the coming of the heavenly Lamb! How wonderful to all is the heralding of him from whose mouth the world first heard of its absolution!
cunctorumquidemprophetarumfratrescarissi.la: Cunctorum quidem prophetárum, fratres caríssimi, veneránda recordátio est. Beátus Joannes Baptísta, cujus hódie genuínus natális honorátur, in tantum ómnium illórum supergréssus est glóriam, ut Dóminum Jesum Salvatórem nostrum, non solum esse ventúrum, sed adventásse jam et cohabitáre homínibus, veritáte præsentis testimónii reveláret; quem cum inter promíscuas turbas ad baptísmum suum properáre vidísset, velut dígito demonstrans ait: Ecce Agnus Dei, ecce qui tollit peccáta mundi. Quam ínnocens hujus est vita, vel qua possumus devotióne ejus mérita compensáre, qui Agni cæléstis adventum et primus agnovit, et solus osténdit! Quam mirábile est univérsis ejus præcónium, de cujus ore primum absolutiónem suam mundus audívit!

hicestcarissimidequoprodictumestvoxclama.en: This is he, dearest brethren, of whom it was foretold: The voice of one crying in the desert: Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make straight the paths of our God. For he was to cry, as also he did cry, that, by the loud proclamation of salvation, the heavenly preaching might open the ears of mortals long stopped. Who then would not receive such a prophet with all admiration, when he recognizeth that he obtained so much from God, that his merits were praised before his birth was formed?
hicestcarissimidequoprodictumestvoxclama.la: Hic est, caríssimi, de quo prodictum est: Vox clamántis in desérto: Paráte viam Dómini, rectas fácite sémitas Dei nostri. Clamatúrus erat enim, sicut et clamávit, ut vociferánte salútis præcónio, obturátas diu aures mortálium prædicátio cæléstis aperíret. Quis ergo hujusmodi prophétam non tota admiratióne suscípiat, quem tantum recognóscit obtinuísse a Deo, ut ante ejus mérita laudarentur, quam natívitas formarétur?

hicergozacharieiustissimosacerdoticummul.en: This one, therefore, by the care of almighty God, is promised by an Angel to be born to Zachary, a most just priest, when he was far advanced in age, and, through the barrenness of his very aged wife, had despaired of the succession of the offspring he had prayed for. And fitly is a new son given to most aged parents, who should show to the ageing and failing world the Only-begotten of God for the hope of a youth to come. What is that, and with how great amazement is it to be wondered at, that Zachary himself, while he believed somewhat too slowly that the forerunner of the saving Word was to be conceived in an aged womb, was struck dumb with the silence of a sudden speechlessness, nor would have recovered the former use of speech, had not the name of the child, by which he was to be called, loosed for him the bonds of his closed mouth? And so it came about that the merit of the son being born set free the priestly mouth which the fear of one doubting had bound, and the restored tongue of the father bore witness to the glory of the infant.
hicergozacharieiustissimosacerdoticummul.la: Hic ergo Zacharíæ justíssimo sacerdóti, cum multa esset ætáte provéctus, et sterilitáte seníssimæ cónjugis successiónem votívi gérminis desperásset, omnipoténtis Dei cura per Angelum promíttitur nascitúrus. Et bene seníssimis paréntibus novus fílius datur, qui senescénti labentíque mundo Unigénitum Dei ad spem futuræ juventútis osténderet. Quid illud, quantóque est stupóre mirándum, quod Zacharías ipse, dum præcursórem salutáris Verbi concipiéndum seníli alvo paulo tárdius créderet, silentio repentínæ taciturnitátis obmútuit, nec prístinum loquéndi recepísset usum, nisi nomen púeri, quo vocándus esset, clausi oris ei víncula relaxásset? Atque ita factum est, ut os sacerdotále, quod trepidátio colligáverat dubitantis, méritum fílii nascéntis absolveret, et reparáta patris lingua infántis glóriam testarétur.

sermoinnativsioannisbaptnet.en: Sermon 291, On the Nativity of St. John the Baptist, nn. 1 and 2
sermoinnativsioannisbaptnet.la: Sermo 291, In Nativ. S. Joannis Bapt. n. 1 et 2

quemdiemcelebramushodiernumvobisdicinono.en: What day we celebrate today, there is no need to tell you, for ye all heard it when the Gospel was read. Today we have received holy John, the forerunner of the Lord, the son of a barren woman announcing the Son of a Virgin, yet a servant announcing the Lord. For because God made man was to come through a Virgin, a wonderful man went before him from a barren woman: that, when the wonderful man saith he is unworthy to loose the latchet of his shoe, the God-man may be acknowledged. Admire John as much as thou canst: what thou admirest profiteth Christ. It profiteth Christ, I say, not because thou bestowest anything on Christ, but that thou mayest profit in Christ.
quemdiemcelebramushodiernumvobisdicinono.la: Quem diem celebrámus hodiérnum, vobis dici non opus est, quia omnes, cum Evangélium legerétur, audístis. Hódie accepimus sanctum Joannem Dómini præcursórem, stérilis fílium nuntiantem Vírginis Fílium, sed tamen servum nuntiántem Dóminum. Quia enim ventúrus erat per Vírginem Deus homo, præcéssit eum de stérili mirábilis homo: ut, cum se indígnum dicit, cujus calceaménti corrígiam solvat mirábilis homo agnoscátur Deus homo. Miráre Joannem, quantum potes: Christo próficit, quod miráris. Próficit, inquam, Christo, non quia tu præstas áliquid Christo, sed ut tu profícias in Christo.

mirareergoioannemquanpotesaudistiquodmir.en: Admire John then, as much as thou canst. Thou hast heard what thou mayest admire. He is announced by an Angel to his father the priest: the Angel taketh away the voice of the father who believed not; he remaineth dumb, awaiting his tongue at the birth of his son. A barren woman conceived, an old woman too conceived: a twofold unfruitfulness, barrenness and age. It is told by the Angel what manner of man he shall be: in him is fulfilled what is told; and, what is most to be wondered at, he is filled with the Holy Ghost even from his mother's womb. Then, at the coming of holy Mary, he leapeth in the womb; and her whom he could not greet with words, he greeteth with movements. He is born, he giveth his father his voice; the father, speaking, giveth the son his name: all wonder at such great grace. For what else is it but grace? For where did this John merit God? Where did he merit God, before he was, that he might merit? O grace freely given!
mirareergoioannemquanpotesaudistiquodmir.la: Miráre ergo Joánnem, quan potes. Audísti, quod miréris. Annuntiatur per Angelum patri sacerdóti: vocem aufert Angelus patri non credénti; rémanet mutus, in fílii nativitáte exspéctans linguam. Concépit stérilis, concépit et anus: gémina infecúnditas, sterílitas et ætas. Dícitur ab Angelo, qualis futúrus sit: implétur in eo, quod dícitur; et quod máxime mirándum est, implétur Spíritu Sancto adhuc ex útero matris suæ. Deínde, veniente María sancta, exsúltat in útero; et quem non póterat vócibus, salútat mótibus. Náscitur, dat patri vocem; pater loquens dat fílio nomen: mirántur omnes tantam grátiam. Quid enim áliud quam grátia? Ubi enim Joánnes iste proméruit Deum? Ubi proméruit Deum, ántequam esset, qui promererétur? O grátia gratis data!

miranturomnescobstupescuntetmotucordissu.en: All wonder, are amazed, and say in the stirring of their heart, that it might be written for us, to be read: What, thinkest thou, shall this child be? For the hand of the Lord was with him. What, thinkest thou, shall this child be? He passeth the bounds of human nature. We know children: but what, thinkest thou, shall this child be? Why sayest thou, What, thinkest thou, shall this child be? For the hand of the Lord is with him. That the hand of the Lord is with him we know already; but what he shall be we know not. Surely he shall be very great, who hath begun so great. What shall he be, who, so little, is so great? What shall he be? Human weakness groweth dull, the hearts of all that consider it tremble: What, thinkest thou, shall this child be? He shall be great: but what shall he be, who shall be greater than he? This one shall be very great; but what shall he be, who shall be greater than this great one? If he who hath but now begun to be shall be so great, what shall he be who was?
miranturomnescobstupescuntetmotucordissu.la: Mirántur omnes, cobstupe scunt, et motu cordis sui dicunt, ut scriberétur nobis, quod legerétur: Quid, putas, erit puer iste? Nam manus Dómini cum illo. Quid, putas, erit puer iste? Excédit metas humánæ natúræ. Nóvimus púeros: sed, quid, putas, erit puer iste? Quare dicis, Quid, putas, erit puer iste? Manus enim Dómini cum illo. Quia manus Dómini cum illo est, jam scimus; sed quid erit, nescímus. Utique valde magnus erit, qui tam magnus cœpit. Quid erit, qui tantíllus, tantus est? Quid erit? Hebéscit humána infírmitas, ómnium considerántium corda contremíscunt: Quid, putas, erit puer iste? Magnus erit: sed quid erit, qui major illo erit? Valde iste magnus erit; sed quid erit, qui isto magno major erit? Si ille, qui modo cœpit esse, tam magnus erit, quid erit, qui erat?

sermoinnativitsioannissanctusbaptisteivc.en: Sermon 290, On the Nativity of St. John the Baptist IV, chap. 1
sermoinnativitsioannissanctusbaptisteivc.la: Sermo 290, In Nativit. S. Joannis Sanctus Baptiste IV, cap. 1

sanctusioannesbaptistamissusestantefacie.en: St. John the Baptist was sent before the face of Christ to prepare his ways. The testimony of Christ concerning John is: Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist. The testimony of John concerning Christ is: He that cometh after me is greater than I, the latchet of whose shoe I am not worthy to loose. Let us consider both testimonies, that which the Lord bore to the servant, and that which the servant bore to the Lord. What is the testimony of the Lord concerning the servant? Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist. What is the testimony of the servant concerning the Lord? He that cometh after me is greater than I. If then among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist; he who is greater than he, what is he? John is a great man, but a man: Christ is greater than John, because he is God and man.
sanctusioannesbaptistamissusestantefacie.la: Sanctus Joannes Baptista missus est ante faciem Christi præparáre vias ejus. Testimonium Christi de Joanne est: In natis mulierum non surrexit major Joanne Baptista. Testimonium Joannis de Christo est: Qui venit post me, major me est, cujus non sum dignus corrigiam calceamenti solvere. Utrumque testimonium consideremus, quod perhibuit Dominus servo, et quod perhibuit servus Domino. Quod est testimonium Domini de servo? In natis mulierum non surrexit major Joanne Baptista. Quod est testimonium servi de Domino? Qui venit post me, major me est. Si ergo in natis mulierum non surrexit major Joanne Baptista; qui major illo est, quid est? Joannes magnus homo, sed homo: Christus Joánne major, quia Deus et homo.

ambomirabiliternatiprecoiudexlucernetdie.en: Both were wonderfully born, the herald and the Judge, the lamp and the day, the voice and the Word, the servant and the Lord. The Lord himself made for himself a servant in a barren womb, of an aged father and of an old mother: and the same Lord himself made for himself flesh in the womb of a Virgin, without a human father, he who made the first man without father and mother. There hath not risen among them that are born of women a greater than John the Baptist. So great did John appear, that by some he was even thought to be the Christ. Neither did he in his pride follow another's error, nor dared he say: I am what ye think: but, as was good for him, he knew himself, that he might be humbled as a servant at the feet of the Lord and at the latchet of his shoe, lest the lamp should be put out by the wind of pride.
ambomirabiliternatiprecoiudexlucernetdie.la: Ambo mirabíliter nati, præco Judex, lucérna et dies, vox et Verbum, servus et Dóminus. Ipse Dóminus fecit sibi servum in útero stérili, de sene patre, et de anícula matre: et idem ipse Dóminus fecit sibi carnem in útero Vírginis, sine hómine patre, qui fecit primum hóminem sine patre et matre. Nemo surréxit in natis mulíerum major Joanne Baptísta. Tam magnus visus est Joannes, ut a nonnullis étiam Christus putarétur. Nec in supérbia sua aliénum est secutus errorem, nec ausus est dícere: Sum quod putátis: sed, quod bonum erat ei, se agnovit, ut ad pedes Dómini et ad corrígiam calceamenti servus humiliarétur, ne vento supérbiæ lucérna exstinguerétur.

corporaipsoruminpacesepultasuntetnomeneo.en: Their bodies are buried in peace, and their name liveth unto generation and generation. † Let the people shew forth their wisdom, * and the church declare their praise.
corporaipsoruminpacesepultasuntetnomeneo.la: Córpora ipsórum in pace sepúlta sunt, et nomen eórum vivit in generatiónem et generatiónem. † Sapiéntiam ipsórum narrent pópuli, * et laudem eórum núntiet ecclésia.

annuntiaveruntintergentesgloriamdomini.en: They have declared the glory of the Lord among the Gentiles.

legimusananiamazariametmiselembeatissimo.en: We read that Ananias, Azarias and Misael, most blessed children, shut up by the king in the furnace of fire, walked about in the flames of their torments, and trod the balls of fire under their feet. Whence blessed Lawrence also is to be set before them with no less glory; for they walk in the flames of their torments, he even lieth down in the very fire of his punishment; they trod the burning under the soles of their feet, he quenched it by stretching out his sides.
legimusananiamazariametmiselembeatissimo.la: Legimus Ananiam, Azariam et Misaelem beatissimos pueros a rege in camino ignis inclusos in poenarum suarum deambulasse flammis, et igneos globos pedibus conculcasse. Unde et beatus Laurentius non minori gloria est praeferendus; siquidem illi in poenarum suarum flammis ambulant, hic et in ipso supplicii sui igne discumbit; illi vestigiis pedum conculcaverunt incendia, iste laterum suorum diffusione extinxit.

iterumbeatuslaurentiusindorsumsupinusver.en: Again blessed Lawrence is turned upon his back, and his reins are burned with the fires; that the prophecy of the psalm might be fulfilled, which saith in the person of Lawrence: Prove me, O Lord, and try me; burn my reins and my heart. He certainly asketh to be burned with a twofold fire. For if he spake of the one and only fire of the world, it would suffice to have offered his reins alone to be burned by the flames. But the heart no flame burneth save that of Christ.
iterumbeatuslaurentiusindorsumsupinusver.la: Iterum beatus Laurentius in dorsum supinus vertitur, et renes ejus ignibus exuruntur; ut impleretur psalmi prophetia quae dicit ex persona Laurentii: Proba me, Domine, et tenta me; ure renes meos, et cor meum. Duplici se utique postulat igne comburi. Nam si de uno et solo mundi igne loqueretur, sufficeret renes tantum exurendos incendiis obtulisse. Cor autem nisi Christi flamma non urit.

oremusigiturfratresbeatumlaurentiumquidu.en: Let us therefore pray, brethren, to blessed Lawrence, who, while by his faith he overcame the flames of the persecutor, hath shewn us that by the fire of faith we may overcome the burnings of hell, and through the love of Christ not fear the day of judgment. But we, dearly beloved brethren, if we will come to the fellowship of the holy martyrs, let us think upon the imitation of the martyrs. For they ought to recognise in us something of their virtues, that they may deign to make supplication to the Lord for us.
oremusigiturfratresbeatumlaurentiumquidu.la: Oremus igitur, fratres, beatum Laurentium, qui dum fide sua persecutoris flammas vicit, ostendit nobis per ignem fidei gehennae incendia superare, et amore Christi diem judicii non timere. Nos vero, fratres dilectissimi, si ad consortium sanctorum martyrum pervenire volumus, de imitatione martyrum cogitemus. Debent enim in nobis aliquid de suis virtutibus recognoscere, ut pro nobis dignentur Dominum supplicare.

supersalutemetomnempulchritudinemdilecte.en: Above health and all beauty thou art beloved of the Lord, † and thou art worthy to be called the Queen of heaven
supersalutemetomnempulchritudinemdilecte.la: Super salútem et omnem pulchritúdinem dilécta es a Dómino, † et Regína cælórum vocári digna es

gaudentchoriangelorumconsortesetconcives.en: The choirs of the Angels rejoice, our fellows and fellow-citizens.
gaudentchoriangelorumconsortesetconcives.la: Gaudent chori angelórum consórtes et concíves nostri.

solanamquesineexemploplacuistifeminachri.en: For thou alone, a woman without example, hast pleased Christ.
solanamquesineexemploplacuistifeminachri.la: Sola namque sine exémplo placuísti fémina Christo.

istestspeciosainterfiliasierusalemsicutv.en: This is she that is beautiful among the daughters of Jerusalem, † as ye have seen her full of charity and love
istestspeciosainterfiliasierusalemsicutv.la: Ista est speciósa inter filias Jerúsalem, † sicut vidístis eam plenam caritáte et dilectióne

incubilibusetinhortisaromatum.en: In the chambers and in the gardens of spices.
incubilibusetinhortisaromatum.la: In cubílibus et in hortis arómatum.

istestqueascenditdedesertodeliciisafflue.en: This is she that goeth up from the desert, flowing with delights.
istestqueascenditdedesertodeliciisafflue.la: Ista est quæ ascéndit de desérto delíciis áffluens.

hodiemariavirgocelosascenditgaudete.en: This day the Virgin Mary hath ascended into heaven: rejoice
hodiemariavirgocelosascenditgaudete.la: Hódie María virgo cælos ascéndit: gaudéte

quiacumchristoregnatineternum.en: Because she reigns with Christ forever.
quiacumchristoregnatineternum.la: Quia cum Christo regnat in ætérnum.

assumptestmariaincelumgaudentangelilauda.en: Mary is taken up into heaven: † the Angels rejoice, and praising they bless the Lord.
assumptestmariaincelumgaudentangelilauda.la: Assúmpta est María in cælum: † gaudent Angeli laudántes benedícunt Dóminum.

oratioiidedormitdeiparen.en: Oration 2 on the Falling-asleep of the Mother of God, n. 16
oratioiidedormitdeiparen.la: Oratio II de Dormit. Deiparæ, n. 16

iubilemusinarcadominideitotoanimetmurica.en: Let us rejoice with all our soul in the ark of the Lord God, and the walls of Jericho shall fall, the hostile fortresses, I say, of the adverse powers. Let us exult in spirit with David: for the ark of the Lord hath this day come to rest. Let us cry out with Gabriel, who holdeth the first place among the Angels: Hail, full of grace; the Lord is with thee. Hail, inexhaustible sea of joy: hail, only relief of troubles: hail, remedy of all the sorrows of the heart. Hail, holy Virgin, through whom death indeed was cast out, and life brought in.
iubilemusinarcadominideitotoanimetmurica.la: Jubilémus in arca Dómini Dei toto ánimo, et muri cadent Jerichuntíni, contrariárum, ínquam, potestátum inféstæ munitiónes. Cum David exsultémus spíritu: Arca enim Dómini hódie requiévit. Clamémus cum Gabriéle, qui primum locum óbtinet inter Angelos: Ave, grátia plena; Dóminus tecum. Ave, gáudii pélagus inexhaustum: ave, únicum molestiárum levámen : ave, ómnium cordis dolórum medicaméntum. Ave,sancta Virgo, per quam mors quidem fuit expúlsa, vita autem introdúcta.

tuveroosacrorumsepulcrorumsacratissimump.en: But thou, O most sacred of sacred sepulchres, after the sepulchre of the Lord, which gave the beginning of life, which was the fountain of the resurrection (for I will speak with thee as with a living thing), where is the gold which the hands of the Apostles laid up in thee? Where are the riches which cannot be consumed? Where is that precious treasure which received Life? Where is the new volume, in which the Word of God was ineffably written without hand? Where is the abyss of grace, where the sea of healings? Where is that desirable body of the Virgin Mother of God?
tuveroosacrorumsepulcrorumsacratissimump.la: Tu vero, o sacrórum sepulcrorum sacratissimum post Dómini quidem sepulcrum, quod vitæ dedit princípium, quod fuit fons resurrectiónis: (tecum enim loquar, tamquam cum animáto): úbinam est aurum, quod manus Apostolórum in te condidérunt? Ubi divítiæ, quæ consúmi néqueunt? Ubi pretiósus ille thesáurus, qui vitam suscépit? Ubi novum volúmen, in quo ineffabíliter Dei Verbum sine manu inscríptum fuit? Ubi abyssus grátiæ, ubi pélagus curatiónum? Ubi est desiderabile illud Deíparæ Vírginis corpus?

quidqueritisinsepulcreamqueadcelestiatra.en: Why seek ye in the sepulchre her who hath been translated to the heavenly tabernacles? Why demand ye of me an account of my keeping? I cannot resist the divine commands. That most sacred body, which imparted holiness to me also, and filled me with the fragrance of a most precious ointment, and made me a divine temple, leaving the linen cloths, hath gone away, caught up on high, Angels, Archangels and all the heavenly powers accompanying it. Now Angels surround me, now divine grace dwelleth in me. I am become a house of healing for the sick: I am a perpetual fountain of healings: I am a remedy against devils: I am a city of refuge for all that flee unto me.
quidqueritisinsepulcreamqueadcelestiatra.la: Quid quæritis in sepúlcro eam, quæ ad cæléstia transláta est tabernácula? Cur a me custódiæ ratiónem expóscitis? Non possum ego divínis jussis resistere. Sacrosanctum illud corpus, quod mihi quoque sanctitátem impertívit, ac pretiosíssimi unguénti fragrántia me replévit, et divínum templum effécit, relíctis sindónibus, ábiit raptum sublíme, comitántibus Angelis, Archangelis et ómnibus cæléstibus poténtiis. Nunc me circúmdant Angeli, nunc divína in me hábitat grátia. Ego evási officína medicínæ ægrotantibus: ego fons perénnis curatiónum: ego remédium advérsus dæmones: ego cívitas refúgii ómnibus ad me confugiéntibus.

oratdedormitionedeiparen.en: Oration 2 on the Falling-asleep of the Mother of God, n. 18

duosuntordineselectoruminiudiciofuturiun.en: There are two orders of the elect in the judgment to come: one of those who judge with the Lord, of whom he maketh mention in this place, who have left all things, and followed him; the other of those who are judged by the Lord, who did not indeed equally leave all that was theirs, but yet out of those things which they had, were careful to give daily alms to the poor of Christ; whence they also shall hear in the judgment: Come, ye blessed of my Father, possess you the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world; for I was hungry, and you gave me to eat: I was thirsty, and you gave me to drink.
duosuntordineselectoruminiudiciofuturiun.la: Duo sunt órdines electórum in judício futúri : unus judicántium cum Dómino, de quibus hoc loco mémorat, qui reliquérunt ómnia, et secúti sunt illum: álius judicatórum a Dómino qui non quidem ómnia sua páriter reliquérunt, sed de his tamen quæ habébant, quotidiánas dare eleemósynas Christi paupéribus curábant; unde et auditúri sunt in judício : Veníte, benedícti Patris mei, possidéte præparátum vobis regnum a constitutióne mundi; esurívi enim, et dedístis mihi manducáre: sitívi, et dedístis mihi bíbere.

verumhiscuretimoreetpavoredebitepaulispe.en: But having briefly called these things to mind with fear and trembling, as is due, let us rather turn our hearing to the most joyful promises of our Lord and Saviour. Let us see what, of so great grace and loving-kindness, he promiseth to his followers: not the rewards of eternal life only, but surpassing gifts of the present life also.
verumhiscuretimoreetpavoredebitepaulispe.la: Verum his cure timóre et pavóre débite paulísper commemorátis, ad lætíssima pótius Dómini et Salvatòris nostri promíssa convertámus audítum. Videámus quæ tantæ gratim pietátis, non ætérnæ tantúmmodo vitæ prǽmia suis sequácibus, sed et præséntis múnera pollicétur exímia.

etomnisinquitquireliqueritdomumvelfratre.en: And every one, saith he, that hath left house, or brethren, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or lands, for my name's sake, shall receive an hundredfold, and shall possess life everlasting. For he that for the discipleship of Christ hath renounced earthly affections or possessions, the more he hath advanced in his love, the more shall he find who rejoice to receive him with inward affection, and to sustain him with their substance.
etomnisinquitquireliqueritdomumvelfratre.la: Et omnis, inquit, qui relíquerit domum, vel fratres, aut soróres, aut patrem, aut matrem, aut uxórem, aut fílios, aut agros propter nomen meum ; céntuplum accípiet et vitam ætérnam possidébit. Qui enim terrénis afféctibus sive possessiónibus pro Christi discipulátu renunciáverit, quo plus in ejus amórem profécerit, eo plures invéniet, qui se intérno suscípere afféctu, et suis gáudeant sustentáre substántiis.

acsimanifestiusdicantquantesthecautundee.en: As if they said more plainly: How great is she, or whence hath she, going up indeed from the desert, so great an abundance of delights? For not even in us are like delights found, whom in the city of the Lord the stream of the river maketh joyful, who from the face of glory are made to drink of the torrent of pleasure. Who is she that, from under the sun, where there is nothing but labour and sorrow and affliction of spirit, goeth up flowing with spiritual delights? Sermon of St. Bernard, Abbot
acsimanifestiusdicantquantesthecautundee.la: Ac si manifestius dicant: Quanta est hæc, aut, unde ei ascendenti utique de deserto affluentia tanta deliciarum? Nec enim pares inveniuntur deliciae vel in nobis, quos in civitate Dómini laetificat fluminis impetus, qui a vultu gloriae, voluptatis torrente potamur. Quae est ista, quae de sub sole, ubi nihil est nisi labor et dolor et afflictio spiritus, ascendit deliciis spiritualibus affluens? Sermon of St Bernard, abbot

neminemmoveatquodsuscipiensmulierdominum.en: Let no one be moved that the woman who received the Lord is called not Mary, but Martha: since in this one and supreme Mary is found both the business of Martha and the leisure, not idle, of Mary. All the glory indeed of the king's daughter is within: nevertheless she is clothed round about with variety in golden borders. She is not of the number of the foolish virgins: she is a prudent virgin; she hath a lamp, but she carrieth oil in her vessel.
neminemmoveatquodsuscipiensmulierdominum.la: Néminem móveat, quod suscípiens múlier Dóminum, non María, sed Martha vocátur: quando in hac una et summa María et Marthæ negótium, et Maríæ non otiósum ótium invenítur. Omnis quidem glória fíliæ regis ab intus: nihilóminus tamen in fímbriis áureis circumamícta est varietáte. Non est de número fatuárum vírginum: prudens est virgo; lámpadem habet, sed in vase óleum portat.

hodieconceptestbeatavirgomariexprogenied.en: This day was conceived the Blessed Virgin Mary, of the lineage of David.
hodieconceptestbeatavirgomariexprogenied.la: Hodie concepta est beata virgo Maria ex progenie David.

perquamsalusmundicredentibusapparuitcuiu.en: Through whom the salvation of the world hath appeared to believers, whose glorious life hath given light to the world.
perquamsalusmundicredentibusapparuitcuiu.la: Per quam salus mundi credentibus apparuit, cujus vita gloriosa lucem dedit sæculo.

conceptionembeatemarievirginiscumgaudioc.en: Let us celebrate with joy the Conception of the Blessed Virgin Mary.
conceptionembeatemarievirginiscumgaudioc.la: Conceptionem beatæ Mariæ virginis cum gaudio celebremus.

beatissimevirginismarieconceptionemdevot.en: Let us most devoutly celebrate the Conception of the most blessed Virgin Mary:
beatissimevirginismarieconceptionemdevot.la: Beatissimæ virginis Mariæ Conceptionem devotissime celebremus:

utipsapronobisintercedataddominumiesumch.en: That she may pray for us to our Lord Jesus Christ.
utipsapronobisintercedataddominumiesumch.la: Ut ipsa pro nobis intercedat ad Dominum Jesum Christum.

cumiucunditateconceptionembeatemarievirg.en: With gladness let us most devoutly celebrate the Conception of the Blessed Virgin Mary.
cumiucunditateconceptionembeatemarievirg.la: Cum jucunditate Conceptionem beatæ Mariæ virginis devotissime celebremus.

gloriosevirginismarieconceptionemdigniss.en: Let us call to mind the most worthy Conception of the glorious Virgin Mary,
gloriosevirginismarieconceptionemdigniss.la: Gloriosæ virginis Mariæ Conceptionem dignissimam recolamus,

cuiusdominushumilitatemrespexitqueangelo.en: Whose lowliness the Lord regarded, who at the message of an Angel conceived the Saviour of the world.
cuiusdominushumilitatemrespexitqueangelo.la: Cujus Dominus humilitatem respexit, quæ Angelo nuntiante concepit Salvatorem mundi.

regaliexprogeniemariexortarefulget.en: Born of royal lineage, Mary shines resplendent:
regaliexprogeniemariexortarefulget.la: Regali ex progenie Maria exorta refulget:

cuiusprecibusnosadiuvarimenteetspiritude.en: By whose prayers we most devoutly ask to be helped in mind and spirit.
cuiusprecibusnosadiuvarimenteetspiritude.la: Cujus precibus nos adjuvari mente et spiritu devotissime poscimus.

cordeetanimochristocanamusgloriaminhacsa.en: With heart and soul let us sing glory to Christ, in this sacred solemnity of his most exalted Mother.
cordeetanimochristocanamusgloriaminhacsa.la: Corde et animo Christo canamus gloriam, in hac sacra solemnitate præcelsæ genitricis suæ.

cuiusvitainclytacunctasillustratecclesia.en: Whose renowned life sheddeth light upon all the Churches.
cuiusvitainclytacunctasillustratecclesia.la: Cujus vita inclyta cunctas illustrat Ecclesias.

cumiucunditateconceptionembeatemariecele.en: With gladness let us celebrate the Conception of the Blessed Mary.
cumiucunditateconceptionembeatemariecele.la: Cum jucunditate Conceptionem beatæ Mariæ celebremus.

cordeetanimochristocanamusgloriaminhacsa.en: With all our heart and with all our soul let us sing praise to Christ on this the solemn Feastday of Mary the mighty Mother of God.
cordeetanimochristocanamusgloriaminhacsa.la: Corde et animo Christo canamus gloriam, in hac sacra solemnitate præcelsæ genitricis Dei Mariæ.

conceptiotuadeigenitrixvirgogaudiumannun.en: Thy Conception, O Virgin Mother of God, hath announced joy to the whole world:
conceptiotuadeigenitrixvirgogaudiumannun.la: Conceptio tua Dei genitrix virgo, gaudium annuntiavit universo mundo:

exteenimortusestsoliustitiechristusdeusn.en: For out of thee rose the Sun of righteousness, even Christ our God, Who hath taken away the curse and brought a blessing, confounded death, and given unto us everlasting life.
exteenimortusestsoliustitiechristusdeusn.la: Ex te enim ortus est sol justitiæ, Christus Deus noster: Qui solvens maledictionem, dedit benedictionem: et confundens mortem, donavit nobis vitam sempiternam.

cordeetanimochristocanamusgloriaminhacsa.en: With all our heart and with all our soul let us sing praise to Christ on this the solemn Feast-day of Mary, the mighty Mother of God, the Virgin Mary.
cordeetanimochristocanamusgloriaminhacsa.la: Corde et animo Christo canamus gloriam, in hac sacra solemnitate præcelsæ genitricis Dei Virginis Mariæ,

utipsaintercedatpronobisaddominum.en: That she may intercede for us with the Lord.
utipsaintercedatpronobisaddominum.la: Ut ipsa intercedat pro nobis ad Dominum.

cumiucunditateconceptionemsanctemariesol.en: With gladness let us solemnly celebrate the Conception of holy Mary.
cumiucunditateconceptionemsanctemariesol.la: Cum jucunditate, Conceptionem sanctæ Mariæ solembiter celebremus.

hodieconceptestbeatavirgomariexprogenied.en: This day was conceived the Blessed Virgin Mary, of the lineage of David, * through whom the salvation of the world hath appeared to believers.
hodieconceptestbeatavirgomariexprogenied.la: Hodie concepta est beata virgo Maria ex progenie David, * per quam salus mundi credentibus apparuit.

conceptionemhodiernamperpetuevirginisdei.en: Let us solemnly celebrate this day's Conception of Mary, the ever-Virgin Mother of God:
conceptionemhodiernamperpetuevirginisdei.la: Conceptionem hodiernam perpetuæ virginis Dei genitricis Mariæ solemniter celebremus:

quacelsitudothroniprocessit.en: From whom the Height of the throne came forth.

sanctetimmaculatavirginitasquibustelaudi.en: Holy and immaculate virginity, with what praises to extol thee I know not:
sanctetimmaculatavirginitasquibustelaudi.la: Sancta et immaculata virginitas, quibus te laudibus efferam nescio:

quiaquemcelicaperenonpoteranttuogremioco.en: For him whom the heavens could not contain, thou didst bear in thy bosom.
quiaquemcelicaperenonpoteranttuogremioco.la: Quia quem cæli capere non poterant, tuo gremio contulisti.

verumquigratisimpugnaturfortisdebetessee.en: But he who is assailed without cause ought to be strong and constant; how then hath he added: And my heart hath been in awe of thy words? To tremble belongeth to weakness, to fear and dread. But there is also a weakness unto salvation, there is also a fear of the saints: Fear the Lord, all ye his saints; and, Blessed is the man that feareth the Lord. For what reason blessed? Because he shall delight exceedingly in his commandments.
verumquigratisimpugnaturfortisdebetessee.la: Verum, qui gratis impugnátur, fortis debet esse et constans; quómodo ergo subtexuit: Et a verbis tuis trepidávit cor meum? Trepidare infirmitátis est, timoris atque formidinis. Sed est étiam infirmitas ad salútem, est étiam timor sanctórum: Timéte Dóminum, omnes sancti ejus; et, Beátus vir, qui timet Dóminum. Qua ratióne beatus? Quia in mandatis ejus cupit nimis.

beatusmauruspatriciogenereillustrisapuer.en: Blessed Maurus, * illustrious by patrician birth, from a boy esteemed the reproach of Christ the Lord greater riches than the treasures of the world.
beatusmauruspatriciogenereillustrisapuer.la: Beátus Maurus, * patrício génere illústris, a púero majóres divítias æstimávit thesáuris mundi, impropérium Christi Dómini.

obedientiepenniselatussuperaquasgraditur.en: On the wings of obedience * lifted up, he walketh upon the waters, nor could he be sunk by the waves, who was borne by the Spirit of God.
obedientiepenniselatussuperaquasgraditur.la: Obediéntiæ pennis * elátus super aquas gráditur, nec flúctibus mergi pótuit, qui spíritu Dei ferebátur.

beatusmaurusatenerisannissanctibenedicti.en: Blessed Maurus, * from his tender years a disciple of St. Benedict, shewed himself the more abundantly an imitator of his father's virtues.
beatusmaurusatenerisannissanctibenedicti.la: Beátus Maurus, * a téneris annis sancti Benedícti discípulus, abundántius æmulátor éxstitit paternárum virtútum.

exdomoorationistransivitinlocumtabernacu.en: From the house * of prayer he passed into the place of the wonderful tabernacle, even to the house of God, with exceeding love of which he burned.
exdomoorationistransivitinlocumtabernacu.la: Ex domo * oratiónis transívit in locum tabernáculi admirábilis, usque ad domum Dei, cujus nímio amóre flagrábat.

electusestadominoutessetmonachorumexempl.en: He was chosen * by the Lord, to be the pattern of monks, and the chief minister of the holy Rule.
electusestadominoutessetmonachorumexempl.la: Eléctus est * a Dómino, ut esset monachórum exémplar, et præcipuus sanctæ Régulæ miníster.

quiteposthabitisomnibusambiunt.en: They who, all things set aside, seek after thee,

horumpresidiumduxdeusetdecus.en: Of these the defence, the leader, O God, and the glory,
horumpresidiumduxdeusetdecus.la: Horum præsídium, dux, Deus, et decus,

quasmaurimeritismuneribustuis.en: The praises which, for the merits of Maurus, thy gifts,

hicgentilitiismaiorhonoribus.en: He, greater than the honours of his race,

spretisletusaditclaustrapalatiis.en: Spurning palaces, gladly entereth the cloister,

calcatdeliciasprediapurpuram.en: He trampleth on delights, estates, the purple,

utchristisubeatiugum.en: That he may take up the yoke of Christ.

sanctipropositampatrisimaginem.en: The image of the holy Father set before him

gestiscomparibussedulusexprimit.en: With like deeds he diligently expresseth;

spectandispuerilucetinactibus.en: In the admirable acts of the boy shineth

vitenormamonastice.en: The rule of the monastic life.

sesaccorigidusconteritaspero.en: Stern, he weareth himself down with rough sackcloth,

frenatperpetuilegesilentii.en: He bridleth himself by the law of perpetual silence;

noctesinprecibuspervigilexigit.en: Watchful, he spendeth the nights in prayers,

dumiussispatriisexcitusadvolat.en: While, roused by his father's commands, he hasteneth,

siccocalcataquasimpaviduspede.en: Fearless, he treadeth the waters with dry foot,

educitplacidumgurgitesospitem.en: He bringeth Placidus safe out of the whirlpool,

laudumiugishonorsittibitrinitas.en: To thee, O Trinity, be the continual honour of praises,
laudumiugishonorsittibitrinitas.la: Laudum jugis honor sit tibi Trínitas,

quevultussatiasluminecelites.en: Who fillest the heavenly ones with the light of thy countenance:

dasanctefamulistramiteregule.en: Grant to thy servants, by the path of the holy Rule,

mauripremiaconsequi.en: To attain the rewards of Maurus.

obeatumvirumquispretoseculoiugumsanctere.en: O blessed man, who, despising the world, lovingly bore the yoke of the holy Rule from his tender years; and being made obedient even unto death, denied himself, that he might cleave wholly to Christ, alleluia.
obeatumvirumquispretoseculoiugumsanctere.la: O beátum virum, qui, spreto sæculo, jugum sanctæ Régulæ a téneris annis amánter portávit; et factus obédiens usque ad mortem, semetípsum abnegávit, ut Christo totus adhæréret, allelúja.

deusquibeatummaurumadimitandumobedientie.en: O God, who, to set forth an example of obedience to be imitated, didst make blessed Maurus walk with dry foot upon the waters: grant that we may merit both to fulfil the teachings of his virtues, and to obtain a share in his rewards.
deusquibeatummaurumadimitandumobedientie.la: Deus, qui beátum Maurum ad imitándum obediéntiæ exémplum, sicco pede super aquas ambuláre fecísti: concéde; ut et virtútum ipsíus implére documénta, et præmiórum obtinére consórtia mereámur.

puellusplacidusquempaterobtulil.en: The little boy Placidus, whom his father offered,

illibatadeosistiturhostia.en: Is presented to God an unblemished victim,

ettirociniiiamdecusinclytum.en: And already, as the renowned glory of his novitiate,

exemplardaturemulis.en: Is given as a pattern to those who would emulate him.

abbatidocilisfictilevasculum.en: Docile to the Abbot, an earthen vessel

immittensinaquasparvulusamphoram.en: Letting down into the waters, the little one the pitcher

incautussequiturlitoradeserit.en: Heedlessly followeth, he leaveth the shore,

quosicmaurelacusdumterisequora.en: Whither thus, O Maurus, while thou treadest the surface of the lake,
quosicmaurelacusdumterisequora.la: Quo sic, Maure, lacus dum teris æquora,

gressusaccelerasovirobediens.en: Dost thou hasten thy steps? O obedient man,

insuetumperitervoxtepiipatris.en: By an unwonted way the voice of thy loving father
insuetumperitervoxtepiipatris.la: Insuétum per iter vox te pii patris

raptumrestituitmoxplacidumlacus.en: Soon the lake restored Placidus, whom it had snatched:

sedcuiusmeritismaurusanabstulit.en: But by whose merits? Was it Maurus that took him away
sedcuiusmeritismaurusanabstulit.la: Sed cujus méritis? Maurus an ábstulit

nursinusvepatergurgitissinu.en: Or the father of Nursia, from the bosom of the deep?

solvitquesitaparvulus.en: The little one resolveth the question.

prestasummatriasperplacidipreces.en: Grant, O supreme Trinity, through the prayers of Placidus,
prestasummatriasperplacidipreces.la: Præsta, summa Trias, per Plácidi preces,

angustomonachitramiteregule.en: That by the narrow path of the Rule monks

celorumproperentatriaconsequi.en: May hasten to attain the courts of heaven,

immixtisuperumchoris.en: Mingled with the choirs of them above.

cumsanctusvirbenedictusdiuineademsolitud.en: When the holy man Benedict had long grown in virtues and signs in the same wilderness, many were gathered by him in that same place to the service of almighty God: so that there, with the help of almighty Jesus Christ the Lord, he built twelve monasteries, in which, having appointed fathers, he placed twelve monks apiece; but a few he kept with himself, whom he judged it more fitting to be still instructed in his own presence. Then also nobles and devout persons of the city of Rome began to flock to him, and to give him their sons to be brought up for almighty God. Then likewise Eutychius gave Maurus, and Tertullus the patrician gave Placidus, their offspring of good hope: of whom Maurus, being young, since he excelled in good conduct, began to be his master's helper; but Placidus was still of the years of a boyish disposition.
cumsanctusvirbenedictusdiuineademsolitud.la: Cum sanctus vir Benedíctus diu in eádem solitúdine virtútibus signísque succrésceret, multi ab eo in eódem loco ad omnipoténtis Dei sunt servítium congregáti: ita ut illic duódecim monastéria, cum omnipoténtis Jesu Christi Dómini opitulatióne, constrúeret in quibus, statútis pátribus, duodénos mónachos deputávit, paucos vero secum retínuit, quos adhuc in sua præséntia áptius erudíri judicávit. Cœpére étiam tunc ad eum Románæ urbis nóbiles et religiósi concúrrere, suósque ei fílios omnipoténti Deo nutriéndos dare. Tunc quoque bonæ spei suas sóboles, Eutýchius Maurum, Tertúllus vero patrícius Plácidum trádidit: e quibus Maurus júnior, cum bonis polléret móribus, magístri adjútor cœpit exsístere: Plácidus vero puerílis adhuc índolis gerébat annos.

maurusatenerisannissanctobenedictoindisc.en: Maurus, † given over from his tender years by his father Eutychius at Subiaco to St. Benedict for training, expressed the virtues of his master by imitating them:
maurusatenerisannissanctobenedictoindisc.la: Maurus † a téneris annis sancto Benedícto in disciplínam ab Eutýchio patre in Subláco tráditus, magístri sui virtútes imitándo expréssit:

etsimiliseiuseffectusest.en: And he was made like unto him.

inspexitetfecitsecundumexemplarquodipsii.en: He looked, and made according to the pattern that was shewn him in the mount.
inspexitetfecitsecundumexemplarquodipsii.la: Inspéxit, et fecit secúndum exémplar, quod ipsi in monte monstrátum est.

beatummaurumsanctusbenedictuspreomnibuss.en: Blessed Maurus † did holy Benedict ever love more closely than all others, and so formed him in the service of almighty God,
beatummaurumsanctusbenedictuspreomnibuss.la: Beátum Maurum † sanctus Benedíctus præ ómnibus semper árctius diléxit, atque ita in omnipoténtis Dei servítio informávit,

utneminiposteumincenobialiobservationefu.en: That he was second to none after him in the observance of the cloister.
utneminiposteumincenobialiobservationefu.la: Ut némini post eum in cœnobiáli observatióne fúerit secúndus.

maurusadhuciuniorcumbonispolleretmoribus.en: Maurus, † while yet young, since he excelled in good conduct, being made a mirror of monks,
maurusadhuciuniorcumbonispolleretmoribus.la: Maurus † adhuc júnior cum bonis polléret móribus, factus monachórum spéculum,

magistriacpatrissuivenerabilisclarusadiu.en: Began to be the renowned helper of his venerable Master and Father.
magistriacpatrissuivenerabilisclarusadiu.la: Magístri ac Patris sui venerábilis clarus adjútor cœpit exsístere.

infraannosadolescentiemonasticereligioni.en: Within the years of youth he attained the perfection of the monastic life.
infraannosadolescentiemonasticereligioni.la: Infra annos adolescéntiæ, monásticæ religiónis assecútus est perfectiónem.

resmiretpostpetrumapostoluminusitatabene.en: A wonderful thing, and unheard of since Peter the Apostle! For having asked and received the blessing, Maurus went forth in haste at the command of his Father: and, thinking that he went upon the land, he ran upon the water even to the place whither the boy was being carried by the wave, and holding him by the hair, returned with swift course. Who, as soon as he touched the land, coming to himself, looked behind him, and knew that he had run upon the waters, and what he could not have presumed might be done, he marvelled and trembled at the deed. Returning therefore to the Father, he related what had been done. But the venerable man Benedict began to ascribe this not to his own merits, but to the other's obedience. But Maurus on the contrary said it was done by his command alone: and that he had no part in that power, which he had exercised unknowing. But in this friendly contention of mutual humility the boy who had been rescued came as judge, for he said: When I was being drawn out of the water, I saw the Abbot's sheepskin over my head, and I perceived that it was he who brought me out of the waters. Thus far St. Gregory, Pope. An ancient tradition then relateth that Maurus the monk was sent by the same most holy Father into Gaul. And there, as the same tradition hath it, he founded the celebrated monastery of Glanfeuil, which, when he had long ruled it, renowned for holiness and miracles, he passed in a good old age unto the Lord.
resmiretpostpetrumapostoluminusitatabene.la: Res mira, et post Petrum Apóstolum inusitáta! Benedictióne étenim postuláta atque percépta, ad Patris sui impérium cóncitus perréxit Maurus: atque usque ad eum locum, quo ab unda deducebátur puer, per terram se ire exístimans, super aquam cucúrrit, eúmque per capíllos tenens cursu rápido rédiit. Qui mox ut terram tétigit, ad se revérsus, post tergum respéxit, et quia super aquas cucurrísset agnóvit, et quod præsúmere non potuísset ut fíeret, mirátus extrémuit factum. Revérsus ítaque ad Patrem, rem gestam ré-tulit. Vir autem venerabilis Be-nedíctus hoc non suis méritis, sed illíus obediéntiæ deputáre cœpit. At Maurus contra pro solo ejus império factum dicébat: seque cónscium in illa virtúte non esse,quam nésciens fecísset. Sed in hac mútuæ humilitátis amíca contentióne accéssit árbiter puer, qui eréptus est, nam dicébat: Ego, cum ex aqua tráherer, super caput meum Abbátis melótem vidébam, atque ipsum me ex aquis edúcere considerábam. Hæc sanctus Gregórius Papa. Vetus deínde tradítio mémorat. Maurum mónachum ab eódem sanctíssimo Patre in Gálliam diréctum fuísse. Ibíque fundávit, ut éadem tradítio habet, célebre monastérium Glannafoliénse, quod cum diu rexísset, sanctitáte ac miráculis clarus, in senectúte bona migrávit ad Dóminum.

prolapsoinlacumplacidomaurusadvolansspir.en: Placidus having fallen † into the lake, Maurus, hastening thither, was borne by the Spirit of God upon the waters,
prolapsoinlacumplacidomaurusadvolansspir.la: Prolápso † in lacum Plácido, Maurus ádvolans, spíritu Dei ferebátur super aquas,

aquemultenonpotueruntexstinguerecaritate.en: Many waters could not quench his charity, neither could the floods drown it.
aquemultenonpotueruntexstinguerecaritate.la: Aquæ multæ non potuérunt exstínguere caritátem ejus, neque flúmina eam obrúere.

inillotemporerespondenspetrusdixitdomine.en: At that time: Peter answering, said: Lord, if it be thou, bid me come to thee upon the waters. And he said: Come. And so on.
inillotemporerespondenspetrusdixitdomine.la: In illo témpore: Respóndens Petrus dixit: Dómine, si tu es, jube me ad te veníre super aquas. At ipse ait: Veni. Et réliqua.

libcommentinmatthcapv.la: Lib. 2 Comment. In Matth. cap. 14 v. 28-33

inomnibuslocisardentissimefideiinvenitur.en: In all places Peter is found to be of most ardent faith. When the disciples were asked whom men said Jesus to be, he confesseth him the Son of God. When he would go to his passion, he forbiddeth him; and though he err in understanding, yet he erreth not in affection; not willing that he should die, whom a little before he had confessed to be the Son of God. He goeth up into the mountain with the Saviour, first among the first; and in the passion he alone followeth. The sin of denial, which had come of sudden fear, he straightway washed away with bitter tears. After the passion, when they were on the lake of Genesareth and were fishing, and the Lord stood on the shore, while the others came slowly sailing, he suffereth no delay; but girding his coat about him, straightway casteth himself into the waves.
inomnibuslocisardentissimefideiinvenitur.la: In ómnibus locis ardentíssimæ fídei invenítur Petrus. Interrogátis discípulis, quem hómines dícerent Jesum, Dei Fílium confitétur. Voléntem ad passiónem pérgere próhibet; et licet erret in sensu, tamen non errat in afféctu; nolens eum mori, quem Fílium Dei fúerat paulo ante conféssus. In montem cum Salvatóre inter primos primus ascéndit; et in passióne solus séquitur. Peccátum negatiónis, quod ex repentíno timóre descénderat, amáris statim ábluit lácrimis. Post passiónem cum essent in lacu Genésareth et piscaréntur, et Dóminus staret in lítore, áliis paulátim navigántibus, ille non pátitur moras; sed accínctus epéndyte suo statim præcipitátur in fluctus.

eodemigiturfideiardorequosempernuncquoqu.en: With the same ardour of faith therefore as always, now also, while the others are silent, he believeth that he can do by the will of the Master what he could do by nature. Bid me come to thee upon the waters. Do thou command, and forthwith the waves shall be made firm, the body shall become light, which of itself is heavy. And Peter going down out of the boat, walked upon the water, to come to Jesus. Let those who think that the Lord's body was therefore not a true one, because he walked soft and airy upon the soft waters, answer how Peter walked, whom surely they will not deny to have been a true man.
eodemigiturfideiardorequosempernuncquoqu.la: Eódem ígitur fídei ardóre, quo semper, nunc quoque, céteris tacéntibus, credit se posse fácere per voluntátem Magístri, quod ille póterat per natúram. Jube me veníre ad te super aquas. Tu præcipe, et íllico solidabúntur undæ leve fiet corpus, quod per se grave est. Et descéndens Petrus de navícula, ambulábat super aquam, ut veníret ad Jesum. Qui putant, Dómini corpus ídeo non esse verum, quia super molles aquas molle et aéreum incésserit, respóndeant, quómodo ambuláverit Petrus, quem útique verum hóminem non negábunt.

vidensveroventumvalidumtimuitetcummergic.en: But seeing the wind strong, he was afraid; and when he began to sink, he cried out, saying: Lord, save me. The faith of his soul was burning, but human frailty drew him into the deep. He is therefore left a little while to temptation, that his faith may be increased, and that he may understand that he was preserved not by the readiness of his asking, but by the power of the Lord. And immediately Jesus stretching forth his hand took hold of him, and said to him: O thou of little faith, why didst thou doubt? If to the Apostle Peter, of whose faith and ardour of mind we have spoken above, who had confidently asked the Saviour, saying: Lord, if it be thou, bid me come to thee upon the waters; because he feared a little, it is said: O thou of little faith, why didst thou doubt? what is to be said to us, who have not even the least little portion of this little faith?
vidensveroventumvalidumtimuitetcummergic.la: Videns vero ventum válidum, tímuit; et cum mergi, clamávit dicens: Dómime, salvum me fac. Ardébat ánimi fides, sed humána fragílitas in profúndum trahébat. Páululum ergo relínquitur tentatióni, ut augeátur fides, et intélligat se non facilitáte postulatiónis, sed poténtia Dómini conservátum. Et contínuo Jesus exténdens manum, apprehéndit eum, et ait illi: Módicæ fídei, quare dubitásti? Si Apóstolo Petro, de cujus fide et ardóre mentis supra díximus, qui confidénter rogáverat Salvatórem, dicens: Dómine, si tu es, jube me veníre ad te super aquas; quia paululum tímuit, dícitur: Módicæ fidei, quare dubitásti? quid nobis dicéndum est, qui hujus módicæ fídei ne mínimam quidem habémus portiúnculam?

quiauteminnaviculerantveneruntetadoraver.en: And they that were in the boat came and adored him, saying: Indeed thou art the Son of God. At a single sign, the calm of the sea being restored, which after very great storms sometimes cometh even by chance, the sailors and pilots confess him truly the Son of God: and doth Arius preach in the Church that he is a creature?
quiauteminnaviculerantveneruntetadoraver.la: Qui autem in navícula erant, venérunt et adoravérunt eum, dicéntes: Vere Fílius Dei es. Ad unum signum, tranquillitáte maris réddita, quæ post nímias procéllas, intérdum et casu fíeri solet, nautæ atque rectóres vere Fílium Dei confiténtur: et Aríus in Ecclésia prædicat creatúram?

inillotemporerespondenspetrusdixitdomine.en: At that time: Peter answering, said: Lord, if it be thou, bid me come to thee upon the waters. And he said: Come. And Peter going down out of the boat, walked upon the water to come to Jesus. But seeing the wind strong, he was afraid: and when he began to sink, he cried out, saying: Lord, save me. And immediately Jesus stretching forth his hand took hold of him, and said to him: O thou of little faith, why didst thou doubt? And when they were come up into the boat, the wind ceased. And they that were in the boat came and adored him, saying: Indeed thou art the Son of God.
inillotemporerespondenspetrusdixitdomine.la: In illo témpore Respóndens Petrus dixit: Dómine, si tu es, jube me ad te veníre super aquas. At ipse ait: Veni. Et descéndens Petrus de navícula, ambulábat super aquam, ut veníret ad Jesum. Videns vero ventum válidum, tímuit: et cum coepísset mergi, clamávit dicens: Dómine, salvum me fac. Et contínuo Jesus exténdens manum, apprehéndit eum, et ait illi: Módicæ fidei, quare dubitásti? Et cum ascendíssent in navículam, cessávit ventus. Qui autem in navícula erant, venérunt, et adoravérunt eum, dicéntes Vere Fílius Dei es.

nolitimerequiaredemiteetvocavitenominetu.en: Fear not, for I have redeemed thee, and called thee by thy name: thou art mine. † When thou shalt pass through the waters, I will be with thee; * for I am the Lord thy God, the Holy One of Israel, thy Saviour.
nolitimerequiaredemiteetvocavitenominetu.la: Noli timére, quia redémi te, et vocávi te nómine tuo: meus es tu. † Cum transíeris per aquas, tecum ero; * quia ego Dóminus Deus tuus, Sanctus Israël, Salvátor tuus.

etegofiliusfuipatrismeietdocebatmeatqued.en: For I also was my father's son: † and he taught me, and said: Let thy heart receive my words, * keep my commandments, and thou shalt live.
etegofiliusfuipatrismeietdocebatmeatqued.la: Et ego fílius fui patris mei: † et docébat me, atque dicébat: Suscípiat verba mea cor tuum, * custódi præcépta mea, et vives.

fidedemoratusestinterrarepromissionistam.en: By faith he abode in the land of promise, as in a strange country, † dwelling in cottages with the co-heirs of the same promise. * For he looked for a city that hath foundations: whose builder and maker is God.
fidedemoratusestinterrarepromissionistam.la: Fide demoratus est in terra repromissiónis, tamquam in aliéna, † in cásulis habitándo cum coherédibus repromissiónis ejúsdem. * Exspectábat enim fundaménta habéntem civitá tem: cujus ártifex et cónditor Deus.

hodiesanctusmaurussuperciliciumstratusco.en: This day * St. Maurus, laid upon sackcloth before the altar, happily passed away. This day the first-born disciple of blessed Benedict, going up securely under the guidance of the holy Rule, accompanied by the choirs of Angels, came unto Christ. This day the obedient man, speaking of victories, merited to be crowned by the Lord, alleluia.
hodiesanctusmaurussuperciliciumstratusco.la: Hódie * sanctus Maurus super cilícium stratus coram altári felíciter occúbuit. Hódie primogénitus beáti Benedícti discípulus per ducátum sanctæ Régulæ secúrus ascéndens, choris comitátus angélicis, pervénit ad Christum. Hódie vir obédiens loquens victórias a Dómino coronári méruit, allelúja.

deusquibeatumgregoriumconfessoremtuumatq.en: O God, who didst set blessed Gregory thy Confessor and Bishop in thy Church as a defender of the faith and an example of apostolic wisdom and steadfastness: grant us, we beseech thee, that, bearing all adversities with humble heart for the glory of thy name, we may attain unto the glory of eternity.
deusquibeatumgregoriumconfessoremtuumatq.la: Deus, qui beátum Gregórium Confessórem tuum atque Pontíficem fídei defensórem et apostólicæ sapiéntiæ ac firmitátis exémplum in Ecclésia tua constituísti: largíre nobis, quæsumus; ut ómnia advérsa pro nóminis tui glória húmili corde sustinéntes, æternitátis glóriam consequámur.

sanctorumprecibusistorumreddesalutiscorp.en: Through the prayers * of these Saints, O Christ, restore to thy servants the health of body and soul.
sanctorumprecibusistorumreddesalutiscorp.la: Sanctórum * précibus istórum, redde salútis córporis et animæ, Christe, tuis fámulis.

omnipotensetmisericorsdeusquihumanogener.en: Almighty and merciful God, who hast bestowed upon mankind both the remedies of salvation and the gifts of eternal life: grant us, we beseech thee, that by the patronage of the blessed John and Camillus we may merit, in the hour of our departure, to be presented unto thee without stain of sin.
omnipotensetmisericorsdeusquihumanogener.la: Omnípotens et miséricors Deus, qui humáno géneri et salútis remédia et vitæ æterna múnera contulisti: da nobis, quæsumus; ut beatórum Joánnis et Camílli patrocínio in hora éxitus nostri absque peccáti mácula tibi repræsentári mereámur.

adestesanctiplurimo.en: Be present, O ye Saints, while with much

votisfavetesupplicum.en: Look favourably on the prayers of your suppliants.

imumredactainpulverem.en: Tombs, brought down to the lowest dust,

dudumsepulchrissqualleant.en: They have long lain in squalor,

sedsanctapresentifovet.en: But it cherisheth with its present

impletquetemplanumine.en: Godhead, and filleth, the holy temples,

sedetfuturespiritus.en: And also for the glory to come

postseclaservatglorie.en: Keepeth the spirits after the ages.

hincillequinostrislatet.en: Hence that ash which lieth hidden,

egrismedeturefficax.en: It healeth the sick with power,

torquetfugatquedemones.en: It tormenteth and putteth to flight the devils.

custoditdominusomniaosseorum.en: The Lord keepeth all their bones.

unumexhisnonconteretur.en: Not one of them shall be broken.

deusquihancsacrosanctamecclesiamtotvolui.en: O God, who hast willed this most holy church to be adorned with the Relics of so many Saints: increase in us faith in the resurrection; and make us partakers of the immortal glory, whose pledges we venerate in their ashes.
deusquihancsacrosanctamecclesiamtotvolui.la: Deus, qui hanc sacrosánctam ecclésiam tot voluísti Sanctórum decorári Relíquiis: auge in nobis resurrectiónis fidem; et fac nos immortális glóriæ partícipes, cujus in eorum cinéribus pígnora venerámur.

dormiuntinterrepulvere.en: They sleep in the dust of the earth.

evigilanuntinvitameternam.en: They shall awake unto life everlasting.

iustiquasivirensfoliumgerminabunt.en: The just shall spring up as a green leaf.

noncommovebiturradixeorum.en: Their root shall not be moved.

cumchristusapparueritvitavestra.en: When Christ, your life, shall appear.

tuncetvosapparebitiscumipsoingloria.en: Then you also shall appear with him in glory.
tuncetvosapparebitiscumipsoingloria.la: Tunc et vos apparébitis cum ipso in glória.

hisuntquiveneruntdetribulationemagnetlav.en: These are they which came out of great tribulation, and have washed their robes, and made them white in the Blood of the Lamb.
hisuntquiveneruntdetribulationemagnetlav.la: Hi sunt, qui venérunt de tribulatióne magna, et lavérunt stolas suas, et dealbavérunt eas in sánguine Agni.

propterealetaminicelietquihabitatisineis.en: Therefore rejoice, O heavens, and you that dwell therein.
propterealetaminicelietquihabitatisineis.la: Proptérea lætámini cæli, et qui habitátis in eis.

siquisadoraveritbestiametimaginemeiuseta.en: If any man shall adore the beast and his image, and receive his character in his forehead, or in his hand:
siquisadoraveritbestiametimaginemeiuseta.la: Si quis adoráverit béstiam, et imáginem ejus, et accéperit charactérem in fronte sua, aut in manu sua:

quamquamdilectissimihonorumnostrorumsanc.en: Although, dearly beloved, the Saints have no need of our honours, nor is anything bestowed upon them by our devotion; plainly, that we venerate their memory concerneth us, not them. Will ye know how much it concerneth us? I confess that in myself, from this remembrance, I feel a vehement desire kindled, and a threefold desire. The first desire, which the memory of the Saints either awakeneth or stirreth up the more in us, is this, that we may enjoy their so desirable fellowship, and merit to be fellow-citizens and companions of the blessed Spirits, and to rejoice together in the communion of the Saints.
quamquamdilectissimihonorumnostrorumsanc.la: Quamquam, dilectíssimi, honórum nostrórum Sancti non egent, nec quidquam eis nostra devotióne præstátur; plane, quod eórum memóriam venerámur, nostra ínterest, non ipsórum. Vultis scire, quantum ínterest nostra? Ego in me, fáteor, ex hac recordatióne séntio desidérium véhemens inflammári, et desidérium triplex. Primum desidérium, quod in nobis Sanctórum memória vel éxcitat, vel íncitat magis, hoc est, ut eórum tam optábili societáte fruámur, et mereámur concíves et contubernáles esse Spirítuum beatórum, et collætári communióne Sanctórum.

singulorumverorecordationesquasiscintill.en: And the remembrances of each, as so many single sparks, nay rather as most burning torches, kindle devout souls, that they thirst both for the sight of them and for their embrace, so much that oftentimes they deem themselves even to be among them, their hearts reaching out with all eagerness and vehemence, now to all together, now to these or to those. Not only the fellowship, but also the happiness of the Saints is to be desired by us: let us also aspire to their glory with most fervent zeal. This then is the second desire, which from the commemoration of the Saints burneth within us, that as unto them, so unto us also Christ our life may appear, and we also may appear with him in glory.
singulorumverorecordationesquasiscintill.la: Singulórum vero recordatiónes, quasi scintillæ síngulæ, immo quasi ardentíssimæ faces, devótos accéndunt ánimos, ut eórum et conspéctum sítiant et compléxum, ádeo, ut plerúmque étiam inter eos esse se réputent, modo ad omnes simul, modo ad hos, vel ad illos tota aviditáte et veheméntia corda vibrántes. Non tantúmmodo societas, sed étiam felícitas nobis est optánda Sanctórum: glóriam quoque ferventíssimo stúdio ambiámus. Hoc ergo secúndum desidérium, quod ex Sanctórum commemoratióne flagrat in nobis, ut sicut illis, sic nobis étiam Christus appáreat vita nostra, et nos quoque cum ipso appareámus in glória.

saneuteamgloriamnobissperareliceatetadta.en: Truly, that we may be allowed to hope for that glory, and to aspire to so great blessedness, the suffrages also of the Saints are to be most earnestly desired by us: that what our own ability obtaineth not, may be granted us by their intercession. Have pity on me, have pity on me, at least you my friends. Ye yourselves know our danger, ye know our ignorance, the wiles of our adversaries, ye know their assaults, and our frailty. For I speak to you, who have been in the same temptation, who have overcome the same conflicts, escaped the same snares, who have learned compassion from the things which ye suffered. With the greater confidence I flee unto you, I have you as partners in our very humanity, so that it behoveth you more familiarly and more especially to have pity on the bone of your bones, and the flesh of your flesh.
saneuteamgloriamnobissperareliceatetadta.la: Sane, ut eam glóriam nobis sperare liceat, et ad tantam beatitúdinem aspiráre, summópere nobis desideránda sunt suffrágia quoque Sanctórum: ut, quod possibílitas nostra non obtinet, eórum nobis intercessióne donétur. Miserémini mei, miserémini mei, saltem vos, amíci mei. Nostis ipsi perículum nostrum, nostis ignorantiam nostram, dolos adversariórum, nostis eórum ímpetus, et nostram fragilitátem. Vobis enim loquor, qui in eádem tentatióne fuístis, qui eósdem superástis conflíctus, eósdem láqueos evasístis, qui didicístis ex his, quæ passi estis, compassiónem. Amplióri fidúcia ad vos confúgio, vos hábeo in ipsa humanitáte consórtes, ut opórteat vos familiárius et speciálius miseréri ossi de óssibus vestris, et carni de carne vestra.

deniquetranseuntesexhocmundoadpatremsanc.en: Finally, passing out of this world to the Father, left us holy pledges. For with us their bodies are buried in peace, whose names shall live for ever, that is, whose glory is never buried. Far be it, far be it from you, holy souls, that Egyptian cruelty of Pharao's butler, who, being restored to his former place, straightway forgot holy Joseph, who was kept in prison; for they were not members of one head, nor hath the faithful any part with the unbeliever, nor the Israelite any fellowship with the Egyptian, no more than light with darkness. For Egypt is interpreted darkness, but Israel, Seeing God: and therefore, wheresoever Israel was, there was light. But this is the bond between us and the Saints, that we rejoice with them, they suffer with us: we by devout meditation reign in them, they in us and for us fight by loving intercession.
deniquetranseuntesexhocmundoadpatremsanc.la: Dénique transeuntes ex hoc mundo ad Patrem, sancta nobis pígnora reliquerunt. Apud nos síquidem córpora eórum in pace sepúlta sunt, quorum nómina vivent in sæculum, id est, quorum numquam glória sepelítur. Absit, absit a vobis, ánimæ sanctæ, Ægýptia illa crudélitas pincérnæ Pharaónis, qui in gradum prístinum restitútus, statim oblítus est Joseph sancti, qui in cárcere tenebátur; non enim erant uníus cápitis membra, nec áliqua pars fidéli cum infidéli, aut ulla societas Israëlítæ ad Ægyptium, non plus quam luci ad ténebras. Interpretátur enim Ægýptus ténebræ, Israël autem Videns Deum: atque ídeo, ubicúmque Israël erat, lux erat. Hæc vero nostra et Sanctórum cohæréntia est, ut nos congratulémur eis, ipsi compatiántur nobis: nos devóta meditatióne regnémus in eis, ipsi in nobis et pro nobis mílitent pia interventióne.

exposevanglucelibvnet.la: Expos. Evang. Lucæ lib. V, n.60 et 61

videordinemoportettepauperemfierispiritu.en: See the order. Thou must become poor in spirit; for lowliness of spirit is the riches of virtues. Unless thou be poor, thou canst not be meek. He that is meek can mourn for things present: he that mourneth for lower things can desire better: he that seeketh higher things shunneth the lower, that he also may be helped by those above: he that sheweth mercy cleanseth his heart. For what is it to cleanse the soul, but to do away the filth of death? For alms delivereth from death. And patience is the perfection of charity. But he that suffereth persecution, being set in the last struggle, is proved by adversities, that, when he hath striven lawfully, he may be crowned.
videordinemoportettepauperemfierispiritu.la: Vide órdinem. Opórtet te pauperem fieri spíritu; humílitas enim spíritus divítiæ virtútum sunt. Nisi pauper fúeris, mitis esse non poteris. Qui mitis est, potest lugére præsentia: qui inferióra luget, potest desideráre melióra: qui superióra quærit, inferióra devítat, ut et ipse a superióribus adjuvétur: qui miserétur, cor suum mundat. Quid est enim mundáre ánimum, nisi sordem mortis abolére? Eleemosyna enim a morte líberat. Patiéntia vero perféctio est caritátis. Qui autem pátitur persecutiónem, in último certámine constitútus probátur advérsis, ut, cum legítime certáverit, coronétur.

sanctideniquetranseuntesexhocmundoadpatr.en: Finally the Saints, passing out of this world to the Father, left us holy pledges. For with us their bodies are buried in peace, whose names shall live for ever, that is, whose glory is never buried. Far be it, far be it from you, holy souls, that Egyptian cruelty of Pharao's butler, who, being restored to his former place, straightway forgot holy Joseph, who was kept in prison; for they were not members of one head, nor hath the faithful any part with the unbeliever, nor the Israelite any fellowship with the Egyptian, no more than light with darkness. For Egypt is interpreted darkness, but Israel, Seeing God: and therefore, wheresoever Israel was, there was light. But this is the bond between us and the Saints, that we rejoice with them, they suffer with us: we by devout meditation reign in them, they in us and for us fight by loving intercession.
sanctideniquetranseuntesexhocmundoadpatr.la: Sancti dénique transeuntes ex hoc mundo ad Patrem, sancta nobis pígnora reliquérunt. Apud nos síquidem córpora eórum in pace sepúlta sunt, quorum nómina vivent in sæculum, id est, quorum numquam glória sepelítur. Absit, absit a vobis, ánimæ sanctæ, Ægyptia illa crudélitas pincérnæ Pharaónis, qui in gradum prístinum restitútus, statim oblítus est Joseph sancti, qui in cárcere tenebátur; non enim erant uníus cápitis membra, nec aliqua pars fidéli cum infidéli, aut ulla societas Israëlítæ ad Ægyptium, non plus quam luci ad ténebras. Interpretátur enim Ægyptus tenebræ, Israël autem Videns Deum: atque ídeo, ubicúmque Israël erat, lux erat. Hæc vero nostra et Sanctorum cohæréntia est, ut nos congratulémur eis, ipsi compatiantur nobis: nos devóta meditatióne regnémus in eis, ipsi in nobis, et pro nobis mílitent pia interventióne.

hosquidamvoluntessegradusvirtutumperquos.en: Some will have these to be degrees of virtues, by which we may ascend from the lowest to the higher. Finally, as there are increases of virtues, so also are there increases of rewards: for it is more to be a son of God, than to possess the earth and to merit consolation. But since both the first reward is the kingdom of heaven, and the last reward is the kingdom of heaven, is the reward equal for beginners and for the perfect?
hosquidamvoluntessegradusvirtutumperquos.la: Hos quidam volunt esse gradus virtútum, per quos ab últimis ad superióra possímus ascéndere. Dénique sicut increménta virtútum, ita étiam increménta sunt præmiórum: plus est enim Dei esse fílium, quam possidére terram, et consolatiónem meréri.Sed quia et primum præmium regnum cælórum est, et últimum præmium regnum cælórum est, numquid æquále præmium incipiéntibus atque perféctis est?

habesprimumregnumquandosanctirapiunturin.en: Thou hast the first kingdom, when the Saints are taken up in the clouds to meet Christ in the air. For many of those that sleep shall rise, these unto life everlasting, those unto reproach. The first kingdom of heaven, then, is set before the Saints in their release from the body: the second kingdom of heaven is, after the resurrection, to be with Christ. When thou shalt be in the kingdom of heaven, then there is a progress of mansions: though there be one kingdom, yet there are divers merits in the kingdom of heaven.
habesprimumregnumquandosanctirapiunturin.la: Habes primum regnum, quando Sancti rapiúntur in núbibus óbviam Christo in áëra. Multi enim dormiéntium surgent, isti in vitam ætérnam, illi in oppróbrium. Primum ergo regnum cælórum Sanctis propósitum est in absolutióne córporis: secúndum regnum cælórum est, post resurrectiónem esse cum Christo.Cum fúeris in regno cælórum, tunc procéssus est mansiónum: etsi unum regnum, divérsa tamen mérita sunt in regno cælórum.

postresurrectionemterramtuamincipiesposs.en: After the resurrection thou shalt begin to possess thy land, set free from death. For he to whom it is said: Earth thou art, and into earth thou shalt go, possesseth not his own land; for he cannot be a possessor who taketh not the fruit. Set free therefore by the cross of the Lord, if only thou be found within the yoke of the Lord, thou shalt find consolation in the very possession. Delight followeth consolation, the divine mercy followeth delight. And on whom the Lord hath mercy, him he also calleth: he that is called seeth him that calleth: he that hath seen God is taken up into the right of divine sonship: then at length, as a son of God, he delighteth in the riches of the heavenly kingdom.
postresurrectionemterramtuamincipiesposs.la: Post resurrectiónem terram tuam incípies possidére, absolútus a morte. Ille enim cui dícitur: Terra es, et in terram ibis, non possidet terram suam; non enim potest esse possessor, qui non capit fructum. Absolútus ígitur per Domínicam crucem, si tamen intra jugum Dómini fúeris inventus, consolatiónem in ipsa possessióne repéries. Consolatiónem séquitur delectátio, delectatiónem divína miserátio. Quem autem miserátur Dóminus, et vocat: qui vocátur, videt vocántem: qui Deum víderit, in jus divínæ generatiónis assúmitur: tunc demum quasi Dei fílius, cæléstis regni divítiis delectátur.

quodsispirituseiusquisuscitavitiesumamor.en: And if the Spirit of him that raised up Jesus from the dead, dwell in you; he that raised up Jesus Christ from the dead, shall quicken also your mortal bodies, because of his Spirit that dwelleth in you.
quodsispirituseiusquisuscitavitiesumamor.la: Quod si Spíritus ejus, qui suscitávit Jesum a mórtuis, hábitat in vobis: qui suscitávit Jesum Christum a mórtuis, vivificábit, et mortália córpora vestra, propter inhabitántem Spíritum ejus in vobis.

ovosunanimeschristiadumchori.en: O ye united choirs of Christ's people,

sanctorumtumulosetcinerespatrum.en: The tombs of the Saints and the ashes of the Fathers,

carasexuviaspignoracelitum.en: Their dear remains, the pledges of the heavenly ones,

celoquandopiisequalaboribus.en: When in heaven, equal to their holy labours,

felicesanimegaudiapossident.en: The happy souls possess their joys,

penarumsociisdebitaredditur.en: To the bones, companions of their pains, is rendered

hiclausetdecusossibus.en: Here their due praise and honour.

passimsparsadeuspollicitimemor.en: Scattered far and wide, God, mindful of his promise,

custosnepereantpignoracolligit.en: As guardian, lest they perish, gathereth the pledges;

aptandoslapideslocis.en: Stones to be fitted in their places.

quinetreliquiasettumulossibi.en: Nay more, the Relics and the tombs as altars for himself
quinetreliquiasettumulossibi.la: Quin et Relíquias et túmulos sibi

arasipsedeusconsecrathostia.en: God himself consecrateth with the Victim;

coniungensquesuissecaputartubus.en: And joining himself as head to his members,
coniungensquesuissecaputartubus.la: Conjungén sque suis se caput ártubus,

vosquorumcineressupplicibuspia.en: Ye whose ashes, with suppliant kisses, the devout

sivosnostramoventsubsidiumboni.en: If our needs move you, bring help, O ye good,
sivosnostramoventsubsidiumboni.la: Si vos nostra movent, subsídium boni,

vestrisferteclientibus.en: To those who are your clients.

utcumnostranovissplendidadotibus.en: That when our flesh, resplendent with new endowments,
utcumnostranovissplendidadotibus.la: Ut cum nostra novis spléndida dótibus

surgetiunctachorisspirituumcaro.en: Shall rise, joined to the choirs of the spirits,

indivisatriassitdeusomnia.en: The undivided Trinity, God, may be all

nobissemperinomnibus.en: To us for ever in all things.

nostraautemconversatioincelisestundeetia.en: But our conversation is in heaven: from whence also we look for the Saviour, our Lord Jesus Christ, who will reform the body of our lowness, made like to the body of his glory.
nostraautemconversatioincelisestundeetia.la: Nostra autem conversátio in cælis est: unde étiam Salvatórem exspectámus Dóminum nostrum Jesum Christum, qui reformábit corpus humilitátis nostræ, configurátum córpori claritátis suæ.

siexprobraminiinnominechristibeatieritis.en: If you be reproached for the name of Christ, you shall be blessed: for that which is of the honour, glory, and power of God, and that which is his Spirit, resteth upon you.
siexprobraminiinnominechristibeatieritis.la: Si exprobrámini in nómine Christi, beáti éritis: quóniam quod est honóris, glóriæ, et virtútis Dei, et qui est ejus Spíritus, super vos requiéscit.

quisestquivobisnoceatsiboniemulatoresfue.en: Who is he that can hurt you, if you be zealous of good? * But if also you suffer any thing for justice' sake, blessed are ye.
quisestquivobisnoceatsiboniemulatoresfue.la: Quis est, qui vobis nóceat, si boni æmulatóres fuéritis? * sed et si quid patímini propter justítiam, beáti.

gloriosusdeusinsanctissuis.en: God is glorious in his Saints.

consolaborvosetgaudebitcorvestrum.en: I will comfort you, and your heart shall rejoice.
consolaborvosetgaudebitcorvestrum.la: Consolábor vos, et gaudébit cor vestrum.

etossavestraquasiherbagerminabunt.en: And your bones shall flourish like an herb.
etossavestraquasiherbagerminabunt.la: Et ossa vestra quasi herba germinábunt.

precursorisdomininativitassicutsacratiss.en: The nativity of the Forerunner of the Lord, as the most sacred history of the Gospel lesson setteth forth, shineth with great sublimity of miracles, because it was most fitting that he, than whom none greater hath risen among them that are born of women, should shine forth, even at his very birth, with a greater splendour of virtues than the other Saints. His parents, aged and long barren, exult in the gift of a most noble offspring; to the father himself, whom unbelief had made dumb, mouth and tongue are opened to greet the herald of the new grace. Nor is the power of blessing God only restored to him, but the virtue also of prophesying concerning the child is added. Roused by the fame of the deed, all the neighbours are struck with wonder and fear, and the hearts of all who heard it round about are prepared for the coming of the new prophet.
precursorisdomininativitassicutsacratiss.la: Præcursoris Dómini natívitas, sicut sacratíssima lectiónis evangélicæ prodit história, multa miraculórum sublimitáte refúlget, quia nímium decébat, ut ille, quo major inter natos mulíerum nemo surréxit, majóre præ céteris Sanctis in ipso mox ortu virtútum júbare clarésceret. Senes ac diu infecúndi paréntes dono nobilíssimæ prolis exsúltant; ipsi patri, quem incredúlitas mutum reddiderat, ad salutándum novæ præcónem grátiæ os et lingua reserátur. Nec solum facúltas Deum benedicéndi restitúitur, sed de eo étiam prophetándi virtus augétur. Excitáti fama facti, omnes vicíni admiratióne ac metu percellúntur, ómnium, qui audiére circumquáque, ad advéntum novi prophétæ corda præparántur.

undemeritosanctaperorbemecclesiaquetotbe.en: Wherefore rightly the holy Church throughout the world, which keepeth the victories of so many blessed Martyrs, whereby they merited entrance into the heavenly kingdom, hath been wont to celebrate, after the Lord, the birthday of this one alone. Which is by no means to be believed to have come into custom without the authority of the Gospel: but it is to be laid up the more attentively in the mind, that, as when the Lord was born, the Angel appearing to the shepherds said: Behold, I bring you good tidings of great joy, that shall be to all the people; for this day is born to you a Saviour, who is Christ the Lord: so also the Angel, foretelling to Zachary that John should be born, said: And thou shalt have joy and gladness, and many shall rejoice in his nativity. For he shall be great before the Lord.
undemeritosanctaperorbemecclesiaquetotbe.la: Unde mérito sancta per orbem Ecclésia, quæ tot beatórum Mártyrum victórias, quibus ingréssum regni cæléstis meruére, frequéntat, hujus tantúmmodo post Dóminum étiam nativitátis diem celebráre consuévit.
