Quod nullatenus sine evangélica auctoritate in consuetúdinem venísse credéndum est: sed atténtius ánimo recondéndum, quia, sicut, nato Dómino, pastóribus appárens Angelus ait: Ecce evangelízo vobis gáudium magnum, quod erit omni pópulo, quia natus est vobis hódie Salvátor, qui est Christus Dóminus: ita étiam Angelus nascitúrum Zacharíæ prædicans Joannem, Et erit, inquit, gáudium tibi et exsultátio, et multi in nativitáte ejus gaudébunt. Erit enim magnus coram Dómino.

iureigiturutriusquenativitasfestadevotio.en: Rightly therefore is the nativity of both celebrated with festal devotion: but in the nativity of the one, as of Christ the Lord, as of the Saviour of the world, as of the Son of almighty God, as of the Sun of justice, joy is announced to all the people. But in the rising of the other, as of the Forerunner of the Lord, of the eminent servant of God, of the burning and shining lamp, many are recorded as about to rejoice. This one is told to be great before the Lord: of that one the prophet testifieth: For the Lord is great and exceedingly to be praised, and of his greatness there shall be no end. This one, shunning the company of sinners, abstained from all that can inebriate: that one, conversing among sinners, remained free from all sin. This one was filled with the Holy Ghost even from his mother's womb. In that one dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead corporeally, who by the gift of his own Spirit himself consecrated for himself the seat of the virginal womb, in which he should take flesh.
iureigiturutriusquenativitasfestadevotio.la: Jure ígitur utriúsque natívitas festa devotióne celebrátur: sed in illíus tamquam in Christi Dómini, tamquam in Salvatóris mundi, tamquam in Fílii Dei omnipoténtis, tamquam in solis justítiæ nativitáte, omni pópulo gáudium evangelizátur. In hujus autem tamquam in præcursóris Dómini, in servi Dei exímii, in lucérnæ ardéntis et lucéntis exórtu, multi gavisúri memorantur.Iste magnus coram Dómino esse narrátur: de illa prophéta testátur: Quóniam magnus Dóminus et laudabilis nimis, et magnitudinis ejus non erit finis. Iste, peccatorum consortia declinans, ab omni, quod inebriari potest, abstinebat: ille inter peccatores conversatus, peccati omnis immunis permansit. Hic adhuc ex utero matris Spiritu Sancto repletus est. In illo habitat omnis plenitudo divinitatis corporaliter, qui dono sui Spiritus sedem sibi uteri virginalis, in quo carnem susciperet, ipse consecravit.

sanguisiesuchristifiliideiemundatnos.en: The Blood of Jesus Christ, the Son of God, * cleanseth us.
sanguisiesuchristifiliideiemundatnos.la: Sanguis * Jesu Christi, Fílii Dei, emúndat nos. Ps. 115

pretiemptiestisnolitefieriservihominum.en: Ye are bought * with a price: be not made the servants of men.
pretiemptiestisnolitefieriservihominum.la: Prétio * empti estis: nolíte fíeri servi hóminum. Ps. 119

unusmilitumlancealatuseiusaperuitetconti.en: One of the soldiers * with a spear pierced his side, and forthwith came there out Blood and Water.
unusmilitumlancealatuseiusaperuitetconti.la: Unus mílitum * láncea latus ejus apéruit, et contínuo exívit Sanguis et aqua. Ps. 140

torcularcalcavisolusetdegentibusnonestvi.en: I have trodden * the wine-press alone, and of the people there was none with Me.
torcularcalcavisolusetdegentibusnonestvi.la: Tórcular * calcávi solus, et de géntibus non est vir mecum. Ps. 246, 247, 248

gratificavitnosdeusindilectofiliosuo.en: God hath † graced us in his beloved Son:
gratificavitnosdeusindilectofiliosuo.la: Gratificávit † nos Deus in dilécto Fílio suo:

inquohabemusredemptionempersanguinemeius.en: In whom we have redemption through his Blood, unto the remission of sins.
inquohabemusredemptionempersanguinemeius.la: In quo habémus redemptiónem per Sánguinem ejus in remissiónem peccatórum.

eccevenitplenitudotemporisinquomisitdeus.en: Behold, the fulness of time is come, in which God sent his Son upon the earth.
eccevenitplenitudotemporisinquomisitdeus.la: Ecce venit plenitúdo témporis, in quo misit Deus Fílium suum in terras.

eccevoxsanguinisfiliituifratrisnostridet.en: Behold, † the voice of the Blood of thy Son, our brother, crieth to thee from the earth, O Lord.
eccevoxsanguinisfiliituifratrisnostridet.la: Ecce † vox Sánguinis Fílii tui, fratris nostri, de terra clamat ad te, Dómine.

benedictaterraqueaperuitossuumetsuscepit.en: Blessed is the earth, which hath opened her mouth and received the Blood of the Redeemer.
benedictaterraqueaperuitossuumetsuscepit.la: Benedícta terra, quæ apéruit os suum, et suscépit Sánguinem Redemptóris.

hecestsanguinisaspersiomeliusloquensquam.en: This is the sprinkling of Blood, which speaketh better than Abel.
hecestsanguinisaspersiomeliusloquensquam.la: Hæc est Sánguinis aspérsio, mélius loquens quam Abel.

incipitlibersecundusdialogorumsanctigreg.en: Here beginneth the second book of the Dialogues of St. Gregory, Pope
incipitlibersecundusdialogorumsanctigreg.la: Incipit liber secundus Dialogorum sancti Gregórii Papæ

fuitvirvitevenerabilisgratiabenedictuset.en: There was a man of venerable life, Benedict by grace and by name, who from the very time of his boyhood bore the heart of an old man. For, surpassing his age in his ways, he gave his mind to no pleasure; but while he was yet in this world, which he might freely have used for a time, he despised the world with its flower as though already withered. He, born of a free-born family in the province of Nursia, had been sent to Rome to the liberal studies of letters. But when he saw many in them going down the steep ways of vice, he drew back his foot, which he had set as it were on the threshold of the world, lest, if he touched anything of its knowledge, he too should go wholly into the monstrous precipice. Therefore, despising the studies of letters, leaving his father's house and goods, desiring to please God alone, he sought the habit of a holy way of life. He withdrew therefore knowingly ignorant, and wisely unlearned.
fuitvirvitevenerabilisgratiabenedictuset.la: Fuit vir vitae venerabilis, gratia Benedíctus et nomine, ab ipso pueritiæ suæ tempore cor gerens senile. Ætatem quippe moribus transiens, nulli animi voluptati dedit: sed dum in hac terra adhuc esset, quo temporaliter libere uti potuisset, despexit jam quasi aridum mundum cum flore. Qui liberiori genere ex provincia Núrsiæ ortus, Romæ liberalibus litterárum studiis traditus fuerat. Sed cum in eis multos ire per abrupta vitiorum cerneret, eum, quem quasi in ingressu mundi posuérat, retraxit pedem: ne, si quid de scientia ejus attingeret, ipse quoque in immane præcipitium totus iret. Despectis itaque litterarum studiis, relicta domo rebúsque patris, soli Deo placere desiderans, sanctæ conversationis habitum quæsivit. Recessit igitur scienter nescius, et sapienter indocta.

hicitaquecumiamrelictislitterarumstudiis.en: When therefore, having now left the studies of letters, he had resolved to seek the desert, his nurse, who loved him very tenderly, alone followed him. And when they had come to a place which is called Enfide, and, many of the more honourable men detaining them there out of charity, they were staying at the church of blessed Peter, the aforesaid nurse of his asked the neighbouring women to lend her a sieve for cleaning wheat; which, being left carelessly upon the table, was broken by chance, so that it was found divided into two parts. When his nurse, returning soon after, found it so, she began to weep most bitterly, because she saw broken the vessel which she had received on loan. But Benedict, a devout and godly boy, when he saw his nurse weeping, having compassion on her sorrow, took away with him both parts of the broken sieve, and gave himself with tears to prayer; and rising from prayer, he found the vessel beside him so whole, that no traces of a break could be found in it; and forthwith, gently comforting his nurse, he gave back to her whole the sieve which he had taken away broken.
hicitaquecumiamrelictislitterarumstudiis.la: Hic ítaque cum jam relictis litterarum studiis petere deserta decrevisset, nutrix, quæ hunc arctius amabat, sola secúta est. Cumque ad locum veníssent, qui dicitur Enfide, multísque honestioribus viris pro caritáte se illic detinentibus in beáti Petri ecclesia demorarentur, prædicta nutrix illíus ad purgandum triticum a vicinis muliéribus præstari sibi capistérium pétiit: quod super mensam incaute derelictum, casu accidénte fractum est sic, ut in duábus pártibus invenirétur divísum. Quod mox rédiens nutrix illíus ut ita invenit, vehementíssime flere cœpit, quia vas, quod præstitum acceperat, fractum vidébat. Benedíctus autem, religiósus et pius puer, cum nutrícem suam flere conspiceret, ejus dolóri compássus, ablátis secum utrísque fracti capistérii pártibus, sese cum lacrimis in oratiónem dedit: qui ab oratióne surgens, ita juxta se vas sanum réperit, ut in eo inveníri fractúræ nulla vestígia potuíssent: moxque nutrícem suam blande consolátus, ei sanum capistérium réddidit, quod fractum túlerat.

quereseodemlocoacunctisestagnitaatqueint.en: This thing was known by all in that same place, and held in such admiration, that the inhabitants of that place hung up this very sieve at the entrance of the church, that all, both present and to come, might know with how great grace of holy life and perfection the boy Benedict had begun: and it was there many years before the eyes of all, and hung over the doors of the church even unto these times of the Lombards.
quereseodemlocoacunctisestagnitaatqueint.la: Quæ res eódem loco a cunctis est ágnita, atque in tanta admiratióne hábita, ut hoc ipsum capistérium ejus loci íncolæ in ecclésiæ ingréssu suspénderent: quátenus præséntes et secutúri omnes agnoscerent, a quanta Benedíctus puer conversatiónis grátia et perfectióne cœpísset: quod annis multis illic ante ómnium óculos fuit, et usque ad hæc Langobardórum témpora super fores ecclésiæ pepéndit.

incampanieregionefamesincubueratmagneque.en: In the region of Campania a famine had set in, and a great want of food was pressing hard upon all. And now in Benedict's monastery wheat was lacking, and the loaves were almost all consumed, so that no more than five could be found for the brethren at the hour of refection. And when the venerable Father saw them saddened, he sought to correct their faintheartedness with a gentle rebuke, and again to raise them up with a promise, saying: Why is your mind saddened over the want of bread? To-day indeed there is little, but to-morrow ye shall have in abundance. And on the following day two hundred measures of meal were found in sacks before the doors of the cell; by whose hands almighty God had sent them remaineth unknown until now. When the brethren saw this, giving thanks to the Lord, they learned not to doubt of abundance even in want.
incampanieregionefamesincubueratmagneque.la: In Campániæ regióne fames incubuerat, magnæque omnes alimentórum indigentia coangustábat. Jamque in Benedícti monastério tríticum déerat: panes vero pene omnes consumpti fúerant, ut non plus quam quinque ad refectiónis horam fratribus inveníri potuissent.Cumque eos venerabilis Pater contristátos cérneret, eórum pusillanimitátem stúduit modésta increpatióne corrígere, et rursum promissióne subleváre, dicens: Quare de panis inópia vester ánimus contristátur? hódie quidem minus est, sed die crástina abundánter habébitis. Sequenti autem die ducénti farínæ módii ante fores cellæ in saccis invénti sunt: quos omnipotens Deus quibus deferéntibus transmisísset, nunc usque manet incógnitum. Quod cum fratres cérnerent, Dómino grátias deferéntes, didicérunt jam de abundantia nec in egestáte dubitare.

eoquoquetemporequoalimentoruminopiacampa.en: At that same time also, when want of food grievously afflicted Campania, the man of God had given all the goods of his monastery to divers needy persons, so that almost nothing remained in the cellar but a little oil in a glass vessel. Then a certain subdeacon, Agapitus by name, came, earnestly asking that some little oil should be given him. But the man of the Lord, who had resolved to give all things on earth that he might keep all in heaven, commanded that this very little of oil which remained should be given to him that asked. The monk who kept the cellar heard indeed the words of him that commanded, but put off fulfilling them. And when, after a little while, he asked whether what he had commanded had been given, the monk answered that he had not given it at all, because, if he gave it him, nothing whatever would remain for the brethren. Then, being angry, he commanded others to throw out through the window this very glass vessel in which a little oil seemed to remain, lest anything should remain in the cell through disobedience. And so it was done. Now beneath that same window there opened a huge precipice, rough with masses of rock.
eoquoquetemporequoalimentoruminopiacampa.la: Eo quoque témpore quo alimentórum inópia Campániam gráviter affligebat, vir Dei divérsis indigentibus monastérii sui cuncta tribúerat, ut pene nihil in cellário, nisi parum quid ólei in vase vítreo remanéret. Tunc quidam subdiáconus, Agapítus nómine, advenit, magnópere póstulans, ut sibi aliquántulum ólei dari debuísset. Vir autem Dómini, qui cuncta decréverat in terra tribúere, ut in cælo ómnia reserváret, hoc ipsum parum, quod remánserat ólei, jussit peténti dari. Mónachus vero, qui cellárium tenébat, audívit quidem jubéntis verba, sed implére dístulit. Cumque post paululum, si id, quod jússerat, datum esset, inquíreret, respóndit mónachus se mínime dedísse: quia, si illud ei tribúeret, omníno nihil frátribus remanéret, Tunc irátus, áliis præcépit, ut hoc ipsum vas vítreum, in quo parum ólei remansísse videbátur, per fenéstram projícerent, ne in cella áliquid per inobediéntiam remaneret. Factúmque est.Sub fenéstra autem eádem ingens præcipítium patébat, saxórum mólibus ásperum.

proiectumitaquevasvitreumvenitinsaxissed.en: The glass vessel, therefore, being thrown, came upon the rocks, but remained as unharmed as if it had not been thrown at all, so that neither could it be broken nor the oil be spilt. The man of the Lord commanded it to be taken up and, whole as it was, to be given to him that asked. Then, gathering the brethren, he rebuked the disobedient monk before all for his unbelief and pride. And this rebuke ended, he gave himself to prayer with the same brethren. Now in that place where he was praying with the brethren there was a cask, empty of oil and covered. And while the holy man persevered in prayer, the lid of the same cask began to be lifted up by the oil increasing. And when it was moved and lifted, the oil which had increased, passing over the mouth of the cask, flooded the pavement of the place where he lay prostrate. As soon as Benedict, the servant of God, saw this, he forthwith ended his prayer, and the oil ceased to flow upon the pavement.
proiectumitaquevasvitreumvenitinsaxissed.la: Projectum ítaque vas vítreum venit in saxis, sed sic mansit incólume, ac si projéctum mínime fuísset, ita ut neque frangi, neque óleum effúndi potuísset. Quod vir Dómini præcépit levári, atque, ut erat íntegrum, peténti tríbui. Tunc colléctis frátribus, inobedientem mónachum de infidelitáte sua et supérbia coram ómnibus increpávit. Qua increpatióne compléta, sese cum eísdem frátribus in oratiónem dedit. In eo autem loco, ubi cum frátribus orábat, vácuum erat ab óleo dólium et coopértum. Cumque sanctus vir in oratióne persisteret, cœpit operimentum ejúsdem dólii, óleo excrescente, sublevári. Quo commóto atque subleváto, óleum quod excréverat, ora dólii tránsiens, paviméntum loci, in quo incubuerat, inundábat. Quod Benedíctus, Dei fámulus, ut aspéxit, prótinus oratiónem complévit, atque in paviméntum óleum deflúere cessávit.

delibrosecundodialogorumsgregoriipape.en: From the second book of the Dialogues of St. Gregory, Pope
delibrosecundodialogorumsgregoriipape.la: De libro secundo Dialogorum S. Gregórii Papæ

quodamdiecumfratribusadagrioperafuerateg.en: On a certain day he had gone out with the brethren to the work of the field. And a certain countryman, carrying in his arms the body of his dead son, burning with the grief of his bereavement, came to the monastery and asked for Father Benedict. And when he was told that the same Father was staying in the field with the brethren, he forthwith cast down the body of his dead son before the gate of the monastery, and, distraught with sorrow, set off running in haste to find the venerable Father. At that same hour the man of God was already returning with the brethren from the work of the field. And as soon as the bereaved countryman saw him, he began to cry out: Give back my son, give back my son.
quodamdiecumfratribusadagrioperafuerateg.la: Quodam die cum fratribus ad agri opera fuerat egressus. Quidam vero rústicus, defúncti filii corpus in ulnis ferens, orbitátis luctu æstuans, ad monastérium venit, Benedíctum Patrem quæsivit. Cui cum dictum esset, quia idem Pater cum frátribus in agro morarétur, prótinus ante monasterii januam corpus exstincti filii projecit, et dolóre turbátus, ad inveniéndum venerabilem Patrem sese in cursum cóncitus dedit. Eadem vero hora vir Dei ab agri ópere jam cum fratribus revertebátur. Quem mox ut orbátus rústicus aspéxit, clamare cœpit: Redde fílium meum, redde fílium meum.

virautemdeiinhacvocesubstititdicensnumqu.en: But the man of God stopped at this cry, saying: Have I taken thy son from thee? He answered him: He is dead; come, raise him up. As soon as the servant of God heard this, he was much saddened, saying: Go away, brethren, go away; these things are not for us, but for the holy Apostles. Why will ye lay burdens upon us which we cannot bear? But he, whom his exceeding sorrow drove, persisted in his request, swearing that he would not go away unless he raised up his son.
virautemdeiinhacvocesubstititdicensnumqu.la: Vir autem Dei in hac voce substitit dicens: Numquid ego fílium tuum tibi abstuli? Cui ille respóndit: Mórtuus est, veni, resúscita eum. Quod ut mox Dei fámulus audívit, valde contristátus est, dicens: Recédite, fratres, recédite, hæc nostra non sunt, sed sanctórum Apostolórum, Quid nobis ónera vultis impónere, quæ non póssumus portare? At ille, quem nímius cogébat dolor, in sua petitióne pérstitit, jurans, quod non recéderet, nisi ejus fílium resuscitáret.

quemmoxdeifamulusinquisivitdicensubiestc.en: The servant of God forthwith asked him, saying: Where is he? He answered him: Behold, his body lieth at the gate of the monastery. And when the man of God had come thither with the brethren, he bent his knees and lay down upon the little body of the child, and raising himself, he stretched out his hands to heaven, saying: O Lord, look not upon my sins, but upon the faith of this man, who asketh that his son be raised up, and give back to this little body the soul which thou hast taken away. Scarcely had he finished the words of his prayer, when, the soul returning, the whole little body of the boy so trembled, that before the eyes of all who were present it was seen to quiver with a wondrous shaking. And forthwith he took him by the hand, and gave him back to his father living and whole.
quemmoxdeifamulusinquisivitdicensubiestc.la: Quem mox Dei fámulus inquisívit, dicens: Ubi est? Cui ille respondit: Ecce corpus ejus ad jánuam monasterii jacet. Quo cum vir Dei cum fratribus pervenísset, flexit génua, et super corpúsculum infántis incubuit, seséque érigens, ad cælum palmas teténdit, dicens: Dómine, non aspícias peccáta mea, sed fidem hujus hóminis, qui resusicitári fílium suum rogat, et redde in hoc corpúsculum ánimam, quam abstulísti. Vix in oratióne verba compléverat, et, regrendiénte ánima, ita corpúsculum púeri omne contrémuit, ut sub óculis ómnium, qui áderant, apparuerit concussióne mirífica tremendo palpitásse. Cujus mox manum tenuit, et eum patri viventem atque incolumem dedit.

delibrotertioregum.en: From the third book of Kings

etaitadeameliasdamihifiliumtuumtulitquee.en: And Elias said to her: Give me thy son. And he took him out of her bosom, and carried him into the upper chamber where he abode, and laid him upon his own bed.
etaitadeameliasdamihifiliumtuumtulitquee.la: Et ait ad eam Elías: Da mihi fílium tuum. Tulítque eum de sinu ejus, et portávit in cœnáculum ubi ipse manébat, et pósuit super léctulum suum.

sermodesbenedictoabbinfine.en: Sermon on St. Benedict, Abbot, towards the end
sermodesbenedictoabbinfine.la: Sermo de S. Benedicto Abb., In fine

ubicumquesanctecclesiadiffunditurpertrib.en: Wheresoever holy Church is spread abroad, through tribes, through nations, through tongues, the praise of Benedict is sung. For if in the multitude of the people is the dignity of the king, as Solomon saith, how great think we is the dignity of this king, whom so numerous an army of monks followeth? What king or emperor ever ruled in so many parts of the world, or gathered to himself from nations so divers such legions as this man ordereth, of every sex and age, sworn of their own will to the warfare of Christ?
ubicumquesanctecclesiadiffunditurpertrib.la: Ubicumque sancta Ecclésia diffunditur, per tribus, per natiónes, per linguas, laus Benedícti frequentátur. Si enim in multitúdine pópuli dígnitas regis est, ut ait Sálomon, quantam putámus esse dignitátem istíus regis, quem tam numerósus proséquitur exércitus monachórum? Quis umquam rex aut imperátor in tantis mundi pártibus imperávit, aut ex tam divérsis natiónibus sibi tantas legiónes condúxit, quantas vidélicet iste cujúslibet sexus et ætátis in Christi milítia voluntárie jurátas dispónit?

quemquasipresentemintuentesetvexillumins.en: Beholding him as though present, and following the standard of his institute, they manfully break the battle-lines of the devil. To them is fitted that saying of the prophet: Thine eyes shall see thy teacher. Lastly, it is a faithful belief that each of the saints shall rise in the regeneration with those whom he hath gained for the Lord. When therefore all the followers of this his institute shall be gathered together into one, what a sign of apostleship will that great army then show itself to Benedict! O with what joy will he then exult, who shall have been able to mingle himself with those cohorts!
quemquasipresentemintuentesetvexillumins.la: Quem quasi præsentem intuéntes, et vexíllum institutiónis sequéntes, diabólicas ácies viríliter infríngunt. Quibus illud prophéticum coaptátur: Erunt óculi tui vidéntes præceptórem tuum. Dénique fidélis opínio est, quod unusquísque sanctórum cum illis surget in regeneratióne, quos Dómino aquisívit. Cum ígitur univérsi hujúsce institutiónis ejus sequáces in unum coácti fúerint, quale signum apostolátus Benedícto tunc ille copiósus exércitus se ipsum exhibébit? O quali gáudio tunc ille tripudiábit, qui sese illis cohortibus immiscére potúerit!

nuncomnesvellocovelaffectuviciniineumcor.en: Now let all who are near to him, whether in place or in affection, direct the gaze of their heart upon him, for he became all things to all. For children have in the child a pattern to follow, that, since after the example of Isaac they have been offered to God, they may beware of leavening their beginnings. And thereafter let each, through the succession of their ages, be perfect in understanding, that they degenerate not from the fatherly goodness of their fosterer; lest perchance, if they fall from a higher degree, they be the more grievously dashed. But let us also, whosoever have sinned, in no wise fall away from the clemency we are to hope for; for living and after his death he raised the dead, restored things broken, healed things despaired of.
nuncomnesvellocovelaffectuviciniineumcor.la: Nunc omnes vel loco vel afféctu vicíni in eum cordis intúitum dírigant, ómnia enim ómnibus factus est. Habent enim púeri formam in púero, quam sequántur, ut, quóniam ad exémplum Isaac Deo obláti sunt, primórdia sua cáveant fermentáre. Ac deínceps quique per ætátum successiónes sint perfécti sensu, ut a patérna sui nutrícii pietáte non degénerent; ne forte, si ab excellentióri gradu ceciderint, grávius elidántur. Sed et nos, quicúmque delíquimus, nullo modo ab speránda clementia deficiámus; quia vivens et post óbitum mórtuos suscitávit, confrácta restaurávit, desperáta curávit.

etquamvisnonfecerimuseiusvoluntatemdomin.en: And though we have not done his will, let us nevertheless call upon him as our master, and let our eyes be upon his hands, waiting until he lift up his own upon us, and have mercy on us. Let Benedict be ever with us, Benedict in the heart, Benedict in the mouth, Benedict in deed; so that, if there be any virtue, if any praise of discipline, imitating that saying of the Apostle, we may follow the things which we have seen in him, and heard in him, and heard from him, that the God of peace may be with us through him, for ever and ever. Amen.
etquamvisnonfecerimuseiusvoluntatemdomin.la: Et quamvis non fecerimus ejus voluntátem, Dóminum tamen invocémus eum, et sint óculi nostri in manibus ejus intendéntes, donec ipse suos attóllat super nos, et misereátur nostri. Sit nobis semper Benedíctus in corde, Benedíctus in ore, Benedíctus in actu, quátenus, si qua virtus, si qua laus disciplínæ, ut, illud Apostólicum imitántes, quæ vídimus in illo, et audívimus in illo, et audívimus ab illo, sectémur, ut nobíscum sit Deus pacis per ipsum, in sæcula sæculórum. Amen.

inopgaufridiabbdeolamationesdecolloquios.en: From the works of Geoffrey, Abbot: Declamations on the Conversation of Simon with Jesus. I.
inopgaufridiabbdeolamationesdecolloquios.la: In op. Gaufridi Abb.: Deolamationes de Colloquio Simonis cum Jesu. I.

arbitrorverbalectionishuiuseessedequibus.en: I think that the words of this lesson are those of which the Church crieth from the ends of the earth to her immortal Bridegroom: For the sake of the words of thy lips, I have kept hard ways. These indeed are the words which have persuaded men throughout the whole world to contempt of the world and to voluntary poverty. These are they which fill cloisters with monks, and deserts with anchorites. These, I say, are the words which despoil Egypt, and carry off all its best vessels. This is the word living and effectual, converting souls by a happy emulation of holiness and by a faithful promise of truth.
arbitrorverbalectionishuiuseessedequibus.la: Arbitror verba lectiónis hujus ea esse, de quibus ad immortálem Sponsum a fínibus terræ clamat Ecclésia: Propter verba labiórum tuórum ego custodívi vias duras. Hæc nempe sunt verba, quæ contémptum mundi in universo mundo, et voluntáriam persuasére homínibus paupertátem. Hæc sunt, quæ mónachis claustra replent, desérta anachorétis. Hæc, inquam sunt verba, quæ Ægyptum spóliant, et óptima quæque ejus vasa dirípiunt. Hic sermo vivus et éfficax, convértens ánimas felíci æmulatióne sanctitátis et veritátis promissióne fidéli.

nametmundustransitetconcupiscentieiusetr.en: For the world passeth away, and the concupiscence thereof; and it is better to leave these things than to be left by them. Behold, saith he, we have left all things, and have followed thee: no wonder, for he hath rejoiced as a giant to run the way, and thou couldst not follow him running if thou wert laden. Nor yet is it an unprofitable exchange to have left all things for him who is above all things: for together with him all things are given, and when thou hast laid hold of him, he alone shall be all things in all who for him have left all things. All things, I would say indeed, not only possessions, but also desires, and these above all.
nametmundustransitetconcupiscentieiusetr.la: Nam et mundus transit, et concupiscentia ejus et relínquere hæc magis éxpedit quam relínqui. Ecce, inquit, relíquimus ómnia, et secúti sumus te: nimírum, quia exsultávit ut gigas ad curréndam viam, nec curréntem sequi póteras onerátus. Sed nec inútilis commutátio, pro Eo, qui super ómnia est ómnia reliquísse: nam et simul cum Eo donántur ómnia, et ubi apprehenderis Eum, erit unus ipse ómnia in ómnibus, qui pro Ipso ómnia reliquerunt. Omnia sane díxerim, non tantum possessiónes, sed étiam cupiditátes, et eas máxime.

petruscogitatumsuumiactansindominetomnem.en: Peter, casting his thought upon the Lord, and throwing all his care upon him, sure that he would have care of him, left all things and followed the Lord, not even asking about the reward, until, from the danger of the rich which the Saviour was setting forth, he took occasion to ask: What then shall we have? Jesus said to him: Amen I say to you. A word of confirmation is set first: know that what followeth is great. In the regeneration ye also shall sit. Ye shall attain, he saith, him whom ye follow, so that when he shall sit, ye also may sit with him. O sitting! Who will grant me to express in worthy words what I conceive in the affection of my heart concerning this sitting? Nay, who will grant me to enjoy the undisturbed rest of this sitting, which I desire, which I long for, which I seek?
petruscogitatumsuumiactansindominetomnem.la: Petrus cogitátum suum jactans in Dómino, et omnem sollicitúdinem suam in eum projíciens, certus quod illi foret cura de eo, relíquit ómnia, et secútus est Dóminum, ne intérrogans quidem de præmio, domec ex perículo dívitum, quod Salvátor prosequebátur, súmeret occasiónem percontándi: Quid ergo erit nobis? Ait illi Jesus: Amen, dico vobis. Verbum confirmatiónis præmíttitur: magnum nóveris esse, quod séquitur. In regeneratióne sedébitis et vos. Consequémini, ait, quem sequímini, ut, cum ipse séderit, et vos páriter sedeátis. O séssio! Quis mihi tríbuat, ut dignis éxprimam verbis, quod de sessióne hac cordis affectióne concípio? Immo quis tribuat mihi sessiónis hujus imperturbáta frui réquie, quam desídero, quam cúpio, quam requíro?

ecceenimutdixinihilinmesedetsedcunctainm.en: For behold, as I said, nothing in me sitteth still, but all things are in motion; all things waver, all are tossed to and fro. Lastly, where the flesh still lusteth against the spirit, and the spirit against the flesh, what of man seemeth to sit? Already indeed the Son of man sitteth on the seat of majesty, since he hath ascended into heaven, and sitteth at the right hand of God. But it is said, when he shall sit: that is, when he shall appear sitting, as the Apostle saith: For when Christ shall appear, who is your life, then you also shall appear with him in glory. What is more glorious? Let the children of pride judge now and judge beforehand: let them sit with their king, who chose for himself the sides of the north: we shall pass by, and lo, they shall not be.
ecceenimutdixinihilinmesedetsedcunctainm.la: Ecce enim, ut dixi, nihil in me sedet, sed cuncta in motu sunt, ómnia nutant, flúctuant univérsa. Postrémo, ubi concupíscit adhuc caro adversus spíritum, spíritus adversus carnem: quidnam hóminis sedére vidétur? Jam quidem sedet Fílius hóminis in sede majestátis: síquidem ascéndit in cælum, sedet a dextris Dei. Sed, cum séderit, dictum est: hoc est, apparúerit sedens, sicut Apóstolus ait: Cum enim apparúerit Christus vita vestra, tunc et vos apparébitis cum ipso in glória. Quid gloriósius? Júdicent nunc, et præjudicent supérbiæ fílii: cum rege suo sédeant, qui sibi látera Aquilónis elégit: transíbimus, et ecce non erunt.

excitadomineinecclesiaspiritumcuibeatusp.en: Stir up, O Lord, in thy Church the Spirit whom our blessed Father Benedict the Abbot served: that we, being filled with the same, may strive to love what he loved, and to practise in deed what he taught.
excitadomineinecclesiaspiritumcuibeatusp.la: Excita, Dómine, in Ecclésia Spíritum, cui beátus Pater noster Benedíctus Abbas servívit: ut, eódem nos repléti, studeámus amáre, quod amávit; et ópere exercére, quod dócuit.

adhucmodicumetconsummabiturindignatio.en: Yet † a little while, and the indignation shall be accomplished:
adhucmodicumetconsummabiturindignatio.la: Adhuc † módicum et con summábitur indignátio:

etinilladieaufereturonusdehumeronostreti.en: And in that day the burden shall be taken away from our shoulder, and the yoke from our neck.
etinilladieaufereturonusdehumeronostreti.la: Et in illa die auferétur onus de húmero nostro, et jugum de collo nostro.

videantpauperesetletenturqueritedominume.en: Let the poor see and rejoice: seek ye the Lord, and your soul shall live.
videantpauperesetletenturqueritedominume.la: Vídeant páuperes et læténtur: quǽrite Dóminum, et vivet ánima vestra.

oratioiiindormitdeiparen.en: Oration II on the Dormition of the Mother of God, n. 15
oratioiiindormitdeiparen.la: Oratio II in Dormit. Deiparæ, n. 15

nosquideumcolimusdeuminquamnonexnihilopr.en: We who worship God, God, I say, not brought forth out of nothing, but everlasting from the everlasting, and above every cause, reason and thought, both of time and of nature, honour and venerate the Mother of God: not that we hold that his Godhead took its origin from her (for the generation of God is without time, and hath the same eternity with the Father), but we confess a second birth, by the voluntary taking of flesh, whose cause we both know and extol with praises. For on our account, and for the sake of our salvation, he is made flesh who without beginning is incorporeal, that by like he might bring salvation to like; and having taken flesh without the embrace of man, he is born of this holy Virgin, himself remaining wholly God, and made wholly man: himself wholly God together with his flesh, and wholly man with his Godhead. In this manner we acknowledge this Virgin as Mother of God, and celebrate her falling asleep.
nosquideumcolimusdeuminquamnonexnihilopr.la: Nos, qui Deum cólimus, Deum, inquam, non ex nihilo prodúctum, sed sempitérnum ex sempitérno, omníque causa, ratióne et cogitatióne tum témporis tum natúræ superiórem; Dei Matrem honorámus et venerámur: non quod divinitátem ejus ortum ex ea traxísse statuámus (Dei síquidem generátio témpore caret, eamdémque cum Patre æternitátem habet), verum secúndam nativitátem confitémur, per voluntáriam carnis susceptiónem, cujus causam et nóvimus, et láudibus efférimus. Propter nos enim, ac nostræ salútis causa incarnátur, qui sine inítio incorpóreus est, ut símili per símile salútem áfferat: atque assúmpta sine viríli compléxu carne, ex hac sacra Vírgine páritur, ipse totus Deus manens, et totus homo factus: ipse totus Deus una cum carne sua, totúsque homo cum sua divinitáte. Ad hunc modum Dei Matrem Vírginem istam agnóscimus, ejúsque dormitiónem celebrámus.

hancdeiincarnatimatremnosquieolocupletat.en: This Mother of God incarnate let us, who have been so enriched by him that we both are and are called the people of Christ, proclaim to-day with sacred canticles; let us honour her with nightly stations; let us delight her with cleanness of soul and body: her, I say, who is truly pure, and excelleth all after God in purity. For like is wont to rejoice in like. Let us worship and honour her by mercy and compassion towards the needy. For if God is honoured by nothing so much as by mercy, who will deny that his Mother also rejoiceth in the like?
hancdeiincarnatimatremnosquieolocupletat.la: Hanc Dei incarnáti Matrem nos, qui eo locupletáti sumus,ut Christi pópulus et simus et dicámur, sacris hódie cánticis prædicémus; hanc noctúrnis statiónibus honorémus; hanc ánimi et córporis mundítia oblectémus: hanc, inquam, vere puram, atque ómnibus post Deum puritáte præstántem. Solent enim simília simílibus exsultáre. Hanc misericórdia et commiseratióne erga egénos colámus et observémus. Si enim Deus nulla re æque cólitur, atque misericórdia: quis contradícet Matrem quoque non lætári simílibus?

hecineffabilemdivineinnosdilectionisabys.en: She hath made known the unspeakable abyss of the divine love towards us. Through her that long war which was waged against the Creator was brought to an end; through her our reconciliation with him was sealed, and peace and grace were given: whence Angels together with men lead the dance, and we who before were despised are made sons of God. From her we have gathered the grape of the vine; from her we have plucked the bud of immortality. She hath won for us all good things. In her God was made man, and man God. And what is more wonderful than this? what more blessed?
hecineffabilemdivineinnosdilectionisabys.la: Hæc ineffabilem divínæ in nos dilectiónis abyssum pu-blicávit. Per hanc diutúrnum illud bellum, quod cum Creatóre gerebátur, profligátum fuit; per hanc nobis cum eo reconciliatio sancíta, paxque et grátia donáta est: unde Angeli una cum homínibus choros ágitant, et qui prius contémptui erámus, Dei fílii effécti sumus. Ex ea vite uvam collégimus: ex ea immortalitátis germen excérpsimus. Hæc nobis ómnia bona conciliávit. In hac Deus homo factus est, et homo Deus. Et quid hoc admirabílius? quid beátius?

bernardusdoctormellifluusamicussponsivir.en: Bernard, * the mellifluous Doctor, the friend of the Bridegroom, the wondrous herald of the Virgin Mother, shone forth a most illustrious shepherd in Clairvaux.
bernardusdoctormellifluusamicussponsivir.la: Bernárdus, * Doctor mellífluus, amícus Sponsi, Vírginis Matris præco miríficus, in clara valle pastor effúlsit claríssimus.

deusquiperbeatumbernardumnovumanachoreti.en: O God, who through blessed Bernard didst will to begin in thy Church a new kind of anchoretic life: grant, we beseech thee, that, following in his footsteps, we may merit to obtain the rewards of eternal life.
deusquiperbeatumbernardumnovumanachoreti.la: Deus, qui per beátum Bernárdum novum anachoréticæ vitæ genus in Ecclésia tua exordíri voluísti: concéde, quæsumus; ut, ejus vestígiis insisténtes, ætérnæ vitæ præmia cónsequi mereámur.

incordegertrudisinvenietismedicitdominus.en: In the heart of Gertrude * ye shall find me, saith the Lord: my soul hath been well pleased in her.
incordegertrudisinvenietismedicitdominus.la: In corde Gertrúdis * inveniétis me, dicit Dóminus: complácuit sibi in illa ánima mea. Ps. 109

sanctissimachristisponsadilectosuoiugite.en: The most holy * spouse of Christ clave continually to her beloved, and was one spirit with him.
sanctissimachristisponsadilectosuoiugite.la: Sanctíssima * Christi sponsa dilécto suo júgiter adhærébat, et unus cum illo spíritus erat. Ps. 112

quampulchresgertrudisetquamdecoraindelic.en: How fair art thou, Gertrude, * and how comely in delights! in whom God hath prepared for himself a pleasant dwelling.
quampulchresgertrudisetquamdecoraindelic.la: Quam pulchra es Gertrúdis, * et quam decóra in delíciis! in qua jucúndam sibi Deus habitatiónem præparávit. Ps. 121

vivoautemegoiamnonegovivitveroinmechrist.en: And I live, * now not I, but Christ liveth in me: for I bear the marks of the Lord Jesus in my heart.
vivoautemegoiamnonegovivitveroinmechrist.la: Vivo autem ego, * jam non ego, vivit vero in me Christus: ego enim stígmata Domini Jesu in corde meo porto. Ps. 126

apparueruntcelestesspiritusdecelodescend.en: There appeared * heavenly spirits coming down from heaven to earth, who with tuneful voices invited Gertrude to the joys of paradise: Come, come, O lady, for the delights of heaven await thee, alleluia, alleluia.
apparueruntcelestesspiritusdecelodescend.la: Apparuerunt * cæléstes spíritus de cælo descendéntes ad terram, qui Gertrúdem ad paradísi gáudia modulátis vócibus invitábant: Veni, veni dómina, quia te exspéctant cæli delíciæ, allelúia, allelúia.

exbulladogmaticapiipapeix.en: From the Dogmatic Bull of Pope Pius IX.
exbulladogmaticapiipapeix.la: Ex Bulla dogmatica Pii Papæ IX

hunceximiumsingularemquevirginistriumphu.en: This excellent and singular triumph of the Virgin, and her most excellent innocence, purity and holiness, and her freedom from every stain of sin, and the unspeakable abundance and greatness of all heavenly graces, virtues and privileges, the same Fathers saw now in that ark of Noe, which, divinely appointed, wholly safe and unharmed from the common shipwreck of the whole world
hunceximiumsingularemquevirginistriumphu.la: Hunc eximium singularemque Virginis triumphum, excellentissimamque innocentiam, puritatem, sanctitatem, eiusque ab omni peccati labe integritatem, atque ineffabilem cælestium omnium gratiarum, virtutum, ac privilegiorum copiam, et magnitudinem iidem Patres videiunt tum in arca illa Noe, quæ divinitus constituta a communi totius mundi naufragio plane salva et incolumis

evasittuminscalaillaquamdeterraadcelumus.en: escaped; now in that ladder which Jacob saw reaching from earth even unto heaven, by whose steps the Angels of God ascended and descended, and on whose top the Lord himself leaned; now in that bush which Moses in the holy place beheld burning on every side, and amid the crackling flames of fire not consumed nor suffering the least loss, but fairly growing green and blossoming; now in that impregnable tower before the face of the enemy, from which hang a thousand bucklers and all the armour of the valiant; now in the garden enclosed, which cannot be violated nor corrupted by any frauds of snares; now in that resplendent city of God, whose foundations are in the holy mountains; now in that most august temple of God, which, shining with divine splendours, is full of the glory of the Lord; now in very many other figures of the same kind, wherein the Fathers have handed down that the exalted dignity of the Mother of God, and her spotless innocence, and her holiness never subject to any blemish, were signally foretold.
evasittuminscalaillaquamdeterraadcelumus.la: evasit; tum in scala illa, quam de terra ad cælum usque pertingere vidit Iacob, cuius gradibus Angeli Dei ascendebant et descendebant, cuiusque vertici ipse initebatur Dominus, tum in rubo illo, quem in loco sancto Moyses undique ardere ac inter crepitantes ignis flammas non iam comburi aut iacturam vel minimam pati, sed pulchre virescere ac florescere conspexit; tum in illa inexpugnabili turre a facie inimici, ex qua mille clypei pendent, omnisque armatura fortium; tum in horto concluso, qui nescit violari neque corrumpi ullis insidiarum fraudibus; tum in corusca illa Dei civitate, cuius fundamenta in montibus sanctis; tum in augustissimo illo Dei templo, quod divinis refulgens splendoribus plenum est gloria Domini; tum in aliis eiusdem generis omnino plurimis, quibus excelsa in Deiparæ dignitatem, eiusque illibatam innocentiam, et nulli umquam nævo obnoxiam sanctitatem insigniter prænunciatam fuisse Patres tradiderunt.

adhanceandemdivinorummunerumvelutisummam.en: For describing this same, as it were, sum of divine gifts, and the original integrity of the Virgin, of whom Jesus was born, the same Fathers, using the words of the Prophets, celebrated the august Virgin herself in no other wise than as the clean dove, and the holy Jerusalem, and the exalted throne of God, and the ark of sanctification, and the house which the eternal Wisdom built for itself, and that Queen who, abounding in delights and leaning upon her Beloved, came forth from the mouth of the Most High wholly perfect, beautiful and altogether dear to God, and never stained with any spot of blemish.
adhanceandemdivinorummunerumvelutisummam.la: Ad hanc eandem divinorum munerum veluti summam, originalemque Virginis, de qua natus est Iesus, integritatem describendam iidem Prophetarum adhibentes eloquia non aliter ipsam augustam Virginem concelebrarunt, ac uti columbam mundam, et sanctam Ierusalem, et excelsum Dei thronum, et arcam sanctificationis et domum, quam sibi æterna ædificavit Sapientia, et Reginam illam, quæ deliciis affluens et innixa super Dilectum suum, ex ore Altissimi providit omnino perfecta, speciosa ao penitus cara Deo, et nullo umquam labis nævo maculata.

cumveroipsipatresecclesiequescriptoresan.en: And when the Fathers themselves and the writers of the Church considered in heart and mind that the most blessed Virgin, when the Angel Gabriel announced to her the most sublime dignity of Mother of God, had been called full of grace in the name and by the command of God himself, they taught that by this singular and solemn salutation, never heard elsewhere, it is shown that the Mother of God was the seat of all divine graces, and adorned with all the gifts of the divine Spirit, nay, an almost infinite treasury of the same gifts, and an inexhaustible abyss, so that, never subject to the curse, and together with her Son partaker of perpetual blessing, she merited to hear from Elisabeth, moved by the divine Spirit: Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb. Hence the opinion of the same Fathers, no less clear than concordant, that the most glorious Virgin, to whom he that is mighty hath done great things, stood forth as that unspeakable miracle of God among all heavenly things, nay, the summit of all miracles, and the worthy Mother of God, and, approaching as near as may be to God himself, so far as created nature allows, rose higher than all praises, both human and angelic.
cumveroipsipatresecclesiequescriptoresan.la: Cum vero ipsi Patres, Ecclesiæque scriptores animo menteque reputarent, beatissimam Virginem ab Angelo Giabriele sublimissimam Dei Matris dignitatem ei nuntiante, ipsius Dei nomine et iussu gratia plenam fuisse nuncupatam, docuerunt hac singulari sollemnique salutatione numquam alias audita ostendi, Deiparam fuisse omnium divinarum gratiarum sedem, omnibusque divini Spiritus charismatibus exornatam, immo eorundem charismatum infinitum prope thesaurum, abyssumque inexhaustam, adeo ut numquam maledicto obnoxia, et una cum Filio perpetuæ benedictionis particeps ab Elisabeth divino acta Sipiritu audire meruerit benedicta tu inter mulieres, et benedictus fructus ventris tui. Hinc non luculenta minus quam concors eorumdem sententia, gloriosissimam Virginem, cui fecit magna qui potens est, ea cælestium omnium ineffabile Dei miraculum, immo omnium miraculorum apex, ac digna Dei mater exstiterit, et ad Deum ipsum, pro ratione creatæ naturæ, quam proxime accedens omnibus, qua humanis, qua angelicis præconiis celsior evaserit.

repletisuntomnesspiritusanctetceperuntlo.en: They were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and began to speak, according as the Holy Ghost gave them to speak:
repletisuntomnesspiritusanctetceperuntlo.la: Repléti sunt omnes Spíritu sancto, et cœpérunt loqui, prout Spíritus sanctus dabat éloqui illos:

etconvenitmultitudodicentiumalleluia.en: And the multitude came together, saying: Alleluia.

loquebanturvariislinguisapostolimagnalia.en: The Apostles spoke in diverse tongues the wonderful works of God.
loquebanturvariislinguisapostolimagnalia.la: Loquebántur váriis linguis Apóstoli magnália Dei:

illuminareilluminareierusalemquiavenitlu.en: Shine, shine, O Jerusalem, for thy light is come;
illuminareilluminareierusalemquiavenitlu.la: Illumináre, illumináre Jerúsalem, quia venit lux tua:

etgloriadominisuperteortest.en: And the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee.
etgloriadominisuperteortest.la: Et glória Dómini super te orta est.

etambulabuntgentesinluminetuetregesinspl.en: And the Gentiles shall walk in thy light, and kings in the brightness of thy rising.
etambulabuntgentesinluminetuetregesinspl.la: Et ambulábunt Gentes in lúmine tuo, et reges in splendóre ortus tui:

fulgebuntiustisicutsolinconspectudei.en: The just shall shine * as the sun in the sight of God.
fulgebuntiustisicutsolinconspectudei.la: Fulgébunt justi * sicut sol in conspéctu Dei.

deusquiintuecaritatisexemplumadfideliumr.en: O God, who, for an example of thy charity, didst divinely teach Saints Peter and Raymund to enrich thy Church with a new offspring for the redemption of the faithful: grant us by their intercession, that, loosed from the bondage of sin, we may rejoice in perpetual freedom in our heavenly fatherland.
deusquiintuecaritatisexemplumadfideliumr.la: Deus, qui in tuae caritatis exemplum, ad fidelium redemptionem sanctos Petrum et Raymundum Ecclesiam tuam nova prole fecundare divinitus docuisti: ipsorum nobis intercessione concede; a peccati servitute solutis, in caelesti patria perpetua libertate gaudere.

commemoratiosioannisboscoconfessoris.en: Commemoration of St. John Bosco, Confessor

deusquisanctumioannemconfessoremtuumadol.en: O God, who didst raise up thy blessed Confessor John, to be a father and teacher of youth, and didst will that through him, with the help of the Virgin Mary, new families should flourish in the Church, grant we pray that enkindled with the same fire of charity we may be strong to seek after souls and to serve thee alone.
deusquisanctumioannemconfessoremtuumadol.la: Deus, qui sanctum Joánnem Confessórem tuum adolescéntium patrem et magístrum excitásti, ac per eum, auxiliatríce Vírgine María, novas in Ecclésia tua famílias floréscere voluísti: concéde, quǽsumus; ut eódem caritátis igne succénsi, ánimas quǽrere, tibíque soli servíre valeámus.

deusquinosbeatibenedictiabbatisdoctrinet.en: O God, who didst will that we be instructed by the teaching and example of blessed Benedict the Abbot: † mercifully grant, that what, by thy gift, we have promised, * we may by his patronage faithfully fulfil.
deusquinosbeatibenedictiabbatisdoctrinet.la: Deus, qui nos beáti Benedícti Abbátis doctrína et exémplo erudíri voluísti: † concéde propítius; ut quod, te donánte, promísimus, * ejúsdem patrocínio fidéliter adimplére valeámus.

sapientiamsanctorumnarrentpopulietlaudes.en: Let the people shew forth the wisdom * of the saints, and let the Church declare their praise.
sapientiamsanctorumnarrentpopulietlaudes.la: Sapiéntiam * sanctórum narrent pópuli, et laudes eórum núntiet Ecclésia. Ps. 109

beatipacificibeatimundocordequoniamipsid.en: Blessed are the peacemakers, * blessed are the clean of heart: for they shall see God.
beatipacificibeatimundocordequoniamipsid.la: Beáti pacífici, * beáti mundo corde: quóniam ipsi Deum vidébunt. Ps. 112

sacerdotesdeibenedicitedominumservidomin.en: Ye priests of God, bless the Lord: ye servants of the Lord, sing a hymn to God.
sacerdotesdeibenedicitedominumservidomin.la: Sacerdótes Dei, benedícite Dóminum: servi Dómini, hymnum dícite Deo. Ps. 131

illivirimisericordiesuntquorumpietatesno.en: These are men of mercy, whose godly deeds have not failed: good things continue with their seed.
illivirimisericordiesuntquorumpietatesno.la: Illi viri misericórdiæ sunt, quorum pietátes non defuérunt. Cum sémine eórum pérmanent bona.

hereditassanctanepoteseorumetintestament.en: Their posterity are a holy inheritance, and their seed hath stood in the covenants.
hereditassanctanepoteseorumetintestament.la: Heréditas sancta nepótes eórum, et in testaméntis stetit semen eórum.

indiebussuisedificaveruntdomumetexaltave.en: In their days they built the house, and set up a holy temple to the Lord, prepared for everlasting glory.
indiebussuisedificaveruntdomumetexaltave.la: In diébus suis ædificavérunt domum, et exaltavérunt templum sanctum Dómino, parátum in glóriam sempitérnam.

ostenditmihimariathesaurosincomparabiles.en: Mary showed me * incomparable treasures, which she promised to give me in heaven.
ostenditmihimariathesaurosincomparabiles.la: Osténdit mihi María * thesáuros incomparábiles, quos mihi dáturam in cælis repromísit.

humiliumdeusprotectoretamatorquifamulamt.en: O God, protector and lover of the humble, who didst gladden thy handmaid Mary Bernard with the apparition and converse of the Immaculate Virgin Mary: grant, we beseech thee, that by the simple paths of faith we may merit to come to the vision of thee in heaven.
humiliumdeusprotectoretamatorquifamulamt.la: Humílium, Deus, protéctor et amátor, qui fámulam tuam Maríam Bernárdam Immaculátæ Vírginís Maríæ apparitióne et allóquio recreásti: præsta, quǽsumus; ut, per símplices fídei sémitas, ad tuam in cœlis visiónem perveníre mereámur.

exsultabuntsanctiingloria.en: The saints shall rejoice in glory:

letabunturincubilibus.en: They shall be joyful in their beds.

amendicovobisquoduniexminimismeisfecisti.en: Amen I say to you: * as long as ye did it to one of my least, ye did it to me: come, ye blessed of my Father, possess the kingdom prepared for you from the beginning of the world.
amendicovobisquoduniexminimismeisfecisti.la: Amen dico vobis: * quod uni ex mínimis meis fecístis, mihi fecístis: veníte, benedícti Patris mei, possidéte parátum vobis regnum ab inítio sǽculi.

omnipotensetmisericorsdeusquihumanogener.en: Almighty and merciful God, who hast bestowed upon mankind both the remedies of salvation and the gifts of eternal life: grant us, we beseech thee, that by the patronage of blessed John and Camillus we may merit to be presented to thee in the hour of our departure without stain of sin.
omnipotensetmisericorsdeusquihumanogener.la: Omnípotens et miséricors Deus, qui humáno géneri et salútis remédia et vitæ ætérnæ múnera contulísti: da nobis, quæsumus; ut beatórum Joánnis et Camílli patrocínio in hora éxitus nostri absque peccáti mácula tibi repræsentári mereámur.

gabrielemarchangelumscimusdivinitusteess.en: We know that the Archangel Gabriel spoke to thee from God: we believe that thy womb conceived of the Holy Ghost: let the unhappy Jew blush for shame, who saith that Christ was born of the seed of Joseph.
gabrielemarchangelumscimusdivinitusteess.la: Gabriélem Archángelum scimus divínitus te esse affátum: úterum tuum de Spíritu Sancto crédimus impregnátum: erubéscat Judǽus ínfelix, qui dicit Christum ex Joseph sémine esse natum.

deusquigressusbeatiludovicimariepresbyte.en: O God, who didst will to direct the steps of blessed Louis Mary, priest, in the way of salvation and of the love of Christ, the Blessed Virgin accompanying him: grant that, by his example, meditating on the mysteries of thy love, we may strive unweariedly to build up thy Church.
deusquigressusbeatiludovicimariepresbyte.la: Deus, qui gressus beáti Ludovíci Maríae, presbýteri, in viam salútis et dilectiónis Christi, beáta Vírgine comitánte, dirígere voluísti, da ut, ejus exémplo, tui amóris mystéria meditántes Ecclésiam tuam aedificáre indefésse studeámus.

omnipotenseternedeusquisanctumludovicumm.en: Almighty, everlasting God, who didst make Saint Louis Mary, priest, an outstanding witness and teacher of complete self-giving to Christ thy Son through the hands of his blessed Mother: grant us that, following the same spiritual way, we may be able continually to extend thy kingdom.
omnipotenseternedeusquisanctumludovicumm.la: Omnípotens ætérne Deus, qui sanctum Ludovícum Maríam presbýterum plenæ Christo Fílio tuo deditiónis per ejus beátæ Matris manus exímium testem et magístrum effecísti, concéde nobis, ut, eándem spiritálem viam sectántes, regnum tuum iúgiter exténdere valeámus.

ecceioannavirgosimplexetpiissimaquoniamt.en: Behold Joan, * a virgin simple and most devout, for she feared the Lord greatly, nor was there any that spoke of her † an ill word.
ecceioannavirgosimplexetpiissimaquoniamt.la: Ecce Joánna * virgo simplex et piíssima, quóniam timébat Dóminum valde, nec erat qui loquerétur de illa † verbum malum Ps. 109

suscitaviteamdominusetideopuellainduitar.en: The Lord raised her up, * and therefore the maiden put on the armour of God, that she might stand against the snares † of the enemies.
suscitaviteamdominusetideopuellainduitar.la: Suscitávit eam dóminus, * et ídeo puélla índuit armatúram Dei, ut posset stare advérsus insídias † inimicórum Ps. 112

stetitsuccinctalumbossuosinveritateetind.en: She stood, * having her loins girt about with truth, and having put on the breastplate of justice, she took the shield and the helmet † of salvation.
stetitsuccinctalumbossuosinveritateetind.la: Stetit * succíncta lumbos suos in veritáte, et indúta lorícam justítiæ, assúmpsit scutum et gáleam † salútis Ps. 121

eccelevavitadgentesmanumsuametadpopulosa.en: Behold, she lifted up * her hand to the nations, and raised the standard of the Lord to the peoples, that the adversaries † might flee.
eccelevavitadgentesmanumsuametadpopulosa.la: Ecce levávit * ad gentes manum suam, et ad pópulos axaltávit signum Dómini, ut fúgerent partes † advérsæ Ps. 126

custodiviteamangeluseiusethinceuntemetib.en: His Angel * kept her, both going hence, and abiding there, and returning thence, and in the midst of the fire did not forsake † her.
custodiviteamangeluseiusethinceuntemetib.la: Custodívit eam * Angelus ejus, et hinc eúntem, et ibi commorántem, et inde reverténtem, atque in médio ignis non derelíquit † eam.

proposuisapientiamadduceremihiadconviven.en: I purposed to take wisdom to me to live with me: † knowing that she will communicate to me of her good things, and will be a comfort in my cares and grief. * For her I shall have glory among the multitude, and honour with the ancients, though I be young.
proposuisapientiamadduceremihiadconviven.la: Propósui sapiéntiam addúcere mihi ad convivéndum: † sciens quóniam mecum communicábit de bonis, et erit allocútio cogitatiónis et tǽdii mei. * Habébo, propter hanc, claritátem ad turbas, et honórem apud senióres júvenis.

audifilietvideetinclinaauremtuam.en: Hearken, O daughter, and see, * and incline thy ear.
audifilietvideetinclinaauremtuam.la: Audi fília, et vide, * Et inclína aurem tuam.

obliviscerepopulumtuumetdomumpatristui.en: Forget thy people, and thy father's house.
obliviscerepopulumtuumetdomumpatristui.la: Oblivíscere pópulum tuum, et domum patris tui.

christirefersimaginem.en: Thou showest forth the image of Christ.

iesurepletalumine.en: Filled with the light of Jesus,

dumfatapandispatrie.en: While thou unfoldest the fates of thy country,

silentpaventqueiudices.en: The judges are silent and afraid.

oppressaflammisclamitas.en: Overwhelmed by the flames, thou criest out

amplexaadipsumsimplicis.en: Embracing, to him, like a simple

chorisbeatisvirginum.en: To the blessed choirs of Virgins

tedeprecantesingulis.en: Through thy prayer, to each one

deturcoronaglorie.en: May the crown of glory be given.

sitlauspatrisitfilio.en: Praise be to the Father, praise to the Son,

viresetaugetlanguidis.en: And increaseth strength to the faint.

meritisetprecibusbeateioanne.en: By the merits and prayers of Blessed Joan.

propitiusestodominepopulotuo.en: Be thou, O Lord, propitious to thy people.

hecestioannavirgoaurelianensishecestquem.en: This is Joan, * the Virgin of Orleans: this is she that prayeth much for the people, and for the whole French † nation.
hecestioannavirgoaurelianensishecestquem.la: Hæc est Joánna * virgo Aurelianénsis: hæc est quæ multum orat pro pópulo, et pro univérsa Gallórum † gente.

deusquibeatamioannamvirginemadfidemacpat.en: O God, who didst wonderfully raise up blessed Joan the Virgin to defend the faith and her country: † grant, we beseech thee, by her intercession, * that thy Church, having overcome the snares of her enemies, may enjoy perpetual peace.
deusquibeatamioannamvirginemadfidemacpat.la: Deus, qui beátam Joánnam Vírginem ad fidem ac pátriam tuéndam mirabíliter suscitásti: † da, quæsumus, ejus intercessióne; * ut Ecclésia tua, hóstium superátis insídiis, perpétua pace fruátur.

aurelianiturribus.en: The men of Orleans by the towers

frustrapremunturhostium.en: Of the enemy are pressed in vain:

quamvellethostiparcere.en: How fain would she have spared the foe!

huncvoceamicapremonet.en: With friendly voice she warneth him

sponteutrecedensliberum.en: That, departing of his own will, the free

regnumrelinquatgallie.en: Kingdom of France he may leave.

negatsedagmengallicum.en: He refuseth; but the French host

turmefuganturhostium.en: The troops of the foe are put to flight:

rhemospatescitsemita.en: The path to Rheims lieth open.

contramalumcertantibus.en: To them that strive against evil

elevatestmagnificentiaioannesupercelos.en: The magnificence * of Joan is exalted above the heavens.
elevatestmagnificentiaioannesupercelos.la: Eleváta est * magnificéntia Joánnæ super cælos. Ps. 8

venielectameetponamintethronummeumquiaco.en: Come, my chosen one, * and I will set my throne in thee, for the King hath greatly desired thy beauty.
venielectameetponamintethronummeumquiaco.la: Veni, elécta mea, * et ponam in te thronum meum, quia concupívit Rex spéciem tuam. Ps. 18

accepitbenedictionemadominetmisericordia.en: She hath received * a blessing from the Lord, and mercy from God her Saviour.
accepitbenedictionemadominetmisericordia.la: Accépit * benedictiónem a Dómino, et misericórdiam a Deo salutári suo. Ps. 23

propterveritatemetmansuetudinemetiustiti.en: Because of truth, * and meekness, and justice: thy right hand shall conduct thee wonderfully.
propterveritatemetmansuetudinemetiustiti.la: Propter veritátem, * et mansuetúdinem, et justítiam: dedúcet te mirabíliter déxtera tua. Ps. 44

arcumconteretetconfringetarmetscutacombu.en: He shall destroy the bow, * and break the weapons, and burn the shields with fire.
arcumconteretetconfringetarmetscutacombu.la: Arcum cónteret, * et confrínget arma, et scuta combúret igni. Ps. 45

iustitietmisericordiaplenestdexteratua.en: With justice and mercy * thy right hand is full.
iustitietmisericordiaplenestdexteratua.la: Justítia et misericórdia * plena est déxtera tua. Ps. 47

confessietpulchritudoinconspectueiussanc.en: Praise and beauty * are before him: holiness and majesty in his sanctuary.
confessietpulchritudoinconspectueiussanc.la: Conféssio et pulchritúdo * in conspéctu ejus, sánctitas et magnificéntia in sanctificatióne ejus. Ps. 95

annuntiaveruntceliiustitiameiusetviderun.en: The heavens declared * his justice, and all the peoples saw his glory.
annuntiaveruntceliiustitiameiusetviderun.la: Annuntiavérunt cæli * justítiam ejus, et vidérunt omnes pópuli glóriam ejus. Ps. 96

iudicavitiniustitietpopulosinequitate.en: He hath judged in justice, and the peoples with equity.
iudicavitiniustitietpopulosinequitate.la: Judicávit in justítia, et pópulos in æquitáte. Ps. 97, 98

factusestdominussusceptormeus.en: The Lord is become my support.

etrefugiummeumindietribulationis.en: And my refuge in the day of tribulation.
etrefugiummeumindietribulationis.la: Et refúgium meum in die tribulatiónis.

posuistidominesupercaputeius.en: Thou hast set, O Lord, upon her head.

delibrecclesiastici.en: Lesson from the book of Ecclesiasticus

confitebortibidominerexetcollaudabotedeu.en: I will give glory to thee, O Lord, O King, and I will praise thee, O God my Saviour. I will give glory to thy name: for thou hast been a helper and protector to me, and hast preserved my body from destruction, from the snare of an unjust tongue, and from the lips of them that forge lies, and in the sight of them that stood by, thou wast my helper. And thou hast delivered me, according to the multitude of the mercy of thy name, from them that did roar, prepared to devour, out of the hands of them that sought my life, and from the gates of afflictions, which compassed me about: from the oppression of the flame which surrounded me, and in the midst of the fire I was not burnt: from the depth of the belly of hell, and from an unclean tongue, and from lying words, from an unjust king, and from an unjust tongue.
confitebortibidominerexetcollaudabotedeu.la: Confitébor tibi, Dómine, Rex, et collaudábo te Deum Salvatórem meum. Confitébor nómini tuo: quóniam adjútor et protéctor factus es mihi, et liberásti corpus meum a perditióne, a láqueo linguæ iníquæ et a lábiis operántium mendácium, et in conspéctu astántium factus est mihi adjútor. Et liberásti me secúndum multitúdinem misericórdiæ nóminis tui a rugiéntibus, præparátis ad escam, de mánibus quæréntium ánimam meam, et de portis tribulatiónum, quæ circumdedérunt me: a pressúra flammæ, quæ circúmdedit me, et in médio ignis non sum æstuáta: de altitúdine ventris ínferi, et a lingua coinquináta, et a verbo mendácii, a rege iníquo, et a lingua injústa.

deusomniumexauditorestipsemisitangelumsu.en: God is the hearer of all: he sent his Angel, and took me from my father's sheep:
deusomniumexauditorestipsemisitangelumsu.la: Deus ómnium exaudítor est: ipse misit Angelum suum, et tulit me de óvibus patris mei:

etunxitmeunctionemisericordiesue.en: And anointed me with the unction of his mercy.
etunxitmeunctionemisericordiesue.la: Et unxit me unctióne misericórdiæ suæ.

preparatecordavestradominetserviteilliso.en: Prepare your hearts unto the Lord, and serve him only, who hath sent me to your help.
preparatecordavestradominetserviteilliso.la: Præparáte corda vestra Dómino, et servíte illi soli, qui misit me in adjutórium vobis.

laudabitusqueadmortemanimameadominumetvi.en: My soul shall praise the Lord even to death, and my life was drawing near to hell beneath. They compassed me on every side, and there was no one that would help me. I looked for the succour of men, and there was none. I remembered thy mercy, O Lord, and thy works, which are from the beginning of the world: for thou deliverest them that wait for thee, O Lord, and settest them free out of the hands of the nations.
laudabitusqueadmortemanimameadominumetvi.la: Laudábit usque ad mortem ánima mea Dóminum, et vita mea appropínquans erat in inférno deórsum. Circumdedérunt me úndique, et non erat qui adjuváret. Respíciens eram ad adjutórium hóminum, et non erat. Memoráta sum misericórdiæ tuæ, Dómine, et operatiónis tuæ, quæ a sǽculo sunt: quóniam éruis sustinéntes te, Dómine, et líberas eos de mánibus géntium.

egotulitededomopatristuietaudirefecitibi.en: I took thee from thy father's house, and made thee hear my voice:
egotulitededomopatristuietaudirefecitibi.la: Ego tuli te de domo patris tui, et audíre feci tibi vocem meam:

fuiquetecuminomnibusubicumqueambulasti.en: And I was with thee in all things, whithersoever thou didst walk.
fuiquetecuminomnibusubicumqueambulasti.la: Fuíque tecum in ómnibus, ubicúmque ambulásti.

fecitibinomengrandeinuniversopopulotuoiu.en: I have made thee a great name in all thy people, like unto the name of the great ones that are on the earth.
fecitibinomengrandeinuniversopopulotuoiu.la: Feci tibi nomen grande in univérso pópulo tuo, juxta nomen magnórum, qui sunt in terra.

exaltastisuperterramhabitationemmeametpr.en: Thou hast exalted my dwelling place upon the earth, and I have prayed for death to pass away. I called upon the Lord, the Father of my Lord, that he would not leave me in the day of my trouble, and in the time of the proud without help. I will praise thy name continually, and will praise it with thanksgiving, and my prayer was heard. And thou hast saved me from destruction, and hast delivered me from the evil time. Therefore I will give thanks, and praise thee, and bless the name of the Lord.
exaltastisuperterramhabitationemmeametpr.la: Exaltásti super terram habitatiónem meam, et pro morte defluénte deprecáta sum. Invocávi Dóminum Patrem Dómini mei, ut non derelínquat me in die tribulatiónis meæ, et in témpore superbórum sine adjutório. Laudábo nomen tuum assídue, et collaudábo illud in confessióne, et exaudíta est orátio mea. Et liberásti me de perditióne, et eripuísti me de témpore iníquo. Proptérea confitébor, et laudem dicam tibi, et benedícam nómini Dómini.

adonaidominedeusmagneetmirabilisquidedis.en: O Adonai, O Lord, God great and wonderful, who hast given salvation by the hand of a woman,
adonaidominedeusmagneetmirabilisquidedis.la: Adonái, Dómine, Deus magne et mirábilis, qui dedísti salútem in manu féminæ,

exaudiprecesservorumtuorum.en: Graciously hear the prayers of thy servants.

benedictusesdominequinonderelinquispresu.en: Blessed art Thou, O Lord, Who failest none that put their trust in thee, and humblest such as boast themselves in their own strength.
benedictusesdominequinonderelinquispresu.la: Benedíctus es, Dómine, qui non derelínquis præsuméntes de te, et de sua virtúte gloriántes humílias.

ioannadearcinoppidodomremensiolimdiecesi.en: Joan of Arc was born in the town of Domremy, formerly of the diocese of Toul, now of Saint-Dié, of parents notable for their faith and the integrity of their lives, in the year of Christ fourteen hundred and twelve. She was scarcely thirteen years old, and had been taught only household tasks, the work of the fields, and the first elements of divine things, when she was warned that she had been chosen by God to free France from her enemies and to restore the kingdom to its former state. After Michael the Archangel, and Catharine and Margaret, holy virgins, with whom she was on familiar terms, had for five years informed her how she should carry out the thing commanded her, judging that God must be obeyed, she asked of the governor of Vaucouleurs, and after some refusals obtained, that he should give her men to lead her to King Charles.
ioannadearcinoppidodomremensiolimdiecesi.la: Joánna de Arc, in óppido Domreménsi, olim diœcésis Tulénsis, nunc Sancti Deódati, conspícuis fide et morum integritáte paréntibus, orta est anno Christi millésimo quadringentésimo duodécimo. Vix trédecim annos habébat, solúmmodo doméstica negótia, opus rústicum, et prima rerum divinárum eleménta edócta erat, cum se a Deo electam esse admónita est, ad Gálliam ab hóstibus liberándam, et ad prístinum regnum restituéndum. Postquam per quinque annos Míchaël Archángelus atque Catharína et Margaríta, vírgines sanctæ, quibus familiáriter utebátur, certiórem eam fecérunt, quómodo rem jussam perágeret, Deo paréndum esse rata, a præfécto Vallis Colórum pétiit, et, post nonnúllas repúlsas, obtínuit, ut viros sibi daret, qui se ad Cárolum regem dúcerent.

benedicattedominusinvirtutesuaquipertead.en: The Lord bless thee by His power, Who hath brought our enemies to nought through thee.
benedicattedominusinvirtutesuaquipertead.la: Benedícat te Dóminus in virtúte sua, qui per te ad níhilum redégit inimícos nostros:

utnondeficiatlaustuadeorehominum.en: And may the praise of thee never fail from the mouth of men.
utnondeficiatlaustuadeorehominum.la: Ut non defíciat laus tua de ore hóminum.

tuletitiatuhonorificentiapopulinostriqui.en: Thou art the joy, thou the honour of our people, for the Lord hath so magnified thy name.
tuletitiatuhonorificentiapopulinostriqui.la: Tu lætítia, tu honorificéntia pópuli nostri, quia nomen tuum ita magnificávit Dóminus.

supernismonitisobtemperanssuperatislongi.en: Obeying the warnings from on high, and having overcome the difficulties of a long journey, she came to the castle of Chinon in the country of Tours, and, having convinced King Charles that she was sent by God, she set out for the city of Orleans. In a few days, by a terrible onslaught, she inflicted a threefold defeat on the enemy, stormed their forts, and raised up her standard. Thence, after other deeds of war, in which the help of God appeared in wondrous manner, she led Charles to Rheims, that he might be anointed with the royal consecration. Nor did she judge that she should rest: but when she had learned from the heavenly messengers that, by God's permission, she would come into the power of the enemy, she accepted with a willing mind what must needs be done.
supernismonitisobtemperanssuperatislongi.la: Supérnis mónitis obtémperans, superátis longi itíneris difficultátibus, ad Castrum Cainonénse in agro Turónico pervénit, et, Cárolo regi facta fide se a Deo missam esse, in urbem Auréliam profécta est. Paucis diébus, terríbili ímpetus, tríplicem cladem hóstibus inflíxit, castélla expugnávit, suúmque sústulit vexíllum. Inde, post ália béllica facta, in quibus mirum in modum appáruit auxílium Dei, Rhemos Cárolum duxit, ut régia consecratióne inungerétur. Nec quiescéndum esse cénsuit: sed cum a cæléstibus núntiis accepísset, se, Deo permitténte, in hóstium potestátem esse ventúram, libénti ánimo, quæ fíeri necésse esset, suscépit.

ornaveruntfaciemtemplicoronisaureisunxer.en: They adorned the front of the temple with crowns of gold, they anointed the king, and going up rejoicing they said: God save the king.
ornaveruntfaciemtemplicoronisaureisunxer.la: Ornavérunt fáciem templi corónis áureis, unxérunt regem, et ascendéntes læti dixérunt: Vivat rex.

etfactestletitiamagnainpopulo.en: And there was very great gladness among the people.
etfactestletitiamagnainpopulo.la: Et facta est lætítia magna in pópulo.

inhymnisetconfessionibusbenedicebantdomi.en: With hymns and praises they blessed the Lord, who by the hand of a woman had wrought the victory.
inhymnisetconfessionibusbenedicebantdomi.la: In hymnis et confessiónibus benedicébant Dóminum, qui per manum féminæ fecit victóriam.

captaioannaincivitatecompendiethostibusp.en: Joan, taken at the city of Compiègne and sold for a price to the enemy, was soon brought to Rouen; and when she had been dragged there to trial, she was charged with very many accusations, save only as to the chastity of her life; but she bore all things patiently for Jesus. The case having been conducted by most corrupt judges, the innocent and gentle virgin was condemned to the penalty of burning. And so, refreshed with the holy Eucharist, which she had so long desired, with her eyes turned to the cross, repeating very often the name of Jesus, she flew up to heaven on the thirtieth day of May, not having yet completed the twentieth year of her age. The Roman Church, which she had ever loved and to which she had often appealed, under the Supreme Pontiff Callistus the Third took care that she should be cleared of every charge. As the nineteenth century drew to its close, Leo the Thirteenth permitted the cause of the Maid of Orleans to be introduced. Lastly, the Supreme Pontiff Pius the Tenth enrolled Joan of Arc in the number of the blessed, and Benedict the Fifteenth in the number of the holy Virgins.
captaioannaincivitatecompendiethostibusp.la: Capta Joánna in civitáte Compéndio, et hóstibus prétio trádita, Rothómagum mox ducta, cum ibi in jus rapta esset, quamplúrimis criminatiónibus, excépta morum castitáte, fuit obnóxia; sed ómnia pro Jesu patiénter tolerávit. Acta per corruptíssimos júdices causa, ínnocens et mitis virgo damnáta est pœna combustiónis. Igitur sacra Eucharístia, quam támdiu desideráverat, refécta, óculis ad crucem convérsis, nomen Jesu sæpíssime ingéminans, ad cælum evolávit die trigésima Maji, nondum expléto ætátis suæ anno vigésimo. Romána Ecclésia, quam semper diléxerat et ad quam sǽpius provocáverat, eam ab omni crímine vindicándam, Callísto tértio summo Pontífice, curávit. Vergénte in finem sǽculo undevicésimo, Leo décimus tértius Aurelianénsis puéllæ causam introdúci permísit. Postrémo Joánnam de Arc summus Póntifex Pius décimus in beatárum, Benedíctus vero décimus quintus in sanctárum Vírginum númerum rétulit.

puellameanolitimerequiegotecumsumdicitdo.en: My child, fear not, for I am with thee, saith the Lord:
puellameanolitimerequiegotecumsumdicitdo.la: Puélla mea, noli timére, quia ego tecum sum, dicit Dóminus:

sitransierisperignemflammanonnocebitanim.en: If thou pass through fire, the flame shall not hurt thy soul, and I will glorify it.
sitransierisperignemflammanonnocebitanim.la: Si transíeris per ignem, flamma non nocébit ánimæ tuæ, et ego glorificábo eam.

mittamtibiangelummeumetinmedioflammelaud.en: I will send thee my Angel, and in the midst of the flame thou shalt praise my name.
mittamtibiangelummeumetinmedioflammelaud.la: Mittam tibi Angelum meum, et in médio flammæ laudábis nomen meum.

inillotemporedixitiesusdiscipulissuissiq.en: At that time, Jesus said unto His disciples: If any man will come after Me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow Me. And so on.
inillotemporedixitiesusdiscipulissuissiq.la: In illo témpore: Dixit Jesus discípulis suis: Si quis vult post me veníre, ábneget semetípsum, et tollat crucem suam, et sequátur me. Et réliqua.

obeatumdamnumetiacturafelixditescerenosd.en: O blessed loss and happy forfeit! The Lord willed that we should be enriched by the loss of soul and body, and he exhorteth us to be like unto him: for he, being in the form of God, and made humble and obedient even unto death, received the sovereignty of all power which is in God. He is therefore to be followed with the cross taken up, and to be accompanied in his passion, if not in lot, yet in will. For what doth it profit to have seized the world, and with the whole lordship of earthly power to brood over the riches of the world, if the soul must be lost and the loss of life be undergone?
obeatumdamnumetiacturafelixditescerenosd.la: O beátum damnum et jactúra felix! ditéscere nos Dóminus detriménto ánimæ et córporis vóluit, et esse sui símiles hortátur: quia ipse in figúra Dei constitútus, usque ad mortem húmilis et obédiens factus, principátum potestátis totíus, quæ in Deo est, accépit. Sequéndus ígitur est cruce assúmpta, et passionis suæ si non sorte, áttamen voluntáte comitándus est. Quid enim prodest occupásse mundum, et toto terrénæ potestátis dominátu ópibus sǽculi incubáre, si perdénda ánima et suscipiéndum vitæ detriméntum est?

exaudiatdominusorationempuellesuequaorav.en: May the Lord hear the prayer of his maiden, which she prayed for us, that God may be reconciled with us:
exaudiatdominusorationempuellesuequaorav.la: Exaúdiat Dóminus oratiónem puéllæ suæ, qua orávit pro nobis, ut reconciliétur nobíscum Deus:

facdomineutmaneatnomensanctumtuuminterra.en: Grant, O Lord, that thy holy Name may abide in our land.
facdomineutmaneatnomensanctumtuuminterra.la: Fac, Dómine, ut máneat Nomen sanctum tuum in terra nostra.

respicedomineetvisitapopulumtuumnedefici.en: Look down, O Lord, and visit thy people, lest the Victim and the Sacrifice fail therein.
respicedomineetvisitapopulumtuumnedefici.la: Réspice, Dómine, et vísita pópulum tuum, ne defíciat in eo Hóstia et Sacrifícium.

queautemcommutatioproanimacumfueritamiss.en: But what exchange shall be sought for the soul, when it hath been lost? For Christ shall come with the Angels, rendering to each as they shall deserve. What shall we offer for life? Treasures, I suppose, of earthly riches laid up for future traffic, the ambitious titles of dignities and of fame, or the old images of an inherited nobility? All these must be denied, that we may abound in better things: and Christ must be followed with contempt of all things, and the eternity of spiritual things must be purchased at the loss of earthly things.
queautemcommutatioproanimacumfueritamiss.la: Quæ autem commutátio pro ánima, cum fúerit amíssa, quærétur? cum Angelis enim Christus áderit, reddens síngulis ut merebúntur. Quid offerémus ad vitam? Præparátos credo terrenárum opum futúris commérciis thesáuros, ambitiósos dignitátum, famǽque títulos, aut véteres delegátæ nobilitátis imágines? Negánda sunt hæc ómnia, ut melióribus abundémus: et contémptu universórum Christus sequéndus est, et ætérnitas spirituálium, terrenórum est damno comparánda.

domineprevenistieaminbenedictionibusdulc.en: O Lord, thou hast prevented her with blessings of sweetness:
domineprevenistieaminbenedictionibusdulc.la: Dómine, prævenísti eam in benedictiónibus dulcédinis:

quiminasiudicumnontimuitnecterrenedignit.en: Who feared not for the threats of judges, nor sought to be great with the glory of this world, but pressed on unto the kingdom of heaven.
quiminasiudicumnontimuitnecterrenedignit.la: Qui minas judícum non tímuit, nec terrénæ dignitátis glóriam quæsívit, sed ad cæléstia regna pervénit.

graveonusinfirmatihumaneimposueratutcums.en: He had laid a heavy burden upon human infirmity, that, whereas men had begun to have the sense of life from the love of living, they should lose the fruit of that life which, being present, flattered their bodies: and should deny themselves, that is, should be unwilling to be that which they had begun to be; since they had had the beginning of this sense from the affection of the will. There was need therefore of the authority of a true and manifest example, that, against the force and sense of judgment, the loss of present things might become desirable, for a gain thereafter not doubtful of things to come.
