Therefore, after he had admonished that the cross must be taken up, and the soul be lost, and the eternity of life be gained in exchange for the loss of the world, turning to the disciples he saith: That there should be some of these who should not taste death, till they should behold the Son of man in the glory of his kingdom.
graveonusinfirmatihumaneimposueratutcums.la: Grave onus infirmáti humánæ imposúerat, ut cum sensum vitæ hómines ex vivéndi afféctu habére cœpíssent, fructum ejus, qui præsens corpóribus blandiebátur, amitterent: negaréntque se sibi, id est, quod esse cœpíssent, esse se nollent; cum sensus hujus exórdium ex afféctu voluntátis habuíssent. Opus ergo erat veri ac manifésti exémpli auctoritáte, ut contra vim sensúmque judícii, optábile fíeret præséntium damnum, lúcro deínceps non ambíguo futurórum. Igitur postquam et tolléndam crucem, et perdéndam ánimam, et damno mundi commutándam vitæ æternitátem monúerat, convérsus ad discípulos, ait: Quosdam ex his futúros, qui gustatúri mortem non essent, donec Fílium hóminis in regni sui glória contueréntur.

hostiumvictrixproperantecursu.en: Victress over the foe, with hastening course,

carolumadsanctamcomitarisedem.en: Thou dost accompany Charles to the holy temple,

uttriumphantemsacraritesignet.en: That the sacred rites may duly seal him in his triumph.

gaudiofundenslacrimasioanna.en: Shedding tears for joy, O Joan,

principiplaudisdominorependis.en: Thou applaudest the prince: to the Lord thou payest

debitasgratesretinesquedextra.en: The thanks that are due, and holdest in thy right hand

erigenslongapopulumruina.en: Raising up the people from long ruin,

mirafecistigenerosavirgo.en: Thou hast done wonders, O noble virgin:

iuretenostrepatrieparentem.en: Rightly thee the mother of our fatherland

sedmanetmaiormeliorquemerces.en: But a greater and better reward remaineth:

tenovusposcitlaborettriumphus.en: A new labour and a new triumph claim thee:
tenovusposcitlaborettriumphus.la: Te novus poscit labor et triúmphus:

tedeusmittensdabitipsevires.en: God, who sendeth thee, shall himself give strength
tedeusmittensdabitipsevires.la: Te Deus mittens, dabit ipse vires

quideditpressopopulosalutem.en: Who gave salvation to the oppressed people,

laudetersanctumdominumcolamus.en: With praise let us worship the thrice-holy Lord,

semperuttantemeritispatrone.en: That ever, by the merits of so great a patroness,

magnestglorieiusinsalutarituo.en: His glory is great in thy salvation.
magnestglorieiusinsalutarituo.la: Magna est glória ejus in salutári tuo.

gloriametmagnumdecoremimponessupereum.en: Honour and great majesty shalt Thou lay upon him.
gloriametmagnumdecoremimponessupereum.la: Glóriam et magnum decórem impónes super eum.

stansbeataioannainmedioflammeoculisadcru.en: Blessed Joan, standing * in the midst of the flame, with her eyes turned to the cross, thus prayed, saying: Lord Jesus, receive my spirit; lay not † this sin to their charge.
stansbeataioannainmedioflammeoculisadcru.la: Stans beáta Joánna * in médio flammæ, óculis ad crucem convérsis, sic orábat, dicens: Dómine Jesu, áccipe spíritum meum; ne státuas † illis hoc peccátum.

tacentemmesustinebuntetloquentemmerespic.en: They shall wait for me when I hold my peace, and they shall look upon me when I speak, and if I talk much, they shall lay their hands on their mouths.
tacentemmesustinebuntetloquentemmerespic.la: Tacéntem me sustinébunt, et loquéntem me respícient, et sermocinánte me plura, manus ori suo impónent.

habeboperhancimmortalitatemetmemoriamete.en: By her I shall have immortality, and shall leave behind me an everlasting memory to them that come after me.
habeboperhancimmortalitatemetmemoriamete.la: Habébo, per hanc, immortalitátem, et memóriam ætérnam his, qui post me futúri sunt, relínquam.

ioannasponsachristitutrixetcustospatriee.en: Joan, * spouse of Christ, protectress and guardian of our country, be thou to thy servants an impregnable wall by thy constant † intercessions.
ioannasponsachristitutrixetcustospatriee.la: Joánna, * sponsa Christi, tutrix et custos pátriæ, esto tuis fámulis murus inexpugnábilis assíduis † suffrágiis.

clarisconiubilagallialaudibus.en: Rejoice, O Gaul, with glorious praises,

leterisbenedictipatrisossibus.en: Be glad in the bones of Father Benedict:

felixquegremioconditaproprio.en: Happy art thou, who, laid up in thine own bosom,

mirisitaliafulseratactibus.en: Italy had shone with his wondrous deeds;

gallosirradiatcorporemortuus.en: Dead, he enlighteneth the Gauls with his body;

signisadtumulumcrebriusemicat.en: At his tomb he shineth forth with frequent signs,

hincvatumveterumfactaresuscitat.en: Hence he reneweth the deeds of the prophets of old,

mortiquodlibuitmortuusimperat.en: Dead, he commandeth death as he pleaseth,

extinctumproprisossibusexcitat.en: He raiseth up the dead by his own bones:

iamceloresidensopateroptime.en: Now dwelling in heaven, O best of Fathers,
iamceloresidensopateroptime.la: Jam cælo résidens, o Pater óptime,

divinisfamulosimbueregulis.en: Imbue thy servants with the divine rules,

angustumperiterscanderelargiens.en: And, granting them to climb by the narrow way,

tuquisedepoliconspicisomnia.en: Thou who from the throne of heaven beholdest all things,
tuquisedepoliconspicisomnia.la: Tu, qui sede poli cónspicis ómnia,

psallentumplacidesuscipecantica.en: Graciously receive the songs of them that sing psalms,

votisvoceprecantia.en: Praying with vows and with voice.

exsultetomniumturbafideliumprogloriaalmi.en: Let all the throng * of the faithful exult for the glory of our gracious Father Benedict; let the companies of monks above all rejoice, celebrating his Translation on earth, in whose fellowship the Saints rejoice together in heaven.
exsultetomniumturbafideliumprogloriaalmi.la: Exsúltet ómnium * turba fidélium pro glória almi Patris Benedícti; læténtur præcípue catérvæ monachórum, celebrántes ejus Translatiónem in terris, de cujus societáte sancti congáudent in cælis.

mariergounxitpedesiesuetextersitcapillis.en: Mary therefore * anointed the feet of Jesus, and wiped them with her hair; and the house was filled with the odour of the ointment.
mariergounxitpedesiesuetextersitcapillis.la: María ergo * unxit pedes Jesu et extérsit capíllis suis et domus impléta est ex odóre unguénti. Ps. 109

quidmolestiestishuicmulieriopusenimbonum.en: Why do you trouble * this woman? for she hath wrought a good work upon me.
quidmolestiestishuicmulieriopusenimbonum.la: Quid molésti estis * huic muliéri opus enim bonum operáta est in me. Ps. 112

mittenshecmulierincorpusmeumhocunguentum.en: This woman, in pouring * this ointment upon my body, hath done it for my burial.
mittenshecmulierincorpusmeumhocunguentum.la: Mittens haec múlier * in corpus meum hoc unguéntum ad sepeliéndum me fecit Ps. 121

nominabiturquodfecitmulieristaingenerati.en: It shall be told * what this woman hath done, in the generation of all ages.
nominabiturquodfecitmulieristaingenerati.la: Nominabitur * quod fecit múlier ista in generatióne ómnium seculórum Ps. 126

abipsafaucetartari.en: From the very jaws of hell

reditadvitelimina.en: Returneth to the threshold of life.

egracurritadmedicum.en: Sick, she runneth to the physician,

verbocuraturmedici.en: Is healed by the word of the physician.

contriticordisunctio.en: The anointing of a contrite heart,

etpietatisactio.en: And the deed of loving devotion

reamsolvitavitio.en: Releaseth the guilty woman from vice.

iesumvidetabinferis.en: From the dead she seeth Jesus;

queplusardebatceteris.en: Who burned more than the others.

unideositgloria.en: To the one God be glory,

peccantiumquicrimina.en: Who forgiveth the crimes of sinners,

indiebusillismulierqueeratincivitatepecc.en: In those days, * a woman that was in the city, a sinner, when she knew that Jesus sat at meat in the house of Simon the leper, brought an alabaster box of ointment: and standing behind at the feet of the Lord Jesus, she began to wash his feet with tears, and wiped them with the hairs of her head: and kissed his feet, and anointed them with the ointment.
indiebusillismulierqueeratincivitatepecc.la: In diébus illis, * múlier quæ erat in civitáte peccátrix, ut cognóvit quod Jesus accúbuit in domo Simónis leprósi, áttulit alabástrum unguénti: et stans retro secus pedes Dómini Jesu, lácrimis cœpit rigáre pedes éjus, et capíllis cápitis sui tergébat: et osculabátur pedes éjus, et unguénto ungébat.

dumfleremadmonumentumvididominummeumalle.en: While I wept * at the sepulchre, I saw my Lord, alleluia.
dumfleremadmonumentumvididominummeumalle.la: Dum flerem * ad monuméntum vidi dóminum meum allelúja.

venitmarianuntiansdiscipulisquiavididomi.en: Mary came * telling the disciples: I have seen the Lord, alleluia.
venitmarianuntiansdiscipulisquiavididomi.la: Venit María * núntians discípulis quia vidi dóminum, allelúja.

inlectulomeopernoctesquesiviquemdiligita.en: In my bed by night I sought him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, and found him not. I will rise, and will go about the city: in the streets and the broad ways I will seek him whom my soul loveth.
inlectulomeopernoctesquesiviquemdiligita.la: In léctulo meo per noctes quæsívi quem díligit ánima mea: quæsívi illum, et non invéni. Surgam, et circuíbo civitátem: per vicos et platéas quæram quem díligit ánima mea.

numquemdiligitanimameavidistispaululumcu.en: Have you seen him whom my soul loveth? When I had a little passed by them, I found him whom my soul loveth: I held him, and I will not let him go.
numquemdiligitanimameavidistispaululumcu.la: Num quem díligit ánima mea vidístis? Páululum cum pertransíssem eos, invéni quem díligit ánima mea: ténui eum, nec dimíttam.

optimampartemelegitsibimaria.en: Mary hath chosen for herself the best part,

quenonaufereturabeaineternum.en: Which shall not be taken away from her for ever.
quenonaufereturabeaineternum.la: Quae non auferétur ab ea in aetérnum

ponemeutsignaculumsupercortuumutsignacul.en: Put me as a seal upon thy heart, as a seal upon thy arm, for love is strong as death, jealousy as hard as hell, the lamps thereof are fire and flames.
ponemeutsignaculumsupercortuumutsignacul.la: Pone me ut signáculum super cor tuum, ut signáculum super bráchium tuum, quia fortis est ut mors diléctio, dura sicut inférnus æmulátio: lámpades ejus lámpades ignis atque flammárum.

commemoratiossabdonetsennenmartyrum.en: Commemoration of Ss. Abdon and Sennen, Martyrs
commemoratiossabdonetsennenmartyrum.la: Commemoratio SS. Abdon et Sennen Martyrum

deusquisanctistuisabdonetsennenadhancglo.en: O God, Who didst give unto thy saints Abdon and Sennen the abundant grace whereby to attain unto this glory, Grant unto thy servants the remission of all their sins, that, with the pleading of the worthy deeds of thy Saints, they may worthily be delivered from all things hurtful.
deusquisanctistuisabdonetsennenadhancglo.la: Deus, qui sanctis tuis Abdon et Sennen ad hanc glóriam veniéndi copiósum munus grátiæ contulísti: da fámulis tuis suórum véniam peccatórum; ut, Sanctórum tuórum intercedéntibus méritis, ab ómnibus mereántur adversitátibus liberári.

benedictatuadeotuoquoniaminomnigentequea.en: Blessed art thou * by thy God, for in every nation which shall hear thy name, the God of Israel shall be magnified on occasion of thee.
benedictatuadeotuoquoniaminomnigentequea.la: Benedícta tu * a Deo tuo, quóniam in omni gente, quæ audíerit nomen tuum, magnificábitur super te Deus Isræl. Ps. 109

dominuselegitteutsiseietfaciatteinlaudem.en: The Lord hath chosen thee, * that thou mayest be his, and that he may make thee unto his praise, and name, and glory.
dominuselegitteutsiseietfaciatteinlaudem.la: Dominus elégit te, * ut sis ei, et fáciat te in laudem, et nomen, et glóriam suam. Ps. 112

eriscoronaglorieinmanudominietdiademareg.en: Thou shalt be a crown of glory * in the hand of the Lord, and a royal diadem in the hand of thy God, because the Lord hath been well pleased with thee.
eriscoronaglorieinmanudominietdiademareg.la: Eris coróna glóriæ * in manu Dómini, et diadéma regni in manu Dei tui, quia complácuit Dómino in te. Ps. 121

dominusfacietettecummisericordiametverit.en: The Lord also will shew unto thee * mercy and truth, because thou hast shewn grace and faith.
dominusfacietettecummisericordiametverit.la: Dominus fáciet et tecum * misericórdiam et veritátem, quia ostendísti grátiam et fidem. Ps. 126

erumpetquasimanelumentuumetanteibitfacie.en: Thy light shall break forth * as the morning, and thy justice shall go before thy face, and the glory of the Lord shall gather thee up.
erumpetquasimanelumentuumetanteibitfacie.la: Erúmpet quasi mane * lumen tuum, et anteíbit fáciem tuam justítia tua, et glória Dómini cólliget te.

animameexsultabitindomino.en: My soul * shall rejoice in the Lord.

etdelectabitursupersalutarisuo.en: And shall be delighted in his salvation.

nomendecusqueconcinant.en: Let them sing the name and the glory

quisanctadiviparvuli.en: Who the holy gifts of the divine Little One

sponsipremensvestigia.en: Pressing the footsteps of her Spouse.

afflataiesunumine.en: Inspired by the power of Jesus,

secretapanditgratie.en: She discloseth the secrets of grace;

magistramundosimplices.en: A teacher to the world, the simple

infantiumdocetvias.en: Ways of little children she teacheth.

virtutisipsaflosculos.en: With the little flowers of her virtue

olentsacratalimina.en: The hallowed thresholds themselves are fragrant,

quecastavirutangelus.en: Which she, chaste as an angel

necseptamagnosclaudere.en: Nor can the cloister walls enclose the great

iesutibisitgloria.en: O Jesu, glory be to thee,

quiterevelasparvulis.en: Who revealest thyself to little ones,

cumpatreetalmospiritu.en: With the Father and the loving Spirit,

egoautemindominogaudebo.en: But I will rejoice in the Lord.

etexsultaboindeoiesumeo.en: And I will joy in God my Jesus.
etexsultaboindeoiesumeo.la: Et exsultábo in Deo Jesu meo.

egodominussponsabotemihiinsempiternumets.en: I the Lord * will espouse thee to me for ever; and I will espouse thee to me in justice and judgment, and in mercy and in commiserations; and I will espouse thee to me in faith.
egodominussponsabotemihiinsempiternumets.la: Ego Dóminus * sponsábo te mihi in sempitérnum; et sponsábo te mihi in iustítia et iudício, et in misericórdia et miseratiónibus; et sponsábo te mihi in fide.

hecdicitdominusecceegodeclinabosupereamq.en: Thus saith the Lord: Behold I will bring upon her as it were a river of peace, and as an overflowing torrent the glory of the Gentiles, which you shall suck: † you shall be carried at the breasts, * and upon the knees they shall caress you.
hecdicitdominusecceegodeclinabosupereamq.la: Hæc dicit Dóminus: Ecce ego declinábo super eam quasi flúvium pacis, et quasi torréntem inundántem glóriam géntium, quam sugétis: † ad úbera portabímini, * et super génua blandiéntur vobis.

exsultabetletabordomineinmisericordiatua.en: I will be glad and rejoice, O Lord, * In thy mercy.
exsultabetletabordomineinmisericordiatua.la: Exsultábo et lætábor, Dómine, * In misericórdia tua.

quoniamrespexithumilitatemmeam.en: Because he hath regarded my lowliness.

apostolorumetmartyrum.en: With the crown of Apostles and of Martyrs

optansamorisvictima.en: Longing, as a victim of love,

exigneadurimystico.en: To be consumed by the mystic fire,

sponsumprecaturultimas.en: She prayeth her Spouse that the last

hecingemenstediligo.en: Sighing these words: I love thee!

fruensabarcesiderum.en: Enjoying, from the citadel of the stars,

quaslargiterpromiseras.en: The roses which thou didst bountifully promise,

tucorderexmitissime.en: O King, most meek of heart,

quiparvulisregnumparas.en: Who preparest the kingdom for little ones,

noshancsecutosingredi.en: Grant that we, following her, may enter

deopatrietfilio.en: To God the Father and the Son,

erittibidominusinlucemsempiternam.en: The Lord shall be unto thee for an everlasting light.
erittibidominusinlucemsempiternam.la: Erit tibi Dóminus in lucem sempitérnam.

etdeustuusingloriamtuam.en: And thy God for thy glory.
etdeustuusingloriamtuam.la: Et Deus tuus in glóriam tuam.

requiemtibidabitdominussemperetimplebits.en: The Lord will give thee rest * continually, and will fill thy soul with brightness; and thou shalt be like a watered garden, and like a fountain of waters whose waters shall not fail.
requiemtibidabitdominussemperetimplebits.la: Requiem tibi dabit * Dóminus semper, et implébit splendóribus ánimam tuam; et eris quasi hortus irríguus, et sicut fons aquárum, cujus non defícient aquæ.

quomodosicuimaterblandiaturitegoconsolab.en: As one whom the mother caresseth, † so will I comfort you, * and you shall be comforted in Jerusalem.
quomodosicuimaterblandiaturitegoconsolab.la: Quómodo si cui mater blandiátur, † ita ego consolábor vos, * et in Jerúsalem consolabímini.

videbitisetgaudebitcorvestrumetossavestr.en: You shall see, and your heart shall rejoice, † and your bones shall flourish like an herb, * and the hand of the Lord shall be known to his servants, and he shall be angry with his enemies.
videbitisetgaudebitcorvestrumetossavestr.la: Vidébitis, et gaudébit cor vestrum, † et ossa vestra quasi herba germinábunt * et cognoscétur manus Dómini servis ejus, et indignábitur inimícis suis.

laudatedominumquiabonusdominus.en: Praise ye the Lord, for the Lord is good.

psallitenominieiusquoniamsuave.en: Sing ye to his name, for it is sweet.

lucedivinarutilantisaule.en: In the divine light of the shining court

sedibusvirgofruerissecundans.en: Thou enjoyest its seats, O virgin; favouring

votapromissorefovesprecantes.en: Our prayers, thou refreshest them that pray with the promised

sintrosenobisfideisuperne.en: Let the roses be to us of heavenly faith

lumenaffulgenscolumenquerebus.en: The shining light, and, as a stay in our affairs,

spesinadversisetamorisalmi.en: Hope in adversities, and of gracious love
spesinadversisetamorisalmi.la: Spes in advérsis, et amóris almi

sintrosenobistuusillefidens.en: Let the roses be to us that trusting
sintrosenobistuusillefidens.la: Sint rosæ nobis tuus ille fidens

candorinfantisdominopaterno.en: Candour of thine as a child toward the Lord, who with fatherly

grataquiprebetvelacerbanostre.en: Hand giveth things pleasant or bitter to our
grataquiprebetvelacerbanostre.la: Grata qui præbet vel acérba nostræ

prestethocnobisdeitasbeata.en: May the blessed Godhead grant us this,

patrisacnatipariterquesancti.en: Of the Father, and the Son, and likewise of the Holy

spirituscuiusreboatinomni.en: Spirit, whose glory resoundeth in all

manusdominiconfortavitte.en: The hand of the Lord hath strengthened thee.

etideerisbenedictaineternum.en: And therefore thou shalt be blessed for ever.
etideerisbenedictaineternum.la: Et ídeo eris benedícta in ætérnum.

benedictusdominusquiahodienomentuumitama.en: Blessed be the Lord, * for this day he hath so magnified thy name, that thy praise shall not depart out of the mouth of men, who shall be mindful of the power of the Lord for ever.
benedictusdominusquiahodienomentuumitama.la: Benedíctus Dóminus, * quia hódie nomen tuum ita magnificávit, ut non recédat laus tua de ore hóminum, qui mémores fúerint virtútis Dómini in ætérnum.

extremummorbumpatientissimetolerantisubi.en: As she was bearing her last illness most patiently, the thought of the divine judgment suddenly struck such fear into her that, with trembling and weeping, clasping the Crucifix, she besought mercy for herself: but soon the consolations of God gladdened her soul. And so, as a victim of charity made perfect, she flew away to her Spouse on the seventeenth day of October, being forty-three years of age. Her heavenly glory was confirmed by miracles; and these having been duly proved, the Sovereign Pontiff Pius the Ninth, to the great rejoicing of the devout, enrolled her in the company of the blessed Virgins on the eighteenth of September in the year one thousand eight hundred and sixty-four.
extremummorbumpatientissimetolerantisubi.la: Extremum morbum patientissime toleranti subito divini iudicii cogitatio tantum iniecit metum, ut cum tremore ac fletu Crucifixum stringens misericordiam sibi precaretur: sed mox consolationes Dei lætificaverunt animam eius. Igitur tamquam consummata charitatis victima, die decima septima Octobris ad sponsum evolavit, annos nata tres et quadraginta. Cælestem eius gloriam miracula confirmaverunt, quibus rite probatis, eam Pius Nonus Pontifex Maximus magna piorum gratulatione quartodecimo Kalendas Octobris Anni Millesimi octingentesimi sexagesimi quarti beatarum Virginum cætum inscripsit.

laudemuslaudaveruntinterranostretlaudamu.en: Let us praise: * they have praised in our land, and we praise the Mother of God above all.
laudemuslaudaveruntinterranostretlaudamu.la: Laudemus * laudaverunt in terra nostra, et laudamus super Dei Genitrix.

quasiarcusrefulgensinternebulasglorie.en: As the rainbow giving light in the clouds of glory.
quasiarcusrefulgensinternebulasglorie.la: Quasi arcus refúlgens inter nébulas glóriæ.

etquasiflosrosarumindiebusvernis.en: And as the flower of roses in the days of the spring.
etquasiflosrosarumindiebusvernis.la: Et quasi flos rosárum in diébus vernis.

eccevenitrexoccurramusobviamsalvatorinos.en: Behold, the King cometh, * Let us go forth to meet our Saviour.
eccevenitrexoccurramusobviamsalvatorinos.la: Ecce venit Rex, * Occurrámus óbviam Salvatóri nostro.

excitadominepotentiamtuametveniutsalvosf.en: Stir up thy might, O Lord, and come to save us. * Thou who art to reign over the people of Israel.
excitadominepotentiamtuametveniutsalvosf.la: Excita, Dómine, poténtiam tuam, et veni: ut salvos fácias nos. * Qui regnatúrus es in pópulo Israël.

auditeverbumdominigentesetannuntiateillu.en: Hear the word of the Lord, O ye nations, and declare it in the ends of the earth, and in the islands that are afar off, say:
auditeverbumdominigentesetannuntiateillu.la: Audíte verbum Dómini, gentes, et annuntiáte illud in fínibus terræ, et in ínsulis, quæ procul sunt dícite:

eccevirgoconcipietetparietfiliumdicitdom.en: Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, saith the Lord, and his name shall be called
eccevirgoconcipietetparietfiliumdicitdom.la: Ecce virgo concípiet, et páriet fílium, dicit Dóminus, et vocábitur nomen ejus,

mementonostridomineinbeneplacitopopulitu.en: Remember us, O Lord, with the favour that Thou showest unto thy people; O visit us with thy salvation.
mementonostridomineinbeneplacitopopulitu.la: Meménto nostri, Dómine, in beneplácito pópuli tui, vísita nos in salutári tuo:

egoveniamdicitdominusetsanabocontritione.en: I will come, saith the Lord, and I will heal the bruise of my people.
egoveniamdicitdominusetsanabocontritione.la: Ego véniam, dicit Dóminus, et sanábo contritiónem pópuli mei.

confusioautemmarisetfluctuumnecdumnovexo.en: But the confusion of the sea and of the waves hath not yet newly arisen. But since many things foretold are already fulfilled, there is no doubt that the few which remain will also follow: for the showing forth of things past is the certainty of things to come.
confusioautemmarisetfluctuumnecdumnovexo.la: Confúsio autem maris et flúctuum necdum nova exórta est. Sed cum multa prænuntiáta jam compléta sint, dúbium non est quin sequántur étiam pauca, quæ restant: quia sequéntium rerum certitúdo est præteritárum exhibítio.

confortaminimanusfatigateetgenuadissolut.en: Be strengthened, ye weary hands, and ye feeble knees be made strong: ye that are of a fearful heart, take courage; fear me, saith the Lord, for I come
confortaminimanusfatigateetgenuadissolut.la: Confortámini manus fatigátæ, et génua dissolúta roborámini: qui pusíllo ánimo estis mente convaléscite, me timéte, dicit Dóminus, quia vénio,

dirumpereiugumcaptivitatisvestre.en: To break the yoke of your captivity.

civitasierusalemnoliflerequicitovenietsa.en: O city of Jerusalem, weep not, for thy salvation shall come speedily.
civitasierusalemnoliflerequicitovenietsa.la: Cívitas Jerúsalem, noli flere, qui cito véniet salus tua.

ierusalemrespiceadorientemetvidealleluia.en: O Jerusalem, * look towards the East, and see, alleluia.
ierusalemrespiceadorientemetvidealleluia.la: Jerúsalem, * réspice ad Oriéntem, et vide, allelúia.

erumpantmontesiucunditatemetcollesiustit.en: Let the mountains break forth * into joy, and the hills into justice, for the Lord, the light of the world, cometh with power.
erumpantmontesiucunditatemetcollesiustit.la: Erúmpant montes * jucunditátem, et colles justítiam, quia lux mundi Dóminus cum poténtia venit.

proptersionnontardabodonecegrediaturutsp.en: For Sion's sake * I will not tarry, till her Just One come forth as brightness.
proptersionnontardabodonecegrediaturutsp.la: Propter Sion * non tardábo, donec egrediátur ut splendor justus ejus.

prophetepredicaveruntnascisalvatoremdevi.en: The Prophets foretold * that the Saviour should be born of the Virgin Mary.
prophetepredicaveruntnascisalvatoremdevi.la: Prophétæ prædicavérunt * nasci Salvatórem de Vírgine María.

spiritusdominisupermeevangelizarepauperi.en: The Spirit * of the Lord is upon me: he hath sent me to preach the gospel to the poor.
spiritusdominisupermeevangelizarepauperi.la: Spíritus * Dómini super me, evangelizáre paupéribus misit me.

lexpermoysendatestgratietveritasperiesum.en: The law was given by Moses, * but grace and truth came by Jesus Christ.
lexpermoysendatestgratietveritasperiesum.la: Lex per Móysen data est; * grátia et véritas per Jesum Christum facta est.

annuntiatepopulisetdiciteeccedeussalvato.en: Tell it out among the people, * and say: Behold, God, our Saviour cometh.
annuntiatepopulisetdiciteeccedeussalvato.la: Annuntiáte * pópulis, et dícite: Ecce, Deus Salvátor noster véniet.

constantesestotevidebitisauxiliumdominis.en: Be ye steadfast, * and you shall see the help of the Lord upon you.
constantesestotevidebitisauxiliumdominis.la: Constántes estóte, * vidébitis auxílium Dómini super vos.

ponentdominogloriametlaudemeiusininsulis.en: They shall give glory * to the Lord, and shall declare his praise in the islands; for behold, he will come, and will not tarry.
ponentdominogloriametlaudemeiusininsulis.la: Ponent Dómino * glóriam, et laudem ejus in ínsulis nuntiábunt, quia ecce véniet, et non tardábit.

venidomineetnolitardarerelaxafacinoraple.en: Come, O Lord, * and tarry not: forgive the misdeeds of thy people Israel.
venidomineetnolitardarerelaxafacinoraple.la: Veni, Dómine, * et noli tardáre: reláxa facínora plebi tuæ Israël.

deusalibanovenietetsplendoreiussicutlume.en: God shall come from Libanus, * and his brightness shall be as the light.
deusalibanovenietetsplendoreiussicutlume.la: Deus a Líbano véniet, * et splendor ejus sicut lumen erit.

egoautemaddominumaspiciametexspectabodeu.en: But I * will look towards the Lord, and will wait for God my Saviour.
egoautemaddominumaspiciametexspectabodeu.la: Ego autem * ad Dóminum aspíciam, et exspectábo Deum, Salvatórem meum.

roratecelidesuperetnubespluantiustumaper.en: Drop down dew, ye heavens, from above, * and let the clouds rain the Just One: let the earth be opened, and bud forth a Saviour.
roratecelidesuperetnubespluantiustumaper.la: Roráte coeli désuper, * et nubes pluant Justum : aperiátur terra, et gérminet Salvatórem.

consurgeconsurgeinduerefortitudinembrach.en: Arise, arise, * put on strength, O arm of the Lord.
consurgeconsurgeinduerefortitudinembrach.la: Consúrge, consúrge: * indúere fortitúdinem bráchium Dómini.

gaudeteindominosemperiterumdicogaudetedo.en: Rejoice in the Lord always: * again I say, rejoice: for the Lord is nigh; be nothing solicitous.
gaudeteindominosemperiterumdicogaudetedo.la: Gaudéte in Dómino semper: * íterum dico gaudéte: Dóminus enim prope est, nihil sollíciti sitis.

exspectetursicutpluvieloquiumdominietdes.en: Let the word of the Lord be awaited as the rain, * and let our God come down upon us as the dew.
exspectetursicutpluvieloquiumdominietdes.la: Exspectétur sicut plúvia * elóquium Dómini: et descéndat, sicut ros, super nos Deus noster.

dabiteidominussedemdavidpatriseiusetregn.en: The Lord shall give unto him * the throne of David his father, and he shall reign for ever.
dabiteidominussedemdavidpatriseiusetregn.la: Dabit ei Dóminus * sedem David patris ejus, et regnábit in ætérnum.

virgoisrelrevertereadcivitatestuasusqueq.en: O virgin of Israel, return to thy cities: how long wilt thou turn away in sorrow?
virgoisrelrevertereadcivitatestuasusqueq.la: Virgo Israël, revértere ad civitátes tuas, usquequo dolens avertéris?

generabisdominumsalvatoremoblationemnova.en: Thou shalt bring forth the Lord, the Saviour, a new offering upon the earth: * Men shall walk unto salvation.
generabisdominumsalvatoremoblationemnova.la: Generábis Dóminum Salvatórem, oblatiónem novam in terra: * Ambulábunt hómines in salvatiónem.

incharitateperpetuadilexiteideoattraxite.en: I have loved thee with an everlasting love: therefore have I drawn thee, taking pity on thee.
incharitateperpetuadilexiteideoattraxite.la: In charitáte perpétua diléxi te: ídeo attráxi te míserans.

generabisdominumsalvatoremoblationemnova.en: Thou shalt bring forth the Lord, the Saviour, a new offering upon the earth.
generabisdominumsalvatoremoblationemnova.la: Generábis Dóminum Salvatórem, oblatiónem novam in terra.

diesdominisicutfurinnocteitavenietetvose.en: The day of the Lord, as a thief * in the night, so shall come: and be ye ready, for at what hour you think not, the Son of man will come.
diesdominisicutfurinnocteitavenietetvose.la: Dies Dómini sicut fur * in nocte ita véniet, et vos estóte paráti, quia qua hora non putátis, Fílius hóminis véniet.

ecceadvenitdominatordeusetregnuminmanuei.en: Behold, there cometh * the Lord the Ruler, and the kingdom is in his hand, and power, and dominion for ever, alleluia.
ecceadvenitdominatordeusetregnuminmanuei.la: Ecce advénit * Dominátor Deus, et regnum in manu ejus, et potéstas, et impérium in ætérnum, allelúia. Ps. 20, 21

natodominoangelorumchoruscanebatdicensgl.en: When the Lord was born, * the choir of Angels sang, saying: Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace to men of good will.
natodominoangelorumchoruscanebatdicensgl.la: Nato Dómino, * Angelórum chorus canébat, dicens: Glória in excélsis Deo, et in terra pax homínibus bonæ voluntátis. Ps. 24, 25

natusestnobishodiesalvatorquiestchristus.en: Unto us is born * this day a Saviour, who is Christ the Lord, in the city of David.
natusestnobishodiesalvatorquiestchristus.la: Natus est nobis * hódie Salvátor, qui est Christus Dóminus, in civitáte David. Ps. 26, 27

virgoverboconcepitvirgopermansitvirgopep.en: A Virgin conceived by the Word, * a Virgin she remained, a Virgin she brought forth the King of all kings.
virgoverboconcepitvirgopermansitvirgopep.la: Virgo Verbo concépit, * Virgo permánsit, Virgo péperit Regem ómnium regum. Ps. 28, 29

beatusventerquiteportavitchristeetbeatau.en: Blessed is the womb * that bore thee, O Christ, and blessed are the paps that gave suck to thee, the Lord and Saviour of the world, alleluia.
beatusventerquiteportavitchristeetbeatau.la: Beátus venter, * qui te portávit, Christe, et beáta úbera quæ te lactavérunt Dóminum, et Salvatórem mundi, allelúia. Ps. 30, 31

parvulusfiliushodienatusestnobisetvocabi.en: A little child, * a son, is born to us this day: † and he shall be called God, the Mighty, alleluia, alleluia.
parvulusfiliushodienatusestnobisetvocabi.la: Párvulus * fílius hódie natus est nobis: † et vocábitur Deus, Fortis, allelúja, allelúja. Ps. 263, 264, 265

propternimiamcharitatemsuamquadilexitnos.en: For his exceeding charity wherewith God the Father loved us, he sent his Son
propternimiamcharitatemsuamquadilexitnos.la: Propter nímiam charitátem suam, qua diléxit nos Deus Pater, Fílium suum misit

insimilitudinemcarnispeccatiutomnessalva.en: In the likeness of sinful flesh, that he might save all.
insimilitudinemcarnispeccatiutomnessalva.la: In similitúdinem carnis peccáti, ut omnes salváret.

ecceiamvenitplenitudotemporisinquomisitd.en: Behold, the fullness of the time is come, wherein God hath sent forth His Son into the world, born of a Virgin, made under the law;
ecceiamvenitplenitudotemporisinquomisitd.la: Ecce jam venit plenitúdo témporis, in quo misit Deus Fílium suum in terras, natum de Vírgine, factum sub lege.

domineaudiviauditumtuumettimuiconsiderav.en: O Lord, I have heard thy hearing, and was afraid: I considered thy works, and trembled, in the midst of two beasts.
domineaudiviauditumtuumettimuiconsiderav.la: Dómine audívi audítum tuum, et tímui: considerávi ópera tua, et expávi in médio duórum animálium.

ecceagnusdeieccequitollitpeccatamundiecc.en: Behold the Lamb of God, behold him who taketh away the sins of the world: behold him of whom I said unto you:
ecceagnusdeieccequitollitpeccatamundiecc.la: Ecce Agnus Dei, ecce qui tollit peccáta mundi: ecce de quo dicébam vobis:

quipostmevenitantemefactusestcuiusnonsum.en: He that cometh after me is preferred before me: the latchet of whose shoe I am not worthy to loose.
quipostmevenitantemefactusestcuiusnonsum.la: Qui post me venit, ante me factus est: cujus non sum dignus corrígiam calceaménti sólvere.

hocesttestimoniumquodperhibuitioannesdic.en: This is the testimony which John gave, saying:
hocesttestimoniumquodperhibuitioannesdic.la: Hoc est testimónium, quod perhíbuit Joánnes, dicens:

benedictusquivenitinnominedomini.en: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord:
benedictusquivenitinnominedomini.la: Benedíctus qui venit in nómine Dómini:

deusdominusetilluxitnobis.en: The Lord is God, and he hath shone upon us.

lapidemquemreprobraveruntedificanteshicf.en: The stone which the builders rejected, the same is become the head of the corner.
lapidemquemreprobraveruntedificanteshicf.la: Lápidem, quem reprobravérunt, ædificántes, hic factus est in caput ánguli.

inprincipieratverbumetverbumeratapuddeum.en: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. The same was in the beginning with God.
inprincipieratverbumetverbumeratapuddeum.la: In princípio erat Verbum, et Verbum erat apud Deum, et Deus erat Verbum: hoc erat in princípio apud Deum.

omniaperipsumfactasuntetsineipsofactumes.en: All things were made by Him, and without Him was not anything made.
omniaperipsumfactasuntetsineipsofactumes.la: Omnia per ipsum facta sunt, et sine ipso factum est nihil.

quodfactumestinipsoviteratetviteratluxho.en: That which was made, in him was life, and the life was the light of men.
quodfactumestinipsoviteratetviteratluxho.la: Quod factum est, in ipso vita erat, et vita erat lux hóminum.

verbumcarofactumestethabitavitinnobisetv.en: The Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us: and we saw his glory, the glory as it were of the only begotten of the Father,
verbumcarofactumestethabitavitinnobisetv.la: Verbum caro factum est, et habitávit in nobis: et vídimus glóriam ejus, glóriam quasi Unigéniti a Patre,

inprincipieratverbumetverbumeratapuddeum.en: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
inprincipieratverbumetverbumeratapuddeum.la: In princípio erat Verbum, et Verbum erat apud Deum, et Deus erat Verbum.

genuitpuerperaregemcuinomeneternumetgaud.en: The Mother brought forth the King, * Whose name is called The Eternal; the joy of a Mother was hers, remaining a Virgin unsullied; neither before nor henceforth hath there been or shall be such another, alleluia.
genuitpuerperaregemcuinomeneternumetgaud.la: Génuit puérpera * Regem, cui nomen ætérnum, et gáudia matris habens cum virginitátis honóre: nec primam símilem visa est, nec habére sequéntem, allelúja.

angelusadpastoresaitannuntiovobisgaudium.en: The Angel said unto the shepherds * I bring you good tidings of great joy; for unto you is born this day a Saviour of the world, alleluia.
angelusadpastoresaitannuntiovobisgaudium.la: Angelus * ad pastóres ait: Annúntio vobis gáudium magnum: quia natus est vobis hódie Salvátor mundi, allelúia.

factestcumangelomultitudocelestisexercit.en: There was * with the Angel a multitude of the heavenly host, praising and saying: Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace to men of good will, alleluia.
factestcumangelomultitudocelestisexercit.la: Facta est * cum Angelo multitúdo cœléstis exércitus laudántium, et dicéntium: Glória in excélsis Deo, et in terra pax homínibus bonæ voluntátis, allelúia.

pastoresloquebanturadinvicemtranseamusus.en: The shepherds * said one to another: Let us go over to Bethlehem, and let us see this word that is come to pass, which the Lord hath shewed to us, alleluia.
pastoresloquebanturadinvicemtranseamusus.la: Pastóres * loquébantur ad ínvicem: Transeámus usque Béthlehem, et videámus hoc Verbum quod factum est, quod Dóminus osténdit nobis, allelúia

etveneruntfestinantesetinveneruntmariame.en: And they came with haste, * and found Mary and Joseph, and the Babe lying in a manger. Alleluia.
etveneruntfestinantesetinveneruntmariame.la: Et venérunt * festinántes: et invenérunt Maríam, et Joseph, et infántem pósitum in præsépio, allelúia.

confiteminidominetinvocatenomeneius.en: Give glory to the Lord, * And call upon his Name.
confiteminidominetinvocatenomeneius.la: Confitémini Dómino, * Et invocáte Nomen ejus.

annuntiateintergentesopereius.en: Declare his deeds among the Gentiles.

nomeniesugloriosumveniteadoremus.en: The glorious Name of Jesus, * Come, let us adore.

admirabileestnomentuumdomineiesuinuniver.en: Admirable * is thy Name, O Lord Jesus, in the whole earth, and thy magnificence above the heavens.
admirabileestnomentuumdomineiesuinuniver.la: Admirábile est * Nomen tuum, Dómine Jesu, in univérsa terra, et magnificéntia tua super cœlos. Ps. 8

cantabodominoquibonatribuitmihietpsallam.en: I will sing to the Lord, * who hath given me good things: and I will sing to the Name of the Lord the most High.
cantabodominoquibonatribuitmihietpsallam.la: Cantábo Dómino * qui bona tríbuit mihi: et psallam Nómini Dómini altíssimi. Ps. 12

hiincurribusethiinequisnosauteminnominei.en: Some in chariots, * and some in horses: but we will call upon the Name of Jesus our God.
hiincurribusethiinequisnosauteminnominei.la: Hi in cúrribus, * et hi in equis: nos autem in Nómine Jesu Dei nostri invocábimus. Ps. 19

beatusvircuiusestnomendominispeseiusetno.en: Blessed is the man * whose hope is the Name of the Lord, and who hath not had regard to vanities and lying follies.
beatusvircuiusestnomendominispeseiusetno.la: Beátus vir, * cujus est Nomen Dómini spes ejus: et non respéxit in vanitátes et insánias falsas. Ps. 39

speciosusformaprefiliishominumtuespropte.en: Beautiful in form * above the sons of men art thou: therefore will I be mindful of thy Name, O Lord Jesus.
speciosusformaprefiliishominumtuespropte.la: Speciósus forma * præ fíliis hóminum tu es, proptérea memor ero Nóminis tui, Dómine Jesu. Ps. 44

secundumnomentuumdeussicetlaustuainfines.en: According to * thy Name, O God, so also is thy praise unto the ends of the earth.
secundumnomentuumdeussicetlaustuainfines.la: Secúndum * Nomen tuum, Deus, sic et laus tua in fines terræ. Ps. 96

exspectabonomentuumdomineiesuquoniambonu.en: I will wait * on thy Name, O Lord Jesus, for it is good.
exspectabonomentuumdomineiesuquoniambonu.la: Exspectábo * Nomen tuum, Dómine Jesu, quóniam bonum est. Ps. 51

dedistidominehereditatemtimentibusnomens.en: Thou hast given, O Lord, * an inheritance to them that fear thy holy Name, to which I will sing a psalm for ever and ever.
dedistidominehereditatemtimentibusnomens.la: Dedísti, Dómine, * hæreditátem timéntibus Nomen sanctum tuum, cui psalmum dicam in sæculum sæculi. Ps. 60

omnisterraadorettedomineiesuchristepsalm.en: Let all the earth * adore thee, O Lord Jesus Christ; let it sing a psalm to thy Name.
omnisterraadorettedomineiesuchristepsalm.la: Omnis terra * adóret te, Dómine Jesu Christe, psalmum dicat Nómini tuo. Ps. 65

magnuminisrelnomentuumdomineiesuterribil.en: Great in Israel * is thy Name, O Lord Jesus, terrible with the kings of the earth.
magnuminisrelnomentuumdomineiesuterribil.la: Magnum in Israël * Nomen tuum, Dómine Jesu, terríbile apud reges terræ. Ps. 75

proptergloriamnoministuidomineiesulibera.en: For the glory * of thy Name, O Lord Jesus, deliver us, and be merciful to our sins for thy Name's sake.
proptergloriamnoministuidomineiesulibera.la: Propter glóriam * Nóminis tui, Dómine Jesu, líbera nos, et propítius esto peccátis nostris, propter Nomen tuum. Ps. 78

confiteanturpopuliomnesnominituomagnodom.en: Let all peoples * give praise to thy great Name, O Lord Jesus, for it is terrible and holy.
confiteanturpopuliomnesnominituomagnodom.la: Confiteántur * pópuli omnes Nómini tuo magno, Dómine Jesu, quóniam terríbile et sanctum est. Ps. 98

fortitudomeetlausmeadominusiesuschristus.en: My strength * and my praise is the Lord Jesus Christ, for he is become my salvation.
fortitudomeetlausmeadominusiesuschristus.la: Fortitúdo mea, * et laus mea Dóminus Jesus Christus, quia factus est mihi in salútem. Ps. 263, 264, 265

bonumestconfiteridomino.en: It is good to give praise to the Lord.

etpsallerenominituoaltissime.en: And to sing to thy Name, O most High.

beatieritiscummaledixerintvoshominesetpe.en: Blessed shall you be when men shall revile you, and persecute you, and speak all that is evil against you, untruly,
beatieritiscummaledixerintvoshominesetpe.la: Beáti éritis cum maledíxerint vos hómines, et persecúti vos fúerint, et díxerint omne malum advérsum vos, mentiéntes,

gaudeteetexsultatequoniammercesvestracop.en: Be glad and rejoice, for your reward is very great in heaven.
gaudeteetexsultatequoniammercesvestracop.la: Gaudéte et exsultáte: quóniam merces vestra copiósa est in cœlo.

sermsupercantica.en: Sermon 15 on the Canticle of Canticles.

nonotiosespiritussanctusnomensponsioleoc.en: Not idly doth the Holy Ghost liken the name of the Bridegroom to oil, when he teacheth the bride thus to cry to the Bridegroom: Thy name is as oil poured out. For oil giveth light, feedeth, and anointeth. It cherisheth fire, nourisheth the flesh, assuageth pain: it is light, food, medicine. See now the same also of the Bridegroom's name: preached, it giveth light; pondered, it feedeth; invoked, it soothes and anointeth. And let us run through each of these. Whence thinkest thou came in the whole world so great and so sudden a light of faith, if not from the preaching of the Name of Jesus?
nonotiosespiritussanctusnomensponsioleoc.la: Non otióse Spíritus Sanctus nomen sponsi óleo cómparat, cum ita dóceat sponsam ad sponsum clamáre: Oleum effúsum nomen tuum. Oleum enim lucet, pascit et ungit. Fovet ignem, nutrit carnem, lenit dolórem: lux, cibus, medicína. Vide idem nunc et de Sponsi nómine: Lucet prædicátum, pascit recogitátum, invocátum lenit et ungit. Et percurrámus síngula. Unde putas in toto orbe tanta et tam súbita fídei lux, nisi de prædicáto Nómine Jesu?

omniaquecumquefacitisinverboautinoperein.en: Whatsoever you do in word or in work, do all in the Name of the Lord Jesus Christ:
omniaquecumquefacitisinverboautinoperein.la: Omnia, quæcúmque fácitis in verbo, aut in ópere, in Nómine Dómini Jesu Christi fácite:

quiabenedictumestnomenmaiestatiseiusinet.en: For blessed is the Name of his majesty for ever.
quiabenedictumestnomenmaiestatiseiusinet.la: Quia benedíctum est Nomen Majestátis ejus in ætérnum.

innominedomininostriiesuchristiadomniaco.en: In the Name of our Lord Jesus Christ let us ever go forward to all our counsels, and to all the actions we have to do:
innominedomininostriiesuchristiadomniaco.la: In Nómine Dómini nostri Jesu Christi ad ómnia consília, omnésque actus geréndos semper progrediámur:

nonnehocnomencoramregibusetgentibusetfil.en: Was not Paul the Apostle bidden to carry this name before kings, and the Gentiles, and the children of Israel? And he carried that Name as a light, and enlightened his country, and cried everywhere: The night is passed, and the day is at hand. How did that light shine forth, and dazzle the eyes of all that beheld it, when, going forth like lightning from the mouth of Peter, it made firm the bodily feet and soles of one lame man, and enlightened many that were spiritually blind? Did it not scatter fire, when he said: In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, arise and walk?
nonnehocnomencoramregibusetgentibusetfil.la: Nonne hoc nomen coram régibus, et Géntibus, et fíliis Israël portáre jussus est Paulus Apóstolus, et portábat Nomen illud tamquam lumen, et illuminábat pátriam, et clamábat ubíque: Nox præcéssit, dies autem appropinquávit? Quómodo lux ista splénduit, ac perstrínxit cunctórum intuéntium óculos, quando de ore Petri, tamquam fulgur egrédiens, claudi uníus corporáles plantas solidávit et bases, multósque spirituáliter cæcos illuminávit? Numquid non ignem sparsit, cum ait: In nómine Jesu Christi Nazaréni surge, et ámbula?

nectantumluxestnomeniesusedestetcibusann.en: Nor is the Name of Jesus light only, but it is also food. Art thou not strengthened as often as thou rememberest it? What doth so enrich the mind of him that pondereth it? What doth so restore the wearied senses, strengthen virtues, quicken good and honest manners, and cherish chaste affections? Dry is all food of the soul, if it be not moistened with this oil; insipid it is, if it be not seasoned with this salt. If thou write, it hath no savour for me, unless I read there Jesus. If thou dispute or confer, it hath no savour for me, unless Jesus sound there. Jesus is honey in the mouth, melody in the ear, jubilation in the heart.
nectantumluxestnomeniesusedestetcibusann.la: Nec tantum lux est Nomen Jesu, sed est et cibus. An non tóties confortáris, quóties recordáris? Quid æque méntem cogitántis impínguat? Quid ita exercitátos réparat sensus, virtútes róborat, végetat mores bonos atque honéstos, castas fovet affectiónes? Aridus est omnis ánimæ cibus, si non óleo isto infúnditur: insípidus est, si non hoc sale condítur. Si scribas, non sapit mihi, nisi légero ibi Jesum. Si dísputes aut cónferas, non sapit mihi, nisi sonúerit ibi Jesus. Jesus mel in ore, in aure melos, in corde júbilus.

nihilaliudostendamusnosscirenisiiesumeth.en: Let us show that we know nothing else but Jesus, and him crucified:
nihilaliudostendamusnosscirenisiiesumeth.la: Nihil áliud ostendámus nos scire nisi Jesum, et hunc crucifíxum:

cuiusnominisdeditnobisdeuscognosceresacr.en: The mystery of whose Name God hath given us to know.
cuiusnominisdeditnobisdeuscognosceresacr.la: Cujus Nóminis dedit nobis Deus cognóscere sacraméntum.

interponamussemperoperinostronomendomini.en: Let us ever set the Name of the Lord Jesus in the midst of our work:
interponamussemperoperinostronomendomini.la: Interponámus semper óperi nostro Nomen Dómini Jesu:

estetmedicinatristaturaliquisnostrumveni.en: It is also medicine. Is any of us sad? Let Jesus come into his heart, and thence leap into his mouth: and behold, at the rising light of the Name, every cloud fleeth away, and the calm returneth. Doth any fall into crime, and moreover run by despairing into the snare of death: will he not, if he call upon the Name of life, straightway breathe again unto life? To whom, trembling and fearful at any time amid dangers, hath not the Name of power, when invoked, at once given confidence and driven away fear? To whom, I pray, tossed and wavering amid doubts, hath not certainty suddenly shone forth at the invocation of the glorious Name? To whom, distrustful in adversity and now on the point of failing, was strength wanting, if the Name of help sounded?
estetmedicinatristaturaliquisnostrumveni.la: Est et medicína. Tristátur áliquis nostrum? Véniat in cor ejus Jesus, et inde sáliat in os: et ecce ad exórtum Nóminis lumen, núbilum omne díffugit, redit serénum. Lábitur quis in crimen, currit ínsuper ad láqueum mortis desperándo: nonne, si ínvocet Nomen vitæ, conféstim respirábit ad vitam? Cui aliquándo in perículis palpitánti et trepidánti, invocátum virtútis Nomen non statim fidúciam præstitit, dépulit metum? Cui quæso in dúbiis æstuánti et fluctuánti non súbito ad invocatiónem clari Nóminis emícuit certitúdo? Cui in advérsis diffidénti, jamjámque deficiénti, si Nomen adjutórii sónuit, défuit fortitúdo?

unigenitofiliosuodeusquemconstituithered.en: To his only-begotten Son, whom he hath appointed heir of all things, God hath given a Name,
unigenitofiliosuodeusquemconstituithered.la: Unigénito Fílio suo Deus, quem constítuit hærédem universórum, Nomen donávit,

nomeniesunomendeiestsuperomnenomen.en: The Name of Jesus, the Name of God, is above every name,
nomeniesunomendeiestsuperomnenomen.la: Nomen Jesu, Nomen Dei est super omne nomen,

quodnonnisicelestioraculonobisfuitmanife.en: Which was not made manifest to us save by a heavenly oracle.
quodnonnisicelestioraculonobisfuitmanife.la: Quod non nisi cœlésti oráculo nobis fuit maniféstum.

mementotequodmagnumetexcelsumestnomendom.en: Remember that great and exalted is the Name of the Lord Jesus:
mementotequodmagnumetexcelsumestnomendom.la: Mementóte quod magnum et excélsum est Nomen Dómini Jesu:

triasuntmuneraqueobtuleruntmagidominoaur.en: Three are the gifts * which the Magi offered to the Lord, gold, frankincense and myrrh: to the Son of God, the great King, alleluia.
triasuntmuneraqueobtuleruntmagidominoaur.la: Tria sunt * múnera quæ obtulérunt Magi Dómino, aurum, thus et myrrham: Fílio Dei, Regi magno, allelúia. Ps. 20, 21

luxdeluceapparuistichristcuimagimuneraof.en: Light of light, * thou hast appeared, O Christ, to whom the Magi offer gifts, alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.
luxdeluceapparuistichristcuimagimuneraof.la: Lux de luce * apparuísti, Christ, cui Magi múnera ófferunt, allelúia, allelúia, allelúia. Ps. 22, 23

christodatusestprincipatusethonorregniom.en: To Christ is given * principality and the honour of the kingdom: all peoples, tribes and tongues shall serve him for ever.
christodatusestprincipatusethonorregniom.la: Christo datus est * principátus et honor regni: omnis pópulus, tribus et linguæ sérvient ei in ætérnum. Ps. 24, 25

videntesstellammagigavisisuntgaudiomagne.en: The Magi, seeing the star, * rejoiced with exceeding great joy; and entering into the house, they offered to the Lord gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
videntesstellammagigavisisuntgaudiomagne.la: Vidéntes stellam Magi, * gavísi sunt gáudio magno, et intrántes domum obtulérunt Dómino aurum, thus, et myrrham. Ps. 26, 27

vidimusstellameiusinorienteetvenimuscumm.en: We have seen his star * in the East, and are come with gifts to adore him.
vidimusstellameiusinorienteetvenimuscumm.la: Vídimus stellam ejus * in Oriénte, et vénimus cum munéribus adoráre eum. Ps. 30, 31

omnesdesabavenientaurumetthusdeferentese.en: All they from Saba shall come, bringing gold and frankincense, and
omnesdesabavenientaurumetthusdeferentese.la: Omnes de Saba vénient, aurum et thus deferéntes, et

laudemdominoannuntiantes.en: Shewing forth praise to the Lord.

exaudideusdeprecationemmeamintendeoratio.en: Hear, O God, my supplication: be attentive to my prayer.
exaudideusdeprecationemmeamintendeoratio.la: Exáudi, Deus, deprecatiónem meam: inténde oratióni meæ:

afinibusterreadteclamavidomine.en: To thee have I cried from the ends of the earth, O Lord.
afinibusterreadteclamavidomine.la: A fínibus terræ ad te clamávi, Dómine.

dumanxiareturcormeuminpetrexaltastimeetd.en: When my heart was in anguish, thou hast exalted me on a rock, and hast led me.
dumanxiareturcormeuminpetrexaltastimeetd.la: Dum anxiarétur cor meum, in petra exaltásti me, et deduxísti me.

misereremeideusmisereremeiquoniamintecon.en: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me, for my soul trusteth in thee:
misereremeideusmisereremeiquoniamintecon.la: Miserére mei, Deus, miserére mei, quóniam in te confídit ánima mea:

deusintesperavidominenonconfundarinetern.en: O God, in thee have I hoped, O Lord, let me never be confounded:
deusintesperavidominenonconfundarinetern.la: Deus, in te sperávi, Dómine, non confúndar in ætérnum:

iniustitiatualiberameeteripeme.en: Deliver me in thy justice, and rescue me.
iniustitiatualiberameeteripeme.la: In justítia tua líbera me, et éripe me.

estomihiindeumprotectoremetinlocummunitu.en: Be thou unto me a God, a protector, and a place of strength, that thou mayst make me safe.
estomihiindeumprotectoremetinlocummunitu.la: Esto mihi in Deum protectórem, et in locum munítum, ut salvum me fácias.

etdabittibipetitionescordistui.en: And he will give thee the requests of thy heart.
etdabittibipetitionescordistui.la: Et dabit tibi petitiónes cordis tui.

reveladominoviamtuametsperaineetipsefaci.en: Commit thy way to the Lord, and trust in him, and he will do it.
reveladominoviamtuametsperaineetipsefaci.la: Revéla Dómino viam tuam, et spera in eo, et ipse fáciet.

mihiautemadhereredeobonumest.en: But it is good for me to adhere to God,
mihiautemadhereredeobonumest.la: Mihi autem adhærére Deo bonum est,

ponereindominodeospemmeam.en: To put my hope in the Lord God.
ponereindominodeospemmeam.la: Pónere in Dómino Deo spem meam.

fiatcormeumimmaculatumutnonconfundar.en: Let my heart be undefiled, that I may not be confounded.
fiatcormeumimmaculatumutnonconfundar.la: Fiat cor meum immaculátum, ut non confúndar.

deusiniquiinsurrexeruntsupermeetfortesqu.en: O God, the wicked are risen up against me, and the mighty have sought my soul:
deusiniquiinsurrexeruntsupermeetfortesqu.la: Deus, iníqui insurrexérunt super me, et fortes quæsiérunt ánimam meam:

auribuspercipedeuslacrimasmeas.en: Give ear, O God, to my tears:

nesileasameremittemihiquoniamincolegosum.en: Be not silent toward me; forgive me, for I am a stranger with thee, and a sojourner.
nesileasameremittemihiquoniamincolegosum.la: Ne síleas a me, remítte mihi, quóniam íncola ego sum apud te, et peregrínus.

dixicustodiamviasmeasutnondelinquaminlin.en: I said: I will take heed to my ways, that I sin not with my tongue.
dixicustodiamviasmeasutnondelinquaminlin.la: Dixi: Custódiam vias meas, ut non delínquam in lingua mea.

eripemedeinimicismeisdeusmeusetabinsurge.en: Deliver me from my enemies, O my God. and defend me from them that rise up against me.
eripemedeinimicismeisdeusmeusetabinsurge.la: Eripe me de inimícis meis Deus meus, et ab insurgéntibus in me líbera me.

devastavitvineamtuamaperdesilvetsingular.en: The boar out of the wood hath laid waste thy vineyard, and a singular wild beast hath devoured it: behold, O Lord, and stir up thy might:
devastavitvineamtuamaperdesilvetsingular.la: Devastávit víneam tuam aper de silva, et singuláris ferus depástus est in eam: vide, Dómine, et éxcita poténtiam tuam:

nepereatquodplantavitdexteratua.en: Lest that perish which thy right hand hath planted.
nepereatquodplantavitdexteratua.la: Ne péreat quod plantávit déxtera tua.

dominedeusvirtutumconvertererespicedecel.en: O Lord God of hosts, turn again, look down from heaven, and see, and visit this vineyard:
dominedeusvirtutumconvertererespicedecel.la: Dómine, Deus virtútum, convértere, réspice de cœlo et vide, et vísita víneam istam:

deusultionumdominusdeusultionumlibereegi.en: The Lord is the God to whom revenge belongeth: the God of revenge hath acted freely.
deusultionumdominusdeusultionumlibereegi.la: Deus ultiónum Dóminus, Deus ultiónum líbere egit.

preoccupemusfaciemdominietinpsalmisiubil.en: Let us come before the presence of the Lord * and make a joyful noise unto Him with Psalms.
preoccupemusfaciemdominietinpsalmisiubil.la: Praeoccupémus fáciem Dómini: * Et in psalmis jubilémus ei.

notasmihifecistidomineviasviteadimplebis.en: Thou hast made known to me, O Lord, the ways of life; thou shalt fill me with joy with thy countenance:
notasmihifecistidomineviasviteadimplebis.la: Notas mihi fecísti, Dómine, vias vitæ, adimplébis me lætítia cum vultu tuo:

delectationesindexteratuausqueinfinem.en: At thy right hand are delights even to the end.
delectationesindexteratuausqueinfinem.la: Delectatiónes in déxtera tua usque in finem.

conservamedominequoniamintesperavidixido.en: Preserve me, O Lord, for I have put my trust in thee: I have said to the Lord, Thou art my God.
conservamedominequoniamintesperavidixido.la: Consérva me, Dó­mine, quóniam in te sperávi: dixi Dómino: Deus meus es tu.

diligamtedominevirtusmea.en: I will love thee, O Lord, my strength:

dominusfirmamentummeumetrefugiummeum.en: The Lord is my firmament, and my refuge.
dominusfirmamentummeumetrefugiummeum.la: Dóminus firmaméntum meum, et refúgium meum.

laudansinvocabodominumetabinimicismeissa.en: Praising, I will call upon the Lord, and I shall be saved from my enemies.
laudansinvocabodominumetabinimicismeissa.la: Laudans invocábo Dóminum, et ab inimícis meis salvus ero.

inmanueiussuntomnesfinesterreetaltitudin.en: In his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his:
inmanueiussuntomnesfinesterreetaltitudin.la: In manu ejus sunt omnes fines terræ: et altitúdines móntium ipsíus sunt:

nequeirrideantmeinimicimeietenimuniversi.en: Neither let my enemies laugh at me: for none of them that wait on thee shall be confounded.
nequeirrideantmeinimicimeietenimuniversi.la: Neque irrídeant me inimíci mei: étenim univérsi qui sústinent te non confundéntur.

audiamdominevocemlaudistue.en: Let me hear, O Lord, the voice of thy praise:

utenarremuniversamirabiliatua.en: That I may tell of all thy wondrous works.

dominedilexidecoremdomustueetlocumhabita.en: O Lord, I have loved the beauty of thy house, and the place where thy glory dwelleth:
dominedilexidecoremdomustueetlocumhabita.la: Dómine, diléxi decórem domus tuæ, et locum habitatiónis glóriae tuæ:

absconditamquamaurumpeccatameetcelaviins.en: I have hidden my sins as gold, and have concealed my iniquity in my bosom:
absconditamquamaurumpeccatameetcelaviins.la: Abscóndi tamquam aurum peccáta mea: et celávi in sinu meo iniquitátem meam:

misereremeideussecundummagnammisericordi.en: Have mercy on me, O God, according to thy great mercy.
misereremeideussecundummagnammisericordi.la: Miserére mei Deus, secundum magnam misericórdiam tuam.

tibisolipeccavietmalumcoramtefeci.en: To thee only have I sinned, and have done evil before thee.
tibisolipeccavietmalumcoramtefeci.la: Tibi soli peccávi, et malum coram te feci.

fratresglorificateetportatedominumincorp.en: Brethren, * glorify and bear the Lord in your body, alleluia.
fratresglorificateetportatedominumincorp.la: Fratres, * glorificáte, et portáte Dóminum in córpore vestro, allelúia.

dominepuermeusiacetparalyticusindometmal.en: Lord, * my servant lieth at home sick of the palsy, and is grievously tormented. Amen I say to thee, I will come and heal him.
dominepuermeusiacetparalyticusindometmal.la: Dómine, * puer meus jacet paralyticus in domo, et male torquétur. Amen dico tibi, ego véniam, et curábo eum.

scitisfratresquiatemplumdeiestisetspirit.en: You know, brethren, * that you are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you: but if any man violate this temple, him shall the Lord destroy: for the temple of God is holy, which you are, alleluia.
scitisfratresquiatemplumdeiestisetspirit.la: Scitis, fratres, * quia templum Dei estis, et Spíritus Dei hábitat in vobis: si quis autem violáverit templum hoc, despérdet illum Dóminus: templum enim Dei sanctum est, quod estis vos, allelúia.

surgensiesusimperavitventisetmarietfacte.en: Jesus rising up * commanded the winds and the sea, and there came a great calm, and they all marvelled.
surgensiesusimperavitventisetmarietfacte.la: Surgens Jesus * imperávit ventis et mari, et facta est tranquíllitas magna, et miráti sunt univérsi.

fratresexistimenimquodnonsuntcondignepas.en: Brethren, * for I reckon that the sufferings of this time are not worthy to be compared with the glory to come, that shall be revealed in us, alleluia.
fratresexistimenimquodnonsuntcondignepas.la: Fratres, * exístimo enim quod non sunt condígnæ passiónes hujus témporis ad futúram glóriam, quæ revelábitur in nobis, allelúia.

quoniamdeusmagnusdominusetrexmagnussuper.en: For the Lord is a great God, * And a great King above all gods.
quoniamdeusmagnusdominusetrexmagnussuper.la: Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus: * Et Rex magnus super omnes deos.

igiturperfectisuntcelietterretomnisornat.en: So the heavens and the earth were finished, and all the furniture of them: and on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made: and he rested
igiturperfectisuntcelietterretomnisornat.la: Igitur perfécti sunt cæli et terra, et omnis ornátus eórum: complevítque Deus die séptimo opus suum, quod fécerat: et requiévit

abomnioperequodpatrarat.en: From all the work which he had done.

etbenedixitdeusdieiseptimetsanctificavit.en: And God blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it, because in it he had rested
etbenedixitdeusdieiseptimetsanctificavit.la: Et benedíxit Deus diéi séptimo, et sanctificávit illum, quia in ipso cessáverat

hocnuncosexossibusmeisetcarodecarnemea.en: This now is bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh:
hocnuncosexossibusmeisetcarodecarnemea.la: Hoc nunc os ex óssibus meis, et caro de carne mea:

multienimsuntvocatipauciverelecti.en: For many * are called, but few chosen.
multienimsuntvocatipauciverelecti.la: Multi * enim sunt vocáti, pauci vero elécti.

insudorevultustuivescerispanetuodixitdom.en: In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat thy bread, said the Lord unto Adam: when thou hast tilled the ground,
insudorevultustuivescerispanetuodixitdom.la: In sudóre vultus tui vescéris pane tuo, dixit Dóminus ad Adam: cum operátus fúeris terram,

nondabitfructussuossedspinasettribulosge.en: It shall not yield thee its fruits, but thorns and thistles shall it bring forth to thee.
nondabitfructussuossedspinasettribulosge.la: Non dabit fructus suos: sed spinas, et tríbulos germinábit tibi.

preoquodobedistivociuxoristueplusquammee.en: Because thou hast obeyed the voice of thy wife rather than mine, cursed is the earth in thy work.
preoquodobedistivociuxoristueplusquammee.la: Pro eo quod obedísti voci uxóris tuæ, plusquam meæ, maledícta terra in ópere tuo.

cherubimcollocavitdominusetflammeumgladi.en: The Lord placed Cherubims, and a flaming sword, turning every way, to keep the way of the tree of life, and said:
cherubimcollocavitdominusetflammeumgladi.la: Chérubim collocávit Dóminus, et flámmeum gládium atque versátilem, ad custodiéndam viam ligni vitæ, et ait:

corcontritumethumiliatumdeusnondespicies.en: A contrite * and humbled heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.
corcontritumethumiliatumdeusnondespicies.la: Cor contrítum * et humiliátum, Deus, non despícies.

adiutormeusestodeusnederelinquasme.en: Be thou my helper, O God, * Forsake me not.
adiutormeusestodeusnederelinquasme.la: Adjútor meus esto, Deus, * Ne derelínquas me.

nequedespiciasmedeussalutarismeus.en: Neither despise me, O God my Saviour.
nequedespiciasmedeussalutarismeus.la: Neque despícias me, Deus, salutáris meus.

etnomenfluviisecundigehonipseestquicircu.en: And the name of the second river is Gehon: the same is it that compasseth all the land of Ethiopia.
etnomenfluviisecundigehonipseestquicircu.la: Et nomen flúvii secúndi Gehon; ipse est qui circúmit omnem terram Æthiópiae.

nomenverofluministertiitigrisipsevaditco.en: And the name of the third river is Tigris: the same passeth along by the Assyrians. And the fourth river is Euphrates.
nomenverofluministertiitigrisipsevaditco.la: Nomen vero flúminis tértii, Tigris: ipse vadit contra Assýrios. Flúvius autem quartus, ipse est Euphrátes.

exlibrenchiridiisanctibernardiabbatis.en: From the Enchiridion of St. Bernard, Abbot.
exlibrenchiridiisanctibernardiabbatis.la: Ex libro Enchíridii sancti Bernárdi Abbátis.

immisitdominussoporeminadamimmisitetinse.en: The Lord cast a deep sleep upon Adam. He cast it also upon himself, being made indeed the second Adam: but there is a difference, perhaps not a small one. For the former seemeth to have been cast into sleep by the excess of contemplation; Christ by the affection of compassion: so that truth cast the sleep upon the one, charity upon the other, since both are the Lord. For John the Evangelist saith: God is charity. And the Lord himself: I am the way, the truth and the life.
immisitdominussoporeminadamimmisitetinse.la: Immísit Dóminus sopórem in Adam. Immísit et in seípsum, factus nimírum secúndus Adam: sed est distántia forte non parva. Ille enim soporátus vidétur præ excéssu contemplatiónis; Christus miseratiónis afféctu: ut in illum sopórem immíserit véritas, in hunc cháritas, cum útraque sit Dóminus. Ait enim Joánnes Evangelísta: Deus cháritas est. Et ipse Dóminus: Ego sum via, véritas et vita.

sanesoporemchristisoliuscharitatisfuisse.en: Truly no one who is a Christian even in name doubteth that the sleep of Christ was of charity alone. For he couched as a lion, not vanquished indeed, but victor, laying down his life by his own power, receiving the sleep of death by his own will. But of what kind must that sleep also be said or believed to have been, which the Lord cast upon Adam, in which, wholly without sense of pain, a rib was taken from the side of the sleeper, to build up the woman?
sanesoporemchristisoliuscharitatisfuisse.la: Sane sopórem Christi solíus charitátis fuísse nemo dúbitat, vel nómine tenus Christiánus. Síquidem accúbuit ut leo, non victus plane, sed victor, potestáte própria ponens ánimam, somnum mortis excípiens própria voluntáte. Céterum qualis et ille sopor dicéndus sit fuísse, vel credéndus, quem Dóminus immísit in Adam, in quo sine sensu omnino dolóris, in mulíerem ædificándam costa subláta est de látere dormiéntis?

mihiquidemnonnisiincommutabilisveritatis.en: To me indeed he seemeth to have fallen asleep, passing beyond his bodily senses, by nothing else than the contemplation of the unchangeable truth and the abyss of the divine wisdom: which may be gathered most of all from his own words. For, returning, he showeth whither he had gone, coming as one drunken out of the wine-cellar, and uttering that great mystery which so long after the Apostle commended in Christ and in the Church. This now, saith he, is bone of my bones. And: Wherefore a man shall leave father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife, and they shall be two in one flesh. Doth he seem to thee to have slept utterly, who, being awakened, broke forth into these words?
mihiquidemnonnisiincommutabilisveritatis.la: Mihi quidem non nisi incommutábilis veritátis intúitu, et abysso divínæ sapiéntiæ corpóreis excédens sénsibus obdormísse vidétur: quod ex ejus verbis vel máximæ cónjici potest. Rédiens nimírum índicat quo abiísset, dum tamquam ébrius de cella vinária véniens, et erúctans illud magnum sacraméntum, quod tanto post in Christo et in Ecclésia Apóstolus commendávit. Hoc nunc, inquit, os ex óssibus meis. Et, Propter hoc, relínquet homo patrem et matrem, et adhærébit uxóri suæ, et erunt duo in carne una. An tibi pénitus obdormísse vidétur, qui in hanc vocem excitátus erúpit?

inlibertateposuiteumdeusutintersummetinf.en: God placed him in liberty, that, moving between the highest things and the lowest, he might both rise unto the former without difficulty, and descend unto the latter without allurement or necessity. Not so is reason free in us, but it must struggle on every side. For thus it is both held captive by the lowest things as by a kind of birdlime, and is repelled as unworthy from the highest, so that neither can it be torn away from the one without pain, nor be admitted to the other save with great groaning, or but rarely. Hence indeed they use violence that seek my soul, so that it is needful to cry out: Unhappy man that I am, who shall deliver me from the body of this death?
inlibertateposuiteumdeusutintersummetinf.la: In libertáte pósuit eum Deus, ut inter summa et ínfima versans, et in illa excéderet sine difficultáte, et ad hæc sine illécebra aut necessitáte descénderet. Non sic in nobis líbera rátio, sed úndique ei luctándum est. Sic enim et ab ínfimis visco quodam captíva tenétur, et a summis indígna repéllitur, ut nec ab his sine dolóre possit avélli, nec ad illa sine magno gémitu vel raro queat admítti. Hinc nempe vim fáciunt qui quærunt ánimam meam, ut clamáre necésse sit: Infélix ego homo, quis me liberábit de córpore mortis hujus?

semenceciditinterrambonametortumfecitfru.en: Some seed fell * upon good ground, and sprang up and yielded fruit a hundredfold.
semenceciditinterrambonametortumfecitfru.la: Semen cécidit * in terram bonam, et ortum fecit fructum céntuplum.

fortitudomeetlausmeadominusexaudivitvoce.en: The Lord is my strength * and my praise: he hath heard my voice, and is become my salvation.
fortitudomeetlausmeadominusexaudivitvoce.la: Fortitúdo mea, * et laus mea Dóminus, exaudívit vocem meam, et factus est mihi in salútem.

siculmenverihonorisqueritisadcelestempat.en: If ye seek * the height of true honour, hasten with all speed unto the heavenly fatherland.
siculmenverihonorisqueritisadcelestempat.la: Si culmen * veri honóris quæritis, ad cœléstem pátriam quantócius properáte.

semenestverbumdeisatorautemchristusomnis.en: The seed is * the word of God, and the sower is Christ: every one that heareth him shall abide for ever.
semenestverbumdeisatorautemchristusomnis.la: Semen est * Verbum Dei, sator autem Christus: omnis qui audit eum, manébit in ætérnum.

quiverbumdeiretinentcordeperfectetoptimo.en: They who keep * the word of God with a good and perfect heart, bring forth fruit in patience.
quiverbumdeiretinentcordeperfectetoptimo.la: Qui verbum Dei rétinent * corde perfécto et óptimo, fructum áfferunt in patiéntia.

iesushecdicensclamabatquihabetauresaudie.en: As Jesus said these things, he cried out: * He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.
iesushecdicensclamabatquihabetauresaudie.la: Jesus hæc dicens, clamábat: * Qui habet aures audiéndi, áudiat.

emisiteumdominusdeusdeparadisovoluptatis.en: And the Lord God sent him out of the paradise of pleasure, to till the earth from which he was taken.
emisiteumdominusdeusdeparadisovoluptatis.la: Emísit eum Dóminus Deus de paradíso voluptátis, ut operarétur terram de qua sumptus est.

eiecitqueadametcollocavitanteparadisumvo.en: And he cast out Adam: and placed before the paradise of pleasure Cherubims, and a flaming sword, turning every way, to keep the way of the tree of life.
eiecitqueadametcollocavitanteparadisumvo.la: Ejecítque Adam: et collocávit ante paradísum voluptátis Chérubim, et flámmeum gládium, atque versátilem, ad custodiéndam viam ligni vitæ.

vobisdatumestnossemysteriumregnideiceter.en: To you it is given * to know the mystery of the kingdom of God, but to the rest in parables, said Jesus to his disciples.
vobisdatumestnossemysteriumregnideiceter.la: Vobis datum est * nosse mystérium regni Dei: céteris autem in parábolis, dixit Jesus descípulis suis.

quadragintadiesetnoctesapertisuntceliete.en: For forty days and nights the heavens were opened, and of all flesh having the breath of life
quadragintadiesetnoctesapertisuntceliete.la: Quadragínta dies et noctes apérti sunt cæli, et ex omni carne habénte spíritum vitæ

ingressasuntinarcametclausitaforisostium.en: They went in into the ark, and the Lord shut the door from without.
ingressasuntinarcametclausitaforisostium.la: Ingréssa sunt in arcam, et clausit a foris óstium Dóminus.

neveretfiliieiusuxoreiusetuxoresfiliorum.en: But Noe and his sons, his wife, and the wives of his sons.
neveretfiliieiusuxoreiusetuxoresfiliorum.la: Noë vero, et fílii ejus, uxor ejus, et uxóres filiórum ejus.

fenestraminarcafaciesetincubitoconsummab.en: Thou shalt make a window in the ark, and in a cubit shalt thou finish the top of it: and the door of the ark thou shalt set in the side: with lower, middle chambers, and third stories shalt thou make it.
fenestraminarcafaciesetincubitoconsummab.la: Fenéstram in arca fácies, et in cúbito consummábis summitem ejus: óstium autem arcæ pones ex látere: deórsum, cœnácula, et trístega fácies in ea.

ecceegoadducamaquasdiluviisuperterramuti.en: Behold, I will bring the waters of the flood upon the earth, to destroy all flesh wherein is the breath of life under heaven: all things that are in the earth shall be consumed.
ecceegoadducamaquasdiluviisuperterramuti.la: Ecce ego addúcam aquas dilúvii super terram, ut interfíciam omnem carnem, in qua spíritus vitæ est subter cœlum: univérsa quæ in terra sunt, consuméntur.

cumquesublevassetoculosapparuerunteitres.en: And when he had lifted up his eyes, there appeared to him three men standing near him.
cumquesublevassetoculosapparuerunteitres.la: Cumque sublevásset óculos, apparuérunt ei tres viri stantes juxta eum.

tentavitdominusabrahametdixitadeumtollef.en: The Lord tried Abraham, and said to him: Take thy son Isaac, whom thou lovest, and offer him there for a holocaust
tentavitdominusabrahametdixitadeumtollef.la: Tentávit Dóminus Abraham, et dixit ad eum: Tolle fílium tuum, quem díligis, Isaac, et offer illum ibi in holocáustum,

superunummontiumquemdixerotibi.en: Upon one of the mountains which I will show thee.
superunummontiumquemdixerotibi.la: Super unum móntium, quem díxero tibi.

transeuntedominoclamabatcecusadeummisere.en: As the Lord passed by, * a blind man cried out to him: Have mercy on me, thou Son of David.
transeuntedominoclamabatcecusadeummisere.la: Transeúnte Domino, * clamábat cæcus ad eum: Miserére mei, Fili David.

venihodieadfontemaqueetoravidominumdicen.en: I came this day to the well of water, and prayed the Lord, saying: O Lord God of Abraham,
venihodieadfontemaqueetoravidominumdicen.la: Veni hódie ad fontem aquæ, et orávi Dóminum, dicens: Dómine, Deus Abraham,

dexteradominivirtutemfaciatutcumimpulsus.en: Let the right hand of the Lord * do valiantly, that when I am thrust, it may hold me up as I fall.
dexteradominivirtutemfaciatutcumimpulsus.la: Déxtera Dómini * virtútem fáciat, ut cum impúlsus fúero, cadéntem me suscípiat.

cecussedebatsecusviametclamabatmisererem.en: A blind man sat * by the way side, and cried out: Have mercy on me, thou son of David.
cecussedebatsecusviametclamabatmisererem.la: Cæcus sedébat * secus viam, et clamábat: Miserére mei, fili David.

tradeturgentibusadilludendumetflagelland.en: He shall be delivered to the Gentiles * to be mocked, and scourged, and crucified.
tradeturgentibusadilludendumetflagelland.la: Tradétur Géntibus * ad illudéndum, et flagellándum, et crucifigéndum.

ecceascendimusierosolymametconsummabuntu.en: Behold, we go up * to Jerusalem, and all things shall be accomplished which were written by the Prophets concerning the Son of man.
ecceascendimusierosolymametconsummabuntu.la: Ecce ascéndimus * Jerosólymam, et consummabúntur ómnia, quæ scripta sunt per Prophétas de Fílio hóminis.

iterfacienteiesudumappropinquaretiericho.en: As Jesus went on His way, * as He was come nigh unto Jericho, a certain blind man cried unto Him, that he might worthily receive his sight.
iterfacienteiesudumappropinquaretiericho.la: Iter faciénte * Jesu, dum appropinquáret Jericho, cæcus clamábat ad eum, ut lumen recípere mererétur.

quareieiunavimusetnonaspexistihumiliavim.en: Why have we fasted, * and thou hast not regarded? have we humbled our souls, and thou hast not taken notice?
quareieiunavimusetnonaspexistihumiliavim.la: Quare jejunávimus, * et non aspexísti? humiliávimus ánimas nostras, et nescísti?

perarmaiustitievirtutisdeicommendemusnos.en: By the armour of justice of the power of God, let us approve ourselves in much patience.
perarmaiustitievirtutisdeicommendemusnos.la: Per arma justítiæ virtútis Dei commendémus nosmetípsos in multa patiéntia.

eccenunctempusacceptabileeccenuncdiessal.en: Behold, now is the acceptable time; behold, now is the day of salvation: let us approve ourselves in much patience.
eccenunctempusacceptabileeccenuncdiessal.la: Ecce nunc tempus acceptábile, ecce nunc dies salútis: commendémus nosmetípsos in multa patiéntia,

inieiuniismultisperarmaiustitievirtutisd.en: In many fastings, by the armour of justice of the power of God.
inieiuniismultisperarmaiustitievirtutisd.la: In jejúniis multis, per arma justítiæ virtútis Dei.

inomnibusexhibeamusnosmetipsossicutdeimi.en: In all things let us approve ourselves as the ministers of God, in much patience;
inomnibusexhibeamusnosmetipsossicutdeimi.la: In ómnibus exhibeámus nosmetípsos sicut Dei minístros, in multa patiéntia,

peccavimuscumpatribusnostrisiniusteegimu.en: We have sinned with our fathers: we have acted unjustly, we have wrought iniquity.
peccavimuscumpatribusnostrisiniusteegimu.la: Peccávimus cum pátribus nostris: injúste égimus, iniquitátem fécimus.

eccenunctempusacceptabileeccenuncdiessal.en: Behold, now is the acceptable time, behold, now is the day of salvation: giving no offence to any man,
eccenunctempusacceptabileeccenuncdiessal.la: Ecce nunc tempus acceptábile, ecce nunc dies salútis: némini dantes ullam offensiónem,

honoradominumdetuasubstantietdeprimitiis.en: Honour the Lord with thy substance, and of the firstfruits of all thy fruits give to the poor.
honoradominumdetuasubstantietdeprimitiis.la: Honóra Dóminum de tua substántia et de primítiis ómnium frugum tuárum da paupéribus.

etpetrumlacrymantemsuscepistimisericorsd.en: And thou didst receive Peter weeping, O merciful Lord,
etpetrumlacrymantemsuscepistimisericorsd.la: Et Petrum lacrymántem suscepísti, miséricors Dómine,

scapulissuisobumbrabittibidominusetsubpe.en: The Lord will overshadow thee with his shoulders, and under his wings thou shalt trust:
scapulissuisobumbrabittibidominusetsubpe.la: Scápulis suis obumbrábit tibi Dóminus, et sub pennis ejus sperábis:

scutocircumdabitteveritaseius.en: His truth shall compass thee with a shield.

noninsolopanevivithomosedinomniverboquod.en: Man shall not live by bread alone, * but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.
noninsolopanevivithomosedinomniverboquod.la: Non in solo pane * vivit homo, sed in omni verbo quod procédit de ore Dei. Ps. 269, 270, 271

scinditecordavestretnonvestimentavestra.en: Rend your hearts, and not your garments,
scinditecordavestretnonvestimentavestra.la: Scíndite corda vestra, et non vestiménta vestra,

etconvertiminiaddominumdeumvestrumquiabe.en: And turn to the Lord your God, for he is gracious and merciful.
etconvertiminiaddominumdeumvestrumquiabe.la: Et convertímini ad Dóminum Deum vestrum, quia benígnus et miséricors est.

revertiminiunusquisqueaviasuamaletapessi.en: Return ye every one from his evil way, and from your most wicked thoughts:
revertiminiunusquisqueaviasuamaletapessi.la: Revertímini unusquísque a via sua mala, et a péssimis cogitatiónibus vestris:

dominedeuspropitiusestopopulotuo.en: O Lord God, be merciful to thy people,
dominedeuspropitiusestopopulotuo.la: Dómine Deus propítius esto pópulo tuo,

etconvertetribulationemnostramingaudium.en: And turn our tribulation into joy.
etconvertetribulationemnostramingaudium.la: Et convérte tribulatiónem nostram in gáudium.

reliquiteumtentatoretaccesseruntangeliet.en: The tempter left him, * and Angels came and ministered to him.
reliquiteumtentatoretaccesseruntangeliet.la: Relíquit eum tentátor, * et accessérunt Angeli, et ministrábant ei.

abiitiesusforasextracivitateminbethaniam.en: Jesus went * forth out of the city into Bethania: and there he taught them of the kingdom of God.
abiitiesusforasextracivitateminbethaniam.la: Abiit * Jesus foras extra civitátem in Bethániam: ibíque docébat eos de regno Dei.

dominenonhabeohominemutcummotafueritaqua.en: Lord, * I have no man, when the water is troubled, to put me into the pond.
dominenonhabeohominemutcummotafueritaqua.la: Dómine, * non hábeo hóminem, ut, cum mota fúerit aqua, mittat me in piscínam.

adoremusdeumquiaipsefecitnos.en: Let us adore God: * For he hath made us.
adoremusdeumquiaipsefecitnos.la: Adorémus Deum: * Quia ipse fecit nos.

ecceodorfiliimeisicutodoragriplenicuiben.en: Behold, the smell of my son is as the smell of a plentiful field, which the Lord hath blessed:
ecceodorfiliimeisicutodoragriplenicuiben.la: Ecce odor fílii mei sicut odor agri pleni, cui benedíxit Dóminus:
