osacramentumpietatisosignumunitatisovinc.la: O Sacraméntum * pietátis, o signum unitátis, o vínculum charitátis, nos in via refíciens sub aliéna spécie; post preséntis vitæ cursum réfice nos in pátria, jam reveláta fácie sine spécie média, allelúia.

novusabelchristushostiamgratampronobisof.en: Christ, * the new Abel, offering for us to God the Father an acceptable victim, hath dedicated a new testament in his own Blood.
novusabelchristushostiamgratampronobisof.la: Novus Abel, * Christus, hóstiam gratam pro nobis ófferens Deo Patri, novum dedicávit in suo Sánguine testaméntum.

edificavitnealtaredominoofferenssuperill.en: Noe built * an altar to the Lord, offering holocausts upon it: and the Lord smelled a sweet savour, and blessed him.
edificavitnealtaredominoofferenssuperill.la: Ædificávit Noë * altáre Dómino, ófferens super illud holocáusta: odoratúsque Dóminus odórem suavitátis, benedíxit ei.

introducensiosephdomumfratressuosinstrux.en: Joseph, * bringing his brethren into the house, made a feast, and when bread was set before them, he ate and drank with them.
introducensiosephdomumfratressuosinstrux.la: Introdúcens Joseph * domum fratres suos, instrúxit convívium, et appósito pane comédit, et bibit cum eis.

mandavitdominusnubibusdesuperetianuascel.en: The Lord commanded the clouds from above: * and opened the doors of heaven. And he rained down manna upon them to eat: * and gave them the bread of heaven. Man ate the bread of Angels, * he sent them provisions in abundance.
mandavitdominusnubibusdesuperetianuascel.la: Mandávit Dóminus núbibus désuper: * et jánuas cæli apéruit. Et pluit illis manna ad manducándum: * et panem cæli dedit eis. Panem Angelórum manducávit homo, * cibária misit eis in abundántia.

panisisteverusestquidecelodescendit.en: This is the true bread, * Which came down from heaven.
panisisteverusestquidecelodescendit.la: Panis iste verus est, * Qui de cælo descéndit.

etdatvitammundo.en: And giveth life to the world.

egosumpanisvitequidecelodescendisiquisma.en: I am * the bread of life, which came down from heaven; if any man eat of this bread, he shall live for ever.
egosumpanisvitequidecelodescendisiquisma.la: Ego sum * panis vitæ, qui de cœlo descéndi, si quis manducáverit ex hoc pane, vivet in ætérnum.

opanisvitenatusdevirginequitepuramentesu.en: O Bread of life, * born of the Virgin, who to them that receive thee with a pure mind givest the life of grace in this life, give us in our fatherland the life of everlasting glory.
opanisvitenatusdevirginequitepuramentesu.la: O Panis vitæ, * natus de Vírgine, qui te pura mente suméntibus vitam grátiæ donas in vita, da nobis in pátria vitam glóriæ sempitérnæ.

panemcelidediteis.en: He gave them the bread of heaven.

cognoveruntomnesadanusquebersabeequodfid.en: All knew, * from Dan even to Bersabee, that Samuel was a faithful Prophet of the Lord.
cognoveruntomnesadanusquebersabeequodfid.la: Cognovérunt omnes * a Dan usque Bersabée, quod fidélis Sámuel Prophéta esset Dómini.

paraturnobismensadominiadversusomnesquit.en: The table of the Lord * is prepared for us against all that afflict us.
paraturnobismensadominiadversusomnesquit.la: Parátur * nobis mensa Dómini advérsus omnes qui tríbulant nos. Ps. 22, 23

iratusrexsauldixitmihimilledederuntetfil.en: King Saul * was angry and said: They have given me a thousand, and to the son of Isai they have given ten thousand.
iratusrexsauldixitmihimilledederuntetfil.la: Irátus * rex Saül dixit: Mihi mille dedérunt, et fílio Isai dedérunt decem míllia.

quiseniminomnibussicutdavidfidelisinvent.en: For who * among all is found so faithful in thy kingdom as David, going out, and coming in, and going at the king's bidding?
quiseniminomnibussicutdavidfidelisinvent.la: Quis enim * in ómnibus, sicut David fidélis invéntus est in regno tuo, egrédiens, et regrédiens, et pergens ad impérium regis?

nonneisteestdaviddequocanebantinchorodic.en: Is not this David, * of whom they sang in the choir, saying: Saul slew a thousand, and David ten thousand among his thousands?
nonneisteestdaviddequocanebantinchorodic.la: Nonne iste est David * de quo canébant in choro, dicéntes: Saül percússit mile, et David decem míllia in míllibus suis?

doleosupertefratermiionathaamabilisvalde.en: I grieve for thee, my brother Jonathan, exceeding lovely, above the love of women: and as a mother loveth her only son, so did I love thee: the arrow of Jonathan never turned back, neither did his shield turn aside from battle, and his spear was not turned away.
doleosupertefratermiionathaamabilisvalde.la: Dóleo super te, frater mi Jónatha, amábilis valde super amórem mulíerum: et sicut mater únicum amat fílium, ita te diligébam: sagítta Jónathæ numquam ábiit retrórsum, nec declinávit clypeus ejus de bello, et hasta ejus non est avérsa.

nonomnisquidicitmihidominedomineintrabit.en: Not every one * that saith to me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven: but he that doth the will of my Father who is in heaven, he shall enter into the kingdom of heaven, alleluia.
nonomnisquidicitmihidominedomineintrabit.la: Non omnis, * qui dicit mihi: Dómine, Dómine, intrábit in regnum cœlórum: sed qui facit voluntátem Patris mei, qui in cœlis est, ipse intrábit in regnum cœlórum, allelúia.

rexautemdavidcoopertocapiteincedenslugeb.en: But King David, * going with his head covered, mourned for his son, saying: Absalom my son, my son Absalom, who would grant me that I might die for thee, my son Absalom?
rexautemdavidcoopertocapiteincedenslugeb.la: Rex autem David * coopérto cápite incédens lugébat fílium suum, dicens: Absalom fili mi, fili mi Absalom, quis mihi det ut ego móriar pro te, fili mi Absalom?

etsiinhisalienaquesuntalienumestautemnob.en: And if in these things, which are another's (and all that is of the world is another's to us), you have not been faithful; who will be able to trust you with that which is your own, and properly allotted to man?
etsiinhisalienaquesuntalienumestautemnob.la: Et si in his, aliéna quæ sunt (aliénum est autem nobis omne quod sǽculi est), infidels fuístis; ea, quæ vestra sunt, et próprie hómini deputáta, quis vobis crédere póterit?

quistibivideturproximusfuisseilliquiinci.en: Which * seemeth to thee to have been neighbour unto him that fell among the robbers? And he said to him: He that shewed mercy to him. Go, and do thou in like manner, alleluia.
quistibivideturproximusfuisseilliquiinci.la: Quis tibi vidétur * próximus fuísse illi, qui íncidit in latrónes? Et ait illi: Qui fecit misericórdiam in illum. Vade, et tu fac simíliter, allelúia.

nonnedecemmundatisuntetnovemubisuntnones.en: Were not ten * made clean? and where are the nine? There is no one found to return and give glory to God, but this stranger. Go, for thy faith hath made thee whole, alleluia.
nonnedecemmundatisuntetnovemubisuntnones.la: Nonne decem * mundáti sunt? et novem ubi sunt? Non est invéntus qui redíret, et daret glóriam Deo, nisi hic alienígena. Vade, quia fides tua te salvum fecit, allelúia.

sapientiaclamitatinplateissiquisdiligits.en: Wisdom * crieth in the streets: If any man love wisdom, let him come unto me, and he shall find her and when once he hath found her, blessed shall he be if he hold her.
sapientiaclamitatinplateissiquisdiligits.la: Sapiéntia * clámitat in platéis: Si quis díligit sapiéntiam, ad me declínet, et eam invéniet: et, cum invénerit, beátus erit si tenúerit eam.

dominusposseditmeininitioviarumsuarumant.en: The Lord possessed me * in the beginning of his ways, before he made any thing from the beginning: the depths were not as yet, and I was already conceived: when he prepared the heavens, I was present, making all things with him.
dominusposseditmeininitioviarumsuarumant.la: Dóminus possédit me * in inítio viárum suárum, ántequam quidquam fáceret a princípio: necdum erant abyssi, et ego parturiébar: quando præparábat cœlos, áderam, cum eo compónens ómnia.

inillotemporeeratiosephetmariamateriesum.en: At that time: Joseph and Mary the mother of Jesus were wondering at those things which were spoken concerning him. And so on.
inillotemporeeratiosephetmariamateriesum.la: In illo témpore: Erat Joseph, et María mater Jesu, mirántes super his, quæ dicebántur de illo. Et réliqua.

videsubereminomnesgratiamdominigeneratio.en: Thou seest grace abundant toward all, spread abroad by the birth of the Lord, and prophecy denied to the unbelieving, not to the just. Behold, Simeon also prophesieth that the Lord Jesus Christ is come for the fall and the resurrection of many, that he may discern the merits of the just and of the wicked; and that, according to the quality of our deeds, as true and just judge, he may decree either punishments or rewards.
videsubereminomnesgratiamdominigeneratio.la: Vides úberem in omnes grátiam, Dómini generatióne diffúsam, et prophetíam incrédulis negátam esse, non justis. Ecce et Símeon prophétat, in ruínam et resurrectiónem plurimórum venisse Dóminum Jesum Christum, ut justórum, iníquorúmque merita discérnat; et pro nostrórum qualitate factórum, judex verus et justus aut supplícia decérnat, aut præmia.

nesciensmatervirgovirumpeperitsinedolore.en: The Virgin Mother, knowing not man, brought forth without sorrow the Saviour of the ages.
nesciensmatervirgovirumpeperitsinedolore.la: Nésciens Mater Virgo virum, péperit sine dolóre Salvatórem sæculórum.

ipsumregemangelorumsolavirgolactabatuber.en: The King of Angels himself the Virgin alone did suckle at a breast filled from heaven.
ipsumregemangelorumsolavirgolactabatuber.la: Ipsum Regem Angelórum, sola Virgo lactábat úbere de cælo pleno.

ettuamipsiusanimampertransibitgladiusnec.en: And thy own soul a sword shall pierce. Neither Scripture nor history teacheth that Mary passed from this life by suffering a bodily death. For not the soul, but the body, is pierced by a material sword. And therefore it sheweth the prudence of Mary, not ignorant of the heavenly mystery.
ettuamipsiusanimampertransibitgladiusnec.la: Et tuam ipsíus ánimam pertransíbit gládius. Nec líttera, nec história docet, ex hac vita Maríam corporális necis passióne migrásse. Non enim ánima, sed corpus materiáli gládio transverberátur. Et ídeo prudéntiam Maríæ haud ignáram mystérii cœléstis osténdit.

vivumenimverbumdeietvalidumetacutiusomni.en: For the word of God is living, and strong, and sharper than any most sharp sword, reaching even unto the division of the soul and the spirit, of the joints also and the marrow; it searcheth the thoughts of the heart and the secrets of minds, for all things are naked and open to the Son of God, whom the secrets of conscience deceive not.
vivumenimverbumdeietvalidumetacutiusomni.la: Vivum enim verbum Dei, et válidum, et acútius omni gládio acutíssimo, pénetrans usque ad divisiónem ánimæ et spíritus, ártuum quoque et medullárum, cogitatiónes cordis et secréta scrutátur animórum, quia nuda et apérta sunt ómnia Dei Fílio, quem consciéntiæ secréta non fallunt.

salvatoremexpectamusdominumnostrumiesumc.en: We look for the Saviour, our Lord Jesus Christ, who hath reformed the body of our lowliness, made like to the body of his glory.
salvatoremexpectamusdominumnostrumiesumc.la: Salvatórem expectámus Dóminum nostrum Jesum Christum, qui reformávit corpus humilitátis nostrae, configurátum córpori claritátis suae.

emitteagnumdominedominatoremterre.en: Send forth, O Lord, the Lamb, the ruler of the earth.

depetradesertiadmontemfiliesion.en: From Petra of the desert, to the mount of the daughter of Sion.
depetradesertiadmontemfiliesion.la: De Petra desérti ad montem fíliæ Sion.

tuexurgensdominemisereberission.en: Thou shalt arise, O Lord, * And have mercy on Sion.

quiatempusmiserendieiusquiavenittempus.en: For it is time to have mercy on it, for the time is come.
quiatempusmiserendieiusquiavenittempus.la: Quia tempus miseréndi ejus, quia venit tempus.

eccenunctempusacceptabileeccenuncdiessal.en: Behold, now is the acceptable time; behold, now is the day of salvation. Giving no offence to any man, that our ministry be not blamed.
eccenunctempusacceptabileeccenuncdiessal.la: Ecce nunc tempus acceptábile, ecce nunc dies salútis. Némini dantes ullam offensiónem, ut non vituperétur ministérium nostrum.

dicetdominosusceptormeusestuetrefugiumme.en: He shall say to the Lord: Thou art my protector, and my refuge.
dicetdominosusceptormeusestuetrefugiumme.la: Dicet Dómino: Suscéptor meus es tu, et refúgium meum.

deusmeussperaboineum.en: My God, in him will I trust.

adoremusdominumquinosredemitpercrucem.en: Let us adore the Lord, * Who hath redeemed us by the cross.
adoremusdominumquinosredemitpercrucem.la: Adorémus Dóminum, * Qui nos redémit per crucem.

christussemeloblatusestadmultorumexhauri.en: Christ was offered once to exhaust the sins of many: * the second time he shall appear without sin to them that expect him unto salvation.
christussemeloblatusestadmultorumexhauri.la: Christus semel oblátus est ad multórum exhauriénda peccáta: * secúndo sine peccáto apparébit expectántibus se, in salútem.

homopacismeeinquosperabam.en: The man of my peace, in whom I trusted.
homopacismeeinquosperabam.la: Homo pacis meæ in quo sperábam.

diviseruntsibivestimentamea.en: They part my garments among them.

etsupervestemmeammiseruntsortem.en: And cast lots upon my vesture.
etsupervestemmeammiseruntsortem.la: Et super vestem meam misérunt sortem.

insurrexeruntinmetestesiniqui.en: False witnesses are risen up against me.

dederuntinescammeamfel.en: They gave me gall for my food.

etinsitimeapotaveruntmeaceto.en: And in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.
etinsitimeapotaveruntmeaceto.la: Et in siti mea potavérunt me acéto.

sanctadeigenitrixvirgosempermariainterce.en: Holy Mother of God, Mary ever Virgin, intercede for us with the Lord our God. Alleluia, alleluia.
sanctadeigenitrixvirgosempermariainterce.la: Sancta Dei Génitrix, Virgo semper María, intercéde pro nobis ad Dóminum Deum nostrum. Allelúja, allelúja.

dessbenedictobernardetroberto.en: Of Saints Benedict, Bernard and Robert
dessbenedictobernardetroberto.la: De SS. Benedicto, Bernardo et Roberto

corporasanctoruminpacesepultasuntetviven.en: The bodies of the Saints are buried in peace, and their names shall live for evermore. Alleluia, alleluia.
corporasanctoruminpacesepultasuntetviven.la: Córpora Sanctórum in pace sepúlta sunt, et vivent nómina eórum in ætérnum. Allelúja, allelúja.

beatiquoselegistidominealleluia.en: Blessed are they whom thou hast chosen, O Lord. Alleluia.

habitabuntinatriistuisalleluia.en: They shall dwell in thy courts. Alleluia.

prestaquesumusomnipotensdeusutquisanctor.en: Grant, we beseech thee, almighty God: * that we who keep the commemoration of thy Saints Benedict, Bernard and Robert, may also imitate their virtues.
prestaquesumusomnipotensdeusutquisanctor.la: Præsta, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: * ut qui sanctórum tuórum Benedícti, Bernárdi et Robérti commemoratiónem cólimus,  eórum étiam virtútes imitémur.

quiadominusregnavitalignoalleluia.en: That the Lord reigneth from the tree, Alleluia
quiadominusregnavitalignoalleluia.la: Quia Dóminus regnávit a ligno, allelúia.

hodienobiscelorumrexdevirginenascidignat.en: This day the King of heaven deigned to be born for us of a Virgin, that he might call back lost man to the heavenly kingdom: The host of Angels rejoiceth:
hodienobiscelorumrexdevirginenascidignat.la: Hódie nobis cælórum Rex de Vírgine nasci dignátus est, ut hóminem pérditum ad cæléstia regna revocáret: Gaudet exércitus Angelórum:

quiasaluseternahumanogeneriapparuit.en: For eternal salvation hath appeared to mankind.
quiasaluseternahumanogeneriapparuit.la: Quia salus ætérna humáno géneri appáruit.

gloriainexcelsisdeetinterrapaxhominibusb.en: Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, to men of goodwill.
gloriainexcelsisdeetinterrapaxhominibusb.la: Glória in excélsis Deo, et in terra pax homínibus bonæ voluntátis.

unigenitumdeifiliumquempatermisitinmundu.en: The only-begotten Son of God, whom the Father sent into the world, the blessed Virgin conceived in her holy womb:
unigenitumdeifiliumquempatermisitinmundu.la: Unigénitum Dei Fílium, quem Pater misit in mundum, in útero sacro concépit Virgo beáta:

oquamgloriosumestregnuminquocumchristoga.en: O how glorious * is the kingdom, in which the Innocents rejoice with Christ; clothed in white robes, they follow the Lamb whithersoever he goeth.
oquamgloriosumestregnuminquocumchristoga.la: O quam * gloriósum est regnum, in quo cum Christo gaudent Innocéntes, amícti stolis albis sequúntur Agnum quocúmque íerit.

omnesdesabavenient.en: All they from Saba shall come.

aurumetthusdeferentesetlaudemdominiannun.en: Bringing gold and frankincense, and shewing forth praise to the Lord.
aurumetthusdeferentesetlaudemdominiannun.la: Aurum et thus deferéntes, et laudem Dómini annuntiántes.

adoratedominumalleluiainaulasancteiusall.en: O worship the Lord, * alleluia, in His holy temple, alleluia.
adoratedominumalleluiainaulasancteiusall.la: Adoráte Dóminum, * allelúja: in aula sancta ejus, allelúja. Ps. 95

adoratedominumalleluiaomnesangelieiusall.en: Adore the Lord, * alleluia: all ye his Angels, alleluia.
adoratedominumalleluiaomnesangelieiusall.la: Adoráte Dóminum, * allelúja: omnes Angeli ejus, allelúja. Ps. 96

interrogabatmagosherodesquodsignumvidist.en: Herod asked the Magi: What sign have ye seen over the new-born King? A great star shining,
interrogabatmagosherodesquodsignumvidist.la: Interrogábat Magos Heródes: Quod signum vidístis super natum Regem? Stellam magnam fulgéntem,

cuiussplendorilluminatmundumetnoscognovi.en: Whose brightness enlighteneth the world, and we have known it and are come to adore the Lord.
cuiussplendorilluminatmundumetnoscognovi.la: Cujus splendor illúminat mundum, et nos cognóvimus et vénimus adoráre Dóminum.

vidimusenimstellameiusinoriente.en: For we have seen his star in the East.
vidimusenimstellameiusinoriente.la: Vídimus enim stellam ejus in Oriénte.

magiveniuntaborienteierosolymamquerentes.en: The Magi come from the East to Jerusalem, seeking, and saying:
magiveniuntaborienteierosolymamquerentes.la: Magi véniunt ab Oriénte Jerosólymam, quæréntes, et dicéntes:

ubiestquinatusestcuiusstellamvidimusetve.en: Where is he that is born, whose star we have seen, and are come to adore the Lord?
ubiestquinatusestcuiusstellamvidimusetve.la: Ubi est qui natus est, cujus stellam vídimus, et vénimus adoráre Dóminum?

cumnatusessetiesusinbethlehemiudaindiebu.en: When Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Juda, in the days of king Herod, behold, there came wise men from the East to Jerusalem, saying:
cumnatusessetiesusinbethlehemiudaindiebu.la: Cum natus esset Jesus in Béthlehem Juda in diébus Herodis regis, ecce Magi ab Oriénte venérunt Jerosolymam, dicéntes:

stellaquamviderantmagiinorienteantecedeb.en: The star which the Magi had seen in the East went before them, until they came to the place where the child was: and seeing it,
stellaquamviderantmagiinorienteantecedeb.la: Stella, quam víderant Magi in Oriénte, antecedébat eos, donec venírent ad locum, ubi puer erat: vidéntes autem eam,

gavisisuntgaudiomagno.en: They rejoiced with exceeding great joy.

etintrantesdomuminveneruntpuerumcummaria.en: And when they were come into the house, they found the young Child with Mary His Mother, and fell down and worshipped Him.
etintrantesdomuminveneruntpuerumcummaria.la: Et intrántes domum, invenérunt púerum cum María matre ejus, et procidéntes adoravérunt eum.

videntesstellammagigavisisuntgaudiomagne.en: When the wise men saw the star, they rejoiced with exceeding great joy. And when they were come into the house, they found the young Child with Mary His Mother, and fell down and worshipped Him;
videntesstellammagigavisisuntgaudiomagne.la: Vidéntes stellam Magi, gavísi sunt gáudio magno, et intrántes domum invenérunt púerum cum María matre ejus, et procidéntes adoravérunt eum:

etapertisthesaurissuisobtulerunteimunera.en: And opening their treasures, they offered him gifts, gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
etapertisthesaurissuisobtulerunteimunera.la: Et apértis thesáuris suis obtulérunt ei múnera, aurum, thus, et myrrham.

aborienteveneruntmagiinbethlehemadorared.en: From the East came the Magi to Bethlehem to adore the Lord.
aborienteveneruntmagiinbethlehemadorared.la: Ab Oriénte venérunt Magi in Béthlehem adoráre Dóminum.

magivideruntstellametdixeruntadinvicemho.en: The Magi * saw the star, and said one to another: This is the sign of the great King: let us go and seek him, and offer him gifts, gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
magivideruntstellametdixeruntadinvicemho.la: Magi * vidérunt stellam, et dixérunt ad ínvicem: Hoc signum magni Regis est: eámus et inquirámus eum, et offerámus ei múnera, aurum, thus, et myrrham.

baptizatmilesregemservusdominumsuumioann.en: The soldier * baptizeth the King, the servant his Lord, John the Saviour: the water of the Jordan was astonished: the dove beareth witness: the Father's voice was heard: This is my Son.
baptizatmilesregemservusdominumsuumioann.la: Baptízat * miles Regem, servus Dóminum suum, Joánnes Salvatórem: aqua Jordánis stúpuit: colúmba protestátur: Patérna vox audíta est: Hic est Fílius meus.

veteremhominemrenovanssalvatorvenitadbap.en: Renewing the old man, * the Saviour cometh to baptism, that he might restore through water the nature that was corrupted: clothing us round about with an incorruptible garment.
veteremhominemrenovanssalvatorvenitadbap.la: Véterem hóminem * rénovans Salvátor venit ad baptísmum, ut natúram quæ corrúpta est, per aquam recuperáret: incorruptíbili veste circumamíctans nos.

tequiinspirituetignepurificashumanaconta.en: Thee, who in the Spirit * and in fire purifiest the defilements of men, we all glorify as God and Redeemer.
tequiinspirituetignepurificashumanaconta.la: Te, qui in spíritu * et igne puríficas humána contágia, Deum et Redemptórem omnes glorificámus.

baptistacontremitetnonaudettangeresanctu.en: The Baptist trembleth, * and dareth not touch the holy head of God, but crieth with trembling: Sanctify me, O Saviour.
baptistacontremitetnonaudettangeresanctu.la: Baptísta cóntremit, * et non audet tángere sanctum Dei vérticem, sed clamat cum tremóre: Sanctífica me, Salvátor.

caputdraconissalvatorconteruitiniordanef.en: The head of the dragon * the Saviour crushed in the river Jordan, and delivered all from his power.
caputdraconissalvatorconteruitiniordanef.la: Caput dracónis * Salvátor contéruit in Jordáne flúmine, ab ejus potestáte omnes erípuit.

magnummysteriumdeclaraturhodiequiacreato.en: A great mystery * is declared this day, for the Creator of all things in the Jordan washeth away our crimes.
magnummysteriumdeclaraturhodiequiacreato.la: Magnum mystérium * declarátur hódie, quia Creátor ómnium in Jordáne expúrgat nostra facínora.

precursorioannesexultatiniordanebaptizat.en: The Forerunner * John exulteth in the Jordan, the Lord being baptized: the whole world is made to rejoice: the remission of our sins is wrought, the waters being sanctified: let us all cry unto him: Have mercy on us.
precursorioannesexultatiniordanebaptizat.la: Præcúrsor * Joánnes exúltat in Jordáne baptizáto Dómino: facta est orbis terrárum exultátio: facta est peccatórum nostrórum remíssio sanctificátis aquis: ipsi omnes clamémus: Miserére nobis.

fontesaquarumsanctificatisuntchristoappa.en: The fountains of waters * are sanctified, Christ appearing in glory. O world, draw ye waters out of the fountains of the Saviour; for Christ our God hath now sanctified every creature.
fontesaquarumsanctificatisuntchristoappa.la: Fontes aquárum * sanctificáti sunt, Christo apparénte in glória. Orbis terrárum, hauríte aquas de fóntibus Salvatóris; sanctificávit enim nunc omnem creatúram Christus Deus noster.

hilariusinaquitanianobiligenerenatusdoct.en: Hilary, born of a noble family in Aquitaine, excelled in learning and eloquence. He first lived in marriage as it were the life of a monk: then, for his singular virtues, he was made Bishop of Poitiers. At which time the emperor Constantius was harassing the Catholics, unless they went over to the side of the Arians; Hilary, setting himself against the Arians as a most firm wall, stirred up their fury against himself.
hilariusinaquitanianobiligenerenatusdoct.la: Hilárius, in Aquitánia nóbili génere natus, doctrína et eloquéntia excélluit. Qui primum in matrimónio quasi mónachi vitam egit: deínde propter singuláres virtútes Pictavórum Epíscopus creátur. Quo témpore, Constántius imperátor Cathólicos vexábat, nisi ad Ariánas partes transírent; Hilárius tamquam firmíssimum murum se Ariánis oppónens, illórum furórem in se concitávit.

iuravitdominusetnonpenitebiteumtuessacer.en: The Lord hath sworn, and he will not repent: Thou art a priest for ever,
iuravitdominusetnonpenitebiteumtuessacer.la: Jurávit Dóminus, et non pœnitébit eum: Tu es sacérdos in ætérnum,

secundumordinemmelchisedech.en: According to the order of Melchisedech.

dixitdominusdominomeosedeadextrismeis.en: The Lord said unto my Lord Sit Thou at My right hand.
dixitdominusdominomeosedeadextrismeis.la: Dixit Dóminus Dómino meo, Sede a dextris meis.

itaquemultispetitusinsidiisinphrygiamrel.en: Wherefore, being assailed by many snares, he was banished into Phrygia; and four years after, when a Council was assembled at Seleucia, a city of Isauria, he was compelled to be present; and then, having gone to Constantinople, at last, the heretics being routed, he was sent back into Gaul. Thenceforth governing the Church of Poitiers in great tranquillity, he passed to heaven on the Ides of January, Valentinian and Valens being emperors, in the three hundred and sixty-ninth year after the birth of Christ.
itaquemultispetitusinsidiisinphrygiamrel.la: Itaque multis petítus insídiis, in Phrygiam relegátur et quadriénnio post coácto Concílio ad Seléuciam Isáuriæ urbem, adésse compéllitur, ac deínde Constantinópolim proféctus, novíssime, profligátis hæréticis, in Gállias remíssus est. Magna deínceps tranquillitáte Pictavórum Ecclésiam adminístrans, migrávit in cœlum Idibus Januárii, Valentiniáno et Valénte imperatóribus, anno post Christum natum trecentésimo sexagésimo nono.

misitdominusmanumsuamettetigitoseius.en: The Lord put forth his hand, and touched his mouth:
misitdominusmanumsuamettetigitoseius.la: Misit Dóminus manum suam, et tétigit os ejus:

commemoratiosguariniepiscopietconfessori.en: Commemoration of St. Guarinus, Bishop and Confessor
commemoratiosguariniepiscopietconfessori.la: Commemoratio S. Guarini, Episcopi et Confessoris

eugeserveboneetfidelisquiainpaucafuistif.en: Well done, thou good and faithful servant * thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things, saith the Lord.
eugeserveboneetfidelisquiainpaucafuistif.la: Euge, serve bone * et fidélis, quia in pauca fuísti fidélis, supra multa te constítuam, dicit Dóminus.

quiindiebussuisplacuitdeetinventusestius.en: Who in his days pleased God, and was found just.
quiindiebussuisplacuitdeetinventusestius.la: Qui in diébus suis plácuit Deo, et invéntus est justus.

deusquiecclesiamtuamdispositionemirabili.en: O God, who by a wonderful disposition dost ever enlighten thy Church with the new splendours of thy Saints: grant, we beseech thee, that we who rejoice in the solemnity of blessed Guarinus, thy Confessor and Bishop, may happily be brought unto his fellowship.
deusquiecclesiamtuamdispositionemirabili.la: Deus, qui Ecclésiam tuam dispositióne mirábili, novis semper illústras Sanctórum splendóribus: tríbue, quǽsumus; ut, qui beáti Guaríni, Confessóris tui atque Pontíficis, solémniis gratulámur, ad ejus consórtium felíciter perducámur.

sacerdosetpontifexetvirtutumopifexpastor.en: O thou Priest and Bishop, * thou worker of mighty works, thou good shepherd over God’s people, pray for us unto the Lord.
sacerdosetpontifexetvirtutumopifexpastor.la: Sacérdos et Póntifex, * et virtútum ópifex, pastor bone in pópulo, ora pro nobis Dóminum.

maurusnobilisromanuspuerapatreeutychiode.en: Maurus, a noble Roman, offered to God as a boy by his father Eutychius under the discipline of St. Benedict, in a short time made such progress by divine grace that he was an object of admiration to the Master himself; who often set him before the other disciples to imitate, as a pattern of regular observance and of all the virtues. For when the monk Placidus had fallen into the lake and was being carried away by the force of the waters, Maurus, running at the command of the holy Father, and walking upon the waters, seized his companion by the hair and drew him to land.
maurusnobilisromanuspuerapatreeutychiode.la: Maurus nóbilis Románus, puer a patre Eutychio Deo sub sancti Benedícti disciplína oblátus, brevi tantum divína grátia profécit, ut ipsi Magístro admiratióni esset; qui illum sæpe, véluti reguláris observántiæ et virtútum ómnium spécimen, céteris discípulis ad imitándum proponébat. Nam cum Plácidus Mónachus in lacum prolápsus, aquárum ímpetu raperétur, sancti Patris jussu accúrrens Maurus, et super aquas incédens, sócium capíllis apprehénsum, ad terram attráxit.

continentietantefuitutperquadragesimambi.en: He was of such abstinence that during Lent he took food but twice in the week, and that most sparingly. He took his sleep standing, or, when excessive weariness had overcome him, sitting upon a heap of lime and sand spread with a haircloth. Being sent into Gaul by the same St. Benedict, he built a famous Monastery, over which he presided forty years, and wonderfully spread the monastic discipline. At length, renowned for holiness and miracles, being more than seventy years of age, he passed to heaven, about the year of salvation five hundred and sixty-five.
continentietantefuitutperquadragesimambi.la: Continéntiæ tantæ fuit, ut per Quadragésimam bis tantum in hebdómada, et quidem parcíssime, cibum súmeret. Somnum stando, vel cum nímia eum lassitúdo compulísset, sedéndo super aggéstum calcis et sábuli strato cilício, capiébat. Missus in Gálliam ab eódem sancto Benedícto, célebri Monastério exstrúcto, cui annos quadragínta præfuit, monásticam disciplínam mirífice propagávit. Dénique sanctitáte et miráculis clarus, septuagenário major migrávit in cœlum, anno salútis círciter quingentésimo sexagésimo quinto.

obeativirinsanctapreconiaoinestimabilisd.en: O holy praises of the blessed man N., O inestimable love of charity!
obeativirinsanctapreconiaoinestimabilisd.la: O beáti viri N. sancta præcónia, o inæstimábilis diléctio charitátis!

quidumseculipompamcontempsiteterneviteco.en: Who, while he despised the pomp of the world, was joined to life eternal.
quidumseculipompamcontempsiteterneviteco.la: Qui, dum sæculi pompam contémpsit, ætérnæ vitæ conjúnctus est.

antoniusegyptiusnobilibusetchristianispa.en: Anthony of Egypt, born of noble and Christian parents, of whom he was bereaved as a youth, when, having entered the Church, he had heard from the Gospel: If thou wilt be perfect, go, and sell all that thou hast, and give to the poor; judged that he must obey Christ the Lord as though these words had been said to himself. Wherefore, having sold his estate, he distributed all the money to the poor. Freed from these hindrances, he resolved to lead on earth a kind of heavenly life. None was more abstinent than he, none more watchful. In patience, meekness, mercy, humility, labour, and the study of the divine Scriptures, he surpassed all. He so shrank from meeting and conversing with heretics, especially the Arians, that he said one ought not even to go near them. Lying on the ground, he took the briefest sleep: he so kept fasting that he used only salt with his bread, quenched his thirst with water, and did not refresh himself with food or drink before sunset: often also he abstained from food for two days; very often he passed the night in prayer.
antoniusegyptiusnobilibusetchristianispa.la: Antónius Ægyptius, nobílibus et Christiánis paréntibus natus, quibus adoléscens orbátus est, cum ingréssus Ecclésiam audivísset ex Evangelio: Si vis perféctus esse, vade, et vende ómnia quæ habes, et da paupéribus; tamquam ea sibi dicta essent, sic Christo Dómino obtemperándum existimávit. Itaque, véndita re familiári, pecúniam omnem paupéribus distríbuit. Quibus solútus impediméntis, cœléstis vitæ genus in terris cólere instítuit. Nihil eo continéntius, nihil vigilántius erat. Patiéntia, mansuetúdine, misericórdia, humilitáte, labóre, ac stúdio divinárum litterárum, superábat omnes. Ab hæreticórum, máxime Arianórum congréssu et collóquio sic abhorrébat, ut ne prope quidem ad eos accedéndum díceret. Humi jacens, brevíssimum capiébat somnum: jejúnium ádeo cóluit, ut salem tantúmmodo ad panem adhibéret, sitim aqua exstíngueret, neque se ante solis occásum cibo aut potu recreáret: sæpe étiam bíduo cibo abstinébat; sæpíssime in oratióne pernoctábat.

itaquecontulitseinvastissimamegyptisolit.en: Wherefore he betook himself into the vast wilderness of Egypt, where, daily advancing in Christian perfection, he became so dreadful to the devils that many in Egypt who were troubled by them were set free by calling upon the name of Anthony. And so great was his fame for holiness that Constantine the Great and his sons commended themselves by letter to his prayers. At length, in his hundred and fifth year, when he had countless imitators of his way of life, having called together the Monks and instructed them in the perfect rule of Christian life, renowned for holiness and miracles, he passed to heaven.
itaquecontulitseinvastissimamegyptisolit.la: Itaque cóntulit se in vastíssimam Ægypti solitúdinem, ubi quotídie in Christiána perfectióne profíciens, ita dæmónibus evásit formidolósus, ut multi in Ægypto ab illis agitáti, invocáto nómine Antónii liberaréntur. Tanta autem erat ejus fama sanctitátis, ut per lítteras se ejus oratiónibus Constantínus Magnus et fílii commendárent. Qui tandem quintum et centésimum annum agens, cum innumerábiles sui institúti imitatóres habéret, convocátis Mónachis, et ad perféctam Christiánæ vitæ régulam instrúctis, sanctitáte et miraculis clarus, migrávit in cœlum.

quodcumqueligaverissuperterrameritligatu.en: Whatsoever thou shalt bind upon earth, it shall be bound also in heaven;
quodcumqueligaverissuperterrameritligatu.la: Quodcúmque ligáveris super terram, erit ligátum et in cælis;

etquodcumquesolverissuperterrameritsolut.en: And whatsoever thou shalt loose upon earth, it shall be loosed also in heaven.
etquodcumquesolverissuperterrameritsolut.la: Et quodcúmque sólveris super terram, erit solútum et in cælis.

tuespetrusetsuperhancpetramedificabeccle.en: Thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my Church, and I will give to thee the keys of the kingdom of heaven.
tuespetrusetsuperhancpetramedificabeccle.la: Tu es Petrus, et super hanc petram ædificábo Ecclésiam meam, et tibi dabo claves regni cælórum.

petrusquidemservabaturincarcere.en: Peter therefore was kept in prison;

oratioautemfiebatsineintermissioneabeccl.en: But prayer was made without ceasing by the Church unto God for him.
oratioautemfiebatsineintermissioneabeccl.la: Orátio autem fiébat sine intermissióne ab Ecclésia ad Deum pro eo.

eratpetrusdormiensinterduosmilitesvinctu.en: Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains:
eratpetrusdormiensinterduosmilitesvinctu.la: Erat Petrus dórmiens inter duos mílites, vinctus caténis duábus:

nuncsciovereaitpetrusadsereversus.en: Now I know in very deed, said Peter, coming to himself:
nuncsciovereaitpetrusadsereversus.la: Nunc scio vere, ait Petrus ad se revérsus:

quiamisitdominusangelumsuum.en: That the Lord hath sent his Angel.

eteripuitmedemanuherodisetdeomniexspecta.en: And hath delivered me out of the hand of Herod, and from all the expectation of the people of the Jews.
eteripuitmedemanuherodisetdeomniexspecta.la: Et erípuit me de manu Heródis et de omni exspectatióne plebis Judæórum.

egoproterogavipetre.en: Peter, I have prayed for thee,

utnondeficiatfidestuettualiquandoconvers.en: That thy faith fail not; And when thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren.
utnondeficiatfidestuettualiquandoconvers.la: Ut non defíciat fides tua: et tu aliquándo convérsus confírma fratres tuos.

eccesatanasexpetivitvosutcribraretsicutt.en: Behold, Satan hath desired to have you, that he may sift you as wheat, but I have prayed for thee.
eccesatanasexpetivitvosutcribraretsicutt.la: Ecce sátanas expetívit vos, ut cribráret sicut tríticum, ego autem rogávi pro te.

corneliuscenturiovirreligiosusactimensde.en: Cornelius the Centurion, a religious man, and fearing God, saw manifestly an Angel of God, saying to him:
corneliuscenturiovirreligiosusactimensde.la: Cornélius Centúrio, vir religiósus, ac timens Deum, vidit maniféste Angelum Dei, dicéntem sibi:

cornelimitteetaccersisimonemquicognomina.en: Cornelius, send and call hither Simon, who is surnamed Peter; he will tell thee what thou must do.
cornelimitteetaccersisimonemquicognomina.la: Cornéli, mitte et accérsi Simónem, qui cognominátur Petrus; hic dicet tibi quid te opórteat fácere.

cumorassetcorneliusnonduminchristorenatu.en: When Cornelius had prayed, being not yet born again in Christ, an Angel appeared to him, saying:
cumorassetcorneliusnonduminchristorenatu.la: Cum orásset Cornélius, nondum in Christo renátus, appáruit ei Angelus, dicens:

deepistolabeatipauliapostoliadtitum.en: Lesson from the letter of St. Paul the Apostle to Titus
deepistolabeatipauliapostoliadtitum.la: De Epístola beáti Pauli Apóstoli ad Titum.

oportetepiscopumsinecrimineessesicutdeid.en: For a bishop must be without crime, as the steward of God: not proud, not subject to anger, not given to wine, no striker, not greedy of filthy lucre:
oportetepiscopumsinecrimineessesicutdeid.la: Opórtet Epíscopum sine crímine esse, sicut Dei dispensatórem: non supérbum, non iracúndum, non vinoléntum, non percussórem, non turpis lucri cúpidum:

sedhospitalembenignumsobriumiustumsanctu.en: But given to hospitality, gentle, sober, just, holy, continent:
sedhospitalembenignumsobriumiustumsanctu.la: sed hospitálem, benígnum, sóbrium, justum, sanctum, continéntem,

amplectentemeumquisecundumdoctrinamestfi.en: Embracing that faithful word which is according to doctrine, that he may be able to exhort in sound doctrine, and to convince the gainsayers.
amplectentemeumquisecundumdoctrinamestfi.la: amplecténtem eum, qui secúndum doctrínam est, fidélem sermónem: ut potens sit exhortári in doctrína sana, et eos, qui contradícunt‚ argúere.

beatusgulielmusaprimevaetateavunculosuos.en: Blessed William was from his earliest years entrusted by his parents to his uncle, the Archdeacon of Soissons, to be formed in manners and learning. After this, having been made a Canon, and longing to flee the hurtful allurements of the world, he betook himself to the hermitage of Grandmont: whence, providing for the greater security of his soul, he passed to the Monastery of Pontigny of the Cistercian Order. Made Abbot first of Fontaine-Jean, then of Chaalis, he was at length elected Primate of the Church of Bourges. Placed in the height of this dignity, he kept, together with his outward habit and the former austerity of his fare, the same humility of mind, earnestness in prayer, and holiness of life as before.
beatusgulielmusaprimevaetateavunculosuos.la: Beátus Guliélmus, a primæva ætáte avúnculo suo Suessionénsi Archidiácono a paréntibus tráditus est, móribus et lítteris informándus. Post hæc Canónicus efféctus, et nóxia sæculi blandiménta fúgere géstiens, ad Grandimonténsem erémum convolávit: unde majóri ánimi securitáti cónsulens, ad Pontiniacénse Cisterciénsis Ordinis Monastérium se tránstulit. Primo Fontis Joánnis, deínde Carolíloci Abbas efféctus, tandem in Primátem Bituricénsis Ecclésiæ eléctus est. In hujus dignitátis fastígio collocátus, simul cum exterióri hábitu, ac pristína victus austeritáte, eámdem mentis humilitátem, oratiónum instántiam, morúmque sanctitátem, quam ántea, retínuit.

fuitipsiuspauperesmisericordiexuberanser.en: His mercy toward the poor was overflowing; his charity toward all the afflicted singular; his patience in bearing contradictions and persecutions wonderful; lastly, his zeal for the defence of the Catholic truth admirable, so that even when worn out with old age he prepared an expedition against the Albigensian heretics, and would have fulfilled his desires, had he not been hindered by ill health of body. As the sickness grew heavier, since he knew for certain the day of his death, he took care to be fortified betimes with the protection of the Sacraments; and in the following night, the Office of Matins being ended, which he had commanded to be sung in his presence, having laid aside his Pontifical vestments, he laid himself by his own effort upon the ground, and, having given the sign of the cross to those standing by, happily gave up his spirit.
fuitipsiuspauperesmisericordiexuberanser.la: Fuit ipsíus páuperes misericórdia exúberans; erga omnes afflíctos singuláris cháritas; in sustinéndis contradictiónibus, et persecutiónibus mira patiéntia; dénique pro Cathólicæ veritátis defensióne zelus admirábilis, ita ut étiam sénio conféctus contra hæréticos Albigénses profectiónem paráret, votísque fecísset satis, nisi advérsa córporis valetúdine præpedítus fuísset. Ingravescénte morbo cum óbitus sui diem certo præscíret, se Sacramentórum præsídio matúre præmuníri curávit, ac nocte subsequénte, compléto matutináli Offício, quod coram se cantári jússerat, depósitis Pontificálibus vestiméntis, se próprio nisu depónens in terram, signáculo crucis adstántibus colláto, felíciter emísit spíritum.

fidelisnamqueacprudensdispensatorinmagni.en: For he had been set as a faithful and wise steward in the house of the great householder,
fidelisnamqueacprudensdispensatorinmagni.la: Fidélis namque, ac prudens dispensátor in magni patrisfamílias domo constitútus erat,

utconservissuisintemporemensuramtriticie.en: To give his fellow servants their measure of wheat in due season.
utconservissuisintemporemensuramtriticie.la: Ut consérvis suis in témpore mensúram trítici erogáret.

prosaluteetaugmentogregissibicommissicur.en: For the salvation and increase of the flock committed to him he was solicitous with watchful care:
prosaluteetaugmentogregissibicommissicur.la: Pro salúte, et augménto gregis sibi commíssi cura pervígili sollícitus erat:

etcandidaseasfeceruntinsanguineagni.en: And have made them white in the blood of the Lamb.
etcandidaseasfeceruntinsanguineagni.la: Et cándidas eas fecérunt in sánguine Agni.

istisuntquiveneruntexmagnatribulationeet.en: These are they who are come out of great tribulation, and have washed their robes:
istisuntquiveneruntexmagnatribulationeet.la: Isti sunt qui venérunt ex magna tribulatióne, et lavérunt stolas suas:

ingressaagnesturpitudinislocumangelumdom.en: Agnes entered * the place of shame, and found the Angel of the Lord ready.
ingressaagnesturpitudinislocumangelumdom.la: Ingréssa Agnes * turpitúdinis locum, Angelum Dómini præparátum invénit. Ps. 109

mecumenimhabeocustodemcorporismeiangelum.en: For I have with me * an Angel of the Lord to keep my body.
mecumenimhabeocustodemcorporismeiangelum.la: Mecum enim hábeo * custódem córporis mei, Angelum Dómini. Ps. 112

annulosuosubarrhavitmedominusmeusiesusch.en: With his ring hath my Lord Jesus Christ * espoused me, and as a bride hath he adorned me with a crown.
annulosuosubarrhavitmedominusmeusiesusch.la: Annulo suo subarrhávit me * Dóminus meus Jesus Christus, et tamquam sponsam decorávit me coróna. Ps. 121

benedicotepaterdominimeiiesuchristiquiap.en: I bless thee, * O Father of my Lord Jesus Christ, that through thy Son the fire is quenched at my side.
benedicotepaterdominimeiiesuchristiquiap.la: Benedíco te, * Pater Dómini mei Jesu Christi, quia per Fílium tuum ignis extínctus est a látere meo. Ps. 126

congaudetemecumetcongratulaminiquiacumhi.en: Rejoice with me * and make merry, because I also have received a throne in light among all these.
congaudetemecumetcongratulaminiquiacumhi.la: Congaudéte mecum * et congratulámini, quia cum his ómnibus lúcidas sedes accépi. Ps. 146

christivirgonecterroreconcutiturnecbland.en: The Virgin of Christ * is neither shaken by terror, nor seduced by flatteries.
christivirgonecterroreconcutiturnecbland.la: Christi Virgo * nec terróre concútitur, nec blandiméntis sedúcitur.

stansadextriseiusagnusnivecandidiorchris.en: Standing at her right hand, * the Lamb whiter than snow, Christ, hath consecrated her to himself as his spouse and Martyr.
stansadextriseiusagnusnivecandidiorchris.la: Stans a dextris ejus * Agnus nive candídior, Christus sibi sponsam et Mártyrem consecrávit. Ps. 96

misitdominusangelumsuumetliberavitmedeme.en: The Lord hath sent * his Angel, and hath delivered me from the midst of the fire, and I was not burned.
misitdominusangelumsuumetliberavitmedeme.la: Misit Dóminus * Angelum suum, et liberávit me de médio ignis, et non sum æstuáta. Ps. 97

iamamplexibuschristicastisadstrictasumet.en: Now am I bound * in the chaste embraces of Christ, and united to his body.
iamamplexibuschristicastisadstrictasumet.la: Jam ampléxibus Christi * castis adstrícta sum, et córpori ejus sociáta sum. Ps. 98

venisponsachristiaccipecoronamquamtibido.en: Come, Spouse of Christ, receive the crown which the Lord hath prepared for thee,
venisponsachristiaccipecoronamquamtibido.la: Veni Sponsa Christi, áccipe corónam, quam tibi Dóminus præparávit,

procuiusamoresanguinemtuumfudistietcuman.en: For whose love thou didst shed thy blood, and didst enter into paradise with the Angels.
procuiusamoresanguinemtuumfudistietcuman.la: Pro cujus amóre sánguinem tuum fudísti, et cum Ángelis in paradísum introísti.

afferenturregivirginesposteamproximeeius.en: After her shall virgins be brought to the King, her neighbours shall be brought to thee,
afferenturregivirginesposteamproximeeius.la: Afferéntur Regi Vírgines post eam, próximæ ejus afferéntur tibi,

prudentesvirginesaptatelampadesvestrasec.en: Ye wise Virgins, trim your lamps: behold, the bridegroom cometh, go ye forth to meet him:
prudentesvirginesaptatelampadesvestrasec.la: Prudéntes Vírgines, aptáte lámpades vestras: ecce sponsus venit, exíte óbviam ei:

ornavitinestimabilidextrochiriodexteramm.en: He hath adorned my right hand with a bracelet beyond price, and hath girded my neck with precious stones.
ornavitinestimabilidextrochiriodexteramm.la: Ornávit inæstimábili dextrochírio déxteram meam, collúmque meum cinxit lapídibus pretiósis.

vincentiusosceinhispaniaciteriorenatussa.en: Vincent, born at Huesca in Hither Spain, learned the sacred Scriptures from Valerius, Bishop of Saragossa, whose office of preaching the Gospel he also took upon himself. This being reported to Dacian, he was ordered to be brought in chains to Valencia: where, having overcome scourges, the rack, the gridiron, iron hooks, red-hot plates, broken potsherds, the filth of the prison, the cruelty of the torturers, and the fury and the blandishments of the tyrant, he flew as a victor to the heavenly crown of martyrdom.
vincentiusosceinhispaniaciteriorenatussa.la: Vincéntius, Oscæ in Hispánia citerióre natus, sacras lítteras a Valério Cæsaraugustáno Epíscopo didicit: cujus etiam partes suscépit prædicándi Evangélium. Ea re ad Daciánum deláta, vinctus Valéntiam addúci jubétur: ubi verbéribus, equúleo, cratícula, férreis únguibus, candéntibus láminis, testáceis fragméntis, cárceris squalóribus, tortórum immanitáte, tyranníque furóribus et blandítiis superátis, victor ad cœléstem martyrii corónam advolávit.

anastasiuspersamonachusheraclioimperator.en: Anastasius, a Persian monk, in the time of the emperor Heraclius, having visited the holy land of Jerusalem, constantly endured chains and scourges at Caesarea in Palestine for the religion of Christ. Soon after, being subjected to divers torments by the Persians for the same cause, he was beheaded with the axe by king Chosroes, together with seventy other Christians.
anastasiuspersamonachusheraclioimperator.la: Anastásius Persa, mónachus, Heraclío imperatóre, cum sanctam Jerosolymórum terram visitásset, ad Cæsaréam Palæstínæ pro Christi religióne víncula et vérbera constánter perpéssus est. Mox a Persis ob eámdem causam váriis cruciátibus afféctus, a rege Chósroa, una cum septuagínta áliis Christiánis secúri percútitur.

egoplantaviapollorigavitdeusautemincreme.en: I have planted, * Apollos watered, but God gave the increase, alleluia.
egoplantaviapollorigavitdeusautemincreme.la: Ego plantávi, * Apollo rigávit, Deus autem increméntum dedit, allelúja.

gratiadeiinmevacuanonfuitsedgratieiussem.en: The grace of God * in me hath not been void, but his grace abideth in me always.
gratiadeiinmevacuanonfuitsedgratieiussem.la: Grátia Dei * in me vácua non fuit, sed grátia ejus semper in me manet.

tervirgiscesussumsemellapidatussumternau.en: Thrice was I beaten with rods, * once was I stoned, thrice I suffered shipwreck, for Christ's name's sake.
tervirgiscesussumsemellapidatussumternau.la: Ter virgis cæsus sum, * semel lapidátus sum, ter naufrágium pértuli pro Christi nómine.

damasciprepositusgentisareteregisvoluitm.en: In Damascus the governor * under Aretas the king was desirous to apprehend me; by the brethren in a basket was I let down by the wall, and so escaped I his hands, in the name of the Lord.
damasciprepositusgentisareteregisvoluitm.la: Damásci, præpósitus * gentis Arétæ regis vóluit me comprehéndere: a frátribus per murum demíssus sum in sporta, et sic evási manus ejus in nómine Dómini.

libentergloriaborininfirmitatibusmeisuti.en: Gladly will I glory * in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may dwell in me.
libentergloriaborininfirmitatibusmeisuti.la: Libénter gloriábor * in infirmitátibus meis, ut inhábitet in me virtus Christi.

vadeananietqueresaulumecceenimoratquiava.en: Ananias, go thy way * and seek Saul for, behold, he prayeth for he is a chosen vessel unto Me, to bear My name before the Gentiles, and kings, and the children of Israel.
vadeananietqueresaulumecceenimoratquiava.la: Vade, Ananía, * et quære Saulum, ecce enim orat; quia vas electiónis est mihi, ut portet nomen meum coram géntibus et régibus et fíliis Israël. Ps. 253, 254, 255

quioperatusestpetroinapostolatumoperatus.en: He who wrought in Peter to the apostleship, wrought in me also among the Gentiles: and they knew the grace of God,
quioperatusestpetroinapostolatumoperatus.la: Qui operátus est Petro in apostolátum, operátus est et mihi inter Gentes: et cognovérunt grátiam Dei,

sciocuicredidietcertussumquiapotensestde.en: I know Whom I have believed, and am persuaded that He is able to keep that which I have committed unto Him against that day.
sciocuicredidietcertussumquiapotensestde.la: Scio cui crédidi, et certus sum, quia potens est depósitum meum serváre in illum diem.

repositestmihicoronaiustitiequamreddetmi.en: There is laid up for me a crown of justice, which the Lord will render to me at that day.
repositestmihicoronaiustitiequamreddetmi.la: Repósita est mihi coróna justítiæ, quam reddet mihi Dóminus in illum diem.

abundantiusemulatorextititraditionumpate.en: I was more abundantly zealous for the traditions of my fathers.
abundantiusemulatorextititraditionumpate.la: Abundántius æmulátor éxtiti traditiónum paternárum meárum.

cumautemplacuiteiquimesegregavitexuterom.en: But when it pleased him, who separated me from my mother's womb, and called me by his grace, to reveal his Son in me,
cumautemplacuiteiquimesegregavitexuterom.la: Cum autem plácuit ei, qui me segregávit ex útero matris meæ, et vocávit per grátiam suam, ut reveláret Fílium suum per me,

utevangelizaremillumingentibus.en: That I might preach him among the Gentiles.

continuononacquievicarnietsanguininequev.en: Immediately I condescended not to flesh and blood, neither went I to Jerusalem to the Apostles who were before me,
continuononacquievicarnietsanguininequev.la: Contínuo non acquiévi carni et sánguini, neque veni Jerosólymam ad antecessóres meos Apóstolos,

saulusautemmagisacmagisconvalescebatetco.en: But Saul increased much more in strength, and confounded the Jews who dwelt at Damascus:
saulusautemmagisacmagisconvalescebatetco.la: Saulus autem magis ac magis convalescébat, et confundébat Judæos, qui habitábant Damásci:

affirmansquoniamhicestchristus.en: Affirming that this is the Christ.

etcontinuoingressuspaulussynagogampredic.en: And immediately Paul, entering into the synagogue, preached Jesus;
etcontinuoingressuspaulussynagogampredic.la: Et contínuo ingréssus Paulus synagógam prædicábat Jesum;

nemagnitudorevelationumextollatmedatuses.en: Lest the greatness of the revelations should exalt me, there was given me a sting of my flesh, an angel of Satan, to buffet me: for which thing thrice I besought the Lord that it might depart from me, and the Lord said to me: My grace is sufficient for thee, Paul.
nemagnitudorevelationumextollatmedatuses.la: Ne magnitúdo revelatiónum extóllat me, datus est mihi stímulus carnis meæ, ángelus sátanæ, qui me colaphízet: propter quod ter Dóminum rogávi ut auferrétur a me, et dixit mihi Dóminus: Súfficit tibi, Paule, grátia mea.

namvirtusininfirmitateperficitur.en: For power is made perfect in infirmity.

libenterigiturgloriaborininfirmitatibusm.en: Gladly therefore will I glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may dwell in me.
libenterigiturgloriaborininfirmitatibusm.la: Libénter ígitur gloriábor in infirmitátibus meis, ut inhábitet in me virtus Christi.

gratiamsupernebenedictionisexpostuletnob.en: May St. Paul, the vessel of election, obtain for us the grace of heavenly blessing.
gratiamsupernebenedictionisexpostuletnob.la: Grátiam supérnæ benedictiónis expóstulet nobis sanctus Paulus vas electiónis.

sanctepauleapostolepredicatorveritatiset.en: O Holy Apostle Paul, Preacher of the truth, and teacher of the Gentiles,
sanctepauleapostolepredicatorveritatiset.la: Sancte Paule Apóstole, prædicátor veritátis et Doctor Géntium,

intercedepronobisaddeumquiteelegit.en: Pray for us to God Who hath chosen thee.
intercedepronobisaddeumquiteelegit.la: Intercéde pro nobis ad Deum, qui te elégit.

utdigniefficiamurgratiadei.en: That we may be made worthy of the grace of God

evangeliummeumquodevangelizatumestnonest.en: My Gospel, * which was preached, is not from me, neither did I receive it of man, but by the revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ.
evangeliummeumquodevangelizatumestnonest.la: Evangélium meum, * quod evangelizátum est, non est a me, neque ab hómine accépi illud, sed per revelatiónem Dómini nostri Jesu Christi.

exparvexordiocenobiietordiniscisterciens.en: From the Little Exordium of the Monastery and Order of Citeaux
exparvexordiocenobiietordiniscisterciens.la: Ex parvo Exordio Cœnobii et Ordinis Cisterciensis

viduatasuopastorerobertocisterciensisecc.en: The Church of Citeaux, bereaved of its Pastor (Robert), assembled, and by regular election promoted to be its Abbot a certain brother, Alberic by name; a man, to wit, lettered, well versed in things divine and human, a lover of the Rule and of the brethren, who had long held the office of Prior both in the Church of Molesme and in that one, and had laboured much and long in striving that they might remove from Molesme to that place, and for this business had suffered many reproaches, prison and stripes.
viduatasuopastorerobertocisterciensisecc.la: Viduáta suo Pastóre (Robérto) Cisterciénsis Ecclésia convénit ac regulári electióne quemdam fratrem, Alberícum nómine, in Abbátem sibi promóvit; virum scílicet litterátum, in divínis et humánis satis gnarum, amatórem régulae et fratrum, quique Prióris offícium, et in Molisménsi, et in illa diútius gerébat Ecclésia, multúmque diu niténdo laboráverat‚ ut ad illum de Molísmo transmigrárent locum, et pro hoc negótio multa oppróbria, cárcerem et vérbera perpéssus fúerat.

dehincsanctusabbasetfratreseiusnonimmemo.en: Thereafter the holy Abbot and his brethren, not unmindful of their promise, unanimously resolved to establish the Rule of blessed Benedict in that place and to keep it; rejecting from themselves whatsoever, as well in food as in clothing, was contrary to the purity of the Rule; and so, having put off the old man, they rejoiced that they had put on the new, so that, despising the riches of the world, they began, with the poor Christ, to be poor soldiers of Christ; insomuch that almost all, seeing and hearing the unwonted and as it were unheard-of austerity of their life, hastened rather to keep themselves far from them in heart and body than to draw near to them, and ceased not to waver concerning their perseverance.
dehincsanctusabbasetfratreseiusnonimmemo.la: Dehinc sanctus Abbas et fratres ejus non immémores sponsiónis suæ, Régulam beáti Benedícti in illo loco ordináre, et unanímiter statuérunt tenére; rejiciéntes a se quidquid tam in victu quam in vestítu puritáti Régulæ adversabátur; sicque exúti véterem hóminem, novum se induísse gaudébant, ita ut, spretis sæculi divítiis, cœperint cum páupere Christo esse páuperes Christi mílites, in tantum ut fere omnes vidéntes et audiéntes vitæ eórum asperitátem insolítam, et quasi inaudítam plus corde et córpore elongáre, quam eis approximáre se festinábant‚ et de perseverántia ipsórum titubáre non cessábant.

seddeimisericordiaquihancmilitiamspiritu.en: But the mercy of God, who inspired this spiritual warfare in his own, ceased not afterward to enlarge and perfect it excellently to the profit of many. And the man of the Lord Alberic, having been happily exercised in regular discipline in the school of Christ for nine years and a half, passed to the Lord on the seventh day before the Kalends of February, in the year of the Lord one thousand one hundred and seven, glorious in faith and virtues, and therefore deservedly to be made blessed by God in life eternal; to whom succeeded a certain brother, Stephen by name, an Englishman by nation, who had himself also come with the others from Molesme, and who was a lover of the Rule and of the place.
seddeimisericordiaquihancmilitiamspiritu.la: Sed Dei misericórdia, qui hanc milítiam spirituálem suis inspirávit, ad multórum proféctum egrégie eam póstea amplificáre et consummáre non cessávit. Vir autem Domini Alberícus in schola Christi per novem annos et dimídium regulári disciplína felíciter exercitátus, migrávit ad Dóminum séptimo Kaléndas Februárii anno Dómini millésimo centésimo séptimo‚ fide et virtútibus gloriósus et ídeo in vita ætérna a Deo mérito beándus; cui succéssit quidam frater Stéphanus nómine, Anglus natióne, qui et ipse cum áliis de Molísmo advénerat, quique amátor Régulæ et loci erat.

ioannesantiochenuscognomentochrysostomus.en: John of Antioch, surnamed Chrysostom, turned from the law courts to the sacred Scriptures. Having been made a Priest, upon the death of Nectarius, by the efforts of the emperor Arcadius, he was set against his will over the Church of Constantinople. Having taken up this pastoral charge, and rebuking very vehemently the depraved morals of men, he was cast into exile at the instigation of Eudoxia, and was recalled thence a little after, and afterward was again driven out.
ioannesantiochenuscognomentochrysostomus.la: Joánnes Antiochénus, cognoménto Chrysóstomus, a forénsibus ad divínas lítteras se cóntulit. Présbyter factus, mórtuo Nectário, Arcádii imperatóris opera, invítus Constantinopolitánæ Ecclésiæ præfícitur. Quo suscépto pastoráli múnere, et depravátos hóminum mores veheméntius objúrgans, niténte Eudóxia, ejícitur in exílium, indéque paulo post revocátur, iterúmque postea expéllitur.

incredibileestquantamalaperpessussitinex.en: It is incredible how many evils he endured in exile, and how many he converted to the faith of Jesus Christ. By the soldiers who guarded him he was afflicted on the journey with wonderful hardships and calamities. And when he was being led through Armenia, the holy Martyr Basiliscus, in whose church he had prayed before, thus spoke to him in the night: Brother John, to-morrow shall join us in one place. Wherefore on the next day, having received the Sacrament of the Eucharist, and fortifying himself with the sign of the cross, he gave up his soul to God on the eighteenth day before the Kalends of October. And four days after, the Empress departed this life.
incredibileestquantamalaperpessussitinex.la: Incredíbile est, quanta mala perpéssus sit in exílio, et quam multos ad Jesu Christi fidem convérterit. A milítibus, qui eum custodiébant, miris in itínere malis et calamitátibus affícitur. Cumque per Arméniam ducerétur, sanctus Basilíscus Martyr, in cujus templo ántea oráverat, noctu sic eum affátus est: Joánnes frater, crastínus dies nos loco conjúnget. Quare postrídie sumpto Eucharistíæ Sacraménto, seque crucis signo múniens, ánimam Deo réddidit décimo octávo Kaléndas Octóbris. Et quatríduo post Augústa cessit e vita.

commemoratiosiulianiepiscopietconfessori.en: Commemoration of St. Julian, Bishop and Confessor
commemoratiosiulianiepiscopietconfessori.la: Commemoratio S. Juliani, Episcopi et Confessoris

amedeusinagroviennensiexprosapiaconradir.en: Amadeus, sprung in the district of Vienne from the lineage of Conrad, King of the Romans, betook himself while still a boy, together with his father Amadeus and other noblemen, to the Monastery of Bonnevaux of the Cistercian Order. Thence, by the will of his father, who hoped that he would make more progress in the study of letters, leaving Bonnevaux, he passed to Cluny, where he was received with the greatest honour. Hence arose the dissensions between the Cluniac and the Cistercian Monks, which the venerable Abbot Peter described, and which St. Bernard, having written an apology, strove to settle. Meanwhile Amadeus was sent into Germany to the Emperor, that he might be taught by more learned masters. And King Conrad being dead, the pious youth, excellently instructed in human and divine letters, sought Clairvaux, where, received most lovingly by St. Bernard, he was afterward set by the same holy Father, with the applause of the whole community of Clairvaux, as Abbot over the Monastery of Hautecombe, the Monks of that place earnestly asking for this very thing.
amedeusinagroviennensiexprosapiaconradir.la: Amedéus in agro Viennénsi ex prosápia Conrádi Romanórum regis oriúndus, una cum patre Amedéo, et áliis nobílibus viris, in Monastérium Bonævállis Ordinis Cisterciénsis, pueríli adhuc ætáte, sese recépit. Inde patris sui voluntáte, magis eum in litterárum stúdiis profectúrum sperántis, Bonaválle relícta, Cluníacum tránsiit, ubi honorificentíssime suscéptus est. Hinc dissídia inter Cluniacénses et Cisterciénses Mónachos exórta, quæ venerábilis Petrus Abbas descrípsit, et sanctus Bernárdus, conscrípta apología, compónere stúduit. Interim Amedéus in Germániam ad Imperatórem míttitur, ut a peritióribus magístris edocerétur. Defúncto autem Conrádo rege, pius adoléscens humánis divinísque lítteris óptime instrúctus, Claramvállem pétiit, ubi a sancto Bernárdo amantíssime accéptus, postmódum ab eódem sancto Patre, plaudénte toto Claravallénsi convéntu, Altæcúmbæ Cœnóbio, Mónachis ejúsdem loci id ipsum eníxe peténtibus, Abbas præfícitur.

sedmagismagisqueindiescrescentevenerabil.en: But as the fame of the venerable Abbot's wisdom and holiness grew more and more from day to day, he was elected Bishop of the Church of Lausanne by the consent of all the clergy and people. And when he refused to take up this burden, by command of the Supreme Pontiff he acquiesced in the divine disposition: and mindful of that Apostolic oracle: It behoveth a Bishop to be blameless, he shone wonderfully upon the whole Church with the splendour of all virtues. He had Eugene the Third, Sovereign Pontiff, King Conrad, and the emperor Frederick most favourable to renewing, confirming and increasing the privileges of his Church. He composed eight elegant and sweet homilies in praise of the most blessed Mother of God. And after he had most holily governed the people of Lausanne for fourteen years, he departed this life in the year of man's salvation one thousand one hundred and fifty-eight, and was enrolled in the number of the Saints.
sedmagismagisqueindiescrescentevenerabil.la: Sed magis magísque in dies crescénte venerábilis Abbatis sapiéntiæ ac sanctitátis fama, Lausannénsis Ecclésiæ totíus cleri et pópuli consénsu Epíscopus elígitur. Quod onus cum ipse suscípere detrectáret, summi Pontíficis jussu, divínæ dispositióni acquiévit: ac memor illíus Apostólici oráculi: Opórtet Epíscopum esse irreprehensíbilem, ómnium virtútum splendóre univérsæ Ecclésiæ mirabíliter illúxit. Eugénium tértium, Pontíficem Máximum, Conrádum regem, et Frederícum imperatórem, ad renovánda, confirmánda, augendáque suæ Ecclésiæ privilégia propensíssimos hábuit. Octo homilías elegántes et dulces in laudem beatíssimæ Deíparæ concinnávit. Postquam autem Lausannénsibus annis quatuórdecim sanctíssime præfuísset, anno humánæ salútis millésimo centésimo quinquagésimo octávo e vita migrávit, et in Sanctórum númerum fuit relátus.

excitadomineintercedentebeatoamedeoponti.en: Stir up, O Lord, by the intercession of blessed Amadeus, thy Bishop and Confessor, the hearts of thy faithful: that, being intent upon holy teachings, they may both understand what they should follow, and by following may faithfully lay hold of it.
excitadomineintercedentebeatoamedeoponti.la: Excita, Dómine, intercedénte beáto Amedéo, Pontífice et Confessóre, tuórum corda fidélium: ut sacris inténta doctrinis, et intélligant quod sequátur; et sequéndo fidéliter apprehéndant.

franciscusinoppidosalesioundefamiliecogn.en: Francis, born of pious and noble parents in the town of Sales, whence the family's surname, from his tender years gave signs of his future holiness by the innocence and gravity of his manners. As a youth he bound himself by a vow of perpetual virginity, which he renewed in the holy house of Loreto. From this purpose of virtue he could never be moved by any frauds of the devils, nor by any allurements of the senses. Having refused a most high dignity in the Senate of Savoy, he enlisted in the clerical warfare. Ordained to the priesthood and having obtained the provostship of the Church of Geneva, he fulfilled the duties of that office so perfectly that he was appointed by Granier, the Bishop, preacher of the divine word for the overthrowing of heresy among the people of Chablais and the neighbouring peoples. Undertaking this mission with an eager mind, he suffered every most grievous hardship: but amid many and great dangers and struggles his invincible constancy ever shone forth; and, protected by the help of God, he is said to have brought back seventy-two thousand heretics to the Catholic faith.
franciscusinoppidosalesioundefamiliecogn.la: Francíscus in óppido Salésio, unde famíliæ cognómen, piis et nobílibus paréntibus natus, a téneris annis futúræ sanctitátis indícia præbuit, morum innocéntia et gravitáte. Adoléscens perpétuæ virginitátis voto se obstrinxit, quod in sacra æde Lauretána innovávit. A cujus virtútis propósito nullis umquam dæmonum fráudibus, nullis sénsuum illécebris pótuit dimovéri. Recusáta in Sabáudiæ Senátu amplíssima dignitáte, Clericáli milítiæ nomen dedit. Sacerdótio initiátus et Genevénsis Ecclésiæ præpositúram adéptus, ejus múneris partes ádeo perfécte explévit, ut a Granírio Epíscopo in profligánda hæresi apud Chaballicénses finitimósque pópulos divíni verbi præco fúerit destinátus. Quam expeditiónem álacri ánimo suscípiens, aspérrima quæque perpéssus est: sed inter multa magnáque discrímina et agónes ínsuperábilis ejus constántia semper enítuit; Deíque ope protéctus, septuagínta duo míllia hæreticórum ad catholicam fidem reduxísse dícátur.

factusgenevensisepiscopussanctitatissuer.en: Made Bishop of Geneva, he spread the rays of his holiness on every side, conspicuous for zeal for ecclesiastical discipline, for the love of peace, and for every virtue. He founded a new Order of nuns, named after the Visitation of the Blessed Virgin Mary, under the Rule of St. Augustine; to which he added constitutions wonderful for wisdom, discretion and gentleness. By his writings also, filled with heavenly doctrine, he enlightened the Church. At length, in his fifty-fifth year, while he was returning from France to Annecy, after celebrating Mass at Lyons on the day of St. John the Evangelist, he was seized with a grievous sickness, and on the following day departed to heaven, in the year of restored salvation one thousand six hundred and twenty-two; and by the Supreme Pontiff Pius the Ninth, on the advice of the Sacred Congregation of Rites, he was declared a Doctor of the universal Church.
factusgenevensisepiscopussanctitatissuer.la: Factus Genevénsis Epíscopus, sanctitátis suæ rádios circumquáque diffúdit, zelo Ecclesiásticæ disciplínæ, pacis stúdio omníque virtúte conspícuus. Novum Ordinem sanctimoniálium instítuit, a Visitatióne beátæ Maríæ Vírginis nuncupátum, sub Régula sancti Augustíni; cui áddidit constitutiónes sapiéntia, discretióne et suavitáte mirábiles. Suis étiam scriptis cœlésti doctrína refértis, Ecclésiam illustrávit. Annum dénique agens quinquagésimum quintum, dum e Gállia Annesium regréditur, post Sacrum in die sancti Joánnis Evangelístæ Lugdúni celebrátum, gravi morbo corréptus, sequénti die migrávit in cœlum, anno reparátæ salútis millesimo sexcentésimo vigésimo secúndo, et a summo Pontífice Pio nono, ex Sacrórum Rítuum Congregatiónis consúlto, universális Ecclésiæ Doctor fuit declarátus.

desermonesanctibernardiabbatis.en: From the Sermon of St. Bernard, Abbot.

cernitisofiliiquamiustussitdolormeuspros.en: Ye see, O my sons, how just is my sorrow for Gerard taken from me. He was my brother by birth, but more my brother by religion. I was weak in body, and he carried me; I was faint of heart, and he strengthened me; slothful and negligent, and he roused me; improvident and forgetful, and he admonished me. Who was so needful to me? To whom was I equally beloved? Whither art thou torn from me, man of one mind with me, man after mine own heart? Surely thou hast, O Gerard, in place of poor me, the presence of Christ laid up for thee; nor dost thou feel the loss of our absence, mingled with the choirs of Angels, entered into the abyss of light, and swallowed up in that sea of eternal happiness, wherein the Lord of Majesty hath abundantly granted thee the fulness of himself and of his own.
cernitisofiliiquamiustussitdolormeuspros.la: Cérnitis, o fílii, quam justus sit dolor meus pro subtrácto mihi Gerárdo. Frater ille erat génere, sed religióne germánior. Infírmus córpore eram, et ille portábat me; pusíllus corde eram, et confortábat me; piger et négligens, et excitábat me; impróvidus et obliviósus, et commonébat me. Quis ita mihi pernecessárius? Cui æque diléctus ego? Quo mihi avúlsus es, homo unánimis, homo secúndum cor meum? Habes certe, o Gerárde, pro me tantíllo repósitam tibi Christi præséntiam; nec dispéndium sentis abséntiæ nobis tuæ, Angelórum admíxtus choris, ingréssus abyssum lúminis, atque illo pelágo ætérnæ felicitátis absórptus, cui áffatim sui, suorúmque cópiam Dóminus Majestátis indúlsit.

dederatautemillidominuslinguameruditamut.en: Now the Lord had given him a learned tongue, that he might know when he ought to speak a word: for so, by the prudence of his answers, and by the grace given him from above, did he satisfy both those of the household and those without, that scarce anyone sought me whom Gerard had chanced to meet first. Who went away from him empty-handed? If rich, he carried away counsel; if poor, help. Nor did he seek the things that are his own, who thrust himself into the midst of cares, that my pursuits in the Lord might be in some measure free. For indeed he laboured more than all, and received less than all, so that often, while he ministered necessaries to others, he himself was in want of many things.
dederatautemillidominuslinguameruditamut.la: Déderat autem illi Dóminus linguam erudítam, ut sciret, quando debéret proférre sermónem: ita enim in prudéntia responsórum suórum, et in grátia sibi data désuper, et domésticis satisfaciébat, et éxteris, ut pene me nemo requíreret, cui prior forte Gerárdus occurrísset. Quis vacua ab eo recéssit manu? Si dives, consílium, si pauper, subsídium reportábat. Nec quærébat, quæ sua sunt, qui se médiis ingerébat curis, ut mea in Dómino stúdia utcúmque líbera essent. Síquidem plus ómnibus laborábat, et minus ómnibus accipiébat, ita ut sæpe cum áliis necessária ministráret, egéret ipse in plúribus.

deusquianimambeatigerardianimesanctibern.en: O God, who didst so join together the soul of blessed Gerard with the soul of St. Bernard, his brother, in religion and holiness, that they seemed to be one and the same in Christ: we beseech thee, by the intercession of both, join our minds to thee in charity; that all of us together, serving thee in unity of spirit upon earth, may merit to enjoy thee alone in heaven.
deusquianimambeatigerardianimesanctibern.la: Deus, qui ánimam beáti Gerárdi ánimæ sancti Bernárdi, fratris ejus, in religióne et sanctitáte ita conglutinásti, ut una et eadem in Christo esse viderétur: quæsumus, utriúsque intervéntu, mentes nostras tibi in charitáte conjúnge; ut omnes simul in spíritus unitáte tibi inserviéntes in terris, te uno pérfrui mereámus in cœlis.

videtemiraculummatrisdominiconcepitvirgo.en: Behold the miracle of the Mother of the Lord: a virgin hath conceived, knowing not the fellowship of man; Mary standeth laden with a noble burden, and joyfully knoweth herself a Mother.
videtemiraculummatrisdominiconcepitvirgo.la: Vidéte miráculum Matris Dómini, concépit virgo, virílis ignára consórtii, stat oneráta nóbili ónere María, et Matrem se læta cognóscit.

quesenescituxorem.en: Who knoweth not herself a wife.

virgoconcepitetpostpartumvirgopermansit.en: A virgin conceived, and after childbirth remained a virgin.
virgoconcepitetpostpartumvirgopermansit.la: Virgo concépit, et post partum virgo permánsit.

postpartumvirgoinviolatapermansisti.en: After childbirth, O Virgin, * thou didst remain inviolate.

deigenitrixintercedepronobis.en: Mother of God, intercede for us.

inprolematerinpartuvirgogaudeetletarevir.en: Mother in thy Child, * Virgin in childbirth, rejoice and be glad, O Virgin Mother of the Lord.
inprolematerinpartuvirgogaudeetletarevir.la: In Prole Mater, * in partu Virgo, gaude et lætáre, Virgo Mater Dómini. Ps. 23

sanctadeigenitrixvirgosempermariainterce.en: Holy Mother of God, * Mary ever Virgin, intercede for us with the Lord our God.
sanctadeigenitrixvirgosempermariainterce.la: Sancta Dei Génitrix * Virgo semper María, intercéde pro nobis ad Dóminum Deum nostrum. Ps. 44

induerevestimentisglorietuecivitassancti.en: Put on * the garments of thy glory, O city of the Holy One, and receive Christ the King.
induerevestimentisglorietuecivitassancti.la: Indúere * vestiméntis glóriæ tuæ, cívitas Sancti, et súscipe Regem Christum. Ps. 45

virgoconcepitetvirgopeperitetpostpartumv.en: A Virgin * conceived, and a virgin brought forth, and after childbirth remained a virgin.
virgoconcepitetvirgopeperitetpostpartumv.la: Virgo * concépit, et virgo péperit, et post partum virgo permánsit. Ps. 84

hodiemariavirgopuerumoffertintemploquems.en: This day the Virgin Mary * offereth the child in the temple, whom the old man Simeon received into his hands, and Anna the widow acknowledged that Christ was come upon earth.
hodiemariavirgopuerumoffertintemploquems.la: Hódie María Virgo * púerum offert in templo, quem Símeon senex accépit in mánibus, et Anna vídua Christum agnóvit advenísse in terris. Ps. 249, 250, 251

induerevestimentisglorietuecivitassancti.en: Put on the garments of thy glory, O city of the Holy One:
induerevestimentisglorietuecivitassancti.la: Indúere vestiméntis glóriæ tuæ, cívitas Sancti:

simeoninmanibusinfirmitatemaccepitsedmai.en: Simeon received weakness into his hands, but within he acknowledged Majesty, and said:
simeoninmanibusinfirmitatemaccepitsedmai.la: Símeon in manibus infirmitátem accepit, sed Majestátem intus agnóvit, et dixit:

responsumaccepitsimeonaspiritusanctononv.en: Simeon had received an answer from the Holy Ghost, that he should not see death, before he had seen the Christ of the Lord: and he blessed God, and said:
responsumaccepitsimeonaspiritusanctononv.la: Respónsum accépit Símeon a Spíritu Sancto, non visúrum se mortem, nisi vidéret Christum Dómini: et benedíxit Deum, et dixit:

nuncdimittisservumtuuminpacequiaviderunt.en: Now thou dost dismiss thy servant in peace, because my eyes have seen thy salvation, O Lord.
nuncdimittisservumtuuminpacequiaviderunt.la: Nunc dimíttis servum tuum in pace, quia vidérunt óculi mei salutáre tuum, Dómine.

beatesmariaquedominumportasticreatoremmu.en: Blessed art thou, O Mary, who didst bear the Lord, the Creator of the world,
beatesmariaquedominumportasticreatoremmu.la: Beáta es María, quæ Dóminum portásti Creatórem mundi,

genuistiquitefecitetineternumpermanesvir.en: Thou hast borne Him Who created thee, and thou abidest a virgin for ever.
genuistiquitefecitetineternumpermanesvir.la: Genuísti, qui te fecit, et in ætérnum pérmanes Virgo.

hodiemariavirgopuerumoffertintemplo.en: This day the Virgin Mary offereth the child in the temple,
hodiemariavirgopuerumoffertintemplo.la: Hódie María Virgo púerum offert in templo,

quemsimeoniustusaccepitinbrachietannavid.en: Whom just Simeon received into his arms, and Anna the widow acknowledged that Christ was come upon earth.
quemsimeoniustusaccepitinbrachietannavid.la: Quem Símeon justus accépit in bráchia, et Anna vídua Christum agnóvit advenísse in terris.

magnumhereditatismysteriumchristuspronob.en: O great mystery of inheritance! Christ, made man for us, entereth into the temple:
magnumhereditatismysteriumchristuspronob.la: Magnum hæreditátis mystérium! Christus pro nobis homo factus, ingréditur in templum:

cuminducerentpuerumiesumparenteseiusacce.en: When his parents brought in the child Jesus, Simeon took him into his arms, and blessed God, and said:
cuminducerentpuerumiesumparenteseiusacce.la: Cum indúcerent púerum Jesum paréntes ejus, accépit eum Símeon in ulnas suas, et benedíxit Deum, et dixit:

nuncdimittisdomineservumtuuminpace.en: Now thou dost dismiss thy servant, O Lord, in peace.
nuncdimittisdomineservumtuuminpace.la: Nunc dimíttis, Dómine, servum tuum in pace.

quiavideruntoculimeisalutaretuumquodpara.en: Because my eyes have seen thy salvation, which thou hast prepared before the face of all peoples.
quiavideruntoculimeisalutaretuumquodpara.la: Quia vidérunt óculi mei salutáre tuum, quod parásti ante fáciem ómnium populórum.

gabrielemarchangelumcredumisdivinitustee.en: We believe that the Archangel Gabriel was sent from God to speak to thee: we believe that thy womb was made fruitful by the Holy Ghost: let the unhappy Jew blush for shame, who saith that Christ was born of the seed of Joseph:
gabrielemarchangelumcredumisdivinitustee.la: Gabriélem Archángelum crédumis divínitus te esse affátum: úterum tuum de Spíritu Sancto crédimus impregnátum: erubéscat Judǽus ínfelix, qui dicit Christum ex Joseph sémine esse natum:

simeoniustusettimoratusexspectabatredemp.en: Just Simeon * and devout waited for the redemption of Israel, and the Holy Ghost was in him.
simeoniustusettimoratusexspectabatredemp.la: Símeon justus * et timorátus exspectábat redemptiónem Israël, et Spíritus Sanctus erat in eo.

senexpuerumportabatpuerautemsenemregebat.en: The old man * carried the Child, but the Child ruled the old man: whom a virgin brought forth, and after childbirth remained a virgin: the very one whom she bore, she adored.
senexpuerumportabatpuerautemsenemregebat.la: Senex * Púerum portábat, puer autem senem regébat: quem virgo péperit, et post partum virgo permánsit: ipsum quem génuit, adorávit.

responsumaccepitsimeonaspiritusanctononv.en: Simeon had received an answer * from the Holy Ghost, that he should not see death, before he had seen the Lord.
