responsumaccepitsimeonaspiritusanctononv.la: Respónsum accépit Símeon * a Spíritu Sancto, non visúrum se mortem, nisi vidéret Dóminum.

accipienssimeonpueruminmanibusgratiasage.en: Simeon, taking * the child into his hands, giving thanks, blessed the Lord.
accipienssimeonpueruminmanibusgratiasage.la: Accípiens Símeon * púerum in mánibus, grátias agens benedíxit Dóminum.

obtuleruntpreodominoparturturumautduospu.en: They offered * for him unto the Lord a pair of turtle-doves, or two young pigeons.
obtuleruntpreodominoparturturumautduospu.la: Obtulérunt * pro eo Dómino par túrturum aut duos pullos columbárum.

elredusexprimariaanglorumetscotorumnobil.en: Aelred, sprung from the foremost nobility of the English and the Scots, and brought up at the court of David, King of Scotland, was most dear to the king himself. As piety and wisdom grew in him with his years, resolving to bid farewell to the world, he was received into the Cistercian habit in the Monastery of Rievaulx in the Diocese of York. Thereafter placed in charge of the instruction of the novices, and afterwards appointed Abbot of Revesby and soon of Rievaulx, he showed himself a pattern of all virtues. He gave himself wholly to the contemplation of heavenly things and to sacred reading, which he continually watered with tears. Excellently instructed in every kind of learning, in his manner of writing he was most like our mellifluous Doctor (whose footsteps also he most diligently followed in every exercise of virtue): seeing that he had the same anointing of the Holy Ghost for his teacher as he, as many of his works that have been made public bear witness. Wholly averse to ecclesiastical dignities, he most steadfastly refused a bishopric freely offered to him.
elredusexprimariaanglorumetscotorumnobil.la: Ælrédus ex primária Anglórum et Scotórum nobilitáte oriúndus, in aula David Scótiae regis educátus, ipsi regi charíssimus éxtitit. Crescénte cum annis pietáte et sapiéntia, sæculo núntium remíttere státuens, ad hábitum Cisterciénsem in Monastério Rievállis Eboracénsis Diœcésis recéptus est. Exínde novítiis instituéndis præféctus, posteáque Abbas de Revésby et mox Rievállis constitútus, se ómnium virtútum exémplar exhíbuit. Cœléstium rerum contemplatióni sacræque lectióni, quam júgiter lácrymis irrigábat, se totum dedit. Omni scientiárum génere egrégie instrúctus, in scribéndi rátione nostro Doctóri mellífluo (cujus étiam in quocúmque virtútis exercítio diligentíssime sectabátur vestígia) simíllimus éxtitit: quippe qui eámdem cum ipso Spíritus sancti unctiónem habúerit magístram, quemádmodum plura ejus ópera públici juris facta testántur. A dignitátibus Ecclesiásticis prorsus aliénus‚ Episcopátum sibi ultro oblátum constantíssime recusávit.

proveretlegitimopontificealexandrotertio.en: For the true and lawful pontiff Alexander the Third he contended strenuously against the antipope Octavian and the conventicle of Pavia. He bore injuries most patiently, and nothing was nearer to his heart than to bring about and foster peace and concord among all. He trained a hundred and forty monks and five hundred brothers in his Monastery by most holy precepts and admonitions. Many labouring under divers ailments of soul or body he comforted or healed. He often sat in a certain pit dug in his oratory, constantly meditating on death; and, refreshed by the visitation of Angels, he was renowned for the gift of miracles and the spirit of prophecy. Afflicted with sickness for ten years before his death, he bore most grievous pains with wonderful patience. At length, having foreseen the day of his death, the holy man departed to the Lord in the year of salvation one thousand one hundred and sixty-six.
proveretlegitimopontificealexandrotertio.la: Pro vero et legítimo pontífice Alexándro tértio advérsus Octaviánum antipápam et conciliábulum Papiénse strénue decertávit. Injúrias patientíssime tolerávit, níhilque ei magis cordi fuit, quam pacem et concórdiam inter omnes conciliáre et fovére. Mónachos centum quadragínta, et fratres quingéntos in Monastério suo sanctíssimis praecéptis et mónitis instítuit. Multos váriis languóribus ánimae vel córporis laborantes confortávit aut sanávit. Sedébat crebro in quadam oratórii sui effóssa fóvea, mortem assídue méditans, et Angelórum visitatióne recreátus Miraculórum dono et spíritu prophétiæ cláruit. Per decénnium ante óbitum ægritúdine vexátus, mira patiéntia gravíssimos dolóres sustínuit. Tandem die mortis prævísa, vir sanctus ad Dóminum migrávit anno salútis humánae millésimo centésimo sexagésimo sexto.

hicestvirquinonestderelictusadeoindiecer.en: This is the man who was not forsaken by God in the day of his combat, and he trod upon the head of the old serpent:
hicestvirquinonestderelictusadeoindiecer.la: Hic est vir, qui non est derelíctus a Deo in die certáminis sui, et ipse conculcávit caput serpéntis antíqui:

modocoronatusestquiafidelitervixitinmand.en: Now is he crowned, because he lived faithfully in the commandments of the Lord.
modocoronatusestquiafidelitervixitinmand.la: Modo coronátus est, quia fidéliter vixit in mandátis Dómini.

quisesthicetlaudabimuseumfecitenimmirabi.en: Who is he, and we will praise him? for he hath done wonderful things in his life.
quisesthicetlaudabimuseumfecitenimmirabi.la: Quis est hic, et laudábimus eum? fecit enim mirabília in vita sua.

omnipotenssempiternedeusquiecclesietuefi.en: Almighty everlasting God, who, as thou ceasest not to instruct the children of thy Church, so dost not cease to help them: grant to thy faithful, by the intercession of blessed Aelred, Abbot, whom thou gavest them as a minister of eternal salvation; that, by thy mercy, they may receive both the knowledge of doing what is right, and the power to perform it.
omnipotenssempiternedeusquiecclesietuefi.la: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, qui Ecclésiæ tuæ fílios sicut non cessas erudíre, ita non désinis adjuváre: da fidélibus tuis intercessióne beáti Ælredi, Abbátis, quem eis ætérnæ salútis minístrum tribuísti; ut et sciéntiam, te miseránte, recta faciéndi, et possibilitátem cápiant exequéndi.

mentemsanctamspontaneumhonoremdeetpatrie.en: A holy mind, * honour freely offered to God, and the deliverance of her country.
mentemsanctamspontaneumhonoremdeetpatrie.la: Mentem sanctam, * spontáneum honórem Deo, et pátriæ liberatiónem.

beataagathaingressacarceremexpanditmanus.en: Blessed Agatha, * having entered the prison, stretched forth her hands to God and said: O Lord, who hast made me to overcome the torments of the executioners, bid me come unto thy mercy.
beataagathaingressacarceremexpanditmanus.la: Beata Agatha * ingréssa cárcerem, expándit manus suas ad Deum et dixit: Dómine qui me fecísti víncere torménta carnifícium, jube me ad tuam misericórdiam perveníre. Ps. 249, 250, 251

adiuvamedominedeusmeusquiapropterfidemca.en: Help me, O Lord my God, for because of the faith of chastity
adiuvamedominedeusmeusquiapropterfidemca.la: Adjuva me, Dómine Deus meus, quia propter fidem castitátis

venielectameetponamintethronummeum.en: Come, O My chosen one, and I will establish My throne in thee;
venielectameetponamintethronummeum.la: Veni, elécta mea, et ponam in te thronum meum:

quiaconcupivitrexspeciemtuam.en: For the King hath greatly desired thy beauty.

surgeproperaamicameavenidelibanetcoronab.en: Arise, make haste, my love, come from Libanus, and thou shalt be crowned.
surgeproperaamicameavenidelibanetcoronab.la: Surge, própera, amíca mea, veni de Líbano, et coronáberis.

egoautemadiutaadominoperseveraboinconfes.en: But I, helped by the Lord, will persevere in confessing him,
egoautemadiutaadominoperseveraboinconfes.la: Ego autem adjúta a Dómino, perseverábo in confessióne ejus,

quimesalvamfecitetconsolatusestme.en: Who hath saved me, and hath comforted me.
quimesalvamfecitetconsolatusestme.la: Qui me salvam fecit, et consolátus est me.

gratiastibiagodomineiesuchristequimisist.en: I give thee thanks, O Lord Jesus Christ, who hast sent thine Apostle unto me:
gratiastibiagodomineiesuchristequimisist.la: Grátias tibi ago, Dómine Jesu Christe, qui misísti ad me Apóstolum tuum:

raymunduscanonicusecclesieturiasonensisi.en: Raymund, a Canon of the Church of Tarazona in the kingdom of Aragon, by the inspiration of the Spirit from above, withdrew into solitude. Then, as the fame of the Cistercian Monks was spreading on every side, he embraced that institute; and, the holiness of his life being noised abroad far and wide, he was appointed Abbot of the monastery of Blessed Mary of Fitero. After he had led his brethren by word and example to every work of piety, he gathered a large army of the faithful, and received from the hand of Sancho, King of Castile, the fortress of Turungen and Calatrava, to defend them against the Moors. By a new example, unheard of until those times, Raymund joined knighthood to the monastic life, and founded the Order named of Calatrava, most renowned in all Europe, and approved by many Supreme Pontiffs, under the rule, laws and visitation of the Cistercians.
raymunduscanonicusecclesieturiasonensisi.la: Raymúndus, Canonicus Ecclésiæ Turiasonénsis in regno Arragóniæ, supérno Spíritu afflánte, in solitúdinem se recépit. Deínde cum Cisterciénsium Monachórum fama undequáque diffunderétur, illud amplexátus est institútum; ac longe latéque evulgáta ejus vitæ sanctimónia, Abbas monastérii beátæ Maríæ de Fitéro constitútus est. Postquam verbo et exémplo ad omne opus pietátis suos induxísset, copiósum exércitum fidélium collégit, castrum de Turúngen et Calatrávam a Mauris tuéndam de manu Sánctii Castéllæ regis suscépit. Novo et usque ad ea témpora inaudíto exémplo, Raymúndus monachátui milítiam conjúnxit et Ordinem de Calatráva nuncupátum, in tota Europa celebérrimum, ac a plúribus summis Pontifícibus approbátum, instítuit sub régula, légibus, et visitatióne Cisterciénsium.

huiusnoviordinismilitesquamdiuaprelioabs.en: The knights of this new Order, so long as they abstained from battle, came so near in discipline to the monastic life, that, after deliberation of the General Chapter of Citeaux, by the common consent of the fathers they merited to be received as sons of the monastery of Morimond. At length the holy man, supreme leader of both warfares, the heavenly and the earthly, after many victories won over the Saracens, after training men fit for the arms of both, who should imitate by turns lions and lambs, the one in battle, the other in the cloister, full of days and virtues, in the year of salvation one thousand one hundred and sixty-three, and the sixth of his rule of the Order begun by him, gave up his soul, renowned after death for many miracles.
huiusnoviordinismilitesquamdiuaprelioabs.la: Hujus novi Ordinis mílites, quámdiu a prælio abstinébant, ad vitam monásticam disciplína ita próxime accedébant, ut hábita deliberatióne Capítuli Generális Cisterciénsis, commúni patrum consénsu in fílios monastérii Morimúndi récipi merúerint. Tandem vir sanctus utriúsque milítiæ cæléstis et terrénæ suprémus ductor, post multas victórias de Saracénis partas, post hómines aptátos utriúsque armis, qui leónes vicíssim et agnos, illud in prælio, hoc in claustris, imitaréntur, plenus diérum et virtútum, anno salútis millésimo centésimo sexagésimo tértio, et sexto regíminis Ordinis a se inchoáti, ánimam emísit, multis post mortem miráculis illústris.

deusquibeatoraymundoabbatipreliariprelia.en: O God, who didst grant to blessed Raymund, Abbot, to fight thy battles and to overcome the enemies of the faith: grant that we, defended by his intercession, may be delivered from the enemies of mind and body.
deusquibeatoraymundoabbatipreliariprelia.la: Deus, qui beáto Raymúndo, Abbáti, præliári prælia tua, et fídei inimícos superáre dedísti: concéde, ut ejus nos intercessióne muníti, ab hóstibus mentis et córporis liberémur.

commemoratiosdorotheevirginisetmartyris.en: Commemoration of St. Dorothy, Virgin and Martyr
commemoratiosdorotheevirginisetmartyris.la: Commemoratio S. Dorotheæ, Virginis et Martyris

scholasticasanctibenedictisororomnipoten.en: Scholastica, the sister of St. Benedict, dedicated to Almighty God from the very time of her infancy, was wont to come to him once a year; and the man of God went down to her, not far outside the gate, on a property of the monastery. But on a certain day, when he had come to her according to custom, and wished to return to his monastery that same day, and would not yield to his sister's prayers that he should spend the night watching with her in the praises of God and in divine converse, suddenly, as Scholastica prayed, so great a storm of rain and thunder arose, that the man of God was forced to remain there with the brethren, and to prolong their holy discourse until the next day.
scholasticasanctibenedictisororomnipoten.la: Scholástica, sancti Benedícti soror, omnipoténti Dómino ab ipso infántiæ témpore dedicáta, ad eum semel per annum veníre consuéverat; ad quam vir Dei non longe extra jánuam, in possessióne monastérii descendébat. Quadam vero die cum ex more ad eam accessísset, et eádem die monastérium suum vellet repétere, nec acquiésceret soróris précibus, ut cum ea pervígilem noctem in Dei láudibus, et divínis collóquiis transígeret, súbito, oránte Scholástica, tanta ímbrium et tonitruórum tempéstas exórta est, ut vir Dei cum frátribus ibi manére, et usque ad álterum diem sacros sermónes prodúcere cogerétur.

sedposttriduumincellaconsistensvirdeiben.en: But three days after, the man of God, Benedict, standing in his cell, lifting up his eyes into the air, saw the soul of that same sister of his, gone forth from the body, entering the secret places of heaven in the likeness of a dove: and he made known her death to the brethren. Whom also he sent forthwith to bring her body to the monastery, and to lay it in the tomb which he had prepared for himself. Which being done, it came to pass that those whose mind had ever been one in God, their bodies also not even the grave should separate.
sedposttriduumincellaconsistensvirdeiben.la: Sed post tríduum in cella consístens vir Dei Benedíctus elevátis in áëra óculis, vidit ejúsdem soróris suæ ánimam de córpore egréssam, in colúmbæ spécie cœli secréta penetráre: ejúsque óbitum frátribus declarávit. Quos étiam prótinus misit, ut ejus corpus ad monastérium deférrent, atque in sepúlchro, quod sibi ipsi præparáverat, pónerent. Quo facto cóntigit, ut quorum mens una semper in Deo fúerat, eórum quoque córpora nec sepultúra separáret.

mulieremfortemquisinvenietproculetdeulti.en: Who shall find a valiant woman? Far and from the uttermost coasts is the price of her.
mulieremfortemquisinvenietproculetdeulti.la: Mulíerem fortem quis invéniet? procul, et de últimis fínibus prétium ejus.

confiditineacorvirisuietspoliisnonindige.en: The heart of her husband trusteth in her, and he shall have no need of spoils.
confiditineacorvirisuietspoliisnonindige.la: Confídit in ea cor viri sui, et spóliis non indigébit.

reddeteibonumetnonmalumomnibusdiebusvite.en: She will render him good, and not evil, all the days of her life.
reddeteibonumetnonmalumomnibusdiebusvite.la: Reddet ei bonum, et non malum, ómnibus diébus vitæ suæ.

factestquasinavisinstitorisdelongeportan.en: She is like the merchant's ship, she bringeth her bread from afar.
factestquasinavisinstitorisdelongeportan.la: Facta est quasi navis institóris, de longe portans panem suum.

etdenoctesurrexitdeditquepredamdomestici.en: And she hath risen in the night, and given a prey to her household, and victuals to her maidens.
etdenoctesurrexitdeditquepredamdomestici.la: Et de nocte surréxit, dedítque prædam domésticis suis, et cibária ancíllis suis.

humbelinasanctipatrisbernardisororgerman.en: Humbeline, own sister of the holy Father Bernard, carefully brought up in piety from her earliest years by a most religious mother, answering but little to her holy wishes, followed human pride and worldly delights. But when once, for the sake of visiting Bernard and her other brothers, she had gone to Clairvaux with a proud retinue and adorned with womanly finery, she was pricked at heart because an interview was at first refused her; then, changed into another woman by the admonitions of her brothers, and above all by the heavenly eloquence of Bernard, she entered upon a more religious life; and, returning home, for two years she led a pious life together with her husband. This being ended, with the consent of that same husband, bidding farewell to the world, she withdrew into a neighbouring monastery of Benedictine nuns called Jully, where, having taken the holy habit of religion, and being consecrated to God by solemn vows, she shone before the other nuns as a pattern of Christian perfection.
humbelinasanctipatrisbernardisororgerman.la: Humbelína sancti Patris Bernárdi soror germána, a primis annis in pietáte sédulo a religiosíssima matre educáta, sanctis illíus votis mínime respóndens, humánum fastum sæcularésque sectabátur delícias. Cum autem aliquándo, Bernárdum ceterósque fratres suos viséndi grátia Claramvállem supérbo comitátu, et muliébri mundo exornáta petiísset, ob negátum primo sibi collóquium corde compúncta, fratrum inde mónitis ac præcípue cœlésti Bernárdi eloquéntia in áliam mutáta, religiosiórem vitam agréssa est; reversáque ad própria per biénnium simul cum cónjuge piam vitam instítuit. Quo expléto, de ejúsdem cónjugis consénsu, sæculo valedicens‚ in vicínum monastérium Benedictinárum, Juléyum dictum, secéssit ubi sacro assúmpto religiónis hábitu, Deóque per solémnia vota consecráta, céteris sanctimoniálibus tamquam Christiánæ perfectiónis exémplar prælúxit.

diesnoctesqueiniugipsalmorumlectioneetas.en: Days and nights she spent in the continual reading of the Psalms and in assiduous meditation on the torments and death of Christ the Lord. Girt always with a rough hair shirt, she lay for a little while at night upon the ground, and, striving day by day after the better gifts, she led in all things an Angelic life in the flesh. At length, when she had for some time governed the house of Jully most holily, she fell into a sickness; and as it grew worse, having sent for the holy Father Bernard and her other brothers, she wished to be refreshed with the Sacraments of the Church; and as the hour of her departure was now at hand, with eyes still serene and a cheerful countenance, looking upon each of those standing round and greeting each, she said: I rejoiced at the things that were said to me: We shall go into the house of the Lord. And so piously and holily she fell asleep in the Lord.
diesnoctesqueiniugipsalmorumlectioneetas.la: Dies noctésque in jugi Psalmórum lectióne et assídua Christi Dómini cruciátuum mortísque meditatióne insumébat. Aspero cincta semper cilício humi paulísper noctu decumbébat‚ atque melióra in dies æmuláta charísmata Angélicam per ómnia vitam in carne ducébat. Tandem cum Juléyi ascetérium aliquámdiu sanctíssime rexísset, in morbum incídit, quo ingravescénte, accersíto sancto Patre Bernárdo, aliísque frátribus, Ecclésiæ Sacraméntis réfici vóluit, ac imminénte jam sui éxitus hora, serénis adhuc óculis, hilaríque vultu circumstántes síngulos respíciens síngulos salutans: Lætáta sum, inquit, in his, quæ dicta sunt mihi: In domum Dómini íbimus sicque pie et sancte obdormívit in Dómino.

gaudeamusomnesindomino.en: Let us all rejoice in the Lord,

diemfestumcelebrantessubhonorebeatendecu.en: Celebrating a festival day in honour of blessed N., at whose solemnity the Angels rejoice, and together praise the Son of God.
diemfestumcelebrantessubhonorebeatendecu.la: Diem festum celebrántes, sub honóre beátæ N., de cujus solemnitáte gaudent Angeli, et colláudant Fílium Dei.

exultemusomnesindominetspiritaliiucundit.en: Let us all exult in the Lord, and be glad with spiritual joy:
exultemusomnesindominetspiritaliiucundit.la: Exultémus omnes in Dómino, et spiritáli jucunditáte lætémur:

deusinquemsperatomnisanimaquelongeadhuca.en: O God, in whom every soul hopeth, which, being still set far from thee, feeleth itself truly widowed and desolate: be with us, we beseech thee, by the intercession of blessed Humbeline; that, subject to thee in sincere humility, we may so pass through temporal goods, that we lose not the eternal.
deusinquemsperatomnisanimaquelongeadhuca.la: Deus, in quem sperat omnis ánima, quæ longe adhuc a te pósita, se vere víduam sentit, ac desolátam: adésto nobis, quæsumus, intercedénte beáta Humbelína; ut sincéra humilitáte tibi subjécti, sic transeámus per bona temporália, ut non amittámus ætérna.

stephanusgrandimontensisordinisinstituto.en: Stephen, founder of the Order of Grandmont, born of an illustrious family among the Arverni, was taken into Italy by his father, a pious man, and was given to Milo, Archbishop of Benevento, to be educated. Taught under his instruction, and moved by the examples of the hermits of Calabria, he returned into Aquitaine with the leave of the Supreme Pontiff, and fixed his abode on a wooded mountain called Muret. There he set up a way of life as near to that of the Angels in purity as it was raised above human conversation in severity.
stephanusgrandimontensisordinisinstituto.la: Stéphanus Grandimonténsis Ordinis institútor, apud Arvérnos illústri loco natus, a patre viro pio in Itáliam ductus, Milóni Beneventáno Archiepíscopo educándus tráditur. Cujus magistério edóctus, exemplísque eremitárum de Calábria permótus in Aquitániam de summi Pontíficis licéntia revérsus est, et in monte nemoróso, qui Murétum dicitur, sedem fixit. Ibi vitam instítuit puritáte quidem, tantum Angélicæ próximam‚ quantum severitáte supra humánam conversatiónem eréctam.

hinccumlucernaaccensalaterenonpossetsubm.en: Hence, since a lighted lamp could not lie hidden under a bushel, some joined themselves to him, to whom he showed himself a most perfect pattern of all virtues. To many in the world he pointed out the way of salvation. Deeming himself unequal to the Priesthood, he fulfilled only the office of the Diaconate. Excelling in the gift of humility and of virginity, he breathed forth the fragrance of a wonderful odour. At length, when he had completed fifty years in the solitude of Muret, having exhorted his disciples, and received the help of the Sacraments, he rested in the Lord on the Ides of February: and Clement the Third enrolled him in the number of the Saints.
hinccumlucernaaccensalaterenonpossetsubm.la: Hinc cum lucérna accénsa latére non posset sub módio, nonnúlli se ad eum adjunxérunt‚ quibus ómnium virtútum exémplar absolutíssimum se præbuit. Multis de sæculo viam salútis indicávit. Imparem se Sacerdótio réputans Diaconátus tantum offício functus est. Humilitátis ac virginitátis dono præcéllens‚ miri odóris fragrántiam spirábat. Demum cum in Muréti solitúdine quinquagínta annos explevisset, discípulos adhortátus, susceptísque Sacramentórum subsidiis in Dómino requiévit Idibus Februárii: Quem Clemens tértius Sanctórum número adscrípsit.

conradushenricicognomentonigribavarieduc.en: Conrad, son of Henry, surnamed the Black, Duke of Bavaria, prevented by the grace of God from his very childhood, despising the pomp of the world, held it his delight to give himself to prayer far from the disturbance of men. Sent by his father to Cologne, to be instructed in human and divine letters in the cloister of the Canons, he so advanced in them and at the same time in virtues, that he was thought worthy of the highest honours. But perceiving that he was called by God to higher things, roused by the fame of St. Bernard, he embraced the monastic institute in the monastery of Clairvaux, and in a short time shone with such holiness, that he merited to obtain from that same holy Father, who well knew how to try the spirits, leave to set out for Palestine, and there to lead the life of a hermit.
conradushenricicognomentonigribavarieduc.la: Conrádus Henríci cognoménto nigri, Baváriæ ducis fílius, ab ipsa puerítia Dei grátia prævéntus, sæculi pompam contémnens longe a conturbatióne hóminum oratióni vacáre in delíciis habébat. A patre Colóniam missus in Canonicórum claustro humánis divinísque lítteris instituéndus, ádeo in illis simul et virtútibus profécit, ut summis honóribus dignus haberétur. Séntiens autem se a Deo ad altióra vocátum, divi Bernárdi éxcitus fama in Claravallénsi cœnóbio monásticum institútum ampléxus est, tantáque brevi sanctimónia enítuit, ut ab eódem sancto Patre, qui spíritus probáre bene nóverat, véniam in Palæstinam proficiscéndi, ibíque vitam agéndi eremíticam obtinére merúerit.

postquamperaliquotannoscumpioquodamprove.en: After he had dwelt for some years on a solitary mountain with a certain pious ascetic of more advanced age, whom he served in all things as a servant with unconquered humility, the old man being dead, and those places lying open, through the adverse fortune of the Christians, to the savagery of the Mahometans, he began, especially when he had received the sad news of the almost ruined health of St. Bernard, to think of returning into France and to his monastery. Taking ship therefore from Palestine, he was forced, by the growing infirmity from which he had already begun to suffer, to put in at Bari, the city of St. Nicholas: and, that he might not depart even in the least from his former purpose, he hid himself in a certain crypt, four miles from Bari, dedicated to the most blessed Mother of God; where after some time, the odour of his holiness being spread abroad, on the sixteenth of the Kalends of April he rested in the kiss of the Lord.
postquamperaliquotannoscumpioquodamprove.la: Postquam per áliquot annos cum pio quodam provectióris ætátis ascéta, cui in ómnibus tamquam servus invícta humilitáte ministrabant, in solitário monte degísset, defúncto sene, et locis illis, advérsa Christianórum fortúna, Mahumedanórum feritáti paténtibus, cœpit ipse, máxime cum triste núntium de divi Bernárdi fere pérdita valetúdine accépisset, de réditu in Gálliam et ad suum monastérium cogitáre. E Palæstína ígitur navem conscéndens‚ Bárium, sancti Nicolái civitátem, ingravescénte qua jam laboráre cœperat in firmitáte‚ appéllere coáctus est: ac ne a pristíno propósito vel mínimum recéderet, in quamdam cryptam, quarto a Bário milliário, beatíssimæ Deíparæ dicátam sese ábdidit; ubi post áliquod tempus, odóre sanctitátis diffúso, décimo sexto Kaléndas Aprílis in ósculo Dómini quiévit.

deusquibeatumconradumconfessoremtuumerem.en: O God, who didst will to make blessed Conrad, thy Confessor and a dweller in the desert, a citizen of the heavenly fatherland: mercifully grant; that we who venerate his festival, trampling on the affections of earthly things, may be kindled with heavenly desires.
deusquibeatumconradumconfessoremtuumerem.la: Deus, qui beátum Conrádum, Confessórem tuum eremíque cultórem, cœléstis pátriæ civem effícere voluísti: concéde propítius; ut ejus festivitátem venerántes, calcátis terrenórum afféctibus, supérnis desidériis accendámur.

bonifaciusbruxellisinbelgionatuscumabine.en: Boniface, born at Brussels in Belgium, since from his earliest age he gave wonderful proofs of many virtues, but above all of chastity, showed while yet a boy with how great grace he had been prevented by God, and to how great holiness he had been foreordained. As a youth, while he applied himself at Paris to the learning of philosophy and theology, by watchings, fasts and the hair shirt he kept unstained the gift received from heaven, and, persevering constantly in prayer, he obtained from the Lord the knowledge of the Saints and the right rule of life. After he had been ordained to the Priesthood and had taught the sacred sciences publicly with praise for nine years, he was raised to the Bishopric of Lausanne for the merit of his life and the excellence of his doctrine, and, as one set upon a high place, he shed forth upon his subjects the brighter rays of his virtues; and preaching by examples and by words, he brought back many from the mire of vices to the way of salvation. But when he had most steadfastly endured very grievous hardships and persecutions in reforming the morals of the Clergy, broken at length by his labours, he obtained from Innocent the Fourth, by many prayers and tears, that he should be released from the pastoral charge.
bonifaciusbruxellisinbelgionatuscumabine.la: Bonifácius Bruxéllis in Bélgio natus, cum ab ineúnte ætáte multárum virtútum, sed in primis castimóniæ mira specímina daret, quanta esset a Deo prævéntus grátia, ad quantam præordinátus sanctitátem, adhuc puer ostendébat. Adoléscens cum philosophíæ ac theologíæ addíscéndis Parísiis óperam daret, vigíliis, jejúniis, cilício accéptum cœlitus donum illibátum custodívit, ac précibus assídue insístens, sciéntiam Sanctorum rectámque vitæ normam a Dómino consecútus est. Postquam Sacerdótio initiátus sacras disciplínas per novem annos públice cum laude docuísset, ad Episcopátum Lausannénsem ob vitæ méritum et doctrínæ excelléntiam evéctus, tamquam in excélso loco constitútus, fulgentióres virtútum rádios suis súbditis transfúdit; et exémplis ac verbis prædicans, multos e vitiórum cœno ad salútis viam redúxit. At cum in reformándis Cleri móribus gravíssimas ærúmnas et persecutiónes constantíssime pertulísset, fractus tandem labóribus, ab Innocéntio quarto multis précibus et lácrymis, ut a pastoráli cura eximerétur, obtínuit.

tantooneresolutusbonifaciusbruxellasregr.en: Freed from so great a burden, Boniface returned to Brussels, and put on the religious habit in a neighbouring Monastery of the Cistercian Order, called the Chamber of St. Mary; and there, renowned for holiness and for the gift of miracles and the spirit of prophecy, and terrible also to the devils, whom he cast out of possessed bodies by his prayers or by the mere laying on of hands, he remained until his death, at the bidding of the Blessed Virgin Mary. Having therefore spent eighteen years most piously in religion, blessed Boniface, seized with a grievous sickness, taking the Gospel into his hands, broke forth into these words: These things I have learned, these I have received from the Church, in these I have lived, in these I believe, in these I hope, and in these I desire to die. Having uttered which, the holy man fell asleep in the Lord on the nineteenth day of February, in the year one thousand two hundred and sixty-five.
tantooneresolutusbonifaciusbruxellasregr.la: Tanto ónere solútus, Bonifácius Bruxéllas regréssus, in propínquo Monastério Ordinis Cisterciénsis, Cámera sanctæ Mariæ nuncupáto, religiósum hábitum índuit, ibidémque sanctitáte ac dono miraculórum et spíritu prophético clarus, necnon dæmónibus terribilis, quos ab obséssis corpóribus, précibus vel sola mánuum impositióne ejiciébat, beátæ Maríæ Vírginis mónitu, usque ad óbitum permánsit. Octódecim ígitur annis piíssime in religióne transáctis, beátus Bonifácius, gravi morbo corréptus, Evangélio mánibus assúmpto, in has voces erúpit: Hæc ego dídici, hac ab Ecclésia accépi, in his vixi, in his credo, in his spero, et mori cúpio. Quibus prolátis, vir sanctus die décima nona Februárii anno millésimo ducentésimo sexagésimo quinto obdormívit in Dómino.

quesumusomnipotensdeusutbeatusbonifacius.en: We beseech thee, almighty God, that blessed Boniface, thy Confessor and Bishop, whose feast we keep this day, may implore thy help for us: that, being absolved from our sins, we may also be delivered from all dangers.
quesumusomnipotensdeusutbeatusbonifacius.la: Quæsumus, omnípotens Deus, ut beátus Bonifácius, Conféssor tuus atque Póntifex, cujus hódie festa percólimus, tuum pro nobis implóret auxílium: ut a nostris reátibus absolúti a cunctis étiam perículis eruámur.

lectiosanctievangeliisecundumioannem.en: From the Holy Gospel according to John

inillotemporedixitiesusdiscipulissuishoc.en: In that time Jesus said to his disciples: This is my commandment, that you love one another, as I have loved you. And so on.
inillotemporedixitiesusdiscipulissuishoc.la: In illo témpore: Dixit Jesus discípulis suis: Hoc est præcéptum meum, ut diligátis ínvicem, sicut diléxi vos. Et réliqua.

cumcunctasacreloquiadominicisplenasintpr.en: Whereas all the sacred words are full of the Lord's commandments, why is it that the Lord speaketh of love as of a singular commandment: This is my commandment, that you love one another: save that every commandment is of love alone, and all are one commandment? for whatsoever is commanded is made firm in charity alone. For as many branches of a tree come forth from one root, so many virtues are begotten of the one charity. Nor hath the branch of good work any greenness, if it abide not in the root of charity.
cumcunctasacreloquiadominicisplenasintpr.la: Cum cuncta sacra elóquia Domínicis plena sint præcéptis, quid est quod de dilectióne, quasi de singulári mandáto, Dóminus dicit: Hoc est præcéptum meum, ut diligátis ínvicem: nisi quia omne mandátum de sola dilectióne est: et ómnia unum præcéptum sunt? quia quidquid praecípitur, in sola charitáte solidátur. Ut enim multi árboris rami ex una radíce pródeunt: sic multæ virtútes ex una charitáte generántur. Nec habet áliquid viriditátis ramus boni óperis, si non manet in radíce charitátis.

preceptergodominicetmultasuntetunummulta.en: The Lord's commandments therefore are both many and one: many by the diversity of work, one in the root of love. And how this love is to be held, he himself showeth, who in many sentences of his Scripture biddeth both that friends be loved in him, and enemies for his sake. For he truly hath charity, who both loveth his friend in God, and loveth his enemy for God's sake. For there are some who love their neighbours, but through the affection of kinship and of the flesh: to whom, however, the sacred words do not gainsay this love: but it is one thing which is freely given to nature, another which is owed by charity to obedience to the Lord's commandments.
preceptergodominicetmultasuntetunummulta.la: Præcépta ergo Domínica et multa sunt, et unum: multa per diversitátem óperis, unum in radíce dilectiónis. Quáliter autem ista diléctio tenénda sit, ipse insínuat, qui in plerísque Scriptúræ suæ senténtiis et amícos jubet díligi in se, et inimícos propter se. Ille enim veráciter charitátem habet, qui et amícum díligit in Deo, et inimícum díligit propter Deum. Nam sunt nonnúlli, qui díligunt próximos, sed per afféctum cognatiónis et carnis: quibus tamen in hac dilectióne sacra elóquia non contradícunt: sed áliud est quod sponte impénditur natúræ, áliud quod præcéptis Domínicis ex charitáte debétur obediéntiæ.

hinimirumetproximumdiliguntettamenillasu.en: These indeed both love their neighbour, and yet attain not those sublime rewards of love: because they spend their love not spiritually, but carnally. Wherefore, when the Lord said: This is my commandment, that you love one another: he straightway added: As I have loved you: as if he said openly: Love for that end for which I have loved you. In which matter, dearest brethren, we must carefully consider that the old enemy, while he draweth our mind to the love of temporal things, stirreth up against us a weaker neighbour, who striveth to take away those very things which we love.
hinimirumetproximumdiliguntettamenillasu.la: Hi nimírum et próximum díligunt, et tamen illa sublímia dilectiónis præmia non assequúntur: quia amórem suum non spiritáliter, sed carnáliter impéndunt. Proínde cum Dóminus díceret: Hoc est præcéptum meum, ut diligátis ínvicem: prótinus áddidit: Sicut diléxi vos: ac si apérte dicat: Ad hoc amáte, ad quod amávi vos. Qua in re, fratres charíssimi, solérter intuéndum est, quod antíquus hostis, dum mentem nostram ad rerum temporálium dilectiónem trahit, infirmiórem contra nos próximum éxcitat, qui ea ipsa, quæ dilígimus, auférre moliátur.

petrusdecastronovopietateacdoctrinaconsp.en: Peter of Castelnau, conspicuous for piety and learning, from being Archdeacon of the Church of Maguelone became a Cistercian Monk in the Monastery of Fontfroide, in the diocese of Narbonne, and together with Arnold, Abbot of Citeaux, and Ralph, a Monk, was appointed by Innocent the Third Apostolic legate and first inquisitor of the faith against the Albigensian heretics, the charge being laid on them to bring back the straying sheep to the fold of Christ; and to restrain by ecclesiastical censures and other penalties those, if any there were, who truly persisted in contumacy. It seemeth incredible how many hardships and dangers blessed Peter especially endured for the spreading of the orthodox faith, in deposing from their dignity Bishops defiled with the stain of heresy, and in bringing back very many heretics to sound doctrine by public disputations; by whom therefore, being hated above the others, he foretold not long before his martyrdom, which Pope Innocent described in his letter.
petrusdecastronovopietateacdoctrinaconsp.la: Petrus de Castronóvo pietáte ac doctrína conspícuus, ex Archidiácono Ecclésiæ Magalonénsis Mónachus Cisterciénsis in Monastério Fontis Frígidi, diœcésis Narbonénsis, una cum Arnáldo Abbáte Cisterciénsi, et Radúlpho Mónacho, contra hæréticos Albigénses ab Innocéntio tértio legátus Apostólicus et primus inquisítor fídei destinátus fuit, mandáto iis impósito, ut ad ovíle Christi oves redúcerent errántes; in contumácia vere persisténtes, si quæ forent, Ecclesiásticis censúris aliísque pœnis reprímerent. Incredíbile vidétur quot incómmoda et perícula, præcípue beatus Petrus pro dilatatióne orthodóxæ fídei sustinúerit, in Epíscopis hærética labe pollútis a dignitáte deponéndis, ac plúrimis hæréticis per públicas disputatiónes ad doctrínam sanam reducéndis; a quibus proínde super álios ódio hábitus, martyrium suum non multo ante prædíxit, quod Innocéntius Papa in sua epístola descrípsit.

exlitterisinnocentiipapetertii.en: From the letters of Pope Innocent the Third.

cumsanctememoriepetrusdecastronovomonach.en: When Peter of Castelnau, of holy memory, Monk and Priest, a man assuredly virtuous among men, illustrious in life, learning and renown, having been sent with others to preach the gospel of peace and to strengthen the faith in the province of Languedoc, had made praiseworthy progress in the ministry committed to him, and had not ceased to make progress, the devil stirred up against him his minister Raymund, Count of Toulouse; whose henchman, while the harmless soldier of Christ, having celebrated Mass, was preparing himself for the crossing of the river Rhone, brandishing his lance, wounded below between the ribs the aforesaid Peter, founded with unshaken firmness upon Christ the rock, and unwary of so great a treachery. Who, first looking upon the striker himself, and following the example of Christ his master with blessed Stephen, said to him: May God forgive thee, for I forgive thee. Then the athlete of Christ, thus pierced through, forgot the very bitterness of the wound inflicted, through hope of heavenly things, and as the moment of his precious death drew near, he urged upon the companions of his ministry that they should promote the faith and not cease to establish peace; and after due prayers he fell asleep faithfully in Christ. Who indeed shed his blood for faith and peace, than which there is no cause whatever more praiseworthy for martyrdom.
cumsanctememoriepetrusdecastronovomonach.la: Cum sanctæ memóriæ Petrus de Castronóvo, Mónachus et Sacérdos, vir inter viros útique virtuósus, vita, sciéntia et fama præclárus, ad evangelizándam pacem, confirmandámque fidem in província Occitániæ cum áliis destinátus, in commísso sibi ministério laudabíliter profecísset, et profícere non cessásset, concitávit advérsus ipsum diábolus minístrum suum cómitem Tolosánum Raymúndum, cujus satélles, dum innócuus Christi miles, Missa celebráta, ad tránsitum Rhódani flúvii se præparáret, lánceam suam vibrans prænominátum Petrum supra Christum petram immóbili firmitáte fundátum, tantæ proditiónis incáutum inter costas inférius vulnerávit. Qui prius ipsum respíciens percussórem, et Christi magístri sui cum beáto Stéphano secútus exémplum, dixit ad ipsum: Deus tibi dimíttat, quia ego dimítto. Deínde Christi athléta sic transfíxus, ipsam acerbitátem illáti vúlneris spe cœléstium est oblítus, et instánte suæ pretiósæ mortis artículo, inculcávit ministérii sui sóciis, ut fidem promovérent, et pacem non desínerent ordináre, ac post justas oratiónes in Christo fidéliter obdormívit. Qui profécto ob fídem et pacem, quibus nulla est prorsus causa laudabílior ad martyrium, sánguinem suum fudit.

omnipotenssempiternedeusquibeatumpetrumm.en: Almighty everlasting God, who didst endow blessed Peter, a valiant Martyr, a minister in the spreading of thy faith, with that charity which seeketh not her own: root out the thorns of covetousness, the root of all evils; that we, by hating well, may truly love, and, being well lost, may happily find ourselves unto life eternal.
omnipotenssempiternedeusquibeatumpetrumm.la: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, qui beátum Petrum, Mártyrem strénuum in propagatióne fídei tuæ minístrum ea charitáte donásti, quæ non quærit quæ sua sunt: cupiditátis, ómnium malórum radícis, spinas evélle; ut nos bene odiéndo vere amémus, et bene pérditos in vitam ætérnam felíciter inveniámus.

thomaslandulphocomiteaquinateettheodoran.en: Thomas, born of noble parents, Landulph, Count of Aquino, and Theodora of Naples, in his fifth year was given into the keeping of the Monks of St. Benedict at Monte Cassino. Thence, sent to Naples for the sake of his studies, while yet a youth he entered the Order of Friars Preachers. But as his mother and brothers took this ill, he was sent to Paris.
thomaslandulphocomiteaquinateettheodoran.la: Thomas, Landúlpho cómite Aquináte, et Theodóra Neapolitána, nobílibus parénti-bus natus, quintum annum agens, Mónachis sancti Benedícti Cassinátibus custodiéndus tráditur. Inde Neápolim studiórum causa missus, jam adoléscens Fratrum Prædicatórum Ordinem suscépit. Sed matre ac frátribus id indígne feréntibus, Lutétiam Parisiórum míttitur.

quemfratresinitinerepervimraptuminarcemc.en: His brothers, seizing him by force on the way, brought him to the fortress of the castle of San Giovanni: where, being variously harassed that he might change his holy purpose, he even put to flight with a firebrand a woman who had been brought in to overthrow his constancy. Soon the blessed youth, praying on bended knees before the sign of the Cross, and there overcome by sleep, seemed in his rest to feel his loins girt tight by Angels; from which time he was ever afterwards free from every feeling of lust.
quemfratresinitinerepervimraptuminarcemc.la: Quem fratres in itínere per vim raptum, in arcem castri sancti Joánnis perdúcunt: ubi várie exagitátus, ut sanctum propósitum mutáret, muliérem étiam, quæ ad labefáctandam ejus constántiam introdúcta fúerat, titióne fugávit. Mox beátus júvenis, fléxis génibus ante signum Crucis orans, ibíque somno corréptus, per quiétem sentíre visus est, sibi ab Angelis constríngi lumbos; quo ex témpore omni póstea libídinis sensu cáruit.

emissusecastroperfenestramneapolimreduci.en: Let out of the castle through a window, he was brought back to Naples; whence, taken to Rome and afterwards to Paris, he applied himself to Philosophy and Theology. He never gave himself to reading or writing except after prayer. In the difficulties of passages of holy Scripture, he joined fasting to prayer. At Naples, when he was praying very earnestly before an image of the Crucified, he heard this voice: Thou hast written well of me, Thomas; what reward then wilt thou receive? To whom he answered: None other, Lord, but thyself.
emissusecastroperfenestramneapolimreduci.la: Emíssus e castro per fenéstram, Neápolim redúcitur; unde Romam, póstea Parísium ductus, Philosophíæ ac Theologíæ óperam dedit. Numquam se lectióni aut scriptióni dedit, nisi post oratiónem. In difficultátibus locórum sacræ Scriptúræ, ad oratiónem jejúnium adhibébat. Neápoli cum ad imáginem Crucifixi veheméntius oráret, hanc vocem audívit: Bene scripsísti de me, Thoma; quam ergo mercédem accípies? Cui ille: Non áliam, Dómine, nisi teípsum.

aburbanoquartoromamvocatusadducinonpotui.en: Called to Rome by Urban the Fourth, he could not be induced to accept honours. He also refused the Archbishopric of Naples, when Pope Clement the Fourth offered it to him. Sent by Gregory the Tenth to the Council of Lyons, he fell sick in the monastery of Fossa Nova of the Cistercian Order, where, while sick, he expounded the Canticle of Canticles. There he died, fifty years of age, in the year of salvation one thousand two hundred and seventy-four.
aburbanoquartoromamvocatusadducinonpotui.la: Ab Urbáno quarto Romam vocátus, addúci non pótuit, ut honóres accíperet. Archiepiscopátum Neapolitanum étiam deferénte Cleménte quarto Pontífice recusávit. Missus a Gregório décimo ad Concílium Lugdunénse, in monastério Fossæ Novæ Cisterciénsis Ordinis in morbum íncidit, ubi ægró­tus Cántica Canticórum explanávit. Ibídem óbiit quinquagenárius, anno salútis millésimo ducentésimo septuagésimo quarto.

gregoriusmagnusromanusgordianisenatorisf.en: Gregory the Great, a Roman, son of the Senator Gordian, as a youth applied himself to philosophy, and, having discharged the office of praetor, on his father's death he built six monasteries in Sicily, and a seventh at Rome in his own house, named after St. Andrew, where he professed the life of a Monk, and was afterwards Abbot. Soon, created Cardinal Deacon, he was sent by Pope Pelagius as legate to Constantinople, to the emperor Tiberius Constantine.
gregoriusmagnusromanusgordianisenatorisf.la: Gregórius Magnus, Románus, Gordiáni Senatóris fílius, adoléscens philosóphiæ ópe­ram dedit, et prætório offício functus, patre mórtuo, sex monastéria in Sicília ædificávit, Romæ séptimum sancti Andreæ nómine in suis ædibus, ubi Mónachi vitam proféssus, postéa Abbas fuit. Mox Diáconus Cardinális creátus, Constantinópolim a Pelágio Pontífice ad Tibérium Constantínum imperatórem legátus míttitur.

ibieutychiumpatriarchamquiscripseratcont.en: There he so refuted the Patriarch Eutychius, who had written against the true and palpable resurrection of bodies, that the Emperor cast his book into the fire. Wherefore Eutychius, as death drew near, held the skin of his hand, saying: I confess that we shall all rise again in this flesh. Pelagius being carried off by the pestilence, he was chosen Pontiff: and that he might not accept this honour, he hid himself in a cave in another's clothing: where, being discovered by the token of a fiery pillar, he was consecrated.
ibieutychiumpatriarchamquiscripseratcont.la: Ibi Eutychium Patriárcham, qui scrípserat contra veram ac tractábilem córporum resurrectiónem, ita convícit, ut ejus librum Imperátor in ignem injíceret. Quare Eutychius, instánte morte, pellem manus suæ tenébat, dicens: Confíteor quia omnes in hac carne resurgémus. Pelágio pestiléntia subláto, Póntifex elígitur: quem honórem ne accíperet, aliéno vestítu in spelúnca delítuit: ubi deprehénsus indício igneæ colúmnæ, consecrátur.

peregrinosquotidieadmensamadhibebatinqui.en: He daily brought strangers to his table: among whom he received both an Angel, and the Lord of Angels in the guise of a stranger. He kindly supported the poor, both of the city and from without, whose number he had written down. He restored the Catholic faith, which had been shaken in many places. Having sent into Britain learned and holy men, Augustine and other monks, he converted the island to the faith of Jesus Christ. He broke the boldness of John, Patriarch of Constantinople, who arrogated to himself the name of Bishop of the universal Church.
peregrinosquotidieadmensamadhibebatinqui.la: Peregrínos quotídie ad mensam adhibébat: in quibus et Angelum, et Dóminum Angelórum peregríni fácie accépit. Páuperes et urbános et extérnos, quorum númerum descríptum habébat, benígne sustentábat. Cathólicam fidem multis locis labefactátam restítuit. Missis in Británniam doctis et sanctis viris Augustíno et áliis mónachis, ínsulam ad Jesu Christi fidem convértit. Joánnis Patriárchæ Constantinopolitáni audáciam fregit, qui sibi universális Ecclésiæ Epíscopi nomen arrogábat.

mauritiumimperatoremeosquimilitesfuissen.en: He turned the emperor Maurice from his decree forbidding those who had been soldiers to become monks. He adorned the Church with most holy institutions and laws. He composed many books: and Peter the Deacon testified that, while he dictated them, he often saw the Holy Ghost in the likeness of a dove upon his head. At length, having wrought many miracles, he was called to heavenly bliss.
mauritiumimperatoremeosquimilitesfuissen.la: Maurítium imperatórem, eos qui mílites fuíssent, mónachos fiéri prohibéntem, a senténtia detérruit. Ecclésiam ornávit sanctíssimis institútis et légibus. Multos libros confécit: quos cum dictáret, testátus est Petrus Diáconus, se Spíritum sanctum colúmbæ spécie in ejus cápite sæpe vidísse. Deníque multis éditis miráculis, ad cœléstem beatitúdinem evocátus est.

considerandumnobisestutquiuneademqueexho.en: We must consider that he who doth not suffice to admonish all together with one and the same voice of exhortation, should strive to instruct each one, so far as he is able, and to edify them by private conversations. For we ought continually to ponder what is said to the holy Apostles, and through the Apostles to us: You are the salt of the earth. If therefore we are salt, we ought to season the minds of the faithful.
considerandumnobisestutquiuneademqueexho.la: Considerándum nobis est, ut, qui una eadémque exhortatiónis voce non súfficit simul cunctos admonére, stúdeat síngulos, in quantum valet, instrúere, privátis locutiónibus ædificáre. Debémus namque pensáre contínuo, quod sanctis Apóstolis dícitur, et per Apóstolos nobis: Vos estis sal terræ. Si ergo sal sumus, condíre mentes fidélium debémus.

vosigiturquipastoresestispensatequiadeia.en: Ye therefore who are pastors, consider that ye feed the animals of God; of which animals indeed it is said to God by the Psalmist: Thy animals shall dwell therein. And often we see that a block of salt is set before brute animals, that they may lick from that same block of salt, and be bettered. As a block of salt among brute animals, therefore, ought the priest to be among the peoples.
vosigiturquipastoresestispensatequiadeia.la: Vos ígitur, qui pastóres estis, pensáte, quia Dei animália páscitis; de quibus profécto animálibus Deo per Psalmístam dícitur: Animália tua habitábunt in ea. Et sæpe vidémus, quod petra salis brutis animálibus antepónitur, ut ex éadem salis petra lámbere débeant, et meliorári. Quasi ergo inter bruta animália petra salis, debet esse sacérdos in pópulis.

curarenamquesacerdotemnecesseestquesingu.en: For it is needful that the priest take care what he say to each, how he admonish every one: that whosoever is joined to the priest, may be seasoned as by the touch of salt with the savour of eternal life. For we are not the salt of the earth, if we season not the hearts of our hearers: which seasoning indeed he truly bestoweth on his neighbour, who withholdeth not the word of preaching. But then do we truly preach right things to others, if we show forth our words by deeds and examples.
curarenamquesacerdotemnecesseestquesingu.la: Curáre namque sacerdótem necésse est, quæ síngulis dicat, unumquémque quáliter admóneat: ut quisquis sacerdóti júngitur, quasi ex salis tactu ætérnæ vitæ sapóre condiátur. Sal étenim terræ non sumus, si corda audiéntium non condímus: quod profécto condiméntum ille veráciter próximo impéndit, qui prædicatiónis verbum non súbtrahit. Sed tunc vere áliis recta prædicámus, si dicta rebus et exémplis osténdimus.

comperistandempatriosreducis.en: Thou findest him at last; thou leadest him back to his native

astraquicelosregitatqueterras.la: Astra qui cœlos regit, atque terras,

infericuiustremuerenumen.en: Whose majesty they below have trembled at,

cumessetdesponsatamateriesumariaiosephan.en: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child, of the Holy Ghost. And so on.
cumessetdesponsatamateriesumariaiosephan.la: Cum esset desponsáta Mater Jesu Maria Joseph, ántequam convenírent, invénta est in útero habens de Spíritu Sancto. Et réliqua.

illautiquefuitratiodesponsationismariequ.en: That indeed was the reason of the espousal of Mary which was also the reason of the doubting of Thomas. For it was the custom of the Jews that, from the day of their espousal until the time of the marriage, the brides were given over to the bridegrooms to be guarded: so that they might keep their chastity for themselves the more carefully, the more faithful they themselves should prove to themselves.
illautiquefuitratiodesponsationismariequ.la: Illa útique fuit rátio desponsatiónis Maríæ,quæ et dubitatiónis Thomæ. Mos siquidem Judæórum erat, ut a die desponsatiónis suæ, usque ad tempus nuptiárum, sponsis sponsæ traderéntur custodiéndæ: quátenus eárum ipsi eo sibi pudicítiam curiósius servárent, quo sibi ipsi fidelióres exísterent.

sicutergothomasdubitandetpalpandoconstan.en: As therefore Thomas, by doubting and by touching, was made a most steadfast witness of the Lord's resurrection: so also Joseph, by espousing Mary to himself, and by proving her conduct the more carefully in the time of his guardianship, was made a most faithful witness of her chastity.
sicutergothomasdubitandetpalpandoconstan.la: Sicut ergo Thomas dubitándo, et palpándo, constantíssimus factus est Dominicæ conféssor resurrectiónis: ita et Joseph Maríam sibi desponsándo, ejúsque conversatiónem in témpore custodiæ studiósius comprobándo, factus est pudicítiæ fidelíssimus testis.

pulchrautriusquereiconvenientietdubitati.en: A fair agreement of both things: both the doubting of Thomas and the espousal of Mary. They could indeed have cast upon us the snare of a like error, namely, to bring into suspicion the truth of faith in the one, and of chastity in the other: but it was done very wisely and piously the contrary way, that whence suspicion was feared, thence there should be firm certainty.
pulchrautriusquereiconvenientietdubitati.la: Pulchra utriúsque rei conveniéntia: et dubitátio Thomæ et desponsátio Mariæ. Póterant quidem símilis erróris láqueum nobis injícere, fidei vidélicet in illo, castitátis in illa, veritátem in suspiciónem addúcere: sed valde prudenter et pie factum est per contrárium, ut unde metuebátur suspício, firma sit certitúdo.

nametdefiliiresurrectionecitiusquidemego.en: For concerning the resurrection of the Son, I (who am weak) would sooner believe Thomas doubting and touching than Cephas hearing and believing: and concerning the continence of the Mother, more readily her spouse who guarded and proved it, than the Virgin herself defending herself by her own conscience alone.
nametdefiliiresurrectionecitiusquidemego.la: Nam et de Fílii resurrectióne cítius quidem ego (qui infírmus sum) credíderim Thomæ dubitánti et palpánti, quam Cephæ audiénti et credénti: et de Matris continéntia facílius sponso ejus custodiénti, et experiénti, quam ipsi quoque Vírgini de sola sua consciéntia se defendénti.

istesanctusdigneinmemoriamvertiturhominu.en: This Saint * is worthily kept in the memory of men, who hath passed to the joy of the Angels; because, set in this pilgrimage in the body alone, in thought and desire he had his conversation in that eternal fatherland.
istesanctusdigneinmemoriamvertiturhominu.la: Iste Sanctus * digne in memóriam vértitur hóminum, qui ad gáudium tránsiit Angelórum; quia in hac peregrinatióne solo córpore constitútus, cogitatióne et aviditáte in illa aetérna patria, conversátus est.

iustumdeduxitdominusperviasrectasetosten.en: The Lord conducted the just * through the right ways, and shewed him the kingdom of God, and gave him the knowledge of the holy things: made him honourable in his labours, and accomplished his labours.
iustumdeduxitdominusperviasrectasetosten.la: Justum dedúxit Dóminus * per vias rectas, et osténdit illi regnum Dei, et dedit illi sciéntiam Sanctórum: honestávit illum in labóribus, et complévit labóres illíus.

amaviteumdominusetornaviteumstolamglorie.en: The Lord loved him * and beautified him. He clothed him with a robe of glory, and crowned him at the gates of Paradise.
amaviteumdominusetornaviteumstolamglorie.la: Amávit eum Dóminus, * et ornávit eum: Stolam glóriæ induit eum, et ad portas paradísi coronávit eum.

istecognovitiustitiametviditmirabiliamag.en: This man knew * justice, and saw great wonders, and prayed to the Most High, and was found in the number of the Saints.
istecognovitiustitiametviditmirabiliamag.la: Iste cognóvit * justítiam, et vidit mirabília magna, et exorávit Altíssimum, et invéntus est in número Sanctórum.

sanctusbenedictusplusappetiitmalamundipe.en: St. Benedict desired rather to suffer the ills of the world than its praises,
sanctusbenedictusplusappetiitmalamundipe.la: Sanctus Benedíctus plus appétiit mala mundi pérpeti, quam laudes,

malensprodeolaboribusfatigariquamvitehui.en: Choosing rather to be wearied with labours for God than to be lifted up by the favours of this life. Alleluia.
malensprodeolaboribusfatigariquamvitehui.la: Malens pro Deo labóribus fatigári, quam vitæ hujus favóribus extólli. Allelúia.

divinanamquepreventusgratiamagisacmagisa.en: For, prevented by divine grace, he sighed in spirit more and more after the things above:
divinanamquepreventusgratiamagisacmagisa.la: Divína namque prævéntus grátia, magis ac magis ad supérna ánimo suspirábat:

interardentesseraphimcatervas.en: Amid the burning hosts of the Seraphim

excitadomineinecclesiatuaspiritumcuibeat.en: Stir up, O Lord, in thy Church the Spirit which blessed Benedict, Abbot, served: that, being filled with the same, we may strive to love what he loved, and to practise in deed what he taught.
excitadomineinecclesiatuaspiritumcuibeat.la: Excita, Dómine, in Ecclésia tua Spíritum, cui beátus Benedíctus, Abbas, servívit: ut, eódem nos repléti, studeámus amáre quod amávit, et ópere exercére quod dócuit.

abipsopueritiesuetemporecorgerenssenilee.en: From the very time * of his boyhood bearing the heart of an old man, surpassing his age in conduct, he gave his mind to no pleasure.

nursieprovinciaortusromeliberalibuslitte.en: Born in the province * of Nursia, he had been given by his parents to the liberal studies of letters at Rome.
nursieprovinciaortusromeliberalibuslitte.la: Núrsiæ * província ortus, Romæ liberálibus litterárum stúdiis tráditus a paréntibus fúerat. Ps. 5

recessitigiturscienternesciensetsapiente.en: He withdrew therefore, * knowingly unknowing, and wisely unlearned.
recessitigiturscienternesciensetsapiente.la: Recéssit ígitur * sciénter nésciens, et sapiénter indóctus. Ps. 10

hicitaquecumiamrelictislitterarumstudiis.en: And so when he, * having now left the studies of letters, had resolved to seek the desert, his nurse, who loved him very dearly, followed him.
hicitaquecumiamrelictislitterarumstudiis.la: Hic ítaque * cum jam relíctis litterárum stúdiis pétere desérta decrevísset, nutrix quæ hunc árctius amábat, secúta est. Ps. 14

predictanutrixilliusadpurgandumtriticuma.en: His aforesaid * nurse asked the neighbouring women to lend her a sieve to cleanse wheat, which by mischance was broken.
predictanutrixilliusadpurgandumtriticuma.la: Prædícta * nutrix illíus ad purgándum tríticum a vicínis muliéribus præstári sibi capistérium pétiit, quod casu accidénte fractum est. Ps. 20

compassusnutriciorationemfuditbenedictus.en: Having compassion * on his nurse, the boy Benedict poured forth prayer with tears, and repaired the sieve.
compassusnutriciorationemfuditbenedictus.la: Compássus * nutríci oratiónem fudit Benedíctus puer cum lácrymis, et capistérium reparávit. Ps. 23

benedictusdeifamulusmagnumfecitmiraculum.en: Benedict, the servant of God, * wrought a great miracle: he poured forth prayers to the Lord, and joined the sieve together again.
benedictusdeifamulusmagnumfecitmiraculum.la: Benedíctus Dei fámulus * magnum fecit miráculum, fudit preces ad Dóminum, et rejúnxit capistérium. Ps. 63

sanctimonialisautemfeminacumnegantisverb.en: But the nun, * when she had heard the words of him refusing, poured forth prayer, and a flood of rain burst forth.
sanctimonialisautemfeminacumnegantisverb.la: Sanctimoniális autem fœmina, * cum negántis verba audísset, oratiónem fudit et inundátio plúviæ erúpit. Ps. 256, 257, 258

fuitvirvitevenerabilisgratiabenedictuset.en: There was a man of venerable life, Benedict both by grace and by name, † from the very time of his boyhood bearing the heart of an old man
fuitvirvitevenerabilisgratiabenedictuset.la: Fuit vir vitæ venerábilis grátia Benedíctus et nómine, † ab ipso puerítæ suæ témpore cor gerens seníle

etatemquippemoribustransiensnullianimumv.en: For, surpassing his age in conduct, he gave his mind to no pleasure.
etatemquippemoribustransiensnullianimumv.la: Ætátem quippe móribus tránsiens nulli ánimum voluptáti dedit.

recessitigiturscienternesciusetsapienter.en: He withdrew therefore, knowingly unknowing and wisely unlearned.
recessitigiturscienternesciusetsapienter.la: Recéssit ígitur sciénter néscius et sapiénter indóctus.

beatusbenedictusfamulusdominimagnumfecit.en: Blessed Benedict, the servant of the Lord, wrought a great miracle: he poured forth prayers to the Lord,
beatusbenedictusfamulusdominimagnumfecit.la: Beátus Benedíctus fámulus Dómini magnum fecit miráculum, fudit preces ad Dóminum,

etresolidavitconfractumcapisterium.en: And made whole again the broken sieve.

benedictuspuercumnutricemsuamflereconspi.en: The boy Benedict, when he saw his nurse weeping, had compassion on her grief.
benedictuspuercumnutricemsuamflereconspi.la: Benedíctus puer, cum nutrícem suam flere conspíceret, ejus dolóri compássus est.

initoconsiliovenenumvinomiscuerequooblat.en: Having taken counsel, they mixed poison with the wine: and when it was offered, as the custom was, to the Father to bless, the man of God made the sign of the Cross, and the vessel of the deadly drink was so broken,
initoconsiliovenenumvinomiscuerequooblat.la: Inito consílio venénum vino miscuére: quo obláto ex more ad benedicéndum Patri, vir Dei signo Crucis édidit, et vas pestíferi potus ita confráctum est,

acsiprosignolapidemdedisset.en: As though he had given a stone instead of the sign.
acsiprosignolapidemdedisset.la: Ac si pro signo lápidem dedísset.

intellexitprotinusvirdeiquiapotummortish.en: The man of God by and by perceived that the glass had in it the drink of death, which could not endure the sign of life.
intellexitprotinusvirdeiquiapotummortish.la: Intelléxit prótinus vir Dei, quia potum mortis habúerat, quod portáre non póterat signum vitæ.

sanctusbenedictusplusappetiitmalamundipe.en: St. Benedict desired rather to suffer the ills of the world than its praises; † to be wearied with labours for God,
sanctusbenedictusplusappetiitmalamundipe.la: Sanctus Benedíctus plus appétiit mala mundi pérpeti quam laudes; † pro Deo labóribus fatigári,

quamvitehuiusfavoribusextolli.en: Rather than to be lifted up by the favours of this life.

dominenonaspiciaspeccatameasedfidemhuius.en: O Lord, look not upon my sins, but upon the faith of this man, who asketh that his son be raised to life: and restore to this little body the soul which thou hast taken away. And when the prayer was ended, he came to life again:
dominenonaspiciaspeccatameasedfidemhuius.la: Dómine, non aspícias peccáta mea, sed fidem hujus hóminis, qui rogat resuscitári fílium suum: et redde in hoc corpúsculum ánimam quam tulísti. Et compléta oratióne revíxit:

etsanumreddiditpatrisuo.en: And he gave him back to his father healthy.

etregredienteanimacorpusculumomnecontrem.en: And as the soul returned, the whole little body trembled, † and before the eyes of all who were present he appeared alive.
etregredienteanimacorpusculumomnecontrem.la: Et regrediénte ánima corpúsculum omne contrémuit, † et sub óculis ómnium qui áderant, vivus appáruit.

cumquesanctusbenedictusincellaconsistere.en: And when St. Benedict was standing in his cell, lifting up his eyes on high, he saw the soul of his sister, gone forth from her body,
cumquesanctusbenedictusincellaconsistere.la: Cumque sanctus Benedíctus in cella consísteret, elevátis sursum óculis, vidit soróris suæ ánimam de córpore ejus egréssam,

incolumbespeciecelisecretapenetrare.en: Enter the secret places of heaven in the likeness of a dove.
incolumbespeciecelisecretapenetrare.la: In colúmbæ spécie cæli secréta penetráre.

quitanteeiusgloriecongaudensomnipotentid.en: Who, rejoicing in her so great glory, gave thanks to almighty God, and announced her death to the brethren.
quitanteeiusgloriecongaudensomnipotentid.la: Qui tantæ ejus glóriæ congáudens omnipoténti Deo grátias rétulit, ejúsque óbitum frátribus denuntiávit.

intempestenoctishoravirdeiinstansvigilii.en: At the hour of the dead of night, the man of God, intent upon the vigils of unceasing prayer, as under one ray of the sun,
intempestenoctishoravirdeiinstansvigilii.la: Intempéstæ noctis hora vir dei instans vigíliis assíduæ oratiónis, velut sub uno solis radio,

omnemmundumcollectumconspexit.en: Saw the whole world gathered together.

videntienimcreatoremangustestomniscreatu.en: For to him that seeth the Creator all creation is narrow.
videntienimcreatoremangustestomniscreatu.la: Vidénti enim Creatórem angústa est omnis creatúra.

patersanctusdumintentamoculorumacieminsp.en: While the holy Father was seen to hold the gaze of his eyes intent upon the splendour of the flashing light, † he saw the soul of Germanus, Bishop of Capua,
patersanctusdumintentamoculorumacieminsp.la: Pater sanctus dum inténtam oculórum áciem in splendóre corúscæ lucis habére viderétur, † vidit Germáni ánimam Capuáni epíscopi

inspheraigneaabangelisincelumdeferri.en: Carried up by Angels into heaven in a fiery globe.
inspheraigneaabangelisincelumdeferri.la: In sphæra ígnea ab angelis in cælum deférri.

factumqueestutreverendissimumvirumgerman.en: And it came to pass that he who had been sent found the most reverend man Germanus, the bishop, already dead.
factumqueestutreverendissimumvirumgerman.la: Factúmque est, ut reverendíssimum virum Germánum epíscopum is qui missus fúerat, jam defúnctum réperit.

homilinnatalisben.en: Homily on the Birthday of St. Benedict.

perfectusilleestquiabiensvenditomniaqueh.en: He is perfect who goeth and selleth all that he hath, and giveth to the poor, and cometh and followeth Christ; for he shall have a treasure in heaven which faileth not. Whence well did Jesus, when Peter asked, say to such: Amen I say to you, that you who have followed me, in the regeneration, when the Son of man shall sit on the seat of his majesty, you also shall sit on twelve seats judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
perfectusilleestquiabiensvenditomniaqueh.la: Perféctus ille est, qui ábiens véndit ómnia quæ habet, et dat paupéribus, ac véniens séquitur Christum; habébit enim thesáurum non deficiéntem in cœlis. Unde bene, interrogánte Petro, dixit tálibus Jesus: Amen dico vobis, quod vos qui secúti estis me, in regeneratióne, cum séderit Fílius hóminis in sede majestátis suæ, sedébitis et vos super sedes duódecim, judicántes duódecim tribus Israël.

eodemvereannoquodehacviteratexiturusquib.en: In the very year in which he was to depart from this life, to some disciples living with him, and to some dwelling far off,
eodemvereannoquodehacviteratexiturusquib.la: Eódem vere anno, quo de hac vita erat exitúrus, quibúsdam discípulis secum conversántibus, quibúsdam longe manéntibus,

sanctissimisuiobitusdenuntiavitdiem.en: He announced the day of his most holy death.

presentibusindicensutauditapersilentiumt.en: Bidding those present to keep in silence what they had heard: † showing those absent what sign, and of what kind, should be given them when his soul should go forth from the body.
presentibusindicensutauditapersilentiumt.la: Præséntibus indicens, ut audíta per siléntium tégerent: † abséntibus índicans, quod vel quale eis signum fíeret quando ejus ánima de córpore exíret.

inhacquippevitapreiusnominelaborantesina.en: For he taught those who labour in this life for his name to hope for their reward in another, that is, in the regeneration; namely, when we, who were born mortally into a perishable life, shall have been regenerated by rising again into immortal life. And it is a most just recompense, that they who here for Christ's sake have despised the glory of human loftiness, should there be glorified by Christ as judges and sit singularly with him, they who could by no means be torn away from following his footsteps.
inhacquippevitapreiusnominelaborantesina.la: In hac quippe vita pro ejus nómine laborántes, in ália præmium speráre dócuit, id est, in regeneratióne; cum vidélicet in vitam immortálem fuérimus resurgéndo regeneráti, qui in vitam cadúcam mortáliter erámus géniti. Et justa prorsus retribútio, ut, qui hic pro Christo humánæ glóriam celsitúdinis neglexérunt, illic a Christo júdices glorificáti singuláriter cum eo assídeant qui a sequéndis ejus vestígiis nulla ratióne póterant avélli.

sextonamquedieportariseinoratoriumadisci.en: For on the sixth day he had himself carried by his disciples into the Oratory, and there he fortified his departure with the Lord's sacraments;
sextonamquedieportariseinoratoriumadisci.la: Sexto namque die portári se in Oratórium a discípulis suis fecit, ibíque éxitum suum Domínicis sacraméntis munívit;

atqueinterdiscipulorummanusexpiravit.en: Then, in the arms of his disciples he breathed his last

cumquepersingulosdieslanguoringravescere.en: And when his weakness grew heavier day by day, he stood with his hands raised up to heaven.
cumquepersingulosdieslanguoringravescere.la: Cumque per síngulos dies languor ingravésceret, eréctis in cœlum mánibus stetit.

nemoautemputetduodecimtantumapostolosqui.en: But let no one think that only the twelve Apostles (since Matthias was chosen in place of the prevaricating Judas) shall then be judges: as neither are the twelve tribes of Israel alone to be judged: otherwise the tribe of Levi, which is the thirteenth, will go away unjudged. And shall Paul, who is the thirteenth Apostle, be deprived of the lot of judging? when he himself saith: Know you not that we shall judge angels? how much more things of this world?
nemoautemputetduodecimtantumapostolosqui.la: Nemo autem putet duódecim tantum Apóstolos, quia pro Juda prævaricánte Matthias eléctus est, tunc esse judicatúros: sicut nec duódecim solæ sunt tribus Israël judicándæ: alióquin tribus Levi, quæ tertiadécima est, injudicáta recédet. Et Paulus, qui tertiusdécimus est Apóstolus, judicándi sorte privábitur? cum ipse dicat: Nescítis quóniam ángelos judicábimus, quanto magis sæculária?

viarectoorientistramiteabeiuscellaincelu.en: A way, in a straight course toward the east, stretched from his cell even unto heaven; † and a man of venerable aspect, shining from above, standing by it, asked whose way it was that they beheld:
viarectoorientistramiteabeiuscellaincelu.la: Via, recto oriéntis trámite ab ejus cella in cælum usque tendebátur; † cui venerándo hábitu vir désuper clarus assístens, cujus esset via, quam cérnerent, inquisívit:

illiautemsenescireprofessisunt.en: But they professed that they knew not.
illiautemsenescireprofessisunt.la: Illi autem se nescíre proféssi sunt.

quibusipseaithecestviaquadilectusdominib.en: To whom he said: † This is the way by which Benedict, the beloved of the Lord, ascended into heaven.
quibusipseaithecestviaquadilectusdominib.la: Quibus ipse ait: † Hæc est via, qua diléctus Dómini Benedíctus cælos ascéndit.

sciendumnamqueestomnesquiadexemplumapost.en: For it is to be known that all who, after the example of the Apostles, have left all things and followed Christ, shall come with him as judges, even as the whole race of mortals is to be judged. For since in the Scriptures the whole is often wont to be signified by the number twelve, by the twelve seats of the Apostles is shown the whole multitude of them that judge, and by the twelve tribes of Israel the whole number of them that are to be judged.
sciendumnamqueestomnesquiadexemplumapost.la: Sciéndum namque est, omnes, qui ad exémplum Apostolórum, sua reliquérunt ómnia et secúti sunt Christum, júdices cum eo ventúros, sicut étiam omne mortálium genus esse judicándum. Quia enim duodenário sæpe número solet in Scriptúris univérsitas designári, per duódecim sedes Apostolórum ómnium numerósitas judicántium, et, per duódecim tribus Israël, univérsitas eórum qui judicándi sunt, osténditur.

electusafratribusinvitusobtinuitquodscie.en: Chosen * by the brethren, he consented against his will, because he knew well that he could not agree with their manners.
electusafratribusinvitusobtinuitquodscie.la: Eléctus * a frátribus invítus obtínuit, quod sciénter scivit se illórum móribus conveníre non posse.

cumquesibiconspicerentillicitanonlicerea.en: And when they saw * that unlawful things were not lawful for them, and that they must leave their accustomed ways, they set about plotting his death.
cumquesibiconspicerentillicitanonlicerea.la: Cumque sibi conspícerent * illícita non licére, assuéta relínquere, conáti sunt de ejus morte tractáre.

initoconsiliovenenumvinomiscuerequooblat.en: Having taken counsel, * they mixed poison with the wine; and when it was offered, he signed the vessel, and so it was broken, as though he had given a stone instead of the sign.
initoconsiliovenenumvinomiscuerequooblat.la: Inito consílio, * venénum vino miscuére, quo obláto, signávit vas, sicque confráctum est, ac si pro signo lápidem dedísset.

puerquidamparvuluselephantinomorbopercus.en: A certain little boy, * stricken with the disease of elephantiasis, was brought to the man of God, and having recovered his former health, he returned home unharmed.
puerquidamparvuluselephantinomorbopercus.la: Puer quidam párvulus * elephantíno morbo percússus, ad Dei hóminem est addúctus, prístina sanitáte recépta, incólumis remeávit ad própria.

tantamgratiameivirtusdivinacontuleratuts.en: So great a grace * had the divine power bestowed on him, that under one ray of the sun he beheld the whole world gathered together.
tantamgratiameivirtusdivinacontuleratuts.la: Tantam grátiam * ei virtus divína contúlerat, ut sub uno solis rádio omnem mundum colléctum conspíceret.

dilectusdeethominibuscuiusmemoriainbened.en: Beloved of God and men, whose memory is in benediction. He made him like the saints in glory.
dilectusdeethominibuscuiusmemoriainbened.la: Diléctus Deo et homínibus, cujus memória in benedictióne est. Símilem illum fecit in glória Sanctórum.

patersanctusdumintentamoculorumacieminsp.en: The holy Father, * while he was seen to hold the gaze of his eyes intent upon the splendour of the flashing light, saw the soul of Germanus, Bishop of Capua, carried up into heaven by Angels in a fiery globe. Alleluia.
patersanctusdumintentamoculorumacieminsp.la: Pater sanctus * dum inténtam oculórum áciem in splendóre corúscæ lucis habére, viderétur, vidit Germáni ánimam Capuáni Epíscopi, in sphæra ígnea ab Angelis in cælum deférri. Allelúia.

deditconfessionemsanctetexcelsoinverbogl.en: He gave praise to the Holy One, and to the Most High, with words of glory. With his whole heart he praised the Lord, and loved God that made him.
deditconfessionemsanctetexcelsoinverbogl.la: Dedit confessiónem Sancto, et Excélso in verbo glóriæ. De omni corde suo laudávit Dóminum, et diléxit Deum qui fecit illum.

orabatsanctusbenedictusdominenonaspicias.en: St. Benedict prayed: * O Lord, look not upon my sins, but upon the faith of this man, who asketh that his son be raised to life; and before the eyes of all he gave back the boy alive to his father. Alleluia.
orabatsanctusbenedictusdominenonaspicias.la: Orábat sanctus Benedíctus: * Dómine, non aspícias peccáta mea, sed fidem hujus hóminis, qui rogat resuscitári fílium suum, et sub óculis ómnium vivéntem púerum réddidit patri suo. Allelúia.

ingressozachariatemplumdominiapparuiteig.en: When Zacharias went * into the Temple of the Lord, the Angel Gabriel appeared unto him, standing on the right side of the altar of incense.
ingressozachariatemplumdominiapparuiteig.la: Ingrésso Zacharía * templum Dómini, appáruit ei Gábriel Angelus, stans a dextris altáris incénsi.

aitautemangelusnetimeaszachariaquoniamex.en: But the Angel said: * Fear not, Zacharias, for thy prayer is heard.
aitautemangelusnetimeaszachariaquoniamex.la: Ait autem Angelus: * Ne tímeas, Zacharía, quóniam exaudíta est deprecátio tua.

gabrielangeluslocutusestmariedicenseccec.en: The Angel Gabriel * spake unto Mary, saying: Behold, thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and shalt bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name Jesus.
gabrielangeluslocutusestmariedicenseccec.la: Gábriel Angelus * locútus est Maríæ, dicens: Ecce concípies in útero, et páries fílium, et vocábis nomen ejus Jesum.

gabrielangelusdescenditadzachariametaiti.en: The Angel Gabriel * came down unto Zacharias, and said unto him: Thy wife shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John, and many shall rejoice in his nativity. For he shall go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways.
gabrielangelusdescenditadzachariametaiti.la: Gabriel Angelus * descéndit ad Zacharíam, et ait illi: Uxor tua páriet tibi fílium, et vocábis nomen ejus Joánnes, et multi in Nativitáte ejus gaudébunt. Ipse enim præíbit ante fáciem Dómini paráre vias ejus.

gloriosusapparuistiinconspectudomini.en: Glorious didst thou appear * In the sight of the Lord.

proptereadecoreminduittedominus.en: Therefore hath the Lord clothed thee with comeliness.

inconspectudomini.en: In the sight of the Lord.

adhucmeloquenteinorationeeccevirgabrielq.en: As I was yet * speaking in prayer, behold the man Gabriel, whom I had seen in the vision at the beginning, flying swiftly touched me at the time of the evening sacrifice.
adhucmeloquenteinorationeeccevirgabrielq.la: Adhuc * me loquénte in oratióne, ecce vir Gábriël, quem víderam in visióne a princípio, cito volans tétigit me in témpore sacrifícii vespertíni.

deusquiperarchangelumgabrielemsalvatorem.en: O God, who by the Archangel Gabriel didst announce to the most holy Virgin that she should conceive the Saviour of the world: grant that we may both conceive him with a pure mind, and imitate him with fervent affection.
deusquiperarchangelumgabrielemsalvatorem.la: Deus, qui per Archángelum Gabriëlem Salvatórem mundi Sacratíssimæ Vírgini concipiéndum nuntiásti: da, ut eúndem et mente pura concipiámus, et férvido imitémur afféctu.

ingressusgabrielangelusadmariamvirginemd.en: Being come in * unto the Virgin Mary, the Angel Gabriel said: Hail, full of grace, the Lord is with thee: blessed art thou among women.
ingressusgabrielangelusadmariamvirginemd.la: Ingréssus * Gabriël Angelus ad Maríam Vírginem dixit: Ave grátia plena, Dóminus tecum, benedícta tu in muliéribus. Ps. 97

missusestangelusgabrieladeononarbitrorhu.en: The Angel Gabriel was sent from God. I do not think that this Angel is of the lesser ones, who for whatever cause are wont to discharge frequent embassies; which is given to be plainly understood from his name, which being interpreted is said to be Strength of God. And because he is declared to be sent, not by some other spirit perhaps more excellent than himself (as is usual), but by God himself, for this reason it is set down: from God.
missusestangelusgabrieladeononarbitrorhu.la: Missus est Angelus Gábriel a Deo. Non árbitror hunc Angelum de minóribus esse, qui quálibet ex causa crebra sóleant fungi legatióne; quod ex ejus nómine palam intélligi datur, quod interpretátum fortitúdo Dei dícitur. Et quia non ab áliquo álio forte excellentióre se (ut ássolet) spíritu, sed ab ipso Deo mitti perhibétur, propter hoc pósitum est: a Deo.
