velideodictumestadeonecuivelbeatorumspir.en: Or else it is said: from God, lest God should be thought to have revealed his counsel to any even of the blessed spirits before the Virgin, save only the Archangel Gabriel. Who indeed could be found of such excellence among his fellows, that he was held worthy both of such a name and of such a message. Nor doth the name disagree with the message: for whom did it better befit to announce Christ, the power of God, than him whom a like name honoureth? For what else is strength than power? Nor doth it seem to us unbecoming or incongruous that the Lord and the messenger be reckoned under a common word: since, though the appellation in both be alike, yet the cause of it is not alike in both.
velideodictumestadeonecuivelbeatorumspir.la: Vel ídeo dictum est: a Deo, ne cui vel beatórum spirítuum suum Deus, ántequam Vírgini, revelásse putétur consílium, excepto duntáxat Archángelo Gabriéle. Qui útique tantæ inter suos inveníri potúerit excelléntiæ, ut, tali et nómine dignus haberétur et nuntio. Nec discórdat nomen a núntio: Dei quippe virtútem Christum, quem mélius nuntiáre decébat, quam hunc, quem símile nomen honórat? Numquid est áliud fortitúdo, quam virtus? Non autem dédecus et incóngruum vidémur, Dóminum et Núntium commúni censéri vocábulo: cum símilis in utróque appellatiónis, non sit tamen utrísque símilis causa.

aliterquippechristusfortitudovelvirtusde.en: For in one way is Christ called the strength or power of God, in another the Angel. For the Angel only in name, but Christ also in substance. Christ is called, and is, the power of God: which, coming upon the strong armed man who was wont to keep his court in peace, being stronger, overcame him with its own arm: and so mightily snatched from him the vessels of captivity.
aliterquippechristusfortitudovelvirtusde.la: Aliter quippe Christus fortitúdo, vel virtus Dei dícitur, áliter Angelus. Angelus enim tantum nuncupatíve. Christus autem étiam substantíve. Christus Dei virtus dícitur, et est: quæ forti armáto, qui suum átrium in pace custodíre solébat, fórtior supervéniens, ipsum suo bráchio debellávit: et sic ei vasa captivitátis poténter erípuit.

angelusverofortitudodeiappellatusestvelq.en: But the Angel was called the strength of God, either because he merited such a prerogative of office, that he should announce the coming of that same power: or because he was to strengthen the Virgin, by nature timid, simple and modest, lest she should be affrighted at the newness of the miracle: which also he did, saying: Fear not, Mary, for thou hast found grace with God. Fittingly therefore is Gabriel chosen for this work: nay rather, because such a business is enjoined upon him, he is rightly designated by such a name.
angelusverofortitudodeiappellatusestvelq.la: Angelus vero fortitúdo Dei appellátus est, vel quod hujuscémodi merúerit prærogatívam offícii, quo ejúsdem nuntiáret advéntum virtútis: vel quia Vírginem natúra pávidam, símplicem, verecúndam, ne miráculi novitáte expavésceret, confortáre debéret: quod et fecit. Ne tímeas ínquiens: Maria, invenísti enim grátiam apud Deum. Conveniénter ítaque Gábriel ad hoc opus elígitur: imo quia tale illi negótium injúngitur, recte tali nómine designátur.

inillotemporemissusestangelusgabrieladeo.en: At that time the angel Gabriel was sent from God into a city of Galilee, called Nazareth, To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin's name was Mary. And so on.
inillotemporemissusestangelusgabrieladeo.la: In illo témpore: Missus est Angelus Gábriel a Deo in civitátem Galilææ, cui nomen Názareth, ad Vírginem desponsátam Viro, cui nomen erat Joseph de domo David, et nomen Vírginis María. Et réliqua.

toletlibcontraiudeos.en: Of Toledo. Book 2 against the Jews.

sacramentumilludseptuagintahebdomadarumd.en: Daniel learned through an Angel that mystery of the seventy weeks concerning the Nativity of Christ: likewise Zacharias, when an Angel appeared, heard that a son John should be begotten of him; and Mary, when the Angel foretold to her that Christ should be born of her, both believed and assented. These three things we see spoken and fulfilled through an Angel.
sacramentumilludseptuagintahebdomadarumd.la: Sacraméntum illud septuagínta hebdomadárum de Christi Nativitáte, Dániel per Angelum dídicit: Simíliter Zacharías apparénte Angelo Joánnem fílium de se generándum audívit, et María Angelo sibi prædicénti, Christum ex se nascéndum, et crédidit et assénsit. Hæc tria per Angelum dicta et compléta vidémus.

iamergosoliciteintuendumestutrumangelusi.en: Now therefore it must be carefully considered whether this Angel, who appeared to Zacharias and to Mary, also foretold those things to Daniel himself. Indeed Daniel himself, in the volume of his prophecy, when he learned through an Angel those mysteries of the weeks that were to come concerning the Nativity of Christ, thus plainly expressed the name of that Angel. For he saith: Behold the man Gabriel, whom I had seen in the beginning, flying swiftly, touched me, and said: Daniel, consider the word; and the rest which are there related.
iamergosoliciteintuendumestutrumangelusi.la: Jam ergo solícite intuéndum est, utrum Angelus iste, qui Zacharíæ et Maríæ appáruit, ipsi quoque Daniéli illa prædíxerit. Equidem ipse Dániel in prophetíæ volúmine, quando illa sacraménta hebdomadárum de Christi Nativitáte per Angelum futúra cognóvit, sic ipsíus Angeli nomen evidénter expréssit. Dicit enim: Ecce Vir Gábriel, quem víderam in princípio, cito volans, tétigit me, et dixit Dániel animadvérte sermónem, et réliqua, quæ ibi commemorántur.

itemhistemporibussecundumevangeliumangel.en: Likewise in these times, according to the Gospel, the wonderful name of that Angel is found thus expressed. For the same Angel said to Zacharias: I am Gabriel, who stand before God: and am sent to speak to thee, and to bring thee these good tidings. Which also, concerning the childbearing of the Blessed Virgin Mary, is read thus in the same Gospel: The Angel Gabriel, it saith, was sent from God into a city of Galilee, called Nazareth, to a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin's name was Mary.
itemhistemporibussecundumevangeliumangel.la: Item his tempóribus secúndum Evangelium, Angeli ipsíus nomen miríficum sic invenítur expréssum. Dixit enim idem Angelus Zacharíæ: Ego sum Gábriel, qui adsto ante Deum, et missus sum loqui ad te, et hæc tibi evangelizáre. Quod étiam de Beátæ Maríæ Vírginis partu sic in eódem Evangélio légitur: Missus est, inquit, Angelus Gábriel a Deo in civitátem Galilææ, cui nomen Názareth, ad Vírginem desponsátam Viro, cui nomen erat Joseph de domo David, et nomen Vírginis María.

gabrielangeluslocutusestmariedicenseccec.en: The Angel Gabriel spake unto Mary, saying: Behold, thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and shalt bring forth a son
gabrielangeluslocutusestmariedicenseccec.la: Gábriel Angelus locútus est Maríæ, dicens: Ecce concípies in útero, et páries Fílium

etvocabisnomeneiusiesumalleluia.en: And thou shalt call His Name Jesus. Alleluia.

ipseenimsalvumfacietpopulumsuumapeccatis.en: For He shall save His people from their sins.
ipseenimsalvumfacietpopulumsuumapeccatis.la: Ipse enim salvum fáciet pópulum suum a peccátis eórum.

iamergomanifestumestunusidemqueangelusga.en: Now therefore it is manifest that it was one and the same Angel Gabriel who both opened to Daniel those appointed times concerning the Nativity of Christ, and showed that the childbearing of the Virgin was at hand. He came therefore at the time foreordained, and proveth that what he had once said is fulfilled by the accomplishment of the work. And there he was faithful in the prophecy of the weeks, and here faithful through the mystery revealed.
iamergomanifestumestunusidemqueangelusga.la: Jam ergo maniféstum est, unus idémque Angelus Gábriel fúerit, qui et præfíxa illa témpora Daniéli de Christi Nativitáte apéruit, et partum Vírginis præséntem esse monstrávit. Ad tempus itaque præfinítum occúrrit, et olim a se dicta, óperis efficiéntia compléta esse convíncit. Et illic fidélis in prophetía hebdomadárum, et hic fidélis per mystérium revelátum.

egosumgabrielangelusquiastoantedeumetmis.en: I am Gabriel, * the Angel, who stand before God, and am sent to speak to thee, and to bring thee these good tidings.
egosumgabrielangelusquiastoantedeumetmis.la: Ego sum Gábriel * Angelus, qui asto ante Deum, et missus sum loqui ad te et hæc tibi evangelizáre.

angelusdomininuntiavitmariealleluia.en: The Angel of the Lord declared unto Mary. (Alleluia.)

etconcepitdespiritusanctoalleluia.en: And she conceived of the Holy Ghost. (Alleluia.)

ecceconcipiesinuteretpariesfiliumetvocab.en: Behold, thou shalt conceive * in thy womb, and shalt bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name Jesus: he shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the most High. (Alleluia.)
ecceconcipiesinuteretpariesfiliumetvocab.la: Ecce concípies * in útero, et páries Fílium, et vocábis nomen ejus Jesum: hic erit magnus, et Fílius Altíssimi vocábitur. (Allelúia.)

avemariagratiaplenadominustecumbenedicta.en: Hail Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with thee: * Blessed art thou among women.
avemariagratiaplenadominustecumbenedicta.la: Ave, María, grátia plena, Dóminus tecum: * Benedícta tu in muliéribus.

veraxnamquemisericordiadeicumadreparandu.en: For though the true mercy of God had infinitely many schemes to hand for the restoration of mankind, it chose that particular design which put in force for destroying the devil's work, not the efficacy of might but the dictates of justice. For the pride of the ancient foe not undeservedly made good its despotic rights over all men, and with no unwarrantable supremacy tyrannized over those who had been of their own accord lured away from God's commands to be the slaves of his will. And so there would be no justice in his losing the immemorial slavery of the human race, were he not conquered by that which he had subjugated.
veraxnamquemisericordiadeicumadreparandu.la: Verax namque misericórdia Dei, cum ad reparándum humánum genus ineffabíliter ei multa suppéterent, hanc potíssimum consuléndi viam elégit, qua ad destruéndum opus diáboli non virtúte uterétur poténtiæ, sed ratióne justítiæ. Nam supérbia hostis antíqui non inmérito sibi in omnes hómines jus tyránnicum vindicábat, nec indébito dominátu premébat, quos a mandáto Dei spontáneos in obséquium suæ voluntátis illéxerat. Non ítaque juste amítteret originálem humáni géneris servitútem, nisi de eo quod subégerat vincerétur.

etbeneutrumqueposuitscripturautetdespons.en: And well hath the Scripture set down both, that she was both espoused and a virgin: a virgin, that she might be seen to be free from intercourse with man; espoused, lest she be branded with the infamy of violated virginity, since her heavy womb would seem to bear the mark of corruption. And the Lord preferred that some should doubt of his birth rather than of his mother's purity. For he knew that the modesty of a virgin is tender, and the fame of purity easily lost: nor did he think that faith in his birth should be built up by wrongs to his mother.
etbeneutrumqueposuitscripturautetdespons.la: Et bene utrúmque pósuit Scriptúra, ut et desponsáta esset, et virgo: virgo, ut expers virílis consórtii viderétur: desponsáta, ne temerátæ virginitátis adurerétur infámia, cujus gravis alvus corruptélæ viderétur insigne præférre. Máluit autem Dóminus áliquos de suo ortu quam de matris pudóre dubitáre. Sciébat enim téneram esse vírginis verecúndiam, et lúbricam famam pudóris: nec putávit ortus sui fidem matris injúriis adstruéndam.

egredieturvirgaderadiceiesseetreplebitur.en: There shall come forth a rod * out of the root of Jesse, and all the earth shall be filled with the glory of the Lord, and all flesh shall see the salvation of God. (Alleluia, alleluia.)
egredieturvirgaderadiceiesseetreplebitur.la: Egrediétur virga * de radíce Jesse, et replébitur omnis terra glória Dómini, et vidébit omnis caro salutáre Dei. (Allelúia, allelúia.)

spiritussanctusintedescendetmarianetimea.en: The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, * O Mary; fear not, thou shalt bear in thy womb the Son of God. Alleluia.
spiritussanctusintedescendetmarianetimea.la: Spíritus sanctus * in te descéndet‚ María, ne tímeas, habébis in útero Fílium Dei. (Allelúia.)

deusomipotenscuiusservitussummetplenestf.en: Almighty God, whose service is the highest and full happiness: * grant us, by the intercession of blessed Hugh, Abbot, § to serve thee without fear in holiness and justice.
deusomipotenscuiusservitussummetplenestf.la: Deus omípotens, cujus sérvitus summa et plena est felícitas: * concéde nobis, intercedénte beáto Hugóne, Abbáte, § in sanctitáte et justítia sine timóre tibi servíre.

suntenimmultietiaminobedientesvaniloquie.en: For there are also many disobedient, vain talkers, and seducers: especially they who are of the circumcision:
suntenimmultietiaminobedientesvaniloquie.la: Sunt enim multi étiam inobediéntes vaníloqui, et seductóres: máxime qui de circumcisióne sunt:

quosoportetredarguiquiuniversasdomossubv.en: Who must be reproved, who subvert whole houses, teaching things which they ought not, for filthy lucre’s sake.
quosoportetredarguiquiuniversasdomossubv.la: quos opórtet redárgui: qui univérsas domos subvértunt, docéntes quæ non opórtet‚ turpis lucri grátia.

quamobcausamincrepaillosdureutsanisintin.en: Wherefore rebuke them sharply, that they may be sound in the faith;
quamobcausamincrepaillosdureutsanisintin.la: Quam ob causam íncrepa illos dure, ut sani sint in fide,

nonintendentesiudaicisfabulisetmandatish.en: Not giving heed to Jewish fables and commandments of men, who turn themselves away from the truth.
nonintendentesiudaicisfabulisetmandatish.la: non intendéntes Judáicis fábulis, et mandátis hóminum, aversántium se a veritáte.

tuautemloquerequedecentsanamdoctrinam.en: But speak thou the things that become sound doctrine:
tuautemloquerequedecentsanamdoctrinam.la: Tu autem lóquere quæ decent sanam doctrínam:

senesutsobriisintpudiciprudentessaniinfi.en: That the aged men be sober, chaste, prudent, sound in faith, in love, in patience.
senesutsobriisintpudiciprudentessaniinfi.la: Senes ut sóbrii sint, pudíci, prudéntes, sani in fide, in dilectióne, in patiéntia:

anussimiliterinhabitusanctononcriminatri.en: The aged women, in like manner, in holy attire, not false accusers, not given to much wine, teaching well:
anussimiliterinhabitusanctononcriminatri.la: Anus simíliter in hábitu sancto, non criminatríces, non multo vino serviéntes, bene docéntes:

utprudentiamdoceantadolescentulasutviros.en: That they may teach the young women to be wise, to love their husbands, to love their children,
utprudentiamdoceantadolescentulasutviros.la: ut prudéntiam dóceant adolescéntulas, ut viros suos ament, fílios suos díligant,

prudentescastassobriasdomuscuramhabentes.en: To be discreet, chaste, sober, having a care of the house, gentle, obedient to their husbands, that the word of God be not blasphemed.
prudentescastassobriasdomuscuramhabentes.la: prudéntes, castas, sóbrias, domus curam habéntes, benígnas, súbditas viris suis, ut non blasphemétur verbum Dei:

iuvenessimiliterhortareutsobriisint.en: Young men, in like manner, exhort that they be sober.
iuvenessimiliterhortareutsobriisint.la: Júvenes simíliter hortáre ut sóbrii sint.

inomnibusteipsumprebeexemplumbonorumoper.en: In all things shew thyself an example of good works, in doctrine, in integrity, in gravity,
inomnibusteipsumprebeexemplumbonorumoper.la: In ómnibus teípsum præbe exémplum bonórum óperum, in doctrína, in integritáte, in gravitáte,

verbumsanumirreprehensibileutisquiexadve.en: The sound word that can not be blamed: that he, who is on the contrary part, may be afraid, having no evil to say of us.
verbumsanumirreprehensibileutisquiexadve.la: verbum sanum, irreprehensíbile: ut is, qui ex advérso est, vereátur, nihil habens malum dícere de nobis.

fidelissermestetdehisvoloteconfirmareutc.en: It is a faithful saying: and these things I will have thee affirm constantly: that they, who believe in God, may be careful to excel in good works. These things are good and profitable unto men.
fidelissermestetdehisvoloteconfirmareutc.la: Fidélis sermo est: et de his volo te confirmáre: ut curent bonis opéribus præésse qui credunt Deo. Hæc sunt bona, et utília homínibus.

iulianavirgopiisetnobilibusparentibusapu.en: Juliana, a virgin, born of pious and noble parents at Liège in Belgium, was at five years of age trained unto all perfection in the regular house of Mont-Cornillon, under the discipline of Sapientia, a most holy Nun. Wholly given to humility, the foundation of the other virtues, she eagerly performed all the meanest tasks of the monastery. Wearing down her body from her earliest years with abstinence and continual labours, she reduced it to the utmost leanness: for thirty years she was content with food once only in the day, and that of the meanest and slenderest. And although she bitterly bewailed the sins of men, she yet proclaimed herself guilty of all sins, deeming herself void of a fitting sorrow for the faults of mankind.
iulianavirgopiisetnobilibusparentibusapu.la: Juliána virgo, piis et nobílibus paréntibus apud Leódium in Bélgio orta, quinquénnis in regulári domo montis Cornélii sub Sapiéntiæ Moniális sanctíssimæ disciplína ad omnem perfectiónem efformáta est. Humilitáti, ceterárum virtútum fundaménto, pénitus addícta, vilíssima quæque monastérii múnia alácriter obíbat. Corpus suum abstinéntia et assíduis labóribus ab ineúnte ætáte átterens, ipsum ad extrémam usque máciem redégit: per trigínta annos semel dumtáxat in die, vilíssimo ac tenuíssimo cibo conténta. Quamquam autem hominum peccáta amáre deflébat, se tamen omnium peccatorum ream proclamábat, rata se condígni dolóris de humáni géneris culpis expértem esse.

otioperpetuumbellumindixitnamquidquidado.en: She declared perpetual war on idleness: for whatever time was left over from domestic cares she gave to prayer and holy reading. She often read through the divine Scripture: she learned the Psalter word for word; she diligently studied the books of the holy Fathers, and, being wonderfully refreshed above all by the works of the holy Father Bernard, she committed to memory more than twenty sermons written by that holy Abbot on the Canticle of Canticles; and she venerated that blessed Doctor with the highest affection of devotion. Her sleep was very short, and on the vigils of the Saints she passed almost whole nights without sleep. Having suffered long and various vexations from the princes of darkness, she triumphed over them by prayer and the venerable Eucharist.
otioperpetuumbellumindixitnamquidquidado.la: Otio perpétuum bellum indíxit: nam quidquid a domésticis curis supérerat témporis, illud oratióni et sacræ lectióni tribuébat. Divínam Scriptúram frequénter perlégit: Psaltérium ad verbum edídicit; sanctórum Patrum libros accuráte evólvit, et praecípue sancti Patris Bernárdi opéribus mirífice recreáta, plusquam vigínti sermónes in Canticórum Cántica ab eódem sancto Abbáte conscríptos memóriæ commendávit; ipsúmque beátum Doctórem summo devotiónis afféctu venerabátur. Somnus ei brevíssimus erat, et in Sanctórum pervigíliis noctes fere totas ducébat insómnes. A princípibus tenebrárum diutúrnas variásque vexatiónes perpéssa, oratióne ac venerábili Eucharistía de illis triumphávit.

plenissuffragiisinpriorissamdomusmontisc.en: Blessed Juliana, elected by full suffrages Prioress of the house of Mont-Cornillon, shone before the Sisters by the example of wonderful holiness, and advanced them to every kind of virtue. Her confessor often testified that she had never been stained with mortal sin. This treasure of an unsullied mind she increased day by day by continual meditation on the Lord's passion, and at the sight of an image of the suffering Saviour she often swooned from grief of soul and abundance of tears. Frequently rapt in ecstasy, she was several times favoured with the appearance and converse of the Princes of the Apostles. She helped the souls detained in purgatory with constant prayers and suffrages. She shone with the gift of prophecy, and appeared remarkable in penetrating the secrets of hearts.
plenissuffragiisinpriorissamdomusmontisc.la: Plenis suffrágiis in Prioríssam domus Montis Cornélii beáta Juliána elécta, Soróribus miræ sanctitátis prælúxit exémplo, atque eas ad omne virtútum genus promóvit. Ejusdem confessárius multóties protestátus est, eam numquam letháli labe inféctam fuísse. Hunc illibátæ mentis thesáurum in jugi Domínicae passiónis meditatióne per dies augescébat, ac visa Salvatóris patiéntis imágine prae ánimi dolóre et lacrymárum abundántia, saepenúmero delíquium patiebátur. Frequénter in éxtasin rapta, aliquóties Príncipum Apostolórum apparitióne dignáta est atque collóquio. Animas in purgatório deténtas assíduis précibus ac suffrágiis juvábat. Prophetíae dono emícuit, et in córdium arcánis penetrándis insígnis appáruit.

incelestiscibicommunioneplerumquealiquos.en: In the communion of the heavenly food her mind was very often enlightened by some secret from on high. She knew by heavenly means where the most holy Body of Christ, hidden under the species, was reserved. After many foregoing revelations she was appointed by God to promote the feast of the venerable Sacrament. The blessed Virgin long endured most grievous persecutions. Driven out of the house of Cornillon, she withdrew with her Nuns to various monasteries of the Cistercian Order, and afterwards, betaking herself to Salzinnes, she put herself under its Abbess. She foreknew the day of her death long beforehand, and made it known to others, and chose the place of her burial at Villers. Being brought into the church on Easter Day, and refreshed with the saving Viaticum, she earnestly begged to be anointed with the holy Oil, and before the venerable Eucharist passed by a most happy death to the nuptials of the heavenly Spouse, on the Nones of April, in the year of the Lord one thousand two hundred and fifty-seven, the sixty-sixth of her age.
incelestiscibicommunioneplerumquealiquos.la: In cœléstis cibi communióne plerúmque áliquo supérno arcáno mens ejus illustrabátur. Sanctíssimum Christi Corpus sub speciébus latens, ubi asservarétur cœlitus agnoscébat. Multis præcedéntibus revelationibus a Deo destináta est ad festum venerábilis Sacraménti promovéndum. Gravissimas persecutiónes beáta Virgo diu sustínuit. Domo Corneliána expúlsa, in vária Cisterciénsis Ordinis ascetéria cum suis Moniálibus divértit, ac póstmodum Salsíniam sese recípiens, ejus Abbatíssae se subjécit. Diem óbitus sui longe ántea praescívit, aliísque indicávit, et locum sepultúræ in Villário elégit. Dedúcta in Ecclésiam die Páschatis, et salutári Viático refécta, Oleo sancto se ungi efflagitávit, ac coram venerábili Eucharistía ad cœléstis Sponsi núptias felicíssima morte perréxit Nonis Aprílis, anno Dómini millésimo ducentésimo quinquagésimo séptimo, ætátis suae sexagésimo sexto.

caveamusfratresnevasoruminterimvacuosple.en: Let us beware, brethren, lest, deceived meanwhile by the empty brightness of the vessels, we have too late to complain that our lamps are going out. For I think that those were by no means lit which then seem to go out. For thus thou hast it: The kingdom of heaven is like to ten virgins, who taking their lamps. Taking, he said, not lighting. For how did they light them, who took no oil with them? Or where the matter of fire was lacking, how was there fire? Yet chastity shineth even of itself.
caveamusfratresnevasoruminterimvacuosple.la: Caveámus, fratres, ne vasórum ínterim vácuo splendóre decépti, sero conquéri habeámus, quod lámpades nostrae extinguúntur. Ego enim reor mínime fuísse accénsas, quæ tunc vidéntur extíngui. Sic nempe habes: Símile est regnum cœlórum decem virgínibus, quæ accipiéntes lámpades suas. Accipiéntes dixit, non accendéntes. Quómodo enim accendérunt, quæ non sumpsérunt óleum secum? Aut ubi ignis matéria défuit, quómodo ignis fuit? At lucet cástitas étiam ex seípsa.

sedquantolucidiorlampasardensquamsineign.en: But as much brighter as a burning lamp is than one without fire, so much fairer is a chaste generation with brightness. So also temperance from other pleasures, and patience in adversities, uprightness in conduct, and circumspection in speech, almsgiving too and such works of piety, seem to please by a certain natural grace, and to shine with as it were an inborn comeliness even among the foolish virgins. But since they shone with a brightness of glass rather than of fire, they thought their lamps were going out by this very thing, that they saw this empty splendour rejected by the eternal light.
sedquantolucidiorlampasardensquamsineign.la: Sed quanto lucídior lampas ardens, quam sine igne, tanto púlchrior casta generátio cum claritáte. Sic et a céteris voluptátibus temperántia, et patiéntia in adversitátibus, honéstas in conversatióne, et circumspéctio in sermóne, eleemósyna quoque et ejúsmodi ópera pietátis naturáli quadam placére grátia, et velut ingénito decóre étiam apud fátuas vírgines renitére vidéntur. At quóniam vítrea magis quam ígnea claritáte fulgébant, eo ipso lámpades suas arbitrabántur extíngui, quo nimírum inánem hunc splendórem ab ætérna conspéxerint luce reprobári.

exsermdesioannebaptista.en: From the Sermon on St. John the Baptist.
exsermdesioannebaptista.la: Ex Serm. de S. Joanne Baptista.

esttantumlucerevanumtantumardereparumard.en: Only to shine is vain, only to burn is too little: to burn and to shine is perfect. Hear what the Scripture saith: The wise man continueth as the sun, but the fool is changed as the moon. For the moon shineth without heat; now it appeareth full, now small, now not at all. For its light, being borrowed, never continueth in the same state, but it groweth, faileth, is thinned, is brought to nothing, and appeareth not at all. So they who have placed their consciences on the lips of others are now great, now small, now nothing, according as it hath pleased the tongues of flatterers either to blame or to praise. But the splendour of the sun is fiery; when it burneth more fiercely, it is shown even brighter to the eyes. So the inward ardour of the wise man shineth outwardly: and if both be not given him, he careth always rather to burn, that his Father, who seeth in secret, may repay him.
esttantumlucerevanumtantumardereparumard.la: Est tantum lucére vanum, tantum ardére parum: ardére et lucére perféctum. Audi quid dicat Scriptúra: Sápiens pérmanet ut sol, stultus autem ut luna mutátur. Quia enim splendet luna sine fervóre; modo plena, modo exígua, modo nulla vidétur. Mutuátum síquidem lumen suum numquam in eódem pérmanet statu, sed crescit, déficit, extenuátur, annihilátur, et pénitus non cómparet. Sic qui consciéntias suas in aliénis lábiis posuérunt, modo magni, modo parvi sunt, modo nulli, secúndum quod adulántium linguis vel vituperáre placúerit, vel laudáre. At vero solis splendor ígneus est, cum fervet ácrius, étiam óculis lucídior exhibétur. Sic sapiéntis ardor intérnus foris lucet: etsi non ei datur utrúmque, curat semper ardére magis, ut Pater suus, qui videt in abscóndito, reddat ei.

venobisfratressiluxerimustantumnamlucemu.en: Woe to us, brethren, if we have only shone. For we do indeed shine, and are magnified by men: but to me it is a very small thing to be judged by man's day. For he that judgeth me is the Lord, who requireth fervour of all, but brightness not so. To the Apostles and apostolic men in particular it is said: Let your light shine before men, as to men indeed kindled, and vehemently kindled, and for whom no blast whatsoever, nor the driving of the winds, need be feared. For there are some who shine not because they burn, but rather burn that they may shine: but these plainly burn not with the spirit of charity, but with the pursuit of vanity. But if thou have only a little oil, wherewith to be anointed, choose rather to keep it more safely in the vessel than in the lamp.
venobisfratressiluxerimustantumnamlucemu.la: Væ nobis, fratres, si luxérimus tantum. Nam lucémus quidem, et magnificámur ab homínibus: sed mihi pro mínimo est, ut ab humáno júdicer die. Qui enim júdicat me, Dóminus est, qui fervorem ab ómnibus éxigit, splendórem vero non ita. Singuláriter Apóstolis et Apostólicis viris dícitur: Lúceat lux vestra coram homínibus, nimírum tamquam accénsis, et veheménter accénsis, et quibus non timeátur afflátu quólibet, aut impulsione ventórum. Sunt enim qui non eo lucent, quia fervent: sed magis fervent ut lúceant: at isti plane non fervent charitátis spíritu, sed stúdio vanitátis. Non sit autem tibi nisi módicum ólei, quo ungáris; velis illud in vase tútius, quam in lámpade possidére.

domineiesuquibeatamiulianamvirginemtuamm.en: O Lord Jesus, who didst adorn blessed Juliana thy Virgin with a wonderful love toward the sacred mysteries of thy Body and Blood: mercifully grant that the fatness of spirit which she received from this divine banquet we also may merit to receive.
domineiesuquibeatamiulianamvirginemtuamm.la: Dómine Jesu, qui beátam Juliánam, Vírginem tuam, mirífica erga Córporis et Sánguinis tui sacra mystéria dilectióne decorásti: concéde propítius; ut, quam illa ex hoc divíno convívio spíritus percépit pinguédinem, eándem et nos percípere mereámur.

beatusvirquimetuitdominumalleluiainmanda.en: Blessed is the man that feareth the Lord, alleluia: he shall delight exceedingly in his commandments, alleluia.
beatusvirquimetuitdominumalleluiainmanda.la: Beátus vir qui métuit Dóminum, allelúia: In mandátis ejus cupit nimis, allelúia.

potensinterreritsemeneiusgeneratiorector.en: His posterity shall be mighty upon the earth; the upright generation shall be blessed.
potensinterreritsemeneiusgeneratiorector.la: Potens in terra erit semen ejus: generátio rectórum benedicétur.

isidorusnationehispanusasanctisepiscopis.en: Isidore, a Spaniard by nation, was piously and liberally brought up by the holy Bishops his brothers, Leander of Seville and Fulgentius of Carthagena, and became most excellent in every kind of learning and of Christian virtues. As a youth he openly opposed the Arian heresy with such constancy that he came near to being put to death by the heretics. When Leander had departed this life, he was raised, against his will but with great consent of the clergy and people, to the see of Seville, and was appointed by St. Gregory the Great Vicar of the Apostolic See in all Spain. How constant he was in his episcopate, how humble, patient and merciful, how solicitous in restoring Christian and ecclesiastical discipline, and how unwearied in establishing it by word and by writings, and lastly how distinguished with every ornament of virtues, no man's tongue would suffice to tell.
isidorusnationehispanusasanctisepiscopis.la: Isidórus natióne Hispánus, a sanctis Epíscopis Leándro Hispalénsi et Fulgéntio Carthaginénsi frátribus suis pie, et liberáliter educátus, omni scientiárum, atque Christianárum virtútum génere præstantíssimus evásit. Adoléscens hæresim Ariánam tanta constántia palam oppugnávit, ut parum abfúerit, quin ab hæréticis necarétur. Leándro vita functo, ad Hispalénsem cáthedram invítus, sed magno cleri populíque consénsu assúmitur, et a sancto Gregório Magno Apostólicæ Sedis in univérsa Hispánia Vicárius constitúitur. In Episcopátu quantum fúerit constans, húmilis, pátiens, miséricors, in Christiána et Ecclesiástica disciplína instauránda sollícitus, éaque verbo et scriptis stabiliénda indeféssus, atque demum omni virtútum ornaménto insignítus, nullíus lingua enarráre suffíceret.

monasticiquoqueinstitutiperhispaniamprom.en: He was also an eminent promoter and enlarger of the monastic institute throughout Spain; he built many monasteries, and likewise erected colleges, very many disciples flocking to him, among whom St. Ildephonsus, Bishop of Toledo, shone forth. In a Council gathered at Seville he crushed the heresy of the Acephali by an eloquent disputation. He wrote many books so useful for ecclesiastical discipline that Pope St. Leo the Fourth did not hesitate to commend them to the Bishops of Britain as equal to the books of Sts. Jerome and Augustine. At length, when he had banished the Arian heresy from Spain, having publicly foretold his own death and the laying waste of the kingdom by the arms of the Saracens, after he had ruled his Church for about forty years, he passed at Seville into heaven, in the year six hundred and thirty-six, having gained among all so great a fame of holiness and learning, that scarcely sixteen years after his death, with the applause of the Synod of Toledo, and St. Ildephonsus himself giving his vote, he merited to be called an excellent Doctor, the latest glory of the Catholic Church, and one to be named with reverence.
monasticiquoqueinstitutiperhispaniamprom.la: Monástici quoque institúti per Hispániam promótor et amplificátor exímius, plura constrúxit monastéria, collégia ítidem ædificávit, plúrimis ad eum confluéntibus discípulis, inter quos sanctus Ildefónsus Toletánus Epíscopus emícuit. Coácto Híspali Concílio, Acephalórum hæresim eloquénti disputatióne contrívit. Scripsit plures libros disciplínae Ecclesiásticæ ádeo útiles, ut sanctus Leo Papa quartus illos non dubitáverit Epíscopis Británniæ, instar librórum sanctórum Hierónymi et Augustíni commendáre. Dénique cum ab Hispánia Ariánam hæresim eliminásset, morte sua et regni vastatióne a Saracenórum armis públice prænuntiáta, postquam quadragínta círciter annos suam rexísset Ecclésiam, Híspali migrávit in cœlum, anno sexcentésimo trigésimo sexto, tantam apud omnes sanctitátis et doctrínae famam adéptus, ut elápso vix ab ejus óbitu sexto décimo anno, plaudénte Toletána Synodo, ipsóque sancto lldefónso suffragánte, Doctor egrégius, Cathólicæ Ecclésiæ novíssimum decus, et cum reveréntia nominándus, appellári merúerit.

leoprimusetruscuseotemporeprefuitecclesi.en: Leo the First, a Tuscan, ruled the Church at the time when Attila, king of the Huns, surnamed the Scourge of God, invading Italy, took Aquileia after a siege of three years, and plundered and burned it: whence, when he was being borne towards Rome with burning fury, and was already preparing to lead his forces across where the Mincio flows into the Po, Leo met him and persuaded him to turn back: and a little after he brought it about at Rome that Genseric abstained from slaughter and from burning.
leoprimusetruscuseotemporeprefuitecclesi.la: Leo primus, Etrúscus, eo témpore præfuit Ecclésiæ, cum rex Hunnórum Attila, cognoménto Flagéllum Dei, in Itáliam invádens, Aquiléiam triénnii obsidióne captam dirípuit et incéndit: unde cum Romam ardénti furóre raperétur, jamque cópias, ubi Míncius in Padum ínfluit, trajícere paráret, occúrrit ei Leo, persuasítque ut regrederétur: et paulo post effécit Romæ, ut Genserícus a cædibus abstinéret, et incéndiis.

sedcumecclesiamamultisheresibusoppugnari.en: But when he saw the Church assailed by many heresies, and most of all harassed by the Nestorians and the Eutychians, to purge her he summoned the Council of Chalcedon, where Eutyches and Dioscorus, and Nestorius again, were condemned. These things done, the holy Pontiff turned himself to repairing and building churches; and after very many other deeds nobly done, when he had written much in a holy and lucid manner, he fell asleep in the Lord.
sedcumecclesiamamultisheresibusoppugnari.la: Sed cum Ecclésiam a multis hærésibus oppugnári, maximéque a Nestoriánis, et Eutychiánis exagitári vidéret, ad eam purgándam, Concílium Chalcedonénse indíxit, ubi Eutyches, et Dióscorus, et íterum Nestórius, condemnáti sunt. His actis, sanctus Póntifex, se ad reficiéndas et ædificándas Ecclésias convértit, aliísque quam plúrimis præcláre gestis, cum multa sancte et luculénter scripsísset, obdormívit in Dómino.

inconspectuomnispopulieius.en: In the presence of all his people.

valerianusromanusnobiligenereortusalexan.en: Valerian, a Roman, sprung of a noble family, in the reign of the emperor Alexander Severus, at the exhortation of the blessed Virgin Cecilia, whom he had betrothed to himself as wife, was baptized together with Tiburtius his brother by Pope St. Urban. When Almachius, prefect of the City, learned that they were Christians, he summoned them and rebuked them severely: and when he saw them steadfastly confessing Christ to be God, he commanded them to be beaten with rods.
valerianusromanusnobiligenereortusalexan.la: Valeriánus Románus, nóbili génere ortus, Alexándro Sevéro imperatóre, hortátu beátæ Cæciliæ Virginis, quam sibi uxórem despónderat, una cum Tibúrtio fratre a sancto Urbáno Papa baptizátur. Quos ubi præféctus Urbis Almáchius Christiános esse cognóvit, accersítos gráviter reprehéndit: atque ubi Christum Deum constánter confiténtes videt, virgis cædi jubet.

sedcumverberibuscoginonpossentutiovissim.en: But when they could not be compelled by stripes to worship the image of Jupiter, they were struck with the axe at the fourth milestone from the City. Maximus, the prefect's chamberlain, who had led them to execution, marvelling at their courage, professed himself a Christian, with many others, who a little after, being beaten with leaded scourges, from ministers of the devil all became Martyrs of Christ the Lord.
sedcumverberibuscoginonpossentutiovissim.la: Sed cum verbéribus cogi non possent, ut Jovis simulácrum veneraréntur, ad quartum ab Urbe lápidem secúri feriúntur. Quorum virtútem admirátus Máximus præfécti cubiculárius, qui eos ad supplícium perdúxerat, Christiánum se esse proféssus est, cum multis áliis, qui paulo post plumbátis contúsi, omnes ex diáboli minístris, Christi Dómini Mártyres evasérunt.

induiteosdominusstolaglorieetcoronaviteo.en: The Lord hath clothed them with a robe of glory, and hath crowned them:
induiteosdominusstolaglorieetcoronaviteo.la: Induit eos Dóminus stola glóriæ, et coronávit eos:

beatorummartyrumtuorumtiburtiivalerianie.en: May the feasts of thy blessed Martyrs Tiburtius, Valerian and Maximus protect us, we beseech thee, O Lord: § and may their venerable prayer commend us.
beatorummartyrumtuorumtiburtiivalerianie.la: Beatórum Mártyrum tuórum Tibúrtii, Valeriáni et Máximi, nos, quæsumus, Dómine, festa tueántur: § et eórum comméndet orátio veneránda.

anselmusaugustepretorieinitalianatusapue.en: Anselm, born at Aosta in Italy, from boyhood followed the study of letters; and although with youthful ardour he was at times drawn to the allurements of the world, yet soon, from a desire of a more perfect life, he betook himself to the monastery of Bec, of the Order of St. Benedict, where, having made his regular profession, he advanced with such fervour of soul, and constant zeal in attaining learning and virtues, under Lanfranc, Prior of the monastery and a most learned man, that he was held by all as a pattern of holiness and learning. When Lanfranc was taken to govern the abbey of Caen, Anselm was put in his place, and afterwards, the Abbot having died, he was set over the monastery of Bec by the votes of all, and shone everywhere with such fame of religion and wisdom, that he was not only held in veneration by kings and Bishops, but was also acceptable to St. Gregory the Seventh, who, being then harassed by great persecutions, commended himself and the Catholic Church to his prayers.
anselmusaugustepretorieinitalianatusapue.la: Ansélmus Augústæ Prætóriæ in Itália natus, a puerítia stúdia litterárum sectátus, licet juveníli ardóre aliquándo ad sæculi illécebras traherétur, brevi tamen perfectióris vitæ desidério, ad monastérium Beccénse, Ordinis sancti Benedícti, se cóntulit, ubi emíssa regulári professióne, tanto ánimi fervóre, et jugi stúdio in lítteris et virtútibus assequéndis, sub Lanfránco, monastérii Prióre et viro doctíssimo profécit, ut tamquam sanctitátis et doctrínæ exémplar ab ómnibus haberétur. Assúmpto Lanfránco ad Cadoménsis cœnóbii régimen in ejus locum sufféctus Ansélmus, et póstea, defúncto Abbáte, ómnium suffrágiis Beccénsi monastério præféctus, tanta religiónis et sapiéntiæ fama ubíque refúlsit, ut non modo régibus et Epíscopis veneratióni esset, sed sancto Gregório séptimo étiam accéptus, qui tum magnis persecutiónibus agitatus, se et Ecclésiam Cathólicam ejus oratiónibus commendábat.

mortuolanfrancoquiexabbatecadomensifactu.en: When Lanfranc died, who from Abbot of Caen had been made Archbishop of Canterbury, Anselm succeeded him also, to the great rejoicing of the whole kingdom. But soon a dissension arising between William, king of England, who was unjustly claiming for himself the rights of the Church, and Anselm, who defended the liberty of the same Church, he was compelled to go into exile once and again; he came to Rome, and, being honourably received by Urban the Second, he took part in the Council of Bari, where he contended vigorously against the error of the Greeks. At length, being recalled into England by king Henry, William's brother, and having obtained the liberty of the Church, for which he had laboured, he fell asleep in the Lord, renowned for the fame of his miracles and holiness, and commended also for his singular devotion to the passion of our Lord and to the blessed Virgin his Mother.
mortuolanfrancoquiexabbatecadomensifactu.la: Mórtuo Lanfránco, qui ex Abbáte Cadoménsi factus fúerat Archiepíscopus Cantuariénsis, ei étiam succéssit Ansélmus, magna totíus regni gratulatióne. Sed mox dissídio orto inter Wilhélmum Angliæ regem Ecclésiæ jura iníque sibi vindicántem, et Ansélmum ejúsdem Ecclésiæ libertátem tuéntem, semel et íterum exuláre compúlsus, Romam venit, honorificéque ab Urbáno secúndo excéptus, Concílio Barénsi intérfuit, ubi contra Græcórum errórem strénue decertávit. Tandem ab Henríco rege Wilhélmi fratre in Angliam revocátus, et libertátem Ecclésiæ, pro qua laboráverat, adéptus, obdormívit in Dómino, fama miraculórum et sanctitátis clarus, et étiam ob insígnem devotiónem erga Dómini nostri passiónem et beátam Vírginem ejus Matrem commendátus.

beatorummartyrumpariterquepontificumsote.en: May the feasts of the blessed Martyrs and likewise Pontiffs Soter and Caius protect us, we beseech thee, O Lord: and may their venerable prayer commend us.
beatorummartyrumpariterquepontificumsote.la: Beatórum Mártyrum paritérque Pontíficum Sotéri et Caii nos, quǽsumus, Dómine, festa tueántur: et eórum comméndet orátio veneránda.

beatusrobertusincampanianobilibusortuspa.en: Blessed Robert, born in Champagne of noble parents, shone forth like a beautiful flower of the field, whose comeliness in uprightness of morals was pleasing to those who beheld it, and the fragrance of his holy repute, spread far and wide, invited very many to the imitation of him. When his mother was with child of him, the Mother of God appeared to her, and espoused his finger with a ring, saying that she willed that the son whom she bore in her womb should be her spouse; which was the reason why he afterwards consecrated all his monasteries to the name of the Mother of God herself. Being therefore in his eleventh year, he received the regular habit at St. Peter's of Celle, where, by God's disposing, he was afterwards elected Prior, and at length was elected Abbot by the brethren of the monastery of St. Michael of Tonnerre.
beatusrobertusincampanianobilibusortuspa.la: Beátus Robértus in Campánia nobílibus ortus paréntibus, quasi quidam flos campi speciósus enítuit, cujus decor in honestáte morum intuéntibus gratus erat, et sanctæ opiniónis odor longe latéque diffúsus, ad imitatiónem sui plúrimos invitábat. Matri de illo prægnánti Dei Mater appáruit, et digitum ejus ánnulo subarrhávit, dicens: Velle se, ut suus esset sponsus, fílius quem in útero portábat, quæ causa fuit, cur ille póstea ómnia monastéria sua ipsíus Dei Matris nómini consecráret. Annum ítaque agens undécimum, apud sanctum Petrum de Cella habitum suscépit regulárem, ubi, Deo disponénte, póstmodum eléctus in Priórem, tandem a frátribus monastérii sancti Michaélis Tornodóri eléctus est in Abbátem.

inquoddamnemuscuiusnomenmolismuseratcuma.en: Afterwards withdrawing with some brethren into a certain wood, whose name was Molesme, they there, labouring with their own hands, cut down branches from the trees, and of them built dwellings and an Oratory, in which they frequently offered to the Lord saving victims and the sacrifice of a contrite spirit. But because abundance of things for the most part brings in poverty of morals, when they had little by little begun to abound in temporal things, they began to fail in spiritual things.
inquoddamnemuscuiusnomenmolismuseratcuma.la: In quoddam nemus, cujus nomen Molísmus erat, cum alíquibus frátribus póstea secédens, ibi própriis mánibus laborántes ramos de arbóribus excidérunt, et ex eísdem domicília et Oratórium construxérunt, in quo Dómino frequénter salutáres hóstias et sacrificium contríti spiritus offerébant. Sed quia plerúmque rerum cópia morum íngerit egestátem, cum paulátim cœpíssent temporálibus abundáre, cœpérunt in spirituálibus defícere.

vidensautemvirdeiquodinplerisqueilloruma.en: But the man of God, seeing that he profited nothing in admonishing and correcting most of them, resolved to leave them, lest, while he sought spiritual gain in them in vain, he himself should suffer loss to his own soul. Taking therefore companions from among their number, who had their desire set upon the Rule, they came to a wood called Citeaux, in which, with the consent and authority both of Hugh, Archbishop of Lyons and Legate of the Holy See, and of Odo, duke of Burgundy, they built a new Monastery, afterwards named Citeaux from the same wood, in which, casting away whatever was contrary to the Rule of St. Benedict, they embraced the observance of that same Rule to the letter with such fervour that they thought not even one tittle of it might be passed over by them.
vidensautemvirdeiquodinplerisqueilloruma.la: Videns autem vir Dei quod in plerísque illórum admonéndis et corripiéndis nihil profíceret, státuit eos relínquere, ne dum in eis frustra quæreret spirituále lucrum, ipse ánimæ suæ fáceret detriméntum. Assúmptis ígitur ex eórum número sóciis, votum in Régula habéntibus, ad silvam, Cistércium nuncupátam, devenérunt, in qua tam Hugónis, Lugdunénsis Archiepíscopi, et Legáti sanctæ Sedis, quam Odónis ducis Burgúndiæ consénsu, et auctoritáte novum Monastérium, ab eádem silva Cistércium póstea nominátum, extruxérunt, in quo quidquid Régulæ sancti Benedícti refragabátur abjiciéntes, ejúsdem Regulæ observántiam ad litteram tanto cum fervóre amplexáti sunt, ut nec illíus ápicem sibi prætereúndum putárent.

verumdesecessuvirideimonachimolismensesc.en: But the Monks of Molesme, grieved at the departure of the man of God, went to the supreme Pontiff Urban, the Second of this name, and by his authority compelled the same their Abbot to return to Molesme. In the said new Monastery of Citeaux Alberic succeeded him, and so, the foundations of the Cistercian Order having been laid, he returned to Molesme, the Cistercians indeed weeping over his departure, the men of Molesme on the other hand exulting at his return. But the man of God, longing day by day to be dissolved and to be with Christ, having received a little after a revelation from God of his death, in the ninety-third year of his age, full of merits and renowned for miracles, sent forth his spirit to heaven.
verumdesecessuvirideimonachimolismensesc.la: Verum de secéssu viri Dei Mónachi Molisménses contristáti, summum Pontíficem Urbánum huius nóminis Secúndum adiérunt, et ejus auctoritáte eúmdem Abbátem suum Molísmum redire coëgérunt. Cui in dicto Cisterciénsi novo Monastério succéssit Alberícus, sicque Ordinis Cisterciénsis fundaméntis præstitútis, Molismum rédiit, Cisterciénsibus quidem plorántibus de illíus secéssu, Molisménsibus contra exultántibus de regréssu. Vir autem Dei in dies dissólvi cúpiens et esse cum Christo, accépta paulo post a Deo revelatióne mortis suæ, anno ætátis suæ nonagésimo tértio, méritis plenus ac miráculis clarus, spíritum transmísit ad cœlos.

petrusveroneparentibusmanicheorumheresii.en: Peter was born at Verona of parents infected with the heresy of the Manichees, and from almost his very infancy he fought against heresies. As a youth he came to Bologna for the sake of study, where, taking the habit of the Order of Preachers, he shone in that religious life with great splendour of virtues. He carefully guarded his body and soul from every deadly stain, exercising his flesh with fastings and watchings, and his mind with divine contemplations; and by the gift of a special grace he sharply confuted the heretics.
petrusveroneparentibusmanicheorumheresii.la: Petrus Verónae paréntibus Manichaeórum haeresi inféctis natus, ab ipsa pene infántia contra haereses pugnávit. Adoléscens Bonóniam studiórum causa venit, ubi Ordinis Praedicatórum suscípiens institútum, magno in ea religióne virtútum splendóre elúxit. Corpus et ánimum ab omni labe mortífera caute custodívit, carnem jejúniis et vigíliis, mentem divínis contemplatiónibus exércens, peculiáris gratiae dono, haeréticos ácriter confutávit.

inconcionandovimhabuitplurimamfideiardor.en: In preaching he had very great power; inflamed with the ardour of the faith, and earnestly longing to undergo death for it, he was slain by the heretics, as he had even foretold. For as he was returning from Como to Milan, a wicked assassin wounded him once and again on the head with a sword. And when he was now almost dead, reciting the creed of the faith, his side pierced through with a dagger, he obtained the palm of martyrdom, in the year one thousand two hundred and fifty-two; and Innocent the Fourth in the following year enrolled him among the Saints.
inconcionandovimhabuitplurimamfideiardor.la: In concionándo vim hábuit plúrimam, fídei ardóre incénsus, et pro ea mortem subíre eníxius optans, ab haeréticis uti étiam praedíxerat, fuit interémptus. Cum enim Como redíret Mediolánum, impius eum sicárius semel ac iterum in cápite gládio vulnerávit. Jamque pene mórtuus, symbolum fidei récitans, mucróne látera transverberátus, martyrii palmam obtínuit, anno millésimo ducentésimo quinquagésimo secúndo, quem Innocéntius quartus anno sequénti Sanctis adscrípsit.

stabuntiustiinmagnaconstantiaadversuseos.en: The just shall stand * with great constancy against those that have afflicted them, and taken away their labours, alleluia.
stabuntiustiinmagnaconstantiaadversuseos.la: Stabunt justi * in magna constántia advérsus eos qui se angustiavérunt et qui abstulérunt labóres eórum, allelúia.

deusquinosannuaapostolorumtuorumphilippi.en: O God, who dost gladden us by the yearly solemnity of thine Apostles Philip and James: grant, we beseech thee, that we may be instructed by the examples of those in whose merits we rejoice.
deusquinosannuaapostolorumtuorumphilippi.la: Deus, qui nos ánnua Apostolórum tuórum Philíppi et Jacóbi solemnitáte lætíficas: præsta, quǽsumus; ut, quorum gaudémus méritis, instruámur exémplis.

istisuntdueoliveetduocandelabralucentiaa.en: These are two olive trees, and two candlesticks, giving light in the presence of the Lord.
istisuntdueoliveetduocandelabralucentiaa.la: Isti sunt duæ olívæ, et duo candelábra lucéntia ante Dóminum.

habentpotestatemclauderecelumnubibusetap.en: They have power to shut up heaven with clouds, and to open the gates thereof, because their tongues are made the keys of heaven.
habentpotestatemclauderecelumnubibusetap.la: Habent potestátem cláudere cœlum núbibus, et aperíre portas ejus, quia linguæ eórum claves cœli factæ sunt.

istisuntduofiliisplendorisquiassistuntdo.en: These are the two sons of brightness, who stand before the Ruler of the earth:
istisuntduofiliisplendorisquiassistuntdo.la: Isti sunt duo fílii splendóris, qui assístunt Dominatóri terræ:

tantotemporevobiscumsumetnoncognovistism.en: Have I been so long a time with you, and have you not known me? Philip, he that seeth me seeth my Father also, alleluia. Do you not believe,
tantotemporevobiscumsumetnoncognovistism.la: Tanto témpore vobíscum sum, et non cognovístis me? Philíppe, qui videt me, videt et Patrem meum, allelúja. Non créditis,

quiegoinpatreetpaterinmeestalleluiaallel.en: That I am in the Father, and the Father is in me? * Alleluia, alleluia.
quiegoinpatreetpaterinmeestalleluiaallel.la: Quia ego in Patre, et Pater in me est? * Allelúja, allelúja.

sicognovissetismeetpatremmeumutiquecogno.en: If you had known me, you would without doubt have known my Father also: and from henceforth you shall know him.
sicognovissetismeetpatremmeumutiquecogno.la: Si cognovissétis me, et Patrem meum útique cognovissétis, et ámodo cognoscétis eum.

quiegoinpatreetpaterinmeest.en: That I am in the Father, and the Father is in me?
quiegoinpatreetpaterinmeest.la: Quia ego in Patre, et Pater in me est?

istisuntdueoliveetduocandelabralucentiaa.en: These are two olive trees * and two candlesticks, giving light in the presence of the Lord; these have power to shut heaven with clouds, and have power again to open the gates thereof, for their tongues are become keys of heaven , alleluia.
istisuntdueoliveetduocandelabralucentiaa.la: Isti sunt * duæ olívæ, et duo candelábra lucéntia ante Dóminum; habent potestátem cláudere cælum núbibus et aperíre portas ejus, quia linguæ eórum claves cæli factæ sunt, allelúia.

nonturbeturcorvestrumnequeformidetcredit.en: Let not your heart be troubled, * nor let it be afraid; you believe in God, believe also in me: in my Father's house there are many mansions, alleluia, alleluia.
nonturbeturcorvestrumnequeformidetcredit.la: Non turbétur * cor vestrum, neque formídet; Créditis in Deum, et in me crédite, in domo Patris mei mansiónes multæ sunt, allelúia, allelúia.

athanasiusalexandrinusabalexandrepiscopo.en: Athanasius of Alexandria, made Deacon by Bishop Alexander, succeeded to his place; he had also before followed him to the Council of Nicaea, where, having repressed the impiety of Arius, he incurred such hatred of the Arians that from that time they never ceased to lay snares for him. Wherefore, being driven into exile, he lived as an exile in Gaul at Treves. Afterwards, tossed by grievous and long tempests under the emperor Constantius, a favourer of the Arians, and having suffered incredible calamities, he travelled through a great part of the world: and he was often cast out of his Church, and often also restored to the same.
athanasiusalexandrinusabalexandrepiscopo.la: Athanásius Alexandrínus, ab Alexándro Epíscopo Diáconus factus, in ejus locum succéssit, quem étiam ántea secútus fúerat ad Nicaenum Concílium, ubi cum Aríi impietátem repressísset, tantum ódium Arianórum suscépit, ut ex eo témpore ei insídias molíri numquam destíterint. Quamóbrem in exílium actus, in Gállia apud Tréviros exulávit. Grávibus deínceps ac diutúrnis sub Constántio imperatóre, Arianórum fautóre, tempestátibus jactátus, et incredíbiles calamitátes perpéssus, magnam orbis terrae partem peragrávit: ac sæpe e sua Ecclésia ejéctus, sæpe étiam in eámdem restitútus est.

istesanctusdigneinmemoriamvertiturhominu.en: This Saint is worthily kept in the memory of men, who hath passed to the joy of the Angels;
istesanctusdigneinmemoriamvertiturhominu.la: Iste Sanctus digne in memóriam vértitur hóminum, qui ad gáudium tránsiit Angelórum;

quiainhacperegrinationesolocorporeconsti.en: For in this pilgrimage, being set here in body only, in thought and longing he dwelt in that eternal fatherland.
quiainhacperegrinationesolocorporeconsti.la: Quia in hac peregrinatióne solo córpore constitútus, cogitatióne et aviditáte in illa ætérna pátria conversátus est.

vinculiscarnisabsolutustalentumsibicredi.en: Set free from the bonds of the flesh, he brought back to his Lord with gain the talent entrusted to him.
vinculiscarnisabsolutustalentumsibicredi.la: Vínculis carnis absolútus taléntum sibi créditum Dómino suo cum lucro reportávit.

arianisintereaillisemperinfestiseorumper.en: Meanwhile, the Arians being ever hostile to him, fleeing their stubborn wrath, he hid himself for five years in a dry cistern; and when Constantius was dead, returning to Alexandria, he was received with the highest honour. But not long after, being harassed by Julian the apostate, he was compelled to depart again; and being sought out for death, he escaped, and returning to Alexandria, he remained hidden there until the death of Julian. Another storm arising, he lay hid for four months in his father's tomb; and at length, delivered by God out of so many and so great dangers, he died at Alexandria in his bed, under Valens, when he had most holily governed the Church of Alexandria for forty years amid the greatest changes of the times.
arianisintereaillisemperinfestiseorumper.la: Ariánis intérea illi semper inféstis, eórum pertinácem iram fúgiens, in sicca cistérna quinque annis se ábdidit, et Constántio mórtuo, Alexandríam revérsus, summo honóre excéptus est. Sed non multo post, a Juliáno apóstata exagitátus, rursus discédere cógitur, et ad necem conquísitus effúgit, atque Alexandríam rédiens, ibídem usque ad Juliáni óbitum occúltus permánsit. Alia exórta tempestáte, quátuor menses in patérno sepúlchro delítuit, ac dénique ex tot tantísque perículis divínitus eréptus, Alexandríæ mortuus est in suo léctulo, sub Valénte, cum quadragínta annos in summa témporum varietáte Alexandrínam Ecclésiam sanctíssime gubernásset.

ocruxbenedictaquiaintepependitsalvatormu.en: O blessed Cross! * for on thee hung the Saviour of the world, and on thee triumphed the King of Angels, alleluia.
ocruxbenedictaquiaintepependitsalvatormu.la: O Crux benedícta! * quia in te pepéndit Salvátor mundi, et in te triumphávit Rex Angelórum, allelúia.

ocruxgloriosaocruxadorandaolignumpretios.en: O glorious Cross, O Cross to be adored, O precious wood, and wondrous sign!
ocruxgloriosaocruxadorandaolignumpretios.la: O Crux gloriósa, o Crux adoránda, o lignum pretiósum, et admirábile signum!

perquodetdiabolusestvictusetmunduschrist.en: Whereby both the devil was overcome, and the world was redeemed by the blood of Christ, alleluia, alleluia.
perquodetdiabolusestvictusetmunduschrist.la: Per quod et diábolus est victus, et mundus Christi sánguine redémptus, allelúia, allelúia.

adoremuscrucissignaculumperquodsalutissu.en: Let us adore the sign of the Cross, through which we have received the sacrament of salvation:
adoremuscrucissignaculumperquodsalutissu.la: Adorémus Crucis signáculum, per quod salútis súmpsimus sacraméntum:

eccecrucemdominifugitepartesadversevicit.en: Behold, the Cross of the Lord! * fly, ye ranks of the adversary! The Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, hath prevailed. Alleluia.
eccecrucemdominifugitepartesadversevicit.la: Ecce Crucem Dómini, * fúgite, partes advérsæ, vicit Leo de tribu Juda, radix David, allelúia.

ocruxsplendidiorcunctisastrismundocelebr.en: O Cross, more splendid * than all the stars, renowned in the world, much beloved of men, holier than all things; who alone wast worthy to bear the ransom of the world: sweet wood, sweet nails, bearing a sweet burden; save the company here present, gathered today in thy praises. (Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.)
ocruxsplendidiorcunctisastrismundocelebr.la: O Crux splendídior * cunctis astris, mundo célebris, homínibus multum amábilis, sánctior univérsis; quæ sola fuísti digna portáre taléntum mundi, dulce lignum, dulces clavos, dúlcia ferens póndera; salva præséntem catérvam in tuis hódie láudibus congregátam. (Allelúia, allelúia, allelúia.)

martinusquietsacerdosappellaturnobilishi.en: Martin, who is also called Sacerdos, a noble Spaniard, was offered by his mother to the Abbot Blasius in the monastery of Cantavos. Clothed with the Cistercian habit, and having made his profession, after the death of Blasius and the translation of the monastery to Huerta, he was elected Abbot while still young. And being made Bishop of Siguenza after about twenty years, he reformed his clergy, bound the Canons by rules, defended the rights of his Church, not neglecting the liberation of captives.
martinusquietsacerdosappellaturnobilishi.la: Martínus qui et Sacérdos appellátur, nóbilis Hispánus, Abbáti Blásio in monastério de Cántavos offértur a matre. Cisterciénsi indutus hábitu, et professióne facta post mortem Blásii, et monastérii in Hortam translatiónem, júvenis eléctus est in Abbátem. Factus vero post annos círciter vigínti Saguntínus Epíscopus, Clerum suum reformávit, Canonicos régulis astrínxit, Ecclésiæ suæ jura túitus est, captivórum liberatiónem non omíttens.

postannossepteminpontificatutransactosde.en: After seven years spent in the episcopate, he resigned with the Pope's leave, and returning to Huerta, led there a private life, but one shining with the glory of virtues. At length, overcome by sickness, when he was turning aside from Oviedo to his own monastery, he died in the town of Cetina; and his body, carried back to Huerta, shone with very many miracles, among which this is wonderful, and proved, that an Angel drew the head from the body, and carried it to the Canons of Siguenza, on the fifth day of May, on which day his feast is celebrated.
postannossepteminpontificatutransactosde.la: Post annos septem in Pontificátu transáctos, de Papæ licéntia cessit, et Hortam rédiens, privátam ibi vitam, sed virtútum glória coruscántem duxit. Morbo dénique pressus, cum ex Ovísa in próprium monastérium deflécteret, in Cétoca óppido mórtuus est, corpúsque ejus Hortam reportátum quamplúrimis fulsit miráculis, ex quibus illud admirándum, et probátum, quod Angelus caput de córpore extráxerit, Saguntúmque Canónicis detúlerit, die quinta Maji, quo die festívitas ejus celebrátur.

stanislauspolonusapudcracoviamnobiligene.en: Stanislaus, a Pole, born near Cracow of a noble family and of pious parents, from his early years gave a token of his future holiness; and when they were dead, having made great progress in the sacred learning of the Canons and of Theology, he distributed his ample patrimony to the poor, from a desire of the monastic life. But being made a Canon of Cracow by Bishop Lambert, he was afterwards put in his place, though against his will.
stanislauspolonusapudcracoviamnobiligene.la: Stanisláus Polónus apud Cracóviam, nóbili génere et piis paréntibus natus ab ineúnte ætáte futúræ sanctitátis spécimen dedit, quibus mórtuis cum plúrimum in sacra Cánonum et Theologíæ doctrína profecísset amplum patrimónium paupéribus distríbuit, vitæ monásticæ desidério. Sed Canónicus Cracoviénsis factus a Lambérto Epíscopo, in ejus póstea locum, quamvis invítus, suffícitur.

quoinmunereomniumpastoraliumvirtutumlaud.en: In which office he shone with the praise of all pastoral virtues, and especially with mercy towards the poor. Boleslaus was then king of Poland, whom, having often in vain admonished him for his lust, Stanislaus at length removed from the communion of the faithful. He, raging with anger, when he could effect nothing by his soldiers, with his own hand slew him as he was offering the sacrifice; and his body, cut limb from limb, and by his order cast out into the fields, eagles defended from wild beasts. Innocent the Fourth enrolled him, illustrious for miracles, among the Saints.
quoinmunereomniumpastoraliumvirtutumlaud.la: Quo in múnere, ómnium pastorálium virtútum laude, et præcípue misericórdia in páuperes enítuit. Erat tum Polóniæ rex Bolesláus, quem frustra sæpe ob libídinem admónitum, Stanisláus tandem a fidélium communióne rémovet. Ille furens iracúndia, cum per mílites nihil effíceret, sua manu, sacrifícium offeréntem obtrúncat, corpúsque membrátim concísum, ejúsque jussu per agros projéctum‚ áquilæ a feris deféndunt. Hunc miráculis illústrem Innocéntius Quartus Sanctis adjúnxit.

dumsacrummysteriumcerneretioannesarchang.en: While John beheld * the sacred mystery, the Archangel Michael sounded the trumpet: Thou art worthy, O Lord our God, to take the book, and to open the seals thereof, alleluia.
dumsacrummysteriumcerneretioannesarchang.la: Dum sacrum mystérium * cérneret Joánnes, Archángelus Míchaël tuba cécinit: Dignus es, Dómine, Deus noster, accípere librum, et aperíre signácula ejus, allelúia.

datasunteiincensamulta.en: There was given to him much incense.

utadolereteaantealtareaureum.en: That he might burn it before the golden altar.
utadolereteaantealtareaureum.la: Ut adoléret ea ante altáre áureum.

factumestsilentiumincelodumcommitteretbe.en: There was silence in heaven, while the dragon joined battle with Michael the Archangel: the voice was heard of thousands of thousands saying: Salvation, honour and power
factumestsilentiumincelodumcommitteretbe.la: Factum est siléntium in cœlo, dum commítteret bellum draco cum Michaéle Archángelo: audíta est vox míllia míllium dicéntium: Salus, honor et virtus

milliamilliumministrabanteietdeciescente.en: Thousands of thousands ministered unto Him, and ten thousand times hundreds of thousands stood before Him.
milliamilliumministrabanteietdeciescente.la: Míllia míllium ministrábant ei, et décies centéna míllia assistébant ei.

beatummichelemarchangelumsepiushominibus.en: It is proved that blessed Michael the Archangel hath very often appeared to men. But when Gelasius the First was supreme Pontiff, his apparition in Apulia on the summit of Mount Gargano was famous. For it came to pass that from the herds of cattle of a certain Garganus a bull wandered far away; which, after long search, they found standing fast at the entrance of a cave. But when one of them had shot an arrow to pierce the bull, the arrow was turned back and fell upon the archer himself.
beatummichelemarchangelumsepiushominibus.la: Beátum Michaélem Archangelum sæpius homínibus apparuísse probátum est. Gelásio autem primo Pontífice Máximo, in Apúlia in vértice Gargani montis, illústris fuit ipsíus apparítio. Factum est enim, ut ex grégibus armentórum Gargáni cujúsdam taurus longe discéderet: quem diu conquisítum, in aditu spelúncæ hæréntem invenérunt. Cum vero quidam ex illis, ut taurum confígeret, sagíttam emisisset, retórta sagítta in ipsum récidit sagittárium.

queresadeopresentesacetiamadmonitumepisc.en: This thing so moved those present, and also the Bishop when he was told of it, that, a fast being proclaimed, he commanded that the matter be asked of God. After three days the Archangel warned the Bishop that the place was under his protection, and that he willed that worship be paid there to God, in memory of himself and of the Angels. The Bishop therefore went to the cave, and seeing the place in a manner formed like a church, he celebrated divine offices in it; and it was afterwards made illustrious by many miracles.
queresadeopresentesacetiamadmonitumepisc.la: Quæ res ádeo præséntes ac étiam admónitum Epíscopum commóvit, ut indícto jejúnio rem a Deo postulándam mandáverit. Post tríduum Archángelus Epíscopum monet, in sua tutéla esse eum locum, velléque ut ibi cultus Deo, in sui et Angelórum memóriam haberétur. Spelúncam ígitur ádiit, vidénsque locum templo quodámmodo conformátum, divínis illum celebrávit offíciis, qui multis póstea miráculis fuit illustrátus.

archangelimichelisinterventionesuffultit.en: Upheld by the intercession of the Archangel Michael, we beseech thee, O Lord,
archangelimichelisinterventionesuffultit.la: Archángeli Michaélis interventióne suffúlti, te Dómine deprecámur,

utquoshonoreprosequimurcontingamusetment.en: That those whom we follow with honour, we may also reach in mind. * Alleluia, alleluia.
utquoshonoreprosequimurcontingamusetment.la: Ut quos honóre proséquimur, contingámus et mente. * Allelúia, allelúia.

utquoshonoreprosequimurcontingamusetment.en: That those whom we follow with honour, we may also reach in mind.
utquoshonoreprosequimurcontingamusetment.la: Ut quos honóre proséquimur, contingámus et mente.

gregoriusexsingularidivinarumlitterarums.en: Gregory, who for his singular knowledge of the divine Scriptures obtained the surname of the Theologian, was born at Nazianzus in Cappadocia, and, having been instructed at Athens in every kind of learning together with St. Basil, he turned himself to the study of the sacred Scriptures. Returning home, he was first Bishop of Sasima, then administrator of the Church of Nazianzus, then he was summoned to Constantinople to govern that Church. Purging the city of the errors of heresies and bringing it back to the Catholic faith, he drew upon himself the envy of many.
gregoriusexsingularidivinarumlitterarums.la: Gregórius ex singulári divinárum litterárum sciéntia Theólogi cognómen consecútus, Naziánzi in Cappadócia natus, Athénis in omni disciplinárum génere una cum sancto Basilío erudítus, ad stúdia sacrárum litterárum se convértit. Domum revérsus, primum Sasimórum Epíscopus, deinde Nazianzénæ Ecclésiæ administrátor, tum Constantinópolim ad eam regéndam Ecclésiam fuit accersítus. Civitátem hæresum purgátam erróribus, ad Cathólicam fidem redúcens, multórum sibi comparávit invídiam.

itaquecuminterepiscoposmagnaproptereesse.en: Wherefore, when for this cause a great dissension had arisen among the Bishops, he of his own accord resigned the episcopate, and returning to Nazianzus, caused Eulalius to be set over that Church, and then betook himself to the contemplation of divine things and to writing of them. He was a most ardent champion of the consubstantiality of the Son. Leading the life of a monk in the country, in these studies of writing and reading, in the reign of the emperor Theodosius, worn out with old age, he passed to the heavenly life.
itaquecuminterepiscoposmagnaproptereesse.la: Itaque cum inter Epíscopos magna proptérea esset facta sedítio, sponte cessit Episcopátu, et Naziánzum revérsus, illi Ecclésiæ Eulálium præficiéndum curávit, tumque se ad contemplatiónem et scriptiónem divinárum rerum cóntulit. Consubstantialitátis Fílii fuit acérrimus propugnátor. In iis scribéndi ac legéndi stúdiis ruri vitam mónachi exércens, imperatóre Theodósio, ad cœléstem vitam sénio conféctus migrávit.

beatuspetrusinviennensidiecesipiisadmodu.en: Blessed Peter, born in the Diocese of Vienne of very pious parents, being himself most pious from his early years, received the habit of holy conversation in the monastery of Bonnevaux of the Cistercian Order: where, when he had shown himself to the brethren a pattern of all virtues, he was by the consent of all elected the first Abbot of the new monastery of Tamié. In which office he showed truly wonderful examples of charity, not only towards his own brethren, but also towards strangers and pilgrims. Afterwards, being asked for as Pastor by the clergy of Tarentaise, at the exhortation of the whole Order, but chiefly of our holy Father Bernard, he undertook this archiepiscopal office: yet with such sparingness in food and clothing, that he surpassed his brethren the Monks no less by the austerity of his life than by the authority of his office; and so great was his liberality and charity towards the poor, that he often gave away his own food to the poor, even when making a journey.
beatuspetrusinviennensidiecesipiisadmodu.la: Beátus Petrus in Viennénsi Diœcési, piis ádmodum paréntibus natus, piíssimus ipse ab ineúnte ætáte in monastério Bonævállis Ordinis Cisterciénsis sanctae conversatiónis hábitum suscépit: ubi cum se frátribus ómnium virtútum exémplar exhibuisset, ómnium consénsu novi monastérii Stamediénsis primus Abbas eléctus est. Quo in múnere mira prorsus non tantum erga suos fratres, sed étiam erga extérnos et peregrínos charitátis exémpla perhíbuit. Póstmodum a Tarentasiénsi Clero in Pastórem expetítus, totíus Ordinis, máxime vero sancti Patris nostri Bernárdi hortátu istud Archiepiscopále munus súbiit: cum tanta tamen in victu et vestítu parcitáte, ut non minus vitæ austeritáte, quam múneris auctoritáte, fratres suos Mónachos antecéderet, tantáque erat erga páuperes liberalitáte et charitáte, ut sua sæpe cibária, étiam iter fáciens, paupéribus erogáret.

urgebatadmodumsanctissimumpastoremchrist.en: The charity of Christ so greatly urged the most holy Pastor, that he let no moment of an hour slip by in which he did not think of the reformation of his Diocese, which through the negligence of his predecessor had gone to ruin: whence it came to pass that in a short time the Church of Tarentaise recovered the splendour of its ancestral piety. And, that the Lord might add to his voice the voice of power, he brought it about that the grace of miracles accompanied the holiness of his life. But, fearing the glory of the world, when he had turned aside unknown to a certain monastery in Germany of the aforesaid Cistercian Order, he was there miraculously discovered: and so he was led back to his see with the greatest devotion and exultation of the people. At length, held in the greatest veneration by the highest princes, namely the emperor Frederick, and Louis the Younger, king of France, when he had completed seventy-three years, in the midst of his brethren singing psalms and praying, he gave back his soul to God.
urgebatadmodumsanctissimumpastoremchrist.la: Urgébat ádmodum sanctíssimum Pastórem Christi cháritas, ita ut nullam horæ mórulam labi síneret, in qua de reformatióne suæ Diœcésis, quæ prædecessóris incúria pessum íerat, non cogitáret: quo factum est, ut brevi Tarentasiénsis Ecclésia avítæ pietátis splendórem recuperáverit. Et, ut ipsíus voci vocem virtútis Dóminus ádderet, effécit, ut vitæ ipsíus sanctimóniam miraculórum grátia comitarétur. Sed mundi glóriam pertiméscens, cum ad quoddam Germániæ prædícti Ordinis Cisterciénsis monastérium ignótus divertísset, ibi miraculóse detéctus est: sicque ad suam sedem cum summa pópuli devotióne et exultatióne redúctus est. Tandem summa in veneratióne a summis princípibus, imperatóre nempe Frederíco, et rege Gálliæ Ludovíco Junióre hábitus, cum annos septuagínta tres complevísset, in médio fratrum psalléntium, et orántium ánimam Deo réddidit.

piusebononiaoriundusexnobilighisleriorum.en: Pius, a native of Bologna of the noble family of the Ghislieri, entered the Order of Preachers when he was fourteen years of age, and excelled in admirable patience, profound humility, the utmost austerity of life, and continual zeal for prayer and for regular discipline. Applying himself diligently to the sacred sciences, he made such progress in them that he taught them for many years with great praise, and preached public sermons with great fruit to his hearers. He long bore the office of Inquisitor with inviolable fortitude of soul, and kept many cities free from heresy. Raised by Paul the Fourth, to whom he was most dear for his eminent virtues, to the bishopric of Nepi and Sutri, and after two years enrolled among the Cardinals of the Roman Church, he was at length translated by Pius the Fourth to the Church of Mondovi; and having learned that many abuses had crept into it, he visited the whole diocese, and having set things in order, being called to be employed in most weighty affairs, he returned to Rome.
piusebononiaoriundusexnobilighisleriorum.la: Pius e Bonónia oriúndus ex nóbili Ghisleriórum família, cum quatuórdecim esset annórum, Ordinem Prædicatórum ingréssus, admirábili patiéntia, profúnda humilitáte, summa vitæ austeritáte, continuóque oratiónis et reguláris disciplínæ stúdio excélluit. Sacris disciplínis assídue incúmbens‚ ádeo in iis profécit, ut illas per plures annos magna cum laude docúerit, et públicas conciónes cum ingénti auditórum fructu habúerit. Inquisitóris offícium inviolábili ánimi fortitúdine diu sustínuit, multásque civitátes ab hæresi immúnes servávit. A Paulo quarto, cui, ob exímias virtútes charíssimus erat, ad Nepesínum et Sutrínum Episcopátum promótus, et post biénnium inter Románæ Ecclésiæ Cardináles adscríptus, demum ad Ecclésiam Montis Regális a Pio quarto translátus, cum plures in eam ábusus irrepsísse cognovísset, totam diœcésim lustrávit‚ rebúsque compósitis, gravíssimis applicándus negótiis, Romam revérsus est.

mortuoautempontificepreteromniumexpectat.en: And when the Pontiff was dead, being chosen in his place beyond the expectation of all, he changed nothing in his manner of life, save his outward dress. There was in him an unwearied labour for propagating religion and restoring ecclesiastical discipline; a constant beneficence in relieving the necessities of the needy, and an unconquered strength in vindicating the rights of the Apostolic See. Selim, emperor of the Turks, puffed up by many victories, he overcame at Lepanto with a great fleet gathered together, not so much by arms as by prayers poured forth to God. Which victory, at the very hour in which it was won, he knew by God's revealing it, and made it known to those of his household. But while he was preparing a new expedition, he fell into a grievous sickness, and having most patiently borne the most bitter pains, coming to his end, when he had received the Sacraments according to custom, he gave back his soul to God most peacefully in the year one thousand five hundred and seventy-two; and his body is honoured with the greatest veneration of the faithful in the Basilica of St. Mary at the Crib.
mortuoautempontificepreteromniumexpectat.la: Mórtuo autem Pontífice, præter omnium expectatiónem in ejus locum sufféctus, nihil in vitæ ratióne excépto exterióri hábitu, immutávit. Fuit in eo religiónis propagándæ et Ecclesiásticæ disciplínæ restituéndæ indeféssus labor; in sublevándis egéntium necessitátibus jugis beneficéntia, ac in Sedis Apostólicæ júribus vindicándis robur invíctum. Selímum Turcárum Imperatórem, multis elátum victóriis, ingénti comparáta classe, ad Naupáctum, non tam armis, quam fusis ad Deum précibus devícit. Quam victóriam ea ipsa hora, qua obtinebátur, Deo revelánte, cognóvit, suísque familiáribus indicávit. Dum vero novam molirétur expeditiónem, in gravem morbum íncidit, et acerbíssimis dolóribus patientíssime tolerátis, ad extréma devéniens‚ cum Sacraménta de more suscepísset, ánimam Deo placidíssime réddidit anno millésimo quingentésimo septuagésimo secúndo; cujus corpus in Basílica sanctæ Maríæ ad Præsépe summa fidélium veneratióne cólitur.

deepistolasancticyprianiepiscopietmartyr.en: From the Epistle of St. Cyprian, Bishop and Martyr, to the Martyrs and Confessors.
deepistolasancticyprianiepiscopietmartyr.la: De Epístola sancti Cypriáni Epíscopi et Mártyris ad Mártyres et Confessóres.

quibusegovoslaudibuspredicemfortissimima.en: With what praises shall I proclaim you, most valiant Martyrs? with what heraldry of voice shall I adorn the strength of your breast and the perseverance of your faith? Ye have borne the most cruel torture even unto the consummation of glory: nor have ye yielded to the torments, but rather the torments have yielded to you. The end of your pains, which the tortures gave not, crowns have given. The more grievous butchery continued long to this end, not that it might cast down the standing faith, but that it might send the men of God the more swiftly to God.
quibusegovoslaudibuspredicemfortissimima.la: Quibus ego vos láudibus prædicem, fortíssimi Mártyres? robur péctoris vestri, et perseverántiam fidei, quo præcónio vocis exórnem? Tolerástis usque ad consummatiónem glóriæ duríssimam quæstiónem: nec cessístis supplíciis, sed vobis pótius supplícia cessérunt. Finem dolóribus, quem torménta non dabant, corónæ dedérunt. Laniéna grávior ad hoc diu perseverávit‚ non ut stantem fidem dejíceret, sed ut hómines Dei ad Deum velócius mítteret.

viditadmiranspresentiummultitudocelestec.en: The multitude of those present saw with wonder the heavenly contest, the contest of God, the spiritual contest, the battle of Christ: that his servants stood with free voice, with mind uncorrupted, with divine strength, naked indeed of worldly weapons, but armed with the arms of burning faith. The tortured stood stronger than the torturers: and the members beaten and torn overcame the beating and tearing hooks.
