viditadmiranspresentiummultitudocelestec.la: Vidit admírans præséntium multitúdo cœléste certámen, certámen Dei, certámen spiritále, prælium Christi: stetísse servos ejus voce libera, mente incorrúpta‚ virtúte divína, telis quidem sæculáribus nudos, sed armis fidei ardéntis armátos. Stetérunt torti torquéntibus fortióres: et pulsántes ac laniántes úngulas, pulsáta ac laniáta membra vicérunt.

petruscelestinusesernieinsamnitibusexmat.en: Peter Celestine came forth wonderfully from his mother's womb at Isernia among the Samnites, his little body covered with a blackish membrane, like a monastic habit. As a little boy he was often taught by the Virgin Mother of God and by St. John the Evangelist. While still a boy, seeking the rough and pathless places of the mountains, he dwelt for five years in a hidden cave, whence also he drove out by divine power a huge dragon. An eminent dweller in the desert, he led a life rough indeed in food, but shining with the marks of virtues.
petruscelestinusesernieinsamnitibusexmat.la: Petrus Cœlestínus, Æsérniæ in Samnítibus ex matérna alvo pellícula súbnigra, monástici hábitus instar corpúsculo obdúcta‚ mirabíliter pródiit. Puérulus a Deípara Vírgine, et divo Joánne Evangelísta sæpenúmero erudítur. Adhuc puer, áspera ac dévia móntium petens in latebrósa specu, unde et immánem dracónem divina virtúte éxpulit, quinquénnio commorátur. Erémi cultor præcípuus, victu quidem ásperam, sed virtútum insígniis coruscántem vitam duxit.

multisadeumundiqueconfluentibusordinemsa.en: Many flocking to him from every side, he spread the Order of St. Benedict, in which as a youth he had made his solemn profession, by the founding of the Celestine Monks. Thence, having returned to the desert, he was designated supreme Pontiff; in which office, using the same manner of living as before, and having conducted himself piously for about six months, he of his own accord abdicated the Papacy, and withdrew once more to the woods. He was renowned for miracles before and after his death. At length, worn out with old age and hardships, he passed to the Lord.
multisadeumundiqueconfluentibusordinemsa.la: Multis ad eum úndique confluéntibus, Ordinem sancti Benedícti, in quo adoléscens solémnem emíserat professiónem‚ institutióne Monachórum Cœlestinórum propagávit. Inde ad erémum revérsus Summus Póntifex designátur; quo in múnere, eódem, quo dudum vivéndi génere utens, ac círciter sex menses pie versátus, Papátu sese ultro abdicávit‚ et ad némora iteráto se recépit. Miráculis ante et post óbitum cláruit. Dénique sénio conféctus, et ærúmnis, migrávit ad Dóminum.

gregoriuspapaseptimusanteahildebrandusso.en: Pope Gregory the Seventh, formerly Hildebrand, was born at Soana in Tuscany; being yet of tender age he went to Rome, and was brought up under the protection of St. Peter. As a young man, grieving most vehemently that the liberty of the Church was oppressed by laymen, and that the morals of churchmen were depraved, he took the regular habit in the monastery of Cluny, and served the divine Majesty with such ardour of piety that he was elected Prior by the holy fathers of the same abbey. Divine Providence disposing greater things for him, he was brought out of Cluny, and was first elected Abbot of St. Paul's without the walls of the City, and afterwards created Cardinal of the Roman Church; under five supreme Pontiffs in turn he fulfilled chief offices and legations with great praise and vigorous virtue, and was called by blessed Peter Damian a man of most holy and most pure counsel. When Alexander the Second died, he was, against his will and sorrowing, elected supreme Pontiff by the unanimous consent of all, and shone like the sun in the House of God; for, mighty in work and word, he applied himself with such zeal to repairing ecclesiastical discipline, propagating the faith, and restoring ecclesiastical liberty, that it is held that since the age of the Apostles there was no Pontiff who bore greater labours and troubles for the Church of God, or who fought more keenly for her liberty.
gregoriuspapaseptimusanteahildebrandusso.la: Gregórius Papa séptimus ántea Hildebrándus‚ Soánæ in Hetrúria natus ténera adhuc ætáte Romam proféctus‚ sub protectióne sancti Petri educátus est. Júvenis Ecclésiæ libertátem a láicis oppréssam, ac depravátos Ecclesiasticórum mores veheméntius dolens, in Cluniacénsi monastério hábitum regulárem índuit, tantóque pietátis ardóre divínæ Majestáti servívit, ut a sanctis ejúsdem cœnóbii pátribus Prior fúerit eléctus. Divina Providéntia majóra de eo disponénte, Cluníaco edúctus, Abbas primum sancti Pauli extra muros Urbis eléctus, ac póstmodum Románæ Ecclésiæ Cardinális creátus, sub quinque vicissim Summis Pontifícibus præcípua múnera et legatiónes cum laude magna, et strénua virtúte implévit‚ vir sanctíssimi ac puríssimi consílii a beáto Petro Damiáno nuncupáns. Mórtuo Alexándro secúndo, invítus et mœrens unánimi ómnium consénsu Summus Póntifex eléctus, sicut sol effúlsit in Domo Dei; nam potens ópere et sermóne, Ecclesiásticæ disciplínæ reparándæ, fídei propagándæ, libertáti Ecclesiásticæ restituéndæ, tanto stúdio incúbuit, ut ex Apostolórum ætáte nullus Pontíficum fuísse tradátur, qui majóres pro Ecclésia Dei labóres molestiásque pertúlerit‚ aut qui pro ejus libertáte ácrius pugnáverit.

dummissarumsolemniaperageretvisestcolumb.en: While he was celebrating the solemnities of Mass, a dove was seen descending from heaven, with outspread wings, to veil his head; whereby it was signified that he governed the Church by the breathing of the Holy Ghost, not by the counsels of human prudence. When he was pressed at Rome by a grievous siege by the army of the emperor Henry, whom, fallen into the depth of evils, he had deprived of the communion of the faithful and of his kingdom, he put out with the sign of the Cross a fire kindled by the enemy. Delivered at length from his hand, he betook himself to Monte Cassino and thence to Salerno, where, when he had once preached to the people, worn out with hardships he fell into a sickness, of which he foreknew that he would die. The last words of the dying Gregory were: I have loved justice and hated iniquity, therefore I die in exile. Innumerable are the things which he either bravely endured, or wisely ordained in Synods, a man truly holy, an avenger of crimes, and a most keen defender of the Church. Having therefore completed twelve years in the pontificate, he passed into heaven, in the year of salvation one thousand and eighty-five, dear for very many miracles in life and after death.
dummissarumsolemniaperageretvisestcolumb.la: Dum Missárum solémnia perágeret, visa est colúmba e cœlo delápsa, alis expánsis, caput ejus veláre; quo significabátur ipsum Spíritus sancti afflátu, non humánæ prudéntiæ consíliis Ecclésiam gubernáre. Cum ab exércitu imperatóris Henríci‚ quem in profúndum malórum prolápsum‚ fidélium communióne regnóque priváverat, Romæ gravi obsidióne premerétur, excitátum ab hóstibus incéndium, signo Crucis extínxit. De ejus manu tandem liberátus, Cassínum et inde Salérnum se cóntulit, ubi cum aliquándo sermónem habuísset ad pópulum ærúmnis conféctus in morbum íncidit, quo se interitúrum præscívit. Postréma Gregórii moriéntis verba fuére: Diléxi justítiam et odívi iniquitátem, proptérea mórior in exílio. Innumerabília sunt quæ vel fórtiter sustínuit, vel in Synodis sapiénter constítuit, vir vere sanctus‚ críminum vindex, et acérrimus Ecclésiæ defénsor. Exáctis itaque in Pontificátu annis duódecim, migrávit in cœlum, anno salútis millésimo octogésimo quinto, plúrimis in vita et post mortem miráculis carus.

philippusflorentienatushereditatedimissa.en: Philip, born at Florence, having given up his inheritance, betook himself to Rome, where he dedicated himself wholly to Christ. Intent on abstinence, watchings and prayers, he often spent the night in the cemetery of Callistus. Made a Priest out of obedience, he was wholly given to procuring the salvation of souls. He begot many to Christ, and, desiring to nourish them with the food of the word of God, with frequenting of the Sacraments, with assiduity in prayer, and with other pious exercises, he instituted the Congregation of the Oratory.
philippusflorentienatushereditatedimissa.la: Philíppus Floréntiæ natus, hæreditáte dimíssa, Romam se contulit, ubi totum se Christo dicávit. Abstinéntiæ, vigíliis et oratiónibus inténtus, apud cœmetérium Callísti sæpius pernoctávit. Sacérdos ex obediéntia factus, in animárum salúte procuránda totus fuit. Multos Christo péperit, quos verbi Dei pábulo, Sacramentórum frequéntia, oratiónis assiduitáte, aliísque piis exercitatiónibus enutríri cúpiens, Oratórii Congregatiónem instítuit.

charitatedeiproximiquevulneratuslangueba.en: Wounded with the love of God and of his neighbour, he languished continually. Given to humility, and renowned for the gift of prophecy, he preserved his virginity perpetually unstained; and he restored to health very many sick persons, and some near to death, and also recalled a dead man to life. Enlightened by divine apparitions, and having foretold the hour of his death with joy, at eighty years of age he fell asleep in the Lord, and was enrolled in the number of the Saints by Gregory the Fifteenth.
charitatedeiproximiquevulneratuslangueba.la: Charitáte Dei proximíque vulnerátus, languébat júgiter. Humilitáti addíctus, et dono prophetíae clarus, virginitátem perpétuo illibátam conservávit, et ægrótos plúrimos, et morti próximos, sanitáti restítuit, mórtuum quoque ad vitam revocávit. Divínis apparitiónibus illustrátus, et mortis hora cum gáudio prænuntiáta, octogenárius obdormívit in Dómino, et a Gregório décimo quinto in Sanctórum númerum est relátus.

martyrumtuorumbernardimarieetgratiememor.en: Recalling the memory of thy Martyrs Bernard, Mary and Grace, we humbly beseech thee, O Lord, * that, rooted and founded in thy charity, we may be able, for love of that glory which shall be revealed in us, to bear the sufferings of this time with an unconquered and willing mind.
martyrumtuorumbernardimarieetgratiememor.la: Mártyrum tuórum Bernárdi, Maríæ et Grátiæ memóriam recenséntes, súpplices te, Dómine, deprecámur; * ut in tua charitáte radicáti et fundáti, passiónes hujus témporis, amóre illíus glóriæ, quæ revelánda est in nobis, invícto ac libénti ánimo sustinére valeámus.

robertuseboraciinanglianatuspuerilesludo.en: Robert, born at York in England, shunning childish games from his infancy, applied his mind to the study of letters. Made a Priest and rector of a certain church, from a desire of solitude he took the habit of St. Benedict. For the sake of a stricter observance, passing to the Cistercian Order and the Monastery of Fountains, after his virtue had been proved, he was set over a new Monastery by Abbot Richard. He practised abstinence wonderfully, and, not content with the accustomed task of the Office, he recited the whole psalter daily.
robertuseboraciinanglianatuspuerilesludo.la: Robértus Eboráci in Anglia natus, pueríles ludos ab infántia vitans, litterárum stúdio ánimum applícuit. Factus Sacérdos‚ et cujúsdam ecclésiæ rector, solitúdinis desidério sancti Benedícti hábitum suscépit. Strictióris observántiæ causa, ad Ordinem Cisterciénsem, et Monastérium de Fóntibus tránsiens, post probátam virtútem‚ a Richárdo Abbáte, novo Monastério præfícitur. Abstinéntiam mirífice cóluit, solitóque Offícii penso non conténtus quotídie psaltérium ex integro recitábat.

divinituseimultafuererevelatademoniaperi.en: Many things were revealed to him by God, devils were put to flight by him, and being made intimate with blessed Father Bernard, he received from him a girdle as a token of love, and a testimony of his innocence and purity. Having often conversed of divine things with Godric the Hermit, a most holy man, he rested in a holy end in the year one thousand one hundred and fifty-nine, on the seventh of the Ides of June. And his soul was seen by Godric among the Angels, and a dumb man praying at his tomb received speech.
divinituseimultafuererevelatademoniaperi.la: Divínitus ei multa fuére reveláta, dæmónia per ipsum fugáta, et familiáris beáto Patri Bernárdo factus, ab ipso zonam recépit in amóris arguméntum‚ et ipsíus innocéntiæ ac puritátis testimónium. Cum Godríco Eremíta viro sanctíssimo sæpe de divínis collocútus, sancto fine quiévit anno millésimo centésimo quinquagésimo nono, séptimo Idus Júnii. Ejus autem ánima inter Angelos visa est a Godríco, et mutus ad ejus túmulum orans loquélam accépit.

oquampulchrisupermontespedes.en: O how beautiful upon the mountains are the feet:
oquampulchrisupermontespedes.la: O quam pulchri super montes pedes:

annuntiantiumpacemannuntiantiumbona.en: Of them that preach peace, of them that preach good things!

inomnemterramexivitsonuseorumetinfinesor.en: Their sound is gone out through all the earth, and their words to the ends of the world.
inomnemterramexivitsonuseorumetinfinesor.la: In omnem terram exívit sonus eórum: et in fines orbis terræ verba eórum.

celienarrantgloriamdeietoperamanuumeiusa.en: The heavens shew forth the glory of God, and the firmament declareth the works of his hands.
celienarrantgloriamdeietoperamanuumeiusa.la: Cæli enárrant glóriam Dei, et ópera mánuum ejus annúntiat firmaméntum.

inomnemterramexivitsonuseorum.en: Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth:
inomnemterramexivitsonuseorum.la: In omnem terram exívit sonus eórum:

etinfinesorbisterreverbeorum.en: And their words unto the ends of the world.
etinfinesorbisterreverbeorum.la: Et in fines orbis terræ verba eórum.

nonsuntloquelenequesermonesquorumnonaudi.en: There are no speeches nor languages, where their voices are not heard.
nonsuntloquelenequesermonesquorumnonaudi.la: Non sunt loquélæ neque sermónes, quorum non audiántur voces eórum.

vosestisquipermansistismecumintentationi.en: You are they who have continued with me in my temptations, saith the Lord, and I dispose to you a kingdom:
vosestisquipermansistismecumintentationi.la: Vos estis, qui permansístis mecum in tentatiónibus meis, dicit Dóminus, et ego dispóno vobis regnum:

utedatisetbibatissupermensammeaminregnom.en: That you may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and may sit upon thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
utedatisetbibatissupermensammeaminregnom.la: Ut edátis, et bibátis super mensam meam in regno meo, et sedeátis super thronos judicántes duódecim tribus Israël.

nonvosmeelegistissedegelegivosetposuivos.en: Ye have not chosen Me, but I have chosen you, and ordained you
nonvosmeelegistissedegelegivosetposuivos.la: Non vos me elegístis, sed ego elégi vos, et pósui vos:

vosestisluxmundidicitdominus.en: You are the light of the world, saith the Lord:
vosestisluxmundidicitdominus.la: Vos estis lux mundi, dicit Dóminus:

quiinpatientiavestrapossidebitisanimasve.en: Who in your patience shall possess your souls.
quiinpatientiavestrapossidebitisanimasve.la: Qui in patiéntia vestra possidébitis ánimas vestras.

etegodisponovobissicutdisposuitmihipater.en: And I dispose to you, as my Father hath disposed to me, a kingdom:
etegodisponovobissicutdisposuitmihipater.la: Et ego dispóno vobis, sicut dispósuit mihi Pater meus regnum:

lutgardisvirgobrabantinaduodecimannosnat.en: Lutgard, a virgin of Brabant, being twelve years old, was given to the Nuns of St. Benedict to be brought up. There, when she had grown up, and suitors pressing her, she was inclining to marriage, she was so wounded by the presence of Christ wounded, that, spurning the allurements of the world, she sought the nuptials of the heavenly Spouse alone. Given thenceforth to contemplation, she became a pattern of religious life, illustrious also for prophecy, and renowned for miracles. Strengthened by converse with the Virgin Mother of God and St. Catherine, clasped by the arm of Christ crucified, she drew from his life-giving side, exchanging heart for heart. By a heavenly warning she entered the Cistercian Order, happy in the patronage of Mary, to be an example to many; and soon, being sought on every side as Abbess, she refused the honour, obtaining this from her singular patroness, that she could never learn the French tongue; whence, being made useless to others, she might attend to her own advancement.
lutgardisvirgobrabantinaduodecimannosnat.la: Lutgárdis virgo Brabantína‚ duódecim annos nata, Moniálibus sancti Benedícti educánda tráditur. Ibi cum adolevísset, et instántibus procis in matrimónium propendéret, Christi vulneráti præséntia ita fuit sauciáta‚ ut spretis mundi illécebris, solíus cœléstis Sponsi núptias ambíerit. Contemplatióni deínceps addícta, religiónis forma facta est, prophetía étiam illústris‚ et miráculis clara. Deíparæ Vírginis ac sanctæ Catharínæ roboráta collóquio, Christi crucifíxi constrícta bráchio, vivíficum latus exúgit, cor mútuans corde. Cœlésti mónitu, Cisterciénsem Ordinem Mariæ felícem patrocínio, multis exémplo futúra, ingréditur; ac brevi undequáque expetíta in Abbatíssam, honórem ábnuit, id óbtinens a patróna singulári, ut idióma Gállicum nusquam edíscere potúerit; unde céteris inútilis facta, própriis studéret increméntis.

grassanteingalliaalbigensiumheresiieiuni.en: While the heresy of the Albigenses was raging in France, she twice undertook a fast of seven years, in which she sustained her life on bread and beer alone, to appease God. She was a help to the souls groaning in purgatory, and a terror to the demons, whom she drove far from her by the lightning of the word of God. The virtues glowed in her as if vying with one another, but above all a profound humility and a perfect charity, in whose burning she longed for the martyrdom of Agnes. She wrought many miracles, healing the sick, converting those that lived evil lives, moving the despairing to hope of pardon. And being deprived of her sight for eleven years, she gave an example of patience, and at length Christ stood by her as she was dying, on the fourth of the Ides of June, in the year one thousand two hundred and forty-six, in the sixty-fourth year of her age.
grassanteingalliaalbigensiumheresiieiuni.la: Grassánte in Gallia Albigénsium hæresi, jejúnium septénnii, quo solo pane et zytho vitam sustentábat, Deum placatúra, suscépit semel ac íterum. Animábus in purgatório geméntibus fuit auxílio, dæmónibus terróri, quos verbi Dei fúlgure longe a se abigébat. Certátim in ea fervébant virtútes, sed profúnda potíssimum humílitas et perfécta cháritas, qua urénte, ad Agnétis martyrium suspirávit. Plura confécit mirácula, sanans infírmos, male vivéntes convértens, desperátos in spem véniæ cómmovens. Undecim vero annis orbáta lúmine, patiéntiæ spécimen dedit, ac moriénti tandem Christus ástitit, quarto Idus Júnii anno millésimo ducentésimo quadragésimo sexto, ætátis sexagésimo quarto.

audifilietvideetinclinaauremtuametoblivi.en: Hearken, O daughter, and see, and incline thy ear, and forget thy people, and thy father's house, and the king shall greatly desire thy beauty:
audifilietvideetinclinaauremtuametoblivi.la: Audi, fília, et vide, et inclína aurem tuam, et oblivíscere pópulum tuum, et domum Patris tui, et concupíscet Rex spéciem tuam:

quoniamipseestdominusdeustuus.en: For he is the Lord thy God.
quoniamipseestdominusdeustuus.la: Quóniam ipse est Dóminus Deus tuus.

induittedominusvestimentissalutisetindum.en: The Lord hath clothed thee with the garments of salvation, and with the robe of gladness hath he encompassed thee:
induittedominusvestimentissalutisetindum.la: Induit te Dóminus vestiméntis salútis, et induménto lætítiæ circúmdedit te:

deusquibeatamelisabethsanctarumtuarumvir.en: O God, who didst vouchsafe to gather blessed Elizabeth into the company of thy holy Virgins: § grant us, we beseech thee, that by her prayers and merits we may be cleansed from all our sins, § and may enjoy the everlasting fellowship of thy majesty. *
deusquibeatamelisabethsanctarumtuarumvir.la: Deus, qui beátam Elísabeth sanctárum tuárum Vírginum collégio aggregáre dignátus es: § tríbue nobis, quaésumus; ut ejus précibus et méritis a culpis ómnibus expiémur, § et ætérno tuæ majestátis consórtio perfruámur. *

responsoriuminternatosmulierumnonsurrexi.en: Responsory. Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist: * Who prepared the way of the Lord in the desert.
responsoriuminternatosmulierumnonsurrexi.la: Responsorium. Inter natos mulíerum non surréxit major Joánne Baptísta : * Qui viam Dómini præparávit in éremo.

fuithomomissusadeocuinomeneratioannes.en: There was a man sent from God, whose name was John.
fuithomomissusadeocuinomeneratioannes.la: Fuit homo missus a Deo, cui nomen erat Joánnes.

quiviamdominipreparavitineremo.en: Who prepared the way of the Lord in the desert.
quiviamdominipreparavitineremo.la: Qui viam Dómini præparávit in éremo.

ioannesestnomeneiusvinumetsiceramnonbibe.en: John * is his name; he shall drink no wine nor strong drink, and many shall rejoice in his birth.
ioannesestnomeneiusvinumetsiceramnonbibe.la: Joánnes * est nomen ejus, vinum et síceram non bibet, et multi in nativitáte ejus gaudébunt. Ps. 63

preoquodnoncredidistiverbismeiseristacen.en: Because * thou hast not believed my words, thou shalt be dumb, and shalt not be able to speak until the day of his birth.
preoquodnoncredidistiverbismeiseristacen.la: Pro eo * quod non credidísti verbis meis, eris tacens, et non póteris loqui usque in diem nativitátis ejus. Ps. 256, 257, 258

hicvenitintestimoniumuttestimoniumperhib.en: This man came for a witness, to give testimony of the light.
hicvenitintestimoniumuttestimoniumperhib.la: Hic venit in testimónium, ut testimónium perhibéret de lúmine.

netimeasafacieeorumquiatecumegosum.en: Be not afraid at their presence: for I am with thee:
netimeasafacieeorumquiatecumegosum.la: Ne tímeas a fácie eórum: quia tecum ego sum:

ipsepreibitanteilluminspirituetvirtuteel.en: He shall go before Him in the spirit and power of Elias.
ipsepreibitanteilluminspirituetvirtuteel.la: Ipse præíbit ante illum in spíritu et virtúte Elíæ:

utconvertatcordapatruminfiliosetincredul.en: That he may turn the hearts of the fathers unto the children, and the incredulous to the wisdom of the just, † to prepare unto the Lord a perfect people.
utconvertatcordapatruminfiliosetincredul.la: Ut convértat corda patrum in fílios, et incrédulos ad prudéntiam justórum, † paráre Dómino plebem perféctam.

eritenimmagnuscoramdominetspiritusanctor.en: For he shall be great before the Lord; and he shall be filled with the Holy Ghost.
eritenimmagnuscoramdominetspiritusanctor.la: Erit enim magnus coram Dómino, et Spíritu Sancto replébitur.

locutusestangelusdominiadzachariamdicens.en: The Angel of the Lord spake unto Zacharias, saying: Thou shalt beget a child in thine old age,
locutusestangelusdominiadzachariamdicens.la: Locútus est Angelus Dómini ad Zacharíam, dicens: Generábis púerum in senectúte tua,

ethabebitnomenioannes.en: And his name shall be John.

istepuereritmagnuscoramdominonametmanuse.en: This child shall be great before the Lord, for his hand also is with him:
istepuereritmagnuscoramdominonametmanuse.la: Iste puer erit magnus coram Dómino, nam et manus ejus cum ipso est:

fuitindesertopredicansbaptismumpenitenti.en: He was in the desert preaching the baptism of penance unto the remission of sins:
fuitindesertopredicansbaptismumpenitenti.la: Fuit in desérto prædicans baptísmum pœniténtiæ in remissiónem peccatórum:

etmisitdominusmanumsuamettetigitosmeumet.en: And the Lord put forth his hand, and touched my mouth: and the Lord said to me: Behold, I have given my words in thy mouth: Lo, I have set thee this day over the nations, and over kingdoms, to root up, and to pull down, and to waste, and to destroy, and to build, and to plant.
etmisitdominusmanumsuamettetigitosmeumet.la: Et misit Dóminus manum suam, et tétigit os meum: et dixit Dóminus ad me: Ecce dedi verba mea in ore tuo: Ecce constítui te hódie super gentes, et super regna, ut evéllas, et déstruas, et dispérdas, et díssipes, et ædífices, et plantes.

pararedominoplebemperfectam.en: To prepare unto the Lord a perfect people.

inspirituetvirtuteelie.en: In the spirit and power of Elias.

gaudentincelisanimesanctorumquichristive.en: In heaven rejoice * the souls of the Saints, who have followed the footsteps of Christ: and because for his love they shed their blood, therefore do they exult with Christ without end.
gaudentincelisanimesanctorumquichristive.la: Gaudent in cœlis * ánimæ Sanctórum, qui Christi vestígia sunt secúti: et quia pro ejus amóre sánguinem suum fudérunt, ídeo cum Christo exúltant sine fine.

iustiinperpetuumviventetapuddominumestme.en: The just shall live for evermore, and their reward is with the Lord, and the care of them with the most High:
iustiinperpetuumviventetapuddominumestme.la: Justi in perpétuum vivent, et apud Dóminum est merces eórum, et cogitátio illórum apud Altíssimum:

ideoqueaccipientregnumdecorisdemanudomin.en: Therefore shall they receive a kingdom of glory from the hand of the Lord.
ideoqueaccipientregnumdecorisdemanudomin.la: Ideóque accípient regnum decóris de manu Dómini.

deustentavitillosetinveniteosdignosse.en: God hath tried them, and found them worthy of himself.
deustentavitillosetinveniteosdignosse.la: Deus tentávit illos et invénit eos dignos se:

sicoramhominibustormentapassisuntspesele.en: Though before men * they suffered torments, the hope of the elect is immortal for ever.
sicoramhominibustormentapassisuntspesele.la: Si coram homínibus * torménta passi sunt, spes electórum est immortális in ætérnum. Ps. 109

tamquamauruminfornaceprobavitelectosdomi.en: As gold in the furnace * hath the Lord proved his elect, and as a victim of a holocaust he hath received them.
tamquamauruminfornaceprobavitelectosdomi.la: Tamquam aurum in fornáce * probávit eléctos Dóminus, et quasi holocáusti hóstiam accépit illos. Ps. 110

istorumestenimregnumcelorumquicontempser.en: For theirs * is the kingdom of heaven, who despised the life of the world, and attained to the rewards of the kingdom, and washed their robes in the blood of the Lamb.
istorumestenimregnumcelorumquicontempser.la: Istórum est enim * regnum cœlórum, qui contempsérunt vitam mundi, et pervenérunt ad præmia regni, et lavérunt stolas suas in sánguine Agni. Ps. 111

viaiustorumrectafactestetitersanctorumpr.en: The way of the just * is made straight, and the path of the Saints is prepared.
viaiustorumrectafactestetitersanctorumpr.la: Via Justórum * recta facta est, et iter Sanctórum præparátum est. Ps. 112

christumregemregumadoremusdominumquimart.en: Let us adore Christ, the King of kings, the Lord, * Who glorified the blessed Apostle Peter by the martyrdom of the cross.
christumregemregumadoremusdominumquimart.la: Christum Regem regum adorémus Dóminum, * Qui martyrio crucis beátum glorificávit Petrum Apóstolum.

petrusetioannesascendebantintemplumadhor.en: Peter and John * went up into the temple at the ninth hour of prayer.
petrusetioannesascendebantintemplumadhor.la: Petrus et Joánnes * ascendébant in templum ad horam oratiónis nonam. Ps. 18

claudusquidamcumvidissetpetrumetioannemc.en: A certain lame man, * when he had seen Peter and John, began to ask them that he might receive an alms.
claudusquidamcumvidissetpetrumetioannemc.la: Claudus quidam * cum vidísset Petrum et Joánnem, cœpit rogáre eos, ut eleemósynam accíperet. Ps. 23

argentumetaurumnonestmihiquodautemhabeoh.en: Silver and gold * I have none; but what I have, that I give thee.
argentumetaurumnonestmihiquodautemhabeoh.la: Argéntum et aurum * non est mihi: quod autem hábeo, hoc tibi do. Ps. 32

innomineiesuchristinazarenisurgeetambula.en: In the name * of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, arise, and walk in peace.
innomineiesuchristinazarenisurgeetambula.la: In nómine * Jesu Christi Nazaréni surge, et ámbula in pace. Ps. 33

exiliitclaudusetambulabatetintravitcumil.en: The lame man leaped up, * and walked, and went in with them walking, and praising God.
exiliitclaudusetambulabatetintravitcumil.la: Exíliit claudus, * et ambulábat, et intrávit cum illis ámbulans, et laudans Deum. Ps. 44

viditpopulusclaudumambulantemetlaudantem.en: The people saw * the lame man walking and praising God; and they were filled with wonder and amazement at that which had happened to him.
viditpopulusclaudumambulantemetlaudantem.la: Vidit pópulus * claudum ambulántem, et laudántem Deum; et repléti sunt stupóre et éxtasi in eo quod contígerat illi. Ps. 46

petrusquidemservabaturincarcereetoratiof.en: Peter therefore * was kept in prison, and prayer was made without ceasing by the Church unto God for him.
petrusquidemservabaturincarcereetoratiof.la: Petrus quidem * servabátur in cárcere, et orátio fiébat pro eo sine intermissióne ab Ecclésia ad Deum. Ps. 60

dixitangelusadpetrumcircumdatibivestimen.en: The Angel said unto Peter: * Cast thy garment about thee, and follow me.
dixitangelusadpetrumcircumdatibivestimen.la: Dixit Angelus ad Petrum: * Circúmda tibi vestiméntum tuum, et séquere me. Ps. 63

misitdominusangelumsuumetliberavitmedema.en: The Lord hath sent * his Angel, and hath delivered me out of the hand of Herod.
misitdominusangelumsuumetliberavitmedema.la: Misit Dóminus * Angelum suum, et liberávit me de manu Heródis. Ps. 64

corneliuscenturiovirreligiosusactimensde.en: Cornelius the centurion, * a religious man, and fearing God, saw manifestly an Angel of God saying to him: Cornelius, send and call hither Simon, who is surnamed Peter; he will tell thee what thou must do.
corneliuscenturiovirreligiosusactimensde.la: Cornélius Centúrio, * vir religiósus, ac timens Deum, vidit maniféste Angelum Dei, dicéntem sibi: Cornéli, mitte et accérsi Simónem, qui cognominátur Petrus; hic dicet tibi quid te opórteat fácere. Ps. 74

beatuspetrusapostolusviditsibichristumoc.en: The blessed Apostle Peter * saw Christ coming to meet him, and adoring him he said: Lord, whither goest thou? I come to Rome to be crucified again.
beatuspetrusapostolusviditsibichristumoc.la: Beátus Petrus * Apóstolus vidit sibi Christum occúrrere, adórans eum, et ait: Dómine, quo vadis? Vénio Romam íterum crucifígi. Ps. 96

simonioannisdiligismeplushistuscisdomine.en: Simon, son of John, * lovest thou me more than these? Thou knowest, Lord, that I love thee.
simonioannisdiligismeplushistuscisdomine.la: Simon Joánnis, * díligis me plus his? Tu scis, Dómine, quia amo te. Ps. 98

adhucloquentepetroceciditspiritussanctus.en: While Peter was yet speaking, * the Holy Ghost fell on all them that heard the word, and they were speaking with tongues, and magnifying God: then Peter commanded them to be baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ.
adhucloquentepetroceciditspiritussanctus.la: Adhuc loquénte Petro, * cécidit Spíritus sanctus super omnes, qui audiébant verbum, et erant loquéntes longuis, et magnificántes Deum: tunc Petrus jussit eos baptizári in nómine Dómini Jesu Christi. Ps. 253, 254, 255

exsermdenataliapostolorumpetrietpauli.en: From Sermon 1 on the Birthday of the Apostles Peter and Paul.
exsermdenataliapostolorumpetrietpauli.la: Ex Serm. 1. de Natali Apostolorum Petri et Pauli.

pretiosestinconspectudominimorssanctorum.en: Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his Saints. Nor can any kind of cruelty destroy the religion founded on the mystery of the Cross of Christ. The Church is not diminished by persecutions, but increased: and the Lord's field is ever clothed with a richer harvest, while the grains, which fall one by one, spring up multiplied.
pretiosestinconspectudominimorssanctorum.la: Pretiósa est in conspéctu Dómini mors Sanctórum ejus. Nec ullo crudelitátis génere déstrui potest sacraménto Crucis Christi fundáta relígio. Non minúitur persecutiónibus Ecclésia, sed augétur: et semper Domínicus ager ségete ditióri vestítur, dum grana, quæ síngula cadunt, multiplicáta nascúntur.

undeduoistapreclaradiviniseminisgerminai.en: Wherefore the thousands of blessed Martyrs bear witness unto how great an offspring these two glorious shoots of the divine seed have sprung up: who, emulating the triumphs of the Apostles, have encompassed our city with peoples clad in purple and shining far and wide, and have crowned it as it were with one diadem composed of the honour of many gems.
undeduoistapreclaradiviniseminisgerminai.la: Unde duo ista præclára divíni séminis gérmina, in quantam sóbolem germinárint, beatórum míllia Mártyrum protestántur: qui Apostolicórum æmuli triumphórum, urbem nostram purpurátis et longe latéque rutilántibus pópulis ambiérunt, et quasi ex multárum honóre gemmárum consérto uno diadémate coronárunt.

dequorumpresidiodilectissimidivinitusnob.en: In whose protection, dearly beloved, divinely prepared for us as an example of patience and for the confirmation of faith, we must indeed rejoice universally in the commemoration of all the Saints, but in the excellence of these fathers we must rightly glory more excellently, whom the grace of God hath raised to so high a summit among all the members of the Church, that he hath set them in the body whose head is Christ as it were the twin light of the eyes.
dequorumpresidiodilectissimidivinitusnob.la: De quorum præsídio, dilectíssimi, divínitus nobis ad exémplum patiéntiæ et confirmatiónem fídei præparáto; universáliter quidem in ómnium Sanctórum commemoratióne lætándum est, sed in horum excelléntia patrum mérito est excelléntius gloriándum, quos grátia Dei in tantum ápicem inter ómnia Ecclésiæ membra provéxit, ut eos in córpore, cui caput est Christus, quasi géminum constitúerit lumen oculórum.

dequorummeritisatquevirtutibusqueomnemlo.en: Of whose merits and virtues, which surpass all power of speech, we ought to think nothing different, nothing distinct: because election made them peers, labour made them like, and their end made them equal. But as we ourselves have experienced, and our forefathers have proved, we believe and trust that amid all the labours of this life we shall ever be helped to obtain the mercy of God by the prayers of our special patrons: that as much as we are weighed down by our own sins, so much may we be raised up by the merits of the Apostles.
dequorummeritisatquevirtutibusqueomnemlo.la: De quorum méritis atque virtútibus, quæ omnem loquéndi súperant facultátem, nihil divérsum, nihil debémus sentíre discrétum: quia illos eléctio pares, et labor similes, et finis fecit æquáles. Sicut autem et nos expérti sumus‚ et nostri probavére majóres‚ crédimus atque confídimus, inter omnes labóres istíus vitæ ad obtinéndam misericórdiam Dei, semper nos nos speciálium patronórum oratiónibus adjuvándos: ut quantum própriis peccátis deprímimur tantum Apostólicis méritis erigámur.

petreamasmepasceovesmeastuscisdominequia.en: Peter, lovest thou me? * Feed my sheep. Thou knowest, Lord, that I love thee.
petreamasmepasceovesmeastuscisdominequia.la: Petre, amas me? * Pasce oves meas. Tu scis, Dómine, quia amo te.

significavitdominuspetroquamorteclarific.en: The Lord signified to Peter * by what death he should glorify God.
significavitdominuspetroquamorteclarific.la: Significávit Dóminus Petro, * qua morte clarificatúrus esset Deum.

egoproterogavipetreutnondeficiatfidestue.en: I have prayed for thee, Peter, * that thy faith fail not: and thou, being once converted, confirm thy brethren.
egoproterogavipetreutnondeficiatfidestue.la: Ego pro te rogávi Petre, * ut non defíciat fides tua, et tu aliquándo convérsus confírma fratres tuos.

tuespetrusetsuperhancpetramedificabeccle.en: Thou art Peter * and upon this Rock I will build My Church.
tuespetrusetsuperhancpetramedificabeccle.la: Tu es Petrus, * et super hanc petram ædificábo Ecclésiam meam.

beatusessimonbarionaquianoncaretsanguisr.en: Blessed art thou, * Simon Bar-Jona, because flesh and blood hath not revealed it to thee, but my Father who is in heaven, saith the Lord.
beatusessimonbarionaquianoncaretsanguisr.la: Beátus es, * Simon Bar Jona, quia non caro et sanguis revelávit tibi, sed Pater meus, qui est in cœlis, dicit Dóminus.

commemoratioomniumssapostolorum.en: Commemoration of All the Holy Apostles

deusquinosperbeatosapostolostuosadagniti.en: O God, who hast granted us to come to the knowledge of thy name through thy blessed Apostles: * grant us both to celebrate their everlasting glory by advancing, § and to advance by celebrating it.
deusquinosperbeatosapostolostuosadagniti.la: Deus, qui nos per beátos Apóstolos tuos ad agnitiónem tui nóminis veníre tribuísti: * da nobis eórum glóriam sempitérnam et proficiéndo celebráre, § et celebrándo profícere.

magnificatanimameadominumetexsultavitspi.en: My soul doth magnify the Lord: and my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour.
magnificatanimameadominumetexsultavitspi.la: Magníficat ánima mea Dóminum: et exsultávit spíritus meus in Deo, salutári meo.

quiarespexithumilitatemancillesue.en: Because he hath regarded the humility of his handmaid.

ecceenimexhocbeatammedicentomnesgenerati.en: For, behold, from henceforth all generations shall call me blessed.
ecceenimexhocbeatammedicentomnesgenerati.la: Ecce enim ex hoc beátam me dicent omnes generatiónes.

visitatiotuadeigenitrixvirgo.en: Thy Visitation, * O Virgin Mother of God.

gaudiumannuntiavituniversomundo.en: Hath announced joy to the whole world.

oquantavisamorisillibatetuncmentemaccend.en: O how great a force * of love had then kindled the mind of the spotless Virgin, that, rapt in the Holy Ghost, she exulted: My soul doth magnify the Lord.
oquantavisamorisillibatetuncmentemaccend.la: O quanta vis * amóris illibátæ tunc mentem accénderat Vírginis, ut in Spíritu sancto rapta jubiláret: Magnificat ánima mea Dóminum.

omnipotenssempiternedeusquiexabundantiac.en: Almighty, everlasting God, who out of the abundance of thy charity didst inspire blessed Mary, when she was with child of thy Son, to go and greet Elizabeth: ↊ grant, we beseech thee, * that through her Visitation we may be filled with heavenly gifts, ↊ and delivered from all adversities.
omnipotenssempiternedeusquiexabundantiac.la: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, qui ex abundántia charitátis, beátam Maríam tuo Fílio fœcundátam ad salutatiónem Elísabeth inspirásti: ↊ præsta quæsumus; * ut per ejus Visitatiónem donis cœléstibus repleámur, ↊ et ab ómnibus adversitátibus eruámur.

endilectusmeusloquiturmihi.en: Behold, my beloved speaketh to me:

intraprecordiameadatvocemsuam.en: Within my heart he uttereth his voice.
intraprecordiameadatvocemsuam.la: Intra præcórdia mea dat vocem suam.

quamdulciafaucibusmeiseloquiatuadominesu.en: How sweet are thy words to my palate, O Lord! more than honey to my mouth.
quamdulciafaucibusmeiseloquiatuadominesu.la: Quam dúlcia fáucibus meis elóquia tua, Dómine, super mel ori meo.

iboadmontemmyrrhefestinanteretvideboverb.en: I will go in haste to the mountain of myrrh, and I will see this word,
iboadmontemmyrrhefestinanteretvideboverb.la: Ibo ad montem myrrhæ festinánter, et vidébo verbum hoc,

quodfactumestinauribusmeisabangelosaluta.en: Which was done in mine ears by the Angel greeting me.
quodfactumestinauribusmeisabangelosaluta.la: Quod factum est in áuribus meis ab Angelo salutánte.

viammandatorumtuorumcucurriiuxtaverbumtu.en: I have run the way of thy commandments, according to thy word.
viammandatorumtuorumcucurriiuxtaverbumtu.la: Viam mandatórum tuórum cucúrri, juxta verbum tuum.

voxturturisauditestsurgeproperaamicameet.en: The voice of the turtle is heard: arise, make haste, my love, and come, my dove, in the clefts of the rock, in the hollow places of the wall.
voxturturisauditestsurgeproperaamicameet.la: Vox túrturis audíta est, surge, própera, amíca mea, et veni, colúmba mea, in foramínibus petræ, in cavérna macériæ.

ostendemihifaciemtuamsonetvoxtuainauribu.en: Shew me thy face, let thy voice sound in my ears
ostendemihifaciemtuamsonetvoxtuainauribu.la: Osténde mihi fáciem tuam, sonet vox tua in áuribus meis.

voxenimtuadulcisetfaciestuadecora.en: For thy voice is sweet, and thy face comely.
voxenimtuadulcisetfaciestuadecora.la: Vox enim tua dulcis, et fácies tua decóra.

felicesmatressedetnatifeliciores.en: Happy the mothers, but happier still the sons:
felicesmatressedetnatifeliciores.la: Felíces matres, sed et nati felicióres:

etquegesserefeliciafactafuere.en: And happy were the deeds that they wrought.
etquegesserefeliciafactafuere.la: Et quæ géssere felícia facta fuére.

felixdomusfelixfamiliaquibussuntvisatotm.en: Happy the house, happy the household, by whom so many wonders were seen.
felixdomusfelixfamiliaquibussuntvisatotm.la: Felix domus, felix família, quibus sunt visa tot mirabília.

odiesomnivotorecolendaodiesomnistudioven.en: O day to be recalled with every vow! O day to be venerated with all devotion!
odiesomnivotorecolendaodiesomnistudioven.la: O dies omni voto recolénda! o dies omni stúdio veneránda!

inquatotmiserofulseruntgaudiamundo.en: In which so many joys shone forth upon the wretched world.
inquatotmiserofulseruntgaudiamundo.la: In qua tot mísero fulsérunt gáudia mundo.

hecdiesquamfecitdominusexultemusetletemu.en: This is the day which the Lord hath made: let us rejoice and be glad therein.
hecdiesquamfecitdominusexultemusetletemu.la: Hæc dies quam fecit Dóminus, exultémus et lætémur in ea.

opreclarastellamarisvirgomatersingularis.en: O bright star of the sea, Virgin Mother singular, who didst visit thy kinswoman, and didst enlighten John by thy most glorious offspring:
opreclarastellamarisvirgomatersingularis.la: O præclára stella maris, Virgo Mater singuláris, quæ cognátam visitásti, Joánnem illuminásti prole præclaríssima:

teprecamurinhocfestosissolamenomnimestof.en: Thee we pray on this feast, be thou the solace of every mourner, put death to flight, bestow on us a lot in the heavenly fatherland.
teprecamurinhocfestosissolamenomnimestof.la: Te præcámur in hoc festo, sis solámen omni mœsto, fuga mortem, confer sortem nobis in cœli pátria.

adteclamantomnesreilargadatrixsanctespei.en: To thee cry all the guilty, O bountiful giver of holy hope, O never-failing fountain.
adteclamantomnesreilargadatrixsanctespei.la: Ad te clamant omnes rei, larga datrix sanctæ spei, o fons indefíciens.

gaudemariamaterchristiquesingulariprivil.en: Rejoice, O Mary, * Mother of Christ, who by a singular privilege didst merit to bear Christ the Lord.
gaudemariamaterchristiquesingulariprivil.la: Gaude María * Mater Christi, quæ singulári privilégio meruísti portáre Christum Dóminum.

speciosasfiliascumulantesdivitias.en: The fair daughters that heaped up riches,

thesauroventrisgraviditranscenditmaterdo.en: The Mother of the Lord surpassed by the treasure of her fruitful womb.
thesauroventrisgraviditranscenditmaterdo.la: Thesáuro ventris grávidi transcéndit Mater Dómini.

exultetlaudahabitatiosionquiamagnusinmed.en: Rejoice, and praise, O thou habitation of Sion: for great is he that is in the midst of thee, the Holy One of Israel.
exultetlaudahabitatiosionquiamagnusinmed.la: Exúlta, et lauda, habitátio Sion, quia magnus in médio tui Sanctus Israël.

aitautemmariafecitmihimagnaquipotensest.en: And Mary said: He that is mighty hath done great things to me:
aitautemmariafecitmihimagnaquipotensest.la: Ait autem María: Fecit mihi magna qui potens est:

etmisericordieiusaprogenieinprogeniestim.en: And his mercy is on them that fear Him, from generation to generation.
etmisericordieiusaprogenieinprogeniestim.la: Et misericórdia ejus, a progénie in progénies timéntibus eum.

suscepitisrelpuerumsuumrecordatusmiseric.en: He hath received Israel his servant, being mindful of his mercy.
suscepitisrelpuerumsuumrecordatusmiseric.la: Suscépit Israël púerum suum, recordátus misericórdiæ suæ.

sicutlocutusestabrahametseminieiusinsecu.en: As he spoke to Abraham, and to his seed for ever.
sicutlocutusestabrahametseminieiusinsecu.la: Sicut locútus est Ábraham, et sémini ejus in sæcula.

iuravitdominusdavidveritatemdefructuvent.en: The Lord hath sworn truth to David: Of the fruit of thy womb I will set upon thy throne.
iuravitdominusdavidveritatemdefructuvent.la: Jurávit Dóminus David veritátem, de fructu ventris tui ponam super sedem tuam.

inmarievirginisuteroparatasedestuadeusas.en: In the womb of the Virgin Mary * was thy seat prepared, O God, from everlasting.
inmarievirginisuteroparatasedestuadeusas.la: In Maríæ * Vírginis útero paráta sedes tua, Deus, a sæculo.

iubiletdeoomnisterretcelestishierarchias.en: Let all the earth * shout with joy to God, and let the heavenly Hierarchy serve him.
iubiletdeoomnisterretcelestishierarchias.la: Júbilet Deo * omnis terra, et cœlestis Hierarchía sérviat ei.

fecitdominuspotentiaminbrachiosuodispers.en: The Lord hath shewed * might in his arm: he hath scattered the proud in the conceit of their heart.
fecitdominuspotentiaminbrachiosuodispers.la: Fecit Dóminus * poténtiam in bráchio suo, dispérsit supérbos mente cordis sui.

deposuitpotentesdesedeetexaltavithumiles.en: He hath put down the mighty * from their seat, and hath exalted the humble.
deposuitpotentesdesedeetexaltavithumiles.la: Depósuit poténtes * de sede, et exaltávit húmiles.

esurientesimplevitbonisetdivitesdimisiti.en: The hungry he hath filled with good things, * and the rich he hath sent empty away.
esurientesimplevitbonisetdivitesdimisiti.la: Esuriéntes implévit bonis * et dívites dimísit inánes.

ecceistevenitsaliensinmontibustransilien.en: Behold, he cometh leaping upon the mountains, § skipping over the hills: * my beloved is like a roe, or a young hart.
ecceistevenitsaliensinmontibustransilien.la: Ecce iste venit sáliens in móntibus, § transíliens colles: * símilis est diléctus meus cápreæ, hinnulóque cervórum.

benedictusdominusdeusisrelquiavisitavite.en: Blessed be * the Lord God of Israel, because he hath visited and wrought the redemption of his people, as he spoke by the mouth of his holy ones
benedictusdominusdeusisrelquiavisitavite.la: Benedíctus * Dóminus, Deus Israël, quia visitávit, et fecit redemptiónem plebis suæ, sicut locútus est per os sanctórum

surgeproperaamicameacolumbameaformosamee.en: Arise, make haste, my love, my dove, my beautiful one, and come. * For winter is now past, § the rain is over and gone. * The flowers have appeared in our land, § the time of pruning is come.
surgeproperaamicameacolumbameaformosamee.la: Surge, própera, amíca mea, colúmba mea, formósa mea, et veni. * Jam enim hiems tránsiit, § imber ábiit, et recéssit. * Flores apparuérunt in terra nostra, § tempus putatiónis advénit.

voxturturisauditestinterranostraficuspro.en: The voice of the turtle is heard in our land: § the fig tree hath put forth her green figs: * the vines in flower yield their sweet smell.
voxturturisauditestinterranostraficuspro.la: Vox túrturis audíta est in terra nostra: § ficus prótulit grossos suos: * víneæ floréntes dedérunt odórem suum.

magnificetdominumtotumgenusfideliumconcr.en: Let the whole race of the faithful * magnify the Lord; let the Angelic host resound with harmonious praise unto the joys of Mary.
magnificetdominumtotumgenusfideliumconcr.la: Magníficet * Dóminum totum genus fidélium, cóncrepet harmónica laude cohors Angélica in Maríæ gáudia.

fonshortorumputeusaquarumviventiumqueflu.en: The fountain of gardens: * the well of living waters, which run with a strong stream from Libanus.
fonshortorumputeusaquarumviventiumqueflu.la: Fons hortórum, * púteus aquárum vivéntium, quæ fluunt ímpetu de Líbano.

veniatdilectusmeusinhortumsuumetcomedatf.en: Let my beloved come * into his garden, and eat the fruit of his apple trees.
veniatdilectusmeusinhortumsuumetcomedatf.la: Véniat * diléctus meus in hortum suum, et cómedat fructum pomórum suórum.

veniinhortummeumsorormeasponsamessuimyrr.en: I am come * into my garden, O my sister, my spouse, I have gathered my myrrh with my aromatical spices.
veniinhortummeumsorormeasponsamessuimyrr.la: Veni * in hortum meum, soror mea sponsa, méssui myrrham meam cum aromátibus meis.

unestcolumbameaperfectameaunestmatrissue.en: One is my dove, my perfect one is but one, she is the only one of her mother, the chosen of her that bore her. The daughters saw her, and declared her most blessed: the queens and concubines, and they praised her. Who is she that cometh forth as the morning rising, fair as the moon, bright as the sun, terrible as an army set in array?
unestcolumbameaperfectameaunestmatrissue.la: Una est colúmba mea, perfécta mea, una est matris suæ, elécta genetríci suæ. Vidérunt eam fíliæ, et beatíssimam prædicavérunt; regínæ et concubínæ, et laudavérunt eam. Quæ est ista quæ progréditur quasi auróra consúrgens, pulchra ut luna, elécta ut sol, terríbilis ut castrórum ácies ordináta?

dignaremelaudaretevirgosacrata.en: Vouchsafe that I may praise thee, * O holy Virgin.
dignaremelaudaretevirgosacrata.la: Dignáre me laudáre te, * Virgo sacráta.

damihivirtutemcontrahostestuos.en: Give me strength against thine enemies.
damihivirtutemcontrahostestuos.la: Da mihi virtútem contra hostes tuos.

cuiusfestumcolimusipsavirgovirginuminter.en: May she whose feast we keep, § the Virgin of virgins herself, intercede for us with the Lord. §
cuiusfestumcolimusipsavirgovirginuminter.la: Cujus festum cólimus, § ipsa Virgo Vírginum intercédat pro nobis ad Dóminum. §

eugeniushuiusnoministertiusbernardusante.en: Eugene, the third of this name, formerly called Bernard, was a Pisan by birth. When his youth was ended, he enlisted in the clerical warfare, and, being afterwards ordained to the priesthood, for the excellent endowments of his mind he merited to be chosen among the Canons of the metropolitan church of Pisa. Drawn by the example of St. Bernard, who had then come to Pisa, he gave himself to him to be trained, and put on the monastic habit at Clairvaux. He so advanced under the discipline of so great a man, that he was first set over the Monastery of Farfa by him, and then elected Abbot of the Monastery of Saints Vincent and Anastasius at the Aquæ Salviæ by the Supreme Pontiff Innocent the Second. In discharging this office, when he had become renowned for the wonderful splendour of his holiness and prudence, after the death of Lucius the Second he was created Sovereign Pontiff by the Cardinals with all their votes. But scarcely had his Pontificate begun, when, as the tumults of rebels were striving to overthrow the sovereignty of the Roman Church, he was forced once and again to depart from the City; and the storm being afterwards calmed, he returned to it again with the highest honour and amid the rejoicing of the good.
eugeniushuiusnoministertiusbernardusante.la: Eugénius hujus nóminis tértius, Bernárdus ántea dictus, pátria Pisánus fuit. Exácta adolescéntia, clericáli milítiæ nomen dedit, et sacerdótio póstea initiátus, ob egrégias ánimi dotes inter Canónicos Metropolitánæ Pisánæ cooptári méruit. Sancti Bernárdi, qui tunc Pisas advénerat, exémplo illéctus, eidem sese instituéndum dedit, atque in Claraválle monásticum índuit hábitum. Tanti viri disciplína ádeo profécit, ut primum Farfénsi Monastério ab eo praepósitus, deínde Abbas Cœnóbii sanctórum Vincéntii et Anastásii ad Aquas Sálvias ab Innocéntio secúndo Summo Pontífice eléctus fúerit. Quo in obeúndo múnere, cum sanctimóniae ac prudéntiæ miro splendóre inclaruísset, a Cardinálibus post Lúcii secúndi óbitum, cunctis suffrágiis Póntifex Máximus creátus est. Vix autem ab ínito Pontificátu, perduéllium turbis Ecclésiæ Románæ principátum evértere adniténtibus semel atque íterum ab Urbe discédere cógitur, sedatáque deínde tempestáte, íterum ad eam, summo honóre, et bonórum gratulatióne regréditur.

viterbiicommoransanglielegatosscotiegerm.en: While staying at Viterbo, he received the Legates of England, Scotland, Germany, Spain and France, who professed obedience and homage to blessed Peter in his person; and likewise certain Bishops of Armenia, who moreover, in the name of their Metropolitan and of their nation, sought his judgment on the weightier affairs of the Eastern Church. Having set out for France, he held Councils at Rheims and at Trier, in which he condemned the errors of Eon and of Gilbert de la Porrée, and wisely established many other things for the discipline of the clergy and the liberty of the Church. He then visited the monasteries of Clairvaux and Cîteaux together with St. Bernard, leaving everywhere illustrious examples of holy life. From the same Bernard he sought wholesome counsels for governing the Church and protecting the rights of the Apostolic See; and Bernard gave him the precious book On Consideration, in which the prerogatives and duties of the Pontiff and Prince are set forth with heavenly wisdom. Being also an eminent cultivator of letters, he both reformed the studies of theology and of jurisprudence, and instituted the Academic degrees, as they are called, that he might render the minds of young men more eager.
viterbiicommoransanglielegatosscotiegerm.la: Vitérbii cómmorans, Angliæ Legátos, Scótiæ, Germániæ, Hispániæ et Gálliæ excépit, beáto Petro in ejus persóna obediéntiam et obséquium profiténtes: itémque nonnúllos Arméniæ Epíscopos, qui ínsuper Metropolitáni ac gentis suæ nómine, de gravióribus Orientális Ecclésiæ negótiis ejus exquisivérunt senténtiam. Proféctus in Gálliam, Concília Rhemis ac Tréviris celebrávit, in quibus Eónis et Gilbérti Porretáni proscrípsit erróres, aliáque plura sapiénter constítuit ad cleri disciplínam, et Ecclésiæ libertátem. Cœnóbia deínde Claravallénse ac Cisterciénse una cum sancto Bernárdo invísit, præcláris ubíque sanctæ conversatiónis exémplis relíctis. Ab eódem Bernárdo salutária mónita exquisívit ad Ecclésiam administrándam, et Apostólicæ Sedis jura protuénda; ille vero ei pretiósum librum de Consideratióne dedit, quo Pontíficis Principísque praerogatívae et offícia cœlésti sapiéntia declarántur. Litterárum quoque cultor exímius, cum Theologíæ ac jurisprudéntiæ reformávit stúdia, tum Académicos, uti vocant, gradus instítuit quo adolescéntium ánimos alacrióres rédderet.

singularipacisfovendecupiditatecurasomne.en: With a singular desire of fostering peace, he bent all his cares to settle the discords between the Pisans and the Lucchese. He greatly loved the beauty of the House of God: for he both adorned the Liberian Basilica with fairer ornament, and either restored very many other churches or enriched them with precious gifts: and to the Vatican Basilica he granted the fourth part of the offerings which by custom belonged to him, besides the tenth already assigned to the Prince of the Apostles by St. Leo the Ninth. He enrolled in the list of the Saints the Emperor Henry, a noble pattern of Catholic princes. At length at Tivoli, whither he had withdrawn from the City to avoid the summer heats, being seized with a grievous sickness, he met the death of the just on the eighth of the Ides of July, in the year one thousand one hundred and fifty-three, after he had sat in the Chair of Peter eight years and four months. His body was carried to Rome and buried in the Vatican, together with the remains of St. Gregory the Third and of blessed Peter the Levite. The sacred cult, moreover, paid to him even then, with the added lustre of miracles, and in other regions also, and flourishing up to these times, the Supreme Pontiff Pius the Ninth, on the advice of the Sacred Congregation of Rites, ratified and confirmed.
singularipacisfovendecupiditatecurasomne.la: Singulári pacis fovéndæ cupiditáte curas omnes inténdit ut discórdias Pisános inter et Lucénses compóneret. Decórem Domus Dei summópere diléxit: nam et Basílicam Liberiánam pulchrióri decorávit ornátu, et ália templa quamplúra aut refécit, aut pretiósis donis ditávit: Vaticánæ autem Basílicae quartam oblatiónum partem sibi de more competéntem, praeter décimam jam a sancto Leóne nono Apostolórum Príncipi attribútam, elargítus est. Henrícum imperatórem, Catholicórum príncipum nóbile exémplar, Sanctórum in album rétulit. Tandem Tíbure, quo aestívos calóres vitándi causa ab Urbe concésserat, gravi morbo implícitus, mortem justórum oppétiit octávo Idus Julii, anno millésimo centésimo quinquagésimo tértio, postquam in Petri Cáthedra sedísset annos octo, et menses quátuor. Corpus Romam delátum, cónditum fuit in Vaticáno, una cum sancti Gregórii tértii, et beáti Petri Levítæ exúviis. Sacrum porro cultum jam tunc miraculórum accedénte fulgóre, ei exhíbitum, et in áliis quoque regiónibus, ad hæc usque témpora vigéntem, Summus Póntifex Pius nonus, ex Sacrórum Rítuum Congregatiónis consúlto, ratum hábuit et confirmávit.

exepistolasanctibernardiabbatisadeugeniu.en: From the Letter of St. Bernard, Abbot, to Eugene the Third.
exepistolasanctibernardiabbatisadeugeniu.la: Ex Epístola sancti Bernárdi Abbátis ad Eugénium tértium.

queestaddominumpapameugeniumprima.en: Which is the first to the Lord Pope Eugene.
queestaddominumpapameugeniumprima.la: Quæ est ad Dominum Papam Eugenium prima.

loquaraddominummeumiamenimfiliumdicereno.en: I will speak to my lord. For I no longer dare to call thee son, because the son is changed into the father, the father into the son. He that cometh after me is preferred before me: but I envy not, for what was lacking to me I trust that I have in him, who came not only after me, but also through me. For, if thou deign to allow it, in a manner I have begotten thee through the Gospel. What then is our hope, and our joy, and crown of glory? Are not you, before God? In short, a wise son is the glory of his father. Henceforth, however, thou shalt not be called son, but thou shalt be called by a new name, which the mouth of the Lord hath named. This is the change of the right hand of the most High, and many shall rejoice in this change. For as of old Abram was changed into Abraham, Jacob into Israel, and, to set before thee rather some of thine own predecessors, as Simon into Cephas, Saul into Paul: so my son Bernard hath been advanced into my Father Eugene, by a change wholly joyful and, as we hope, profitable. This is the finger of God, raising up the needy from the dust, and lifting up the poor out of the dunghill, that he may sit with princes, and hold the throne of glory. It remaineth that, this change of thee being made, she also who hath been committed to thee, the Bride of thy Lord, may be changed for the better, and be henceforth no more called Sarai, but Sara. Understand what I say: for the Lord will give thee understanding.
loquaraddominummeumiamenimfiliumdicereno.la: Loquar ad Dóminum meum. Jam enim fílium dícere non áudeo, quia fílius in patrem, pater mutátus est in fílium. Qui post me venit, ante me factus est: sed non invídeo, quia quod mihi déerat, in eo me habére confido, qui non solum post me, sed étiam per me venit. Nam si dignáris, quodámmodo per Evangélium ego te génui. Quæ est ergo spes nostra, et gáudium nostrum, et coróna glóriæ? Nonne vos ante Deum? Dénique fílius sápiens glória est patris. Amodo tamen non vocáberis fílius, sed vocábitur tibi nomen novum, quod os Dómini nominávit. Hæc est mutátio déxteræ Excélsi, et multi in mutatióne ista gaudébunt. Nam, quemádmodum olim Abram in Abraham, Jacob in Israël, et, ut de tuis magis prædecessóribus tibi propónam, sicut Simon in Cepham, Saulus in Paulum: sic fílius meus Bernárdus in Patrem meum Eugénium, læta prorsus et útili, ut sperámus, translatióne promótus est. Dígitus Dei est iste, súscitans de púlvere egénum, et de stércore érigens páuperem, ut sédeat cum princípibus, et sólium glóriæ téneat. Súperest, ut facta hac mutatióne tui, ipsa quoque quæ tibi commíssa est, Dómini tui Sponsa mutétur in mélius, et jam nequáquam Sárai, sed Sara de cétero nominétur. Intéllige quæ dico: dabit enim tibi Dóminus intelléctum.

daquesumusomnipotensdeusbeatieugeniiconf.en: Grant, we beseech thee, almighty God, by the intercession of blessed Eugene, thy Confessor and Bishop, that we may serve thee with our whole heart; * for no hostility shall prevail against us, § if we truly trust in thee.
daquesumusomnipotensdeusbeatieugeniiconf.la: Da, quæsumus, omnípotens Deus, beáti Eugénii, Confessóris tui atque Pontíficis intercessióne, ut toto tibi corde famulémur; * quia nulla nobis prævalébit hostílitas, § si in te veráciter confidámus.

deusquinosconspicisexnostrainfirmitatede.en: O God, who seest that we fail through our own weakness: § be favourably present; * and through the intercession of blessed Theobald, Abbot, in all our actions both go before us by thine inspiration, and keep us by thy help; § that every prayer and work of ours may always begin from thee, and through thee be ended. *
deusquinosconspicisexnostrainfirmitatede.la: Deus, qui nos cónspicis ex nostra infirmitáte defícere: § adésto propítius; * atque intercedénte beáto Theobáldo, Abbáte, in ómnibus actiónibus nostris et aspirándo nos prævéni, et adjuvándo custódi; § ut cuncta nostra orátio et operátio a te semper incípiat, et per te cœpta finiátur. *

veniatdilectusmeusinhortumsuumetcomedatf.en: Let my beloved come into his garden, and eat the fruit of his apple trees. I am come into my garden, O my sister, my spouse, I have gathered my myrrh, with my aromatical spices: I have eaten the honeycomb with my honey, I have drunk my wine with my milk: eat, O friends, and drink, and be inebriated, my dearly beloved.
veniatdilectusmeusinhortumsuumetcomedatf.la: Véniat diléctus meus in hortum suum, et cómedat fructum pomórum suórum. Veni in hortum meum soror mea sponsa, méssui myrrham meam cum aromátibus meis: comédi favum cum melle mea, bibi vinum meum cum lacte meo: comédite amici, et bibite, et inebriámini charíssimi.

egodormietcormeumvigilatvoxdilectimeipul.en: I sleep, and my heart watcheth: the voice of my beloved knocking: Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled. I arose up to open to my beloved: my hands dropped with myrrh, and my fingers were full of the choicest myrrh. I opened the bolt of my door to my beloved: but he had turned aside, and was gone.
egodormietcormeumvigilatvoxdilectimeipul.la: Ego dórmio, et cor meum vígilat: vox dilécti mei pulsántis: Aperi mihi soror mea, amíca mea, colúmba mea, immaculáta mea. Surréxi, ut aperírem dilécto meo: manus meæ stillavérunt myrrham, et dígiti mei pleni myrrha probatíssima. Péssulum óstii mei apérui dilécto meo: at ille declináverat, atque transíerat.

animamealiquefactestutlocutusestquesivie.en: My soul melted when he spoke: I sought him, and found him not: I called, and he did not answer me. The keepers that go about the city found me: they struck me, and wounded me: the keepers of the walls took away my veil from me. I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, if you find my beloved, that you tell him that I languish with love.
animamealiquefactestutlocutusestquesivie.la: Anima mea liquefácta est, ut locútus est: quæsívi, et non invéni illum: vocávi, et non respóndit mihi. Invenérunt me custódes qui circúmeunt civitátem: percussérunt me, et vulneravérunt me: tulérunt pállium meum mihi custódes murórum. Adjúro vos fíliæ Jerúsalem, si invenéritis diléctum meum, ut nuntiétis ei quia amóre lángueo.

qualisestdilectustuusexdilectoopulcherri.en: What manner of one is thy beloved of the beloved, O thou most beautiful among women? what manner of one is thy beloved of the beloved, that thou hast so adjured us? My beloved is white and ruddy, chosen out of thousands. His head is as the finest gold: his locks as branches of palm trees, black as a raven. His eyes as doves upon brooks of waters, which are washed with milk, and sit beside the plentiful streams.
qualisestdilectustuusexdilectoopulcherri.la: Qualis est diléctus tuus ex dilécto, o pulchérrima mulíerum? qualis est diléctus tuus ex dilécto, quia sic adjurásti nos? Diléctus meus cándidus et rubicúndus, eléctus ex míllibus. Caput ejus aurum óptimum: Comæ ejus sicut elátæ palmárum, nigræ quasi corvus. Oculi ejus sicut colúmbæ super rívulos aquárum, quæ lacte sunt lotæ, et résident juxta fluénta pleníssima.

deverbisapoccsignummagnum.en: On the words of Apoc. chap. 12: A great sign.
deverbisapoccsignummagnum.la: De verbis Apoc. c. 12. Signum magnum.

vehementerquidemnobisdilectissimivirunus.en: Exceedingly indeed, dearly beloved, did one man and one woman harm us: but, thanks be to God, by one man likewise and one woman all things are restored; and that not without a great increase of graces. For not as the offence, so also the gift; but the greatness of the benefit exceedeth the reckoning of the loss. Thus truly the most wise and most merciful craftsman did not break what had been bruised, but remade it altogether more profitably, namely that he might form for us a new Adam out of the old, and transfuse Eve into Mary.
vehementerquidemnobisdilectissimivirunus.la: Veheménter quidem nobis, dilectíssimi, vir unus et múlier una nocuére: sed, grátias Deo, per unum nihilóminus virum et mulíerem unam ómnia restaurántur; nec sine magno fœnore gratiárum. Neque enim sicut delíctum, ita et donum; sed excédit damni æstimatiónem benefícii magnitúdo. Sic nimírum prudentíssimus et clementíssimus ártifex, quod quassátum fúerat, non confrégit, sed utílius omníno refécit, ut vidélicet nobis novum formáret Adam ex véteri, et Hevam transfúnderet in Maríam.

etquidemsufficerepoteratchristussiquidem.en: And indeed Christ could have sufficed: since even now all our sufficiency is from him: but it was not good for us that man should be alone. It was more fitting that both sexes should be present at our restoration, as neither had been absent from our corruption. Now therefore not even that woman, blessed among women, shall be seen idle: a place indeed shall be found for her in this reconciliation. For there is need of a mediator to that Mediator, nor is any other more profitable to us than Mary.
etquidemsufficerepoteratchristussiquidem.la: Et quidem suffícere póterat Christus: síquidem et nunc omnis sufficiéntia nostra ex eo est: sed nobis bonum non erat esse hóminem solum. Cóngruum magis, ut adésset nostræ reparatióni sexus utérque, quorum corruptióni neuter defuísset. Jam ítaque nec ipsa múlier benedícta in muliéribus vidébitur otiósa: inveniétur équidem locus ejus in hac reconciliatióne. Opus est enim mediatóre ad Mediatórem istum, nec alter nobis utílior, quam Maria.

amplectamurmarievestigiafratresmeietdevo.en: Let us embrace the footsteps of Mary, my brethren, and with most devout supplication cast ourselves down at her blessed feet. Let us hold her, and not let her go until she hath blessed us: for she is mighty. For she is the fleece placed between the dew and the floor, the woman between the sun and the moon, Mary placed between Christ and the Church.
amplectamurmarievestigiafratresmeietdevo.la: Amplectámur Maríæ vestígia, fratres mei, et devotíssima supplicatióne beátis illíus pédibus provolvámur. Teneámus eam, nec dimittámus donec benedíxerit nobis: potens est enim. Nempe vellus est médium inter rorem et áream, múlier inter solem et lunam, María inter Christum et Ecclésiam constitúta.

sedfortemirarisnontamvellusopertumrorequ.en: But perhaps thou marvellest not so much at the fleece covered with dew, as at the woman clothed with the sun. Great indeed is the familiarity, but altogether wondrous the nearness of the sun and the woman. For how doth so frail a nature subsist in so vehement a heat? Rightly indeed dost thou marvel, holy Moses, and desirest more curiously to behold it. Nevertheless put off the shoes from thy feet, and lay aside the wrappings of carnal thoughts, if thou desirest to draw near.
sedfortemirarisnontamvellusopertumrorequ.la: Sed forte miráris non tam vellus opértum rore, quam amíctam sole mulíerem. Magna síquidem familiáritas, sed mira omníno vicínitas solis et mulíeris. Quómodo enim in tam veheménti fervóre tam frágilis natúra subsístit? Mérito quidem admiráris, Moyses sancte, et curiósius desíderas intuéri. Verúmtamen solve calceaménta de pédibus tuis, et involúcra pone carnálium cogitatiónum, si accédere concupíscis.

inillotemporeexurgensmariaabiitinmontana.en: At that time: Mary rising up went into the hill country with haste into a city of Juda: and she entered into the house of Zacharias, and saluted Elizabeth. And so on.
inillotemporeexurgensmariaabiitinmontana.la: In illo témpore: Exúrgens, María ábiit in montána cum festinatióne, in civitátem Juda: et intrávit in domum Zacharíæ, et salutávit Elísabeth. Et réliqua.

sermoinvisitvirgmarie.en: Sermon on the Visitation of the Virgin Mary.

lectiosanctievangeliiquamaudivimusfratre.en: The lesson of the holy Gospel which we have heard, dearest brethren, both proclaimeth to us the ever venerable beginnings of our redemption, and commendeth to us the ever wholesome remedies of humility to be imitated. For since the human race, stricken by the plague of pride, had perished, it was fitting that the first times of salvation, as soon as it began, should hold forth the medicine of humility whereby it might be healed: and since through the rashness of a woman led astray death had entered into the world, it was fitting that, in token of life returning, women should go before one another in the services of devout humility and godliness.
lectiosanctievangeliiquamaudivimusfratre.la: Léctio sancti Evangélii, quam audívimus, fratres charíssimi, et redemptiónis nostræ nobis semper veneránda primórdia prædicat, et salutária semper humilitátis imitándæ remédia comméndat. Nam quia peste supérbiæ attáctum genus humánum períerat, decébat, ut medicaméntum humilitátis, quo sanarétur, prima mox incipiéntis salútis témpora præténderent: et quia per temeritátem sedúctæ mulieris mors in mundum introíerat, cóngruum fúerat, ut in indícium vitæ reverténtis, mulíeres se devótæ humilitátis ínvicem ac pietátis prævenírent obséquiis.

priorergonobisbeatadeigenitrixadsublimit.en: First therefore the blessed Mother of God sheweth us the way of humility to the height of the heavenly fatherland: venerable by her example no less of religion than of chastity. For the glory of her virginal and undefiled body intimateth what manner of life is that of the city above, for which we sigh, where they shall neither marry nor be married, but are as the Angels of God in heaven: and it pointeth out the excellent virtue of mind whereby we ought to attain thereto.
priorergonobisbeatadeigenitrixadsublimit.la: Prior ergo nobis beáta Dei Génitrix ad sublimitátem pátriæ cœléstis iter osténdit humilitátis: non minus religiónis, quam castitátis exémplo venerábilis. Síquidem glória virgínei et intemeráti córporis, qualis sit vita supérnæ civitátis, ad quam suspirámus, insínuat, ubi neque nubent, neque nubéntur, sed sunt sicut Angeli Dei in cœlis: atque virtútem mentis exímiam, qua ad hanc pertíngere debeámus, índicat.

namquesicutexprecedentesanctievangeliile.en: For (as we have learned from the preceding lesson of the holy Gospel), after she had merited to be exalted by the vision and address of the Angel, after she learned that she was to be laden with a heavenly offspring, she in no wise exalted herself because of the heavenly gifts, as though they were from herself: but, that she might be ever more and more fit for the divine gifts, she fixed the step of her mind in the keeping of humility, thus answering the Archangel who brought her the good tidings: Behold the handmaid of the Lord: be it done to me according to thy word.
namquesicutexprecedentesanctievangeliile.la: Namque, (sicut ex præcedénte sancti Evangélii lectióne cognóvimus) postquam Angélica visióne, et allocutióne méruit sublimári, postquam se cœlésti onustándam partu dídicit, nequáquam se de donis cœléstibus, quasi a se hæc essent, éxtulit: sed ut magis magísque donis esset apta divínis, in custódia humilitátis gressum mentis fixit, ita evangelizánti sibi Archángelo, respóndens: Ecce ancílla Dómini: fiat mihi secúndum verbum tuum.

utverexhodiernalectioneaudivimuseamdemqu.en: But as we have heard from today's lesson, the same humility which she had shown to the Angel she took care to show to men also: and, what is of greater virtue, even to lesser ones. For who knoweth not that a virgin consecrated to God holdeth a higher rank than a woman devoted to God? Who doubteth that the Mother of the eternal King is by right to be preferred to the mother of a soldier? Yet she, mindful of the Scripture which enjoineth, The greater thou art, humble thyself in all things, as soon as the Angel who spoke to her had returned to heaven, ariseth and goeth up into the hill country; and bearing God in her womb, she seeketh the dwelling of the servants of God, and requireth their converse.
utverexhodiernalectioneaudivimuseamdemqu.la: Ut vero ex hodiérna lectióne audívimus: eámdem, quam Angelo exhibúerat humilitátem, homínibus quoque curávit exhibére: et quod majóris est virtútis, hoc étiam minóribus. Quis enim nésciat, vírginem Deo consecrátam, mulíere Deo dédita gradum habére potiórem? Quis dúbitet Matrem Regis ætérni, jure matri mílitis præferéndam? Attamen ipsa memor Scriptúræ præcipiéntis, quanto magnus es, te in ómnibus humília, mox ut Angelus, qui loquebátur ei, ad cœléstia rédiit, surgit ac montána conscéndit; gestánsque in útero Deum, servórum Dei habitácula petit ac requírit allóquia.

ioannesgualbertusflorentienatusmiraculoc.en: John Gualbert, born at Florence, was converted by the miracle of the Crucifix bowing its head to him, and against his father's will he cut off his hair and put on the monastic habit. Being elected Abbot, he set out to Romuald, a dweller in the hermitage of Camaldoli, from whom he received a prophecy of his own institute (which a little later he founded at Vallombrosa); and with very many whom he took as companions he fought, not without hardships, against the depravity of heresy and simony.
ioannesgualbertusflorentienatusmiraculoc.la: Joánnes Gualbértus Floréntiæ natus miráculo Crucifíxi sibi caput inclinántis convértitur, ac invíto patre sibi comam totóndit, et hábitum monásticum índuit. Eléctus in Abbátem ad Camaldulénsis erémi íncolam Romuáldum proficíscitur, a quo sui institúti‚ (quod paulo post apud Vallem Umbrósam fundat) vaticínium áccipit; et cum plúrimis, quos in sócios adscívit, hæréticam et simoníacam pravitátem non sine incómmodis, oppugnávit.

multafundituserexitmonasteriapluraqueins.en: He raised many monasteries from the foundations, and strengthened very many, when restored, with holy laws. He was the father of the needy, the ruler of the elements, and the terror of demons. At length, worn out by abstinences, vigils, prayers and old age, thirsting for God, having exhorted his brethren, having professed the faith, and having been vouchsafed for three days the service of Angels, being almost eighty years old he passed to the Lord, in the year one thousand and seventy-three, on the fourth of the Ides of July.
multafundituserexitmonasteriapluraqueins.la: Multa fúnditus eréxit Monastéria, plúraque instauráta sanctis légibus communívit. Egenórum pater, elementórum rector, et dæmonum terror éxtitit. Demum abstinéntiis‚ vigíliis, oratiónibus et sénio conféctus, Deum sítiens, fratres cohortátus, proféssus fide, triduáno Angelórum dignátus obséquio, fere octogenárius migrávit ad Dóminum, anno millésimo septuagésimo tértio, quarto Idus Júlii.

bonaventurabalneoregiiinetrurianatusinfa.en: Bonaventure, born at Bagnorea in Etruria, was dedicated as an infant, by his mother's vow, to the religious order of blessed Francis. And so as a young man he wished to be enrolled in the Order of Friars Minor: where, under Alexander of Hales as his master, he soon came to the highest perfection of learning. Whence in the seventh year after, he publicly expounded the books of the Sentences at Paris with the highest praise: which he also afterwards illustrated with excellent commentaries. After six years, being made Minister General of his Order at Rome, he discharged the office with such praise of prudence and holiness, that he was in the mouth and admiration of all.
bonaventurabalneoregiiinetrurianatusinfa.la: Bonaventúra, Balneorégii in Etrúria natus infans ex matris voto religióni beáti Francísci dicátur. Itaque adoléscens in Ordinem Fratrum Minórum adscríbi vóluit: ubi Alexandro de Ales magístro‚ ad summam doctrínæ perfectiónem brevi pervénit. Unde séptimo post anno libros Sententiárum Parísiis públice summa cum laude est interpretátus: quos étiam præcláris póstea commentáriis illustrávit. Post sex annos, sui Ordinis Generális Miníster Romæ factus, ea prudéntiæ ac sanctitátis laude ministérium gessit, ut in ómnium ore et admiratióne esset.

multascripsitinquibussummameruditionemcu.en: He wrote many things, in which, joining the highest learning with an equal ardour of piety, he moveth the reader while he teacheth him. Gregory the Tenth, moved by the fame of his holiness and wisdom, created him Cardinal and Bishop of Albano. While he was yet living, blessed Thomas Aquinas called him a saint. For when he had found him writing the life of St. Francis, he said: Let us leave a saint to labour for a saint. He departed this life on the day before the Ides of July, at the Council of Lyons, being fifty-three years of age, after many miracles had been wrought. Sixtus the Fourth enrolled him in the number of the Saints.
multascripsitinquibussummameruditionemcu.la: Multa scripsit in quibus summam eruditiónem cum pari pietátis ardóre conjúngens, lectórem docéndo movet. Quem Gregórius décimus, ejus sanctimóniæ et sapiéntiæ fama commótus, cardinálem et Epíscopum Albanénsem creávit. Eumdem adhuc vivéntem beátus Thomas Aquínas sanctum appellávit. Cum enim vitam sancti Francísci scribéntem comperísset: Sinámus, inquit, sanctum pro sancto laboráre. Migrávit e vita prídie Idus Júlii, in Concílio Lugdunénsi, quinquagínta tres annos natus, multis éditis miráculis. Quem Xystus quartus rétulit in Sanctórum númerum.

magnificaviteuminconspecturegum.en: He glorified him in the sight of kings,

etdeditillicoronamglorie.en: And gave him a crown of glory.

statuitillitestamentumsempiternumetbeati.en: He made an everlasting covenant with him, and blessed him.
statuitillitestamentumsempiternumetbeati.la: Státuit illi testaméntum sempitérnum, et beatificávit illum.

serveboneetfidelisquiasuperpaucafuistifi.en: Good * and faithful servant, because thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will place thee over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy Lord.
serveboneetfidelisquiasuperpaucafuistifi.la: Serve bone, * et fidélis, quia super pauca fuísti fidélis, supra multa te constítuam, intra in gáudium Dómini tui.

obeativiristephanisanctapreconiaoinestim.en: O holy praises of the blessed man Stephen, O inestimable love of charity!
obeativiristephanisanctapreconiaoinestim.la: O beáti viri Stéphani sancta præcónia, o inæstimábilis diléctio charitátis!

orapronobisbeatepaterstephane.en: Pray for us, O blessed Father Stephen.
orapronobisbeatepaterstephane.la: Ora pro nobis, beáte Pater Stéphane.

excitadomineinecclesiatuaspiritumcuibeat.en: Stir up, O Lord, in thy Church the Spirit which blessed Stephen, Abbot, served: * that we, being filled with the same, may strive to love what he loved, § and to practise in deed what he taught.
excitadomineinecclesiatuaspiritumcuibeat.la: Excita, Dómine, in Ecclésia tua Spíritum, cui beátus Stéphanus, Abbas, servívit: * ut, eódem nos repléti, studeámus amáre quod amávit, § et ópere exercére quod dócuit.

stephanuscognomentohardingusgenerenobili.en: Stephen, surnamed Harding, noble by birth, English by nation, put on the regular habit as a youth in the monastery of Sherborne. He crossed over to Scotland for the sake of study, and soon to Paris in France: where, being thoroughly instructed in humane letters and the sacred disciplines, he set out for Rome, taking a cleric as his companion, with whom each day he sang the whole psalter. Having visited the sacred thresholds, they were returning joyfully to France, when lo, the new solitude of Molesme drew Stephen, wherein he joined himself as companion to the blessed fathers Robert and Alberic.
stephanuscognomentohardingusgenerenobili.la: Stéphanus cognoménto Hardíngus, génere nóbilis, natióne Anglus, adoléscens in Schirburnénsi Monastério hábitum índuit regulárem.
