In Scótiam‚ studiórum causa, mox in Gálliam Parísios transfretávit: ubi humanióribus lítteris, et sacris disciplínis ápprime instrúctus, Romam proficíscitur‚ clérico sócio sibi adjúncto‚ cum quo síngulis diébus psaltérium ex íntegro decantábat. Sacris limínibus visitátis‚ Gállias læti repetébant‚ cum ecce nova Molísmi solitúdo Stéphanum alléxit, in qua se beátis pátribus Robérto et Alberíco cómitem adjúnxit.

inpartemcureassumptusetdeformatamposteai.en: Being taken into a share of the government, and afterwards grieving at the discipline which had become deformed at Molesme, he so wrought that, when the word of renewing the religious life had been raised, he himself, first among the first, laboured with most fervent zeal, and insisted by all means that the place and Order of Cîteaux should be established: wherefore, with the approval of Hugh, Archbishop of Lyons, then Legate of the Apostolic See, he built the New Monastery together with his companions, where he was made first Subprior under St. Robert the first Abbot, then Prior under Alberic, and at length, when Alberic was taken from among the living, he was put in his place by the votes of all.
inpartemcureassumptusetdeformatamposteai.la: In partem curæ assúmptus, et deformátam póstea in Molísmo disciplínam cóndolens, tantum effécit, ut cum verbum innovándæ religiónis motum fuísset, ipse primus inter primos ferventíssimo stúdio laboráverit, ac modis ómnibus instíterit‚ ut locus et Ordo Cisterciénsis instituerétur: quod approbante Hugóne Lugdunénsi Archiepiscopo Apostólicæ Sedis tunc Legáto, novum Monastérium una cum sóciis ædificávit‚ ubi primum sub sancto Robérto primo Abbáte Súpprior, mox sub Alberíco Prior efféctus, ipsi demum e vivis subláto, ómnium cálculis sufféctus est.

divinooperipersolvendovirilledeitalemadh.en: That man of God brought such reverence to the performance of the divine work, that when about to enter the oratory he laid aside his thoughts at the door: he so cultivated regular observance, that he banished the courts of princes from the monastery: he so loved poverty, that he charged those after him to observe slenderness even in the furnishings of the church. Saddened at the death of his sons, with no offspring apparent, he soon learned, by the apparition of one of the brethren lately deceased, and by the coming of St. Bernard and his companions, the Lord revealing it, that the fruitfulness of his Order would be wonderful.
divinooperipersolvendovirilledeitalemadh.la: Divíno óperi persolvéndo vir ille Dei talem adhibébat reveréntiam, ut cogitatiónes suas oratórium ingressúrus, depóneret ad óstium: regulárem observántiam ádeo excolébat‚ ut cúrias príncipum a cœnóbio relegáret: paupertátem ita diligébat, ut ipsíus étiam Ecclesiásticæ suppelléctilis tenuitátem observándam pósteris demandáret. De filiórum morte, sine apparénti prole contristátus, mox per apparitiónem unius e frátribus nuper defúncti, ét per advéntum sancti Bernárdi sociorúmque ejus, miram Ordinis sui fœcunditátem Dómino revelánte futúram agnóvit.

multiplicatamitaquegentemsuamconspiciens.en: Beholding therefore his people multiplied, and at the same time gathering it together in the Lord, he strove to conform all its monasteries to like laws and statutes, and for this reason he composed, with the counsel of his brethren, the Charter of Charity, confirmed by Callistus the Second and praised by the Supreme Pontiffs his successors. Being most devoted to the Virgin Mother of God, he committed this new plantation to her singular patronage: and, worn out with old age, weighed down by sicknesses and labours, he gave up the government, taking care that Raynard should be put in his place, Guy having been removed. At length, full of merits and humble in spirit, he passed to the Lord on the fifth of the Kalends of April in the year one thousand one hundred and thirty-four, and his body was solemnly laid by the neighbouring Abbots beside the tomb of his predecessor Alberic.
multiplicatamitaquegentemsuamconspiciens.la: Multiplicátam ítaque gentem suam conspíciens, eamque simul in Dómino cólligens‚ ómnia illíus Monastéria légibus statutísque simílibus stúduit conformáre, ob idque Chartam charitátis a Callísto secúndo confirmátam, et a successóribus Summis Pontificibus collaudátam‚ cum consílio fratrum suórum compósuit. Vírgini Deíparæ summe devótus, novéllam hanc plantatiónem ipsíus addíxit clientélæ singulári: et sénio conféctus, morbis et labóribus prægravátus, cessit præfectúræ, Rainárdum sibi substítui curans, amóto Uvidóne. Tandem méritis plenus, et húmilis spíritu migrávit ad Dóminum quinto Kaléndas Aprílis anni millésimi centésimi trigésimi quarti, ejúsque corpus juxta prædecessóris Alberíci sepultúram solémniter a vicínis Abbátibus appósitum fuit.

collaudabuntmultisapientiameiusetusquein.en: Many shall praise * his wisdom, and it shall never be forgotten.
collaudabuntmultisapientiameiusetusquein.la: Collaudábunt multi * sapiéntiam ejus, et usque in sæculum non delébitur.

cognoviteumdominusinbenedictionibussuise.en: The Lord knew him * in his blessings, and he found grace in the sight of the Lord.
cognoviteumdominusinbenedictionibussuise.la: Cognóvit eum Dóminus * in benedictiónibus suis, et invénit grátiam coram óculis Dómini.

iustuscorsuumtradetadvigilandumdiluculoa.en: The just man * will give his heart to resort early to the Lord that made him, and he will pray in the sight of the most High.
iustuscorsuumtradetadvigilandumdiluculoa.la: Justus * cor suum tradet ad vigilándum dilúculo ad Dóminum, qui fecit illum, et in conspéctu Altíssimi deprecábitur.

inillotemporeloquenteiesuadturbasextolle.en: At that time, as Jesus spoke unto the multitudes, a certain woman of the company lifted up her voice and said unto Him: Blessed is the womb that bore thee. And so on.
inillotemporeloquenteiesuadturbasextolle.la: In illo témpore: Loquénte Jesu ad turbas; extóllens vocem quædam múlier de turba, dixit illi: Beátus venter, qui te portávit. Et réliqua.

sermdeassumptbmv.en: Sermon 4 on the Assumption of the B.V.M.
sermdeassumptbmv.la: Serm. 4. de Assumpt. B. M. V.

quenampoteritlinguetiamsiangelicasitdign.en: What tongue, even though it be Angelic, will be able to extol with worthy praises the Virgin Mother; and the mother not of any one whatsoever, but of God? A twofold novelty, a twofold prerogative: a twofold miracle, but befitting most worthily and aptly. For neither did another son befit a virgin, nor another birth befit God. For see how manifestly the canticle of our Virgin and the nuptial song accord together: since, indeed, her womb was the bridegroom's chamber. Hear Mary in the Gospel: He hath regarded, she saith, the humility of his handmaid. Hear the same in the marriage song: While the king was at his repose, she saith, my spikenard sent forth the odour thereof. For spikenard is a lowly herb, and cleanseth the breast: that it may be manifest that humility is signified by the name of spikenard, whose fragrance and beauty found grace with God.
quenampoteritlinguetiamsiangelicasitdign.la: Quaenam póterit lingua, etiámsi Angélica sit, dignis extóllere láudibus Vírginem Matrem; matrem autem non cujuscúmque, sed Dei? Duplex nóvitas‚ duplex prærogatíva: duplex miráculum, sed digne prorsus aptissiméque convéniens. Neque enim fílius álius vírginem‚ nec Deum décuit partus alter. Vide enim quam maniféste sibi cóncinant Vírginis nostræ cánticum‚ et nuptiále carmen: nimírum, cujus úterus, sponsi thálamus fuit. Audi Maríam in Evangélio: Respéxit, inquit, humilitátem ancíllæ suæ. Audi eámdem in epithalámio: Cum esset Rex, inquit, in accúbitu suo, nardus mea dedit odórem suum. Nardus quippe herba húmilis est, et pectus purgat: ut maniféstum sit, humilitátem nardi nómine designári, cujus odor et decor invénerit grátiam apud Deum.

sileatmisericordiamtuamvirgobeatasiquise.en: Let him be silent about thy mercy, O blessed Virgin, if there be any who remembereth that thou, when invoked in his necessities, didst fail him. We thy little servants rejoice with thee indeed in thy other virtues, but in this one rather with ourselves. We praise thy virginity, we wonder at thy humility: but mercy tasteth sweeter to the wretched; we embrace mercy more dearly, remember it more often, invoke it more frequently. For this it is that obtained the restoration of the whole world, and won the salvation of all. For it is manifest that she was solicitous for the whole human race, to whom it was said: Fear not, Mary, thou hast found grace, namely that which thou soughtest. Who then, O Blessed one, can search out the length and breadth, the height and depth of thy mercy?
sileatmisericordiamtuamvirgobeatasiquise.la: Síleat misericórdiam tuam, Virgo beáta‚ si quis est, qui invocátam te in necessitátibus suis sibi memínerit defuísse. Nos quidem sérvuli tui céteris in virtútibus congaudémus tibi, sed in hac pótius nobis ipsis. Laudámus virginitátem, humilitátem mirámur: sed misericórdia míseris sapit dúlcius, misericórdiam ampléctimur chárius‚ recordámur sæpius, crébrius invocámus. Hæc est enim quæ totíus mundi reparatiónem obtínuit, salútem ómnium impetrávit. Constat enim pro univérso génere humáno fuísse sollícitam, cui dictum est: Ne tímeas María, invenísti grátiam, útique quam quærébas. Quis ergo misericórdiæ tuæ, o Benedícta, longitúdinem et latitúdinem, sublimitátem et profúndum queat investigáre?

longitudomisericordieeiususqueindiemnovi.en: The length of her mercy succoureth all who call upon her even to the last day. Its breadth filleth the whole world, so that the whole earth also is full of thy mercy. So also its height hath found the restoration of the city above, and its depth hath obtained redemption for them that sit in darkness and in the shadow of death. For through thee heaven hath been filled, hell emptied, the ruins of the heavenly Jerusalem restored, and lost life given to the wretched who awaited it. Thus most mighty and most loving charity aboundeth both in the affection of compassion and in the effect of succour, equally rich in both. To this fountain therefore let our thirsting soul hasten: to this heap of mercy let our misery have recourse with all solicitude.
longitudomisericordieeiususqueindiemnovi.la: Longitúdo misericórdiæ ejus usque in diem novíssimum invocántibus eam súbvenit univérsis. Latitúdo ejus replet orbem terrárum, ut tua quoque misericórdia plena sit omnis terra. Sic et sublímitas ejus civitátis supérnæ invénit restauratiónem, et profúndum ejus sedéntibus in ténebris et in umbra mortis obtínuit redemptiónem. Per te enim cœlum replétum, inférnus evacuátus est, instaurátæ ruínæ cœléstis Jerúsalem, expectántibus míseris vita pérdita data. Sic potentíssima et piíssima cháritas et afféctu compatiéndi, et subveniéndi abúndat efféctu, æque lócuples in utróque. Ad hunc ígitur fontem sitibúnda próperet ánima nostra: ad hunc misericórdiæ cúmulum tota sollicitúdine miséria nostra recúrrat.

serminnativbmv.en: Sermon on the Nativity of the B.V.M.
serminnativbmv.la: Serm. in Nativ. B. M. V.

sedquiddeeiussupereminentialoquarcuienim.en: But what shall I say of her pre-eminence? For to which of the Angels hath it been said at any time: The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the most High shall overshadow thee: and therefore also the Holy which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God? In short, Truth is sprung out of the earth, not from the Angelic creature: nor doth he take hold of the Angels, but of the seed of Abraham. It is a great thing for an Angel to be a minister of the Lord; but Mary merited something higher, to be his Mother. The fruitfulness of the Virgin therefore is a surpassing glory, and she is made by a singular gift so much more excellent than the Angels, as she hath received the name of Mother, more different than that of ministers. She, already full of grace, found this grace, that being fervent in charity, unimpaired in virginity, devout in humility, she should nevertheless become with child without knowing man, and bring forth without the pain of women. That is little: That which is born of her is called Holy, and is the Son of God.
sedquiddeeiussupereminentialoquarcuienim.la: Sed quid de ejus supereminéntia loquar? Cui enim Angelórum aliquándo dictum est: Spíritus sanctus supervéniet in te, et virtus Altíssimi obumbrábit tibi: ideóque et quod nascétur ex te Sanctum vocábitur Fílius Dei? Dénique Véritas de terra orta est, non de Angélica creatúra: nec Angelos, sed semen Abrahæ apprehéndit. Magnum est Angelo ut miníster sit Dómini; sed Maria sublímius quiddam méruit, ut sit Mater. Fœcúnditas ítaque Vírginis superéminens glória est, tantóque excelléntior Angelis facta múnere singulári quanto differéntius præ minístris nomen Matris accépit. Hanc invénit grátiam plena jam grátia, ut charitáte férvida, virginitáte íntegra, humilitáte devóta, fíeret nihilóminus sine viri cognitióne grávida‚ sine muliébri dolóre puérpera; Parum est: Quod ex ea natum est, Sanctum vocátur, et est Fílius Dei.

iustusutpalmaflorebitsicutcedruslibanimu.en: The just shall flourish * like the palm tree: he shall grow up like the cedar of Libanus.
iustusutpalmaflorebitsicutcedruslibanimu.la: Justus ut palma * florébit: sicut cedrus Líbani multiplicábitur

quasistellamatutinainmedionebuleetquasil.en: As the morning star in the midst of a cloud, § and as the moon at the full, he shineth in his days. * And as the sun when it shineth, so did he shine in the temple of God. § And as the planting of a cedar on mount Libanus about him, * so about him did they stand as branches of palm trees.
quasistellamatutinainmedionebuleetquasil.la: Quasi stella matutína in médio nébulæ, § et quasi luna plena in diébus suis lucet. * Et quasi sol refúlgens, sic ille effúlsit in templo Dei. § Et circa illum plantátio cedri in monte Líbano, * sic circa illum stetérunt quasi rami palmæ.

iustusutpalmaflorebit.en: The just man, * Shall flourish like the palm tree.

sicutcedruslibanimultiplicabitur.en: He shall grow up like the cedar of Libanus.

utpalmaflorebit.en: Shall flourish like the palm tree.

cuiusfestumcolimusipseintercedatpronobis.en: May he whose feast we keep, § himself intercede for us with the Lord. §
cuiusfestumcolimusipseintercedatpronobis.la: Cujus festum cólimus, § ipse intercédat pro nobis ad Dóminum. §

ardensestcormeumdesiderovideredominummeu.en: My heart is on fire, * I long to see my Lord: I seek, and find not where they have laid him, alleluia.
ardensestcormeumdesiderovideredominummeu.la: Ardens est cor meum, * desídero vidére Dóminum meum: quæro, et non invénio, ubi posuérunt eum, allelúia. Ps. 109

alleluiaquemquerismulieralleluiaviventem.en: Alleluia, * whom seekest thou, O woman, alleluia, the living among the dead? alleluia, alleluia.
alleluiaquemquerismulieralleluiaviventem.la: Allelúia, * quem quæris múlier, allelúia, vivéntem cum mórtuis? allelúia, allelúia. Ps. 112

alleluianolifleremariaalleluiaresurrexit.en: Alleluia, * weep not, Mary, alleluia: the Lord is risen, alleluia, alleluia.
alleluianolifleremariaalleluiaresurrexit.la: Allelúia, * noli flere María, allelúia: resurréxit Dóminus, allelúia, allelúia. Ps. 121

nigrasumsedformosafilieierusalemideodile.en: I am black, * but beautiful, O ye daughters of Jerusalem; therefore hath the King loved me, and brought me into his chamber.
nigrasumsedformosafilieierusalemideodile.la: Nigra sum, * sed formósa, fíliæ Jerúsalem; ídeo diléxit me Rex, et introdúxit me in cubículum suum. Ps. 18

pulchresetdecorafiliaierusalemterribilis.en: Thou art fair * and comely, O daughter of Jerusalem, terrible as an army of a camp set in array.
pulchresetdecorafiliaierusalemterribilis.la: Pulchra es * et decóra fília Jerúsalem, terríbilis ut castrórum ácies ordináta. Ps. 23

reverterereverteresunamitisrevertereutin.en: Return, * return, O Sulamitess; return, that we may behold thee.
reverterereverteresunamitisrevertereutin.la: Revértere, * revértere, Sunamítis; revértere, ut intueámur te. Ps. 47

simileestregnumcelorumhomininegotiatoriq.en: The kingdom of heaven * is like to a merchant seeking good pearls: who when he had found one of great price, gave all that he had, and bought it.
simileestregnumcelorumhomininegotiatoriq.la: Símile est * regnum cælórum hómini negotiatóri quærénti bonas margarítas: invénta una pretiósa, dedit ómnia sua, et comparávit eam. Ps. 84

simileestregnumcelorumsagenemisseinmaree.en: The kingdom of heaven * is like to a net cast into the sea, and gathering together of all kind of fishes: which, when it was filled, they drew out, and sitting by the shore, they chose out the good into vessels, but the bad they cast forth.
simileestregnumcelorumsagenemisseinmaree.la: Símile est * regnum cœlórum sagénæ, missæ in mare, et ex omni génere píscium cóngreganti: quam, cum impléta esset, educéntes, et secus littus sedéntes, elegérunt bonos in vasa sua, malos autem foras misérunt. Ps. 95

dumtransissetsabbatummariamagdaleneetmar.en: When the Sabbath was passed, Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James, and Salome, had bought sweet spices,
dumtransissetsabbatummariamagdaleneetmar.la: Dum transísset Sábbatum, María Magdaléne, et María Jacóbi, et Salóme emérunt arómata,

utvenientesungerentiesum.en: That they might come and anoint Jesus.

etvaldemaneunasabbatorumveniuntadmonumen.en: And very early in the morning, the first day of the week, they came unto the sepulchre, at the rising of the sun.
etvaldemaneunasabbatorumveniuntadmonumen.la: Et valde mane una Sabbatórum véniunt ad monuméntum, orto jam sole:

surgeproperaamicameetveniiamenimhiemstra.en: Arise, make haste, my love, and come: for winter is now past, the rain is over and gone:
surgeproperaamicameetveniiamenimhiemstra.la: Surge, própera, amíca mea, et veni: jam enim hiems tránsiit, imber ábiit et recéssit:

floresapparueruntinterra.en: The flowers have appeared in the land.

voxturturisauditestinterranostraficuspro.en: The voice of the turtle is heard in our land, the fig tree hath put forth her green figs.
voxturturisauditestinterranostraficuspro.la: Vox túrturis audíta est in terra nostra, ficus prótulit grossos suos.

exhomiliaqueestdesancteusebio.en: From Homily 59, which is the 2nd on St. Eusebius.
exhomiliaqueestdesancteusebio.la: Ex Homilia 59. quæ est 2. de sancto Eusebio.

beatipatrisstephanimeritaiamintutoposita.en: Let us, now secure, magnify the merits of blessed Father Stephen, now placed in safety: who, holding manfully the helm of faith, hath now cast the anchor of hope in a tranquil haven, and hath brought his ship, full of heavenly riches and eternal merchandise, to rest on the longed-for shore: who against all adversaries held unweariedly the shield of the fear of God, until he came to the victory.
beatipatrisstephanimeritaiamintutoposita.la: Beáti Patris Stéphani mérita jam in tuto pósita secúri magnificémus: qui gubernáculum fídei viríliter tenens, ánchoram spei tranquílla jam in statióne compósuit, et plenam cœléstibus divítiis et ætérnis mércibus navem optáto in líttore collocávit: qui contra omnes adversários scutum timóris Dei támdiu infatigabiliter ténuit, donec ad victóriam perveníret.

quantosperlongamincuriampeccatilaberesol.en: How many, dissolved through long carelessness by the stain of sin, and as it were overspread with the contagion of leprosy, did he cleanse, purifying them by chastisements and exhortations, God working in him? The souls of how many, already dead though living in the body, overwhelmed and buried under the mass of their sins, did he raise up to God by calling them to amendment as to the light; that, a wonderful imitator of his Lord, he might in turn put to death to sin, by a life-giving death, those that had been dead to God?
quantosperlongamincuriampeccatilaberesol.la: Quantos per longam incúriam peccáti labe resolútos, et quadam lepræ contagióne perfúsos, castigatiónibus et exhortatiónibus expiándo, Deo in se operánte mundávit? Quantórum ánimas vivéntes in córpore jam defúnctas, delictórum mole óbrutas ac sepúltas, ad emendatiónem tamquam ad lucem vocándo, Deo resuscitávit ; ut Dómini sui admirándus imitátor, jam mórtuas Deo, e contrário mortíficet vitáli morte peccáto?

balduinusnobiligenereortusrainardicassin.en: Baldwin, born of a noble family, own brother of Rainald, Abbot of Monte Cassino and Cardinal of the holy Roman Church, a monk of Clairvaux, a disciple of the holy Father Bernard and loved by him with a special privilege of affection, was a man renowned for a singular reputation of holiness, and was set by the same holy Doctor over the Monastery of St. Pastor, of the Cistercian Order, in the diocese of Rieti. After the blessed Abbot had ruled that monastery ten years, and had formed the monks committed to his care by his most devout manners and by the example of an angelic way of life, renowned for holy works and miracles he took his flight to heaven, in the year of salvation one thousand one hundred and forty; and, honourably buried in the Cathedral of Rieti, he is honoured with the highest veneration.
balduinusnobiligenereortusrainardicassin.la: Balduínus nóbili génere ortus, Rainárdi, Cassinénsis Abbátis ac sanctæ Románæ Ecclésiæ Cardinális frater germánus, mónachus Clarævallénsis, sancti Patris Bernárdi discípulus, et ab eo speciáli amóris prærogatíva diléctus, vir fuit singulári sanctitátis opinióne célebris‚ atque ab eódem sancto Doctóre Monastério sancti Pastóris‚ Ordinis Cisterciénsis in diœcési Reatína præféctus. Postquam beátus Abbas decem annos illud Cœnóbium rexísset, ac piíssimis móribus et Angélicæ conversatiónis exémplo mónachos suæ curæ commíssos informásset, sanctis opéribus et miráculis clarus ad cœlos evolávit, anno salútis millésimo centésimo quadragésimo, et in Cathedráli Reatína honorifice sepúltus, summa veneratióne cólitur.

extatofficiosissimasanctibernardiabbatis.en: There is extant a most kindly letter of the holy Abbot Bernard to blessed Baldwin, who had then lately been sent into Italy, in which the holy Father says, among other things: As a mother loveth her only son, so did I love thee while thou didst cling to my side and wast pleasing to my heart. Let me love thee absent also, lest I should seem to have loved my comfort from thee, and not thee. Thou wast most necessary to me; and hence above all it is clear how sincerely I love thee. For today I should not be without thee, had I sought the things that are mine: but now thou seest that, setting aside my own advantage, I have not grudged thee thy gain, placing thee there whence thou mayest some day be set over all the goods of thy Lord.
extatofficiosissimasanctibernardiabbatis.la: Extat officiosíssima sancti Bernárdi Abbátis epístola ad beátum Balduínum‚ tunc recénter ad Itáliam transmíssum, in qua hæc inter ália habet sanctus Pater: Sicut mater únicum amat fílium, ita te diligébam hæréntem láteri meo, placéntem cordi meo. Díligam et abséntem ne solátium meum ex te, et te non vídear dilexísse. Eras pernecessárius mihi; atque hinc vel máxime claret, quam sincére te díligam. Hódie nempe non te caruíssem, si quæsivíssem quæ mea sunt: nunc autem vides, quod, spretis utilitátibus meis, tuis compéndiis non invídi, ponens te útique ibi, unde aliquándo transponáris super ómnia bona Dómini tui.

deusquiperbeatumbalduinumabbatemecclesia.en: O God, who through blessed Baldwin, Abbot, didst vouchsafe wonderfully to make thy Church illustrious: * grant unto us thy servants: § that him whom we venerate as our patron on earth, we may merit to have as our intercessor in heaven.
deusquiperbeatumbalduinumabbatemecclesia.la: Deus, qui per beátum Balduínum, Abbátem, Ecclésiam tuam mirabíliter illustráre dignátus es: * concéde nobis fámulis tuis: § ut, quem Patrónum venerámur in terris, intercessórem habére mereámur in cœlis.

orbisexultanscelebrethocfestum.en: Let the world, exulting, celebrate this feast,

prosequensannammatremmatrischristi.en: Honouring Anne, the mother of the Mother of Christ,

quamsacriscreditactibusadeptam.en: Whom it believes to have attained it by holy deeds,

abraheprolessacerdotumsemen.en: Offspring of Abraham, seed of priests,

filiaregumspeciemhebreum.en: Daughter of kings, the beauty of the Hebrews,

stirpemsanctorummeritisetvita.en: The stock of the Saints in merits and in life,

steriliventrepriusinfecunda.en: Before unfruitful, with a barren womb,

nutudivinopeperitmariam.en: By the will of God she brought forth Mary,

dominamrerumtitulumfloremque.en: The Lady of all things, the glory and the flower

hacmedianteiesuchristenostros.en: Through her mediation, O Jesus Christ, our

tergereatusnoxiapropulsans.en: Sins wipe away, driving off all harm,

filiesuetuematrisprece.en: At the prayer of her daughter, thy Mother,

donethocnobispietaspaterna.en: May the Father's loving-kindness grant us this,

simulcumnatospirituquesancto.en: Together with the Son and the Holy Ghost:

utmatrisanneprecibusiuvemur.en: That by the prayers of Mother Anne we may be helped

gaudematermagneprolisexteenimprocessitru.en: Rejoice, * mother of a great offspring, for from thee came forth the glittering star of the most high sun.
gaudematermagneprolisexteenimprocessitru.la: Gaude, * mater magnæ prolis, ex te enim procéssit rútillans stella summi solis.

deusquibeateannegratiamconferredignatuse.en: O God, who didst vouchsafe to bestow grace upon blessed Anne, that she might merit to become the mother of her who bore thine only-begotten Son, § mercifully grant: * that we who celebrate her solemnity, § may be helped by her patronage with thee.
deusquibeateannegratiamconferredignatuse.la: Deus, qui beátæ Annæ grátiam conférre dignátus es, ut Genitrícis Unigéniti Fílii tui Mater éffici mererétur, § concéde propítius: * ut cujus solémnia celebrámus, § ejus apud te patrocíniis adjuvémur.

deidaturamfilium.en: The Virgin who shall give the Son of God

caputtenebrisexcitans.en: Raising its head from the darkness,

annecoruscantemsinu.en: Shining in the bosom of Anne.

hancvotapuripectoris.en: Her the vows of a pure heart

prolemmerenturomnium.en: Merit to bring forth as offspring,

matremsalutisgignere.en: The Mother of the salvation of all.

claredieigaudiis.en: With the joys of the bright day

annamqueiudeedecus.en: And Anne, the glory of Judea,

matremmarieconcinit.en: The Mother of Mary, she singeth.

regumpiorumsanguini.en: To the blood of pious kings

thorifidelisvinculum.en: The bond of a faithful marriage:

effetadudumcorpore.en: Long since worn out in body,

castoqueformatpectore.en: And in her chaste breast she formeth

celestebeneficiumintroivitinannamdequana.en: A heavenly blessing * entered into Anne, of whom was born to us the loving Virgin Mary.
celestebeneficiumintroivitinannamdequana.la: Cœléste benefícium * introívit in Annam, de qua nata est nobis pia Virgo María.

iucundaregenitrixmariequevirgodeumpeperi.en: Rejoice, O mother * of Mary, who as a Virgin brought forth God, and is Mother of the Messias.
iucundaregenitrixmariequevirgodeumpeperi.la: Jucundáre génitrix * Maríæ, quæ Virgo Deum péperit, et Mater est Messíæ.

camillusbucclanicitheatinediecesisoppide.en: Camillus, born at Bucchianico, a town of the diocese of Chieti, of the noble family of the Lelli, followed soldiering as a youth and for some time indulged in the vices of the world, until, in his twenty-fifth year, filled with a more abundant light and sweetness of heavenly grace, he firmly resolved to wash away the defilements of his former life and to put on the new man. Wherefore, hastening to the Friars Minor whom they call Capuchins, he besought with most earnest prayers to be enrolled among their number. But divine providence disposing greater things concerning him, he laid aside the habit of that religious order which he had received, and having gone to Rome, was received into the hospital which is called that of the Incurables: the administration of which also, entrusted to him on account of his eminent virtues, he carried out with the utmost integrity and a truly fatherly solicitude. Reckoning himself the servant of all the sick, and intent above all on the relief of souls in peril at their last end, he gave most illustrious examples of admirable patience and of heroic charity. Afterwards initiated into the priesthood, he laid the first foundations of the congregation of Clerks Regular Ministering to the Sick; and in furthering this most wholesome institute he was wonderfully strengthened by a heavenly voice uttered from an image of Christ crucified, who by an admirable prodigy stretched forth his hands, even torn from the wood; and with constant mind he overcame all adverse difficulties.
camillusbucclanicitheatinediecesisoppide.la: Camíllus Bucclánici, Theatínæ diœcésis óppido ex nóbili Lelliórum família natus, adoléscens milítiam secútus, sæculi vítiis aliquándiu indúlsit, donec vigésimum quintum agens ætátis annum, abundantióri supérnæ grátiæ lumine et dulcédine perfúsus, anteáctæ vitæ sordes abstérgere, novúmque induére hóminem fírmiter decrévit. Unde ad Fratres Minóres, quos Cappucínos vocant, cónvolans‚ eórum número adscribi summis précibus exorávit. Verum majóra de eo divína disponénte providéntia illius religiónis suscéptum hábitum dimísit, et Romam proféctus in Nosocómium‚ quod insanabílium dícitur, recéptus est: cuius étiam administratiónem, ob exímias virtútes sibi demandátam, summa integritáte‚ ac sollicitúdine vere patérna perégit. Omnium ægrórum servum se réputans ac præcípue animárum in extrémis periclitántium levámini inténdens, præclaríssima præbuit admirábilis patiéntiæ, et heróicæ charitátis exémpla. Sacerdótio póstea initiátus, prima jecit congregatiónis Clericórum Regulárium infírmis ministrántium fundaménta‚ in quo salubérrimo promovéndo institúto cœlésti voce e simulácro emíssa Christi crucifíxi, manus étiam de ligno avúlsas admirándo prodígio protendéntis, mirabíliter confortátus, advérsas omnes constánti ánimo superávit difficultátes.

mirumestquaalacritatenullisfractuslabori.en: It is wonderful with what eagerness, broken by no labours, deterred by no dangers to his life, he watched day and night, even to his last breath, over the comfort of the sick. Made all things to all men, he took upon himself every most lowly office with a cheerful and ready mind; and that he might more freely spend himself, and be spent, for the needs of all the needy, he of his own accord laid aside the general governance of the Order and the delights of heaven in which he abounded when rapt in contemplation. At length, worn out by vigils, fastings and continual labours, having bravely endured five illnesses as troublesome as they were lasting, which he called the mercies of the Lord, he fell asleep in the Lord at Rome, amid the most sweet names of Jesus and Mary, at these words: Mild and joyful may the face of Christ Jesus appear to thee; in the year of salvation one thousand six hundred and fourteen: and him, illustrious for many miracles, Benedict the Fourteenth with solemn rite enrolled in the calendar of the Saints.
mirumestquaalacritatenullisfractuslabori.la: Mirum est, qua alacritáte, nullis fractus labóribus, nullis detérritus vitæ perículis, diu noctúque ad suprémum usque spíritum ægrotántium cómmodis vigiláverit. Omnibus ómnia factus vilíssima quæque offícia hilári promptóque ánimo accipiébat, utque se libérius ómnium impénderet indigéntium necessitátibus, atque superimpénderet, generálem Ordinis præfectúram cœlíque delícias, quibus in contemplatióne defíxus affluébat‚ sponte dimísit. Tandem vigíliis, jejúniis‚ et assíduis attrítus labóribus‚ quinque moléstis æque ac diutúrnis morbis, quos misericórdias Dómini appellábat‚ fórtiter tolerátis, Romæ inter suavíssima Jesu et Mariæ nómina, ad ea verba: Mitis atque festívus Christi Jesu tibi aspéctus appáreat, obdormívit in Dómino‚ anno salútis millésimo sexcentésimo décimo quarto: quem plúribus illústrem miráculis Benedíctus décimus quartus solémni ritu Sanctórum fastis adscrípsit.

vincentiusapaulonationegalluspodiinonpro.en: Vincent de Paul, a Frenchman by nation, born at Pouy, not far from Dax in Aquitaine, even from boyhood showed an outstanding charity towards the poor. Called from the keeping of his father's flock to letters, and afterwards honoured with the priesthood, he fell among the Turks, who carried him away captive into Africa. But having won his master himself to Christ, he escaped together with him from the barbarous shores by the help of the Mother of God, and took the road to the threshold of the Apostles; whence, returning into France, he devoted himself unweariedly to the ministry of souls. Named by the king chief chaplain of the galleys of France, it is wonderful with what zeal he laboured for the salvation both of officers and of oarsmen. Set over the Nuns of the Visitation by St. Francis de Sales, he sustained that charge for about forty years with such prudence as fully to confirm the judgement of the most holy Prelate, who confessed that he knew no priest worthier than Vincent. To evangelizing the poor, especially country folk, he bound by perpetual vow both himself and the members of the Congregation which he founded under the name of Priests of the Mission. And how much he laboured for the increase of the discipline of the Clergy, and how much for the spreading of faith and piety, is witnessed, among other things, by the seminaries erected for clerics in major orders, and by the many heralds of the word of God sent not only to the provinces of France and of Europe, but even as far as the Barbarians and the Indians.
vincentiusapaulonationegalluspodiinonpro.la: Vincéntius a Paulo, natióne Gallus, Pódii non procul ab Aquis Tarbéllis in Aquitánia natus, jam tum a púero exímiam in páuperes charitátem præ se tulit. A custódia patérni gregis ad lítteras vocátus, et póstea sacerdótio insignítus, in Turcas incídit, qui captívum in Africam abduxérunt. Sed cum herum ipsum Christo lucrifecísset, ex bárbaris oris una cum eo, opitulánte Deípara se prorípiens, ad Apostólica límina iter instítuit; unde in Gálliam revérsus, animárum ministério indeféssus incúbuit. Primárius sacrórum miníster in Gálliæ trirémibus renuntiátus a rege, mirum quo zelo et ducum et rémigum salúti óperam posúerit. Moniálibus Visitatiónis a sancto Francísco Salésio præpósitus, tanta prudéntia per annos círciter quadragínta eam curam sustínuit, ut máxime comprobáverit judícium sanctíssimi Præsulis, qui sacerdótem Vincéntio digniórem nullum se nosse fatebátur. Evangelizándis paupéribus, præsértim rurícolis, tum se, tum alúmnos Congregatiónis, quam sub nómine Presbyterórum Missiónis instítuit, perpétuo voto obstrínxit. Quantum autem augéndæ Cleri disciplínæ, et quantum amplificándæ fídei et pietáti allaboráverit‚ testántur, inter ália, erécta majórum Clericórum seminária, et multi verbi Dei præcónes non ad solas Gálliæ et Európæ províncias missi, sed et usque ad Bárbaros et Indos.

nullumfuitcalamitatisgenuscuipaternenono.en: There was no kind of calamity which he did not meet with a father's care. The faithful groaning under the yoke of the Turks, foundling infants, maidens in danger, scattered nuns, men condemned to the galleys, sick pilgrims, disabled workmen, and even the insane, and countless beggars, he received and lovingly cherished with succours and with houses of shelter, which survive even now. He abundantly relieved divers provinces laid waste by plague, famine and war. He founded very many associations for seeking out and relieving the wretched, among which the celebrated assembly of matrons, and the widely spread Society of the Daughters of Charity. Yet he himself, amid these and other most weighty affairs, ever intent upon God, affable to all, and always true to himself, simple, upright, humble, ever shrank from honours, riches and pleasures. At length, worn out with labours and old age, in the year one thousand six hundred and sixty, the eighty-fifth of his age, he peacefully fell asleep at Paris in the house of St. Lazarus, which is the head house of the Congregation of the Mission. Him, renowned for virtues, merits and miracles, Clement the Twelfth numbered among the Saints.
nullumfuitcalamitatisgenuscuipaternenono.la: Nullum fuit calamitátis genus, cui patérne non occúrrerit. Fidéles sub Turcárum jugo geméntes‚ infántes expósitos, vírgines periclitántes‚ moniáles dispérsas, ad trirémes damnátos, peregrínos infírmos, artífices inválidos, ipsósque mente captos, ac innúmeros mendícos subsídiis et hospítiis etiámnum superstítibus excépit ac pie fovit. Divérsas províncias peste, fame bellóque vastátas prolíxe refécit. Plúrima ad perquiréndos et sublevándos míseros sodalítia fundávit‚ inter quæ célebris matronárum cœtus, et late diffúsa sub nómine Charitátis puellárum Socíetas. Ipse vero hæc inter et ália gravíssima negótia, Deo júgiter inténtus, cunctis affábilis, ac sibi semper constans, simplex, rectus, húmilis, ab honóribus, divítiis ac delíciis semper abhórruit. Demum labóribus et sénio conféctus, anno supra millésimum sexcentésimo sexagésimo, ætátis suæ octogésimo quinto, Parísiis in domo sancti Lázari‚ quæ caput est Congregatiónis Missiónis, plácide obdormívit. Quem virtútibus, méritis ac miráculis clarum Clemens duodécimus inter Sanctos rétulit.

marthachristidominihospitioclaraposteius.en: Martha, renowned for having received Christ the Lord as her guest, after his ascension into heaven, was seized by the Jews together with her brother and sister and many Christians, and put into a ship without sail or oars; and by God's guidance she came to land at Marseilles. By that miracle the neighbouring peoples believed in Christ: and Lazarus was made Bishop of Marseilles, and Maximinus of Aix. But Magdalen, accustomed to prayer, not forsaking the best part which she had chosen, hid herself in a vast cave.
marthachristidominihospitioclaraposteius.la: Martha, Christi Dómini hospítio clara, post ejus ascénsum in cœlum, cum germánis et multis Christiánis comprehénsa a Judæis, in navem sine velo, ac remígio impósita, Deo gubernánte, Massíliam appéllit. Eo miráculo finítimæ gentes in Christum credidérunt: Lazarúsque Massiliénsium, et Maximínus Aquénsium Epíscopus creátur. Magdaléna vero oratióni assuéta, partem óptimam, quam elégerat, non relínquens, in vastam spelúncam se cóndidit.

marthaautemmirabilivitesanctitatemassili.en: But Martha, by the wonderful holiness of her life, turning the hearts of the people of Marseilles to love of her, withdrew to a place remote from men, where she lived devoutly with some women; and at length, having foretold her death long before, renowned for miracles she passed to the Lord on the fourth day before the Kalends of August. Her body is held in great veneration at Tarascon.
marthaautemmirabilivitesanctitatemassili.la: Martha autem, mirábili vitæ sanctitáte, Massiliénsium ánimos in sui amórem convértens, in locum remótum a viris se recépit, ubi cum áliquot fœminis pie vixit, ac demum, morte sua multo ante praedícta, miráculis clara migrávit ad Dóminum, quarto Kaléndas Augústi. Cujus corpus apud Taráscum magnam habet veneratiónem.

hieronymusemilianuspatriciastirpevenetii.en: Jerome Emiliani, of patrician stock, born at Venice, given from his youth to soldiering, was set, in most difficult times for the commonwealth, over Castelnuovo at Quero in the mountains of Treviso. The fortress being taken by the enemy, he himself was thrust into a most foul prison; whence, being wonderfully delivered by the most blessed Virgin, moved by his prayers, he returned to Venice and began to practise the pursuits of piety more earnestly. Wonderfully lavish towards the poor, but pitying especially the boys who, bereft of their parents, wandered needy and squalid through the city, he received them into houses hired by himself, to be fed at his own cost and imbued with Christian manners. Soon, through the efforts of blessed Cajetan and of Peter Caraffa, who was afterwards Paul the Fourth, he was brought into the hospital of the Incurables, that he might there at once bring up the orphans and serve the sick with equal charity. At their exhortation he set out for the neighbouring mainland, and erected new orphanages, first at Brescia, then at Bergamo. At length, settling at Somasca, a humble village in the territory of Bergamo, he established there a seat for himself and his followers, and gave form to the congregation which for that reason took its name from Somasca; which, afterwards increased and spread, and devoted not only to the governance of orphans and the service of churches but also to the instruction of youth, St. Pius the Fifth enrolled among the religious Orders.
hieronymusemilianuspatriciastirpevenetii.la: Hierónymus Æmiliánus, patrícia stirpe, Venétiis ortus, ab adolescéntia milítiæ addíctus, difficíllimis reipúblicæ tempóribus Castronóvo ad Quarum in móntibus Tarvisínis præfícitur. Capta ab hóstibus arce, ipse in tetérrimum cárcerem detrúditur, unde a beatíssima Virgine, ejus précibus exoráta‚ mirabíliter liberátus, Venétias revérsus, cœpit pietátis stúdia impénsius cólere. In páuperes mire effúsus, sed puerórum præsértim misértus, qui paréntibus orbáti‚ egéni et sórdidi per urbem vagabántur, illos in aedes a se condúctas recépit, de suo aléndos et Christiánis móribus imbuéndos. Mox ópera beáti Cajetáni et Petri Caráfæ‚ qui póstmodum Paulus quartus fuit, in hospítium incurabílium addúctus est, in quo órphanos simul educáret, et ægrótis pari charitáte inservíret. Eorúmdem hortátu in próximam continéntem proféctus, Bríxiæ primum, deínde Bérgomi nova eréxit orphánotrophía. Somáschæ demum subsístens, in húmili pago agri Bergoménsis sibi ac suis ibídem sedem constítuit, formámque indúxit congregatiónis, cui proptérea a Somáscha nomen factum, quam sub inde auctam et propagátam nedum orphanórum regímini et ecclesiárum cúltui, sed et adolescéntium institutióni addíctam sanctus Pius quintus inter religiósos Ordines adscrípsit.

orphaniscolligendisintentusmediolanumpro.en: Intent on gathering orphans, he set out for Milan and Pavia, and in both places, having gathered together throngs of boys, with the favour of noble men, he providently established new houses. Returning thence to Somasca, made all things to all men, he shrank from no work which he foresaw would turn to his neighbour's good. Mingling with the husbandmen scattered through the fields, while he offered himself as their helper in their labours, he explained to them the mysteries of the faith; he cleansed and tended the heads of boys foul with scurf, and healed the putrid wounds of the country folk with such success that he was deemed to be endowed with the grace of healing. In the mountain which overhangs Somasca he found a cave, and hid himself in it; where, scourging himself, passing whole days fasting, and persevering in prayer, he paid the penalty of his own sins and those of others. At length, having caught a disease while he served the sick in a time of contagion and carried the dead on his own shoulders to burial, he ended a precious life by a more precious death in the year one thousand five hundred and thirty-seven; and him, illustrious for many miracles in life and after death, Clement the Thirteenth numbered among the Saints.
orphaniscolligendisintentusmediolanumpro.la: Orphanis colligéndis inténtus Mediolánum proficíscitur atque Ticínum, et utrobíque collectis agmínibus puerórum‚ nobílibus viris favéntibus, novas domos próvide constítuit. Inde Somáscham redux ómnibus ómnia factus a nullo abhorrébat ópere, quod in próximi bonum cedére prævidéret. Agrícolis immíxtus per agros sparsis, dum se illis in labóribus adjutórem præbet, mystéria fídei explicábat, puerórum cápita, porrígine fœda abstérgens curábat, putridísque rusticórum vulnéribus medebátur eo succéssu, ut grátia curatiónum donátus censerétur. In monte, qui Somáschæ ímminet, repérta specu, in illam se ábdidit, ubi se flagéllis cædens‚ dies íntegros jejúnus tránsigens‚ oratióni insístens, sui aliorúmque noxárum pœnas luébat. Tandem contrácto morbo, dum témpore contagiónis ægrotántibus inservíret, et vita functos própriis húmeris ad sepultúram deférret, pretiósam vitam pretiosióri morte finívit anno millésimo quingentésimo trigésimo séptimo, quem plúribus in vita et post mortem miráculis illústrem Clemens décimus tértius in númerum Sanctórum rétulit.

ignatiusloyoleincantabrianatusinpropugna.en: Ignatius, born at Loyola in Cantabria, lying grievously ill from a wound received in the defence of Pamplona, was, through a chance reading of pious books, wonderfully fired to follow in the footsteps of Christ and of the Saints. Going to Montserrat, he hung up his arms before the altar of the most blessed Virgin and, keeping watch through the night, made his novitiate in the sacred warfare. Thence withdrawing to Manresa, he was there refreshed by wonderful illuminations.
ignatiusloyoleincantabrianatusinpropugna.la: Ignátius, Loyólæ in Cantábria natus, in propugnatióne Pampelonénsi, accépto vúlnere, gráviter decúmbens, ex fortúita piórum librórum lectióne, ad Christi Sanctorúmque sectánda vestígia mirabíliter exársit. Ad montem Serrátum proféctus, ante Aram beatíssimæ Vírginis suspénsis armis, noctem éxcubans, sacræ milítiæ tyrocínium pósuit. Inde Manrésam secédens, præcláris ibi fuit illustratiónibus recreátus.

lutetieparisioruminmontemartyrumprimaord.en: At Paris, on the Mount of Martyrs, he laid the first foundations of his Order. He declared war on heathen superstition and on heresy, opening everywhere schools for piety and letters. The beauty of churches, the teaching of the Catechism, and the frequenting of sermons and of the Sacraments received increase from him. He put demons to flight, was seen with a radiant countenance, and in the sixty-fifth year of his age passed to the embrace of his Lord. Him, illustrious for merits and miracles, Gregory the Fifteenth enrolled in the calendar of the Saints.
lutetieparisioruminmontemartyrumprimaord.la: Lutétiae Parisiórum, in monte Mártyrum prima Ordinis fundaménta jecit. Ethnicæ superstitióni, hæresíque bellum indíxit, apértis ubíque ad pietátem et lítteras gymnasiis. Templórum nitor, Catechísmi tradítio, conciónum ac Sacramentórum frequéntia ab ipso increméntum accepérunt. Dæmones fugávit, vultu radiánti conspéctus est, ac ætátis annum agens sexagésimum quintum, ad Dómini sui ampléxum migrávit. Hunc Gregórius decimus quintus, méritis et miráculis illústrem, fastis Sanctórum adscrípsit.

iustusgerminabitsicutlilium.en: The just shall spring as the lily.

etflorebitineternumantedominum.en: And shall flourish for ever before the Lord.
etflorebitineternumantedominum.la: Et florébit in ætérnum ante Dóminum.

patefactesuntianuecelichristimartyristep.en: The gates of heaven * were opened to Christ's Martyr Stephen, who was found the first in the number of the Martyrs, and therefore he triumpheth crowned in heaven, alleluia.
patefactesuntianuecelichristimartyristep.la: Patefáctæ sunt * jánuæ cœli Christi Mártyri Stéphano, qui in número Mártyrum invéntus est primus, et ídeo triúmphat in cœlis coronátus, allelúia.

intuensincelumbeatusstephanusviditgloria.en: Looking up to heaven, * blessed Stephen saw the glory of God, and said: Behold, I see the heavens opened, and the Son of man standing on the right hand of God.
intuensincelumbeatusstephanusviditgloria.la: Intuens in cœlum * beátus Stéphanus vidit glóriam Dei, et ait: Ecce vídeo cœlos apértos, et Fílium hóminis stantem a dextris Dei.

detorrenteinviabibetproptereexaltabitcap.en: He shall drink * of the torrent in the way: therefore shall he lift up the head, and he shall reign, clothed with beauty and with strength.
detorrenteinviabibetproptereexaltabitcap.la: De torrénte * in via bibet, proptérea exaltábit caput, et regnábit indútus decórem, et fortitúdinem.

requievitsupereumspiritustimorisdominico.en: There hath rested * upon him the spirit of the fear of the Lord, and a crown of wisdom and of gladness hath adorned him.
requievitsupereumspiritustimorisdominico.la: Requiévit * super eum spíritus timóris Dómini, coróna sapiéntiæ, et exultatiónis decorávit illum.

induiteumdominusvestimentissalutisetindu.en: The Lord hath clothed * him with the garments of salvation, and with the robe of justice, as a bridegroom decked with a crown.
induiteumdominusvestimentissalutisetindu.la: Induit * eum Dóminus vestiméntis salútis, et induménto justítiæ, quasi sponsum decorátum coróna.

cinxeruntdavidinmodumcoronesauletvirieiu.en: They compassed David * round like a crown, Saul and his men.
cinxeruntdavidinmodumcoronesauletvirieiu.la: Cinxérunt David * in modum corónæ Saül et viri ejus.

rexeternegloriepronobiscoronatusbenedice.en: The King of eternal glory, * crowned for us, shall bless the crown of the year of his goodness.
rexeternegloriepronobiscoronatusbenedice.la: Rex ætérnæ glóriæ * pro nobis coronátus, benedícet corónæ anni benignitátis suæ.

exitesionfilie.en: Go forth, ye daughters of Sion,

quammateripsatexuit.en: Which his mother herself hath woven.

spiniscruentatumcaput.en: Is the head bloodied by the thorns,

dumisrigensetsentibus.en: Stiff with briars and with thorns,

quesevamessuitmanus.en: What cruel hand hath reaped it?

christirubescenssanguine.en: Reddening with the Blood of Christ,

aculeosmutatrosis.en: It changeth its prickles into roses,

palmamquevincensfructibus.en: And, surpassing the palm in its fruits,

spinesttriumphisaptior.en: The thorn is fitter for triumphs.

culpissatemortalium.en: Sown by the sins of mortals,

techristespinevulnerant.en: The thorns, O Christ, wound thee;

evellenostrascordibus.en: Pluck out ours from our hearts,

posueruntsupercaputeius.en: They put it upon his head.

egrediminietvidetefiliesionregemsalomone.en: Go forth * and see, ye daughters of Sion, King Solomon in the diadem wherewith his mother crowned him, preparing the cross for her Saviour.
egrediminietvidetefiliesionregemsalomone.la: Egredímini * et vidéte fíliæ Sion regem Salomónem in diadémate, quo coronávit eum mater sua, parans crucem Salvatóri suo.

prestaquesumusomnipotensdeusutquiinmemor.en: Grant, we beseech thee, almighty God: * that we who, in memory of the Passion of our Lord Jesus Christ, venerate his Crown of thorns on earth, § may merit to be crowned by him with glory and honour in heaven.
prestaquesumusomnipotensdeusutquiinmemor.la: Præsta quǽsumus omnípotens Deus: * ut qui in memóriam Passiónis Dómini nostri Jesu Christi Corónam ejus spíneam venerámur in terris, § ab ipso glória et honóre coronári mereámur in cœlis.

egrediminifiliesionetvidetechristumregem.en: Go forth, ye daughters of Sion, and behold Christ the King crowned with thorns, * O come, let us adore.
egrediminifiliesionetvidetechristumregem.la: Egredímini fíliæ Sion, et vidéte Christum Regem spinis coronátum, * Veníte adorémus.

erittamquamlignumquodplantatumestsecusde.en: He shall be like a tree * which is planted near the running waters, and he shall yield his fruit in due season.
erittamquamlignumquodplantatumestsecusde.la: Erit tamquam lignum, * quod plantátum est secus decúrsus aquárum, et fructum suum dabit in témpore suo. Ps. 1

conveneruntinunumadversusdominumetadvers.en: They met together * against the Lord, and against his Christ.
conveneruntinunumadversusdominumetadvers.la: Convenérunt * in unum advérsus Dóminum, et advérsus Christum ejus. Ps. 2

intribulationedilatastimihi.en: When I was in distress * thou hast enlarged me.

domineutscutobonevoluntatistuecoronastie.en: O Lord, * thou hast crowned him as with a shield of thy good will.
domineutscutobonevoluntatistuecoronastie.la: Dómine, * ut scuto bonæ voluntátis tuæ coronásti eum. Ps. 5

minuistieumpaulominusabangelisgloriethon.en: Thou hast made him * a little less than the angels, thou hast crowned him with glory and honour.
minuistieumpaulominusabangelisgloriethon.la: Minuísti eum * paulo minus ab Ángelis, glória et honóre coronásti eum. Ps. 8

peccatoresintenderuntarcumparaveruntsagi.en: The wicked * have bent their bow: they have prepared their arrows in the quiver, to shoot at the just.
peccatoresintenderuntarcumparaveruntsagi.la: Peccatóres * intendérunt arcum: paravérunt sagíttas suas in pháretra, ut sagíttent justum. Ps. 10

ingressussinemaculetoperatusiustitiamcor.en: He that entered in * without blemish, and wrought justice, was crowned in thy holy mountain.
ingressussinemaculetoperatusiustitiamcor.la: Ingréssus * sine mácula, et operátus justítiam, coronátus est in monte sancto tuo. Ps. 14

supercaputeiuscoronamdelapidepretiosopos.en: Upon his head * thou hast set a crown of precious stones, O Lord.
supercaputeiuscoronamdelapidepretiosopos.la: Super caput ejus * corónam de lápide pretióso posuísti Dómine. Ps. 20

adversuseosquitribulantmeimpinguastiinol.en: Against them * that afflict me, thou hast anointed my head with oil.
adversuseosquitribulantmeimpinguastiinol.la: Advérsus eos, * qui tríbulant me, impinguásti in óleo caput meum. Ps. 22

requievitsupereumspiritustimorisdominico.en: There hath rested * upon him the spirit of the fear of the Lord: a crown of wisdom and of gladness hath adorned him.
requievitsupereumspiritustimorisdominico.la: Requiévit * super eum spíritus timóris Dómini: coróna sapiéntiæ et exsultatiónis decorávit illum. Ps. 63

peccatorumconfringamcornuetexaltabunturc.en: The horns of sinners * I will break, and the horn of the just shall be exalted.
peccatorumconfringamcornuetexaltabunturc.la: Peccatórum * confríngam córnua, et exaltábúntur córnu justi. Ps. 74

coronaaureasupercaputeius.en: A crown of gold upon his head.

maledictaterrainoperehominis.en: Cursed is the earth in the work of man,

spinasettribulosgerminavitchristo.en: It hath brought forth thorns and thistles to Christ.

quiacomeditadamdelignexquopreceperatdeus.en: Because Adam did eat of the tree whereof God had commanded that he should not eat.
quiacomeditadamdelignexquopreceperatdeus.la: Quia comédit Adam de ligno, ex quo præcéperat Deus ne coméderet.

apparuitmoysidominusinflammaignisdemedio.en: The Lord appeared to Moses in a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush:
apparuitmoysidominusinflammaignisdemedio.la: Appáruit Móysi Dóminus in flamma ignis de médio rubi:

etvidebatquodrubusarderetetnoncombureret.en: And he saw that the bush was on fire, and was not burnt.
etvidebatquodrubusarderetetnoncombureret.la: Et vidébat quod rubus ardéret, et non comburerétur.

dixitergomoysesvadametvidebovisionemhanc.en: And Moses said: I will go, and see this great sight.
dixitergomoysesvadametvidebovisionemhanc.la: Dixit ergo Móyses: Vadam, et vidébo visiónem hanc magnam.

cernensautemdominusquodpergeretadvidendu.en: And when the Lord saw that he went forward to see,
cernensautemdominusquodpergeretadvidendu.la: Cernens autem Dóminus quod pérgeret ad vidéndum,

vocaviteumdemediorubi.en: He called to him out of the midst of the bush.

neappropieshucsolvecalceamentumdepedibus.en: Come not nigh hither; put off the shoes from thy feet: for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground.
neappropieshucsolvecalceamentumdepedibus.la: Ne apprópies huc, solve calceaméntum de pédibus tuis: locus enim, in quo stas, terra sancta est.

cumapparueritprincepspastorumquopercusso.en: When the prince of pastors shall appear, at whose smiting the sheep of the flock were scattered,
cumapparueritprincepspastorumquopercusso.la: Cum apparúerit princeps pastórum, quo percússo, dispérsæ sunt oves gregis,

percipietisimmarcescibilemgloriecoronam.en: You shall receive a never-fading crown of glory.

cumfeceritgrandeconviviumutostendatdivit.en: When he shall make a great feast, to show the riches of the glory of his kingdom.
cumfeceritgrandeconviviumutostendatdivit.la: Cum fécerit grande convívium, ut osténdat divítias glóriæ regni sui.

balduinusconstantinopolitanusimperatorag.en: Baldwin, Emperor of Constantinople, while staying in France, told the holy King Louis that the nobles of Constantinople had come to such a pitch of want that they were forced to sell, or at least to pawn, the treasure of the Lord's Crown to strangers. He therefore asks the King to receive the Crown freely, rescued out of their hands, that it might redound to the glory of the Church of France.
balduinusconstantinopolitanusimperatorag.la: Balduínus, Constantinopolitánus imperátor, agens in Gállia, sancto regi Ludovíco rétulit primóres Constantinopolitános eo penúriæ devenísse, ut thesáurum Domínicæ Corónæ extráneis véndere‚ vel saltem oppigneráre cogeréntur. Itaque rogat regem, ut eréptam ab eórum mánibus Corónam gratis recípiat, ut céderet illa in decus Ecclésiæ Gállicæ.

ecceignisetlignadeusprovidebitsibi.en: Behold the fire and the wood: God will provide himself
ecceignisetlignadeusprovidebitsibi.la: Ecce ignis et ligna: Deus providébit sibi

levavitabrahamoculossuosviditquepostterg.en: Abraham lifted up his eyes, and saw behind his back a ram sticking fast among the briers.
levavitabrahamoculossuosviditquepostterg.la: Levávit Ábraham óculos suos, vidítque post tergum aríetem inter vepres hæréntem.

rexetreginamatersibietregnofrancieplurim.en: The King and the Queen Mother rejoiced greatly at this, for themselves and for the kingdom of France: and, sending two messengers of the Order of Preachers, James and Andrew, with others, and a special messenger of Baldwin, they sought back that incomparable treasure, which had already been pledged as security to the Venetians dwelling in Constantinople.
rexetreginamatersibietregnofrancieplurim.la: Rex et regina mater, sibi et regno Fránciæ plúrimum ob id gratulántur: atque missis duóbus núntiis ex Ordine Prædicatórum, Jacóbo et Andræa cum aliis, et speciáli Balduíni núntio, thesáurum illum incomparábilem, jam Vénetis intra Constantinópolim degéntibus nómine pígnoris obligátum, repetivérunt.

arcamdelignissetimdeaurabisauromundissim.en: Thou shalt overlay the ark of setim wood with the purest gold within and without:
arcamdelignissetimdeaurabisauromundissim.la: Arcam de lignis Setim deaurábis auro mundíssimo intus et foris:

faciesquesupracoronamaureampercircuitum.en: And over it thou shalt make a golden crown round about.
faciesquesupracoronamaureampercircuitum.la: Faciésque supra corónam áuream per circúitum.

ponesinarcatestificationemquamdabotibi.en: Thou shalt put in the ark the testimony which I will give thee.
ponesinarcatestificationemquamdabotibi.la: Pones in arca testificatiónem, quam dabo tibi.

coronaitaquesicutconventumfueratvenetias.en: The Crown therefore, as had been agreed, is carried to Venice, and by several messengers of the holy King, who received the vessel unbroken and the seals of the Greeks and of the Venetian nobles intact, it is redeemed, brought away, and through many perils of the roads conveyed into France. And it came to pass that over such long distances, though heavy rain often fell by night, not so much as a drop of rain touched them.
coronaitaquesicutconventumfueratvenetias.la: Coróna ítaque, sicut convéntum fúerat, Venétias defértur, et a plúribus sancti regis núntiis, qui vas illibátum, et sigílla Græcórum, atque Venetórum prócerum integra recepérunt; redímitur, edúcitur‚ et per multa viárum discrímina in Gálliam transfértur. Accidítque ut tam longis spátiis, cum sæpe nóctibus lárgior imber cecidísset, nullo modo eos vel plúviæ gutta contíngeret.

faciesaltareadadolendumthymiamadeligniss.en: Thou shalt make an altar to burn incense, of setim wood:
faciesaltareadadolendumthymiamadeligniss.la: Fácies altáre ad adoléndum thymíama de lignis Setim:

faciesqueeicoronamaureolampergyrum.en: And thou shalt make to it a golden crown round about.
faciesqueeicoronamaureolampergyrum.la: Faciésque ei corónam auréolam per gyrum.

ponesquealtarecontravelumcorampropitiato.en: And thou shalt set the altar over against the veil before the propitiatory.
ponesquealtarecontravelumcorampropitiato.la: Ponesque altáre contra velum coram propitiatório.

adveniunttrecasindequereginuntiantadvent.en: They come to Troyes, and thence announce their coming to the King. He, setting out to meet them with his mother, and the nobles, and two Bishops, Walter of Sens and Bernard of Le Puy, at Villeneuve-l'Archevêque, on the feast of St. Lawrence, opens the vessel itself, gazes upon that trophy with many sighs, and himself with his brother Robert, barefoot, bearing it upon their shoulders, carries the Lord's Crown of thorns into Paris, the Clergy and people coming to meet them. At length, a chapel having been built at the Palace, he laid it up there with the other emblems of the Lord's Passion and many relics of the Saints.
adveniunttrecasindequereginuntiantadvent.la: Advéniunt Trecas, índeque regi núntiant advéntum suum. Qui cum matre, et procéribus, et duóbus Epíscopis, Gualtéro Senonénsi‚ et Bernárdo Aniciénsi óbviam proféctus, apud Villam novam Archiepíscopi, vas ipsum sancti Lauréntii festo reclúdit‚ multis suspíriis trophæum illud cónspicit‚ atque ipse cum fratre Robérto, núdipes subjéctis húmeris Parisios Corónam Dómini spíneam infert, Clero et pópulo occurrénte. Demum ædificáto ad Palátium sacéllo, cum céteris Domínicæ Passiónis insígniis, et Sanctórum plúribus relíquiis, depósuit.

expressasignosanctitatisgloriahonoriseto.en: Wherein was engraved Holiness, an ornament of honour, and a work of power.
expressasignosanctitatisgloriahonoriseto.la: Expréssa signo sanctitátis, glória honóris et opus fortitúdinis.

inillotemporeapprehenditpilatusiesumetfl.en: At that time: Pilate took Jesus, and scourged him. And the soldiers platting a crown of thorns, put it upon his head. And the rest.
inillotemporeapprehenditpilatusiesumetfl.la: In illo témpore: Apprehéndit Pilátus Jesum, et flagellávit. Et mílites plecténtes corónam de spinis, imposuérunt cápiti ejus. Et réliqua.

militesquidemilludenteshocfaciuntutnudat.en: The soldiers indeed do this in mockery: having stripped him of his former garments, they clothe him in purple, which the kings of old used; and in place of a diadem they put on him a crown of thorns, in place of a royal sceptre they give him a reed, as Matthew writes, and they worship him as a king.
militesquidemilludenteshocfaciuntutnudat.la: Mílites quidem illudéntes hoc fáciunt, ut nudátum prístinis véstibus índuant púrpura, qua reges véteres utebántur: et pro diadémate impónunt ei corónam spíneam, pro sceptro regáli dant cálamum, ut Matthæus scribit, et adórant quasi regem.

accepitregnumdecoris.en: He hath received a kingdom of glory,

deusexaltavitillumetdeditillinomenquodes.en: God hath exalted him, and hath given him a name which is above every name.
deusexaltavitillumetdeditillinomenquodes.la: Deus exaltávit illum, et dedit illi nomen, quod est super omne nomen.

nosautemomniahecmysticeintelligamusquomo.en: But let us understand all these things mystically. For as Caiphas said: It is expedient that one man should die for the people, not knowing what he said: so these also, whatever they did, although they did it with another mind, yet were imparting sacraments to us who believe.
nosautemomniahecmysticeintelligamusquomo.la: Nos autem ómnia hæc mystice intelligámus. Quómodo enim Cáiphas dixit: Opórtet unum hóminem mori pro pópulo‚ nésciens quid díceret: sic et isti quodcúmque fecérunt, licet ália mente fécerint, tamen nobis, qui crédimus, sacraménta tribuébant.

coronanscoronavittetribulationedominus.en: The Lord hath crowned thee with a crown of tribulation:

sedcoronatribulationiseffloruitincoronam.en: But the crown of tribulation hath blossomed into a crown of glory, and a garland of gladness.
sedcoronatribulationiseffloruitincoronam.la: Sed coróna tribulatiónis efflóruit in corónam glóriæ, et sertum exultatiónis.

inilladiecantabiturcanticumistudinterrai.en: In that day shall this canticle be sung in the land of Juda.
inilladiecantabiturcanticumistudinterrai.la: In illa die cantábitur cánticum istud in terra Juda.

mysticeergoinpurpuraquaindutusestipseius.en: Mystically, therefore, in the purple wherewith he was clothed is signified his very flesh, which he exposed to sufferings; of which the Prophet had said: Why then is thy apparel red, and thy garments like theirs that tread in the winepress? And in the crown of thorns which he bore is shown the taking upon himself of our sins, for which he vouchsafed to become mortal.
mysticeergoinpurpuraquaindutusestipseius.la: Mystice ergo in púrpura qua indútus est, ipsa ejus caro, quam passiónibus objécit, insinuátur; de qua díxerat Prophéta: Quare ergo rubrum est induméntum tuum, et vestiménta tua quasi calcántium tórcular? In coróna vero spínea, quam portábat, nostrórum suscéptio peccatórum, pro qua mortális fíeri dignátus est, osténditur.

gravastisupermemanumtuam.en: Thou hast laid thy hand heavy upon me,

etspiniscoronastimeconversussuminerumnam.en: And hast crowned me with thorns; I am turned in my anguish, whilst the thorn is fastened.
etspiniscoronastimeconversussuminerumnam.la: Et spinis coronásti me, convérsus sum in ærúmna mea, dum confígitur spina.

positurussupercaputmeumcoronamdelapidepr.en: Being about to set upon my head a crown of precious stones,
positurussupercaputmeumcoronamdelapidepr.la: Positúrus super caput meum corónam de lápide pretióso,

iuxtaquodeiusprecursordixitecceagnusdeie.en: According to what his forerunner said: Behold the Lamb of God, behold him who taketh away the sins of the world: for that thorns are wont to be set for a sign of sins the Lord himself testifieth, who said to the first-formed man when he had fallen into sin: Thy land shall bring forth thorns and thistles to thee; which is to say plainly: Thy conscience shall not cease to bring forth for thee the prickings and stings of vices.
iuxtaquodeiusprecursordixitecceagnusdeie.la: Juxta quod ejus præcúrsor dixit: Ecce Agnus Dei, ecce qui tollit peccáta mundi: namque spinas in significatióne peccatórum poni solére testátur ipse Dóminus, qui protoplásto in peccátum prolápso, dicébat: Terra tua spinas et tríbulos germinábit tibi; quod est apérte dícere: Consciéntia tua punctiónes tibi, et acúleos vitiórum procreáre non desístet.

christussciensdoloremetinfirmitatemspini.en: Christ, acquainted with sorrow and infirmity, crowned with thorns,
christussciensdoloremetinfirmitatemspini.la: Christus sciens dolórem et infirmitátem, spinis coronátus,

ipseestquicoronatvosinmisericordietmiser.en: It is he that crowneth you with mercy and compassion.
ipseestquicoronatvosinmisericordietmiser.la: Ipse est qui corónat vos in misericórdia et miseratiónibus.

vulneratuspropteriniquitatesnostrasattri.en: Wounded for our iniquities, bruised for our sins, by whose bruises we are healed.
vulneratuspropteriniquitatesnostrasattri.la: Vulnerátus propter iniquitátes nostras, attrítus propter scélera nostra, cujus Hvore sanáti sumus.

egrediminietvidetefiliesionregemsalomone.en: Go forth, ye daughters of Sion, and see King Solomon in the diadem, * wherewith his mother crowned him.
egrediminietvidetefiliesionregemsalomone.la: Egredímini et vidéte fíliæ Sion regem Salomónem in diadémate, * quo coronávit eum mater sua.

tuamcoronamadoramusdomine.en: Thy Crown * We adore, O Lord.

tuamgloriosamrecolimuspassionem.en: Thy glorious passion we call to mind.

legisfigurispingitur.en: In the figures of the Law is painted

ardensquetestaturrubus.en: And the burning Bush bear witness.

arcamcoronacinxerat.en: A Crown had girt the Ark,

mensequesacrumcirculum.en: And the sacred circle of the Table,

aramquethurefumidam.en: And the altar smoking with incense

christidolorumconscia.en: Thou that knewest the sorrows of Christ,

vincenscoronassiderum.en: Surpassing the Crowns of the stars.

exivitiesusportansspineamcoronametpurpur.en: Jesus came forth * bearing the Crown of thorns, and the purple garment.
exivitiesusportansspineamcoronametpurpur.la: Exívit Jesus * portans spíneam Corónam, et purpúreum vestiméntum.

vidietecceequusalbusetquisedebatsuperill.en: I saw: and behold a white horse, § and he that sat on him had a bow, * and there was a crown given him, § and he went forth conquering that he might conquer.
vidietecceequusalbusetquisedebatsuperill.la: Vidi: et ecce equus albus, § et qui sedébat super illum habébat arcum, * et data est ei coróna, § et exívit vincens ut vínceret.

inilladieeritdominusexercituumcoronaglor.en: In that day the Lord of hosts shall be a crown of glory, * and a garland of joy to the residue of his people.
inilladieeritdominusexercituumcoronaglor.la: In illa die erit Dóminus exercítuum coróna glóriæ, * et sertum exaltatiónis resíduo pópuli sui.

etgenuflexoanteeumilludebanteidicentesav.en: And bowing the knee * before him, they mocked him, saying: Hail, King of the Jews: and spitting upon him, they took the reed, and struck his head.
etgenuflexoanteeumilludebanteidicentesav.la: Et genu flexo * ante eum, illudébant ei, dicéntes: Ave Rex Judæórum: et expuéntes in eum accepérunt arúndinem, et percutiébant caput ejus.

claravirgoassisiafranciscumconcivemsuumi.en: Clare, a virgin of Assisi, imitating Francis her fellow citizen, lived with wonderful holiness in the community of sisters which she founded. When the Saracens were besieging the city and trying to break into the Monastery, she obtained by her prayers that, at a voice heard from heaven, some of them took to flight, and others fell headlong from the wall.
claravirgoassisiafranciscumconcivemsuumi.la: Clara virgo Assísia, Francíscum concívem suum imitáta, in sorórum Collégio quod instítuit, admirábili vixit sanctitáte. Saracénis urbem obsidéntibus, et Monastérium invádere conántibus, précibus obtínuit, ut voce de cœlo exaudíta, partim se fugæ mandáverint, partim ex muro præcípites cecíderint.

ipsavirgoieiuniisorationibusacvigiliisco.en: The virgin herself, worn out with fastings, prayers and vigils, after she had governed the Monastery with the highest praise for forty-two years and wrought many miracles, on the day before the Ides of August, having received the holy Eucharist, gave up her soul to God, in the pontificate of Innocent the Fourth: and Alexander the Fourth numbered her among the holy Virgins.
ipsavirgoieiuniisorationibusacvigiliisco.la: Ipsa virgo jejúniis, oratiónibus, ac vigíliis confécta, cum duóbus et quadragínta annis summa cum laude Monastérium gubernásset, multáque edidísset mirácula, prídie Idus Augusti, sacra Eucharistía sumpta, ánimam Deo réddidit, Innocéntio quarto Summo Pontífice: quam Alexánder quartus inter sanctas Vírgines rétulit.

responsoriumbeatesvirgomariadeigenitrixq.en: Responsory. Blessed art thou, O Virgin Mary, Mother of God, who didst believe the Lord: those things are accomplished in thee that were spoken to thee: behold, thou art exalted above the choirs of Angels: * Intercede for us with the Lord our God.
responsoriumbeatesvirgomariadeigenitrixq.la: Responsorium. Beáta es, Virgo María, Dei Génitrix, quæ credidísti Dómino: perfécta sunt in te quæ dicta sunt tibi: ecce exaltáta es super choros Angelórum: * Intercéde pro nobis ad Dóminum Deum nostrum.

avemariagratiaplenadominustecum.en: Hail Mary, full of grace: the Lord is with thee.
avemariagratiaplenadominustecum.la: Ave María, grátia plena: Dóminus tecum.

intercedepronobisaddominumdeumnostrum.en: Plead for us with the Lord our God.
intercedepronobisaddominumdeumnostrum.la: Intercéde pro nobis ad Dóminum Deum nostrum.

ascenditchristussupercelosetpreparavitsu.en: Christ ascended * above the heavens, and prepared for his most chaste Mother a place of immortality; and this is that glorious festival, beyond compare with the festivals of all the Saints, on which, glorious and happy, while the orders of the heavenly court marvelled, she came to the heavenly bridal chamber, where in her loving-kindness she is in no wise unmindful of those who are mindful of her.
ascenditchristussupercelosetpreparavitsu.la: Ascéndit Christus * super cœlos, et præparávit suæ castíssimæ Matri immortalitátis locum; et hæc est illa præclára festívitas ómnium Sanctórum festivitátibus incomparábilis, in qua gloriósa et felix, mirántibus cœléstis cúriæ ordínibus, ad æthéreum pervénit thálamum, quo pia sui mémorum ímmemor nequáquam exístat.

etsicinsionfirmatasumetincivitatesanctif.en: And so was I established in Sion, and in the holy city likewise I rested, and my power was in Jerusalem. And I took root in an honourable people, and in the portion of my God his inheritance, and my abode is in the full assembly of saints.
etsicinsionfirmatasumetincivitatesanctif.la: Et sic in Sion firmáta sum, et in civitáte sanctificáta simíliter requiévi, et in Jerúsalem potéstas mea. Et radicávi in pópulo honorificáto, et in parte Dei mei heréditas illíus, et in plenitúdine sanctórum deténtio mea.

inplateissicutcinnamomumetbalsamumaromat.en: In the streets I gave a sweet smell like cinnamon and aromatical balm: I yielded a sweet odour like the best myrrh.
inplateissicutcinnamomumetbalsamumaromat.la: In platéis sicut cinnamómum et bálsamum aromatízans odórem dedi: quasi myrrha elécta, dedi suavitátem odóris.

totapulchresamicameetmaculanonestintefav.en: Thou art all fair, * O my love, and there is not a spot in thee: thy lips are as a dropping honeycomb, honey and milk are under thy tongue, the odour of thy ointments is above all aromatical spices: for winter is now past, the rain is over and gone, the flowers have appeared, the flourishing vines have yielded their sweet smell, and the voice of the turtle is heard in our land: arise, make haste, my love, come from Libanus, come, thou shalt be crowned.
totapulchresamicameetmaculanonestintefav.la: Tota pulchra es, * amíca mea, et mácula non est in te: favus distíllans lábia tua, mel et lac sub lingua tua, odor unguentórum tuórum super ómnia arómata: jam enim hiems tránsiit, imber ábiit et recéssit, flores apparuérunt, víneæ floréntes odórem dedérunt, et vox túrturis audíta est in terra nostra: surge, própera amíca mea, veni de Líbano, veni, coronáberis.

paradisiportaperevamcunctisclausestetper.en: The gate of Paradise * was shut to all men by Eve, and by the Virgin Mary it hath been opened again, alleluia.
paradisiportaperevamcunctisclausestetper.la: Paradísi porta * per Evam cunctis clausa est, et per Maríam Vírginem íterum patefácta est, allelúia.

viderunteamfiliesionetbeatissimampredica.en: The daughters of Sion saw her, and declared her most blessed: * and the queens praised her.
viderunteamfiliesionetbeatissimampredica.la: Vidérunt eam fíliæ Sion, et beatíssimam prædicavérunt: * et regínæ laudavérunt eam.

beatusbernardusabinfantiaspiritumsortitu.en: Blessed Bernard * from his infancy received a good spirit, whereby he was a docile child and very lovable.
beatusbernardusabinfantiaspiritumsortitu.la: Beátus Bernárdus * ab infántia spíritum sortítus est bonum, per quem erat puer docílis, et amábilis valde.

indisciplinamorumprofectuquevirtutumsupe.en: In discipline of manners * and in progress in virtues he soon outshone his teachers, with the anointing for his master.
indisciplinamorumprofectuquevirtutumsupe.la: In disciplína morum * profectúque virtútum super docéntes se in brevi enítuit unctióne magístra.

crescenteetatecrescebatsimulsapientietgr.en: As his age increased, * there increased together wisdom and grace with God and men.
crescenteetatecrescebatsimulsapientietgr.la: Crescénte ætáte * crescébat simul sapiéntia, et grátia apud Deum, et hómines.

hodiepositocorporepatersanctusdivesmerit.en: Today, * having laid aside the body, the holy Father, rich in merits, hath entered into the holy place, made like to the Saints in glory.
hodiepositocorporepatersanctusdivesmerit.la: Hódie, * pósito córpore, Pater sanctus, dives méritis penetrávit in sancta, símilis factus in glória Sanctórum.

beatusbernardusquasivasaurisolidumornatu.en: Blessed Bernard, like a vessel of massy gold, adorned with every precious stone, poured out to the people the streams of grace:
beatusbernardusquasivasaurisolidumornatu.la: Beátus Bernárdus quasi vas auri sólidum, ornátum omni lápide pretióso, fluénta grátiæ propinávit in pópulo:

etaccepitstolamglorieinconsummationevirt.en: And he received the robe of glory in the perfection of virtue.
etaccepitstolamglorieinconsummationevirt.la: Et accépit stolam glóriæ in consummatióne virtútis.

factusestquasiigniseffulgensetquasithusr.en: He became like a shining fire, and like frankincense giving forth its fragrance in the days of summer:
factusestquasiigniseffulgensetquasithusr.la: Factus est quasi ignis effúlgens, et quasi thus rédolens in diébus æstátis:

splendorpaterneglorie.en: The Brightness of the Father's glory.

splendorpaternegloriehymnusadlaudesdomin.en: The Brightness of the Father's glory: Hymn at Sunday Lauds, when the nights are longer.
splendorpaternegloriehymnusadlaudesdomin.la: Splendor patérnæ glóriæ: Hymnus ad Laudes Dominicales, quando noctes longiores.

quemconiungiscelestibus.en: Whom thou joinest to the heavenly ones,

exultetcelumlaudibushymnusadvesperasapos.en: Let heaven exult with praises: Hymn at Vespers of the Apostles. O Jesu, our redemption: Hymn for the Ascension of the Lord.
exultetcelumlaudibushymnusadvesperasapos.la: Exúltet cœlum laudibus: Hymnus ad Vesperas Apostolorum. Jesu nostra redémptio. Hymnus ad Ascensionem Domini.

rufumdorsopercatulum.en: By a whelp with a red back

prefigurastipuerum.en: Thou didst foreshow that the boy

conditoralmesiderum.en: O kindly Creator of the stars.

conditoralmesiderumhymnusadvesperasadven.en: O kindly Creator of the stars: Hymn at Vespers of Advent.
conditoralmesiderumhymnusadvesperasadven.la: Cónditor alme síderum. Hymnus ad Vesperas Adventus.

nascentiseiclaruit.en: To him at his birth shone forth

hocatedonumhabuit.en: This gift he had from thee,

oluxbeatatrinitashymnusadsstrinitatemqui.en: O Light, blessed Trinity: Hymn to the Most Holy Trinity, which is also sung on the “green” Saturdays.
oluxbeatatrinitashymnusadsstrinitatemqui.la: O lux beáta Trínitas. Hymnus ad SS. Trinitatem, qui quoque in Sabbatis “viridibus” canitur.

arcanasacrepagine.en: The secrets of the sacred page

quodeffecitinvirgine.en: Which he wrought in the Virgin,

deuscreatoromnium.en: O God, Creator of all things.

deuscreatoromniumhymnusadvesperasdominic.en: O God, Creator of all things: Hymn at Sunday Vespers, when the nights are longer.
deuscreatoromniumhymnusadvesperasdominic.la: Deus Creátor ómnium. Hymnus ad Vesperas Dominicales, quando noctes longiores.

roreperfusumgratie.en: Steeped in the dew of grace

monstratdulcoreloquii.en: The sweetness of his speech showeth him:

pertefonssapientie.en: Through thee, O fount of wisdom,

summilargitorpremiihymnusadvigiliasquadr.en: Bestower of the highest reward: Hymn at Matins of Lent.
summilargitorpremiihymnusadvigiliasquadr.la: Summi largítor præmii. Hymnus ad Vigilias Quadragesimæ.

sanatmorboslanguentium.en: He healeth, the diseases of the languishing

curatconfertdolentibus.en: He cureth, he bringeth to the sorrowing

magnumsalutisgaudiumhymnusadprocessionem.en: The great joy of salvation: Hymn for the Procession of Palm Sunday.
magnumsalutisgaudiumhymnusadprocessionem.la: Magnum salútis gaudium. Hymnus ad Processionem Dominicæ Palmarum.

cummariachristifera.en: With Mary, the bearer of Christ,

eternachristimunerahymnusadvigiliasapost.en: The eternal gifts of Christ: Hymn at Matins of the Apostles.
eternachristimunerahymnusadvigiliasapost.la: Ætérna Christi múnera. Hymnus ad Vigilias Apostolorum.

tibisitlausetgloria.en: To thee be praise and glory:

dapostcursummiserie.en: Grant after the course of misery

beatanobisgaudiahymnusadlaudespentecoste.en: Blessed joys to us: Hymn at Lauds of Pentecost.
beatanobisgaudiahymnusadlaudespentecoste.la: Beáta nobis gáudia. Hymnus ad Laudes Pentecostes.

orapronobisbeatebernarde.en: Pray for us, O blessed Bernard.

magnificavitsanctumsuumdominusetdeditill.en: The Lord hath magnified * his Saint, and hath given him the knowledge of the Saints, that his works might be accomplished unto good, and the peace of God be upon him for ever.
magnificavitsanctumsuumdominusetdeditill.la: Magnificávit * Sanctum suum Dóminus, et dedit illi sciéntiam Sanctórum, ut consummaréntur in bonum ópera ejus, et pax Dei super eum in ætérnum.
