perficequesumusdominepiuminnobissanctere.en: Perfect in us, we beseech thee, O Lord, the devout affection of holy religion: * and, that we may obtain the bounty of thy grace, § may blessed Bernard, Abbot and illustrious Doctor, ever intercede for us with thee by his merits and prayers.
perficequesumusdominepiuminnobissanctere.la: Pérfice, quæsumus Dómine, pium in nobis sanctæ religiónis afféctum: * et ad obtinéndam tuæ grátiæ largitátem, § beátus Bernárdus, Abbas et Doctor egrégius, suis apud te semper pro nobis méritis et précibus intercédat.

inconfessionelaudisadoremusdominumquisto.en: In the confession of praise let us adore the Lord, * Who hath adorned his Confessor Bernard with the robe of glory.
inconfessionelaudisadoremusdominumquisto.la: In confessióne laudis adorémus Dóminum, * Qui stola glóriæ Confessórem suum decorávit Bernárdum.

preclarusmeritiscumclarisfratribus.en: Renowned in merits, with his noble brothers

fugitinabditispaternisopibus.en: Fleeth into hidden places, his father's riches

spretisetmundiflosculo.en: Spurned, and the fading flower of the world.

latratorstrenuussanctusexutero.en: A strenuous barker, holy from the womb,

doctorprecipuusnectaresupero.en: A foremost Doctor, with nectar from above:

vigilassiduussubsalutifero.en: A constant watchman, under a saving

monstraturmatricatulo.en: Whelp is he shown to his mother.

tardantvigiliedormitadostium.en: The Vigils are delayed; he sleepeth at the door.

moxventermarieproducitfilium.en: Straightway Mary's womb bringeth forth the Son.

laudishomilieprovocantstudium.en: They stir his zeal for the homilies of praise.

datpuernummosclanculo.en: The boy giveth coins in secret.

pulsantefeminalatronesclamitat.en: When a woman knocketh, he crieth out: Thieves!

defixaluminastagnoprecipitat.en: For his fixed gaze he plungeth into the pool:

abhorretcarminaluxumsuppeditat.en: He shunneth songs, he treadeth down wantonness,

iacteceditinlectulo.en: He giveth place to her who cast herself into his bed.

sitlausingenitodecusetgloria.en: Praise be to the Unbegotten, honour and glory,
sitlausingenitodecusetgloria.la: Sit laus Ingénito, decus et glória,

abunigenitositreisvenia.en: From the Only-begotten be pardon to the guilty:

vievirisanctiviepulchreetomnessemiteeius.en: The ways of the holy man * are beautiful ways, and all his paths are peaceable, for he hath laid hold on the tree of life.
vievirisanctiviepulchreetomnessemiteeius.la: Viæ viri sancti * viæ pulchræ, et omnes sémitæ ejus pacíficæ, quia lignum vitæ apprehéndit. Ps. 1

semitasiustitieviasquesanctorumcustodien.en: Keeping the paths of justice * and the ways of the Saints, the blessed man finished the course of his life in peace.
semitasiustitieviasquesanctorumcustodien.la: Sémitas justítiæ * viásque Sanctórum custódiens Vir beátus, cursum vitæ in pace consummávit. Ps. 2

benedictiodominisupercaputiustimemorieiu.en: The blessing of the Lord * is upon the head of the just; his memory is for ever and ever.
benedictiodominisupercaputiustimemorieiu.la: Benedíctio Dómini * super caput justi, memória ejus in sæcula sæculórum. Ps. 4

consurgensdiluculoquesivitbonapatersanct.en: Rising * early, the holy Father sought good things; like a blooming lily he blossomed.
consurgensdiluculoquesivitbonapatersanct.la: Consúrgens * dilúculo quæsívit bona Pater sanctus, quasi florens lílium germinávit. Ps. 5

intestamentispacisstetitsemenilliusetusq.en: In the covenants of peace * his seed hath stood, and his glory abideth even for ever.
intestamentispacisstetitsemenilliusetusq.la: In testaméntis pacis * stetit semen illíus, et usque in ætérnum pérmanet glória ejus. Ps. 8

exaltavitdominusineternumcornuchristisui.en: The Lord hath exalted * for ever the horn of his anointed, and hath given him the covenant of life, and the seat of his glory.
exaltavitdominusineternumcornuchristisui.la: Exaltávit Dóminus * in ætérnum cornu Christi sui, et dedit illi testaméntum vitæ, et sedem glóriæ suæ. Ps. 10

quasiolivapullulansetcypressusinaltitudi.en: As an olive tree * budding forth, and a cypress tree rearing itself on high: so the blessed man ascended to the glory of holiness.
quasiolivapullulansetcypressusinaltitudi.la: Quasi olíva * púllulans, et cypréssus in altitúdine se tollens: sic Vir beátus ad glóriam sanctitátis ascéndit. Ps. 14

porrexitmanumsuamvirsanctusinlibationema.en: The holy man stretched forth * his hand to the libation of the Altar, and of the blood of the grape poured out a divine odour to the most high Prince.
porrexitmanumsuamvirsanctusinlibationema.la: Porréxit * manum suam Vir sanctus in libatiónem Altáris, et de sánguine uvæ effúdit odórem divínum excélso Príncipi. Ps. 20

ampliavitgentemsuamviriustusadeptusglori.en: The just man enlarged * his nation, having gained glory in his way of life.
ampliavitgentemsuamviriustusadeptusglori.la: Ampliávit * gentem suam vir justus, adéptus glóriam in conversatióne ejus. Ps. 23

honoravitdeumvirsanctusinoperibussuiseti.en: The holy man honoured * God in his works, and was received by him with delight.
honoravitdeumvirsanctusinoperibussuiseti.la: Honorávit * Deum Vir sanctus in opéribus suis, et in oblectatióne suscéptus est ab eo. Ps. 63

extulitmanussuaspatervenerabilisdareglor.en: The venerable Father lifted up * his hands to give glory to God with his lips, and to glory in his name.
extulitmanussuaspatervenerabilisdareglor.la: Extulit * manus suas Pater venerábilis dare glóriam Deo a lábiis suis, et in nómine ipsíus gloriári. Ps. 64

deditdominussanctosuoiucunditatemcordisf.en: The Lord gave * to his Saint joyfulness of heart, that there should be peace in his days among the people of God.
deditdominussanctosuoiucunditatemcordisf.la: Dedit Dóminus * Sancto suo jucunditátem cordis, fíeri pacem diébus suis in pópulo Dei. Ps. 91

replevitsanctumsuumdominusspirituintelli.en: The Lord filled * his Saint with the spirit of understanding, and he ministered the streams of doctrine to the people of God.
replevitsanctumsuumdominusspirituintelli.la: Replévit * Sanctum suum Dóminus spíritu intelligéntiæ, et ipse fluénta doctrínæ ministrávit pópulo Dei. Ps. 256, 257, 258

primavirtusvirisanctihabituscorporissuiq.en: The first virtue of the holy man was the bearing of his body, which he carried so composedly and ever in one manner:
primavirtusvirisanctihabituscorporissuiq.la: Prima virtus viri sancti, hábitus córporis sui, quod ita compósite, et uno semper modo agébat:

utnilappareretineoquodpossetoffendereint.en: That nothing appeared in him which could offend those who beheld him.
utnilappareretineoquodpossetoffendereint.la: Ut nil apparéret in eo , quod posset offéndere intuéntes.

totumineodisciplinatumtotuminsignevirtut.en: All in him was disciplined, all was a mark of virtue, a pattern of perfection.
totumineodisciplinatumtotuminsignevirtut.la: Totum in eo disciplinátum, totum insígne virtútis, perfectiónis forma.

virtutemultetscientiapreditussanctusdeip.en: Endowed with great virtue and knowledge, the Saint of God drew nigh to the dignity of the Saints,
virtutemultetscientiapreditussanctusdeip.la: Virtúte multa, et sciéntia præditus Sanctus Dei proximábat dignitáti Sanctórum,

cumfructuoperumproferenscelestissapienti.en: Uttering, with the fruit of works, the words of heavenly wisdom.
cumfructuoperumproferenscelestissapienti.la: Cum fructu óperum próferens cœléstis sapiéntiæ verba.

apueritiarequisivitauctoremviteetanimumd.en: From childhood he sought the Author of life, and gave his mind to the words of God:
apueritiarequisivitauctoremviteetanimumd.la: A puerítia requisívit Auctórem vitæ , et ánimum dedit ad elóquia Dei:

operasanctipatrisvelutsolinconspectudei.en: The works of the holy Father are as the sun in the sight of God:
operasanctipatrisvelutsolinconspectudei.la: Opera sancti Patris velut sol in conspéctu Dei :

etoculieiussineintermissionerespiciebant.en: And his eyes were continually upon his ways.
etoculieiussineintermissionerespiciebant.la: Et óculi ejus sine intermissióne respiciébant in vias ejus.

nonsuntabsconditaabeotestamentadei.en: The testaments of God are not hidden from him:
nonsuntabsconditaabeotestamentadei.la: Non sunt abscóndita ab eo testaménta Dei:

intimoredeipatrissanctigloriatietinsensu.en: In the fear of God is the glory of the holy Father, and in his mind are the thoughts of God:
intimoredeipatrissanctigloriatietinsensu.la: In timóre Dei , Patris sancti gloriátio , et in sensu ejus cogitátus Dei:

etomnisnarratieiusinpreceptisaltissimi.en: And all his discourse is in the commandments of the Most High.
etomnisnarratieiusinpreceptisaltissimi.la: Et omnis narrátio ejus in præcéptis Altíssimi.

pastorpopulideifactusestinsapientiasermo.en: He was made shepherd of the people of God in the wisdom of sacred speech.
pastorpopulideifactusestinsapientiasermo.la: Pastor pópuli Dei factus est in sapiéntia sermónis sacri.

bernardusfontanisinburgundianobililocona.en: Bernard, born of a noble family at Fontaines in Burgundy, being as a youth, because of his remarkable comeliness, vehemently solicited by women, could never be moved from his resolve to keep chastity. When about twenty-two years of age, he determined to enter the Cistercian Monastery. His brothers strove with all their might to deter him from this purpose: wherein he himself was the more eloquent and the more successful. For he so brought them and many others round to his mind, that more than thirty companions embraced the same Religious life with him.
bernardusfontanisinburgundianobililocona.la: Bernárdus Fontánis in Burgúndia nóbili loco natus, adoléscens propter egrégiam formam veheménter sollicitátus a muliéribus, numquam de senténtia coléndæ castitátis dimovéri pótuit. Duos et vigínti círciter annos natus, Monastérium Cisterciénse ingrédi constítuit. Quem fratres summópere conáti sunt a propósito deterrére: in quo ipse eloquéntior ac felícior suit. Nam sic eos aliósque multos in suam perdúxít senténtiam‚ ut cum eo plusquam trigínta sócii eamdem Religiónem suscéperint.

oodoriferumliliumspargensubiquevivificum.en: O fragrant lily, spreading everywhere the life-giving odour of sweetness:
oodoriferumliliumspargensubiquevivificum.la: O odoríferum lílium spargens ubíque vivíficum suavitátis odórem:

cuiusapudnosmemoriainbenedictioneapudsup.en: Whose memory with us is in benediction, whose presence with them above is in honour.
cuiusapudnosmemoriainbenedictioneapudsup.la: Cujus apud nos memória in benedictióne, apud súperos præséntia in honóre.

faccanentestetanteplenitudinisparticipio.en: Grant that we who sing of thee be not deprived of a share in so great a fulness:
faccanentestetanteplenitudinisparticipio.la: Fac canéntes te tantæ plenitúdinis particípio non privári:

monasticohabitususceptoinieiuniisvigilii.en: Having taken the monastic habit, he exercised himself wonderfully in fastings, watchings and prayers: and cultivating Christian poverty, he led as it were a heavenly life on earth, estranged from all care and desire of perishable things. There shone forth in him a wondrous humility, an unspeakable mercy, the greatest kindness. And he was so given to contemplation, that he scarcely used his senses, save for the duties of piety: in which nevertheless he excelled in the praise of prudence.
monasticohabitususceptoinieiuniisvigilii.la: Monástico hábitu suscépto, in jejúniis, vigíliis et oratiónibus mirífice se exercébat: et Christiánam paupertátem colens, quasi cœléstem vitam agébat in terris, ab omni caducárum rerum cura et cupiditáte aliénam. Elucébat in eo mira humílitas, ineffábilis misericórdia, summa benígnitas. Contemplatióni autem sic addíctus erat, ut vix sénsibus, nisi ad offícia pietátis, uterétur: in quibus tamen prudéntiæ laude excellébat.

accepitvirsanctusadominopotestateminprec.en: The holy man received from the Lord power in the commandments, to teach his subjects the testimonies of truth:
accepitvirsanctusadominopotestateminprec.la: Accépit vir sanctus a Dómino potestatem in præcéptis, testimónia veritátis docére súbditos:

etinlegedeilucemdarepopulo.en: And in the law of God to give light to the people.
etinlegedeilucemdarepopulo.la: Et in lege Dei lucem dare pópulo.

addiditeigloriamdominushereditatempacisp.en: The Lord added glory unto him, to possess the inheritance of peace for ever:
addiditeigloriamdominushereditatempacisp.la: Addidit ei glóriam Dóminus, hæreditátem pacis possidére in ætérnum:

quoinstudiooccupatusadedificandumclareva.en: While he was occupied in this pursuit, he was sent with some Monks to build the Monastery of Clairvaux, and was set over them as Abbot. In many other places he built Monasteries. He refused the Bishoprics of Genoa and Milan, and others that were offered him, professing himself unworthy of the burden of so great an office. He wrote many things in a style altogether incomparable, wherein it appeareth that he was instructed by a learning given from God rather than gained by labour.
quoinstudiooccupatusadedificandumclareva.la: Quo in stúdio occupátus, ad ædificándum Clarævallénse Cœnóbium, cum nonnúllis Mónachis míttitur, eísque Abbas præfícitur. Multis áliis in locis ædificávit Monastéria. Genuénsem ac Mediolanénsem, aliísque Episcopátus oblátos recusávit, proféssus se tanti offícii múnere indígnum esse. Multa stilo prorsus incomparábili scripsit‚ in quibus appáret, eum doctrína pótius divinítus trádita, quam labóre comparáta, instrúctum fuísse.

lexveritatisinorepatrissancti.en: The law of truth was in the mouth of the holy Father:
lexveritatisinorepatrissancti.la: Lex veritátis in ore Patris sancti:

etiniquitasnonestinventainlabiiseius.en: And iniquity was not found in his lips.
etiniquitasnonestinventainlabiiseius.la: Et iníquitas non est invénta in lábiis ejus.

inpaceetequitateambulavitcoramdeo.en: He walked before God in peace and equity:
inpaceetequitateambulavitcoramdeo.la: In pace et æquitáte ambulávit coram Deo:

insummavirtutumlaudeexoratusamaximisprin.en: Being in the highest repute for virtue, he was entreated by the greatest princes concerning the settling of their disputes, and concerning the ordering of Ecclesiastical affairs, and he came often into Italy. He gave eminent help to the Supreme Pontiff Innocent the Second in overcoming the schism of Peter Leonis, both with the Emperor and with Henry King of England, and in the Council assembled at Pisa. At length, at sixty-three years of age, he fell asleep in the Lord, and, being famous for miracles, he was enrolled among the Saints by Pope Alexander the Third. And Pius the Eighth, Supreme Pontiff, on the advice of the Congregation of Sacred Rites, declared and confirmed Saint Bernard Doctor of the universal Church, and also commanded that the Mass and Office of Doctors be recited by all, and granted plenary indulgences every year in perpetuity to those who visit the churches of the Cistercian Order on the feast day of this Saint.
insummavirtutumlaudeexoratusamaximisprin.la: In summa virtútum laude exorátus a máximís princípibus de eórum componéndis controvérsiis, et de Ecclesiásticis rebus constituéndis, sæpius in Itáliam venit. Innocéntium secúndum Pontíficem Máximum in confutándo schísmate Petri Leónis, tum apud Imperatórem, et Henrícum Angliæ regem, tum in Concílio Pisis coácto, egrégie adjúvít. Dénique tres et sexagínta annos natus obdormívit in Dómino, ac miráculis illústris, ab Alexándro tértio Papa inter Sanctos relátus est. Pius vero octávus Póntifex Máximus ex Sacrórum Rítuum Congregatiónis consílio sanctum Bernárdum universális Ecclésiæ Doctórem declarávit‚ et confirmávit, nec non Missam, et Offícium de Doctóribus ab ómnibus recitári jussit, atque indulgéntias Plenárias quotánnis in perpétuum Ordinis Cisterciénsium ecclésias visitántibus die hujus Sancti festo concéssit.

testamentumeternumcumbeatopatrebernardoc.en: The Lord made an everlasting covenant with the blessed Father Bernard:
testamentumeternumcumbeatopatrebernardoc.la: Testamentum ætérnum cum beáto Patre Bernárdo constítuit Dóminus:

etiustitiamaciudiciasuaostenditilli.en: And shewed him his justice and his judgments.
etiustitiamaciudiciasuaostenditilli.la: Et justítiam, ac judícia sua osténdit illi.

magnaliahonorisdeividitoculuseius.en: His eye saw the majesty of the glory of God:
magnaliahonorisdeividitoculuseius.la: Magnália honóris Dei vidit óculus ejus:

fortesapientiaasaporedenominaturquodvirt.en: Perhaps wisdom (sapientia) is named from savour (sapor), because, coming to virtue as a kind of seasoning, it maketh savoury that which of itself was felt to be in some way insipid and harsh. Nor would I think him to be blamed, who should define wisdom as the savour of good. This savour we lost almost from the very beginning of our race. From the time that the poison of the old serpent infected the palate of the heart, the sense of the flesh prevailing, the soul began to have no savour of good, and a noxious savour crept in.
fortesapientiaasaporedenominaturquodvirt.la: Forte sapiéntia a sapóre denominátur, quod virtúti accédens quoddam véluti condiméntum, sápidam reddat, quæ per se insúlsa quodámmodo et áspera sentiebátur. Nec dúxerim reprehendéndum, si quis sapiéntiam sapórem boni defíniat. Hunc sapórem perdídimus ab ipso pene exórtu géneris nostri. Ex quo cordis palátum sensu carnis prævalénte infécit virus serpéntis antíqui, cœpit ánimæ non sápere bonum, ac sapor nóxius subintráre.

oolivafructiferaindomodeiooleumletitiefo.en: O fruitful olive in the house of God! O oil of gladness, cherishing with benefits, shining with miracles!
oolivafructiferaindomodeiooleumletitiefo.la: O olíva fructífera in domo Dei! o óleum lætítiæ fovens benefíciis, corúscans miráculis!

facnoseiusquafruerislucissuavitatisquepa.en: Make us partakers of the light and sweetness which thou enjoyest.
facnoseiusquafruerislucissuavitatisquepa.la: Fac nos ejus, qua frúeris lucis, suavitatísque partícipes.

introistiinpotentiasdominietiampotentior.en: Thou hast entered into the powers of the Lord, and now art more powerful to obtain.
introistiinpotentiasdominietiampotentior.la: Introísti in poténtias Dómini, et jam poténtior ad impetrándum.

nuncassiduesapientiavincitmalitiaminment.en: Now wisdom continually overcometh malice in the minds which it hath entered, driving out with a better savour the savour of evil which malice brought in; wisdom entering, while it maketh foolish the sense of the flesh, purifieth the understanding, healeth and restoreth the palate of the heart. The palate being healed, now good hath savour, wisdom itself hath savour, than which in good things there is nothing better.
nuncassiduesapientiavincitmalitiaminment.la: Nunc assídue sapiéntia vincit malítiam in méntibus‚ ad quas intráverit, sapórem mali, quem illa invéxit‚ sapóre extérminans melióri, intrans sapiéntia‚ dum sensum carnis infátuat, puríficat intelléctum, cordis palátum sanat et réparat. Sano paláto sapit jam bonum, sapit ipsa sapiéntia, qua in bonis nullum mélius.

quammultafiuntbonetnonsapiuntfacientibus.en: How many good things are done, and have no savour for those who do them! For indeed they are driven to them not by the savour of good, but either by reason, or by some occasion or other, or by necessity: and on the contrary, many who do evil things have no savour of evil, but are led to them either by fear, or by desire of some thing, rather than by the savour of evil. But they who have passed into the affection of the heart, are either wise, and are delighted by the very savour of good: or they are wicked, and take pleasure in malice itself, even though no hope of any other advantage allure them.
quammultafiuntbonetnonsapiuntfacientibus.la: Quam multa fiunt bona, et non sápiunt faciéntibus! Síquidem non sapóre boni ad illa, sed aut ratióne, aut qualicúmque occasióne‚ seu necessitáte impellúntur: et e contrário multis, quæ fáciunt, non sápiunt mala, sed ad hæc inducúntur, aut metu, aut cupiditáte rei cujúspiam pótius, quam sapóre mali. Qui autem transiérunt in afféctum cordis, aut sapiéntes sunt, et ipso delectántur sapóre boni: aut malígni sunt, et in ipsa cómplacent sibi malítia, étiam nulla spe altérius cómmodi blandiénte.

habebatpatervenerabilisinsapientiadoctri.en: The venerable Father had, in the wisdom of his teaching, clearness before the multitudes:
habebatpatervenerabilisinsapientiadoctri.la: Habébat Pater venerábilis in sapiéntia doctrínæ claritátem ad turbas:

etfaciesprincipumadmirabantureum.en: And the faces of princes marvelled at him.

invultupotentiumamabiliseratetmemoriamsu.en: In the sight of the mighty he was lovely, and he left the memory of himself to posterity in benediction:
invultupotentiumamabiliseratetmemoriamsu.la: In vultu poténtium amábilis erat , et memóriam sui relíquit pósteris in benedictióne:

malitiaveroquidnisisaporestmalibeatamens.en: But what is malice, but the savour of evil? Blessed is the mind which the savour of good and the hatred of evil have wholly claimed for themselves. This is to be reformed unto wisdom, this is happily to experience the victory of wisdom. For wherein is wisdom more evidently proved to overcome malice, than when, the savour of evil, which is nothing other than malice itself, being shut out, a certain inmost savour of good is felt to fill the inmost parts of the mind with all sweetness?
malitiaveroquidnisisaporestmalibeatamens.la: Malítia vero quid, nisi sapor est mali? Beáta mens, quam sibi totam vindicávit sapor boni, et ódium mali. Hoc reformári ad sapiéntiam est, hoc sapiéntiæ victóriam felíciter experíri. Nam in quo evidéntius sapiéntia víncere malítiam comprobátur, quam cum exclúso sapóre mali, qui non aliud quam ipsa malítia est, boni quidam íntimus sapor mentis íntima occupáre tota suavitáte sentítur?

deditconfessionemsanctetexcelsoinverbogl.en: He gave praise to the Holy One, and to the most High, with words of glory. With his whole heart he praised the Lord,
deditconfessionemsanctetexcelsoinverbogl.la: Dedit confessiónem Sancto, et Excélso in verbo glóriæ. De omni corde laudávit Dóminum,

etdilexitdeumquifecitillum.en: And loved God that made him.
etdilexitdeumquifecitillum.la: Et diléxit Deum, qui fecit illum.

deditdecusincelebrationeoperissanctietor.en: He gave beauty in the celebration of the holy work, and adorned his times even unto the end:
deditdecusincelebrationeoperissanctietor.la: Dedit decus in celebratióne óperis sancti, et ornávit témpora sua usque in finem:

domumtuamdominedecetsanctitudoinquatante.en: Holiness, * O Lord, becometh thy house, in which the memory of so great holiness is kept.
domumtuamdominedecetsanctitudoinquatante.la: Domum tuam, * Dómine, decet sanctitúdo, in qua tantæ frequentátur memória sanctitátis.

intratcisterciumcumtricenario.en: He entereth Citeaux with thirty companions,

fratrisconnubiumsolvitreligio.en: Religion looseth the wedlock of his brother:

gerardushostiumperfossusgladio.en: Gerard, pierced by the sword of the enemy,

liberexitcumvinculo.en: Goeth forth free with his fetter.

iussupontificisobeditrustico.en: At the Pontiff's bidding he obeyeth a rustic:

oleumcalicisbibitprothetico.en: He drinketh oil from the chalice instead of the potion:

statinveridiciscordeprophetico.en: He standeth among the truthful with prophetic heart,

rastrumcequatannulo.en: He maketh the rake equal to the ring.

scribitepistolaminimbrismedio.en: He writeth a letter in the midst of the rain,

musceparabolamaffertextinctio.en: The extinction of the flies bringeth forth a proverb:

feminamdiscolamplenamdemonio.en: A wayward woman full of a devil

curatcrucissignaculo.en: He healeth with the sign of the cross.

mariecitharascripturasexplicat.en: The harp of Mary, he expoundeth the Scriptures,

spoliattartarafunctosvivificat.en: He despoileth hell, he quickeneth the dead:

necnongensbarbarahuncsanctumpredicat.en: And even the barbarous nation proclaimeth this saint
necnongensbarbarahuncsanctumpredicat.la: Necnon gens bárbara hunc sanctum prædicat

orestylomiraculo.en: By mouth, by pen, by miracle.

benedictusdominusdeuspatrisnostriquieius.en: Blessed * be the Lord God of our Father, who by his teaching and example hath built up his Church: by his happy assumption hath gladdened his city above: by his solemn remembrance consoleth this day his household here present.
benedictusdominusdeuspatrisnostriquieius.la: Benedíctus * Dóminus Deus Patris nostri, qui ejus doctrína et exémplo ædificávit Ecclésiam suam: ejus felíci assumptióne supérnam lætificávit civitátem suam: ejus solémni recordatióne præséntem hódie consolátur famíliam suam.

exsultetindominospiritusvirisanctiquodmo.en: Let the spirit of the holy Man * exult in the Lord, for that, lifted up from the weight of the body, he goeth wholly unto God, and cleaving unto him is made one spirit with him for ever.
exsultetindominospiritusvirisanctiquodmo.la: Exsúltet * in Dómino spíritus Viri sancti, quod mole levátus corpórea totus pergit in Deum, et adhǽrens illi unus fit cum eo spíritus in ætérnum.

perpetuisnosdominesanctiioannisbaptistet.en: Protect us, O Lord, * with the perpetual defence of Saint John the Baptist; and the frailer we are, the more do thou uphold us by his needful intercession.
perpetuisnosdominesanctiioannisbaptistet.la: Perpétuis * nos, Dómine, sancti Joánnis Baptístæ tuére præsídiis; et quanto fragilióres sumus, tanto magis necessáriis attólle suffrágiis.

nativitasesthodiesanctemarievirginiscuiu.en: Today is the Nativity * of holy Mary the Virgin, whose renowned life sheddeth lustre on all the Churches.
nativitasesthodiesanctemarievirginiscuiu.la: Natívitas est hódie * sanctæ Maríæ Vírginis, cujus vita ínclita cunctas illústrat Ecclésias. Ps. 109

cumiucunditatenativitatembeatemarieceleb.en: With joyfulness * let us celebrate the Nativity of blessed Mary, that she may intercede for us with the Lord Jesus Christ.
cumiucunditatenativitatembeatemarieceleb.la: Cum jucunditáte * Nativitátem beátæ Maríæ celebrémus, ut ipsa pro nobis intercédat ad Dóminum Jesum Christum. Ps. 112

regaliexprogeniemariexortarefulgetcuiusp.en: Of royal lineage * Mary, arisen, shineth forth; by whose prayers we most devoutly ask with mind and spirit to be helped.
regaliexprogeniemariexortarefulgetcuiusp.la: Regáli ex progénie * María exórta refúlget; cujus précibus nos adjuvári, mente et spíritu devotíssime póscimus. Ps. 121

cordeetanimochristocanamusgloriaminhacsa.en: With heart and soul * let us sing glory to Christ on this sacred solemnity of the most exalted Mother of God, Mary.
cordeetanimochristocanamusgloriaminhacsa.la: Corde et ánimo * Christo canámus glóriam in hac sacra solemnitáte præcélsæ Genetrícis Dei Maríæ. Ps. 126

nativitasgloriosevirginismarieexsemineab.en: The Nativity of the glorious * Virgin Mary, of the seed of Abraham, sprung from the tribe of Juda, illustrious of the stock of David.
nativitasgloriosevirginismarieexsemineab.la: Natívitas gloriósæ * Vírginis Maríæ ex sémine Abrahæ, ortæ de tribu Juda, clara ex stirpe David.

oquamgloriosestmaterquecelireginamgenuit.en: O how glorious is the mother who brought forth the Queen of heaven!
oquamgloriosestmaterquecelireginamgenuit.la: O quam gloriósa est mater, quæ cæli Regínam génuit!

nativitastuadeigenitrixvirgo.en: Thy Nativity, * O Virgin Mother of God.

nativitastuadeigenetrixvirgogaudiumannun.en: Thy Nativity, O Virgin Mother of God, announced joy to the whole world: for from thee arose the sun of justice, Christ our God:
nativitastuadeigenetrixvirgogaudiumannun.la: Natívitas tua, Dei Génetrix Virgo, gáudium annuntiávit univérso mundo: ex te enim ortus est sol justítiæ, Christus Deus noster:

quisolvensmaledictionemdeditbenedictione.en: Who, taking away the curse, gave the blessing; and confounding death, bestowed on us life everlasting.
quisolvensmaledictionemdeditbenedictione.la: Qui, solvens maledictiónem, dedit benedictiónem; et confúndens mortem, donávit nobis vitam sempitérnam.

cordeetanimochristocanamusgloriam.en: With heart and soul let us sing glory to Christ,
cordeetanimochristocanamusgloriam.la: Corde et ánimo Christo canámus glóriam,

inhacsacrasolemnitateprecelsegenetricisd.en: On this sacred solemnity of the most exalted Mother of God, the Virgin Mary.
inhacsacrasolemnitateprecelsegenetricisd.la: In hac sacra solemnitáte præcélsæ Genetrícis Dei Virginis Mariæ.

omnesparitercongregatidominumcollaudemus.en: All gathered together alike, let us praise the Lord,

fulcitemefloribusstipatememalis.en: Stay me up with flowers, compass me about with apples:
fulcitemefloribusstipatememalis.la: Fulcíte me flóribus, stipáte me malis:

adiurovosfilieierusalemsiinveneritisdile.en: I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, if you find my beloved, that you tell him.
adiurovosfilieierusalemsiinveneritisdile.la: Adjúro vos, fíliæ Jerúsalem, si invenéritis diléctum, ut annuntiétis ei.

beataprogeniesundechristusnatusestoquamg.en: Blessed lineage, * whence Christ was born: O how glorious is the mother who brought forth the Queen of heaven!
beataprogeniesundechristusnatusestoquamg.la: Beáta progénies, * unde Christus natus est: o quam gloriósa est mater, quæ cæli Regínam génuit!

quampulchresamicameaquampulchresetdecora.en: How beautiful art thou, my love, how beautiful art thou and comely! thy eyes are doves' eyes:
quampulchresamicameaquampulchresetdecora.la: Quam pulchra es, amíca mea, quam pulchra es et decóra! óculi tui columbárum:

sicutvittacoccinealabiatueteloquiumtuumd.en: Thy lips are as a scarlet lace, and thy speech sweet.
sicutvittacoccinealabiatueteloquiumtuumd.la: Sicut vitta coccínea lábia tua, et elóquium tuum dulce.

queratdiligenslectoretdicatcumiosephnons.en: The diligent reader may ask and say: Since Joseph is not the father of the Lord and Saviour, what hath the order of generation traced down to Joseph to do with the Lord? To whom we shall answer, first, that it is not the custom of the scriptures that the order of women be woven into genealogies. Next, that Joseph and Mary were of one tribe: whence by the law he was bound to take her as his kinswoman: and that they were enrolled together in Bethlehem, as being, namely, sprung from one stock.
queratdiligenslectoretdicatcumiosephnons.la: Quærat díligens lector et dicat: Cum Joseph non sit pater Domini Salvatóris, quid pértinet ad Dóminum generatiónis ordo dedúctus usque ad Joseph? Cui respondébimus primum, non esse consuetúdinis scripturárum, ut mulíerum in generatiónibus ordo texátur. Deínde‚ ex una tribu fuísse Joseph et Maríam: unde ex lege eam accípere cogebátur ut propínquam: et quod simul censéntur in Béthlehem, ut de una vidélicet stirpe generáti.

egoquasivitisfructificavisuavitatemodori.en: As the vine I have brought forth a pleasant odour: § and my flowers are the fruit of honour and riches. * I am the mother of fair love, and of fear, and of knowledge, and of holy hope.
egoquasivitisfructificavisuavitatemodori.la: Ego quasi vitis fructificávi suavitátem odóris: § et flores mei fructus honóris et honestátis. * Ego mater pulchræ dilectiónis, et timóris, et agnitiónis, et sanctæ spei.

transiteadmeomnesquiconcupiscitismeetage.en: Come over to me, all ye that desire me, and be filled with my fruits: § for my spirit is sweet above honey, and my inheritance above honey and the honeycomb: * my memory is unto everlasting generations.
transiteadmeomnesquiconcupiscitismeetage.la: Transíte ad me, omnes qui concupíscitis me, et a generatiónibus meis implémini: § spíritus enim meus super mel dulcis, et hæréditas mea super mel et favum: * memória mea in generatiónes sæculórum.

quieduntmeadhucesurientetquibibuntmeadhu.en: They that eat me, shall yet hunger: § and they that drink me, shall yet thirst. * He that hearkeneth to me, shall not be confounded: § and they that work by me, shall not sin. * They that explain me shall have life everlasting.
quieduntmeadhucesurientetquibibuntmeadhu.la: Qui edunt me, adhuc esúrient: § et qui bibunt me, adhuc sítient. * Qui audit me, non confundétur: § et qui operántur in me, non peccábunt. * Qui elúcidant me, vitam ætérnam habébunt.

nosautemgloriarioportetincrucedomininost.en: But it behoveth us * to glory in the Cross of our Lord Jesus Christ.
nosautemgloriarioportetincrucedomininost.la: Nos autem * gloriári opórtet in Cruce Dómini nostri Jesu Christi.

salvanoschristesalvatorpervirtutemcrucis.en: Save us, O Christ our Saviour, * by the power of the Cross: thou who didst save Peter in the sea, have mercy on us.
salvanoschristesalvatorpervirtutemcrucis.la: Salva nos, Christe Salvátor, * per virtútem Crucis: qui salvásti Petrum in mari, miserére nobis.

tuamcrucemadoramusdominetuamgloriosamrec.en: Thy Cross * we adore, O Lord, thy glorious passion we call to mind: have mercy on us, thou who didst suffer for us.
tuamcrucemadoramusdominetuamgloriosamrec.la: Tuam Crucem * adorámus, Dómine, tuam gloriósam recólimus passiónem: miserére nostri, qui passus es pro nobis.

persignumcrucisdeinimicisnostrisliberano.en: By the sign of the Cross * deliver us from our enemies, O our God.
persignumcrucisdeinimicisnostrisliberano.la: Per signum Crucis * de inimícis nostris líbera nos, Deus noster.

cruxfidelisinteromnesarborunanobilisnull.en: Faithful Cross, * among all trees the one noble tree; no forest bringeth forth such, in leaf, in flower, in bud: sweet the wood, sweet the nails, sweet the weight it beareth.
cruxfidelisinteromnesarborunanobilisnull.la: Crux fidélis, * inter omnes arbor una nóbilis, nulla silva talem profert, fronde, flore, gérmine: dulce lignum, dulces clavos, dulce pondus sústinet.

commemoratiodieiinfraoctavamnativitatisb.en: Commemoration of the day within the Octave of the Nativity of the B.V.M.
commemoratiodieiinfraoctavamnativitatisb.la: Commemoratio diei infra Octavam Nativitatis B.M.V.

dumpreliareturmichelarchangeluscumdracon.en: While Michael the Archangel * fought with the dragon, the voice of them that said was heard: Salvation to our God, alleluia.
dumpreliareturmichelarchangeluscumdracon.la: Dum præliarétur * Míchaël Archángelus cum dracóne, audíta est vox dicéntium: Salus Deo nostro, allelúia.

dumcommitteretbellumdracocummichelearcha.en: When the dragon * joined battle with Michael the Archangel, the voice of thousands of thousands was heard, saying: Salvation to our God.
dumcommitteretbellumdracocummichelearcha.la: Dum commítteret * bellum draco cum Michaéle Archángelo, audíta est vox míllia míllium dicéntium: Salus Deo nostro.

michelgabrielcherubimetseraphimquinonces.en: Michael, Gabriel, * Cherubim and Seraphim, who cease not to cry out daily, saying: Thou art worthy, O Lord, to receive glory, alleluia
michelgabrielcherubimetseraphimquinonces.la: Míchael, Gábriel, * Chérubim et Séraphim, qui non cessant clamáre quotídie, dicéntes: Dignus es, Dómine, accípere glóriam, allelúia

angelidominidominumbenediciteineternum.en: Angels of the Lord, * bless ye the Lord for ever.
angelidominidominumbenediciteineternum.la: Angeli Dómini, * Dóminum benedícite in ætérnum.

angeliarchangelithronietdominationesprin.en: Angels, Archangels, * Thrones and Dominations, Principalities and Powers, Virtues of the heavens, praise ye the Lord from the heavens, alleluia.
angeliarchangelithronietdominationesprin.la: Angeli, Archángeli, * Throni et Dominatiónes, Principátus et Potestátes, Virtútes cælórum, laudáte Dóminum de cælis, allelúia.

michelprepositeparadisiquemhonorificanta.en: Michael, * Provost of paradise, whom the citizens of the Angels honour, intercede for us with the Lord.
michelprepositeparadisiquemhonorificanta.la: Míchaël * Præpósite paradísi, quem honoríficant Angelórum cives, intercéde pro nobis ad Dóminum. Ps. 18

micheletangelieiuspugnabantcumdiaboletil.en: Michael * and his Angels fought with the devil, and that old enemy was overcome by them.
micheletangelieiuspugnabantcumdiaboletil.la: Míchaël * et Angeli ejus pugnábant cum diábolo, et ille hostis antíquus victus est ab eis. Ps. 98

archangelimichelisinterventionesuffultit.en: Upheld by the intercession * of Michael the Archangel, we beseech thee, O Lord, that whom we follow with honour, we may attain unto in mind also, alleluia.
archangelimichelisinterventionesuffultit.la: Archángeli Michaélis * interventióne suffúlti, te Dómine deprecámur, ut, quos honóre proséquimur, contingámus et mente, allelúia. Ps. 266, 267, 268

nolitetimereopprobriahominumetblasphemia.en: Fear ye not the reproach of men, and be not afraid of their blasphemies.
nolitetimereopprobriahominumetblasphemia.la: Nolíte timére oppróbria hóminum, et blasphémias eórum ne metuátis.

datasunteiincensamultautadolereteaanteal.en: There was given to him much incense, that he should offer it before the altar.
datasunteiincensamultautadolereteaanteal.la: Data sunt ei incénsa multa, ut adoléret ea ante altáre.

docebotequeventurasuntpopulotuoinnovissi.en: I will teach thee what things shall befall thy people in the latter days, which is set down in the Scripture of truth
docebotequeventurasuntpopulotuoinnovissi.la: Docébo te quæ ventúra sunt pópulo tuo in novíssimis diébus, quod expréssum est in Scriptúris veritátis

etnemestadiutormeusinomnibushisnisimiche.en: And none is my helper in all these things, but Michael the Archangel your prince.
etnemestadiutormeusinomnibushisnisimiche.la: Et nemo est adjútor meus in ómnibus his, nisi Míchaël Archángelus princeps vester.

exdiequaposuisticortuumadintelligendumut.en: From the day that thou didst set thy heart to understand, to afflict thyself in the sight of the Lord, thy words have been heard, and I am come for thy words.
exdiequaposuisticortuumadintelligendumut.la: Ex die qua posuísti cor tuum ad intelligéndum, ut te afflígeres in conspéctu Dómini, exaudíta sunt verba tua, et ego veni propter sermónes tuos.

numquidscisquarevenerimadteetnuncreverta.en: Knowest thou wherefore I am come to thee, and now I will return to fight against the prince of the Persians, who withstandeth thy prayers and my embassy?
numquidscisquarevenerimadteetnuncreverta.la: Numquid scis quare vénerim ad te, et nunc revértar, ut prælier advérsus príncipem Persárum contradicéntem tuis précibus et meæ legatióni?

verumtamenmichelarchangelusprincepsmagnu.en: But Michael the Archangel, the great prince, who standeth for the children of thy people, shall be my helper.
verumtamenmichelarchangelusprincepsmagnu.la: Verúmtamen Míchaël Archángelus princeps magnus, qui stat pro fíliis pópuli tui, erit adjútor meus.

princepsregnipersarumrestititmihiviginti.en: The prince of the kingdom of the Persians resisted me one and twenty days.
princepsregnipersarumrestititmihiviginti.la: Princeps regni Persárum réstitit mihi vigínti et uno diébus.

fidelissermetomniacceptionedignusmichela.en: A faithful saying, and worthy of all acceptation: † Michael the Archangel,
fidelissermetomniacceptionedignusmichela.la: Fidélis sermo, et omni acceptióne dignus: † Míchaël Archángelus,

quipugnavitcumdiabologratiadeivictorexst.en: Who fought with the devil, by the grace of God came forth victor, and that old enemy suffered a great overthrow.
quipugnavitcumdiabologratiadeivictorexst.la: Qui pugnávit cum diábolo, grátia Dei victor éxstitit, et ille hostis antíquus passus est ruínam magnam.

stetitangelusiuxtaaramtemplihabensthurib.en: An Angel stood * near the altar of the temple, having a golden censer in his hand, and there was given to him much incense, and the smoke of the spices ascended before the Lord from the hand of the Angel.
stetitangelusiuxtaaramtemplihabensthurib.la: Stetit Angelus * juxta aram templi, habens thuríbulum áureum in manu sua, et data sunt ei incénsa multa, et ascéndit fumus arómatum in conspéctu Dómini de manu Angeli.

exaudidominepopulumtotatibimentesubditum.en: Hear, O Lord, thy people, subject unto thee with their whole mind: § and keep them by the supplication of blessed Martin, Abbot: * that, protected in body and in heart, they may desire what they devoutly believe, § and obtain what they rightly hope for. *
exaudidominepopulumtotatibimentesubditum.la: Exáudi, Dómine, pópulum tota tibi mente súbditum: § et beáti Martíni, Abbátis, supplicatióne custódi: * ut córpore et corde protéctus, quod pie credit, áppetat, § et quod juste sperat, obtíneat. *

deusvitafideliumgloriahumiliumetbeatitud.en: O God, the life of the faithful, the glory of the humble and the blessedness of the just: by the intercession of blessed Maurice, Abbot, look graciously upon the prayers of thy suppliants; that the souls which thirst for thy promises may ever be filled from the abundance of thy charity.
deusvitafideliumgloriahumiliumetbeatitud.la: Deus, vita fidélium, glória humílium et beatitúdo justórum: interveniénte beáto Maurítio, Abbáte, propítius réspice súpplicum preces; ut ánimæ, quæ promissiónes tuas sítiunt, de tuæ charitátis semper abundántia repleántur.

hecestquenescivitthorumindelictohabebitf.en: This is she who hath not known * the bed in sin; she shall have fruit in the visitation of holy souls
hecestquenescivitthorumindelictohabebitf.la: Hæc est quæ nescívit, * thorum in delícto, habébit fructum in respectióne animárum sanctárum Ps. 109

unguentumeffusumnomentuumideoadolescentu.en: Thy name is as oil poured out: * therefore young maidens have loved thee exceedingly.
unguentumeffusumnomentuumideoadolescentu.la: Unguéntum effúsum * nomen tuum, ídeo adolescéntulæ dilexérunt te nimis. Ps. 112

medianocteclamorfactusesteccesponsusveni.en: At midnight * there was a cry made: Behold the bridegroom cometh, go ye forth to meet him.
medianocteclamorfactusesteccesponsusveni.la: Média nocte * clamor factus est: Ecce sponsus venit, exíte óbviam ei. Ps. 121

virginumchoruslaudatedominumincelisallel.en: Ye choir of Virgins, * praise the Lord in the heavens, alleluia.
virginumchoruslaudatedominumincelisallel.la: Vírginum chorus * laudáte Dóminum in cœlis, allelúia. Ps. 126

tuncsurrexeruntomnesvirginesilleetornave.en: Then all * those Virgins arose, and trimmed their lamps.
tuncsurrexeruntomnesvirginesilleetornave.la: Tunc surrexérunt omnes * Vírgines illæ, et ornavérunt lámpades suas.

unguentumeffusumnomentuum.en: Thy name is as oil * poured out.

ideoadolescentuledilexerunttenimis.en: Therefore young maidens have loved thee exceedingly.

danobisquesumusdominedeusnostersanctarum.en: Grant us, we beseech thee, O Lord our God, to venerate with unceasing devotion the palms of thy holy Virgins and Martyrs Ursula and her Companions: that those whom we cannot celebrate with worthy mind, we may at least honour often with humble service.
danobisquesumusdominedeusnostersanctarum.la: Da nobis, quǽsumus, Dómine, Deus noster, sanctárum Vírginum et Mártyrum tuárum Ursulæ et Sociárum ejus palmas incessábili devotióne venerári: ut, quas digna mente non póssumus celebráre, humílibus saltem frequentémus obséquiis.

tradideruntcorporasuaadsuppliciaideocoro.en: They delivered up * their bodies to torments: therefore are they crowned, and receive palms.
tradideruntcorporasuaadsuppliciaideocoro.la: Tradidérunt * córpora sua ad supplícia: ídeo coronántur, et accípiunt palmas.

deusquibeatumbernardumconfessoremtuumatq.en: O God, who didst set blessed Bernard, thy Confessor and Bishop, in thy Church as a faithful minister in the Gospel of thy Son: * direct and strengthen our hearts in thy charity; § that we may be found both steadfast in faith and effectual in work.
deusquibeatumbernardumconfessoremtuumatq.la: Deus, qui beátum Bernárdum, Confessórem tuum atque Pontíficem, fidélem in Evangélio Fílii tui minístrum in Ecclésie tua constituísti: * dírige in charitáte tua et confírma corda nostra; § ut et in fide inveniámur stábiles, et in ópere efficáces.

beatorummartyrumtuorumdominecrispinietcr.en: May the prayer of thy blessed Martyrs Crispin and Crispinian, we beseech thee, O Lord, be with us: that we may continually experience the loving help of those whom we venerate with homage.
beatorummartyrumtuorumdominecrispinietcr.la: Beatórum Mártyrum tuórum, Dómine, Crispíni et Crispiniáni, quǽsumus, adsit nobis orátio: ut, quos venerámur obséquio, eórum pium júgiter experiámur auxílium.

responsoriumfecitnosregnumetsacerdotesde.en: Responsory. He hath made us a kingdom and priests to God and his Father: * To him be glory and empire for ever and ever.
responsoriumfecitnosregnumetsacerdotesde.la: Responsorium. Fecit nos regnum et sacerdótes Deo et Patri suo: * Ipsi glória et impérium, in sǽcula sæculórum.

ipseestprimogenitusmortuorumetprincepsre.en: He is the first begotten of the dead, and the prince of the kings of the earth.
ipseestprimogenitusmortuorumetprincepsre.la: Ipse est primogénitus mortuórum, et princeps regum terræ.

ipsiglorietimperiuminseculaseculorum.en: To him be glory and empire for ever and ever.
ipsiglorietimperiuminseculaseculorum.la: Ipsi glória et impérium, in sǽcula sæculórum.

responsoriumbeataverematerecclesiaquamsi.en: Responsory. Truly blessed is mother Church, whom the honour of divine condescension so enlighteneth, whom the glorious blood of victorious Martyrs adorneth, * Whom the white virginity of inviolate confession clotheth.
responsoriumbeataverematerecclesiaquamsi.la: Responsorium. Beáta vere mater Ecclésia, quam sic honor divínæ dignatiónis illúminat, quam victoriosórum gloriósus Mártyrum sanguis exórnat, * Quam inviolátæ confessiónis cándida índuit virgínitas.

floribuseiusnecrosenecliliadesunt.en: Neither roses nor lilies are wanting to her flowers.
floribuseiusnecrosenecliliadesunt.la: Flóribus ejus nec rosæ, nec lília desunt.

quaminviolateconfessioniscandidinduitvir.en: Whom the white virginity of inviolate confession clotheth.
quaminviolateconfessioniscandidinduitvir.la: Quam inviolátæ confessiónis cándid índuit virgínitas.

fulgebuntiustiettamquamscintilleinarundi.en: The just shall shine, * and shall run to and fro like sparks among the reeds. They shall judge nations, and shall reign for ever.
fulgebuntiustiettamquamscintilleinarundi.la: Fulgébunt justi: * et tamquam scintíllæ in arundinéto discúrrent. Judicábunt natiónes, et regnábunt in ætérnum.

beatieritiscumvosoderinthominesetcumsepa.en: Blessed shall you be * when men shall hate you, and when they shall separate you, and shall reproach you, and cast out your name as evil, for the Son of man's sake: be glad and rejoice, for behold your reward is great in heaven.
beatieritiscumvosoderinthominesetcumsepa.la: Beáti éritis, * cum vos óderint hómines, et cum separáverint vos, et exprobráverint, et ejécerint nomen vestrum tamquam malum propter Fílium hóminis: gaudéte et exsultáte, ecce enim merces vestra multa est in cœlo.

beatimundocordequoniamipsideumvidebunt.en: Blessed are the clean of heart: * for they shall see God.
beatimundocordequoniamipsideumvidebunt.la: Beáti mundo corde: * quóniam ipsi Deum vidébunt.

beatiquipersecutionempatiunturpropterius.en: Blessed are they * that suffer persecution for justice' sake.
beatiquipersecutionempatiunturpropterius.la: Beáti, * qui persecutiónem patiúntur propter justítiam.

beatiestissanctideiomnesquimeruistiscons.en: Blessed are ye, * all ye Saints of God, who have merited to be made companions of the heavenly powers, and to enjoy the glory of eternal brightness: therefore we pray that, mindful of us, ye vouchsafe to intercede for us with the Lord our God.
beatiestissanctideiomnesquimeruistiscons.la: Beáti estis * Sancti Dei omnes, qui meruístis consórtes fíeri cæléstium virtútum, et pérfrui ætérnæ claritátis glória: idéoque precámur, ut mémores nostri, intercédere dignémini pro nobis ad Dóminum Deum nostrum.

deusquibeatummalachiampontificemsanctiss.en: O God, who didst sweetly unite blessed Malachy, Bishop, to the most holy Father Bernard in a bond of true charity: † graciously grant: * that we may warily shun the hurtful fellowship of all the wicked, † and ever long for the holy friendships of the heavenly host.
deusquibeatummalachiampontificemsanctiss.la: Deus, qui beátum Malachíam, Pontíficem, sanctíssimo Patri Bernárdo veræ charitátis fœdere dúlciter sociásti: † concéde propítius: * ut et pravórum ómnium consénsus nóxios caute vitémus, † et cœléstis milítiæ sacras amicítias semper optémus.

oquantusluctusomniumquantaprecipuelament.en: O how great the mourning of all! * how great above all the lamentations of the Monks and of the Virgins! for it is holy both to rejoice for Martin, and holy to weep for Martin.
oquantusluctusomniumquantaprecipuelament.la: O quantus luctus ómnium! * quanta præcípue laménta Monachórum, et Vírginum! quia et pium est gaudére Martíno et pium est flere Martínum.

gaudentincelisanimesanctorumquichristive.en: In heaven rejoice * the souls of the Saints, who have followed the footsteps of Christ: and because for his love they despised the world, therefore they exult with Christ without end.
gaudentincelisanimesanctorumquichristive.la: Gaudent in cælis * ánimæ Sanctórum, qui Christi vestígia sunt secúti: et quia pro ejus amóre sæculum sprevérunt, ídeo cum Christo exsúltant sine fine.

sanctidominidominumbenediciteineternum.en: Ye Saints of the Lord, * bless the Lord for ever.
sanctidominidominumbenediciteineternum.la: Sancti Dómini * Dóminum benedícite in ætérnum.

claustriquemitesincole.en: Of the solitude and of the cloister,

calcastisetfedissima.en: Ye have trodden underfoot, and the most foul

humusqueduralectulum.en: And the hard ground your bed.

portentanecteterrima.en: Nor did the most hideous portents

divumqueiunctacetui.en: And, joined to the company of the Saints,

summoparenticelitum.en: To the supreme Father of the heavenly ones,

magnequeprolivirginis.en: And to the great Offspring of the Virgin,

exultabuntsanctiingloria.en: The Saints shall rejoice in glory.

letabunturincubilibussuis.en: They shall be joyful in their beds.

inregenerationecumsederitfiliushominisin.en: In the regeneration, * when the Son of man shall sit on the seat of his majesty, you also shall sit on twelve seats, judging the twelve tribes of Israel, saith the Lord.
inregenerationecumsederitfiliushominisin.la: In regeneratióne, * cum séderit Fílius hóminis in sede Majestátis suæ, sedébitis et vos, super sedes duódecim, judicántes duódecim tribus Israël, dicit Dóminus.

concedequesumusomnipotensdeusutadmeliore.en: Grant, we beseech thee, almighty God: * that the examples of thy Saints may provoke us to a better life: § so that, as we celebrate their solemnities, we may also imitate their deeds.
concedequesumusomnipotensdeusutadmeliore.la: Concéde, quǽsumus omnípotens Deus: * ut ad meliórem vitam Sanctórum tuórum exémpla nos próvocent: § quátenus, quorum solémnia ágimus, étiam actus imitémur.

hecestverafraternitasquenumquampotuitvio.en: This is true brotherhood, which could never be violated by strife: † who, having shed their blood, followed the Lord:
hecestverafraternitasquenumquampotuitvio.la: Haec est vera fratérnitas, quae numquam pótuit violári certámine: † qui, effúso súnguine secúti sunt Dóminum:

contemnentesaulamregiamperveneruntadregn.en: Despising the royal court, they attained unto the heavenly kingdom.
contemnentesaulamregiamperveneruntadregn.la: Contemnéntes aulam régiam, pervenérunt ad regna caeléstia.

inhistoriabeatiiosaphatcapcircafinem.en: In the history of blessed Josaphat, chap. 2, near the end
inhistoriabeatiiosaphatcapcircafinem.la: In historia beati Josaphat, cap. 2. circa finem

sacerdotesdeibenedicitedeum.en: O ye priests of God, bless God

sanctiethumilescordelaudatedeum.en: ye saints and humble of heart, praise God.
sanctiethumilescordelaudatedeum.la: Sancti et húmiles corde laudáte Deum.

spiritusetanimeiustarumhymnumdicitedeono.en: O ye spirits and souls of the just, sing a hymn to our God.
spiritusetanimeiustarumhymnumdicitedeono.la: Spíritus et ánimae iustárum, hymnum dícite Deo nostro.

beatiilliacterbeatiquoniamfirmismentisoc.en: Blessed, yea, thrice blessed are they, because with sure spiritual vision they discerned the vanity of this present world and the uncertainty and inconstancy of mortal fortune, and cast it aside, and laid up for themselves everlasting blessings, and laid hold of that life which never faileth, nor is broken by death.
beatiilliacterbeatiquoniamfirmismentisoc.la: Beáti illi ac ter beáti, quóniam firmis mentis óculis praeséntium rerum vanitátem, atque humánae prosperitátis incertitúdinem et inconstántiam perspexérunt, eáque reíecta, sempitérna bona sibi ipsis condidérunt, ac vitam eam, quae nunquam óccidit, nec morte interrúmpitur, arripuérunt.

hosigitiuradmirandosetsanctosvirosnosquo.en: These wonderful and holy men, therefore, we also, unworthy and despicable, strive to imitate. Yet we by no means attain to the height of their heavenly life, but according to the measure of our infirmity and wretched ability we express their life; and we wear their habit, even though we attain not to their works. For we hold it as perceived that this divine profession driveth away sin, and is the companion and helper of the incorruption granted unto us through divine baptism.
hosigitiuradmirandosetsanctosvirosnosquo.la: Hos ígitiur admirándos et sanctos viros nos quoque indígni ac despicábiles imitári studémus. Verum eórum vitae caeléstis fastígium mínime asséqimur, sed pro infirmitátis nostrae ac míserae facultátis módulo eórum vitam exprímus; atque ipsórum hábitum gérimus, étiam sui ópera non assequámur. Etenim, divínam hanc professiónem, peccátum propulsáre, atque incorruptiónis per divínum baptísma nobis concéssae sóciam et opitulatrícem esse, perspéctum habémus.

modoutiquefratresaudistisinevangelioprom.en: Just now, brethren, ye heard in the Gospel the Lord promising and saying to his disciples: Ye shall sit upon seats, judging the twelve tribes of Israel. Behold the rest of sitting and the honour of judgment. For the Lord himself also would not come to these things, save through humility and labour. Whence also he was condemned to a most shameful death, questioned with torments, and filled with reproaches: surely that the enemy might be clothed with confusion, he likewise and all who imitate him and go beyond the way. He it is, O wicked one, he it is who shall sit on the seat of his majesty, like to the Most High, and most high together with him. This surely the holy Angels considered, who, when the evil one fell, consented not to his apostasy, leaving us an example, that, as they chose to serve, so we also should do.
modoutiquefratresaudistisinevangelioprom.la: Modo útique, fratres, audístis in Evangélio promitténtem Dóminum et dic éntem discípulis: Sedébitis super sedes, iudicántes duódecim tribus Israël. Ecce quies sessiónis et honor iudícii. Nam et ipse Dóminus ad haec nóluit perveníre, nisi per humilitátem et labórem. Unde et morte turpíssima condemnátus est, interrogátus torméntis, et oppróbriis saturátus: útique ut inimícus induátur confusióne, ipse páriter et omnes, qui imitántur eum, et praetergrediúntur viam. Ipse est, o iníque, ipse est, qui sessúrus est in sede maiestátis suae símilis Altíssimo, et coaltíssimus ei. Hoc útique cogitavérunt Angeli sancti, qui, cadénte malígno, apostasíae illíus non consensérunt, nobis relinquéntes exémplum, ut, quemádmodum ipsi elegérunt ministráre, sic et nos faciámus.

quienimlaboremfugiuntethonoremcaptantill.en: For let them who flee labour and seek after honour know that they imitate him who sought the seat and the height: and if his fault doth not sufficiently terrify them, let at least his punishment terrify them. To avoid these things the Saints of God have left us prudence, who indeed shall sit; they, I say, little worms of the earth, shall sit judging. Know ye not, saith the Apostle, that we shall judge Angels? They surely, who went and wept, casting their seeds, but coming they shall come with joyfulness, carrying their sheaves. They who have sown labour and lowliness shall reap honour and rest alike. For for their double confusion and labour, they shall receive double in their land. Whence also one said: See my humiliation and my labour.
quienimlaboremfugiuntethonoremcaptantill.la: Qui enim labórem fúgiunt et honórem captant, illum se nóverint imitári, qui sessiónem altitudinémque quaesívit: et si non satis terret eos illíus culpa, térreat vel vindícta. Ad haec vitánda prudéntiam nobis reliquérunt Sancti Dei, qui profécto sedébunt; ipsi, inquam, vermículi terrae iudicántes sedébunt. Nescítis, ait Apóstolus, quia et Angelos iudicábimus? Ipsi útique, qui ibant et flebant, mitténtes sémina sua, veniéntes autem vénient cum exsultatióne, portántes manípuolos suos. Qui seminavérunt labórem et vilitátem, metent honórem páriter et quiétem. Pro confusiónem enim sua dúplici et labóre, in terra sua duplícia possidébunt. Unde et dicébat quidam: Vide humilitátem meam et labórem meum.

nonsolumautemipsavitasedetpromissiovitee.en: And not only life itself, but also the promise of eternal life and the expectation of the just, is joy, and joy so great, that all that is desired cannot be compared with it. This prudence also the holy Apostles sowed for us, when, while those departed who followed the wisdom of this world, which is foolishness with God, and the prudence of the flesh, which worketh death and is an enemy to God, they themselves cleaved unto the Lord. And it is manifest that the Martyrs sowed fortitude. Moreover the Confessors pursued justice in all their life. For this is the difference between Martyrs and Confessors, which is between Peter leaving all things at once, and Abraham spending the substance of the world in good uses: for thus the former, being made perfect in a short space, fulfilled a long time; but the latter drew out long and manifold martyrdoms. It is plain that the holy Virgins sowed temperance, who thus trod lust underfoot.
nonsolumautemipsavitasedetpromissiovitee.la: Non solum autem ipsa vita, sed et promíssio vitae aetérnae et expectátio iustórum, laetítia est, et tanta laetítia, ut omne, quod concupíscitur, ei non váleat comparári. Hanc quoque prudéntiam nobis Apóstoli sancti seminavérunt, quando, recedéntibus his, qui sapiéntiam huius mundi sequebántur, quae stultítia est apud Deum, et prudéntiam carnis, quae mortem operátur et inimíca est Deo; ipsi Dóminuo adhaesérunt. Mártyres vero maniféstum est fortitúdinem seminásse. Porro Confessóres sectáti sunt iustítiam in omni vita sua. Hoc enim ínterest inter Mártyres et Confessóres, quod inter Petrum simul ómnia relinquéntem, et Abraham substántiam mundi in bonos usus expendéntem: sic enim illi consummáti in brevi explevérunt témpora multa; isti vero longa et multímoda traxére martýria. Vírgines sanctae planum est, quia temperántiam seminavérunt, quae sic libídinem calcavérunt.

hacdoctrinanosetiaminstruitnostercelesti.en: With this doctrine also our heavenly father, leader, master and lawgiver Benedict instructeth us, and directeth our steps into the way of peace. Moreover the justice of his life wholly strengtheneth and quickeneth us, that we be the more kindled to do the things which he taught, as we are certain that he taught no other things than he did. Indeed the example of work is a living and effectual sermon, making very persuasive that which is said, while it showeth to be possible that which is urged. In this manner, therefore, his holiness comforteth, his piety formeth, his justice confirmeth. For of how great piety was it, that he not only profited those present, but was also solicitous for those to come? He feedeth by his life, he feedeth by his teaching, he feedeth by his intercession. Helped by him unceasingly, do ye also bear fruit, dearly beloved, since ye are set for this, that ye should go and bring forth fruit. Let us imitate him also; since he came for this, to hand on to us a pattern, and to show the way.
hacdoctrinanosetiaminstruitnostercelesti.la: Hac doctrína nos étiam ínstruit noster caeléstis pater, dux, magíster et légifer Benedíctus, et dírigit gressus nostros in viam pacis. Porro vitae iustítia omníno róborat et ánimat nos, ut tanto magis accendámur ad agénda quae dócuit, quanto certi sumus eum non ália docuísse quam fécerit. Sermo quidem vivus et éfficax, exemplum óperis est, plúrimum fáciens suadíbile quod dícitur, dum monstrat factíbile quod suadétur. In hunc ergo modum sánctitas confórtat, pietátis infórmat, iustítia confírmat. Quantae enim pietátis fuit, quod non solum praeséntibus prófuit, sed et pro futúris sollícitus fuit? Pascit vita, pascit doctrína, pascit intercessióne. Per quam incessánter adiúti, fructificáte et vos, caríssimi, quóniam in hoc pósiti estis, ut eátis et fructum afferátis. Imitémur et hunc; quóniam ad hoc venit, ut formam nbis tráderet, et viam demonstráret.

sapientiamsanctorumnarrentpopulietlaudem.en: Let the peoples show forth the wisdom of the Saints, † and let the Church declare their praise.
sapientiamsanctorumnarrentpopulietlaudem.la: Sapiéntiam Sanctórum narrent pópuli, † et laudem eórum pronúntiet Ecclésia.

adestodominesupplicationibusnostrisquasi.en: Be present, O Lord, to our supplications, which we offer on the solemnity of blessed Leopold thy Confessor: that we who have no confidence in our own justice may be helped by the prayers of him who pleased thee.
adestodominesupplicationibusnostrisquasi.la: Adésto, Dómine, supplicatiónibus nostris, quas in beáti Leopóldi, Confessóris tui, solemnitáte deférimus: ut, qui nostræ justítiæ fidúciam non habémus, ejus, qui tibi plácuit, précibus adjuvémur.

deusquilargifluebonitatisconsiliecclesia.en: O God, who by the counsel of thy bountiful goodness hast adorned thy Church with the merits of the illustrious life of blessed Edmund, thy Confessor and Bishop, and hast gladdened her with glorious miracles: mercifully grant unto us thy servants, that we may both be reformed for the better by his examples, and be protected from all adversities by his patronage.
deusquilargifluebonitatisconsiliecclesia.la: Deus, qui largífluæ bonitátis consílio Ecclésiam tuam beáti Edmúndi, Confessóris tui atque Pontíficis, præcláræ vitæ méritis decorásti, et gloriósis lætificásti miráculis, concéde propítius nobis fámulis tuis, ut et ipsíus in mélius reformémur exémplis, et ab ómnibus ejus patrocínio protegámur advérsis.

exaudiquesumusdomineprecesnostrasquasinb.en: Hear, we beseech thee, O Lord, our prayers, which we offer on the solemnity of blessed Eligius, thy Confessor and Bishop: and by the intercession of the merits of him who was found worthy to serve thee, absolve us from all sins.
exaudiquesumusdomineprecesnostrasquasinb.la: Exáudi, quǽsumus, Dómine, preces nostras, quas in beáti Elígii, Confessóris tui atque Pontíficis, solemnitáte deférimus: et, qui tibi digne méruit famulári, ejus intercedéntibus méritis, ab ómnibus nos absólve peccátis.

magnificatanimameadominum.en: My soul * doth magnify the Lord;

quiafecitmihimagnaquipotensestetsanctumn.en: For He That is mighty hath done to me great things, and holy is His name.
quiafecitmihimagnaquipotensestetsanctumn.la: Quia fecit mihi magna qui potens est, et sanctum nomen ejus.

ecceegomittovossicutovesinmedioluporumdi.en: Behold I send you * as sheep in the midst of wolves, saith the Lord. Be ye therefore wise as serpents, and simple as doves.
ecceegomittovossicutovesinmedioluporumdi.la: Ecce ego mitto vos * sicut oves in médio lupórum, dicit Dóminus. Estóte prudéntes sicut serpéntes, et símplices sicut colúmbæ.

dumsteteritisanteregesetpresidesnolitepr.en: When ye shall stand * before kings and governors, take no thought beforehand how ye shall answer; for it shall be given you in that hour what to speak.
dumsteteritisanteregesetpresidesnolitepr.la: Dum stetéritis * ante reges et prǽsides, nolíte præmeditári quáliter respondeátis; dábitur enim vobis in illa hora, quid loquámini.

levatecapitavestrecceappropinquatredempt.en: Lift up your heads: * behold your redemption is at hand.
levatecapitavestrecceappropinquatredempt.la: Leváte cápita vestra: * ecce appropínquat redémptio vestra.

vosquiinpulvereestisexpergisciminietlaud.en: Ye that dwell in the dust, awake and give praise: behold the Lord shall come with salvation.
vosquiinpulvereestisexpergisciminietlaud.la: Vos qui in púlvere estis, expergiscímini, et laudáte: ecce Dóminus véniet cum salúte.

oiudetierusalemnolitetimerecrasegrediemi.en: O Juda and Jerusalem, fear not: tomorrow ye shall go forth, and the Lord will be with you.
oiudetierusalemnolitetimerecrasegrediemi.la: O Juda et Jerúsalem, nolíte timére: cras egrediémini, et Dóminus erit vobíscum.

iudeetierusalemnolitetimerecrasegrediemi.en: O Judea and Jerusalem, * fear not: tomorrow ye shall go forth, and the Lord will be with you, alleluia.
iudeetierusalemnolitetimerecrasegrediemi.la: Judǽa et Jerúsalem, * nolíte timére: cras egrediémini, et Dóminus erit vobíscum, allelúja.

hodiescietisquiavenietdominusetmanevideb.en: This day ye shall know * that the Lord will come: and in the morning ye shall see his glory.
hodiescietisquiavenietdominusetmanevideb.la: Hódie sciétis * quia véniet Dóminus: et mane vidébitis glóriam ejus.

crastineritvobissalusdicitdominusdeusexe.en: Tomorrow shall be your salvation, * saith the Lord God of hosts.
crastineritvobissalusdicitdominusdeusexe.la: Crástina erit vobis salus, * dicit Dóminus Deus exercítuum.

scitotequiapropeestregnumdeiamendicovobi.en: Know ye * that the kingdom of God is at hand: Amen I say to you, it shall not tarry.
scitotequiapropeestregnumdeiamendicovobi.la: Scitóte * quia prope est regnum Dei: Amen dico vobis, quia non tardábit.

antequamconvenirentinventestmariahabensi.en: Before they came together, * Mary was found with child of the Holy Ghost, alleluia.
antequamconvenirentinventestmariahabensi.la: Antequam convenírent * invénta est María habens in útero de Spíritu sancto, allelúia. Ps. 109

iosephfilidavidnolitimereacciperemariamc.en: Joseph, thou Son of David, * fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife; for That Which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost alleluia.
iosephfilidavidnolitimereacciperemariamc.la: Joseph fili David * noli timére accípere Maríam cónjugem tuam: quod enim in ea natum est, de Spíritu sancto est, allelúia. Ps. 110

completisuntdiesmarieutpareretfiliumsuum.en: The days of Mary * were accomplished, that she should bring forth her firstborn Son.
completisuntdiesmarieutpareretfiliumsuum.la: Compléti sunt * dies Maríæ, ut páreret Fílium suum primogénitum. Ps. 111

gaudeamusomnesfidelessalvatornosternatus.en: Let us all rejoice, ye faithful, * our Saviour is born into the world: this day hath come forth the offspring of a glorious stock, and the purity of virginity endureth.
gaudeamusomnesfidelessalvatornosternatus.la: Gaudeámus omnes fidéles, * Salvátor noster natus est in mundo: hódie procéssit proles magnífici gérminis, et persevérat pudos virginitátis. Ps. 112

ecceiamvenitplenitudotemporisinquomisitd.en: Behold now is come * the fulness of time, in which God sent his Son upon earth, born of a Virgin, made under the law, that he might redeem them who were under the law.
ecceiamvenitplenitudotemporisinquomisitd.la: Ecce jam venit * plenitúdo témporis, in quo misit Deus fílium suum in terras, natum de Vírgine, factum sub lege, ut eos qui sub lege erant redímeter. Ps. 116

crasegredieminietdominuseritvobiscum.en: Tomorrow ye shall go out, and the Lord will be with you.
crasegredieminietdominuseritvobiscum.la: Cras egrediémini, et Dóminus erit vobíscum.

cumessetdesponsatamateriesumariaiosephan.en: When Mary the Mother of Jesus * was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child: for that which is born in her is of the Holy Ghost, alleluia.
cumessetdesponsatamateriesumariaiosephan.la: Cum esset * desponsáta Mater Jesu María Joseph, ántequam convenírent, invénta est in útero habens: quod enim in ea natum est, de Spíritu sancto est, allelúia.

verbumcarofactumestalleluiethabitavitinn.en: The Word was made flesh, * alleluia: and dwelt among us, alleluia.
verbumcarofactumestalleluiethabitavitinn.la: Verbum caro factum est, * allelúia: et habitávit in nobis, allelúia. Ps. 96

libcommentinmatthv.en: Book 1 of the Commentary on Matthew, v. 1

inisaialegimusgenerationemeiusquisenarra.en: In Isaias we read: Who shall declare his generation? Let us not therefore think that the Evangelist is contrary to the Prophet, so that what the one said impossible to utter, the other beginneth to relate: for there it is spoken of the generation of the Godhead, here of the incarnation. And he began from things of the flesh, that through the man we may begin to learn God.
inisaialegimusgenerationemeiusquisenarra.la: In Isaía légimus: Generatiónem ejus quis enarrábit? Non ergo putémus Evangelístam Prophétæ esse contrárium, ut quod ille impossíbile dixit effátu, hic narráre incípiat: quia ibi de generatióne Divinitátis, hic de incarnatióne est dictum. A carnálibus autem cœpit, ut per hóminem, Deum díscere incipiámus.

inillotemporeexiitedictumacesareaugustou.en: At that time: There went out a decree from Caesar Augustus, that the whole world should be enrolled. And so on.
inillotemporeexiitedictumacesareaugustou.la: In illo témpore: Exiit edíctum a Cæsare Augústo, ut describerétur univérsus orbis. Et réliqua.

quidestquodnasciturodominomundusdescribi.en: Why is it that, when the Lord is about to be born, the world is enrolled, save that this is plainly shown, that he was appearing in the flesh who should enrol his elect in eternity? Whereas of the reprobate it is said by the Prophet: Let them be blotted out of the book of the living, and with the just let them not be written. Who fitly also is born in Bethlehem: for Bethlehem is interpreted the house of bread. For he it is who saith: I am the living bread, which came down from heaven. The place, therefore, in which the Lord is born, was before called the house of bread; because it was indeed to come to pass, that he should there appear in the substance of flesh, who should refresh the minds of the elect with inward fulness.
quidestquodnasciturodominomundusdescribi.la: Quid est quod nascitúro Dómino mundus descríbitur, nisi hoc, quod aperte monstrátur, quia ille apparébat in carne, qui eléctos suos adscríberet in æternitáte? Quo contra de réprobis per Prophétam dícitur: Deleántur de libro vivéntium, et cum justis non scribántur. Qui bene étiam in Béthlehem náscitur: Bethlehem quippe domus panis interpretátur. Ipse namque est, qui ait: Ego sum panis vivus, qui de cœlo descéndi. Locus ergo, in quo Dóminus náscitur, domus panis antea vocátus est; quia futúrum profécto erat, ut ille ibi per matériam carnis apparéret, qui electórum mentes intérna satietáte refíceret.

inillotemporepastoresloquebanturadinvice.en: At that time, the shepherds said one to another: Let us go over to Bethlehem, and let us see this word that is come to pass, which the Lord hath showed to us. And so on.
inillotemporepastoresloquebanturadinvice.la: In illo témpore: Pastores loquebántur ad invicem: Transeámus usque Béthlehem, et videámus hoc verbum, quod factum est, quod Dóminus osténdit nobis. Et réliqua.

videteecclesiesurgentisexordiumchristusn.en: See the beginning of the rising Church: Christ is born, and the shepherds began to watch; that they might gather into the fold of the Lord the flocks of the Gentiles, which before lived after the manner of cattle, lest they should suffer the incursions of spiritual beasts through the outspread darkness of the nights. And well do the shepherds watch, whom the good shepherd formeth. The flock therefore is the people, the night the world, the shepherds are the priests. Or perhaps he too may be a shepherd, to whom it is said: Be watchful, and strengthen. For the Lord hath ordained not only Bishops to guard the flock, but hath appointed Angels also.
videteecclesiesurgentisexordiumchristusn.la: Vidéte Ecclésiæ surgéntis exórdium: Christus náscitur, et pastóres vigiláre cœpérunt; qui Géntium greges, pécudum modo ante vivéntes, in caulam Dómini congregárent, ne quos spiritálium bestiárum per offúsas noctium ténebras pateréntur incúrsus. Et bene pastóres vígilant, quos bonus pastor infórmat. Grex ígitur pópulus, nox sæculum, pastóres sunt sacerdótes. Aut fortásse etiam ille sit pastor, cui dícitur: Esto vigilans, et confírma. Quia non solum Epíscopos ad tuéndum gregem Dóminus ordinávit, sed etiam Angelos destinávit.

inprincipieratverbumetverbumeratapuddeum.en: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. And so on.
inprincipieratverbumetverbumeratapuddeum.la: In principio erat Verbum, et Verbum erat apud Deum, et Deus erat Verbum. Et réliqua.

nevilealiquidputaresqualeconsuevisticogi.en: Lest thou shouldst think it some mean thing, such as thou art wont to think of when thou wast used to hear human words, hear what thou art to think: The Word was God. Let now some unbelieving Arian or other come forth, and say that the Word of God was made. How can it be that the Word of God was made, when God made all things by the Word? If the Word of God itself also was made: by what other word was it made? If thou sayest this, that it is the word of the Word by which that was made; that very one I call the only Son of God. But if thou sayest not the word of the Word, grant that he was not made, by whom all things were made. For that by which all things were made could not be made by itself. Believe therefore the Evangelist.
nevilealiquidputaresqualeconsuevisticogi.la: Ne vile áliquid putáres quale consuevísti cogitáre, cum verba humána soléres audíre, audi quid cógites: Deus erat Verbum. Exeat nunc néscio quis infidélis Ariánus, et dicat quia Verbum Dei factum est. Quómodo potest fíeri, ut Verbum Dei factum sit, quando Deus per Verbum fecit ómnia? Si et Verbum Dei ipsum factum est: per quod aliud verbum factum est? Si hoc dicis, quia hoc est verbum Verbi, per quod factum est illud; ipsum dico ego únicum Fílium Dei. Si autem non dicis verbum Verbi, concéde non factum, per quod facta sunt ómnia. Non enim per seípsum fíeri pótuit, per quod facta sunt ómnia. Crede ergo Evangelístæ.

luxortestsupernosquiahodienatusestsalvat.en: Light hath risen * upon us: for this day is born the Saviour, alleluia.
luxortestsupernosquiahodienatusestsalvat.la: Lux orta est * super nos: quia hódie natus est Salvátor, allelúia.

virgohodiefidelisetsiverbumgenuitincarna.en: The faithful Virgin this day, * though she brought forth the Word incarnate, remained a Virgin even after childbirth; whom praising we all say: Blessed art thou among women.
virgohodiefidelisetsiverbumgenuitincarna.la: Virgo hódie fidélis, * etsi Verbum génuit incarnátum, Virgo mansit et post partum, quam laudántes omnes dícimus: Benedícta tu in muliéribus.

gaudeamusomnesfidelessalvatornosternatus.en: Let us all rejoice, ye faithful, * our Saviour is born into the world: this day hath come forth the offspring of a glorious stock, and the purity of virginity endureth.
gaudeamusomnesfidelessalvatornosternatus.la: Gaudeámus omnes fidéles, * Salvátor noster natus est in mundo: hódie procéssit proles magnífici gérminis, et persevérat pudor virginitátis.

hodieintactavirgodeumnobisgenuittenerisi.en: This day * the spotless Virgin hath brought forth God for us, clothed in tender limbs, whom she was found worthy to suckle: let us all adore him, who cometh to save us.
hodieintactavirgodeumnobisgenuittenerisi.la: Hódie * intácta Virgo Deum nobis génuit téneris indútum membris, quem lactáre méruit: omnes ipsum adorémus, qui venit salváre nos.

inprincipietanteseculadeuseratverbumipse.en: In the beginning * and before the worlds the Word was God: he is born to us the Saviour of the world.
inprincipietanteseculadeuseratverbumipse.la: In princípio * et ante sǽcula Deus erat Verbum: ipse natus est nobis Salvátor mundi. Ps. 109

illuxitnobisdiesredemptionisnovereparati.en: There hath dawned upon us the day * of new redemption, of ancient restoration, of eternal happiness.
illuxitnobisdiesredemptionisnovereparati.la: Illúxit nobis dies * redemptiónis novæ, reparatiónis antíquæ, felicitátis ætérnæ. Ps. 131

cumautemessetplenusspiritusanctetfidebea.en: And when blessed Stephen was full of the Holy Ghost, and of faith:
cumautemessetplenusspiritusanctetfidebea.la: Cum autem esset plenus Spíritu Sancto, et fide, beátus Stéphanus:

etconcurrentesrapuerunteumetadduxeruntin.en: And running together they took him, and brought him to the council:
etconcurrentesrapuerunteumetadduxeruntin.la: Et concurréntes rapuérunt eum, et adduxérunt in concílium:

impetumfeceruntunanimiterineumeteiecerun.en: They ran violently upon him with one accord, and casting him forth without the city
impetumfeceruntunanimiterineumeteiecerun.la: Impetum fecérunt unanímiter in eum, et ejecérunt eum extra civitátem

invocantemetdicentemdomineiesuaccipespir.en: Calling upon and saying: Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.
invocantemetdicentemdomineiesuaccipespir.la: Invocántem et dicéntem: Dómine Jesu, áccipe spíritum meum.

ettestesdeposueruntvestimentasuasecusped.en: And the witnesses laid down their garments at the feet of a young man, whose name was Saul: and they stoned him,
ettestesdeposueruntvestimentasuasecusped.la: Et testes deposuérunt vestiménta sua secus pedes adulescéntis, qui vocabátur Saulus: et lapidábant eum,

pretiosusathletadoministephanuspositisge.en: Stephen, the precious champion of the Lord, kneeling down prayed, saying:
pretiosusathletadoministephanuspositisge.la: Pretiósus athléta Dómini Stéphanus, pósitis génibus orávit, dicens:

domineiesuchristenestatuasillishocpeccat.en: O Lord Jesus Christ, lay not this sin to their charge.
domineiesuchristenestatuasillishocpeccat.la: Dómine Jesu Christe, ne státuas illis hoc peccátum.

lapidabantiudeistephanumatilleorabatdice.en: The Jews stoned Stephen: but he prayed, saying:
lapidabantiudeistephanumatilleorabatdice.la: Lapidábant Judæi Stéphanum: at ille orábat, dicens:

positisgenibusbeatusstephanusclamavitvoc.en: Falling on his knees, blessed Stephen cried with a loud voice, saying: O Lord Jesus Christ, lay not this sin to their charge:
positisgenibusbeatusstephanusclamavitvoc.la: Pósitis génibus, beátus Stéphanus clamávit voce magna, dicens: Dómine Jesu Christe, ne státuas illis hoc peccátum:

etcumhocdixissetobdormivitindomino.en: And when he had said this, he fell asleep in the Lord.
etcumhocdixissetobdormivitindomino.la: Et cum hoc dixísset, obdormívit in Dómino.

lapidabantstephanuminvocantemetdicentemd.en: They stoned Stephen, invoking and saying: O Lord Jesus, receive my spirit:
lapidabantstephanuminvocantemetdicentemd.la: Lapidábant Stéphanum invocántem et dicéntem: Dómine Jesu, áccipe spíritum meum:

sanctedeipretioseprotomartyrstephanequiv.en: O precious Saint of God, Stephen, Protomartyr, who, compassed about on every side by the power of charity, didst entreat the Lord for a hostile people:
sanctedeipretioseprotomartyrstephanequiv.la: Sancte Dei pretióse Protomártyr Stéphane, qui virtúte caritátis circumfúltus úndique, Dóminum pro inimico exorásti pópulo:

fundeprecesprodevototibinunccollegio.en: Pour forth prayers for the company now devoted to thee.
fundeprecesprodevototibinunccollegio.la: Funde preces Pro devóto tibi nunc collégio.

uttuopropitiatusinterventudominusnospurg.en: That the Lord, appeased by thine intercession, may join us, cleansed from our sins, unto the citizens of heaven.
uttuopropitiatusinterventudominusnospurg.la: Ut tuo propitiátus intervéntu, Dóminus nos purgátos a peccátis jungat cæli cívibus.

cumautemessetplenusspiritusanctointenden.en: But he, being full of the Holy Ghost, looking up steadfastly to heaven, saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing on the right hand of God.
cumautemessetplenusspiritusanctointenden.la: Cum autem esset plenus Spíritu sancto, inténdens in cœlum, vidit glóriam Dei, et Jesum stantem ad dextris Dei.

commemoratioomniumssmartyrum.en: Commemoration of all the Holy Martyrs

deusquinosannuaomniumsanctorummartyrumtu.en: O God, who dost gladden us by the yearly commemoration of all thy holy Martyrs: § mercifully grant; * that we may be kindled by the examples § of those in whose merits we rejoice.
deusquinosannuaomniumsanctorummartyrumtu.la: Deus, qui nos annua ómnium sanctórum Mártyrum tuórum commemoratióne lætíficas: § concéde propítius; * ut, quorum gaudémus méritis, § accendámur exémplis.
