adoremusregemapostolorumquiprivilegioamo.en: Let us adore the King of the Apostles, * Who by a privilege of love loved John the Apostle.
adoremusregemapostolorumquiprivilegioamo.la: Adorémus regem Apostolórum, * Qui privilégio amóris Joánnem diléxit Apóstolum.

quitestimoniumperhibuitverbodeiettestimo.en: Who hath given testimony to the word of God, and the testimony of Jesus Christ, what things soever he hath seen.
quitestimoniumperhibuitverbodeiettestimo.la: Qui testimónium pérhibuit verbo Dei, et testimónium Jesu Christi, quæcúmque vidit.

muliereccefiliustuusaddiscipulumautemecc.en: Woman, behold thy son; and to the disciple: Behold thy Mother.
muliereccefiliustuusaddiscipulumautemecc.la: Múlier, ecce fílius tuus; ad discípulum autem: Ecce Mater tua.

isteestioannesquisuprapectusdominiincena.en: This is that John which leaned on the Lord's Breast at supper
isteestioannesquisuprapectusdominiincena.la: Iste est Joánnes, qui supra pectus Dómini in cena recúbuit:

beatusapostoluscuirevelatasuntsecretacel.en: Even that blessed Apostle unto whom were made known the secret things of heaven.
beatusapostoluscuirevelatasuntsecretacel.la: Beátus Apóstolus, cui reveláta sunt secréta cæléstia.

isteestioannescuichristusincrucematremvi.en: This is John, to whom Christ on the cross commended his virgin Mother, a virgin to a virgin.
isteestioannescuichristusincrucematremvi.la: Iste est Joánnes, cui Christus in cruce Matrem virginem virgini commendávit.

virgestelectusadominoatqueinterceterosma.en: He is a virgin chosen by the Lord, and beloved more than the rest, † who, reclining upon his breast, drank the streams of the Gospel from that very sacred fountain of the Lord's breast, and the grace of the word of God
virgestelectusadominoatqueinterceterosma.la: Virgo est eléctus a Dómino atque inter céteros magis diléctus, † qui supra pectus ejus recúmbens Evangélii fluénta de ipso sacro domínici péctoris fonte potávit, et verbi Dei grátiam

intototerrarumorbediffudit.en: He poured forth over the whole world.

quasiunusexparadisifluminibusevangelista.en: As one of the rivers of paradise, John the Evangelist the grace of the word of God,
quasiunusexparadisifluminibusevangelista.la: Quasi unus ex paradísi flumínibus Evangelísta Joánnes verbi Dei grátiam,

misitdominusmanussuamettetigitoseius.en: The Lord put forth his hand, and touched his mouth:
misitdominusmanussuamettetigitoseius.la: Misit Dóminus manus suam, et tétigit os ejus:

inmediecclesieaperuitdominusoseiusetimpl.en: In the midst * of the Church the Lord opened his mouth, and filled him with the spirit of wisdom and understanding, alleluia.
inmediecclesieaperuitdominusoseiusetimpl.la: In médio * Ecclésiæ apéruit Dóminus os ejus, et implévit eum spíritu sapiéntiæ et intelléctus, allelúia.

mirabilemdeuminsanctissuisveniteadoremus.en: God wonderful in his Saints, * Come, let us adore.
mirabilemdeuminsanctissuisveniteadoremus.la: Mirábilem Deum in Sanctis suis, * Veníte adorémus.

subaltaredeiaudivivocesoccisorumdicentiu.en: Under the altar of God I heard the voices of the slain, saying: Why dost thou not defend our blood? And they received the divine answer:
subaltaredeiaudivivocesoccisorumdicentiu.la: Sub altáre Dei audívi voces occisórum dicéntium: Quare non deféndis sánguinem nostrum? Et accepérunt divínum respónsum:

adhucsustinetemodicumtempusdonecimpleatu.en: Rest yet for a little season, until the number of your brethren be fulfilled.
adhucsustinetemodicumtempusdonecimpleatu.la: Adhuc sustinéte módicum tempus, donec impleátur númerus fratrum vestrórum.

etdatesuntillissingulestolealbeetdictume.en: And white robes were given to every one of them, and it was said to them:
etdatesuntillissingulestolealbeetdictume.la: Et datæ sunt illis síngulæ stolæ albæ, et dictum est eis:

istisuntquinoninquinaveruntvestimentasua.en: These are they who have not defiled their garments: They shall walk with me in white,
istisuntquinoninquinaveruntvestimentasua.la: Isti sunt, qui non inquinavérunt vestiménta sua: Ambulábunt mecum in albis,

etnondelebonomineorumdelibrovite.en: And I will not blot out their names out of the book of life:
etnondelebonomineorumdelibrovite.la: Et non delébo nómina eórum de libro vitæ:

hisuntquicummulieribusnonsuntcoinquinati.en: These are they which were not defiled with women for they are virgins.
hisuntquicummulieribusnonsuntcoinquinati.la: Hi sunt, qui cum muliéribus non sunt coinquináti: Vírgines enim sunt,

etsequunturagnumquocumqueierit.en: And they follow the Lamb whithersoever he goeth.

coronaviteosdominuscoronaiustitie.en: The Lord hath crowned them with a crown of justice,

quiapassisuntprodominetsequunturagnum.en: Because they have suffered for the Lord, and they follow the Lamb.
quiapassisuntprodominetsequunturagnum.la: Quia passi sunt pro Dómino, et sequúntur Agnum.

laveruntstolassuasetcandidaseasfecerunti.en: They have washed their robes, and have made them white in the blood of the Lamb.
laveruntstolassuasetcandidaseasfecerunti.la: Lavérunt stolas suas et cándidas eas fecérunt in sánguine Agni.

centumquadragintaquatuormilliaquiemptisu.en: A hundred forty-four * thousand, who were purchased from the earth, these are they who were not defiled with women, for they are virgins, therefore they reign with God, and with the Lamb without spot.
centumquadragintaquatuormilliaquiemptisu.la: Centum quadragínta * quátuor míllia, qui empti sunt de terra, hi sunt, qui cum muliéribus non sunt coinquináti, Vírgines enim sunt, ídeo regnant cum Deo, et Agno sine mácula.

subthronodeisancticlamant.en: Under the throne of God the Saints cry out:

vindicasanguinemnostrumdeusnoster.en: Avenge our blood, O our God.

ambulabuntmecuminalbisquoniamdignisunt.en: They shall walk with me in white, because they are worthy:
ambulabuntmecuminalbisquoniamdignisunt.la: Ambulábunt mecum in albis, quóniam digni sunt:

centumquadragintaquatuormilliaquiemptisu.en: A hundred forty-four thousand, who were purchased from the earth, these are they who were not defiled with women: for they have remained virgins:
centumquadragintaquatuormilliaquiemptisu.la: Centum quadragínta quátuor míllia, qui empti sunt de terra, hi sunt, qui cum muliéribus non sunt coinquináti: Vírgines enim permansérunt:

ideoregnantcumdeetagnosinemacula.en: Therefore they reign with God, and with the Lamb without spot.
ideoregnantcumdeetagnosinemacula.la: Ideo regnant cum Deo, et Agno sine mácula.

abimatuetinfraocciditmultospuerosherodes.en: Herod slew many children * from two years old, and under, for the Lord's sake.
abimatuetinfraocciditmultospuerosherodes.la: A bimátu * et infra occídit multos púeros Heródes propter Dóminum.

siniteparvulosadmeveniretaliumestenimreg.en: Suffer the little children * to come unto me, for of such is the kingdom of heaven.
siniteparvulosadmeveniretaliumestenimreg.la: Sínite párvulos * ad me veníre, tálium est enim regnum cœlórum.

hiemptisuntexhominibusprimitiedeetagneti.en: These were purchased * from among men, the firstfruits to God and to the Lamb; and in their mouth there was found no lie.
hiemptisuntexhominibusprimitiedeetagneti.la: Hi empti sunt * ex homínibus primítiæ Deo et Agno; et in ore eórum non est invéntum mendácium.

munimineregioseptusnullatenusestabadvers.en: Fenced about with a kingly defence, he was in no wise overcome by his adversaries:
munimineregioseptusnullatenusestabadvers.la: Munímine régio septus, nullátenus est ab adversáriis superátus:

eccesacerdosmagnusquiindiebussuisplacuit.en: Behold an high priest, * who in his days pleased God, and was found righteous.
eccesacerdosmagnusquiindiebussuisplacuit.la: Ecce sacérdos magnus, * qui in diébus suis plácuit Deo, et invéntus est justus.

eugeserveboneinmodicofidelisintraingaudi.en: Well done, thou good servant, * thou hast been faithful in a very little, enter thou into the joy of thy Lord.
eugeserveboneinmodicofidelisintraingaudi.la: Euge serve bone, * in módico fidélis, intra in gáudium Dómini tui.

fidelisservusetprudensquemconstituitdomi.en: A faithful and wise servant * whom his Lord hath made ruler over His household.
fidelisservusetprudensquemconstituitdomi.la: Fidélis servus, et prudens, * quem constítuit Dóminus super famíliam suam.

beatusilleservuscumveneritdominuseiusetp.en: Blessed is that servant, * whom, when his Lord shall come and knock at the door, he shall find watching.
beatusilleservuscumveneritdominuseiusetp.la: Beátus ille servus, * cum vénerit Dóminus ejus, et pulsáverit jánuam, et invénerit eum vigilántem.

eccevereisrelitainquodolusnonest.en: Behold an Israelite * indeed, in whom there is no guile.
eccevereisrelitainquodolusnonest.la: Ecce vere * Israëlita, in quo dolus non est.

silvesterromanuspatrerufinoaprimaetateop.en: Silvester, a Roman, whose father was Rufinus, from his earliest years gave himself to the priest Cyrinus: whose teaching and manners he excellently imitated, and in his thirtieth year he was made a Priest of the holy Roman Church by Pope Marcellinus. And since in that office he excelled the other clerics in all praise, he afterwards succeeded to the place of Melchiades, under the emperor Constantine.
silvesterromanuspatrerufinoaprimaetateop.la: Silvéster Románus, patre Rufíno, a prima ætáte operam dedit Cyríno Presbytero: cujus doctrínam et mores egrégie imitátus, trigésimum annum agens, Presbyter sanctæ Románæ Ecclésiæ a Marcellíno Pontífice creátur. Quo in múnere cum omni laude cléricis áliis antecélleret, in Melchíadis póstea locum succéssit, imperatóre Constantíno.

huicimperatoricumleprecurandecausasibiex.en: When this emperor, for the healing of his leprosy, had, by the counsel of the physicians, commanded a bath to be prepared for him of the blood of infants, the holy Apostles Peter and Paul appeared to him in his sleep, bidding him, if he would be freed from the leprosy, to give up the cruelty of the impious bath and to send for Silvester, who lay hidden on Mount Soracte: and, being restored by him with the saving laver, to command that churches be built after the Christian manner throughout all the dominion of the Roman Empire, and, the images of the vain gods being taken away, to render worship to the true God.
huicimperatoricumleprecurandecausasibiex.la: Huic imperatóri, cum lepræ curandae causa, sibi ex infántium sánguine, medicórum consílio, bálneum parári jussísset, sancti Apóstoli Petrus et Paulus in quiéte apparuérunt, præcipiéntes ei, ut si ex lepra liberári vellet, omíssa ímpii bálnei immanitáte, Silvéstrum in Sorácte monte latitántem accérseret: a quo salutári lavácro recreátus, in omni ditióne Románi Impérii templa Christiáno more ædificári imperáret, sublatísque inánium deórum simulácris, vero Deo cultum adhíberet.

constantinusigiturcelestibusmonitisobtem.en: Constantine therefore, obeying the heavenly warnings, called Silvester, who had been most diligently sought out: and recognising from him the images of the Apostles, he was healed by baptism, and was inflamed to defend and spread the religion of Christ. And so, at Silvester's instance, he built many Basilicas, which he adorned with sacred images, and with most magnificent gifts and offerings: giving also to the Christians leave, which before had been denied, to build churches openly.
constantinusigiturcelestibusmonitisobtem.la: Constantínus ígitur cœléstibus mónitis obtémperans, Silvéstrum diligentíssime conquisítum vocat: a quo Apostolórum imágines recognóscens, baptísmo sanátur, et ad tuéndam propagandámque Christi religiónem inflammátur. Itaque auctóre Silvéstro multas Basílicas ædificávit, quas sacris imagínibus, donísque ac munéribus magnificentíssimis exornávit: facultáte étiam data Christiánis, quod antea negátum erat, públice templa extruéndi.

hocpontificehabitasuntduoconcilianicenum.en: Under this Pontiff were held two Councils, of Nicaea and of Rome, wherein Arius was condemned. He likewise made many decrees profitable to the Church of God. And to that heavenly prudence with which he governed the Church there ever answered a signal holiness of life and kindness towards the poor.
hocpontificehabitasuntduoconcilianicenum.la: Hoc Pontífice hábita sunt duo Concília, Nicænum et Románum, ubi Arius condemnátus est. Multa item decréta fecit Ecclésiæ Dei utília. Cui cœlésti prudéntiæ, qua Ecclésiam administrábat, insígnis vitæ sánctitas, et benígnitas in páuperes perpétuo respóndit.

hocestpreceptummeumutdiligatisinvicemsic.en: This is my commandment * that you love one another, as I have loved you.
hocestpreceptummeumutdiligatisinvicemsic.la: Hoc est præcéptum meum, * ut diligátis ínvicem, sicut diléxi vos.

maioremcharitatemnemohabetutanimamsuampo.en: Greater love * than this no man hath, that a man lay down his life for his friends.
maioremcharitatemnemohabetutanimamsuampo.la: Majórem charitátem * nemo habet, ut ánimam suam ponat quis pro amícis suis.

vosamicimeiestissifeceritisqueprecipiovo.en: You are my friends * if you do the things that I command you, said the Lord.
vosamicimeiestissifeceritisqueprecipiovo.la: Vos amíci mei estis, * si fecéritis quæ præcípio vobis, dicit Dóminus.

gaudeteetexultatequianominavestrascripta.en: Rejoice and be glad: * For your names are written in heaven.
gaudeteetexultatequianominavestrascripta.la: Gaudéte, et exultáte: * Quia nómina vestra scripta sunt in cœlis.

hecestgeneratioquerentiumdominumquerenti.en: This is the generation of them that seek the Lord, * that seek the face of the God of Jacob.
hecestgeneratioquerentiumdominumquerenti.la: Hæc est generátio * quæréntium Dóminum, quæréntium fáciem Dei Jacob. Ps. 23

verbodominicelifirmatisuntetspirituorise.en: By the word * of the Lord the heavens were established: and all the power of them by the spirit of his mouth.
verbodominicelifirmatisuntetspirituorise.la: Verbo * Dómini cœli firmáti sunt: et spíritu oris ejus omnis virtus eórum. Ps. 32

clamaveruntiustietdominusexaudiviteos.en: The just cried * and the Lord heard them.
clamaveruntiustietdominusexaudiviteos.la: Clamavérunt justi, * et Dóminus exaudívit eos. Ps. 33

constitueseosprincipessuperomnemterramme.en: Thou shalt make them princes * over all the earth. They shall remember thy name, O Lord.
constitueseosprincipessuperomnemterramme.la: Constítues eos * príncipes super omnem terram: mémores erunt nóminis tui, Dómine. Ps. 44

principespopulorumcongregatisuntcumdeoab.en: The princes of the people * are gathered together, with the God of Abraham.
principespopulorumcongregatisuntcumdeoab.la: Príncipes populórum * congregáti sunt cum Deo Ábraham. Ps. 46

dedistihereditatemtimentibusnomentuumdom.en: Thou hast given an inheritance * to them that fear thy name, O Lord.
dedistihereditatemtimentibusnomentuumdom.la: Dedísti hereditátem * timéntibus nomen tuum, Dómine. Ps. 60

annuntiaveruntoperadeietfacteiusintellex.en: They declared * the works of God, and understood his doings.
annuntiaveruntoperadeietfacteiusintellex.la: Annuntiavérunt * ópera Dei, et facta ejus intellexérunt. Ps. 63

beatiquoselegistidominehabitabuntinatrii.en: Blessed are they * whom thou hast chosen, O Lord; they shall dwell in thy courts.
beatiquoselegistidominehabitabuntinatrii.la: Beáti, * quos elegísti, Dómine, habitábunt in átriis tuis. Ps. 64

peccatorumconfringamcornuetexaltabunturc.en: All the horns of sinners * I will break, and the horns of the just shall be exalted.
peccatorumconfringamcornuetexaltabunturc.la: Peccatórum * confríngam córnua, et exaltabúntur córnua justi. Ps. 74

luxortestiustorectiscordeletitiaalleluia.en: Light is risen * to the just, and joy to the right of heart, alleluia.
luxortestiustorectiscordeletitiaalleluia.la: Lux orta est * justo, rectis corde lætítia, allelúja. Ps. 96

custodiebanttestimonieiusetprecepteiusal.en: They kept * his testimonies, and his commandments, alleluia.
custodiebanttestimonieiusetprecepteiusal.la: Custodiébant * testimónia ejus, et præcépta ejus, allelúja. Ps. 98

inpatientiavestrapossidebitisanimasvestr.en: In your patience * you shall possess your souls.
inpatientiavestrapossidebitisanimasvestr.la: In patiéntia vestra * possidébitis ánimas vestras. Ps. 253, 254, 255

iamnondicamvosservossedamicosmeosquiaomn.en: I will not now call * you servants, but my friends: for all things whatsoever I have heard of my Father, I have made known to you.
iamnondicamvosservossedamicosmeosquiaomn.la: Jam non dicam * vos servos, sed amícos meos: quia ómnia quæcúmque audívi a Patre meo, nota feci vobis. Ps. 109

tolliteiugummeumsupervosquiamitissumethu.en: Take up * my yoke upon you, for I am meek and humble of heart.
tolliteiugummeumsupervosquiamitissumethu.la: Tóllite * jugum meum super vos, quia mitis sum et húmilis corde. Ps. 112

iugumenimmeumsuaveestetonusmeumlevedicit.en: For my yoke * is sweet, and my burden light, saith the Lord.
iugumenimmeumsuaveestetonusmeumlevedicit.la: Jugum enim meum * suáve est, et onus meum leve, dicit Dóminus. Ps. 115

tradentenimvosinconciliisetinsynagogissu.en: For they will deliver you up * in councils, and they will scourge you in their synagogues: and you shall be brought before kings and governors for my sake, for a testimony to them and to the Gentiles.
tradentenimvosinconciliisetinsynagogissu.la: Tradent enim vos * in concíliis, et in synagógis suis flagellábunt vos: et ante reges et præsides ducémini proper me in testimónium illis, et Géntibus. Ps. 125

maneteindilectionemeasicutdilexivos.en: Abide in my love, as I have loved you.
maneteindilectionemeasicutdilexivos.la: Manéte in dilectióne mea, sicut diléxi vos.

utmemoriterteneantalleluietoredecantenta.en: That they may keep it in memory, alleluia, and sing it with their mouth, * Alleluia, alleluia.
utmemoriterteneantalleluietoredecantenta.la: Ut memóriter téneant, allelúia, et ore decántent, * Allelúia, allelúia.

filiiquinascenturetexurgentenarrabuntfil.en: The children that shall be born and shall rise up shall declare it to their children:
filiiquinascenturetexurgentenarrabuntfil.la: Fílii qui nascéntur et exúrgent, enarrábunt fíliis suis:

utmemoriterteneantalleluietoredecantent.en: That they may keep it in memory, alleluia, and sing it with their mouth.
utmemoriterteneantalleluietoredecantent.la: Ut memóriter téneant, allelúia, et ore decántent.

gaudeteiustiindominoalleluiarectosdecetc.en: Rejoice in the Lord, ye just, alleluia; praise becometh the upright,
gaudeteiustiindominoalleluiarectosdecetc.la: Gaudéte justi in Dómino, allelúia, rectos decet collaudátio,

cantateeicanticumnovumbenepsalliteeiiniu.en: Sing to him a new canticle: sing well unto him with a loud noise.
cantateeicanticumnovumbenepsalliteeiiniu.la: Cantáte ei cánticum novum: bene psállite ei in jubilatióne.

voxexsultationisetsalutisintabernaculisi.en: The voice of rejoicing and of salvation is in the tabernacles of the just.
voxexsultationisetsalutisintabernaculisi.la: Vox exsultatiónis, et salútis in tabernáculis justórum.

istisuntdueoliveetduocandelabralucentiaa.en: These are the two olive trees, and the two candlesticks shining before the Lord, alleluia.
istisuntdueoliveetduocandelabralucentiaa.la: Isti sunt duæ olívæ, et duo candelábra lucéntia ante Dóminum, allelúia.

habentpotestatemclauderecelumnubibusetap.en: They have power to shut heaven with clouds, and to open its gates, for their tongues are made the keys of heaven, alleluia.
habentpotestatemclauderecelumnubibusetap.la: Habent potestátem cláudere cœlum núbibus, et aperíre portas ejus, quia linguæ eórum claves cœli factæ sunt, allelúia.

inomnemterramexivitsonuseorumalleluiaall.en: Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth, Alleluia, alleluia.
inomnemterramexivitsonuseorumalleluiaall.la: In omnem terram exívit sonus eórum, Allelúia, allelúia.

constitueseosprincipessuperomnemterramal.en: Thou shalt make them Princes over all the earth, alleluia, alleluia.
constitueseosprincipessuperomnemterramal.la: Constítues eos Príncipes super omnem terram, allelúia, allelúia.

memoreseruntnoministuidomine.en: They shall remember thy name, O Lord.

incelestibusregnissanctorumhabitatiestal.en: In the heavenly kingdoms * is the dwelling of the Saints, alleluia, and their rest is for ever, alleluia.
incelestibusregnissanctorumhabitatiestal.la: In cœléstibus regnis * Sanctórum habitátio est, allelúia, et in ætérnum réquies eórum, allelúia.

beatusvirquisufferttentationemquiacumpro.en: Blessed is the man * that endureth temptation: for when he hath been proved, he shall receive the crown of life, which God hath promised to them that love him.
beatusvirquisufferttentationemquiacumpro.la: Beátus vir, * qui suffert tentatiónem: quia cum probátus fúerit, accípiet corónam vitæ, quam repromísit Deus his, qui díligunt eum.

regemsempiternumveniteadoremusquimartyre.en: Come, let us adore the everlasting King, * Who hath crowned his Martyr N.
regemsempiternumveniteadoremusquimartyre.la: Regem sempitérnum veníte adorémus: * Qui Mártyrem suum coronávit N..

beatusvirquiinlegedominimeditaturvolunta.en: Blessed is the man * that doth meditate in the law of the Lord; his delight is therein day and night, and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper.
beatusvirquiinlegedominimeditaturvolunta.la: Beátus vir, * qui in lege Dómini meditátur, volúntas ejus pérmanet die ac nocte; et ómnia quæcúmque fáciet, semper prosperabúntur. Ps. 1

beatusistesanctusquiconfisusestindominop.en: Blessed and holy is he * that putteth his trust in the Lord, that declareth the decree of the Lord, and is set upon His holy hill.
beatusistesanctusquiconfisusestindominop.la: Beátus * iste Sanctus, qui confísus est in Dómino, prædicávit præcéptum Dómini, constitútus est in monte sancto ejus. Ps. 2

invocantemexaudivitdominussanctumsuumdom.en: When His holy one called, * the Lord heard him, yea, the Lord heard him, and gave him peace.
invocantemexaudivitdominussanctumsuumdom.la: Invocántem * exaudívit Dóminus sanctum suum: Dóminus exaudívit eum, et constítuit eum in pace. Ps. 4

scutobonevoluntatistuecoronastieumdomine.en: O Lord, Thou hast compassed him * with thy favour as with a shield.
scutobonevoluntatistuecoronastieumdomine.la: Scuto bonæ voluntátis * tuæ coronásti eum Dómine. Ps. 5

dominedominusnosterquamadmirabileestnome.en: O Lord, our Ruler, * how excellent is thy Name in all the earth, Who hast crowned thine holy one with glory and honour, and made him to have dominion over the works of thy hands.
dominedominusnosterquamadmirabileestnome.la: Dómine, * Dóminus noster, quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra! quia glória et honóre coronásti Sanctum tuum, et constituísti eum super ópera mánuum tuárum. Ps. 8

iustusdominusetiustitiamdilexitequitatem.en: The righteous Lord * loveth righteousness; His countenance doth behold uprightness.
iustusdominusetiustitiamdilexitequitatem.la: Justus Dóminus, * et justítiam diléxit: æquitátem vidit vultus ejus. Ps. 10

domineistesanctushabitabitintabernaculot.en: O Lord, * this Saint shall dwell in thy tabernacle: he hath wrought thy justice, he shall rest in thy holy mountain.
domineistesanctushabitabitintabernaculot.la: Dómine, * iste Sanctus habitábit in tabernáculo tuo: operátus est justítiam tuam, requiéscet in monte sancto tuo. Ps. 14

vitampetiitateettribuistieidominegloriam.en: He asked life * of thee, and thou gavest it him, O Lord: glory and great beauty hast thou laid upon him, thou hast set on his head a crown of precious stones.
vitampetiitateettribuistieidominegloriam.la: Vitam * pétiit a te, et tribuísti ei, Dómine: glóriam et magnum decérem imposuísti super eum, posuísti in cápite ejus corónam de lápide pretióso. Ps. 20

hicaccipietbenedictionemadominetmiserico.en: He shall receive * a blessing from the Lord, and mercy from the God of his salvation, for this is the generation of them that seek the Lord.
hicaccipietbenedictionemadominetmiserico.la: Hic accípiet * benedictiónem a Dómino, et misericórdiam a Deo salutári suo: quia hæc est generátio quæréntium Dóminum. Ps. 23

letabituriustusindominetsperabitineetlau.en: The just shall rejoice * in the Lord, and shall hope in him: and all the upright in heart shall be praised.
letabituriustusindominetsperabitineetlau.la: Lætábitur justus * in Dómino et sperábit in eo, et laudabúntur omnes recti corde Ps. 63

beatusquemelegistidominehabitabitinatrii.en: Blessed is * he whom thou hast chosen: he shall dwell in thy courts.
beatusquemelegistidominehabitabitinatrii.la: Beátus * quem elegísti Dómine, habitábit in átriis tuis Ps. 64

nisigranumfrumenticadensinterrammortuumf.en: Unless the grain of wheat * falling into the ground die, itself remaineth alone.
nisigranumfrumenticadensinterrammortuumf.la: Nisi granum fruménti * cadens in terram, mórtuum fúerit; ipsum solum manet. Ps. 256, 257, 258

hicestveremartyrquiprochristinominesangu.en: This is truly a Martyr, * who for the name of Christ shed his blood, who feared not the threats of judges, nor sought the glory of earthly dignity, but happily attained unto the heavenly kingdom.
hicestveremartyrquiprochristinominesangu.la: Hic est vere Martyr, * qui pro Christi nómine sánguinem suum fudit, qui minas júdicum non tímuit, nec terrénæ dignitátis glóriam quæsívit, sed ad cœléstia regna felíciter pervénit.

inillotemporedixitiesusdiscipulissuisame.en: In that time Jesus said to his disciples: Amen, amen I say to you, unless the grain of wheat falling into the ground die, Itself remaineth alone. And so on.
inillotemporedixitiesusdiscipulissuisame.la: In illo témpore: Dixit Jesus discípulis suis: Amen, amen dico vobis, nisi granum fruménti cadens in terram, mórtuum fúerit; ipsum solum manet. Et réliqua.

dulcispresensvitestetmulteplenavoluptati.en: This present life is sweet, and full of many pleasures, not indeed for all, but for those who love it. But if one should have cast his looks heavenward, and studied the excellent things that are there, he will forthwith despise this present life and hold it of no moment. So is bodily comeliness esteemed, only as long as we see none fairer, but as soon as a comelier appeareth, the first is held cheap.
dulcispresensvitestetmulteplenavoluptati.la: Dulcis præsens vita est, et multæ plena voluptátis, non tamen ómnibus, sed iis tantum qui illi sunt affíxi. Quod si quis in cœlum suspéxerit‚ et quæ ibi præclára sunt, contemplátus fúerit, statim hanc contémnet, ac nullíus prétii existimábit. Nam et córporum pulchritúdo quoad púlchrius non deprehénditur‚ in admiratióne habétur: cum vero áliud præstántius apparúerit, illa prior despícitur.

quodsiillampulchritudinemetiamnosintueri.en: And thus if we will look at the beauty above, and study the loveliness of the kingdom in heaven, we shall forthwith loose the ties that bind us to this world. The ties that bind us to this world are the love of earthly things. Listen to what Christ saith, to draw us to loosen these ties. He that loveth his life shall lose it, and he that hateth his life in this world shall keep it unto life eternal.
quodsiillampulchritudinemetiamnosintueri.la: Quod si illam pulchritúdinem étiam nos intuéri voluérimus, et cœléstis regni spéciem consideráre, conféstim nos hujus sæculi vínculis dissolvémus. Vinculum namque est terrenárum rerum afféctio: ad cujus dissolutiónem ut nos indúceret Christus, quid dicat, atténde. Qui amat ánimam suam, perdet eam: et qui odit ánimam suam in hoc mundo‚ in vitam ætérnam custódit eam.

enigmatisimilehocdictumvideturnontamenit.en: This saying seemeth like a riddle: yet it is not so, but rather is full of excellent wisdom. And how shall he that loveth his life lose it? He that obeyeth its senseless desires, he that indulgeth it beyond what is due; even as, on the contrary, he that hateth it in this world keepeth it: that is, he that obeyeth it not when it biddeth things hurtful.
enigmatisimilehocdictumvideturnontamenit.la: Ænígmati símile hoc dictum vidétur: non tamen ita est, imo vero præcípuæ sapiéntiæ plenum. Et quómodo qui amat ánimam suam, perdet eam? Qui absúrdis ejus cupiditátibus obtémperat, qui præter débitum ei indúlget; quemádmodum e contrário, qui odit eam in hoc mundo, custódit eam: hoc est, qui non paret ei, cum nóxia jubet.

etnondixitquinonparetsedquioditsicutieni.en: Christ saith not, He that obeyeth it not, but, He that hateth it. For even as we cannot bear to hear the voice or see the face of them whom we hate, so doth it behove us to turn angrily away from our own life, if it demand from us anything contrary to the will of God. He was about to speak to them touching death, even His Own death, and He foresaw their grief and faintness, and spake in strong expressions, as though He said: What shall I say, if ye take not My death bravely? Unless ye also die, ye shall gain no profit.
etnondixitquinonparetsedquioditsicutieni.la: Et non dixit, qui non paret sed, qui odit. Sícuti enim quos ódio habémus, ne vocem quidem audíre, nec vultum eórum vidére æquo ánimo pátimur: ita et ánimæ, si quid præter Dei voluntátem nobis ímperat, veheménter aversári opórtet. Cum enim jam de morte ad eos verba factúrus esset, de morte vidélicet sua, et prævidéret eórum tristítiam et exanimatiónem, per excéssum locútus est, ínquiens: Quid dico, si mortem meam generóse non ferétis? nisi vos ipsi moriámini, nullum vos sequétur emoluméntum.

sequentiasanctievangeliisecundumioannem.en: Continuation ✠ of the Holy Gospel according to John

inillotemporedixitiesusdiscipulissuisame.en: At that time, Jesus said to His disciples, Amen, amen, I say to you, unless the grain of wheat falls into the ground and dies, it remains alone. But if it dies, it brings forth much fruit. He who loves his life, loses it; and he who hates his life in this world, keeps it unto life everlasting. If anyone serves Me, let him follow Me; and where I am there also shall My servant be. If anyone serves me, My Father will honor him.
inillotemporedixitiesusdiscipulissuisame.la: In illo témpore: Dixit Jesus discípulis suis: Amen, amen dico vobis, nisi granum fruménti cadens in terram, mórtuum fúerit; ipsum solum manet. Si autem mórtuum fúerit, multum fructum affert. Qui amat ánimam suam, perdet eam: et qui odit ánimam suam in hoc mundo, in vitam ætérnam custódit eam. Si quis mihi minístrat, me sequátur: et ubi sum ego, illic et miníster meus erit. Si quis mihi ministráverit, honorificábit eum Pater meus.

iustiinperpetuumviventalleluia.en: The just shall live for evermore, alleluia.

etapuddominumestmerceseorumalleluia.en: And their reward is with the Lord, alleluia.
etapuddominumestmerceseorumalleluia.la: Et apud Dóminum est merces eórum, allelúia.

iustorumanimeinmanudeisunt.en: The souls of the just are in the hand of God,
iustorumanimeinmanudeisunt.la: Justórum ánimæ in manu Dei sunt,

etnontangetillostormentummortisalleluiaa.en: And the torment of death shall not touch them, alleluia, alleluia.
etnontangetillostormentummortisalleluiaa.la: Et non tanget illos torméntum mortis, allelúia, allelúia.

visisuntoculisinsipientiummoriilliautems.en: In the sight of the unwise they seemed to die, but they are in peace.
visisuntoculisinsipientiummoriilliautems.la: Visi sunt óculis insipiéntium mori, illi autem sunt in pace.

etcandidaseasfeceruntinsanguineagniallel.en: And they have made them white in the blood of the Lamb, Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.
etcandidaseasfeceruntinsanguineagniallel.la: Et cándidas eas fecérunt in sánguine Agni, Allelúia, allelúia, allelúia.

sanctituidominebenedicenttealleluiaallel.en: Thy Saints, O Lord, shall bless thee. Alleluia, alleluia.
sanctituidominebenedicenttealleluiaallel.la: Sancti tui, Dómine, benedícent te. Allelúja, allelúja.

gloriamregnituidicentetpotentiamtuamloqu.en: They shall speak of the glory of thy kingdom, and shall tell of thy power.
gloriamregnituidicentetpotentiamtuamloqu.la: Glóriam regni tui dicent, et poténtiam tuam loquéntur.

exultentiustiinconspectudeialleluiaallel.en: Let the just rejoice in the sight of God, * Alleluia, alleluia.
exultentiustiinconspectudeialleluiaallel.la: Exúltent justi in conspéctu Dei, * Allelúia, allelúia.

etdelectenturinletitia.en: And let them be delighted with gladness.

iustiinperpetuumvivent.en: The just shall live for evermore.

etapuddominumestmerceseorum.en: Their reward also is with the Lord.
etapuddominumestmerceseorum.la: Et apud Dóminum est merces eórum.

istisuntsanctiquiprotestamentodeisuacorp.en: These are the Saints * who for the covenant of God delivered up their bodies, and washed their robes in the blood of the Lamb.
istisuntsanctiquiprotestamentodeisuacorp.la: Isti sunt sancti * qui pro testaménto Dei sua córpora tradidérunt, et in sánguine Agni lavérunt stolas suas.

secusdecursusaquarumplantavitvineamiusto.en: By the running waters * he hath planted the vineyard of the just, and their will was in the law of the Lord.
secusdecursusaquarumplantavitvineamiusto.la: Secus decúrsus aquárum * plantávit víneam justórum, et in lege Dómini fuit volúntas eórum. Ps. 1

predicantespreceptumdominiconstitutisunt.en: Preaching * the commandment of the Lord, they were set upon his holy mountain.
predicantespreceptumdominiconstitutisunt.la: Prædicántes * præcéptum Dómini constitúti sunt in monte sancto ejus. Ps. 2

letenturomnesquisperantintedominequoniam.en: Let all them be glad, * that hope in thee, O Lord, for thou hast blessed the just: thou hast crowned them as with a shield of thy good will.
letenturomnesquisperantintedominequoniam.la: Læténtur omnes, * qui sperant in te, Dómine, quóniam tu benedixísti justis: scuto bonæ voluntátis tuæ coronásti eos. Ps. 5

sanctisquiinterrasunteiusmirificavitomne.en: To the Saints that are in the earth * Thou hast made all my counsels admirable.
sanctisquiinterrasunteiusmirificavitomne.la: Sanctis, qui in terra sunt ejus, * mirificávit omnes voluntátes meas inter illos. Ps. 15

iustorumautemanimeinmanudeisuntetnontang.en: But the souls of the just * are in the hand of God, and the torment of death shall not touch them.
iustorumautemanimeinmanudeisuntetnontang.la: Justórum autem ánimæ * in manu Dei sunt, et non tanget illos torméntum mortis. Ps. 33

fulgebuntiustisicutsolinregnopatriseorum.en: The just shall shine * as the sun in the kingdom of their Father, alleluia.
fulgebuntiustisicutsolinregnopatriseorum.la: Fulgébunt justi * sicut sol in regno Patris eórum, allelúia. Ps. 45

sanctituidominemirabileconsecutisuntiter.en: Thy Saints, O Lord, went a wonderful way, serving thy commandments,
sanctituidominemirabileconsecutisuntiter.la: Sancti tui, Dómine, mirábile consecúti sunt iter, serviéntes præcéptis tuis,

utinvenirenturillesiinaquisvalidisterraa.en: That they might be found unhurt in the mighty waters: the dry land appeared: and in the Red Sea a way without hindrance.
utinvenirenturillesiinaquisvalidisterraa.la: Ut inveniréntur illǽsi in aquis válidis: terra appáruit árida: et in Mari Rubro via sine impediménto.

victricemmanumtuamlaudaveruntpariteretde.en: They praised with one accord thy victorious hand, and sang, O Lord, thy holy name.
victricemmanumtuamlaudaveruntpariteretde.la: Victrícem manum tuam laudavérunt páriter, et decantavérunt, Dómine, nomen sanctum tuum.

memorieorumnonderelinqueturetnomeneorumi.en: Their memory shall not be forsaken, and their name abideth for ever:
memorieorumnonderelinqueturetnomeneorumi.la: Memória eórum non derelinquétur, et nomen eórum in ætérnum manet:

etnontangetillostormentummortis.en: The torment of death shall not touch them.
etnontangetillostormentummortis.la: Et non tanget illos torméntum mortis.

sanctituidominebenedicentte.en: Thy Saints, O Lord, * shall bless thee.

iustumdeduxitdominusperviasrectasetosten.en: The Lord guided the just in right paths, † and showed him the kingdom of God, and gave him the knowledge of the holy things;
iustumdeduxitdominusperviasrectasetosten.la: Justum dedúxit Dóminus per vias rectas, † et osténdit illi regnum Dei, et dedit illi sciéntiam sanctórum;

honestavitilluminlaboribussuis.en: He made him honourable in his labours.

magnificaviteuminconspecturegumetdeditil.en: He magnified him in the sight of kings, and gave him a crown of glory.
magnificaviteuminconspecturegumetdeditil.la: Magnificávit eum in conspéctu regum, et dedit illi corónam glóriæ.

benedictionemomniumgentiumdeditillidomin.en: The Lord gave him the blessing of all nations, * and confirmed his covenant upon his head.
benedictionemomniumgentiumdeditillidomin.la: Benedictiónem ómnium Géntium dedit illi Dóminus, * et testaméntum suum confirmávit super caput ejus.

hecsibiobsequentibusprecipithonorumculmi.en: This wisdom teacheth its followers to seek the heights of honours, to rejoice in the vanity of temporal glory when it is gained, to return manifold the evils done them by others; when strength sufficeth, to yield to none that resist; when the power of strength is wanting, whatever they cannot accomplish by malice, to feign in peaceable goodness.
hecsibiobsequentibusprecipithonorumculmi.la: Hæc sibi obsequéntibus præcipit honórum cúlmina quærere, adépta temporális glóriæ vanitáte gaudére, irrogáta ab áliis mala multiplícius réddere: cum vires súppetunt, nullis resisténtibus cédere: cum virtútis possibílitas deest, quidquid explére per malítiam non valent, hoc in pacífica bonitáte simuláre.

atcontrasapientiaiustorumestnilperostens.en: But on the contrary, the wisdom of the just is this: to feign nothing for show, to lay open the mind by words, to love true things as they are, to shun false things; to bestow good things freely, to bear evil rather than to do it; to seek no revenge for injury, to count insult for the truth's sake as gain. But this simplicity of the just is laughed to scorn; because by the wise of this world the virtue of purity is believed to be foolishness.
atcontrasapientiaiustorumestnilperostens.la: At contra, sapiéntia justórum est: nil per ostensiónem fíngere, sensum verbis aperíre, vera ut sunt dilígere, falsa devitáre; bona gratis exhibére, mala libéntius toleráre quam fácere; nullam injúriæ ultiónem quærere, pro veritáte contuméliam lucrum putáre. Sed hæc justórum simplícitas deridétur; quia ab hujus mundi sapiéntibus puritátis virtus fatúitas créditur.

omneenimquodinnocenteragiturabeisproculd.en: For everything that is done innocently is without doubt thought foolish by them; and whatsoever truth approveth in deed soundeth foolish to carnal wisdom. For what seemeth more foolish to the world than to show the mind by words, to feign nothing by crafty device, to return no insults for injuries, to pray for them that curse, to seek poverty, to forsake possessions, not to resist him that robbeth, to offer the other cheek to him that striketh?
omneenimquodinnocenteragiturabeisproculd.la: Omne enim quod innocénter ágitur, ab eis proculdúbio stultum putátur; et quidquid in ópere véritas ápprobat, carnáli sapiéntiæ fátuum sonat. Quid namque stúltius vidétur mundo, quam mentem verbis osténdere, nil cállida machinatióne simuláre, nullas injúriis contumélias réddere, pro maledicéntibus oráre, paupertátem quærere, posséssa relínquere, rapiénti non resístere, percutiénti álteram maxíllam præbére?

stolaiucunditatisinduiteumdominus.en: The Lord hath put on him a robe of honour,

etcoronampulchritudinisposuitsupercapute.en: And put about his head a crown of joy.
etcoronampulchritudinisposuitsupercapute.la: Et corónam pulchritúdinis pósuit super caput ejus.

cibavitillumdominuspaneviteetintellectus.en: With the bread of life and understanding hath the Lord fed him, and given him the water of health and wisdom to drink.
cibavitillumdominuspaneviteetintellectus.la: Cibávit illum Dóminus pane vitæ et intelléctus: et aqua sapiéntiæ salutáris potávit illum.

iustumdeduxitdominusperviasrectas.en: The Lord guided the just * In right paths.
iustumdeduxitdominusperviasrectas.la: Justum dedúxit Dóminus * Per vias rectas.

etostenditilliregnumdei.en: And showed him the kingdom of God.

hecestvirgosapiensquamdominusvigilantemi.en: This is one of the wise virgins, * whom the Lord found watching.
hecestvirgosapiensquamdominusvigilantemi.la: Hæc est Virgo sápiens, * quam Dóminus vigilántem invénit. Ps. 112

oquampulchrestcastageneratiocumclaritate.en: O how lovely and glorious * is the generation of the chaste.
oquampulchrestcastageneratiocumclaritate.la: O quam pulchra * est casta generátio cum claritáte! Ps. 8

dumessetrexinaccubitusuonardusmeadeditod.en: While the king * was at his repose, my spikenard sent forth the odour thereof.
dumessetrexinaccubitusuonardusmeadeditod.la: Dum esset Rex * in accúbitu suo, nardus mea dedit odórem suum. Ps. 95

venientesponsoprudensvirgopreparataintro.en: When the bridegroom came, * the wise Virgin, being ready, went in with him to the marriage.
venientesponsoprudensvirgopreparataintro.la: Veniénte sponso, * prudens Virgo præparáta introívit cum eo ad núptias. Ps. 97

prudentesvirginesaptatevestraslampadesec.en: O wise Virgins, * trim your lamps: behold, the bridegroom cometh, go ye forth to meet him.
prudentesvirginesaptatevestraslampadesec.la: Prudéntes Vírgines, * aptáte vestras lámpades: ecce sponsus venit, exíte óbviam ei. Ps. 249, 250, 251

quinqueprudentesvirginesacceperuntoleumi.en: The five wise virgins took oil in their vessels,
quinqueprudentesvirginesacceperuntoleumi.la: Quinque prudéntes vírgines accepérunt óleum in vasis suis,

mediaautemnocteclamorfactusesteccesponsu.en: And at midnight there was a cry made: Behold, the bridegroom cometh: go ye forth to meet him.
mediaautemnocteclamorfactusesteccesponsu.la: Média autem nocte clamor factus est: Ecce, sponsus venit: exíte óbviam ei.

quinqueprudentesvirginesacceperuntoleumi.en: The five wise Virgins * took oil in their vessels with the lamps: and at midnight there was a cry made: Behold the bridegroom cometh, go ye forth to meet Christ the Lord.
quinqueprudentesvirginesacceperuntoleumi.la: Quinque prudéntes Vírgines * accepérunt óleum in vasis suis cum lampádibus: média autem nocte clamor factus est: Ecce sponsus venit, exite óbviam Christo Dómino.

nuncnobisadvirginessermestquarumquosubli.en: Now our word is to the virgins, for whom our care is the greater as their glory is the more sublime. They are the flower of the Church's seed, the beauty and ornament of spiritual grace, a joyous nature, a work of praise and honour, whole and incorrupt, the image of God answering to the holiness of the Lord, the more illustrious portion of the flock of Christ.
nuncnobisadvirginessermestquarumquosubli.la: Nunc nobis ad vírgines sermo est, quarum quo sublímior glória est, major et cura est. Flos est ille ecclesiástici gérminis, decus atque ornaméntum grátiæ spiritális, læta índoles, laudis et honóris opus íntegrum atque incorrúptum, Dei imágo respóndens ad sanctimóniam Dómini, illústrior pórtio gregis Christi.

gaudetperillasatqueinillislargiterfloret.en: Through them and in them the glorious fruitfulness of Mother Church rejoiceth and abundantly flourisheth: and the more plenteous virginity addeth to its number, the more the joy of the mother increaseth. To these we speak, these we exhort, with affection rather than with authority: not that we, the last and least and well aware of our lowliness, claim any freedom to censure; but because, being the more watchful in our solicitude, we fear the more from the assaults of the devil.
gaudetperillasatqueinillislargiterfloret.la: Gaudet per illas atque in illis lárgiter floret Ecclésiæ matris gloriósa fœcúnditas: quantóque plus copiósa virgínitas número suo addit, tanto plus gáudium matris augéscit. Ad has lóquimur, has adhortámur affectióne pótius quam potestáte: non quod, extrémi et mínimi et humilitátis nostræ ádmodum cónscii, áliquid ad censúram licéntiæ vindicémus; sed quod ad sollicitúdinem magis cauti, plus de diáboli infestatióne timeámus.

diemfestumcelebrantessubhonorebeatenvirg.en: Celebrating a festal day in honour of blessed N., Virgin, at whose solemnity the Angels rejoice, and together praise the Son of God.
diemfestumcelebrantessubhonorebeatenvirg.la: Diem festum celebrántes, sub honóre beátæ N. Vírginis, de cujus solemnitáte gaudent Angeli, et colláudant Fílium Dei.

venisponsachristiaccipecoronamquamtibido.en: Come, Bride of Christ, * receive the crown which the Lord hath prepared for thee for ever.
venisponsachristiaccipecoronamquamtibido.la: Veni, Sponsa Christi, * áccipe corónam, quam tibi Dóminus præparávit in ætérnum. Ps. 47

consideravitagrumetemiteumdefructumanuum.en: She hath considered a field, and bought it: with the fruit of her hands she hath planted a vineyard.
consideravitagrumetemiteumdefructumanuum.la: Considerávit agrum, et emit eum: de fructu mánuum suárum plantávit víneam.

gustavitetviditquiabonestnegotiatieiusno.en: She hath tasted and seen that her traffic is good: her lamp shall not be put out in the night.
gustavitetviditquiabonestnegotiatieiusno.la: Gustávit, et vidit quia bona est negotiátio ejus: non extinguétur in nocte lucérna ejus.

manumsuammisitadfortietdigitieiusapprehe.en: She hath put out her hand to strong things, and her fingers have taken hold of the spindle.
manumsuammisitadfortietdigitieiusapprehe.la: Manum suam misit ad fórtia, et dígiti ejus apprehendérunt fusum.

nontimebitdomuisueafrigoribusnivisomnese.en: She shall not fear for her house in the cold of snow: for all her domestics are clothed with double garments.
nontimebitdomuisueafrigoribusnivisomnese.la: Non timébit dómui suæ a frigóribus nivis: omnes enim doméstici ejus vestíti sunt duplícibus.

stragulatamvestemfecitsibibyssusetpurpur.en: She hath made for herself clothing of tapestry: fine linen, and purple is her covering.
stragulatamvestemfecitsibibyssusetpurpur.la: Stragulátam vestem fecit sibi: byssus, et púrpura induméntum ejus.

nobilisinportisvireiusquandosederitcumse.en: Her husband is honourable in the gates, when he sitteth among the senators of the land.
nobilisinportisvireiusquandosederitcumse.la: Nóbilis in portis vir ejus, quando séderit cum senatóribus terræ.

sindonemfecitetvendiditetcingulumtradidi.en: She made fine linen, and sold it, and delivered a girdle to the Chanaanite.
sindonemfecitetvendiditetcingulumtradidi.la: Síndonem fecit, et véndidit, et cíngulum trádidit Chananæo.

fortitudetdecorindumentumeiusetridebitin.en: Strength and beauty are her clothing, and she shall laugh in the latter day.
fortitudetdecorindumentumeiusetridebitin.la: Fortitúdo et decor induméntum ejus, et ridébit in die novíssimo.

ossuumaperuitsapientieetlexclementieinli.en: She hath opened her mouth to wisdom, and the law of clemency is on her tongue.
ossuumaperuitsapientieetlexclementieinli.la: Os suum apéruit sapiéntiæ, et lex cleméntiæ in lingua ejus.

consideravitsemitasdomussueetpanemotiosa.en: She hath looked well to the paths of her house, and hath not eaten her bread idle.
consideravitsemitasdomussueetpanemotiosa.la: Considerávit semitas domus suæ, et panem otiósa non comédit.

surrexeruntfiliieiusetbeatissimampredica.en: Her children rose up, and called her blessed: her husband, and he praised her.
surrexeruntfiliieiusetbeatissimampredica.la: Surrexérunt fílii ejus, et beatíssimam prædicavérunt: vir ejus. et laudávit eam.

multefiliecongregaveruntdivitiastusuperg.en: Many daughters have gathered together riches: thou hast surpassed them all.
multefiliecongregaveruntdivitiastusuperg.la: Multæ fíliæ congregavérunt divítias: tu supergréssa es univérsas.

fallaxgratietvanestpulchritudomuliertime.en: Favour is deceitful, and beauty is vain: the woman that feareth the Lord, she shall be praised.
fallaxgratietvanestpulchritudomuliertime.la: Fallax grátia, et vana est pulchritúdo: múlier timens Dóminum ipsa laudábitur.

dateeidefructumanuumsuarumetlaudenteamin.en: Give her of the fruit of her hands, and let her own works praise her in the gates.
dateeidefructumanuumsuarumetlaudenteamin.la: Date ei de fructu mánuum suárum: et laudent eam in portis ópera ejus.

dumessetrexinaccubitusuo.en: While the King was at his repose,
dumessetrexinaccubitusuo.la: Dum esset Rex in accúbitu suo,

nardusmeadeditodoremsuum.en: My spikenard sent forth the odour thereof.

pulchrasumetdecorafiliaierusalem.en: I am fair and comely, O daughter of Jerusalem:
pulchrasumetdecorafiliaierusalem.la: Pulchra sum, et decóra, fília Jerúsalem:

paxeternaabeternopatrehuicdomuipaxperenn.en: Eternal peace * from the eternal Father be to this house; peace everlasting, the Word of the Father, be peace to this house; may the loving Comforter grant peace to this house.
paxeternaabeternopatrehuicdomuipaxperenn.la: Pax æterna * ab ætérno Patre, huic domui pax perénnis, Verbum Patris sit pax huic dómui, pacem pius consolátor huic præstet dómui.

exultemusdominoregisummoquisuumsanctific.en: Let us rejoice in the Lord, the King most high, * Who hath sanctified his tabernacle.
exultemusdominoregisummoquisuumsanctific.la: Exultémus Dómino, Regi summo, * Qui suum sanctificávit tabernáculum.

tolliteportasprincipesvestrasetelevamini.en: Lift up your gates, O ye princes, * and be ye lift up, ye everlasting doors.
tolliteportasprincipesvestrasetelevamini.la: Tóllite portas, * príncipes vestras, et elevámini, portæ æternáles. Ps. 23

introiboadaltaredeiaddeumquiletificatiuv.en: I will go in * to the Altar of God, to God who giveth joy to my youth.
introiboadaltaredeiaddeumquiletificatiuv.la: Introíbo * ad Altáre Dei, ad Deum, qui lætíficat juventútem meam. Ps. 42

sanctificavitdominustabernaculumsuum.en: The Lord hath sanctified * his tabernacle.

eritmihidominusindeumetlapisistevocabitu.en: The Lord shall be my God, * and this stone shall be called God's house.
eritmihidominusindeumetlapisistevocabitu.la: Erit mihi Dóminus * in Deum, et lapis iste vocábitur domus Dei. Ps. 46

edificavitmoysesaltaredominodeo.en: Moses built an altar * to the Lord God.
edificavitmoysesaltaredominodeo.la: Ædificávit * Móyses altáre Dómino Deo. Ps. 47

nonesthicaliudnisidomusdeietportaceli.en: This is none other * but the house of God, and the gate of heaven.
nonesthicaliudnisidomusdeietportaceli.la: Non est hic áliud, * nisi domus Dei, et porta cæli. Ps. 64

viditiacobscalamsummitaseiuscelostangeba.en: Jacob saw a ladder, * the top thereof touched the heavens, and Angels descending, and he said: Truly this place is holy.
viditiacobscalamsummitaseiuscelostangeba.la: Vidit Jacob scalam, * súmmitas ejus cælos tangébat, et descendéntes Angelos, et dixit: Vere locus iste sanctus est. Ps. 83

erexitiacoblapidemintitulumfundensoleumd.en: Jacob set up * the stone for a title, pouring oil upon the top of it.
erexitiacoblapidemintitulumfundensoleumd.la: Eréxit Jacob * lápidem in títulum, fundens óleum désuper. Ps. 86

templumdominisanctumestdeistructurestdei.en: The temple of the Lord * is holy, it is God's workmanship, it is God's building.
templumdominisanctumestdeistructurestdei.la: Templum Dómini * sanctum est, Dei structúra est, Dei ædificátio est. Ps. 87

quihabitatinadiutorioaltissimiinprotecti.en: He that dwelleth * in the aid of the most High, shall abide under the protection of the God of heaven.
quihabitatinadiutorioaltissimiinprotecti.la: Qui hábitat * in adjutório Altíssimi, in protectióne Dei cæli commorábitur. Ps. 90

benedictagloriadominidelocosanctosuo.en: Blessed be * the glory of the Lord from his holy place.
benedictagloriadominidelocosanctosuo.la: Benedícta * glória Dómini, de loco sancto suo. Ps. 95

cumevigilassetiacobasomnoaitveredominuse.en: When Jacob awaked * out of sleep, he said: Indeed the Lord is in this place.
cumevigilassetiacobasomnoaitveredominuse.la: Cum evigilásset * Jacob a somno, ait: Vere Dóminus est in loco isto. Ps. 98

fundamentatemplihuiussapientiasuafundavi.en: The foundations * of this temple God hath laid in his wisdom, wherein the Angels praise the Lord of heaven; though the winds rush upon it and the floods flow, they can never move it: for it is founded upon a rock.
fundamentatemplihuiussapientiasuafundavi.la: Fundaménta * templi hujus sapiéntia sua fundávit Deus, in quo Dóminum cæli colláudant Angeli; si írruant venti et fluant flúmina, non possunt illud movére umquam: fundátum enim est supra petram. Ps. 260, 261, 262

fundatestdomusdomini.en: The house of the Lord is founded.

supraverticemmontium.en: Upon the top of the mountains.

beatiquihabitantindomotuadomine.en: Blessed are they that dwell in thy house, O Lord.
beatiquihabitantindomotuadomine.la: Beáti, qui hábitant in domo tua, Dómine.

inseculaseculorumlaudabuntte.en: They shall praise thee for ever and ever.

quireminisciminidomininetaceatisetnedeti.en: You that are mindful of the Lord, hold not your peace, and give him no silence.
quireminisciminidomininetaceatisetnedeti.la: Qui reminiscímini Dómini, ne taceátis, et ne detis siléntium ei.

veredominusestinlocoistetegonesciebam.en: Surely the Lord is in this place, and I knew it not.
veredominusestinlocoistetegonesciebam.la: Vere Dóminus est in loco isto, et ego nesciébam.

domusmeadomusorationisvocabiturdicitdomi.en: My house shall be called a house of prayer, saith the Lord:
domusmeadomusorationisvocabiturdicitdomi.la: Domus mea, domus oratiónis vocábitur, dicit Dóminus:

ineaomnisquipetitaccipitetquiqueritinven.en: In it every one that asketh, receiveth; and he that seeketh, findeth: and to him that knocketh it shall be opened.
ineaomnisquipetitaccipitetquiqueritinven.la: In ea omnis qui petit, áccipit; et qui quærit, ínvenit: et pulsánti aperiétur.

beataverematerecclesiaquamsichonordivine.en: Truly blessed is Mother Church, whom the honour of the divine favour so enlighteneth, † whom the glorious blood of victorious Martyrs adorneth,
beataverematerecclesiaquamsichonordivine.la: Beáta vere mater Ecclésia quam sic honor divínæ dignatiónis illúminat, † quam victoriosórum gloriósus Mártyrum sanguis exórnat

quaminviolataconfessioniscandidainduitvi.en: Whom the inviolate virginity of confession clotheth in white.
quaminviolataconfessioniscandidainduitvi.la: Quam invioláta confessiónis cándida índuit virgínitas.

egomaterpulchredilectionisettimorisetagn.en: I am the mother of fair love, and of fear, and of knowledge, and of holy hope.
egomaterpulchredilectionisettimorisetagn.la: Ego mater pulchræ dilectiónis, et timóris, et agnitiónis, et sanctæ spei.

exsermdevirginedeiparaaliasdeaqueductu.en: From the 2nd Sermon on the Virgin Mother of God, otherwise, on the Aqueduct.
exsermdevirginedeiparaaliasdeaqueductu.la: Ex Serm. 2. de Virgine Deipara‚ alias, de Aquæductu.

altiusintueminifratresmeiquantodevotioni.en: Consider more deeply, my brethren, with what affection of devotion he would have Mary honoured by us, who hath placed in Mary the fulness of all good: so that hence, if there be any hope in us, any grace, any salvation, we may know that it overfloweth from her who ascended abounding with delights. A garden of delights indeed, which that divine south wind hath not only breathed upon in coming, but hath blown through in coming upon it, that her spices, that is, the gifts of graces, may flow and overflow on every side.
altiusintueminifratresmeiquantodevotioni.la: Altius intuémini, fratres mei, quanto devotiónis afféctu a nobis Mariam volúerit honorári, qui totius boni plenitúdinem pósuit in María: ut proinde si quid spei in nobis est, si quid grátiæ, si quid salútis, ab ea novérimus redundáre, quæ ascéndit delíciis áffluens. Hortus plane deliciárum, quem non modo affláverit véniens‚ sed et perfláverit supervéniens auster ille divínus, ut úndique fluant et áffluant arómata ejus‚ charísmata scílicet gratiárum.

tollecorpushocsolarequodilluminatmundumu.en: Take away this bodily sun which enlighteneth the world, and where is the day? Take away Mary, this star of the sea, of the sea indeed great and wide, and what is left but enveloping gloom, and the shadow of death, and thickest darkness? With all the marrow of our hearts, therefore, with all the affections of our inmost souls, and with all our desires, let us venerate this Mary: for such is the will of him who would have us receive all through Mary.
tollecorpushocsolarequodilluminatmundumu.la: Tolle corpus hoc soláre, quod illúminat mundum, ubi dies? Tolle Mariam hanc maris stellam, maris útique magni et spatiósi, quid nisi calígo invólvens, et umbra mortis, ac densíssimæ ténebræ relinquúntur? Totis ergo medúllis córdium, totis præcordiórum afféctibus‚ et votis ómnibus Mariam hanc venerémur: quia sic est volúntas ejus, qui totum nos habére vóluit per Maríam.

queestistaqueprogrediturquasiauroraconsu.en: Who is she that cometh forth as the morning rising, § fair as the moon, bright as the sun, * terrible as an army set in array?
queestistaqueprogrediturquasiauroraconsu.la: Quæ est ista, quæ progréditur quasi auróra consúrgens, § pulchra ut luna, elécta ut sol, * terríbilis ut castrórum ácies ordináta?

quomodofietistudquoniamvirumnoncognoscet.en: How shall this be done, because I know not man? And the Angel Gabriel answering, said to her:
quomodofietistudquoniamvirumnoncognoscet.la: Quómodo fiet istud, quóniam virum non cognósco? Et respóndens Gábriel Angelus, dixit ei:

eccetupulchresamicameeccetupulchresoculi.en: Behold thou art fair, * O my love, behold thou art fair, thy eyes are doves' eyes.
eccetupulchresamicameeccetupulchresoculi.la: Ecce tu pulchra es, * amíca mea, ecce tu pulchra es; óculi tui columbárum. Ps. 8

sicutliliuminterspinassicamicameainterfi.en: As the lily * among thorns, so is my love among the daughters.
sicutliliuminterspinassicamicameainterfi.la: Sicut lílium * inter spinas, sic amíca mea inter fílias. Ps. 18

favusdistillanslabiatuasponsetodorvestim.en: Thy lips are as a dropping honeycomb, * O my spouse, and the smell of thy garments as the smell of frankincense.
favusdistillanslabiatuasponsetodorvestim.la: Favus distíllans * lábia tua, Sponsa, et odor vestimentórum tuórum sicut odor thuris. Ps. 23

emissionestueparadisusmalorumpunicorumcu.en: Thy plants * are a paradise of pomegranates with the fruits of the orchard.
emissionestueparadisusmalorumpunicorumcu.la: Emissiónes tuæ * paradísus malórum punicórum, cum pomórum frúctibus. Ps. 44

comedifavumcummellemeobibivinummeumcumla.en: I have eaten the honeycomb * with my honey, I have drunk my wine with my milk.
comedifavumcummellemeobibivinummeumcumla.la: Comédi favum * cum melle meo, bibi vinum meum cum lacte meo. Ps. 86

animamealiquefactestutdilectuslocutusest.en: My soul * melted when my beloved spoke: I sought him, and found him not; I called, and he did not answer me: the keepers that go about the city found me, they struck me, and wounded me, the keepers of the walls took away my veil: O daughters of Jerusalem, tell my beloved that I languish with love.
animamealiquefactestutdilectuslocutusest.la: Anima mea * liquefácta est, ut diléctus locútus est: quæsívi, et non invéni illum; vocávi, et non respóndit mihi: invenérunt me custódes civitátis, percussérunt me, et vulneravérunt me, tulérunt pállium meum custódes murórum: fíliæ Jerúsalem, nuntiáte dilécto, quia amóre lángueo. Ps. 95

talisestdilectusmeusetipseestamicusmeusf.en: Such is * my beloved, and he is my friend, O ye daughters of Jerusalem.
talisestdilectusmeusetipseestamicusmeusf.la: Talis est * diléctus meus, et ipse est amícus meus, fíliæ Jerúsalem. Ps. 96

descendiinhortumnucumutviderempomaconval.en: I went down * into the garden of nuts, to see the fruits of the valleys, and to look if the vineyard had flourished, and the pomegranates budded: return, return, O Sulamitess, return, return, that we may behold thee.
descendiinhortumnucumutviderempomaconval.la: Descéndi * in hortum nucum, ut vidérem poma convállium, et inspícerem, si floruísset vínea, et germinássent mala púnica: revértere, tevértere, Sulamítis, revértere, revértere, ut intueámur te. Ps. 97

iacobautemgenuitiosephvirummariedequanat.en: And Jacob begat Joseph * the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, Who is called Christ.
iacobautemgenuitiosephvirummariedequanat.la: Jacob autem * génuit Joseph virum Maríæ; de qua natus est Jesus, qui vocátur Christus. Ps. 109

angelusdominiapparuitinsomnisiosephdicen.en: The angel of the Lord * appeared to Joseph in his sleep, saying: Joseph, son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife, for that which is conceived in her, is of the Holy Ghost.
angelusdominiapparuitinsomnisiosephdicen.la: Angelus Dómini * appáruit in somnis Joseph, dicens: Joseph, fili David, noli timére accípere Maríam cónjugem tuam; quod enim in ea natum est, de Spíritu Sancto est. Ps. 112

pastoresveneruntfestinantesetinveneruntm.en: The shepherds came * with haste; and they found Mary and Joseph, and the infant lying in the manger.
pastoresveneruntfestinantesetinveneruntm.la: Pastóres venérunt * festinántes, et invenérunt Maríam, et Joseph, et Infántem pósitum in præsépio. Ps. 121

mirabanturomnesinverbisgratiequeprocedeb.en: All wondered * at the words of grace that proceeded from his mouth, and they said: Is not this the son of Joseph?
mirabanturomnesinverbisgratiequeprocedeb.la: Mirabántur omnes * in verbis grátiæ, quæ procedébant de ore ipsíus, et decébant: Nonne hic est fílius Joseph? Ps. 126

magiintrantesdomuminveneruntpuerumcummar.en: The Magi, entering into the house, * found the child with Mary his mother.
magiintrantesdomuminveneruntpuerumcummar.la: Magi, intrántes domum, * invenérunt Púerum cum María, matre ejus.

suscipiensiesuminulnassuassimeonexclamav.en: Simeon, taking Jesus * into his arms, cried out and said: Thou art truly a light to the enlightening of the Gentiles.
suscipiensiesuminulnassuassimeonexclamav.la: Suscípiens Jesum * in ulnas suas Símeon, exclamávit, et dixit: Tu es vere lumen ad illuminatiónem géntium. Ps. 23

eratpateriesuetmatermirantessuperhisqued.en: The father and mother of Jesus * marvelled at those things which were spoken of Him; and Simeon blessed them.
eratpateriesuetmatermirantessuperhisqued.la: Erat Pater Jesu, * et Mater mirántes super his, quæ dicebántur de illo: et benedíxit illis Símeon. Ps. 44

propternosegenusfactusestcumessetdives.en: For our sakes he became poor, being rich.
propternosegenusfactusestcumessetdives.la: Propter nos egénus factus est cum esset dives.

utilliusinopianosdivitesessemus.en: That through his poverty we might be rich.
utilliusinopianosdivitesessemus.la: Ut illíus inópia nos dívites essémus.

hostiametoblationemnoluisti.en: Sacrifice and oblation thou wouldst not,

corpusautemaptastimihi.en: But a body thou hast fitted to me.

incapitelibriscriptumestdemeutfaciamdeus.en: In the head of the book it is written of me, that I should do thy will, O God.
incapitelibriscriptumestdemeutfaciamdeus.la: In cápite libri scriptum est de me, ut fáciam, Deus, voluntátem tuam.

desermonesanctiambrosiiepiscopi.en: From the Sermon of St. Ambrose, Bishop.

subditusestodominetobsecreumchristusfaci.en: Be thou subject to the Lord, and pray to him. Christ, by doing the will of the Father, fulfilled the law. And therefore he is the end of the law and the fulness of charity; for, loving the Father, he gave all his affection to his will. Moreover, it was out of dutiful love, not out of weakness, that he was subject to his parents Joseph and Mary. He took upon him, therefore, our compassion, he took upon him also subjection. For that he subjected all things to himself is his own: that he was subject is ours. It was the soul, he saith, that was subject, not the Godhead; the soul made subject, not the power of God. Through it therefore was obedience, through it humility: which yet were taken up not unto weakness of power, but for the teaching of discipline.
subditusestodominetobsecreumchristusfaci.la: Súbditus esto Dómino, et óbsecra eum. Christus faciéndo voluntátem Patris, legem implévit. Et ídeo finis est legis et plenitúdo est charitátis; quia díligens Patrem, afféctum omnem ejus adhíbuit voluntáti. Dénique pro pietáte erat non pro infirmitáte Joseph et Maríæ paréntibus súbditus. Suscépit ítaque compassiónem nostram suscépit et subjectiónem. Quod enim subjécit sibi ómnia, suum est: quod subjéctus est, nostrum est. Anima, inquit, súbdita, non divínitas, ánima subjécta, non Dei virtus. Per ipsam ergo obediéntia, per ipsam humílitas: quæ tamen non ad infirmitátem poténtiæ suscépta sunt, sed ad magistérium disciplínae.

quasihomergexhisquepassusestdidicitobedi.en: As man, therefore, he learned obedience by the things which he suffered, that he might be made perfect in the flesh, and, by the succession of obedience poured into us, might become the cause of eternal salvation unto us, to whom before, by the inheritance of disobedience, that first Adam was made the cause of death. Subjection, therefore, is the teaching of human virtue, not the lessening of divine power.
quasihomergexhisquepassusestdidicitobedi.la: Quasi homo ergo ex his, quæ passus est, dídicit obediéntiam, ut consummarétur in carne et per obediéntiæ transfúsam in nos successiónem causa fíeret nobis salútis ætérnæ, quibus ante per inobediéntiæ hæreditátem primus ille Adam causa factus est mortis. Subjéctio ergo magistérium virtútis humánæ, non divínæ imminútio potestátis est.

namsiillumminoremfiliumetinequalempatrid.en: For if they call the Son less than and unequal to the Father, because he was subject to God the Father; is he therefore also less than his mother, because he was subject to his mother? For we read of Joseph and Mary: and he was subject to them. But dutiful love is to all of us not a loss but an increase; by which the Lord Jesus hath poured into all of us faith and grace, that he may make us subject with a faithful spirit to God the Father.
namsiillumminoremfiliumetinequalempatrid.la: Nam si illum minórem Fílium et inæquálem Patri dicunt, quia erat súbditus Patri Deo; numquid et matre ídeo minor, quia súbditus erat matri? Lectum est enim de Joseph et María: et erat súbditus illis. Sed píetas ómnibus nobis non dispéndio, sed increménto est; per quam ómnibus nobis Dóminus Jesus fidem infúdit et grátiam, ut nos spíritu fidéli súbditos Patri fáciat Deo.

ibidinpsnnet.en: The same, on Ps. 118, nn. 32 and 34.

deniquesiconsideremusinparadisodefecithu.en: Moreover, if we consider, in paradise humility failed, and therefore it came from heaven. In paradise disobedience arose, and therefore obedience came down with the Saviour. The flesh was puffed up, whence the subjection of meekness could not be found on earth. The Lord Jesus, coming, first emptied himself, not thinking it robbery to be equal with God, taking the form of a servant, and in habit found as a man, he humbled himself, becoming obedient unto death. Let him say therefore: I am young and despised: for Christ redeemed the world in one poor and despised, for Christ by humility overcame the devil.
deniquesiconsideremusinparadisodefecithu.la: Dénique, si considerémus, in paradíso defécit humílitas, et ídeo venit de cœlo. In paradíso orta est inobediéntia, et ídeo obediéntia cum Salvatóre descéndit. Inflabátur caro, unde subjéctio mansuetúdinis inveníri non póterat in terris. Véniens Dóminus Jesus primum se exinanívit, non rapínam arbitrátus esse se æquálem Deo, formam servi sibi accípiens, et spécie invéntus ut homo, humiliávit semetípsum factus obédiens usque ad mortem. Dicat ergo: júvenis sum et despéctus: quia Christus in páupere atque despécto mundum redémit, quia Christus humilitáte diábolum vicit.

paupersumegetinlaboribus.en: I am poor, and in labours,
paupersumegetinlaboribus.la: Pauper sum ego, et in labóribus,

exaltatusautemhumiliatussumetconturbatus.en: And being exalted, I have been humbled and troubled.
exaltatusautemhumiliatussumetconturbatus.la: Exaltátus autem, humiliátus sum et conturbátus.

propternosegenusfactusest.en: For our sakes he became poor;

etambulabimusinsemitiseius.en: And we will walk in his paths.

filiquidfecistinobissiceccepatertuuseteg.en: Son, * why hast thou done so to us? Behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing. How is it that you sought me? Did you not know that I must be about the things that are my Father's?
filiquidfecistinobissiceccepatertuuseteg.la: Fili, * quid fecísti nobis sic? Ecce pater tuus et ego doléntes quærebámus te. Quid est quod me quærebátis? nesciebátis quia in his, quæ Patris mei sunt, opórtet me esse?

descenditiesuscumeisetvenitnazarethetera.en: Jesus went down with them, * and came to Nazareth, and was subject unto them.
descenditiesuscumeisetvenitnazarethetera.la: Descéndit Jesus * cum eis, et venit Názareth, et erat súbditus illis.

etiesusproficiebatsapientietetateetgrati.en: And Jesus advanced * in wisdom, and age, and grace with God and men.
etiesusproficiebatsapientietetateetgrati.la: Et Jesus proficiébat * sapiéntia, et ætate, et grátia apud Deum et hómines.

mirabanturomnesinverbisgratiequeprocedeb.en: All wondered * at the words of grace that proceeded from his mouth, and they said: Is not this the son of Joseph?
mirabanturomnesinverbisgratiequeprocedeb.la: Mirábantur omnes * in verbis grátiæ, quæ procedébat de ore ipsíus, et dicébant: Nonne hic est fílius Joseph?

etdicebantundehuicsapientiahecetvirtutes.en: And they said: * How came this man by this wisdom and miracles? Is not this the carpenter's son?
etdicebantundehuicsapientiahecetvirtutes.la: Et dicébant: * Unde huic sapiéntia hæc, et virtútes? Nonne hic est fabri fílius?

passiodominiipsameiusmatremcarnaliorbita.en: The Passion of the Lord * most grievously saddened his very Mother, sorely stricken by the bereavement of her flesh.
passiodominiipsameiusmatremcarnaliorbita.la: Pássio Dómini * ipsam ejus Matrem, carnáli orbitáte gráviter percússam, vehementíssime contristávit. Ps. 69

ferrumlanceemilitarislatusquidemsalvator.en: The iron of the soldier's lance * pierced indeed the side of the Saviour, but the soul of the Virgin.
ferrumlanceemilitarislatusquidemsalvator.la: Ferrum lánceæ militáris * latus quidem Salvatóris, ánimam vero transívit Vírginis. Ps. 81

doleosupertefilimidecorusnimisetamabilis.en: I grieve for thee, * my son, exceeding beautiful and lovely above the love of women.
doleosupertefilimidecorusnimisetamabilis.la: Dóleo super te * fili mi, decórus nimis et amábilis super amórem mulíerum. Ps. 246, 247, 248

intenderuntarcumsuumremamaram.en: They have bent their bow, a bitter thing:

utsagittentinoccultisimmaculatum.en: To shoot in secret the undefiled.

namcurhocfeceritquodsequiturindicataiten.en: For why he did this, what followeth showeth. For the Evangelist saith: From that hour the disciple took her to his own; speaking of himself: for so he is wont to make mention of himself, as the one whom Jesus loved, who indeed loved all, but him above the rest and more familiarly, so that at supper he made him lean upon his breast; I believe, that in this way he might commend the divine excellence of this Gospel which he was to preach through him.
namcurhocfeceritquodsequiturindicataiten.la: Nam cur hoc fécerit, quod séquitur, índicat. Ait enim Evangelísta: Ex illa hora accépit eam discípulus in sua; de seípso dicens: sic quippe commemoráre solet, quod eum diligébat Jesus, qui útique omnes, sed ipsum prae céteris et familiárius diligébat, ita ut in convívio eum supra suum pectus discúmbere fáceret; credo, ut istíus Evangélii, quod per eum fúerat praedicatúrus, divínam excelléntiam hoc modo commendáret.

sedinquesuaioannesmatremdominiaccepitneq.en: But unto what own of his did John take the Mother of the Lord? For was he not of those who said to him: Behold, we have left all things and have followed thee? But there also he had heard: Whosoever shall leave these things for my sake shall receive in this world a hundredfold. The disciple therefore had a hundredfold more than he had left, wherein to receive the Mother of him who had given him these things? But in that fellowship blessed John had received the hundredfold, where no one said that aught was his own, but they had all things common: as it is written in the Acts of the Apostles. For so the Apostles were as having nothing, and possessing all things.
sedinquesuaioannesmatremdominiaccepitneq.la: Sed in quæ sua Joánnes Matrem Dómini accépit? Neque enim non ex eis erat, qui dixérunt ei: Ecce nos dimísimus ómnia et secúti sumus te. Sed ibi quoque audíerat: Quicúmque ista dimíserit propter me, accípiet in hoc sæculo cénties tantum. Habébat ergo discípulus centuplíciter plura quam dimíserat, in quæ suscíperet ejus Matrem, qui hæc illi donáverat? Sed in ea societáte beátus Joánnes recéperat céntuplum, ubi nemo dicébat áliquid suum, sed erant illis ómnia commúnia: sicut in Apostolórum Actibus scriptum est. Sic enim Apóstoli erant quasi nihil habéntes, et ómnia possidéntes.

nesciensmatervirgovirumpeperitsinedolore.en: The Virgin Mother, knowing not man, brought forth without pain the Saviour of the ages; the Virgin alone fed the very King of Angels at her breast filled from heaven.
nesciensmatervirgovirumpeperitsinedolore.la: Nésciens Mater Virgo virum, péperit sine dolóre Salvatórem sæculórum, ipsum Regem Angelórum sola Virgo lactábat úbere de cœlo pleno.

hominnativdomini.en: Homily 1, 7, on the Nativity of the Lord

pastoresquidemillifelicigaudiofestinarun.en: Those shepherds indeed hastened with happy joy to see what they had heard: and because they sought with burning love, they straightway merited to find the Saviour whom they sought. But they showed also, alike by their words and their deeds, with what earnestness of mind the shepherds of spiritual flocks, nay all the faithful, ought to seek Christ. Let us go over, they say, to Bethlehem, and let us see this word that is come to pass. Let us therefore also go over, dearly beloved brethren, in thought unto Bethlehem the city of David, and call to mind with love that in it the Word was made flesh, and celebrate his incarnation with worthy honours. Let us go over, casting away carnal desires, with all the longing of our mind, unto the Bethlehem above, that is, the house of the living bread, not made with hands, but eternal in the heavens, and call to mind with love that the Word was made flesh. Thither let us follow him with all earnestness of virtues, and with careful chastening of heart and body let us strive, that him whom they saw crying in the manger, we may merit to see reigning on the Father's throne.
pastoresquidemillifelicigaudiofestinarun.la: Pastóres quidem illi felíci gáudio festinárunt vidére quod audíerant: et quia ardénti amóre quæsiérunt, contínuo Salvatórem quem quæsiérunt, inveníre meruérunt. Sed et intellectuálium pastóres gregum, immo cuncti fidéles qua mentis indústria Christum quǽrere débeant, dictis páriter suis ostendérunt, et factis. Transeámus, ínquiunt, usque Béthlehem, et videámus hoc verbum quod factum est. Transeámus ergo et nos, fratres caríssimi, cogitándo usque Béthlehem civitátem David, et recolámus amándo quod in ea verbum caro factum est, atque ejus incarnatiónem dignis celebrémus honóribus. Transeámus, abjéctis concupiscéntiis carnálibus, toto mentis desidério usque Béthlehem supérnam, id est, domum panis vivi non manufáctam, sed ætérnam in cælis, et recolámus amándo, quia verbum caro factum est. Illo eum tota virtútum instántia sequámur, et sollícita cordis et córporis castigatióne procurémus, ut quem illi in præsépio vidére vagiéntem, nos in patris sólio mereámur vidére regnántem.

etveneruntfestinantesetinveneruntmariame.en: And they came with haste: and they found Mary and Joseph, and the infant lying in the manger. The shepherds came with haste, and found God born as man, together with the ministers of that same birth. Let us also, my brethren, make haste, not with the steps of our feet but with the progress of good works, to see that same glorified humanity, with its ministers rewarded with the worthy wage of their service: let us make haste to see him shining in the divine majesty of the Father and his own. Let us make haste, I say; for so great a blessedness is not to be sought with sloth and torpor, but the footsteps of Christ are to be followed eagerly. For he himself desireth to help our course by giving us his hand, and delighteth to hear from us: Draw us after thee; we will run to the odour of thy ointments. Let us therefore follow more quickly with the steps of virtues, that we may merit to attain. Let no man delay to be converted to the Lord, let no man defer it from day to day, praying to him through all things and before all things, that he direct our steps according to his word, and that no injustice have dominion over us.
etveneruntfestinantesetinveneruntmariame.la: Et venérunt festinántes, et invenérunt Maríam et Joseph, et Infántem pósitum in præsépio. Venérunt pastóres festinántes, et invenérunt Deum hóminem natum, simul et ejúsdem nativitátis minístros. Festinémus et nos, fratres mei, non pássibus pedum, sed bonórum proféctibus óperum vidére eándem glorificátam humanitátem cum ejúsdem minístris digna servitútis suæ mercéde remunerátis: festinémus vidére illum in divína Patris ac sua majestáte fulgéntem. Festinémus, inquam; nam non est tanta beatitúdo cum desídia ac torpóre quærénda, sed alácriter sunt Christi sequénda vestígia. Nam ipse cursum nostrum data manu juváre desíderat, delectatúrque audíre a nobis: Trahe nos post te, currémus in odórem unguentórum tuórum. Cítius ergo virtútum gréssibus sequámur, ut mereámur cónsequi. Nemo tardet convérti ad Dóminum, nemo dífferat de die in diem, ipsum per ómnia et ante ómnia precántes, ut gressus nostros dírigat secúndum elóquium suum, et non dominétur nostri omnis injustítia.

videntesautemcognoveruntdeverboquoddictu.en: And seeing, they understood of the word that had been spoken to them concerning this child. Let us also, dearly beloved brethren, make haste meanwhile to receive with pious faith, and to embrace with full love, the things that have been told us of our Saviour, true God and man, that in the life to come we may be able to comprehend them in the perfect vision of knowledge. For this alone is the true life, not only of blessed men but also of the Angels: to behold for ever the face of their Creator; which the Psalmist ardently desired, when he said: My soul hath thirsted after the living God; when shall I come and appear before the face of God? And he signified that his desire could be satisfied by the vision of him alone, and not by any abundance of earthly things, when he saith: I shall be satisfied when thy glory shall appear. But because not the idle and slothful, but they that toil in the works of the virtues, are worthy of the divine contemplation, he carefully said beforehand: But I will appear before thy sight in justice.
videntesautemcognoveruntdeverboquoddictu.la: Vidéntes autem cognovérunt de verbo, quod dictum erat illis de Púero hoc. Et nos, fratres dilectíssimi, quæ dicta sunt nobis de Salvatóre nostro Deo vero et hómine, ínterim pia fide percípere, et plena dilectióne festinémus amplécti, ut hæc in futúro perfécta cognitiónis visu comprehéndere valeámus. Hæc étenim sola ac vera est beatórum non solum hóminum, sed et Angelórum vita, fáciem perpétuo sui cérnere Creatóris, quam desiderábat ardénter Psalmísta, qui dicébat: Sitívit ánima mea ad Deum vivum, quando véniam et apparébo ante fáciem Dei? Cujus solíus visióne non autem ulla terrenárum rerum affluéntia desidérium suum satiári posse signávit, cum ait: Satiábor dum manifestábitur glória tua. Verum quia non otiósi ac désides, sed qui virtútum opéribus insúdant, divína contemplatióne sunt digni, sollícite præmísit: Ego autem cum justítia apparébo in conspéctu tuo.

verbumcarofactumestethabitavitinnobisetv.en: The Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us: and we saw his glory, the glory as it were of the only begotten of the Father, full of grace and truth, alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.
verbumcarofactumestethabitavitinnobisetv.la: Verbum caro factum est, et habitávit in nobis: et vídimus glóriam ejus, glóriam quasi Unigéniti a Patre plenum grátiæ, et veritátis, allelúia, allelúia, allelúia.

desponsatiesthodiesanctemarievirginiscui.en: This day is the Espousal * of holy Mary the Virgin, whose renowned life enlighteneth all the Churches.
desponsatiesthodiesanctemarievirginiscui.la: Desponsátio est hódie * sanctæ Maríæ Vírginis, cujus vita ínclita cunctas illústrat Ecclésias. Ps. 109
