cumiucunditatedesponsationembeatemariece.en: With joyfulness * let us celebrate the Espousal of blessed Mary, that she may intercede for us with the Lord Jesus Christ.
cumiucunditatedesponsationembeatemariece.la: Cum jucunditáte * Desponsatiónem beátæ Maríæ celebrémus, ut ipsa pro nobis intercédat ad Dóminum Jesum Christum. Ps. 112

desponsatiogloriosevirginismarieexsemine.en: The Espousal of the glorious * Virgin Mary, of the seed of Abraham, sprung from the tribe of Juda, of the illustrious stock of David.
desponsatiogloriosevirginismarieexsemine.la: Desponsátio gloriósæ * Vírginis Maríæ ex sémine Abrahæ, ortæ de tribu Juda, clara ex stirpe David.

desponsatiotuadeigenitrixvirgo.en: Thy Espousal, * O Virgin Mother of God.

omnipotensetmitissimedeusquibeatumioseph.en: O almighty and most gentle God, who didst provide blessed Joseph, the just son of David, as Spouse for the Blessed Virgin Mary thy Mother, and didst choose him as thy foster-father: * grant, we beseech thee, that by his prayers and merits thy Church may rejoice in tranquil peace, § and be brought to the consolation of the everlasting vision.
omnipotensetmitissimedeusquibeatumioseph.la: Omnípotens et mitíssime Deus, qui Beátum Joséphum, justum Fílium David, Beátæ Maríæ Vírgini, Matri tuæ Sponsum providísti, tuúmque Nutrítium elegísti: * da quǽsumus, ut ejus précibus et méritis Ecclésia tua tranquílla pace lætétur, § et ad perpétuæ visiónis consolatiónem perducátur.

desponsatiotuadeigenetrixvirgogaudiumann.en: Thy Espousal, O Virgin Mother of God, hath announced joy to the whole world: for from thee hath risen the Sun of justice, Christ our God:
desponsatiotuadeigenetrixvirgogaudiumann.la: Desponsátio tua, Dei Génetrix Virgo, gáudium annuntiávit univérso mundo: ex te enim ortus est sol justítiæ, Christus Deus noster:

etquamquamilludaliterquomodovelletperfic.en: And although he could have accomplished it otherwise, in whatever way he would; yet it pleased him rather to reconcile man to himself in that manner and order in which he knew that he had fallen: that as the devil first seduced the woman, and afterward overcame the man through the woman, so he should first be beguiled by a woman, a Virgin, and afterward be openly vanquished by a man, Christ: so that, while the art of loving-kindness mocked the fraud of malice, and the might of Christ crushed the strength of the evil one, God might appear wiser and stronger than the devil.
etquamquamilludaliterquomodovelletperfic.la: Et quamquam illud áliter quómodo vellet, perfícere potuísset; plácuit tamen eo pótius modo et órdine hóminem sibi reconciliáre, quo nóverat cecidísse: ut sicut diábolus prius sedúxit Fœminam, et póstmodum Virum per Fœminam vicit, ita prius a Fœmina Vírgine seducerétur, et post a Viro Christo apérte debellarétur: quátenus malítiæ fraudi dum ars pietátis illúderet, ac malígni fortitúdinem Christi virtus contéreret, diábolo Deus prudéntior apparéret et fórtior.

conveniensergeratutsuaviterquoqueomniace.en: It was fitting therefore that he should also dispose all things sweetly, namely things heavenly and earthly: so that both, casting down thence the restless one, he might establish the rest in peace, and here, being about to vanquish the envious one, he might first leave us a most necessary example of his humility and meekness; and that thus by a wonderful governance of wisdom it might come to pass that he should appear both sweet to his own and strong to his enemies.
conveniensergeratutsuaviterquoqueomniace.la: Convéniens ergo erat, ut suáviter quoque ómnia cœléstia scílicet et terréna dispóneret: quátenus et illinc dejíciens inquiétum, réliquos firmáret in pace et hic debellatúrus ínvidum, nobis prius suæ humilitátis et mansuetúdinis valde necessárium exémplum relinquerétur, sicque mirábili fíeret moderámine sapiéntiæ, ut et suis suávis et hóstibus fortis apparéret.

quidenimprodestdiabolumadeovincinobisman.en: For what doth it profit that the devil be overcome by God, while we remain proud? Necessarily therefore was Mary espoused to Joseph, since thereby both the Holy One is hidden from the dogs, and her virginity is attested by her spouse, and the modesty of the Virgin is spared as well as her good name provided for. What could be wiser? What more worthy of divine Providence? By one such counsel a witness is admitted to the heavenly secrets, and the good name of the Virgin Mary is kept unblemished.
quidenimprodestdiabolumadeovincinobisman.la: Quid enim prodest diábolum a Deo vinci, nobis manéntibus supérbis? necessário ígitur desponsáta est María Joseph, quando per hoc et a cánibus Sanctum abscónditur, et a sponso Virgínitas comprobátur et Vírginis tam verecúndiæ párcitur, quam famæ providétur. Quid sapiéntius? quid dígnius Divína Providéntia? uno tali consílio secrétis cœléstibus et admíttitur testis, et íntegra servátur fama Vírginis Maríæ.

mechtildisinsaxonianobilissimogenereorte.en: Mechtilde was born in Saxony of a most noble family. At seven years of age she fled to the neighbouring monastery of Nuns of our Order at Helfta, and consecrated herself wholly to Christ, the Spouse of virgins: and having received the religious habit, she grew in a short time so much in virtues and in the love of God, that she merited even to enjoy familiar converse with God. She was most ready for obedience, at once leaving the things with which she was occupied, according to the precept of the holy Rule. She let no moment of time slip by uselessly; but she was always either praying, or meditating, or reading, or teaching, or working with her hands. Sublime was her contemplation, in which she was flooded with so great an abundance of divine grace, that for a long space of time she remained without the use of her senses in the enjoyment of God: being enlightened by God meanwhile with many revelations and heavenly visions. She was also affected with such sweetness while she read or heard the holy Gospel, that through the abundance of its delight she was very often rendered almost lifeless.
mechtildisinsaxonianobilissimogenereorte.la: Mechtíldis in Saxónia nobilíssimo génere orta est. Septénnis ad vicínum Sanctimoniálium Monastérium de Helfta, Ordinis nostri, confúgiens, totam se Christo vírginum Sponso consecrávit: susceptóque religióso hábitu, brevi in virtútibus ac Dei amóre ita excrévit, ut étiam familiári Dei collóquio frui mererétur. Ad obediéntiam, relíctis statim iis quibus vacábat, juxta sanctæ Régulæ praescríptum promptíssima erat. Nullum témporis moméntum inutíliter elábi sinébat; sed semper vel orábat, vel meditabátur, vel legébat, aut docébat aut mánibus operabátur. Sublímis fuit ejus contemplátio, in qua tanta divínæ grátiæ abundántia perfundebátur, ut longo témporis spátio absque sénsibus in fruitióne Dei demorarétur: multis ínterim revelatiónibus ac visis cœléstibus a Deo illustráta. Tanta étiam suavitáte afficiebátur, dum sanctum Evangélium legébat, vel audiébat, ut præ dulcédinis affluéntia pene exánimis sæpius redderétur.

ergadulcissimumcoriesuchristimirafuiteiu.en: Wonderful was her devotion towards the most sweet Heart of Jesus Christ. When she lay sick unto death, and the blessed virgin Gertrude asked of the Lord what he was doing with her, he said: I rest with her in the bridal chamber of a sweet embrace: for although she is tormented with divers and continual pains, yet, trusting in my loving-kindness, she believeth that all things will profit her unto eternal salvation, and persevering in continual thanksgiving, she committeth herself wholly and confidently to my fatherly providence. At length, when the hour of her death was at hand, being wonderfully refreshed by Christ Jesus with divine light, and invited to the heavenly nuptials, she gave up her soul on the thirteenth day before the Kalends of December.
ergadulcissimumcoriesuchristimirafuiteiu.la: Erga dulcíssimum Cor Jesu Christi mira fuit ejus devótio. Cum ad mortem ægrotáret, et beáta virgo Gertrúdis quæreret a Dómino, quidnam cum ea operarétur: Ego, inquit, cum ea in thálamo suávis ampléxus requiésco: quia licet divérsis continuísque dolóribus torqueátur, de mea tamen pietáte confídens ómnia ad ætérnam salútem sibi profutúra credit, et in contínuis gratiárum actiónibus persevérans, patérnæ providéntiæ meæ totam se fiduciáliter commíttit. Dénique hora mortis suæ instánte divíno lúmine a Christo Jesu mirabíliter recreáta, et ad cœléstes núptias invitáta réddidit décimo tértio Kaléndas Decémbris.

deusquiindevotissimobeatemechtildisvirgi.en: O God, who in the most devout heart of blessed Mechtilde thy Virgin didst establish for thyself a pleasant dwelling: * grant us, we beseech thee, by the intercession of the same Virgin, that while we live we may ever be raised in spirit from earthly things to heavenly, § and may likewise triumph with her in the resurrection of the just. *
deusquiindevotissimobeatemechtildisvirgi.la: Deus, qui in devotíssimo beátæ Mechtíldis, Vírginis tuæ, corde jucúndam tibi mansiónem constituísti: * da nobis, quǽsumus, ejúsdem Vírginis intercessióne, dum vívimus, a terrénis semper ad cœléstia spíritu sublevári § et cum ea in resurrectióne justórum páriter triumpháre. *

vincentiuskadlubekpolonusnatusestutantiq.en: Vincent Kadlubek, a Pole, was born, as the ancient acts relate, in the village of Karvau in the diocese of Cracow, in the palatinate of Sandomir, of the most ancient family of the Rosae. His father was Bogumit, his mother Benigna, illustrious in nobility of blood and in piety; and being holily brought up by them in the Catholic faith and in the fear of the Lord, he gave many signs of holiness even in his tender years, by innocence of life, by constant zeal for prayer, by humility, modesty and ready obedience towards his parents. Having become a young man, and being instructed in the studies of philosophy and theology, he obtained the doctor's laurel in the Academy of Cracow, ever joining singular piety with the study of letters, abhorring idleness and the company of the wicked, given to prayer, frequenting the Sacraments, and practising with a strong mind the other acts of Christian piety.
vincentiuskadlubekpolonusnatusestutantiq.la: Vincéntius Kádlubek Polónus natus est, ut antíqua acta ferunt, in Villa Karvau Diœcésis Cracoviénsis Palatinátus Sandomirénsis, ex vetustíssima Rosárum família. Patre Bogumíto, matre Benígna, sánguinis claritáte et pietáte illústribus, a quibus in fide Cathólica et in timóre Dómini sancte educátus, plura édidit in ipsis téneris annis sanctitátis specímina, innocéntia morum, jugi orándi stúdio, humilitáte, modéstia ac prompta erga suos paréntes obediéntia. Adoléscens factus, Philosóphicis ac Theológicis stúdiis imbútus, in Académia Cracoviénsi láuream Doctorálem adéptus est, cum litterárum stúdio singulárem pietátem semper cópulans, ótium et pravórum consórtia abhorrens, oratióni addíctus, Sacraménta frequéntans, aliósque Christiánæ pietátis actus forti ánimo exércens.

tantesanctimoniavitecaptusfulcepiscopusc.en: Captivated by such holiness of life, Fulco, Bishop of Cracow, took Vincent among his own, and made use of his labours in the government of his diocese. Since besides an excellent integrity of life he was also strong in a keen mind and singular prudence, having been ordained to the priesthood, he was raised by the same Bishop to the Provostship of the illustrious Collegiate church of Sandomir; in which dignity he fulfilled all the parts of his office so holily, that, having become a pattern of modesty, chastity and the other virtues, he merited to be appointed by Leszek the White, King of Poland, as envoy, to conduct the King's own daughter, blessed Salome, as bride to the King of Halicz. Meanwhile, Fulco, Bishop of Cracow, having died, he was taken up to the same see; Innocent III, the Sovereign Pontiff, confirming his election.
tantesanctimoniavitecaptusfulcepiscopusc.la: Tantæ sanctimónia vitæ captus Fulco Epíscopus Cracoviénsis Vincéntium inter suos cooptávit, ejúsque ópera usus est in regímine suæ Diœcésis. Cum præter exímiam vitæ integritátem, acri étiam polléret ingénio, singulárique prudéntia, Sacerdótio initiátus, evéctus fuit ab eódem Epíscopo ad Præpositúram insígnis Collegiátæ Sandomirénsis, in qua dignitáte omnes sui múneris partes ádeo sancte explévit, ut exémplar factus modéstiæ, castimóniæ, aliarúmque virtútum promerúerit designári a Lefco Albo Polóniæ rege in Oratórem, ut própriam fíliam beátam Saloméam in sponsam dedúceret ad regem Halíciæ. Defúncto intérea Fulcóne Epíscopo Cracoviénsi assúmptus ille fuit ad eándem sedem; Ejúsdem electiónem confirmánte Innocéntio III. Pontífice Máximo.

decurrenteverodecimeiusepiscopatusanneva.en: But in the course of the tenth year of his episcopate, desirous of evangelical perfection, he resolved to withdraw into the camp of religion, that he might give himself to the contemplation of heavenly things and to the rule of a stricter life. Hence, having with a strong mind overcome by prayers and tears the opposition of the Chapter and of the people of Cracow, with the previous consent of Pope Honorius the Third, he dispersed all his goods and gave to the poor; and having laid down the episcopal insignia before the college of the Canons of Cracow, setting out with bare feet he betook himself, a journey of ten leagues, to the monastery of Andreow, in which he professed the monastic life of the Cistercian Order: and there for five whole years he shone in regular observance, in fasts and in the contemplation of heavenly things, being also enriched by God with many supernatural gifts. At length, full of days and of works, he died a death precious in the sight of the Lord on the eighth of March, in the year one thousand two hundred and twenty-three. He was renowned for the fame of holiness and of miracles. His ecclesiastical cult, duly approved, was confirmed by Clement XIII, the Sovereign Pontiff, who also granted that these proper lessons be recited in his honour.
decurrenteverodecimeiusepiscopatusanneva.la: Decurrénte vero décimo ejus Episcopátus anno, Evangélicæ perfectiónis cúpidus, in religiósa castra secédere decrévit, ut cœléstium rerum contemplátioni et rigidióris vitæ Institúto vacáre posset. Hinc forti ánimo, précibus et lácrymis devícta Capítuli, et pópuli Cracoviénsis contradictióne, prævio beneplácito Pontíficis Honórii tértii, ómnia sua dispérsit et dedit paupéribus, et Insígniis Episcopálibus depósitis coram collégio Canonicórum Cracoviénsium nudis pédibus proficíscens per decem leucas se cóntulit ad Cœnóbium Andreoviénse, in quo Monásticam vitam Ordinis Cisterciénsis proféssus est: ibíque regulári observántia, jejúniis et cœléstium rerum contemplátione quinque júgiter annis praelúxit, plúribus étiam supernaturálibus donis a Deo locupletátus. Plenus tandem diérum et óperum, pretiósam in conspéctu Dómini mortem óbiit octáva Mártii anno millésimo ducentésimo vigésimo tértio. Fama sanctitátis et miraculórum clarus. Ecclesiásticum ejus cultum rite probátum, confirmávit Clemens XIII. Póntifex Máximus. Qui et has lectiónes próprias ejus in honórem recitándas concéssit.

deusquibeatumvincentiumconfessoremtuumat.en: O God, who didst adorn blessed Vincent, thy Confessor and Bishop, with the glory of humility, when he had despised the pomps of the world, § grant, we beseech thee: * that, profiting by the example of such virtue, § we may by his merits be made partakers of heavenly glory.
deusquibeatumvincentiumconfessoremtuumat.la: Deus, qui beátum Vincéntium Confessórem tuum atque Pontíficem spretis sæculi pompis humilitátis glória decorásti, § præsta quæsumus: * ut tantæ virtútis proficiéntes exémplo, § ejus méritis cœléstis glóriæ consórtes efficiámur.

adalbertusnobilissimogenereinbohemiaortu.en: Adalbert was born in Bohemia of a most noble family; when, while still an infant, he was grievously sick, by the help of the most Blessed Virgin, to whom his parents had vowed him, he was laid at her altar and wonderfully recovered. Being sent to Magdeburg to learn the liberal arts, since he excelled in talent, he made great progress in them. Having returned to his own people, on the death of Dithmar he was created Bishop of Prague with the full consent of all: in which office, while he fed his flock by word and example, he fulfilled all the parts of an excellent Prelate.
adalbertusnobilissimogenereinbohemiaortu.la: Adalbértus nobilíssimo génere in Bohémia ortus, cum gráviter adhuc infans ægrotáret, Beatissimæ Vírginis ope, cui illum parentes devóverant, ejúsdem aræ admótus mire conváluit. Missus Magdebúrgum ad liberáles hauriéndas disciplínas, cum præstáret ingénio, magnos in iísdem progréssus hábuit. Revérsus ad suos Ditmáro demórtuo, summo ómnium consénsu Episcopus Pragénsis creátur: quo in múnere, dum verbo et exémplo gregem pascit, omnes óptimi Antístitis partes implévit.

nonresponditlaborifructusitaqueeumsenihi.en: The fruit did not answer to the labour. Therefore, when he perceived that he was profiting nothing, he came to Rome, intending to set out for Jerusalem. Departing thence to the monastery of Cassino, and having cast aside the plan of a longer pilgrimage at the admonition of blessed Nilus, he returned to the City and became a monk at St. Boniface.
nonresponditlaborifructusitaqueeumsenihi.la: Non respóndit labóri fructus. Itaque eum se nihil proficere animadvérteret, Jerosólymam profectúrus Romam venit. Digréssus inde ad Cassinénse Monastérium longióris peregrinatiónis abjécto consilio beáti Nili mónitu ad Urbem rédiens ad sanctum Bonifácium Mónachus effícitur.

quinquenniumibiincredibilipietateacrelig.en: When he had spent five years there with incredible piety and devotion, an embassy having been sent to the Sovereign Pontiff, he was recalled to Bohemia. Being commanded to return, he obeyed. But since the people did not depart from their disposition, he went back to the monastery whence he had departed. Nor could he rest long there; for when Otto the Third came to Rome, and the Prelate of Mainz demanded him back, he was compelled to depart again.
quinquenniumibiincredibilipietateacrelig.la: Quinquénnium ibi incredíbili pietáte ac religióne cum egísset, missa ad Summum Pontificem legatióne in Bohémiam revocátur. Jussus revérti páruit. Sed cum pópulus ab ingénio non recéderet, ad Monastérium, unde discésserat, migrávit. Nec diu quiéscere ibídem pótuit, Othóne tértio Romam adveniénte, cum Moguntínus Antístes illum repéteret, iterum discédere cógitur.

sedreiectusasuispiisquosproximeinpolonia.en: But being rejected by his own people, and by no means content with the pious labours which he had lately undertaken in Poland, and earlier in Hungary, for the sake of the faith, he set himself, as he had obtained leave from the Sovereign Pontiff, to win souls among the nations which knew not Christ. Scarcely had he come into Prussia when, being ill received by the inhabitants, he was soon slain by them. His body was ransomed by Boleslaus, Duke of Bohemia, for an equal weight of gold. It was at length translated to Prague, and is there venerated most devoutly.
sedreiectusasuispiisquosproximeinpolonia.la: Sed rejéctus a suis, piis, quos próxime in Polónia, prius vero in Hungária fidei causa suscéperat, labóribus mínime conténtus, quod a Summo Pontifice impetráverat, ad Gentes, quæ Christum non nóverant lucrifaciéndas ánimas adjécit. Vix Prússiam vénerat cum male accéptus ab íncolis, mox ab iísdem est interémptus. Corpus a Bolesláo Bohémiæ Duce, æquáli auri póndere redémptum fuit. Quod demum Pragam translátum, ibídem religiosissime cólitur.

deusquibeatumadalbertummartyremtuumatque.en: O God, who didst vouchsafe to crown blessed Adalbert, thy Martyr and Bishop, with glory and honour: * grant, we beseech thee, that him whom we had on earth as minister of eternal salvation, § we may merit to have as our intercessor in heaven.
deusquibeatumadalbertummartyremtuumatque.la: Deus, qui beátum Adalbértum Mártyrem tuum, atque Pontíficem glória et honóre coronáre dignátus es: * præsta quǽsumus, ut quem salútis ætérnæ minístrum habúimus in terris, § intercessórem habére mereámur in cœlis.

beatavirgofranchasubcatulelatrantisfigur.en: The blessed virgin Franca, whose mother, while with child, saw her in the likeness of a barking puppy, was born at Piacenza of the stock of the Counts of Vitalta. And when she had scarcely reached her seventh year, she was given by her parents to the Nuns of St. Cyrus to be brought up; then, in her fourteenth year, she was joined to the community by taking the habit, and, her probation being completed, by the making of her vows (an Angel by divine power placing the veil upon her). She was of such austerity that in Lent she ate nothing cooked save bread and unsalted herbs.
beatavirgofranchasubcatulelatrantisfigur.la: Beáta virgo Francha sub cátulæ latrántis figúra a matre prægnánte visa, náscitur Placéntiæ ex stirpe Cómitum de Vidálta. Cumque séptimum vix annum attigisset, a paréntibus Moniálibus sancti Cyri educánda tráditur; annum deínde quartumdécimum agens, per hábitus susceptiónem, et expléta probatióne, per votórum emissiónem (Angelo velámen divinítus imponénte) sociátur convéntui. Tantæ fuit austeritátis, ut in Quadragésima nihil coctum præter panem et herbas insúlsas coméderet.

eligiturinabbatissametatisannovigesimoqu.en: She was elected Abbess in the twenty-fifth year of her age. The sister of the Bishop coveting the dignity, and she being harassed by him for many years, she at length gave way, and hastening to the stricter observance of Citeaux, she founded the new monastery of Valeria, and from thence that of Plectoli. At length, renowned for many miracles, and shining with holy works, she commended her pious soul to the Lord and gave it up on the seventh day before the Kalends of May, about the year one thousand two hundred and eighteen. Through her merits sight was restored to a blind woman and to a thief deprived of his eyes, and those possessed by the devil were delivered, and other miracles were wrought.
eligiturinabbatissametatisannovigesimoqu.la: Elígitur in Abbatíssam ætátis anno vigésimo quinto. Ambiénte dignitátem soróre Epíscopi, et ab eódem per annos plures vexáta, tandem cessit, et ad Cistércii observántiam strictiórem cónvolans, novum Valériæ cœnóbium fundat, indeque Pléctolem. Tandem plúribus clara miráculis, sanctisque corúscans opéribus, piam Dómino commendávit ánimam, et réddidit séptimo Kaléndas Maji, anno circiter millésimo ducentésimo décimo Octávo. Cæcæ mulíeri, et furi óculis capto lumen méritis ipsíus restitútum est obsessique a dæmone liberáti sunt et ália mirácula perpetráta.

sigismundusburgundierexquamabeatoavitovi.en: Sigismund, King of Burgundy, nobly cultivated the piety which he had drawn from blessed Avitus, Bishop of Vienne. He was illustrious for charity towards the poor, abstinence of life, lowliness of mind, and in short every kind of virtue, but above all for devotion toward God and veneration toward the Saints. Among the others he wonderfully honoured the Theban Martyrs and their leader Maurice.
sigismundusburgundierexquamabeatoavitovi.la: Sigismúndus Burgúndiæ Rex, quam a Beáto Avíto Viennénsi Epíscopo pietátem háuserat, egrégie excóluit. Charitáte in páuperes, vitæ abstinéntia, demissióne ánimi, omni dénique virtútum genere, sed præsértim religióne in Deum, veneratióne in Sanctos illústris fuit. Inter cæteros Thebéos Mártyres, eorúmque Ducem Maurítium mirífice cóluit.

quorumagaunensetemplumubieorumsacracorpo.en: Their church at Agaunum, where their sacred bodies were kept, and the monastery, almost deserted through the injury of the times, he not only restored, but also built more magnificently, increased it in the number of monks, and enriched it with most ample revenues. When he often came to the tomb of these Martyrs, he was wont above all to ask this, that by their intercession he might be received by God into their company.
quorumagaunensetemplumubieorumsacracorpo.la: Quorum Agaunénse templum, ubi eórum sacra córpora servabántur, et Monastérium injúria Témporum pene desértum non modo restítuit, sed magnificéntius étiam extrúctum, Monachorúmque número auctum amplíssimis redítibus locupletávit. Ad horum Mártyrum túmulum cum frequénter accéderet, illud rogáre imprímis consuéverat, ut in eórum societátem, ipsis exorántibus a Deo reciperétur.

hocintemplodumprecesfunderetmonitusabang.en: While he was pouring forth prayers in this church, he was divinely admonished by an Angel to exhort the monks to sing the psalms in alternate verses, as the choirs of heaven were presently about to do in his hearing. Finally, the death of his son Syagrius, which he had inflicted upon him through the guile and at the instigation of his stepmother, he bewailed most abundantly in this same place, prostrate at the tomb of the holy Martyrs, and by their intercession obtained pardon from the Lord.
hocintemplodumprecesfunderetmonitusabang.la: Hoc in templo dum preces fúnderet, mónitus ab Angelo divínitus est, ut quod cœléstium chori ipso audiénte mox erant factúri, Mónachos ad psalmos altérnis versículis decantándos hortarétur. Dénique Syágrii fílii necem, quam novércæ dolo atque impúlsu illi intúlerat, hoc eódem in loco, ad Sanctórum Mártyrum túmulum provolútus, ubérrime deflévit, veniámque a Dómìno ipsis deprecántibus impetrávit.

interimeuminburgundiamfranciirrupissents.en: Meanwhile, when the Franks had burst into Burgundy, Sigismund, together with his brother Godomar, went out to meet them. Being routed by the enemy, when he had fled to the monastery of Agaunum as to a refuge, he was betrayed by his own and came into the power of Clodomir. Being carried away by his command into Gaul, and first cast into prison, he was soon thrown headlong into a well, together with his wife and children. The relics of his sacred body were after three years brought to the church of Agaunum, and lay there, until, carried to Prague by the Emperor Charles the Fourth, they found there a glorious tomb.
interimeuminburgundiamfranciirrupissents.la: Interim eum in Burgúndiam Franci irrupíssent: Sigismúndus una cum Gondemáro Fratre illis occúrrit. Fusus ab hóstibus, cum ad Agaunénse Monastérium quasi in ortum confugísset, prodéntibus suis in Chlodomíri potestátem venit. Abdúctus ejúsdem jussu in Gállias, atque in cárcerem primo conjéctus, mox étiam in púteum, una cum uxóre et líberis præceps est datus. Sacri córporis Reliquiæ post triénnium ad Agaunénse templum delátæ, in eódem jacuére, donec a Cárolo Quarto Cæsare Pragam advéctæ, gloriósum ibidem túmulum invenére.

deusquibeatumsigismundumregemutroquediad.en: O God, who didst vouchsafe to honour blessed Sigismund the King with a twofold diadem, namely temporal and eternal, together with the palm he desired: * and didst reveal his relics from the deep abyss of the waters to be honoured by the faithful, § grant, we beseech thee: * that we who venerate his merits, § may by his intercession be protected from all adversities.
deusquibeatumsigismundumregemutroquediad.la: Deus, qui Beátum Sigismúndum Regem utróque diadémate, temporáli scílicet et ætérno, cum desideráta palma honoráre dignátus es: * et ejus Relíquias ex profúndo gúrgite aquárum ad celebrándum fidélibus revelásti, § tríbue quǽsumus: * ut qui ejus mérita venerámur, § ipsíus intercessiónibus ab ómnibus protegámur advérsis.

sevientediocletianietmaximianiimperatoru.en: When the persecution of the Emperors Diocletian and Maximian was raging against the blood of Christians, and Aquilinus, Governor of Noricum Ripense, was proceeding most sharply against those same worshippers of Christ, and had cast into prison some forty of them in chains and evilly treated, Florian, their fellow in religion and in military service, heard that these things were being done at Lauriacum.
sevientediocletianietmaximianiimperatoru.la: Sæviénte Diocletiáni et Maximiáni Imperatórum in Christianórum sánguinem persecutióne, cum Aquilínus Nórici Repénsis Præses in eósdem Christi cultóres acérrime animadvérteret, et ad quadragínta nómine vinctos maléque tractátos in cárcerem conjecísset, Floriánus iísdem Religióne et milítiæ societáte hæc Lauréaci fíeri audívit.

hicsanctofideiardoreincensusacsanguinemp.en: He, inflamed with a holy ardour of faith, and desiring to shed his blood for Christ, hastened to the same place, and thus strove in a glorious contest for the crown of a more excellent warfare. Seeing therefore that the Christians were being sought out for the sacrifices of idols, fearing nothing the cruelty of the savage enemies of the faith, he came forth of his own accord into their midst, and cried out freely:
hicsanctofideiardoreincensusacsanguinemp.la: Hic sancto fídei ardóre incénsus, ac sánguinem pro Christo profúndere cúpiens eódem ádvolat sicque ad excellentióris milítiæ corónam glorióso certámine conténdit. Videns ergo Christiános ad idolórum Sacrifícia perquíri, nihil truculentórum fídei hóstium immanitátem véritus, in médium se ultro profert, liberéque exclámat.

quemaliuminquiensqueritisecceegochristia.en: Whom else, said he, do ye seek? Behold, I am a Christian: go, tell the Governor that I am here. The matter being reported to the Governor, Florian was brought in bonds, and being questioned concerning his confession, since he persisted most firmly in it and in his detestation of the vain gods, he was cruelly beaten with clubs, and his shoulders were most cruelly wounded and broken with iron.
quemaliuminquiensqueritisecceegochristia.la: Quem álium, ínquiens, quæritis? ecce ego Christiánus sum: ite, nuntiáte Præsidi, me hic adésse. Re ad Præsidem deláta, Floriánus vinctus addúcitur, ac de confessióne sua interrogátus, eum in eádem et inánium Deórum detestatióne firmíssime persísteret, fústibus dire cæditur, ferróque scápulæ ejus crudelíssime sauciántur, et confringúntur.

tandeminvictuschristiathletavariistormen.en: At length the unconquered champion of Christ, having overcome divers kinds of torments, for his unshaken constancy in the faith joyfully received the final sentence of death. A stone therefore being tied to his neck, he was cast from a bridge into the river Enns. Divine vengeance was not lacking. For the eyes of him who, violently laying hands on him, threw the Martyr down, presently burst.
tandeminvictuschristiathletavariistormen.la: Tandem invíctus Christi Athléta, váriis tormentórum genéribus superátis, ob inconcússam fídei constántiam últimam mortis lætus éxcipit senténtiam. Ligáto ígitur ad collum ejus saxo e ponte in Anísum flúvium dejícitur. Non défuit Divina últio. Nam óculi ejus, qui injéctis violénter mánibus Mártyrem præcipitávit, mox crepuérunt.

deusquinosbeatiflorianimartyristuiglorio.en: O God, who dost gladden us with the solemnity of blessed Florian thy glorious Martyr, § mercifully grant: * that we who with loving devotion venerate on earth the glorious triumph of his victory, § may by thy bounty merit to attain unto his joy in heaven.
deusquinosbeatiflorianimartyristuiglorio.la: Deus, qui nos beáti Floriáni Mártyris tui gloriósi solemnitáte lætíficas, § concéde propítius: * ut cujus gloriósum victóriæ triúmphum pio amóre venerámur in terris, § ejus lætítiam adipísci te largiénte mereámur in cœlis.

sapientiaiustorumestnilperostensionemfin.en: The wisdom of the just is to feign nothing for show, to open their mind by their words, to love things true as they are, to avoid things false, to do good freely, to bear evil more willingly than to do it; to seek no vengeance for injury, to count reproach for the truth as gain. But this simplicity of the just is derided; for by the wise of this world the virtue of purity is believed to be folly.
sapientiaiustorumestnilperostensionemfin.la: Sapiéntia justórum est, nil per ostensiónem fíngere, sensum verbis aperíre, vera ut sunt dilígere, falsa devitáre, bona gratis exhibére, mala libéntius toleráre, quam fácere; nullam injúriæ ultiónem quærere, pro veritáte contuméliam lucrum putáre. Sed hæc justórum simplícitas deridétur; quia ab hujus mundi sapiéntibus puritátis virtus, fatúitas créditur.

hicestveremartyrquiprochristinominesangu.en: This is a Martyr indeed, who shed his blood for Christ's Name's sake
hicestveremartyrquiprochristinominesangu.la: Hic est vere Martyr, qui pro Christi nómine sánguinem suum fudit:

quiminasiudicumnontimuitnecterrenedignit.en: Who feared not the threats of judges, nor sought the glory of earthly dignity, but came unto the heavenly kingdom. (Alleluia.)
quiminasiudicumnontimuitnecterrenedignit.la: Qui minas júdicum non tímuit, nec terrénæ dignitátis glóriam quæsívit, sed ad cæléstia regna pervénit. (Allelúia.)

iustumdeduxitdominusperviasrectasetosten.en: The Lord guided the righteous in right paths, and showed him the kingdom of God.
iustumdeduxitdominusperviasrectasetosten.la: Justum dedúxit Dóminus per vias rectas, et osténdit illi regnum Dei.

deusquiobinvictumbeatiioannissacramental.en: O God, who because of the unconquered sacramental silence of blessed John didst adorn thy Church with a new crown of Martyrdom: * grant us by his intercession and example to guard our tongue with care, § and to suffer in this world all evils rather than the harm of the soul. *
deusquiobinvictumbeatiioannissacramental.la: Deus, qui ob invíctum beáti Joánnis Sacramentále siléntium nova Ecclésiam tuam Martyrii coróna decorásti: * da nobis ejus intercessióne et exémplo linguam caute custodíre, § ac ómnia pótius mala, quam ánimæ detriméntum, in hoc sæculo toleráre. *

ioannesnepomucibohemieoppidoundenepomuce.en: John was born at Nepomuk, a town of Bohemia, whence he took the surname Nepomucene, of parents advanced in years, not without a presage of his future holiness, flames shining wonderfully above the house at his birth. When as an infant he had fallen into a grievous sickness, he escaped unharmed from danger of life by the help of the Blessed Virgin, to whom his parents ascribed the gift of his birth. Of an excellent disposition, and with a pious upbringing answering to the heavenly signs, he spent his boyhood in holy and religious exercises; for having learnt the form of serving priests who were to offer the divine Sacrifice, of his own accord he was wont to run very early in the morning to the monastery of the Cistercian monks next to Nepomuk, and to serve each of the ministers of God's mysteries who were about to offer at the altars. At Saaz he was formed to humane learning in the finer letters; and at Prague, being trained in the weightier disciplines, he merited the mastership and the laurel in philosophy, theology and the sacred canons. Being ordained to the priesthood, and duly prepared by the science of the Saints for the gain of souls, he devoted himself wholly to the ministry of the word of God.
ioannesnepomucibohemieoppidoundenepomuce.la: Joánnes Nepomúci Bohémiæ óppido, unde Nepomucéni cognómen duxit, a Paréntibus ætáte provéctis, non sine futúræ Sanctitátis præságio flammis supra nascéntis domum mirabíliter collucéntibus ortus est. Cum infans in gravem morbum incidisset, Beátæ Virginis ope, cui natum Parentes referébant accéptum e vitæ perículo evásit incólumis. Egrégia índole, piáque institutióne cœléstibus indíciis obsequénte inter sanctas religiosásque exercitatiónes puerítiam egit; Fórmula enim Presbyteris Divínum Sacrifícium factúris inserviéndi percépta; sponte sua ad Cœnóbium Monachórum Cisterciénsium Nepomúco ádjacens‚ primo mane decúrrere, singulísque Dei Mystis ad Aras operatúris ministráre consuévit. Zatécii politióribus líteris ad humanitátem informátus; Pragæ vero gravióribus disciplínis excúltus, Philosophíæ, Theologíæ, Sacrorúmque Cánonum Magistérium et Láuream eméruit. Sacerdotio initiátus, atque a sciéntia Sanctórum ad lucra animárum rite comparátus, ministério verbi Dei se pénitus addíxit.

cumigiturinvitiisextirpandisetrevocandis.en: When therefore by his eloquence and piety he was bringing forth abundant fruits in rooting out vices and recalling the erring into the way of salvation, he was chosen among the Canons of the Metropolitan Church of Prague, and soon took up the charge, entrusted to him, of preaching the Gospel before King Wenceslaus IV, with such success, that by John's persuasion the King did many things, and held his virtues in great honour. Yet the servant of God most steadfastly refused the conspicuous dignities which the King offered him, lest he should be called away from the preaching of the divine word. Queen Joanna took him, who had been set over the distribution of the royal alms to the poor, as the director of her conscience. But when Wenceslaus had departed from his duty and his former way of life, and was being carried headlong into vices, and bore ill the entreaties and admonitions of his pious consort, he dared to strive that the secrets confided by the Queen to the priesthood in the sacramental tribunal should be disclosed to him by John. But the minister of God, tempted first by blandishments, then by torments and the filth of prison, bravely withstood the wicked desire of the King.
cumigiturinvitiisextirpandisetrevocandis.la: Cum igitur in vítiis extirpándis et revocándis in viam salútis errántibus eloquéntia et pietáte úberes éderet fructus inter Canónicos Metropolitánæ Ecclésiæ Pragénsis cooptátus, mox sibi demandátam Evangélii coram Rege Wencesláo IV. prædicándi provínciam suscépit eo succéssu, ut Joánnis suásu multa Rex fáceret, magnóque in honóre ejus virtútes habéret. Conspícuas tamen, quas ille óbtulit dignitátes Dei servus, ne a Divini verbi præcónio avocarétur, constantíssime recusávit. Régiis illum eleemósynis in páuperes erogándis præféctum Joánna Regina consciéntiæ sibi Moderatórem adscívit. Cum autem Wencesláus ab offício institutóque decessísset, atque in vítia præceps abriperétur: piæ autem Cónjugis obtestátiónes et mónita graváte ferret, conténdere ausus est, ut in Sacramentáli Judício Sacerdótii crédita Regínæ arcána sibi a Joánne panderéntur. At Dei miníster blandítiis primum, torméntis deinde, et cárceris squalóre tentátus, nefáriæ Regis cupiditáti fórtiter óbstitit.

furentemtamenwenceslaianimumeumabexecran.en: But since neither human nor divine laws deterred the raging mind of Wenceslaus from his accursed purpose, the champion of Christ, knowing that his final contest was at hand, foretold it not obscurely, having admonished the people in a sermon also of the calamities that impended over the kingdom. Soon, having gone to Boleslaw, to an image of the Blessed Virgin renowned by ancient veneration, he implored with fervent prayers the help of heaven to fight the good fight. As he was returning thence in the evening, on the Vigil of the Lord's Ascension, the King, catching sight of him from a window, summoned him, and urged him more vehemently, and threatened him with speedy drowning in the waters if he went on resisting. John with unconquered constancy rejected the terrors and threats. Wherefore by the King's command he was thrown by night into the river Moldau, which floweth through Prague, and obtained the illustrious crown of Martyrdom. A remarkable prodigy divinely made manifest the sacrilegious crime, secretly committed, and the glory of the Martyr. For when the lifeless body began to be borne down the stream, burning torches appeared floating upon the waters and moving to and fro.
furentemtamenwenceslaianimumeumabexecran.la: Furéntem tamen Wenceslái ánimum eum ab execrándo proposito nec humána, nec divína jura deterrérent‚ suprémum agónem, quem instáre sibi Athléta Christi nóverat, pópulo in concióne de impendéntibus etiam Regni calamitátibus admónito, non obscúre prænuntiávit. Mox Bolesláviam proféctus ad Beátæ Virginis Imáginem antíquo cultu célebrem, cœléste præsídium ad certandum bonum certámen effúsis précibus implorávit. Inde vésperi reverténtem, in Pervigílio Domínicæ Ascensiónis, Rex e fenéstra conspicátus arcéssit, eumque veheméntius urgéret, et próximam in aquis‚ si obluctári pérgeret‚ submersiónem intentáret. Joánnes invícta cónstántia terrores minásque refutávit. Itaque Regis império in Moldávam flumen Pragam intérfluens noctu dejéctus, illústrem Martyrii corónam est consecútus. Sacrílegum fácinus clam patrátum, et Mártyris glóriam insígne prodígium divínitus patefécit. Ubi enim exánime corpus secúndo flúmine vehi cœpit, ardéntes faces aquis supernatántes et discurréntes apparuérunt.

quamobremexarenapostridiemanecorpuselatu.en: Wherefore the body, taken up from the sand on the morning of the following day, the Canons, fearing nothing the wrath of the King, carried with solemn pomp into the Metropolitan Church, and committed it to burial. And as the memory of the unconquered priest grew from day to day by miracles and by the very great veneration of the faithful, especially of those whose good name is in peril, at length, after more than three hundred years, at the judicial recognition of the body, which had lain so long under the earth, his tongue was found incorrupt and lifelike; which, being shown six years later to the judges delegated by the Apostolic See, by a new prodigy suddenly swelled, and changed its darkish red colour to purple. These and other signs therefore having been duly proved, Benedict XIII, the Sovereign Pontiff, on the nineteenth day of the month of March, in the year of salvation one thousand seven hundred and twenty-nine, enrolled in the catalogue of the holy Martyrs this first defender of the sacramental seal, who sealed with his blood his fidelity to the secret.
quamobremexarenapostridiemanecorpuselatu.la: Quamóbrem ex aréna, postrídie mane corpus elátum, Canónici deínde Regis iram nihil timéntes, in Metropolitánam Ecclésiam solémni pompa intulérunt et sepultúræ mandárunt. Cum autem indíes invícti Sacerdótis memória miráculis et máxima fidélium, eórum præcipue, qui fama periclitántur, veneratióne crésceret, post annos demum ámplius tercéntos in jurídica recognitióne córporis, quod sub humo tam diu jacúerat, lingua ejus incorrúpta et vívida repérta est; quæ sexto post anno judícibus a Sede Apostólica delegátis exhíbita, novo prodígio repénte intúmuit, et subobscúrum rubórem in purpúreum commutávit. His ítaque aliísque signis rite probátis, Benedictus XIII. Póntifex Máximus‚ die décima nona mensis Mártii anno Salútis millésimo septingentésimo vigésimo nono primum hunc Sacramentális Sigílli Assertórem, Arcáni fidem sánguine obsignántem Sanctórum Mártyrum catálogo adscrípsit.

omnipotensetmisericorsdeusquibeatissimeo.en: O almighty and merciful God, who didst give to blessed Simeon and his Companions the grace of persevering in the faith even unto martyrdom, * grant, we beseech thee, § that we, celebrating their memory with joy, * may learn to prefer nothing to the love of Christ thy Son.
omnipotensetmisericorsdeusquibeatissimeo.la: Omnípotens et miséricors Deus, qui beátis Simeóni et Sóciis grátiam in fide usque ad martýrium perseverándi dedísti, * concéde, quaesumus, § ut nos, eórum memóriam cum gáudio celebrántes, * nihil Christi, Fílii tui, amóri praepónere discámus.

bedapresbytergirviinbritannieetscotiefin.en: Bede the priest was born at Jarrow, on the borders of England and Scotland. Having become a monk, he so ordered his life that, while he gave himself wholly to the study of the arts and of learning, he never relaxed anything of the regular discipline. There was no kind of learning in which he was not most diligently versed; but his chief care was the meditation of the divine Scriptures, so that, having been ordained to the priesthood, he undertook to explain the sacred books; in which he so closely followed the teachings of the holy Fathers, that he put forth nothing that was not approved by their judgment, using even almost their very words.
bedapresbytergirviinbritannieetscotiefin.la: Beda présbyter, Girvi in Británniæ et Scótiæ fínibus ortus est. Mónachus factus, vitam sic instítuit, ut dum se ártium et doctrinárum stúdiis totum impénderet, nihil umquam de regulári disciplína remítteret. Nullum fuit doctrínæ genus, in quo non esset diligentíssime versátus; sed præcípua illi cura fuit divinárum Scripturárum meditátio, ita ut, sacerdótio initiátus, sacros explanáre libros aggréssus sit; in quo sanctórum Patrum doctrínis ádeo inhæsit, ut nihil proférret nisi illórum judício comprobátum, eorúndem étiam fere verbis usus.

otiumperosussemperexlectioneadorationemt.en: Ever hating idleness, he passed from reading to prayer, and in turn from prayer to reading. He wrote many books for the amendment of the morals of the faithful, and for the defence and assertion of the faith, by which he gained so great a repute among all, that his writings were read publicly in the churches while he was yet alive. At length, broken by age and labours, he fell piously asleep in the Lord. Leo the Thirteenth declared him a Doctor of the universal Church.
otiumperosussemperexlectioneadorationemt.la: Otium perósus semper, ex lectione ad oratiónem transíbat, ac vicíssim ex oratióne ad lectiónem. Emendándis fidélium móribus, fídei vindicándæ atque asseréndæ libros plures conscrípsit, quibus tantam sui apud omnes opiniónem fecit, ut ejus scripta, eo adhuc vivénte, públice in ecclésiis legeréntur. Ætáte demum et labóribus fractus, pie obdormívit in Dómino. Eum Leo décimus tértius universális Ecclésiæ Doctórem declarávit.

aleydisvirgoinbrabantianataatenerisannis.en: Alice, a Virgin, born in Brabant, giving from her tender years bright signs of her future holiness, at seven years of age consecrated her virginity to God in the monastery called the Chamber of St. Mary, of the Cistercian Order, near Brussels, in which she gave herself wholly to humility. With constant patience she bore throughout her whole life most grievous pains and a loathsome leprosy. Wherefore, being separated from her sisters, she cleaved continually to God by prayer, and took pleasure in infirmities and distresses for Christ, in whose wounds she often experienced a heavenly healing. Renowned for heavenly gifts and many miracles, she especially cured very many stricken with leprosy by the mere laying on of hands. She assisted at the Sacrifice of the Mass with so great a feeling of devotion, that she often seemed to be consumed by the fire of divine love.
aleydisvirgoinbrabantianataatenerisannis.la: Aléydis Virgo in Brabántia nata, a téneris annis præclára futúræ sanctitátis indícia præbens, septénnis virginitátem suam Deo consecrávit in monastério quod dícitur Camera sanctæ Ma­ríæ‚ Cisterciénsis Ordinis prope Bruxéllas, in quo humilitáti sese pénitus addíxit. Constánti pátiéntia per totam vitam gravíssimos dolóres et fœdam lepram pértulit. Quaprópter separáta a sodálibus, Deo per oratiónem perpétuo adhæsit, placuítque sibi infirmitátibus et angústiis pro Christo‚ in cujus vulnéribus supernam medélam crebro experiebátur. Cœléstibus charismátibus ac multis miráculis clara, præcípue complúres lepra percússos sola manuum impositióne curávit. Tanto pietátis sensu Missæ sacrifício assistébat, ut divíni amóris igne consúmi sæpe viderétur.

diebeatobarnabeapostolosacraaleydisinlim.en: On the day sacred to blessed Barnabas the Apostle, Alice, lying at the threshold of death, and anointed with the holy oil, was admonished by the Lord that she would live yet a whole year, and meanwhile would undergo far more grievous sicknesses for the honour of her beloved Spouse; which also came to pass: for the light of her eyes being extinguished, and her hands contracted, the skin of her head and of all her limbs appeared like the bark of a tree, marked with divers ulcers, from which worms and continual corruption broke forth abundantly. These dreadful torments the blessed Virgin bore with most unconquered and wonderful patience, until in the following year, one thousand two hundred and fifty, on the third day before the Ides of June, when the solemnity of St. Barnabas came round again, she breathed forth her most devout soul in the embrace of Christ.
diebeatobarnabeapostolosacraaleydisinlim.la: Die beato Bárnabæ Apóstolo sacra, Aléydis in límine mortis hærens, et óleo sancto inúncta, a Dómino admónita fuit se íntegro adhuc anno victúram‚ interímque morbos multo gravióres pro dilécti sponsi honóre subitúram, quod et accídit: nam oculórum lúmine extíncto mánibus contráctis cápitis omniúmque membrórum cutis ad córticis árboris instar, váriis distíncta ulcéribus appáruit, ex quibus vermes et jugis sánies copióse erumpébant. Immánes istos cruciátus invictíssima et mirábili tolerántia beáta Virgo sustínuit, donec anno insequénte, millésimo ducentésimo quinquagésimo, tertio Idus Júnii, recurrénte solemnitáte sancti Bárnabæ piíssimam in amplexu Christi efflávit ánimam.

daquesumusomnipotensdeusutquiintotadvers.en: Grant, we beseech thee, almighty God: * that we who in so many adversities fail through our weakness, § may, by the intercession of blessed Alice thy Virgin, be delivered from all evils and serve thee with a secure mind.
daquesumusomnipotensdeusutquiintotadvers.la: Da, quæsumus, omnípotens Deus: * ut, qui in tot advérsis ex nostra infirmitáte defícimus, § intercedénte beáta Aléyde, Vírgine tua, liberáti a malis ómnibus, secúra tibi mente serviámus.

vitusadmodumpuerinsciopatrebaptizatusest.en: Vitus, while yet a very young boy, was baptized without his father's knowledge: and when he had learnt of it, he left nothing undone to turn his son away from Christian piety; and as he remained in this resolve, he handed him over to the judge Valerian to be chastised with stripes. But as he nevertheless persisted in his purpose, he was handed back to his father. But while his father was thinking how to punish him more severely, Vitus, at the admonition of an Angel, with Modestus and Crescentia, who had brought him up, accompanying him, went away into foreign lands.
vitusadmodumpuerinsciopatrebaptizatusest.la: Vitus ádmodum puer ínscio Patre baptizátus est: quod cum ille rescivísset, nihil prætermísit, quo fílium a Christiána pietáte removéret, qua in voluntáte permanéntem Valeriáno Júdici verbéribus castigándum trádidit. Sed nihilóminus in senténtia persístens, Patri tráditus est. Dum vero eum Pater grávius puníre cógitat; Vitus Angeli mónitu comitántibus Modésto atque Crescéntia ejus educatóribus migrant in aliénas terras.

quotemporetonitruafulguramagniqueterremo.en: At that time there were thunders, lightnings and great earthquakes, by which the temples of the gods fell down, and many were crushed. Their relics Florentia, a noble woman, embalmed with ointments and honourably buried. The arm of St. Vitus was given as a gift by blessed Wenceslaus to the Metropolitan church which he himself had built at Prague. His bones the Emperor Charles IV received from the city of Pavia, and placed them in the same church.
quotemporetonitruafulguramagniqueterremo.la: Quo témpore tonítrua, fúlgura, magníque terræmótus fuére, quibus templa Deórum corruérunt, et multi oppréssi sunt. Eórum Relíquias Floréntia nóbilis fœmina unguéntis condítas honorífice sepelívit. Sancti Viti bráchium a Beáto Wencesláo templo Metropolitáno, quod ipse Pragæ constrúxerat, dono datum. Ejúsdem ossa Cárolus IV. Imperátor Ticinénsi ex urbe accépta, in eádem æde collocávit.

inillotemporedixitiesusdiscipulissuisnol.en: At that time: Jesus said unto his disciples: Think not that I am come to send peace on earth: I came not to send peace, but a sword. And so on, and that which followeth.
inillotemporedixitiesusdiscipulissuisnol.la: In illo témpore: Dixit Jesus discípulis suis : Nolíte arbitrári, quia pacem vénerim míttere in terram, non veni pacem míttere, sed gládium. Et réliqua.

queestistadivisiointerprimenimlegisprece.en: What is this division? For among the first precepts of the law we have received: Honour thy father and thy mother. And the Lord himself saith: Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you. What meaneth it, then, that a sword rather is sent upon earth, and the son is set apart from his father, and the daughter from her mother, and the daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law, and that a man's enemies shall be they of his own household? Therefore from thenceforth public authority is preferred to impiety.
queestistadivisiointerprimenimlegisprece.la: Quæ est ista divísio? inter prima enim legis præcépta accépimus: Honóra patrem tuum et matrem tuam. Et ipse Dóminus ait: Pacem relínquo vobis, pacem meam do vobis. Quid sibi vult missus pótius gládius in terram, et separátus a patre fílius, et fília a matre, et nurus advérsus socrum, et hómines doméstici, ejus inimíci? Igitur exínde pública authóritas impietáti præfértur.

ubiqueodiaubiquebelletgladiusdominiinter.en: Hatred everywhere, warfare everywhere, the sword of the Lord furiously raging between father and son, mother and daughter. The sharpest weapon of all weapons is the sword, whereby is enforced the law of might, the severity of judgment, the punishment of sinners. Furthermore, the word Sword is in common use amongst the Prophets as a figure of the preaching of the new Gospel.
ubiqueodiaubiquebelletgladiusdominiinter.la: Ubíque ódia, ubíque bella, et gládius Dómini inter patrem et fílium, et inter fíliam matrémque desæviens. Gládius telórum ómnium telum acutíssimum est, in quo sit jus potestátis, et judícii sevéritas, et animadvérsio peccatórum. Et, hujus quidem teli nómine, novi Evangélii prædicatiónem appellátam frequens in Prophétis auctóritas est.

deiergoverbumnuncupatummeminerimusinglad.en: Let us remember, therefore, that the word of God is called a sword; which sword is sent upon earth, that is, his preaching poured into the hearts of men. And there cometh to be a grievous dissension in one house, and they of his household shall be enemies to the new man; because he, divided from them by the word of God, will rejoice to remain both inward and outward, that is, both body and soul, in newness of spirit.
deiergoverbumnuncupatummeminerimusinglad.la: Dei ergo verbum nuncupátum meminérimus in gládio; qui gládius missus in terram est, id est, prædicátio ejus hóminum córdibus infúsa. Fitque gravis in domo una dissénsio, et doméstica novo hómini erunt inimíca; quia ille, per verbum Dei divísus ab illis, manére et intérior et extérior, id est, et corpus et anima, in spíritus novitáte gaudébit.

decclesietuequesumusdominesanctomartyret.en: Grant to thy Church, we beseech thee, O Lord, by the intercession of thy holy Martyr Vitus, not to be proudly wise, § but to advance in the humility pleasing unto thee, * that, despising things perverse, § she may practise with free charity whatsoever things are right.
decclesietuequesumusdominesanctomartyret.la: Da Ecclésiæ tuæ, quæsumus, Dómine, sancto Mártyre tuo Vito intercedénte supérbe non sápere, § sed tibi plácita humilitáte profícere, * ut prava despíciens; § quæ recta sunt, líbera exérceat charitáte.

procopiuspostliberaliumstudiadisciplinar.en: Procopius, after studying the liberal arts, spent some time in the religious life in the monastery of Brevnov. Then, seized with the love of solitude, he chose with great courage to dwell in a cave overhanging the river Sazava, haunted by ghosts and spectres, which no one dared approach.
procopiuspostliberaliumstudiadisciplinar.la: Procópius post liberálium stúdia disciplinárum in Monastério Brzewnoviénsi vitam aliquámdiu religióse tradúxit. Solitúdinis deínde amóre captus, spelúncam Sázavæ flúmini incumbéntem larvis ac spectris obnóxiam, quam adíre nullus audébat, magno ánimo incoléndam sibi delégit.

necvirisanctitatemferremonstradiutiusval.en: Nor could the monsters long endure the holiness of the man; but straightway vanishing, they left to him the free and quiet possession of that place. The fame of this prodigy being spread abroad, when great crowds began to flock to him, he easily understood that it was not the divine counsel that he should lie hidden. Therefore he gathered together some who were fired with zeal for a more perfect life, whom he trained to all holiness, chiefly by his own example.
necvirisanctitatemferremonstradiutiusval.la: Nec Viri Sanctitátem ferre monstra diútius valuérunt ; sed contínuo dilápsa, líberam illi, quietámque ejus loci possessiónem reliquére. Ejus prodígii fama vulgáta, cum magni ad illum concúrsus fíeri cœpíssent, fácile intelléxit divíni consílii non esse, ut latéret. Itaque perfectióris stúdio vitæ incénsos nonnúllos collégit, quos ad omnem sanctitátem suo præsértim exémplo informávit.

udalricumbohemieprincipemavenationefessu.en: Udalric, Prince of Bohemia, when weary from hunting, he refreshed with water changed into wine. Devils he not only cast out of bodies, but also, putting them under the yoke, compelled them to plough. At length, having foretold his death and other things, renowned for virtues and divine gifts he passed to heaven: nor did he cease after death to shine with miracles.
udalricumbohemieprincipemavenationefessu.la: Udalrícum Bohémiæ Príncipem a venatióne fessum aqua in vinum versa recreávit. Dæmones non modo e corpóribus ejécit, sed étiam sub jugum missos aráre cómpulit. Dénique cum óbitum suum, aliáque prædixísset, virtútibus, divinísque munéribus clarus migrávit in cœlum : nec désiit post mortem miráculis coruscáre.

interaliailludinsignequodcuidamquiinmagn.en: Among others this is remarkable, that for a certain man, who in great peril while fleeing had implored his help, he made a way to pursue his journey by turning the river into ice. This also is memorable, that when the Abbot of his monastery could not obtain at Rome that he be numbered among the Saints, he admonished Innocent III in sleep to grant the petition. Nor was there need of further labour with the Pontiff. Wherefore he was enrolled by him in the number of the Saints in the year of salvation one thousand two hundred and four.
interaliailludinsignequodcuidamquiinmagn.la: Inter ália illud insígne, quod cuídam, qui in magno discrímine fúgiens ejus opem imploráverat, flúvio in gláciem verso, ad iter prosequéndum viam expedívit. Illud étiam memorábile, quod, cum sui Monastérii Abbas, ut inter Sanctos referrétur in Urbe non impetráret, Innocéntium III. per somnum admónuit, ut postulátis annúeret. Nec diútius cum Pontífice laborándum fuit. Quare ab eódem anno Salútis millésimo ducentésimo quarto Sanctórum número est adscríptus.

plenaminnobiseternesalvatortuevirtutisop.en: Work in us, O eternal Saviour, the full healing of thy power: * that we who venerate the illustrious merits of blessed Procopius, thine Abbot and Confessor, § being helped by his prayers, * may be delivered from all the sicknesses of our souls.
plenaminnobiseternesalvatortuevirtutisop.la: Plenam in nobis ætérne Salvátor tuæ virtútis operáre medélam: * ut, qui præclára Beáti Procópii Abbátis et Confessóris tui mérita venerámur; § ipsíus adjúti suffrágiis, * a cunctis animárum nostrárum languóribus liberémur.

exbreviariopragensietpropriomoravie.en: From the Breviary of Prague and the Proper of Moravia.
exbreviariopragensietpropriomoravie.la: Ex Breviário Pragénsi et Próprio Moráviæ.

cyrillusvitesanctitatererumquegestarumgl.en: Cyril was most illustrious for holiness of life and the glory of his deeds. When Nicholas the First was Sovereign Pontiff, the body of the holy Pope Clement was brought by him to Rome, and laid in the church which had earlier been built in honour of that most blessed Martyr. He had as brother Methodius, plainly his own brother in manner of life and in character, who, as John the Eighth testifieth, was sent by Hadrian II to propagate the faith.
cyrillusvitesanctitatererumquegestarumgl.la: Cyríllus vitæ sanctitáte, rerúmque gestárum glória máxime illústris fuit. Nicoláo primo Summo Pontífice sancti Cleméntis Papae corpus Romam ab illo advéctum, atque in templo quod in ejúsdem beatíssimi Mártyris honórem ántea extrúctum fúerat, recónditum est. Methúdium hábuit fratrem vitæ génere, ac móribus plane germánum, quem ab Hadriáno II. ad fidem propagándam missum Joánnes octávus testátur.

multarumregionumgentesunacumeorumregibus.en: The nations of many regions, together with their kings, they led to the faith of Christ; and first of all Swatopluk, who ruled widely among the Moravians. By his example Borziwoj, Duke of the Bohemians, then his wife Ludmilla, more illustrious by martyrdom than by her princely rank, and their children received Baptism. Thus the faith of Christ was brought into Bohemia and the neighbouring provinces, and in the times that followed it was wonderfully spread by the same.
multarumregionumgentesunacumeorumregibus.la: Multárum regiónum gentes una cum eórum régibus ad Christi fidem perduxére; ac imprímis Swatóplucum, qui apud Morávos late imperábat. Hujus exémplo Borzivógius Bohemórum Dux, tum ejus uxor Ludmílla Martyrio, quam principátu clárior, liberíque Baptísmum suscepérunt. Ita Christi fides in Bohémiam‚ finitimásque provinciás fuit indúcta, consequéntibus deínde tempóribus per eósdem est mirífice propagáta.

delatusadioannemoctavummethudiusquodabap.en: Methodius, having been accused before John the Eighth of departing from the doctrines of the Apostolic See, was summoned to Rome; and a Synod having been assembled, when he had proved his faith to all, he was dismissed by the same Pontiff with great honour, and was diligently commended to the Prince of Moravia, all being bidden to obey him.
delatusadioannemoctavummethudiusquodabap.la: Delátus ad Joánnem octávum Methúdius‚ quod ab Apostólicæ Sedis dogmátibus deflécteret Romam est accítus, coácta Synodo, cum fidem suam ómnibus probavísset, ab eódem Pontífice magno cum honóre dimíssus, ac Moráviæ Príncipi diligénter commendátus fuit, univérsis eídem parére jussis.

multadeindepassuscummaximasquibuspremeba.en: Afterwards, having suffered many things, when he had made known to the same Pontiff the very great straits by which he was oppressed, he merited to receive from him letters of consolation, by which he was greatly encouraged to act with fortitude. The body of Cyril, together with the ashes of Methodius, is most devoutly kept in that very church of St. Clement which he had enriched with the sacred relics of that same most blessed Pope.
multadeindepassuscummaximasquibuspremeba.la: Multa deinde passus, cum máximas, quibus premebátur angústias eídem Pontífici indicásset, consolatórias ab illo lítteras méruit accípere, quibus ad fórtiter agéndum fuit summópere animátus. Cyrílli corpus illo ipso in templo sancti Cleméntis, quod ejúsdem beatíssimi Papæ sacris relíquiis ditáverat, una cum Methúdii cinéribus religiosíssime asservátur.

omnipotenssempiternedeusquinosetslavonie.en: Almighty, everlasting God, who didst vouchsafe to call us and the Slavonic nations, through thy blessed Confessors and Bishops Cyril and Methodius, to the unity of the Christian Faith: § grant, we beseech thee; * that we who rejoice in their present festival, § may by their merits also deserve to attain eternal glory. *
omnipotenssempiternedeusquinosetslavonie.la: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, qui nos et Slavóniæ gentes per beátos Confessóres tuos atque Pontífices Cyríllum et Methódium, ad unitátem Fídei Christiánæ vocáre dignátus es: § præsta quǽsumus; * ut qui præsénti eórum festivitáte lætámur, § ipsórum étiam méritis glóriam cónsequi mereámur ætérnam. *

exbreviariisantiquioribusordinissanctibe.en: From the older Breviaries of the Order of St. Benedict.
exbreviariisantiquioribusordinissanctibe.la: Ex Breviariis antiquioribus Ordinis sancti Benedicti.

cumgenslongobardoruminterceterasuafacino.en: When the nation of the Lombards, among its other crimes, after the death of the holy father Benedict, had plundered the monastery which he had built on Monte Cassino, yet there it could not hold even one man: but the Lord fulfilled what he had promised to his servant Benedict, who is read to have foretold this overthrow: That he would deliver the place itself to the Gentiles, but would keep the souls. The monks therefore having fled, and many years having passed after this overthrow, the same place, reduced to a wilderness, which before had been a dwelling of men, began to be a dwelling of wild beasts.
cumgenslongobardoruminterceterasuafacino.la: Cum gens Longobardórum inter cétera sua facínora, post óbitum sancti patris Benedícti, monastérium, quod in monte Cassíno constrúxerat, deprædáta esset : ibi tamen nec unum tenére pótuit hóminem : sed implévit Dóminus quod fámulo suo Benedícto, qui hanc eversiónem légitur prædixísse, promíserat; Quod et locum ipsum Géntibus tráderet, ánimas custodíret. Fugiéntibus ítaque mónachis, et post hanc eversiónem multis effluéntibus annis, idem locus redáctus ad erémum, qui prius habitátio fúerat hóminum, cœpit esse ferárum.

tandemregnantesuperfrancosregeclodoveose.en: At length, when King Clovis the Second, son of Dagobert, was reigning over the Franks, and the venerable Abbot Mommolus was ruling the monastery of Fleury, he sent one of his monks, Aigulf by name, who afterwards became a martyr, to Monte Cassino (as he had been forewarned in sleep), that he might bring thence the body of the same father Benedict. Aigulf, desiring to fulfil the command he had received, made for Monte Cassino, where, when he had prayed to the Lord, finding a certain venerable old man, he heard these things from him: This very night watch carefully to mark the place in this solitude which thou shalt see shining with a most bright light: for in that same place thou shalt find that whereby an end may be put to thy care.
tandemregnantesuperfrancosregeclodoveose.la: Tandem regnánte super Francos rege Clodovæo secúndo, Dagobérti fílio, cum venerábilis Abbas Mómmolus monastério Floriacénsi præesset, unum de suis mónachis, nómine Aygúlfum, qui póstea martyr efféctus est, misit ad montem Cassínum (sicut in somnis praemónitus fúerat) ut exínde corpus ejúsdem patris Benedícti deférret. Aygúlfus mandátum quod accéperat, perfícere cúpiens, montem Cassínum, expétiit, ubi cum orásset Dóminum, quemdam venerábilem senem repériens, hæc ab eo audívit: Hac instánti nocte solitúdinis ejus locum, quem lúmine claríssimo radiáre conspéxeris, notáre diligénter invígilas : nam ibídem unde tuæ curæ finis imponátur, invénies.

cumsanctusbenedictusincellaconsisteretel.en: When St. Benedict was standing in his cell, lifting up his eyes, he saw the soul of his sister gone forth from her body,
cumsanctusbenedictusincellaconsisteretel.la: Cum sanctus Benedíctus in cella consísteret, elevátis sursum óculis, vidit soróris suæ ánimam de córpore ejus egréssam,

nocteigiturinsequentievigilansaygulfuset.en: On the following night, therefore, Aigulf, keeping watch and considering the place, saw the tomb of blessed Benedict lit up from heaven with a great light: and going to it reverently in the morning, whatsoever he found there he placed in a little basket which he had prepared for this. And when he and his companions, coming into the district of Orleans, had halted on an estate named Bonodium, a certain blind man, who with loud cries was calling upon blessed Benedict to grant him the sight which nature had denied, presently received his sight.
nocteigiturinsequentievigilansaygulfuset.la: Nocte ígitur insequénti evígilans Aygúlfus, et locum consíderans, beáti Benedícti sepúlchrum vidit magno lúmine cœlitus illustrátum : ad quod mane reverénter accédens, quidquid ibídem réperit ; in sportélla, quam ad hoc præparáverat, collocávit. Cumque ipse, et ejus sócii veniéntes in pagum Aurelianénsem, in quam prædio Bonódio nómine, consedíssent; cæcus quidam, qui beátum Benedíctum magnis vócibus invocábat, ut sibi præstáret lúmina quae negáverat natura, mox visum recépit.

corpusitaquebeatissimibenedictiprefatimo.en: The aforesaid Abbot Mommolus and the venerable Aigulf therefore laid the body of the most blessed Benedict in the Basilica of St. Peter the Apostle: which nevertheless they afterwards honourably entombed, on the fifth day of December, in the more seemly adorned church of the Blessed Virgin. For when the same Abbot Mommolus was praying one night, suddenly a light sent from heaven appeared visibly to him, in the manner of a torch, before the front of that same church: which most plainly marked out the place where the most holy body ought to be laid. There were translated also the bones of blessed Scholastica the virgin, his sister, which, being distinguished from the bones of Benedict by the raising of a dead girl, were brought to Le Mans: and there at great cost was built a Basilica of noble Nuns, which hath been made illustrious by great signs of miracles.
corpusitaquebeatissimibenedictiprefatimo.la: Corpus ítaque beatíssimi Benedícti præfáti Mómmolus Abbas, et venerábilis Aygúlfus in Basílica sancti Petri Apóstoli posuérunt : quod tamen póstmodum in Ecclésia beátæ Vírginis ornáta decéntius, quinta die Decémbris honorífice tumulárunt. Cum enim idem Abbas Mómmolus nocte quadam oráret, súbito lux emíssa de cœlo, in modum facis ante frontem ejusdem Ecclésiæ visibíliter sibi appáruit : quæ locum ubi corpus sanctíssimum repóni déberet, manifestíssime denotávit. Transláta sunt étiam ossa beátæ Scholásticae vírginis soróris ejus, quæ resuscitatióne puéllæ mórtuæ et Benedicti óssibus discréta, Cœnománis illáta fuérunt : ibíque magnis súmptibus ædificáta est Basílica nobílium Sanctimoniálium, quae magnis miraculórum insígnibus est illustráta.

apostolidictisdominihecredduntreliquisse.en: The Apostles answer these words of the Lord: that they have left all things, and are with him. To whom the Lord promised that, when he shall sit on the seat of his majesty, they shall sit upon twelve seats, and shall judge as many tribes of Israel: and that for all who have left all things for his name's sake, the fruit of a hundredfold reward is kept in store. And that many of the last shall be first, and of the first shall be last: there are many things which do not suffer us to receive the words of the Gospel with a simple understanding.
apostolidictisdominihecredduntreliquisse.la: Apóstoli dictis Dómini hæc reddunt: reliquísse se ómnia, et cum ipso esse. Quibus Dóminus‚ cum séderit in majestátis suæ sede, sessúros super sedes duódecim‚ ac tótidem tribus Israël judicatúros spopóndit: omnibúsque qui univérsa relíquerint propter nomen ejus‚ fructum céntupli præmii reservátum. Multos autem ex novíssimis primos futúros et ex primis futúros novíssimos : multa sunt, quæ non sinunt nos símplici intelléctu dicta Evangélica suscípere.

interpositisnonnullisrebusqueexnaturahum.en: Some things being set between which, by the nature of human sense, are contrary to one another, we are admonished to seek the reason of a heavenly understanding. The Apostles say both that they follow Christ, and that they have left all things. How then are they made sorrowful, and how do they fear, saying that no one can be saved? For it could have been done by others also, if they themselves had done anything. Then, since they themselves had done it, why was there fear, or whence was it taken up?
interpositisnonnullisrebusqueexnaturahum.la: Interpósitis nonnúllis rebus‚ quæ ex natúra humáni sensus sibi contrária sunt, ratiónem quærere cœléstis intelligéntiæ admonémur. Apóstoli dicunt, et sequi se Christum‚ et se ómnia reliquísse. Quómodo ígitur fiunt tristes‚ et quómodo métuunt dicéntes salvum esse néminem posse? Namque et ab áliis fíeri póterat, si quid fecíssent ipsi. Deínde cum fecíssent ipsi; quare metus vel unde suscéptus est?

addituretiaminresponsionedominihecapudho.en: It is added also in the Lord's answer: These things are impossible with men, possible with God. Were those things impossible with man which the Apostles also glory that they have done, and which the Lord acknowledgeth that they have done? This whole saying therefore is spiritual. But what is so possible to the power of God, as that he should save through faith; regenerate through water; conquer through the cross; adopt through the Gospels; quicken from death through the resurrection? Having heard these things, the Apostles quickly believe: and profess that they have left all things.
addituretiaminresponsionedominihecapudho.la: Additur étiam in responsióne Dómini‚ hæc apud hómines impossibília, possibília apud Deum. Nunquid apud hóminem impossibília erant quæ et Apóstoli fecísse se gloriántur : et fecísse eos Dóminus agnóscit! Omnis ítaque hic sermo est spirituális. Quid autem Dei virtúti tam possíbile est, quam ut per fidem salvet; ut per aquam regéneret; ut per crucem vincat; ut per Evangélia adóptet; ut per resurrectiónem ex morte vivíficet? Quibus audítis, Apóstoli cito credunt: seséque ómnia reliquísse profiténtur.

sedhanceorumobedientiamcitodominusremune.en: But the Lord quickly rewardeth this their obedience, resolving all the difficulty of the former question, when he saith: You who have followed me, in the regeneration shall judge the twelve tribes of Israel. For this is that regeneration which the Apostles followed, which the law could not grant, which joined them, upon twelve thrones for the judging of the twelve tribes of Israel, to the glory of the twelve Patriarchs.
sedhanceorumobedientiamcitodominusremune.la: Sed hanc eórum obediéntiam cito Dóminus remunerátur, omnem difficultátem superióris quæstiónis absólvens‚ cum dicit: Vos‚ qui secúti estis me, in regeneratióne judicábitis duódecim tribus Israël. Hæc enim illa regenerátio est, quam Apóstoli sunt secúti, quam lex indulgére non pótuit‚ quæ eos super duódecim thronos in judicándis duódecim tribubus Israël‚ in duódecim Patriarchárum glória copulávit.

beataprogeniesundemarianatest.en: Blessed offspring, of whom Mary was born.
beataprogeniesundemarianatest.la: Beáta progénies, unde María nata est.

deusquibeatumfamianumconfessoremtuumindi.en: O God, who didst make blessed Famianus thy Confessor conspicuous among the peoples of divers nations by the holiness of his works and the glory of his miracles: * grant us to be reformed for the better by his examples, § and to be protected amid adversities by his help. *
deusquibeatumfamianumconfessoremtuumindi.la: Deus, qui beátum Famiánum, Confessórem tuum, in divérsis natiónum pópulis óperum sanctitáte et miraculórum glória fecísti conspícuum: * da nobis, ut ejus in mélius reformémur exémplis, § et inter advérsa protegámur auxíliis. *

deusquibeatumguerricumabbatemdoctrinahum.en: O God, who didst adorn blessed Guerric the Abbot with learning, humility and constancy in adversity: * grant us, we beseech thee, so to follow his counsels and examples on earth, § that with him in heaven we may merit to put on eternal glory. *
deusquibeatumguerricumabbatemdoctrinahum.la: Deus, qui beátum Guerrícum Abbátem doctrína, humilitáte et in advérsis constántia decorásti: * praesta, quǽsumus, nobis sic ejus mónita et exémpla sectári in terris, § ut cum ipso in cœlis aetérnam indúere glóriam mereámur. *

trahemeposttecurremusinodoremunguentorum.en: Draw me: * we will run after thee to the odour of thy ointments.
trahemeposttecurremusinodoremunguentorum.la: Trahe me; * post te currémus in odórem unguentórum tuórum. Ps. 109

dilectusmeusloquiturmihisurgeproperaamic.en: My beloved * speaketh to me: Arise, make haste, my love.
dilectusmeusloquiturmihisurgeproperaamic.la: Diléctus meus * lóquitur mihi: Surge, própera, amíca mea. Ps. 112

fulcitemefloribusstipatememalisquiaamore.en: Stay me up with flowers, * compass me about with apples: because I languish with love.
fulcitemefloribusstipatememalisquiaamore.la: Fulcíte me flóribus, * stipáte me malis, quia amóre lángueo. Ps. 121

adiurovosfilieierusalemnesuscitetisdilec.en: I adjure you, * O daughters of Jerusalem, that you stir not up the beloved, till she herself please.
adiurovosfilieierusalemnesuscitetisdilec.la: Adjúro vos, * fíliæ Jerúsalem, ne suscitétis diléctam quoadúsque ipsa velit. Ps. 126

egodormietcormeumvigilat.en: I sleep, * and my heart watcheth.
egodormietcormeumvigilat.la: Ego dórmio, * et cor meum vígilat.

factumestcormeumtamquamceraliquescens.en: My heart is become * Like wax melting.
factumestcormeumtamquamceraliquescens.la: Factum est Cor meum * Tamquam cera liquéscens.

inmedioventrismei.en: In the midst of my bowels.

exultainomnicordefiliaierusalem.en: Rejoice with all thy heart, O daughter of Jerusalem.
exultainomnicordefiliaierusalem.la: Exúlta in omni corde, Fília Jerúsalem.

rexisreldominusinmediotui.en: The King of Israel, the Lord, is in the midst of thee.
rexisreldominusinmediotui.la: Rex Israël Dóminus in médio tui.

exsultavitcormeumindominetexaltatumestco.en: My heart hath rejoiced * in the Lord, and my horn is exalted in my God: because I have joyed in thy salvation.
exsultavitcormeumindominetexaltatumestco.la: Exsultávit * Cor meum in Dómino, et exaltátum est cornu meum in Deo meo, qui lætáta sum in salutári tuo.

deuscordismeietparsmeadeusineternum.en: God of my heart, * And God is my portion for ever.
deuscordismeietparsmeadeusineternum.la: Deus cordis mei, * Et pars mea Deus in ætérnum.

mihiadhereredeobonumest.en: It is good for me to adhere to God.

etparsmeadeusineternum.en: And God is my portion for ever.
etparsmeadeusineternum.la: Et pars mea Deus in ætérnum.

quimeinveneritinvenietvitam.en: He that shall find me, shall find life.

ethaurietsalutemadomino.en: And shall draw salvation from the Lord.

extollensvocemquedammulierdeturbadixitbe.en: Lifting up her voice, * a certain woman of the crowd said: Blessed is the womb that bore thee, and the paps that gave thee suck.
extollensvocemquedammulierdeturbadixitbe.la: Extóllens vocem * quædam múlier de turba, dixit: Beátus venter qui te portávit, et úbera quæ suxísti.

egexorealtissimiprodiviprimogenitaanteom.en: I came out of the mouth of the Most High, the firstborn before all creatures: § I made that in the heavens there should rise light that never faileth, * and as a cloud I covered all the earth.
egexorealtissimiprodiviprimogenitaanteom.la: Ego ex ore Altíssimi prodívi primogénita ante omnem creatúram, § ego feci in cœlis, ut orirétur lumen indefíciens, * et sicut nébula texi omnem terram.

inomniterrastetietinomnipopuletinomnibus.en: In every land have I stood, and in every people, § and in all these I sought rest, * and I shall abide in the inheritance of the Lord.
inomniterrastetietinomnipopuletinomnibus.la: In omni terra steti et in omni pópulo, § et in ómnibus réquiem quæsívi, * et in hereditáte Dómini morábor.

viammandatorumtuorumcucurri.en: I have run the way of thy commandments,

cumdilatasticormeum.en: When thou didst enlarge my heart.

exsultavitcormeumindeosalutarimeoquiafec.en: My heart hath rejoiced * in God my Saviour, because he that is mighty hath done great things to me.
exsultavitcormeumindeosalutarimeoquiafec.la: Exsultávit * Cor meum in Deo salutári meo, quia fecit mihi magna qui potens est.

danobisomnipotensdeusbeatiogleriiabbatis.en: Grant us, almighty God, § to follow the counsels and examples of blessed Oglerius the Abbot: * that we may be able to overcome the deceits of evil spirits, § and ever to abide in thy love. *
danobisomnipotensdeusbeatiogleriiabbatis.la: Da nobis, omnípotens Deus, § beáti Oglérii Abbátis mónita et exémpla sectári: * ut, malórum spirítuum fraudes víncere, § ac in tua semper valeámus dilectióne permanére. *

aiuventnosquesumusprecesetmeritasanctelu.en: May the prayers and merits of holy Ludmilla thy Martyr help us, we beseech thee, O Lord our God: * that, cleaving to her footsteps, we may be found steadfast in faith, § and effectual in holy works.
aiuventnosquesumusprecesetmeritasanctelu.la: Ajuvent nos, quæsumus, preces et mérita sanctæ Ludmíllæ Mártyris tuæ, Dómine Deus noster: * ut ejus vestígiis inhæréntes, in fide inveniámur stábiles, § et in sanctis opéribus efficáces.

inillotemporedixitiesusdiscipulissuissiq.en: At that time, Jesus said to his disciples: If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me. And so on.
inillotemporedixitiesusdiscipulissuissiq.la: In illo témpore: Dixit Jesus discípulis suis: Si quis vult veníre post me, ábneget semetípsum, et tollat crucem suam et sequátur me. Et réliqua.
