duobusmodiscruxtolliturautcumperabstinen.en: The cross is taken up in two ways: either when the body is afflicted by abstinence, or when the mind is afflicted by compassion for one's neighbour. Let us consider how Paul had taken up his cross in both ways, who said: I chastise my body, and bring it into subjection: lest perhaps, when I have preached to others, I myself should become a castaway.
duobusmodiscruxtolliturautcumperabstinen.la: Duóbus modis crux tóllitur, aut cum per abstinéntiam afflígitur corpus aut per compassiónem próximi afflígitur ánimus. Pensémus quáliter utróque modo Paulus crucem suam túlerat, qui dicébat: Castígo corpus meum, et in servitútem rédigo, ne forte prædicans áliis, ipse réprobus effíciar.

ecceinafflictionecorporisaudivimuscrucem.en: Behold, in the affliction of the body we have heard of the cross of the flesh; let us now hear, in compassion for the neighbour, of the cross of the mind. For he saith: Who is weak, and I am not weak? who is scandalized, and I am not on fire? For the perfect Preacher, that he might give an example of abstinence, bore the cross in his body: and because he drew upon himself the hurts of another's infirmity, he bore the cross in his heart.
ecceinafflictionecorporisaudivimuscrucem.la: Ecce, in afflictióne córporis audívimus crucem carnis, audiámus nunc in compassióne próximi crucem mentis; Ait enim: Quis infirmátur, et ego non infírmor? quis scandalizátur, et ego non uror? perféctus quippe Prædicátor, ut exémplum daret abstinéntiæ, crucem portábat in córpore: et quia trahébat in se damna infirmitátis aliénæ, crucem portábat in corde.

sedquiaipsisvirtutibusquedamvitiaiuxtasu.en: But because certain vices lie close beside the very virtues, we must say what vice besetteth abstinence of the flesh, and what besetteth compassion of the mind. For vainglory, from near at hand, sometimes besetteth abstinence of the flesh: because while thinness in the body, while paleness in the face is seen, the virtue laid open is praised, and it poureth itself out the more quickly, the more it goeth forth to human eyes through the paleness that is shown.
sedquiaipsisvirtutibusquedamvitiaiuxtasu.la: Sed quia ipsis virtútibus quædam vítia juxta sunt, dicéndum nobis est: quod vítium abstinéntiam carnis et quod obsídeat compassiónem mentis, e vicíno namque abstinéntiam carnis nonnúnquam vana glória óbsidet: quia dum tenúitas in córpore, dum palos in vultu respícitur, virtus patefácta laudátur, et tanto se celérius foras fundit, quanto ad humános óculos per osténsum palórem exit.

compassionemveroanimiplerumqueobsidetpie.en: But false pity often besetteth compassion of the mind: so that it sometimes draweth it on to condescend to vices: whereas no one ought to exercise compassion towards faults, but zeal: for compassion is due to the man, and rectitude to the vices, that in one and the same man we may love the good which was made, and pursue the evils which he hath done: lest, while we heedlessly remit faults, we seem no longer to suffer with him through charity, but to condescend through negligence.
compassionemveroanimiplerumqueobsidetpie.la: Compassiónem vero ánimi plerúmque óbsidet píetas falsa: ut hanc nonnúnquam ad condescéndendum vítiis pértrahat: cum ad culpas quisque non débeat compassiónem exercére, sed zelum: Compássio quippe hómini, et rectitúdo vítiis debétur, ut in uno eodémque hómine diligámus bonum, quod factum est, persequámur mala, quæ fecit: ne dum culpas incáute remíttimus, non jam per charitátem cómpati‚ sed per negligéntiam condescéndere videámur.

missusestgabrielangelusadmariamvirginemd.en: The Angel Gabriel was sent to Mary, a Virgin espoused to Joseph, bringing her the word: and the Virgin is affrighted at the light. Fear not, Mary, thou hast found grace with the Lord: behold, thou shalt conceive, and shalt bring forth,
missusestgabrielangelusadmariamvirginemd.la: Missus est Gábriel Angelus ad Maríam Vírginem desponsátam Joseph, núntians ei verbum: et expavéscit Virgo de lúmine. Ne tímeas, María, invenísti grátiam apud Dóminum: ecce concípies, et páries,

etvocabituraltissimifilius.en: And he shall be called the Son of the Most High.

dabiteidominusdeussedemdavidpatriseiuset.en: The Lord God shall give unto Him the throne of His father David, and He shall reign over the house of Jacob for ever.
dabiteidominusdeussedemdavidpatriseiuset.la: Dabit ei Dóminus Deus sedem David, patris ejus, et regnábit in domo Jacob in ætérnum.

hecdicitdominusdeusconvertiminiadmeetsal.en: Thus saith the Lord God: Be converted to me, and you shall be saved.
hecdicitdominusdeusconvertiminiadmeetsal.la: Hæc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.

iteetdiciteioannicecividentetsurdiaudiun.en: Go and tell John: The blind see and the deaf hear, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed.
iteetdiciteioannicecividentetsurdiaudiun.la: Ite, et dicíte Joánni: Cæci vident et surdi áudiunt: claudi ámbulantur, leprósi mundántur.

indieillavineamericantabitei.en: In that day there shall be singing to the vineyard of pure wine.
indieillavineamericantabitei.la: In die illa vínea meri cantábit ei.

indignationonestmihi.en: There is no indignation in me.

omnesenimmenserepletesuntvomitusordiumqu.en: For all the tables were full of vomit and filth, so that there was no more place.
omnesenimmenserepletesuntvomitusordiumqu.la: Omnes enim mensæ replétæ sunt vómitu sordiúmque, ita ut non esset ultra locus.

quemdocebitscientiametquemintelligerefac.en: Whom shall he teach knowledge? and whom shall he make to understand the hearing? them that are weaned from the milk, that are drawn away from the breasts.
quemdocebitscientiametquemintelligerefac.la: Quem docébit sciéntiam? et quem intellígere fáciet audítum? Ablactátos a lacte, avúlsos ab ubéribus.

quiamandaremandamandaremandexspectareexs.en: For command, command again; command, command again; expect, expect again; expect, expect again; a little there, a little there.
quiamandaremandamandaremandexspectareexs.la: Quia manda remánda, manda remánda, exspécta reexspécta, exspécta reexspécta, módicum ibi, módicum ibi.

inloquelenimlabiietlinguaalteraloquetura.en: For with the speech of lips, and with another tongue he will speak to this people.
inloquelenimlabiietlinguaalteraloquetura.la: In loquéla enim lábii, et lingua áltera loquétur ad pópulum istum.

cuidixithecestrequiesmeareficitelassumet.en: To whom he said: This is my rest, refresh the weary, and this is my refreshing: and they would not hear.
cuidixithecestrequiesmeareficitelassumet.la: Cui dixit: Hæc est réquies mea, refícite lassum: et hoc est meum refrigérium: et noluérunt audíre.

surgitevigilemusveniteadoremusquianescit.en: Arise, let us watch; come, let us adore: * For ye know not the hour when the Lord will come.
surgitevigilemusveniteadoremusquianescit.la: Súrgite vigilémus, veníte, adorémus: * Quia nescítis horam quando véniet Dóminus.

etaurestueaudientverbumposttergummonenti.en: And thy ears shall hear the word of one admonishing thee behind thy back: This is the way, walk ye in it: and go not aside neither to the right hand, nor to the left.
etaurestueaudientverbumposttergummonenti.la: Et aures tuæ áudient verbum post tergum monéntis: Hæc est via, ambuláte in ea, et non declinétis neque ad déxteram, neque ad sinístram.

etcontaminabislaminassculptiliumargentit.en: And thou shalt defile the plates of thy graven things of silver, and the garment of thy molten things of gold, and shalt cast them away as the uncleanness of a menstruous woman.
etcontaminabislaminassculptiliumargentit.la: Et contaminábis láminas sculptílium argénti tui, et vestiméntum conflátilis auri tui, et dispérges ea sicut immundítiam menstruátæ.

festinaquesumusdominenetardaverisetauxil.en: Make haste, we beseech thee, O Lord, tarry not: and bestow upon us the help of heavenly power; that they who trust in thy loving-kindness may be relieved by the consolations of thy coming:
festinaquesumusdominenetardaverisetauxil.la: Festína, quǽsumus, Dómine, ne tardáveris: et auxílium nobis supérnæ virtútis impénde; ut advéntus tui consolatiónibus sublevéntur, qui in tua pietáte confídunt:

quomodofietistudangeledeiquiaviruminconc.en: How shall this be, O Angel of God, since I have not known man in conceiving? Hear, O Mary, Virgin of Christ: the Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Most High shall overshadow thee.
quomodofietistudangeledeiquiaviruminconc.la: Quómodo fiet istud, Angele Dei, quia virum in concipiéndo non pértuli? Audi, María, Virgo Christi: Spíritus Sanctus supervéniet in te, et virtus Altíssimi obumbrábit tibi.

exsionspeciesdecoriseiusdeusnosterveniet.en: Out of Sion the loveliness of his beauty: our God shall come.
exsionspeciesdecoriseiusdeusnosterveniet.la: Ex Sion spécies decóris ejus: Deus noster véniet.

omnisvallisimplebituretomnismonsetcollis.en: Every valley shall be filled, and every mountain and hill shall be brought low: and all flesh shall see the salvation of God.
omnisvallisimplebituretomnismonsetcollis.la: Omnis vallis implébitur, et omnis mons et collis humiliábitur: et vidébit omnis caro salutáre Dei.

ecceiamvenitplenitudotemporisinquomisitd.en: Behold, now is come the fullness of the time, in which God sent his Son, born of a Virgin, made under the law: * Come, let us adore.
ecceiamvenitplenitudotemporisinquomisitd.la: Ecce jam venit plenitúdo témporis, in quo misit Deus Fílium suum natum de Vírgine, factum sub lege: * Veníte, adorémus.

quiimmolatbovemquasiquiinterficiatvirum.en: He that sacrificeth an ox, is as if he slew a man.
quiimmolatbovemquasiquiinterficiatvirum.la: Qui ímmolat bovem, quasi qui interfíciat virum.

sicstabitsemenvestrumetnomenvestrum.en: so shall your seed stand, and your name.
sicstabitsemenvestrumetnomenvestrum.la: sic stabit semen vestrum et nomen vestrum.

verbumcarofactumestethabitavitinnobiscui.en: The Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us: whose glory we saw, as it were of the Only-begotten of the Father,
verbumcarofactumestethabitavitinnobiscui.la: Verbum caro factum est, et habitávit in nobis: cujus glóriam vídimus, quasi Unigéniti a Patre,

letenturomnesquisperantintedomineinetern.en: Let all them be glad that hope in thee, O Lord: they shall rejoice for ever, and thou shalt dwell in them: and all they shall glory in thee
letenturomnesquisperantintedomineinetern.la: Læténtur omnes qui sperant in te, Dómine: in ætérnum exsultábunt, et habitábis in eis: et gloriabúntur in te omnes

domineinluminevultustuiambulabuntetinnom.en: They shall walk, O Lord, in the light of thy countenance; and in thy Name shall they rejoice all the day.
domineinluminevultustuiambulabuntetinnom.la: Dómine, in lúmine vultus tui ambulábunt, et in nómine tuo exsultábunt tota die.

estproculdubiointeroleumetnomensponsisim.en: Without doubt there is a likeness between oil and the name of the Bridegroom, nor did the Holy Ghost compare the one with the other idly. But I say it is in a certain threefold quality of oil, that it giveth light, it feedeth, and it anointeth, unless you have something better. From the Sermons of St. Bernard, Abbot (of Clairvaux)
estproculdubiointeroleumetnomensponsisim.la: Est procul dúbio inter óleum et nomen Sponsi similitúdo, nec otióse Spíritus Sanctus altérutrum comparávit. Ego autem dico in triplici quadam qualitáte ólei, quod lucet, pascit et ungit, si vos mélius non habétis. From the Sermons of St. Bernard, Abbot (of Clairvaux)

iesumregemangelorumsolavirgolactabatuber.en: Jesus, the King of Angels, the Virgin alone did suckle, with a breast filled from heaven.
iesumregemangelorumsolavirgolactabatuber.la: Jesum Regem Angelórum, sola Virgo lactábat úbere de cælo pleno.

sitnomendominibenedictum.en: Blessed be the Name of the Lord.

exhocnuncetusqueinseculum.en: From this time forth, and for evermore.
exhocnuncetusqueinseculum.la: Ex hoc nunc et usque in sǽculum.

descenditiesuscumparentibusetvenitnazare.en: Jesus went down with his parents, and came to Nazareth: and was subject to them. And his Mother kept all these words in her heart.
descenditiesuscumparentibusetvenitnazare.la: Descéndit Jesus cum paréntibus, et venit Názareth: et erat súbditus illis. Et Mater ejus conservábat ómnia verba hæc in corde suo.

honorapatremtuumetmatremtuamsicprecepera.en: Honour thy father and thy mother: thus had the Lord God commanded in the Law of Moses, and so in his Son hath he given us an example.
honorapatremtuumetmatremtuamsicprecepera.la: Honóra patrem tuum et matrem tuam: sic præcéperat Dóminus Deus in Lege Móysi, et ita in Fílio suo exémplum nobis præbuit.

eccetestempopulisdedieum.en: Behold, I have given him for a witness to the people,

ducemacpraceptoremgentibus.en: For a leader and a master to the Gentiles.

alleluiaomnesdesabavenientalleluiaaurume.en: Alleluia. All they from Saba shall come, alleluia: bringing gold and frankincense, alleluia, alleluia.
alleluiaomnesdesabavenientalleluiaaurume.la: Allelúja. Omnes de Saba vénient, allelúja: aurum et thus deferéntes, allelúja, allelúja.

speraindominetfacbonitatemetinhabitaterr.en: Trust in the Lord, and do good: and dwell in the land, and thou shalt be fed with the riches thereof.
speraindominetfacbonitatemetinhabitaterr.la: Spera in Dómino, et fac bonitátem: et inhábita terram, et pascéris in divítiis ejus.

exspectansexspectavidominumetrespexitme.en: With expectation I have waited for the Lord, and he had regard to me.
exspectansexspectavidominumetrespexitme.la: Exspéctans exspectávi Dóminum, et respéxit me.

misereremeiquoniaminteconfiditanimamea.en: Have mercy on me, for my soul trusteth in thee.
misereremeiquoniaminteconfiditanimamea.la: Miserére mei, quóniam in te confídit ánima mea.

deusintesperavidominenonconfundarinetern.en: In thee, O God, have I hoped, O Lord, let me never be confounded: in thy justice
deusintesperavidominenonconfundarinetern.la: Deus, in te sperávi, Dómine, non confúndar in ætérnum: in tua justítia

deusneelongerisamedeusmeusinauxiliummeum.en: O God, be not thou far from me: O my God, look towards my help.
deusneelongerisamedeusmeusinauxiliummeum.la: Deus, ne elongéris a me: Deus meus, in auxílium meum réspice.

eteripuistianimammeamexinfernoinferiori.en: And Thou hast delivered my soul from the lowest hell.
eteripuistianimammeamexinfernoinferiori.la: Et eripuísti ánimam meam ex inférno inferióri.

deusiniquiinsurrexeruntmeetfortesquesier.en: O God, the wicked are risen up against me, and the mighty have sought after my soul.
deusiniquiinsurrexeruntmeetfortesquesier.la: Deus, iníqui insurrexérunt me, et fortes quæsiérunt ánimam meam.

deepistolaprimaadcorinthios.en: Lesson from the first letter of St. Paul the Apostle to the Corinthians

escaautemnosnoncommendatdeo.en: But meat doth not commend us to God.
escaautemnosnoncommendatdeo.la: Esca autem nos non comméndat Deo.

omnisautemquiinagonecontenditabomnibusse.en: And every one that striveth for the mastery, refraineth himself from all things: and they indeed that they may receive a corruptible crown; but we an incorruptible one.
omnisautemquiinagonecontenditabomnibusse.la: Omnis autem qui in agóne conténdit, ab ómnibus se ábstinet, et illi quidem ut corruptíbilem corónam accípiant: nos autem incorrúptam.

anemulamurdominumnumquidfortioresillosum.en: Do we provoke the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than he?
anemulamurdominumnumquidfortioresillosum.la: An æmulámur Dóminum? numquid fortióres illo sumus?

omniamihilicentsednonomniexpediunt.en: All things are lawful for me, but all things are not expedient.
omniamihilicentsednonomniexpediunt.la: Omnia mihi licent, sed non ómnia expédiunt.

hecautemomniaoperaturunusatqueidemspirit.en: But all these things one and the same Spirit worketh, dividing to every one according as he will.
hecautemomniaoperaturunusatqueidemspirit.la: Hæc autem ómnia operátur unus atque idem Spíritus, dívidens síngulis prout vult.

sicutenimcorpusunumestetmembrahabetmulta.en: For as the body is one, and hath many members; and all the members of the body, whereas they are many, yet are one body: so also is Christ.
sicutenimcorpusunumestetmembrahabetmulta.la: Sicut enim corpus unum est, et membra habet multa, ómnia autem membra córporis cum sint multa, unum tamen corpus sunt: ita et Christus.

eteniminunospirituomnesnosinunumcorpusba.en: For in one Spirit were we all baptized into one body, whether Jews or Gentiles, whether bond or free: and in one Spirit we have all been made to drink.
eteniminunospirituomnesnosinunumcorpusba.la: Etenim in uno Spíritu omnes nos in unum corpus baptizáti sumus, sive Judǽi, sive gentíles, sive servi, sive líberi: et omnes in uno Spíritu potáti sumus.

nametcorpusnonestunummembrumsedmulta.en: For the body also is not one member, but many.
nametcorpusnonestunummembrumsedmulta.la: Nam et corpus non est unum membrum, sed multa.

sidixeritpesquoniamnonsummanusnonsumdeco.en: If the foot should say: Because I am not the hand, I am not of the body: is it therefore not of the body?
sidixeritpesquoniamnonsummanusnonsumdeco.la: Si díxerit pes: Quóniam non sum manus, non sum de córpore: num ídeo non est de córpore?

deepistolasecundaadcorinthios.en: Lesson from the second letter of St. Paul the Apostle to the Corinthians

deepistolaadgalatas.en: Lesson from the letter of St. Paul the Apostle to the Galatians

itaqueiamnonestservussedfiliusquodsifili.en: Therefore now he is not a servant, but a son. And if a son, an heir also through God.
itaqueiamnonestservussedfiliusquodsifili.la: Itaque jam non est servus, sed fílius: quod si fílius, et hæres per Deum.

dicoautemspirituambulateetdesideriacarni.en: I say then, walk in the spirit, and you shall not fulfil the lusts of the flesh.
dicoautemspirituambulateetdesideriacarni.la: Dico autem: Spíritu ambuláte, et desidéria carnis non perficiétis.

carenimconcupiscitadversusspiritumspirit.en: For the flesh lusteth against the spirit: and the spirit against the flesh; for these are contrary one to another: so that you do not the things that you would.
carenimconcupiscitadversusspiritumspirit.la: Caro enim concupíscit advérsus spíritum, spíritus autem advérsus carnem: hæc enim sibi ínvicem adversántur, ut non quæcúmque vultis, illa faciátis.

sispirituvivimusspirituetambulemus.en: If we live in the Spirit, let us also walk in the Spirit.
sispirituvivimusspirituetambulemus.la: Si spíritu vívimus, spíritu et ambulémus.

nonefficiamurinanisgloriecupidiinvicempr.en: Let us not be made desirous of vain glory, provoking one another, envying one another.
nonefficiamurinanisgloriecupidiinvicempr.la: Non efficiámur inánis glóriæ cúpidi, ínvicem provocántes, ínvicem invidéntes.

deepistolaadephesios.en: Lesson from the letter of St. Paul the Apostle to the Ephesians

quisuamuxoremdiligitseipsumdiligit.en: He that loveth his wife loveth himself.
quisuamuxoremdiligitseipsumdiligit.la: Qui suam uxórem díligit, seípsum díligit.

proptereaaccipitearmaturamdeiutpossitisr.en: Therefore take unto you the armour of God, that you may be able to resist in the evil day, and to stand in all things perfect.
proptereaaccipitearmaturamdeiutpossitisr.la: Proptérea accípite armatúram Dei, ut possítis resístere in die malo, et in ómnibus perfécti stare.

deepistolaadphilippenses.en: Lesson from the letter of St. Paul the Apostle to the Philippians

quamquamegohabeamconfidentiametincarne.en: though I might also have confidence in the flesh.
quamquamegohabeamconfidentiametincarne.la: quamquam ego hábeam confidéntiam et in carne.

siquisaliusvideturconfidereincarneegomag.en: If any other thinketh he may have confidence in the flesh, I more,
siquisaliusvideturconfidereincarneegomag.la: Si quis álius vidétur confídere in carne, ego magis,

nostraautemconversatioincelisest.en: But our conversation is in heaven.
nostraautemconversatioincelisest.la: Nostra autem conversátio in cælis est.

itaquefratresmeicarissimietdesideratissi.en: Therefore, my dearly beloved brethren, and most desired, my joy and my crown; so stand fast in the Lord, my dearly beloved.
itaquefratresmeicarissimietdesideratissi.la: Itaque fratres mei caríssimi, et desideratíssimi, gáudium meum, et coróna mea: sic state in Dómino, caríssimi.

spesmeadomine.en: Thou art my hope, O Lord,

inteconfirmatussumexuterodeventrematrism.en: By thee have I been confirmed from the womb: from my mother's womb thou art my protector.
inteconfirmatussumexuterodeventrematrism.la: In te confirmátus sum ex útero: de ventre matris meæ tu es meus protéctor.

estonobisdomine.en: Be thou unto us, O Lord,

afacieinimici.en: Against the face of the enemy.

estonobisdomineturrisfortitudinis.en: Be thou unto us, O Lord, * A tower of strength.

educdecarcereanimammeam.en: Bring my soul out of prison,

utconfiteaturnominituodomine.en: That it may praise thy name, O Lord.

periitfugaameetnonestquirequiratanimamme.en: Flight hath failed me, and there is no one that hath regard to my soul.
periitfugaameetnonestquirequiratanimamme.la: Périit fuga a me, et non est qui requírat ánimam meam.

eruntpriminovissimietnovissimiprimimulti.en: The first shall be last, and the last first: for many are called, but few chosen, saith the Lord.
eruntpriminovissimietnovissimiprimimulti.la: Erunt primi novíssimi, et novíssimi primi: multi enim sunt vocáti, pauci vero elécti, dicit Dóminus.

benedicensergoillineaitnequaquamultramal.en: Blessing him therefore, Noe said: I will no more curse the earth for the sake of man:
benedicensergoillineaitnequaquamultramal.la: Benedícens ergo illi, Noë ait: Nequáquam ultra maledícam terræ propter hóminem:

adimaginemquippedeifactusesthomo.en: For man was made to the image of God.
adimaginemquippedeifactusesthomo.la: Ad imáginem quippe Dei factus est homo.

hoceritsignumfederisintermeetinterterram.en: This shall be the sign of the covenant between me and the earth: I will set my bow in the clouds of heaven.
hoceritsignumfederisintermeetinterterram.la: Hoc erit signum fœ́deris inter me et inter terram: arcum meum ponam in núbibus cæli.

neauteminvenitgratiamantedominum.en: But Noe found grace before the Lord.
neauteminvenitgratiamantedominum.la: Noë autem invénit grátiam ante Dóminum.

delibrogenesis.en: Lesson from the book of Genesis

fecitergoneomniaquemandaverateidominus.en: And Noe did all things which the Lord had commanded him.
fecitergoneomniaquemandaverateidominus.la: Fecit ergo Noë ómnia quæ mandáverat ei Dóminus.

ingressesuntadneinarcam.en: went in to Noe into the ark.
ingressesuntadneinarcam.la: ingréssæ sunt ad Noë in arcam.

factumqueestdiluviumquadragintadiebussup.en: And the flood was forty days upon the earth, and the waters increased, and lifted up the ark on high from earth.
factumqueestdiluviumquadragintadiebussup.la: Factúmque est dilúvium quadragínta diébus super terram: et multiplicátæ sunt aquæ, et elevavérunt arcam in sublíme a terra.

volensnesciresiiamcessassentaqueemisitco.en: Noe, wishing to know whether the waters had now ceased, sent forth a dove: which, bearing in her mouth a bough of green olive,
volensnesciresiiamcessassentaqueemisitco.la: Volens Noë scire si jam cessássent aquæ, emísit colúmbam: quæ ramum viréntis olivæ in ore suo déferens,

deferensautemsignumclementiedeicolumbain.en: And the dove bore in her mouth a sign of the clemency of God.
deferensautemsignumclementiedeicolumbain.la: Déferens autem signum cleméntiæ Dei colúmba in ore suo.

eritarcusmeusinnubibusetvideboillumetrec.en: My bow shall be in the clouds, and I shall see it, and shall remember my everlasting covenant.
eritarcusmeusinnubibusetvideboillumetrec.la: Erit arcus meus in núbibus, et vidébo illum, et recordábor fœ́deris mei sempitérni.

etaperiensnetectumarceaspexitviditquequo.en: And Noe opening the covering of the ark, looked, and saw that the face of the earth was dried.
etaperiensnetectumarceaspexitviditquequo.la: Et apériens Noë tectum arcæ, aspéxit, vidítque quod exsiccáta esset superfícies terræ.

quodautemceciditinterrambonamhisuntquiin.en: But that which fell * upon good ground: these are they who in a good and very good heart keep the word, and bring forth fruit in patience.
quodautemceciditinterrambonamhisuntquiin.la: Quod autem cécidit * in terram bonam: hi sunt, qui in corde bono et óptimo verbum rétinent, et fructum áfferunt in patiéntia.

benedicensbenedicamtibietmultiplicabote.en: Blessing I will bless thee, and I will multiply thee.
benedicensbenedicamtibietmultiplicabote.la: Benedícens benedícam tibi, et multiplicábo te.

dixitautemdominusadabramegosumetpactumme.en: And the Lord said to Abram: I am, and my covenant is with thee: let every male among you be sanctified:
dixitautemdominusadabramegosumetpactumme.la: Dixit autem Dóminus ad Abram: Ego sum, et pactum meum tecum: sanctificétur in vobis omne masculínum:

eteritsignumintermeetsementuum.en: And it shall be a sign between me and thy seed.
eteritsignumintermeetsementuum.la: Et erit signum inter me et semen tuum.

extenamqueegredieturinquoomnesgentesbene.en: For out of thee shall he come forth, in whom all nations shall be blessed.
extenamqueegredieturinquoomnesgentesbene.la: Ex te namque egrediétur, in quo omnes gentes benedicéntur.

inmatutinisdominemeditaborintequiafactus.en: In the morning, O Lord, I will meditate on thee, for thou hast been my helper.
inmatutinisdominemeditaborintequiafactus.la: In matutinis, Dómine, meditábor in te, quia factus adjútor meus.

benedicamuspatremetfiliuminseculacumsanc.en: Let us bless the Father and the Son, with the Holy Ghost, for ever.
benedicamuspatremetfiliuminseculacumsanc.la: Benedicámus Patrem et Fílium in sǽcula cum Sancto Spíritu.

revertentiabramacedequatuorregumoccurrit.en: As Abram was returning from the slaughter of the four kings, Melchisedech the king of Salem came to meet him, offering bread and wine, for he was the priest of God:
revertentiabramacedequatuorregumoccurrit.la: Reverténti Abram a cæde quátuor regum, occurrit rex Salem Melchísedech, ófferens panem et vinum, erat enim Dei sacerdos:

benedictusabramdeoaltissimoquicreavitcel.en: Blessed be Abram by the most high God, who created heaven and earth.
benedictusabramdeoaltissimoquicreavitcel.la: Benedíctus Abram Deo altíssimo, qui creávit cælum et terram.

clamorinquitdominussodomorumetgomorrheve.en: The cry, saith the Lord, of Sodom and Gomorrha is come unto me:
clamorinquitdominussodomorumetgomorrheve.la: Clamor, inquit Dóminus, Sodomórum et Gomórrhæ venit ad me:

descendametvideboutrumclamoremoperecompl.en: I will go down, and see whether they have done according to the cry.
descendametvideboutrumclamoremoperecompl.la: Descéndam, et vidébo utrum clamórem ópere compléverint.

abrahamstabatcoramdeetaitabsitatedoinine.en: Abraham stood before God, and said: Far be it from thee, O Lord, to destroy the just with the wicked.
abrahamstabatcoramdeetaitabsitatedoinine.la: Abraham stabat coram Deo, et ait: Absit a te, Dóinine, ut perdas justum cum impiis.

generationeautemquartarevertenturhuc.en: But in the fourth generation they shall return hither.

ascendensergodeusababrahampluitignemetsu.en: God therefore going up from Abraham, rained fire and brimstone upon Sodom:
ascendensergodeusababrahampluitignemetsu.la: Ascéndens ergo Deus ab Abraham, pluit ignem et sulphur super Sódomam:

abrahammaneconsurgensstetiteteversasurbe.en: Abraham rising early in the morning stood, and beheld from afar the cities overthrown.
abrahammaneconsurgensstetiteteversasurbe.la: Abraham mane consúrgens stetit, et evérsas urbes a longe conspéxit.

recordatusestdeusabrahametliberavitlotde.en: God remembered Abraham, and delivered Lot from the overthrow of Sodom.
recordatusestdeusabrahametliberavitlotde.la: Recordátus est Deus Abraham, et liberávit Lot de subversióne Sódomæ.

quianonnullorumestconsuetudocarissimiadv.en: Because it is the custom of some, dearly beloved, to anticipate the approaching days of Lent with a more devout fasting, the present lesson of the Gospel hath of necessity been read, in which our Lord, the rewarder of spiritual virtues, hath given us a holy and perfect rule of fasting, saying: When you fast, be not as the hypocrites, sad: for they disfigure their faces, that they may appear unto men to fast. For whosoever by the display of his fasting seeketh human glory, fasteth not to God, but to men.
quianonnullorumestconsuetudocarissimiadv.la: Quia nonnullórum est consuetúdo, carissimi, adveniéntes Quadragésimæ dies devotióre jeiúnio præveníre, necessário præsens Evangélii decúrsa est léctio, in qua Dóminus noster, virtútum spirituálium retribútor, sanctam nobis perfectámque dedit régulam jejunándi, dicens: Cum jejunátis, non éritis sicut hypócritæ tristes: extérminant enim fácies suas, ut appareant homínibus jejunáre. Non enim Deo jeiúnat, sed homínibus, quicúmque ostentatióne jeiúnii sui glóriam requirit humánam.

exterminantautemfaciessuasquimeroresimul.en: And they disfigure their faces who, feigning sorrow, counterfeit a religious countenance before the eyes of the people. For the Master of heavenly discipline willeth not that that be done irreligiously which is commanded to be done for religion: nor doth he suffer the labour of them that call upon him, for whom he prepareth an eternal reward, to perish by the vice of fruitless boasting. Be not, he saith, as the hypocrites, sad. For if thou art truly sorrowful and sad because thou fastest, thou wilt keep for thyself no favour with God, as one ungrateful: because, although thou doest a good work, yet by the perverseness of a degenerate mind thou workest it unwillingly.
exterminantautemfaciessuasquimeroresimul.la: Exterminant autem fácies suas qui, mæróre simuláto, religiósum vultum populórum óculis mentiúntur. Non vult enim disciplinæ cæléstis Magister irreligióse agi quod fieri pro religióne præcipitur: nec pátitur invocántium se labórem, quibus ætérnam parat mercédem, infructuósæ jactántiæ vitio deperire. Non éritis, inquit, sicut hypócritæ tristes. Si enim vere mæstus et tristis es quia jeiúnas, nullam tibi ut ingrátus apud Deum grátiam reservábis: quia, quamvis opus fácias bonum, pravitáte tamen degéneris ánimi invitus operáris.

sisanctitatisimaginadamprostitiamsimulas.en: If thou feignest sadness for an image of holiness, as a displayer of thy service thou losest all the fruit of the divine promise. But if thou offerest thy fasting to God, why, as a follower of vainglory, dost thou display it to men who live in the same condition as thyself? Following this judgement the Apostle said: Be not desirous of vain glory. For that is empty and vain, whatsoever standeth on the firmness of no weight or virtue. That is empty, which, failing with the passing world, passeth not to eternal life.
sisanctitatisimaginadamprostitiamsimulas.la: Si sanctitatis imaginadam pro stítiam símulas, omnem fructum promissiónis divínæ, obséquii tui ostentátor, amittis. Quod si Deo jeiúnium tuum defers, cur illud hominibus pari tecum conditióne vivéntibus, vanæ glóriæ sectátor, osténtas? Hanc Apóstolus secútus senténtiam dicébat: Nolíte fieri inánis glóriæ cúpidi. Ináne est enim et vanum, quidquid nullius pónderis aut virtútis firmitate consístit. Ináne est, quod cum sæculo prætereúnte deficiens, ad vitam non transit ætérnam.

canitetubainsionsanctificateieiuniumvoca.en: Blow the trumpet in Sion, sanctify a fast, call a solemn assembly,
canitetubainsionsanctificateieiuniumvoca.la: Cánite tuba in Sion, sanctificáte jeiúnium, vocáte cœtum,

congregatepopulumsanctificateecclesiamco.en: gather together the people, sanctify the church, assemble the ancients, gather together the little ones, and them that suck at the breasts: let the bridegroom go forth from his bed, and the bride out of her bride chamber.
congregatepopulumsanctificateecclesiamco.la: congregáte pópulum, sanctificáte ecclésiam, coadunáte senes, congregáte párvulos, et sugéntes úbera: egrediátur sponsus de cubíli suo, et sponsa de thálamo suo.

intervestibulumetaltareplorabuntsacerdot.en: Between the porch and the altar the priests, the Lord's ministers, shall weep, and shall say: Spare, O Lord, spare thy people: and give not thy inheritance to reproach, that the heathens should rule over them. Why should they say among the nations: Where is their God?
intervestibulumetaltareplorabuntsacerdot.la: Inter vestíbulum et altáre plorábunt sacerdótes, minístri Dómini, et dicent: Parce Dómine, parce pópulo tuo: et ne des hereditátem tuam in oppróbrium, ut dominéntur eis natiónes. Quare dicunt in pópulis: Ubi est Deus eórum?

zelatusestdominusterramsuametpepercitpop.en: The Lord hath been zealous for his land, and hath spared his people.
zelatusestdominusterramsuametpepercitpop.la: Zelátus est Dóminus terram suam, et pepércit pópulo suo.

noliteieiunaresicutusqueadhancdiemutaudi.en: Do not fast as you have done until this day, to make your cry to be heard on high.
noliteieiunaresicutusqueadhancdiemutaudi.la: Nolíte jejunáre sicut usque ad hanc diem, ut audiátur in excélso clamor vester.

frangeesurientipanemtuumetegenosvagosque.en: Deal thy bread to the hungry, and bring the needy and the harbourless into thy house: when thou shalt see one naked, cover him, and despise not thy own flesh.
frangeesurientipanemtuumetegenosvagosque.la: Frange esuriénti panem tuum, et egénos vagósque induc in domum tuam: cum víderis nudum, óperi eum, et carnem tuam ne despéxeris.

tuncerumpetquasimanelumentuumetsanitastu.en: Then shall thy light break forth as the morning, and thy health shall speedily arise.
tuncerumpetquasimanelumentuumetsanitastu.la: Tunc erúmpet quasi mane lumen tuum, et sánitas tua cítius oriétur.

ductusestiesusindesertumaspirituuttentar.en: Jesus was led into the desert by the Spirit, to be tempted by the devil:
ductusestiesusindesertumaspirituuttentar.la: Ductus est Jesus in desértum a Spíritu, ut tentarétur a diábolo:

etaccedenstentatordixiteisifiliusdeiesdi.en: And the tempter coming said to him: If thou be the Son of God, command that these stones be made bread.
etaccedenstentatordixiteisifiliusdeiesdi.la: Et accédens tentátor dixit ei: Si Filius Dei es, dic ut lápides isti panes fiant.

etcumieiunassetquadragintadiebusetquadra.en: And when he had fasted forty days and forty nights, afterwards he was hungry.
etcumieiunassetquadragintadiebusetquadra.la: Et, cum jejunásset quadragínta diébus et quadragínta nóctibus, póstea esúriit.

sifiliusdeiesdicutlapidesistipanesfiant.en: If thou be the Son of God, command that these stones be made bread.
sifiliusdeiesdicutlapidesistipanesfiant.la: Si Filius Dei es, dic ut lápides isti panes fiant.

inomnibusexhibeamusnosmetipsossicutdeimi.en: In all things let us exhibit ourselves as the ministers of God, in much patience, in many fastings, by the armour of justice.
inomnibusexhibeamusnosmetipsossicutdeimi.la: In ómnibus exhibeámus nosmetípsos sicut Dei minístros, in multa patiéntia, in jejúniis multis, per arma justítiæ.

quisigiturilleestquidudumcaptamvenatione.en: Who then is he that a while ago brought me venison that he took, and I ate of all before thou camest?
quisigiturilleestquidudumcaptamvenatione.la: Quis igitur ille est qui dudum captam venatiónem áttulit mihi, et comédi ex ómnibus priúsquam tu venires?

benedixiqueeieteritbenedictus.en: And I blessed him, and he shall be blessed.

dominumtuumillumconstituietomnesfratrese.en: I have appointed him thy lord, and have made all his brethren his servants.
dominumtuumillumconstituietomnesfratrese.la: Dóminum tuum illum constítui, et omnes fratres eius servitúti illíus subiugávi.

nequaquamvocaberisiacobsedisreleritnomen.en: Thou shalt not be called Jacob, but Israel shall be thy name.
nequaquamvocaberisiacobsedisreleritnomen.la: Nequáquam vocáberis Jacob, sed Israël erit nomen tuum.

paterabrahammisereremeietmittelazarumuti.en: Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water, to cool my tongue.
paterabrahammisereremeietmittelazarumuti.la: Pater Abraham, miserére mei, et mitte Lázarum ut intíngat extrémum dígiti sui in aquam, ut refrigeret linguam meam.

loquensiosephfratribussuisdixit.en: Joseph, speaking to his brethren, said:

paxvobisnolitetimereprosaluteenimvestram.en: Peace be to you, fear not: For God sent me before you for your preservation.
paxvobisnolitetimereprosaluteenimvestram.la: Pax vobis, nolite timére: Pro salúte enim vestra misit me Dóminus ante vos.

elevavitquevocemcumfletuquamaudieruntegy.en: And he lifted up his voice with weeping, which the Egyptians and all the house of Pharao heard. And he said to his brethren:
elevavitquevocemcumfletuquamaudieruntegy.la: Elevavítque vocem cum fletu, quam audiérunt Ægypti omnísque domus Pharaónis. Et dixit frátribus suis.

prosaluteenimvestramisitmedominusantevos.en: For God sent me before you for your preservation.
prosaluteenimvestramisitmedominusantevos.la: Pro salúte enim vestra misit me Dóminus ante vos.

congregatisautemcunctisliberiseiusutdeli.en: And when all his children were gathered together to comfort their father in his sorrow, he would not hear them, but said:
congregatisautemcunctisliberiseiusutdeli.la: Congregátis autem cunctis líberis ejus ut delinírent dolórem patris, nóluit eos audíre, sed dixit.

loquensiosephfratribussuisdixitpaxvobisn.en: Joseph, speaking to his brethren, said: * Peace be to you, fear not: For God sent me before you for your preservation.
loquensiosephfratribussuisdixitpaxvobisn.la: Loquens Ioseph frátribus suis dixit: * Pax vobis, nolite timére: Pro salúte enim vestra misit me Dóminus ante vos.

divertitaboneribusdorsumeius.en: He removed his back from the burdens.

concedequesumusomnipotensdeusutieiunioru.en: Grant, we beseech thee, almighty God: that the holy devotion of fasting may both bestow on us purification, and render us acceptable to thy majesty.
concedequesumusomnipotensdeusutieiunioru.la: Concéde, quæsumus, omnipotens Deus: ut jejuniórum nobis sancta devótio et purificatiónem tribuat, et maiestáti tuæ nos reddat accéptos.

veriadoratoresadorabuntpatreminspirituet.en: The true adorers shall adore the Father in spirit and in truth.
veriadoratoresadorabuntpatreminspirituet.la: Veri adoratóres adorábunt Patrem in spíritu et veritáte.

locutusestdominusadmoysendicensdescendei.en: The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Go down into Egypt, and tell Pharao to let my people go: Pharao's heart is hardened: he will not let my people go, unless
locutusestdominusadmoysendicensdescendei.la: Locútus est Dóminus ad Móysen, dicens: Descénde in Ægýptum, et dic Pharaóni ut dimíttat pópulum meum: indurátum est cor Pharaónis: non vult dimíttere pópulum meum, nisi

vidensvidiafflictionempopulimeiinegyptet.en: I have seen the affliction of my people in Egypt, and I have heard their groaning, and am come down to deliver them.
vidensvidiafflictionempopulimeiinegyptet.la: Videns vidi afflictiónem pópuli mei in Ægypto, et gémitum eórum audívi, et descéndi liberáre eum.

abiitiesustransmaregalileequodesttiberia.en: Jesus went over the sea of Galilee, which is that of Tiberias: and a great multitude followed him, because they saw the miracles which he did on them that were diseased. Jesus therefore went up into a mountain, and there he sat with his disciples. Now the pasch, the festival day of the Jews, was near at hand.
abiitiesustransmaregalileequodesttiberia.la: Abiit Jesus trans mare Galilǽæ, quod est Tiberíadis: et sequebátur eum multitúdo magna, quia vidébant signa, quæ faciébat super his qui infirmabántur. Súbiit ergo in montem Jesus et ibi sedébat cum discípulis suis. Erat autem próximum Pascha dies festus Judæórum.

accessitiesusettetigitloculumhiautemquip.en: Jesus came near, * and touched the bier. And they that carried it stood still. And he said: Young man, I say to thee, arise. And he that was dead sat up, and began to speak.
accessitiesusettetigitloculumhiautemquip.la: Accéssit Jesus, * et tétigit lóculum. Hi autem qui portábant, stetérunt. Et ait: Adoléscens, tibi dico, surge. Et resédit qui erat mórtuus, et cœpit loqui.

quisexvobisarguetmedepeccatosiveritatemd.en: Which of you shall convince me of sin? If I say the truth to you, why do you not believe me? He that is of God, heareth the words of God: therefore you hear them not, because you are not of God.
quisexvobisarguetmedepeccatosiveritatemd.la: Quis ex vobis árguet me de peccáto? Si veritátem dico vobis, quare non créditis mihi? Qui ex Deo est, verba Dei audit: proptérea vos non audítis, quia ex Deo non estis.

deusdeusmeusrespiceinme.en: O God, my God, look upon me.
deusdeusmeusrespiceinme.la: Deus, Deus meus, réspice in me.

etquiinquirebantmalamihilocutisuntvanita.en: And they that sought evils to me spoke vain things, and studied deceits all the day long.
etquiinquirebantmalamihilocutisuntvanita.la: Et qui inquirébant mala mihi, locúti sunt vanitátes: et dolos tota die meditabántur.

memoriacompassionisbeatemarievirginis.en: Commemoration of the Compassion of the Blessed Virgin Mary

eccepositusesthicinsignumcuicontradicetu.en: Behold, this child is set for a sign which shall be contradicted: and thy own soul a sword shall pierce, that out of many hearts thoughts may be revealed.
eccepositusesthicinsignumcuicontradicetu.la: Ecce pósitus est hic in signum cui contradicétur: et tuam ipsíus ánimam pertransíbit gládius, ut reveléntur ex multis córdibus cogitatiónes.

mariavirgopervirtutemtotdolorum.en: O Virgin Mary, by the power of so many sorrows,
mariavirgopervirtutemtotdolorum.la: María Virgo, per virtútem tot dolórum.

facnosgaudereinregnocelorum.en: Make us to rejoice in the kingdom of heaven.
facnosgaudereinregnocelorum.la: Fac nos gaudére in regno cælórum.

interveniatpronobisquesumusdomineiesuchr.en: Let the Blessed Virgin Mary, thy Mother, intercede for us, we beseech thee, O Lord Jesus Christ, now and at the hour of our death, before thy clemency: whose most sacred soul in the hour of thy blessed passion the sword of sorrow pierced, and in thy glorious resurrection exceeding great joy made glad.
interveniatpronobisquesumusdomineiesuchr.la: Intervéniat pro nobis, quǽsumus, Dómine, Jesu Christe, nunc et in hora mortis nostræ apud tuam cleméntiam beáta Virgo María mater tua: cujus sacratíssimam ánimam in hora benedíctæ passiónis tuæ dolóris gládius pertransívit, et in gloriósa resurrectióne tua ingens gáudium lætificávit.

desideriodesideravihocpaschamanducarevob.en: With desire I have desired * to eat this Passover with you before I suffer.
desideriodesideravihocpaschamanducarevob.la: Desidério desiderávi * hoc Pascha manducáre vobíscum, ántequam pátiar.

usquequolugebitterretherbaomnisregioniss.en: How long shall the land mourn, and the herb of every field wither for the wickedness of them that dwell therein? The beasts and the birds are consumed: because they have said: He shall not see our last end.
usquequolugebitterretherbaomnisregioniss.la: Usquequo lugébit terra, et herba omnis regiónis siccábitur, propter malítiam habitántium in ea? consúmptum est ánimal et vólucre, quóniam dixérunt: Non vidébit novíssima nostra.

factestmihihereditasmeaquasileoinsilvade.en: My inheritance is become to me as a lion in the wood: it hath cried out against me, therefore have I hated it.
factestmihihereditasmeaquasileoinsilvade.la: Facta est mihi heréditas mea quasi leo in silva: dedit contra me vocem, ídeo odívi eam.

numquidavisdiscolorhereditasmeamihinumqu.en: Is my inheritance to me as a speckled bird? Is it as a bird dyed throughout? come ye, assemble yourselves, all the beasts of the earth, make haste to devour.
numquidavisdiscolorhereditasmeamihinumqu.la: Numquid avis díscolor heréditas mea mihi? numquid avis tincta per totum? Veníte, congregámini omnes béstiæ terræ, properáte ad devorándum.

pastoresmultidemolitisuntvineammeamconcu.en: Many pastors have destroyed my vineyard, they have trodden my portion under foot: they have changed my delightful portion into a desolate wilderness.
pastoresmultidemolitisuntvineammeamconcu.la: Pastóres multi demolíti sunt víneam meam, conculcavérunt partem meam, dedérunt portiónem meam desiderábilem in desértum solitúdinis.

inillotemporecumappropinquassetiesusiero.en: At that time: When Jesus drew nigh to Jerusalem, and was come to Bethphage, unto mount Olivet: then he sent two disciples, saying to them: Go ye into the village that is over against you, and immediately you shall find an ass tied, and a colt with her: loose them and bring them to me. And so on.
inillotemporecumappropinquassetiesusiero.la: In illo témpore: Cum appropinquásset Jesus Jerosólymis, et venísset Béthphage ad montem Olivéti: tunc misit duos discípulos, dicens eis. Ite in castéllum, quod contra vos est, et statim inveniétis ásinam alligátam et pullum cum ea: sólvite, et addúcite mihi. Et réliqua.

mediatordeiethominumhomochristusiesusqui.en: The Mediator of God and men, the man Christ Jesus (who, being about to suffer for the salvation of mankind, had come down from heaven to earth), as the hour of his passion drew near, willed to draw near to the place of his passion, that by this also it might be made clear that he suffered not unwillingly, but of his own accord. He willed to come upon an ass, and to be called and praised as King by the multitudes, that by this also every instructed man might know him to be the Christ, whom the prophecy sent before of old had marked as to come thus. He willed to come five days before the Pasch, as we have learnt from the Gospel of John: that by this also he might show himself to be the immaculate Lamb, who should take away the sins of the world.
mediatordeiethominumhomochristusiesusqui.la: Mediátor Dei et hóminum, homo Christus Jesus (qui pro humáni géneris salúte passúrus de cælo descénderat ad terras) appropinquánte hora passiónis, appropinquáre vóluit loco passiónis, ut étiam per hoc clarésceret, quia non invítus, sed sponte paterétur. In ásino veníre, et a turbis Rex appellári ac laudári vóluit, ut étiam per hoc erudítus quisque cognósceret ipsum esse Christum, quem sic illo ventúrum prophetía olim præmissa signáverat. Ante quinque dies Paschæ veníre vóluit, sicut ex Joánnis Evangélio didícimus: ut étiam per hoc osténderet se esse Agnum immaculatum, qui peccáta tólleret mundi.

occurruntturbecumfloribusetpalmisredempt.en: The multitudes go out to meet the Redeemer with flowers and palms, and pay to the triumphant conqueror the homage that is his due: the Gentiles proclaim the Son of God with their mouth, and in praise of Christ their voices thunder through the clouds: Hosanna!
occurruntturbecumfloribusetpalmisredempt.la: Occúrrunt turbæ cum flóribus et palmis Redemptóri óbviam, et victóri triumphánti digna dant obséquia: Filium Dei ore gentes prǽdicant, et in laudem Christi voces tonant per núbila: Hosánna!

tantotemporevobiscumeramdocensintempletn.en: So long a time * was I with you teaching in the temple, and you laid not hold on me: and now, having scourged me, you lead me to be crucified.
tantotemporevobiscumeramdocensintempletn.la: Tanto témpore * vobíscum eram docens in templo, et non me tenuístis: et modo flagellátum dúcitis ad crucifigéndum.

nondiciturquitecumnequeamennequebenedica.en: Qui tecum is not said, nor Amen, nor Benedicamus Domino, nor Fidelium.
nondiciturquitecumnequeamennequebenedica.la: Non dicitur Qui tecum, neque Amen, neque Benedicámus Dómino, neque Fidélium.

inmonteolivetioravitadpatrempatersifieri.en: On the mount of Olivet he prayed to the Father: Father, if it be possible, let this chalice pass from me. The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh weak.
inmonteolivetioravitadpatrempatersifieri.la: In monte Olivéti orávit ad Patrem: Pater, si fíeri potest, tránseat a me calix iste. Spíritus quidem promptus est, caro autem infírma.

verumtamennonsicutegovolosedsicuttuvis.en: Nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt.
verumtamennonsicutegovolosedsicuttuvis.la: Verúmtamen non sicut ego volo, sed sicut tu vis.

sermodepassionedepassionedomini.en: Sermon 7 on the Passion of the Lord
sermodepassionedepassionedomini.la: Sermo 7 de Passione de passione Dómini

incipientesdilectissimitractaredivinoint.en: As we begin, dearly beloved, to treat of this, we understand that it was ordained by divine counsel that the sacrilegious princes of the Jews and the impious priests, who had often sought occasions of raging against Christ, should receive power to exercise their fury only at the paschal solemnity. For it behoved that the things which had long been promised in figurative mystery should be fulfilled in manifest effect: and that the diversity of various victims should be fulfilled by one sacrifice. That therefore the shadows might give way to the body, and the images cease in the presence of the truth: the ancient observance is shut out by a new sacrament. Victim passeth into victim, and blood is taken away by blood: and the legal festival, while it is changed, is fulfilled.
incipientesdilectissimitractaredivinoint.la: Incipiéntes, dilectissimi, tractáre, divino intelligimus dispósitum fuisse consílio, ut sacrilegi Judæórum príncipes et impii sacerdotes, qui sæviéndi in Christum occasiones sæpe quæsiverant, nonnisi in solemnitáte paschali exercéndi furoris sui acciperent potestátem. Oportébat enim ut manifesto impleréntur efféctu, quæ diu fúerant figuráto promíssa mystério: et uno explerétur sacrifício variárum differéntia victimárum. Ut ergo umbræ céderent córpori et cessárent imágines sub præséntia veritátis: antiqua observántia novo exclúditur sacraménto. Hóstia in hóstiam transit, et sánguine sanguis aufértur: et legális festivitas, dum mutátur, implétur.

filiusquidemhominisvaditsicutscriptumest.en: The Son of man indeed goeth, as it is written of him: but woe to that man by whom he shall be betrayed.
filiusquidemhominisvaditsicutscriptumest.la: Fílius quidem hóminis vadit, sicut scriptum est de illo: væ autem hómini illi, per quem tradétur.

incipienteenimfestivitatepaschaliquiorna.en: For as the paschal festival was beginning, they who should have adorned the temple, cleansed the vessels, provided the victims, conspire together in one crime: so that they both did not lay hold of the new mysteries, and violated the old. Taking care therefore that no tumult should arise on the holy day, they were zealous not for the festival, but for the crime, and they feared, not that the people should not sin, but lest Christ should escape. But Jesus, sure of his own counsel, was fulfilling the old testament and founding the new Pasch. And while in the court of Caiphas it was being debated how Christ ought to be slain: he, ordaining the sacrament of his Body and Blood, was teaching what manner of victim ought to be offered to God: nor was the traitor put away, that it might be shown that he was provoked by no injury.
incipienteenimfestivitatepaschaliquiorna.la: Incipiénte enim festivitáte paschali, qui ornáre templum, vasa mundáre, víctimas providére debúerant, in unum fácinus coniúrant: ut et nova mystéria non apprehénderent, et antiqua violárent. Providéntibus ergo ne in die sancto tumúltus orirétur, non festivitáti, sed facinori studebátur metuebántque, non ut pópulus non peccaret, sed ne Christus eváderet. At Jesus consilii sui certus, vetus testamentum consummábat et novum Pascha condébat. Et cum in Cáiphæ átrio tractarétur, quómodo Christus debéret occidi: ille Córporis et Sánguinis sui órdinans sacraméntum, docébat qualis Deo hóstia debéret offérri: nec traditóre submóto, ut ostenderétur nulla injúria exasperátus.

dicensquoqueunusvestrummetraditurusestno.en: Saying also, One of you is about to betray me, he showed that the conscience of the traitor and betrayer was known to him: not confounding the wicked one with harsh nor open rebuke, but meeting him with gentle and silent admonition: that repentance might the more easily correct him whom no casting off had disfigured. Why, unhappy Judas, dost thou not make use of such great kindness? Behold, the Lord spareth thy daring, and Christ pointeth thee out to none but to thyself. Neither thy name nor thy person is disclosed: but by a word of truth and mercy, only the secrets of thy heart are touched. Neither the honour of the Apostolic order, nor the communion of the sacraments, is denied thee. Return to soundness, and laying aside thy fury, come to thy senses. Clemency inviteth thee, salvation knocketh: life calleth thee back to life.
dicensquoqueunusvestrummetraditurusestno.la: Dicens quoque, Unus vestrum me traditúrus est, notam sibi traditóris ac proditóris consciéntiam demonstrávit: non áspera, nec apérta ímpium increpatióne confúndens, sed leni ac tácita admonitióne convéniens: ut facilius corrigeret pænitúdo, quem nulla deformásset abiectio. Cur, infélix Juda, tanta benignitáte non úteris? Ecce parcit áusibus tuis Dóminus, et nulli te, nisi tibi, índicat Christus. Nec nomen tuum, nec persóna detégitur: sed veritátis et misericórdiæ verbo, cordis tui tantum arcána tangúntur. Non Apostólici órdinis honor, non sacramentorum tibi commúnio denegátur. Redi in integrum, et depósito furóre resipisce. Cleméntia invítat, salus pulsat: ad vitam te vita révocat.

homideproditioneiude.en: Homily 1 on the betrayal of Judas

tuncabiitinquitnoninvitatusaprincipibuss.en: Then went, he saith. Not invited by the chief priests; of his own accord he went forth. One of the twelve. To the seventy disciples things so inward were committed. This was the royal band: from this choir Judas went forth. Judas, he saith, Iscariot. Why tellest thou me his country? Would that it had been allowed not to know him also! And he said to them: What will you give me, and I will deliver him unto you? O the rashness of a voice worthy of punishment! Was it for this the Master preached that thou oughtest to despise riches? O cruelty! Say, what is the cause of the betrayal? Perhaps that he gave thee power over devils, that he made thee succour the sick, that thou didst learn to raise the dead. O word of utter pride! Thou betrayest him who preserveth all things, who commandeth the devils, whom the seas obey, to whom all powers are subject.
tuncabiitinquitnoninvitatusaprincipibuss.la: Tunc ábiit, inquit. Non invitátus a princípibus; sponte procéssit. Unus de duódecim. Septuaginta discípulis tam interióra commissa sunt. Hæc erat catérva regális: de hoc choro Judas egréssus est. Judas, inquit, Iscariótes. Quid mihi ejus pátriam dicis? Utinam ipsum quoque nescire licuísset! Et dixit eis: Quid vultis mihi dare, et ego eum vobis tradam? O puniéndæ vocis temeritátem! Ideo Magister te divitias debére contémnere prædicábat? O crudelitátem! Dic, quæ causa proditiónis. Fórsitan quod tibi dæmonum trádidit potestátem, quod fecit languéntibus subvenire, quod mortuos suscitáre didicísti. O verbum totíus supérbiæ! Tradis eum, qui cuncta consérvat, qui dæmónibus imperat, cui obtémperant mária, cui omnes súbjacent potestátes.

sediamadterribilemmensamcumdebitareveren.en: But now the fitting time inviteth us to the awesome table with due reverence, with befitting watchfulness. Let no Judas be found there, let no wicked one approach: nor let snares be hidden in the mind. Let none approach feigning, none with a counterfeit soul. Let the mind therefore be pure, pure the thought: for the sacrifice also is pure. Our Lord indeed, being about to take from our eyes the body he had assumed and to bear it to the stars, on this day consecrated the sacrament of his Body and Blood: that that perpetual victim might live in memory, and be ever present in grace. When therefore thou goest up to the venerable altar, look upon the sacred Body and Blood of thy God with faith, marvel at it with honour, touch it with the mind, receive it with the hand of the heart, and take it with the inner taste.
sediamadterribilemmensamcumdebitareveren.la: Sed jam ad terribilem mensam cum débita reverentia, cum cóngrua vigilántia, opportunum tempus invitat. Nullus ibi Judas reperiátur, nullus malignus accédat: nec insídiæ mente condántur. Nullus fictus accédat, nullus fucáto ánimo. Pura igitur sit mens, pura cogitátio: quia et sacrificium purum est. Dóminus quidem noster, corpus assúmptum ablatúrus óculis nostris et sidéribus illatúrus, in hac die sacraméntum Córporis et Sánguinis sui consecrávit: ut perénnis illa víctima viveret in memória, et semper præsens esset in grátia. Cum igitur ad reveréndum altáre ascéndis, sacrum Dei tui Corpus et Sánguinem fide réspice, honore miráre, mente continge, cordis manu súscipe et gustu interióri assúme.

revelabuntceliiniquitatemiudeetterraadve.en: The heavens shall reveal the iniquity of Juda, and the earth shall rise up against him: and his sin shall be made manifest in the day of the wrath of the Lord:
revelabuntceliiniquitatemiudeetterraadve.la: Revelábunt cæli iniquitátem Judæ, et terra advérsus eum consúrget: et maniféstum erit peccátum illíus in die furóris Dómini:

cumeisquidixeruntdominodeorecedeanobissc.en: With them that said to the Lord God: Depart from us, we desire not the knowledge of thy ways.
cumeisquidixeruntdominodeorecedeanobissc.la: Cum eis qui dixérunt Dómino Deo: Recéde a nobis, sciéntiam viárum tuárum nólumus.

indiemperditionisservabituretaddiemultio.en: He shall be reserved unto the day of destruction, and shall be brought to the day of vengeance.
indiemperditionisservabituretaddiemultio.la: In diem perditiónis servábitur, et ad diem ultiónis ducétur.

christusfactusestpronobisobediensusquead.en: Christ * became obedient for us unto death, even the death of the cross.
christusfactusestpronobisobediensusquead.la: Christus * factus est pro nobis obédiens usque ad mortem, mortem autem crucis.

hodiepostcompletoriumbenedictionondaturo.en: Today after Compline the blessing is not given, the antiphon Salve, Regina is omitted, and holy water is not sprinkled.
hodiepostcompletoriumbenedictionondaturo.la: Hodie post Completorium benedictio non datur, omittitur ant. Salve, Regina, nec aspergitur aqua benedicta.

repetitapostbenedictusantiphonaduofratre.en: When the antiphon has been repeated after the Benedictus, two Brothers standing before the steps of the altar say:
repetitapostbenedictusantiphonaduofratre.la: Repetita post Benedictus antiphona, duo Fratres stantes ante gradus altaris dicunt:

adeaquesequunturfratresstantversiadaltar.en: (For what follows the Brothers stand turned toward the altar.)
adeaquesequunturfratresstantversiadaltar.la: (Ad ea quæ sequuntur Fratres stant versi ad altare.)

etchororespondente.en: And when the choir has responded

deindealiiduofratresstantesinmediochorid.en: Then two other Brothers standing in the middle of the choir say:
deindealiiduofratresstantesinmediochorid.la: Deinde alii duo Fratres stantes in medio chori dicunt:

christusdominusfactusestobediensusqueadm.en: Christ the Lord became obedient unto death.
christusdominusfactusestobediensusqueadm.la: Christus Dóminus factus est obédiens usque ad mortem.

itemfratresantegradus.en: Again the Brothers before the steps:

quipassurusadvenistipropternos.en: Who didst come to suffer for our sake.

quiexpansisincrucemanibustraxistiomniaad.en: Who, with thy hands stretched out upon the cross, didst draw all the ages unto thee.
quiexpansisincrucemanibustraxistiomniaad.la: Qui, expánsis in cruce mánibus, traxísti ómnia ad te sǽcula.

quipropheticeprompsistieromorstuaomors.en: Who didst say by the prophet: I will be thy death, O death!
quipropheticeprompsistieromorstuaomors.la: Qui prophétice prompsísti: Ero mors tua, o mors!

deindefratresinmediochori.en: Then the Brothers in the middle of the choir:

etfratresantegradus.en: And the Brothers before the steps:

itemfratresantegradusdicuntaltavoce.en: Again the Brothers before the steps say with a loud voice:
itemfratresantegradusdicuntaltavoce.la: Item Fratres ante gradus dicunt alta voce:

mortemautemcrucis.en: Even the death of the cross.

finitoversumortemautemcrucisprosternunts.en: When the verse Mortem autem crucis is finished, all prostrate themselves and say the Our Father entirely in silence.
finitoversumortemautemcrucisprosternunts.la: Finito versu Mortem autem crucis prosternunt se omnes et dicunt Pater noster totum secreto.

abinsurgentibusinme.en: From them that rise up against me.

delamentationeieremieprophete.en: From the Lamentation of Jeremias the Prophet

ierusalemierusalemconvertereaddominumdeu.en: Jerusalem! Jerusalem! Return unto the Lord thy God.
ierusalemierusalemconvertereaddominumdeu.la: Jerúsalem, Jerúsalem, convértere ad Dóminum Deum tuum.

omnesamicimeidereliqueruntmeetprevalueru.en: All my friends have forsaken me, and they that lay in wait for me have prevailed: he whom I loved hath betrayed me: and striking me with terrible eyes and a cruel wound,
omnesamicimeidereliqueruntmeetprevalueru.la: Omnes amíci mei dereliquérunt me, et prævaluérunt insidiántes mihi: trádidit me quem diligébam: et terribílibus óculis plaga crudéli percutiéntes,

acetopotabantme.en: They gave me vinegar to drink.

etdederuntinescammeamfeletinsitimea.en: And they gave me gall for my food: and in my thirst.
etdederuntinescammeamfeletinsitimea.la: Et dedérunt in escam meam fel: et in siti mea.

velumtempliscissumestetomnisterratremuit.en: The veil of the temple was rent, and all the earth trembled: the thief cried out from the cross, saying:
velumtempliscissumestetomnisterratremuit.la: Velum templi scissum est, et omnis terra trémuit: latro de cruce clamábat, dicens:

mementomeidominedumvenerisinregnumtuum.en: Remember me, O Lord, when thou shalt come into thy kingdom.
mementomeidominedumvenerisinregnumtuum.la: Meménto mei, Dómine, dum véneris in regnum tuum.

amendicotibihodiemecumerisinparadiso.en: Amen I say to thee: this day thou shalt be with me in paradise.
amendicotibihodiemecumerisinparadiso.la: Amen dico tibi: hódie mecum eris in paradíso.

egoquidemplantavitevineammeamelectamomne.en: Yet I planted thee a chosen vineyard, all true seed.
egoquidemplantavitevineammeamelectamomne.la: Ego quidem plantávi te víneam meam eléctam, omne semen verum.

cumverbisorationissuedominusdeclarassetv.en: When the Lord by the words of his prayer had declared that both the human and the divine nature were most truly and most fully in him, showing whence it was that he would not suffer, and whence that he would; having driven out the fear of weakness and confirmed the magnanimity of strength, he returned to the purpose of his eternal design: and to the devil raging through the ministry of the Jews he set against him the form of a servant having no sin, that through him the cause of all might be pleaded, in whom alone was the nature of all without guilt. The children of darkness therefore rushed upon the Light, and, using torches and lanterns, they escaped not the night of their unbelief. They seize him who is willing to be held, and drag him who is willing to be dragged. For if he had willed to resist, impious hands could have done nothing; but the redemption of the world would have been delayed: and he who was to die for the salvation of all, being unharmed, would have saved none.
cumverbisorationissuedominusdeclarassetv.la: Cum verbis oratiónis suæ Dóminus declarásset, veríssime sibi atque pleníssime et humánam et divinam inésse natúram, osténdens unde esset quod pati nollet, et unde quod vellet; depúlsa trepidatióne infirmitátis et confirmáta virtútis, magnanimitáte rédiit in sententiam suæ dispositiónis ætérnæ: sæviénti diábolo per ministéria Judæorum formam servi nihil peccáti habéntis objécit, ut per eum agerétur ómnium causa, in quo solo erat ómnium natúra sine culpa. Irruérunt ergo in lumen filii tenebrárum, et, uténtes fáculis et latérnis, non evasérunt infidelitátis suæ noctem. Occupant voléntem tenéri, et trahunt voléntem trahi. Quod si vellet obníti, nihil impiæ manus possent; sed mundi redémptio differrétur: et nullum salváret illæsus, qui pro ómnium erat salúte moritúrus.

tamquamadlatronemexistiscumgladiiscompre.en: Ye are come out as it were against a thief, with swords to apprehend me: I was daily with you in the temple teaching, and ye laid not hold on me: and behold, having scourged me, ye lead me away
tamquamadlatronemexistiscumgladiiscompre.la: Tamquam ad latrónem exístis cum gládiis comprehéndere me: quotídie apud vos eram in templo docens, et non me tenuístis: et ecce flagellátum dúcitis

tenebrefactesuntdumcrucifixissentiesumiu.en: Darkness was made, when the Jews had crucified Jesus: and about the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a loud voice: My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?
tenebrefactesuntdumcrucifixissentiesumiu.la: Ténebræ factæ sunt, dum crucifixíssent Jesum Judǽi: et circa horam nonam exclamávit Jesus voce magna: Deus meus, Deus meus, ut quid me dereliquísti?

etinclinatocapiteemisitspiritum.en: And He bowed His Head, and gave up the Ghost.

cumergoaccepissetacetumdixitconsummatume.en: When therefore he had taken the vinegar, he said: It is consummated.
cumergoaccepissetacetumdixitconsummatume.la: Cum ergo accepísset acétum, dixit: Consummátum est.

quideumgravarisinisopilateðeaffectatapot.en: Why, O Pilate, dost thou suffer him to be burdened with the charge of seeking power, whose especial teaching was of humility? He contradicted not the Roman laws, he submitted to the census, he paid the didrachma, he forbade not the tributes, he ordained that the things that are Caesar's be rendered to Caesar: he chose poverty, he counselled obedience, he preached meekness. This is truly not to fight against Caesar, but to help him. Nevertheless, lest the objection of the Jews seem wholly empty, examine more diligently, O governor, what is known of the works of the Lord Jesus, what hath been found out of his power. To the blind he gave sight, to the deaf hearing, to the lame walking, to the dumb speech. He drove away fevers, he loosed pains, he cast out devils, he brought the dead to life. Let the Jews then object this power: and let them bring forth with the mouth what they hold in the heart. Why do they bring false charges concerning earthly things, who persecute the heavenly?
quideumgravarisinisopilateðeaffectatapot.la: Quid eum gravári sinis, o Piláte,ðe affectáta poténtia, cujus speciális fuit de humilitáte doctrina? Románis légibus non contradíxit, censum súbiit, didráchma solvit, vectigália non inhibuit, quæ sunt Cæsaris Césari reddénda constítuit: paupertátem elégit, obediéntiam suásit, mansuetúdinem prædicávit. Hoc est vere non impugnáre Cæsarem, sed juváre. Verumtamen ne in totum inánis videátur Judæórum obiéctio, díscute diligéntius, præses, quid de Dómini Jesu opéribus notum sit, quid de potestáte compértum. Cæcis visum, surdis audítum, claudis gressum, mutis donávit elóquium. Febres abégit, dolóres resólvit, dæmónia ejécit, mórtuos vivificávit. Hanc ergo Judæi obíciant potestátem: et hoc próferant ore, quod tenent corde. Quare de terrénis calumniántur, qui cæléstia persequúntur?

barabbaslatrodimittituretinnocenschristu.en: Barabbas the robber is released, and the innocent Christ is slain: for Judas also, skilled in the weapons of wickedness, who through peace learned to make war,
barabbaslatrodimittituretinnocenschristu.la: Barábbas latro dimíttitur et ínnocens Christus occíditur: nam et Judas armis doctus scéleris, qui per pacem dídicit fácere bellum,

osculandotradiditdominumiesumchristum.en: With a kiss betrayed the Lord Jesus Christ.

ecceturbetquivocabaturiudasvenitetdumapp.en: Behold a multitude, and he that was called Judas came: and when he drew near to Jesus.
ecceturbetquivocabaturiudasvenitetdumapp.la: Ecce turba, et qui vocabátur Judas, venit: et dum appropinquáret ad Jesum.

excessitquidempilaticulpamfacinusiudeoru.en: The crime of the Jews indeed exceeded the guilt of Pilate, for they, frightening him with the name of Caesar, drove him to carry out their wickedness. But neither did he himself escape guilt, who forsook his own judgment and passed over into the crime of another. That Pilate therefore permitted Jesus to be dishonoured with mockeries and vexed with injuries; and that he showed him, beaten with scourges, crowned with thorns, and clothed in a garment of mockery, to the sight of his persecutors: he thought that the minds of his enemies were to be soothed; that, their hatred being glutted, they would no longer think him to be persecuted whom they beheld afflicted in so many ways. But when the anger of them that cried out blazed up, they obtained unto their own damnation what they obstinately demanded. The Lord therefore, delivered up to the will of the raging, in mockery of his royal dignity, was commanded to be the bearer of his own instrument of punishment; that that might be fulfilled: Whose government is upon his shoulder. For in the fair show of his triumph he bore his trophy, and brought in the saving sign to be adored by all kingdoms.
excessitquidempilaticulpamfacinusiudeoru.la: Excéssit quidem Piláti culpam facinus Judæórum, qui illum nómine Césaris térritum, ad efféctum sui scéleris impulérunt. Sed nec ipse evásit reátum, qui reliquit judicium próprium et in crimen transívit aliénum. Quod ergo Pilátus Jesum dehonestári ludibriis, vexári permisit injúriis; quodque eum flagéllis cæsum, spinis coronátum et amictu irrisóriæ vestis indútum, persequéntium aspéctui ostentávit: mitigándos inimicórum ánimos existimavit; ut exsaturátis ódiis, non ultra jam créderent persequéndum, quem tot modis intuebántur afflictum. Sed, cum inardésceret ira clamántium, obtinuérunt in damnatiónem suam, quod pertináciter exigébant. Tráditus itaque Dóminus sæviéntium voluntáti, ad irrisiónem régiæ dignitátis, supplicii sui jussus est esse gestátor; ut implerétur illud: Cujus impérium super húmerum ejus. Quia pulchra spécie triúmphi sui portábat trophæum et signum salutáre adorándum regnis ómnibus inferébat.

astiteruntregesterreetprincipesconveneru.en: The kings of the earth set themselves, and the rulers take counsel together
astiteruntregesterreetprincipesconveneru.la: Astitérunt reges terræ, et príncipes convenérunt in unum.

euntibusautemcumiesuturbissimonquidamcyr.en: And as the multitudes went with Jesus, a certain Simon of Cyrene was found, upon whom the wood of punishment was transferred from the Lord: that by such a deed the faith of the Gentiles might be foreshown, to whom the cross of Christ was to be not confusion, but glory. And not in the temple, nor within the enclosure of the city, but without the camp was he crucified: that, the mystery of the old victims ceasing, a new Victim might be laid upon a new altar, and the cross of Christ might be the altar not of the temple, but of the world. Christ therefore, dearly beloved, being lifted up by the cross, let not that sight only present itself to the eye of the mind which was in the eyes of the wicked, to whom it was said by Moses: And thy life shall be hanging before thy eyes, and thou shalt fear day and night, and shalt not trust thy life. But let our understanding receive with a pure heart the glory of the cross, shining in heaven and on earth, and see what the Lord said: Now is the judgment of the world, now shall the prince of this world be cast out: and I, if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all things to myself.
euntibusautemcumiesuturbissimonquidamcyr.la: Eúntibus autem cum Jesu turbis, Simon quidam Cyrenǽus invéntus est, in quem lignum supplícii transfértur a Dómino: ut tali facto præsignarétur géntium fides, quibus crux Christi non confúsio erat futúra, sed glória. Non autem in templo, nec intra septa civitátis, sed extra castra crucifíxus est: ut, véterum victimárum cessánte mystério, nova hóstia novo imponerétur altári, et crux Christi non templi esset ara, sed mundi. Exaltáto ígitur, dilectíssimi, per crucem Christo, non illa tantum spécies aspéctui mentis occúrrat, quæ fuit in óculis impiórum, quibus per Móysen dictum est: Et erit pendens vita tua ante óculos tuos, et timébis die ac nocte, et non credes vitæ tuæ. Sed intelléctus noster glóriam crucis, cælo terráque radiántem, puro corde suscípiat, et vídeat quod Dóminus dixit: Nunc judícium mundi est, nunc princeps hujus mundi eiciétur foras: et ego, si exaltátus fúero a terra, ómnia traham ad me ipsum.

iesumtradiditimpiussummisprincipibussace.en: The wicked one delivered Jesus to the chief priests and the ancients of the people: but Peter followed afar off,
iesumtradiditimpiussummisprincipibussace.la: Jesum trádidit ímpius summis princípibus sacerdótum et senióribus pópuli: Petrus autem sequebátur a longe,

utvideretfinem.en: That he might see the end.

etingressusestpetrusatriumprincipissacer.en: And Peter went into the court of the high priest.
etingressusestpetrusatriumprincipissacer.la: Et ingréssus est Petrus átrium príncipis sacerdótum.

oadmirabilispotentiacrucisoineffabilisgl.en: O wonderful power of the cross, O unspeakable glory of the passion, in which is both the tribunal of the Lord, and the judgment of the world, and the power of the Crucified! For thou hast drawn all things to thee, O Lord: when the whole world received the sense to confess thy majesty. Thou hast drawn all things to thee, O Lord: when, in execration of the crime of the Jews, all the elements brought forth one sentence: when, the lights of heaven being darkened, the earth also was shaken with unwonted motions, and the whole creation refused itself to the use of the wicked. Thou hast drawn all things to thee, O Lord: for, the veil of the temple being rent, the Holy of holies departed from the unworthy high priests: that the figure might be turned into truth, prophecy into manifestation, and the law into the Gospel. Thou hast drawn all things to thee, O Lord: that what in the one temple of Judea was covered under shadowy signs, the devotion of all nations might celebrate in an open mystery.
oadmirabilispotentiacrucisoineffabilisgl.la: O admirábilis potentia crucis, o ineffabilis glória passiónis, in qua et tribúnal Dómini et judícium mundi et potéstas est Crucifixi! Traxísti enim, Dómine, ómnia ad te: cum confiténdæ majestátis tuæ sensum totus mundus accépit. Traxísti, Dómine, ómnia ad te: cum in exsecratiónem judáici scéleris unam protulérunt ómnia eleménta senténtiam: cum obscurátis lumináribus cæli, terra quoque mótibus quaterétur insólitis, universáque creatúra impiórum se úsui denegáret. Traxísti, Dómine, ómnia ad te: quóniam, scisso templi velo, Sancta sanctórum ab indígnis pontificibus recessérunt: ut figúra in veritátem, prophetía in manifestatiónem, et lex in Evangélium verterétur. Traxísti, Dómine, ómnia ad te: ut quod in uno Judææ templo obumbrátis significatiónibus tegebátur, apérto sacraménto universárum natiónum devotio celebráret.

utvivificaretpopulumsuum.en: That he might quicken his people.

ipsevulneratusestpropteriniquitatesnostr.en: He was wounded for our iniquities: he was bruised for our sins.
ipsevulneratusestpropteriniquitatesnostr.la: Ipse vulnerátus est propter iniquitátes nostras: attrítus est propter scélera nostra.

agnomitibasiacuilupusdeditvenenosa.en: The meek Lamb, to whom the wolf gave venomous kisses.
agnomitibasiacuilupusdeditvenenosa.la: Agno miti básia cui lupus dedit venenósa.

vitainlignomoriturinfernusetmorslugenssp.en: Life dieth upon the wood; hell and death, mourning, are despoiled.
vitainlignomoriturinfernusetmorslugenssp.la: Vita in ligno móritur, inférnus et mors lugens spoliátur.

tequivincirivoluistinosqueamortisvinculi.en: Thee, who didst will to be bound, and hast rescued us from the bonds of death.
tequivincirivoluistinosqueamortisvinculi.la: Te qui vincíri voluísti, nosque a mortis vínculis eripuísti.

sepultodominosignatumestmonumentumvolven.en: After that the Lord was buried, they sealed the sepulchre, rolling a stone to the door of the sepulchre
sepultodominosignatumestmonumentumvolven.la: Sepúlto Dómino, signátum est monuméntum: volvéntes lápidem ad óstium monuménti,

neforteveniantdiscipulieiusetfurentureum.en: Lest perhaps his disciples come and steal him away, and say to the people: He is risen from the dead.
neforteveniantdiscipulieiusetfurentureum.la: Ne forte véniant discípuli ejus et furéntur eum et dicant plebi: Surréxit a mórtuis.

ululatepastoresetclamateaspergitevoscine.en: Howl, ye shepherds, and cry: sprinkle yourselves with ashes.
ululatepastoresetclamateaspergitevoscine.la: Ululáte, pastóres, et clamáte: aspérgite vos cínere.

caligaveruntoculimeiafletumeoquielongatu.en: Mine eyes are darkened with my weeping: for he that comforted me is gone far from me: see, all ye people,
caligaveruntoculimeiafletumeoquielongatu.la: Caligavérunt óculi mei a fletu meo: quia elongatus est a me qui consolabátur me: vidéte, omnes pópuli,

siestdolorsimilissicutdolormeus.en: If there be any sorrow like unto my sorrow.
siestdolorsimilissicutdolormeus.la: Si est dolor similis sicut dolor meus.

ovosomnesquitransitisperviamattenditeetv.en: O all ye that pass by the way, attend, and see.
ovosomnesquitransitisperviamattenditeetv.la: O vos omnes qui transitis per viam, attendite, et vidéte.

peractodilectissimisalvatoristriumphetco.en: The triumph of the Saviour being accomplished, dearly beloved, and the dispensations fulfilled which all the utterances of the old testament foretold, let the carnal Jew mourn, but let the spiritual Christian rejoice; and let the festival which for them was turned into night, shine forth for us into light. For the cross of Christ is at once the glory of believers and the punishment of unbelievers. For although the fury of the persecutors wrought nothing else against the Lord of majesty than atrocious cruelty and a merciless punishment: yet in this passion of the Lord there is a truer and juster reason for rejoicing than for grieving.
peractodilectissimisalvatoristriumphetco.la: Perácto, dilectíssimi, Salvatóris triúmpho et consummátis dispensatiónibus, quas ómnia véteris testaménti elóquia nuntiárunt, lúgeat carnális Judæus, sed spiritális gáudeat Christiánus; et festívitas, quæ illis convérsa est in noctem, nobis corúscet in lucem. Quóniam crux Christi éadem est et credéntium glória et non credéntium pœna. Quamvis enim persequéntium furor nihil aliud in Dóminum majestátis operátus sit, quam atrócem crudelitátem et immite supplícium: hac Dómini passióne vérior justiórque lætándi est rátio quam doléndi.

eccequomodomorituriustusetnemopercipitco.en: Behold how the just man dieth, and no man taketh it to heart: and just men are taken away, and no one considereth: the just man is taken away from before the face of iniquity,
eccequomodomorituriustusetnemopercipitco.la: Ecce quómodo móritur justus, et nemo pércipit corde: et viri justi tollúntur, et nemo consíderat: a fácie iniquitátis sublátus est justus,

eteritinpacememorieius.en: And his memory is in peace.
eteritinpacememorieius.la: Et erit in pace memória ejus.

inpacefactusestlocuseiusetinsionhabitati.en: His place is in peace: and his abode in Sion.
inpacefactusestlocuseiusetinsionhabitati.la: In pace factus est locus ejus: et in Sion habitátio ejus.

nuncautempostquamtatissusceptioneinfirmi.en: But now, after the weakness taken up with our nature hath been glorified with power, the paschal solemnity is to be darkened by no sadness of the faithful; nor is the order of the events to be recalled by us with sorrow: since the Lord so used the malice of the Jews, that through the intent of the crime the will of the Merciful One was fulfilled. And if, at the going out of Israel from Egypt, the blood of a lamb was the restoration of liberty, and that festival was made most sacred which by the sacrifice of a beast turned away the wrath of the destroyer: how great joys are to be conceived by Christian peoples, for whom the almighty Father spared not his own Son, but delivered him up for us all! So that in the slaying of Christ the Pasch might be the true and singular sacrifice: by which not one people from the dominion of Pharao, but the whole world is delivered from the captivity of the devil.
