nuncautempostquamtatissusceptioneinfirmi.la: Nunc autem postquam tatis susceptione infirmicata virtutis, nulla fidelium maestitudine paschális est obscuránda solémnitas; nec cum tristítia nobis gestórum ordo recoléndus est: cum ita Dóminus usus sit malitia Judæórum, ut intentióne facinoris volúntas sit impléta miseréntis. Si autem in éxitu Israël de Ægypto agni sanguis fuit restitútio libertátis, et sacratíssima est facta festivitas, quæ per hostiam pécudis iram avérteret vastatóris: quanta pópulis christianis concipiénda sunt gáudia, pro quibus omnipotens Pater Fílio suo non pepercit, sed pro nobis ómnibus tradidit illum! Ut in occisióne Christi, Pascha esset verum et singuláre sacrificium: quo non ex dominatióne Pharaónis unus pópulus, sed ex diáboli captivitáte totus mundus erúitur.

agnusdeichristusimmolatusestprosalutemun.en: Christ the Lamb of God was immolated for the salvation of the world: for at the deceit done to our first-formed parent * the Maker, grieving, when by the bite of the baneful apple he fell into death, himself then marked out a tree,
agnusdeichristusimmolatusestprosalutemun.la: Agnus Dei Christus immolátus est pro salúte mundi: nam de paréntis protoplásti fraude * Factor cóndolens, quando pomi noxiális morsu in mortem córruit, ipse lignum tunc notávit,

damnaligniutsolveret.en: That he might undo the harm of the tree.

lustrissexquiiamperactistempusimplenscor.en: Thirty years being now accomplished, fulfilling the time of his bodily life, born for this of his own will, given up to his passion, the Lamb is lifted up on the trunk of the cross to be immolated.
lustrissexquiiamperactistempusimplenscor.la: Lustris sex qui jam peráctis tempus implens córporis, se volénte natus ad hoc, passióni déditus, Agnus in crucis levátur immolándus stípite.

nondiciturconclusietsicterminaturhora.en: The conclusion is not said. And thus the Hour ends.
nondiciturconclusietsicterminaturhora.la: Non dicitur conclusio. Et sic terminatur hora.

completoriumdiciturtantumabiisquisolemni.en: Compline is said only by those who do not assist at the solemn Paschal Vigil.
completoriumdiciturtantumabiisquisolemni.la: Completorium dicitur tantum ab iis qui solemni vigiliæ paschali non intersunt.

quodenimvivitvivitdeoalleluiaalleluia.en: For in that he liveth, he liveth unto God, alleluia, alleluia.
quodenimvivitvivitdeoalleluiaalleluia.la: Quod enim vivit, vivit Deo, allelúja, allelúja.

dicantnunciudeiquomodomilitescustodiente.en: Let the Jews now say how the soldiers guarding the sepulchre lost the King at the placing of the stone. Why did they not keep the Rock of justice? Let them either give back him that was buried, or adore him rising again, saying with us.
dicantnunciudeiquomodomilitescustodiente.la: Dicant nunc Judæi quómodo mílites custodiéntes sepúlcrum perdidérunt Regem ad lápidis positiónem. Quare non servábant Petram justítia? Aut sepúltum reddant, aut resurgéntem adórent, nobiscum dicéntes.

alleluiaresurrexitdominusalleluiasicutdi.en: Alleluia. The Lord is risen, alleluia: as he said to you, alleluia, alleluia.
alleluiaresurrexitdominusalleluiasicutdi.la: Allelúja. Resurréxit Dóminus, allelúja: sicut dixit vobis, allelúja, allelúja.

spiritumnobisdominetuecaritatisinfundeut.en: Pour forth upon us, O Lord, the Spirit of thy love: that those whom thou hast filled with the paschal sacraments, thou mayest by thy loving kindness make to be of one mind. Through our Lord... in the unity of the same.
spiritumnobisdominetuecaritatisinfundeut.la: Spíritum nobis, Dómine, tuæ caritátis infúnde: ut, quos sacraméntis paschalibus satiásti, tua fácias pietáte concórdes. Per Dóminum... in unitáte ejusdem.

surrexitdominusverealleluia.en: The Lord is risen indeed, * Alleluia.

surrexitchristusetilluxitpopulosuoquemre.en: Christ is risen and hath shone upon his people, whom he redeemed with his blood, alleluia.
surrexitchristusetilluxitpopulosuoquemre.la: Surréxit Christus et illúxit pópulo suo, quem redémit sánguine suo, allelúja. Ps. 4, 5, 6

citeuntesdicitediscipulieiusetpetroquias.en: Go quickly, tell his disciples and Peter that the Lord is risen.
citeuntesdicitediscipulieiusetpetroquias.la: Cito euntes dicíte discípuli ejus et Petro quia surréxit Dóminus.

nonnesitoportuitpatichristumetintrareing.en: Ought not Christ to have suffered these things, and so to enter into his glory? Alleluia.
nonnesitoportuitpatichristumetintrareing.la: Nonne sit opórtuit pati Christum, et intráre in glóriam suam? Allelúja.

inillotemporestetitiesusinmediodiscipulo.en: At that time: Jesus stood in the midst of his disciples, and saith to them: Peace be to you; it is I, fear not. And so forth.
inillotemporestetitiesusinmediodiscipulo.la: In illo témpore: Stetit Jesus in médio discipulórum, et dicit eis: Pax vobis: ego sum, nolíte timére. Et réliqua.

libercommentinlucamcapantefinem.en: Book 10 on Luke, chap. 24, before the end
libercommentinlucamcapantefinem.la: Liber 10. Comment. in Lucam, cap. 24, ante finem

nonperincorporeamnaturamsedperresurrecti.en: Not by an incorporeal nature, but by the quality of the resurrection, did the Lord pass, in no usual manner, through things shut. For what is touched is a body: what is handled is a body. And in the body we shall rise again. For it is sown a natural body, it riseth a spiritual body: but the one more subtle, the other more gross, as being still compacted of the quality of earthly corruption. For how is that not a body, in which remained the marks of the wounds, the traces of the scars, which the Lord offered to be handled? Wherein he not only strengtheneth faith, but also quickeneth devotion: in that he chose to bring into heaven the wounds received for us, and would not abolish them: that he might show to God the Father the price of our liberty.
nonperincorporeamnaturamsedperresurrecti.la: Non per incorpóream naturam, sed per resurrectiónis qualitátem, minus usu clausa Dóminus penetrávit. Nam quod tángitur, corpus est: quod palpátur, corpus est. In córpore autem resurgémus. Seminátur enim corpus animále, surgit corpus spiritále: sed illud subtilius, hoc crássius, útpote adhuc terrénæ labis qualitáte concrétum. Nam quómodo non corpus, in quo manébant insígnia vúlnerum, vestígia cicatrícum, quæ Dóminus palpánda óbtulit? In quo non solum fidem firmat, sed étiam devotiónem ácuit: quod vulnera suscépta pro nobis cælo inférre máluit, abolére nóluit: ut Deo Patri nostræ prétia libertátis osténderet.

talemdexteramsibilocatpateraddexteramloc.en: Such a one he placeth at his right hand, the Father placeth him at his right hand, embracing the trophy of our salvation: such martyrs hath the crown of his scars shown us there. And since our discourse hath come thus far, let us consider by what grace the Apostles, according to John, believed, and rejoiced; according to Luke, are rebuked as unbelieving: there they received the Holy Ghost, here they are bidden to sit in the city till they be endued with power from on high. And it seemeth to me that the one, as an Apostle, touched upon greater and higher things, the other upon the things that followed and were nearest to human things: the one used the circuit of a historian, the other brevity. For although Luke saith at first that they believed not, yet afterwards he showeth that they believed. And if we consider the first things, they are contrary: if those that follow, it is certain that they agree.
talemdexteramsibilocatpateraddexteramloc.la: Talem déxteram sibi locat, Pater ad déxteram locat, trophæum nostræ salútis ampléctens: tales illic mártyres nobis cicatrícis suæ coróna monstrávit. Et quóniam sermo huc noster usque evasit, considerémus qua grátia secúndum Joánnem crediderint Apóstoli, qui gavísi sunt; secúndum Lucam quasi incréduli redarguántur: ibi Spíritum Sanctum accéperint, hic sedére in civitáte jubeántur, quoadúsque induántur virtúte ex alto. Et vidétur mihi ille quasi Apóstolus majóra et altióra tetigisse, hic sequéntia et humánis próxima: hic histórico usus circúitu, ille compendio. Nam etsi primo Lucas eos non credidísse dicat, póstea tamen credidisse demonstrat. Et si prima considerémus, contrária sunt: si sequéntia, certum est convenire.

tuleruntdominummeumetnescioubiposuerunte.en: They have taken away my Lord: and I know not where they have laid him. The Angel saith to her: Weep not, Mary:
tuleruntdominummeumetnescioubiposuerunte.la: Tulérunt Dóminum meum: et néscio ubi posuérunt eum. Dicit ei Angelus: Noli flere, María:

surrexitsicutdixitprecedetvosingalileami.en: He is risen, as he said: he will go before you into Galilee: there you shall see him, alleluia, alleluia.
surrexitsicutdixitprecedetvosingalileami.la: Surréxit sicut dixit: præcédet vos in Galilæam: ibi eum vidébitis, allelúja, allelúja.

stetitinquitinmedieorumetdixitpaxvobiseg.en: He stood, it saith, in the midst of them, and said: Peace be to you: it is I, fear not. But they being troubled and frighted, supposed that they saw a spirit. He seemeth to have shown himself separately to these eleven, as he had already shown himself apart in the evening to Ammaon and Cleophas. And as those two, so also those eleven seem to have been able to come together to strengthen the rest. Lastly, they were troubled: and therefore he opened their understanding, that they might understand the things that are written. And the Holy Ghost he either breathed upon those eleven as being more perfect, and promiseth that he is to be given to the rest afterwards: or he breathed him upon the same there, and here he promiseth him. Nor doth this seem contrary, since there are diversities of graces. There the grace of remitting sins was given, which seemeth to be more august: and therefore it is breathed by Christ. But Luke described the grace of tongues poured forth.
stetitinquitinmedieorumetdixitpaxvobiseg.la: Stetit, inquit, in médio eórum et dixit: Pax vobis: ego sum, nolíte timére. Conturbáti vero et contérriti, existimábant se spíritum vidére. Vidétur separatim se istis úndecim demonstrasse, sicut se Amaóni et Cléophæ seorsum jam véspere demonstráverat. Et quemádmodum isti duo, ita étiam vidéntur illi úndecim ad confirmándos réliquos convenire potuisse. Dénique conturbáti sunt: et ideo apéruit sensum, ut intelligerent ea quæ scripta sunt. Spíritum autem Sanctum vel illis úndecim quasi perfectióribus insufflávit, et réliquis póstea tribuéndum esse promíttit: vel eísdem ibi insufflávit, hic spondet. Nec vidétur esse contrárium. cum divisiones gratiárum sint. Ibi remittendórum grátia tribúta est peccatórum, quod esse vidétum augústius: et ideo insufflátur a Christo. Lucas autem linguarum grátiam descrípsit effúsam.

noninfermentamalitieetnequitiesedinazymi.en: Not with the leaven of malice and wickedness: but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.
noninfermentamalitieetnequitiesedinazymi.la: Non in fermenta malitiæ et nequitiæ: sed in ázymis sinceritátis et veritátis.

surrexitpastorbonusquiposuitanimamsuampr.en: The good Shepherd is risen, who laid down his life for his sheep,
surrexitpastorbonusquiposuitanimamsuampr.la: Surréxit Pastor bonus, qui pósuit ánimam suam pro óvibus suis,

etprosuogregemoridignatusestalleluiaalle.en: And deigned to die for his flock, Alleluia, alleluia.
etprosuogregemoridignatusestalleluiaalle.la: Et pro suo grege mori dignátus est, Allelúja, allelúja.

etenimpaschanostrumimmolatusestchristus.en: For Christ our pasch is sacrificed.
etenimpaschanostrumimmolatusestchristus.la: Etenim Pascha nostrum immolátus est Christus.

alleluiasurrexitdominusvereveniteadoremu.en: Alleluia, The Lord is risen indeed: * Come, let us adore, alleluia.
alleluiasurrexitdominusvereveniteadoremu.la: Allelúja, Surréxit Dóminus vere: * Veníte, adorémus, allelúja.

delibroapocalypsisbeatiioannisapostoli.en: Lesson from the book of the Apocalypse of St. John the Apostle
delibroapocalypsisbeatiioannisapostoli.la: De libro Apocalýpsis beáti Joánnis Apóstoli

abintusinfimbriisaureiscircumamictavarie.en: Within, in golden borders, clothed round about with varieties.
abintusinfimbriisaureiscircumamictavarie.la: Ab intus, in fímbriis áureis, circumamícta varietátibus.

coronaaureasupercaputeiusexpressasignosa.en: A crown of gold upon his head, engraved with the seal of holiness.
coronaaureasupercaputeiusexpressasignosa.la: Coróna áurea super caput ejus, expréssa signo sanctitátis.

eccedabodesynagogasatanequidicuntseiudeo.en: Behold, I will bring of the synagogue of Satan, who say they are Jews and are not, but do lie.
eccedabodesynagogasatanequidicuntseiudeo.la: Ecce dabo de synagóga Sátanæ, qui dicunt se Judǽos esse, et non sunt, sed mentiúntur.

eccefaciamillosutveniantetadorentanteped.en: Behold, I will make them to come and adore before thy feet: and they shall know that I have loved thee.
eccefaciamillosutveniantetadorentanteped.la: Ecce fáciam illos ut véniant, et adórent ante pedes tuos: et scient quia ego diléxi te.

indiadematecapitisaaronlapidespretiosifu.en: On the diadem of Aaron's head precious stones shone,
indiadematecapitisaaronlapidespretiosifu.la: In diadémate cápitis Aaron lápides pretiósi fulgébant,

dumperficereturopusdeialleluiaalleluiaal.en: While as the work of God was in doing. Alleluia, Alleluia, Alleluia.
dumperficereturopusdeialleluiaalleluiaal.la: Dum perficerétur opus Dei, allelúja, allelúja, allelúja.

etprimusangelustubacecinitetfactestgrand.en: And the first angel sounded the trumpet, and there followed hail and fire, mingled with blood, and it was cast on the earth.
etprimusangelustubacecinitetfactestgrand.la: Et primus Ángelus tuba cécinit, et facta est grando, et ignis, mista in sánguine, et missum est in terram.

ettertiaparsterrecombustestettertiaparsa.en: And the third part of the earth was burnt up, and the third part of the trees was burnt up, and all green grass was burnt up.
ettertiaparsterrecombustestettertiaparsa.la: Et tértia pars terræ combústa est, et tértia pars árborum concremáta est, et omne fœnum víride combústum est.

etabiiadangelumdicenseiutdaretmihilibrum.en: And I went to the angel, saying unto him that he should give me the book.
etabiiadangelumdicenseiutdaretmihilibrum.la: Et ábii ad Ángelum, dicens ei, ut daret mihi librum.

etinuterohabensclamabatparturiensetcruci.en: and being with child, she cried travailing in birth, and was in pain to be delivered.
etinuterohabensclamabatparturiensetcruci.la: et in útero habens, clamábat partúriens, et cruciabátur ut páriat.

etflebuntetplangentsesuperillamregesterr.en: And the kings of the earth shall weep, and bewail themselves over her.
etflebuntetplangentsesuperillamregesterr.la: Et flebunt, et plangent se super illam reges terræ.

quiaveretiustaiudiciasunteiusquiiudicavi.en: For true and just are his judgments, who hath judged the great harlot which corrupted the earth with her fornication, and hath revenged the blood of his servants, at her hands.
quiaveretiustaiudiciasunteiusquiiudicavi.la: quia vera et justa judícia sunt ejus, qui judicávit de meretríce magna, quæ corrúpit terram in prostitutióne sua, et vindicávit sánguinem servórum suórum de mánibus ejus.

etiterumdixeruntalleluietfumuseiusascend.en: And again they said: Alleluia. And her smoke ascendeth for ever and ever.
etiterumdixeruntalleluietfumuseiusascend.la: Et íterum dixérunt: Allelúja. Et fumus ejus ascéndit in sǽcula sæculórum.

etcecideruntsenioresvigintiquatuoretquat.en: And the four and twenty ancients, and the four living creatures fell down and adored God that sitteth upon the throne, saying: Amen; Alleluia.
etcecideruntsenioresvigintiquatuoretquat.la: Et cecidérunt senióres vigínti quátuor, et quátuor animália, et adoravérunt Deum sedéntem super thronum, dicéntes: Amen: allelúja.

etvoxdethronexivitdicenslaudemdicitedeon.en: And a voice came out from the throne, saying: Give praise to our God, all ye his servants; and you that fear him, little and great.
etvoxdethronexivitdicenslaudemdicitedeon.la: Et vox de throno exívit, dicens: Laudem dícite Deo nostro omnes servi ejus: et qui timétis eum pusílli et magni.

etaudiviquasivocemturbemagneetsicutvocem.en: And I heard as it were the voice of a great multitude, and as the voice of many waters, and as the voice of great thunders, saying, Alleluia: for the Lord our God the Almighty hath reigned.
etaudiviquasivocemturbemagneetsicutvocem.la: Et audívi quasi vocem turbæ magnæ, et sicut vocem aquárum multárum, et sicut vocem tonitruórum magnórum, dicéntium: Allelúja: quóniam regnávit Dóminus Deus noster omnípotens.

gaudeamusetexsultemusetdemusgloriameiqui.en: Let us be glad and rejoice, and give glory to him; for the marriage of the Lamb is come, and his wife hath prepared herself.
gaudeamusetexsultemusetdemusgloriameiqui.la: Gaudeámus, et exsultémus: et demus glóriam ei: quia venérunt núptiæ Agni, et uxor ejus præparávit se.

etdatumestilliutcooperiatsebyssinosplend.en: And it is granted to her that she should clothe herself with fine linen, glittering and white. For the fine linen are the justifications of saints.
etdatumestilliutcooperiatsebyssinosplend.la: Et datum est illi ut coopériat se býssino splendénti et cándido. Býssinum enim justificatiónes sunt sanctórum.

etaudivivocemmagnamdethronodicentemeccet.en: And I heard a great voice from the throne, saying: Behold the tabernacle of God with men, and he will dwell with them.
etaudivivocemmagnamdethronodicentemeccet.la: Et audívi vocem magnam de throno dicéntem: Ecce tabernáculum Dei cum homínibus, et habitábit cum eis.

etipsipopuluseiuseruntetipsedeuscumeiser.en: And they shall be his people; and God himself with them shall be their God.
etipsipopuluseiuseruntetipsedeuscumeiser.la: Et ipsi pópulus ejus erunt, et ipse Deus cum eis erit eórum Deus:

etdixitquisedebatinthroneccenovafacioomn.en: And he that sat on the throne said: Behold, I make all things new.
etdixitquisedebatinthroneccenovafacioomn.la: Et dixit qui sedébat in throno: Ecce nova fácio ómnia.

etdixitmihiscribequiahecverbafidelissima.en: And he said to me: Write, for these words are most faithful and true.
etdixitmihiscribequiahecverbafidelissima.la: Et dixit mihi: Scribe, quia hæc verba fidelíssima sunt, et vera.

etsustulitmeinspirituinmontemmagnumetalt.en: And he took me up in spirit to a great and high mountain: and he shewed me the holy city Jerusalem coming down out of heaven from God,
etsustulitmeinspirituinmontemmagnumetalt.la: Et sústulit me in spíritu in montem magnum et altum, et osténdit mihi civitátem sanctam Jerúsalem descendéntem de cælo a Deo,

habentemclaritatemdeietlumeneiussimilela.en: Having the glory of God, and the light thereof was like to a precious stone, as to the jasper stone, even as crystal.
habentemclaritatemdeietlumeneiussimilela.la: habéntem claritátem Dei: et lumen ejus símile lápidi pretióso tamquam lápidi jáspidis, sicut crystállum.

ethabebatmurummagnumetaltumhabentemporta.en: And it had a wall great and high, having twelve gates, and in the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel.
ethabebatmurummagnumetaltumhabentemporta.la: Et habébat murum magnum, et altum, habéntem portas duódecim: et in portis ángelos duódecim, et nómina inscrípta, quæ sunt nómina duódecim tríbuum filiórum Israël.

eteratstructuramurieiusexlapideiaspideip.en: And the building of the wall thereof was of jasper stone: but the city itself pure gold, like to clear glass.
eteratstructuramurieiusexlapideiaspideip.la: Et erat structúra muri ejus ex lápide jáspide: ipsa vero cívitas aurum mundum símile vitro mundo.

quintumsardonyxsextumsardiusseptimumchry.en: The fifth, sardonyx: the sixth, sardius: the seventh, chrysolite: the eighth, beryl: the ninth, a topaz: the tenth, a chrysoprasus: the eleventh, a jacinth: the twelfth, an amethyst.
quintumsardonyxsextumsardiusseptimumchry.la: quintum, sardónyx: sextum, sárdius: séptimum, chrysólithus: octávum, berýllus: nonum, topázius: décimum, chrysóprasus: undécimum, hyacínthus: duodécimum, amethýstus.

etduodecimporteduodecimmargaritesuntpers.en: And the twelve gates are twelve pearls, one to each: and every several gate was of one several pearl. And the street of the city was pure gold, as it were transparent glass.
etduodecimporteduodecimmargaritesuntpers.la: Et duódecim portæ, duódecim margarítæ sunt, per síngulas: et síngulæ portæ erant ex síngulis margarítis: et platéa civitátis aurum mundum, tamquam vitrum perlúcidum.

ettemplumnonvidiineadominusenimdeusomnip.en: And I saw no temple therein. For the Lord God Almighty is the temple thereof, and the Lamb.
ettemplumnonvidiineadominusenimdeusomnip.la: Et templum non vidi in ea: Dóminus enim Deus omnípotens templum illíus est, et Agnus.

etcivitasnonegetsolenequelunautluceantin.en: And the city hath no need of the sun, nor of the moon, to shine in it. For the glory of God hath enlightened it, and the Lamb is the lamp thereof.
etcivitasnonegetsolenequelunautluceantin.la: Et cívitas non eget sole neque luna ut lúceant in ea, nam cláritas Dei illuminávit eam, et lucérna ejus est Agnus.

etdixitmihihecverbafidelissimasuntetvere.en: And he said to me: These words are most faithful and true. And the Lord God of the spirits of the prophets sent his angel to show his servants the things which must be done shortly.
etdixitmihihecverbafidelissimasuntetvere.la: Et dixit mihi: Hæc verba fidelíssima sunt, et vera. Et Dóminus Deus spirítuum prophetárum misit ángelum suum osténdere servis suis quæ opórtet fíeri cito.

etecceveniovelociterbeatusquicustoditver.en: And, Behold I come quickly. Blessed is he that keepeth the words of the prophecy of this book.
etecceveniovelociterbeatusquicustoditver.la: Et ecce vénio velóciter. Beátus, qui custódit verba prophetíæ libri hujus.

etegoioannesquiaudivietvidihecetpostquam.en: And I, John, who have heard and seen these things. And after I had heard and seen, I fell down to adore before the feet of the angel, who showed me these things.
etegoioannesquiaudivietvidihecetpostquam.la: Et ego Joánnes, qui audívi, et vidi hæc. Et postquam audíssem, et vidíssem, cécidi ut adorárem ante pedes ángeli, qui mihi hæc ostendébat.

etdixitmihividenefecerisconservusenimtuu.en: And he said to me: See thou do it not: for I am thy fellow servant, and of thy brethren the prophets, and of them that keep the words of the prophecy of this book. Adore God.
etdixitmihividenefecerisconservusenimtuu.la: Et dixit mihi: Vide ne féceris: consérvus enim tuus sum, et fratrum tuórum prophetárum, et eórum qui servant verba prophetíæ libri hujus: Deum adóra.

etdicitmihinesignaverisverbaprophetielib.en: And he saith to me: Seal not the words of the prophecy of this book: for the time is at hand.
etdicitmihinesignaverisverbaprophetielib.la: Et dicit mihi: Ne signáveris verba prophetíæ libri hujus: tempus enim prope est.

quinocetnoceatadhucetquiinsordibusestsor.en: He that hurteth, let him hurt still: and he that is filthy, let him be filthy still: and he that is just, let him be justified still: and he that is holy, let him be sanctified still.
quinocetnoceatadhucetquiinsordibusestsor.la: Qui nocet, nóceat adhuc: et qui in sórdibus est, sordéscat adhuc: et qui justus est, justificétur adhuc: et sanctus, sanctificétur adhuc.

ecceveniocitetmercesmeamecumestreddereun.en: Behold, I come quickly; and my reward is with me, to render to every man according to his works.
ecceveniocitetmercesmeamecumestreddereun.la: Ecce vénio cito, et merces mea mecum est, réddere unicuíque secúndum ópera sua.

egosumalphetomegaprimusetnovissimusprinc.en: I am Alpha and Omega, the first and the last, the beginning and the end.
egosumalphetomegaprimusetnovissimusprinc.la: Ego sum Alpha et Oméga, primus et novíssimus, princípium et finis.

beatiquilavantstolassuasinsanguineagniut.en: Blessed are they that wash their robes in the blood of the Lamb: that they may have a right to the tree of life, and may enter in by the gates into the city.
beatiquilavantstolassuasinsanguineagniut.la: Beáti, qui lavant stolas suas in sánguine Agni: ut sit potéstas eórum in ligno vitæ, et per portas intrent in civitátem.

narrabonomentuumfratribusmeisalleluiainm.en: I will declare thy name to my brethren, alleluia: in the midst of the Church
narrabonomentuumfratribusmeisalleluiainm.la: Narrábo nomen tuum frátribus meis, allelúja: in médio Ecclésiæ

laudabotealleluiaalleluia.en: I will praise thee, alleluia, alleluia.

confitebortibiinecclesiemagnapopulogravi.en: I will give praise to thee in a great church, among a grave people.
confitebortibiinecclesiemagnapopulogravi.la: Confitébor tibi in ecclésiæ magna, pópulo gravi.

inecclesiisbenedicitedeodominodefontibus.en: In the churches bless ye God, the Lord, from the fountains of Israel,
inecclesiisbenedicitedeodominodefontibus.la: In ecclésiis benedícite Deo, Dómino de fóntibus Israël,

omneshonoratefraternitatemdiligitedeumti.en: Honour all men. Love the brotherhood. Fear God. Honour the king.
omneshonoratefraternitatemdiligitedeumti.la: Omnes honoráte: fraternitátem dilígite: Deum timéte: regem honorificáte.

deepistolaprimabeatipetriapostoli.en: Lesson from the first letter of St. Peter the Apostle
deepistolaprimabeatipetriapostoli.la: De Epístola prima beáti Petri Apóstoli

christussemelpropeccatisnostrismortuuses.en: Christ died once for our sins, the just for the unjust, that he might offer us to God, being put to death indeed in the flesh, but enlivened in the spirit.
christussemelpropeccatisnostrismortuuses.la: Christus semel pro peccátis nostris mórtuus est, justus pro injústis, ut nos offérret Deo, mortificátus quidem carne, vivificátus autem spíritu.

christoigiturpassoincarneetvoseademcogit.en: Christ therefore having suffered in the flesh, be you also armed with the same thought: for he that hath suffered in the flesh, hath ceased from sins:
christoigiturpassoincarneetvoseademcogit.la: Christo ígitur passo in carne, et vos eádem cogitatióne armámini: quia qui passus est in carne, désiit a peccátis:

utiamnondesideriishominumsedvoluntatidei.en: That now he may live the rest of his time in the flesh, not after the desires of men, but according to the will of God.
utiamnondesideriishominumsedvoluntatidei.la: ut jam non desidériis hóminum, sed voluntáti Dei, quod réliquum est in carne vivat témporis.

sufficitenimpreteritumtempusadvoluntatem.en: For the time past is sufficient to have fulfilled the will of the Gentiles, for them who have walked in riotousness, lusts, excess of wine, revellings, banquetings, and unlawful worshipping of idols.
sufficitenimpreteritumtempusadvoluntatem.la: Súfficit enim prætéritum tempus ad voluntátem géntium consummándam his qui ambulavérunt in luxúriis, desidériis, vinoléntiis, comessatiónibus, potatiónibus, et illícitis idolórum cúltibus.

omnisquipetitaccipitetquiqueritinvenitet.en: Every one that asketh, receiveth: and he that seeketh, findeth: and to him that knocketh, it shall be opened, alleluia.
omnisquipetitaccipitetquiqueritinvenitet.la: Omnis qui petit áccipit: et qui quærit, ínvenit: et pulsánti aperiétur, allelúja.

prestaquesumusomnipotensdeusutnostrement.en: Grant, we beseech thee, almighty God: that the intent of our mind may ever tend thither whither the glorious Author of the coming solemnity hath entered; and that whither it goeth by faith, it may attain by its manner of life.
prestaquesumusomnipotensdeusutnostrement.la: Præsta, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut nostræ mentis inténtio quo solemnitátis ventúræ gloriósus Auctor ingréssus est semper inténdat; et quo fide pergit, conversatióne perveniat.

ascendenschristusinaltumcaptivamduxitcap.en: Christ, ascending on high, led captivity captive, he gave gifts to men, alleluia.
ascendenschristusinaltumcaptivamduxitcap.la: Ascéndens Christus in altum, captívam duxit captivitátem, dedit dona homínibus, allelúja. Ps. 112, 116, 145, 146, 147

supercelosdeusalleluia.en: Above the heavens, O God, alleluia.

mundiregisquifabricam.en: Who rulest the fabric of the world,

adtesupernagratia.en: To thee by grace from above.

utcumrepenteceperis.en: That when suddenly thou shalt begin

clarerenubeiudicis.en: To shine in the cloud as Judge,

penasrepellasdebitas.en: Thou mayest put away the punishments due,

reddascoronasperditas.en: And restore the crowns we lost.

quiesfuturuspremium.en: Who art to be our reward:

sitnostraintegloria.en: Let our glory be in thee,

elevatestmagnificentiatuaalleluiaallelui.en: Thy magnificence is elevated, * Alleluia, alleluia.
elevatestmagnificentiatuaalleluiaallelui.la: Eleváta est, magnificéntia tua, * Allelúja, allelúja.

alleluiaascendenschristusinaltumalleluia.en: Alleluia. Christ ascending on high, alleluia, led captivity captive, alleluia, alleluia.
alleluiaascendenschristusinaltumalleluia.la: Allelúja. Ascéndens Christus in altum, allelúja, captívam duxit captivitátem, allelúja, allelúja.

nonrelinquamvosorphanosalleluiavadetveni.en: I will not leave you orphans, alleluia: I go, and I come to you:
nonrelinquamvosorphanosalleluiavadetveni.la: Non relínquam vos órphanos, allelúja: vado et vénio ad vos:

egorogabopatremetaliumparaclitumdabitvob.en: I will pray the Father, and He shall give you another Comforter.
egorogabopatremetaliumparaclitumdabitvob.la: Ego rogábo Patrem, et álium Paráclitum dabit vobis.

euntesinmundumuniversumpredicateevangeli.en: Go ye into the whole world, and preach the Gospel to every creature: he that believeth and is baptized shall be saved, alleluia: but he that believeth not shall be condemned, alleluia.
euntesinmundumuniversumpredicateevangeli.la: Eúntes in mundum univérsum prædicáte Evangélium omni creatúræ: qui credíderit et baptizátus fúerit, salvus erit, allelúja: qui vero non credíderit, condemnábitur, allelúja.

inillotemporedixitiesusdiscipulissuiscum.en: At that time, Jesus said unto His disciples: When the Comforter is come, Whom I will send unto you from the Father, even the Spirit of truth, Which proceedeth from the Father, He shall testify of Me. And so on.
inillotemporedixitiesusdiscipulissuiscum.la: In illo témpore: Dixit Jesus discípulis suis: Cum vénerit Paráclitus, quem ego mittam vobis a Patre, Spíritum veritátis, qui a Patre procédit, ille testimónium perhibébit de me. Et réliqua.

homiliasancticyrilliepiscopialexandrini.en: Homily by St. Cyril, Bishop of Alexandria

identitatemsubstantiefiliiacpatrisostend.en: Showing the identity of substance of the Son and the Father, when he had said the Spirit of truth, he affirmed that he proceedeth from the Father: that the Trinity might be bound together in one principle of Godhead. When therefore the Paraclete shall come, he saith, the Spirit of truth, that is, mine, who proceedeth from the Father, he shall give testimony of me. And how shall he give testimony? Working great miracles in you and through you, he will be a most weighty witness of my divine power and might. For it is my Spirit that will work in you: but as he is mine, so is he also God the Father's.
identitatemsubstantiefiliiacpatrisostend.la: Identitátem substántiæ Filii ac Patris osténdens, cum veritátis Spíritum díxerit, a Patre illum procédere asséruit: ut in unam ratiónem Deitátis Trinitas constringerétur. Quando ígitur vénerit Paráclitus, ait, Spiritus veritátis, id est meus, qui a Patre procédit, ille testimónium perhibébit de me. Quómodo autem perhibébit? Magna in vobis et per vos mirácula fáciens, divinæ meæ potestátis atque virtútis testis erit gravíssimus. Spíritus enim meus est, qui operábitur in vobis: sed sicut meus est, sic et Dei Patris.

heclocutussumvobisutnonscandalizeminisie.en: These things have I spoken to you, that you may not be scandalized. For if, he saith, with you as witnesses, I have done so many and so great wonders, so also will the Paraclete do the like in you: and yet the Jews will not be brought back to better things. Be not troubled if you shall not be able to convert them by your prayer; but remember everywhere my word: that the disciple is not above the master, nor the servant greater than his lord.
heclocutussumvobisutnonscandalizeminisie.la: Hæc locutus sum vobis, ut non scandalizémini. Si enim, inquit, vobis téstibus, tot tantáque mirabília feci, sic Paráclitus quoque in vobis simília fáciet: nec tamen Judæi ad melióra reducéntur. Nolíte conturbári, si oratióne vestra convértere illos non poteritis; sed mementóte ubique sermónis mei: non esse discípulum super magístrum, sed nec servum dómino suo majórem.

absquesynagogisfacientvossedvenithorauto.en: They will put you out of the synagogues: but the hour cometh, that whosoever killeth you will think that he doth a service to God. He foretold the greatest of all dangers: not that by fear he might bring the minds of the disciples to cowardice, but that the greatest dread of death, being despised (since it was foreknown), might make them braver to undergo dangers. For they that despise the greater, how shall they fear the less?
absquesynagogisfacientvossedvenithorauto.la: Absque synagógis fácient vos: sed venit hora, ut omnis qui intérficit vos arbitrétur obséquium se præstáre Deo. Summum ómnium periculórum prædixit: non ut formídine ad ignáviam discipulórum redúceret ánimos, sed ut máximus mortis pavor (quóniam præscirétur) contémptus, fortióres ad subeúnda perícula rédderet. Nam qui majus contemnunt, ii quomodo minóra timébunt?

factumestautemincrastinumutcongregarentu.en: And it came to pass on the morrow, that their princes, and ancients, and scribes, were gathered together in Jerusalem;
factumestautemincrastinumutcongregarentu.la: Factum est autem in crástinum, ut congregaréntur príncipes eórum, et senióres, et scribæ, in Jerúsalem:

etannasprincepssacerdotumetcaiphasetioan.en: And Annas the high priest, and Caiphas, and John, and Alexander, and as many as were of the kindred of the high priest.
etannasprincepssacerdotumetcaiphasetioan.la: et Annas princeps sacerdótum, et Caíphas, et Joánnes, et Alexánder, et quotquot erant de génere sacerdotáli.

etstatuenteseosinmediointerrogabantinqua.en: And setting them in the midst, they asked: By what power, or by what name, have you done this?
etstatuenteseosinmediointerrogabantinqua.la: Et statuéntes eos in médio, interrogábant: In qua virtúte, aut in quo nómine fecístis hoc vos?

tuncrepletusspiritusanctopetrusdixitadeo.en: Then Peter, filled with the Holy Ghost, said to them: Ye princes of the people, and ancients, hear:
tuncrepletusspiritusanctopetrusdixitadeo.la: Tunc replétus Spíritu Sancto Petrus, dixit ad eos: Príncipes pópuli, et senióres, audíte:

sinoshodiediiudicamurinbenefactohominisi.en: If we this day are examined concerning the good deed done to the infirm man, by what means he hath been made whole:
sinoshodiediiudicamurinbenefactohominisi.la: si nos hódie diiudicámur in benefácto hóminis infírmi, in quo iste salvus factus est,

hicestlapisquireprobatusestavobisedifica.en: This is the stone which was rejected by you the builders, which is become the head of the corner.
hicestlapisquireprobatusestavobisedifica.la: Hic est lapis qui reprobátus est a vobis ædificántibus, qui factus est in caput ánguli:

etnonestinalioaliquosalusnecenimaliudnom.en: Neither is there salvation in any other. For there is no other name under heaven given to men, whereby we must be saved.
etnonestinalioaliquosalusnecenimaliudnom.la: et non est in álio áliquo salus. Nec enim áliud nomen est sub cælo datum homínibus, in quo opórteat nos salvos fíeri.

astiteruntregesterreetprincipesconveneru.en: The kings of the earth stood up, and the princes met together against the Lord, and against his Christ.
astiteruntregesterreetprincipesconveneru.la: Astitérunt reges terræ, et príncipes convenérunt in unum advérsus Dóminum, et advérsus Christum ejus.

nequeenimquisquamegenseratinterillos.en: For neither was there any one needy among them.
nequeenimquisquamegenseratinterillos.la: Neque enim quisquam egens erat inter illos.

inillotemporedixitiesusdiscipulissuissid.en: At that time, Jesus said unto His disciples: If ye love Me, keep My commandments. And I will pray the Father, and He shall give you another Comforter. And so on.
inillotemporedixitiesusdiscipulissuissid.la: In illo témpore: Dixit Jesus discípulis suis: Si dilígitis me, mandáta mea serváte. Et ego rogábo Patrem, et álium Paráclitum dabit vobis. Et réliqua.

hicestintrinitatespiritussanctusquempatr.en: This is the Holy Ghost in the Trinity, whom the Catholic faith confesseth to be consubstantial and coeternal with the Father and the Son. He it is of whom the Apostle saith: The charity of God is poured forth in our hearts by the Holy Ghost, who is given to us. How then doth the Lord say, If you love me, keep my commandments, and I will ask the Father, and he shall give you another Paraclete: since he saith this of the Holy Ghost, whom unless we have, we can neither love God nor keep his commandments? How shall we love, that we may receive him, whom unless we have, we are not able to love? Or how shall we keep the commandments, that we may receive him, whom unless we have, we cannot keep the commandments?
hicestintrinitatespiritussanctusquempatr.la: Hic est in Trinitáte Spíritus Sanctus: quem Patri et Fílio consubstantiálem et coætérnum fides cathólica confitétur. Ipse est, de quo dicit Apóstolus: Cáritas Dei diffúsa est in córdibus nostris per Spíritum Sanctum, qui datus est nobis. Quomodo ergo Dóminus dicit, Si dilígitis me, mandáta mea serváte, et ego rogábo Patrem, et álium Paráclitum dabit vobis: cum hoc dicat de Spíritu Sancto, quem nisi habeámus, nec Deum dilígere póssumus, nec ejus mandáta serváre? Quómodo diligémus, ut eum accipiámus, quem nisi habeámus, dilígere non valémus? Aut quómodo mandáta servábimus, ut eum accipiámus, quem nisi habeámus, mandáta serváre non póssumus?

anfortepreceditinnobiscaritasquadiligamu.en: Or perhaps doth the charity by which we love Christ go before in us, that by loving Christ and doing his commandments we may merit to receive the Holy Ghost, so that the charity, not of Christ, which had already gone before, but of God the Father, may be poured forth in our hearts? That is a perverse opinion. For he that believeth that he loveth the Son of God, and loveth not the Father, assuredly loveth not the Son either, but that which he hath feigned for himself. Moreover, it is the voice of the Apostle: No man saith, The Lord Jesus, but in the Holy Ghost. And who saith, The Lord Jesus, but he that loveth him, if he saith it in that manner in which the Apostle wished it to be understood?
anfortepreceditinnobiscaritasquadiligamu.la: An forte præcédit in nobis cáritas, qua diligámus Christum, ut diligéndo Christum eiúsque mandáta faciéndo, mereámur accípere Spíritum Sanctum, ut cáritas, non Christi, quæ jam præcésserat, sed Dei Patris, diffundátur in córdibus nostris? Pervérsa est ista senténtia. Qui enim se Fílium Dei dilígere credit, et Patrem non diligit, profécto nec Fílium díligit, sed quod sibi ipse confínxit. Deinde Apostólica vox est: Nemo dicit, Dóminus Jesus, nisi in Spíritu Sancto. Et quis Dóminum Jesum, nisi qui eum díligit, dicit: si eo modo dicit, quo Apóstolus intélligi vóluit?

iamitaqueapostolidicebantdominusiesusets.en: The Apostles therefore were already saying: The Lord Jesus. And if they said it in such a way as not to say it feignedly, confessing with the mouth, denying with the heart and with deeds: in short, if they said this truly, without doubt they loved. How then did they love, but in the Holy Ghost? It remaineth therefore that we understand that he who loveth hath the Holy Ghost: and by having him meriteth to have more, and by having more loveth more. The disciples therefore already had the Spirit whom the Lord was promising, without whom they did not call him Lord: and yet they did not yet have him as the Lord was promising him.
iamitaqueapostolidicebantdominusiesusets.la: Jam ítaque Apóstoli dicébant: Dóminus Jesus. Et si eo modo dicébant, ut non ficte dícerent, ore confiténtes, corde et factis negántes: prorsus, si veráciter hoc dicébant, procul dúbio diligébant. Quómodo ígitur diligébant, nisi in Spíritu Sancto? Restat ergo ut intelligámus Spíritum Sanctum habére qui díligit: et habéndo meréri ut plus hábeat, et plus habéndo plus díligat. Jam ítaque habébant Spíritum discípuli, quem Dóminus promittébat, sine quo eum Dóminum non dicébant: nec tamen eum adhuc habébant, sicut eum Dóminus promittébat.

prestaquesumusomnipotensdeusutclaritatis.en: Grant, we beseech thee, almighty God, that the brightness of thy glory may shine forth upon us, and that the light of thy light may, by the illumination of the Holy Ghost, strengthen the hearts of those who by thy grace have been born again.
prestaquesumusomnipotensdeusutclaritatis.la: Præsta, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus, ut claritátis tuæ super nos splendor effúlgeat, et lux tuæ lucis corda eórum, qui per grátiam tuam sunt renáti, Sancti Spíritus illustratióne confírmet.

venisanctespiritusrepletuorumcordafideli.en: Come, Holy Ghost, fill the hearts of thy faithful, and kindle in them the fire of thy love: who through the diversity of many tongues hast gathered the nations in the unity of faith, alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.
venisanctespiritusrepletuorumcordafideli.la: Veni Sancte Spíritus: reple tuórum corda fidélium, et tui amóris in eis ignem accénde: qui per diversitátem linguárum multárum gentes in unitáte fídei congregásti, allelúia, allelúia, allelúia. Ps. 145, 146, 147

quiergodeumverediligitquieiusmandatacust.en: Whoso therefore truly loveth God, whoso keepeth his commandments, into his heart the Lord both cometh and maketh his abode: for the love of the Godhead so penetrateth him, that in the time of temptation he departeth not from this love. He therefore truly loveth, whose mind, to wit, evil delight overcometh not by consent.
quiergodeumverediligitquieiusmandatacust.la: Qui ergo Deum vere diligit, qui ejus mandáta custódit, in ejus corde Dóminus et venit et mansiónem facit: quia sic eum amor penetrat Divinitátis, ut ab hoc amóre tentatiónis témpore non recédat. Ille ergo vere amat, cujus vidélicet mentem delectatio prava ex consensu non súperat.

apparueruntapostolisdispertitelinguetamq.en: There appeared to the Apostles parted tongues as it were of fire, and the Holy Ghost sat upon every one of them.
apparueruntapostolisdispertitelinguetamq.la: Apparuérunt Apóstolis dispertítæ linguæ tamquam ignis, sedítque supra síngulos eórum Spíritus Sanctus.

factaautemhacvoceconvenitmultitudetmente.en: And when this was noised abroad, the multitude came together, and were confounded in mind, because that every man heard them speak in his own tongue.
factaautemhacvoceconvenitmultitudetmente.la: Facta autem hac voce, convénit multitúdo, et mente confúsa est, quóniam audiébat unusquísque lingua sua illos loquéntes.

inillotemporedixitiesusnicodemosicdeusdi.en: At that time, Jesus said unto Nicodemus: God so loved the world that He gave His Only-begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in Him should not perish, but have everlasting life. And so on.
inillotemporedixitiesusnicodemosicdeusdi.la: In illo témpore: Dixit Jesus Nicodémo: Sic Deus diléxit mundum, ut Fílium suum unigénitum daret: ut omnis, qui credit in eum, non péreat, sed hábeat vitam ætérnam. Et réliqua.

nostisfratresquiainvidiadiabolimorsintra.en: You know, brethren, that by the envy of the devil death came into the world. But Jesus the Son of God took death upon him and hung death upon the cross, and by that very death mortals are delivered. As Moses, he saith, lifted up the serpent in the desert, so must the Son of man be lifted up. A great mystery. As they that looked upon that serpent perished not by the bites of the serpents; so they that look by faith upon the death of Christ are healed of the bites of sins. But those were healed unto temporal life, these unto life eternal.
nostisfratresquiainvidiadiabolimorsintra.la: Nostis, fratres, quia invidia diáboli mors intrávit in mundum. Jesus autem Filius Dei mortem suscepit et mortem suspéndit in cruce, et de ipsa morte liberántur mortáles. Sicut, inquit, Móyses exaltávit serpéntem in desérto, ita exaltári opórtet Filium hóminis. Magnum sacramentum. Quomodo qui intuebantur illum serpéntem, non períbant morsibus serpentum; sic qui intuentur fide mortem Christi, sanántur a mórsibus peccatórum. Sed illi sanabántur ad vitam temporálem, hi autem ad vitam ætérnam.

nonenimmisitdeusfiliumsuuminmundumutiudi.en: For God sent not his Son into the world to judge the world, but that the world may be saved by him. Therefore, as far as lieth in the physician, he came to heal the sick man. He slayeth himself who will not keep the precepts of the physician. The Saviour came into the world. Why was he called the Saviour of the world, but that he might save the world, not judge the world? Thou wilt not be saved by him? Thou shalt be judged of thyself. And why do I say, Thou shalt be judged? See what he saith: He that believeth in him is not judged. But he that believeth not: what didst thou hope he would say, but, Is judged? Already, he saith, he is judged.
nonenimmisitdeusfiliumsuuminmundumutiudi.la: Non enim misit Deus Filium suum in mundum, ut judicet mundum, sed ut salvétur mundus per ipsum. Ergo, quantum in médico est, sanáre venit ægrótum. Ipse se interimít, qui præcépta médici serváre non vult. Venit Salvátor in mundum. Quare Salvátor dictus est mundi, nisi ut salvet mundum, non ut júdicet mundum? Salvári non vis ab ipso? ex te judicáberis. Et quid dicam, Judicáberis? Vide quid ait: Qui credit in eum, non judicátur. Qui autem non credit: quid dictúrum sperábas, nisi, Judicátur? Jam, inquit, judicátus est.

disciplinametsapientiamdocuiteosdominusa.en: The Lord taught them discipline and wisdom, alleluia: he strengthened in them the grace of the Holy Ghost,
disciplinametsapientiamdocuiteosdominusa.la: Disciplinam et sapiéntiam dócuit eos Dóminus, allelúja: firmávit in illis grátiam Spíritus Sancti,

etintellectuadimplevitcordeorumalleluiaa.en: And filled their hearts with understanding, alleluia, alleluia.
etintellectuadimplevitcordeorumalleluiaa.la: Et intelléctu adimplévit corda eórum, allelúja, allelúja.

repentinonamquesonituspiritussanctussupe.en: For with a sudden sound the Holy Ghost came upon them.
repentinonamquesonituspiritussanctussupe.la: Repentíno namque sónitu Spíritus Sanctus super eos venit.

nondumapparuitiudiciumsediamfactumestiud.en: The judgment hath not yet appeared: but the judgment is already made. For the Lord knoweth who are his: he knoweth who abide unto the crown, who abide unto the flame. He knoweth in his floor the wheat, he knoweth also the chaff: he knoweth the corn, he knoweth also the cockle. He that believeth not is already judged. Why judged? Because he believeth not in the name of the only-begotten Son of God. And this is the judgment: because the light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than the light: for their works were evil.
nondumapparuitiudiciumsediamfactumestiud.la: Nondum apparuit judicium: sed jam factum est judicium. Novit enim Dóminus qui sunt ejus: novit qui permaneant ad corónam, qui permaneant ad flammām. Novit in área sua tríticum, novit et páleam: novit ségetem, novit et zizánia. Jam judicátus est qui non credit. Quare judicátus? Quia non credit in nomine unigéniti Fílii Dei. Hoc est autem judicium: quja lux venit in mundum, et dilexérunt hómines magis ténebras quam lucem: erant enim mala ópera eórum.

forteipsiperianuamintraveruntabsit.en: Did they perchance enter in by the door? God forbid.
forteipsiperianuamintraveruntabsit.la: Forte ipsi per jánuam intravérunt? Absit.

inillotemporedixitiesusturbisiudeorumnem.en: At that time, Jesus said unto the multitudes of the Jews: No man can come to Me, except the Father, Which hath sent me, draw him. And so on.
inillotemporedixitiesusturbisiudeorumnem.la: In illo témpore: Dixit Jesus turbis Judæórum: Nemo potest veníre ad me, nisi Pater, qui misit me, tráxerit eum. Et réliqua.

tractinioannpostinit.en: Treatise 26 on John, after the beginning

magnagratiecommendationemovenitnisitract.en: A great commendation of grace. No man cometh unless drawn. Whom he draweth, and whom he draweth not, why he draweth this one, and draweth not that one, seek not to judge, if thou wouldst not err. Once for all receive it, and understand. Art thou not yet drawn? Pray that thou mayest be drawn. What do we say here, brethren? If we are drawn to Christ, then we believe unwillingly, then violence is used, the will is not aroused. Think not that thou art drawn against thy will: the mind is drawn also by love. Nor say thou, How do I believe with my will, if I am drawn? I say: It is little to be drawn by the will; thou art drawn even by delight.
magnagratiecommendationemovenitnisitract.la: Magna grátiæ commendátio. Nemo venit, nisi tractus. Quem trahat, et quem non trahat, quare istum trahat, et illum non trahat, noli velle judicáre, si non vis erráre. Semel áccipe, et intéllige. Nondum tráheris: ora ut traháris. Quid hic dicimus, fratres? Si tráhimur ad Christum, ergo inviti crédimus, ergo violéntia adhibétur, non volúntas excitátur. Noli cogitáre te invítum trahi: trahitur ánimus et amóre. Nec dicas, Quómodo voluntáte credo, si trahor? Ego dico: Parum est voluntáte étiam tráheris voluptáte.

estquedamvoluptascisestillecelestisporro.en: There is a certain pleasure of the body; there is that heavenly one also. Moreover, if the poet could say, Each man is drawn by his own pleasure; not necessity, but pleasure; not obligation, but delight: how much more strongly ought we to say that a man is drawn to Christ, who delighteth in truth, delighteth in blessedness, delighteth in justice, delighteth in everlasting life, all which Christ is! Give me one that loveth, and he feeleth what I say: give me one that longeth, give me one that is fervent, give me one that is a pilgrim in this wilderness and thirsteth, and sigheth for the fountain of the eternal fatherland: give me such a one, and he knoweth what I say.
estquedamvoluptascisestillecelestisporro.la: Est quædam voluptas cis est ille cæléstis. Porro si poétæ dícere lícuit, Trahit sua quemque volúptas; non necessitas, sed voluptas; non obligátio, sed delectatio: quanto fórtius nos dícere debémus trahi hóminem ad Christum, qui delectátur veritáte, delectátur beatitúdine, delectátur justítia, delectátur sempitérna vita, quod totum Christus est! Da amántem et sentit quod dico: da desiderántem, da fervéntem, da in ista solitúdine peregrinántem atque sitientem et fontem ætérnæ pátriæ suspirántem: da talem, et scit quid dicam.

factaautemhacvoceconvenitmultitudetmente.en: And when this voice was made, the multitude came together, and were confounded in mind, because that every man heard in his own tongue
factaautemhacvoceconvenitmultitudetmente.la: Facta autem hac voce, convénit multitúdo, et mente confúsa est, quóniam audiébat unusquísque lingua sua

illosloquentesmagnaliadeialleluiaallelui.en: Them speaking the wonderful works of God, alleluia, alleluia.
illosloquentesmagnaliadeialleluiaallelui.la: Illos loquéntes, magnália Dei, allelúja, allelúja.

nonneecceomnesistiquiloquunturgalileisun.en: Behold, are not all these that speak Galileans? and how have we heard every man our own tongue wherein we were born?
nonneecceomnesistiquiloquunturgalileisun.la: Nonne ecce omnes isti qui loquúntur, Galilǽi sunt? et quómodo nos audívimus unusquísque linguam nostram in qua nati sumus?

etegoresuscitabeuminnovissimodiereddoill.en: And I will raise him up in the last day. I render unto him that which he loveth; I render that which he hopeth. He shall see that which, not yet seeing, he believed; he shall eat that for which he hungered; he shall be filled with that for which he thirsted. Where? In the resurrection of the dead, because I will raise him up in the last day. For it is written in the Prophets: And they shall all be taught of God. Why have I said this, O ye Jews? The Father hath not taught you: how can ye know me? All the men of that kingdom shall be taught of God: they shall not hear from men. And even if they hear from men; yet that which they understand is given within, shineth within, is revealed within.
etegoresuscitabeuminnovissimodiereddoill.la: Et ego resuscitabo eum in novíssimo die. Reddo illi quod amat; reddo quod sperat. Vidébit quod adhuc non vidéndo créco didit, manducabit quod esúriit, saturábitur quod sitívit. Ubi? In resurrectióne mortuórum, quia ego resuscitábo eum in novissimo die. Scriptum est enim in Prophétis: Et erunt omnes docíbiles Dei. Quare hoc dixi, o Judæi? Pater vos non dócuit: quómodo me potéstis agnóscere? Omnes regni illíus hómines docíbiles Dei erunt: non ab hominibus audient. Et si ab hominibus áudiunt; tamen, quod intelligunt intus datur, intus corúscat, intus revelátur.

inillotemporesurgensiesusdesynagogaintro.en: At that time Jesus arose out of the synagogue, and entered into Simon's house. And Simon's wife's mother was taken with a great fever. And so on.
inillotemporesurgensiesusdesynagogaintro.la: In illo témpore: Surgens Jesus de synagóga, introívit in domum Simónis. Socrus autem Simónis tenebátur magnis fébribus. Et réliqua.

sivirumademonioliberatumanimumabimmundac.en: If we have said that the man delivered from the devil signifieth the soul cleansed from unclean thought: the woman held by fevers, but healed at the Lord's command, showeth the flesh bridled from the heat of its concupiscence by the precepts of continence. For all bitterness and anger and indignation and clamour and blasphemy is the fury of the unclean spirit: but fornication, uncleanness, lust, evil concupiscence and covetousness, which is the service of idols, understand to be the fever of the enticing flesh.
sivirumademonioliberatumanimumabimmundac.la: Si virum a dæmónio liberátum, ánimum ab immúnda cogitatióne purgátum significáre dixérimus: fémina fébribus tenta, sed ad impérium Dómini curáta, carnem osténdit a concupiscéntiæ suæ fervóre per continéntiæ præcépta frenátam. Omnis enim amaritúdo et ira et indignátio et clamor et blasphémia spíritus immúndi furor est: fornicatiónem vero, immunditiam, libidinem, concupiscéntiam malam et avarítiam, quæ est simulacrórum sérvitus, febrem illecebrósæ carnis intéllige.

etrogaveruntillumpreetstanssuperillamimp.en: And they besought him for her. And standing over her, he commanded the fever: and it left her. Now when besought, now of his own accord, the Saviour healeth the sick: showing that against the passions of sinners also he ever granteth the prayers of the faithful, and that those things which they themselves least understand in themselves he either giveth them to understand, or even forgiveth them though not understood: according to that which the Psalmist asketh: Who can understand sins? From my secret ones cleanse me, O Lord.
etrogaveruntillumpreetstanssuperillamimp.la: Et rogavérunt illum pro ea. Et stans super illam imperávit febri: et dimisit illam. Modo Salvátor rogátus, modo ultro curat ægrótos: osténdens se contra peccatórum quoque passiónes précibus semper annúere fidélium, et ea, quæ ipsi mínime in se intélligunt, vel intelligénda dare vel étiam non intellécta dimíttere: juxta quod Psalmísta póstulat: Delicta quis intélligit? Ab occúltis meis munda me, Dómine.

etcontinuosurgensministrabatillisnaurale.en: And immediately rising, she ministered to them. It is natural to those who are sick of a fever, when health beginneth, to grow weary and to feel the burden of the sickness: but the health which is conferred by the command of the Lord returneth whole at once. Nor doth it only return: but with such strength accompanying it, that it sufficeth to minister immediately: and according to the laws of the moral sense, the members which had served uncleanness unto iniquity, that they might bring forth fruit unto death, should serve justice unto life everlasting.
etcontinuosurgensministrabatillisnaurale.la: Et contínuo surgens ministrábat illis. Naurále est febricitántibus incipiénte sanitáte lasséscere et ægrotatiónis seníre moléstiam: verum sánitas, quæ Dómini confértur império, simul tota redit. Nec solum ipsa redit: sed et tanto róbore comitánte, ut contínuo ministráre suffíciat: et juxta leges tropologíæ, membra, quæ servíerant immundítiæ ad iniquitátem, ut fructificárent morti, sérviant justítiæ in vitam ætérnam.

vespereautemfactocumsoloccidissetvenieba.en: And when it was evening, after sunset, all that were ill came to Jesus: and he, laying his hands on every one of them, healed them, alleluia.
vespereautemfactocumsoloccidissetvenieba.la: Véspere autem facto, cum sol occidísset, veniébant ad Jesum omnes male habéntes: at ille, síngulis manus impónens, curábat eos, allelúja.

obeatetbenedictetgloriosatrinitaspateret.en: O blessed * and blessed and glorious Trinity: Father and Son and Holy Ghost.
obeatetbenedictetgloriosatrinitaspateret.la: O beáta * et benedícta et gloriósa Trínitas: Pater et Fílius et Spíritus Sanctus. Ps. 112, 116, 145, 146, 147

tecelorummilitia.en: Thee the host of the heavens

triplexquemundimachina.en: And the threefold fabric of the world

adduoprioresversussequentisstrophegenfle.en: At the first two lines of the following strophe all kneel:
adduoprioresversussequentisstrophegenfle.la: Ad duo priores versus sequentis strophæ genflectitur:

adsumusetnoscernui.en: We also are here, bowed down,

votaprecesquesupplicum.en: The vows and prayers of thy suppliants

hymnisiungecelestium.en: Join to the hymns of them of heaven.

unumtelumencredimus.en: One light we believe thee to be,

quodetteridemcolimus.en: Which thrice the same we also worship:

alphetomegaquemdicimus.en: Whom we call Alpha and Omega,

lauspatrisitingenito.en: Praise be to the Father unbegotten,

laussitsanctospiritui.en: Praise be to the Holy Ghost,

unaigiturpaterlogosparaclitusquesubstant.en: One therefore is the substance of the Father, the Word, and the Paraclete: O blessed Trinity.
unaigiturpaterlogosparaclitusquesubstant.la: Una ígitur Pater, Logos, Paraclitúsque substántia est: o beáta Trínitas. Ps. 97

deepistolaprimabeatiioannisapostoli.en: Lesson from the first letter of St. John the Apostle
deepistolaprimabeatiioannisapostoli.la: De Epístola prima beáti Joánnis Apóstoli

magnusdominusetlaudabilisnimis.en: Great is the Lord, and greatly to be praised;

etmagnitudiniseiusnonestfinis.en: And of his greatness there is no end.
etmagnitudiniseiusnonestfinis.la: Et magnitúdinis ejus non est finis.

patrisnatiparacliti.en: Of the Father, the Son, the Paraclete

extergesordesmentium.en: Wipe away the stains of our minds,

sortimisertuspauperum.en: Having pity on the lot of the poor.

orodomineutfiatspiritustuusduplexinmeati.en: I pray thee, O Lord, that thy double spirit may be in me. And he said: If thou see me when I am taken from thee, thou shalt have what thou hast asked.
orodomineutfiatspiritustuusduplexinmeati.la: Oro, Dómine, ut fiat spíritus tuus duplex in me. At ille inquit: Si víderis, quando tollar a te, erit tibi quod petísti.

veniteliasinbersabeeiudetdimisitibipueru.en: He came to Bersabee of Juda, and left his servant there,
veniteliasinbersabeeiudetdimisitibipueru.la: Venit Elías in Bersabée Juda, et dimísit ibi púerum suum,

comedifavumcummellemeoalleluia.en: I have eaten the honeycomb with my honey, alleluia.
comedifavumcummellemeoalleluia.la: Comédi favum cum melle meo, allelúja.

bibivinummeumcumlactemeoalleluia.en: I have drunk my wine with my milk, alleluia.
bibivinummeumcumlactemeoalleluia.la: Bibi vinum meum cum lacte meo, allelúja.

alleluiapanisquemegodederoalleluiacarome.en: Alleluia. The bread that I will give, alleluia, is my flesh for the life of the world, alleluia, alleluia.
alleluiapanisquemegodederoalleluiacarome.la: Allelúja. Panis quem ego dédero, allelúja, caro mea est pro mundi vita, allelúja, allelúja.

laudatedominumquoniamconfirmatestsuperno.en: Praise ye the Lord, for his mercy is confirmed upon us.
laudatedominumquoniamconfirmatestsuperno.la: Laudáte Dóminum, quóniam confirmáta est super nos misericórdia ejus. Ps. 112, 116, 145, 146, 147

miseratoretmisericorsdominus.en: The Lord is compassionate and merciful.

haurietisaquasingaudioalleluiadefontibus.en: You shall draw waters with joy, alleluia, out of the Saviour's fountains, alleluia, alleluia.
haurietisaquasingaudioalleluiadefontibus.la: Hauriétis aquas in gáudio, allelúja, de fóntibus Salvatóris, allelúja, allelúja.

cumsenuissetsamuelposuitfiliossuosiudice.en: When Samuel was old, he appointed his sons to be judges over Israel.
cumsenuissetsamuelposuitfiliossuosiudice.la: Cum senuísset Sámuel, pósuit fílios suos júdices Israël.

quoniamquasipeccatumariolandiestrepugnar.en: Because it is like the sin of witchcraft, to rebel: and like the crime of idolatry, to refuse to obey.
quoniamquasipeccatumariolandiestrepugnar.la: Quóniam quasi peccátum ariolándi est, repugnáre: et quasi scelus idololatríæ, nolle acquiéscere.

etaitdaviddominusquieripuitmedemanuleoni.en: And David said: The Lord who delivered me out of the paw of the lion, and out of the paw of the bear, he will deliver me out of the hand of this Philistine.
etaitdaviddominusquieripuitmedemanuleoni.la: Et ait David: Dóminus qui erípuit me de manu leónis, et de manu ursi, ipse me liberábit de manu Philisthǽi hujus.

etaccipiensiesusseptempanesgratiasagensb.en: And Jesus, taking * the seven loaves, giving thanks, blessed, and broke, and gave to his disciples for to set before them; and they set them before the people, alleluia.
etaccipiensiesusseptempanesgratiasagensb.la: Et accípiens * Jesus septem panes, grátias agens, benedíxit, et fregit, et dedit discípulis suis ut appónerent, et apposuérunt turbæ, allelúja.

delibrosecundoregum.en: Lesson from the second book of Samuel

adquosrexaitquodvobisvideturrectumhocfac.en: And the king said to them: What seemeth good to you, that will I do. And the king stood by the gate.
adquosrexaitquodvobisvideturrectumhocfac.la: Ad quos rex ait: Quod vobis vidétur rectum, hoc fáciam. Stetit ergo rex juxta portam.

egrediebaturquepopulusperturmassuascente.en: And all the people went forth by their troops, by hundreds and by thousands.
egrediebaturquepopulusperturmassuascente.la: Egrediebatúrque pópulus per turmas suas centéni et milléni.

sadocverosacerdosetbanaiasfiliusioiadeet.en: But Sadoc the priest, and Banaias the son of Joiada, and Nathan the prophet, and Semei, and Rei, and the strength of David's army was not with Adonias.
sadocverosacerdosetbanaiasfiliusioiadeet.la: Sadoc vero sacérdos, et Banájas fílius Jójadæ, et Nathan prophéta, et Sémei et Rei, et robur exércitus David non erat cum Adonía.

villicusproprievillegubernatoresteconomu.en: A villicus is properly the governor of a farm: but a steward is the dispenser both of money and of produce and of all things which the master possesseth. This steward therefore was accused unto his lord, that he had wasted his goods. And he called him, and said: How is it that I hear this of thee? Give an account of thy stewardship: for now thou canst be steward no longer. And he said within himself: What shall I do, because my lord taketh away from me the stewardship? To dig I am not able; to beg I am ashamed.
villicusproprievillegubernatoresteconomu.la: Víllicus próprie villæ gubernátor est: œcónomus autem tam pecuniæ quam frugum et ómnium, quæ dóminus póssidet, dispensátor est. Iste igitur dispensátor accusátus est apud dóminum suum, quod dissipáret substántiam ejus. Quo vocáto, dixit: Quid hoc áudio de te? Redde ratiónem dispensatiónis tuæ: neque enim in ea ultra dispensábis. Qui dixit in semetípso: Quid fáciam, quia dóminus meus aufert a me dispensatiónem? fódere non váleo, mendicáre erubésco.

dixitquedavidaddominumcumvidissetangelum.en: And David said to the Lord, when he saw the Angel striking the people: It is I that have sinned, I have done wickedly; these that are the sheep, what have they done?
dixitquedavidaddominumcumvidissetangelum.la: Dixítque David ad Dóminum, cum vidísset Angelum cædéntem pópulum: Ego sum qui peccávi, ego qui iníque egi; isti, qui oves sunt, quid fecérunt?

filioautemeiusdabotribumunam.en: but to his son I will give one tribe.
filioautemeiusdabotribumunam.la: fílio autem ejus dabo tribum unam.

etabiitisrelintabernaculasua.en: So Israel departed to their dwellings.
etabiitisrelintabernaculasua.la: Et ábiit Israël in tabernácula sua.

sermdeverbisdominicircamedium.en: Sermon 36 on the words of the Lord, about the middle
sermdeverbisdominicircamedium.la: Serm. 36 de verbis Domini, circa medium

gratiastibideusquianonsumsicutceterihomi.en: I give thee thanks, O God, that I am not as the rest of men. He might at least have said, As many men. What is, As the rest of men, but all except himself? I, saith he, am just, the rest are sinners. I fast twice in a week: I give tithes of all that I possess. What he asked of God, seek in his words, and thou shalt find nothing. He went up to pray: he would not ask God, but praise himself. It is a small thing not to ask God, but to praise himself; but moreover to insult him that asked.
gratiastibideusquianonsumsicutceterihomi.la: Grátias tibi Deus, quia non sum sicut céteri hómines. Diceret saltem, Sicut multi hómines. Quid est, Sicut céteri hómines, nisi omnes præter ipsum? Ego, inquit, justus sum, céteri peccatóres. Jeiúno bis in sábbato: décimas do ómnium quæ possídeo. Quid rogáverit Deum, quære in verbis ejus, et nihil invénies. Ascéndit oráre: nóluit Deum rogáre, sed se laudáre. Parum est, non Deum rogáre, sed se laudáre; insuper et rogánti insultáre.

duohominesascenderuntintemplumutorarentu.en: Two men went up into the temple to pray, the one a Pharisee and the other a publican: this man went down into his house justified rather than the other, alleluia.
duohominesascenderuntintemplumutorarentu.la: Duo hómines ascendérunt in templum ut orárent, unus pharisæus et alter publicánus: descéndit hic justificátus in domum suam ab illo, allelúja.

delibroquartoregum.en: Lesson from the second book of Kings

cumquevenissentadiordanemcedebantligna.en: And when they were come to the Jordan, they cut down wood.
cumquevenissentadiordanemcedebantligna.la: Cumque veníssent ad Jordánem, cædébant ligna.

cumqueorasseteliseusaitdomineaperioculos.en: And Eliseus prayed, and said: Lord, open his eyes, that he may see.
cumqueorasseteliseusaitdomineaperioculos.la: Cumque orásset Eliséus, ait: Dómine, áperi óculos huius, ut vídeat.

etaperuitdominusoculospuerietviditetecce.en: And the Lord opened the eyes of the servant, and he saw: and behold, the mountain was full of horses, and chariots of fire round about Eliseus.
etaperuitdominusoculospuerietviditetecce.la: Et apéruit Dóminus óculos púeri, et vidit: et ecce mons plenus equórum et cúrruum igneórum in circúitu Eliséi.

duxitergeosinsamariam.en: So he led them into Samaria:

atilleaitnonpercutiesnequeenimcepistieos.en: And he said: Thou shalt not kill them: for thou didst not take them with thy sword, or thy bow.
atilleaitnonpercutiesnequeenimcepistieos.la: At ille ait: Non percúties: neque enim cepísti eos gládio et arcu tuo.

dixitqueeieliseusvadediceisanaberisporro.en: And Eliseus said to him: Go tell him: Thou shalt recover: but the Lord hath shown me that he shall surely die.
dixitqueeieliseusvadediceisanaberisporro.la: Dixítque ei Eliséus: Vade, dic ei: Sanáberis: porro osténdit mihi Dóminus quia morte moriétur.

conversusqueestetedificavitexcelsaquedis.en: And he turned, and built up the high places, which Ezechias his father had destroyed.
conversusqueestetedificavitexcelsaquedis.la: Conversúsque est, et ædificávit excélsa quæ dissipáverat Ezechías pater ejus.

eterexitarasbaaletfecitlucossicutfecerat.en: And he set up altars to Baal, and made groves, as Achab the king of Israel had done, and he adored all the host of heaven, and served it.
eterexitarasbaaletfecitlucossicutfecerat.la: Et eréxit aras Baal, et fecit lucos sicut fécerat Achab rex Israël, et adorávit omnem milítiam cæli, et cóluit eam.

ettraduxitfiliumsuumperignemetariolatuse.en: And he made his son pass through fire: and he used divinations, and observed omens, and appointed pythons.
ettraduxitfiliumsuumperignemetariolatuse.la: Et tradúxit fílium suum per ignem: et ariolátus est, et observávit augúria, et fecit pythónes.

similisillinonfuitanteeumrexquirevertere.en: There was no king before him like unto him, that returned to the Lord with all his heart, and with all his soul, and with all his strength.
similisillinonfuitanteeumrexquirevertere.la: Símilis illi non fuit ante eum rex, qui reverterétur ad Dóminum in omni corde suo, et in tota ánima sua, et in univérsa virtúte sua.

homoquidamdescendebatabierusaleminierich.en: A certain man went down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and fell among robbers. Jericho is a figure of this world, into which Adam, cast out of paradise, that is, out of that heavenly Jerusalem, went down by the fall of his transgression, that is, passing from the things of life to the things of hell: for whom not a change of place, but a change of manners made the exile of his nature. For he was far changed from that Adam who enjoyed unblemished blessedness. When he turned aside unto worldly sins, he fell among robbers: among whom he would not have fallen, had he not, straying from the heavenly commandment, made himself liable to them.
homoquidamdescendebatabierusaleminierich.la: Homo quidam descendébat ab Jerúsalem in Jéricho, et incidit in latrónes. Jéricho figúra hujus mundi est, in quam de paradíso, hoc est, de Jerúsalem illa cælésti eiéctus Adam, prævaricatiónis prolapsióne descéndit, hoc est, de vitálibus ad inférna démigrans: cui non loci, sed morum mutátio natúræ suæ fecit exsílium. Longe enim mutátus ab illo Adam, qui inoffénsa beatitúdine fruebátur. Ubi in sæculária peccáta defléxit, íncidit in latrónes: in quos non incidisset, nisi his, mandáti cæléstis dévius, se fecisset obnoxium.

libcomminmatthcap.en: Book of Commentary on Matthew, chap. 6

nonpotestisdeoservireetmammonemammonaser.en: You cannot serve God and mammon. In the Syriac tongue riches are called mammon. Let the covetous man hear this: let him hear who is reckoned by the Christian name, that he cannot serve at the same time riches and Christ. And yet he said not, He that hath riches: but, He that serveth riches. For he that is the servant of riches keepeth riches as a servant: but he that hath shaken off the yoke of servitude distributeth them as a master.
nonpotestisdeoservireetmammonemammonaser.la: Non potéstis Deo servíre et mammónae. Mammóna sermóne Syríaco divítiæ nuncupántur. Audiat hoc avárus: áudiat, qui censétur vocábulo christiáno, non posse se simul divitiis Christóque servíre. Et tamen non dixit, Qui habet divítias: sed, Qui servit divitiis. Qui enim divitiárum servus est, divitias custódit ut servus: qui autem servitútis excússit jugum, distribuit eas ut dóminus.

hydropismorbusabaquosohumorevocabulumtra.en: The disease of dropsy draweth its name from a watery humour: for in Greek water is called hydor. Now it is a humour under the skin, born of a fault of the bladder, with a swelling inflation and fetid breath. And it is proper to the dropsical man, the more he aboundeth with disordered humour, the more to thirst. And therefore he is rightly compared to him whom the overflowing flood of carnal pleasures weigheth down. He is compared also to the covetous rich man, who the more abundant he is in riches, which he useth not well, the more ardently doth he covet such things.
hydropismorbusabaquosohumorevocabulumtra.la: Hydrópis morbus ab aquóso humóre vocábulum trahit: Græce enim hydor aqua vocátur. Est autem humor subcutáneus de vítio vesícæ natus cum inflatióne turgénte, et anhélitu fœtido. Propriúmque est hydrópici, quanto magis abúndat humore inordináto, tanto ámplius sitíre. Et ideo recte comparátur ei, quem fluxus carnálium voluptátum exúberans ággravat. Comparátur étiam diviti aváro, qui quanto est copiósior divitiis, quibus non bene útitur, tanto ardéntius tália concupiscit.

quoddiciturrespondisseiesusadhocrespicit.en: That Jesus is said to have answered, looketh to that which was set before: And they watched him. For the Lord knoweth the thoughts of men. But rightly do they hold their peace when questioned, who see that whatsoever they should say is said against themselves. For if it be lawful to heal on the sabbath, why do they watch the Saviour whether he will heal? If it be not lawful, why do they themselves care for their cattle on the sabbath? But he, taking him, healed him, and sent him away.
quoddiciturrespondisseiesusadhocrespicit.la: Quod dicitur respondísse Jesus, ad hoc respicit, quod præmissum est: Et ipsi observábant eum. Dóminus enim novit cogitatiónes hóminum. Sed mérito interrogáti tacent, qui contra se dictum, quidquid díxerint, vident. Nam si licet sábbato curare, quare Salvatórem, an curet, obsérvant? Si non licet, quare ipsi in sábbato pécora curant? Ipse vero apprehénsum sanávit eum, ac dimísit.

providadispensationedominusantelegisperi.en: By a provident dispensation the Lord healeth the man with the dropsy before the lawyers and Pharisees; and soon disputeth against covetousness, that namely by this sickness of the body the sickness of heart in them might be expressed. Lastly, after many exhortations of his discourse it is added: Now the Pharisees, who were covetous, heard all these things, and they derided him.
providadispensationedominusantelegisperi.la: Provida dispensatióne Dóminus ante Legisperítos, et Pharisæos hydrópicum curat; et mox contra avaritiam dísputat, ut vidélicet per hanc ægritúdinem córporis in illis exprimerétur ægritúdo cordis. Dénique post multa disputa-tiónis ejus hortaménta subjúnctum est: Audiébant autem ómnia hæc Pharisæi, qui erant avári, et deridébant illum.

indiversmatthlochom.en: On divers places of Matthew, Homily 16.

conveneruntutmultitudinevincerentquemrat.en: They came together, that by numbers they might conquer him whom they could not overcome by reason. They confessed themselves naked of truth, who armed themselves with numbers. For they said among themselves: Let one speak for all, and let all of us speak through one: so that if he conquer, we may all seem conquerors; but if he be conquered, he alone may seem confounded. O ye Pharisees, who think and do all things because of men! First indeed coming with one, ye are to be conquered by one.
conveneruntutmultitudinevincerentquemrat.la: Convenérunt, ut multitúdine vincerent, quem ratióne superáre non póterant. A veritáte nudos se esse professi sunt, qui multitudine se armavérunt. Dicébant enim apud se : Unus loquátur pro ómnibus, et omnes loquámur per unum: ut si quidem vicerit, omnes videámur victóres; si autem victus fúerit, vel solus videátur confúsus. O Pharisæi, qui ómnia propter hómines cogitátis, et fácitis! Primum quidem veniéntes cum uno, vincéndi estis per unum.

tamenputatisquiaunovictohominesnonintell.en: Yet ye think that, one being conquered, men will not understand that ye are all conquered. Do not your consciences feel that they are confounded? For it is a light consolation to him who is confounded in himself, that it is unknown to others. Master, which is the great commandment in the Law? He calleth him Master, whose disciple he will not be. A most simple questioner, and a most malicious plotter: he asketh about the great commandment, who keepeth not even the least: for he ought to ask about the greater justice who hath already fulfilled the lesser.
tamenputatisquiaunovictohominesnonintell.la: Tamen putátis, quia uno victo, hómines non intélligant omnes vos victos. Numquid consciéntiæ vestræ non séntiunt se esse confúsas? Levis enim est consolátio, qui in seípso confúsus est, quod ab áliis ignorátur. Magister, quod est mandátum magnum in Lege? Magistrum vocat, cujus non vult esse discípulus. Simplicissimus interrogátor, et maligníssimus insidiátor: de magno mandáto intérrogat, qui nec mínimum obsérvat: ille enim debet interrogáre de majóri justítia, qui jam minórem implévit.

dominusautemsiceumreprehenditutinterroga.en: But the Lord so rebuked him, as to strike at once with his first answer the feigned conscience of his question, saying: Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with thy whole heart: that is, not as thou, who showest devotion in thy mouth, and meditatest fraud in thy heart. Now we call a commandment great and least according to the dignity of the commandments, not according to their usefulness. Otherwise the usefulness of all the commandments is one; and all the commandments, which seem to be one commandment, so cohere together, that one cannot be without the other.
dominusautemsiceumreprehenditutinterroga.la: Dóminus autem sic eum reprehendit, ut interrogatiónis ejus fictam consciéntiam statim primo respónso percúteret, dicens: Diliges Dóminum Deum tuum ex toto corde tuo: id est, non sicut tu, qui devotiónem osténdis in ore, et fraudem meditáris in corde. Magnum autem, et mínimum mandátum dícimus, quantum ad dignitátem mandatórum, non quantum ad utilitátem. Alióquin utilitas ómnium mandatorum una est; et ómnia mandáta que unum vidéntur esse mandátum, it sibi cohærent, ut álterum sin áltero esse non possit.

videntesautemturbetimueruntetglorificave.en: And the multitudes seeing it, feared, and glorified God that gave such power to men.
videntesautemturbetimueruntetglorificave.la: Vidéntes autem turbæ timuérunt, et glorificavérunt Deum, qui dedit potestátem talem hominibus.

princepshiclexesseintelligiturquedominum.en: This ruler is understood to be the Law; which prayeth the Lord that he would restore life to the dead maiden. For we read of no ruler that believed. Wherefore the person of this ruler praying shall rightly be fitted to the type of the Law. To him indeed the Lord promised help, and set forth to give it: but first, with the Apostles, the multitude of sinners is saved.
princepshiclexesseintelligiturquedominum.la: Princeps hic Lex esse intelligitur; quæ Dóminum orat, ut vitam mórtuæ reddat. Nam nullum príncipem credidisse légimus. Ex quo persóna príncipis hujus orántis mérito in typum Legis aptábitur. Cui quidem Dóminus opem spopóndit, ad quam præstándam proféctus est: sed prior cum Apóstolis peccatórum turba salvátur.

loquenteiesuadturbasecceprincepsunusacce.en: As Jesus was speaking to the multitudes, behold a certain ruler came up and adored him, saying: Lord, my daughter is even now dead; but come, lay thy hand upon her, and she shall live, alleluia.
loquenteiesuadturbasecceprincepsunusacce.la: Loquénte Jesu ad turbas, ecce princeps unus accéssit et adorábat eum dicens: Dómine, fília mea modo defúncta est; sed veni, impóne manum tuam super eam, et vivet, allelúja.

confidefiliafidestuatesalvamfecitetsanat.en: Be of good heart, daughter, thy faith hath made thee whole. And the woman was made whole from that hour, alleluia.
confidefiliafidestuatesalvamfecitetsanat.la: Confíde fília, fides tua te salvam fecit. Et sanáta est múlier ex illa hora, allelúja.

indiciumdominusnosteriesuschristussuiadv.en: Our Lord Jesus Christ hath set down a sign of his coming that is to be, to be understood when they shall see the abomination of desolation standing in the holy place. And of this indeed, since most blessed Daniel and Paul have preached it, I think it superfluous for us to discourse. For he spoke these things of the times of Antichrist. He is called an abomination for this, that coming against God he claimeth for himself the honour of God: and the abomination of desolation, because with wars and slaughters he is to lay waste the earth with sacrilege.
indiciumdominusnosteriesuschristussuiadv.la: Indicium Dóminus noster Jesus Christus sui advéntus futúri, cum abominatiónem desolatiónis stantem in loco sancto vidébunt, intelligéndum pósuit. Et de hoc quidem, beatíssimo Daniele et Paulo prædicántibus, supérfluum puto nos habére sermónem. De Antichrísti enim tempóribus hæc locútus est.
