Abominátio ex eo dictus, quod advérsus Deum véniens, honorem sibi Dei víndicet: Desolatiónis autem abominátio, quia bellis et cædibus terram cum piáculo desolatúrus sit.

sapientiaedificavitsibidomumexciditcolum.en: Wisdom hath built herself a house, she hath hewn out her seven pillars.
sapientiaedificavitsibidomumexciditcolum.la: Sapiéntia ædificávit sibi domum: excídit colúmnas septem.

immolavitvictimassuasmiscuitvinumetpropo.en: She hath slain her victims, mingled her wine, and set forth her table.
immolavitvictimassuasmiscuitvinumetpropo.la: Immolávit víctimas suas, míscuit vinum, et propósuit mensam suam.

misitancillassuasutvocarentadarcemetadme.en: She hath sent her maids to invite to the tower, and to the walls of the city:
misitancillassuasutvocarentadarcemetadme.la: Misit ancíllas suas ut vocárent ad arcem et ad mœ́nia civitátis:

siquisestparvulusveniatadmeetinsipientib.en: Whosoever is a little one, let him come to me. And to the unwise she said:
siquisestparvulusveniatadmeetinsipientib.la: Si quis est párvulus, véniat ad me. Et insipiéntibus locúta est:

venitecomeditepanemmeumetbibitevinumquod.en: Come, eat of my bread, and drink of the wine which I have mingled for you.
venitecomeditepanemmeumetbibitevinumquod.la: Veníte, comédite panem meum, et bíbite vinum quod míscui vobis.

dasapientioccasionemetaddetureisapientia.en: Give an occasion to a wise man, and wisdom shall be added to him.
dasapientioccasionemetaddetureisapientia.la: Da sapiénti occasiónem, et addétur ei sapiéntia.

doceiustumetfestinabitaccipere.en: Teach a just man, and he shall make haste to receive it.

supersalutemetomnempulchritudinemdilexis.en: Above health and all beauty I loved wisdom, and chose to have her instead of light:
supersalutemetomnempulchritudinemdilexis.la: Super salútem et omnem pulchritúdinem diléxi sapiéntiam, et propósui pro luce habére illam:

veneruntmihiomniabonaparitercumilla.en: Now all good things came to me together with her.
veneruntmihiomniabonaparitercumilla.la: Venérunt mihi ómnia bona páriter cum illa.

dixisapientiesorormeesetprudentiamvocavi.en: I said to wisdom: Thou art my sister: and I called prudence my friend.
dixisapientiesorormeesetprudentiamvocavi.la: Dixi sapiéntiæ, soror mea es: et prudéntiam vocávi amícam meam.

magnenimsuntiudiciatuadomineetinenarrabi.en: Great are thy judgments, O Lord, and thy words cannot be expressed.
magnenimsuntiudiciatuadomineetinenarrabi.la: Magna enim sunt judícia tua, Dómine, et inenarrabília verba tua:

magnificastipopulumtuumethonorasti.en: Thou didst make thy people mighty and honourable.

deduxistisicutovespopulumtuuminmanumoysi.en: Thou hast led thy people like sheep by the hand of Moses and Aaron.
deduxistisicutovespopulumtuuminmanumoysi.la: Deduxísti sicut oves pópulum tuum in manu Móysi et Aaron.

idcircounusinteritusesthominisetiumentor.en: Therefore the death of man and of beasts is one, and the condition of them both is equal.
idcircounusinteritusesthominisetiumentor.la: Idcírco unus intéritus est hóminis et jumentórum, et æqua utriúsque condítio.

delibrecclesiaste.en: Lesson from the book of Ecclesiastes

meliorestpuerpauperetsapiensregeseneetst.en: Better is a child that is poor and wise, than a king that is old and foolish, who knoweth not to foresee for hereafter.
meliorestpuerpauperetsapiensregeseneetst.la: Mélior est puer pauper et sápiens, rege sene et stulto, qui nescit prævidére in pósterum.

suntiustiatquesapientesetopereoruminmanu.en: There are just men and wise men, and their works are in the hand of God: and yet man knoweth not whether he be worthy of love, or hatred.
suntiustiatquesapientesetopereoruminmanu.la: Sunt justi atque sapiéntes, et ópera eórum in manu Dei: et tamen nescit homo utrum amóre an ódio dignus sit.

sedomniainfuturumservanturincerteoquodun.en: But all things are kept uncertain for the time to come, because all things equally happen to the just and to the wicked, to the good and to the evil, to the clean and to the unclean, to him that offereth victims, and to him that despiseth sacrifices.
sedomniainfuturumservanturincerteoquodun.la: Sed ómnia in futúrum servántur incérta, eo quod univérsa æque evéniant justo et ímpio, bono et malo, mundo et immúndo, immolánti víctimas et sacrifícia contemnénti.

sicutbonussicetpeccatorutperiurusitetill.en: As the good is, so also is the sinner: as the perjured, so he also that sweareth truth.
sicutbonussicetpeccatorutperiurusitetill.la: Sicut bonus, sic et peccátor: ut periúrus, ita et ille qui verum déierat.

nemestquisempervivatetquihuiusreihabeatf.en: There is no man that liveth always, or that hopeth for this.
nemestquisempervivatetquihuiusreihabeatf.la: Nemo est qui semper vivat, et qui hujus rei hábeat fidúciam.

meliorestcanisvivusleonemortuo.en: A living dog is better than a dead lion.
meliorestcanisvivusleonemortuo.la: Mélior est canis vivus leóne mórtuo.

cumqueessetsapientissimusecclesiastesdoc.en: And whereas Ecclesiastes was very wise, he taught the people, and declared the things that he had done.
cumqueessetsapientissimusecclesiastesdoc.la: Cumque esset sapientíssimus Ecclesiástes, dócuit pópulum, et enarrávit quæ fécerat.

delibrosapientie.en: Lesson from the book of Wisdom

quextinctaciniseritcorpusnostrumetspirit.en: which being put out, our body shall be ashes, and our spirit shall be poured abroad as soft air.
quextinctaciniseritcorpusnostrumetspirit.la: qua extíncta, cinis erit corpus nostrum, et spíritus diffundétur tamquam mollis aër.

ettransibitvitanostratamquamvestigiumnub.en: And our life shall pass away as the trace of a cloud, and shall be dispersed as a mist, which is driven away by the beams of the sun, and overpowered with the heat thereof.
ettransibitvitanostratamquamvestigiumnub.la: Et transíbit vita nostra tamquam vestígium nubis, et sicut nébula dissolvétur, quæ fugáta est a rádiis solis, et a calóre illíus aggraváta.

hecprofugumirefratrisiustumdeduxitpervia.en: She conducted the just, when he fled from his brother's wrath, through the right ways, and shewed him the kingdom of God.
hecprofugumirefratrisiustumdeduxitpervia.la: Hæc prófugum iræ fratris justum dedúxit per vias rectas, et osténdit illi regnum Dei.

direxitopereoruminmanibusprophetesancti.en: She prospered their works in the hands of the holy prophet.
direxitopereoruminmanibusprophetesancti.la: Diréxit ópera eórum in mánibus prophétæ sancti.

steteruntcontrahostesetdeinimicissevindi.en: They stood against their enemies, and avenged themselves of their adversaries.
steteruntcontrahostesetdeinimicissevindi.la: Stetérunt contra hostes, et de inimícis se vindicavérunt.

omniainmensuretnumeretponderedisposuisti.en: Thou hast ordered all things in measure, and number, and weight.
omniainmensuretnumeretponderedisposuisti.la: Ómnia in mensúra, et número et póndere disposuísti.

ideoqueeosquiexerrantpartibuscorripisetd.en: And therefore thou chastisest them that err, by little and little: and admonishest them, and speakest to them, concerning the things wherein they offend: that leaving their wickedness, they may believe in thee, O Lord.
ideoqueeosquiexerrantpartibuscorripisetd.la: Ideóque eos qui exérrant pártibus córripis, et de quibus peccant ádmones et allóqueris, ut relícta malítia credant in te Dómine.

filiconservatempusetdevitaamalo.en: Son, observe the time, and fly from evil.
filiconservatempusetdevitaamalo.la: Fili consérva tempus, et devíta a malo.

proanimatuaneconfundarisdicereverum.en: For thy soul be not ashamed to say the truth.
proanimatuaneconfundarisdicereverum.la: Pro ánima tua ne confundáris dícere verum.

remittemihiutrefrigererpriusquamabeam.en: Suffer me, therefore, that I may lament a little before I go.
remittemihiutrefrigererpriusquamabeam.la: Remítte mihi, ut refrígerer priúsquam ábeam.

etnonreverteturoculusmeusutvideatbona.en: And mine eye shall not return to see good things.
etnonreverteturoculusmeusutvideatbona.la: Et non revertétur óculus meus, ut vídeat bona.

fervensetfremenssorbetterramnecreputattu.en: Chafing and raging he swalloweth the ground, neither doth he make account when the noise of the trumpet soundeth.
fervensetfremenssorbetterramnecreputattu.la: Fervens et fremens sorbet terram, nec réputat tubæ sonáre clangórem.

ingressusraphelangelusadtobiamsalutavite.en: The Angel Raphael went in to Tobias and saluted him, saying: Joy be to thee always. And Tobias said to him: What manner of joy shall be to me, who sit in darkness, and see not the light of heaven? And the Angel said to him: Be of good courage, for thy cure from God is at hand.
ingressusraphelangelusadtobiamsalutavite.la: Ingréssus Ráphaël Angelus ad Tobíam salutávit eum, dicens: Gaudium tibi semper sit. Cui Tobías ait: Quale gáudium mihi erit, qui in ténebris sedeo, et lumen cæli non video? Cui Angelus inquit: Forti animo esto, in próximo enim est, ut a Deo curéris.

dominerexomnipotensinditionetuacunctasun.en: O Lord, almighty King, all things are set in thy power, and there is none that can resist thy will: deliver us
dominerexomnipotensinditionetuacunctasun.la: Dómine, rex omnípotens, in ditióne tua cuncta sunt pósita, et non est qui possit resistere voluntáti tuæ: libera nos

exaudidomineorationemnostrametconvertelu.en: Hear, O Lord, our prayer, and turn our mourning into joy.
exaudidomineorationemnostrametconvertelu.la: Exaudi, Dómine, oratiónem nostram, et convérte luctum nostrum in gáudium.

delibrotobie.en: Lesson from the book of Tobias

quodautemdictumestfrequentercumetinignem.en: But in that it is said, Oftentimes he hath cast him into the fire and into waters; the greatest crimes of human madness are signified. For the heat of fire is to be referred to the vehemence of wrath: water to the pleasures of the flesh, which are wont to dissolve the mind through delights. Or surely the possessed man is borne into the fire, wherewith the hearts of adulterers are inflamed, and into the waters, which are wont to quench charity. But well doth the Lord, who driveth the unclean spirit out of the man, command at the same time that he enter no more into him: because he is truly delivered from the dominion of the devil, who by living ill shunneth to return to the sins from which he hath once been cleansed by doing penance.
quodautemdictumestfrequentercumetinignem.la: Quod autem dictum est, Frequenter cum et in ignem et in aquas misit; máxima humánæ vecórdiæ facínora designántur. Ignis namque ardor ad fervórem iracundiæ referéndus est: aqua ad voluptátes carnis, quæ dissolvere mentem per delícias solent. Vel certe in ignem fertur dæmoníacus, quo adulterántium corda succénsa sunt, et in aquas, quæ solent exstinguere caritátem. Bene autem Dóminus, qui spíritum immúndum pellit ab hómine, simul ne ámplius in eum ingrediátur ímperat: quia ille veráciter a dæmoníaca dominatióne liberátur, qui ad peccáta, a quibus semel pæniténdo mundátus est, vitat male vivéndo revérti.

laudatedominumdeumnostrum.en: Praise ye the Lord our God,

quinondeseruitsperantesinseetinmeadimple.en: Who hath not forsaken them that hope in him: and in me he hath fulfilled his mercy, which he promised to the house of Israel.
quinondeseruitsperantesinseetinmeadimple.la: Qui non deséruit sperántes in se: et in me adimplévit misericórdiam suam, quam promísit domui Israël.

laudatedominumomnesgentesetcollaudateeum.en: O praise the Lord, all ye nations: and praise him together, all ye people.
laudatedominumomnesgentesetcollaudateeum.la: Laudáte Dóminum, omnes gentes: et collaudáte eum, omnes pópuli.

prestaquesumusdominefamilietuesupplicant.en: Grant, we beseech thee, O Lord, to thy suppliant family: that, while it abstaineth from bodily food, it may fast also in mind from vices.
prestaquesumusdominefamilietuesupplicant.la: Præsta, quæsumus, Dómine, famíliæ tuæ supplicánti: ut, dum a cibis corporálibus se ábstinet, a vitiis quoque mente jejúnet.

etdixiteiangelusapprehendebranchiameiuse.en: And the angel said to him: Take him by the gill, and draw him to thee.
etdixiteiangelusapprehendebranchiameiuse.la: Et dixit ei ángelus: Apprehénde bránchiam ejus, et trahe eum ad te.

quodcumfecissetattraxiteuminsiccumetpalp.en: And when he had done so, he drew him out upon the land, and he began to pant before his feet.
quodcumfecissetattraxiteuminsiccumetpalp.la: Quod cum fecísset, attráxit eum in siccum, et palpitáre cœpit ante pedes ejus.

inillotemporerogabatiesumquidamdepharise.en: At that time: One of the Pharisees desired Jesus to eat with him. And he went into the house of the Pharisee, and sat down to meat. And behold a woman that was in the city, a sinner, when she knew that he sat at meat in the Pharisee's house, brought an alabaster box of ointment. And so on.
inillotemporerogabatiesumquidamdepharise.la: In illo témpore: Rogábat Jesum quidam de pharisǽis, ut manducáret cum illo. Et ingréssus domum pharisǽi discúbuit. Et ecce múlier, quæ erat in civitáte peccátrix, ut cognóvit quod accubuísset in domo Pharisǽi, áttulit alabástrum unguénti. Et réliqua.

liquetfratresquodillicitisactibuspriusmu.en: It is clear, brethren, that the woman, formerly intent upon unlawful deeds, used ointment upon herself for the perfuming of her flesh. What therefore she had shamefully bestowed upon herself, this she now offered to God in praiseworthy wise. With her eyes she had coveted earthly things: but now, wearing them out by penance, she wept. Her hair she had displayed for the setting off of her face: but now with her hair she wiped away her tears. With her mouth she had spoken proud things, but kissing the Lord's feet, she fixed it upon the footsteps of her Redeemer. As many delights therefore as she had had in herself, so many burnt-offerings did she find of herself. She turned the number of her crimes into a number of virtues: that whatsoever in her had despised God in sin might wholly serve God in penance.
liquetfratresquodillicitisactibuspriusmu.la: Liquet, fratres, quod illicitis áctibus priùs múlier inténta, unguéntum sibi pro odóre carnis adhibuit. Quod ergo sibi túrpiter exhibúerat, hoc jam Deo laudabiliter offerébat. Oculis terréna concupierat: sed hos jam per pæniténtiam cónterens, flebat. Capillos ad compositiónem vultus exhibúerat: sed jam capíllis lácrimas tergébat. Ore supérba díxerat sed pedes Dómini ósculans, hoc in Redemptóris sui vestígia figébat. Quot ergo in se hábuit oblectaménta, tot de se invénit holocausta. Convértit ad virtútum númerum, númerum criminum: ut totum servíret Deo in pæniténtia, quidquid ex se Deum contémpserat in culpa.

quemveropeccatrixmulieradvestigiadominiv.en: But whom doth the sinful woman, coming to the Lord's feet and weeping, signify, but the Gentiles converted? Who came with an alabaster box, poured out ointment, stood behind at the Lord's feet, washed his feet with tears, wiped them with her hair, and ceased not to kiss those same feet which she anointed and wiped. Us therefore, us did that woman set forth, if with our whole heart we return to the Lord after our sins, if we imitate the mourning of her penance. For what is expressed by the ointment, but the odour of good report? If therefore we do right works, wherewith we may sprinkle the Church with the odour of good report, what do we but pour ointment upon the Lord's body?
quemveropeccatrixmulieradvestigiadominiv.la: Quem vero peccátrix múlier, ad vestígia Dómini véniens et plorans, nisi convérsam Gentilitátem designat? Quæ cum alabástro venit, unguéntum fudit, retro secus pedes Dómini stetit, lácrimis pedes rigávit, capillis tersit, eosdémque, quos infundébat et tergébat, pedes osculári non désiit. Nos ergo, nos illa múlier expréssit, si toto corde ad Dóminum post peccáta redeamus, si ejus pœniténtiæ luctus imitémur. Quid namque unguénto, nisi bonæ odor opiniónis exprímitur? Si ergo recta ópera ágimus, quibus opiniónis bonæ odóre Ecclésiam respergámus, quid, nisi in Dómini córpore unguéntum fúndimus?

sedsecuspedesiesumulierstetitcontrapedes.en: But the woman stood behind at the feet of Jesus. For we stood against the Lord's feet when, being set in sins, we resisted his ways. But if after sins we be converted to true penance, we now stand behind at his feet: because we follow the footsteps of him whom we fought against. The woman washeth his feet with tears. Which we also truly do, if with the affection of compassion we stoop down to any of the least members of the Lord, if we suffer with his saints in tribulation, if we account their sorrow our own. The woman wiped with her hair the feet which she had washed. We wipe the Lord's feet with our hair, when we have mercy upon his saints out of those things which we have to spare. She kisseth the feet which she wipeth: which we also do fully, if we love with zeal those whom we support of our bounty.
sedsecuspedesiesumulierstetitcontrapedes.la: Sed secus pedes Jesu mulier stetit. Contra pedes enim Dómini stétimus, cum in peccátis pósiti, ejus itinéribus renitebámur. Sed si ad veram pœniténtiam post peccáta convértimur, jam retro secus pedes stamus : quia ejus vestigia séquimur, quem impugnabámus. Lácrimis múlier pedes ejus rigat. Quod nos quoque veráciter ágimus, si quibúslibet últimis membris Dómini per compassiónis afféctum inclinámur, si sanctis ejus in tribulatióne compátimur, si eórum tristitiam, nostram putamus. Capillis múlier pedes, quos rigáverat, tersit. Capillis pedes Dómini térgimus, quando sanctis ejus ex his, quæ nobis supérfluunt, miserémur. Osculátur pedes, quos tergit: quod nos quoque plene ágimus, si studióse diligimus, quos ex largitáte continémus.

prestaquesumusdominesicnosabepulisabstin.en: Grant, we beseech thee, O Lord, that we may so abstain from fleshly feasting, that we may likewise fast from the vices that assail us.
prestaquesumusdominesicnosabepulisabstin.la: Præsta, quæsumus, Dómine, sic nos ab épulis abstinére carnálibus, ut a vítiis irruéntibus páriter jejunémus.

accepitquecivitateseorumetseditibipertri.en: and he took possession of their cities, and stayed there for thirty days.
accepitquecivitateseorumetseditibipertri.la: accepítque civitátes eórum, et sedit ibi per trigínta dies.

delibroiudith.en: Lesson from the book of Judith

omnesparaveruntsepariteradpugnamcontrafi.en: All prepared themselves together to fight against the children of Israel.
omnesparaveruntsepariteradpugnamcontrafi.la: Omnes paravérunt se páriter ad pugnam contra fílios Israël.

nihiltameninterroganteseamdimiserunttran.en: But they asked her no question, and let her pass.
nihiltameninterroganteseamdimiserunttran.la: Nihil tamen interrogántes eam, dimisérunt transíre.

cumqueintrassetantefaciemeiusstatimcaptu.en: And when she was come into his presence, forthwith Holofernes was caught by his eyes.
cumqueintrassetantefaciemeiusstatimcaptu.la: Cumque intrásset ante fáciem ejus, statim captus est in suis óculis Holoférnes.

vasthiquoquereginafecitconviviumfeminaru.en: Also Vasthi the queen made a feast for the women in the palace, where king Assuerus was used to dwell.
vasthiquoquereginafecitconviviumfeminaru.la: Vasthi quoque regína fecit convívium feminárum in palátio, ubi rex Assuérus manére consuéverat.

delibresther.en: Lesson from the book of Esther

etmittanturquiconsiderentperuniversaspro.en: and let some be sent through all the provinces to look for beautiful maidens and virgins: and let them bring them to the city of Susan.
etmittanturquiconsiderentperuniversaspro.la: et mittántur qui consíderent per univérsas províncias puéllas speciósas et vírgines: et addúcant eas ad civitátem Susan.

eratviriudeusinsusancivitatevocabulomard.en: There was a man in the city of Susan, a Jew, named Mardochai, the son of Jair, the son of Semei, the son of Cis, of the race of Jemini,
eratviriudeusinsusancivitatevocabulomard.la: Erat vir Judǽus in Susan civitáte, vocábulo Mardochǽus fílius Jair, fílii Sémei, fílii Cis, de stirpe Jémini,

quitranslatusfueratdeierusalemeotemporeq.en: Who had been carried away from Jerusalem at the time that Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon carried away Jechonias king of Juda,
quitranslatusfueratdeierusalemeotemporeq.la: qui translátus fúerat de Jerúsalem eo témpore quo Jechoníam regem Juda Nabuchodónosor rex Babylónis transtúlerat,

quifuitnutritiusfiliefratrissuiedisseque.en: who had brought up his brother's daughter Edissa, who by another name was called Esther: and she had lost both her parents: and was exceeding fair and beautiful.
quifuitnutritiusfiliefratrissuiedisseque.la: qui fuit nutrítius fíliæ fratris sui Edíssæ, quæ áltero nómine vocabátur Esther, et utrúmque paréntem amíserat: pulchra nimis, et decóra fácie.

mortuisquepatreeiusacmatremardocheussibi.en: And her father and mother being dead, Mardochai adopted her for his daughter.
mortuisquepatreeiusacmatremardocheussibi.la: Mortuísque patre ejus ac matre, Mardochǽus sibi eam adoptávit in fíliam.

queplacuiteietinvenitgratiaminconspectui.en: And she pleased him, and found favour in his sight.
queplacuiteietinvenitgratiaminconspectui.la: Quæ plácuit ei, et invénit grátiam in conspéctu illíus.

evolutoautemtemporeperordineminstabatdie.en: And as the time came orderly about, the day was at hand, when Esther, the daughter of Abihail the brother of Mardochai, whom he had adopted for his daughter, was to go in to the king. But she sought not women's ornaments, but whatsoever Egeus the eunuch the keeper of the virgins had a mind, he gave her to adorn her. For she was exceeding fair, and her incredible beauty made her appear agreeable and amiable in the eyes of all.
evolutoautemtemporeperordineminstabatdie.la: Evolúto autem témpore per órdinem, instábat dies quo Esther fília Abíhail fratris Mardochǽi, quam sibi adoptáverat in fíliam, debéret intráre ad regem. Quæ non quæsívit mulíebrem cultum, sed quæcúmque vóluit Egéus eunúchus custos vírginum, hæc ei ad ornátum dedit. Erat enim formósa valde, et incredíbili pulchritúdine: ómnium óculis gratiósa et amábilis videbátur.

ductestitaqueadcubiculumregisassuerimens.en: So she was brought to the chamber of king Assuerus the tenth month, which is called Tebeth, in the seventh year of his reign.
ductestitaqueadcubiculumregisassuerimens.la: Ducta est ítaque ad cubículum regis Assuéri mense décimo, qui vocátur Tebeth, séptimo anno regni ejus.

etadamaviteamrexplusquamomnesmuliereshab.en: And the king loved her more than all the women, and she had favour and kindness before him above all the women, and he set the royal crown on her head, and made her queen instead of Vasthi.
etadamaviteamrexplusquamomnesmuliereshab.la: Et adamávit eam rex plus quam omnes mulíeres, habuítque grátiam et misericórdiam coram eo super omnes mulíeres: et pósuit diadéma regni in cápite ejus, fecítque eam regnáre in loco Vasthi.

delibroprimomachabeorum.en: Lesson from the first book of Machabees

sanctificatieiusdesolatestsicutsolitudo.en: Her sanctuary was desolate like a wilderness.
sanctificatieiusdesolatestsicutsolitudo.la: Sanctificátio ejus desoláta est sicut solitúdo.

etappropinquaveruntdiesmathathiemoriendi.en: Now the days drew near that Mathathias should die, and he said to his sons: Now hath pride and chastisement gotten strength, and the time of destruction, and the wrath of indignation:
etappropinquaveruntdiesmathathiemoriendi.la: Et appropinquavérunt dies Mathathíæ moriéndi, et dixit fíliis suis: Nunc confortáta est supérbia, et castigátio, et tempus eversiónis, et ira indignatiónis.

nuncergoofiliiemulatoresestotelegisetdat.en: Now therefore, O my sons, be ye zealous for the law, and give your lives for the covenant of your fathers.
nuncergoofiliiemulatoresestotelegisetdat.la: Nunc ergo, o fílii, æmulatóres estóte legis, et date ánimas vestras pro testaménto patrum vestrórum,

etmementoteoperumpatrumquefeceruntingene.en: And call to remembrance the works of the fathers, which they have done in their generations: and you shall receive great glory, and an everlasting name.
etmementoteoperumpatrumquefeceruntingene.la: et mementóte óperum patrum, quæ fecérunt in generatiónibus suis: et accipiétis glóriam magnam, et nomen ætérnum.

etsurrexitiudasquivocabaturmachabeusfili.en: Then his son Judas, called Machabeus, rose up in his stead.
etsurrexitiudasquivocabaturmachabeusfili.la: Et surréxit Judas, qui vocabátur Machabǽus, fílius ejus, pro eo:

etadiuvabanteumomnesfratreseiusetunivers.en: And all his brethren helped him, and all they that had joined themselves to his father, and they fought with cheerfulness the battle of Israel.
etadiuvabanteumomnesfratreseiusetunivers.la: et adiuvábant eum omnes fratres ejus, et univérsi qui se coniúnxerant patri ejus, et prœliabántur prœ́lium Israël cum lætítia.

etpersecutusestiniquosperscrutanseosetqu.en: And he pursued the wicked and sought them out, and them that troubled his people he burnt with fire:
etpersecutusestiniquosperscrutanseosetqu.la: Et persecútus est iníquos perscrútans eos: et qui conturbábant pópulum suum, eos succéndit flammis.

etrepulsisuntinimicieiuspretimoreeiuseto.en: And his enemies were driven away for fear of him, and all the workers of iniquity were troubled: and salvation prospered in his hand.
etrepulsisuntinimicieiuspretimoreeiuseto.la: et repúlsi sunt inimíci ejus præ timóre ejus, et omnes operárii iniquitátis conturbáti sunt: et dirécta est salus in manu ejus.

etexacerbabatregesmultosetletificabatiac.en: And he grieved many kings, and made Jacob glad with his works, and his memory is blessed for ever.
etexacerbabatregesmultosetletificabatiac.la: Et exacerbábat reges multos, et lætificábat Jacob in opéribus suis, et in sǽculum memória ejus in benedictióne.

etperambulavitcivitatesiudetperdiditimpi.en: And he went through the cities of Juda, and destroyed the wicked out of them, and turned away wrath from Israel.
etperambulavitcivitatesiudetperdiditimpi.la: Et perambulávit civitátes Juda, et pérdidit ímpios ex eis, et avértit iram ab Israël.

etcongregavitapolloniusgentesetasamariav.en: And Apollonius gathered together the Gentiles, and a numerous and great army from Samaria, to make war against Israel.
etcongregavitapolloniusgentesetasamariav.la: Et congregávit Apollónius gentes, et a Samaría virtútem multam et magnam ad bellándum contra Israël.

etcognovitiudasetexiitobviamillietpercus.en: And Judas understood it, and went forth to meet him: and he overthrew him, and killed him: and many fell down slain, the rest fled away.
etcognovitiudasetexiitobviamillietpercus.la: Et cognóvit Judas, et éxiit óbviam illi: et percússit, et occídit illum: et cecidérunt vulneráti multi, et réliqui fugérunt.

etaccepitspolieorumetgladiumapolloniiabs.en: And he took their spoils, and Judas took the sword of Apollonius, and fought with it all his lifetime.
etaccepitspolieorumetgladiumapolloniiabs.la: Et accépit spólia eórum: et gládium Apollónii ábstulit Judas, et erat pugnans in eo ómnibus diébus.

etcongregatusestconventusutessentparatii.en: And the assembly was gathered that they might be ready for battle: and that they might pray, and ask mercy and compassion.
etcongregatusestconventusutessentparatii.la: Et congregátus est convéntus ut essent paráti in prœ́lium, et ut orárent et péterent misericórdiam et miseratiónes.

etierusalemnonhabitabatursederatsicutdes.en: Now Jerusalem was not inhabited, but was like a desert: there was none of her children that went in or out: and the sanctuary was trodden down: and the children of strangers were in the castle, there was the habitation of the Gentiles: and joy was taken away from Jacob, and the pipe and harp ceased there.
etierusalemnonhabitabatursederatsicutdes.la: Et Jerúsalem non habitabátur, sed erat sicut desértum: non erat qui ingrederétur et egrederétur de natis ejus. Et sanctum conculcabátur: et fílii alienigenárum erant in arce: ibi erat habitátio géntium: et abláta est volúptas a Jacob, et defécit ibi tíbia et cíthara.

etcongregatisuntetveneruntinmasphacontra.en: And they assembled together, and came to Maspha over against Jerusalem: for in Maspha was a place of prayer heretofore in Israel.
etcongregatisuntetveneruntinmasphacontra.la: Et congregáti sunt, et venérunt in Maspha contra Jerúsalem, quia locus oratiónis erat in Maspha ante in Israël.

etieiunaveruntilladieetindueruntsecilici.en: And they fasted that day, and put on haircloth, and put ashes upon their heads: and they rent their garments:
etieiunaveruntilladieetindueruntsecilici.la: Et jejunavérunt illa die, et induérunt se cilíciis, et cínerem imposuérunt cápiti suo, et discidérunt vestiménta sua:

etexpanderuntlibroslegisdequibusscrutaba.en: And they laid open the books of the law, in which the Gentiles searched for the likeness of their idols:
etexpanderuntlibroslegisdequibusscrutaba.la: et expandérunt libros legis, de quibus scrutabántur gentes similitúdinem simulacrórum suórum.

etattuleruntornamentasacerdotalietprimit.en: And they brought the priestly ornaments, and the firstfruits and tithes, and stirred up the Nazarites that had fulfilled their days:
etattuleruntornamentasacerdotalietprimit.la: Et attulérunt ornaménta sacerdotália, et primítias, et décimas: et suscitavérunt Nazarǽos, qui impléverant dies:

etclamaveruntvocemagnaincelumdicentesqui.en: And they cried with a loud voice toward heaven, saying: What shall we do with these, and whither shall we carry them?
etclamaveruntvocemagnaincelumdicentesqui.la: et clamavérunt voce magna in cælum, dicéntes: Quid faciémus istis, et quo eos ducémus?

etsanctatuaconculcatasuntetcontaminatasu.en: For thy holies are trodden down, and are profaned, and thy priests are in mourning, and are brought low.
etsanctatuaconculcatasuntetcontaminatasu.la: Et sancta tua conculcáta sunt, et contamináta sunt, et sacerdótes tui facti sunt in luctum, et in humilitátem.

dixitautemiudasetfratreseiuseccecontriti.en: Then Judas, and his brethren said: Behold our enemies are discomfited: let us go up now to cleanse the holy places and to repair them.
dixitautemiudasetfratreseiuseccecontriti.la: Dixit autem Judas, et fratres ejus: Ecce contríti sunt inimíci nostri: ascendámus nunc mundáre sancta, et renováre.

annocentesimooctogesimooctavopopulusquie.en: In the year one hundred and eighty-eight, the people that is at Jerusalem, and in Judea, and the senate, and Judas, to the Jews that are in Egypt, health and welfare.
annocentesimooctogesimooctavopopulusquie.la: Anno centésimo octogésimo octávo, pópulus qui est Jerosólymis et in Judǽa, senatúsque et Judas, his qui in Ægýpto sunt Judǽis, salútem et sanitátem.

delibrosecondomachabeorum.en: Lesson from the second book of Machabees

delibrosecundomachabeorum.en: Lesson from the second book of Machabees

accinctequemulieresciliciispectusperplat.en: And the women, girded with haircloth about their breasts, came together in the streets.
accinctequemulieresciliciispectusperplat.la: Accinctǽque mulíeres cilíciis pectus, per platéas confluébant.

sedetvirginesqueconcluseerantprocurreban.en: and the virgins also that were shut up came forth, some to Onias, and some to the walls, and others looked out of the windows:
sedetvirginesqueconcluseerantprocurreban.la: sed et vírgines quæ conclúsæ erant, procurrébant ad Oníam, áliæ autem ad muros, quædam vero per fenéstras aspiciébant:

accingiminietestotefiliipotentesetestote.en: Gird yourselves, and be valiant sons, and be ready to fight in battle: for it is better for us to die in war than to see the evils of our nation and of the holies. As it shall be the will in heaven, so be it done.
accingiminietestotefiliipotentesetestote.la: Accingímini, et estóte fílii poténtes, et estóte paráti pugnáre in prœlio: quóniam mélius est nobis mori in bello, quam vidére mala gentis nostræ, et sanctórum. Sicut fúerit volúntas in cælo, sic fiat.

atillevelocitermisitnicanorempatroclidep.en: And he with all speed sent Nicanor, the son of Patroclus, one of his chief friends, giving him no fewer than twenty thousand armed men of different nations, to root out the whole race of the Jews.
atillevelocitermisitnicanorempatroclidep.la: At ille velóciter misit Nicánorem Pátrocli de primóribus amícum, datis ei de permístis géntibus, armátis non minus vigínti míllibus, ut univérsum Judæórum genus deléret.

adhecconsideransdeproximopotentesquosque.en: Moreover, considering that the mighty men near at hand, and the neighbours, wait for opportunities, and expect what shall be the event, I have appointed my son Antiochus king.
adhecconsideransdeproximopotentesquosque.la: Ad hæc, consíderans de próximo poténtes quosque et vicínos tempóribus insidiántes, et evéntum exspectántes, designávi fílium meum Antíochum regem.

etassumpsitmespiritusetaudivipostmevocem.en: And the spirit took me up, and I heard behind me the voice of a great commotion, saying: Blessed be the glory of the Lord, from his place.
etassumpsitmespiritusetaudivipostmevocem.la: Et assúmpsit me spíritus, et audívi post me vocem commotiónis magnæ: Benedícta glória Dómini de loco suo.

etvocemalarumanimaliumpercutientiumalter.en: And the noise of the wings of the living creatures striking one against another, and the noise of the wheels following the living creatures, and the noise of a great commotion.
etvocemalarumanimaliumpercutientiumalter.la: Et vocem alárum animálium percutiéntium álteram ad álteram, et vocem rotárum sequéntium animália, et vocem commotiónis magnæ.

etcontempsitiudiciameautplusessetimpiaqu.en: And she hath despised my judgments, so as to be more wicked than the Gentiles; and my commandments, more than the countries that are round about her.
etcontempsitiudiciameautplusessetimpiaqu.la: Et contémpsit judícia mea, ut plus esset ímpia quam gentes, et præcépta mea ultra quam terræ quæ in circúitu ejus sunt.

iudicienimmeaproieceruntetinpreceptismei.en: for they have cast off my judgments, and have not walked in my commandments.
iudicienimmeaproieceruntetinpreceptismei.la: judícia enim mea proiecérunt, et in præcéptis meis non ambulavérunt.

etfactusestsermodominiadmedicens.en: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
etfactusestsermodominiadmedicens.la: Et factus est sermo Dómini ad me, dicens:

etrecordabunturmeiliberativestriingentib.en: And they that are saved of you shall remember me amongst the nations, to which they are carried captives: because I have broken their heart that was faithless, and revolted from me: and their eyes that went a fornicating after their idols.
etrecordabunturmeiliberativestriingentib.la: Et recordabúntur mei liberáti vestri in géntibus ad quas captívi ducti sunt: quia contrívi cor eórum fórnicans et recédens a me, et óculos eórum fornicántes post idóla sua.

dedanielepropheta.en: Lesson from the book of Daniel

etdecornibusdecemquehabebatincapite.en: and concerning the ten horns that he had on his head.
etdecornibusdecemquehabebatincapite.la: et de córnibus decem, quæ habébat in cápite.

porrohircushabebatcornuinsigneinteroculo.en: And the he goat had a notable horn between his eyes.
porrohircushabebatcornuinsigneinteroculo.la: Porro hircus habébat cornu insígne inter óculos suos.

cumqueappropinquassetpropearietemefferat.en: And when he was come near the ram, he was enraged against him, and struck the ram: and broke his two horns, and the ram could not withstand him.
cumqueappropinquassetpropearietemefferat.la: Cumque appropinquásset prope aríetem, efferátus est in eum, et percússit aríetem: et commínuit duo córnua ejus, et non póterat áries resístere ei.

sustinuimuspacemetnonvenitdominequesivim.en: We have looked for peace, and it hath not come, O Lord: we have sought good things, and behold trouble: we acknowledge, O Lord, our sins; forget us not for ever, O God of Israel.
sustinuimuspacemetnonvenitdominequesivim.la: Sustinúimus pacem, et non venit, Dómine: quæsívimus bona, et ecce turbátio: cognóvimus, Dómine, peccáta nostra; ne in ætérnum obliviscáris nos, Deus Israël.

deoseepropheta.en: Lesson from the book of Osee

depetradesertiadmontemfiliasion.en: From the rock of the desert to the mount of the daughter of Sion.
depetradesertiadmontemfiliasion.la: De Petra desérti ad montem fília Sion.

venietliberanosdeusnoster.en: Come and deliver us, O our God.
venietliberanosdeusnoster.la: Veni et líbera nos, Deus noster.

tuamdomineexcitepotentiametveniadsalvand.en: Stir up thy might, O Lord, and come to save us.
tuamdomineexcitepotentiametveniadsalvand.la: Tuam, Dómine, éxcite poténtiam, et veni ad salvándum nos.

intuoadventueruenosdomine.en: At thy coming deliver us, O Lord.
intuoadventueruenosdomine.la: In tuo advéntu érue nos, Dómine.

participemmefacdeusomniumtimentiumte.en: Make me partaker, O God, with all them that fear thee.
participemmefacdeusomniumtimentiumte.la: Partícipem me fac, Deus, ómnium timéntium te.

aspiceinmeetmisereremeisecundumiudiciumd.en: Look thou upon me, and have mercy on me, according to the judgment of them that love thy name.
aspiceinmeetmisereremeisecundumiudiciumd.la: Aspice in me, et miserére mei secúndum judícium diligéntium nomen tuum.

dicetdominosusceptormeusestu.en: He shall say to the Lord: Thou art my protector.
dicetdominosusceptormeusestu.la: Dicet Dómino: Suscéptor meus es tu.

abomniviamalaprohibuipedesmeos.en: I have restrained my feet from every evil way:
abomniviamalaprohibuipedesmeos.la: Ab omni via mala prohíbui pedes meos:

utcustodiammandatatuadomine.en: That I may keep thy commandments, O Lord.

aiudiciistuisnondeclinaviquiatulegemposu.en: I have not declined from thy judgments, because thou hast set me a law.
aiudiciistuisnondeclinaviquiatulegemposu.la: A judíciis tuis non declinávi, quia tu legem posuísti mihi.

septiesindielaudemdixitibidominedeusmeus.en: Seven times a day I have given praise to thee, O Lord my God.
septiesindielaudemdixitibidominedeusmeus.la: Sépties in die laudem dixi tibi, Dómine Deus meus.

erravisicutovisqueperieratrequireservumt.en: I have gone astray like a sheep that is lost: * seek thy servant, O Lord, because I have not forgotten thy commandments.
erravisicutovisqueperieratrequireservumt.la: Errávi sicut ovis quæ períerat: * requíre servum tuum, Dómine, quia mandáta tua non sum oblítus.

christequiluxesetdies.en: O Christ, who art the light and day,
christequiluxesetdies.la: Christe, qui lux es et dies,

noctistenebrasdetegis.en: Thou layest bare the darkness of the night,

lucisquelumencrederis.en: And art believed the Light of light,

precamursanctedomine.en: We pray thee, O holy Lord,

sitnobisinterequies.en: Let our rest be in thee,

negravissomnusirruat.en: Let no heavy sleep fall upon us,

nechostisnossubripiat.en: Nor the enemy steal upon us,

neccaroilliconsentiens.en: Nor the flesh, consenting unto him,

coradtesempervigilet.en: Let our heart ever watch unto thee:

defensornosteraspice.en: O our defender, look upon us,

insidiantesreprime.en: Repress them that lie in wait,

quossanguinemercatuses.en: Whom thou hast bought with thy Blood.

quiesdefensoranime.en: Thou who art the defender of the soul,

adestonobisdomine.en: Be near unto us, O Lord.

evigilasupernoseternesalvatornenosappreh.en: Watch over us, * O eternal Saviour, lest the crafty tempter lay hold on us, for thou art made our everlasting helper.
evigilasupernoseternesalvatornenosappreh.la: Evígila super nos, * ætérne Salvátor, ne nos apprehéndat cállidus tentátor, quia tu nobis factus es sempitérnus adjútor.

mediavitainmortesumusquemquerimusadiutor.en: In the midst of life we are in death: whom do we seek for a helper, but thee, O Lord, who for our sins art justly angered? * O holy God, O holy and mighty, O holy and merciful Saviour, deliver us not unto bitter death.
mediavitainmortesumusquemquerimusadiutor.la: Média vita in morte sumus: quem quǽrimus adjutórem, nisi te, Dómine, qui pro peccátis nostris juste irásceris? * Sancte Deus, Sancte fortis, Sancte et miséricors Salvátor, amáræ morti ne tradas nos.

intendeanimemeeetlibeream.en: Attend to my soul, and deliver it.
intendeanimemeeetlibeream.la: Inténde ánimæ meæ, et líbera eam.

propterinimicosmeoseripeme.en: Save me because of my enemies.

erueaframeadeusanimammeam.en: Deliver, O God, my soul from the sword.
erueaframeadeusanimammeam.la: Érue a frámea, Deus, ánimam meam.

etdemanucanisunicammeam.en: My only one from the hand of the dog.
etdemanucanisunicammeam.la: Et de manu canis únicam meam.

salvameexoreleonisetacornibusunicorniumh.en: Save me from the lion's mouth, and my lowness from the horns of the unicorns. My only one from the hand of the dog.
salvameexoreleonisetacornibusunicorniumh.la: Salva me ex ore leónis, et a córnibus unicórnium humilitátem meam. Et de manu canis únicam meam.

deoreleonisliberamedomine.en: From the lion's mouth deliver me, O Lord.
deoreleonisliberamedomine.la: De ore leónis Líbera me, Dómine.

etacornibusunicorniumhumilitatemmeam.en: And my lowness from the horns of the unicorns.
etacornibusunicorniumhumilitatemmeam.la: Et a córnibus unicórnium humilitátem meam.

principespersecutisuntmegratisetaverbist.en: Princes have persecuted me without cause: and my heart hath been in awe of thy words.
principespersecutisuntmegratisetaverbist.la: Príncipes persecúti sunt me gratis, et a verbis tuis formidávit cor meum.

letaboregosupereloquiatua.en: I will rejoice at thy words.

quasiquiinvenitspoliamultaletaboregosupe.en: As one that hath found great spoil. I will rejoice at thy words.
quasiquiinvenitspoliamultaletaboregosupe.la: Quasi qui invénit spólia multa. Lætábor ego super elóquia tua.

orexglorioseintersanctostuosquisemperesl.en: O glorious King amidst thy Saints, who art ever worthy of praise and yet ineffable: thou art in us, O Lord, and thy holy name is called upon us: forsake us not, O our God: that in the day of judgment thou mayest vouchsafe to set us among thy Saints and Elect, O blessed King.
orexglorioseintersanctostuosquisemperesl.la: O Rex glorióse inter Sanctos tuos, qui semper es laudábilis et tamen ineffábilis: tu in nobis es, Dómine, et nomen sanctum tuum invocátum est super nos: ne derelínquas nos Deus noster: ut in die judícii nos collocáre dignéris inter Sanctos et Eléctos tuos, Rex benedícte.

resurrexitdominusalleluiaalleluia.en: The Lord is risen, * Alleluia, alleluia.

ascendoadpatremmeumetpatremvestrumallelu.en: I ascend to my Father and to your Father, alleluia.
ascendoadpatremmeumetpatremvestrumallelu.la: Ascéndo ad Patrem meum et Patrem vestrum, allelúja.

deummeumetdeumvestrumalleluia.en: To my God and your God, alleluia.
deummeumetdeumvestrumalleluia.la: Deum meum et Deum vestrum, allelúja.

alleluiaspiritusparaclitusalleluiadocebi.en: Alleluia. The Spirit, the Paraclete, alleluia, shall teach you all things, alleluia, alleluia.
alleluiaspiritusparaclitusalleluiadocebi.la: Allelúja. Spíritus Paráclitus, allelúja, docébit vos ómnia, allelúja, allelúja.

deusquinobisnatisalvatorisdiemcelebrarec.en: O God, who grantest us to celebrate the eighth day of the birth of our Saviour: grant, we beseech thee, that we may be fortified by the everlasting Godhead of him by whose fellowship in our flesh we have been restored:
deusquinobisnatisalvatorisdiemcelebrarec.la: Deus, qui nobis nati Salvatóris diem celebráre concédis octávum: fac nos, quæsumus, eius perpétua divinitáte muníri, cuius sumus carnáli commércio reparáti:

delibroiosue.en: Lesson from the book of Josue

quiomnescircumcisierantpopulusautemquina.en: for these were all circumcised. But the people that were born in the desert,
quiomnescircumcisierantpopulusautemquina.la: qui omnes circumcísi erant. Pópulus autem qui natus est in desérto,

perquadragintaannositinerislatissimesoli.en: during the forty years of the journey in the wide wilderness, were uncircumcised: till they were consumed that had not heard the voice of the Lord.
perquadragintaannositinerislatissimesoli.la: per quadragínta annos itíneris latíssimæ solitúdinis incircumcísus fuit: donec consumeréntur qui non audíerant vocem Dómini.

lapidemquemreprobaveruntedificanteshicfa.en: The stone which the builders rejected: the same is become the head of the corner.
lapidemquemreprobaveruntedificanteshicfa.la: Lápidem, quem reprobavérunt ædificántes: hic factus est in caput ánguli.

deepistolaadromanos.en: Lesson from the letter of St. Paul the Apostle to the Romans

quicelumterrramqueregitinseculasolus.en: Who alone ruleth heaven and earth for ever.
quicelumterrramqueregitinseculasolus.la: Qui cælum terrrámque regit in sǽcula solus.

alleluiaverbumcarofactumestalleluiethabi.en: Alleluia. The Word was made flesh, alleluia, and dwelt among us, alleluia, alleluia.
alleluiaverbumcarofactumestalleluiethabi.la: Allelúja. Verbum caro factum est, allelúja, et habitávit in nobis, allelúia, allelúia.

queritedominumduminveniripotestinvocatee.en: Seek ye the Lord, while he may be found: call upon him, while he is near.
queritedominumduminveniripotestinvocatee.la: Quǽrite Dóminum dum inveníri potest: invocáte eum dum prope est.

derelinquatimpiusviamsuametviriniquuscog.en: Let the wicked forsake his way, and the unjust man his thoughts, and let him return to the Lord, and he will have mercy on him: and to our God, for he is bountiful to forgive.
derelinquatimpiusviamsuametviriniquuscog.la: Derelínquat ímpius viam suam, et vir iníquus cogitatiónes suas, et revertátur ad Dóminum, et miserébitur eius: et ad Deum nostrum, quóniam multus est ad ignoscéndum.

posteadiciturevangeliumfactumestautem.en: Then the Gospel is said: And it came to pass
posteadiciturevangeliumfactumestautem.la: Postea dicitur Evangelium Factum est autem

adnosvenitpervirginem.en: Came unto us through a Virgin,

decelocelsusprodiit.en: From heaven on high he came forth,

excepitformamhominis.en: He took the form of man:

hocteredemptorquesumus.en: This, O Redeemer, we beseech thee:

lumenprebefidelibus.en: Give clear light, to thy faithful.

quemiamvenissenovimus.en: Thou whom we know to have come already,

superteierusalemorieturdominusetglorieiu.en: Upon thee, O Jerusalem, shall the Lord arise, and his glory shall be seen upon thee. And the Gentiles shall walk in thy light, and kings in the brightness of thy rising.
superteierusalemorieturdominusetglorieiu.la: Super te, Jerúsalem, oriétur Dóminus, et glória eius in te vidébitur. Et ambulábunt gentes in lúmine tuo, et reges in splendóre ortus tui.

timentibusnomentuumdomine.en: To them that fear thy name, O Lord.

adsuntdominicisertisolemnialaudemultipli.en: Here is the solemn feast of the Lord's Crown: * let the Church applaud with manifold praise, alleluia.
adsuntdominicisertisolemnialaudemultipli.la: Adsunt Domínici Serti solémnia: * Laude multíplici plaudat Ecclésia, allelúja.

eterneregiglorie.en: To the eternal King of glory

fidelessolvanthodie.en: Let the faithful pay this day

procoronadominica.en: For the Crown of the Lord.

coronatregemomnium.en: The King of all things is crowned

despinarumaculeis.en: Of the sharp points of thorns

christicoronaplectitur.en: Is the Crown of Christ plaited,

quaministristartareis.en: Whereby from the ministers of hell

mundipotestastollitur.en: The power over the world is taken away.

reospurgatacrimine.en: Cleanseth the guilty from their crime.

lauschristoregiglorie.en: Praise to Christ, the King of glory,

procoronevirtutibus.en: For the powers of the Crown,

coronetincelestibus.en: May he crown us in heaven.

christumsubsertospineoderidetplebsperfid.en: The faithless people mock Christ beneath the wreath of thorns: by whose rosy blood the wreath of glory is bestowed, alleluia.
christumsubsertospineoderidetplebsperfid.la: Christum sub Serto spíneo derídet plebs perfídiæ: cuius cruóre róseo Sertum confértur glóriæ, allelúja. Ps. 1, 2, 3

tuamcoronamadoramusdominealleluia.en: We adore thy Crown, O Lord, alleluia.

tuumgloriosumrecolimustriumphumalleluia.en: We celebrate thy glorious triumph, alleluia.

deepistolabeatipauliapostoliadhebreos.en: From the letter of the blessed Apostle Paul to the Hebrews
deepistolabeatipauliapostoliadhebreos.la: De Epístola beáti Pauli Apóstoli ad Hebrǽos

nonangelissubiecitdeusorbemterrefuturumd.en: For God hath not subjected unto angels the world to come, whereof we speak. But one in a certain place hath testified, saying: What is man, that thou art mindful of him: or the son of man, that thou visitest him? Thou hast made him a little lower than the angels: thou hast crowned him with glory and honour, and hast set him over the works of thy hands: thou hast subjected all things under his feet. For in that he hath subjected all things to him, he left nothing not subject to him. But now we see not as yet all things subject to him. But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels, for the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honour: that, through the grace of God, he might taste death for all.
nonangelissubiecitdeusorbemterrefuturumd.la: Non ángelis subjécit Deus orbem terræ futúrum de quo lóquimur. Testátus est autem in quodam loco quis dicens: Quid est homo, quod memor es eius, aut fílius hóminis, quóniam vísitas eum ? Minuísti eum paulo minus ab ángelis; glória et honóre coronásti eum, et constituísti eum super ópera mánuum tuárum: ómnia subjecísti sub pédibus ejus. In eo enim quod ómnia ei subjécit, nihil dimísit non subjéctum ei; nunc autem necdum vidémus ómnia subjécta ei. Eum autem, qui módico quam ángeli minorátus est, vidémus Jesum propter passiónem mortis glória et honóre coronátum, ut grátia Dei pro ómnibus gustáret mortem.

spinacarensflosspinapungiturperquamculpe.en: The Flower without thorn is pierced by the thorn, by which the thorn of sin is broken:
spinacarensflosspinapungiturperquamculpe.la: Spina carens Flos spina púngitur, per quam culpæ spina confríngitur:

spinamortisspinisretunditurdumvitamoritu.en: The thorn of death is blunted by thorns, while Life dieth, alleluia.
spinamortisspinisretunditurdumvitamoritu.la: Spina mortis spinis retúnditur, dum Vita móritur, allelúja.

perhocludibriumhostisdeluditurmortisdomi.en: By this mockery the enemy is mocked: the dominion of death is taken away by death.
perhocludibriumhostisdeluditurmortisdomi.la: Per hoc ludíbrium hostis delúditur: mortis domínium per mortem tóllitur.

decebatenimeumpropterquemomnietperquemom.en: For it became him, for whom are all things, and by whom are all things, who had brought many children into glory, to perfect the author of their salvation by his passion. For both he that sanctifieth, and they who are sanctified, are all of one. For which cause he is not ashamed to call them brethren, saying: I will declare thy name to my brethren; in the midst of the church will I praise thee. And again: I will put my trust in him. And again: Behold I and my children, whom God hath given me. Therefore because the children are partakers of flesh and blood, he also himself in like manner hath been partaker of the same: that, through death, he might destroy him who had the empire of death, that is to say, the devil: and might deliver them, who through the fear of death were all their lifetime subject to servitude.
decebatenimeumpropterquemomnietperquemom.la: Décebat enim eum, propter quem ómnia et per quem ómnia, qui multos fílios in glóriam addúxerat, auctórem salútis eórum per passiónem consummáre. Qui enim sanctíficat et qui sanctificántur, ex uno omnes; propter quam causam non confúnditur fratres eos vocáre, dicens: Nuntiábo nomen tuum frátribus meis, in médio ecclésiæ laudábo te; et íterum: Ego ero fidens in eum; et íterum: Ecce ego et púeri mei, quos dedit mihi Deus. Quia ergo púeri communicavérunt carni et sánguini, et ipse simíliter participávit eísdem, ut per mortem destrúeret eum qui habébat mortis impérium, id est diábolum; et liberáret eos qui timóre mortis per totam vitam obnóxii erant servitúti.

coronatregemomniumiudeasertospineostatin.en: Judea crowneth the King of all with a wreath of thorns: the lily standeth among thorns, blooming with rosy blood,
coronatregemomniumiudeasertospineostatin.la: Corónat Regem ómnium Judǽa Serto spíneo: stat inter spinas lílium vernans cruóre róseo,

spinarumculpenesciumspinepunctumaculeoal.en: Knowing naught of the thorns of sin, pierced by the point of the thorn, alleluia.
spinarumculpenesciumspinepunctumaculeoal.la: Spinárum culpæ néscium, spinæ punctum acúleo, allelúja.

subdecorefulgetpurpureocorpusnitenscando.en: Beneath the purple beauty shineth the body, gleaming with snowy whiteness.
subdecorefulgetpurpureocorpusnitenscando.la: Sub decóre fulget purpúreo corpus nitens candóre níveo.

felixspinacuiusaculeiguttisrubentrorissa.en: O happy Thorn, whose points are red with drops of bloody dew,
felixspinacuiusaculeiguttisrubentrorissa.la: Felix Spina, cuius acúlei guttis rubent roris sanguínei,

viresfranguntregistartareiseraspanduntre.en: They break the strength of the king of hell, they open the bolts of the starry kingdom, alleluia.
viresfranguntregistartareiseraspanduntre.la: Vires frangunt regis tartárei, seras pandunt regni sidérei, allelúja.

ospinarumimmensagloriaquetotnobisprestan.en: O boundless glory of the Thorns, which afford us so many remedies.
ospinarumimmensagloriaquetotnobisprestan.la: O Spinárum imménsa glória, quæ tot nobis præstant remédia.

cumsanctusludovicusrexfrancorumabalduino.en: When St. Louis, King of the Franks, had received the Lord's Crown of thorns as a gift from Baldwin the Second, Emperor of Constantinople, he sent two brethren of the Order of Preachers, Andrew and James, to Constantinople. These, on the morrow of St. Lawrence, Martyr, in the year one thousand two hundred and thirty-nine, brought the Crown to the king at Sens. It was carried with great solemnity to Paris, and at length was placed at the royal palace, in the chapel built by Louis himself. This precious treasure, impiously stolen in the lamentable times of the French upheaval at the close of the eighteenth century, and afterwards restored, was translated to the metropolitan basilica. Certain thorns of the sacred Crown King Louis gave as a gift to the Friars Preachers, and entrusted to them the celebration of the anniversary of their reception in the chapel dedicated to the Crown. The feast of the Most Holy Crown was inserted in the calendar of the Order of Preachers about the middle of the thirteenth century.
cumsanctusludovicusrexfrancorumabalduino.la: Cum sanctus Ludovícus, rex Francórum, a Balduíno secúndo, Constantinopolitáno imperatóre, Corónam Dómini spíneam dono accepísset, duos ex órdine Prædicatórum fratres, Andréam et Jacóbum, Constantinópolim misit. Qui in crástino sancti Lauréntii Mártyris, anno millésimo ducentésimo trigésimo nono, Corónam regi Sénone detulérunt. Quæ, magna cum solemnitáte Parísios deláta, postrémo apud régium palátium collocáta est, in capélla ab ipso Ludovíco ædificáta. Thesáurus iste pretiósus, lugéndis tumúltus gállici tempóribus sǽculo décimo octávo exeúnte ímpie subréptus ac póstmodum restitútus, in metropolitánam basílicam translátus est. Quasdam vero Corónæ sacræ spinas rex Ludovícus Frátribus Prædicatóribus dono dedit, illísque susceptiónis anniversárium in capélla Corónæ dicáta celebrándum commísit. Festum Sanctíssimæ Corónæ, circa medietátem sǽculi décimi tértii, kalendário órdinis Prædicatórum insértum est.

iustusutpalmaflorebitindomodominiallelui.en: The just shall flourish like the palm tree in the house of the Lord, alleluia.
iustusutpalmaflorebitindomodominiallelui.la: Justus ut palma florébit in domo Dómini, allelúja.

sicutcedruslibanimultiplicabituralleluia.en: He shall grow up like the cedar of Libanus, alleluia.

deusquibeatumludovicummariamconfessoremt.en: O God, who didst make blessed Louis Mary thy Confessor an eminent herald of the mystery of the Cross and of the most holy Rosary, and through him didst make thy Church fruitful with a new family: grant, by his merits and intercession, that through the life, death and resurrection of thine only-begotten Son we may obtain the rewards of eternal salvation.
deusquibeatumludovicummariamconfessoremt.la: Deus, qui beátum Ludovícum Maríam Confessórem tuum Crucis mystérii et sacratíssimi Rosárii præcónem exímium effecísti, ac nova per eum família Ecclésiam fecundásti: ejus méritis et intercessióne concéde ut per unigéniti Fílii tui vitam, mortem ac resurrectiónem, salútis ætérnæ prǽmia consequámur.

celestisexercitusregemadoremusetpropalma.en: Let us adore the King of the heavenly host: * And for the palm of his soldier let us rejoice, alleluia.
celestisexercitusregemadoremusetpropalma.la: Cæléstis exércitus Regem adorémus: * Et pro palma mílitis ejus jubilémus, allelúja.

festumquecelicurie.en: And a feast of the court of heaven,

offerturregiglorie.en: Is offered to the King of glory.

fidemverbipreconio.en: The faith by preaching the word,

profidetandemceditur.en: For the faith at last he is slain

dumsicinpetrafidei.en: While thus upon the rock of faith

petritenetvestigia.en: He keepeth the footsteps of Peter,

adpetramchristumprovehi.en: To Christ the Rock to be borne

christumregemregumsupplicesadoremusquiim.en: Christ, the King of kings, let us humbly adore: * Who endowed the virgin Catherine of Siena with immortal glory, alleluia.
christumregemregumsupplicesadoremusquiim.la: Christum, Regem regum, súpplices adorémus: * Qui immortáli glória vírginem Senénsem dotávit Catharínam, allelúja.

laudibusvirgonimisefferenda.en: O virgin, exceedingly to be extolled with praises

iurecenserisquoniamtriumphos.en: Art thou rightly deemed, since the triumphs

ipsacelorumprobitatemira.en: Of heaven, by thy wondrous goodness,

nactarefulges.en: Thou hast won, and shinest forth.

premiumsanctetamenipsavite.en: Yet the reward of thy holy life,

etsimulmunusprobitatisalme.en: And therewith the gift of thy kindly goodness,

accipiscelocumulatacunctis.en: Thou receivest in heaven, enriched with all

tugravemsacrismeritisrefertum.en: Thou, the grave Father, filled with holy merits,

orbisexemplarpietateplenum.en: The world's pattern, full of piety,

predicatorumveneratapatrem.en: The Father of the Preachers having revered,

nullaiamrerumplacuitvoluptas.en: No pleasure of things now pleased thee,

corporissemperfugiensinique.en: Of body; ever fleeing from the wicked

quampieflagriscruorhincetinde.en: How piously, with scourges, did the blood on this side and on that
quampieflagriscruorhincetinde.la: Quam pie flagris cruor hinc et inde

fluxeratrivishominumquedemum.en: Flow in streams, and at last the sins of men

quiperingentesvariosquecasus.en: Who through great and divers mishaps

orbeterrarumcrucianturomnes.en: Throughout the world are all tormented,

quotquevelcurisagitanturipsi.en: And as many as are themselves tossed by cares

suppetentnobistotidemcanenda.en: As many things shall we have to sing,

situelaudesrepetanturomnes.en: If all thy praises be recounted:

tuquidemlongepietatecunctis.en: Thou indeed far above all in piety

gratiassummashabeamusomnes.en: Let us all give highest thanks

filiomagnigenitorisalmo.en: To the kindly Son of the great Father:

spiritumsanctumveneremuretsit.en: Let us worship the Holy Ghost, and let there be

admirabilemdeinostriclementiamcontemplar.en: The very great constancy of Catherine will ever make us contemplate the wonderful clemency of our God, alleluia.
admirabilemdeinostriclementiamcontemplar.la: Admirábilem Dei nostri clémentiam contemplári máxima Catharínæ constántia nos semper effíciet, allelúja. Ps. 8

misericordiasummergegenosatqueegrotossum.en: Moved most greatly with the highest mercy toward the needy and the sick, this virgin was wont to weep for their sorrows, alleluia.
misericordiasummergegenosatqueegrotossum.la: Misericórdia summa erga egénos atque ægrótos summópere affécta, ipsórum ærúmnas deflére hæc virgo solébat, allelúja. Ps. 18

christianosquidemtantacaritateprosequeba.en: She followed Christians with such great charity that, kindled with love of them, she burned day and night, alleluia.
christianosquidemtantacaritateprosequeba.la: Christiános quidem tanta caritáte prosequebátur, ut eórum amóre incénsa diu noctúque flagráret, allelúja. Ps. 23

filieierusalemveniteetvidetemartyremcumc.en: Ye daughters of Jerusalem, come and see the Martyr with the crown wherewith the Lord crowned him
filieierusalemveniteetvidetemartyremcumc.la: Fíliæ Jerúsalem, veníte, et vidéte Mártyrem cum coróna, qua coronávit eum Dóminus

indiesolemnitatisetletitiealleluia.en: In the day of solemnity and gladness, alleluia.
indiesolemnitatisetletitiealleluia.la: In die solemnitátis et lætítiæ, allelúja.

induitillumdominusstolamglorieetcoronavi.en: The Lord hath clothed him with a robe of glory, and hath crowned him.
induitillumdominusstolamglorieetcoronavi.la: Induit illum Dóminus stolam glóriæ, et coronávit eum.

fonshortorumputeusaquarumviventiumqueflu.en: The fountain of gardens, the well of living waters, which run with a strong stream from Libanus, alleluia.
fonshortorumputeusaquarumviventiumqueflu.la: Fons hortórum, púteus aquárum vivéntium, quæ fluunt ímpetu de Líbano, allelúja. Ps. 8

manusmeestillaveruntmyrrhametdigitimeipl.en: My hands dropped with myrrh, and my fingers were full of the choicest myrrh, alleluia.
manusmeestillaveruntmyrrhametdigitimeipl.la: Manus meæ stillavérunt myrrham, et dígiti mei pleni myrrha probatíssima, allelúja. Ps. 18

vadamadmontemmyrrheetadcollemthurisallel.en: I will go to the mountain of myrrh, and to the hill of frankincense, alleluia.
vadamadmontemmyrrheetadcollemthurisallel.la: Vadam ad montem myrrhæ et ad collem thuris, allelúja. Ps. 23

ostendattenobisdomineiesuposthocexsilium.en: May the clement and loving Virgin Mary, thy Mother, show thee unto us, O Lord Jesus, after this exile: whom blessed Sadoc and his companions saluting with unceasing voice amid the hostile assaults of the infidels, merited to receive from thee the long-desired palm of martyrdom:
ostendattenobisdomineiesuposthocexsilium.la: Osténdat te nobis, Dómine Jesu, post hoc exsílium clemens et pia Virgo María Mater tua: quam beáti Sadócus et sócii inter hostiles infidélíum impetus incessánti voce salutántes, præoptátam martyrii palmam a te recipere meruérunt:

cumpalmaadregnaperveneruntsancticoronasd.en: With palms * the Saints have attained unto the kingdom; they have merited crowns of beauty from the hand of the Lord.
cumpalmaadregnaperveneruntsancticoronasd.la: Cum palma * ad regna pervenérunt Sancti, corónas decóris meruérunt de manu Dómini.

deusquibeatosmartyrestuospetrumpontifice.en: O God, who didst endow thy blessed Martyrs, Peter the Bishop and his companions, with equal steadfastness and charity for preaching the faith to the nations: grant, we beseech thee, that by their example and intercession we may abide constant in thy faith.
deusquibeatosmartyrestuospetrumpontifice.la: Deus, qui beátos Mártyres tuos Petrum Pontíficem eiúsque sócios, ad fidem géntibus prædicándam, pari firmitáte et caritáte donásti; præsta, quæsumus, eórum exémplo et intercessióne nos in tua fide permanére constántes.

exaudiquesumusdomineprecesnostrasquasinb.en: Graciously hear, we beseech thee, O Lord, our prayers, which we offer on the solemn feast of blessed Medard thy Confessor and Bishop: that by the pleading merits of him who worthily served thee, thou mayest absolve us from all our sins. Through.
exaudiquesumusdomineprecesnostrasquasinb.la: Exáudi, quæsumus, Dómine, preces nostras, quas in beáti Medárdi Confessóris tui atque Pontíficis solemnitate deférimus: ut, qui tibi digne méruit famulári, ejus intercedéntibus méritis, ab ómnibus nos absólvas peccátis. Per.

deusquibeatamdianamvirginemtuamadmirabil.en: O God, who didst endow blessed Diana thy Virgin with wonderful strength of spirit, and didst give her blessed Cecilia and Amata as companions in treading the way of evangelical perfection: mercifully grant that by their example we may be strengthened in hardships, and protected by their help in adversities.
deusquibeatamdianamvirginemtuamadmirabil.la: Deus, qui beátam Diánam Virginem tuam admirábili spíritus fortitúdine donásti, eique in terénda evangélicæ perfectionis via beátas Cæciliam et Amátam cómites dedisti: concéde propítius ut eárum exémpló roboremur in árduis, et in adversís protegámur auxilio.

deuslargitorcaritatisquibeatumioannemcon.en: O God, the giver of charity, who didst strengthen blessed John, thy Confessor and Bishop, with power in preserving the unity of the Church and in restoring regular discipline: through his intercession grant us to think and to do the same thing in Christ Jesus our Lord:
deuslargitorcaritatisquibeatumioannemcon.la: Deus, largitor caritatis, qui beátum Joánnem Confessórem atque Pontífficem in conservánda Ecclésiæ unitáte instaurandáque regulári disciplína virtúte roborásti, per ipsíus intercessiónem tríbue nobis idípsum sentíre et fácere in Christo Jesu Dómino nostro:i

gregemtuumpastoreternenondeserassedperbe.en: Forsake not thy flock, O eternal Shepherd, but through thy blessed Apostles
gregemtuumpastoreternenondeserassedperbe.la: Gregem tuum, Pastor ætérne, non déseras, sed per beátos Apóstolos tuos

protegedominepopulumtuumetapostolorumtuo.en: Protect, O Lord, thy people, trusting also in the patronage of thy Apostles.
protegedominepopulumtuumetapostolorumtuo.la: Prótege, Dómine, pópulum tuum, et Apostolórum tuórum patrocinio confidéntem.

quesumusomnipotensdeusutbeatusbarnabasap.en: We beseech thee, almighty God, that blessed Barnabas thy Apostle may implore thy help for us: that, absolved from our offences, we may also be delivered from all dangers.
quesumusomnipotensdeusutbeatusbarnabasap.la: Quæsumus, omnipotens Deus: ut beátus Bárnabas Apóstolus tuum pro nobis implóret auxílium; ut, a nostris reátibus absolúti, a cunctis étiam perículis eruámur.

deusquibeatuminnocentiumconfessorematque.en: O God, who didst make blessed Innocent, thy Confessor and Bishop, adorned with the gifts of knowledge and prudence, a maker of peace and unity: grant us by his intercession to savour heavenly things, and to pursue all good things with one accord.
deusquibeatuminnocentiumconfessorematque.la: Deus, qui beátum Innocéntium Confessórem atque Pontíficem, sciéntiæ ac prudéntiæ donis decorátum, pacis et unitátis conciliatorem effecisti; ejus intercessióne nobis concéde cœléstia sapere, et ómnia bona concordi stúdio sectari.

internatosmulierumnonsurrexitmaiorioanne.en: Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist
internatosmulierumnonsurrexitmaiorioanne.la: Inter natos mulíerum non surréxit major Joánne Baptísta

auditeinsuleetattenditepopulidelongedomi.en: Give ear, ye islands, and hearken, ye people from afar. The Lord hath called me from the womb, from the bowels of my mother he hath been mindful of my name.
auditeinsuleetattenditepopulidelongedomi.la: Audíte ínsulæ, et atténdite, pópuli de longe: Dóminus ab útero vocávit me: de ventre matris meæ recordátus est nóminis mei.

eratquideminfecundacorporesedservatamyst.en: She was indeed barren in body, but kept for a mystery: and she was freed from the reproach of barrenness by bearing a son promised from heaven.
eratquideminfecundacorporesedservatamyst.la: Erat quidem infecunda corpore, sed servata mysterio: caruitque sterilitatis opprobrio, gignendo filium de cælo promissum.

consolaminiconsolaminipopulemeusdicitdeu.en: Be comforted, be comforted, my people, saith your God.
consolaminiconsolaminipopulemeusdicitdeu.la: Consolámini, consolámini pópule meus, dicit Deus vester.

loquiminiadcorierusalemetadvocateeamquon.en: Speak ye to the heart of Jerusalem, and call to her: for her evil is come to an end, her iniquity is forgiven: she hath received of the hand of the Lord double for all her sins.
loquiminiadcorierusalemetadvocateeamquon.la: Loquímini ad cor Jerúsalem, et advocáte eam, quóniam compléta est malítia ejus, dimíssa est iníquitas illíus: suscépit de manu Dómini duplícia pro ómnibus peccátis suis.

voxclamantisindesertoparateviamdominirec.en: The voice of one crying in the desert: Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make straight in the wilderness the paths of our God.
voxclamantisindesertoparateviamdominirec.la: Vox clamántis in desérto: Paráte viam Dómini, rectas fácite in solitúdine sémitas Dei nostri.

omnisvallisexaltabituretomnismonsetcolli.en: Every valley shall be exalted, and every mountain and hill shall be made low, and the crooked shall become straight, and the rough ways plain.
omnisvallisexaltabituretomnismonsetcolli.la: Omnis vallis exaltábitur, et omnis mons et collis humiliábitur, et erunt prava in dirécta, et áspera in vias planas.

netimeaszachariaquoniamexauditestoratiot.en: Fear not, Zachary, for thy prayer is heard: and thy wife Elizabeth shall bear thee a son.
netimeaszachariaquoniamexauditestoratiot.la: Ne timeas, Zachária, quóniam exaudita est orátio tua: et Élisabeth uxor tua pariet tibi filium.

viciniquoqueetcognatieiusveneruntcircumc.en: His neighbours also and kinsfolk came to circumcise the child, and they inquired by what name he should be called.
viciniquoqueetcognatieiusveneruntcircumc.la: Vicíni quoque et cognáti ejus vénérunt circumcidere puerum, et sciscitáti sunt cum quo nómine vocarétur.

priusquamteformareminuteronoviteetantequ.en: Before I formed thee in the bowels of thy mother, I knew thee: and before thou camest forth out of the womb, I sanctified thee, and made thee a prophet unto the nations.
priusquamteformareminuteronoviteetantequ.la: Priúsquam te formárem in útero, novi te: et ántequam exíres de vulva, sanctificávi te, et prophétam in géntibus dedi te.

posuitosmeumquasigladiumacutuminumbraman.en: He hath made my mouth like a sharp sword: in the shadow of his hand he hath protected me, and hath made me as a chosen arrow.
posuitosmeumquasigladiumacutuminumbraman.la: Pósuit os meum quasi gládium acútum, in umbra manus suæ protéxit me, et pósuit me sicut sagíttam eléctam.

beatimartireschristiioannesetpaulusdixer.en: The blessed Martyrs of Christ, John and Paul, said to Julian: We have no other but one God,
beatimartireschristiioannesetpaulusdixer.la: Beáti Mártires Christi Joánnés et Paulus dixérunt Juliáno: Nobis álius non est nisi unus Deus,

pateretfiliusetspiritussanctus.en: The Father, and the Son, and the Holy Ghost.
pateretfiliusetspiritussanctus.la: Pater et Fílius et Spíritus Sanctus.

unafidesunumbaptismaunusspirituseratinei.en: One faith, one baptism, one spirit was in them.
unafidesunumbaptismaunusspirituseratinei.la: Una fides, unum baptísma, unus spíritus erat in eis.

quialingueeorumclavescelifactesunt.en: For their tongues were made the keys of heaven.
quialingueeorumclavescelifactesunt.la: Quia linguæ eórum claves cœli factæ sunt.

beatimartireschristiioannesetpaulusdixer.en: The blessed Martyrs of Christ, John and Paul, said to Julian: We have no other but one God, the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Ghost, alleluia.
beatimartireschristiioannesetpaulusdixer.la: Beáti Mártires Christi Joánnés et Paulus dixérunt Juliáno: Nobis álius non est nisi unus Deus, Pater et Fílius et Spíritus Sanctus , alleluia.

hicdicettibiquidteoporteatfacere.en: He will tell thee what thou must do.
hicdicettibiquidteoporteatfacere.la: Hic dicet tibi quid te opórteat fácere.

inplateisponebanturinfirmiinlectulisutve.en: They laid the sick in the streets on beds, that when Peter came, his shadow at the least might overshadow any of them, and they might be delivered from their infirmities.
inplateisponebanturinfirmiinlectulisutve.la: In platéis ponebántur infirmi in léctulis, ut, veniente Petro, saltem umbra illíus obumbráret quemquam illórum, et liberaréntur ab infirmitátibus suis. Ps. 18

aitpetrusprincipibussacerdotumiesumquemv.en: Peter said to the chief priests: Jesus, whom you put to death, hanging him upon a tree, him hath God raised up: and hath exalted him to be Prince and Saviour, to give repentance unto the remission of sins.
aitpetrusprincipibussacerdotumiesumquemv.la: Ait Petrus principibus sacerdotum: Jesum, quem vos interemístis, suspendentes in ligno, hunc Deus suscitávit: et Principem et Salvátorem exaltávit ad dandam pæniténtiam in remissionem peccatórum. Ps. 33

petrusapostolusdixitparalyticeneasanette.en: Peter the Apostle said to the paralytic: Eneas, the Lord Jesus Christ healeth thee: arise, and make thy bed. And immediately he arose: and all that saw him were converted to the Lord.
petrusapostolusdixitparalyticeneasanette.la: Petrus Apóstolus dixit paralytico: Ænéa, sanet te Dóminus Jesus Christus: surge et sterne tibi. Qui continuo surrexit: et omnes, qui viderunt, convérsi sunt ad Dóminum. Ps. 44

factumestautemutquedamdiscipulanominetab.en: And it came to pass that a certain disciple named Tabitha, full of good works and almsdeeds, fell sick and died: and the disciples sent unto Peter, desiring him: Be not slack to come on to us.
factumestautemutquedamdiscipulanominetab.la: Factum est autem ut quædam discipula, nómine Tabítha, plena opéribus bonis et eleemósynis, infirmáta morerétur: misérunt autem discipuli ad Petrum, rogántes: Ne pigritéris venire usque ad nos. Ps. 46

advenientepetrocircumsteteruntillumomnes.en: When Peter was come, all the widows stood about him weeping, and shewing him the coats and garments which Dorcas made them.
advenientepetrocircumsteteruntillumomnes.la: Adveniénte Petro, circumstetérunt illum omnes víduæ flentes et ostendéntes túnicas et vestes, quas faciébat illis Dorcas. Ps. 60

ponenspetrusgenusuaoravitetconversusadco.en: Peter, kneeling down, prayed, and turning to the body he said: Tabitha, arise. And she opened her eyes: and seeing Peter, she sat up: and giving her his hand, he lifted her up, and presented her alive to the saints and widows.
ponenspetrusgenusuaoravitetconversusadco.la: Ponens Petrus génu sua orávit, et convérsus ad corpus dixit: Tabítha, surge. At illa apéruit óculos: et viso Petro resédit: dansque illi manum eréxit eam, et sanctis ac víduis assignávit vivam. Ps. 63

aperienspetrusossuumdixitinveritatecompe.en: Peter, opening his mouth, said: In very deed I perceive that God is not a respecter of persons, but in every nation, he that feareth God and worketh justice is acceptable to him.
aperienspetrusossuumdixitinveritatecompe.la: Apériens Petrus os suum dixit: In veri-táte cómperi quóniam non est personárum accéptor Deus, sed in omni gente, qui timet Deum et ope-rátur justítiam, accéptus est illi. Ps. 96

adhucloquentepetroceciditspiritussanctus.en: While Peter was yet speaking, the Holy Ghost fell on all them that heard the word: and they were speaking with tongues and magnifying God. Then Peter commanded them to be baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ.
adhucloquentepetroceciditspiritussanctus.la: Adhuc loquente Petro, cécidit Spíritus Sanctus super omnes qui audiébant verbum: et erant; loquéntes linguis et ma-gnificántes Deum. Tunc Petrus jussit eos baptizári in nómine Dómini Jesu Christi. Ps. 98

tibienimadominocollatestpotestasligandia.en: For to thee hath been given by the Lord the power of binding and of loosing.
tibienimadominocollatestpotestasligandia.la: Tibi enim a Dómino colláta est potéstas ligándi atque solvéndi.

simoneccesatanexpetivitvosutcribraretsic.en: Simon, behold Satan hath desired to have you, that he may sift you as wheat: but I have prayed for thee.
simoneccesatanexpetivitvosutcribraretsic.la: Simon, ecce Satan expetivit vos ut cribráret sicut triticum: ego autem rogávi pro te.

olivebinepietatisunice.en: Ye two olive trees of one single piety,

fidedevotossperobustosmaxime.en: Devout in faith, most mightily strong in hope,

fonterepletoscaritatisgemine.en: Filled from the fount of twofold charity,

postmortemcarnisimpetratevivere.en: Obtain for us to live after the death of the flesh.

sittrinitatisempiternagloria.en: To the Trinity be everlasting glory,

inunitatecuimanetimperium.en: In unity, whose is the empire

extuncetmodopereternasacula.en: From then and now through ages everlasting.
extuncetmodopereternasacula.la: Ex tunc et modo per ætérna sácula.

angelusdominiastititetlumenrefulsitinhab.en: An Angel of the Lord stood by him, and a light shined in the room: and he, striking Peter on the side, raised him up, saying: Arise quickly. And the chains fell off from his hands.
angelusdominiastititetlumenrefulsitinhab.la: Angelus Dómini ástitit, et lumen refúlsit in habitáculo, percussóque látere Petri excitávit eum dicens: Surge velóciter. Et cecidérunt caténæ de má nibus ejus.

laudemusdeumnostruminsolemnitateapostoli.en: Let us praise our God * On the solemnity of the Apostle Paul.
laudemusdeumnostruminsolemnitateapostoli.la: Laudemus Deum nostrum * In solemnitate Apostoli Pauli.

sanctepauleapostolepredicatorveritatiset.en: O holy Apostle Paul, preacher of the truth and Teacher of the Gentiles, intercede for us with God,
sanctepauleapostolepredicatorveritatiset.la: Sancte Paule Apóstole, prædicátor veritátis et Doctor Géntium, intercéde pro nobis ad Deum,

homiliadelaudpauli.en: Homily 8 on the Praises of Paul

sepefulvidoceliglobodelectatusoculusadsp.en: Often the eye, delighted by the tawny globe of heaven, strains itself violently toward the sight of the light in the opposite region: and though it feel its gaze to be unequal to the contest of the rays, yet from the desire of beholding that most beautiful light, it gladly struggles against the inaccessible flashing of the radiant orb. Some such thing therefore do I myself suffer, who, though I see the eyes of mine own mind dimmed by the rays of the apostolic splendour, yet long to behold, as it were from afar, the soul of Paul glowing with the wondrous brightness of virtues, and to undergo a contentious struggle against the unbearable flashings of the sun. For Paul is a kind of sun to men, who hath illumined the whole world with the shining rays of his tongue: and who, going round all the nations, hath altogether imitated the course of the sun.
sepefulvidoceliglobodelectatusoculusadsp.la: Sæpe fúlvido cæli globo delectátus óculus, ad spectáculum oppósie regione lúminis sese violénter inténdit: et licet séntiat áciem suam imparem radiórum esse certámini, desidério tamen illius pulchérrimí lúminis intuéndi, libénter inaccessibili radiántis orbis reluctátur córúscó. Tale igitur quídam ego ipse perpétior, qui cum videam próprie mentis óculos ex rádiis apostólici splendóris hebetári, cúpio tamen Pauli ánimam, miro fulgóre virtútum rutilántem, velut éminus intuéri, et contra importábiles solis micátus contentiósa subíre certámina. Sol enim quidam est hominibus Paulus, qui totum prorsus orbem fulgéntibus linguæ suæ rádiis illuminávit: quique universas circumeúndo gentes, cursum omnino solis imitátus est.

magnificabiturchristusincorporemeosivepe.en: Christ shall be magnified in my body, whether it be by life, or by death. For to me, to live is Christ, and to die is gain.
magnificabiturchristusincorporemeosivepe.la: Magnificábitur Christus in córpore meo, sive per vitam, sive per mortem. Mihi enim vívere Christus est, et mori lucrum.

egenimiamdeliborettempusmeeresolutionisi.en: For I am even now ready to be sacrificed, and the time of my dissolution is at hand. I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith. There remaineth for me a crown of justice, which the Lord the just judge will render to me in that day.
egenimiamdeliborettempusmeeresolutionisi.la: Ego enim jam delibor et tempus meae resolutionis instat. Bonum certamen certavi, cursum consummavi, fidem servavi. Súperest mihi coróna justitiæ, quam reddet mihi Dóminus in illa die justus judex.

scienimcuicredidietcertussumquiapotenses.en: For I know whom I have believed, and I am certain that he is able to keep that which I have committed unto him, against that day.
scienimcuicredidietcertussumquiapotenses.la: Scio enim cui crédidi, et certus sum quia potens est depósitum meum serváre in illum diem.

bonumcertamencertavicursumconsummavifide.en: I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith. As to the rest, there is laid up for me a crown of justice, which the Lord the just judge will render to me in that day.
