bonumcertamencertavicursumconsummavifide.la: Bonum certámen certávi, cursum consummávi, fidem servávi. In réliquo repósita est mihi coróna justítiæ, quam reddet mihi Dóminus in illa die, justus judex.

omnipotensetmisericorsdeusmaiestatemtuam.en: Almighty and merciful God, we humbly entreat thy majesty: that as thou didst reveal thine Only-begotten to the child shut up in the womb through the Visitation and greeting of his Mother, so, by the merits and prayers of the same Mother, thou wouldst make us to behold him for ever with unveiled face:
omnipotensetmisericorsdeusmaiestatemtuam.la: Omnípotens et misericors Deus, maiestatem tuam suppliciter exorámus: ut, sicut Unigénitum tuum per Visitationem et salutationem Genetrícis ejus púero clauso in útero revelásti, ita, méritis ejusdem Genetrícis et précibus, ipsum nos fácias reveláta facie perpétuo contemplári:

gloriosevirginismarievisitationemdigniss.en: Let us tell again of the right worthy Visitation of the Blessed Virgin Mary.
gloriosevirginismarievisitationemdigniss.la: Gloriósæ Virginis Mariæ Visitatiónem digníssimam recolámus:

cuiusdominushumilitatemrespexitqueangelo.en: The same is she whose lowliness the Lord regarded, she who by the message of an Angel conceived the Saviour of the world.
cuiusdominushumilitatemrespexitqueangelo.la: Cujus Dóminus humilitátem respéxit: quæ Angelo nuntiánte concépit Redemptórem mundi.

hodievisitavitelisabethbeatavirgomariexp.en: This day the blessed Virgin Mary, of the lineage of David, visited Elizabeth.
hodievisitavitelisabethbeatavirgomariexp.la: Hódie visitávit Elísabeth beáta Virgo María ex progénie David.

stirpsiessevirgamproduxitvirgaqueflorem.en: The stem of Jesse hath brought forth a rod, and the rod a flower:
stirpsiessevirgamproduxitvirgaqueflorem.la: Stirps Jesse virgam prodúxit, virgáque florem:

etsuperhuncfloremrequiescitspiritusalmus.en: And upon this flower resteth the kindly Spirit.
etsuperhuncfloremrequiescitspiritusalmus.la: Et super hunc florem Requiéscit Spíritus almus.

virgodeigenetrixvirgestflosfiliuseius.en: The Virgin Mother of God is the rod: the flower is her Son.
virgodeigenetrixvirgestflosfiliuseius.la: Virgo Dei Génetrix virga est: flos Filius ejus.

visitatiogloriosevirginismarieexsemineab.en: The Visitation of the glorious Virgin Mary, of the seed of Abraham, sprung from the tribe of Juda, of the illustrious lineage of David:
visitatiogloriosevirginismarieexsemineab.la: Visitatio gloriósæ Virginis Mariæ ex sémine Abrahæ, ortæ de tribu Juda, clara ex stirpe David:

cuiusvitainclitacunctasillustratecclesia.en: Whose famous life still sheddeth lustre upon all the Churches.
cuiusvitainclitacunctasillustratecclesia.la: Cujus vita ínclita cunctas illústrat Ecclésias.

visitatiotuadeigenatrixvirgogaudiumannun.en: Thy Visitation, O Virgin Mother of God, hath proclaimed joy to the whole world:
visitatiotuadeigenatrixvirgogaudiumannun.la: Visitatio tua, Dei Génatrix Virgo, gáudium annuntiávit univérso mundo:

felixnamqueesquesolagenetricisdignitatem.en: For blessed art thou, who alone hast obtained the dignity of a Mother, and hast not lost thy virginal chastity.
felixnamqueesquesolagenetricisdignitatem.la: Felix namque es, quæ sola Genetrícis dignitatem obtinuísti, et virginálem pudicitiam non amisísti.

adnutumdomininostrumditantishonorem.en: At the will of the Lord, who enricheth our honour,
adnutumdomininostrumditantishonorem.la: Ad nutum Dómini nostrum ditántis honórem,

sicutspinarosamgenuitiudeamariam.en: As the thorn the rose, Judea brought forth Mary.
sicutspinarosamgenuitiudeamariam.la: Sicut spina rosam, génuít Judæa Mariam.

utvitiumvirtusoperiretgratiaculpam.en: That virtue might cover vice, and grace our fault.
utvitiumvirtusoperiretgratiaculpam.la: Ut vitium virtus operíret, grátia culpam.

inhacsacrasolemnitateprecelsegenetricisd.en: On this sacred solemnity of Mary, the most exalted Mother of God.
inhacsacrasolemnitateprecelsegenetricisd.la: In hac sacra solemnitáte præcélsæ Genetrícis Dei Mariæ.

surgeproperaamicameacolumbameaformosamee.en: Arise, make haste, my love, my dove, my beautiful one, and come. For winter is now past, the rain is over and gone. The flowers have appeared in our land.
surgeproperaamicameacolumbameaformosamee.la: Surge, própera, amíca mea, colúmba mea, formósa mea, et veni. Jam enim hiems tránsiit, imber ábiit, et recéssit. Flores apparuérunt in terra nostra.

elegiteamdeusetpreelegiteam.en: God hath chosen her, and fore-chosen her.
elegiteamdeusetpreelegiteam.la: Elégit eam Deus, et præelégit eam.

ethabitareeamfecitintabernaculosuo.en: And hath made her to dwell in His tabernacle.
ethabitareeamfecitintabernaculosuo.la: Et habitáre eam fecit in tabernáculo suo.

visitationemhodiernamperpetuevirginisgen.en: Let us solemnly celebrate this day's Visitation of Mary, the ever-Virgin Mother of God, wherein the loftiness of her throne went forth, alleluia.
visitationemhodiernamperpetuevirginisgen.la: Visitatiónem hodiérnam perpétuæ Vírginis Genitrícis Dei Maríæ solémniter celebrémus, qua celsitúdo throni procéssit, allelúja.

virgosempermariasanctadeigenatrix.en: Mary, ever Virgin. Holy Mother of God.
virgosempermariasanctadeigenatrix.la: Virgo semper Mariá. Sancta Dei Génatrix.

eccedilectusmeusvenitsaliensinmontibustr.en: Behold my beloved cometh leaping upon the mountains, skipping over the hills: he is like a roe, or a young hart.
eccedilectusmeusvenitsaliensinmontibustr.la: Ecce diléctus meus venit sáliens in móntibus, transiliens colles: similis est cápreæ hinnulóque cervórum.

ostendemihifaciemtuamsonetvoxtuainauribu.en: Shew me thy face, let thy voice sound in my ears: for thy voice is sweet, and thy face comely.
ostendemihifaciemtuamsonetvoxtuainauribu.la: Osténde mihi fáciem tuam, sonet vox tua in áuribus meis: vox enim tua dulcis, et fácies tua decóra.

gloriosusdeiamicusireneusiesudominiconfe.en: Irenæus, the glorious friend of God, grounded in the confession of the Lord Jesus, stood undaunted amid the pains of torments:
gloriosusdeiamicusireneusiesudominiconfe.la: Gloriósus Dei amicus Irenæus, Jesu Dómini confessióne fundátus, inter tormentórum supplícia stetit impertérritus:

acdemumtriumphalimorteinsigniscelospetiv.en: And at last, renowned by a triumphant death, he sought the heavens, crowned with the laurel of his blood.
acdemumtriumphalimorteinsigniscelospetiv.la: Ac demum triumpháli morte insignis, Cælos petívit sángine laureátus.

felicicommercioproterreniscelestiaproper.en: By a happy exchange, giving earthly things for heavenly, perishing things for eternal.
felicicommercioproterreniscelestiaproper.la: Felici commércio, pro terrénis cæléstia, pro peritúris æténa commútans.

celospetivitsanginelaureatus.en: He sought the heavens, crowned with the laurel of his blood.

deusquibeatumbenedictumpontificembenedic.en: O God, who didst raise blessed Benedict thy Bishop to heaven by the grace of thy blessing: sanctify, we beseech thee, thy people with a new blessing; and by his merits and prayers defend them by thy power from all evils that threaten.
deusquibeatumbenedictumpontificembenedic.la: Deus, qui beátum Benedíctum Pontíficem benedictionis tuæ grátia ad cælum sublevasti: pópulum tuum, quǽsumus, nova benedictióne sanctífica; et a cunctis malis imminentibus, ejus méritis et précibus, tua virtúte defende.

pabulumprebentpopulosalutis.en: They give the food of salvation to the people:

necmineterrentdeusipsecorda.en: Nor do threats affright them: God himself, foreseeing,
necmineterrentdeusipsecorda.la: Nec minæ terrent: Deus ipse corda

sitpatrivirtushonoretpotestas.la: Sit Patri virtus, honor et potéstas,

filiositlausparilisperevum.en: To the Son be equal praise for ever,
filiositlausparilisperevum.la: Filio sit laus párilis per ævum,

flaminisanctoresonentperenni.en: To the Holy Spirit let there resound unending

deusquibeatorummartyrumtuorumioannisetso.en: O God, who didst adorn with the laurel of eternity the glorious struggle for thy faith of thy blessed Martyrs John and his companions: mercifully grant that, striving on earth by their merits and imitation, we may merit to be crowned with them in heaven.
deusquibeatorummartyrumtuorumioannisetso.la: Deus, qui beatórum Mártyrum tuórum Joánnis et sociórum ejus gloriósum pro fide tua certámen æternitátis láurea decorásti: concéde propítius ut, eórum méritis et imitatione certátes in terris, cum ipsis coronári mereámur in cælis.

deumquisuosmartyreseterniscoronisdecorav.la: Deum, qui suos Mártýres ætérnis corónis decorávit, * Veníte, adorémus.

sicdiemfortesobeuntsupremum.en: Thus the brave meet their last day,

hostisinsaniferavistriumphat.en: The fierce might of the raging foe triumpheth,

membraspargunturtemerataterram.en: The violated limbs are scattered, the earth

nonabieruntinconsilioimpiorumsedinlegedo.en: They have not walked in the counsel of the ungodly, but their will was in the law of the Lord.
nonabieruntinconsilioimpiorumsedinlegedo.la: Non abiérunt in consílio impiórum, sed in lege Dómini fuit volúntas eórum. Ps. 1

supersionmontemsanctumdominipredicabantp.en: Upon Sion, the holy mountain of the Lord, they preached his commandment.
supersionmontemsanctumdominipredicabantp.la: Super Sion, montem sanctum Dómini, prædicábant præcéptum ejus. Ps. 2

oculidominiinpauperesrespiciuntquoniamiu.en: The eyes of the Lord look upon the poor, for the Lord is just, and hath loved justice.
oculidominiinpauperesrespiciuntquoniamiu.la: Oculi Dómini in páuperes respíciunt, quóniam justus Dóminus et justítias diléxit. Ps. 10

habitabuntintabernaculodeietrequiescentv.en: They shall dwell in the tabernacle of God, and the victors shall rest in his holy mountain.
habitabuntintabernaculodeietrequiescentv.la: Habitábunt in tabernáculo Dei, et requiéscent victóres in monte sancto ejus. Ps. 14

dominusparshereditatiseorumetcaliciseoru.en: The Lord is the portion of their inheritance and of their cup: it is he that restoreth their inheritance to them.
dominusparshereditatiseorumetcaliciseoru.la: Dóminus pars hereditátis eórum et cálicis eórum: ipse est qui restítuit hereditátem eis. Ps. 15

ascendentinmontemdominietstabuntinlocosa.en: They shall ascend into the mountain of the Lord, and shall stand in his holy place: and they shall receive a blessing from the Lord.
ascendentinmontemdominietstabuntinlocosa.la: Ascéndent in montem Dómini et stabunt in loco sancto ejus: et accípient benedictiónem a Dómino. Ps. 23

oculidominisuperiustosuteruatamorteanima.en: The eyes of the Lord are upon the just, to deliver their souls from death.
oculidominisuperiustosuteruatamorteanima.la: Oculi Dómini super justos, ut éruat a morte ánimas eórum. Ps. 32

iuxtestdominusiisquitribulatosuntcordeet.en: The Lord is nigh unto them that are of a contrite heart, and he will save the humble of spirit: the Lord will redeem the souls of his servants.
iuxtestdominusiisquitribulatosuntcordeet.la: Juxta est Dóminus iis qui tribuláto sunt corde, et húmiles spíritu salvábít: rédimet Dóminus ánimas servórum suórum. Ps. 33

dominusvirtutumnobiscumsusceptornosterde.en: The Lord of hosts is with us: the God of Jacob is our protector.
dominusvirtutumnobiscumsusceptornosterde.la: Dóminus virtútum nobiscum: suscéptor noster Deus Jacob. Ps. 45

auditestquasivoxturbarummultarumincelodi.en: I heard as it were the voice of many multitudes in heaven, saying: Alleluia:
auditestquasivoxturbarummultarumincelodi.la: Audita est quasi vox turbárum multárum in cælo dicéntium: Allelúja:

salusetglorietvirtusdeonostroinseculasec.en: Salvation and glory and power to our God For ever and ever.
salusetglorietvirtusdeonostroinseculasec.la: Salus et glória et virtus Deo nostro In sæcula sæculórum.

quiaveretiustasuntiudicieiusetvindicavit.en: For true and just are his judgments, and he hath revenged the blood of his servants.
quiaveretiustasuntiudicieiusetvindicavit.la: Quia vera et justa sunt judicia ejus, et vindicávit ságuinem servórum suórum.

seculumdecimumsextumcalvinianepravitatis.en: The sixteenth century, memorable for the tumults of the Calvinist depravity, produced in Holland a signal example of Christian fortitude. For nineteen martyrs, called those of Gorcum, gloriously contended for the assertion of the real presence of the Body of Christ in the Eucharist and of the primacy of the Roman Pontiff. Among these is numbered John of Germany, of the Order of Preachers, a son of the convent of Cologne. When, at the bidding of his superiors, he was administering the parish of Hoornaar in Holland, and was going to the town of Gorcum in order to baptize an infant, he was seized by soldiers and cast into prison, and was made a sharer of the lot of the other priests and religious who were already there for the cause of the faith. Their constancy was harried with divers mockeries and torments through very many days and nights. Then, put on board a ship half-naked, they were brought to Brielle, having suffered incredible things on the way from the soldiers, the sailors and the heretical rabble. At length, hanged from a beam, with nooses drawn tight about their throats, they received the palm of martyrdom on the ninth day of July in the year fifteen hundred and seventy-two. Pius the Ninth inscribed them, famed for miracles, in the roll of the Saints.
seculumdecimumsextumcalvinianepravitatis.la: Sæculum décimum sextum, Calvinianæ pravitátis tumultibus memorábile, insigne christiánæ fortitudinis in Hollándia tulit exéplum. Novédecim quippe mártyres, Gorcomiéses nuncupáti, pro asseréda reáli Córporis Christi in Eucharistia præséntia et Románi Pontificis primátu, glorióse certárunt. His adnumerátur Joánnes Germánus ordinis Prædicatórum, cénóbii Coloniésis alúmus. Is cum, superiórum nutu, Hornariésem in Hollándia paróciam administráret atque infántuli baptizándi grátia oppidum Gorcom adiret, a satellitibus deprehésus et in carcerem coniéctus, ceterórum sacerdotum et religiosórum pro causa fidei ibi jam degéntium sortis párticeps factus est. Váriis ludibriis et tormétis per dies noctésque plúrimas exagitáta est eórum constantia. Deinde in navem impósiti seminúdi Brilam adducúntur, incredibilia in itinere a militibus, nautis et hærética plebe passi. Tandem trahi appénsi, adstrictis láqueo fáucibus, martýrii palmam accepérunt die nono iúlii anni millésimi quingentésimi septuagésimi secúdi. Miráculis claros Pius nonus Sanctórum fastis adscripsit.

induitdominussanctossuosfortitudineettes.en: The Lord hath clothed his Saints with strength, and his testimonies are become exceedingly credible.
induitdominussanctossuosfortitudineettes.la: Induit Dóminus Sanctos suos fortitudine, et testimónia ejus credibilia facta sunt nimis.

ovespascedominiintroieruntportaseiusinco.en: The sheep of the Lord's pasture have entered into his gates with praise, and into his courts with hymns.
ovespascedominiintroieruntportaseiusinco.la: Oves páscae Dómini introiérunt portas ejus in confessióe et átria ejus in hymnis.

labiisexsultationislaudabuntdominumobstr.en: With joyful lips shall they praise the Lord: the mouth of them that speak wicked things is stopped.
labiisexsultationislaudabuntdominumobstr.la: Lábiis exsultatiónis laudábunt Dóminum: obstrúctum est os loquéntium iniqua.

benedicitesacerdotesdominidominumlaudate.en: O ye priests of the Lord, bless the Lord: praise and exalt him above all for ever.
benedicitesacerdotesdominidominumlaudate.la: Benedícite, sacerdótes Dómini, Dóminum: laudáte et superexaltáte eum in sǎcula.

exsultabuntsanctiinglorietletabunturincu.en: The Saints shall rejoice in glory, and shall be joyful in their beds.
exsultabuntsanctiinglorietletabunturincu.la: Exsultábunt Sancti in glória, et lætabúntur in cubílibus suis.

sanctiviceruntproptersanguinemagnietprop.en: The Saints overcame by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony: and they loved not their lives unto death.
sanctiviceruntproptersanguinemagnietprop.la: Sancti vicérunt propter sánguinem Agni et propter verbum testimónii sui: et non dilexérunt ánimas suas usque ad mortem.

huctuisadsismemoracpotenti.la: Huc tuis adsis memor, ac poténti

dominusdeusisrelvisitavitetfecitredempti.en: The Lord God of Israel hath visited, and wrought the redemption of his servants: he hath glorified their name for ever, and hath raised up a horn of salvation for us.
dominusdeusisrelvisitavitetfecitredempti.la: Dóminus, Deus Israél, visitávit et fecit redemptionem servórum suórum: glorificávit nomen eórum in ætérnum, et eréxit cornu salútis nobis.

accessistisadsionmontemetcivitatemdeiviv.en: You are come to mount Sion, and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to the company of many thousands of angels, and to the church of the firstborn, who are written in the heavens.
accessistisadsionmontemetcivitatemdeiviv.la: Accessístis ad Sion montem, et civitátem Dei vivéntis, Jerúsalem cæléstem, et multórum míllium angelórum frequéntiam, et Ecclésiam primitivórum, qui conscrípti sunt in cælis.

orapronobisbeateioannescumsociistuis.en: Pray for us, blessed John, with thy companions.
orapronobisbeateioannescumsociistuis.la: Ora pro nobis, beáte Joánnes cum sóciis tuis.

exaltavitdominushumilesservossuosetsusce.en: The Lord hath exalted his humble servants, and hath taken them up into the holy tabernacles, being mindful of his mercy.
exaltavitdominushumilesservossuosetsusce.la: Exaltávit Dóminus húmiles servos suos, et suscepit eos in tabernácula sancta, recordátus misericórdiæ suæ.

laveruntstolassuasetcandidaseasfecerunt.la: Lavérunt stolas suas, et cándidas eas fecérunt

septemfratresfiliisanctefelicitatisromei.en: The seven brethren, sons of St. Felicity, at Rome, in the persecution of Marcus Aurelius Antoninus, were tempted by the prefect Publius first with blandishments, then with terrors, that they might renounce Christ and worship the gods: and persevering in the confession of the faith, by their own courage and at their mother's exhortation, they were put to death in divers ways. Januarius was beaten with leaded scourges; Felix and Philip were bruised to death with cudgels; Silvanus was cast headlong from a very high place; Alexander, Vitalis and Martial were beheaded. Their mother obtained the same palm of martyrdom four months after; they gave up their spirit to the Lord on the sixth of the Ides of July.
septemfratresfiliisanctefelicitatisromei.la: Septem fratres, filii sanctæ Felicitátis, Romæ in persecutióne Marci Aurélii Antonini a Públio præfécito primum blanditiis, deinde terróribus tentáti, ut Christo renuntiántes deos veneraréntur: et sua virtúte et matre hortánte in fidei confessióne perseverántes, várie necáti sunt. Januárius plumbátis cæsus; Felix et Philippus fústibus contúsi; Silvánus ex altíssimo loco præceps deiéctus est; Alexánder, Vitális et Martiális cápite plectúntur. Mater eórum quarto post mense eándem martýrii palmam consecúta est; illi sexto Idus júlii spíritum Dómino reddidérunt.

deusquibeatorumpontificumignatiietdomini.en: O God, who didst will that the lands of the Annamites should be watered with the blood of the blessed Bishops Ignatius and Dominic and their companions: by the intercession of so great Martyrs make them to flourish in the Christian religion.
deusquibeatorumpontificumignatiietdomini.la: Deus, qui beatórum Pontificum Ignátii et Domínici ac sociórum sanguine Annamitarum terras rigári voluísti; intercedéntibus tantis Martýribus, fac eas christiána religióne florére.

deusquibeatumiacobumconfessorematquepont.en: O God, who didst make blessed James, thy Confessor and Bishop, an eminent herald of truth and a maker of peace: grant us by his intercession that we may love peace and truth, and may come unto thee, in whom is highest peace and pure truth.
deusquibeatumiacobumconfessorematquepont.la: Deus, qui beátum Jacóbum, Confessórem atque Pontíficem, exímium veritátis præcónem et pacis conciliatórem effecísti: ejus nobis intercessióne concéde ut pacem et veritátem diligámus, et ad te, in quo pax summa est et pura véritas, perveniámus.

commemorationemhodiernamperpetuevirginis.en: Let us solemnly celebrate this day's Commemoration of Mary, the ever-Virgin Mother of God, wherein the loftiness of her throne went forth, alleluia.
commemorationemhodiernamperpetuevirginis.la: Commemoratiónem hodiérnam perpétuæ Virgínis Genetrícis Dei Mariæ solémniter celebrémus, qua celsitúdo throni procéssit, allelúja.

deusquibeatumceslaumvirgineomorumcandore.en: O God, who didst make blessed Ceslaus, endowed with virginal purity of life and kindled with zeal for the salvation of souls, wonderful among the peoples of divers nations by the holiness of his works and the spreading of the faith: grant, we beseech thee, that by his intercession we may ever be steadfast in the faith, and by the gift of thy mercy may be able to come unto thee, who alone art the author and giver of eternal salvation.
deusquibeatumceslaumvirgineomorumcandore.la: Deus, qui beátum Cesláum, virgíneo morum candóre præditum et salútis animárum zelo succénsus, in diversis nationum pópulis óperum sanctitáte et fidei propagatione miráblem effecísti: præsta, quæsumus, ut ejus intercessióne simus semper in fide stábiles, et ad te, qui solus es ætérnæ salútis auctor ac largítor, misericórdiæ tuæ múnere pervenire valeámus.

largirenobisclementissimepaterutsicutbea.en: Grant us, most clement Father: that, as blessed Mary Magdalen, by loving our Lord Jesus Christ above all things, obtained pardon of her sins, so she may obtain for us everlasting blessedness with thy mercy.
largirenobisclementissimepaterutsicutbea.la: Largire nobis, clementissime Pater: ut, sicut beáta María Magdaléna, Dóminum nostrum Jesum Christum super ómnia diligendo, suorum obtinuit véniam peccatorum, ita nobis, apud misericórdiam tuam, sempitérnam impetret beatitúdinem.

eternumtrinumquedeumlaudemusetunumquisib.en: Let us praise God, eternal, threefold and one, * Who hath borne holy Mary unto himself into the heavens.
eternumtrinumquedeumlaudemusetunumquisib.la: Ætérnum trinúmque Deum laudémus et unum, * Qui sibi Mariam transvéxit in æthera sanctam.

secuspedesdominiastansincessantecrinesol.en: Standing at the feet of the Lord, unceasingly, with loosened hair, full of tears she kissed the divine footsteps.
secuspedesdominiastansincessantecrinesol.la: Secus pedes Dómini astans, incessánte, crine solúto, diva vestigia osculabátur lácrimis plena. Ps. 18

irrigabatigiturdominicosiesupedesfractoq.en: She therefore watered the feet of the Lord Jesus: and the alabaster box being broken, the whole house was fragrant with choicest odours: and she wiped them with the service of her hair.
irrigabatigiturdominicosiesupedesfractoq.la: Irrigábat igitur Domínicos Jesu pedes: fracto quoque alabástro, præcípui odóribus fragrábat domus omnis: atque capillórum officio detergébat. Ps. 23

simonautemintraseinquitsiessetprophetasc.en: But Simon said within himself: If he were a prophet, he would surely know who and what manner of woman this is that toucheth him: for she is a sinner.
simonautemintraseinquitsiessetprophetasc.la: Simon autem intra se inquit: Si esset prophéta, sciret profecto quæ et qualis est, quæ tangit eum: quia peccátrix est. Ps. 44

etconversusdominusdixitpostquamvenitindo.en: And the Lord, turning, said: Since she came into thy house, she hath not ceased, with hair outpoured, to kiss my feet.
etconversusdominusdixitpostquamvenitindo.la: Et convérsus Dóminus, dixit: Postquam venit in domum tuam, non cessat, crine fuso, hæc meos osculári pedes. Ps. 45

quoniammultumdilexerasdimissascitotibipe.en: Because thou hadst loved much, know that thy sins are forgiven thee: and by the faith wherein thou art strong, depart in holy peace.
quoniammultumdilexerasdimissascitotibipe.la: Quóniam multum diléxeras, dimíssa scito tibi peccámina: et fide, qua polles, sacra in pace remíttito.;;86

satagebatigiturmarthasorormariemagdalene.en: Martha, therefore, the sister of Mary Magdalen, was busy about much serving: who, sitting at the feet of the Lord, heard the words of his mouth.
satagebatigiturmarthasorormariemagdalene.la: Satagébat igitur Martha soror Mariæ Magdalénæ circa ministéria: quæ sedens secus pedes Dómini audiébat verba oris ejus. Ps. 95

nonestmarthainquittibicurequodsorormeame.en: Hast thou no care, saith Martha, that my sister hath left me alone to serve? Speak to her therefore, that she help me.
nonestmarthainquittibicurequodsorormeame.la: Non est, Martha inquit, tibi curæ quod soror mea me relíquit solam ministráre? jube illi ut me ádiuvet. Ps. 96

etrespondensdixitillidominusunumestneces.en: And the Lord answering said to her: One thing is necessary: Mary hath chosen the best part, which shall not be taken away from her.
etrespondensdixitillidominusunumestneces.la: Et respóndens dixit illi Dóminus: Unum est necesse: María óptimam sibi partem elégit, quæ non auferétur ab ea. Ps. 97

quamiesuseternusamordilexitplurimum.en: Whom Jesus, eternal love, loved exceedingly.
quamiesuseternusamordilexitplurimum.la: Quam Jesus ætérnus amor diléxit plúrimum.

hecmariafuitilladominogratissimaqueungue.en: This Mary was she, most pleasing to the Lord, who anointed the feet of the Lord with precious ointment.
hecmariafuitilladominogratissimaqueungue.la: Hæc Mariá fuit illa Dómino gratíssima, quæ unguénto pretióso pedes unxit Dómini.

felixmariaunxitpedesdominiiesuetextersit.en: Blessed Mary anointed the feet of the Lord Jesus, and wiped them with her hair:
felixmariaunxitpedesdominiiesuetextersit.la: Felix Maria unxit pedes Dómini Jesu et extérsit capillis suis:

etdomusimpletestexodoreunguenti.en: And the house was filled with the odour of the ointment.
etdomusimpletestexodoreunguenti.la: Et domus impléta est ex odóre unguénti.

mixtumrorembalsamifractofuditalabastroqu.en: She poured out the mingled dew of balm from the broken alabaster box, who anointed the feet of the Lord with precious ointment.
mixtumrorembalsamifractofuditalabastroqu.la: Mixtum rorem bálsami fracto fudit alabástro, quæ unguénto pretióso pedes unxit Dómini.

gloriosahuiusdieisolemniadevotacelebremu.en: Let us all celebrate with devout veneration the glorious solemnity of this day, whereon blessed Mary Magdalen
gloriosahuiusdieisolemniadevotacelebremu.la: Gloriósa hujus diéi solémnia devóta celebrémus omnes veneratióne, qua beáta María Magdaléna

consummatocursupresentisvitecelestievoca.en: Having finished the course of this present life, called forth by heavenly loving-kindness.
consummatocursupresentisvitecelestievoca.la: Consummáto cursu præséntis vitæ, cælésti evocáta pietáte.

rcelosmeruitascendere.en: R. Merited to ascend into heaven.

quanonaufereturabea.en: Which shall not be taken away from her.

laudibusexcelsisomnismundusexsultetinsol.en: Let all the world exult with highest praises on the solemnity of St. Mary Magdalen.
laudibusexcelsisomnismundusexsultetinsol.la: Láudibus excélsis omnis mundus exsúltet in solemnitáte sanctæ Mariæ Magdalænæ.

heccordecompunctavenitadpedesiesuaccesit.en: She came with contrite heart, she drew near to the feet of Jesus: she watered them with tears and wiped them with the hairs of her head.
heccordecompunctavenitadpedesiesuaccesit.la: Hæc corde compúncta venit, ad pedes Jesu accésit: illos lácrimis rigávit et capíllis cápitis sui tersit.

intercedesupplicaassiduepronobisiesudomi.en: Intercede, entreat unceasingly for us the Lord Jesus, O Mary Magdalen.
intercedesupplicaassiduepronobisiesudomi.la: Intercéde, súpplíca assídue pro nobis Jesu Dómino, María Magdaléna.

oboneiesulaustibiremisistipeccatricimult.en: O good Jesus, praise be to thee! Thou hast forgiven the sinful woman her many sins, because she loved thee much.
oboneiesulaustibiremisistipeccatricimult.la: O bone Jesu, laus tibi! Remisísti peccatríci multa peccámina, quia te diléxit multum.

omundilampasetmargaritaprefulgidaqueresu.en: O lamp of the world and pearl most resplendent, who by announcing the resurrection of Christ didst merit to become the Apostle of the Apostles, O Mary Magdalen, be ever with us as a loving intercessor for us with God, who hath chosen thee.
omundilampasetmargaritaprefulgidaqueresu.la: O mundi lampas et margarita præfulgida, quæ resurrectionem Christi nuntiando Apostolorum Apóstola fieri meruisti, María Magdaléna, semper pia exoratrix pro nobis adsis ad Deum, qui te elégit.

obeateiacobeomniumcordeetorelaudandeopat.en: O blessed James, to be praised with the heart and mouth of all, O singular and lovable patron, intercede for us with the Lord.
obeateiacobeomniumcordeetorelaudandeopat.la: O beáte Jacóbe, ómnium corde et ore laudánde, o patróné singuláris et amábilis, intercède pro nobis ad Dóminum. Ps. 112, 116, 145, 146, 147

oluxetdecushispaniesanctissimeiacobequii.en: O light and glory of Spain, most holy James, who holdest the primacy among the Apostles, the first of them to be crowned with martyrdom: O singular protection, who didst merit to see our Redeemer, while yet mortal, transfigured in his Godhead, hear the prayers of thy servants, and intercede for our salvation and that of all peoples.
oluxetdecushispaniesanctissimeiacobequii.la: O lux et decus Hispániæ, sanctíssime Jacóbe, qui inter Apóstolos primátum tenes, primus eórum mátyrio laureátus: o singuláre præsidium, qui meruísti vidére Redemptórem nostrum adhuc mortálem in Deitate transformátum, exáudi preces servórum tuórum et intercède pro nostra salute omniúmque populórum.

deepistolabeatipauliapostoliadephesios.en: From the letter of the blessed Apostle Paul to the Ephesians
deepistolabeatipauliapostoliadephesios.la: De Epístola beáti Pauli Apóstoli ad Ephésios

christumhabitareperfidemincordibusvestri.en: That Christ may dwell by faith in your hearts.
christumhabitareperfidemincordibusvestri.la: Christum habitáre per fidem in córdibus vestris.

respondensautemiesusdixiteisnescitisquid.en: And Jesus answering, said to them: You know not what you ask.
respondensautemiesusdixiteisnescitisquid.la: Respóndens autem Jesus, dixit eis: Néscitis quid petátis.

aitilliscalicemquidemmeumbibetis.en: He saith to them: My chalice indeed you shall drink.
aitilliscalicemquidemmeumbibetis.la: Ait illis: Cálicem quidem meum bibétis.

memoriasschristophorietcucuphatismm.en: Commemoration of Sts. Christopher and Cucuphas, Martyrs
memoriasschristophorietcucuphatismm.la: Memoria Ss. Christophori et Cucuphatis Mm.

prestaquesumusomnipotensdeusutquiglorios.en: Grant, we beseech thee, almighty God: that we who know thy glorious Martyrs Christopher and Cucuphas to have been brave in their confession, may feel them loving in their intercession for us with thee.
prestaquesumusomnipotensdeusutquiglorios.la: Præsta, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, qui gloriósos Mártyres tuos Christóphorum et Cucuphátém fortes in sua confessióne cognóvimus, pios apud te in nostra intercessióne sentiámus.

muliersensatettacitanonestimmutatierudit.en: A wise and silent woman: there is nothing so much worth as a well instructed soul.
muliersensatettacitanonestimmutatierudit.la: Múlier sensáta et tácita, non est immutátio erudítæ ánimæ.

omnisautemponderationonestdignacontinent.en: And no price is worthy of a continent soul.
omnisautemponderationonestdignacontinent.la: Omnis autem ponderátio non est digna continéntis ánimæ.

gaudeamusomnesindominodiemfestumcelebran.en: Let us all rejoice in the Lord, celebrating a festal day in honour of blessed Anne,
gaudeamusomnesindominodiemfestumcelebran.la: Gaudeámus omnes in Dómino, diem festum celebrántes sub honóre beátæ Annæ,

decuiussolemnitategaudentangelietcollaud.en: At whose solemnity the Angels rejoice, and join in praising the Son of God.
decuiussolemnitategaudentangelietcollaud.la: De cujus solemnitáte gaudent Angeli, et colláudant Fílium Dei.

sicutsaraobediebatabrahedominumeumvocans.en: As Sara obeyed Abraham, calling him lord.
sicutsaraobediebatabrahedominumeumvocans.la: Sicut Sara obediébat Abrahæ, dóminum eum vocans.

deepistolaprimabeatipauliapostoliadtimot.en: From the first letter of the blessed Apostle Paul to Timothy
deepistolaprimabeatipauliapostoliadtimot.la: De Epístola prima beáti Pauli Apóstoli ad Timótheum

deusquibeatamannamgenetricistuematremadc.en: O God, who didst raise blessed Anne, the mother of thy Mother, to the joys of the heavenly life: grant, we beseech thee, that by her glorious merits we may attain to eternal blessedness, of whose saving offspring thou didst vouchsafe to take human nature for the salvation of the world: Who livest.
deusquibeatamannamgenetricistuematremadc.la: Deus, qui beátam Annam, Genetrícis tuæ matrem, ad cæléstis vitæ gáudia extulísti: fac nos, quæsumus, gloriósus ejus méritis ad ætérnam pertíngere beatitúdinem, ex cujus salutári puerpério pro salúte mundi humanam natúram assúmere dignátus es: Qui vivis.

martyrumtuorumnosdomineiosephietmelchior.en: May the blessed confession of thy Martyrs Joseph, Melchior and their companions fortify us, O Lord: and graciously implore help for our frailty.
martyrumtuorumnosdomineiosephietmelchior.la: Mártyrum tuórum nos, Dómine, Joséphi, et Melchióris et sociórum conféssio beáta commúniat: et fragilitáti nostræ subsídium dignánter exóret.

gaudefelixparenshispanianoveprolisdansmu.en: Rejoice, O Spain, happy parent, giving to the world the joys of a new offspring: but do thou, Bologna, applaud the more, endowed with the glory of so great a Father: praise him, O Mother Church, all of thee, keeping the solemnity of a new praise.
gaudefelixparenshispanianoveprolisdansmu.la: Gaude felix parens Hispánia, novæ prolis dans mundo gáudia: sed tu magis plaude Bonónia, tanti Patris dotáta glória: lauda tota Mater Ecclésia, novæ laudis agens solémnia. Ps. 112, 116, 145, 146, 147

ospemmiramquamdedistimortishorateflentib.en: O wondrous hope which thou gavest to them that wept for thee in the hour of death, when thou didst promise that after death thou wouldst be of help to thy brethren!
ospemmiramquamdedistimortishorateflentib.la: O spem miram, quam dedísti mortis hora te fléntibus, dum post mortem promisísti te profutúrum frátribus!

implepaterquoddixistinostuisiuvansprecib.en: Fulfil, O Father, what thou hast said, helping us by thy prayers.
implepaterquoddixistinostuisiuvansprecib.la: Imple, Pater, quod dixísti, nos tuis juvans précibus.

quitotsignisclaruistiinegrorumcorporibus.en: Thou who didst shine with so many signs in the bodies of the sick, bringing us the help of Christ, heal our sick ways.
quitotsignisclaruistiinegrorumcorporibus.la: Qui tot signis claruísti in ægrórum corpóribus, nobis opem ferens Christi, ægris medére móribus.

quenoveprolisgaudia.en: Who sendest the joys of a new offspring

mundiiamfulgetterminis.en: Now shineth to the bounds of the world,

carnisliberergastulo.en: Free from the prison-house of the flesh,

celipotiturgloria.en: He possesseth the glory of heaven:

stoladotaturregia.en: He is endowed with a royal robe.

fragransodordetumulo.en: The fragrant odour from the tomb,

clamatprochristifamulo.en: Proclaimeth, for the servant of Christ,

summiregismagnalia.en: The mighty works of the most high King.

quinosprecedominici.en: May he, by the prayer of Dominic, us

ducatadceligaudia.en: Lead to the joys of heaven.

transitpauperadregnisoliumduxadsceptrumv.en: The poor man passeth to the throne of the kingdom, the leader to the sceptre, the victor to the reward, death into life, toil into rest; present mourning giveth way to joy.
transitpauperadregnisoliumduxadsceptrumv.la: Transit pauper ad regni sólium, dux ad sceptrum, victor ad prǽmium, mors in vitam, labor in ótium, præsens cedit luctus in gáudium.

adsuntdominiciletasolemnialaudemultiplic.en: Here is the glad solemnity of Dominic: * let the Church applaud with manifold praise.
adsuntdominiciletasolemnialaudemultiplic.la: Adsunt Domínici læta solémnia * Laude multíplici plaudat Ecclésia.

novusathletadomini.en: The new champion of the Lord,

quiremconformatnomini.en: Who maketh the thing agree with the name,

virfactusevangelicus.en: Being made a man of the Gospel.

mundumcalcanssubpedibus.en: Treading the world under his feet,

manummisitadfortia.en: He put his hand to strong things,

nudusoccurenshostibus.en: Going bare to meet the enemies,

christisuffultusgratia.en: Upheld by the grace of Christ.

pugnatverbomiraculis.en: He fighteth by word, by miracles,

missusperorbemfratribus.en: Sending his brethren throughout the world:

preconovusetcelicusmissusinfineseculipau.en: A new and heavenly herald, sent at the end of the age, Dominic shone forth in poverty, foreseen in the form of a whelp.
preconovusetcelicusmissusinfineseculipau.la: Præco novus et cǽlicus, missus in fine sǽculi, pauper fulsit Domínicus, forma prævísus cátuli. Ps. 1

florempudicitieservansillibatumattigitex.en: Keeping the flower of chastity unblemished, he attained the celibacy of an excellent life.
florempudicitieservansillibatumattigitex.la: Florem pudicítiæ servans illibátum, áttigit exímiæ vitte cælibátum. Ps. 2

documentisartiumeruditussatistransiitads.en: Well instructed in the teachings of the arts, he passed on to the study of the highest truth.
documentisartiumeruditussatistransiitads.la: Documéntis ártium erudítus satis, tránsiit ad stúdium summæ veritátis. Ps. 3

subaugustiniregulamenteprofecitsedulatan.en: Under the rule of Augustine he made progress with diligent mind: at length he enlarged the canon into an apostolic man.
subaugustiniregulamenteprofecitsedulatan.la: Sub Augustíni régula mente profécit sédula: tandem virum canónicum auget in apostólicum. Ps. 4

agonizansprochristinominemundumrepletdiv.en: Striving for the name of Christ, he filleth the world with divine seed, living under the covering of poverty.
agonizansprochristinominemundumrepletdiv.la: Agonízans pro Christi nómine, mundum replet divíno sémine, paupertátis degens sub tégmine. Ps. 5

pernoxcumchristopropriumnonpossidebatlec.en: Watching all night with Christ, he possessed not a bed of his own: after a flood of tears, scarce moistening his little body.
pernoxcumchristopropriumnonpossidebatlec.la: Pernox cum Christo próprium non possidébat léctulum: post lacrimárum flúvium, vix humidans corpúsculum. Ps. 8

sitiebatservuschristimartyriumsicutsitit.en: The servant of Christ thirsted for martyrdom, as the hart thirsteth for the stream of water.
sitiebatservuschristimartyriumsicutsitit.la: Sitiébat servus Christi martýrium, sicut sitit cervus ad aqua flúvium. Ps. 14

migranspaterfiliisvitefirmamentumpaupert.en: The Father, departing, maketh for his sons, as the stay of life, the testament of humble poverty.
migranspaterfiliisvitefirmamentumpaupert.la: Migrans Pater fíliis, vitæ firmaméntum, paupertátis húmilis condit testaméntum. Ps. 20

libercarnisvinculocelumintroivitubipleno.en: Freed from the bond of the flesh, he entered heaven, where with full cup he tasteth that for which he thirsted.
libercarnisvinculocelumintroivitubipleno.la: Liber carnis vínculo cælum introívit, ubi pleno póculo gustat quod sitívit. Ps. 23

nonnestultamfecitdeussapientiamhuiusmund.en: Hath not God made foolish the wisdom of this world?
nonnestultamfecitdeussapientiamhuiusmund.la: Nonne stultam fecit Deus sapiéntiam hujus mundi?

mundumvocansadagninuptiashoracenepaterfa.en: Calling the world to the marriage of the Lamb, at the hour of supper the Master of the house sendeth his servant,
mundumvocansadagninuptiashoracenepaterfa.la: Mundum vocans ad Agni núptias, hora cenæ Paterfamílias servum mittit,

promittensvariasvitedelicias.en: Promising the divers delights of life.

adhocconviviumtampermagnificumelegitnunt.en: For this so magnificent banquet he chose a holy messenger, Dominic.
adhocconviviumtampermagnificumelegitnunt.la: Ad hoc convívium tam permagníficum elégit núntium sanctum Domínicum.

quodsietiamopertumestevangeliumnostrumin.en: And if our gospel be also hid, it is hid to them that are lost:
quodsietiamopertumestevangeliumnostrumin.la: Quod si étiam opértum est Evangélium nostrum, in iis, qui péreunt, est opértum:

datummundopromundigloriamirachristipresi.en: Him, given to the world for the glory of the world, the wondrous grace of Christ marked out beforehand:
datummundopromundigloriamirachristipresi.la: Datum mundo pro mundi glória, mira Christi præsígnat grátia:

cuiusortumpracurruntnuntiaveripressagia.en: Whose birth heralds went before, presages of the truth.
cuiusortumpracurruntnuntiaveripressagia.la: Cujus ortum pracúrrunt núntia, veri præsságia.

stellamicansinfronteparvulinovumiubarpre.en: A star shining on the infant's brow foresheweth a new radiance for the world.
stellamicansinfronteparvulinovumiubarpre.la: Stella micans in fronte párvuli novum jubar præmónstrat sǽculi.

habemusautemthesaurumistuminvasisfictili.en: But we have this treasure in earthen vessels, that the excellency may be of the power of God, and not of us.
habemusautemthesaurumistuminvasisfictili.la: Habémus autem thesáurum istum in vasis fictílibus: ut sublímitas sit virtútis Dei, et non ex nobis.

inomnibustribulationempatimursednonangus.en: In all things we suffer tribulation, but are not distressed; we are straitened, but are not destitute;
inomnibustribulationempatimursednonangus.la: In ómnibus tribulatiónem pátimur, sed non angustiámur: aporiámur, sed non destitúimur:

verbumvitedumpalampromitursurgunthostesl.en: While the word of life is openly brought forth, enemies rise up, a book is written, all give their favour:
verbumvitedumpalampromitursurgunthostesl.la: Verbum vitæ dum palam prómitur, surgunt hostes, liber conscríbitur, favent omnes:

sicerrorvinciturfidesextollitur.en: Thus error is overcome, the Faith is exalted.

terinflammaslibellustraditusterexivitill.en: Thrice was the little book cast into the flames, thrice it came forth wholly unharmed.
terinflammaslibellustraditusterexivitill.la: Ter in flammas libéllus tráditus, ter exívit illǽsus pénitus.

extheodoricodeapoldiasantoninetaliisgest.en: From Theodoric of Apolda, St. Antoninus and other writers of his deeds
extheodoricodeapoldiasantoninetaliisgest.la: Ex Theodorico de Apoldia, S. Antonino et aliis gestorúm ejus auctoribus

sanctssimuspaterdominicuscalarogeinhispa.en: The most holy Father Dominic was born at Calaruega in Spain, of the most noble family of the Guzmans. His mother, when with child, seemed to herself in her sleep to bear in her womb a whelp, which, carrying a torch in its mouth, set the whole world on fire: by which dream it was signified that by the splendour of his holiness and his teaching the nations would be enkindled unto Christian piety. After the studies of the liberal arts and of theology, from which he gained for himself singular learning, he was first a canon regular of the Church of Osma: then he founded the most illustrious Order of Preachers, from which innumerable examples of all holiness and learning have flowed forth into the Church, and which was confirmed by Honorius the Third, Supreme Pontiff, in the year of salvation one thousand two hundred and sixteen.
sanctssimuspaterdominicuscalarogeinhispa.la: Sanctssimus Pater Dominicus Calaróge in Hispánia ex nobilíssima Guzmanórum família natus est. Hujus mater grávida sibi visa est per quiétam continére in alvo cátulum, qui facem ore préferens, orbem terrárum incénderet: quo sómnio significabátur fore ut splendóre sanctitátis ac doctrína ejus gentes ad christiánam pietátem inflammaréntur. Post liberálium ártium ac theologíe stúdia, ex quibus singulárem sibi eruditiónem comparávit, primum Oxoménsis Ecclésie canónicus reguláris fuit: deínde claríssimum Praedicatórum órdinem, unde innúmera totíus sanctitátis et doctrínæ exémpla in Ecclésiam promanárunt, instítuit, ab Honório tértio Summo Pontífice confirmátum anno salútis millésimo ducentésimo décimo sexto.

paupertatisascendensculminaclamatmundide.en: Ascending the heights of poverty, he crieth out, detesting the crimes of the world; he breaketh the enemies and putteth their hosts to flight:
paupertatisascendensculminaclamatmundide.la: Paupertátis ascéndens cúlmina, clamat mundi detéstans crímina, frangit hostes et fugat ágmina:

nocteceliperlustransliminadieterisdatver.en: By night searching through the thresholds of heaven, by day he giveth to the earth the seeds of the word.
nocteceliperlustransliminadieterisdatver.la: Nocte cæli perlústrans límina, die teris dat verbi sémina.

postconfirmatumordinemnoctesinecclesiape.en: After the order was confirmed, he spent his nights in the church almost sleepless: and he prayed now kneeling on his knees, now prostrate with his whole body. And if ever a heavier sleep overcame his wearied limbs, he rested a little, standing leaning against the altar or reclining against a hard stone. Every night he scourged his bare body with an iron chain so sharply that streams of blood flowed down. He continually shed a very great abundance of tears, and above all when he was offering the holy sacrifice of the Mass. In nothing did he so rejoice as in contempt of himself: he kept perpetually a most unimpaired purity both of body and of soul.
postconfirmatumordinemnoctesinecclesiape.la: Post confirmátum órdinem, noctes in ecclésia pæne ducébat insómnes: ac modo in génua procúmbens, modo toto córpore prostrátus orábat. Et si quando grávior somnus fessa membra obrúeret, stans nixus altári vel ad durum lápidem inclinátus, páululum quiescébat. Caténa férrea síngulis nóctibus ádeo ácriter nudum corpus aflligébat, ut sánguinis rivi deflúerent. Máximam lacrimárum vim assídue profundébat: atque in primis cum sacrum Missæ sacrifícium peragébat. Nulla re æque letabátur ac sui contémptu: puritátem tum córporis tum ánimi integérrimam perpétuo servávit.

panisoblatuscelitusfratrumsuppletinopiam.en: Bread brought from heaven supplieth the want of the brethren:
panisoblatuscelitusfratrumsuppletinopiam.la: Panis oblátus cǽlitus fratrum supplet inópiam:

vitequenatusredditusmatrispellittristiti.en: And a son restored to life driveth away his mother's sadness.
vitequenatusredditusmatrispellittristiti.la: Vitǽque natus rédditus matris pellit tristítiam.

signocrucisobeditpluvialinguaverbatransf.en: The rain obeyeth the sign of the Cross, his tongue transformeth divers words.
signocrucisobeditpluvialinguaverbatransf.la: Signo Crucis obédit plúvia, lingua verba transfórmat vária.

peccatiseterumnishumanisvehementerdiscru.en: He was grievously tormented by the sins and miseries of men. He made his journeys barefoot, even through rough places, singing hymns. Of rare abstinence, he never ate flesh: nor did he break his fasts even when sick. He passed his whole life entirely free from mortal sin. A most observant guardian of his tongue, he spoke only with God or of God: and he scarcely had speech of other things. He was most thirsty for the salvation of souls, and also most desirous of martyrdom. He spent seven years in overthrowing the Albigensian heretics, many of them being brought to the Catholic faith. He shone with the greatest miracles both in life and after death: and among others, at Rome he raised three dead persons to life. He was a man plainly of apostolic heart and spirit, the pillar of the faith, the trumpet of the Gospel, the eye of the world, the lamp of Christ, a second Precursor, and a great steward of souls: whom the manifold crowns of such great virtues adorn in heaven.
peccatiseterumnishumanisvehementerdiscru.la: Peccátis et ærúmnis humánis veheménter discruciabátur. Itínera nudis pédibus, étiam per loca áspera, hymnos cóncinens, conficiébat. Abstinéntia rara, carnes numquam edébat: jejúnia nec æger solvébat. Letális críminis totam vitam expértem omníno duxit. Linguæ observantíssimus custos, non nisi cum Deo aut de Deo colloquebátur: ac vix de áliis rebus illi sermo erat. Salútis animárum sitientíssimus, martýrii quoque cupidíssimus fuit. In everténdis heréticis Albigénsibus septem consúmpsit annos, multis corum ad cathólicam fidem addúctis. Máximis vivens et post mortem miráculis fulsit: et inter ália, Romeæ tres mórtuos suscitávit. Fuit vir plane apostólici péctoris ac spíritus, fídei cólumen, Evangélii tuba, orbis óculus, Christi lucérna, secúndus Præcúrsor, et magnus animárum œcónomus: quem multíplices tantárum virtútum in cælo coróna décorant.

granumexcussumpaleanexusolutoluteodepaup.en: The grain, shaken from the chaff, its bond of clay loosed, from the threshing-floor of poverty is laid up in the granary of heaven:
granumexcussumpaleanexusolutoluteodepaup.la: Granum excússum pálea, nexu solúto lúteo, de paupertátis área cæli locátur hórreo:

cummercedevirgineadoctorumfulgenscuneo.en: With the reward of virgins, shining in the company of the Doctors.
cummercedevirgineadoctorumfulgenscuneo.la: Cum mercéde virgínea Doctórum fulgens cúneo.

flosinflorumvirensareolabinagaudetsortis.en: A flower flourishing in the garden-bed of flowers, he rejoiceth in a twofold aureole of his lot.
flosinflorumvirensareolabinagaudetsortis.la: Flos in florum virens aréola, bina gaudet sortis auréola.

felixvitisdecuiussurculotantumgermenredu.en: Happy vine, from whose shoot so great a growth overfloweth upon the world,
felixvitisdecuiussurculotantumgermenredu.la: Felix vitis, de cujus súrculo tantum germen redúndat século,

celivinumpropinanspopulovitalipoculo.en: Pledging to the people the wine of heaven in a life-giving cup.
celivinumpropinanspopulovitalipoculo.la: Cæli vinum propinans pópulo vitáli póculo.

exubertatepalmitummundiiamcinxitambitum.en: From the fruitfulness of its branches it hath now encircled the compass of the world.
exubertatepalmitummundiiamcinxitambitum.la: Ex ubertáte pálmitum mundi jam cinxit ámbitum.

ascendentidevallelubricimundichoriplaudu.en: As he goeth up from the vale of the slippery world, the choirs of Angels applaud:
ascendentidevallelubricimundichoriplaudu.la: Ascendénti de valle lúbrici mundi, chori plaudunt angélici:

iesuboneprecedominicitibiprestanosgratos.en: Good Jesus, by the prayer of Dominic, grant that we may be made pleasing to thee.
iesuboneprecedominicitibiprestanosgratos.la: Jesu bone, prece Domínici, tibi præsta nos gratos éffici.

perquemmultosamortesuscitaspenasnobisrel.en: Through whom thou raisest many from death, remit unto us the punishments we owe.
perquemmultosamortesuscitaspenasnobisrel.la: Per quem multos a morte súscitas, pœnas nobis reláxa débitas.

adestdiesletitiequobeatusdominicusaulamc.en: The day of gladness is come, on which blessed Dominic, a citizen, entereth magnificent into the hall of the heavenly court.
adestdiesletitiequobeatusdominicusaulamc.la: Adest dies letítiæ, quo beátus Domínicus aulam cæléstis curim civis intrat magníficus.

pauperinpeculiodivesvitapurapaupertatisp.en: Poor in his purse, rich in pure life, by the price of poverty he holdeth the rights of heaven.
pauperinpeculiodivesvitapurapaupertatisp.la: Pauper in pecúlio, dives vita pura, paupertátis prétio cæli tenet jura.

scalaceloprominensfratrirevelaturperquam.en: A ladder reaching up to heaven is revealed to a brother, by which the Father passing over was borne upward.
scalaceloprominensfratrirevelaturperquam.la: Scala cælo próminens fratri revelátur, per quam Pater tránsiens sursum ferebátur.

linguemanusstudioscalamhancerexituamvirg.en: By the zeal of tongue and hand he set up this ladder, which the Virgin Mother with her Son drew upward.
linguemanusstudioscalamhancerexituamvirg.la: Linguæ, manus stúdio scalam hanc eréxit, uam Virgo cum Filio Mater sursum vexit.

fulgetinchorovirginumdoctorveritatissert.en: The teacher of truth shineth in the choir of virgins, wearing with the blessed a twofold garland of honour,
fulgetinchorovirginumdoctorveritatissert.la: Fulget in choro vírginum doctor veritátis, sertum honóris géminum gerens cum beátis,

quasistellamatutinainmedionebuleetquasil.en: As the morning star in the midst of a cloud, and as the moon at the full in her days doth shine: and as the sun when it shineth, so did he shine in the temple of God.
quasistellamatutinainmedionebuleetquasil.la: Quasi stella matutína in médio nébulæ, et quasi luna plena in diébus suis lucet: et quasi sol refúlgens, sic ille effúlsit in templo Dei.

nosterdepromathodie.en: Let our choir pour forth today

vergentemundivespere.en: As the evening of the world draweth on,

etclausisculpecarcere.en: And to them that are shut in the prison of guilt

precosalutismittitur.en: A herald of salvation is sent.

spargensperorbiscardinem.en: Scattering throughout the bounds of the earth,

pestemfugathereticam.en: He putteth to flight the plague of heresy,

quimundoiammirificus.en: Which now, wondrous, unto the world

carnisvirormentismartyriummundumreplensl.en: The vigour of the flesh, the martyrdom of the mind, the preaching of the tongue filling the world, O poor man of Christ, after the stadium of thy course, purchase for thee the reward of life.
carnisvirormentismartyriummundumreplensl.la: Carnis viror, mentis martýrium, mundum replens linguæ præcónium, pauper Christi, post cursus státium, vitæ tibi mercántur pr'aemium.

spiritusmeusquiestinteetverbameaqueposui.en: My spirit that is in thee, and my words that I have put in thy mouth, shall not depart out of thy mouth, nor out of the mouth of thy seed, saith the Lord, from henceforth and for ever.
spiritusmeusquiestinteetverbameaqueposui.la: Spíritus meus, qui est in te, et verba mea quæ pósui in ore tuo, non recédent de ore tuo et de ore séminis tui, dicit Dóminus, ámodo et usque in sempitérnum.

lexveritatisfuitinoreeiusetiniquitasnone.en: The law of truth was in his mouth, and iniquity was not found in his lips: he walked with me in peace, and in equity, and turned many away from iniquity.
lexveritatisfuitinoreeiusetiniquitasnone.la: Lex veritátis fuit in ore ejus, et iníquitas non est invénta in lábiis ejus: in pace et in æquitáte ambulávit mecum, et multos avértit ab iniquitáte.

olumenecclesiedoctorveritatisrosapatient.en: O light of the Church, teacher of truth, rose of patience, ivory of chastity, thou didst freely give to drink the water of wisdom: preacher of grace, join us to the blessed.
olumenecclesiedoctorveritatisrosapatient.la: O lumen Ecclésiæ, Doctor veritátis, Rosa patiéntiæ, Ebur castitátis, Aquam sapiéntiæ propinásti gratis : Prædicátor grátiæ, nos junge beátis.

felixnamqueessacravirgomarietomnilaudedi.en: O Holy Virgin Mary, happy indeed art thou, and right worthy of all praise
felixnamqueessacravirgomarietomnilaudedi.la: Felix namque es, sacra Virgo María, et omni laude digníssima:

quiexteortusestsoliustitiechristusdeusno.en: For out of thee arose the Sun of justice, * Christ our God.
quiexteortusestsoliustitiechristusdeusno.la: Quia ex te ortus est sol justítiæ, * Christus, Deus noster.

orapropopulointerveniproclerointercedepr.en: Pray for the people, plead for the clergy, intercede for the devout female sex: let all feel thy help, whosoever celebrate thy Solemnity.
orapropopulointerveniproclerointercedepr.la: Ora pro pópulo, intérveni pro clero, intercéde pro devóto femíneo sexu: séntiant omnes tuum juvámen, quicúmque célebrant tuam Solemnitátem.

dumoraretiesusfactestspeciesvultuseiusal.en: While Jesus prayed, the shape of his countenance was altered, and his raiment became white and glittering: and two men were talking with him,
dumoraretiesusfactestspeciesvultuseiusal.la: Dum oráret Jesus, facta est spécies vultus ejus áltera, et vestitus ejus albus refúlgens: et duo viri loquebántur cum illo,

moyseseteliasvisiinmaiestate.en: Moses and Elias, appearing In majesty.
moyseseteliasvisiinmaiestate.la: Móyses et Elías visi In majestáte.

dicebantautemexcessueiusquemcompleturuse.en: And they spoke of his decease that he should accomplish in Jerusalem.
dicebantautemexcessueiusquemcompleturuse.la: Dicébant autem excéssu ejus, quem completúrus erat in Jerúsalem.

summumregemgloriechristumadoremusetprodo.en: Let us adore Christ, the supreme King of glory: * And for the gift of his grace let us rejoice.
summumregemgloriechristumadoremusetprodo.la: Summum Regem glóriæ, Christum adorémus: * Et pro dono grátiæ ejus jubilémus.

primosigiturapostolorumseorsumassumpsite.en: He took therefore the chief of the Apostles apart. And he brought them up into a mountain: and he was transfigured before them. And his face did shine as the sun: and his garments became white as snow. Wherefore took he these? Because, to wit, they were more excellent than the rest. And Peter indeed excelled because he loved Christ exceedingly; John, because he was exceedingly loved; and James by the answer which he gave with his brother when he was asked, saying, We can drink this chalice.
primosigiturapostolorumseorsumassumpsite.la: Primos ígitur Apostolórum seórsum assúmpsit. Et addúxit in montem: et transfigurátus est ante eos. Et resplénduit fácies ejus sicut sol: vestiménta vero ejus facta sunt alba sicut nix. Quam ob rem hos accépit? Quia excellentiôres ceteris videlicet erant. Et Petrus quidem, quia valde Christum diligébat, idcirco præstábat; Joánnes vero, qui nímium diligebátur, ac Jacóbus a respónso, quod dedit cum fratre interrogátus, dicens, Póssumus hunc cálicem bíbere.

emittelucemtuametveritatemtuam.en: Send forth thy light and thy truth.
emittelucemtuametveritatemtuam.la: Emítte lucem tuam et veritátem tuam.

ipsamededuxeruntetadduxeruntinmontemsanc.en: They have conducted me, and brought me unto thy holy mount, and into thy tabernacles.
ipsamededuxeruntetadduxeruntinmontemsanc.la: Ipsa me deduxérunt, et adduxérunt in montem sanctum tuum et in tabernácula tua.

deusquibeateioannefamuletuegratiamsupern.en: O God, who didst wonderfully show unto blessed Joan thy handmaid the grace of the heavenly calling of her son Dominic: we beseech thee, that, imitating her and the son foreshown to her, we may by the loving intercession of both obtain eternal rewards.
deusquibeateioannefamuletuegratiamsupern.la: Deus, qui beátæ Joánnæ fámulæ tuæ grátiam supérnæ vocatiónis filii sui Domínici mirábiliter ostendisti: quæsumus ut, ipsam præmonstrátumque filium imitátes, pio utriúsque intervéntu ætéerna præmia consequámur.

carnificesverourgentesministrabantcarbon.en: But the executioners, pressing on, supplied coals beneath the iron grate.
carnificesverourgentesministrabantcarbon.la: Carnífices vero urgéntes ministrábant carbónes subter cratem férream.

accusatusnonnegavinomensanctumtuumetinte.en: Being accused, I denied not thy holy name, and being questioned.
accusatusnonnegavinomensanctumtuumetinte.la: Accusátus non negávi nomen sanctum tuum, et interrogátus.

cumergocausearticulusvenerituthecconditi.en: When therefore the point of the case shall come, that this condition is set forth, either to act against the commandment of God or to depart out of this life: if a man be compelled to choose one of these two, the persecutor threatening death: there let him choose rather to die with God loved than to live with God offended. There let him hate his soul in this world, that he may keep it unto life eternal.
cumergocausearticulusvenerituthecconditi.la: Cum ergo causæ artículus vénerit, ut hæc conditio proponatur, aut faciendum esse contra Dei præceptum aut ex hac vita emigrandum: quorum duorum homo si cogatur alterum eligere, comminante mortem persecutore: ibi eligat Deo dilecto émori quam offénso vivere. Ibi óderit in hoc mundo animam suam, ut in vitam ætérnam custódiat eam.

orapronobisbeatelaurenti.en: Pray for us, O blessed Laurence.

inclitusmartyrtiburtiuscumnudatisplantis.en: The renowned Martyr Tiburtius, when with bared feet he walked upon burning coals, said to Fabian the prefect: It seemeth to me that I walk upon rosy flowers in the name of my Lord Jesus Christ.
inclitusmartyrtiburtiuscumnudatisplantis.la: Inclitus Martyr Tibúrtius, cum nudátis plantis super prunas ardéntes incéderet, Fabiáno præfécito dixit: Vidétur mihi quod super róseos flores incédam in nómine Dómini mei Jesu Christi.

famulostuosquesumusdominebeatevirginistu.en: Make thy servants, we beseech thee, O Lord, who keep the solemn birthday of thy blessed Virgin Clare, partakers of heavenly joys by her intercession, and coheirs of thine Only-begotten:
famulostuosquesumusdominebeatevirginistu.la: Fámulos tuos, quæsumus, Domine, beatæ Virginis tuæ Claræ votiva natalitia recensentes, cælestium gaudiorum sua facias interventione participes, et tui Unigeniti coheredes:

ascenditchristussupercelosetpreparavitsu.en: Christ ascended above the heavens, and prepared for his most chaste Mother the place of immortality: and this is that glorious festival, incomparable with the festivals of all the Saints, on which, glorious and happy, while the orders of the heavenly court marvelled, she came to the bridal chamber of heaven: where may she in her kindness never be unmindful of those who are mindful of her.
ascenditchristussupercelosetpreparavitsu.la: Ascéndit Christus super cælos, et præparávit suæ castissimæ Matri immortalitátis locum: et hæc est illa præclára festívitás, ómnium Sanctórum festívitatibus incomparábilis, in qua gloriósa et felix, mirántibus cæléstis cúriæ ordínibus, ad æthéreum pervénit thálamum: quo pia sui mémorum ímmemor nequáquam exsístat.

venerandanobisdominehuiusdieifestivitaso.en: May the venerable festival of this day, O Lord, bring us saving help, on which the holy Mother of God underwent temporal death, yet could not be held down by the bonds of death, she who brought forth of herself thy Son our Lord incarnate:
venerandanobisdominehuiusdieifestivitaso.la: Veneránda nobis, Dómine, hujus diéi festívitás opem cónferat salutárem, in qua sancta Dei Génatrix mortem súbiit temporálem, nec tamen mortis nélixibus déprimi pótuit, quæ Fílium tuum Dóminum nostrum de se génuít incarnátum:

beatesvirgomariadeigenitrixquecredidisti.en: Blessed art thou, O Virgin Mary, Mother of God, who didst believe the Lord: those things are accomplished in thee that were spoken to thee: behold, thou art exalted above the choirs of Angels:
beatesvirgomariadeigenitrixquecredidisti.la: Beáta es, Virgo María Dei Génitrix, quæ credidísti Dómino: perfécta sunt in te, quæ dicta sunt tibi: ecce exaltáta es super chros Angelórum:

benedictetvenerabilisesvirgomariaquesine.en: Blessed and venerable art thou, O Virgin Mary, who without loss of maidenhood wast found the Mother of the Saviour.
benedictetvenerabilisesvirgomariaquesine.la: Benedícta et venerábilis es, Virgo María, quæ sine tactu pudóris invénta es Mater Salvatóris.

hodiemariavirgocelosascendit.en: Today the Virgin Mary ascended into heaven:

gaudetequiacumchristoregnatineternum.en: Rejoice, for she reigneth with Christ for ever.
gaudetequiacumchristoregnatineternum.la: Gaudete, quia cum Christo regnat in ætérnum.

reginamundihodiedeseculonequameripitur.en: Today the Queen of the world is delivered from this wicked world.
reginamundihodiedeseculonequameripitur.la: Regina mundi hódie de sæculo nequam eripitur.

sanctadeigenitrixvirgosempermaria.en: Holy Mother of God, * Mary ever Virgin.
sanctadeigenitrixvirgosempermaria.la: Sancta Dei Génitrix * Virgo semper María.

virgosempermariasanctadeigenitrix.en: Mary ever Virgin, Holy Mother of God,
virgosempermariasanctadeigenitrix.la: Virgo semper María Sancta Dei Génitrix,

deigenetrixintercedepronobis.en: Mother of God, pray for us.

speciosafactesetsuavis.en: Thou art become beautiful * And sweet.

indeliciistuissanctadeigenetrix.en: In thy delights, O holy Mother of God.
indeliciistuissanctadeigenetrix.la: In delíciis tuis, sancta Dei Génetrix.

sancteioachimchristiconfessoraudirogante.en: Holy Joachim, Confessor of Christ, hear thy little servants who entreat thee.
sancteioachimchristiconfessoraudirogante.la: Sancte Joachim, Christi Conféssor, audi rogántes sérvulos.

etimpetratamnobiscelitustudeferindulgent.en: And do thou bring us the pardon obtained from heaven.
etimpetratamnobiscelitustudeferindulgent.la: Et impetrátam nobis cælitus Tu defer indulgéntiam.

osanteioachimsidusaureumdominigratiaserv.en: O holy Joachim, golden star, by the grace of the Lord receive with thy wonted clemency the groans of thy servants.
osanteioachimsidusaureumdominigratiaserv.la: O sante Joachim, sidus áureum, Dómini grátia servórum gémitus sólita súscipe cleméntia.

deumquepulsonubilo.en: And, the cloud being driven away, God

puriscolamusmentibus.en: Let us worship with pure minds.

huncvestesacrainduit.en: Him he clothed with the sacred habit:

cunctisquemoxapparuit.en: And soon to all he appeared

patremsecutusfilius.en: The son, having followed the Father,

ducissecutustramitem.en: Having followed the path of his Leader,

solaturetdatgaudia.en: Comforteth him and giveth him joys:

christicoruscatgratia.en: He shineth by the grace of Christ.

tibideussitgloria.en: To thee, O God, be glory

etnoshyacinthiprecibus.en: And us, by the prayers of Hyacinth,

adiungecelicetibus.en: Join to the companies of heaven.

gratielargitoremadoremusdominumquisaluti.en: Let us adore the Lord, the bestower of grace, * Who hath glorified Hyacinth, the herald of salvation.
gratielargitoremadoremusdominumquisaluti.la: Gratiæ largitórem adorémus Dóminum, * Qui salutis præcónem glorificávit Hyacínthum.

dumpredicatormittitur.en: While he is sent as a preacher,

lateperorbemfunditur.en: Is poured forth far and wide through the world.

ubiqueverbisemina.en: Everywhere the seeds of the word

rectiquespargitlumina.en: And the lights of righteousness he scattereth:

vitecoruscantregule.en: The rules of life shine forth.

verboquetangensanimas.en: And, touching souls with his word,

abhostepredaseripit.en: He snatcheth the prey from the enemy,

celoquedignosefficit.en: And maketh them worthy of heaven,

dumfrangithostisrobor.en: While he breaketh the strength of the foe.

disciplinametscientiamedoctusiniuventute.en: Instructed in discipline and knowledge in his youth, Hyacinth brought forth fruit in his season.
disciplinametscientiamedoctusiniuventute.la: Disciplínam et sciéntiam edóctus in juventute sua, fructum dedit Hyacínthus in témpore suo. Ps. 1

constitutusadominopromulgatorevangeliive.en: Appointed by the Lord a proclaimer of the Gospel, by word, life and miracles he taught the peoples, preaching his commandment.
constitutusadominopromulgatorevangeliive.la: Constitútus a Dómino promulgátor Evangélii, verbo, vita, miráculis dócuit pópulos, prædicans præceptum ejus. Ps. 2

vocesualumendiffundensfideiatenebrisrevo.en: Spreading abroad with his voice the light of faith, he called back thousands of the people from darkness.
vocesualumendiffundensfideiatenebrisrevo.la: Voce sua lumen diffúndens fidei, a ténebris revocávit millia pópuli. Ps. 3

constituistieumdominesingulariterinspequ.en: Thou, O Lord, hast singularly settled him in hope, for day and night he called upon thee.
constituistieumdominesingulariterinspequ.la: Constituísti eum, Dómine, singuláriter in spe, quóniam die ac nocte invocábat te. Ps. 4

intendebantturbevocipredicationiseiusetm.en: The crowds hearkened to the voice of his preaching, and marvelled at the grace of his miracles.
intendebantturbevocipredicationiseiusetm.la: Intendébant turbæ voci prædicatiónis ejus, et mirabántur grátiam miraculórum ejus. Ps. 5

insignisetprodigiisportavitcorampopulism.en: With signs and wonders he bore before many peoples the admirable name of the Lord.
insignisetprodigiisportavitcorampopulism.la: In signis et prodigiis portávit coram pópulis multis admirábile nomen Dómini. Ps. 8

diviniverbiseminechristogenuitpopuloseta.en: By the seed of the divine word he begot peoples unto Christ, and brought the malignant one to nothing.
diviniverbiseminechristogenuitpopuloseta.la: Divíni verbi sémine Christo génuit pópulos, et ad nihilum dedúxit malígnum. Ps. 14

invirtutetuadominemundipurgavitvitiademo.en: In thy strength, O Lord, he cleansed the vices of the world, and valiantly overthrew the dominion of devils and of death.
invirtutetuadominemundipurgavitvitiademo.la: In virtúte tua, Dómine, mundi purgávit vítia, dáemonum ac mortis fórtiter súbruit jura. Ps. 20

innocensmanibusetmundocordeascenditinmon.en: Innocent in hands and clean of heart he ascended into the mountain of the Lord, he who walked fearless upon the waters.
innocensmanibusetmundocordeascenditinmon.la: Innocens mánibus et mundo corde ascéndit in montem Dómini, qui super aquas ambulávit intrépídus. Ps. 23

dumhyacinthumpoloniagenuitpurumfloremede.en: When Poland brought forth Hyacinth, she put forth a pure flower, purer than every flower:
dumhyacinthumpoloniagenuitpurumfloremede.la: Dum Hyacínthum Polónia génuit, purum florem édedit, omni flore puriorem:

gemmamnovamprotulitomnilapidepretiosiore.en: She brought forth a new gem, more precious than every stone.
gemmamnovamprotulitomnilapidepretiosiore.la: Gemmam novam prótulit, omni lápide pretiosiorem.

flosestredolenspuritategemmemicansvirtut.en: He is a flower fragrant with purity, a gem shining with virtue.
flosestredolenspuritategemmemicansvirtut.la: Flos est rédolens puritáte, gemma émicans virtúte.

castitatenitiduscaritatefervidusieiuniis.en: Bright with chastity, fervent with charity, he was instant continually in fastings and prayers,
castitatenitiduscaritatefervidusieiuniis.la: Castitáte nítidus, caritáte férvidus, jeiúniis et oratióibus instábat assídue,

etinlegedominimeditabaturdieacnocte.en: And on the law of the Lord he meditated day and night.
etinlegedominimeditabaturdieacnocte.la: Et in lege Dómini meditabátur die ac nocte.

carnemsuamdomabatpenitentiautdignadeomer.en: He subdued his flesh by penance, that he might merit to become a victim worthy of God.
carnemsuamdomabatpenitentiautdignadeomer.la: Carnem suam domábat pæniténtia, ut digna Deo mererétur fieri hóstia.

dumhyacinthusdesaculeripiturcumingentilu.en: When Hyacinth is taken from the world, he is borne into heaven with a great light:
dumhyacinthusdesaculeripiturcumingentilu.la: Dum Hyacínthus de sáculo erípitur, cum ingénti lúmine in cælum véhitur:

occurritchoruspsallentiumsuscipitreginav.en: The choir of them that sing psalms cometh to meet him, The Queen of virgins receiveth him.
occurritchoruspsallentiumsuscipitreginav.la: Occúrrit chorus psalléntium, Súscipit Regína virginum.

dumscanditcelisideraconsecuturuspremia.en: While he climbeth to the stars of heaven, about to obtain his rewards.
dumscanditcelisideraconsecuturuspremia.la: Dum scandit cæli sídera, consecutúrus præmia.

orapronobisbeatehyacinthe.en: Pray for us, O blessed Hyacinth.

utdigniefficiamurpromissioibuschristi.en: That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.

signocrucisconfregitfluctusquoselevaveru.en: With the sign of the Cross he broke the waves, which the floods had lifted up in many waters.
signocrucisconfregitfluctusquoselevaveru.la: Signo Crucis confrégit fluctus, quos eleváverunt flúmina in aquis multis.

placuitdeoinsanctitateanimesueintroiviti.en: He pleased God in the holiness of his soul: he entered into his courts with rejoicing.
placuitdeoinsanctitateanimesueintroiviti.la: Plácuít Deo in sanctitáte ánimæ suæ: introívit in átria ejus in exultatióne.

quasitubexaltavitvocemsuamutconfiterentu.en: Like a trumpet he lifted up his voice, that the peoples might confess to thee, O God.
quasitubexaltavitvocemsuamutconfiterentu.la: Quasi tuba exaltávit vocem suam, ut confitérentur tibi pópuli, Deus.

benedicantmarietfluminadominoquiaquasflu.en: Let the seas and the rivers bless the Lord, who made firm the waters of the river beneath the feet of Hyacinth.
benedicantmarietfluminadominoquiaquasflu.la: Benedicant mária et flúmina Dómino, qui aquas flúminis solidávit sub pedibus Hyacínthi.

omnespopulilaudentdominumquiviventemetvi.en: Let all peoples praise the Lord, who made his servant Hyacinth wonderful both living and departed this life.
omnespopulilaudentdominumquiviventemetvi.la: Omnes pópuli laudent Dóminum, qui vivéntem et vita functum mirificávit servum suum Hyacínthum.

ipseestdirectusdivinitusinpenitentiamgen.en: He was directed by God unto the repentance of the nation, and he took away the abominations of wickedness. And he directed his heart towards the Lord, and in the days of sinners he strengthened godliness.
ipseestdirectusdivinitusinpenitentiamgen.la: Ipse est diréctus divínitus in pœniténtiam gentis, et tulit abominatiónes impietátis. Et gubernávit ad Dóminum cor ipsíus, et in diébus peccatórum corroborávit pietátem.

voxpuralaudetexitum.en: Let a pure voice praise the passing,

etcorhyacinthimeritum.en: And the heart the merit, of Hyacinth:

coruscalustratagmina.en: He goeth through the shining hosts,

huncvitaclaraindicat.en: His bright life showeth him forth,

secretaquehicnoverat.en: The secrets which he here had known

totumperorbempredicant.en: They proclaim throughout the whole world.

ventisetundisimperat.en: He commandeth the winds and the waves,

aquestupescuntfluminum.en: The waters of the rivers stand amazed,

viteresurguntmortui.en: The dead rise again to life,

claudiquedanturgressui.en: And the lame are restored to walking,

cecispatescuntlumina.en: To the blind their eyes are opened,

fanturdeimagnalia.en: They tell the mighty works of God.

predicavitverbumdeiinomnipopuloaddandams.en: He preached the word of God among all the people, to give knowledge of salvation to his people unto the remission of their sins.
predicavitverbumdeiinomnipopuloaddandams.la: Prædicávit verbum Dei in omni pópulo, ad dandam sciéntiam salútis plebi ejus in remissiónem peccatórum eórum.

ecceservusmeussuscipiameumelectusmeuscom.en: Behold my servant, I will uphold him: my elect, my soul delighteth in him: I have given my spirit upon him.
ecceservusmeussuscipiameumelectusmeuscom.la: Ecce servus meus, suscípiam eum: eléctus meus, complácuit sibi in illo ánima mea: dedi spíritum meum super eum.

hecestreginavirginumquegenuitregemvelutr.en: This is the Queen of virgins, who bore the King, a Virgin comely as the rose. O Mother of God, through whom we have found God and man, loving Virgin, intercede for us all.
hecestreginavirginumquegenuitregemvelutr.la: Hæc est Regína virginum, quæ génuit Regem, velut rosa decóra Virgo. Dei Génetrix, per quam repérimus Deum et hóminem, alma Virgo, intercéde pro nobis ómnibus. Ps. 112, 116, 145, 146, 147

solemnitasgloriosevirginismarieexseminea.en: The solemnity of the glorious * Virgin Mary, of the seed of Abraham, sprung from the tribe of Juda, illustrious of the stock of David.
solemnitasgloriosevirginismarieexseminea.la: Solémnitas gloriósæ * Vírginis Maríæ ex sémine Abrahæ, ortæ de tribu Juda, clara ex stirpe David. Ps. 109, 112, 121, 126, 147

adestodominesupplicationibusnostrisutqui.en: Give ear, O Lord, unto our supplications: that we who know ourselves to be guilty through our own iniquity, may be delivered by the intercession of blessed Rufus thy Martyr and Bishop.
adestodominesupplicationibusnostrisutqui.la: Adésto, Dómine, supplicatiónibus nostris: ut, qui ex iniquitáte nostra reos nos esse cognóscimus, beáti Rufi Mártyris tui atque Pontíficis intercessióne liberémur.

letarematernostraierusalemquiarextuusdis.en: Rejoice, O Jerusalem our mother, for thy King hath redeemed for thee from the bondage of Babylon Augustine, a strenuous steward and a most faithful citizen.
letarematernostraierusalemquiarextuusdis.la: Lætáre, mater nostra Jerúsalem, quia Rex tuus dispensatórem strénuum et civem fidelíssimum de servitúte Babylónis tibi redémit Augustinum. Ps. 112, 116, 145, 146, 147

volebatenimconferrentiestussuosutproferr.en: For he wished, when he conferred with him about his agitations, that he would set forth what was the fit manner of living for one so disposed as he was, to walk in the way of God,
volebatenimconferrentiestussuosutproferr.la: Volébat enim conférrenti æstus suos ut próferret quis esset aptus modus vivéndi sic affécto, ut ipse erat, ad ambulándum in via Dei,

inquaaliussicaliussicibat.en: In which one went this way, another that way.
inquaaliussicaliussicibat.la: In qua álius sic, álius sic ibat.

displicebateiquidquidagebatinseculopredu.en: Whatever he did in the world displeased him, in comparison with the sweetness of God and the beauty of his house, which he loved.
displicebateiquidquidagebatinseculopredu.la: Displicébat ei quidquid agébat in sæculo præ dulcédine Dei et decóre domus ejus, quam diléxit.

etpereasconditori.en: And through them with the Creator

amantveriiudice.en: They love thee, truth being judge:

queobscurapriuserant.en: Those things that before were obscure

tudeverbissalvatoris.en: Thou, from the words of the Saviour,

etpropinaspotumvite.en: And givest to drink the draught of life

depsalmorumnectare.en: From the nectar of the psalms.

tudevitaclericorum.en: Thou, of the life of clerics,

quamquiamantetsequuntur.en: And they who love and follow it

regiregumsalusvita.en: To the King of kings be salvation, life,

trinitatilausethonor.en: To the Trinity praise and honour

quiconcivesnosadscribat.en: Who may enrol us as fellow citizens

orapronobisbeateaugustine.en: Pray for us, O blessed Augustine.

adestdiescelebrisquosolutusnexucarnissan.en: The festive day is come, on which, loosed from the bond of the flesh, the holy bishop Augustine was taken up with the Angels: where he rejoiceth with the Prophets, is glad with the Apostles, of whose spirit being full, he made open to us the mysteries which they foretold: after whom he first shone forth with the second grace of dispensing the word of God.
adestdiescelebrisquosolutusnexucarnissan.la: Adest dies célebris, quo solútus nexu carnis sanctus præsul Augustínus assúptus est cum Angelis: ubi gaudet cum Prophétis, lætátur cum Apóstolis, quorum plenus spíritu, quæ prædixerunt mýstica fecit nobis pèrvia: post quos secúnda dispensándi verbi Dei primus refúlsit grátia.

magnusdominusetlaudabilisvaldequideteneb.en: Great is the Lord, and exceedingly to be praised, * Who out of the darkness of the Gentiles hath called Augustine, the light of his Church.
magnusdominusetlaudabilisvaldequideteneb.la: Magnus Dóminus et laudábilis valde, * Qui de ténebris géntium lumen Ecclésiæ suæ vocávit Augustínus.

aperuitaugustinuscodicemapostolicumetcon.en: Augustine opened the book of the Apostle, and casting his eyes on the first chapter, he read: Put ye on the Lord Jesus Christ: and straightway, as if a light of security had been poured in, all the darkness of doubt fled away from him.
aperuitaugustinuscodicemapostolicumetcon.la: Apéruit Augustínus códicem apostólicum, et coniéctis óculis ad primum capitulum legit: Induímini Dóminum Jesum Christum: et statim, quasi infúsa luce securitátis, ab eo omnes dubietátis ténebræ diffugérunt. Ps. 1

insinuavitergoperlittassanctoviroambrosi.en: He made known therefore by letter to the holy man Ambrose his present desire, that he might advise him what of the holy books he should read, whereby he might become fitter and more prepared for receiving the Christian grace.
insinuavitergoperlittassanctoviroambrosi.la: Insinuávit ergo per líttas sancto viro Ambrósio præsens votum suum, ut monéret quid sibi de libris sanctis legéndum esset, quo percipiéndæ cristiánæ grátiae áptior fieret atque parátior. Ps. 2

atilleiussitisaiamprophetamquodpreceteri.en: But he bade him read Isaias the prophet: because above the rest he is the more open foreteller of the Gospel and of the calling of the Gentiles.
atilleiussitisaiamprophetamquodpreceteri.la: At ille jussit Isaiám prophétam: quod præ céteris Evangélii vocatiónisque géntium sit prænuntiátor apértior. Ps. 3

verumtamenprimamhuiuslectionemnonintelli.en: But not understanding the first lesson of him, and thinking the whole to be such, he put it off, to be taken up again when he was better practised in the Lord's speech.
verumtamenprimamhuiuslectionemnonintelli.la: Verúmtamen primam hujus lectionem non intélligens, totúmque tale árbitrans, dístulit repeténdum exercitátior in Dóminico elóquio. Ps. 4

indeubitempusadvenitquonomeneumdareoport.en: Then, when the time was come at which he must give in his name, leaving the country and returning to Milan, he was baptized by blessed Ambrose: and anxiety for his past life fled from him.
