indeubitempusadvenitquonomeneumdareoport.la: Inde, ubi tempus advénit, quo nomen eum dare oportéret, relicto rure, Madiolánum rémeans, baptizátus est a beáto Ambrósio: fugítque ab eo sollicitúdo vitæ præteritæ. Ps. 5

necsatiabaturillisdiebusdulcedinemirabil.en: Nor was he satisfied in those days with the wondrous sweetness of considering the depth of the divine counsel concerning the salvation of mankind.
necsatiabaturillisdiebusdulcedinemirabil.la: Nec satiabátur illis diébus dulcédine mirábili consideráre altitúdinem consílii divíni super salutem géneris humáni. Ps. 8

flebatautemuberrimeinhymnisetcanticissua.en: And he wept most abundantly in hymns and canticles, being deeply moved by the voices of the sweetly singing Church.
flebatautemuberrimeinhymnisetcanticissua.la: Flebat autem uberrime in hymnis et canticis, suáve sonantis Ecclesiae vócbus vehementer affectus. Ps. 14

vocesigiturilleinfluebantauribuseiusetel.en: Those voices therefore flowed into his ears, and the truth was distilled into his heart, and tears ran down, and it was well with him in them.
vocesigiturilleinfluebantauribuseiusetel.la: Voces igitur illæ influébant áuribus ejus, et eliquabátur véritas in cor ejus, et fluébant lácrimæ, et bene illi erat cum eis. Ps. 20

adiunctusindenebridietevodioremeabatadaf.en: Joined then to Nebridius and Evodius, he was returning to Africa, seeking what place might be more useful for them for living well: but when he was at Ostia on the Tiber, his pious mother died.
adiunctusindenebridietevodioremeabatadaf.la: Adiunctus inde Nebridio et Evodio remeábat ad Africam, quærens quis eos ad bene vivendum locus habéret utilior: sed cum esset apud Ostia Tiberína, pia mater ejus defuncta est. Ps. 23

invenitseaugustinuslongeesseadeoinregion.en: Augustine found himself far from God in the region of unlikeness, as if he heard the voice of God from on high: I am the food of grown men:
invenitseaugustinuslongeesseadeoinregion.la: Invénit se Augustinus longe esse a Deo in regione dissimilitudinis, tamquam audíret vocem Dei de excélso: Cibus sum grándium:

cresceetmanducabisme.en: Grow, and thou shalt feed upon me.

nectumemutabisintesicutcibumcarnistuesed.en: Nor shalt thou change me into thee, as the food of thy flesh: but thou shalt be changed into me.
nectumemutabisintesicutcibumcarnistuesed.la: Nec tu me mutábis in te, sicut cibum carnis tuæ: sed tu mutáberis in me.

sensitigituretexpertusestnonessemirumquo.en: He perceived therefore and found by experience that it is no wonder that bread which to a healthy palate is sweet is loathsome to one not healthy,
sensitigituretexpertusestnonessemirumquo.la: Sensit igitur et expértus est, non esse mirum quod paláto non sano péna est panis, qui sano est suávis,

etoculisegrisodiosaluxquepurisestamabili.en: And that light is hateful to sore eyes which to clear ones is lovely.
etoculisegrisodiosaluxquepurisestamabili.la: Et óculis ægris odiósa lux, quæ puris est amábilis.

propteriniquitatemcorripuistihominemetta.en: For iniquity thou hast corrected man, and thou hast made his soul to waste away like a spider.
propteriniquitatemcorripuistihominemetta.la: Propter iniquitátem corripuísti hóminem, et tabescere fecísti sicut aráneam ánimam ejus.

tumveroinvisibiliadeipereaquefactasuntin.en: Then indeed he beheld the invisible things of God, understood by the things that are made, but he could not fix his gaze:
tumveroinvisibiliadeipereaquefactasuntin.la: Tum vero invisibília Dei per ea quæ facta sunt intellécta conspéxit, sed áciem figere non váluit:

quianonsecumferebatnisiamantemmemoriamet.en: Because he carried with him only a loving memory, And as it were a longing for what he had smelt, but could not yet eat.
quianonsecumferebatnisiamantemmemoriamet.la: Quia non secum ferébat nisi amántem memóriam, Et quasi olfácta desiderántem quæ comédere nondum posset.

quidautemsacramentihaberetverbumcarofact.en: But what mystery there was in, The Word was made flesh, he could not even conjecture.
quidautemsacramentihaberetverbumcarofact.la: Quid autem sacraménti habéret, Verbum caro factum est: nec suspicári quidem póterat.

etquasiolfactadesiderantemquecomederenon.en: And as it were a longing for what he had smelt, but could not yet eat.
etquasiolfactadesiderantemquecomederenon.la: Et quasi olfácta desiderántem quæ comédere nondum posset.

exipsiusscriptispossidiepiscopocalamensi.en: From his own writings, from Possidius, Bishop of Calama, and from the Roman Breviary.
exipsiusscriptispossidiepiscopocalamensi.la: Ex ipsius scriptis, Possidio Episcopo Calamensi et Romano Breviario.

augustinusclarissimumecclesielumentagast.en: Augustine, the most brilliant light of the Church, was born at Tagaste in Africa of respectable parents, and as a boy, far surpassing his equals in aptness of mind, in a short time excelled all in learning. As a youth, while he was at Carthage, he fell into the heresy of the Manichees. Afterwards, having gone to Rome, and being sent thence to Milan to teach rhetoric, since he was there a frequent hearer of the Bishop Ambrose, by his labours he was fired with zeal for the Catholic faith, and at the age of thirty-three he was baptized by him. But he himself also frankly confessed that the unceasing tears of his most holy mother Monica for the conversion of her son had in some manner brought forth Augustine to the Church, when he relates that a certain Bishop said to his mother as she wept abundantly for him: Go from me, as thou livest: for it cannot be that the son of these tears should perish.
augustinusclarissimumecclesielumentagast.la: Augustínus, claríssimum Ecclésiæ lumen, Tagáste in Africa honéstis paréntibus natus ac puer docilitáte ingénii æquáles longe súperans, brevi ómnibus doctrína antecélluit. Adoléscens, dum esset Carthágine, in Manichæórum hæresim incidit. Póstea Romam proféctus, inde Mediolánum missus ut rhetóricam docéret, cum ibi frequens Ambrósii Epíscopi esset audítor, ejus ópera incénsus stúdio cathólicæ fidei, annos natus triginta tres ab ipso baptizátur. Sed et sanctíssimæ matris Mónica juges pro filii conversióne lácrimas Augustinum Ecclésiæ quodámodo peperisse ipse étiam ingénue est proféssus, cum refert matri ubértim pro se flenti dixisse quendam Epíscopum: Vade a me, ita vivas: fieri enim non potest ut filius istárum lacrimárum péreat.

itaqueavidissimelegerecepitpreceterisapo.en: Therefore he began most eagerly to read, above the rest, the Apostle Paul:
itaqueavidissimelegerecepitpreceterisapo.la: Itaque avidíssime légere cépit, præ céteris, Apóstolum Paulum:

etperieruntillequestionesinquibusaliquan.en: And those questions perished, in which at one time the text of his discourses had seemed to him to contradict the testimonies of the Law and the Prophets.
etperieruntillequestionesinquibusaliquan.la: Et perierunt illæ quæstiónes, in quibus aliquándo visus est ei adversári testimoniis Legis et Prophetárum textus sermónum ejus.

etapparuiteiunafacieseloquiorumcastorume.en: And there appeared to him one face of the chaste words: and he learned to rejoice with trembling.
etapparuiteiunafacieseloquiorumcastorume.la: Et appáruit ei una fácies eloquiórum castórum: et exsultáre cum tremóre dídicit.

exauditaquoquevitaantoniimagniaugustinum.en: It is known also that from hearing of the life of Anthony the Great Augustine was vehemently inflamed to embrace the Catholic faith, when he uttered this with groaning: The unlearned rise and take heaven by force; and we with our learning, without heart, lo, where we wallow in flesh and blood. Having returned to Africa, joining holiness of life with religion, he was made a Priest by Valerius, Bishop of Hippo, of known sanctity. At which time he set up a household of religious, with whom he shared a common table and the same dress, and he most diligently trained them in the discipline of the apostolic life and teaching.
exauditaquoquevitaantoniimagniaugustinum.la: Ex audíta quoque vita Antónii Magni Augustinum ad capesséndam cathólicam fidem veheménter fuisse inflammátum constat, cum illud gemebúndus prótulit: Surgunt indócti et cælum rápiunt; et nos in doctrinis nostris sine corde ecce ubi volutámur in carne et ságuine. Revérsus in Africam, cum religiône vitæ sanctimóniam coniúngens, a Valério, notæ sanctitátis Epíscopo Hipponénsi, Présbyter factus est. Quo témpore familiam instituit religiosórum, quibúscum victu commúni codémque cultu utens, eos ad apostólica vitæ doctrinæque disciplínam diligentíssime erudiébat.

misitergodominusinmentemeiusvisumqueestb.en: The Lord therefore put it into his mind, and it seemed good in his sight, to go to Simplicianus, who appeared to him a good servant of God,
misitergodominusinmentemeiusvisumqueestb.la: Misit ergo Dóminus in mentem ejus, visúmque est bonum in conspéctu ejus pèrgere ad Simpliciánum, qui ei bonus apparébat servus Dei,

etlucebatineogratiadivina.en: And the grace of God shone in him.
etlucebatineogratiadivina.la: Et lucébat in eo grátia divína.

audieratenimquodaiuventutesuadevotissime.en: For he had heard that from his youth he had lived most devoutly to God: and so indeed it was.
audieratenimquodaiuventutesuadevotissime.la: Audíerat enim quod a juventúte sua devotíssime Deo viveret: et vere sic erat.

sedcumvigeretmanicheorumheresisvehementi.en: But, as the heresy of the Manichees was flourishing, he began to inveigh against it more vehemently, and confuted Fortunatus the heresiarch. Moved by this piety of Augustine, Valerius took him as his helper in the episcopal office: concerning whose ordination the holy Paulinus, Bishop of Nola, wrote thus to him: We write not only to rejoice in this, that Augustine hath received the Episcopate, but that the Churches of Africa have merited this care of God, that they should receive the heavenly words from the mouth of Augustine.
sedcumvigeretmanicheorumheresisvehementi.la: Sed, cum vigéret Manichæórum hâeresis, veheméntius in illam ínvehi cépit, Fortunatúmque hæresiárcham confutávit. Hac Augustíni pietáte commótus Valérius, eum adiutórem adhíbuit episcopális officii: de cujus ordinatione hæc ad ipsum scripsit sanctus Paulinus Nolánus Epíscopus: Non autem tantum hoc scribimus gratulándum, quod Episcopátum Augustínus accéperit, sed quod hanc Dei curam meruerint Africane Ecclesiae, ut verba caelestia Augustini ore perciperent.

volebatenimconferentiestussuosutproferre.en: For he wished, when he conferred with him about his agitations, that he would set forth what was the fit manner of living for one so disposed as he was, to walk in the way of God,
volebatenimconferentiestussuosutproferre.la: Volébat enim conferenti æstus suos ut proferret quis esset aptus modus vivendi sic affecto, ut ipse erat, ad ambulandum in via Dei,

vulneraveratcaritaschristicoreiusetgesta.en: The charity of Christ had wounded his heart, and he bore his words in his bowels as sharp arrows:
vulneraveratcaritaschristicoreiusetgesta.la: Vulneráverat caritas Christi cor ejus, et gestábat verba ejus in viscéribus quasi sagittas acútas:

etexempaservorumdeiquosdemortuisvivosfec.en: And the examples of the servants of God, whom he had made living from dead, as wasting coals.
etexempaservorumdeiquosdemortuisvivosfec.la: Et exémpa servórum Dei, quos de mórtuis vivos fécerat, tamquam carbónes vastatóres.

ascendetiaconvalleplorationisetcantantic.en: To him that went up from the vale of tears and sang the Canticle of degrees he had given sharp arrows.
ascendetiaconvalleplorationisetcantantic.la: Ascendéti a conválle ploratiónis et cantánti Cánticum gráduum déderat sagittas acútas.

acceptabaptismigratiapositusapudostiatib.en: Having received the grace of Baptism, being at Ostia on the Tiber with his mother, they conversed alone very sweetly, and with the mouth of the heart gaped together after the heavenly streams of the fountain of life:
acceptabaptismigratiapositusapudostiatib.la: Accépta Baptismi grátia, pósitus apud Ostia Tiberína cum matre sua, colloquebántur soli valde dúlciter, et inhiábant ore cordis páriter in supérna fluénta fontis vitæ:

vilescebatquemundusisteinterverbacumdele.en: And this world, with its delights, grew vile to them amid their words.
vilescebatquemundusisteinterverbacumdele.la: Vilescebátque mundus iste inter verba, cum delectatióibus suis.

tuncaitillafilionullareiamdelectorinhacv.en: Then she said to her son: In nothing do I now delight in this life, since I see thee, earthly happiness despised, a servant of Christ.
tuncaitillafilionullareiamdelectorinhacv.la: Tunc ait illa filio: Nulla re jam deléctor in hac vita, cum te, contémpta felicitáte terréna, vídeam servum Christi.

verbumdeiusqueadipsamsuamegritudinemimpr.en: The word of God, even up to his last sickness, without intermission, eagerly and boldly, with sound mind and sound judgment, he preached in the holy Church: sound in all the members of his body, with sight and hearing unimpaired,
verbumdeiusqueadipsamsuamegritudinemimpr.la: Verbum Dei usque ad ipsam suam ægritúdinem imprætermisse, alácriter et fórtiter, sana mente sanóque consílio, in sancta Ecclésia prædicávit: membris ómnibus sui córporis incólumis, integro aspéctu atque audítu,

corampositisfratribusetorantibusdormivit.en: With the brethren standing by and praying, He slept with his fathers.
corampositisfratribusetorantibusdormivit.la: Coram pósitis frátribus et orántibus, Dormívit cum pátribus suis.

testamentumnullumfecitquiaundefaceretpau.en: He made no will: because, a poor man of Christ, he had nothing wherefrom to make one.
testamentumnullumfecitquiaundefaceretpau.la: Testaméntum nullum fecit: quia unde fáceret pauper Christi non hábuit.

postmortemmatrisreversusestaugustinusada.en: After his mother's death Augustine returned to his own lands: where, giving himself with his friends to fastings and prayers, he wrote books and taught the unlearned.
postmortemmatrisreversusestaugustinusada.la: Post mortem matris revêrsus est Augustinus ad agros proprios: ubi, cum amicis jejuniis et orationibus vacans, scribêbat libros et docêbat indôctos.

compertaautemeiusfamabeatusvaleriushippo.en: And his fame being known, blessed Valerius, Bishop of Hippo, caused him to be summoned to him: and though he was unwilling, ordained him priest.
compertaautemeiusfamabeatusvaleriushippo.la: Compêrta autem ejus fama, beâtus Valérius Hipponênsis Episcopus eum ad se accersiri fecit: et licet invitum presbyterum ordinâvit.

factusergopresbytermonasteriumclericorum.en: Being made priest therefore, he soon established a monastery of clerics: and began to live according to the rule established under the holy Apostles.
factusergopresbytermonasteriumclericorum.la: Factus ergo presbyter, monastérium clericorum mox instituit: et cépit vivere secûndum regulam sub sanctis Apóstolis constitutam.

sanctusautemvaleriusordinatoreiusexultab.en: And holy Valerius, who ordained him, rejoiced the more abundantly that such a man had been given him by God, who was fit to edify the Church in sound doctrine.
sanctusautemvaleriusordinatoreiusexultab.la: Sanctus autem Valérius ordinátor ejus exultabat ubérius hómúnem sibi talem datum divinitus, qui in doctrina sana ædificâre Ecclésiá esset idôneus.

eodeteporefortunatuspresbytermanicheorum.en: At the same time Fortunatus, a priest of the Manichees, by his craftiness was seducing very many: whom holy Augustine, disputing in an assembly of all, publicly overcame.
eodeteporefortunatuspresbytermanicheorum.la: Eodé tépore Fortunâtus, presbyter Manichæorum, versûtia plurimos seducêbat: quem sanctus Augustinus in conventu omnium disputans publice superâvit.

solisreduxitorbita.en: The circuit of the sun hath brought back.

quodlinguaforispersonat.en: What the tongue soundeth forth without

necimitaripigeat.en: Nor let it irk us to imitate

quodlaudaremensapprobat.en: What the mind approveth in praising.

huncpostmundicurricula.en: Him, after the courses of the world,

celisuscepitcuria.en: The court of heaven hath received:

conemurtotisviribus.en: Let us strive with all our strength,

iungamusprecesprecibus.en: Let us join prayers to prayers,

utaugustinimeritis.en: That by the merits of Augustine

celifruamurgaudiis.en: We may enjoy the joys of heaven.

prestapaterpiissime.en: Grant this, O most loving Father,

patriquecomparunice.en: And thou, only Son, equal to the Father,

indiebuseiusobsessestcivitashipponensisa.en: In his days the city of Hippo was besieged by an army of barbarians: amid which evils his tears were Augustine's bread day and night: and coming to his last hour amid this event, he fell asleep in peace.
indiebuseiusobsessestcivitashipponensisa.la: In diebus ejus obsessa est civitas Hipponênsis ab exercitu barbarorum: inter quæ mala fuérunt Augustíno lácrimæ suæ panes die ac nocte: atque sub hoc événtu ad extrémam horam véniens, obdormívit in pace.

hodiegloriosuspateraugustinusdissolutahu.en: Today the glorious Father Augustine, the house of this dwelling being dissolved, received a house not made with hands in heaven, which, the grace of God working with him, he fashioned for himself on earth by hand and tongue: where he now tasteth eternally that for which he thirsted inwardly, adorned with one robe, and secure of the other.
hodiegloriosuspateraugustinusdissolutahu.la: Hódie gloriósus Pater Augustinus, dissoluta hujus habitationis domo, domum non manufactam accepit in cælis, quam sibi, cooperante Dei grátia, manu, lingua fabrefecit in terris: ubi jam quod sitivit intèrnum gustat ætèrnum, decorátus una stola, securusque de reliqua.

inmediocarcerisstabatbeatusioannesvocema.en: In the midst of the prison stood blessed John: with a loud voice he cried and said:
inmediocarcerisstabatbeatusioannesvocema.la: In médio cárceris stabat beátus Joánnes: voce magna clamávit et dixit:

dominedeusmeustibicommendospiritummeum.en: O Lord my God, to thee I commend my spirit.
dominedeusmeustibicommendospiritummeum.la: Dómine Deus meus, tibi comméndo spíritum meum.

misitrexetdecollariiussitioannemincarcer.en: The king sent and commanded John to be beheaded in the prison, as he prayed and said.
misitrexetdecollariiussitioannemincarcer.la: Misit rex et decollári jussit Joánnem in cárcere, orántem et dicéntem.

accedentesdiscipulisanctiioannisbaptiste.en: The disciples of holy John the Baptist, coming,

tuleruntcorpuseiusetsepelieruntillud.en: Took his body, And buried it.
tuleruntcorpuseiusetsepelieruntillud.la: Tulérunt corpus ejus, Et sepeliérunt illud.

iussuherodisamputatumestcaputioannisinca.en: By the command of Herod the head of John was cut off in the prison: which when his disciples heard.
iussuherodisamputatumestcaputioannisinca.la: Jussu Heródis amputátum est caput Joánnis in cárcere: quo audíto, discipuli ejus.

orapronobisbeateioannesbaptista.en: Pray for us, O blessed John the Baptist.
orapronobisbeateioannesbaptista.la: Ora pro nobis, beáte Joánnes Baptísta.

tellurisomnesincole.en: Let all the dwellers on the earth

roseplaudantsolemniis.en: Applaud the solemn feast of Rose,

asolisortuadhesperum.en: From the rising of the sun unto the West.

preventadonisgratie.en: Forestalled by the gifts of grace,

deoqueplenavindicem.en: And full of God, an avenging

cibosquefellepolluit.en: And defiled her food with gall.

agnisequensvestigia.en: Following the footsteps of the Lamb.

horumdatorimunereum.en: To the Giver of these gifts

quitrinusunusomnia.en: Who, three and one, all things

regemsempiternumveniteadoremusquirosamco.en: The everlasting King, come, let us adore, * Who hath crowned in heaven the Rose of his heart, worthily according to her merits.
regemsempiternumveniteadoremusquirosamco.la: Regem sempitérnum, veníte, adorémus, * Qui Rosam cordis sui digne pro méritis coronávit in cælis.

regalemunusededit.en: Hath brought forth a royal gift:

rosamdeogratissimam.en: A Rose most pleasing to God,

celestisoreflosculum.en: A little flower of the heavenly shore.

vicitnitoresidera.en: She surpassed the stars in brightness,

pulsasolicaligine.en: The gloom of the earth dispelled:

etparbeatismentibus.en: And, like to the blessed spirits,

numengerebatpectore.en: She bore the Godhead in her breast.

sevestygisnonhorruit.en: Of cruel Styx she dreaded not,

turbamperosetseculum.en: Loathing the crowd and the world.

nosobeatarespice.en: Look upon us, O Blessed one,

tuisvacanteslaudibus.en: Who give ourselves to thy praises,

ducadsupernagaudia.en: Lead us to the joys above.

sitchristesponsevirginum.en: Be glory, O Christ, Spouse of virgins,

tibipatriquegloria.en: To thee and to the Father,

rosamtuamdomineminuistipaulominusabangel.en: Thou hast made thy Rose, O Lord, a little less than the Angels, for thou hast crowned her with glory and honour.
rosamtuamdomineminuistipaulominusabangel.la: Rosam tuam, Dómine, minuísti paulo minus ab Angelis, quia glória et honóre coronásti eam. Ps. 8

tamquamsponsusprocedensdethalamosuoinros.en: As a bridegroom coming out of his bride chamber, he hath set his tabernacle in Rose.
tamquamsponsusprocedensdethalamosuoinros.la: Tamquam sponsus procedens de thálamo suo, in Rosa pósuit tabernáculum suum. Ps. 18

rosainnocensmanibusetmundocordeascenditi.en: Rose, innocent in hands and clean of heart, ascended into the mountain of the Lord, and shall stand in his holy place.
rosainnocensmanibusetmundocordeascenditi.la: Rosa innocens má nibus et mundo corde ascéndit in montem Dómini, et stabit in loco sancto ejus. Ps. 23

omnisgloriaroseabintusinvestitudeauratoc.en: All the glory of Rose is within, in golden borders, clothed round about with varieties: therefore hath the King greatly desired her beauty.
omnisgloriaroseabintusinvestitudeauratoc.la: Omnis glória Rosæ ab intus, in vestitu deauráto, circumamícta varietáte: ideo concupívit Rex spéciem ejus. Ps. 44

adiuvitrosamdominusmanediluculetinmedioc.en: The Lord helped Rose in the morning early, and in the midst of her heart, she shall not be moved.
adiuvitrosamdominusmanediluculetinmedioc.la: Adiúvit Rosam Dóminus mane dilúculo, et in médio cordis ejus, non commovébitur. Ps. 45

fundamentaroseinmontibussanctisetipsefun.en: The foundations of Rose are in the holy mountains: and the Most High himself hath founded her above all the tabernacles of Jacob.
fundamentaroseinmontibussanctisetipsefun.la: Fundaménta Rosæ in móntibus sanctis: et ipse fundávit eam Altissimus super ómnia tabernácula Jacob. Ps. 86

surgenterosagaudebantcampietomniaqueinei.en: When Rose arose, the fields rejoiced and all things that are in them: and all the trees of the woods exulted.
surgenterosagaudebantcampietomniaqueinei.la: Surgénte Rosa, gaudébant campi et ómnia quæ in eis sunt: et exsultábant ómnia ligna silvárum. Ps. 95

exsultetterretletenturinsulemultequiavid.en: Let the earth rejoice, and let many islands be glad, for all peoples have seen the glory of her sanctification.
exsultetterretletenturinsulemultequiavid.la: Exsúltet terra et læténtur insulæ multæ, quia vidérunt omnes pópuli glóriam sanctificatiónis ejus. Ps. 96

moveaturmareetplenitudeiusorbisterrarume.en: Let the sea be moved and the fulness thereof, the world and they that dwell therein: for the Lord hath done wonderful things in Rose.
moveaturmareetplenitudeiusorbisterrarume.la: Moveátur mare et plenitúdo ejus, orbis terrárum et qui hábitant in eo: quia Dóminus in Rosa mirabilia fecit. Ps. 97

attenditepopulidelongedominusabuterovoca.en: Hearken, ye people from afar: the Lord hath called me from the womb, from the bowels of my mother
attenditepopulidelongedominusabuterovoca.la: Atténdite, pópuli de longe: Dóminus ab útero vocávit me, de ventre matris meæ

recordatusestnominismei.en: He hath been mindful of my name.

magnuspastoroviuminsaguinetestamentieter.en: The great pastor of the sheep, in the blood of the everlasting testament, calleth his own sheep by name and leadeth them out.
magnuspastoroviuminsaguinetestamentieter.la: Magnus pastor óvium, in ságuine testaménti ætérni, próprias oves vocat nominatim et educit eas.

etsicdicetisinconfessioneoperadominiuniv.en: And thus you shall say in confession: All the works of the Lord are exceeding good.
etsicdicetisinconfessioneoperadominiuniv.la: Et sic dicétis in confessióne: Opera Dómini univérsa bona valde.

egoquasistoraxetgalbanusetquasilibanusno.en: As storax and galbanum, and as frankincense not cut, I perfumed my dwelling.
egoquasistoraxetgalbanusetquasilibanusno.la: Ego quasi storax et galbanus, et quasi Libanus non incisus vaporavi habitationem meam.

quasibalsamumnonmixtumodormeus.en: My odour is as the purest balm.
quasibalsamumnonmixtumodormeus.la: Quasi balsamum non mixtum odor meus.

deditindicarosaodoremsuavitatisetdomusim.en: The Indian Rose yielded an odour of sweetness, and the house was filled with the odour of the ointment.
deditindicarosaodoremsuavitatisetdomusim.la: Dedit Indica Rosa odorem suavitatis, et domus impleta est ex odore unguenti.

gaudeamusetexultemusquiaveneruntnuptieag.en: Let us be glad and rejoice, for the marriage of the Lamb is come, and his wife hath prepared herself:
gaudeamusetexultemusquiaveneruntnuptieag.la: Gaudeamus et exultemus, quia venerunt nuptiæ Agni, et uxor ejus præparavit se:

datumestilliutcooperiatsebyssinosplenden.en: It is granted to her that she should clothe herself with fine linen, glittering and white, which are The justifications of saints.
datumestilliutcooperiatsebyssinosplenden.la: Datum est illi ut cooperiat se byssino splendenti et candido, quæ sunt Justificationes sanctorum.

posuitrexdiademaregniincapiteeiusfecitqu.en: The king set the royal crown on her head, and made her to reign.
posuitrexdiademaregniincapiteeiusfecitqu.la: Posuit rex diadema regni in capite ejus, fecitque eam regnare.

orapronobisbeatarosa.en: Pray for us, O blessed Rose.

mirabilisinaltisdominusutsponsamsuammiri.en: Wonderful is the Lord on high: that he might make his spouse wonderful, he hath put on beauty, girding himself with strength.
mirabilisinaltisdominusutsponsamsuammiri.la: Mirábilis in altis Dóminus, ut sponsam suam mirificáret, decórem indútus est, præcingens se virtúte.

inletitietexultationeserviensdeobeataros.en: Serving God in gladness and exultation, blessed Rose entered into his courts.
inletitietexultationeserviensdeobeataros.la: In lætítia et exultatione sérvíens Deo, beáta Rosa introívit in átria ejus.

exsultavitrosainvelamentoalarumtuarumqui.en: Rose rejoiced under the covert of thy wings, because thy right hand received her.
exsultavitrosainvelamentoalarumtuarumqui.la: Exsultávit Rosa in velaménto alárum tuárum, quia suscepit eam dextera tua.

benedicatomnisimberetrosdominoquirosambe.en: Let every shower and dew bless the Lord, who watered Rose with blessing from his upper rooms.
benedicatomnisimberetrosdominoquirosambe.la: Benedícat omnis imber et ros Dómino, qui Rosam benedictione irrigávit de superióribus suis.

laudentnomendominiaqueomnesquesupercelos.en: Let all the waters that are above the heavens praise the name of the Lord, where Rose flourisheth, planted near the running waters.
laudentnomendominiaqueomnesquesupercelos.la: Laudent nomen Dómini aquæ omnes quæ super cælos sunt, ubi Rosa vernat plantáta juxta rivos aquárum.

hancamavietexquisiviaiuventutemeetquesiv.en: Her have I loved, and have sought her out from my youth, and have desired to take her for my spouse, and I became a lover of her beauty, saith the Lord almighty.
hancamavietexquisiviaiuventutemeetquesiv.la: Hanc amávi, et exquisívi a juventúte mea, et quæsívi sponsam mihi eam assúmere, et amátor factus sum formæ illíus, ait Dóminus omnipotens.

rosisquemaneconcolor.en: And in the morning, of like hue with the roses,

laudessacratevirginis.en: The praises of the hallowed virgin

rosemonetnospangere.en: Rose it biddeth us to sing.

hancergolaudentangeli.en: Her then let the Angels praise

etomnisordocelitum.en: And every order of the heavenly ones:

laudentchorimortalium.en: Let the choirs of mortals praise

ubiquegestisinclitam.en: Her, everywhere renowned for her deeds.

hancprimamamorisvicitimam.en: Her, the first victim of love,

admovitarisindia.en: The Indies brought to the altars,

datcecisluceperfrui.en: She giveth to the blind to enjoy the light,

solvitquelinguevincula.en: And looseth the bonds of the tongue,

claudosiacenteserigit.en: She raiseth up the lame that lie low,

iugistibilaustrinitas.en: Unceasing praise to thee, O Trinity,

orosaodoriferaspargensubiquevirtutumodor.en: O fragrant Rose, spreading everywhere the odour of virtues, make us partakers of that light and sweetness which thou enjoyest.
orosaodoriferaspargensubiquevirtutumodor.la: O Rosa odorífera, spargens ubíque virtútum odórem, fac nos ejus, qua frúeris, lucis suavítatisque partícipes.

obauditemedivinifructusetquasirosaplanta.en: Hear me, ye divine offspring, and bud forth as the rose planted by the brooks of waters. Give ye a sweet odour as frankincense.
obauditemedivinifructusetquasirosaplanta.la: Obaudíte me, divíni fructus, et quasi rosa plantáta super rivos aquárum fructificáte. Quasi Líbanus odórem suavitátis habéte.

tugloriaierusalemtuletitiaisreltuhonorif.en: Thou art the glory of Jerusalem, thou the joy of Israel, thou the honour of our people: O Rose, thou hast done manfully, and thy heart hath been strengthened.
tugloriaierusalemtuletitiaisreltuhonorif.la: Tu glória Jerúsalem, tu lætítia Israël, tu honorificéntia pópuli nostri: o Rosa, fecísti viríliter, et confortátum est cor tuum.

prestaquesumusomnipotensdeusutquibeatinm.en: Grant, we beseech thee, O Almighty God, that we who keep the birthday of blessed N. thy Martyr may by his intercession be delivered from all the ills that hang over us.
prestaquesumusomnipotensdeusutquibeatinm.la: Præsta, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, qui beáti N., Mártyris tui, natalítia cólimus, a cunctis malis imminéntibus, ejus intercessióne, liberémur.

deusquisanctopatriarchedominicobeatumber.en: O God, who didst join to the holy Patriarch Dominic blessed Bertrand thy Confessor as his companion and eminent imitator: grant us by his loving intercession so to follow in his footsteps, that we may also attain his rewards.
deusquisanctopatriarchedominicobeatumber.la: Deus, qui sancto Patriarchæ Domínico beátum Bertrándum, Confessórem tuum, sócium et imitatórem exímium adiúnxísti: ejus nobis pio intervéntu concéde ita ejúsdem sequi vestígia, ut assequámur et prǽmia.

nativitastuadeigenetrixvirgogaudiumannun.en: Thy Birth, O Virgin Mother of God, was a message of joy to the whole world;
nativitastuadeigenetrixvirgogaudiumannun.la: Natívitas tua, Dei Génetrix Virgo, gáudium annuntiávit univérso mundo:

felixnamquesesquesolagenetricisdignitate.en: For happy art thou, who alone hast obtained the dignity of a Mother, and hast not lost virginal purity.
felixnamquesesquesolagenetricisdignitate.la: Felix namques es, quæ sola Genetrícis dignitátem obtinuísti, et virginálem pudicítiam non amisísti.

sermdenativitbmarie.en: Sermon on the Nativity of the Blessed Mary

intueaminifratresquantodevotionisaffectu.en: Consider, brethren, with what affection of devotion he would have Mary honoured by us, who hath placed the fulness of all good in Mary: that accordingly, if there be any hope in us, any grace, any salvation, we may know that it overfloweth from her who went up abounding with delights. Truly a garden of delights, which that divine South wind not only breathed upon in coming, but also blew through in coming upon it, that on every side its spices might flow and flow forth, namely the gifts of graces.
intueaminifratresquantodevotionisaffectu.la: Intueámini, fratres, quanto devotionis afféctu a nobis Mariam volúerit honorári, qui totius boni plenitudinem posuit in Maria: ut proinde, si quid spei in nobis est, si quid gratiæ, si quid salutis, ab ea novérimus redundare, quæ ascendit deliciis affluens. Hortus plane deliciárum, quem non modo afflaverit veniens, sed et perflaverit superveniens Auster ille divinus, ut undique fluant et effluant aromata ejus, charismata scilicet gratiarum.

cumiucunditatenativitatembeatemarieceleb.en: Let us keep with rejoicing the Birthday of the Blessed Mary,
cumiucunditatenativitatembeatemarieceleb.la: Cum jucunditáte Nativitátem beátæ Maríæ celebrémus.

solemiustitieregempariturasupremum.en: About to bring forth the Sun of justice, the supreme King,

stellamariamarishodieprocessitadortum.en: Mary, the Star of the sea, Today came forth to her rising.
stellamariamarishodieprocessitadortum.la: Stella Maria maris Hódie procéssit ad ortum.

cerneredivinumlumengaudetefideles.en: Rejoice, ye faithful, to behold the divine light.

hodieprocessitadortum.en: Today came forth to her rising.

ducentorumetquinquemartyrumquiseculodeci.en: Of the two hundred and five martyrs who, at the beginning of the seventeenth century, shed their blood for Christ in Japan, a great part belonged to the Philippine province of the Order of Preachers. The first, Alphonsus Navarrete, the superior of the mission, who, boldly scorning an unjust law, had publicly come to the aid of the needs of the faithful, was beheaded at Omura in the year one thousand six hundred and seventeen. In the same year and in the eleven following, other fathers of the same province, partly at Nagasaki, partly at Omura, received the crown of martyrdom. This band of preachers, and others from the orders of St. Francis, St. Augustine and the Society of Jesus, were accompanied to heaven by both clerics and lay brothers, and by brothers and sisters of the Third Order and of the Society of the Rosary, and also by many other Japanese of both sexes, all of whom Pius the Ninth, in the year one thousand eight hundred and sixty-six, enrolled in the list of the Blessed.
ducentorumetquinquemartyrumquiseculodeci.la: Ducentórum et quinque mártyrum, qui sǽculo décimo séptimo ineúnte, in Japónia sánguinem pro Christo fudérunt, ad Philippinárum provínciam órdinis Prædicatórum magna pars attinébat. Primus, Alfónsus Navarréte, missiónis moderátor, qui, iníqua lege audácter sprete, fidélium necessitátibus públice subvénerat, Vómuræ, anno millésimo sexcentésimo décimo séptimo, cápite plexus est. Eódem anno atque sequéntibus úndecim, álii ejúsdem provinciæ patres, partim Nagasáchi, partim Vómuræ, mátyrii corónam percipérunt. Hanc prædicatórum cohórtem, aliósque ex ordínibus sancti Francísci, sancti Augustíni et Societátis Jesu, in cælum comitabántur et clérici et convérsi, fratrésque ac soróres tértii órdinis societatísque Rosárii, necnon et plures álii Japonénses utriúsque sexus, quos omnes Pius nonus, anno millésimo octingentésimo sexagésimo sexto, Beatórum albo accénsuit.

deusquinosbeatorumtuorumalfonsietsocioru.en: O God, who dost gladden us with the triumph of thy blessed Alphonsus and his companions: grant us, we beseech thee, by their merits and intercession, the same constancy in faith, and efficacy in work.
deusquinosbeatorumtuorumalfonsietsocioru.la: Deus, qui nos beatórum tuórum Alfónsi et sociórum ejus triúmpho lætificas: da nobis, quæsumus, córum méritis et intercessióne, eándem in fide constántiam, et in ópere effacíam.

concedequesumusomnipotensdeusutecclesiat.en: Grant, we beseech thee, O Almighty God: that thy Church, which shineth with the glory of the virtues and miracles of blessed Nicholas thy Confessor, may by his intercession and merits rejoice in perpetual peace and unity.
concedequesumusomnipotensdeusutecclesiat.la: Concede, quæsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut Ecclesiá tua, quæ beáti Nicolái Confessoris tui virtutum et miraculórum glória corúscat, ejus intercessióne et méritis, perpétua pace atque unitáte lætétur.

deusquigloriosammatremtuamnominarimariam.en: O God, who didst will that thy glorious Mother should be named Mary: grant, we beseech thee, that they who implore the sweet name of Mary may feel the perpetual help of her blessing:
deusquigloriosammatremtuamnominarimariam.la: Deus, qui gloriósam Matrem tuam nominári Mariám voluisti: concéde, quæsumus, ut, qui dulce Mariæ nomen implórant, perpétuum sésentiant suæ benedictionis auxílium:

ocruxadmirabilisevacuatiovulnerisrestitu.en: O wondrous Cross, the emptying of the wound, the restoring of health!
ocruxadmirabilisevacuatiovulnerisrestitu.la: O Crux admirábilis, evacuátio vúlneris, restitútio sanitátis! Ps. 112, 116, 145, 146, 147

pertuamcrucemsalvanoschristeredemptorqui.en: Through thy Cross save us, O Christ the Redeemer, who by dying didst destroy our death,
pertuamcrucemsalvanoschristeredemptorqui.la: Per tuam Crucem salva nos, Christe Redémptor, qui mortem nostram moriéndó destruxisti,

etvitamresurgendoreparasti.en: And by rising again didst restore life.

misererenostriiesubenignequipassusesclem.en: Have mercy on us, O kind Jesus, who didst suffer mercifully for us.
misererenostriiesubenignequipassusesclem.la: Miserére nostri, Jesu benígne, qui passus es cleménter pro nobis.

salvecruxsanctasalvemundigloria.en: Hail, holy Cross, hail, glory of the world,
salvecruxsanctasalvemundigloria.la: Salve, Crux sancta, salve, mundi glória,

veraspesnostraveraferensgaudia.en: Our true hope, bringing true joys,
veraspesnostraveraferensgaudia.la: Vera spes nostra, vera ferens gáudia,

signumsalutissalusinpericulis.en: Sign of salvation, safety in perils,

vitalelignumvitamferensomnium.en: Life-giving wood bearing the life of all.

teadorandamtecrucemvivificam.en: Thee to be adored, thee the life-giving Cross,

perteredeptidulcedecusseculi.en: We, redeemed through thee, sweet glory of the world,
perteredeptidulcedecusseculi.la: Per te redépti, dulce decus sæculi,

semperlaudamussempertibicanimus.en: Ever praise, ever to thee we sing:

perlignumservipertesumusliberi.en: Through the wood slaves, through thee we are free.
perlignumservipertesumusliberi.la: Per lignum servi, per te sumus liberi.

sitdeopatrilausincrucefilii.en: To God the Father be praise in the Cross of the Son,
sitdeopatrilausincrucefilii.la: Sit Deo Patri laus in Cruce Filii,

sitcequalislaussanctospiritui.en: Equal praise be to the Holy Ghost:

civibussummisgaudiumsitangelis.en: To the Angels, citizens on high, be joy,

honorsitmundocrucisexaltatio.en: Be the Exaltation of the Cross an honour to the world.

cruxfidelisinteromnesarborunanobilisnull.en: Faithful Cross, * among all trees the one noble tree; no forest yieldeth such, in leaf, in flower, in bud: sweet the wood, sweet the nails, sweet the weight that it bore.
cruxfidelisinteromnesarborunanobilisnull.la: Crux fidélis, * inter omnes arbor una nóbilis, nulla silva talem profert, fronde, flore, gérmine: dulce lignum, dulces clavos, dulce pondus sustínuit.

regemdominumquipercrucismysteriumredemit.en: The Lord the King, who through the mystery of the Cross redeemed the world, * Come, let us adore.
regemdominumquipercrucismysteriumredemit.la: Regem Dóminum, qui per Crucis mystérium redémit mundum, * Veníte, adorémus.

crucemtuamadoramusdomineetsanctamresurre.en: We adore thy Cross, O Lord, and we praise and glorify thy holy resurrection: for behold, by reason of the Cross joy hath come into the whole world.
crucemtuamadoramusdomineetsanctamresurre.la: Crucem tuam adorámus, Dómine, et sanctam resurrectioném tuam laudámus et glorificámus: ecce enim propter Crucem venit gáudium in univérsó mundo. Ps. 95

cruxalmafulgetperquamsalusredditestmundo.en: The loving Cross shineth, whereby salvation was restored to the world: the Cross conquereth, the Cross reigneth, the Cross driveth away all sin, alleluia.
cruxalmafulgetperquamsalusredditestmundo.la: Crux alma fulget, per quam salus réddita est mundo: Crux vincit, Crux regnat, Crux repéllit omne crimen, allelúja. Ps. 96

deepistolabeatipauliapostoliadgalatas.en: Lesson from the letter of St. Paul the Apostle to the Galatians
deepistolabeatipauliapostoliadgalatas.la: De Epístola beáti Pauli Apóstoli ad Gálatas

perquodetdiabolusestvictusetmunduschrist.en: Whereby both the devil is overcome, and the world redeemed by the blood of Christ!
perquodetdiabolusestvictusetmunduschrist.la: Per quod et diábolus est victus, et mundus Christi sánguine redémptus!

etmunduschristisanguineredemptus.en: And the world redeemed by the blood of Christ!

inillotemporedixitiesusturbisiudeorumnun.en: At that time, Jesus said unto the multitudes of the Jews: Now is the judgment of this world, now shall the prince of this world be cast out. And so on.
inillotemporedixitiesusturbisiudeorumnun.la: In illo témpore: Dixit Jesus turbis Judæórum: Nunc judícium est mundi: nunc princeps hujus mundi eiciétur foras. Et réliqua.

possidebatdiabolusgenushumanumetreossupp.en: The devil possessed the human race, and held them guilty of punishments by the handwriting of their sins. He ruled in the hearts of unbelievers: he drew them, deceived and captive, to worship the creature, having forsaken the Creator. But through faith in Christ, which was confirmed by his death and resurrection, through his blood, which was shed for the remission of sins, thousands of believers are delivered from the dominion of the devil, are joined to the body of Christ, and under so great a head are quickened by his one spirit as faithful members. This he calleth the Judgment, this the separation, this the casting out of the devil from them that are his redeemed.
possidebatdiabolusgenushumanumetreossupp.la: Possidébat diábolus genus humánum et reos suppliciórum tenébat chirographo peccatórum. Dominabátur in córdibus infidélium: ad creatúram coléndam, desérto Creatóre, decéptos captívosque pertrahébat. Per Christi autem fidem, quæ morte ejus et resurrectione firmáta est, per ejus sanguinem, qui in remissionem fusus est peccatórum, millia credéntium a dominátu liberántur diáboli, Christi córpori copulántur, et sub tanto cápite, uno ejus spíritu fidélia membra vegetántur. Hoc vocat Judícium, hanc discretiónem, hanc a suis redémtis diáboli expulsiónem.

nuncinquitprincepshuiusmundieicieturfora.en: Now, saith he, shall the prince of this world be cast out. The Lord foretold what he knew, that after his passion and glorification many peoples throughout the whole world would believe, in whose hearts the devil was within: whom, when they renounce him by faith, he is cast out. But God forbid that we should think the devil to be called prince of the world in such wise as to believe that he can rule over heaven and earth. But the world is so called in the wicked men, who are spread throughout the whole circle of the earth. Thus therefore it is said, The prince of this world, that is, the prince of all the wicked who dwell in the world.
nuncinquitprincepshuiusmundieicieturfora.la: Nunc, inquit, princeps hujus mundi eiciétur foras. Prædicébat Dóminus, quod sciébat post passióem et glorificatióem suam per univérsum mundum multos pópulos creditúros, in quorum córdibus diábolus intus erat: cui quando ex fide renúntiant, eícitur foras. Absit autem ut diábolum mundi príncipem ita dictum existimémus, ut eum cælo et terræ dominári posse credámus. Sed mundus appellátur in malis homínibus, qui toto terrárum orbe diffúsi sunt. Sic ergo dictum est, Princeps hujus mundi, id est Princeps malórum ómnium, qui hábitant in mundo.

etegoinquitsiexaltatusfueroaterraomniatr.en: And I, saith he, if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all things to myself. But he said not, All men, but, All things: for all men have not faith. Therefore he referred this not to the whole of mankind, but to the wholeness of the creature, that is, spirit, and soul, and body. Or if by All things men themselves are to be understood, we can say all that are predestined unto salvation: or surely all kinds of men, from the highest even to the lowest, from the king even to the beggar. All things, saith he, will I draw to myself, that I may be their head, and they my members.
etegoinquitsiexaltatusfueroaterraomniatr.la: Et ego, inquit, si exaltátus fuéro a terra, ómnia traham post me. Non autem dixit: Omnes: sed, Omnia: non enim ómnium est fides. Non itaque hoc ad universitátem hóminum rétulit, sed ad creatúræ integritátem, id est spíritum et ánimam et corpus. Aut si per Omnia ipsi hómines intelligéendi sunt, ómnia prædestináta ad salutem póssumus dicere: aut certe ómnia hóminum génera, ab excelsíssimis usque ad humíllimos, a rege usque ad mendícum. Omnia, inquit, traham post me, ut sim caput eórum, et illi membra mea.

quiadominusregnavitaligno.en: That the Lord hath reigned from the tree.

cruxbenedictanitetdominusquacarnepependi.en: The blessed Cross shineth, whereon the Lord hung in the flesh, and with his own blood washed our wounds.
cruxbenedictanitetdominusquacarnepependi.la: Crux benedícta nitet, Dóminus qua carne pepéndit atque cruóre suo vúlnera nostra lavit.

originalecrimennecansincruce.en: Thou who didst slay original sin on the Cross,

nosaprivatischristemundamaculis.en: Cleanse us, O Christ, from our own stains:
nosaprivatischristemundamaculis.la: Nos a privátis, Christe, munda máculis:

percrucemsanctamlapsisdonaveniam.en: By the holy Cross grant pardon to the fallen.
percrucemsanctamlapsisdonaveniam.la: Per Crucem sanctam lapsis dona véniam.

populumcunctumcrucispersignaculum.en: All the people by the sign of the Cross:

morboavertecorporisetanime.en: Turn away the sickness of body and of soul:

hoccontrasignumnulumstetpericulum.en: Against this sign let no peril stand.
hoccontrasignumnulumstetpericulum.la: Hoc contra signum nulum stet perículum.

tuamcrucemadoramusdomine.en: We adore thy Cross, O Lord.

verbumcrucispereuntibusstultitiestiisaut.en: The word of the cross, to them that perish, is foolishness: but to them that are saved, that is, to us, it is the power of God.
verbumcrucispereuntibusstultitiestiisaut.la: Verbum crucis pereúntibus stultítia est: iis autem qui salvi fiunt, id est nobis, virtus Dei est.

nosautempredicamuschristumcrucifixumiude.en: But we preach Christ crucified, unto the Jews indeed a stumblingblock, and unto the Gentiles foolishness: but unto them that are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God, and the wisdom of God.
nosautempredicamuschristumcrucifixumiude.la: Nos autem prædicámus Christum crucifíxum: Judǽis quidem scándalum, géntibus autem stultítiam: ipsis autem vocátis Judǽis, atque Græcis Christum Dei virtútem, et Dei sapiéntiam:

innocensetexperscriminismoriturmisertush.en: Innocent and free from sin, he dieth, having had pity on man.
innocensetexperscriminismoriturmisertush.la: Innocens et expers criminis móritur misértus hóminis.

cumsimuscausasuppliciisimusetmerorissoci.en: Since we are the cause of the punishment, let us also be companions of the sorrow: the goad of love of the Virgin Mother and of the Son urgeth us on.
cumsimuscausasuppliciisimusetmerorissoci.la: Cum simus causa supplícii, simus et mæróris sócii: Vírginis Matris et Fílii nos urget stímulus amóris.

recolamuscumlacrimistristitiamgenetricis.en: Let us recall with tears the sadness of the Mother, asking grace of the Son.
recolamuscumlacrimistristitiamgenetricis.la: Recolámus cum lácrimis tristítiam Genetrícis, grátiam peténtes Géniti.

virginismatrisetfiliinosurgetstimulusamo.en: The goad of love of the Virgin Mother and of the Son urgeth us on.
virginismatrisetfiliinosurgetstimulusamo.la: Vírginis Matris et Fílii nos urget stímulus amóris.

defecitindolorevitamea.en: My life is wasted with grief.

christiredeptisanguine.en: Redeemed by the blood of Christ,

tantumdoloremflebili.en: So great a sorrow with tearful

matrisquedetcompassio.en: And his Mother's Compassion may give.

virgomarianonestullasimilempassadoloremi.en: O Virgin Mary, there is none among women that hath suffered sorrow like unto thine, while thou beholdest thy Son crucified and dying. Pray for us, O loving Mother of God.
virgomarianonestullasimilempassadoloremi.la: Virgo María, non est ulla símilem passa dolórem inter mulíeres, dum crucifíxum cernis mori Fílium. Ora pro nobis, pia Dei Génetrix.

omnipotenssempiternedeusquiinfirmamundie.en: O Almighty and everlasting God, who choosest the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty: mercifully grant, that we who keep the solemn feast of blessed N. thy Virgin and Martyr, may feel the power of her intercession with thee.
omnipotenssempiternedeusquiinfirmamundie.la: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, qui infírma mundi éligis, ut fórtia quæque confúndas: concéde propítius; ut, qui beátæ N. Vírginis et Mártyris tuæ solémnia cólimus, ejus apud te patrocínia sentiámus.

ioannesexcompatrisnomineutiferturmassias.en: John, called Massias, as it is said, from the name of his godfather, was born in the year one thousand five hundred and eighty-five, in the town of Rivera, in the diocese of Plasencia in Spain. Bereft of his parents while yet of tender age, he spent his youth in feeding his uncle's sheep, while his soul meanwhile was refreshed by meditation on the mysteries of the most holy Rosary. Having afterwards left his country, and travelled hither and thither in South America for two years to gain wealth, he left all things, and at Lima, in the convent of St. Mary Magdalen of the Order of Preachers, put on the habit of the lay brothers. Most sparing of sleep, given to fasting and haircloth, he served on bended knees the wretched, the sick and the poor, of whom he fed two hundred a day. At length, in the sixty-first year of his age, he passed to heaven. Gregory the Sixteenth enrolled him in the calendar of the Blessed.
ioannesexcompatrisnomineutiferturmassias.la: Joánnes, ex compátris nómine, uti fertur, Massias dictus, anno millésimo quingentésimo octogésimo quinto, in oppido Rivéra, Placentinæ diœcésis in Hispánia, ortum hábuit. Paréntibus ténera adhuc ætate orbátus, in óvibus pátrui pascéndis adolescentiam perégit, dum ánima ínterim in meditatióne mysteriórum sacratissimi Rosárii reficiebátur. Cum pátriam póstea reliquisset, atque huc illuc in América meridionáli per duos annos comparándis ópibus discurrisset, ómnia relínquens, Limæ, in convéntu sanctæ Maríæ Magdalénæ órdinis Prædicatórum, hábitum conversórum induit. Somni parcíssimus, jeiúniis ciliciisque déditus, miseris, ægrótis ac paupéribus, quorum bis centum in die alébat, flexis génibus inserviébat. Demum, ætátis suæ anno sexagésimo primo, in cælum migrávit. Quem beatórum fastis Gregórius décimus sextus adscripsit.

deusquibeatumfranciscumconfessoremtuumsu.en: O God, who didst make blessed Francis thy Confessor, filled with the sweetness of heavenly charity, an excellent herald of thy word: grant by his intercession that, kindled with the fire of thy love, we may ever live in thy love.
deusquibeatumfranciscumconfessoremtuumsu.la: Deus, qui beátum Franciscum Confessórem tuum, supérnæ caritatis dulcedine perfúsus, verbi tui præcónem exímium effecísti: ejus intercessióne concéde ut, igne tui amóris incénsi, in tua dilectióne semper vivámus.

inillotemporeviditiesushominemsedentemin.en: At that time, Jesus saw a man, named Matthew, sitting at the receipt of custom; and he saith unto him: Follow me. And so on.
inillotemporeviditiesushominemsedentemin.la: In illo témpore: Vidit Jesus hóminem sedéntem in telónio, Matthǽum nómine, et ait illi: Séquere me. Et réliqua.

hominmatthpostinit.en: Homily 31 on Matthew, after the beginning.

nonestabsregrandemevangelistephilosophia.en: It is not without reason that we admire the great wisdom of the Evangelist, who concealed not his former life, and set down his own name, which the others had hidden under a changed appellation. But why did he say that he was sitting at the receipt of custom? He wished to show the power of him that called, who, before any end was yet put to the wicked conversation of the publicans, drew him out from the midst of a sea of evils: even as he brought back blessed Paul also, raging and burning with all fury and bringing fire upon the Church.
nonestabsregrandemevangelistephilosophia.la: Non est abs re grandem Evangelistæ philosophiam admirári, qui anteáctam vitam suam non celávit, et nomen suum adscrípsit, quod álii mutáta appellatióne occultáverant. Sed cur dixit in telónio sedisse? Virtútem vocántis vóluit osténdere, qui, non impósito adhuc fine pravæ publicanórum conversatióni, e medio malórum pélago ipsum abstráxit: sicut beátum Paulum quoque, furéntem ac omni rábie ardéntem et ignem Ecclésiæ inferéntem, redúxit.

publicanorumautemstudietexercitatioimpud.en: Now the pursuits and practice of the publicans are full of shamelessness and cruelty: a gain that is a mark of meanness, a base sort of trade, nay rather a robbery allowed by the law of the world: of all which the Lord was not ashamed, when he made a publican his friend. Nor is it any wonder, since he was not ashamed even of a harlot, whom he not only snatched from fornication, but also suffered to kiss his feet. For he came not only to heal bodies, but also much more to bestow health upon sick souls.
publicanorumautemstudietexercitatioimpud.la: Publicanórum autem stúdia et exercitatio impudéntiæ ac crudelitátis plena sunt: quæstus nota illiberalitátis, turpis quædam mercatúra, immo rapina lege sæculári concéssa: quæ ómnia non erúbuit Dóminus, si sibi amicum fecit publicánum. Nec mirum, quando nec meretricem erúbuit, quam non a fornicatióne solum erípuit, verum étiam pedes osculári permisit. Venit enim, non ut córpora solum curáret, verum étiam multo magis, ut ægrótis ánimis incolumitatem præstáret.

quodplanuminparalyticofecitcuiuscumpecca.en: This he plainly did in the case of the paralytic, whose sins when he had forgiven, then he came to Matthew, lest they should be troubled if they saw a publican placed in the company of the disciples. For he who can loose the bonds of sins, why is it a wonder if he made a sinner an Apostle? Thou hast seen the power of him that called: learn now the obedience of him that was called. For he resisted not, neither did he say within himself in doubt, Thinkest thou that he hath rightly and without guile called me, a publican and a sinner? For humility of this kind is not praiseworthy: but forthwith he so obeyed, that he went not even to his house to share the matter with his own.
quodplanuminparalyticofecitcuiuscumpecca.la: Quod planum in paralýtico fecit, cujus cum peccáta dimiserit, tunc ad Matthæum accéssit, ne turbarentur, si publicánum vidérent in discipulorum consórtio collocátum. Nam qui potest delictórum dissolvere vincta, cur mirum est si peccatórem Apóstolum fecit? Vidísti virtútem vocántis: disce nunc vocáti obediéntiam. Non enim repugnávit, nec ambigéndo secum dixit, Putásne publicánum peccatórémque me recte absque fraude vocáverit? Non est enim hujuscémodi humilitas laudábilis: sed conféstim ita obtemperávit, ut nec domum quidem ad comunicándam rem cum suis proféctus sit.

datestpotestasarchangelomichelisuperanim.en: Power was given to the Archangel Michael over the souls of the saints.
datestpotestasarchangelomichelisuperanim.la: Data est potéstas Archángelo Michaéli super ánimas sanctórum.

nisiefficiaminisicutparvulinonintrabitis.en: Unless you become as little children, you shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven. The Apostles are not commanded to have the age of little children, but their innocence: and that what these possess by their years, they may possess by their endeavour: that they may be little ones in malice, not in wisdom. Whosoever therefore shall humble himself as this little child, he is the greater in the kingdom of heaven. As this little child (whom I give you for an example) persevereth not in anger, remembereth not when he is hurt, is not delighted at seeing a beautiful woman, thinketh not one thing and speaketh another: so ye also, unless ye have such innocence and purity of mind, shall not be able to enter the kingdom of heaven.
nisiefficiaminisicutparvulinonintrabitis.la: Nisi efficiámini sicut párvuli, non intrábitis in regnum cælorum. Non præcipitur Apóstolis ut ætatem hábeant parvulorum, sed ut innocéntiam: et quod illi per annos possident, hi possideant per indústriam: ut malitia, non sapiéntia, párvuli sint. Quicumque ergo humiliáverit se sicut párvulus iste, hic est maior in regno cælorum. Sicut iste párvulus (cujus vobis exémplum tríbuo) non persevérat in iracúndia, non læsus méminit, non videns pulchram mulierem delectátur, non áliud cogitat et áliud loquitur: sic et vos, nisi talem habueritis innocéntiam et ánimi puritatem, non potéritis regnum cælorum intráre.

murotuoinexpugnabilituecustodinosangeled.en: Guard us with thine unconquerable wall, O Angel of God.
murotuoinexpugnabilituecustodinosangeled.la: Muro tuo inexpugnábili tuæ custódi nos, Angele Dei.

etarmistuepotentieprotegenossemper.en: And with the arms of thy might protect us always.
etarmistuepotentieprotegenossemper.la: Et armis tuæ poténtiæ prótege nos semper.

sedestuadeusinseculumseculi.en: Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever.
sedestuadeusinseculumseculi.la: Sedes tua, Deus, in sǽculum séculi.

virgadirectionisvirgaregnitui.en: The sceptre of thy kingdom is a sceptre of uprightness.

oratepronobisomnessanctidei.en: Pray for us, all ye Saints of God.
oratepronobisomnessanctidei.la: Oráte pro nobis, omnes Sancti Dei.

utdignieficiamurpromissionibuschristi.en: That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.

inconceptionetuaimmaculatadeigenetrixvir.en: In thy Conception, O immaculate Virgin Mother of God.
inconceptionetuaimmaculatadeigenetrixvir.la: In Conceptione tua, immaculáta, Dei Génetrix Virgo.

proptersionnontacebetpropterierusalemnon.en: For Sion's sake I will not hold my peace, and for the sake of Jerusalem, I will not rest till her just one come forth as brightness, and her saviour be lighted as a lamp.
proptersionnontacebetpropterierusalemnon.la: Propter Sion non tacébo, et propter Jerúsalem non quiéscam, donec egrediátur ut splendor justus ejus, et salvátor ejus ut lampas accendátur.

etvidebuntgentesiustumtuumetcunctiregesi.en: And the Gentiles shall see thy just one, and all kings thy glorious one: and thou shalt be called by a new name, which the mouth of the Lord shall name.
etvidebuntgentesiustumtuumetcunctiregesi.la: Et vidébunt gentes justum tuum, et cuncti reges ínclytum tuum: et vocábitur tibi nomen novum, quod os Dómini nominábit.

nonvocaberisultraderelictetterratuanonvo.en: Thou shalt no more be called Forsaken: and thy land shall no more be called Desolate: but thou shalt be called My pleasure in her, and thy land Inhabited.
nonvocaberisultraderelictetterratuanonvo.la: Non vocáberis ultra Derelícta: et terra tua non vocábitur ámplius Desoláta: sed vocáberis, Volúntas mea in ea, et terra tua Inhabitáta.

populusquiambulabatintenebrisviditlucemm.en: The people that walked in darkness, have seen a great light: to them that dwelt in the region of the shadow of death, light is risen.
populusquiambulabatintenebrisviditlucemm.la: Pópulus, qui ambulábat in ténebris, vidit lucem magnam: habitántibus in regióne umbræ mortis, lux orta est eis.

iudeetierusalemnolitetimere.en: O Judea and Jerusalem, fear not:

etdominuseritvobiscum.en: And the Lord will be with you.

veniredemptorgentium.en: Come, thou Redeemer of the nations,

nonexvirilisemine.en: Not of the seed of man,

verbumdeifactumestcaro.en: The Word of God was made flesh

fructusqueventrisfloruit.en: And the fruit of the womb hath flowered.

vexillavirtutummicant.en: The banners of the virtues glitter,

procedatethalamosuo.en: Let him come forth from his bridal chamber,

alacrisutcurratviam.en: That he may run his way with eager speed.

equaliseternopatri.en: Thou who art equal to the eternal Father,

carnistropeocingere.en: Gird thee with the trophy of the flesh,

lumenquenoxspiratnovum.en: And the night breatheth forth a new light,

fidequeiugiluceat.en: And which may shine with unceasing faith.

verbumenimdeideusfiliusdeipropterliberan.en: For the Word of God, God the Son of God, was made man in order to deliver man from eternal death. And he joined both natures together in so close a bond, that neither did the glorification consume the lower, nor the assumption lessen the higher.
verbumenimdeideusfiliusdeipropterliberan.la: Verbum enim Dei, Deus Fílius Dei, propter liberándum hóminem ab ætérna morte, factus est homo. Et tanto fædere utrámque natúram conséruit, ut nec inferiórem consumeret glorificátio, nec superiórem minúeret assúmptio.

salvaigiturutriusqueproprietatesubstanti.en: The property of each substance therefore being preserved, and both coming together into one person, lowliness is taken up by majesty, weakness by power, mortality by eternity: that, as befitted our healing, one and the same Mediator of God and men might both die by the one, and rise again by the other. For unless he were true God, he would not bring the remedy; unless he were true man, he would not give the example. At the birth of the Lord, Glory to God in the highest is sung by the exulting Angels. How much then ought the lowliness of men to rejoice at this unspeakable work of mercy, when the sublimity of the Angels so greatly rejoiceth?
salvaigiturutriusqueproprietatesubstanti.la: Salva igitur utriúsque proprietáte substántiæ, et in unam coëúnte persónam, suscipitur a maiestáte humilitas, a virtúte infirmitas, ab æternitáte mortálitas: ut quod nostris remédiis congruébat, unus atque idem Dei et hóminum mediátor, et mori ex uno, et resúrgere posset ex áltero. Nisi enim esset verus Deus, non afférret remédium; nisi verus esset homo, non præbéret exémplum. Ab exsultántibus Angelis, nascénte Dómino, Glória in excélsis Deo, cánitur. De hoc ergo inenarrábili pietátis ópere quantum lætári debet humilitas hóminum, cum tantum gaudeat sublimitas Angelórum?

cummattheusabherodelucasatiberiocesarema.en: Whereas Matthew beginneth from Herod, Luke from Tiberius Caesar, Mark from the baptism of John, John, passing over all these, ascendeth above all time and age. But thou, dearly beloved, when thou hearest the Word in this place, do not, I pray thee, agree with them that say that it is a word that is uttered by the mouth. For this Word is a substance in a person, proceeding from the Father himself without passion. And as, In the beginning was the Word, signifieth eternity: so, The same was in the beginning with God, showeth us coeternity. For never was the Father alone without the Word: but always God was with God, and that indeed in his own person.
cummattheusabherodelucasatiberiocesarema.la: Cum Matthæus ab Heróde, Lucas a Tibério Cæsare, Marcus a baptísmate Joánnis exordiátur, his ómnibus Joánnes omissis, supra omne tempus et sæculum ascéndit. Tu autem, dilectíssime, cum Verbum hoc in loco audis, noli, quæso, iis acquiéscere, qui dicunt id verbum esse quod ore profértur. Hoc enim Verbum substantia quædam est in persóna, ex ipso Patre sine passióne provéniens. Quemadmodum autem, In princípio erat Verbum, æternitátem significat: ita, Hoc erat in princípio apud Deum, coæternitatem nobis ostendit. Numquam enim solus Pater sine Verbo fuit: sed semper Deus apud Deum erat, et in persóna quidem própria.

posteadiciturevanegliumlibergenerationis.en: Then is said the Gospel, The book of the generation

ipseinvocabitmealleluiaalleluia.en: He shall cry unto me, * Alleluia, alleluia.

beatusstephanusiugilegisdeimeditationero.en: Blessed Stephen, strengthened by continual meditation on the law of God, like a fruitful tree planted near the running of the waters of salvation, was the first to give the fruit of martyrdom in his season.
beatusstephanusiugilegisdeimeditationero.la: Beátus Stéphanus jugi legis Dei meditatióne roborátus, tamquam lignum fructiferum secus salutárium aquárum plantátum decúrsus, fructum martýrii in témpore suo dedit primus. Ps. 1

constitutusadeopredicatorpreceptorumeius.en: Appointed by God a preacher of his commandments, he strove to serve him in holy fear: and having faithfully fulfilled his office, he was worthy to ascend into his holy mountain.
constitutusadeopredicatorpreceptorumeius.la: Constitútus a Deo prædicátor præceptórum ejus, in timóre sancto illi servíre stúduit: officióque fidéliter perácto, in montem sanctum ejus ascéndere dignus fuit. Ps. 2

intribulationelapidumseprementiumpositus.en: Set in the tribulation of the stones that pressed upon him, he feared not the thousands of the people that surrounded him: for he saw Jesus, his protector, standing up in heaven to save him.
intribulationelapidumseprementiumpositus.la: In tribulatióne lápidum se preméntium pósitus, míllia pópuli se circumdántis non tímuit: quia susceptórem suum Jesum, ut eum salvum fáceret, exsúrgere in cælo vidit. Ps. 3

luminevultustuidomineinsignitusprotomart.en: Marked with the light of thy countenance, O Lord, Stephen the Protomartyr offered himself to thee as a sacrifice of justice: and therefore in gladness of heart, sleeping in peace, he resteth.
luminevultustuidomineinsignitusprotomart.la: Lúmine vultus tui, Dómine, insignitus Protomártyr Stéphanus, sacrifícium justitiæ seípsum tibi sacrificávit: ideóque in lætitia cordis, in pace obdórmiens requiéscit. Ps. 4

benedictionistuedominemunereiustificatus.en: Justified by the gift of thy blessing, O Lord, and defended in his passion by the shield of thy protection, Stephen merited to receive from thee the crown of his name.
benedictionistuedominemunereiustificatus.la: Benedictiónis tuæ, Dómine, múnere justificátus et scuto tuæ protectiónis in passióne munítus, nóminis sui corónam Stéphanus a te percipere méruit. Ps. 5

oquamadmirabileestnomentuumdominedeusnos.en: O how admirable is thy name, O Lord our God, for which blessed Stephen suffered, and was crowned by thee with glory and honour, and exalted above the heavens by the gift of thy magnificence!
oquamadmirabileestnomentuumdominedeusnos.la: O quam admirábile est nomen tuum, Dómine Deus noster, pro quo beátus Stéphanus passus, glória et honóre a te est coronátus, et super cælos dono tuæ magnífícéntiæ exaltátus! Ps. 8

indominodeosuoconfisusfortisathletasteph.en: Trusting in the Lord his God, Stephen, the strong champion, bravely endured the blows of the stones: and therefore he passed victorious to the mountain of the virtues.
indominodeosuoconfisusfortisathletasteph.la: In Dómino Deo suo confísus fortis athléta Stéphanus, lápidum fórtiter sustínuit ictus: et idcírco ad montem virtútum transmigrávit victoriósus. Ps. 10

sinemaculabeatusstephanusingressusestdom.en: Without spot blessed Stephen entered, O Lord, into thy tabernacle: and because he wrought justice, he resteth in thy holy mountain.
sinemaculabeatusstephanusingressusestdom.la: Sine mácula beátus Stéphanus ingréssus est, Dómine, in tabernáculum tuum: et, quia operátus est justítiam, requiéscit in monte sancto tuo. Ps. 14

dominevirtusetletitiarectorumquoniamtupr.en: O Lord, the strength and gladness of the upright: since thou didst prevent Stephen, beloved of thee, with the gift of free blessing, he first followed thee by the death of a glorious passion: wherefore with the crown of martyrdom thou gavest him life for ever and ever.
dominevirtusetletitiarectorumquoniamtupr.la: Dómine, virtus et lætítia rectórum: quóniam tu prævenísti diléctum tibi Stéphanum dono gratúitæ benedictiónis, te primum secútus est morte gloriósæ passiónis: unde cum coróna martýrii dedísti ei vitam in sæculum sæculi. Ps. 20

cumessetplenusspiritusanctobeatusstephan.en: When blessed Stephen was full of the Holy Ghost.
cumessetplenusspiritusanctobeatusstephan.la: Cum esset plenus Spíritu Sancto beátus Stéphanus.

stephanusservusdeiquemlapidabantiudeivid.en: Stephen, the servant of God, who was stoned by the Jews, saw the heavens opened: he saw and entered in.
stephanusservusdeiquemlapidabantiudeivid.la: Stéphanus servus Dei, quem lapidábant Judæi, vidit cælos apértos: vidit et introívit:

beatushomocuicelipatebant.en: Blessed is he, unto whom the heavens were opened.

cumigitursaxorumcrepitantiumturbinequate.en: When therefore he was shaken by the storm of crashing stones, amid the heavenly recesses of the court above the divine brightness shone upon him.
cumigitursaxorumcrepitantiumturbinequate.la: Cum igitur saxórum crepitántium túrbine quaterétur, inter æthéreos aulæ cæléstis sinus divína ei cláritas fulsit.

prodevototibinunccollegio.en: For the company now devoted to thee.

cumessetstephanusplenusspiritusanctointe.en: Stephen, being full of the Holy Ghost, looking up steadfastly to heaven, saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing on the right hand of God.
cumessetstephanusplenusspiritusanctointe.la: Cum esset Stéphanus plenus Spíritu Sancto, inténdens in cælum, vidit glóriam Dei, et Jesum stantem a dextris Dei.

positisautemgenibusbeatusstephanusclamav.en: And blessed Stephen, falling on his knees, cried with a loud voice, saying: Lord, lay not this sin to their charge.
positisautemgenibusbeatusstephanusclamav.la: Pósitis autem génibus, beátus Stéphanus clamávit voce magna, dicens: Dómine, ne státuas illis hoc peccátum.

oquamgloriosusestbeatusstephanusmartyret.en: O how glorious is blessed Stephen, Martyr and Levite, who before the Apostles merited to possess the heavenly kingdom and to see the Son at the right hand of the Father!
oquamgloriosusestbeatusstephanusmartyret.la: O quam gloriósus est beátus Stéphanus Martyr et Levíta, qui ante Apóstolos regna cæléstia possidére méruit et ad Patris déxteram Fílium vidére!

ioannesapostolusetevangelistavirgestelec.en: John, Apostle and Evangelist, a virgin, was chosen by the Lord, and was more beloved than the rest.
ioannesapostolusetevangelistavirgestelec.la: Joánnes, Apóstolus et Evangelísta, virgo est eléctus a Dómino, atque inter céteros magis diléctus. Ps. 18

suprapectusdominiiesurecumbensevangeliif.en: Leaning on the breast of the Lord Jesus, he drank the streams of the Gospel from the very sacred fountain of the Lord's breast.
suprapectusdominiiesurecumbensevangeliif.la: Supra pectus Dómini Jesu recúmbens, Evangélii fluénta de ipso sacro Domínici péctoris fonte potávit. Ps. 33

quasiunusdeparadisifluminibusevangelista.en: As one of the rivers of paradise, John the Evangelist poured forth the grace of the word of God over the whole circle of the earth.
quasiunusdeparadisifluminibusevangelista.la: Quasi unus de paradísi flumínibus, Evangelista Joánnes verbi Dei grátiam in toto terrárum orbe diffúdit. Ps. 44

inferventisoleidoliummissusioannesaposto.en: John the Apostle, cast into a vessel of boiling oil, came forth unharmed, the grace of God protecting him.
inferventisoleidoliummissusioannesaposto.la: In fervéntis ólei dólium missus Joánnes Apóstolus, divína se protegénte grátia, illæsus exívit. Ps. 46

propterinsuperabilemevangelizandiconstan.en: Banished into exile for his unconquerable constancy in preaching the Gospel, he merited to be relieved by the frequent consolation of divine vision and converse.
propterinsuperabilemevangelizandiconstan.la: Propter insuperábilem evangelizándi constántiam exsílio relegátus, divinæ visiónis et allocutiónis méruit crebra consolatióne relevári. Ps. 60

occurritbeatoioanniabexsiliorevertentiom.en: All the people, both men and women, went out to meet blessed John as he returned from exile, crying out and saying: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord.
occurritbeatoioanniabexsiliorevertentiom.la: Occúrrit beáto Joánni, ab exsílio reverténti, omnis pópulus virórum ac mulierum, clamántium et dicéntium: Benedíctus qui venit in nómine Dómini. Ps. 63

apparuitcarosuoioannidominusiesuschristu.en: The Lord Jesus Christ appeared with his disciples to John, his beloved, and said to him: Come to me, my beloved, for it is time that thou feast at my banquet with thy brethren.
apparuitcarosuoioannidominusiesuschristu.la: Appáruit caro suo Joánni Dóminus Jesus Christus cum discípulis suis et ait illi: Veni, dilécte mi, ad me, quia tempus est ut epuléris in convívio meo cum frátribus tuis. Ps. 74

expandensmanussuasaddeumdixitinvitatusad.en: Spreading forth his hands to God he said: Bidden to thy banquet I come, giving thanks, for thou hast vouchsafed, O Lord Jesus Christ, to invite me to thy feast: knowing that with all my heart I desired thee.
expandensmanussuasaddeumdixitinvitatusad.la: Expándens manus suas ad Deum dixit: Invitátus ad convivium tuum vénio, grátias agens, quia me dignátus es, Dómine Jesu Christe, ad tuas épulas invitáre: sciens quod ex toto corde meo desiderábam te. Ps. 96

siceumvolomaneredonecveniamtumesequere.en: So I will have him remain till I come: follow thou me.
siceumvolomaneredonecveniamtumesequere.la: Sic eum volo manére, donec véniam: tu me séquere.

inmediecclesieaperuitoseiusetimpleviteum.en: In the midst of the church he opened his mouth, and the Lord filled him with the spirit of wisdom and understanding, and clothed him with a robe of glory, alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.
inmediecclesieaperuitoseiusetimpleviteum.la: In médio ecclésiæ apéruit os ejus et implévit eum Dóminus spiritu sapiéntiæ et intelléctus, stoláque glóriæ induit eum, allelúja, allelúja, allelúja.

veniteadoremusregemregumquibeatismartyri.en: Come, let us adore the King of kings, * Who hath given the crown of glory to the blessed Martyrs.
veniteadoremusregemregumquibeatismartyri.la: Veníte, adorémus Regem regum, * Qui beátis Martýribus corónam dedit glóriæ.

novitdominusviasinnocentiumquinonsteteru.en: The Lord knoweth the ways of the Innocents, who have not stood in the ways of sinners.
novitdominusviasinnocentiumquinonsteteru.la: Novit Dóminus vias Innocéntium, qui non stetérunt in viis peccatórum. Ps. 1

rexterreinfremuitadversuschristumquiarex.en: The king of the earth raged against Christ: because the King appointed in Sion reigneth over thousands of Innocents.
rexterreinfremuitadversuschristumquiarex.la: Rex terræ infrémuit advérsus Christum: quia Rex in Sion constitútus super Innocentium millia regnat. Ps. 2

deusiudexiustusiuidicanossecunduminnocen.en: O God, just judge, judge us according to our innocence.
deusiudexiustusiuidicanossecunduminnocen.la: Deus iudex iustus, iúídica nos secúndum innocéntiam nostram. Ps. 7

exoreinfantiumdeusetlactentiumlaudeperfe.en: Out of the mouth of infants and of sucklings, O God, by perfect praise thou destroyest the enemy.
exoreinfantiumdeusetlactentiumlaudeperfe.la: Ex ore infántium, Deus, et lacténtium laude perfécta déstruis inimícum. Ps. 8

iudicabitdominuspupillumetviduametpluets.en: The Lord shall judge the fatherless and the widow, and he shall rain snares of fire upon sinners.
iudicabitdominuspupillumetviduametpluets.la: Iudicábit Dóminus pupillum et víduam, et pluet super peccatóres láqueos ignis. Ps. 10

mortisusurasreximpiusexegitsuperinnocent.en: The wicked king exacted the usury of death from the Innocents: but they rest in the holy mountain of God: the malignant is brought to nothing.
mortisusurasreximpiusexegitsuperinnocent.la: Mortis usúras rex ímpius exégit super Innocéntes: sed illi requiéscunt in monte sancto Dei: malígnus ad níhilum est dedúctus. Ps. 14

quisascendetautquisstabitinlocosanctodei.en: Who shall ascend, or who shall stand in the holy place of God? The innocent in hands and clean of heart.
quisascendetautquisstabitinlocosanctodei.la: Quis ascéndet aut quis stabit in loco sancto Dei? Innocens mánibus et mundo corde. Ps. 23

innocentesadheseruntmihiquorumpedesavuls.en: The innocent have adhered to me, whose feet have been plucked out of the snare of death.
innocentesadheseruntmihiquorumpedesavuls.la: Innocéntes adhæsérunt mihi, quorum pedes avúlsi sunt a láqueo mortis. Ps. 24

filioregisdatumestiudiciumutsalvetinnoce.en: To the king's son judgment is given, that he may save the innocent children of the poor: and he shall humble Herod the oppressor.
filioregisdatumestiudiciumutsalvetinnoce.la: Filio regis datum est iudícium, ut salvet innocéntes fílios páuperum: et humiliábit Heródem calumniatórem. Ps. 71

etdatesuntillissingulestolealbeetdictume.en: And white robes were given to every one of them; and it was said to them.
etdatesuntillissingulestolealbeetdictume.la: Et datæ sunt illis singulæ stolæ albæ: et dictum est illis.

idemsermdesanct.en: The same, Sermon 9 on the Saints.

quambeataetasquenecdumchristumpotestloqu.en: How blessed an age, which cannot yet speak of Christ, and is already worthy to be slain for Christ! Not yet ripe for a wound, and already fit for suffering! How happily born, whom eternal life cometh to meet on the very threshold of birth! They incur indeed, amid the very beginnings of the light they have received, the peril and the end of their safety: but from that very end they straightway take the beginnings of eternity. They seem indeed untimely for death: but happily they die unto life.
quambeataetasquenecdumchristumpotestloqu.la: Quam beáta ætas, quæ necdum Christum potest loqui et iam pro Christo merétur occidi! Nondum opportúna vúlneri et iam idónea passióni! Quam feliciter nati, quibus in primo nascéndi limine, ætérna vita óbviam venit! Incurrunt quidem, inter ipsa primórdia accéptæ lucis, perículum et finem salútis: sed de ipso prótinus fine cápiunt princípia æternitátis. Immatúri quidem vidéntur ad mortem: sed felíciter moriúntur ad vitam.

christosacravitvictimas.en: Hath hallowed as victims to Christ.

etegodisponovobissicutdisposuitmihipater.en: And I dispose to you, as my Father hath disposed to me, a kingdom, that you may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom.
etegodisponovobissicutdisposuitmihipater.la: Et ego dispóno vobis, sicut dispósuit mihi Pater meus regnum, ut edátis, et bibátis super mensam meam in regno meo.

luxortestiustorectiscordeletitia.en: Light is risen * to the just, and joy to the right of heart.
luxortestiustorectiscordeletitia.la: Lux orta est * justo, rectis corde lætítia. Ps. 74

inregenerationecumsederitfiliushominisin.en: In the regeneration, when the Son of man shall sit on the seat of his majesty, you also shall sit, judging the twelve tribes of Israel, saith the Lord.
inregenerationecumsederitfiliushominisin.la: In regeneratióne, cum séderit Fílius hóminis in sede majestátis suæ, sedébitis et vos, judicántes duódecim tribus Israël, dicit Dóminus.

ecceegoioannesvidiostiumapertuminceletec.en: Behold, I John saw a door opened in heaven, and behold, there was a throne set therein, and in the midst of the throne and round about it four living creatures, full of eyes before and behind: and they gave glory, and honour, and benediction to him that sitteth on the throne, who liveth for ever and ever.
ecceegoioannesvidiostiumapertuminceletec.la: Ecce ego Joánnes vidi óstium apértum in cælo, et ecce sedes pósita erat in eo, et in médio sedis et in circúitu ejus quátuor animália plena óculis ante et retro: et dabant glóriam et honórem et benedictiónem sedénti super thronum, vivénti in sæcula sæculórum.

regemevangelistarumdominumveniteadoremus.en: The Lord, the King of the Evangelists, * Come, let us adore.

quitimetdeumfacietbonetquicontinensestiu.en: He that feareth God, will do good: and he that possesseth justice, shall lay hold on her, and she will meet him as an honourable mother.
quitimetdeumfacietbonetquicontinensestiu.la: Qui timet Deum, fáciet bona: et qui cóntinens est justítiæ, apprehéndet illam, et obviábit illi quasi mater honorificáta.

inmedietincircuitusedisdeiquatuoranimali.en: In the midst and round about the throne of God are four living creatures, each having six wings, full of eyes round about, and they cease not day and night, saying: Holy, Holy, Holy, Lord God Almighty, who was, and who is, and who is to come.
inmedietincircuitusedisdeiquatuoranimali.la: In médio et in circúitu sedis Dei quátuor animália senas alas habéntia, óculis úndique plena, non cessant nocte ac die dicere: Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus Dóminus Deus omnipotens, qui erat, et qui est, et qui ventúrus est.

cibavitillumpaneviteetintellectusetaquas.en: The Lord our God fed him with the bread of life and understanding, and gave him the water of wholesome wisdom to drink.
cibavitillumpaneviteetintellectusetaquas.la: Cibávit illum pane vitæ et intelléctus, et aqua sapiéntiæ salutáris potávit illum Dóminus, Deus noster.

inmediecclesieaperuitoseiusetimplevitill.en: In the midst of the Church he opened his mouth, and the Lord filled him with the spirit of wisdom and understanding, and clothed him with a robe of glory.
