inmediecclesieaperuitoseiusetimplevitill.la: In médio Ecclésiæ apéruit os ejus, et implévit illum Dóminus spíritu sapiéntiæ et intelléctus, et stolam glóriæ índuit eum.

tuasunthecchristeoperaquisanctostuositag.en: These are thy works, O Christ, who dost so glorify thy Saints, that even by the grace of their dignity thou makest miracles go before that are to come in them: thou didst foreshow the illustrious preachers of the Gospel by the wonderful figure of the heavenly living creatures: for thou didst vouchsafe to show by glorious signs the heavenly office conferred upon them: hence let praise, hence let glory resound to thee for ever.
tuasunthecchristeoperaquisanctostuositag.la: Tua sunt hæc, Christe, ópera, qui Sanctos tuos ita gloríficas, ut étiam dignitátis grátia in eis futúræ præíre mirácula fácias: tu insignes Evangélii prædicatóres animálium cæléstium admirábili figúra præsignásti: his namque cæléste munus collátum gloriósis indíciis es dignátus osténdere: hinc laus, hinc glória tibi résonet in sæcula.

gloriosusdeiamicusniesudominiconfessione.en: The glorious friend of God, N., grounded in the confession of the Lord Jesus, stood undaunted amid the punishments of torments:
gloriosusdeiamicusniesudominiconfessione.la: Gloriósus Dei amicus N., Jesu Dómini confessióne fundátus, inter tormentórum supplícia stetit impertérritus:

acdemumtriumphalimorteinsigniscelospetiv.en: And at length, made illustrious by a triumphant death, crowned with laurel by his blood, he made his way to heaven.
acdemumtriumphalimorteinsigniscelospetiv.la: Ac demum, triumpháli morte insígnis, Cælos petívit sánguine laureátus.

felicicommercioproterreniscelestiaproper.en: By a happy exchange, changing earthly things for heavenly, things perishable for eternal.
felicicommercioproterreniscelestiaproper.la: Felíci commércio, pro terrénis cæléstia, pro peritúris ætérna commútans.

celospetivitsanguinelaureatus.en: Crowned with laurel by his blood, he made his way to heaven.

leteturecclesiatuadeusbeatinmartyristuic.en: Let thy Church rejoice, O God, trusting in the suffrages of blessed N. thy Martyr: and by his glorious prayers may she remain devout and stand secure.
leteturecclesiatuadeusbeatinmartyristuic.la: Lætétur Ecclésia tua, Deus, beáti N. Mártyris tui confísa suffrágiis: atque, ejus précibus gloriósis, et devóta permáneat et secúra consístat.

regemsempiternumveniteadoremusquimartyre.en: Come, let us adore the everlasting King, * Who hath crowned his Martyr in heaven worthily according to his merits.
regemsempiternumveniteadoremusquimartyre.la: Regem sempitérnum veníte adorémus: * Qui Mártyrem suum digne pro méritis coronávit, in cælis.

posuistidominesupercaputeiuscoronamdelap.en: Thou hast set, O Lord, on his head a crown of precious stones: he asked life of thee, and thou hast given it him
posuistidominesupercaputeiuscoronamdelap.la: Posuísti, Dómine, super caput ejus corónam de lápide pretióso: vitam pétiit a te, et tribuísti ei

magnestglorieiusinsalutarituogloriametma.en: His glory is great in thy salvation: glory and great beauty shalt thou lay upon him.
magnestglorieiusinsalutarituogloriametma.la: Magna est glória ejus in salutári tuo: glóriam et magnum decórem impónes super eam.

quoniamelevatestmagnificentiatuasupercel.en: For thy magnificence is elevated above the heavens.
quoniamelevatestmagnificentiatuasupercel.la: Quóniam eleváta est magnificéntia tua, super cælos.

facileesthonoremmartyriscelebraremagnume.en: It is easy to celebrate the honour of a Martyr: it is a great thing to imitate the faith and patience of a Martyr. Let us so do the latter, that we may desire the former: let us so celebrate the former, that we may rather love the latter. What shall we praise in the faith of the Martyr? That he strove even unto death for the truth, and therefore he conquered. He despised the world when it flattered him, he yielded not to it when it raged: therefore he came as conqueror unto God.
facileesthonoremmartyriscelebraremagnume.la: Fácile est honórem Mártyris celebráre: magnum est fidem atque patiéntiam Mártyris imitári. Hoc sic agámus, ut illud optémus: illud sic celebrémus, ut hoc pótius diligámus. Quid laudémus in fide Mártyris? Quia usque ad mortem certávit pro veritáte, et ídeo vicit. Blandiéntem mundum contémpsit, sæviénti non cessit: ideo victor ad Deum accéssit.

beatusvirquisufferttentationemquoniamcum.en: Blessed is the man that endureth temptation; for when he hath been proved, he shall receive a crown of life,
beatusvirquisufferttentationemquoniamcum.la: Beátus vir qui suffert tentatiónem, quóniam, cum probátus fúerit, accípiet corónam vitæ,

quamrepromisitdeusdiligentibusse.en: Which God hath promised to them that love him.

hicaccipietbenedictionemadominetmiserico.en: He shall receive a blessing from the Lord, and mercy.
hicaccipietbenedictionemadominetmiserico.la: Hic accipiet benedictiónem a Dómino et misericórdiam.

abundantinistoseculerroresetterroresbeat.en: Errors and terrors abound in this world: the most blessed Martyr overcame errors by wisdom, terrors by patience. Great is that which he did: following the Lamb, he overcame the lion. When the persecutor raged, the lion roared: but because the Lamb was looked to on high, who by death destroyed death, hung on the tree, shed his blood, redeemed the world: the lion was trodden down beneath.
abundantinistoseculerroresetterroresbeat.la: Abundant in isto sæculo erróres et terróres: beatíssimus Martyr erróres sapiéntia, terróres patiéntia superávit. Magnum est, quod fecit: secútus Agnum, leónem vicit. Quando persecútor sæviébat, leo fremébat: sed, quia Agnus sursum attendebátur, qui morte mortem destrúxit, ligno pepéndit, sánguinem fudit, redémit mundum: leo deórsum calcabátur.

domineprevenistieuminbenedictionibusdulc.en: O Lord, thou hast prevented him with blessings of sweetness: thou hast set on his head
domineprevenistieuminbenedictionibusdulc.la: Dómine, prævenísti eum in benedictiónibus dulcédinis: posuísti in cápite ejus

beatushicmartyrduminexpugnabilifirmitate.en: This blessed Martyr, while by the unconquerable steadfastness of his combat he overcame the adversary, made a way of conquering for others: a victor not by the short road of wounds, but, the pains clinging to him long and remaining, a conqueror by the marvel of a long struggle. Shut up in the custody of a prison, he was in the stocks and in irons: but while his body was laid in bonds, his spirit remained loosed and free. His flesh wasted away with long hunger and thirst: but his soul, living by faith and virtue, God fed with spiritual nourishment.
beatushicmartyrduminexpugnabilifirmitate.la: Beátus hic Martyr, dum inexpugnabili firmitáte certaminis sui adversárium vicit, vincéndi céteris viam fecit: non brevi compéndio vúlnerum victor, sed, adhæréntibus diu et permanentibus pœnis, longæ colluctatiónis miráculo triumphátor. Custódia cárceris septus, in nervo ac ferro fuit: sed pósito in vinculis córpore, solútus ac liber spiritus mansit. Caro famis ac sitis diuturnitáte contábuit: sed ánimam fide et virtúte vivéntem nutriméntis spiritálibus Deus pavit.

sedadcelestiaregnapervenit.en: But he hath come to the heavenly kingdom.

custodivitillumabinimicisetaseductoribus.en: She kept him safe from his enemies, and she defended him from seducers, and gave him a strong conflict, that he might overcome.
custodivitillumabinimicisetaseductoribus.la: Custodívit illum ab inimícis, et a seductóribus tutávit illum, et certámen forte dedit illi, ut vínceret.

proiustitiaagonizareproanimatuetusqueadm.en: Strive for justice for thy soul, and even unto death fight for justice.
proiustitiaagonizareproanimatuetusqueadm.la: Pro justítia agonizáre pro ánima tua, et usque ad mortem certa pro justítia.

isteestquiprolegedeisuimortisetradiditno.en: This is he who for the law of his God delivered himself up to death: he doubted not to die: he was slain by the wicked, and he liveth for ever with Christ: he followed the Lamb, and received the palm.
isteestquiprolegedeisuimortisetradiditno.la: Iste est qui pro lege Dei sui morti se trádidit: non dubitávit mori: ab iníquis interféctus est, et in ætérnum vivit cum Christo: Agnum secútus est, et accépit palmam.

quemadmodumquiludicruminstituitagonemsic.en: As he that holdeth a public contest, if he be joined to one of the champions by the bond of friendship, will never crown him unless he have gone down into the contest: who namely desireth that he should labour himself, and the more he loveth him, the more he desireth to see him victorious: so also Christ willeth that those whom he loveth most should be proved not only by his help, but also by themselves. But he maketh his discourse not at all burdensome, for he setteth these things forth not as threats to them alone, but in common to the whole world, saying: If any will, whether man or woman, whether prince or subject, let him enter upon this way.
quemadmodumquiludicruminstituitagonemsic.la: Quemádmodum qui lúdicrum instituit agónem, si cui athletārum amicitiae vínculo iūngitur, numquam eum, nisi descēderit in certāmen, coronābit: qui proprium illius vidēlicet labōrem desīderat, et quo magis eum dīligit, eo magis victōrem vidēre cupit: sic etiam Christus, quos maxime diligit, eos non solum auxilio suo, verum etiam et a seipsis vult comprobāri. Minime autem onerōsam orātiōnem reddit, quia non sibi solis hæc commīnēre, sed commūniter universō terrārum orbi propōnit, dicens: Si quis vult, sive vir, sive mulier, sive princeps, sive subditus, hanc viam ingrediātur.

etsermoquidemunumquidsignificarevideturt.en: And the saying indeed seemeth to signify one thing, but it containeth three: the denial of thyself, and that thou take up the cross, and thirdly that thou follow Christ: of which two are joined together, one is set by itself apart. Let us therefore consider first what it is to deny another: then thou wilt rightly perceive what it is to deny thyself. R. viii. A crown of gold upon his head, wherein was engraved the sign of holiness, a glory of honour * And a work of strength. V. For thou hast prevented him with blessings of sweetness: thou hast set on his head a crown of precious stones. And a work of strength.
etsermoquidemunumquidsignificarevideturt.la: Et sermo quidem unum quid significāre vidētur, tria vero continet: abnegātiōnem tui ipsius, et ut crucem accipias, et tērtio ut Christum sequāris: quōrum duo coniūncta sunt, unum per seipsum separātim pōnitur. Considerémus ígitur prius, quidnam sit álium abnegáre: tunc recte perspícies, quid sit abnegáre téipsum. R. viii. Coróna áurea super caput ejus, éxpressa signo sanctitátis, glória honōris * Et opus fortitūdinis. Y. Quóniam prævenísti eum in benedictionibús dulcédinís: posuísti in cápite ejus corónam de lápide pretiośo. Et opus fortitūdinis.

quidigiturabnegareteipsumquidigitumabneg.en: What then is it to deny thyself? What then is it to deny another? He that hath once denied another, a brother, say, or a servant, or any other whatsoever, if he see him beaten with rods, if he see him bound with chains, whatever other evil he behold him suffer, he runneth not to him, he helpeth him not, he is not moved to pity, nor is he stirred at all in any wise, as one who is wholly estranged from him. So then he willeth that we spare our body in no wise, so that, whether it be beaten, or driven out, or burned, or suffer any other such thing, we spare it not.
quidigiturabnegareteipsumquidigitumabneg.la: Quid ígitur abnegáre teípsum? Quid ígitum abnegáre álium? Qui álium jam abnegávit, fratrem puta, aut servum, aut quemvis álium, si cædi eum virgis vídeat, si arcéri vínculis, quidquid áliud mali pati eum conspéxerit, non occúrrit, non auxiliátur, non fléctitur, nec prorsus ullo modo movétur, ceu ille qui pénitus ab illo alienātus est. Sic ígitur nullo nos pacto córpori nostro pærcere vult, ut neque si cædit, neque si pellit, neque si úritur, nec si quid áliud huiúsmodi pátuit, ei parcámus.

deepistolabeatipauliapostoliadromanos.en: Lesson from the letter of St Paul the Apostle to the Romans
deepistolabeatipauliapostoliadromanos.la: De Epístola beáti Pauli Apóstoli ad Romános

existimenimquodnonsuntcondignepassionesh.en: For I reckon that the sufferings of this time are not worthy to be compared with the glory to come, that shall be revealed in us.
existimenimquodnonsuntcondignepassionesh.la: Exístimo enim quod non sunt condígnæ passiónes hujus témporis ad futúram glóriam, quæ revelábitur in nobis.

namexspectatiocreaturerevelationemfilior.en: For the expectation of the creature waiteth for the revelation of the sons of God
namexspectatiocreaturerevelationemfilior.la: Nam exspectátio creatúræ revelatiónem filiórum Dei exspéctat.

quietipsacreaturaliberabituraservituteco.en: Because the creature also itself shall be delivered from the servitude of corruption, into the liberty of the glory of the children of God.
quietipsacreaturaliberabituraservituteco.la: quia et ipsa creatúra liberábitur a servitúte corruptiónis in libertátem glóriæ filiórum Dei.

speenimsalvifactisumusspesautemquevidetu.en: For we are saved by hope. But hope that is seen, is not hope. For what a man seeth, why doth he hope for?
speenimsalvifactisumusspesautemquevidetu.la: Spe enim salvi facti sumus. Spes autem, quæ vidétur, non est spes: nam quod videt quis, quid sperat?

scimusautemquoniamdiligentibusdeumomniac.en: And we know that to them that love God, all things work together unto good, to such as, according to his purpose, are called to be saints.
scimusautemquoniamdiligentibusdeumomniac.la: Scimus autem quóniam diligéntibus Deum ómnia cooperántur in bonum, iis qui secúndum propósitum vocáti sunt sancti.

tractinioannemsubmedium.en: Treatise 51 on John, about the middle

ipsedominusiesuseratgranummortificandume.en: The Lord Jesus himself was the grain that was to be put to death and to be multiplied; put to death by the unbelief of the Jews, multiplied by the faith of the peoples. And now, exhorting us to follow the footsteps of his passion, He that loveth his life, saith he, shall lose it. Which may be understood in two ways. He that loveth shall lose; that is, if thou lovest, thou shalt lose. If thou desirest to hold life in Christ, fear not death for Christ. Again in another way: He that loveth his life shall lose it; love it not, lest thou lose it; love it not in this life, lest thou lose it in eternal life.
ipsedominusiesuseratgranummortificandume.la: Ipse Dóminus Jesus erat granum mortificándum et multiplicándum; mortificándum infidelitáte Judæórum, multiplicándum fide populórum. Jam vero exhórtans ad passiónis suæ sectánda vestígia, Qui amat, inquit, ánimam suam, perdet eam. Quod duóbus modis intéllegi potest. Qui amat, perdet; id est, si amas, perdes. Si cupis vitam tenére in Christo, noli mortem timére pro Christo. Item álio modo: Qui amat ánimam suam, perdet eam; noli amáre, ne perdas; noli amáre in hac vita, ne perdas in ætérna vita.

adestodominesupplicationibusnostrisutqui.en: Be present, O Lord, at our supplications: that we who know ourselves to be guilty by reason of our iniquity, may be delivered by the intercession of blessed N. thy Martyr.
adestodominesupplicationibusnostrisutqui.la: Adésto, Dómine, supplicatiónibus nostris: ut, qui ex iniquitáte nostra reos nos esse cognóscimus, beáti N. Mártyris tui intercessióne liberémur.

infirmitatemnostramquesumusdominepropiti.en: Look mercifully, we beseech thee, O Lord, upon our infirmity: and turn away all the evils that we justly deserve, by the intercession of thy holy Martyrs and Bishops N. and N.
infirmitatemnostramquesumusdominepropiti.la: Infirmitátem nostram, quæsumus, Dómine, propítius réspice: et mala ómnia quæ juste merémur, sanctórum Mártyrum tuórum atque Pontíficum N. et N. intercessióne avérte.

gaudentincelisanimesanctorumquichristive.en: The souls of the Saints rejoice * in heaven, who have followed the footsteps of Christ: and because for his love they despised the world, therefore they shall reign with Christ for ever.
gaudentincelisanimesanctorumquichristive.la: Gaudent in cælis * ánimæ Sanctórum, qui Christi vestígia sunt secúti: et quia pro ejus amóre sæculum sprevérunt, ídeo cum Christo regnábunt in ætérnum.

prestaquesumusomnipotensdeusutquiglorios.en: Grant, we beseech thee, almighty God: that we who have known thy glorious Martyrs N. and N. to be brave in their confession, may feel them to be loving in their intercession for us with thee.
prestaquesumusomnipotensdeusutquiglorios.la: Præsta, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, qui gloriósos Mártyres tuos N. et N. fortes in sua confessióne cognóvimus, pios apud te in nostra intercessióne sentiámus.

ovenerandamartyrumgloriosacertaminaquiin.en: O the venerable and glorious combats of the Martyrs, who in their bodies endured cruel torments for Christ!
ovenerandamartyrumgloriosacertaminaquiin.la: O veneránda Mártyrum gloriósa certámina, qui in suis corpóribus pro Christo immánia pertulérunt torménta!

etideoperciperemerueruntimmarcescibileme.en: And therefore they merited to receive the never-fading crown of eternal glory.
etideoperciperemerueruntimmarcescibileme.la: Et ídeo percipere meruérunt immarcescibilem ætérnæ glóriæ corónam.

despectanamquepresentisvitelucecontempto.en: For, despising the light of the present life, and contemning the torture of their bodies, they overcame the raging world for the love of God.
despectanamquepresentisvitelucecontempto.la: Despécta namque præséntis vitæ luce, contemptóque suórum córporum cruciatu, sæviéntem mundum Dei pro amóre vicérunt.

inillotemporedixitiesusdiscipulissuiscum.en: At that time, Jesus said unto His disciples: When ye shall hear of wars and commotions, be not terrified for these things must first come to pass; but the end is not by and by. And so on.
inillotemporedixitiesusdiscipulissuiscum.la: In illo témpore: Dixit Jesus discípulis suis: Cum audiéritis prǽlia, et seditiónes, nolíte terréri: opórtet primum hæc fíeri, sed nondum statim finis. Et réliqua.

ergoquiainoccasusaculisumuspreceduntqued.en: Therefore, because we are at the setting of the world, certain sicknesses of the world go before. A sickness of the world is famine, a sickness of the world is pestilence, a sickness of the world is persecution. But there are also other wars which the Christian man endureth, the battles of divers lusts also, and the conflicts of desires; and the enemies of his own household are much more grievous than those from without.
ergoquiainoccasusaculisumuspreceduntqued.la: Ergo quia in occásu saculi sumus, præcédunt quædam ægritudines mundi. Ægritúdo mundi est fames, ægritúdo mundi est pestilentia, ægritúdo mundi est persecútio. Sunt autem et ália bella, quæ vir sústinet christiánus, diversárum quoque prælia cupiditátum, studiorúmque conflictus; multóque gravióres doméstici hostes quam extranei.

nuncavaritiastimulatnuncaccenditlibidonu.en: Now avarice goadeth, now lust inflameth, now fear terrifieth, now anger troubleth, now ambition moveth, now the spirits of wickedness, which are in the high places, try to affright. And so the affection of the wavering mind is pressed as it were by certain battles, and shaken by certain earthquakes. But the stronger man saith: If armies in camp should stand together against me, my heart shall not fear: if a battle should rise up against me, in this will I be confident.
nuncavaritiastimulatnuncaccenditlibidonu.la: Nunc avaritia stimulat, nunc accéndit libido, nunc metus terret, nunc iracúndia exágitat, nunc ambitio movet, nunc terrére tentant spiritália nequítiæ, quæ sunt in cæléstibus. Itaque quasi quibúsdam urgétur præliis, et quibusdam terræ mótibus quátitur móbilis ánimi nutántis afféctus. Sed fórtior dicit: Si consistant advérsum me castra, non timébit cor meum: si exsúrgat in me prælium, in hoc ego sperábo.

iustorumautemanimeinmanudeisuntetnontang.en: But the souls of the just * are in the hand of God, and the torment of malice shall not touch them.
iustorumautemanimeinmanudeisuntetnontang.la: Justórum autem ánimæ * in manu Dei sunt, et non tanget illos torméntum malítiæ.

corporasanctoruminpacesepultasuntetviven.en: The bodies of the Saints * are buried in peace: and their names shall live for evermore.
corporasanctoruminpacesepultasuntetviven.la: Córpora Sanctórum * in pace sepúlta sunt: et vivent nómina eórum in ætérnum.

martyresdominidominumbenediciteineternum.en: Ye Martyrs of the Lord, * bless the Lord for ever.
martyresdominidominumbenediciteineternum.la: Mártyres Dómini * Dóminum benedícite in ætérnum.

martyrumchoruslaudatedominuminexcelsis.en: Ye choir of Martyrs, * praise the Lord on high.
martyrumchoruslaudatedominuminexcelsis.la: Mártyrum chorus * laudáte Dóminum in excélsis.

sanctiperfidemviceruntregnaoperatisuntiu.en: The Saints by faith conquered kingdoms, wrought justice, obtained promises, in Christ Jesus our Lord.
sanctiperfidemviceruntregnaoperatisuntiu.la: Sancti per fidem vicérunt regna, operáti sunt justítiam, adépti sunt repromissiónes, in Christo Jesu Dómino nostro.

etmartyrumvictorias.en: And the victories of the Martyrs,

letiscanamusmentibus.en: Let us sing with joyful minds.

terrorevictoseculi.en: The terror of the world overcome,

penisquespretiscorporis.en: And the pains of the body despised,

mortissacrecompendio.en: By the short way of a holy death

tradunturignimartyres.en: The Martyrs are given up to the fire

etbestiarumdentibus.en: And to the teeth of beasts:

tortorisinsanimanus.en: The hand of the frenzied torturer.

viteperennisgratia.en: By the grace of everlasting life.

istisuntquiveneruntexmagnatribulationeet.en: These are they which came * out of great tribulation, and have washed their robes in the blood of the Lamb.
istisuntquiveneruntexmagnatribulationeet.la: Isti sunt qui venérunt * ex magna tribulatióne, et lavérunt stolas suas in sánguine Agni. Ps. 112, 116, 145, 146, 147

quamspeciosetgratafestivitasnobisenituit.en: How beautiful and welcome a festival hath shone forth upon us, and this day gleameth more splendid than the days of the whole year, not lit more brightly by the wonted rays of the sun, but made more nobly illustrious by the light of the Martyrs, glittering above every flashing lightning. For the Martyrs are more illustrious than many suns, and brighter than the great lights. Not such are the rays cast upon the earth from the sun's circle on high, as are the flashings of gleaming light that leap forth from their bodies, and blind the very eyes of the envious devil.
quamspeciosetgratafestivitasnobisenituit.la: Quam speciosa et grata festivitas nobis enituit, et totius anni diebus splendidior dies hodierna praefulget, non de usitatis solis radiis illuminata praeclarius; sed de lumine Martyrum, supra coruscum omne fulgur micante, illustrata sublimius. Multis enim solibus illustriores sunt Martyres, et magnis luminaribus clariores. Non tales de superno solis circulo in terram radii jaciuntur, qualles a corporibus eorum prosiliunt corusca luce fulgores, et ipsos diaboli occulos invidentis obcecantes.

ideminsermdemart.en: The same, in a Sermon on the Martyrs.

quisanctorummeritareligiosacaritatemirat.en: He that admireth with devout love the merits of the Saints, and who speaketh of the glories of the just with frequent praise, let him imitate their holy ways and justice: since he whom the merit of any Saint delighteth, ought to be delighted by a like service in the worship of God. Wherefore either he ought to imitate, if he praiseth, or he ought not to praise, if he refuseth to imitate. For if we love the just and the faithful for this reason, that we look up to justice and faith in them, we also can be what they are, if we ourselves do what they do.
quisanctorummeritareligiosacaritatemirat.la: Qui Sanctorum merita religiosa caritate miratur, quique justorum glorias frequenti laude colloquitur, mores sanctos atque justitiam imitetur: quoniam quem delectat Sancti alicujus meritum, delectare debet per circa cultum Dei obsequium. Quare aut imitari debet, si laudat, aut laudare non debet, si imitari detrectat. Nam si propterea justos fidelésque diligimus, quod in ipsis justitiam fidemque suspicimus, possumus nos quoque esse quod sunt, si faciamus ipsi quod faciunt.

inistissemperparesvirtutesdissimilespugn.en: In these the virtues are ever equal, the fights unlike, the victories glorious. Whence thou, O Christian, art a delicate soldier, if thou thinkest thou canst conquer, and triumph without a combat. Put forth thy strength, fight bravely, contend fiercely in this battle. Consider the covenant, mark the condition, know the warfare: the covenant which thou hast pledged, the condition on which thou hast come, the warfare in which thou hast enrolled thy name. For by this covenant all whom thou admirest fight: on this condition they have all conquered, by this warfare they all triumph.
inistissemperparesvirtutesdissimilespugn.la: In istis semper pares virtutes, dissimiles pugnae gloriosae victoriae. Unde tu, Christiane, delicatus es miles, si putas te posse vincere, sine certamine triumphare. Exsere vires, fortiter dimica, atrociter in proelio isto concerta. Considera pactum, conditionem attende, militiam nosce: pactum quod spondisti, conditionem qua accessisti, militiam cui nomen dedisti. Hoc enim pacto, quos miraris, cuncti pugnant: hac conditione universi vicerunt, hac milia omnes triumphant.

inillotemporevidensiesusturbasasceditinm.en: At that time, Jesus, seeing the multitudes, went up into a mountain, and when he was set down, his disciples came unto him, and opening his mouth he taught them, saying: Blessed are the poor in spirit. And so on.
inillotemporevidensiesusturbasasceditinm.la: In illo tempore: Videns Jesus turbas, ascēdit in montem, et, cum sedisset, accesserunt ad eum discipuli ejus, et aperiens os suum docēbat eos, dicens: Beāti pāuperes spiritu. et reliqua.

congregatisigiturpluribusturbismontemcon.en: The multitudes therefore being gathered together in great number, he goeth up into the mountain, and teacheth: that is, set in the height of the Father's majesty, he appointeth the precepts of the heavenly life. For he would not have handed down the ordinances of eternity, unless he were set in eternity. Then it is thus written: He opened his mouth, and taught them. It was ready to hand to say that he had spoken; but because he had taken his stand in the glory of the Father's majesty, and was teaching eternity, therefore the office of the human mouth is shown to have obeyed the motion of the speaking spirit.
congregatisigiturpluribusturbismontemcon.la: Congregatis igitur plūribus turbis, montem conscéndet, et docet: in Patérnæ scilicet maiéstátis pósitus celsitúdine, cæléstis vitæ præcêpta constitut. Non enim æternitátis institůta, nisi in æternitáte pósitus, tradidisset. Denique ita scriptum est: Apéruit os suum, et docébát eos. Locútum em fuiśse prómptus erat dicere; sed, quia in glória maiestátis instíPatérnæ maiestátis instíterat, et æternitátem docébat, idcirco ad motum spíritus eloquéntis, obedisse osténditur humáni officium.

beatipauperesspirituquoniamipsorumestreg.en: Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven. The Lord had taught by example that the glory of human ambition is to be forsaken, saying: The Lord thy God shalt thou adore, and him only shalt thou serve. And whereas he had foretold by the Prophets that he would choose a people lowly and trembling at his words; he set the beginning of perfect beatitude in humility of spirit.
beatipauperesspirituquoniamipsorumestreg.la: Beáti páuperes spíritu: quóniam ipsórum est regnum cælorum. Exémplo Dóminus docúerat humánæ ambitionis glóriam relinquéndam, dicens: Dóminum Deum tuum adorábis, et illi soli sérvies. Et cum se per Prophetas pópulum humílem et ad verba sua treméntem præmónuit esse lecturum; in spíritus humilitáte perféctæ beatitúdinis pósuit exórdium.

nullanosnecsecularisfastusinsolentianeco.en: Let neither the insolent pride of the world, nor the desire of riches, nor the ambition of vain glory corrupt us: but let us be subject to God, and, from the communion of living, be held towards all men by the charity of the common life. Esteeming also that in this, that we were born, there is a great future profit of the divine goodness: whose reward and honour must be merited by the works of the present life: and so, through this humility of spirit, whereby we shall remember both that all things have been granted us by God, and that better things are to be hoped for hereafter, the kingdom of heaven shall be ours.
nullanosnecsecularisfastusinsolentianeco.la: Nulla nos nec sæculáris fastus insoléntia, nec opum cupíditas, nec inánis glóriæ ambitio corrúmpat: sed subiécti Deosimus, et de communióne vivéndi in omnes comúnis vitæ caritáte tenéamur. Magnum étiam in eo, quod nati sumus, divínæ bonitátis futúrum proféctum existimántes: cujus præmium atque honos præséntis vitæ opéribus sit meréndus: atque ita per hanc spíritus humilitátem, qua a Deo nobis meminérimus et indulta omnia, et deínceps potióra speránda, cælórum regnum erit nostrum.

inillotemporedixitiesusdiscipulissuisatt.en: At that time: Jesus said unto His disciples Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy. And so on.
inillotemporedixitiesusdiscipulissuisatt.la: In illo témpore: Dixit Jesus discípulis suis: Atténdite a fermento pharisæórum, quod est hypócrisis. Et réliqua.

dehocfermentoapostolusprecepititaqueepul.en: Of this leaven the Apostle gave command: Therefore let us feast, not with the old leaven, nor with the leaven of malice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth. For as a little leaven corrupteth the whole mass of meal into which it is cast, and soon staineth all the dough with its savour; so assuredly dissimulation will defraud the soul which it hath once imbued of all sincerity and truth of the virtues.
dehocfermentoapostolusprecepititaqueepul.la: De hoc ferménto Apóstolus præcépit: Itáque epulémur, non in ferménto véteri, neque in ferménto malítiæ et nequítiæ, sed in ázymis sinceritátis et veritátis. Nam, sicut módicum ferméntum totam farínæ, cui injícitur, massam corrúmpit, universámque mox conspersiónem suo sapóre commáculat; sic nimírum simulátio, cujus semel ánimum imbúerit, tota virtútum sinceritáte et veritáte fraudábit.

estergosensusattenditeneemuleminisimulat.en: The sense therefore is: Beware lest ye emulate the dissemblers; for the time shall surely come in which both your virtue shall be revealed to all, and their hypocrisy. But that which followeth: For whatsoever ye have spoken in darkness shall be spoken in the light; may fittingly be understood not only of the future, when all the hidden things of hearts shall be brought forth to the light, but also of the present time. For the things which the Apostles once either spoke or suffered amid the darkness of afflictions and the shadows of prisons, are now, the Church being made glorious throughout the world, and their acts being read, publicly proclaimed.
estergosensusattenditeneemuleminisimulat.la: Est ergo sensus: Atténdite ne æmulémini simulatóres; quia véniet profécto tempus, in quo et vestra virtus ómnibus, et eórum revelétur hypócrisis. Verum quod séquitur: Quóniam quæ in ténebris dixístis, in lúmine dicéntur; non solum in futúro, quando cuncta córdium abscóndita proferéntur ad lucem, sed et in præsénti témpore potest congruénter áccipi. Quóniam quæ inter ténebras quondam pressurárum carcerúmque umbras vel locúti vel passi sunt Apóstoli; nunc, clarificáta per orbem Ecclésia, lectis eórum áctibus, públice prædicántur.

dicoautemvobisamicismeisneterreaminiabhi.en: And I say to you, my friends: Be not afraid of them who kill the body. If the persecutors of the Saints, when they have slain their bodies, have nothing more that they can do against them: then they rage with a vain madness who cast out the dead members of the Martyrs to be torn by beasts and birds, since they can in no wise withstand the omnipotence of God, that he should not quicken them by raising them up again. And, because there are two kinds of persecutors: the one raging openly, the other flattering feignedly and deceitfully. The Saviour, willing to fortify and instruct us against both, both above biddeth us beware of the hypocrisy of the Pharisees, and here biddeth us not to fear the slaughter of the executioners.
dicoautemvobisamicismeisneterreaminiabhi.la: Dico autem vobis amicis meis: Ne terreámini ab his qui occídunt corpus. Si persecutóres Sanctórum, occísis corpóribus, non habent ámplius quid contra illos agant: ergo supervácua furunt insánia, qui mórtua Mártyrum membra, feris avibúsque discerpénda projíciunt, cum nequáquam omnipoténtiæ Dei, quin ea resuscitándo vivíficet, obsístere possint. Et, quia duo sunt génera persecutórum: unum palam sæviéntium, álterum ficte fraudulentérque blandiéntium. Contra utrúmque nos muníre atque institúere volens Salvátor, et supra ab hypócrisi pharisæórum atténdere, et hic a carníficum cæde prǽcipit non timére.

sanctenchristiconfessoraudirogantesservu.en: O holy N., Confessor of Christ, hear thy little servants who entreat thee.
sanctenchristiconfessoraudirogantesservu.la: Sancte N., Christi Conféssor, audi rogántes sérvulos.

osantensidusaureumdominigratiaservorumge.en: O holy N., golden star, by the grace of the Lord receive with thy wonted clemency the groans of thy servants.
osantensidusaureumdominigratiaservorumge.la: O sante N., sidus áureum, Dómini grátia servórum gémitus sólita súscipe cleméntia.

confessordomininastantemplebemcorroboras.en: O Confessor of the Lord, N., strengthen the people standing here by thy holy intercession: that we who are pressed down by the weight of our vices may be lifted up by the glory of thy blessedness, and under thy leadership may obtain eternal rewards.
confessordomininastantemplebemcorroboras.la: Conféssor Dómini N., astántem plebem corróbora sancta intercessióne: ut, qui vitiórum póndere prémimur, beatitúdinis tuæ glória sublevémur, et te duce ætérna præmia consequámur.

illiusergoinquantumpossumusvestigiisinsi.en: Let us therefore, as far as we can, follow in his footsteps, by which, hastening through that very narrow way unto the broad places of heaven, he showed us by what way we should follow.
illiusergoinquantumpossumusvestigiisinsi.la: Illius ergo, in quantum póssumus, vestígiis insistámus, quibus per illam nimis arctam viam ad cæli ampla festinans, qua cum sequerémur, osténdit.

utignorantiamillamdieiomnibustacitinonsi.en: That we might know that that ignorance of the day, kept silent from all, is not without the reason of a profitable silence, the Lord admonished us to watch because of the coming of the thief, and, held fast by constancy in prayers, to cleave to all the works of his commandments. For he showeth that the thief is the devil, ever watchful to carry off spoils from us, and lying in wait for the houses of our bodies: that he may pierce them, while we are careless and given to sleep, with the darts of his counsels and allurements.
utignorantiamillamdieiomnibustacitinonsi.la: Ut ignorántiam illam diéi ómnibus táciti, non sine útilis siléntii ratióne esse scirémus, vigiláre nos Dóminus propter advéntum furis admónuit, et oratíonum assiduitáte deténtos ómnibus præceptórum suórum opéribus inhærére. Furem enim esse osténdit zábulum, ad detrahénda ex nobis spólia pervígilem, et córporum nostrórum dómibus insidiántem: ut ea incuriósis nobis, et somno déditis, consiliórum suórum atque illecebrárum jáculis perfódiat.

iustusutpalmaflorebitindomodominisicutce.en: The just shall flourish like the palm tree in the house of the Lord, like the cedar of Libanus shall he be multiplied: planted in the house of the Lord.
iustusutpalmaflorebitindomodominisicutce.la: Justus ut palma florébit in domo Dómini, sicut cedrus Líbani multiplicábitur: plantátus in domo Dómini.

inatriisdomusdeinostriiflorebit.en: In the courts of the house of our God he shall flourish.
inatriisdomusdeinostriiflorebit.la: In átriis domus Dei nostrii florébit.

glorietdivitieindomeiusetiustitieiusmane.en: Glory and wealth shall be in his house: and his justice remaineth for ever and ever.
glorietdivitieindomeiusetiustitieiusmane.la: Glória et divítiæ in domo ejus, et justítia ejus manet in sǽculum sǽculi.

paratosigituressenosconvenitquiadieiigno.en: It behoveth us therefore to be ready: for ignorance of the day should stir up the earnest care of a watchful expectation. Who, thinkest thou, is a faithful and wise servant, whom his lord hath appointed over his family? Although he exhorteth us in common to an unwearied care of watchfulness: yet he enjoineth a special solicitude upon the princes of the people, that is, the bishops, in the expectation of his coming.
paratosigituressenosconvenitquiadieiigno.la: Parátos ígitur esse nos cónvenit: quia diéi ignorátio inténtam sollicitúdinem suspénsæ exspectatiónis exágitet. Quisnam est fidélis servus et prudens, quem constítuit Dóminus super famíliam suam? Quamquam in commúne nos ad indeféssam vigilántiæ curam adhortétur: speciálem tamen pópuli princípibus, id est, epíscopis, in exspectatióne adventúque suo sollicitúdinem mandat.

honestavitilluminlaboribusetcomplevitlab.en: He made him honourable in his labours, and accomplished his labours.
honestavitilluminlaboribusetcomplevitlab.la: Honestávit illum in labóribus, et complévit labóres illíus.

immortalisestenimmemoriailliusquoniamapu.en: For the memory of him is immortal, because it is known both with God and with men.
immortalisestenimmemoriailliusquoniamapu.la: Immortális est enim memória illíus, quóniam apud Deum nota est, et apud hómines.

huncenimservumfidelematqueprudentemprepo.en: For by this faithful and wise servant he signifieth him that is set over the household, caring for the advantage and profit of the people committed to him. Who, if he shall hearken to the word and obey the commandments, that is, if by the timeliness and truth of his doctrine he strengthen the weak, bind up the broken, convert the depraved, and dispense the word of life as the food of eternity for the nourishing of the household, and be found doing these things and abiding in them: he shall obtain glory from the Lord as a faithful steward and a profitable bailiff, and shall be set over all goods; that is, he shall be placed in the glory of God, since there is nothing beyond that is better.
huncenimservumfidelematqueprudentemprepo.la: Hunc enim servum fidélem atque prudéntem, præpósitum famíliæ signíficat, cómmoda atque utilitátes commíssi sibi pópuli curántem. Qui si dicto áudiens, et præcéptis obédiens erit, id est, si doctrínæ opportunitáte et veritáte infírma confírmet, disrúpta consólidet, depraváta convértat, et verbum vitæ in æternitátis cibum aléndæ famíliæ dispéndat, atque hæc agens, hisque ímmorans deprehendátur: glóriam a Dómino tamquam dispensátor fidélis et víllicus útilis consequétur, et super ómnia bona constituétur; id est, in Dei glória collocábitur, quia nihil sit ultra, quod mélius sit.

iustusutpalmaflorebitindomodomini.en: The just shall flourish like the palm tree * In the house of the Lord.
iustusutpalmaflorebitindomodomini.la: Justus ut palma florébit * In domo Dómini.

indomodomini.en: In the house of the Lord.

inillotemporedixitiesusdiscipulissuispar.en: At that time Jesus spake unto His disciples this parable A man, travelling into a far country, called his own servants, and delivered unto them his goods. And so on.
inillotemporedixitiesusdiscipulissuispar.la: In illo témpore: Dixit Jesus discípulis suis parábolam hanc: Homo péregre proficíscens, vocávit servos suos, et trádidit illis bona sua. Et réliqua.

divisioquidempecunieinequalisestsednonad.en: The division of the money indeed is unequal, but the diversity is not to be referred to him that divideth. For he saith that each one received according to his own ability. He signifieth that he himself is the householder. The time of the journey is the space of repentance, in which, sitting in the heavens at the right hand of God, he hath entrusted to the whole human race the power of faith and of evangelical working.
divisioquidempecunieinequalisestsednonad.la: Divísio quidem pecuniæ inæquális est, sed non ad dividentem referénda divérsitas est. Ait enim unumquémque secúndum virtútem suam accepisse. Patrem famílias seipsum esse signíficat. Peregrinatiónis tempus pæniténtiæ spátium est, quo in cælis a dextris Dei ássidens, potestátem univérso géneri humáno fidei atque operatiónis evangélicæ permisit.

igiturunusquisquesecundumfideisuemensura.en: Therefore each one hath received from him that preacheth a talent according to the measure of his faith, that is, the preaching of the Gospel. For this is the incorruptible substance: this is the patrimony of Christ reserved for the eternal heirs. But that servant who received five talents is the people of believers from the Law: setting out from which, having rightly and uprightly discharged its merit, he doubled it by the working of the evangelical Faith.
igiturunusquisquesecundumfideisuemensura.la: Igitur unusquisque secúndum fidei suæ mensúram taléntum, id est, Evangélii prædicatiónem, a prædicánte suscépit. Hæc enim incorrúpta substántia est: hoc Christi patrimónium ætérnis herédibus reservátum. Sed servus ille, qui quinque talénta accépit, pópulus ex Lege credéntium est: ex qua proféctus, méritum ipsíus recte probéque perfunctus evangélicæ Fidei operatióne duplicávit.

inrationeautemponendaiudiciiexamenestquo.en: But in the settling of the account is the examination of the judgement: whereby the use of the heavenly word and the return of the talent dispensed is required. Therefore he to whom five had been committed, when his lord returned, offered ten from the five, being found, to wit, such in the Faith as he was in the Law: who fulfilled the obedience of the precepts of the ten words and of the five books of Moses through the grace of evangelical justification. Therefore he is bidden to enter into the joy of the Lord, that is, he is received into the honour of the glory of Christ.
inrationeautemponendaiudiciiexamenestquo.la: In ratióne autem ponénda judícii exámen est: quo cæléstis verbi usus et réditus dispensáti talénti postulátur. Igitur cui erant quinque commissa, dómino revérso de quinque decem óbtulit, talis scilicet in Fide repértus, qualis in Lege: qui decem verbórum quinque libris Móysi præceptórum obediéntiam per grátiam evangélicæ justificatiónis expléverit. Igitur jubétur in gaudium Dómini introire, id est, in honórem glóriæ Christi recipitur.

sermosanctiephremsyridiaconi.en: Sermon of St. Ephrem the Syrian, Deacon

sapienshicetfidelisnveregressusestvirtut.en: This wise and faithful N. was truly a progress of virtues, a book of praises, a life of miracles: who, walking in the flesh, went forward in the spirit; and, leading on earth a life in common with others, contemplated the things above: a beryl plectrum of the mystic harp, delighting the region of the holy Angels: a sure lamb of the womb of life, giving light to the field and garden of the Holy Ghost, exulting in desire and love, and plucking a flower from the lowest root of the most precious cross: a fair parchment of the divine wisdom, which received divine impressions from heaven.
sapienshicetfidelisnveregressusestvirtut.la: Sapiens hic et fidélis N. vere gressus est virtútum, liber laudum, vita miraculórum: qui in carne grádiens, spiritu incedébat; communémque cum áliis in terra vitam degens, supérna contemplabátur: beryllium plectrum mýsticæ citharæ regiónem sanctórum Angelórum obléctans: certus agnus matricis vitæ, Spiritus Sancti agrum ac hortum illústrans, desidério atque amore exsúltans, ac florem ex ima radice pretiosíssimæ crucis decérpens: membrána pulchra divinæ sapiéntiæ, quæ de cælo divinas impressiónes accépit.

inillotemporerespondensiesusdixitconfite.en: At that time, Jesus answered and said: I confess to thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them to the little ones. And so on.
inillotemporerespondensiesusdixitconfite.la: In illo témpore: Respóndens Jesus dixit: Confíteor tibi, Pater, Dómine cæli et terræ, quia abscondísti hæc a sapiéntibus et prudéntibus, et revelásti ea párvulis. Et réliqua.

quodhicconfiteordixitidemvaletquodgratia.en: That which he here said, I confess, is the same as, I give thanks. I give thanks to thee, he saith, because thou hast hid these things from the prudent and wise. Shall we then say that he rejoiceth at their perdition, and because they have not learnt these things? By no means. He rejoiceth therefore not because the wise have not known, but he is glad because the little ones have perceived. So also Paul saith: I give thanks to my God, that ye were the servants of sin, but have obeyed from the heart unto that form of doctrine into which ye have been delivered. Paul therefore rejoiceth not because they were the servants of sin; but because, being such, they were made worshippers of the truth.
quodhicconfiteordixitidemvaletquodgratia.la: Quod hic, Confiteor, dixit, idem valet quod Grátias ago. Grátias, inquit, tibi ago, quóniam a prudéntibus et sapiéntibus hæc celásti. An igitur perditióne illórum gaudére ipsum dicémus, et quóniam illi hæc non didicére? Mínime. Non ergo quia sapiéntes non cognovérunt, gaudet: sed quia párvuli percepérunt, lætátur. Ita et Paulus dicit: Grátias ago Deo meo, quóniam fuístis servi peccáti: obedístis autem ex corde in quam tráditi estis formam doctrinæ. Non ergo Paulus proptérea gaudet, quia erant servi peccáti; sed quia, cum essent hujusmodi, veritátis cultóres facti sunt.

prudentesautemhicscribasetphariseosappel.en: But here he calleth the scribes and Pharisees prudent: by which words he maketh the disciples more eager: since they understand that they, being fishermen, have obtained those things from which those men, the greatest as they seemed, have fallen away. But when he said the wise: he meaneth not that true and praiseworthy wisdom: but this which is furnished by worldly learning. Wherefore also he said not, Thou hast revealed to the foolish, but, To the little ones: as it were to those not yet formed, but simple.
prudentesautemhicscribasetphariseosappel.la: Prudentes autem hic scribas et pharisæos appéllat: quibus verbis alacrióres reddit discípulos: cum intelligant illa se piscatóres esse consecútos, a quibus illi summi, ut videbántur, viri excidérunt. Cum autem Sapiéntes díxerit: non illam veram laudábilem sapiéntiam intélligit: sed hanc quæ sæculári doctrina præstátur. Idcirco étiam non dixit, Stultis revelásti, sed Párvulis: quasi non formátis adhuc, sed simplicibus.

itaostenditnonindigneillossediurehisrebu.en: Thus he showeth that they were deprived of these things not unworthily, but by right: and through all he teacheth us that the breath of pride is altogether to be shunned, and simplicity to be emulated. Which Paul writeth in fuller words, saying: If any man among you seemeth to be wise in this world, let him become a fool, that he may be wise: for so is the grace of God shown. But why doth he give thanks to the Father, when he himself hath done it? As he prayeth and intercedeth for us with God, declaring his great charity towards us, so also doth he this out of the fervour of charity.
itaostenditnonindigneillossediurehisrebu.la: Ita osténdit non indigne illos, sed jure his rebus fuísse privátos: ac per ómnia nos docet flatum supérbiæ omnino esse fugiéndum ac simplicitátem æmulándam. Quod Paulus amplióribus verbis scribit, dicens: Si quis in vobis vidétur in hoc sæculo sápiens esse, is fiat stultus, ut sápiens efficiátur: sic enim grátia Dei monstrátur. Cur vero grátias agit Patri, cum ipse illud fécerit? Sicut orat et intercédit pro nobis ad Deum, magnam erga nos declárans caritátem, sic étiam et hoc ex caritátis fervóre péragit.

istestvirgosapiensquamdominusvigilantemi.en: This is the wise virgin, whom the Lord found watching: who, having taken her lamp, took oil with her, and when the Lord came, went in with him to the marriage.
istestvirgosapiensquamdominusvigilantemi.la: Ista est Virgo sapiens, quam Dominus vigilantem invenit: quae accepta lampade sumpsit secum oleum, et veniente Domino introivit cum eo ad nuptias.

agnumsponsumvirginumveniteadoremusdominu.en: The Lamb, the Bridegroom of Virgins, * Come, let us adore, the Lord Jesus Christ.
agnumsponsumvirginumveniteadoremusdominu.la: Agnum, sponsum Vírginum, * Veníte, adorémus Dóminum Jesum Christum.

hecestvirgosapiensatquegloriosaquiadomin.en: This is a wise virgin, * and a glorious one, for the Lord of all hath loved her.
hecestvirgosapiensatquegloriosaquiadomin.la: Hæc est Virgo sápiens, * atque gloriósa, quia Dóminus ómnium diléxit eam. Ps. 97

cumintotomundovirgineusflosmarieimmarces.en: Whereas in the whole world the virginal flower of Mary weaveth unfading crowns, and preserveth with spotless affection the sceptred court of chastity: so far did integrity persevere unto the palm, that among maidens it seized the trophy of holiness, and by the footsteps of the Virgin Mother came to the heavenly bridechamber. O how worthy of imitation is the example of thy love which thou, O Virgin, hast handed down to virgins, by despising the riches of the world, by abhorring the concupiscences of the flesh, and by loving the beauty of Christ alone!
cumintotomundovirgineusflosmarieimmarces.la: Cum in toto mundo virgineus flos Mariæ immarcescíbiles corónas innéctat, et sceptrígeram pudóris aulam immaculáto consérvet afféctu: eo usque intégritas perseverávit ad palmam, ut in puéllis trophæum sanctitátis arríperet, et per vestígia Matris Vírgínis ad cæléstem thálamum perveníret. O quam imitábile virginíbus, Virgo, tui amóris tradidísti exémplum, contemnéndo mundi divítias, exsecrándo carnis concupiscéntias, et solam Christi pulchritudininem adamándo!

gratafactestadominoincertaminequiaapudde.en: She was made pleasing to the Lord in the combat, for she was glorified with God and with men: in the sight of princes she spake wisdom,
gratafactestadominoincertaminequiaapudde.la: Grata facta est a Dómino in certámine, quia apud Deum et apud hómines glorificáta est: in conspéctu princípum loquebátur sapiéntiam,

etdominusomniumdilexiteam.en: And the Lord of all loved her.

erectanamqueinvirtutisculminetormentader.en: For, raised up on the summit of virtue, she laughed at torments, she trampled on rewards.
erectanamqueinvirtutisculminetormentader.la: Erécta namque in virtútis cúlmine, torménta derísit, práemia calcávit.

beatissimahecvirgomagnumdesepudicitieexc.en: This most blessed Virgin raised up a great example of chastity in herself, when she preferred virginity to life, seized the trophy of the cross of Christ, and, armed rather with faith than with steel, fought bravely and conquered as well against lusts as against all torments. She knoweth not how to love aught that passeth away: and while she loved virginity exceedingly, she feared neither mockeries, nor flames, nor torments, nor executioners: lastly she dreaded not even the sword of the raging smiter.
beatissimahecvirgomagnumdesepudicitieexc.la: Beatíssima hæc Virgo magnum de se pudicitiæ excitávit exemplum, cum virginitátem prætulit vitæ, trophæum crucis Christi arrīpuit, et tam contra libidínes quam étiam contra supplicia univérsa, fide pótius armáta quam ferro, fórtiter dimicicávit et vicit. Nescit amáre áliquid quod transit: et dum nimis virginitátem díligit, nec ludíbria, nec flammas, nec supplícia, nec carnífices méuit: postrémo nec gládium furéntis percussóris expávit.

hecestvirgosapiensquamdominusvigilantemi.en: This is the wise virgin, whom the Lord found watching: who, having taken her lamp, took oil with her:
hecestvirgosapiensquamdominusvigilantemi.la: Hæc est Virgo sapiens, quam Dominus vigilantem invenit: quae accepta lampade sumpsit secum oleum:

etvenientedominointroivitcumeoadnuptias.en: And when the Lord came, she went in with him to the marriage.
etvenientedominointroivitcumeoadnuptias.la: Et veniente Domino introivit cum eo ad nuptias.

istestunadenumeroprudentumqueaptavitlamp.en: This is one of the number of the prudent, who trimmed her lamps.
istestunadenumeroprudentumqueaptavitlamp.la: Ista est una de número prudéntum, quæ aptávit lámpades suas.

veniiamvirgoadthalamumquemquessistiutspo.en: Come now, O Virgin, to the bridechamber which thou hast sought: that spotless virginity may prove thee the spouse of Christ, and approved confession may seal thee a Martyr. Happy the band of virgins, whose zeal it is to follow the footsteps of thy confession! Wherefore, O thou resplendent unto Christ, fair unto the Son of God, and pleasing to all the Angels and Archangels: we entreat thee with what prayers we can, that thou vouchsafe to remember us: that he may grant us pardon of our sins, who hath given thee the palm of all thy labours.
veniiamvirgoadthalamumquemquessistiutspo.la: Veni jam, Virgo, ad thálamum, quem quæssísti: ut sponsam te virgínítas immaculáta cómprobet Christi, et Mártyrem conféssio probáta consígnet. Felix catérva vírginum, quibus stúdium est tuæ sequi confessiónis vestígia! Itaque o splendída Christo, pulchra Dei Fílio, et ómnibus Angelis atque Archángelis grata: ut nostri meminísse dignéris, quibus póssumus, précibus exorámus: ut nobis ille tríbuat peccatórum indulgéntiam, qui tibi tuórum ómnium labórum trádidit palmam.

audivivocemdecelovenientemveniteomnesvir.en: I heard a voice coming from heaven: Come, all ye most wise virgins,
audivivocemdecelovenientemveniteomnesvir.la: Audívi vocem de cælo veniéntem: veníte, omnes virgines sapientíssimæ,

oleumreconditeinvasisvestrisdumsponsusad.en: Store up oil in your vessels, until the bridegroom shall come.
oleumreconditeinvasisvestrisdumsponsusad.la: Oleum recóndite in vasis vestris, dum sponsus advénerit.

medianocteclamorfactusesteccesponsusveni.en: At midnight there was a cry made: Behold, the bridegroom cometh.
medianocteclamorfactusesteccesponsusveni.la: Média nocte clamor factus est: Ecce sponsus venit.

sedutsicsitopusinpublicoquatenusintentio.en: but so that the work be in public, that the intention may remain in secret. Again the kingdom of heaven is said to be like unto a merchant man who seeketh good pearls, but findeth one precious one, which, when he hath found it, he selleth all and buyeth: because he who hath perfectly known the sweetness of the heavenly life, so far as possibility admitteth, willingly forsaketh all those things which he had loved on earth.
sedutsicsitopusinpublicoquatenusintentio.la: sed ut sic sit opus in público, quá tenus intentio máneat in occulto. Rursum cæléste regnum negotiatóri hómini símile dícitur, qui bonas margaritas quærit, sed unam pretiosam învenit, quam vidélicet invéntam, omnia vendens, emit: quia qui cælestis vitæ dulcédinem, in quantum possib ilítas admíttit, perfécte cognóverit: ea, quæ in terrénis amáverat, libénter cuncta derelínquit.

rectepersalomonemdiciturfortisestutmorsd.en: Rightly is it said by Solomon: Love is strong as death: because, as death destroyeth the body, so the love of eternal life slayeth from the love of bodily things. For him whom it hath perfectly absorbed, it rendereth as it were insensible to earthly desires without. For this Saint, whose birthday we celebrate today, could not have died in the body for the Lord, had she not first been dead in mind to earthly desires. For her mind, raised up on the summit of virtue, despised torments, trampled on rewards. What say we among these things, bearded and weak men, who see maidens going through the sword to the heavenly kingdoms, we whom anger overcometh, pride puffeth up, ambition troubleth, luxury defileth? If we cannot gain the kingdoms of heaven through the wars of persecutions, let this very thing be shameful to us, that we will not follow God at least through peace.
rectepersalomonemdiciturfortisestutmorsd.la: Recte per Salomónem dícitur: Fortis est ut mors diléctio: quia, sicut mors corpus interimit, sic ab amore rerum corporalium æternæ vitæ cáritas occidit. Nam quem perfecte absorbuérit, ad terræna foris desidéria velut insensibile reddit. Nec enim Sancta hæc, cujus hodie natalitia celebrámus, mori pro Dímino potuisset in córporé, si prius a terrēnis desidēriis mórtua non fuisset in mente. Erętus namque in virtútis culmine ánimus tormenta despēxit, præmia calcávit. Quid inter hæc nos barbáti et débiles dícimus, qui ire ad regna cælstia puéllas per ferrum vidémus, quos ira súperat, superbia inflat, ambitio pertúrbat, luxuria ínquitat? Qui si adipisci regna cælórum per bella persecutionum non possumus, hoc ipsum nobis turpe sit, quod Deum núlomus saltem per paccem sequi.

infestovirginispredicandestvirginitashoc.en: On the feast of a Virgin virginity is to be preached. This we have undertaken in this sermon. May Christ help us, the Son of a Virgin and the Spouse of virgins: born bodily of a virginal womb, spiritually wedded in a virginal marriage. Since therefore the whole Church is a virgin, as the Apostle saith, of how great honour are those members worthy which keep even in the flesh itself that which the whole Church keepeth in faith! No fruitfulness of the flesh therefore can be compared to holy virginity, even of the flesh.
infestovirginispredicandestvirginitashoc.la: In festo Virginis praedicanda est virginitas. Hoc in isto sermone suscepimus. Adiuvet Christus Virginis Filius et Virginum sponsus: virginali utero corporalitæ natus, virginali connubio spiritualiter coniugatus. Cum igitur universa Ecclesia virgo sit, sicut dicit Apostolus, quanto digna sunt honore membra, quæ hæc custodiunt etiam in ipsa carne, quæ ipsa tota custodit in fide! Nulla ergo fecunditas carnis sanctæ virginitati, etiam carnis, comparari potest.

hancamavietexquisivisponsammihiassumere.en: Her have I loved and sought out, to take her for my spouse,
hancamavietexquisivisponsammihiassumere.la: Hanc amávi et exquisivi sponsam mihi assúmere,

etamatorfactussumformeillius.en: And I became a lover of her beauty.
etamatorfactussumformeillius.la: Et amátor factus sum formæ illíus.

illaautemvirgoconiugatemeritopreponiturq.en: But that Virgin is rightly preferred to the married woman, who doth not set herself forth to be loved by the multitude, but hath so loved him who is beautiful above the sons of men, that, since she could not conceive him in the flesh as Mary did, having conceived him in her heart she keepeth even her flesh entire for him. Let all fruitfulness of the flesh, all conjugal chastity yield to virginity. The one is not in our power: the other is not in eternity. Carnal fruitfulness hath not free will: conjugal chastity hath not heaven.
illaautemvirgoconiugatemeritopreponiturq.la: Illa autem Virgo coniugatæ mérito præpónitur, quæ nec multitúdine amándam proponit, sed Speciórum forma præ filiis hóminum sic amávit, ut, quia eum sicut Maria concipére carné non posset, ei corde conceptó carnem ætiam íntegram custodíret. Cedat virginitáti omnis fecúnditatis carnis, omnis pudicítia coniugális. Illa non est in potestáte: ista non est in æternitáte. Fecunditátem carnálem non habet libérum arbítrium: pudicítia coniúgalem non habet cælum.

profectohabebuntmagnumaliquidpreterceter.en: Assuredly they shall have something great beyond the rest in that common immortality, who have even now something not of the flesh in the flesh. For when the Lord had said of the eunuchs, I will give them in my house a named place, far better than of sons and daughters: he straightway added: I will give them an everlasting name; which surely signifieth a certain glory proper to them and excellent.
profectohabebuntmagnumaliquidpreterceter.la: Profécto habébunt magnum áliquid præter céteros in illa communi immortalitáte, qui habent áliquid jam non carnis in carne. Cum enim dixísset Dóminus de spadónibus, Dabo eis in domo mea locum nominátum multo meliorem quam filiorum atque filiarum: continuo subiecit: Nomen aeternum dabo eis; quod utique gloririam quandam propriam excellentemque significat.

simileeritregnumcelorumdecemvirginibusqu.en: The kingdom of heaven shall be like to ten virgins, who, taking their lamps, went out to meet the bridegroom and the bride.
simileeritregnumcelorumdecemvirginibusqu.la: Símile erit regnum cælórum decem virgínibus, quæ, accipiéntes lámpades suas, exiérunt óbviam sponso et sponsæ.

laudemusdeumnostruminconfessionebeaten.en: Let us praise our God * For the confession of blessed N.
laudemusdeumnostruminconfessionebeaten.la: Laudémus Deum nostrum * In confessióne beátæ N..

exsultaveruntfilieiudepropteriudiciatuad.en: The daughters of Juda rejoiced because of thy judgements, O Lord.
exsultaveruntfilieiudepropteriudiciatuad.la: Exsultavérunt fíliæ Judæ propter judícia tua, Dómine. Ps. 96

gaudeamusomnesindominodiemfestumcelebran.en: Let us all rejoice in the Lord, keeping a festal day in honour of blessed N.,
gaudeamusomnesindominodiemfestumcelebran.la: Gaudeámus omnes in Dómino, diem festum celebrántes sub honóre beátæ N.,

gratiasupergratiammuliersanctetpudorrata.en: Grace upon grace is a holy and shamefaced woman: and no price is worthy of a continent soul.
gratiasupergratiammuliersanctetpudorrata.la: Grátia super grátiam múlier sancta et pudorráta: omnis autem ponderátio non est digna continéntis ánimæ.

sicutsoloriensmundoinaltissimisdeisicmul.en: As the sun rising to the world in the high places of God, so is the beauty of a good woman for the ornament of her house.
sicutsoloriensmundoinaltissimisdeisicmul.la: Sicut sol óriens mundo in altíssimis Dei, sic mulieris bonæ spécies in ornaméntum domus suæ.

fundamentaeternasuprapetramsolidamsicman.en: Everlasting foundations upon a solid rock, so are the commandments of God in the heart of a holy woman.
fundamentaeternasuprapetramsolidamsicman.la: Fundaménta ætérna supra petram sólidam, sic mandáta Dei in corde mulieris sanctæ.

columneaureesuperbasesargenteasetpedesfi.en: Golden pillars upon bases of silver, and firm feet upon the soles of a steady woman.
columneaureesuperbasesargenteasetpedesfi.la: Colúmnæ áureæ super bases argénteas, et pedes firmí super plantas stábilis mulieris.

edificatiocivitatisconfirmabitnomenetsup.en: The building of a city shall establish a name, and above this a spotless woman shall be counted.
edificatiocivitatisconfirmabitnomenetsup.la: Ædificátio civitátis confirmábit nomen, et super hanc múlier immaculáta computábitur.

inhuiusvitefluctibus.en: Amid the waves of this life

nostrisutadaugesensibus.en: That thou increase in our senses

nescireprorsusomnia.en: Utterly to know nothing of all

sitchristerexpiissime.en: Be, O Christ, most loving King,

manumsuamaperuitinopietpalmassuasextendi.en: She hath opened her hand * to the needy, and stretched out her hands to the poor: strength and beauty are her clothing, and she shall laugh in the latter day.
manumsuamaperuitinopietpalmassuasextendi.la: Manum suam * apéruit ínopi, et palmas suas exténdit ad páuperem, fortitúdo et decor induméntum ejus, et ridébit in die novíssimo.

accinxitfortitudinelumbossuosetroboravit.en: She hath girded her loins with strength, and hath strengthened her arm: she hath tasted and seen that her traffic is good: her lamp shall not be put out in the night.
accinxitfortitudinelumbossuosetroboravit.la: Accínxit fortitúdine lumbos suos, et roborávit bráchium suum: gustávit, et vidit, quia bona est negotiátio ejus: non exstinguétur in nocte lucérna ejus.

laudemusdeumnostruminsolemnitatesancen.en: Let us praise our God * On the solemnity of holy N.
laudemusdeumnostruminsolemnitatesancen.la: Laudémus Deum nostrum * In solemnitáte sancæ N..

accinxitfortitudinelumbossuosetroboravit.en: She hath girded her loins with strength, and hath strengthened her arm: she hath tasted and seen that her traffic is good:
accinxitfortitudinelumbossuosetroboravit.la: Accínxit fortitúdine lumbos suos, et roborávit bráchium suum: gustávit et vidit quia bona est negotiátio ejus:

nonexstingueturinnoctelucerneius.en: Her lamp shall not be put out in the night.
nonexstingueturinnoctelucerneius.la: Non exstinguétur in nocte lucérna ejus.

lucernapedibusmeisverbumtuumetlumensemit.en: Thy word is a lamp to my feet, and a light to my paths.
lucernapedibusmeisverbumtuumetlumensemit.la: Lucérna pédibus meis verbum tuum, et lumen sémitis meis.

nontimebitdomuisueafrigoribusnivium.en: She shall not fear for her house from the cold of snow.
nontimebitdomuisueafrigoribusnivium.la: Non timébit dómui suæ a frigóribus nívium.

dispersitdeditpauperibusiustitieiusmanet.en: She hath distributed, she hath given to the poor: her justice remaineth for ever and ever.
dispersitdeditpauperibusiustitieiusmanet.la: Dispersit dedit pauperibus: justitia ejus manet in seculum sæculi.

dateeidefructumanuumsuarum.en: Give her of the fruit of her hands:
dateeidefructumanuumsuarum.la: Date ei de fructu mánuum suárum:

etlaudenteaminportisopereius.en: And let her works praise her in the gates.
etlaudenteaminportisopereius.la: Et laudent eam in portis ópera ejus.

laboresmanuumtuarumquiamanducabisbeatuse.en: Thou shalt eat the labours of thine hands; blessed art thou, and happy shalt thou be.
laboresmanuumtuarumquiamanducabisbeatuse.la: Labóres mánuum tuárum quia manducábis, beátus es, et bene tibi erit.

tunosabhosteprotege.en: Do thou protect us from the foe,

ethoramortissuscipe.en: And receive us at the hour of death.

oretvocepiapronobisvirgomaria.en: May the Virgin Mary with loving voice pray for us.
oretvocepiapronobisvirgomaria.la: Oret voce pia pro nobis Virgo María.

inomnitribulationeetangustiasubveniatnob.en: In every tribulation and distress may the loving Virgin Mary succour us.
inomnitribulationeetangustiasubveniatnob.la: In omni tribulatióne et angústia subvéniat nobis pia Virgo Maria.

adsocietatemciviumsupernorumperducatnosr.en: May the Queen of Angels lead us to the fellowship of the citizens above.
adsocietatemciviumsupernorumperducatnosr.la: Ad societátem cívium supernórum perdúcat nos Regína Angelórum.

virgoparenschristiparituradeumgenuistifu.en: O Virgin parent of Christ, thou who wast to bring forth God hast borne him: O shining star of the sea, protect us, defend us:
virgoparenschristiparituradeumgenuistifu.la: Virgo parens Christi, paritúra Deum genuísti: fúlgida stella maris, nos prótege, nos tueáris:

dumparisetgaudescantantceliagminalaudes.en: While thou bringest forth and rejoicest, The hosts of heaven sing praises.
dumparisetgaudescantantceliagminalaudes.la: Dum paris, et gaudes, Cantant cæli ágmina laudes.

intercedepiapronobisvirgomaria.en: Intercede for us, O loving Virgin Mary.
intercedepiapronobisvirgomaria.la: Intercéde pia pro nobis Virgo María.

cantantceliagminalaudes.en: The hosts of heaven sing praises.

avestellamatutinapeccatorummedicinamundi.en: Hail, morning star, medicine of sinners, princess and queen of the world, alone worthy to be called Virgin: against the darts of the enemy set up the shield of salvation, the title of thy virtue. O chosen spouse of God, be thou to us the right way to eternal joys.
avestellamatutinapeccatorummedicinamundi.la: Ave stella matutína, peccatórum medicína, mundi princeps et regína, sola Virgo digna dici: contra tela inimíci clipeum pone salútis, tuæ títulum virtútis. O sponsa Dei elécta, esto nobis via recta ad ætérna gáudia.

sanctamariamaterchristiaudirogantesservu.en: Holy Mary, Mother of Christ, * Hear thy little servants who entreat thee.
sanctamariamaterchristiaudirogantesservu.la: Sancta María, Mater Christi, * Audi rogántes sérvulos.

audirogantesservulos.en: Hear thy little servants who entreat thee.

orapronobissanctadeigenetrix.en: Pray for us, * O holy Mother of God.
orapronobissanctadeigenetrix.la: Ora pro nobis, * Sancta Dei Génetrix.

sanctadeigenetrixsempervirgomaria.en: Holy Mother of God, Mary ever Virgin.
sanctadeigenetrixsempervirgomaria.la: Sancta Dei Génetrix, semper Virgo María.

beatissimevirginismariesolemnitatemdevot.en: Let us most devoutly celebrate the Solemnity of the most blessed Virgin Mary, that she herself may intercede for us with the Lord Jesus Christ.
beatissimevirginismariesolemnitatemdevot.la: Beatíssimæ Vírginis Maríæ Solemnitátem devotíssime celebrémus, ut ipsa pro nobis intercédat ad Dóminum Jesum Christum.

supplicationemservorumtuorumdeusmiserato.en: Graciously hear, O God, in thy mercy, the supplication of thy servants: that we who are gathered together on the Solemnity of the Mother of God and Virgin, may by her intercessions be delivered by thee from the dangers that beset us.
supplicationemservorumtuorumdeusmiserato.la: Supplicatiónem servórum tuórum, Deus, miserátor exáudi: ut, qui in Solemnitáte Dei Genetrícis et Virginis congregámur, cius intercessiónibus a te de instántibus periculis eruámur.

solemnitatemvirginismariecelebremuschris.en: Let us celebrate the Solemnity of the Virgin Mary: Christ, her * Son, let us adore, the Lord.
solemnitatemvirginismariecelebremuschris.la: Solemnitátem Vírginis Maríæ celebrémus: Christum ejus. * Fílium adorémus Dóminum.

hodiesolemnitasestbeatevirginismarieexpr.en: Today is the solemnity of the blessed Virgin Mary, of the offspring of David, through whom the salvation of the world hath appeared to believers:
hodiesolemnitasestbeatevirginismarieexpr.la: Hódie solémnitas est beátæ Vírginis Maríæ ex progénie David, per quam salus mundi credentibus apparuit:

cuiusvitagloriosalucemdeditseculo.en: Whose glorious life gave light to the world.
cuiusvitagloriosalucemdeditseculo.la: Cujus vita gloriósa lucem dedit sǽculo.

beatissimevirginismariesolemnitatemdevot.en: Let us most devoutly celebrate the Solemnity of the most blessed Virgin Mary.
beatissimevirginismariesolemnitatemdevot.la: Beatíssimæ Vírginis Maríæ Solemnitátem devotíssime celebrémus.

gloriosevirginismariesolemnitatemdigniss.en: Let us recall the most worthy solemnity of the glorious Virgin Mary:
gloriosevirginismariesolemnitatemdigniss.la: Gloriósæ Vírginis Maríæ solemnitátem digníssimam recolámus:

vhodiesolemnitasestbeatevirginismarieexp.en: V. Today is the solemnity of the blessed Virgin Mary, of the offspring of David.
vhodiesolemnitasestbeatevirginismarieexp.la: V Hódie solémnitas est beátæ Vírginis Maríæ ex progénie David.

solemnitastuadeigenetrixvirgogaudiumannu.en: Thy solemnity, O Virgin Mother of God, hath announced joy to the whole world:
solemnitastuadeigenetrixvirgogaudiumannu.la: Solémnitas tua, Dei Génetrix Virgo, gáudium annuntiávit univérso mundo:

cumiucunditatesolemnitatembeatemariecele.en: With gladness let us celebrate the Solemnity of blessed Mary.
cumiucunditatesolemnitatembeatemariecele.la: Cum jucunditáte Solemnitátem beátæ Maríæ celebrémus.

solemnitasesthodiesanctemarievirginiscui.en: Today is the solemnity * of holy Mary the Virgin, whose renowned life enlighteneth all the churches.
solemnitasesthodiesanctemarievirginiscui.la: Solémnitas est hódie * sanctæ Maríæ Vírginis, cujus vita ínclita cunctas illústrat ecclésias.

cumiucunditatesolemnitatembeatemariecele.en: With gladness * let us celebrate the Solemnity of blessed Mary, that she herself may intercede for us with the Lord Jesus Christ.
cumiucunditatesolemnitatembeatemariecele.la: Cum jucunditáte * Solemnitátem beátæ Maríæ celebrémus, ut ipsa pro nobis intercédat ad Dóminum Jesum Christum.

egoquasivitisfructificavisuavitatemodori.en: As the vine I have brought forth a pleasant odour: and my flowers are the fruit of honour and riches.
egoquasivitisfructificavisuavitatemodori.la: Ego quasi vitis fructificávi suavitátem odóris: et flores mei fructus honóris et honestátis.

solemnitatemhodiernamperpetuevirginisgen.en: Today's Solemnity * of Mary, the ever-Virgin Mother of God, let us solemnly celebrate, wherein the loftiness of her throne went forth, alleluia.
solemnitatemhodiernamperpetuevirginisgen.la: Solemnitátem hodiérnam * perpétuæ Vírginis Genetrícis Dei Maríæ solémniter celebrémus, qua celsitúdo throni procéssit, allelúja.

transiteadmeomnesquiconcupiscitismeetage.en: Come over to me, all ye that desire me, and be filled with my fruits: for my spirit is sweet above honey, and my inheritance above honey and the honeycomb.
transiteadmeomnesquiconcupiscitismeetage.la: Transíte ad me, omnes qui concupíscitis me, et a generatiónibus meis implémini: spíritus enim meus super mel dulcis, et hæréditas mea super mel et favum.

quiauditmenonconfundeturetquioperanturin.en: He that hearkeneth to me, shall not be confounded: and they that work by me, shall not sin. They that explain me shall have life everlasting.
quiauditmenonconfundeturetquioperanturin.la: Qui audit me, non confundétur, et qui operántur in me, non peccábunt: qui elúcidant me, vitam ætérnam habébunt.

solemnitastuadeigenetrixvirgogaudiumannu.en: Thy solemnity, O Virgin Mother of God, hath announced joy to the whole world: for from thee hath arisen the Sun of justice, Christ our God: who, loosing the curse, hath given the blessing; and confounding death, hath bestowed on us life everlasting.
solemnitastuadeigenetrixvirgogaudiumannu.la: Solémnitas tua, Dei Génetrix Virgo, gáudium annuntiávit univérso mundo: Ex te enim ortus est sol justítiæ, Christus Deus noster: qui, solvens maledictiónem, dedit benedictiónem; et confúndens mortem, donávit nobis vitam sempitérnam.

virgomarianonesttibisimilisnatainmundoin.en: O Virgin Mary, there is none born in the world like unto thee among women, blooming as the rose, fragrant as the lily: pray for us, O holy Mother of God.
virgomarianonesttibisimilisnatainmundoin.la: Virgo María, non est tibi símilis nata in mundo inter mulíeres, florens un rosa, fragrans sicut lílium: ora pro nobis, sancta Dei Génetrix.

cordeetanimochristocanamusgloriaminhacsa.en: With heart and soul let us sing glory to Christ on this sacred solemnity of the most exalted Mother of God, Mary.
cordeetanimochristocanamusgloriaminhacsa.la: Corde et ánimo Christo canámus glóriam in hac sacra solemnitáte præcélsæ Genetrícis Dei María.

predixienimeiquodiudicaturusessemdomumei.en: For I have foretold unto him, that I will judge his house for ever, for iniquity, because he knew that his sons did wickedly, and did not chastise them.
predixienimeiquodiudicaturusessemdomumei.la: Prædíxi enim ei quod iudicatúrus essem domum eius in ætérnum propter iniquitátem, eo quod nóverat indígne ágere fílios suos, et non corripúerit eos.

idcircoiuravidomuiheliquodnonexpieturini.en: Therefore have I sworn to the house of Heli, that the iniquity of his house shall not be expiated with victims nor offerings for ever.
idcircoiuravidomuiheliquodnonexpieturini.la: Idcírco iurávi dómui Heli quod non expiétur iníquitas domus eius víctimis et munéribus usque in ætérnum.

venobisnonenimfuittantexsultatioherietnu.en: Woe to us: for there was no such great joy yesterday, and the day before: Woe to us. Who shall deliver us from the hand of these high Gods? these are the Gods that struck Egypt with all the plagues in the desert.
venobisnonenimfuittantexsultatioherietnu.la: Væ nobis: non enim fuit tanta exsultatio heri et nudiustertius: væ nobis. Quis nos salvabit de manu deorum sublimium istorum? Hi sunt dii, qui percusserunt Ægyptum omni plaga in deserto.

currensautemvirdebeniaminexacievenitinsi.en: And there ran a man of Benjamin out of the army, and came to Silo the same day, with his clothes rent, and his head strewed with dust.
currensautemvirdebeniaminexacievenitinsi.la: Currens autem vir de Benjamin ex acie, venit in Silo in die illa, scissa veste, et conspersus pulvere caput.

cumqueillevenissethelisedebatsupersellam.en: And when he was come, Heli sat upon a stool over against the way, watching. For his heart was fearful for the ark of God. And when the man was come into the city, he told it: and all the city cried out.
cumqueillevenissethelisedebatsupersellam.la: Cumque ille venisset, Heli sedebat super sellam contra viam spectans. Erat enim cor ejus pavens pro arca Dei. Vir autem ille postquam ingressus est, nuntiavit urbi : et ululavit omnis civitas.

etaudivithelisonitumclamorisdixitquequis.en: And Heli heard the noise of the cry, and he said: What meaneth the noise of this uproar? But he made haste, and came, and told Heli.
etaudivithelisonitumclamorisdixitquequis.la: Et audivit Heli sonitum clamoris, dixítque : Quis est hic sonitus tumultus hujus ? At ille festinavit, et venit, et nuntiavit Heli.

heliautemeratnonagintetoctoannorumetocul.en: Now Heli was ninety and eight years old, and his eyes were dim, and he could not see.
heliautemeratnonagintetoctoannorumetocul.la: Heli autem erat nonaginta et octo annorum, et oculi ejus caligaverant, et videre non poterat.

etdixitadheliegosumquivenideprelietegoqu.en: And he said to Heli: I am he that came from the battle, and have fled out of the field this day. And he said to him: What is there done, my son?
etdixitadheliegosumquivenideprelietegoqu.la: Et dixit ad Heli : Ego sum qui veni de prælio, et ego qui de acie fugi hodie. Cui ille ait : Quid actum est, fili mi ?

respondensautemillequinuntiabatfugitinqu.en: And he that brought the news answered, and said: Israel is fled before the Philistines, and there has been a great slaughter of the people: moreover thy two sons, Ophni and Phinees, are dead: and the ark of God is taken.
respondensautemillequinuntiabatfugitinqu.la: Respondens autem ille qui nuntiabat : Fugit, inquit, Israël coram Philisthiim, et ruina magna facta est in populo : insuper et duo filii tui mortui sunt, Ophni et Phinees, et arca Dei capta est.

amiaseaorawhalethatthouhastenclosedmeina.en: Am I a sea, or a whale, that thou hast inclosed me in a prison?
amiaseaorawhalethatthouhastenclosedmeina.la: Am I a sea, or a whale, that thou hast enclosed me in a prison?

notumautemvobisfaciofratresevangeliumquo.en: Now I make known unto you, brethren, the gospel which I preached to you, which also you have received and wherein you stand.
notumautemvobisfaciofratresevangeliumquo.la: Notum autem vobis fácio, fratres, Evangélium, quod prædicávi vobis, quod et accepístis, in quo et statis,

perquodetsalvaminiquarationepredicaverim.en: By which also you are saved, if you hold fast after what manner I preached unto you, unless you have believed in vain.
perquodetsalvaminiquarationepredicaverim.la: per quod et salvámini: qua ratióne prædicáverim vobis, si tenétis, nisi frustra credidístis.

tradidienimvobisinprimisquodetaccepiquon.en: For I delivered unto you first of all, which I also received: how that Christ died for our sins, according to the scriptures:
tradidienimvobisinprimisquodetaccepiquon.la: Trádidi enim vobis in primis quod et accépi: quóniam Christus mórtuus est pro peccátis nostris secúndum Scriptúras:

etquiasepultusestetquiaresurrexittertiad.en: And that he was buried: and that he rose again according to the scriptures:
etquiasepultusestetquiaresurrexittertiad.la: et quia sepúltus est, et quia resurréxit tértia die secúndum Scriptúras:

etquiavisusestcepheetposthocundecim.en: And that he was seen by Cephas, and after that by the eleven.
etquiavisusestcepheetposthocundecim.la: et quia visus est Cephæ, et post hoc úndecim:

deindevisusestplusquamquingentisfratribu.en: Then was he seen by more than five hundred brethren at once: of whom many remain until this present, and some are fallen asleep.
deindevisusestplusquamquingentisfratribu.la: deínde visus est plus quam quingéntis frátribus simul: ex quibus multi manent usque adhuc, quidam autem dormiérunt:

deindevisusestiacobodeindeapostolisomnib.en: After that, he was seen by James: then by all the apostles.
deindevisusestiacobodeindeapostolisomnib.la: Deínde visus est Jacóbo, deínde Apóstolis ómnibus:

novissimeautemomniumtamquamabortivovisus.en: And last of all, he was seen also by me, as by one born out of due tine.
novissimeautemomniumtamquamabortivovisus.la: novíssime autem ómnium tamquam abortívo, visus est et mihi.
