egenimsumminimusapostolorumquinonsumdign.en: For I am the least of the apostles, who am not worthy to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of God.
egenimsumminimusapostolorumquinonsumdign.la: Ego enim sum mínimus Apostolórum, qui non sum dignus vocári Apóstolus, quóniam persecútus sum Ecclésiam Dei.

gratiaautemdeisumidquodsumetgratieiusinm.en: But by the grace of God, I am what I am. And his grace in me hath not been void: but I have laboured more abundantly than all they. Yet not I, but the grace of God with me:
gratiaautemdeisumidquodsumetgratieiusinm.la: Grátia autem Dei sum id quod sum, et grátia ejus in me vácua non fuit, sed abundántius illis ómnibus laborávi: non ego autem, sed grátia Dei mecum:

siveenimegosiveillisicpredicamusetsiccre.en: For whether I or they, so we preach: and so you have believed.
siveenimegosiveillisicpredicamusetsiccre.la: sive enim ego, sive illi: sic prædicámus, et sic credidístis.

siautemchristuspredicaturquodresurrexita.en: Now if Christ be preached, that he arose again from the dead, how do some among you say that there is no resurrection of the dead?
siautemchristuspredicaturquodresurrexita.la: Si autem Christus prædicátur quod resurréxit a mórtuis, quómodo quidam dicunt in vobis, quóniam resurréctio mortuórum non est?

factumestautemcumapollessetcorinthiutpau.en: And it came to pass, while Apollo was at Corinth, that Paul, having passed through the upper coasts, came to Ephesus and found certain disciples.
factumestautemcumapollessetcorinthiutpau.la: Factum est autem cum Apóllo esset Corínthi, ut Paulus peragrátis superióribus pártibus veníret Ephesum, et inveníret quosdam discípulos:

dixitqueadeossispiritumsanctumaccepistis.en: And he said to them: Have you received the Holy Ghost since ye believed? But they said to him: We have not so much as heard whether there be a Holy Ghost.
dixitqueadeossispiritumsanctumaccepistis.la: dixítque ad eos: Si Spíritum Sanctum accepístis credéntes? At illi dixérunt ad eum: Sed neque si Spíritus Sanctus est, audívimus.

illeveroaitinquergobaptizatiestisquidixe.en: And he said: In what then were you baptized? Who said: In John's baptism.
illeveroaitinquergobaptizatiestisquidixe.la: Ille vero ait: In quo ergo baptizáti estis? Qui dixérunt: In Ioánnis baptísmate.

dixitautempaulusioannesbaptizavitbaptism.en: Then Paul said: John baptized the people with the baptism of penance saying: That they should believe in him, who was to come after him, that is to say, in Jesus.
dixitautempaulusioannesbaptizavitbaptism.la: Dixit autem Paulus: Joánnes baptizávit baptísmo pœniténtiæ pópulum, dicens in eum qui ventúrus esset post ipsum ut créderent, hoc est, in Jesum.

hisauditisbaptizatisuntinnominedominiies.en: Having heard these things, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
hisauditisbaptizatisuntinnominedominiies.la: His audítis, baptizáti sunt in nómine Dómini Jesu.

etcumimposuissetillismanuspaulusvenitspi.en: And when Paul had imposed his hands on them, the Holy Ghost came upon them: and they spoke with tongues and prophesied.
etcumimposuissetillismanuspaulusvenitspi.la: Et cum imposuísset illis manus Paulus, venit Spíritus Sanctus super eos, et loquebántur linguis, et prophetábant.

erantautemomnesvirifereduodecim.en: And all the men were about twelve.
erantautemomnesvirifereduodecim.la: Erant autem omnes viri fere duódecim.

introgressusautemsynagogamcumfiducialoqu.en: And entering into the synagogue, he spoke boldly for the space of three months, disputing and exhorting concerning the kingdom of God.
introgressusautemsynagogamcumfiducialoqu.la: Introgréssus autem synagógam, cum fidúcia loquebátur per tres menses, dísputans et suádens de regno Dei.

cumautemquidamindurarenturetnoncrederent.en: But when some were hardened and believed not, speaking evil of the way of the Lord before the multitude, departing from them, he separated the disciples, disputing daily in the school of one Tyrannus.
cumautemquidamindurarenturetnoncrederent.la: Cum autem quidam induraréntur, et non créderent, maledicéntes viam Dómini coram multitúdine, discédens ab eis, segregávit discípulos, quotídie dísputans in schola tyránni cujúsdam.

vidisubtusaltareanimasinterfectorumpropt.en: And when he had opened the fifth seal, I saw under the altar the souls of them that were slain for the word of God and for the testimony which they held.
vidisubtusaltareanimasinterfectorumpropt.la: Vidi subtus altáre ánimas interfectórum propter verbum Dei, et propter testimónium, quod habébant:

etclamabantvocemagnadicentesusquequodomi.en: And they cried with a loud voice, saying: How long, O Lord (Holy and True), dost thou not judge and revenge our blood on them that dwell on the earth?
etclamabantvocemagnadicentesusquequodomi.la: et clamábant voce magna, dicéntes: Usquequo Dómine (sanctus et verus), non júdicas, et non víndicas sánguinem nostrum de iis qui hábitant in terra?

etdatesuntillissingulestolealbeetdictume.en: And white robes were given to every one of them one; And it was said to them that they should rest for a little time till their fellow servants and their brethren, who are to be slain even as they, should be filled up.
etdatesuntillissingulestolealbeetdictume.la: Et datæ sunt illis síngulæ stolæ albæ: et dictum est illis ut requiéscerent adhuc tempus módicum donec compleántur consérvi eórum, et fratres eórum, qui interficiéndi sunt sicut et illi.

ideosuntantethronumdeietserviunteidieacn.en: Therefore, they are before the throne of God: and they serve him day and night in his temple. And he that sitteth on the throne shall dwell over them.
ideosuntantethronumdeietserviunteidieacn.la: Ideo sunt ante thronum Dei, et sérviunt ei die ac nocte in templo ejus: et qui sedet in throno, habitábit super illos:

nonesurientnequesitientampliusneccadetsu.en: They shall no more hunger nor thirst: neither shall the sun fall on them, nor any heat.
nonesurientnequesitientampliusneccadetsu.la: non esúrient, neque sítient ámplius, nec cadet super illos sol, neque ullus æstus:

quoniamagnusquiinmediothroniestregetillo.en: For the Lamb, which is in the midst of the throne, shall rule them and shall lead them to the fountains of the waters of life: and God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes.
quoniamagnusquiinmediothroniestregetillo.la: quóniam Agnus, qui in médio throni est, reget illos et dedúcet eos ad vitæ fontes aquárum, et abstérget Deus omnem lácrymam ab óculis eórum.

etproiectusestdracoillemagnusserpensanti.en: And that great dragon was cast out, that old serpent, who is called the devil and Satan, who seduceth the whole world. And he was cast unto the earth: and his angels were thrown down with him.
etproiectusestdracoillemagnusserpensanti.la: Et projéctus est draco ille magnus, serpens antíquus, qui vocátur diábolus, et Sátanas, qui sedúcit univérsum orbem: et projéctus est in terram, et ángeli ejus cum illo missi sunt.

etaudivivocemmagnamincelodicentemnuncfac.en: And I heard a loud voice in heaven, saying: Now is come salvation and strength and the kingdom of our God and the power of his Christ: because the accuser of our brethren is cast forth, who accused them before our God day and night.
etaudivivocemmagnamincelodicentemnuncfac.la: Et audívi vocem magnam in cælo dicéntem: Nunc facta est salus, et virtus, et regnum Dei nostri, et potéstas Christi ejus: quia projéctus est accusátor fratrum nostrórum, qui accusábat illos ante conspéctum Dei nostri die ac nocte.

etipsivicerunteumproptersanguinemagnietp.en: And they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of the testimony: and they loved not their lives unto death.
etipsivicerunteumproptersanguinemagnietp.la: Et ipsi vicérunt eum propter sánguinem Agni, et propter verbum testimónii sui, et non dilexérunt ánimas suas usque ad mortem.

ethicbibetdevinoiredeiquodmistumestmeroi.en: He also shall drink of the wine of the wrath of God, which is mingled with pure wine in the cup of his wrath: and shall be tormented with fire and brimstone in the sight of the holy angels and in the sight of the Lamb.
ethicbibetdevinoiredeiquodmistumestmeroi.la: et hic bibet de vino iræ Dei, quod mistum est mero in cálice iræ ipsíus, et cruciábitur igne, et súlphure in conspéctu angelórum sanctórum, et ante conspéctum Agni:

etfumustormentorumeorumascendetinseculas.en: And the smoke of their torments, shall ascend up for ever and ever: neither have they rest day nor night, who have adored the beast and his image and whoever receiveth the character of his name.
etfumustormentorumeorumascendetinseculas.la: et fumus tormentórum eórum ascéndet in sǽcula sæculórum: nec habent réquiem die ac nocte, qui adoravérunt béstiam, et imáginem ejus, et si quis accéperit charactérem nóminis ejus.

hicpatientiasanctorumestquicustodiuntman.en: Here is the patience of the saints, who keep the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus.
hicpatientiasanctorumestquicustodiuntman.la: Hic patiéntia sanctórum est, qui custódiunt mandáta Dei, et fidem Jesu.

etfactumestverbumdominiadeliasthesbitend.en: And the word of the Lord came to him, saying:
etfactumestverbumdominiadeliasthesbitend.la: Et factum est verbum Dómini ad Elías Thesbíten, dicens:

recedehincetvadecontraorientemetabsconde.en: Get thee hence, and go towards the east, and hide thyself by the torrent of Carith, which is over against the Jordan;
recedehincetvadecontraorientemetabsconde.la: Recéde hinc, et vade contra oriéntem, et abscóndere in torrénte Carith, qui est contra Jordánem,

etibidetorrentebibescorvisqueprecepiutpa.en: And there thou shalt drink of the torrent: and I have commanded the ravens to feed thee there.
etibidetorrentebibescorvisqueprecepiutpa.la: et ibi de torrénte bibes: corvísque præcépi ut pascant te ibi.

abiitergetfecitiuxtaverbumdominicumqueab.en: So he went, and did according to the word of the Lord: and going, he dwelt by the torrent Carith, which is over against the Jordan.
abiitergetfecitiuxtaverbumdominicumqueab.la: Abiit ergo, et fecit juxta verbum Dómini: cumque abiísset, sedit in torrénte Carith, qui est contra Jordánem.

corviquoquedeferebanteipanemetcarnesmane.en: And the ravens brought him bread and flesh in the morning, and bread and flesh in the evening; and he drank of the torrent.
corviquoquedeferebanteipanemetcarnesmane.la: Corvi quoque deferébant ei panem et carnes mane, simíliter panem et carnes vésperi, et bibébat de torrénte.

postdiesautemsiccatusesttorrensnonenimpl.en: But after some time the torrent was dried up: for it had not rained upon the earth.
postdiesautemsiccatusesttorrensnonenimpl.la: Post dies autem siccátus est torrens: non enim plúerat super terram.

factusestergosermodominiadeumdicens.en: Then the word of the Lord came to him, saying:
factusestergosermodominiadeumdicens.la: Factus est ergo sermo Dómini ad eum, dicens:

surgeetvadeinsarephtasidoniorumetmanebis.en: Arise, and go to Sarephta of the Sidonians, and dwell there: for I have commanded a widow woman there to feed thee.
surgeetvadeinsarephtasidoniorumetmanebis.la: Surge, et vade in Saréphta Sidoniórum, et manébis ibi: præcépi enim ibi mulíeri víduæ ut pascat te.

surrexitetabiitinsarephtacumquevenisseta.en: He arose, and went to Sarephta. And when he was come to the gate of the city, he saw the widow woman gathering sticks, and he called her, and said to her: Give me a little water in a vessel, that I may drink.
surrexitetabiitinsarephtacumquevenisseta.la: Surréxit, et ábiit in Saréphta. Cumque venísset ad portam civitátis, appáruit ei múlier vídua cólligens ligna, et vocávit eam, dixítque ei: Da mihi páululum aquæ in vase ut bibam.

cumqueillapergeretutafferretclamavitpost.en: And Elias said to her: Give me thy son. And he took him out of her bosom, and carried him into the upper chamber where he abode, and laid him upon his own bed.
cumqueillapergeretutafferretclamavitpost.la: Cumque illa pérgeret ut afférret, clamávit post tergum ejus, dicens: Affer mihi, óbsecro, et buccéllam panis in manu tua.

queresponditvivitdominusdeustuusquianonh.en: And she answered: As the Lord thy God liveth, I have no bread, but only a handful of meal in a pot, and a little oil in a cruise: behold I am gathering two sticks, that I may go in and dress it, for me and my son, that we may eat it and die.
queresponditvivitdominusdeustuusquianonh.la: Quæ respóndit: Vivit Dóminus Deus tuus, quia non hábeo panem, nisi quantum pugíllus cápere potest farínæ in hýdria, et páululum ólei in lécytho: en cólligo duo ligna ut ingrédiar et fáciam illum mihi et fílio meo, ut comedámus, et moriámur.

adquameliasaitnolitimeresedvadeetfacsicu.en: And Elias said to her: Fear not; but go, and do as thou hast said but first make for me of the same meal a little hearth cake, and bring it to me, and after make for thyself and thy son.
adquameliasaitnolitimeresedvadeetfacsicu.la: Ad quam Elías ait: Noli timére, sed vade, et fac sicut dixísti: verúmtamen mihi primum fac de ipsa farínula subcinerícium panem párvulum, et affer ad me: tibi autem et fílio tuo fácies póstea.

hecautemdicitdominusdeusisrelhydriafarin.en: For thus saith the Lord, the God of Israel: The pot of meal shall not waste, nor the cruise of oil be diminished, until the day wherein the Lord will give rain upon the face of the earth.
hecautemdicitdominusdeusisrelhydriafarin.la: Hæc autem dicit Dóminus Deus Israël: Hýdria farínæ non defíciet, nec lécythus ólei minuétur, usque ad diem in qua Dóminus datúrus est plúviam super fáciem terræ.

queabiitetfecitiuxtaverbumelieetcomediti.en: She went, and did according to the word of Elias: and he ate, and she, and her house: and from that day
queabiitetfecitiuxtaverbumelieetcomediti.la: Quæ ábiit, et fecit juxta verbum Elíæ: et comédit ipse, et illa, et domus ejus: et ex illa die

hydriafarinenondefecitetlecythusoleinone.en: The pot of meal wasted not, and the cruise of oil was not diminished according to the word of the Lord, which he spoke in the hand of Elias.
hydriafarinenondefecitetlecythusoleinone.la: hýdria farínæ non defécit, et lécythus ólei non est imminútus, juxta verbum Dómini quod locútus fúerat in manu Elíæ.

factumestautemposthecegrotavitfiliusmuli.en: And it came to pass after this, that the son of the woman, the mistress of the house, fell sick, and the sickness was very grievous, so that there was no breath left in him.
factumestautemposthecegrotavitfiliusmuli.la: Factum est autem post hæc, ægrotávit fílius mulíeris matrisfamílias, et erat languor fortíssimus, ita ut non remanéret in eo hálitus.

dixitergoadeliamquidmihiettibivirdeiingr.en: And she said to Elias: What have I to do with thee, thou man of God? art thou come to me, that my iniquities should be remembered, and that thou shouldst kill my son?
dixitergoadeliamquidmihiettibivirdeiingr.la: Dixit ergo ad Elíam: Quid mihi et tibi, vir Dei? ingréssus es ad me, ut rememoraréntur iniquitátes meæ, et interfíceres fílium meum?

etclamavitaddominumetdixitdominedeusmeus.en: And he cried to the Lord, and said: O Lord, my God, hast thou afflicted also the widow, with whom I am after a sort maintained, so as to kill her son?
etclamavitaddominumetdixitdominedeusmeus.la: Et clamávit ad Dóminum, et dixit: Dómine Deus meus, etiámne víduam apud quam ego utcúmque susténtor, afflixísti ut interfíceres fílium ejus?

etexpanditseatquemensusestsuperpuerumtri.en: And he stretched, and measured himself upon the child three times, and cried to the Lord, and said: O Lord, my God, let the soul of this child, I beseech thee, return into his body.
etexpanditseatquemensusestsuperpuerumtri.la: Et expándit se, atque mensus est super púerum tribus vícibus, et clamávit ad Dóminum, et ait: Dómine Deus meus, revertátur, óbsecro, ánima púeri hujus in víscera ejus.

etexaudivitdominusvocemelieetreversestan.en: And the Lord heard the voice of Elias: and the soul of the child returned into him, and he revived.
etexaudivitdominusvocemelieetreversestan.la: Et exaudívit Dóminus vocem Elíæ: et revérsa est ánima púeri intra eum, et revíxit.

tulitqueeliaspuerumetdeposuiteumdecenacu.en: And Elias took the child, and brought him down from the upper chamber to the house below, and delivered him to his mother, and said to her: Behold thy son liveth.
tulitqueeliaspuerumetdeposuiteumdecenacu.la: Tulítque Elías púerum, et depósuit eum de cœnáculo in inferiórem domum, et trádidit matri suæ, et ait illi: En vivit fílius tuus.

dixitquemulieradeliamnuncinistocognoviqu.en: And the woman said to Elias: Now by this I know that thou art a man of God, and the word of the Lord in thy mouth is true.
dixitquemulieradeliamnuncinistocognoviqu.la: Dixítque múlier ad Elíam: Nunc in isto cognóvi quóniam vir Dei es tu, et verbum Dómini in ore tuo verum est.

numquidnonvidistiquidpopulushiclocutussi.en: Hast thou not seen what this people hath spoken, saying: The two families which the Lord had chosen, are cast off: and they have despised my people, so that it is no more a nation before them?
numquidnonvidistiquidpopulushiclocutussi.la: Numquid non vidísti quid pópulus hic locútus sit, dicens: Duæ cognatiónes quas elégerat Dóminus abiéctæ sunt: et pópulum meum despexérunt, eo quod non sit ultra gens coram eis?

hecdicitdominussipactummeuminterdiemetno.en: Thus saith the Lord. If I have not set my covenant between day and night, and laws to heaven and earth:
hecdicitdominussipactummeuminterdiemetno.la: Hæc dicit Dóminus: Si pactum meum inter diem et noctem, et leges cælo et terræ non pósui:

equidemetsemeniacobetdavidservimeiproici.en: Surely I will also cast off the seed of Jacob, and of David my servant, so as not to take any of his seed to be rulers of the seed of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob: for I will bring back their captivity, and will have mercy on them.
equidemetsemeniacobetdavidservimeiproici.la: équidem et semen Jacob et David servi mei proíciam, ut non assúmam de sémine ejus príncipes séminis , Isaac, et Jacob: redúcam enim conversiónem eórum, et miserébor eis.

nomenuniphisonipseestquicircuitomnemterr.en: The name of the one is Phison: that is it which compasseth all the land of Hevilath, where gold groweth.
nomenuniphisonipseestquicircuitomnemterr.la: Nomen uni Phison: ipse est qui círcuit omnem terram Hevílath, ubi náscitur aurum:

etaurumterreilliusoptimumestibiinvenitur.en: And the gold of that land is very good: there is found bdellium, and the onyx stone.
etaurumterreilliusoptimumestibiinvenitur.la: et aurum terræ illíus óptimum est; ibi invenítur bdéllium, et lapis onýchinus.

fecitquoquedominusdeusadeetuxorieiustuni.en: And the Lord God made for Adam and his wife garments of skins, and clothed them.
fecitquoquedominusdeusadeetuxorieiustuni.la: Fecit quoque Dóminus Deus Adæ et uxóri eius túnicas pellíceas, et índuit eos:

etaitecceadamquasiunusexnobisfactusestsc.en: And he said: Behold Adam is become as one of us, knowing good and evil: now therefore lest perhaps he put forth his hand and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever.
etaitecceadamquasiunusexnobisfactusestsc.la: Et ait: Ecce Adam quasi unus ex nobis factus est, sciens bonum et malum: nunc ergo ne forte mittat manum suam, et sumat étiam de ligno vitæ, et cómedat, et vivat in ætérnum.

ingressestitaquebethsabeeadregemincubicu.en: So Bethsabee went in to the king into the chamber. Now the king was very old, and Abisag, the Sunamitess, ministered to him.
ingressestitaquebethsabeeadregemincubicu.la: Ingréssa est ítaque Bethsabée ad regem in cubículo: rex autem senúerat nimis, et Abísag Sunamítis ministrábat ei.

inclinavitsebethsabeeetadoravitregemadqu.en: Bethsabee bowed herself, and worshipped the king. And the king said to her: What is thy will?
inclinavitsebethsabeeetadoravitregemadqu.la: inclinávit se Bethsabée, et adorávit regem. Ad quam rex, Quid tibi, inquit, vis?

querespondensaitdominemituiurastiperdomi.en: She answered, and said: My lord, thou didst swear to thy handmaid, by the Lord thy God, saying: Solomon, thy son, shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne.
querespondensaitdominemituiurastiperdomi.la: Quæ respóndens, ait: Dómine mi, tu iurásti per Dóminum Deum tuum ancíllæ tuæ, Sálomon fílius tuus regnábit post me, et ipse sedébit in sólio meo.

eteccenuncadoniasregnattedominemirexigno.en: And behold, now Adonias reigneth, and thou, my lord the king, knowest nothing of it.
eteccenuncadoniasregnattedominemirexigno.la: Et ecce nunc Adonías regnat, te, dómine mi rex, ignoránte.

quesivitlanametlinumetoperatestconsiliom.en: She hath sought wool and flax, and hath wrought by the counsel of her hands.
quesivitlanametlinumetoperatestconsiliom.la: Quæsívit lanam et linum, et operáta est consílio mánuum suárum.

exemplumestofideliuminverboinconversatio.en: Let no man despise thy youth: but be thou an example of the faithful, in word, in conversation, in charity, in faith, in chastity.
exemplumestofideliuminverboinconversatio.la: Exémplum esto fidélium in verbo, in conversatióne, in charitáte, in fide, in castitáte.

dumvenioattendelectioniexhortationietdoc.en: Till I come, attend unto reading, to exhortation and to doctrine.
dumvenioattendelectioniexhortationietdoc.la: Dum vénio, atténde lectióni, exhortatióni, et doctrínæ.

nolinegligeregratiamqueinteestquedatestt.en: Neglect not the grace that is in thee, which was given thee by prophecy, with imposition of the hands of the priesthood.
nolinegligeregratiamqueinteestquedatestt.la: Noli neglígere grátiam, quæ in te est, quæ data est tibi per prophetíam, cum impositióne mánuum presbytérii.

hecmeditareinhisestoutprofectustuusmanif.en: Meditate upon these things, be wholly in these things: that thy profiting may be manifest to all.
hecmeditareinhisestoutprofectustuusmanif.la: Hæc meditáre, in his esto: ut proféctus tuus maniféstus sit ómnibus.

attendetibietdoctrineinstainillishocenim.en: Take heed to thyself and to doctrine: be earnest in them. For in doing this thou shalt both save thyself and them that hear thee.
attendetibietdoctrineinstainillishocenim.la: Atténde tibi, et doctrínæ: insta in illis. Hoc enim fáciens, et teípsum salvum fácies, et eos qui te áudiunt.

etresponditangelusdominietdixitdomineexe.en: And the angel of the Lord answered, and said: O Lord of hosts, how long wilt thou not have mercy on Jerusalem, and on the cities of Juda, with which thou hast been angry? this is now the seventieth year.
etresponditangelusdominietdixitdomineexe.la: Et respóndit Angelus Dómini, et dixit: Dómine exercítuum, úsquequo tu non miseréberis Jerúsalem, et úrbium Juda, quibus irátus es? iste jam septuagésimus annus est.

precipiotibicoramdeoquivivificatomnietch.en: I charge thee before God who quickeneth all things, and before Christ Jesus who gave testimony under Pontius Pilate, a good confession:
precipiotibicoramdeoquivivificatomnietch.la: Præcípio tibi coram Deo, qui vivíficat ómnia, et Christo Jesu, qui testimónium réddidit sub Póntio Piláto, bonam confessiónem,

utservesmandatumsinemaculairreprehensibi.en: That thou keep the commandment without spot, blameless, unto the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ,
utservesmandatumsinemaculairreprehensibi.la: ut serves mandátum sine mácula, irreprehensíbile usque in advéntum Dómini nostri Jesu Christi,

quemsuistemporibusostendetbeatusetsolusp.en: Which in his times he shall shew, who is the Blessed and only Mighty, the King of kings and Lord of lords:
quemsuistemporibusostendetbeatusetsolusp.la: quem suis tempóribus osténdet beátus et solus potens, Rex regum, et Dóminus dominántium:

quisolushabetimmortalitatemetluceminhabi.en: Who only hath immortality and inhabiteth light inaccessible: whom no man hath seen, nor can see: to whom be honour and empire everlasting. Amen.
quisolushabetimmortalitatemetluceminhabi.la: qui solus habet immortalitátem, et lucem inhábitat inaccessíbilem: quem nullus hóminum vidit, sed nec vidére potest: cui honor, et impérium sempitérnum. Amen.

tuncsummiseruntvirosquidicerentseaudivis.en: Then they suborned men to say they had heard him speak words of blasphemy against Moses and against God.
tuncsummiseruntvirosquidicerentseaudivis.la: Tunc summisérunt viros, qui dícerent se audivísse eum dicéntem verba blasphémiæ in Móysen et in Deum.

commoveruntitaqueplebemetsenioresetscrib.en: And they stirred up the people and the ancients and the scribes. And running together, they took him and brought him to the council.
commoveruntitaqueplebemetsenioresetscrib.la: Commovérunt ítaque plebem, et senióres, et Scribas : et concurréntes rapuérunt eum, et adduxérunt in concílium,

etstatueruntfalsostestesquidicerenthomoi.en: And they set up false witnesses, who said: This man ceaseth not to speak words against the holy place and the law.
etstatueruntfalsostestesquidicerenthomoi.la: et statuérunt falsos testes, qui dícerent : Homo iste non cessat loqui verba advérsus locum sanctum, et legem:

audivimusenimeumdicentemquoniamiesusnaza.en: For we have heard him say that this Jesus of Nazareth shall destroy this place and shall change the traditions which Moses delivered unto us.
audivimusenimeumdicentemquoniamiesusnaza.la: Audívimus enim eum dicéntem: Quóniam Jesus Nazarénus hic déstruet locum istum, et mutábit traditiónes, quas trádidit nobis Móyses.

etintuenteseumomnesquisedebantinconcilio.en: And all that sat in the council, looking on him, saw his face as if it had been the face of an angel.
etintuenteseumomnesquisedebantinconcilio.la: Et intuéntes eum omnes qui sedébant in concílio, vidérunt fáciem ejus tamquam fáciem Angeli.

proptereacaptivusductusestpopulusmeusqui.en: Therefore is my people led away captive, because they had not knowledge, and their nobles have perished with famine, and their multitude were dried up with thirst.
proptereacaptivusductusestpopulusmeusqui.la: Proptérea captívus ductus est pópulus meus, quia non hábuit sciéntiam, et nóbiles ejus interiérunt fame, et multitúdo ejus siti exáruit.

proptereadilatavitinfernusanimamsuametap.en: Therefore hath hell enlarged her soul, and opened her mouth without any bounds, and their strong ones, and their people, and their high and glorious ones shall go down into it.
proptereadilatavitinfernusanimamsuametap.la: Proptérea dilatávit inférnus ánimam suam, et apéruit os suum absque ullo término: et descéndent fortes ejus, et pópulus ejus, et sublímes gloriosíque ejus ad eum.

etincurvabiturhomethumiliabiturviretocul.en: And man shall be brought down, and man shall be humbled, and the eyes of the lofty shall be brought low.
etincurvabiturhomethumiliabiturviretocul.la: Et incurvábitur homo, et humiliábitur vir, et óculi sublímium depriméntur.

etexaltabiturdominusexercituuminiudiciet.en: And the Lord of hosts shall be exalted in judgment, and the holy God shall be sanctified in justice.
etexaltabiturdominusexercituuminiudiciet.la: Et exaltábitur Dóminus exercítuum in judício: et Deus sanctus sanctificábitur in justítia.

etpascenturagniiuxtaordinemsuumetdeserta.en: And the lambs shall feed according to their order, and strangers shall eat the deserts turned into fruitfulness.
etpascenturagniiuxtaordinemsuumetdeserta.la: Et pascéntur agni juxta órdinem suum, et desérta in ubertátem versa ádvenæ cómedent.

vequitrahitisiniquitateminfuniculisvanit.en: Woe to you that draw iniquity with cords of vanity, and sin as the rope of a cart.
vequitrahitisiniquitateminfuniculisvanit.la: Væ qui tráhitis iniquitátem in funículis vanitátis, et quasi vínculum plaustri peccátum.

quidicitisfestinetetcitoveniatopuseiusut.en: That say: Let him make haste, and let his work come quickly, that we may see it: and let the counsel of the Holy One of Israel come, that we may know it.
quidicitisfestinetetcitoveniatopuseiusut.la: Qui dícitis: Festínet, et cito véniat opus ejus, ut videámus: et apprópiet, et véniat consílium sancti Israël, et sciémus illud.

vequidicitismalumbonumetbonummalumponent.en: Woe to you that call evil good, and good evil: that put darkness for light, and light for darkness: that put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter.
vequidicitismalumbonumetbonummalumponent.la: Væ qui dícitis malum bonum, et bonum malum: ponéntes ténebras lucem, et lucem ténebras: ponéntes amárum in dulce, et dulce in amárum.

vequisapientesestisinoculisvestrisetcora.en: Woe to you that are wise in your own eyes, and prudent in your own conceits.
vequisapientesestisinoculisvestrisetcora.la: Væ qui sapiéntes estis in óculis vestris, et coram vobismetípsis prudéntes.

indieillavisitabitdominusingladiosuodure.en: In that day the Lord with his hard, and great, and strong sword shall visit leviathan the bar serpent, and leviathan the crooked serpent, and shall slay the whale that is in the sea.
indieillavisitabitdominusingladiosuodure.la: In die illa visitábit Dóminus in gládio suo duro, et grandi, et forti, super Levíathan, serpéntem vectem, et super Levíathan, serpéntem tortuósum, et occídet cetum qui in mari est.

egodominusquiserveamrepentepropinabeinef.en: I am the Lord that keep it, I will suddenly give it drink: lest any hurt come to it, I keep it night and day.
egodominusquiserveamrepentepropinabeinef.la: Ego Dóminus qui servo eam: repénte propinábo ei. Ne forte visitétur contra eam, nocte et die servo eam.

eteriteisverbumdominimandaremandamandare.en: And the word of the Lord shall be to them: Command, command again; command, command again; expect, expect again; a little there, a little there: that they may go, and fall backward, and be broken, and snared, and taken.
eteriteisverbumdominimandaremandamandare.la: Et erit eis verbum Dómini: Manda remánda, manda remánda, exspécta reexspécta, exspécta reexspécta, módicum ibi, módicum ibi: ut vadant, et cadant retrórsum, et conterántur, et illaqueéntur, et capiántur.

hecdicitdominusdeussanctusisrelsireverta.en: For thus saith the Lord God the Holy One of Israel: If you return and be quiet, you shall be saved: in silence and in hope shall your strength be. And you would not:
hecdicitdominusdeussanctusisrelsireverta.la: Hæc dicit Dóminus Deus sanctus Israël: Si revertámini et quiescátis, salvi éritis: in siléntio et in spe erit fortitúdo vestra. Et noluístis:

etdixistisnequaquamsedadequosfugiemuside.en: But have said: No, but we will flee to horses: therefore shall you flee. And we will mount upon swift ones: therefore shall they be swifter that shall pursue after you.
etdixistisnequaquamsedadequosfugiemuside.la: et dixístis: Nequáquam, sed ad equos fugiémus: ídeo fugiétis. Et super velóces ascendémus: ídeo velocióres erunt, qui persequéntur vos.

millehominesafacieterrorisuniusetafaciet.en: A thousand men shall flee for fear of one: and for fear of five shall you flee, till you be left as the mast of ship on the top of a mountain, and as an ensign upon a hill.
millehominesafacieterrorisuniusetafaciet.la: Mille hómines a fácie terróris uníus: et a fácie terróris quinque fugiétis, donec relinquámini quasi malus navis in vértice montis, et quasi signum super collem.

etnunchecdicitdominuscreansteiacobetform.en: And now thus saith the Lord that created thee, O Jacob, and formed thee, O Israel: Fear not, for I have redeemed thee, and called thee by thy name: thou art mine.
etnunchecdicitdominuscreansteiacobetform.la: Et nunc hæc dicit Dóminus creans te Jacob, et formans te Israël: Noli timére, quia redémi te, et vocávi te nómine tuo: meus es tu.

cumtransierisperaquastecumeretfluminanon.en: When thou shalt pass through the waters, I will be with thee, and the rivers shall not cover thee: when thou shalt walk in the fire, thou shalt not be burnt, and the flames shall not burn in thee:
cumtransierisperaquastecumeretfluminanon.la: Cum transíeris per aquas, tecum ero, et flúmina non opérient te: cum ambuláveris in igne, non comburéris, et flamma non ardébit in te.

quiegodominusdeustuussanctusisrelsalvato.en: For I am the Lord thy God, the Holy One of Israel, thy Saviour: I have given Egypt for thy atonement, Ethiopia and Saba for thee.
quiegodominusdeustuussanctusisrelsalvato.la: Quia ego Dóminus Deus tuus sanctus Israël salvátor tuus, dedi propitiatiónem tuam Ægýptum, Æthiópiam, et Saba pro te.

exquohonorabilisfactusesinoculismeisetgl.en: Since thou becamest honourable in my eyes, thou art glorious: I have loved thee, and I will give men for thee, and people for thy life.
exquohonorabilisfactusesinoculismeisetgl.la: Ex quo honorábilis factus es in óculis meis, et gloriósus, ego diléxi te, et dabo hómines pro te, et pópulos pro ánima tua.

nolitimerequiegotecumsumaborienteadducam.en: Fear not, for I am with thee: I will bring thy seed from the east, and gather thee from the west.
nolitimerequiegotecumsumaborienteadducam.la: Noli timére, quia ego tecum sum: ab oriénte addúcam semen tuum, et ab occidénte congregábo te.

dicamaquilonidetaustronoliprohibereaffer.en: I will say to the north: Give up: and to the south: Keep not back: bring my sons from afar, and my daughters from the ends of the earth.
dicamaquilonidetaustronoliprohibereaffer.la: Dicam aquilóni: Da: et austro: Noli prohibére: affer fílios meos de longínquo, et fílias meas ab extrémis terræ.

etomnemquiinvocatnomenmeumingloriammeamc.en: And every one that calleth upon my name, I have created him for my glory. I have formed him, and made him.
etomnemquiinvocatnomenmeumingloriammeamc.la: Et omnem qui ínvocat nomen meum, in glóriam meam creávi eum, formávi eum, et feci eum.

educforaspopulumcecumetoculoshabentemsur.en: Bring forth the people that are blind, and have eyes: that are deaf, and have ears.
educforaspopulumcecumetoculoshabentemsur.la: Educ foras pópulum cæcum, et óculos habéntem: surdum, et aures ei sunt.

omnesgentescongregatesuntsimuletcollecte.en: All the nations are assembled together, and the tribes are gathered: who among you can declare this, and shall make us hear the former things? let them bring forth their witnesses, let them be justified, and hear, and say: It is truth.
omnesgentescongregatesuntsimuletcollecte.la: Omnes gentes congregátæ sunt simul, et colléctæ sunt tribus: quis in vobis annúntiet istud, et quæ prima sunt audíre nos fáciet? Dent testes eórum.

laudasterilisquenonparisdecantalaudemeth.en: Give praise, O thou barren, that bearest not: sing forth praise, and make a joyful noise, thou that didst not travail with child: for many are the children of the desolate, more than of her that hath a husband, saith the Lord.
laudasterilisquenonparisdecantalaudemeth.la: Lauda stérilis quæ non paris: decánta laudem, et hinni quæ non pariébas: quóniam multi fílii desértæ magis quam eius quæ habet virum, dicit Dóminus.

dilatalocumtentoriituietpellestabernacul.en: Enlarge the place of thy tent, and stretch out the skins of thy tabernacles, spare not: lengthen thy cords, and strengthen thy stakes.
dilatalocumtentoriituietpellestabernacul.la: Diláta locum tentórii tui, et pelles tabernaculórum tuórum exténde, ne parcas: longos fac funículos tuos, et clavos tuos consólida.

addexteramenimetadlevampenetrabisetsemen.en: For thou shalt pass on to the right hand, and to the left: and thy seed shall inherit the Gentiles, and shall inhabit the desolate cities.
addexteramenimetadlevampenetrabisetsemen.la: Ad déxteram enim et ad lævam penetrábis, et semen tuum gentes hereditábit, et civitátes desértas inhabitábit.

nolitimerequianonconfunderisnequeerubesc.en: Fear not, for thou shalt not be confounded, nor blush: for thou shalt not be put to shame, because thou shalt forget the shame of thy youth, and shalt remember no more the reproach of thy widowhood.
nolitimerequianonconfunderisnequeerubesc.la: Noli timére, quia non confundéris, neque erubésces: non enim te pudébit, quia confusiónis adolescéntiæ tuæ obliviscéris, et oppróbrii viduitátis tuæ non recordáberis ámplius.

quiadominabiturtuiquifecittedominusexerc.en: For he that made thee shall rule over thee, the Lord of hosts is his name: and thy Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel, shall be called the God of all the earth.
quiadominabiturtuiquifecittedominusexerc.la: Quia dominábitur tui qui fecit te, Dóminus exercítuum nomen eius: et redémptor tuus sanctus Israël, Deus omnis terræ vocábitur.

quiautmulieremderelictametmerentemspirit.en: For the Lord hath called thee as a woman forsaken and mourning in spirit, and as a wife cast off from her youth, said thy God.
quiautmulieremderelictametmerentemspirit.la: Quia ut mulíerem derelíctam et mœréntem spíritu vocávit te Dóminus, et uxórem ab adolescéntia abiéctam, dixit Deus tuus.

adpunctuminmodicodereliquiteetinmiserati.en: For a small moment have I forsaken thee, but with great mercies will I gather thee.
adpunctuminmodicodereliquiteetinmiserati.la: Ad punctum in módico derelíqui te, et in miseratiónibus magnis congregábo te.

inmomentoindignationisabscondifaciemmeam.en: In a moment of indignation have I hid my face a little while from thee, but with everlasting kindness have I had mercy on thee, said the Lord thy Redeemer.
inmomentoindignationisabscondifaciemmeam.la: In moménto indignatiónis abscóndi fáciem meam parúmper a te: et in misericórdia sempitérna misértus sum tui: dixit redémptor tuus Dóminus.

sicutindiebusneistudmihiestcuiiuravinein.en: This thing is to me as in the days of Noe, to whom I swore, that I would no more bring in the waters of Noe upon the earth: so have I sworn not to be angry with thee, and not to rebuke thee.
sicutindiebusneistudmihiestcuiiuravinein.la: Sicut in diébus Noë istud mihi est, cui iurávi ne indúcerem aquas Noë ultra super terram: sic iurávi ut non iráscar tibi, et non íncrepem te.

vosquidereliquistisdominumquioblitiestis.en: And you, that have forsaken the Lord, that have forgotten my holy mount, that set a table for fortune, and offer libations upon it,
vosquidereliquistisdominumquioblitiestis.la: Vos qui dereliquístis Dóminum, qui oblíti estis montem sanctum meum, qui pónitis fortúnæ mensam, et libátis super eam,

numerabovosingladietomnesincedecorruetis.en: I will number you in the sword, and you shall all fall by slaughter: because I called and you did not answer: I spoke, and you did not hear: and you did evil in my eyes, and you have chosen the things that displease me.
numerabovosingladietomnesincedecorruetis.la: numerábo vos in gládio, et omnes in cæde corruétis: pro eo quod vocávi, et non respondístis: locútus sum, et non audístis: et faciebátis malum in óculis meis, et quæ nólui elegístis.

propterhochecdicitdominusdeusecceservime.en: Therefore thus saith the Lord God: Behold my servants shall eat, and you shall be hungry: behold my servants shall drink, and you shall be thirsty.
propterhochecdicitdominusdeusecceservime.la: Propter hoc hæc dicit Dóminus Deus: Ecce servi mei cómedent, et vos esuriétis: ecce servi mei bibent, et vos sitiétis.

ecceservimeiletabunturetvosconfundeminie.en: Behold my servants shall rejoice, and you shall be confounded: behold my servants shall praise for joyfulness of heart, and you shall cry for sorrow of heart, and shall howl for grief of spirit.
ecceservimeiletabunturetvosconfundeminie.la: Ecce servi mei lætabúntur, et vos confundémini: ecce servi mei laudábunt præ exsultatióne cordis, et vos clamábitis præ dolóre cordis, et præ contritióne spíritus ululábitis.

etdimittetisnomenvestruminiuramentumelec.en: And you shall leave your name for an execration to my elect: and the Lord God shall slay thee, and call his servants by another name.
etdimittetisnomenvestruminiuramentumelec.la: Et dimittétis nomen vestrum in juraméntum eléctis meis: et interfíciet te Dóminus Deus, et servos suos vocábit nómine álio.

inquoquibenedictusestsuperterrambenedice.en: In which he that is blessed upon the earth, shall be blessed in God, amen: and he that sweareth in the earth, shall swear by God, amen: because the former distresses are forgotten, and because they are hid from my eyes.
inquoquibenedictusestsuperterrambenedice.la: In quo qui benedíctus est super terram benedicétur in Deo amen: et qui jurat in terra jurábit in Deo amen: quia oblivióni tráditæ sunt angústiæ prióres, et quia abscónditæ sunt ab óculis meis.

ecceenimegocreocelosnovosetterramnovamet.en: For behold I create new heavens, and a new earth: and the former things shall not be in remembrance, and they shall not come upon the heart.
ecceenimegocreocelosnovosetterramnovamet.la: Ecce enim ego creo cælos novos, et terram novam: et non erunt in memória prióra, et non ascéndent super cor.

sedgaudebitisetexsultabitisusqueinsempit.en: But you shall be glad and rejoice for ever in these things, which I create: for behold I create Jerusalem a rejoicing, and the people thereof joy.
sedgaudebitisetexsultabitisusqueinsempit.la: Sed gaudébitis et exsultábitis usque in sempitérnum in his quæ ego creo: quia ecce ego creo Jerúsalem exsultatiónem, et pópulum ejus gáudium.

etexsultaboinierusalemetgaudeboinpopulom.en: And I will rejoice in Jerusalem, and joy in my people, and the voice of weeping shall no more be heard in her, nor the voice of crying.
etexsultaboinierusalemetgaudeboinpopulom.la: Et exsultábo in Jerúsalem, et gaudébo in pópulo meo, et non audiétur in eo ultra vox fletus et vox clamóris.

noneritibiampliusinfansdierumetsenexquin.en: There shall no more be an infant of days there, nor an old man that shall not fill up his days: for the child shall die a hundred years old, and the sinner being a hundred years old shall be accursed.
noneritibiampliusinfansdierumetsenexquin.la: Non erit ibi ámplius infans diérum, et senex qui non ímpleat dies suos, quóniam puer centum annórum moriétur, et peccátor centum annórum maledíctus erit.

hecdicitdominuscelumsedesmeaterraautemsc.en: Thus saith the Lord: Heaven is my throne, and the earth my footstool: what is this house that you will build to me? and what is this place of my rest?
hecdicitdominuscelumsedesmeaterraautemsc.la: Hæc dicit Dóminus: Cælum sedes mea, terra autem scabéllum pedum meórum. Quæ est ista domus quam ædificábitis mihi? et quis est iste locus quiétis meæ?

omniahecmanusmeafecitetfactasuntuniversa.en: My hand made all these things, and all these things were made, saith the Lord. But to whom shall I have respect, but to him that is poor and little, and of a contrite spirit, and that trembleth at my words?
omniahecmanusmeafecitetfactasuntuniversa.la: Omnia hæc manus mea fecit, et facta sunt univérsa ista, dicit Dóminus: ad quem autem respíciam, nisi ad paupérculum, et contrítum spíritu, et treméntem sermónes meos?

quimactatpecusquasiquiexcerebretcanemqui.en: He that sacrificeth an ox, is as if he slew a man: he that killeth a sheep in sacrifice, as if he should brain a dog: he that offereth an oblation, as if he should offer swine's blood; he that remembereth incense, as if he should bless an idol. All these things have they chosen in their ways, and their soul is delighted in their abominations.
quimactatpecusquasiquiexcerebretcanemqui.la: Qui mactat pecus, quasi qui excérebret canem: qui offert oblatiónem, quasi qui sánguinem suíllum ófferat: qui recordátur thuris, quasi qui benedícat idólo. Hæc ómnia elegérunt in viis suis, et in abominatiónibus suis ánima eórum delectáta est.

undeetegeligamillusioneseorumetquetimeba.en: Wherefore I also will choose their mockeries, and will bring upon them the things they feared: because I called, and there was none that would answer; I have spoken, and they heard not; and they have done evil in my eyes, and have chosen the things that displease me.
undeetegeligamillusioneseorumetquetimeba.la: Unde et ego éligam illusiónes eórum, et quæ timébant addúcam eis: quia vocávi, et non erat qui respondéret: locútus sum, et non audiérunt: fecerúntque malum in óculis meis, et quæ nólui elegérunt.

eteritmensisexmenseetsabbatumexsabbatove.en: And there shall be month after month, and sabbath after sabbath: and all flesh shall come to adore before my face, saith the Lord.
eteritmensisexmenseetsabbatumexsabbatove.la: Et erit mensis ex mense, et sábbatum ex sábbato: véniet omnis caro ut adóret coram fácie mea, dicit Dóminus.

etegredienturetvidebuntcadaveravirorumqu.en: And they shall go out, and see the carcasses of the men that have transgressed against me: their worm shall not die, and their fire shall not be quenched: and they shall be a loathsome sight to all flesh.
etegredienturetvidebuntcadaveravirorumqu.la: Et egrediéntur, et vidébunt cadávera virórum qui prævaricáti sunt in me: vermis eórum non moriétur, et ignis eórum non exstinguétur: et erunt usque ad satietátem visiónis omni carni.

etegofratresnonpotuivobisloquiquasispiri.en: And I, brethren, could not speak to you as unto spiritual, but as unto carnal. As unto little ones in Christ.
etegofratresnonpotuivobisloquiquasispiri.la: Et ego, fratres, non pótui vobis loqui quasi spirituálibus, sed quasi carnálibus. Tamquam párvulis in Christo,

lacvobispotumdedinonescamnondumenimpoter.en: I gave you milk to drink, not meat: for you were not able as yet. But neither indeed are you now able: for you are yet carnal.
lacvobispotumdedinonescamnondumenimpoter.la: lac vobis potum dedi, non escam: nondum enim poterátis: sed nec nunc quidem potéstis: adhuc enim carnáles estis.

cumenimsitintervoszelusetcontentiononnec.en: For, whereas there is among you envying and contention, are you not carnal and walk you not according to man?
cumenimsitintervoszelusetcontentiononnec.la: Cum enim sit inter vos zelus, et conténtio: nonne carnáles estis, et secúndum hóminem ambulátis?

cumenimquisdicategoquidemsumpaulialiusau.en: For while one saith: I indeed am of Paul: and another: I am of Apollo: are you not men? What then is Apollo and what is Paul?
cumenimquisdicategoquidemsumpaulialiusau.la: Cum enim quis dicat: Ego quidem sum Pauli: álius autem: Ego Apóllo: nonne hómines estis? Quid ígitur est Apóllo? quid vero Paulus?

ministrieiuscuicredidistisetunicuiquesic.en: The ministers of him whom you have believed: and to every one as the Lord hath given.
ministrieiuscuicredidistisetunicuiquesic.la: minístri ejus, cui credidístis, et unicuíque sicut Dóminus dedit.

egoplantaviapollorigavitseddeusincrement.en: I have planted, Apollo watered: but God gave the increase.
egoplantaviapollorigavitseddeusincrement.la: Ego plantávi, Apóllo rigávit: sed Deus increméntum dedit.

itaquenequequiplantatestaliquidnequequir.en: Therefore, neither he that planteth is any thing, nor he that watereth: but God that giveth the increase.
itaquenequequiplantatestaliquidnequequir.la: Itaque neque qui plantat est áliquid, neque qui rigat: sed qui increméntum dat, Deus.

quiautemplantatetquirigatunumsuntunusqui.en: Now he that planteth and he that watereth, are one. And every man shall receive his own reward, according to his own labour.
quiautemplantatetquirigatunumsuntunusqui.la: Qui autem plantat, et qui rigat, unum sunt. Unusquísque autem própriam mercédem accípiet, secúndum suum labórem.

deienimsumusadiutoresdeiagriculturestisd.en: For we are God's coadjutors. You are God's husbandry: you are God's building.
deienimsumusadiutoresdeiagriculturestisd.la: Dei enim sumus adiutóres: Dei agricultúra estis, Dei ædificátio estis.

secundumgratiamdeiquedatestmihiutsapiens.en: According to the grace of God that is given to me, as a wise architect, I have laid the foundation: and another buildeth thereon. But let every man take heed how he buildeth thereupon.
secundumgratiamdeiquedatestmihiutsapiens.la: Secúndum grátiam Dei, quæ data est mihi, ut sápiens architéctus fundaméntum pósui: álius autem superædíficat. Unusquísque autem vídeat quómodo superædíficet.

fundamentumenimaliudnemopotestponerepret.en: For other foundation no man can lay, but that which is laid: which is Christ Jesus.
fundamentumenimaliudnemopotestponerepret.la: Fundaméntum enim áliud nemo potest pónere præter id quod pósitum est, quod est Christus Jesus.

siquisautemsuperedificatsuperfundamentum.en: Now, if any man build upon this foundation, gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, stubble:
siquisautemsuperedificatsuperfundamentum.la: Si quis autem superædíficat super fundaméntum hoc, aurum, argéntum, lápides pretiósos, ligna, fœnum, stípulam,

uniuscuiusqueopusmanifestumeritdiesenimd.en: Every man's work shall be manifest. For the day of the Lord shall declare it, because it shall be revealed in fire. And the fire shall try every man's work, of what sort it is.
uniuscuiusqueopusmanifestumeritdiesenimd.la: uniuscuiúsque opus maniféstum erit: dies enim Dómini declarábit, quia in igne revelábitur: et uniuscuiúsque opus quale sit, ignis probábit.

sicuiusopusmanseritquodsuperedificavitme.en: If any man's work abide, which he hath built thereupon, he shall receive a reward.
sicuiusopusmanseritquodsuperedificavitme.la: Si cujus opus mánserit quod superædificávit, mercédem accípiet.

sicuiusopusarseritdetrimentumpatieturips.en: If any mans work burn, he shall suffer loss: but he himself shall be saved, yet so as by fire.
sicuiusopusarseritdetrimentumpatieturips.la: Si cujus opus árserit, detriméntum patiétur: ipse autem salvus erit, sic tamen quasi per ignem.

fugitefornicationemomnepeccatumquodcumqu.en: Fly fornication. Every sin that a man doth is without the body: but he that committeth fornication sinneth against his own body.
fugitefornicationemomnepeccatumquodcumqu.la: Fúgite fornicatiónem. Omne peccátum, quodcúmque fécerit homo, extra corpus est: qui autem fornicátur, in corpus suum peccat.

annescitisquoniammembravestratemplumsunt.en: Or know you not that your members are the temple of the Holy Ghost, who is in you, whom you have from God: and you are not your own?
annescitisquoniammembravestratemplumsunt.la: An nescítis quóniam membra vestra, templum sunt Spíritus Sancti, qui in vobis est, quem habétis a Deo, et non estis vestri?

emptienimestispretiomagnoglorificateetpo.en: For you are bought with a great price. Glorify and bear God in your body.
emptienimestispretiomagnoglorificateetpo.la: Empti enim estis prétio magno. Glorificáte, et portáte Deum in córpore vestro.

deiisautemqueidolissacrificanturscimusqu.en: Now concerning those things that are sacrificed to idols: we know we all have knowledge. Knowledge puffeth up: but charity edifieth.
deiisautemqueidolissacrificanturscimusqu.la: De iis autem quæ idólis sacrificántur, scimus quia omnes sciéntiam habémus. Sciéntia inflat, cáritas vero ædíficat.

siquisautemseexistimatscirealiquidnondum.en: And if any man think that he knoweth any thing, he hath not yet known as he ought to know.
siquisautemseexistimatscirealiquidnondum.la: Si quis autem se exístimat scire áliquid, nondum cognóvit quemádmodum opórteat eum scire.

siquisautemdiligitdeumhiccognitusestabeo.en: But if any man love God, the same is known by him.
siquisautemdiligitdeumhiccognitusestabeo.la: Si quis autem díligit Deum, hic cógnitus est ab eo.

deescisautemqueidolisimmolanturscimusqui.en: But as for the meats that are sacrificed to idols, we know that an idol is nothing in the world and that there is no God but one.
deescisautemqueidolisimmolanturscimusqui.la: De escis autem quæ idólis immolántur, scimus quia nihil est idólum in mundo, et quod nullus est Deus, nisi unus.

nametsisuntquidicanturdiisiveincelosivei.en: For although there be that are called gods, either in heaven or on earth (for there be gods many and lords many):
nametsisuntquidicanturdiisiveincelosivei.la: Nam etsi sunt qui dicántur dii sive in cælo, sive in terra (síquidem sunt dii multi, et dómini multi):

nobistamenunusestdeuspaterexquoomnietnos.en: Yet to us there is but one God, the Father, of whom are all things, and we unto him: and one Lord Jesus Christ, by whom are all things, and we by him.
nobistamenunusestdeuspaterexquoomnietnos.la: nobis tamen unus est Deus, Pater, ex quo ómnia, et nos in illum: et unus Dóminus Jesus Christus, per quem ómnia, et nos per ipsum.

sednoninomnibusestscientiaquidamautemcum.en: But there is not knowledge in every one. For some until this present, with conscience of the idol, eat as a thing sacrificed to an idol: and their conscience, being weak, is defiled.
sednoninomnibusestscientiaquidamautemcum.la: Sed non in ómnibus est sciéntia. Quidam autem cum consciéntia usque nunc idóli, quasi idolóthytum mandúcant: et consciéntia ipsórum cum sit infírma, pollúitur.

nequeenimsimanducaverimusabundabimusnequ.en: But meat doth not commend us to God. For neither, if we eat, shall we have the more: nor, if we eat not, shall we have the less.
nequeenimsimanducaverimusabundabimusnequ.la: Neque enim si manducavérimus, abundábimus: neque si non manducavérimus, deficiémus.

videteautemneforteheclicentiavestraoffen.en: But take heed lest perhaps this your liberty become a stumblingblock to the weak.
videteautemneforteheclicentiavestraoffen.la: Vidéte autem ne forte hæc licéntia vestra offendículum fiat infírmis.

sienimquisvideriteumquihabetscientiamini.en: For if a man see him that hath knowledge sit at meat in the idol's temple, shall not his conscience, being weak, be emboldened to eat those things which are sacrificed to idols?
sienimquisvideriteumquihabetscientiamini.la: Si enim quis víderit eum, qui habet sciéntiam, in idolío recumbéntem: nonne consciéntia ejus, cum sit infírma, ædificábitur ad manducándum idolóthyta?

etperibitinfirmusintuascientiafraterprop.en: And through thy knowledge shall the weak brother perish, for whom Christ hath died?
etperibitinfirmusintuascientiafraterprop.la: Et períbit infírmus in tua sciéntia, frater, propter quem Christus mórtuus est?

sicautempeccantesinfratresetpercutientes.en: Now when you sin thus against the brethren and wound their weak conscience, you sin against Christ.
sicautempeccantesinfratresetpercutientes.la: Sic autem peccántes in fratres, et percutiéntes consciéntiam eórum infírmam, in Christum peccátis.

nescitisquodiiquiinstadiocurruntomnesqui.en: Know you not that they that run in the race, all run indeed, but one receiveth the prize. So run that you may obtain.
nescitisquodiiquiinstadiocurruntomnesqui.la: Nescítis quod ii qui in stádio currunt, omnes quidem currunt, sed unus áccipit bravíum? Sic cúrrite ut comprehendátis.

egoigitursiccurrononquasiinincertumsicpu.en: I therefore so run, not as at an uncertainty: I so fight, not as one beating the air.
egoigitursiccurrononquasiinincertumsicpu.la: Ego ígitur sic curro, non quasi in incértum: sic pugno, non quasi áërem vérberans:

sedcastigocorpusmeumetinservitutemredigo.en: But I chastise my body and bring it into subjection: lest perhaps, when I have preached to others, I myself should become a castaway.
sedcastigocorpusmeumetinservitutemredigo.la: sed castígo corpus meum, et in servitútem rédigo: ne forte cum áliis prædicáverim, ipse réprobus effíciar.

nolenimvosignorarefratresquoniampatresno.en: For I would not have you ignorant, brethren, that our fathers were all under the cloud: and all passed through the sea.
nolenimvosignorarefratresquoniampatresno.la: Nolo enim vos ignoráre fratres, quóniam patres nostri omnes sub nube fuérunt, et omnes mare transiérunt,

etomnesinmoysebaptizatisuntinnubeetinmar.en: And all in Moses were baptized, in the cloud and in the sea:
etomnesinmoysebaptizatisuntinnubeetinmar.la: et omnes in Móyse baptizáti sunt in nube, et in mari:

etomneseamdemescamspiritalemmanducaverun.en: And did all eat the same spiritual food:
etomneseamdemescamspiritalemmanducaverun.la: et omnes eámdem escam spiritálem manducavérunt,

etomneseumdempotumspiritalembiberuntbibe.en: And all drank the same spiritual drink: (And they drank of the spiritual rock that followed them: and the rock was Christ.)
etomneseumdempotumspiritalembiberuntbibe.la: et omnes eúmdem potum spiritálem bibérunt (bibébant autem de spiritáli, consequénte eos, petra: petra autem erat Christus):

sednoninpluribuseorumbeneplacitumestdeon.en: But with most of them God was not well pleased: for they were overthrown in the desert.
sednoninpluribuseorumbeneplacitumestdeon.la: sed non in plúribus eórum beneplácitum est Deo: nam prostráti sunt in desérto.

hecauteminfigurafactasuntnostriutnonsimu.en: Now these things were done in a figure of us, that we should not covet evil things, as they also coveted.
hecauteminfigurafactasuntnostriutnonsimu.la: Hæc autem in figúra facta sunt nostri, ut non simus concupiscéntes malórum, sicut et illi concupiérunt.

nequeidololatreefficiaminisicutquidamexi.en: Neither become ye idolaters, as some of them, as it is written: The people sat down to eat and drink and rose up to play.
nequeidololatreefficiaminisicutquidamexi.la: Neque idolólatræ efficiámini, sicut quidam ex ipsis: quemádmodum scriptum est: Sedit pópulus manducáre, et bíbere, et surrexérunt lúdere.

nequefornicemursicutquidamexipsisfornica.en: Neither let us commit fornication, as some of them that committed fornication: and there fell in one day three and twenty thousand.
nequefornicemursicutquidamexipsisfornica.la: Neque fornicémur, sicut quidam ex ipsis fornicáti sunt, et cecidérunt una die vigínti tria míllia.

carissimimihifugiteabidolorumcultura.en: Wherefore, my dearly beloved, fly from the service of idols.
carissimimihifugiteabidolorumcultura.la: Caríssimi mihi, fúgite ab idolórum cultúra:

utprudentibusloquorvosipsiiudicatequoddi.en: I speak as to wise men: judge ye yourselves what I say.
utprudentibusloquorvosipsiiudicatequoddi.la: ut prudéntibus loquor, vos ipsi judicáte quod dico.

calixbenedictioniscuibenedicimusnonnecom.en: The chalice of benediction which we bless, is it not the communion of the blood of Christ? And the bread which we break, is it not the partaking of the body of the Lord?
calixbenedictioniscuibenedicimusnonnecom.la: Calix benedictiónis, cui benedícimus, nonne communicátio sánguinis Christi est? et panis quem frángimus, nonne participátio córporis Dómini est?

quoniamunuspanisunumcorpusmultisumusomne.en: For we, being many, are one bread, one body: all that partake of one bread.
quoniamunuspanisunumcorpusmultisumusomne.la: Quóniam unus panis, unum corpus multi sumus, omnes qui de uno pane participámus.

videteisrelsecundumcarnemnonnequieduntho.en: Behold Israel according to the flesh. Are not they that eat of the sacrifices partakers of the altar?
videteisrelsecundumcarnemnonnequieduntho.la: Vidéte Israël secúndum carnem: nonne qui edunt hóstias, partícipes sunt altáris?

quidergodicoquodidolisimmolatumsitaliqui.en: What then? Do I say that what is offered in sacrifice to idols is any thing? Or that the idol is any thing?
quidergodicoquodidolisimmolatumsitaliqui.la: Quid ergo? dico quod idólis immolátum sit áliquid? aut quod idólum sit áliquid?

sedqueimmolantgentesdemoniisimmolantetno.en: But the things which the heathens sacrifice, they sacrifice to devils and not to God. And I would not that you should be made partakers with devils.
sedqueimmolantgentesdemoniisimmolantetno.la: Sed quæ ímmolant gentes, dæmóniis ímmolant, et non Deo. Nolo autem vos sócios fíeri dæmoniórum:

nonpotestiscalicemdominibibereetcalicemd.en: You cannot drink the chalice of the Lord and the chalice of devils: you cannot be partakers of the table of the Lord and of the table of devils.
nonpotestiscalicemdominibibereetcalicemd.la: non potéstis cálicem Dómini bíbere, et cálicem dæmoniórum: non potéstis mensæ Dómini partícipes esse, et mensæ dæmoniórum.

omniamihilicentsednonomniaedificant.en: All things are lawful for me: but all things do not edify.
omniamihilicentsednonomniaedificant.la: Omnia mihi licent, sed non ómnia ædíficant.

nemoquodsuumestqueratsedquodalterius.en: Let no man seek his own, but that which is another's.
nemoquodsuumestqueratsedquodalterius.la: Nemo quod suum est quærat, sed quod altérius.

omnequodinmacellovenitmanducatenihilinte.en: Whatsoever is sold in the shambles, eat: asking no question for conscience' sake.
omnequodinmacellovenitmanducatenihilinte.la: Omne quod in macéllo venit, manducáte, nihil interrogántes propter consciéntiam.

imitatoresmeiestotesicutetegochristi.en: Be ye followers of me, as I also am of Christ.
imitatoresmeiestotesicutetegochristi.la: Imitatóres mei estóte, sicut et ego Christi.

laudoautemvosfratresquodperomniameimemor.en: Now I praise you, brethren, that in all things you are mindful of me and keep my ordinances as I have delivered them to you.
laudoautemvosfratresquodperomniameimemor.la: Laudo autem vos fratres quod per ómnia mei mémores estis: et sicut trádidi vobis, præcépta mea tenétis.

voloautemvosscirequodomnisviricaputchris.en: But I would have you know that the head of every man is Christ: and the head of the woman is the man: and the head of Christ is God.
voloautemvosscirequodomnisviricaputchris.la: Volo autem vos scire quod omnis viri caput, Christus est: caput autem mulíeris, vir: caput vero Christi, Deus.

omnisviroransautprophetansvelatocapitede.en: Every man praying or prophesying with his head covered disgraceth his head.
omnisviroransautprophetansvelatocapitede.la: Omnis vir orans, aut prophétans veláto cápite, detúrpat caput suum.

omnisautemmulieroransautprophetansnonvel.en: But every woman praying or prophesying with her head not covered disgraceth her head: for it is all one as if she were shaven.
omnisautemmulieroransautprophetansnonvel.la: Omnis autem múlier orans, aut prophétans non veláto cápite, detúrpat caput suum: unum enim est ac si decalvétur.

namsinonvelaturmuliertondeatursiveroturp.en: For if a woman be not covered, let her be shorn. But if it be a shame to a woman to be shorn or made bald, let her cover her head.
namsinonvelaturmuliertondeatursiveroturp.la: Nam si non velátur múlier, tondeátur. Si vero turpe est mulíeri tondéri, aut decalvári, velet caput suum.

virquidemnondebetvelarecaputsuumquoniami.en: The man indeed ought not to cover his head: because he is the image and glory of God. But the woman is the glory of the man.
virquidemnondebetvelarecaputsuumquoniami.la: Vir quidem non debet veláre caput suum: quóniam imágo et glória Dei est, múlier autem glória viri est.

nonenimvirexmuliereestsedmulierexviro.en: For the man is not of the woman: but the woman of the man.
nonenimvirexmuliereestsedmulierexviro.la: Non enim vir ex mulíere est, sed múlier ex viro.

etenimnonestcreatusvirproptermulieremsed.en: For the man was not created for the woman: but the woman for the man.
etenimnonestcreatusvirproptermulieremsed.la: Etenim non est creátus vir propter mulíerem, sed múlier propter virum.

ideodebetmulierpotestatemhaberesupracapu.en: Therefore ought the woman to have a power over her head, because of the angels.
ideodebetmulierpotestatemhaberesupracapu.la: Ideo debet múlier potestátem habére supra caput propter ángelos.

verumtamennequevirsinemulierenequemulier.en: But yet neither is the man without the woman, nor the woman without the man, in the Lord.
verumtamennequevirsinemulierenequemulier.la: Verúmtamen neque vir sine mulíere: neque múlier sine viro in Dómino.

namsicutmulierdeviroitetvirpermulieremom.en: For as the woman is of the man, so also is the man by the woman: but all things of God.
namsicutmulierdeviroitetvirpermulieremom.la: Nam sicut múlier de viro, ita et vir per mulíerem: ómnia autem ex Deo.

vosipsiiudicatedecetmulieremnonvelatamor.en: You yourselves judge. Doth it become a woman to pray unto God uncovered?
vosipsiiudicatedecetmulieremnonvelatamor.la: Vos ipsi judicáte: decet mulíerem non velátam oráre Deum?

necipsanaturadocetvosquodvirquidemsicoma.en: Doth not even nature itself teach you that a man indeed, if he nourish his hair, it is a shame unto him?
necipsanaturadocetvosquodvirquidemsicoma.la: Nec ipsa natúra docet vos, quod vir quidem si comam nútriat, ignomínia est illi:

mulierverosicomamnutriatgloriestilliquon.en: But if a woman nourish her hair, it is a glory to her; for her hair is given to her for a covering.
mulierverosicomamnutriatgloriestilliquon.la: múlier vero si comam nútriat, glória est illi: quóniam capílli pro velámine ei dati sunt.

despiritualibusautemnolovosignorarefratr.en: Now concerning spiritual things, my brethren, I would not have you ignorant.
despiritualibusautemnolovosignorarefratr.la: De spirituálibus autem, nolo vos ignoráre fratres.

scitisquoniamcumgentesessetisadsimulacra.en: You know that when you were heathens, you went to dumb idols, according as you were led.
scitisquoniamcumgentesessetisadsimulacra.la: Scitis quóniam cum gentes essétis, ad simulácra muta prout ducebámini eúntes.

ideonotumvobisfacioquodnemoinspiritudeil.en: Wherefore, I give you to understand that no man, speaking by the Spirit of God, saith Anathema to Jesus. And no man can say The Lord Jesus, but by the Holy Ghost.
ideonotumvobisfacioquodnemoinspiritudeil.la: Ideo notum vobis fácio, quod nemo in Spíritu Dei loquens, dicit anáthema Jesu. Et nemo potest dícere, Dóminus Jesus, nisi in Spíritu Sancto.

divisionesverogratiarumsuntidemautemspir.en: Now there are diversities of graces, but the same Spirit.
divisionesverogratiarumsuntidemautemspir.la: Divisiónes vero gratiárum sunt, idem autem Spíritus:

etdivisionesministrationumsuntidemautemd.en: And there are diversities of ministries. but the same Lord.
etdivisionesministrationumsuntidemautemd.la: et divisiónes ministratiónum sunt, idem autem Dóminus:

unicuiqueautemdaturmanifestatiospiritusa.en: And the manifestation of the Spirit is given to every man unto profit.
unicuiqueautemdaturmanifestatiospiritusa.la: Unicuíque autem datur manifestátio Spíritus ad utilitátem.

aliiquidemperspiritumdatursermosapientie.en: To one indeed, by the Spirit, is given the word of wisdom: and to another, the word of knowledge, according to the same Spirit:
aliiquidemperspiritumdatursermosapientie.la: Alii quidem per Spíritum datur sermo sapiéntiæ: álii autem sermo sciéntiæ secúndum eúmdem Spíritum:

alterifidesineodemspiritualiigratiasanit.en: To another, faith in the same spirit: to another, the grace of healing in one Spirit:
alterifidesineodemspiritualiigratiasanit.la: álteri fides in eódem Spíritu: álii grátia sanitátum in uno Spíritu:

aliioperatiovirtutumaliiprophetiaaliidis.en: To another the working of miracles: to another, prophecy: to another, the discerning of spirits: to another, diverse kinds of tongues: to another, interpretation of speeches.
aliioperatiovirtutumaliiprophetiaaliidis.la: álii operátio virtútum, álii prophetía, álii discrétio spirítuum, álii génera linguárum, álii interpretátio sermónum.

fratresnolitepueriefficisensibussedmalit.en: Brethren, do not become children in sense. But in malice be children: and in sense be perfect.
fratresnolitepueriefficisensibussedmalit.la: Fratres, nolíte púeri éffici sénsibus, sed malítia párvuli estóte: sénsibus autem perfécti estóte.

inlegescriptumestquoniaminaliislinguiset.en: In the law it is written: In other tongues and other lips I will speak to this people: and neither so will they hear me, saith the Lord.
inlegescriptumestquoniaminaliislinguiset.la: In lege scriptum est: Quóniam in áliis linguis et lábiis áliis loquar pópulo huic: et nec sic exáudient me, dicit Dóminus.

itaquelingueinsignumsuntnonfidelibussedi.en: Wherefore tongues are for a sign, not to believers but to unbelievers: but prophecies, not to unbelievers but to believers.
itaquelingueinsignumsuntnonfidelibussedi.la: Itaque linguæ in signum sunt non fidélibus, sed infidélibus: prophetíæ autem non infidélibus, sed fidélibus.

siergoconveniatuniversecclesiainunumetom.en: If therefore the whole church come together into one place, and all speak with tongues, and there come in unlearned persons or infidels, will they not say that you are mad?
siergoconveniatuniversecclesiainunumetom.la: Si ergo convéniat univérsa Ecclésia in unum, et omnes linguis loquántur, intrent autem idiótæ, aut infidéles: nonne dicent quod insanítis?

siautemomnesprophetentintretautemquisinf.en: But if all prophesy, and there come in one that believeth not or an unlearned person, he is convinced of all: he is judged of all.
siautemomnesprophetentintretautemquisinf.la: Si autem omnes prophétent, intret autem quis infidélis, vel idióta, convíncitur ab ómnibus, diiudicátur ab ómnibus:

occultacordiseiusmanifestafiuntetitacade.en: The secrets of his heart are made manifest. And so, falling down on his face, he will adore God, affirming that God is among you indeed.
occultacordiseiusmanifestafiuntetitacade.la: occúlta cordis ejus manifésta fiunt: et ita cadens in fáciem adorábit Deum, pronúntians quod vere Deus in vobis sit.

quidergestfratrescumconvenitisunusquisqu.en: How is it then, brethren? When you come together, every one of you hath a psalm, hath a doctrine, hath a revelation, hath a tongue, hath an interpretation: let all things be done to edification.
quidergestfratrescumconvenitisunusquisqu.la: Quid ergo est, fratres? Cum convenítis, unusquísque vestrum psalmum habet, doctrínam habet, apocalýpsim habet, linguam habet, interpretatiónem habet: ómnia ad ædificatiónem fiant.

sivelinguaquisloquitursecundumduosaututm.en: If any speak with a tongue, let it be by two, or at the most by three, and in course: and let one interpret.
sivelinguaquisloquitursecundumduosaututm.la: Sive lingua quis lóquitur, secúndum duos, aut ut multum tres, et per partes, et unus interpretétur.

siautemnonfueritinterprestaceatinecclesi.en: But if there be no interpreter, let him hold his peace in the church and speak to himself and to God.
siautemnonfueritinterprestaceatinecclesi.la: Si autem non fúerit intérpres, táceat in ecclésia: sibi autem loquátur, et Deo.

notamautemfacimusvobisfratresgratiamdeiq.en: Now we make known unto you, brethren, the grace of God that hath been given in the churches of Macedonia.
notamautemfacimusvobisfratresgratiamdeiq.la: Notam autem fácimus vobis, fratres, grátiam Dei, quæ data est in Ecclésiis Macedóniæ:

quodinmultexperimentotribulationisabunda.en: That in much experience of tribulation, they have had abundance of joy and their very deep poverty hath abounded unto the riches of their simplicity.
quodinmultexperimentotribulationisabunda.la: quod in multo experiménto tribulatiónis abundántia gáudii ipsórum fuit, et altíssima paupértas eórum abundávit in divítias simplicitátis eórum:

quiasecundumvirtutemtestimoniumillisredd.en: For according to their power (I bear them witness) and beyond their power, they were willing:
quiasecundumvirtutemtestimoniumillisredd.la: quia secúndum virtútem testimónium illis reddo, et supra virtútem voluntárii fuérunt,

cummultexhortationeobsecrantesnosgratiam.en: With much entreaty begging of us the grace and communication of the ministry that is done toward the saints.
cummultexhortationeobsecrantesnosgratiam.la: cum multa exhortatióne obsecrántes nos grátiam, et communicatiónem ministérii, quod fit in sanctos.

etnonsicutsperavimussedsemetipsosdederun.en: And not as we hoped: but they gave their own selves, first to the Lord, then to us by the will of God;
etnonsicutsperavimussedsemetipsosdederun.la: Et non sicut sperávimus, sed semetípsos dedérunt primum Dómino, deínde nobis per voluntátem Dei,

itautrogaremustitumutquemadmodumcepitite.en: Insomuch, that we desired Titus, that, as he had begun, so also he would finish among you this same grace.
itautrogaremustitumutquemadmodumcepitite.la: ita ut rogarémus Titum, ut quemádmodum cœpit, ita et perfíciat in vobis étiam grátiam istam.

sedsicutinomnibusabundatisfideetsermonee.en: That as in all things you abound in faith and word and knowledge and all carefulness, moreover also in your charity towards us: so in this grace also you may abound.
sedsicutinomnibusabundatisfideetsermonee.la: Sed sicut in ómnibus abundátis fide, et sermóne, et sciéntia, et omni sollicitúdine, ínsuper et caritáte vestra in nos, ut et in hac grátia abundétis.

nonquasiimperansdicosedperaliorumsollici.en: I speak not as commanding: but by the carefulness of others, approving also the good disposition of your charity.
nonquasiimperansdicosedperaliorumsollici.la: Non quasi ímperans dico: sed per aliórum sollicitúdinem, étiam vestræ caritátis ingénium bonum cómprobans.

scitisenimgratiamdomininostriiesuchristi.en: For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that being rich he became poor for your sakes: that through his poverty you might be rich.
scitisenimgratiamdomininostriiesuchristi.la: Scitis enim grátiam Dómini nostri Jesu Christi, quóniam propter vos egénus factus est, cum esset dives, ut illíus inópia vos dívites essétis.

etconsiliuminhocdohocenimvobisutileestqu.en: And herein I give my advice: for this is profitable for you who have begun not only to do but also to be willing, a year ago.
etconsiliuminhocdohocenimvobisutileestqu.la: Et consílium in hoc do: hoc enim vobis útile est, qui non solum fácere, sed et velle cœpístis ab anno prióre.

abrahedictesuntpromissionesetseminieiusn.en: To Abraham were the promises made and to his seed. He saith not: And to his seeds as of many. But as of one: And to thy seed, which is Christ.
abrahedictesuntpromissionesetseminieiusn.la: Abrahæ dictæ sunt promissiónes, et sémini ejus. Non dicit: Et semínibus, quasi in multis: sed quasi in uno: Et sémini tuo, qui est Christus.

hocautemdicotestamentumconfirmatumadeoqu.en: Now this I say: that the testament which was confirmed by God, the law which was made after four hundred and thirty years doth not disannul, to make the promise of no effect.
hocautemdicotestamentumconfirmatumadeoqu.la: Hoc autem dico, testaméntum confirmátum a Deo: quæ post quadringéntos et trigínta annos facta est lex, non írritum facit ad evacuándam promissiónem.

namsiexlegehereditasiamnonexpromissionea.en: For if the inheritance be of the law, it is no more of promise. But God gave it to Abraham by promise.
namsiexlegehereditasiamnonexpromissionea.la: Nam si ex lege heréditas, jam non ex promissióne. Abrahæ autem per repromissiónem donávit Deus.

quidigiturlexproptertransgressionesposit.en: Why then was the law? It was set because of transgressions, until the seed should come to whom he made the promise, being ordained by angels in the hand of a mediator.
quidigiturlexproptertransgressionesposit.la: Quid ígitur lex? Propter transgressiónes pósita est donec veníret semen, cui promíserat, ordináta per ángelos in manu mediatóris.

mediatorautemuniusnonestdeusautemunusest.en: Now a mediator is not of one: but God is one.
mediatorautemuniusnonestdeusautemunusest.la: Mediátor autem uníus non est: Deus autem unus est.

lexergoadversuspromissadeiabsitsienimdat.en: Was the law then against the promises of God: God forbid! For if there had been a law given which could give life, verily justice should have been by the law.
lexergoadversuspromissadeiabsitsienimdat.la: Lex ergo advérsus promíssa Dei? Absit. Si enim data esset lex, quæ posset vivificáre, vere ex lege esset justítia.

sedconclusitscripturaomniasubpeccatoutpr.en: But the scripture hath concluded all under sin, that the promise, by the faith of Jesus Christ, might be given to them that believe.
sedconclusitscripturaomniasubpeccatoutpr.la: Sed conclúsit Scriptúra ómnia sub peccáto, ut promíssio ex fide Jesu Christi darétur credéntibus.

priusautemquamveniretfidessublegecustodi.en: But before the faith came, we were kept under the law shut up, unto that faith which was to be revealed.
priusautemquamveniretfidessublegecustodi.la: Prius autem quam veníret fides, sub lege custodiebámur conclúsi in eam fidem quæ revelánda erat.

itaquelexpedagogusnosterfuitinchristoute.en: Wherefore the law was our pedagogue in Christ: that we might be justified by faith.
itaquelexpedagogusnosterfuitinchristoute.la: Itaque lex pædagógus noster fuit in Christo, ut ex fide justificémur.

atubivenitfidesiamnonsumussubpedagogo.en: But after the faith is come, we are no longer under a pedagogue.
atubivenitfidesiamnonsumussubpedagogo.la: At ubi venit fides, jam non sumus sub pædagógo.

omnesenimfiliideiestisperfidemqueestinch.en: For you are all the children of God, by faith in Christ Jesus.
omnesenimfiliideiestisperfidemqueestinch.la: Omnes enim fílii Dei estis per fidem, quæ est in Christo Jesu.

quicumqueeniminchristobaptizatiestischri.en: For as many of you as have been baptized in Christ have put on Christ.
quicumqueeniminchristobaptizatiestischri.la: Quicúmque enim in Christo baptizáti estis, Christum induístis.

dicoautemquantotemporeheresparvulusestni.en: As long as the heir is a child, he differeth nothing from a servant, though he be lord of all,
dicoautemquantotemporeheresparvulusestni.la: Dico autem: quanto témpore hæres párvulus est, nihil differt a servo, cum sit dóminus ómnium:

sedsubtutoribusetactoribusestusqueadpref.en: But is under tutors and governors until the time appointed by the father.
sedsubtutoribusetactoribusestusqueadpref.la: sed sub tutóribus et actóribus est usque ad præfinítum tempus a patre:

itetnoscumessemusparvulisubelementismund.en: So we also, when we were children, were serving under the elements of the world.
itetnoscumessemusparvulisubelementismund.la: ita et nos cum essémus párvuli, sub eleméntis mundi erámus serviéntes.

atubivenitplenitudotemporismisitdeusfili.en: But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent his Son, made of a woman, made under the law:
atubivenitplenitudotemporismisitdeusfili.la: At ubi venit plenitúdo témporis, misit Deus Fílium suum factum ex mulíere, factum sub lege,

uteosquisublegeerantredimeretutadoptione.en: That he might redeem them who were under the law: that we might receive the adoption of sons.
uteosquisublegeerantredimeretutadoptione.la: ut eos, qui sub lege erant, redímeret, ut adoptiónem filiórum reciperémus.

quoniamautemestisfiliimisitdeusspiritumf.en: And because you are sons, God hath sent the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying: Abba, Father.
quoniamautemestisfiliimisitdeusspiritumf.la: Quóniam autem estis fílii, misit Deus Spíritum Fílii sui in corda vestra, clamántem: Abba, Pater.

sedtuncquidemignorantesdeumiisquinaturan.en: But then indeed, not knowing God, you served them who, by nature, are not gods.
sedtuncquidemignorantesdeumiisquinaturan.la: Sed tunc quidem ignorántes Deum, iis, qui natúra non sunt dii, serviebátis.

nuncautemcumcognoveritisdeumimmocognitis.en: But now, after that you have known God, or rather are known by God: how turn you again to the weak and needy elements which you desire to serve again?
nuncautemcumcognoveritisdeumimmocognitis.la: Nunc autem cum cognovéritis Deum, immo cógniti sitis a Deo: quómodo convertímini íterum ad infírma et egéna eleménta, quibus dénuo servíre vultis?

diesobservatisetmensesettemporetannos.en: You observe days and months and times, and years.
diesobservatisetmensesettemporetannos.la: Dies observátis, et menses, et témpora, et annos.

timeovosnefortesinecausalaboraveriminvob.en: I am afraid of you, lest perhaps I have laboured in vain among you.
timeovosnefortesinecausalaboraveriminvob.la: Tímeo vos, ne forte sine causa laboráverim in vobis.

estotesicutegoquietegosicutvosfratresobs.en: Be ye as I, because I also am as you brethren, I beseech you. You have not injured me at all.
estotesicutegoquietegosicutvosfratresobs.la: Estóte sicut ego, quia et ego sicut vos: fratres, óbsecro vos. Nihil me læsístis.

scitisautemquiaperinfirmitatemcarnisevan.en: And you know how, through infirmity of the flesh, I preached the gospel to you heretofore: and your temptation in my flesh
scitisautemquiaperinfirmitatemcarnisevan.la: Scitis autem quia per infirmitátem carnis evangelizávi vobis jamprídem: et tentatiónem vestram in carne mea

nonsprevistisnequerespuistissedsicutange.en: You despised not, nor rejected: but received me as an angel of God, even as Christ Jesus.
nonsprevistisnequerespuistissedsicutange.la: non sprevístis, neque respuístis: sed sicut ángelum Dei excepístis me, sicut Christum Jesum.

quodsispirituducimininonestissublege.en: But if you are led by the spirit, you are not under the law.
quodsispirituducimininonestissublege.la: Quod si Spíritu ducímini, non estis sub lege.

manifestasuntautemoperacarnisquesuntforn.en: Now the works of the flesh are manifest: which are fornication, uncleanness, immodesty, luxury,
manifestasuntautemoperacarnisquesuntforn.la: Manifésta sunt autem ópera carnis, quæ sunt fornicátio, immundítia, impudicítia, luxúria,
