etreposueruntillicetfactisuntinlaqueumma.en: And laid them up there: and they became a great snare.
etreposueruntillicetfactisuntinlaqueumma.la: et reposuérunt illic: et facti sunt in láqueum magnum.

etfactumesthocadinsidiassanctificationie.en: And this was a place to lie in wait against the sanctuary, and an evil devil in Israel.
etfactumesthocadinsidiassanctificationie.la: Et factum est hoc ad insídias sanctificatióni, et in diábolum malum in Israël:

eteffuderuntsanguineminnocentempercircui.en: And they shed innocent blood round about the sanctuary, and defiled the holy place.
eteffuderuntsanguineminnocentempercircui.la: et effudérunt sánguinem innocéntem per circúitum sanctificatiónis, et contaminavérunt sanctificatiónem.

etfugerunthabitatoresierusalemproptereos.en: And the inhabitants of Jerusalem fled away by reason of them and the city was made the habitation of strangers, and she became a stranger to her own seed, and her children forsook her.
etfugerunthabitatoresierusalemproptereos.la: Et fugérunt habitatóres Jerúsalem propter eos, et facta est habitátio exterórum, et facta est éxtera sémini suo, et nati ejus reliquérunt eam.

etmisitrexlibrospermanusnuntioruminierus.en: And the king sent letters by the hands of messengers to Jerusalem, and to all the cities of Juda; that they should follow the law of the nations of the earth.
etmisitrexlibrospermanusnuntioruminierus.la: Et misit rex libros per manus nuntiórum in Jerúsalem, et in omnes civitátes Juda, ut sequeréntur leges géntium terræ,

etprohiberentholocaustetsacrificietplaca.en: And should forbid holocausts and sacrifices, and atonements to be made in the temple of God.
etprohiberentholocaustetsacrificietplaca.la: et prohibérent holocáusta et sacrifícia, et placatiónes fíeri in templo Dei,

etprohiberentcelebrarisabbatumetdiessole.en: And should prohibit the sabbath, and the festival days to be celebrated.
etprohiberentcelebrarisabbatumetdiessole.la: et prohibérent celebrári sábbatum, et dies solémnes:

etiussitcoinquinarisanctetsanctumpopulum.en: And he commanded the holy places to be profaned, and the holy people of Israel.
etiussitcoinquinarisanctetsanctumpopulum.la: et jussit coinquinári sancta, et sanctum pópulum Israël.

etiussitedificariarasettempletidoletimmo.en: And he commanded altars to be built, and temples, and idols, and swine's flesh to be immolated, and unclean beasts,
etiussitedificariarasettempletidoletimmo.la: Et jussit ædificári aras, et templa, et idóla, et immolári carnes suíllas, et pécora commúnia,

etrelinquerefiliossuosincircumcisosetcoi.en: And that they should leave their children uncircumcised, and let their souls be defiled with all uncleannesses, and abominations, to the end that they should forget the law, and should change all the justifications of God.
etrelinquerefiliossuosincircumcisosetcoi.la: et relínquere fílios suos incircumcísos, et coinquinári ánimas eórum in ómnibus immúndis, et abominatiónibus, ita ut oblivisceréntur legem, et immutárent omnes justificatiónes Dei:

etquicumquenonfecissentsecundumverbumreg.en: And that whosoever would not do according to the word of king Antiochus, should be put to death.
etquicumquenonfecissentsecundumverbumreg.la: et quicúmque non fecíssent secúndum verbum regis Antíochi, moreréntur.

secundumomniaverbahecscripsitomniregnosu.en: According to all these words he wrote to his whole kingdom: and he appointed rulers over the people that should force them to do these things.
secundumomniaverbahecscripsitomniregnosu.la: Secúndum ómnia verba hæc scripsit omni regno suo: et præpósuit príncipes pópulo, qui hæc fíeri cógerent.

etiusseruntcivitatibusiudasacrificare.en: And they commanded the cities of Juda to sacrifice.

etcongregatisuntmultidepopuloadeosquider.en: Then many of the people were gathered to them that had forsaken the law of the Lord: and they committed evils in the land:
etcongregatisuntmultidepopuloadeosquider.la: Et congregáti sunt multi de pópulo ad eos qui derelíquerant legem Dómini, et fecérunt mala super terram:

eteffugaveruntpopulumisrelinabditisetina.en: And they drove away the people of Israel into lurking holes, and into the secret places of fugitives.
eteffugaveruntpopulumisrelinabditisetina.la: et effugavérunt pópulum Israël in ábditis, et in abscónditis fugitivórum locis.

omniscompositieiusablatestqueeratliberaf.en: All her ornaments are taken away. She that was free is made a slave.
omniscompositieiusablatestqueeratliberaf.la: Omnis composítio ejus abláta est. Quæ erat líbera, facta est ancílla.

etrespondentesquimissierantabantiochodix.en: And they that were sent from Antiochus, answering, said to Mathathias: Thou art a ruler, and an honourable, and great man in this city, and adorned with sons, and brethren.
etrespondentesquimissierantabantiochodix.la: Et respondéntes qui missi erant ab Antíocho, dixérunt Mathathíæ: Princeps et claríssimus, et magnus es in hac civitáte, et ornátus fíliis et frátribus.

ergoaccedeprioretfaciussumregissicutfece.en: Therefore, come thou first, and obey the king's commandment, as all nations have done, and the men of Juda, and they that remain in Jerusalem: and thou, and thy sons shall be in the number of the king's friends, and enriched with gold, and silver, and many presents.
ergoaccedeprioretfaciussumregissicutfece.la: Ergo accéde prior, et fac jussum regis, sicut fecérunt omnes gentes, et viri Juda, et qui remansérunt in Jerúsalem: et eris tu, et fílii tui, inter amícos regis, et amplificátus auro, et argénto, et munéribus multis.

etrenuntiatumestvirisregisetexercituiqui.en: And it was told to the king's men, and to the army that was in Jerusalem, in the city of David, that certain men, who had broken the king's commandment, were gone away into the secret places in the wilderness, and that many were gone after them.
etrenuntiatumestvirisregisetexercituiqui.la: Et renuntiátum est viris regis, et exercítui qui erat in Jerúsalem civitáte David, quóniam discessíssent viri quidam, qui dissipavérunt mandátum regis, in loca occúlta in desérto, et abiíssent post illos multi.

etstatimperrexeruntadeosetconstituerunta.en: And forthwith they went out towards them, and made war against them on the sabbath day.
etstatimperrexeruntadeosetconstituerunta.la: Et statim perrexérunt ad eos, et constituérunt advérsus eos prœ́lium in die sabbatórum,

etdixeruntadeosresistitisetnuncadhucexit.en: And they said to them: Do you still resist? come forth, and do according to the edict of king Antiochus, and you shall live.
etdixeruntadeosresistitisetnuncadhucexit.la: et dixérunt ad eos: Resístitis et nunc adhuc? exíte, et fácite secúndum verbum regis Antíochi, et vivétis.

etdixeruntnonexibimusnequefaciemusverbum.en: And they said: We will not come forth, neither will we obey the king's edict, to profane the sabbath day.
etdixeruntnonexibimusnequefaciemusverbum.la: Et dixérunt: Non exíbimus, neque faciémus verbum regis, ut polluámus diem sabbatórum.

etconcitaveruntadversuseosprelium.en: And they made haste to give them battle.

etnonresponderunteisneclapidemmiseruntin.en: But they answered them not, neither did they cast a stone at them, nor stopped up the secret places,
etnonresponderunteisneclapidemmiseruntin.la: Et non respondérunt eis, nec lápidem misérunt in eos, nec oppilavérunt loca occúlta,

dicentesmoriamuromnesinsimplicitatenostr.en: Saying: Let us all die in our innocency: and heaven and earth shall be witnesses for us, that you put us to death wrongfully.
dicentesmoriamuromnesinsimplicitatenostr.la: dicéntes: Moriámur omnes in simplicitáte nostra: et testes erunt super nos cælum et terra, quod iniúste pérditis nos.

etintuleruntillisbellumsabbatisetmortuis.en: So they gave them battle on the sabbath: and they were slain, with their wives, and their children, and their cattle, to the number of a thousand persons.
etintuleruntillisbellumsabbatisetmortuis.la: Et intulérunt illis bellum sábbatis: et mórtui sunt ipsi, et uxóres eórum, et fílii eórum, et pécora eórum usque ad mille ánimas hóminum.

tunccongregatestadeossynagogaassideorumf.en: Then was assembled to them the congregation of the Assideans, the stoutest of Israel, every one that had a good will for the law.
tunccongregatestadeossynagogaassideorumf.la: Tunc congregáta est ad eos synagóga Assidæórum fortis víribus ex Israël, omnis voluntárius in lege:

etomnesquifugiebantamalisadditisuntadeos.en: And all they that fled from the evils, joined themselves to them, and were a support to them.
etomnesquifugiebantamalisadditisuntadeos.la: et omnes, qui fugiébant a malis, ádditi sunt ad eos, et facti sunt illis ad firmaméntum.

etcollegeruntexercitumetpercusseruntpecc.en: And they gathered an army, and slew the sinners in their wrath, and the wicked men in their indignation: and the rest fled to the nations for safety.
etcollegeruntexercitumetpercusseruntpecc.la: Et collegérunt exércitum, et percussérunt peccatóres in ira sua, et viros iníquos in indignatióne sua: et céteri fugérunt ad natiónes, ut eváderent.

etcircuivitmathathiasetamicieiusetdestru.en: And Mathathias and his friends went round about, and they threw down the altars:
etcircuivitmathathiasetamicieiusetdestru.la: Et circuívit Mathathías et amíci ejus, et destruxérunt aras:

etcircumcideruntpuerosincircumcisosquotq.en: And they circumcised all the children whom they found in the confines of Israel that were uncircumcised: and they did valiantly.
etcircumcideruntpuerosincircumcisosquotq.la: et circumcidérunt púeros incircumcísos quotquot invenérunt in fínibus Israël: et in fortitúdine.

etpersecutisuntfiliossuperbieetprosperat.en: And they pursued after the children of pride, and the work prospered in their hands:
etpersecutisuntfiliossuperbieetprosperat.la: Et persecúti sunt fílios supérbiæ, et prosperátum est opus in mánibus eórum:

etobtinueruntlegemdemanibusgentiumetdema.en: And they recovered the law out of the hands of the nations, and out of the hands of the kings: and they yielded not the horn to the sinner.
etobtinueruntlegemdemanibusgentiumetdema.la: et obtinuérunt legem de mánibus géntium, et de mánibus regum, et non dedérunt cornu peccatóri.

etbenedixiteosmathathiasetappositusestad.en: And he blessed them, and was joined to his fathers.
etbenedixiteosmathathiasetappositusestad.la: Et benedíxit eos (Mathathías) et appósitus est ad patres suos.

etdefunctusestannocentesimetquadragesimo.en: And he died in the hundred and forty-sixth year: and he was buried by his sons in the sepulchres of his fathers, in Modin, and all Israel mourned for him with great mourning.
etdefunctusestannocentesimetquadragesimo.la: Et defúnctus est anno centésimo et quadragésimo sexto: et sepúltus est a fíliis suis in sepúlcris patrum suórum in Modin, et planxérunt eum omnis Israël planctu magno.

etdilatavitgloriampopulosuetinduitselori.en: And he got his people great honour, and put on a breastplate as a giant, and girt his warlike armour about him in battles, and protected the camp with his sword.
etdilatavitgloriampopulosuetinduitselori.la: Et dilatávit glóriam pópulo suo, et índuit se lorícam sicut gigas, et succínxit se arma béllica sua in prœ́liis, et protegébat castra gládio suo.

similisfactusestleoniinoperibussuisetsic.en: In his acts he was like a lion, and like a lion's whelp roaring for his prey.
similisfactusestleoniinoperibussuisetsic.la: Símilis factus est leóni in opéribus suis, et sicut cátulus leónis rúgiens in venatióne.

etaudivitseronprincepsexercitussyriequod.en: And Seron, captain of the army of Syria, heard that Judas had assembled a company of the faithful, and a congregation with him,
etaudivitseronprincepsexercitussyriequod.la: Et audívit Seron princeps exércitus Sýriæ, quod congregávit Judas congregatiónem fidélium, et ecclésiam secum,

etaitfaciammihinomenetglorificaborinregn.en: And he said I will get me a name, and will be glorified in the kingdom, and will overthrow Judas, and those that are with him, that have despised the edict of the king.
etaitfaciammihinomenetglorificaborinregn.la: et ait: Fáciam mihi nomen, et glorificábor in regno, et debellábo Judam, et eos qui cum ipso sunt, qui spernébant verbum regis.

etpreparavitseetascenderuntcumeocastraim.en: And he made himself ready; and the host of the wicked went up with him, strong succours, to be revenged of the children of Israel.
etpreparavitseetascenderuntcumeocastraim.la: Et præparávit se: et ascendérunt cum eo castra impiórum fortes auxiliárii ut fácerent vindíctam in fílios Israël.

etappropinquaveruntusqueadbethoronetexiv.en: And they approached even as far as Bethoron: and Judas went forth to meet him, with a small company.
etappropinquaveruntusqueadbethoronetexiv.la: Et appropinquavérunt usque ad Béthoron: et exívit Judas óbviam illi cum paucis.

utautemvideruntexercitumvenientemsibiobv.en: But when they saw the army coming to meet them, they said to Judas: How shall we, being few, be able to fight against so great a multitude, and so strong, and we are ready to faint with fasting today?
utautemvideruntexercitumvenientemsibiobv.la: Ut autem vidérunt exércitum veniéntem sibi óbviam, dixérunt Judæ: Quómodo potérimus pauci pugnáre contra multitúdinem tantam, et tam fortem, et nos fatigáti sumus jeiúnio hódie?

etaitiudasfacileestconcludimultosinmanus.en: And Judas said: It is an easy matter for many to be shut up in the hands of a few: and there is no difference in the sight of the God of heaven to deliver with a great multitude, or with a small company:
etaitiudasfacileestconcludimultosinmanus.la: Et ait Judas: Fácile est conclúdi multos in manus paucórum: et non est differéntia in conspéctu Dei cæli liberáre in multis, et in paucis.

congregavitlysiasvirorumelectorumsexagin.en: So the year following, Lysias gathered together threescore thousand chosen men, and five thousand horsemen, that he might subdue them.
congregavitlysiasvirorumelectorumsexagin.la: Congregávit Lýsias virórum electórum sexagínta míllia, et équitum quinque míllia, ut debelláret eos.

etveneruntiniudeametcastraposueruntinbet.en: And they came into Judea, and pitched their tents in Bethoron, and Judas met them with ten thousand men.
etveneruntiniudeametcastraposueruntinbet.la: Et venérunt in Judǽam, et castra posuérunt in Béthoron, et occúrrit illis Judas cum decem míllibus viris.

etvideruntexercitumfortemetoravitetdixit.en: And they saw that the army was strong, and he prayed and said: Blessed art thou, O Saviour of Israel, who didst break the violence of the mighty by the hand of thy servant David, and didst deliver up the camp of the strangers into the hands of Jonathan the son of Saul, and of his armour bearer.
etvideruntexercitumfortemetoravitetdixit.la: Et vidérunt exércitum fortem, et orávit, et dixit: Benedíctus es salvátor Israël, qui contrivísti ímpetum poténtis in manu servi tui David, et tradidísti castra alienigenárum in manu Jónathæ fílii Saul, et armígeri ejus.

concludeexercitumistuminmanupopulituiisr.en: Shut up this army in the hands of thy people Israel, and let them be confounded in their host and their horsemen.
concludeexercitumistuminmanupopulituiisr.la: Conclúde exércitum istum in manu pópuli tui Israël, et confundántur in exércitu suo et equítibus.

daillisformidinemettabefacaudaciamvirtut.en: Strike them with fear, and cause the boldness of their strength to languish, and let them quake at their own destruction.
daillisformidinemettabefacaudaciamvirtut.la: Da illis formídinem, et tábefac audáciam virtútis eórum, et commoveántur contritióne sua.

deiceillosgladiodiligentiumteetcollauden.en: Cast them down with the sword of them that love thee: and let all that know thy name praise thee with hymns.
deiceillosgladiodiligentiumteetcollauden.la: Déice illos gládio diligéntium te: et colláudent te omnes, qui novérunt nomen tuum, in hymnis.

etcommiseruntpreliumetcecideruntdeexerci.en: And they joined battle: and there fell of the army of Lysias five thousand men.
etcommiseruntpreliumetcecideruntdeexerci.la: Et commisérunt prœ́lium: et cecidérunt de exércitu Lýsiæ quinque míllia virórum.

vidensautemlysiasfugamsuorumetiudeorumau.en: And when Lysias saw that his men were put to flight, and how bold the Jews were, and that they were ready either to live, or to die manfully, he went to Antioch, and chose soldiers, that they might come again into Judea with greater numbers.
vidensautemlysiasfugamsuorumetiudeorumau.la: Videns autem Lýsias fugam suórum, et Judæórum audáciam, et quod paráti sunt aut vívere, aut mori fórtiter, ábiit Antiochíam, et elégit mílites, ut multiplicáti rursus venírent in Judǽam.

regnantedemetrioannocentesimosexagesimon.en: When Demetrius reigned, in the year one hundred and sixty-nine, we Jews wrote to you in the trouble and violence that came upon us in those years, after Jason withdrew himself from the holy land, and from the kingdom.
regnantedemetrioannocentesimosexagesimon.la: Regnánte Demétrio, anno centésimo sexagésimo nono, nos Judǽi scrípsimus vobis in tribulatióne et ímpetu qui supervénit nobis in istis annis, ex quo recéssit Jason a sancta terra, et a regno.

portamsuccenderunteteffuderuntsanguinemi.en: They burnt the gate, and shed innocent blood: then we prayed to the Lord, and were heard, and we offered sacrifices, and fine flour, and lighted the lamps, and set forth the loaves.
portamsuccenderunteteffuderuntsanguinemi.la: Portam succendérunt, et effudérunt sánguinem innocéntem: et orávimus ad Dóminum, et exaudíti sumus, et obtúlimus sacrifícium et similáginem, et accéndimus lucérnas, et proposúimus panes.

etnuncfrequentatediesscenopegiemensiscas.en: And now celebrate ye the days of Scenopegia in the month of Casleu.
etnuncfrequentatediesscenopegiemensiscas.la: Et nunc frequentáte dies scenopégiæ mensis Casleu.

demagnispericulisadeoliberatimagnificegr.en: Having been delivered by God out of great dangers, we give him great thanks, forasmuch as we have been in war with such a king.
demagnispericulisadeoliberatimagnificegr.la: De magnis perículis a Deo liberáti, magnífice grátias ágimus ipsi, útpote qui advérsus talem regem dimicávimus.

ipseenimebullirefecitdepersideeosquipugn.en: For he made numbers of men swarm out of Persia, that have fought against us, and the holy city.
ipseenimebullirefecitdepersideeosquipugn.la: Ipse enim ebullíre fecit de Pérside eos qui pugnavérunt contra nos et sanctam civitátem.

peromniabenedictusdeusquitradiditimpios.en: Blessed be God in all things, who hath delivered up the wicked.
peromniabenedictusdeusquitradiditimpios.la: Per ómnia benedíctus Deus, qui trádidit ímpios.

orationemautemfaciebantomnessacerdotesdu.en: And all the priests made prayer, while the sacrifice was consuming, Jonathan beginning, and the rest answering.
orationemautemfaciebantomnessacerdotesdu.la: Oratiónem autem faciébant omnes sacerdótes, dum consummarétur sacrifícium, Jónatha inchoánte, céteris autem respondéntibus.

etnehemieeratoratiohunchabensmodumdomine.en: And the prayer of Nehemias was after this manner: O Lord God, Creator of all things, dreadful and strong, just and merciful, who alone art the good king,
etnehemieeratoratiohunchabensmodumdomine.la: Et Nehemíæ erat orátio hunc habens modum: Dómine Deus ómnium creátor, terríbilis et fortis, justus et miséricors, qui solus est bonus rex,

solusprestanssolusiustusetomnipotensetet.en: Who alone art gracious, who alone art just, and almighty, and eternal, who deliverest Israel from all evil, who didst choose the fathers, and didst sanctify them:
solusprestanssolusiustusetomnipotensetet.la: solus præstans, solus justus et omnípotens et ætérnus, qui líberas Israël de omni malo: qui fecísti patres eléctos, et sanctificásti eos:

accipesacrificiumprouniversopopulotuoisr.en: Receive the sacrifice for all thy people Israel, and preserve thy own portion, and sanctify it.
accipesacrificiumprouniversopopulotuoisr.la: áccipe sacrifícium pro univérso pópulo tuo Israël, et custódi partem tuam, et sanctífica.

congregadispersionemnostramlibereosquise.en: Gather together our scattered people, deliver them that are slaves to the Gentiles, and look upon them that are despised and abhorred: that the Gentiles may know that thou art our God
congregadispersionemnostramlibereosquise.la: Cóngrega dispersiónem nostram, líbera eos qui sérviunt géntibus, et contémptos et abominátos réspice, ut sciant gentes quia tu es Deus noster.

affligeopprimentesnosetcontumeliamfacien.en: Punish them that oppress us, and that treat us injuriously with pride.
affligeopprimentesnosetcontumeliamfacien.la: Afflíge oppriméntes nos, et contuméliam faciéntes in supérbia.

constituepopulumtuuminlocosanctotuosicut.en: Establish thy people in thy holy place, as Moses hath spoken.
constituepopulumtuuminlocosanctotuosicut.la: Constítue pópulum tuum in loco sancto tuo, sicut dixit Móyses.

sacerdotesautempsallebanthymnosusquequoc.en: And the priests sung hymns till the sacrifice was consumed.
sacerdotesautempsallebanthymnosusquequoc.la: Sacerdótes autem psallébant hymnos úsquequo consúmptum esset sacrifícium.

cumautemconsumptumessetsacrificiumexresi.en: And when the sacrifice was consumed, Nehemias commanded the water that was left to be poured out upon the great stones.
cumautemconsumptumessetsacrificiumexresi.la: Cum autem consúmptum esset sacrifícium, ex resídua aqua Nehemías jussit lápides maióres perfúndi.

quodutfactumestexeisflammaaccensestsedex.en: Which being done, there was kindled a flame from them: but it was consumed by the light that shined from the altar.
quodutfactumestexeisflammaaccensestsedex.la: Quod ut factum est, ex eis flamma accénsa est: sed ex lúmine quod refúlsit ab altári, consúmpta est.

utveromanifestatestresrenuntiatumestregi.en: And when this matter became public, it was told to the king of Persia, that in the place where the priests that were led away, had hid the fire, there appeared water, with which Nehemias and they that were with him had purified the sacrifices.
utveromanifestatestresrenuntiatumestregi.la: Ut vero manifestáta est res, renuntiátum est regi Persárum quod in loco in quo ignem abscónderant hi qui transláti fúerant sacerdótes, aqua appáruit, de qua Nehemías, et qui cum eo erant, purificavérunt sacrifícia.

constitutaautemdieintrabatdehisheliodoru.en: So on the day he had appointed, Heliodorus entered in to order this matter. But there was no small terror throughout the whole city.
constitutaautemdieintrabatdehisheliodoru.la: Constitúta autem die, intrábat de his Heliodórus ordinatúrus. Non módica vero per univérsam civitátem erat trepidátio.

sacerdotesautemantealtarecumstolissacerd.en: And the priests prostrated themselves before the altar in their priests' vestments, and called upon him from heaven, who made the law concerning things given to be kept, that he would preserve them safe, for them that had deposited them.
sacerdotesautemantealtarecumstolissacerd.la: Sacerdótes autem ante altáre cum stolis sacerdotálibus jactavérunt se, et invocábant de cælo eum qui de depósitis legem pósuit, ut his qui deposúerant ea salva custodíret.

iamveroquividebatsummisacerdotisvultumme.en: Now whosoever saw the countenance of the high priest, was wounded in heart: for his face, and the changing of his colour, declared the inward sorrow of his mind.
iamveroquividebatsummisacerdotisvultumme.la: Jam vero qui vidébat summi sacerdótis vultum, mente vulnerabátur: fácies enim et color immutátus declarábat intérnum ánimi dolórem.

circumfusenimeratmestitiaquedamvirethorr.en: For the man was so compassed with sadness and horror of the body, that it was manifest to them that beheld him, what sorrow he had in his heart.
circumfusenimeratmestitiaquedamvirethorr.la: circumfúsa enim erat mœstítia quædam viro, et horror córporis, per quem maniféstus aspiciéntibus dolor cordis ejus efficiebátur.

aliietiamgregatimdedomibusconfluebantpub.en: Others also came flocking together out of their houses, praying and making public supplication, because the place was like to come into contempt.
aliietiamgregatimdedomibusconfluebantpub.la: Alii étiam gregátim de dómibus confluébant, pública supplicatióne obsecrántes, pro eo quod in contémptum locus esset ventúrus.

universeautemprotendentesmanusincelumdep.en: And all holding up their hands towards heaven made supplication.
universeautemprotendentesmanusincelumdep.la: univérsæ autem protendéntes manus in cælum, deprecabántur:

eratenimmiseracommistemultitudinisetmagn.en: For the expectation of the mixed multitude, and of the high priest, who was in an agony, would have moved any one to pity.
eratenimmiseracommistemultitudinisetmagn.la: erat enim mísera commístæ multitúdinis, et magni sacerdótis in agóne constitúti exspectátio.

dicentesdominusdeusaspicietveritatemetco.en: Saying: The Lord God will look upon the truth, and will take pleasure in us, as Moses declared in the profession of the canticle; And in his servants he will take pleasure.
dicentesdominusdeusaspicietveritatemetco.la: dicéntes: Dóminus Deus aspíciet veritátem, et consolábitur in nobis, quemádmodum in protestatióne cántici declarávit Móyses: Et in servis suis consolábitur.

iudasveromachabeusetquicumillerantintroi.en: But Judas Machabeus, and they that were with him, went privately into the towns: and calling together their kinsmen and friends, and taking unto them such as continued in the Jews' religion, they assembled six thousand men.
iudasveromachabeusetquicumillerantintroi.la: Judas vero Machabǽus, et qui cum illo erant, introíbant laténter in castélla: et convocántes cognátos et amícos, et eos qui permansérunt in Judaísmo assuméntes, eduxérunt ad se sex míllia virórum.

etinvocabantdominumutrespiceretinpopulum.en: And they called upon the Lord, that he would look upon his people that was trodden down by all and would have pity on the temple, that was defiled by the wicked:
etinvocabantdominumutrespiceretinpopulum.la: Et invocábant Dóminum, ut respíceret in pópulum qui ab ómnibus calcabátur, et misererétur templo quod contaminabátur ab ímpiis:

miserereturetiamexterminiocivitatisquees.en: That he would have pity also upon the city that was destroyed, that was ready to be made even with the ground, and would hear the voice of the blood that cried to him:
miserereturetiamexterminiocivitatisquees.la: misererétur étiam extermínio civitátis, quæ esset íllico complanánda, et vocem sánguinis ad se clamántis audíret.

atmachabeuscongregatamultitudineintolera.en: Now when Machabeus had gathered a multitude, he could not be withstood by the heathens: for the wrath of the Lord was turned into mercy.
atmachabeuscongregatamultitudineintolera.la: At Machabǽus, congregáta multitúdine, intolerábilis géntibus efficiebátur: ira enim Dómini in misericórdiam convérsa est.

etsupervenienscastellisetcivitatibusimpr.en: So coming unawares upon the towns and cities, he set them on fire, and taking possession of the most commodious places, he made no small slaughter of the enemies:
etsupervenienscastellisetcivitatibusimpr.la: Et supervéniens castéllis et civitátibus improvísus, succendébat eas: et opportúna loca óccupans, non paucas hóstium strages dabat:

maximeautemnoctibusadhuiuscemodiexcursus.en: And especially in the nights he went upon these expeditions, and the fame of his valour was spread abroad every where.
maximeautemnoctibusadhuiuscemodiexcursus.la: máxime autem nóctibus ad hujuscémodi excúrsus ferebátur, et fama virtútis ejus ubíque diffundebátur.

vidensautemphilippuspaulatimvirumadprofe.en: Then Philip seeing that the man gained ground by little and little, and that things for the most part succeeded prosperously with him, wrote to Ptolemee, the governor of Celesyria and Phenicia, to send aid to the king's affairs.
vidensautemphilippuspaulatimvirumadprofe.la: Videns autem Philíppus paulátim virum ad proféctum veníre, ac frequéntius res ei cédere próspere, ad Ptolemǽum ducem Cœlesýriæ et Phœnícis scripsit ut auxílium ferret regis negótiis.

etdeprelioquodeisadversusgalatasfuitinba.en: And of the battle that they had fought against the Galatians, in Babylonia; how they, being in all but six thousand, when it came to the point, and the Macedonians, their companions, were at a stand, slew a hundred and twenty thousand, because of the help they had from heaven, and for this they received many favours.
etdeprelioquodeisadversusgalatasfuitinba.la: et de prœ́lio quod eis advérsus Gálatas fuit in Babylónia, ut omnes, ubi ad rem ventum est, Macedónibus sóciis hæsitántibus, ipsi sex míllia soli peremérunt centum vigínti míllia, propter auxílium illis datum de cælo, et benefícia pro his plúrima consecúti sunt.

hincigiturcepitexgravisuperbiadeductusad.en: And by this means, being brought from his great pride, he began to come to the knowledge of himself, being admonished by the scourge of God, his pains increasing every moment.
hincigiturcepitexgravisuperbiadeductusad.la: Hinc ígitur cœpit ex gravi supérbia dedúctus ad agnitiónem sui veníre, divína admónitus plaga, per moménta síngula dolóribus suis augménta capiéntibus.

etcumnecipseiamfetoremsuumferrepossetita.en: And when he himself could not now abide his own stench, he spoke thus: It is just to be subject to God, and that a mortal man should not equal himself to God.
etcumnecipseiamfetoremsuumferrepossetita.la: Et cum nec ipse jam fœtórem suum ferre posset, ita ait: Justum est súbditum esse Deo, et mortálem non pária Deo sentíre.

orabatautemhicscelestusdominumaquononess.en: Then this wicked man prayed to the Lord, of whom he was not like to obtain mercy.
orabatautemhicscelestusdominumaquononess.la: Orábat autem hic sceléstus Dóminum, a quo non esset misericórdiam consecutúrus.

etcivitatemadquamfestinansveniebatuteama.en: And the city, to which he was going in haste to lay it even with the ground, and to make it a common burying place, he now desireth to make free:
etcivitatemadquamfestinansveniebatuteama.la: Et civitátem, ad quam festínans veniébat ut eam ad solum dedúceret ac sepúlcrum congestórum fáceret, nunc optat líberam réddere:

etiudeosquosnecsepulturaquidemsedignosha.en: And the Jews, whom he said he would not account worthy to be so much as buried, but would give them up to be devoured by the birds and wild beasts, and would utterly destroy them with their children, he now promiseth to make equal with the Athenians.
etiudeosquosnecsepulturaquidemsedignosha.la: et Judǽos, quos nec sepultúra quidem se dignos habitúrum, sed ávibus ac feris diripiéndos traditúrum, et cum párvulis exterminatúrum díxerat, æquáles nunc Atheniénsibus factúrum pollicétur:

sednoncessantibusdoloribussuperveneraten.en: But his pains not ceasing, (for the just judgment of God was come upon him) despairing of life, he wrote to the Jews, in the manner of a supplication, a letter in these words:
sednoncessantibusdoloribussuperveneraten.la: Sed non cessántibus dolóribus (supervénerat enim in eum justum Dei judícium), despérans scripsit ad Judǽos in modum deprecatiónis epístolam hæc continéntem:

optimiscivibusiudeisplurimamsalutemetben.en: To his very good subjects the Jews, Antiochus, king and ruler, wisheth much health, and welfare, and happiness.
optimiscivibusiudeisplurimamsalutemetben.la: Optimis cívibus Judǽis plúrimam salútem, et bene valére, et esse felíces, rex et príncipes Antíochus.

sibenevaletisetfiliivestrietexsententiav.en: If you and your children are well, and if all matters go with you to your mind, we give very great thanks.
sibenevaletisetfiliivestrietexsententiav.la: Si bene valétis, et fílii vestri, et ex senténtia vobis cuncta sunt, máximas ágimus grátias.

etegoininfirmitateconstitutusvestriautem.en: As for me, being infirm, but yet kindly remembering you, returning out of the places of Persia, and being taken with a grievous disease, I thought it necessary to take care for the common good:
etegoininfirmitateconstitutusvestriautem.la: Et ego in infirmitáte constitútus, vestri autem memor benígne revérsus de Pérsidis locis, et infirmitáte gravi apprehénsus, necessárium duxi pro commúni utilitáte curam habére:

nondesperansmemetipsumsedspemmultamhaben.en: Not distrusting my life, but having great hope to escape the sickness.
nondesperansmemetipsumsedspemmultamhaben.la: non despérans memetípsum, sed spem multam habens effugiéndi infirmitátem.

respiciensautemquodetpatermeusquibustemp.en: But considering that my father also, at what time he led an army into the higher countries, appointed who should reign after him:
respiciensautemquodetpatermeusquibustemp.la: Respíciens autem quod et pater meus, quibus tempóribus in locis superióribus ducébat exércitum, osténdit qui post se suscíperet principátum:

utsiquidcontrariumaccideretautdifficilen.en: To the end that if any thing contrary to expectation should fall out, or any bad tidings should be brought, they that were in the countries, knowing to whom the whole government was left, might not be troubled.
utsiquidcontrariumaccideretautdifficilen.la: ut si quid contrárium accíderet, aut diffícile nuntiarétur, sciéntes hi qui in regiónibus erant, cui esset rerum summa derelícta, non turbaréntur.

nicanorautemutcomperitiudamesseinlocissa.en: But when Nicanor understood that Judas was in the places of Samaria, he purposed to set upon him with all violence, on the sabbath day.
nicanorautemutcomperitiudamesseinlocissa.la: Nicánor autem, ut cómperit Judam esse in locis Samaríæ, cogitávit cum omni ímpetu die sábbati commíttere bellum.

iudeisveroquiillumpernecessitatemsequeba.en: And when the Jews that were constrained to follow him, said: Do not act so fiercely and barbarously, but give honour to the day that is sanctified: and reverence him that beholdeth all things:
iudeisveroquiillumpernecessitatemsequeba.la: Judǽis vero qui illum per necessitátem sequebántur, dicéntibus: Ne ita feróciter et bárbare féceris, sed honórem tríbue diéi sanctificatiónis, et honóra eum qui univérsa cónspicit:

illeinfelixinterrogavitsiestpotensincelo.en: That unhappy man asked, if there were a mighty One in heaven, that had commanded the sabbath day to be kept.
illeinfelixinterrogavitsiestpotensincelo.la: ille infélix interrogávit si est potens in cælo, qui imperávit agi diem sabbatórum.

etrespondentibusillisestdominusvivusipse.en: And when they answered: There is the living Lord himself in heaven, the mighty One, that commanded the seventh day to be kept.
etrespondentibusillisestdominusvivusipse.la: Et respondéntibus illis: Est Dóminus vivus ipse in cælo potens, qui jussit agi séptimam diem:

atilleaitetegopotenssumsuperterramquiimp.en: Then he said: And I am mighty upon the earth, and I command to take arms, and to do the king's business. Nevertheless he prevailed not to accomplish his design.
atilleaitetegopotenssumsuperterramquiimp.la: at ille ait: Et ego potens sum super terram qui ímpero sumi arma, et negótia regis impléri. Tamen non obtínuit ut consílium perfíceret.

etnicanorquidemcumsummasuperbierectuscog.en: So Nicanor being puffed up with exceeding great pride, thought to set up a public monument of his victory over Judas.
etnicanorquidemcumsummasuperbierectuscog.la: Et Nicánor quidem cum summa supérbia eréctus, cogitáverat commúne trophǽum statúere de Juda.

etcumiamomnessperarentiudiciumfuturumhos.en: And now when all expected what judgment would be given, and the enemies were at hand, and the army was set in array, the beasts and the horsemen ranged in convenient places,
etcumiamomnessperarentiudiciumfuturumhos.la: Et cum jam omnes sperárent judícium futúrum, hostésque adéssent atque exércitus esset ordinátus, béstiæ equitésque opportúno in loco compósiti,

consideransmachabeusadventummultitudinis.en: Machabeus considering the coming of the multitude, and the divers preparations of armour, and the fierceness of the beasts, stretching out his hands to heaven, called upon the Lord, that worketh wonders, who giveth victory to them that are worthy, not according to the power of their arms, but according as it seemeth good to him.
consideransmachabeusadventummultitudinis.la: consíderans Machabǽus advéntum multitúdinis, et apparátum várium armórum, et ferocitátem bestiárum, exténdens manus in cælum, prodígia faciéntem Dóminum invocávit, qui non secúndum armórum poténtiam, sed prout ipsi placet, dat dignis victóriam.

nicanorautemetquicumipserantcumtubisetca.en: But Nicanor, and they that were with him came forward, with trumpets and songs.
nicanorautemetquicumipserantcumtubisetca.la: Nicánor autem et qui cum ipso erant, cum tubis et cánticis admovébant.

iudasveretquicumeerantinvocatodeoperorat.en: But Judas, and they that were with him, encountered them, calling upon God by prayers:
iudasveretquicumeerantinvocatodeoperorat.la: Judas vero et qui cum eo erant, invocáto Deo, per oratiónes congréssi sunt:

manuquidempugnantesseddominumcordibusora.en: So fighting with their hands, but praying to the Lord with their hearts, they slew no less than five and thirty thousand, being greatly cheered with the presence of God.
manuquidempugnantesseddominumcordibusora.la: manu quidem pugnántes, sed Dóminum córdibus orántes, prostravérunt non minus trigínta quinque míllia, præséntia Dei magnífice delectáti.

cumquecessassentetcumgaudioredirentcogno.en: And when the battle was over, and they were returning with joy, they understood that Nicanor was slain in his armour.
cumquecessassentetcumgaudioredirentcogno.la: Cumque cessássent, et cum gáudio redírent, cognovérunt Nicánorem ruísse cum armis suis.

factoitaqueclamoreetperturbationeexcitat.en: Then making a shout, and a great noise, they blessed the Almighty Lord in their own language.
factoitaqueclamoreetperturbationeexcitat.la: Facto ítaque clamóre, et perturbatióne excitáta, pátria voce omnipoténtem Dóminum benedicébant.

precepitautemiudasquiperomniacorporeetan.en: And Judas, who was altogether ready, in body and mind, to die for his countrymen, commanded that Nicanor's head, and his hand, with the shoulder, should be cut off, and carried to Jerusalem.
precepitautemiudasquiperomniacorporeetan.la: Præcépit autem Judas, qui per ómnia córpore et ánimo mori pro cívibus parátus erat, caput Nicánoris, et manum cum húmero abscíssam, Jerosólymam perférri.

quocumpervenissetconvocatiscontribulibus.en: And when he was come thither, having called together his countrymen, and the priests to the altar, he sent also for them that were in the castle,
quocumpervenissetconvocatiscontribulibus.la: Quo cum pervenísset, convocátis contribúlibus et sacerdótibus ad altáre, accersíit et eos qui in arce erant.

etostensocapitenicanorisetmanunefariaqua.en: And shewing them the head of Nicanor, and the wicked hand, which he had stretched out, with proud boasts, against the holy house of the Almighty God,
etostensocapitenicanorisetmanunefariaqua.la: Et osténso cápite Nicánoris, et manu nefária quam exténdens contra domum sanctam omnipoténtis Dei magnífice gloriátus est.

linguametiamimpiinicanorisprecisamiussit.en: He commanded also, that the tongue of the wicked Nicanor should be cut out, and given by pieces to birds, and the hand of the furious man to be hanged up over against the temple.
linguametiamimpiinicanorisprecisamiussit.la: Linguam étiam ímpii Nicánoris præcísam jussit particulátim ávibus dari: manum autem deméntis contra templum suspéndi.

omnesigiturcelibenedixeruntdominumdicent.en: Then all blessed the Lord of heaven, saying: Blessed be he that hath kept his own place undefiled.
omnesigiturcelibenedixeruntdominumdicent.la: Omnes ígitur cæli benedixérunt Dóminum, dicéntes: Benedíctus qui locum suum incontaminátum servávit.

spiritusquoquelevavitmeetassumpsitmeetab.en: The spirit also lifted me, and took me up: and I went away in bitterness in the indignation of my spirit: for the hand of the Lord was with me, strengthening me.
spiritusquoquelevavitmeetassumpsitmeetab.la: Spíritus quoque levávit me, et assúmpsit me: et ábii amárus in indignatióne spíritus mei: manus enim Dómini erat mecum, confórtans me.

etveniadtransmigrationemadacervumnovarum.en: And I came to them of the captivity, to the heap of new corn, to them that dwelt by the river Chobar, and I sat where they sat: and I remained there seven days mourning in the midst of them.
etveniadtransmigrationemadacervumnovarum.la: Et veni ad transmigratiónem, ad acérvum novárum frugum, ad eos qui habitábant juxta flumen Chobar: et sedi ubi illi sedébant, et mansi ibi septem diébus mœrens in médio eórum.

cumautempertransissentseptemdiesfactumes.en: And at the end of seven days the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
cumautempertransissentseptemdiesfactumes.la: Cum autem pertransíssent septem dies, factum est verbum Dómini ad me, dicens:

filihominisspeculatoremdeditedomuiisrele.en: Son of man, I have made thee a watchman to the house of Israel: and thou shalt hear the word out of my mouth, and shalt tell it them from me.
filihominisspeculatoremdeditedomuiisrele.la: Fili hóminis, speculatórem dedi te dómui Israël, et áudies de ore meo verbum, et annuntiábis eis ex me.

sidicentemeadimpiummortemorierisnonannun.en: If, when I say to the wicked, Thou shalt surely die: thou declare it not to him, nor speak to him, that he may be converted from his wicked way, and live: the same wicked man shall die in his iniquity, but I will require his blood at thy hand.
sidicentemeadimpiummortemorierisnonannun.la: Si dicénte me ad ímpium: Morte moriéris, non annuntiáveris ei, neque locútus fúeris ut avertátur a via sua ímpia et vivat, ipse ímpius in iniquitáte sua moriétur, sánguinem autem ejus de manu tua requíram.

siautemtuannuntiaverisimpietillenonfueri.en: But if thou give warning to the wicked, and he be not converted from his wickedness, and from his evil way: he indeed shall die in his iniquity, but thou hast delivered thy soul.
siautemtuannuntiaverisimpietillenonfueri.la: Si autem tu annuntiáveris ímpio, et ille non fúerit convérsus ab impietáte sua et a via sua ímpia, ipse quidem in iniquitáte sua moriétur: tu autem ánimam tuam liberásti.

ettufilihominissumetibilateremetponeseum.en: And thou, O son of man, take thee a tile, and lay it before thee: and draw upon it the plan of the city of Jerusalem.
ettufilihominissumetibilateremetponeseum.la: Et tu fili hóminis, sume tibi láterem, et pones eum coram te, et descríbes in eo civitátem Jerúsalem.

etordinabisadversuseamobsidionemetedific.en: And lay siege against it, and build forts, and cast up a mount, and set a camp against it, and place battering rams round about it.
etordinabisadversuseamobsidionemetedific.la: Et ordinábis advérsus eam obsidiónem, et ædificábis munitiónes, et comportábis ággerem, et dabis contra eam castra, et pones aríetes in gyro.

ettusumetibisartaginemferreametponeseami.en: And take unto thee an iron pan, and set it for a wall of iron between thee and the city: and set thy face resolutely against it, and it shall be besieged, and thou shalt lay siege against it: it is a sign to the house of Israel.
ettusumetibisartaginemferreametponeseami.la: Et tu sume tibi sartáginem férream, et pones eam in murum férreum inter te et inter civitátem: et obfirmábis fáciem tuam ad eam, et erit in obsidiónem, et circúmdabis eam: signum est dómui Israël.

ettudormiessuperlatustuumsinistrumetpone.en: And thou shalt sleep upon thy left side, and shalt lay the iniquities of the house of Israel upon it, according to the number of the days that thou shalt sleep upon it, and thou shalt take upon thee their iniquity.
ettudormiessuperlatustuumsinistrumetpone.la: Et tu dórmies super latus tuum sinístrum, et pones iniquitátes domus Israël super eo, número diérum quibus dórmies super illud: et assúmes iniquitátem eórum.

egoautemdeditibiannosiniquitatiseorumnum.en: And I have laid upon thee the years of their iniquity, according to the number of the days three hundred and ninety days: and thou shalt bear the iniquity of the house of Israel.
egoautemdeditibiannosiniquitatiseorumnum.la: Ego autem dedi tibi annos iniquitátis eórum, número diérum trecéntos et nonagínta dies: et portábis iniquitátem domus Israël.

etcumcompleverishecdormiessuperlatustuum.en: And when thou hast accomplished this, thou shalt sleep again upon thy right side, and thou shalt take upon thee the iniquity of the house of Juda forty days: a day for a year, yea, a day for a year I have appointed to thee.
etcumcompleverishecdormiessuperlatustuum.la: Et cum compléveris hæc, dórmies super latus tuum déxterum secúndo, et assúmes iniquitátem domus Juda quadragínta diébus: diem pro anno, diem, inquam, pro anno dedi tibi.

etadobsidionemierusalemconvertesfaciemtu.en: And thou shalt turn thy face to the siege of Jerusalem and thy arm shall be stretched out: and thou shalt prophesy against it.
etadobsidionemierusalemconvertesfaciemtu.la: Et ad obsidiónem Jerúsalem convértes fáciem tuam, et bráchium tuum erit exténtum: et prophetábis advérsus eam.

eccecircumdeditevinculisetnonteconvertes.en: Behold I have encompassed thee with bands: and thou shalt not turn thyself from one side to the other, till thou hast ended the days of thy siege.
eccecircumdeditevinculisetnonteconvertes.la: Ecce circúmdedi te vínculis: et non te convértes a látere tuo in latus áliud, donec cómpleas dies obsidiónis tuæ.

ettufilihominissumetibigladiumacutumrade.en: And thou, son of man, take thee a sharp knife that shaveth the hair: and cause it to pass over thy head, and over thy beard: and take thee a balance to weigh in, and divide the hair.
ettufilihominissumetibigladiumacutumrade.la: Et tu fili hóminis, sume tibi gládium acútum, radéntem pilos: et assúmes eum et duces per caput tuum et per barbam tuam, et assúmes tibi statéram pónderis et dívides eos.

tertiampartemignicomburesinmediocivitati.en: A third part thou shalt burn with fire in the midst of the city, according to the fulfilling of the days of the siege: and thou shalt take a third part, and cut it in pieces with the knife all round about: and the other third part thou shalt scatter in the wind, and I will draw out the sword after them.
tertiampartemignicomburesinmediocivitati.la: Tértiam partem igni combúres in médio civitátis, juxta completiónem diérum obsidiónis: et assúmes tértiam partem, et concídes gládio in circúitu ejus: tértiam vero áliam dispérges in ventum, et gládium nudábo post eos.

etsumesindeparvumnumerumetligabiseosinsu.en: And thou shalt take thereof a small number: and shalt bind them in the skirt of thy cloak.
etsumesindeparvumnumerumetligabiseosinsu.la: Et sumes inde parvum númerum, et ligábis eos in summitáte pállii tui.

etexeisrursumtollesetproicieseosinmedioi.en: And thou shalt take of them again, and shalt cast them in the midst of the fire, and shalt burn them with fire: and out of it shall come forth a fire into all the house of Israel.
etexeisrursumtollesetproicieseosinmedioi.la: Et ex eis rursum tolles, et proícies eos in médio ignis, et combúres eos igni: et ex eo egrediétur ignis in omnem domum Israël.

hecdicitdominusdeusistestierusaleminmedi.en: Thus saith the Lord God: This is Jerusalem, I have set her in the midst of the nations, and the countries round about her.
hecdicitdominusdeusistestierusaleminmedi.la: Hæc dicit Dóminus Deus: Ista est Jerúsalem: in médio géntium pósui eam, et in circúitu ejus terras.

idcircohecdicitdominusdeusquiasuperastis.en: Therefore thus saith the Lord God: Because you have surpassed the Gentiles that are round about you, and have not walked in my commandments, and have not kept my judgments, and have not done according to the judgments of the nations that are round about you:
idcircohecdicitdominusdeusquiasuperastis.la: Idcírco hæc dicit Dóminus Deus: Quia superástis gentes quæ in circúitu vestro sunt, et in præcéptis meis non ambulástis, et judícia mea non fecístis, et juxta judícia géntium quæ in circúitu vestro sunt non estis operáti:

ideohecdicitdominusdeusecceegoadteetipse.en: Therefore thus saith the Lord God: Behold I come against thee, and I myself will execute judgments in the midst of thee in the sight of the Gentiles.
ideohecdicitdominusdeusecceegoadteetipse.la: ídeo hæc dicit Dóminus Deus: Ecce ego ad te, et ipse ego fáciam in médio tui judícia in óculis géntium:

filihominisponefaciemtuamadmontesisrelet.en: Son of man set thy face towards the mountains of Israel, and prophesy against them.
filihominisponefaciemtuamadmontesisrelet.la: Fili hóminis pone fáciem tuam ad montes Israël, et prophetábis ad eos,

etdicesmontesisrelauditeverbumdominideih.en: And say: Ye mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord God: Thus saith the Lord God to the mountains, and to the hills, and to the rocks, and the valleys: Behold, I will bring upon you the sword, and I will destroy your high places.
etdicesmontesisrelauditeverbumdominideih.la: et dices: Montes Israël audíte verbum Dómini Dei. Hæc dicit Dóminus Deus móntibus et cóllibus, rúpibus et vállibus: Ecce ego indúcam super vos gládium, et dispérdam excélsa vestra,

etdemoliararasvestrasetconfringentursimu.en: And I will throw down your altars, and your idols shall be broken in pieces: and I will cast down your slain before your idols.
etdemoliararasvestrasetconfringentursimu.la: et demóliar aras vestras, et confringéntur simulácra vestra, et deíciam interféctos vestros ante idóla vestra.

etdabocadaverafiliorumisrelantefaciemsim.en: And I will lay the dead carcasses of the children of Israel before your idols: and I will scatter your bones round about your altars,
etdabocadaverafiliorumisrelantefaciemsim.la: Et dabo cadávera filiórum Israël ante fáciem simulacrórum vestrórum, et dispérgam ossa vestra circum aras vestras.

inomnibushabitationibusvestrisurbesdeser.en: In all your dwelling places. The cities shall be laid waste, and the high places shall be thrown down, and destroyed, and your altars shall be abolished, and shall be broken in pieces: and your idols shall be no more, and your temples shall be destroyed, and your works shall be defaced.
inomnibushabitationibusvestrisurbesdeser.la: In ómnibus habitatiónibus vestris urbes desértæ erunt, et excélsa demoliéntur, et dissipabúntur: et interíbunt aræ vestræ, et confringéntur: et cessábunt idóla vestra, et conteréntur delúbra vestra, et delebúntur ópera vestra.

etcadetinterfectusinmediovestrietscietis.en: And the slain shall fall in the midst of you: and you shall know that I am the Lord.
etcadetinterfectusinmediovestrietscietis.la: Et cadet interféctus in médio vestri, et sciétis quia ego sum Dóminus.

etrelinquaminvobiseosquifugerintgladiumi.en: And I will leave in you some that shall escape the sword among the nations, when I shall have scattered you through the countries.
etrelinquaminvobiseosquifugerintgladiumi.la: Et relínquam in vobis eos qui fúgerint gládium in géntibus, cum dispérsero vos in terris.

annoprimobaltassarregisbabylonisdanielso.en: In the first year of Baltasar, king of Babylon, Daniel saw a dream: and the vision of his head was upon his bed: and writing the dream, he comprehended it in a few words: and relating the sum of it in short, he said:
annoprimobaltassarregisbabylonisdanielso.la: Anno primo Baltássar regis Babylónis, Dániel sómnium vidit: vísio autem cápitis ejus in cubíli suo: et sómnium scribens, brevi sermóne comprehéndit: summatímque perstríngens, ait:

videbaminvisionemeanocteeteccequatuorven.en: I saw in my vision by night, and behold the four winds of the heavens strove upon the great sea.
videbaminvisionemeanocteeteccequatuorven.la: Vidébam in visióne mea nocte: et ecce quátuor venti cæli pugnábant in mari magno.

etquatuorbestiegrandesascendebantdemarid.en: And four great beasts, different one from another, came up out of the sea.
etquatuorbestiegrandesascendebantdemarid.la: Et quátuor béstiæ grandes ascendébant de mari divérsæ inter se.

primaquasileenetalashabebataquileaspicie.en: The first was like a lioness, and had the wings of an eagle: I beheld till her wings were plucked off, and she was lifted up from the earth, and stood upon her feet as a man, and the heart of a man was given to her.
primaquasileenetalashabebataquileaspicie.la: Prima quasi leǽna, et alas habébat áquilæ: aspiciébam donec evúlsæ sunt alæ ejus, et subláta est de terra, et super pedes quasi homo stetit: et cor hóminis datum est ei.

eteccebestiaaliasimilisursoinpartestetit.en: And behold another beast, like a bear, stood up on one side: and there were three rows in the mouth thereof, and in the teeth thereof, and thus they said to it: Arise, devour much flesh.
eteccebestiaaliasimilisursoinpartestetit.la: Et ecce béstia ália símilis urso in parte stetit: et tres órdines erant in ore ejus, et in déntibus ejus, et sic dicébant ei: Surge, cómede carnes plúrimas.

posthecaspiciebameteccealiaquasiparduset.en: After this I beheld, and lo, another like a leopard, and it had upon it four wings, as of a fowl, and the beast had four heads, and power was given to it.
posthecaspiciebameteccealiaquasiparduset.la: Post hæc aspiciébam, et ecce ália quasi pardus, et alas habébat quasi avis, quátuor super se: et quátuor cápita erant in béstia, et potéstas data est ei.

posthecaspiciebaminvisionenoctiseteccebe.en: After this I beheld in the vision of the night, and lo, a fourth beast, terrible and wonderful, and exceeding strong, it had great iron teeth, eating and breaking in pieces, and treading down the rest with his feet: and it was unlike to the other beasts which I had seen before it, and had ten horns.
posthecaspiciebaminvisionenoctiseteccebe.la: Post hæc aspiciébam in visióne noctis, et ecce béstia quarta terríbilis atque mirábilis, et fortis nimis: dentes férreos habébat magnos, cómedens atque commínuens, et réliqua pédibus suis concúlcans: dissímilis autem erat céteris béstiis quas víderam ante eam, et habébat córnua decem.

aspiciebamergoinvisionenoctiseteccecumnu.en: I beheld, therefore, in the vision of the night, and lo, one like the Son of man came with the clouds of heaven, and he came even to the ancient of days: and they presented him before him.
aspiciebamergoinvisionenoctiseteccecumnu.la: Aspiciébam ergo in visióne noctis, et ecce cum núbibus cæli quasi fílius hóminis veniébat, et usque ad antíquum diérum pervénit: et in conspéctu ejus obtulérunt eum.

etdediteipotestatemethonoremetregnumetom.en: And he gave him power, and glory, and a kingdom: and all peoples, tribes, and tongues shall serve him: his power is an everlasting power that shall not be taken away: and his kingdom that shall not be destroyed.
etdediteipotestatemethonoremetregnumetom.la: Et dedit ei potestátem, et honórem, et regnum: et omnes pópuli, tribus, et linguæ ipsi sérvient: potéstas ejus, potéstas ætérna, quæ non auferétur: et regnum ejus, quod non corrumpétur.

horruitspiritusmeusegodanielterritussumi.en: My spirit trembled; I, Daniel, was affrighted at these things, and the visions of my head troubled me.
horruitspiritusmeusegodanielterritussumi.la: Hórruit spíritus meus: ego Dániel térritus sum in his, et visiónes cápitis mei conturbavérunt me.

accessiadunumdeassistentibusetveritatemq.en: I went near to one of them that stood by, and asked the truth of him concerning all these things, and he told me the interpretation of the words, and instructed me:
accessiadunumdeassistentibusetveritatemq.la: Accéssi ad unum de assisténtibus, et veritátem quærébam ab eo de ómnibus his. Qui dixit mihi interpretatiónem sermónum, et dócuit me:

hequatuorbestiemagnequatuorsuntregnaquec.en: These four great beasts, are four kingdoms, which shall arise out of the earth.
hequatuorbestiemagnequatuorsuntregnaquec.la: Hæ quátuor béstiæ magnæ, quátuor sunt regna, quæ consúrgent de terra.

suscipientautemregnumsanctideialtissimie.en: But the saints of the most high God shall take the kingdom: and they shall possess the kingdom for ever and ever.
suscipientautemregnumsanctideialtissimie.la: Suscípient autem regnum sancti Dei altíssimi, et obtinébunt regnum usque in sǽculum, et sǽculum sæculórum.

posthocvoluidiligenterdisceredebestiaqua.en: After this I would diligently learn concerning the fourth beast, which was very different from all, and exceeding terrible: his teeth and claws were of iron: he devoured and broke in pieces, and the rest he stamped upon with his feet:
posthocvoluidiligenterdisceredebestiaqua.la: Post hoc vólui diligénter díscere de béstia quarta, quæ erat dissímilis valde ab ómnibus, et terríbilis nimis: dentes et ungues ejus férrei: comedébat, et comminuébat, et réliqua pédibus suis conculcábat:

annotertioregnibaltassarregisvisioapparu.en: In the third year of the reign of king Baltasar, a vision appeared to me. I, Daniel, after what I had seen in the beginning,
annotertioregnibaltassarregisvisioapparu.la: Anno tértio regni Baltássar regis, vísio appáruit mihi. Ego Dániel, post id quod víderam in princípio,

vidiinvisionemeacumesseminsusiscastroquo.en: Saw in my vision when I was in the castle of Susa, which is in the province of Elam: and I saw in the vision that I was over the gate of Ulai.
vidiinvisionemeacumesseminsusiscastroquo.la: vidi in visióne mea, cum essem in Susis castro, quod est in Ælam regióne: vidi autem in visióne esse me super portam Ulai.

etlevavioculusmeosetvidietecceariesunuss.en: And I lifted up my eyes, and saw: and behold a ram stood before the water, having two high horns, and one higher than the other, and growing up. Afterward
etlevavioculusmeosetvidietecceariesunuss.la: Et levávi óculus meos, et vidi: et ecce áries unus stabat ante palúdem, habens córnua excélsa, et unum excélsius áltero atque succréscens.

vidiarietemcornibusventilantemcontraocci.en: I saw the ram pushing with his horns against the west, and against the north, and against the south: and no beasts could withstand him, nor be delivered out of his hand: and he did according to his own will, and became great.
vidiarietemcornibusventilantemcontraocci.la: vidi aríetem córnibus ventilántem contra occidéntem, et contra aquilónem, et contra merídiem, et omnes béstiæ non póterant resístere ei, neque liberári de manu ejus: fecítque secúndum voluntátem suam, et magnificátus est.

etegointelligebamecceautemhircuscaprarum.en: And I understood: and behold a he goat came from the west on the face of the whole earth, and he touched not the ground, and the he goat had a notable horn between his eyes.
etegointelligebamecceautemhircuscaprarum.la: Et ego intelligébam: ecce autem hircus caprárum veniébat ab occidénte super fáciem totíus terræ, et non tangébat terram.

etvenitusqueadarietemillumcornutumquemvi.en: And he went up to the ram that had the horns, which I had seen standing before the gate, and he ran towards him in the force of his strength.
etvenitusqueadarietemillumcornutumquemvi.la: Et venit usque ad aríetem illum cornútum, quem víderam stantem ante portam, et cucúrrit ad eum in ímpetu fortitúdinis suæ.

cumqueadhucloquereretoraremetconfitererp.en: Now while I was yet speaking, and praying, and confessing my sins, and the sins of my people of Israel, and presenting my supplications in the sight of my God, for the holy mountain of my God:
cumqueadhucloquereretoraremetconfitererp.la: Cumque adhuc lóquerer, et orárem, et confitérer peccáta mea, et peccáta pópuli mei Israël, et prostérnerem preces meas in conspéctu Dei mei, pro monte sancto Dei mei:

annotertiocyriregispersarumverbumrevelat.en: In the third year of Cyrus, king of the Persians, a word was revealed to Daniel, surnamed Baltassar, and a true word, and great strength: and he understood the word: for there is need of understanding in a vision.
annotertiocyriregispersarumverbumrevelat.la: Anno tértio Cyri regis Persárum, verbum revelátum est Daniéli cognoménto Baltássar, et verbum verum, et fortitúdo magna: intellexítque sermónem: intelligéntia enim est opus in visióne.

indiebusillisegodaniellugebamtriumhebdom.en: In those days I, Daniel, mourned the days of three weeks.
indiebusillisegodaniellugebamtriumhebdom.la: In diébus illis ego Dániel lugébam trium hebdomadárum diébus:

panemdesiderabilemnoncomedietcaretvinumn.en: I ate no desirable bread, and neither flesh, nor wine, entered into my mouth, neither was I anointed with ointment: till the days of three weeks were accomplished.
panemdesiderabilemnoncomedietcaretvinumn.la: panem desiderábilem non comédi, et caro et vinum non introiérunt in os meum, sed neque unguénto unctus sum, donec compleréntur trium hebdomadárum dies.

intemporeautemilloconsurgetmichelprincep.en: But at that time shall Michael rise up, the great prince, who standeth for the children of thy people: and a time shall come, such as never was from the time that nations began, even until that time. And at that time shall thy people be saved, every one that shall be found written in the book.
intemporeautemilloconsurgetmichelprincep.la: In témpore autem illo consúrget Míchaël princeps magnus, qui stat pro fíliis pópuli tui: et véniet tempus quale non fuit ab eo ex quo gentes esse cœpérunt usque ad tempus illud. Et in témpore illo salvábitur pópulus tuus, omnis qui invéntus fúerit scriptus in libro.

etmultidehisquidormiuntinterrepulvereevi.en: And many of those that sleep in the dust of the earth, shall awake: some unto life everlasting, and others unto reproach, to see it always.
etmultidehisquidormiuntinterrepulvereevi.la: Et multi de his qui dórmiunt in terræ púlvere evigilábunt, álii in vitam ætérnam, et álii in oppróbrium ut vídeant semper.

quiautemdoctifuerintfulgebuntquasisplend.en: But they that are learned, shall shine as the brightness of the firmament: and they that instruct many to justice, as stars for all eternity.
quiautemdoctifuerintfulgebuntquasisplend.la: Qui autem docti fúerint, fulgébunt quasi splendor firmaménti: et qui ad justítiam erúdiunt multos, quasi stellæ in perpétuas æternitátes.

tuautemdanielclaudesermonesetsignalibrum.en: But thou, O Daniel, shut up the words, and seal the book, even to the time appointed: many shall pass over, and knowledge shall be manifold.
tuautemdanielclaudesermonesetsignalibrum.la: Tu autem Dániel, claude sermónes, et signa librum usque ad tempus statútum: plúrimi pertransíbunt, et múltiplex erit sciéntia.

etvidiegodanieleteccequasiduoaliistabant.en: And I, Daniel, looked, and behold as it were two others stood: one on this side upon the bank of the river, and another on that side, on the other bank of the river.
etvidiegodanieleteccequasiduoaliistabant.la: Et vidi ego Dániel, et ecce quasi duo álii stabant: unus hinc super ripam flúminis, et álius inde ex áltera ripa flúminis.

etdixiviroquieratindutuslineisquistabats.en: And I said to the man that was clothed in linen, that stood upon the waters of the river: How long shall it be to the end of these wonders?
etdixiviroquieratindutuslineisquistabats.la: Et dixi viro qui erat indútus líneis, qui stabat super aquas flúminis: Usquequo finis horum mirabílium?

etaudivivirumquiindutuseratlineisquistab.en: And I heard the man that was clothed in linen, that stood upon the waters of the river, when he had lifted up his right hand, and his left hand to heaven, and had sworn by him that liveth for ever, that it should be unto a time, and times, and half a time. And when the scattering of the band of the holy people shall be accomplished, all these things shall be finished.
etaudivivirumquiindutuseratlineisquistab.la: Et audívi virum qui indútus erat líneis, qui stabat super aquas flúminis, cum elevásset déxteram et sinístram suam in cælum, et jurásset per vivéntem in ætérnum, quia in tempus, et témpora, et dimídium témporis. Et cum compléta fúerit dispérsio manus pópuli sancti, complebúntur univérsa hæc.

dicitefratribusvestrispopulusmeusetsoror.en: Say ye to your brethren: You are my people: and to your sister: Thou hast obtained mercy.
dicitefratribusvestrispopulusmeusetsoror.la: Dícite frátribus vestris: Pópulus meus: et soróri vestræ, Misericórdiam consecúta.

iudicatematremvestramiudicatequoniamipsa.en: Judge your mother, judge her: because she is not my wife, and I am not her husband. Let her put away her fornications from her face, and her adulteries from between her breasts.
iudicatematremvestramiudicatequoniamipsa.la: Judicáte matrem vestram, judicáte, quóniam ipsa non uxor mea, et ego non vir ejus. Auferat fornicatiónes suas a fácie sua, et adultéria sua de médio úberum suórum.

neforteexpoliemeamnudametstatuameamsecun.en: Lest I strip her naked, and set her as in the day that she was born: and I will make her as a wilderness, and will set her as a land that none can pass through and will kill her with drought.
neforteexpoliemeamnudametstatuameamsecun.la: Ne forte expóliem eam nudam, et státuam eam secúndum diem nativitátis suæ, et ponam eam quasi solitúdinem, et státuam eam velut terram ínviam, et interfíciam eam siti.

etfiliorumilliusnonmisereborquoniamfilii.en: And I will not have mercy on her children. for they are the children of fornications.
etfiliorumilliusnonmisereborquoniamfilii.la: Et filiórum illíus non miserébor, quóniam fílii fornicatiónum sunt.

quiafornicatestmatereorumconfusestquecon.en: For their mother hath committed fornication, she that conceived them is covered with shame: for she said: I will go after my lovers, that give me my bread, and my water, my wool, and my flax, my oil, and my drink.
quiafornicatestmatereorumconfusestquecon.la: Quia fornicáta est mater eórum, confúsa est quæ concépit eos: quia dixit: Vadam post amatóres meos, qui dant panes mihi, et aquas meas, lanam meam, et linum meum, óleum meum, et potum meum.

propterhocecceegosepiamviamtuamspinisets.en: Wherefore, behold, I will hedge up thy way with thorns, and I will stop it up with a wall, and she shall not find her paths.
propterhocecceegosepiamviamtuamspinisets.la: Propter hoc ecce ego sépiam viam tuam spinis, et sépiam eam macéria, et sémitas suas non invéniet.

etsequeturamatoressuosetnonapprehendeteo.en: And she shall follow after her lovers, and shall not overtake them: and she shall seek them, and shall not find, and she shall say: I will go, and return to my first husband: because it was better with me then than now.
etsequeturamatoressuosetnonapprehendeteo.la: Et sequétur amatóres suos, et non apprehéndet eos: et quæret eos, et non invéniet: et dicet: Vadam, et revértar ad virum meum priórem, quia bene mihi erat tunc magis quam nunc.

ethecnescivitquiegodedieifrumentumetvinu.en: And she did not know that I gave her corn, and wine, and oil, and multiplied her silver, and gold, which they have used in the service of Baal.
ethecnescivitquiegodedieifrumentumetvinu.la: Et hæc nescívit, quia ego dedi ei fruméntum, et vinum, et óleum, et argéntum multiplicávi ei, et aurum, quæ fecérunt Baal.

etpreparavitdominuspiscemgrandemutdeglut.en: Now the Lord prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonas: and Jonas was in the belly of a fish for three days and three nights.
etpreparavitdominuspiscemgrandemutdeglut.la: Et præparávit Dóminus piscem grandem ut deglutíret Jonam: et erat Jonas in ventre piscis tribus diébus et tribus nóctibus.

etoravitionasaddominumdeumsuumdeventrepi.en: And Jonas prayed to the Lord, his God, out of the belly of the fish.
etoravitionasaddominumdeumsuumdeventrepi.la: Et orávit Jonas ad Dóminum Deum suum de ventre piscis,

etdixitclamavidetribulationemeaaddominum.en: And he said: I cried out of my affliction to the Lord, and he heard me: I cried out of the belly of hell, and thou hast heard my voice.
etdixitclamavidetribulationemeaaddominum.la: et dixit: Clamávi de tribulatióne mea ad Dóminum, et exaudívit me: de ventre ínferi clamávi, et exaudísti vocem meam.

etproiecistimeinprofundumincordemarisetf.en: And thou hast cast me forth into the deep, in the heart of the sea, and a flood hast compassed me: all thy billows, and thy waves have passed over me.
etproiecistimeinprofundumincordemarisetf.la: Et proiecísti me in profúndum in corde maris, et flumen circúmdedit me: omnes gúrgites tui, et fluctus tui super me transiérunt.

etfactumestverbumdominiadionamsecundodic.en: And the word of the Lord came to Jonas the second time saying:
etfactumestverbumdominiadionamsecundodic.la: Et factum est verbum Dómini ad Jonam secúndo, dicens:

surgeetvadeinninivencivitatemmagnametpre.en: Arise, and go to Ninive, the great city: and preach in it the preaching that I bid thee.
surgeetvadeinninivencivitatemmagnametpre.la: Surge, et vade in Níniven, civitátem magnam, et prǽdica in ea prædicatiónem quam ego loquor ad te.

etsurrexitionasetabiitinniniveniuxtaverb.en: And Jonas arose, and went to Ninive, according to the word of the Lord: now Ninive was a great city of three days' journey.
etsurrexitionasetabiitinniniveniuxtaverb.la: Et surréxit Jonas, et ábiit in Níniven juxta verbum Dómini: et Nínive erat cívitas magna, itínere trium diérum.

etcepitionasintroireincivitatemitineredi.en: And Jonas began to enter into the city one day's journey: and he cried and said: Yet forty days and Ninive shall be destroyed.
etcepitionasintroireincivitatemitineredi.la: Et cœpit Jonas introíre in civitátem itínere diéi uníus: et clamávit, et dixit: Adhuc quadragínta dies, et Nínive subvertétur.

etcredideruntvirininiviteindeumetpredica.en: And the men of Ninive believed in God: and they proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth from the greatest to the least.
etcredideruntvirininiviteindeumetpredica.la: Et credidérunt viri Ninivítæ in Deum, et prædicavérunt jeiúnium, et vestíti sunt saccis, a maióre usque ad minórem.

etpervenitverbumadregemniniveetsurrexitd.en: And the word came to the king of Ninive: and he rose up out of his throne, and cast away his robe from him, and was clothed in sackcloth, and sat in ashes.
etpervenitverbumadregemniniveetsurrexitd.la: Et pervénit verbum ad regem Nínive: et surréxit de sólio suo, et abiécit vestiméntum suum a se, et indútus est sacco, et sedit in cínere.

hocestpactummeumquodobservabitisintermee.en: This is my covenant which you shall observe between me and you, and thy seed after thee: All the male-kind of you shall be circumcised.
hocestpactummeumquodobservabitisintermee.la: Hoc est pactum meum quod observábitis inter me et vos, et semen tuum post te: Circumcidétur ex vobis omne masculínum:

etcircumcidetiscarnempreputiivestriutsit.en: And you shall circumcise the flesh of your foreskin, that it may be for a sign of the covenant between me and you.
etcircumcidetiscarnempreputiivestriutsit.la: et circumcidétis carnem præpútii vestri, ut sit in signum fœ́deris inter me et vos.

infansoctodierumcircumcideturinvobisomne.en: An infant of eight days old shall be circumcised among you, every manchild in your generations: he that is born in the house, as well as the bought servant, shall be circumcised, and whosoever is not of your stock:
infansoctodierumcircumcideturinvobisomne.la: Infans octo diérum circumcidétur in vobis, omne masculínum in generatiónibus vestris: tam vernáculus, quam emptítius circumcidétur, et quicúmque non fúerit de stirpe vestra:

eritquepactummeumincarnevestrainfedusete.en: And my covenant shall be in your flesh for a perpetual covenant.
eritquepactummeumincarnevestrainfedusete.la: erítque pactum meum in carne vestra in fœdus ætérnum.

masculuscuiuspreputiicarocircumcisanonfu.en: The male whose flesh of his foreskin shall not be circumcised, that soul shall be destroyed out of his people: because he hath broken my covenant.
masculuscuiuspreputiicarocircumcisanonfu.la: Másculus, cuius præpútii caro circumcísa non fúerit, delébitur ánima illa de pópulo suo: quia pactum meum írritum fecit.

eotemporeaitdominusadiosuefactibicultros.en: At that time the Lord said to Josue: Make thee knives of stone, and circumcise the second time the children of Israel.
eotemporeaitdominusadiosuefactibicultros.la: Eo témpore ait Dóminus ad Iósue: Fac tibi cultros lapídeos, et circumcíde secúndo fílios Israël.

fecitquodiusseratdominusetcircumciditfil.en: He did what the Lord had commanded, and he circumcised the children of Israel in the hill of the foreskins.
fecitquodiusseratdominusetcircumciditfil.la: Fecit quod iússerat Dóminus, et circumcídit fílios Israël in colle præputiórum.

hecautemcausestsecundecircumcisionisomni.en: Now this is the cause of the second circumcision: All the people that came out of Egypt that were males, all the men fit for war, died in the desert, during the time of the long going about in the way:
hecautemcausestsecundecircumcisionisomni.la: Hæc autem causa est secúndæ circumcisiónis: omnis pópulus, qui egréssus est de Ægýpto géneris masculíni, univérsi bellatóres viri, mórtui sunt in desérto per longíssimos viæ circúitus,

circumcisioquidemprodestsilegemobservess.en: Circumcision profiteth indeed, if thou keep the law: but if thou be a transgressor of the law, thy circumcision is made uncircumcision.
circumcisioquidemprodestsilegemobservess.la: Circumcísio quidem prodest, si legem obsérves: si autem prævaricátor legis sis, circumcísio tua præpútium facta est.

siigiturpreputiumiustitiaslegiscustodiat.en: If then, the uncircumcised keep the justices of the law, shall not this uncircumcision be counted for circumcision?
siigiturpreputiumiustitiaslegiscustodiat.la: Si ígitur præpútium iustítias legis custódiat, nonne præpútium illíus in circumcisiónem reputábitur?

etiudicabitidquodexnaturestpreputiumlege.en: And shall not that which by nature is uncircumcision, if it fulfil the law, judge thee, who by the letter and circumcision art a transgressor of the law?
etiudicabitidquodexnaturestpreputiumlege.la: et iudicábit id quod ex natúra est præpútium, legem consúmmans, te, qui per lítteram et circumcisiónem prævaricátor legis es?

nonenimquiinmanifestoiudeusestnequequein.en: For it is not he is a Jew, who is so outwardly: nor is that circumcision which is outwardly in the flesh.
nonenimquiinmanifestoiudeusestnequequein.la: Non enim qui in manifésto, Iudǽus est: neque quæ in manifésto, in carne, est circumcísio:

sedquiinabsconditoiudeusestetcircumcisio.en: But he is a Jew that is one inwardly and the circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit not in the letter: whose praise is not of men, but of God.
sedquiinabsconditoiudeusestetcircumcisio.la: sed qui in abscóndito, Iudǽus est: et circumcísio cordis in spíritu, non líttera: cuius laus non ex homínibus, sed ex Deo est.

eccegentemquamnesciebasvocabisetgentesqu.en: Behold thou shalt call a nation, which thou knewest not: and the nations that knew not thee shall run to thee, because of the Lord thy God, and for the Holy One of Israel, for he hath glorified thee.
eccegentemquamnesciebasvocabisetgentesqu.la: Ecce gentem quam nesciébas vocábis, et gentes quæ te non cognovérunt ad te current, propter Dóminum Deum tuum, et sanctum Israël, quia glorificávit te.

nonenimcogitationesmeecogitationesvestre.en: For my thoughts are not your thoughts: nor your ways my ways, saith the Lord.
nonenimcogitationesmeecogitationesvestre.la: Non enim cogitatiónes meæ cogitatiónes vestræ, neque viæ vestræ viæ meæ, dicit Dóminus.

quiasicutexaltanturceliaterrasicexaltate.en: For as the heavens are exalted above the earth, so are my ways exalted above your ways, and my thoughts above your thoughts.
quiasicutexaltanturceliaterrasicexaltate.la: Quia sicut exaltántur cæli a terra, sic exaltátæ sunt viæ meæ a viis vestris, et cogitatiónes meæ a cogitatiónibus vestris.

etposuitosmeumquasigladiumacutuminumbram.en: And he hath made my mouth like a sharp sword: in the shadow of his hand he hath protected me, and hath made me as a chosen arrow: in his quiver he hath hidden me.
etposuitosmeumquasigladiumacutuminumbram.la: Et pósuit os meum quasi gládium acútum, in umbra manus suæ protéxit me, et pósuit me sicut sagíttam eléctam: in pháretra sua abscóndit me.

etdixitmihiservusmeusestuisrelquiaintegl.en: And he said to me: Thou art my servant Israel, for in thee will I glory.
etdixitmihiservusmeusestuisrelquiaintegl.la: Et dixit mihi: Servus meus es tu Israël, quia in te gloriábor.

etnuncdicitdominusformansmeexuteroservum.en: And now saith the Lord, that formed me from the womb to be his servant, that I may bring back Jacob unto him, and Israel will not be gathered together: and I am glorified in the eyes of the Lord, and my God is made my strength.
etnuncdicitdominusformansmeexuteroservum.la: Et nunc dicit Dóminus, formans me ex útero servum sibi, ut redúcam Jacob ad eum, et Israël non congregábitur: et glorificátus sum in óculis Dómini, et Deus meus factus est fortitúdo mea.

quoniamspesimpiitamquamlanugestqueavento.en: For the hope of the wicked is as dust, which is blown away with the wind, and as a thin froth which is dispersed by the storm: and a smoke that is scattered abroad by the wind: and as the remembrance of a guest of one day that passeth by.
quoniamspesimpiitamquamlanugestqueavento.la: quóniam spes ímpii tamquam lanúgo est quæ a vento tóllitur, et tamquam spuma grácilis quæ a procélla dispérgitur, et tamquam fumus qui a vento diffúsus est, et tamquam memória hóspitis uníus diéi prætereúntis.

aliisgenerationibusnonestagnitumfiliisho.en: Which in other generations was not known to the sons of men, as it is now revealed to his holy apostles and prophets in the Spirit:
aliisgenerationibusnonestagnitumfiliisho.la: Áliis generatiónibus non est ágnitum fíliis hóminum, sícuti nunc revelátum est sanctis apóstolis ejus et prophétis in Spíritu,

gentesessecoheredesetconcorporalesetcomp.en: That the Gentiles should be fellow heirs and of the same body: and copartners of his promise in Christ Jesus, by the gospel
gentesessecoheredesetconcorporalesetcomp.la: gentes esse coherédes, et concorporáles, et compartícipes promissiónis ejus in Christo Jesu per Evangélium:

cuiusfactussumministersecundumdonumgrati.en: Of which I am made a minister, according to the gift of the grace of God, which is given to me according to the operation of his power.
cuiusfactussumministersecundumdonumgrati.la: cujus factus sum miníster secúndum donum grátiæ Dei, quæ data est mihi secúndum operatiónem virtútis ejus.

mihiomniumsanctorumminimodatestgratiahec.en: To me, the least of all the saints, is given this grace, to preach among the Gentiles the unsearchable riches of Christ:
mihiomniumsanctorumminimodatestgratiahec.la: Mihi ómnium sanctórum mínimo data est grátia hæc, in géntibus evangelizáre investigábiles divítias Christi,

etilluminareomnesquesitdispensatiosacram.en: And to enlighten all men, that they may see what is the dispensation of the mystery which hath been hidden from eternity in God who created all things:
etilluminareomnesquesitdispensatiosacram.la: et illumináre omnes, quæ sit dispensátio sacraménti abscónditi a sǽculis in Deo, qui ómnia creávit:

utinnotescatprincipatibusetpotestatibusi.en: That the manifold wisdom of God may be made known to the principalities and powers in heavenly places through the church,
utinnotescatprincipatibusetpotestatibusi.la: ut innotéscat principátibus et potestátibus in cæléstibus per Ecclésiam, multifórmis sapiéntia Dei,

secundumprefinitionemseculorumquamfeciti.en: According to the eternal purpose which he made in Christ Jesus our Lord:
secundumprefinitionemseculorumquamfeciti.la: secúndum præfinitiónem sæculórum, quam fecit in Christo Jesu Dómino nostro:

inquohabemusfiduciametaccessuminconfiden.en: In whom we have boldness and access with confidence by the faith of him.
inquohabemusfiduciametaccessuminconfiden.la: in quo habémus fidúciam, et accéssum in confidéntia per fidem ejus.

propterquodpetonedeficiatisintribulation.en: Wherefore I pray you not to faint at my tribulations for you, which is your glory.
propterquodpetonedeficiatisintribulation.la: Propter quod peto ne deficiátis in tribulatiónibus meis pro vobis: quæ est glória vestra.

huiusreigratiaflectogenuameaadpatremdomi.en: For this cause I bow my knees to the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ,
huiusreigratiaflectogenuameaadpatremdomi.la: Hujus rei grátia flecto génua mea ad Patrem Dómini nostri Jesu Christi,

exquoomnispaternitasincelisetinterranomi.en: Of whom all paternity in heaven and earth is named:
exquoomnispaternitasincelisetinterranomi.la: ex quo omnis patérnitas in cælis et in terra nominátur,
