utdetvobissecundumdivitiasgloriesuevirtu.en: That he would grant you, according to the riches of his glory, to be strengthened by his Spirit with might unto the inward man:
utdetvobissecundumdivitiasgloriesuevirtu.la: ut det vobis secúndum divítias glóriæ suæ, virtúte corroborári per Spíritum ejus in interiórem hóminem,

gratiamulierisseduledelectabitvirumsuume.en: The grace of a diligent woman shall delight her husband, and shall fat his bones.
gratiamulierisseduledelectabitvirumsuume.la: Grátia mulíeris sédulæ delectábit virum suum, et ossa illíus impinguábit.

disciplinailliusdatumdeiest.en: Her discipline is the gift of God.

gratiasupergratiammuliersanctetpudorata.en: A holy and shamefaced woman is grace upon grace.
gratiasupergratiammuliersanctetpudorata.la: Grátia super grátiam, múlier sancta et pudoráta.

sicutsoloriensmundoinaltissimisdeisicmul.en: As the sun when it riseth to the world in the high places of God, so is the beauty of a good wife for the ornament of her house.
sicutsoloriensmundoinaltissimisdeisicmul.la: Sicut sol óriens mundo in altíssimis Dei, sic mulíeris bonæ spécies in ornaméntum domus ejus.

mulieressubditesintvirissuisutetsiquinon.en: In like manner also, let wives be subject to their husbands: that, if any believe not the word, they may be won without the word, by the conversation of the wives,
mulieressubditesintvirissuisutetsiquinon.la: Mulíeres súbditæ sint viris suis: ut et si qui non credunt verbo, per mulíerum conversatiónem sine verbo lucrifíant:

considerantesintimorecastamconversatione.en: Considering your chaste conversation with fear.
considerantesintimorecastamconversatione.la: considerántes in timóre castam conversatiónem vestram.

quarumnonsitextrinsecuscapillaturaautcir.en: Whose adorning, let it not be the outward plaiting of the hair, or the wearing of gold, or the putting on of apparel:
quarumnonsitextrinsecuscapillaturaautcir.la: Quarum non sit extrínsecus capillatúra, aut circumdátio auri, aut induménti vestimentórum cultus:

sedquiabsconditusestcordishomoinincorrup.en: But the hidden man of the heart, in the incorruptibility of a quiet and a meek spirit which is rich in the sight of God.
sedquiabsconditusestcordishomoinincorrup.la: sed qui abscónditus est cordis homo, in incorruptibilitáte quiéti, et modésti spíritus, qui est in conspéctu Dei lócuples.

sicenimaliquandetsanctemulieressperantes.en: For after this manner heretofore, the holy women also who trusted in God adorned themselves, being in subjection to their own husbands:
sicenimaliquandetsanctemulieressperantes.la: Sic enim aliquándo et sanctæ mulíeres, sperántes in Deo, ornábant se, subiéctæ própriis viris.

volergovirosorareinomnilocolevantespuras.en: I will therefore that men pray in every place, lifting up pure hands, without anger and contention.
volergovirosorareinomnilocolevantespuras.la: Volo ergo viros oráre in omni loco, levántes puras manus sine ira et disceptatióne.

similiteretmulieresinhabituornatocumvere.en: In like manner, women also in decent apparel: adorning themselves with modesty and sobriety, not with plaited hair, or gold, or pearls, or costly attire:
similiteretmulieresinhabituornatocumvere.la: Simíliter et mulíeres in hábitu ornáto, cum verecúndia et sobrietáte ornántes se, et non in tortis crínibus, aut auro, aut margarítis, vel veste pretiósa:

sedquoddecetmulierespromittentespietatem.en: But, as it becometh women professing godliness, with good works.
sedquoddecetmulierespromittentespietatem.la: sed quod decet mulíeres, promitténtes pietátem per ópera bona.

mulierinsilentiodiscatcumomnisubiectione.en: Let the woman learn in silence with all subjection.
mulierinsilentiodiscatcumomnisubiectione.la: Múlier in siléntio discat cum omni subiectióne.

docereautemmulierinonpermittonequedomina.en: But I suffer not a woman to teach, nor to use authority over the man: but to be in silence.
docereautemmulierinonpermittonequedomina.la: Docére autem mulíeri non permítto, neque dominári in virum: sed esse in siléntio.

namquiaindeisapientianoncognovitmunduspe.en: For, seeing that in the wisdom of God, the world, by wisdom, knew not God, it pleased God, by the foolishness of our preaching, to save them that believe.
namquiaindeisapientianoncognovitmunduspe.la: Nam quia in Dei sapiéntia non cognóvit mundus per sapiéntiam Deum: plácuit Deo per stultítiam prædicatiónis salvos fácere credéntes.

quoniametiudeisignapetuntetgrecisapienti.en: For both the Jews require signs: and the Greeks seek after wisdom.
quoniametiudeisignapetuntetgrecisapienti.la: Quóniam et Judǽi signa petunt, et Græci sapiéntiam quærunt:

nosautempredicamuschristumcrucifixumiude.en: But we preach Christ crucified: unto the Jews indeed a stumblingblock, and unto the Gentiles foolishness:
nosautempredicamuschristumcrucifixumiude.la: nos autem prædicámus Christum crucifíxum: Judǽis quidem scándalum, géntibus autem stultítiam,

ipsisautemvocatisiudeisatquegrecischrist.en: But unto them that are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ, the power of God and the wisdom of God.
ipsisautemvocatisiudeisatquegrecischrist.la: ipsis autem vocátis Judǽis, atque Græcis Christum Dei virtútem, et Dei sapiéntiam:

quiaquodstultumestdeisapientiusesthomini.en: For the foolishness of God is wiser than men: and the weakness of God is stronger than men.
quiaquodstultumestdeisapientiusesthomini.la: quia quod stultum est Dei, sapiéntius est homínibus: et quod infírmum est Dei, fórtius est homínibus.

habentesadministrationemiuxtaquodmiseric.en: Therefore seeing we have this ministration, according as we have obtained mercy, we faint not.
habentesadministrationemiuxtaquodmiseric.la: Habéntes administratiónem, juxta quod misericórdiam consecúti sumus, non defícimus,

sedabdicamusoccultadedecorisnonambulante.en: But we renounce the hidden things of dishonesty, not walking in craftiness nor adulterating the word of God: but by manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every man's conscience, in the sight of God.
sedabdicamusoccultadedecorisnonambulante.la: sed abdicámus occúlta dedécoris, non ambulántes in astútia, neque adulterántes verbum Dei, sed in manifestatióne veritátis commendántes nosmetípsos ad omnem consciéntiam hóminum coram Deo.

inquibusdeushuiusseculiexcecavitmentesin.en: In whom the god of this world hath blinded the minds of unbelievers, that the light of the gospel of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God, should not shine unto them.
inquibusdeushuiusseculiexcecavitmentesin.la: in quibus Deus hujus sǽculi excæcávit mentes infidélium, ut non fúlgeat illis illuminátio Evangélii glóriæ Christi, qui est imágo Dei.

nonenimnosmetipsospredicamussediesumchri.en: For we preach not ourselves, but Jesus Christ our Lord: and ourselves your servants through Jesus.
nonenimnosmetipsospredicamussediesumchri.la: Non enim nosmetípsos prædicámus, sed Jesum Christum Dóminum nostrum: nos autem servos vestros per Jesum:

quoniamdeusquidixitdetenebrislucemsplend.en: For God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, hath shined in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God, in the face of Christ Jesus.
quoniamdeusquidixitdetenebrislucemsplend.la: quóniam Deus, qui dixit de ténebris lucem splendéscere, ipse illúxit in córdibus nostris ad illuminatiónem sciéntiæ claritátis Dei, in fácie Christi Jesu.

persecutionempatimursednonderelinquimurd.en: We suffer persecution: but are not forsaken. We are cast down: but we perish not.
persecutionempatimursednonderelinquimurd.la: persecutiónem pátimur, sed non derelínquimur: deícimur, sed non perímus:

sempermortificationemiesuincorporenostro.en: Always bearing about in our body the mortification of Jesus, that the life also of Jesus may be made manifest in our bodies.
sempermortificationemiesuincorporenostro.la: semper mortificatiónem Jesu in córpore nostro circumferéntes, ut et vita Jesu manifestétur in corpóribus nostris.

queestistaqueascenditperdesertumsicutvir.en: Who is she that goeth up by the desert, as a pillar of smoke of aromatical spices, of myrrh, and frankincense, and of all the powders of the perfumer?
queestistaqueascenditperdesertumsicutvir.la: Quæ est ista quæ ascéndit per desértum sicut vírgula fumi ex aromátibus myrrhæ, et thuris, et univérsi púlveris pigmentárii?

duouberatuasicutduohinnulicapreegemelliq.en: Thy two breasts like two young roes that are twins, which feed among the lilies.
duouberatuasicutduohinnulicapreegemelliq.la: Duo úbera tua sicut duo hínnuli, cápreæ gemélli, qui pascúntur in líliis.

donecaspiretdiesetinclinenturumbrevadama.en: Till the day break, and the shadows retire, I will go to the mountain of myrrh, and to the hill of frankincense.
donecaspiretdiesetinclinenturumbrevadama.la: Donec aspíret dies, et inclinéntur umbræ, vadam ad montem myrrhæ, et ad collem thuris.

deusautemquidivesestinmisericordiapropte.en: But God (who is rich in mercy) for his exceeding charity wherewith he loved us
deusautemquidivesestinmisericordiapropte.la: Deus autem, qui dives est in misericórdia, propter nímiam caritátem suam, qua diléxit nos,

etcumessemusmortuipeccatisconvivificavit.en: Even when we were dead in sins, hath quickened us together in Christ (by whose grace you are saved)
etcumessemusmortuipeccatisconvivificavit.la: et cum essémus mórtui peccátis, convivificávit nos in Christo cuius grátia estis salváti,

etconresuscitavitetconsederefecitinceles.en: And hath raised us up together and hath made us sit together in the heavenly places, through Christ Jesus.
etconresuscitavitetconsederefecitinceles.la: et conresuscitávit, et consedére fecit in cæléstibus in Christo Iesu:

utostenderetinseculissupervenientibusabu.en: That he might shew in the ages to come the abundant riches of his grace, in his bounty towards us in Christ Jesus.
utostenderetinseculissupervenientibusabu.la: ut osténderet in sǽculis superveniéntibus abundántes divítias grátiæ suæ, in bonitáte super nos in Christo Iesu.

gratienimestissalvatiperfidemethocnonexv.en: For by grace you are saved through faith: and that not of yourselves, for it is the gift of God.
gratienimestissalvatiperfidemethocnonexv.la: Grátia enim estis salváti per fidem, et hoc non ex vobis: Dei enim donum est:

nonexoperibusutnequisglorietur.en: Not of works, that no man may glory.
nonexoperibusutnequisglorietur.la: non ex opéribus, ut ne quis gloriétur.

ipsiusenimsumusfacturacreatiinchristoies.en: For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus in good works, which God hath prepared that we should walk in them.
ipsiusenimsumusfacturacreatiinchristoies.la: Ipsíus enim sumus factúra, creáti in Christo Iesu in opéribus bonis, quæ præparávit Deus ut in illis ambulémus.

propterquodmemoresestotequodaliquandovos.en: For which cause be mindful that you, being heretofore gentiles is the flesh, who are called uncircumcision by that which is called circumcision in the flesh, made by hands:
propterquodmemoresestotequodaliquandovos.la: Propter quod mémores estóte quod aliquándo vos gentes in carne, qui dicímini præpútium ab ea quæ dícitur circumcísio in carne, manu facta:

quieratisillointemporesinechristoalienat.en: That you were at that time without Christ, being aliens from the conversation of Israel and strangers to the testament, having no hope of the promise and without God in this world.
quieratisillointemporesinechristoalienat.la: quia erátis illo in témpore sine Christo, alienáti a conversatióne Israël, et hóspites testamentórum, promissiónis spem non habéntes, et sine Deo in hoc mundo.

nuncauteminchristoiesuvosquialiquanderat.en: But now in Christ Jesus, you, who some time were afar off, are made nigh by the blood of Christ.
nuncauteminchristoiesuvosquialiquanderat.la: Nunc autem in Christo Iesu, vos, qui aliquándo erátis longe, facti estis prope in sánguine Christi.

ipseenimestpaxnostraquifecitutraqueunume.en: For he is our peace, who hath made both one, and breaking down the middle wall of partition, the enmities in his flesh:
ipseenimestpaxnostraquifecitutraqueunume.la: Ipse enim est pax nostra, qui fecit útraque unum, et médium paríetem macériæ solvens, inimicítias in carne sua,

legemmandatorumdecretisevacuansutduoscon.en: Making void the law of commandments contained in decrees: that he might make the two in himself into one new man, making peace
legemmandatorumdecretisevacuansutduoscon.la: legem mandatórum decrétis evácuans, ut duos condat in semetípso in unum novum hóminem, fáciens pacem:

etreconcilietambosinunocorporedeopercruc.en: And might reconcile both to God in one body by the cross, killing the enmities in himself.
etreconcilietambosinunocorporedeopercruc.la: et reconcíliet ambos in uno córpore, Deo per crucem, interfíciens inimicítias in semetípso.

obauditemedivinifructusetquasirosaplanta.en: By a voice he saith: Hear me, ye divine offspring, and bud forth as the rose planted by the brooks of waters.
obauditemedivinifructusetquasirosaplanta.la: Obaudíte me, divíni fructus, et quasi rosa plantáta super rivos aquárum fructificáte.

quasilibanusodoremsuavitatishabete.en: Give ye a sweet odour as frankincense.

floretefloresquasililiumetdateodoremetfr.en: Send forth flowers, as the lily, and yield a smell, and bring forth leaves in grace, and praise with canticles, and bless the Lord in his works.
floretefloresquasililiumetdateodoremetfr.la: Floréte flores, quasi lílium, et date odórem, et frondéte in grátiam; et collaudáte cánticum, et benedícite Dóminum in opéribus suis.

datenominieiusmagnificentiametconfitemin.en: Magnify his name, and give glory to him with the voice of your lips, and with the canticles of your mouths, and with harps, and in praising him, you shall say in this manner:
datenominieiusmagnificentiametconfitemin.la: Date nómini ejus magnificéntiam, et confitémini illi in voce labiórum vestrórum, et in cánticis labiórum, et cítharis;

vanitatienimcreaturasubiectestnonvolenss.en: For the creature was made subject to vanity: not willingly, but by reason of him that made it subject, in hope.
vanitatienimcreaturasubiectestnonvolenss.la: Vanitáti enim creatúra subiécta est non volens, sed propter eum, qui subiécit eam in spe:

scimusenimquodomniscreaturaingemiscitetp.en: For we know that every creature groaneth and travaileth in pain, even till now.
scimusenimquodomniscreaturaingemiscitetp.la: Scimus enim quod omnis creatúra ingemíscit, et párturit usque adhuc.

nonsolumautemillasedetnosipsiprimitiassp.en: And not only it, but ourselves also, who have the firstfruits of the Spirit: even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption of the sons of God, the redemption of our body.
nonsolumautemillasedetnosipsiprimitiassp.la: Non solum autem illa, sed et nos ipsi primítias spíritus habéntes: et ipsi intra nos gémimus adoptiónem filiórum Dei exspectántes, redemptiónem córporis nostri.

siautemquodnonvidemussperamusperpatienti.en: But if we hope for that which we see not, we wait for it with patience.
siautemquodnonvidemussperamusperpatienti.la: Si autem quod non vidémus, sperámus: per patiéntiam exspectámus.

similiterautemetspiritusadiuvatinfirmita.en: Likewise, the Spirit also helpeth our infirmity. For, we know not what we should pray for as we ought: but the Spirit himself asketh for us with unspeakable groanings,
similiterautemetspiritusadiuvatinfirmita.la: Simíliter autem et Spíritus ádiuvat infirmitátem nostram: nam quid orémus, sicut opórtet, nescímus: sed ipse Spíritus póstulat pro nobis gemítibus inenarrabílibus.

quiautemscrutaturcordascitquiddesiderets.en: And he that searcheth the hearts knoweth what the Spirit desireth: because he asketh for the saints according to God.
quiautemscrutaturcordascitquiddesiderets.la: Qui autem scrutátur corda, scit quid desíderet Spíritus: quia secúndum Deum póstulat pro sanctis.

beatusvirquiinsapientiamorabituretquiini.en: Blessed is the man that shall continue in wisdom, and that shall meditate in his justice, and in his mind shall think of the all seeing eye of God.
beatusvirquiinsapientiamorabituretquiini.la: Beátus vir qui in sapiéntia morábitur, et qui in justítia sua meditábitur, et in sensu cogitábit circumspectiónem Dei.

quiexcogitatviasilliusincordesuetinabsco.en: He that considereth her ways in his heart, and hath understanding in her secrets, who goeth after her as one that traceth, and stayeth in her ways.
quiexcogitatviasilliusincordesuetinabsco.la: Qui excógitat vias illíus in corde suo, et in abscónditis suis intélligens, vadens post illam quasi investigátor, et in viis illíus consístens:

quirespicitperfenestrasilliusetinianuisi.en: He who looketh in at her windows, and hearkeneth at her door.
quirespicitperfenestrasilliusetinianuisi.la: qui réspicit per fenéstras illíus, et in jánuis illíus áudiens:

quirequiescitiuxtadomumilliusetinparieti.en: He that lodgeth near her house, and fastening a pin in her walls shall set up his tent high unto her, where good things shall rest in his lodging for ever.
quirequiescitiuxtadomumilliusetinparieti.la: qui requiéscit juxta domum illíus, et in pariétibus illíus figens palum, státuet cásulam suam ad manus illíus, et requiéscent in cásula illíus bona per ævum.

statuetfiliossuossubtegmineilliusetsubra.en: He shall set his children under her shelter, and shall lodge under her branches:
statuetfiliossuossubtegmineilliusetsubra.la: Státuet fílios suos sub tégmine illíus, et sub ramis ejus morábitur.

protegetursubtegmineilliusafervoreetingl.en: He shall be protected under her covering from the heat, and shall rest in her glory.
protegetursubtegmineilliusafervoreetingl.la: Protegétur sub tégmine illíus a fervóre, et in glória ejus requiéscet.

quiimpletquasiphisonsapientiametsicuttig.en: Who filleth up wisdom as the Phison, and as the Tigris in the days of the new fruits.
quiimpletquasiphisonsapientiametsicuttig.la: Qui implet quasi Phison sapiéntiam, et sicut Tigris in diébus novórum.

quiadimpletquasieuphratessensumquimultip.en: Who maketh understanding to abound as the Euphrates, who multiplieth it as the Jordan in the time of harvest.
quiadimpletquasieuphratessensumquimultip.la: Qui adímplet quasi Euphrátes sensum: qui multíplicat quasi Jordánis in témpore messis.

quimittitdisciplinamsicutlucemetassisten.en: Who sendeth knowledge as the light, and riseth up as Gehon in the time of the vintage.
quimittitdisciplinamsicutlucemetassisten.la: Qui mittit disciplínam sicut lucem, et assístens quasi Gehon in die vindémiæ.

quiperficitprimusscireipsametinfirmiorno.en: Who first hath perfect knowledge of her, and a weaker shall not search her out.
quiperficitprimusscireipsametinfirmiorno.la: Qui pérficit primus scire ipsam, et infírmior non investigábit eam.

amarienimabundavitcogitatieiusetconsiliu.en: For her thoughts are more vast than the sea, and her counsels more deep than the great ocean.
amarienimabundavitcogitatieiusetconsiliu.la: A mari enim abundávit cogitátio ejus, et consílium illíus ab abýsso magna.

egosapientieffudiflumina.en: I, wisdom, have poured out rivers.

egoquasitramesaqueimmensedefluviegoquasi.en: I, like a brook out of a river of a mighty water; I, like a channel of a river, and like an aqueduct, came out of paradise.
egoquasitramesaqueimmensedefluviegoquasi.la: Ego quasi trames aquæ imménsæ de flúvio, ego quasi flúvii dióryx, et sicut aquædúctus exívi de paradíso.

dixirigabohortummeumplantationumetinebri.en: I said: I will water my garden of plants, and I will water abundantly the fruits of my meadow.
dixirigabohortummeumplantationumetinebri.la: Dixi: Rigábo hortum meum plantatiónum, et inebriábo prati mei fructum.

eteccefactusestmihitramesabundansetfluvi.en: And behold my brook became a great river, and my river came near to a sea:
eteccefactusestmihitramesabundansetfluvi.la: Et ecce factus est mihi trames abúndans, et flúvius meus appropinquávit ad mare:

quoniamdoctrinamquasiantelucanumillumino.en: For I make doctrine to shine forth to all as the morning light, and I will declare it afar off.
quoniamdoctrinamquasiantelucanumillumino.la: quóniam doctrínam quasi antelucánum illúmino ómnibus, et enarrábo illam usque ad longínquum.

penetraboomnesinferiorespartesterreetins.en: I will penetrate to all the lower parts of the earth, and will behold all that sleep, and will enlighten all that hope in the Lord.
penetraboomnesinferiorespartesterreetins.la: Penetrábo omnes inferióres partes terræ, et inspíciam omnes dormiéntes, et illuminábo omnes sperántes in Dómino.

adhucdoctrinamquasiprophetiameffundametr.en: I will yet pour out doctrine as prophecy, and will leave it to them that seek wisdom, and will not cease to instruct their offspring even to the holy age.
adhucdoctrinamquasiprophetiameffundametr.la: Adhuc doctrínam quasi prophetíam effúndam, et relínquam illam quæréntibus sapiéntiam, et non désinam in progénies illórum usque in ævum sanctum.

videtequoniamnonsolimihilaboravisedomnib.en: See ye that I have not laboured myself only, but for all that seek out the truth.
videtequoniamnonsolimihilaboravisedomnib.la: Vidéte quóniam non soli mihi laborávi, sed ómnibus exquiréntibus veritátem.

inillotemporeapprehenditpilatusiesumetfl.en: At that time, Pilate took Jesus and scourged him. And the soldiers platting a crown of thorns, put it upon his head: and they put on him a purple garment. And they came to him and said: Hail, king of the Jews. And they gave him blows. Pilate therefore went forth again and saith to them: Behold, I bring him forth unto you, that you may know that I find no cause in him. Jesus therefore came forth, bearing the crown of thorns and the purple garment.
inillotemporeapprehenditpilatusiesumetfl.la: In illo témpore: Apprehéndit Pilátus Jesum et flagellávit. Et mílites plecténtes corónam de spinis, imposuérunt cápiti ejus: et veste purpúrea circumdedérunt eum. Et veniébant ad eum et dicébant: Ave, Rex Judæórum: et dabant ei álapas. Exívit ergo íterum Pilátus foras et dicit eis: Ecce, addúco vobis eum foras, ut cognoscátis, quia nullam invénio in eo causam. Exívit ergo Jesus portans corónam spíneam et purpúreum vestiméntum.

etvirginessuntetrepellunturparumestquiav.en: They are virgins, and yet are shut out. It is little that they are virgins, and have lamps. Virgins by reason of abstinence from unlawful things of the senses, they have lamps by reason of good works. Of which works the Lord saith: Let your works shine before men. Likewise he saith to the disciples: Let your loins be girt, and lamps burning in your hands. In the girt loins, virginity; in the burning lamps, good works. If therefore abstinence from unlawful things is good, whence virginity hath received its name; and good works are praiseworthy, which are signified by the lamps; why are five admitted and five shut out?
etvirginessuntetrepellunturparumestquiav.la: Et vírgines sunt, et repellúntur. Parum est, quia vírgines sunt, et lámpades habent. Vírgines propter abstinentiam ab illícitis, sénsibus, lámpades habent propter ópera bona. De quibus opéribus Dóminus dicit: Lúceant ópera vestra coram homínibus. Item discípulis dicit: Sint lumbi vestri accíncti, et lucérnæ ardéntes. In lumbis accínctis, virgínitas; in lucérnis ardéntibus ópera bona. Si ergo ab illícitis abstinéntia bona est; unde virgínitas nomen accépit: et ópera bona laudabília sunt, quæ significántur lampádibus: quare quinque admittuntur et quinque repellúntur?

siergointelligimusmysteriumfratresmeiioa.en: If therefore, my brethren, we understand the mystery, John is man, Christ is God. Let man be humbled, that God may be exalted, according to that which John himself said of the Lord: He must increase, but I must decrease. That man might be humbled, John was born on this day, from which the days begin to decrease: that God might be exalted, Christ was born on that day from which the days begin to increase. A great mystery, dearly beloved brethren. Therefore we celebrate the birthday of John as also that of Christ, because his birth also is full of mystery. Of what mystery, but of our humility, as the birth of Christ is full of the mystery of our exaltation?
siergointelligimusmysteriumfratresmeiioa.la: Si ergo intellígimus mystérium, fratres mei, Joánnes homo est, Christus Deus est. Humiliétur homo, ut exaltétur Deus, secúndum illud quod de Dómino ipse Joánnes dixit: Illum opórtet créscere, me autem mínui. Ut humiliarétur homo, hódie natus est Joánnes, quo incípiunt decréscere dies: ut exaltétur Deus, eo die natus est Christus, quo incípiunt créscere dies. Magnum sacraméntum, fratres caríssimi. Ideo celebrámus natálem Joánnis sicut et Christi, quia et ipsa natívitas plena est mystério. Quo mystério, nisi humilitátis nostræ, sicut natívitas Christi plena est mystério altitúdinis nostræ?

beatiistiacterbeatiutquideiamoreflagraru.en: Blessed are these, yea thrice blessed, as they who burned with the love of God, and for his charity's sake counted all things as nothing. For they shed tears, and passed day and night in mourning, that they might attain unto everlasting consolation: they willingly abased themselves, that there they might be lifted up on high. They wore out their flesh with hunger and thirst and watchings, that there the delights and exultation of paradise might receive them.
beatiistiacterbeatiutquideiamoreflagraru.la: Beáti isti ac ter beáti, ut qui Dei amóre flagrárunt, atque ob ipsíus caritátem ómnia pro níhilo duxérunt. Síquidem lácrimas profudérunt, diéque ac nocte in luctu versáti sunt, ut perpétuam consolatiónem adisceréntur: seípsos ultro depressérunt, ut illic in altum attolleréntur. Carnes suas fame ac siti et vigíllis confecérunt, ut illic paradísis delíciae et exsultátio Ipsos excíperent.

quandoiudasdetraditionetractabatdicuntdi.en: When Judas was treating of the betrayal, the disciples say: Where wilt thou that we prepare for thee to eat the pasch? See the disciples: see the disciple. These are solicitous about the preparation: he cometh forth as a trafficker in the Lord's blood. And that Pasch indeed of the Jews the disciples were preparing: but this, which is ours, Christ himself instituted. And he said: This is my body, which shall be delivered for you. This is my blood, which shall be shed for many. O the mercy of Christ! O the madness of Judas! He was bargaining for him, that he might sell him: Christ was offering him the blood which he sold, that he might have remission of sins, if only he had been unwilling to remain wicked. For he was granted communion in the sacrifice, and Christ washed his feet: that he might have no excuse for his malice.
quandoiudasdetraditionetractabatdicuntdi.la: Quando Judas de traditióne tractábat. dicunt discípuli: Ubi vis parémus tibi Pascha manducáre? Vide discípulos: vide discípulum. Isti sunt de præparatióne solliciti: ille Dominici sánguinis mercátor exsistit. Et illud quidem Pascha Judæórum discípuli præparábant: istud autem, quod nostrum est, ipse Christus constituit. Et dixit: Hoc est corpus meum, quod pro vobis tradétur. Hic est sanguis meus, qui pro multis effundétur. O Christi misericórdia! O Judæ deméntia! Ille eum paciscebátur, ut vénderet: Christus ei sánguinem, quem véndidit, offerébat, ut habéret remissiónem peccatórum, si tamen ímpius exsistere noluisset. Nam sacrificii communicatiónem méruit, et pedes ejus lavit Christus: ut excusatiónem suæ malitiæ non habéret.

sicutovisadoccisionemductusestetdummalet.en: He was led as a sheep to the slaughter: and while he was evil entreated, he opened not his mouth: he was delivered up to death,
sicutovisadoccisionemductusestetdummalet.la: Sicut ovis ad occisiónem ductus est: et, dum male tractarétur, non apéruit os suum: tráditus est ad mortem,

deusquibeatummannemconfessoremtuumdispos.en: O God, who by a wonderful disposition didst lead blessed Manes thy Confessor into the way of perfection: by the same grace of mercy direct our actions: that we may be able to seek what thou commandest, and to attain what thou promisest.
deusquibeatummannemconfessoremtuumdispos.la: Deus, qui beátum Mannem Confessórem tuum dispositiône mirábili in viam perfectiónis traduxísti; eádem misericórdiæ grátia dirige actus nostros: ut possimus quærere quod jubes, et assequi quod promíttis.

deusquibeatumioannemconfessoremgratietue.en: O God, who didst will that blessed John thy Confessor, prevented by the abundance of thy grace, should flourish in a lowly state of life by the whiteness of his conduct: grant us, we beseech thee, so to follow his footsteps, that we may merit to come unto thee with pure minds.
deusquibeatumioannemconfessoremgratietue.la: Deus, qui beátum Joánnem Confessórem, grátiae tuæ ubertáte prævéntum, in húmili vitæ genere morum candóre florescere voluisti: da nobis, quæsumus, ita ejus vestigia pérsequi, ut ad te puris mentibus pervenire mereámur.

quamvispostapostolossanctipatresetdoctor.en: Although, after the Apostles, many of our holy Fathers and Doctors say so many and such great things concerning the reason of our faith, to confute the foolishness and to break the hardness of unbelievers, and to feed those who, their hearts being already cleansed by faith, delight in the reason of that same faith, after which, its certainty once had, we ought to hunger; so that neither in our times nor in times to come may we hope for any equal to them in the contemplation of truth: yet I think none is to be blamed if, being established in the faith, he will exercise himself in searching out its reason. For they too, because the days of man are short, could not say all that they might have said, had they lived longer; and the reason of truth is so ample and so deep that it cannot be exhausted by mortals; and the Lord in his Church, with which he promiseth to be even to the consummation of the world, ceaseth not to impart the gifts of his grace.
quamvispostapostolossanctipatresetdoctor.la: Quamvis post Apóstolos sancti Patres et Doctóres nostri multi tot et tanta de fidei nostræ ratióne dicant ad confutándum insipiéntiam et frangéndum durítiam infidélium, et ad pascéndum eos, qui, jam corde fide mundáto, eiúsdem fídei ratióne, quam post ejus certitúdinem debémus esuríre, delectántur; ut nec nostris nec futúris tempóribus ullum illis parem in veritátis contemplatióne sperémus: nullum tamen reprehendéndum árbitror, si fide stabilítus, in ratiónis ejus indágine se volúerit exercére. Nam et illi, quia breves dies hóminis sunt, non ómnia quæ possent, si diútius vixíssent, dícere potuérunt; et veritátis rátio tam ampla tamque profúnda est, ut a mortálibus néqueat exhauríri; et Dóminus in Ecclésia sua, cum qua se esse usque ad consummatiónem sæculi promíttit, grátiæ suæ dona non désinit impertíri.

spiritussanctussupervenietinteetvirtusal.en: The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the most High shall overshadow thee.
spiritussanctussupervenietinteetvirtusal.la: Spiritus Sanctus supervéniet in te, et virtus Altíssimi obumbrábit tibi.

sedsupernanospietasnecdeserentessedeseri.en: But the goodness from above forsaketh us not, even when we forsake it. For it recalleth those despised delights to the eyes of our memory, and setteth them before us; by the promise it shaketh off our torpor, and inviteth us to drive away our loathing. For he saith: A certain man made a great supper, and bade many. Who is this man, but he of whom it is said by the prophet: And he is a man, and who hath known him? Who made a great supper: because he hath prepared for us the fulness of inward sweetness. Who bade many, but few come: because sometimes they themselves who are subject to him by faith, gainsay his eternal banquet by living ill. It followeth: And he sent his servant at the hour of supper to say to them that were invited, that they should come. What is the hour of supper but the end of the world? In which, doubtless, we are: as Paul long ago testifieth, saying: We are they upon whom the ends of the world are come. If then it is now the hour of supper, when we are called: so much the less ought we to excuse ourselves from the banquet of God, as we see that the end of the world hath now drawn near. For the more we consider that there is nothing that remaineth, the more ought we to fear lest the time of grace, which is at hand, be lost.
sedsupernanospietasnecdeserentessedeseri.la: Sed superna nos pietas nec deserentes se deserit. Contemptas enim illas delicias ad memoriæ nostræ oculos reuocat, easque nobis proponit, in promissione torporem excutit, atque ut fastidium nostrum repellere debeamus inuitat. ait namque: Homo quidam fecit cenam magnam, et uocauit multos. Quis est homo iste, nisi ille de quo per prophetam dicitur: et homo est: et quis cognouit eum? Qui fecit cenam magnam: quia satietatem nobis dulcedinis internæ præparauit. qui uocauit multos, sed pauci ueniunt: quia nonnumquam ipsi qui ei per fidem subjecti sunt, æterno ejus conujuio male ujuendo contradicunt. Sequitur: Misit autem servum suum hora cenæ dicere inuitatis ut uenirent. Quid hora cenæ nisi finis est mundi? In quo nimirum nos sumus: sicut jam dudum Paulus testatur dicens: Nos sumus, in quo fines sæculorum deuenerunt. Si ergo jam hora cenæ est, cum uocamur: tanto minus nos debemus excusare a conujuio dei, quanto jam propinquasse cernimus finem sæculi. Quo enim pensamus, quia nihil est quod restat, eo debemus pertimescere, ne tempus gratiæ, quod præsto est, pereat.

saletenimterrenonsumussicordaaudientiumn.en: For we are not the salt of the earth if we season not the hearts of the hearers: which seasoning he truly bestoweth on his neighbour who withholdeth not the word of preaching. But we then truly preach right things to others, if we show forth our words by deeds and examples. I think, dearly beloved brethren, that God suffereth no greater harm from others than from priests: when he seeth those whom he hath set for the correction of others give from themselves examples of wickedness: when we ourselves sin, who ought to have restrained sins, seek no gain of souls, give ourselves daily to our own pursuits, covet earthly things, and with eager mind seize upon the glory of men. And because, by the very fact that we are set over others, we have greater licence to do whatsoever we will, we turn the ministry of the blessing we have received into an occasion of ambition; we forsake the cause of God, and give ourselves to earthly business; we take the place of holiness, and are entangled in earthly ways.
saletenimterrenonsumussicordaaudientiumn.la: Sal étenim terræ non sumus, si corda audiéntium non condímus: quod profécto condiméntum ille veráciter próximo impéndit, qui prædicatiónis verbum non súbtrahit. Sed tunc vere áliis recta prædicámus, si dicta rebus et exémplis osténdimus. Nullum puto, fratres caríssimi, ab áliis majus præjudícium, quam a sacerdótibus tólerat Deus: quando eos, quos ad aliórum correctiónem pósuit, dare de se exémpla pravitátis cernit: quando ipsi peccámus, qui compéscere peccáta debúimus, nulla animárum lucra quǽrimus, ad nostra quotídie stúdia vacámus, terréna concupíscimus, humánam glóriam inténta mente captámus. Et quia eo ipso quo céteris præláti sumus, ad agénda quǽlibet majórem licéntiam habémus, suscéptæ benedictiónis ministérium vértimus ad ambitiónis arguméntum; Dei causam relínquimus, et ad terréna negótia vacámus; locum sanctitátis accípimus, et terrénis dúctibus implicámur.

considerandumnobisestutquiuneademqueexho.en: We must consider that he who doth not suffice to admonish all together with one and the same voice of exhortation, should strive to instruct each one, as far as he is able, and to edify them by private discourses. For we ought to ponder continually what is said to the holy Apostles, and through the Apostles to us: You are the salt of the earth. If then we are salt, we ought to season the minds of the faithful. You therefore who are pastors, consider that ye feed the animals of God; of which animals indeed it is said to God by the Psalmist: In it shall thy animals dwell. And we often see that a rock of salt is set before brute animals, that they may lick of that same rock of salt, and be bettered. As a rock of salt among brute animals, therefore, ought the priest to be among the people. For the priest must take care what he saith to each, and how he admonisheth every one: that whosoever is joined to the priest, may be seasoned, as by the touch of salt, with the savour of eternal life. For we are not the salt of the earth, if we season not the hearts of our hearers: which seasoning he truly bestoweth on his neighbour, who withholdeth not the word of preaching. But then do we truly preach right things to others, if we show forth our words by deeds and examples. I think, dearest brethren, that God suffereth no greater harm from others than from priests: when he seeth those whom he hath set for the correction of others giving examples of wickedness in themselves: when we ourselves sin, who ought to restrain sins; seek no gain of souls; give ourselves daily to our own pursuits; covet earthly things; with intent mind grasp at human glory. And because, by the very fact that we are set over others, we have greater licence to do whatever we will, we turn the ministry of the blessing we have received into an occasion of ambition; we forsake the cause of God, and give ourselves to earthly business; we receive a place of holiness, and are entangled in earthly affairs.
considerandumnobisestutquiuneademqueexho.la: Considerándum nobis est, ut, qui una eadémque exhortatiónis voce non súfficit simul cunctos admonére, stúdeat síngulos, in quantum valet, instrúere, privátis locutiónibus ædificáre. Debémus namque pensáre contínuo, quod sanctis Apóstolis dícitur, et per Apóstolos nobis: Vos estis sal terræ. Si ergo sal sumus, condíre mentes fidélium debémus. Vos ígitur, qui pastóres estis, pensáte, quia Dei animália páscitis; de quibus profécto animálibus Deo per Psalmístam dícitur: Animália tua habitábunt in ea. Et sæpe vidémus, quod petra salis brutis animálibus antepónitur, ut ex éadem salis petra lámbere débeant, et meliorári. Quasi ergo inter bruta animália petra salis, debet esse sacérdos in pópulis. Curáre namque sacerdótem necésse est, quæ síngulis dicat, unumquémque quáliter admóneat: ut quisquis sacerdóti júngitur, quasi ex salis tactu ætérnæ vitæ sapóre condiátur. Sal étenim terræ non sumus, si corda audiéntium non condímus: quod profécto condiméntum ille veráciter próximo impéndit, qui prædicatiónis verbum non súbtrahit. Sed tunc vere áliis recta prædicámus, si dicta rebus et exémplis osténdimus. Nullum puto, fratres caríssimi, ab áliis majus præjudícium, quam a sacerdótibus tólerat Deus: quando eos, quos ad aliórum correctiónem pósuit, dare de se exémpla pravitátis cernit: quando ipsi peccámus, qui compéscere peccáta debúimus, nulla animárum lucra quǽrimus, ad nostra quotídie stúdia vacámus, terréna concupíscimus, humánam glóriam inténta mente captámus. Et quia eo ipso quo céteris præláti sumus, ad agénda quǽlibet majórem licéntiam habémus, suscéptæ benedictiónis ministérium vértimus ad ambitiónis arguméntum; Dei causam relínquimus, et ad terréna negótia vacámus; locum sanctitátis accípimus, et terrénis dúctibus implicámur.

saletenimterrenonsumussicordaaudientiumn.en: For we are not the salt of the earth, if we season not the hearts of our hearers: which seasoning he truly bestoweth on his neighbour, who withholdeth not the word of preaching. But then do we truly preach right things to others, if we show forth our words by deeds and examples. I think, dearest brethren, that God suffereth no greater harm from others than from priests: when he seeth those whom he hath set for the correction of others giving examples of wickedness in themselves: when we ourselves sin, who ought to restrain sins; seek no gain of souls; give ourselves daily to our own pursuits; covet earthly things; with intent mind grasp at human glory. And because, by the very fact that we are set over others, we have greater licence to do whatever we will, we turn the ministry of the blessing we have received into an occasion of ambition; we forsake the cause of God, and give ourselves to earthly business; we receive a place of holiness, and are entangled in earthly affairs. When therefore we bring our exhortations to the ears of your holiness, believe that he himself, whose office we discharge, speaketh to you: for we both admonish you with his affection, and preach to you nothing other than what he taught; beseeching you that, having the loins of your mind girded, ye lead a chaste and sober life in the fear of God. Ye are my crown, as the Apostle saith, and my joy, if your faith, which from the beginning of the Gospel hath been preached in the whole world, shall abide in love and holiness. For although it behoveth the whole Church, which is throughout the whole world, to flourish with all virtues; yet it beseemeth you especially among the other peoples to excel in the merits of godliness, who, founded upon the very citadel of the apostolic rock, both our Lord Jesus Christ hath redeemed with all, and the blessed Apostle Peter hath taught before all.
saletenimterrenonsumussicordaaudientiumn.la: Sal étenim terræ non sumus, si corda audiéntium non condímus: quod profécto condiméntum ille veráciter próximo impéndit, qui prædicatiónis verbum non súbtrahit. Sed tunc vere áliis recta prædicámus, si dicta rebus et exémplis osténdimus. Nullum puto, fratres caríssimi, ab áliis majus præjudícium, quam a sacerdótibus tólerat Deus: quando eos, quos ad aliórum correctiónem pósuit, dare de se exémpla pravitátis cernit: quando ipsi peccámus, qui compéscere peccáta debúimus, nulla animárum lucra quǽrimus, ad nostra quotídie stúdia vacámus, terréna concupíscimus, humánam glóriam inténta mente captámus. Et quia eo ipso quo céteris præláti sumus, ad agénda quǽlibet majórem licéntiam habémus, suscéptæ benedictiónis ministérium vértimus ad ambitiónis arguméntum; Dei causam relínquimus, et ad terréna negótia vacámus; locum sanctitátis accípimus, et terrénis dúctibus implicámur. Cum ergo cohortatiónes nostras áuribus vestræ sanctitátis adhibémus, ipsum vobis, cujus vice fúngimur, loqui crédite: quia et illíus vos afféctu monémus, et non áliud vobis, quam quod dócuit, prædicámus; obsecrántes, ut succíncti lumbos mentis vestræ, castam et sóbriam vitam in Dei timóre ducátis. Coróna mea, sicut Apóstolus ait, et gáudium vos estis, si fides vestra, quæ ab inítio Evangélii in univérso mundo prædicáta est, in dilectióne et sanctitáte permánserit. Nam licet omnem Ecclésiam, quæ in toto est orbe terrárum, cunctis opórteat florére virtútibus; vos tamen præcípue inter céteros pópulos decet méritis pietátis excéllere, quos in ipsa apostólicæ petræ arce fundátos, et Dóminus noster Jesus Christus cum ómnibus redémit, et beátus Apóstolus Petrus præ ómnibus erudívit.

conceptiogloriosevirginismarieexsemineab.en: The Conception of the glorious Virgin Mary, of the seed of Abraham, sprung from the tribe of Juda, illustrious of the stock of David,
conceptiogloriosevirginismarieexsemineab.la: Conceptio gloriosæ virginis Mariæ ex semine Abrahæ, ortæ de tribu Juda, clara ex stirpe David,

aliotemporegothusquidampauperspirituadco.en: At another time a certain Goth, poor in spirit, came to be converted, whom Benedict the man of God most gladly received. And on a certain day he commanded that there be given him an iron tool, which from its likeness to a sickle is called a billhook, that he might cut away the briars from a certain place, where a garden was to be made. Now the place itself, which the Goth had undertaken to clear, lay upon the very bank of the lake. And when this same Goth was cutting down the thick briars with the effort of all his strength, the iron sprang off the handle and fell into the lake, where indeed the depth of the waters was so great that there was now no hope of recovering the tool. The iron being thus lost, the Goth ran trembling to Maurus the monk, told him the damage he had done, and did penance for his fault. And this Maurus the monk took care forthwith to make known to Benedict the servant of God. The man of the Lord Benedict therefore, hearing these things, came to the lake, took the handle from the hand of the Goth, and cast it into the lake: and forthwith the iron came back from the depth, and went into the handle. And he straightway gave back the tool to the Goth, saying: Behold, work on, and be not sad.
aliotemporegothusquidampauperspirituadco.la: Alio témpore Gothus quidam pauper spíritu ad conversiónem venit, quem Dei vir Benedíctus libentíssime suscépit. Quadam vero die ei dari ferraméntum jussit, quod ad falcis similitúdinem falcástrum vocátur, ut de loco quodam vepres abscínderet, quátenus illic hortus fíeri debéret. Locus autem ipse, quem mundándum Gothus susceperat, super ipsam laci ripam jacébat. Cumque Gothus idem densitátem véprium totíus virtútis annísu succíderet, ferrum de manúbrio prosíliens in lacum cécidit, ubi scílicet tanta erat aquárum profúnditas, ut spes requiréndi ferraménti nulla jam esset. Itaque ferro pérdito, tremebúndus ad Maurum mónachum cucurrit Gothus, damnum quod fécerat nuntiavit, et reátus sui egit pæniténtiam. Quod Maurus quoque mónachus mox Benedícto fámulo Dei curávit indicáre. Vir ígitur Dómini Benedíctus hæc áudiens accéssit ad lacum tulit de manu Gothi manúbrium, et misit in lacum: et mox ferrum de profúndo rédiit, atque in manúbrium intrávit. Qui statim ferraméntum Gotho réddidit, dicens: Ecce, labóra, et noli contristári.

odignissimumpatrisbenedictidiscipulumque.en: O most worthy disciple of the Father Benedict, whom he left the heir of his spirit.
odignissimumpatrisbenedictidiscipulumque.la: O digníssimum Patris Benedícti discípulum, quem ipse sui spíritus herédem relíquit.

quadamverodiedumidemvenerabilisbenedictu.en: On a certain day, while the same venerable Benedict was in his cell, the aforesaid boy Placidus, a monk of the holy man, went out to draw water from the lake: who, heedlessly letting down into the water the vessel which he held, himself also followed it by falling. And forthwith the wave caught him, and drew him out from the land almost the flight of an arrow. But the man of God, being within his cell, knew this straightway, and called Maurus in haste, saying: Brother Maurus, run, for that boy who went to draw water hath fallen into the lake, and the wave is now carrying him further off.
quadamverodiedumidemvenerabilisbenedictu.la: Quadam vero die dum idem venerábilis Benedíctus in cella consisteret, prædíctus Plácidus puer, sancti viri mónachus, ad hauriéndam de lacu aquam egréssus est: qui vas quod tenébat, in aquam incáute submíttens, ipse quoque cadéndo secútus est. Quem mox unda rápuit, et pene ad uníus sagíttæ cursum eum a terra intrórsus traxit. Vir autem Dei intra cellam pósitus hoc prótinus agnóvit et Maurum festíne vocávit dicens: Frater Maure, curre, quia puer ille, qui ad hauriéndam aquam perréxerat, in lacum cécidit jamque eum lóngius unda trahit.

margaritamariaalacoqueinpagodiecesisaugu.en: Margaret Mary Alacoque, born of a respectable family in a village of the Diocese of Autun, by a wondrous impulse of prevenient grace took up the way of perfection from her tender years, and shaped the first affections of her most innocent heart to that form of interior life to which she had been chosen by God. While yet a little girl, scarcely come to the use of reason, she held nothing more delightful than to set herself on bended knees and with joined hands before her heavenly Spouse, to dedicate her heart to him, and to vow her virginal chastity, he himself inwardly inspiring the vow beyond her years. Her zeal to please Jesus, and her devotion to the Mother of God, to whom she knew that she had been commended by him, grew alike with her years. From this love of Christ, which meditation prolonged for many hours nourished, there blazed forth a great love of suffering, that she might show herself like unto him whom alone she loved. Hence she afflicted her body with fastings, watchings and other austerities even unto sickness: and steadfastly fashioning her soul after the image of him who is meek and humble of heart, amid the long vexations which, bereft of her father, she endured from servants, she came in a short time, while yet in the world, to great holiness.
margaritamariaalacoqueinpagodiecesisaugu.la: Margarita Maria Alacoque in pago Diœcesis Augustodunensis honesto genere nata, miro prævenientis gratiæ instinctu a teneris annis viam perfectionis arripuit, ac primos Innocentissimi cordis affectus ad eam interioris vitæ formam, ad quam divinitus electa erat; composuit. Puellula vix dum rationis compos nihil magis in deliciis habuit, quam genibus positis, iunctisque manibus coelesti sponso sistere se, Ei cor suum dicare, et virginalem devovere castitatem, Ipso interius votum supra ætatem inspirante. Studium placendi Iesu, et pietas in Deiparam, cui se ab illo commendatam novit, pariter crevere cum annis. Ex hoc Christi amore, quem producta ad plures horas meditatio alebat, ingens exarsit patiendi amor, ut Ei, quem unice diligebat, similem se exhiberet. Hinc corpus ieiuniis, vigiliis, aliisque asperitatibus ad morbum usque afflixit: animum vero inter diuturnas vexationes, quas patre orbata à famulis pertulit, ad imaginem Eius, qui mitis est et humilis corde, constanter effingens, brevi ad magnam sanctitatem in ipso sæculo pervenit.

ordinemvisitationissanctemariequoapropin.en: Having entered the Order of the Visitation of Holy Mary at Paray, that she might be farther from her kinsfolk, she straightway gave in her noviceship an undoubted proof of holiness by all the virtues of the religious life. Meanwhile Christ began to enlighten his spouse with the gift of higher prayer, with interior locutions and other graces, and to dispose her more closely to his designs. Among the various apparitions that one was most famous, in which, as she prayed before the Eucharist, Jesus offered himself to her sight, and showed his divine Heart in his open breast, burning with flames and bound round with thorns, and commanded that, in return for such charity, and to make reparation for the injuries of ungrateful men, she should take care that a public worship be instituted to his Heart, great rewards of graces being promised; and when she hesitated by reason of her humility, and kept saying that she was unequal to so great a thing, he strengthened her with the promise of his help and the foretelling of success. Thenceforth the most faithful spouse of Christ was seen to breathe this one thing, and by words, examples, writings, and the continual sacrifice of her life to seek this one thing, that an interior and exterior worship, such as she had learned from him was pleasing to him, should be rendered by all to the most Sacred Heart of Jesus; which then also wondrously began to be done, and with how great fruit it was afterwards brought to perfection, with the approval of the Holy See, the whole Catholic world beareth witness.
ordinemvisitationissanctemariequoapropin.la: Ordinem Visitationis Sanctae Mariæ, quo a propinquis abesset longius, Paredii ingressa, statim in tirocinio cunctis religiosæ vitæ virtutibus indubium sanctitatis specimen præbuit. Interim Christus sublimioris orationis dono, internis locutionibus, aliisque charismatis sponsam suam illustrare et ad sua consilia propius disponere instituit. Inter varias apparitiones illa maxime celebris fuit, qua ante Eucharistiam oranti Iesus semetipsum conspiciendum obtulit, et divinum Cor suum in aperto pectore flammis incensum, et spinis constrictum ostendit, præcepitque, ut pro tali charitate, et ad reparandas ingratorum hominum iniurias illa publicum Cordi suo cultum, magnis propositis gratiarum præmiis, instituendum curaret, et cunctantem humilitatis causa, seque tantæ rei imparem dictitantem, promisso auxilio et prænuntiato successu confirmavit. Exinde fidissima Christi sponsa hoc unum spirare, verbis, exemplis, scriptis, iugi vitæ suæ sacrificio hoc unum quærere visa est, ut sanctissimo Cordi Iesu interior, exteriorque cultus, qualem Ei placere ab Ipso didicerat, ab omnibus tribueretur, quod et tunc fieri mirabiliter cœpit, et postea, approbante sancta Sede, quanto fructu sit perfectum universus orbis catholicus testatur.

quodenixeadominopetieratillustrieiusdona.en: What she had earnestly asked of the Lord, that his illustrious gifts might be turned to her own contempt, she abundantly obtained. For there were never wanting, at home and abroad, those who, believing her miserably deluded, or at least doubting, carped at her spirit with jibes, or at any rate subjected it to constant and hard trials: in which, however, the humility, patience, obedience and charity of the most meek Virgin ever shone forth the more. With unconquered constancy she bore also insults and threats from outsiders, on account of a noble pupil firmly dismissed from the noviceship. Grave and lasting illnesses were added, and the remedies offered by the physicians to relieve them did her harm. Amid these things she, absorbed in the divine Heart of Christ, and on fire with the flame of his charity, ever longed to suffer more and heavier things.
quodenixeadominopetieratillustrieiusdona.la: Quod enixe à Domino petierat, illustria Eius dona in sui contemptum verterentur, abunde obtinuit. Nunquam enim defuere domi et foris qui illam misere illusam credentes, aut saltem dubitantes, eius spiritum dicteriis carperent, vel certe assiduis ac duris subiicerent experimentis : in quibus tamen mitissimæ Virginis humilitas, patientia, obedientia, et charitas magis semper eluxerunt. Contumelias quoque ac minas ab extraneis ob nobilem alumnam a tirocinio fortiter dimissam invicta constantia toleravit. Accessere morbi graves, et diuturni, quibus levandis remedia a medicis oblata nocebant. Inter hæc illa in divino Christi Corde absorpta, et igne charitatis eius incensa plura et graviora pati semper optabat.

curapastoralilicetmultumrenitenssuscepta.en: Having taken up the pastoral charge, though much resisting, he began to consider, as a man of wonderful prudence, what storms of tribulation might at some time shake and trouble the house entrusted to him: and, providing for the future, with the counsel of the brethren he sent two Monks, John and Ilbodus, to Rome, through them beseeching the Lord Pope Paschal that his Church might rest for ever under the wings of Apostolic protection, quiet and safe from the oppression of all persons, ecclesiastical or secular. These brethren went to Rome and returned prosperously, bringing back a privilege of the same Apostolic Lord according to the wish of the Abbot and his companions, drawn up in every point at Troia on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of May, in the year of the Lord's incarnation one thousand one hundred.
curapastoralilicetmultumrenitenssuscepta.la: Cura pastoráli, licet multum renítens, suscépta, cogitáre cœpit, véluti vir mirábilis prudéntiæ, quæ tribulatiónum procéllæ, domum sibi créditam aliquándo concutiéntes vexáre possent: et præcávens in futúrum, cum consílio fratrum transmísit Mónachos duos Joánnem et Ilbódum Romam, Dóminum Paschálem per eos exórans ut Ecclésia sua sub Apostólicæ protectiónis alis, quiéta et tuta ab ómnium Ecclesiasticórum sæculariúmve pressúra personárum perpétuo sedéret. Qui fratres Romam próspere iérunt et rediérunt, reportántes ejúsdem Apostólici privilégium juxta votum Abbátis sociorúmque ejus, per ómnia exarátum Troyæ décimo quarto Kaléndas Maji anno ab incarnatióne Dómini millésimo centésimo.

petrusorigineravennasteneraadhucetateutr.en: Peter, by origin of Ravenna, bereft of both parents while yet of tender age, underwent a hard servitude under the harsh guardianship of a brother. Then, kindly received by Damian, another brother, who pitied his lot, and from whom he is said to have taken his surname, he was instructed in letters by his care, in which he both made astonishing progress in a short time, and afterwards taught them with praise. While still living in the world, he lived in no worldly manner: endowed with an incredible mercy towards the poor, being a severe chastiser of his own body, he gave himself constantly to prayer. Yet burning with the desire of greater perfection, he enlisted in the monastery of Avellana in the Order of Monks of Holy Cross of Fonte Avellana. And when he had afterwards been set over that family, he so increased it by building new houses and by holy institutions, that he is rightly held a second father of that Order. Excelling in the contemplation of divine things, in the mortifications of the body, and in the other examples of approved holiness, he spent most useful labour in restoring fallen ecclesiastical discipline, and in promoting holiness of manners among the Christian people. Moved by these things, Stephen the Ninth, Supreme Pontiff, created him, although unwilling, Cardinal of the holy Roman Church and Bishop of Ostia.
petrusorigineravennasteneraadhucetateutr.la: Petrus, orígine Ravénnas, ténera adhuc ætáte utróque orbátus parénte, sub áspera fratris tutéla duram servitútem exércuit. Inde a Damiáno, áltero fratre, sortem illíus miseráto, a quo cognoméntum sumpsísse fertur, benígne recéptus, ejus cura lítteris erudítur, in quibus et brevi stupéndos fecit progréssus, et póstmodum eas cum laude dócuit. Adhuc in sæculo degens, mínime sæculáriter vixit: incredíbili in páuperes misericórdia præditus, sui córporis sevérus castigátor exístens, oratióni vacábat assídue. Majóris tamen perfectiónis stúdio flagrans in Avellanénsi cœnóbio Ordini Monachórum sanctæ Crucis Fontis Avellánæ nomen dedit. Cui famíliæ cum póstea præféctus fuísset, eam novis extrúctis domicíliis et sanctis institútis ita auxit, ut alter ejus Ordinis parens jure sit hábitus. Divinórum contemplatióne, córporis maceratiónibus, ceterísque spectátæ sanctimóniæ exémplis præcéllens, utilíssimam óperam restituéndæ collápsæ disciplínæ Ecclesiásticæ, morúmque sanctitáti in plebe Christiána promovéndæ impéndit. His motus Stéphanus nonus Póntifex Máximus, eum, licet invítum, sanctæ Románæ Ecclésiæ Cardinálem, et Epíscopum Ostiénsem creávit.

difficillimotemporeromaneecclesiesummisq.en: In a most difficult time he wonderfully helped the Roman Church and the Supreme Pontiffs by his learning, by legations, and by other labours undertaken. He contended strenuously even unto death against the heresies of the Nicolaites and the Simoniacs. He valiantly withstood Benedict and Cadalous, false pontiffs. He recalled the people of Ravenna to the obedience due to the Roman Pontiff, and restored them to the sacraments. In the province of Urbino especially there was scarcely any episcopal church which Peter did not serve well. At length, having laid down the dignity of the Cardinalate and of the Episcopate, he abated nothing of his former zeal in helping his neighbours. He spread the fast of the sixth Feria in honour of the holy Cross, the hourly prayers of the Mother of God, and her worship on the Saturday. At last, commended by holiness, learning, miracles and illustrious deeds, while he was returning from the Legation to Ravenna, he passed to Christ at Faenza on the eighth of the Kalends of March. His body, renowned there among the Cistercians for many miracles, is honoured with the frequent veneration of the people.
difficillimotemporeromaneecclesiesummisq.la: Difficíllimo témpore Románæ Ecclésiæ summísque Pontificibus doctrína, legatiónibus, aliísque suscéptis labóribus mirífice ádfuit. Advérsus Nicolaitárum et Simoníacam hǽreses ad mortem usque strénue decertávit. Benedícto, et Cadalóo, falsis pontifícibus, fórtiter réstitit. Ravennátes ad débita Románo Pontifici obséquia revocátos sacris restítuit. In província præsértim Urbináte vix ulla fuit Episcopális ecclésia, de qua Petrus non sit bene méritus. Tandem Cardinalátu, et Episcopáli dignitáte depósitis, nihil de prístina juvándi próximos sedulitáte remísit. Jejúnium sextæ Fériæ in honórem sanctæ Crucis, horárias Dei Genitrícis preces, ejúsque die Sábbato cultum propagávit. Demum sanctitáte, doctrína, miráculis, et præcláre actis commendátus, dum e Ravennáte Legatióne redíret, Favéntiæ Octávo Kaléndas Mártii migrávit ad Christum. Ejus corpus ibídem apud Cisterciénses multis miráculis clarum, frequénti populórum veneratióne cólitur.

nullumputofratrescarissimiabaliismaiuspr.en: I think, dearest brethren, that God suffereth no greater injury from others than from priests: when he seeth those whom he hath set for the correction of others give from themselves examples of depravity: when we ourselves sin, who ought to restrain sins, seek no gain of souls, give ourselves daily to our own pursuits, covet earthly things, and with eager mind catch at human glory.
nullumputofratrescarissimiabaliismaiuspr.la: Nullum puto, fratres caríssimi, ab áliis majus præjudícium, quam a sacerdótibus tólerat Deus: quando eos, quos ad aliórum correctiónem pósuit, dare de se exémpla pravitátis cernit: quando ipsi peccámus, qui compéscere peccáta debúimus, nulla animárum lucra quǽrimus, ad nostra quotídie stúdia vacámus, terréna concupíscimus, humánam glóriam inténta mente captámus.

huicdumeremumpeteretromanusmonachusobvia.en: As he was seeking the desert, * the monk Romanus met him: who, when he had learned his desire, both kept his secret and gave him help.
huicdumeremumpeteretromanusmonachusobvia.la: Huic, dum erémum péteret, * Románus mónachus obviávit: cujus cum desidérium cognovísset, et secrétum ténuit, et adjutórium impéndit. Ps. 64

dixitautemmariaadangelumquomodofietistud.en: And Mary said * to the Angel: How shall this be done, because I know not man? And the Angel Gabriel answering, said to her: The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the most High shall overshadow thee.
dixitautemmariaadangelumquomodofietistud.la: Dixit autem María * ad Angelum: Quómodo fiet istud, quóniam virum non cognósco? Et respóndens Gábriel Angelus, dixit ei: Spíritus Sanctus supervéniet in te, et virtus altíssimi obumbrábit tibi.

perpetuumnobisdominetuemiserationisprest.en: Grant us, O Lord, the perpetual help of thy mercy, unto whom thou hast granted that the suffrages of the Angels should not be wanting.
perpetuumnobisdominetuemiserationisprest.la: Perpétuum nobis Dómine, tuæ miseratiónis præsta subsídium, quibus et Angélica præstitísti suffrágia non deésse.

bernardusanteaametusappellatusalmanzorii.en: Bernard, formerly called Ahmed, son of Almanzor, chief of Carlet, was brought up in the court of the Saracen king of Valencia, and was so distinguished for prudence and diligence that he was sent by the king of Valencia himself into Catalonia to treat the weightier affairs of the kingdom. But having on the way wondrously turned aside to the monastery of Poblet of the Cistercian Order, he felt himself so moved and pricked at heart by the pious conversation and discourse of those Monks, that, abjuring the customs of the Mahometan sect and laying aside the name of Ahmed, he willed to be washed with the water of baptism, taking the name of Bernard. Then, being more fully instructed in the orthodox faith, he took the regular habit in the same place, and having made his solemn vows, he excelled among the brethren in more signal piety. How pleasing to God was his wonderful liberality to the poor, while he was Cellarer of the monastery, God testified by a signal miracle: for when, having once been accused before the Abbot of squandering the substance of the monastery, he was ordered to render an account of his office, all things in the granaries, casks and chests were found to be wondrously multiplied and overflowing. But the man of God, growing old, having been permitted to go to his kinsmen, the Saracens of Valencia, that he might win them for Christ, came first to his mother's sister, and converted her to the faith of the Lord.
bernardusanteaametusappellatusalmanzorii.la: Bernárdus, ántea Amétus appellátus, Almanzórii, Réguli Carleténsis fílius, in aula regis Saracéni Valéntiæ educátus, ádeo prudéntia et indústria cláruit, ut in Catalóniam ad tractánda gravióra regni negótia ab ipso Valentíno rege missus fúerit. Sed in itínere ad monastérium Populéti Cisterciensis Ordinis, prodigióse digréssus, ádeo illorum Monachórum pia conversatióne et collóquiis commótum se sensit, et compunctum, ut abjurátis Mahométicæ sectæ móribus et depósito Améti nómine, aqua baptismáli áblui volúerit, Bernárdi nómine suscépto. Deinde orthodoxam fidem plénius edoctus, ibídem hábitum índuit regulárem, ac solémnibus votis emíssis, insignióri pietáte inter fratres excélluit. Miram ejus in páuperes liberalitátem, dum monastérii Cellerárium ágeret, quantum Deus gratam habéret, insígni miráculo testátus est: nam cum apud Abbátem de profusióne substantiæ monastérii aliquándo accusátus, ratiónem múneris sui réddere juberétur, ómnia in hórreis, dóliis et thecis mirum in modum multiplicáta redundáre compérta sunt. Senéscens autem vir Dei, ad consanguíneos, ut illos Christo lucrifáceret, ire permíssus, ad matérteram prius véniens, illam ad Dómini fidem convértit.

indealmanzoriifratrisdomumpetiitcuicumad.en: Thence he sought the house of his brother Almanzor, who, when he had set forth the cause of his coming, the chief raged with anger, and threatened him with death if he dared to preach Christ. Bernard, making no account of the chief's threats, approached his sisters Zoraida and Zaida, and announcing to them wonderful things of the divine religion, brought them to the Catholic faith, and, having duly instructed them and cleansed them with holy baptism, named the one Mary and the other Grace, and joined both to the Cistercian Order. The chief, learning these things, straightway commanded Bernard's forehead to be pierced with an iron nail before his sisters; and he ordered Mary and Grace, unmoved in their purpose of the Christian faith, to be thrust through with the sword, in the year one thousand one hundred and eighty. The bodies of the holy Martyrs, long unknown, and at length discovered by heavenly signs, were honourably buried not far from Alcira, a noble town, from which the glorious Martyr is to this day surnamed St. Bernard of Alcira, and is honoured with great veneration as the Patron of the place.
indealmanzoriifratrisdomumpetiitcuicumad.la: Inde Almanzórii fratris domum pétiit, cui, cum advéntus sui causam exposuísset, ira infrémuit Régulus, ac mortem ipsi minátus est, si Christum prædicáre audéret. Bernárdus ínsuper hábitis Réguli minis, soróres Zoráidam et Záidam aggréssus, et mira eis de religióne divína annúntians, illas ad Catholicam fidem adduxit, ac rite instructas et sacro baptísmate expiátas, álteram Maríam, Grátiam álteram nuncupávit, et Cisterciénsi Ordini utrámque aggrehis compértis, statim Bernárdi frontem coram soróribus férreo clavo cónfodi jussit. Maríam autem et Grátiam in Christiánæ fídei propósito immóbiles gládio transfígi mandávit, anno millésimo centésimo octogésimo. Sanctórum Mártyrum córpora diútius ignóta, et tandem cœléstibus signis detecta, honorífice tumuláta sunt non procul ab Alzíra nóbili óppido, a quo gloriósus Martyr hodiéque Sanctus Bernárdus de Alzíra cognominátur et véluti loci Patrónus magna veneratióne cólitur.

quidenimfuittotusviteilliuscursusnisiuni.en: For what was the whole course of his life, but a conflict with one watchful enemy? How many blind, straying from the way of truth, and hanging already from the summit of the rock over the abyss, did he restore to their lost sight, and clear that vision whereby Christ might be seen?
quidenimfuittotusviteilliuscursusnisiuni.la: Quid enim fuit totus vitæ illíus cursus, nisi uníus cum vígili hoste conflictus? Quantis hic cæcis a via veritátis errántibus, et de summa jam in profúndum rupe pendéntibus, amíssum réddidit visum, et illum, quo Christus viderétur, reparávit intúitum?

spiritussanctitabernaculumpercordispurit.en: Through purity of heart they became a tabernacle of the Holy Ghost, as it is written: I will dwell in them, and walk among them. They crucified themselves to the world, that they might stand at the right hand of Christ: they girded their loins in truth, and ever had their lamps ready, awaiting the coming of the immortal Bridegroom. For, being endowed with the eyes of the mind, they ever looked forward to that dreadful day, and kept the contemplation both of the good things to come and of the punishment to come, so fixed in their heart, that they were never torn away from it. And here they strove to labour, that they might be partakers of everlasting glory: free from disturbances, they were even as the Angels, and now with them, whose life they imitated, they lead the dance.
spiritussanctitabernaculumpercordispurit.la: Spíritus Sancti tabernáculum per cordis puritátem exstitérunt, quemádmodum scriptum est: Inhabitábo in ipsis et inambulábo. Seípsis mundo crucifixérunt, ut ad Christi déxteram starent: lumbos suos in veritáte succinxérunt, atque in promptu semper lámpades habuérunt, immortális Sponsi advéntum expectántes. Nam, cum mentis óculis prǽditi essent, hórrendum illum diem semper prospiciébant, atque tum futurórum bonórum, tum futúri supplícii contemplatiónem ita in corde defíxam gerébant, ut ab ipsa nunquam divelleréntur. Atque hic laboráre studuérunt, ut sempitérnae glóriae cómpotes essent: perturbatiónum expértes, non secus atque Angeli fuérunt, ac nunc cum illis, quorum vitam imitáti sunt, choréas agunt.

spiritussanctussupervenietinteetvirtusal.en: The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the most High hath overshadowed thee: for the Holy which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God.
spiritussanctussupervenietinteetvirtusal.la: Spíritus Sanctus supervéniet in te, et virtus Altíssimi obumbrábit tibi: quod enim ex te nascétur Sanctum, vocábitur Fílius Dei.

oportebataprincipemundialiquamdiucelarid.en: It behoved that the mystery of the divine counsel should for a time be hidden from the Prince of this world; not that God, if he willed to do his work, feared that it could be hindered: but because he, who hath done not only mightily whatsoever he would, even as in all his works he is wont to keep certain fitnesses of things or of times for the beauty of order, so also in this so magnificent work of his, namely of our restoration, willed to show not only his power but also his wisdom.
oportebataprincipemundialiquamdiucelarid.la: Oportébat a Príncipe mundi aliquámdiu celári Divíni concílii sacramentum; non quod Deus, si opus suum fácere vellet, impedíri posse illud metúeret: sed quia ipse, qui non solum poténter quæcúmque vóluit, fecit, sicut in ómnibus suis quasdam rerum vel témporum congruéntias propter órdinis pulchritúdinem serváre consuévit: ita in hoc quoque tam magnífico ópere suo, nostræ vidélicet reparatiónis, non tantum poténtiam suam, sed et prudéntiam suam osténdere vóluit.

iosephfilidavidnolitimereacciperemariamu.en: Joseph, son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife. Above we have already said that spouses are called wives; which the book against Helvidius teacheth more fully. And the Angel speaketh to him in sleep with a soothing affection, to approve the justice of his silence. And at the same time it is to be noted that Joseph is said to be the son of David, that Mary also might be shown to be of the stock of David.
iosephfilidavidnolitimereacciperemariamu.la: Joseph, fili David, noli timére accípere Maríam uxórem tuam. Jam et supra díximus, sponsas uxóres appellári: quod plénius liber advérsus Helvídium docet. Et blandiéntis afféctu ei per sómnium Angelus lóquitur, ut justítiam siléntii comprobáret. Simúlque notándum, quod Joseph fílius esse dicátur David, ut María quoque de stirpe David monstrarétur.

inepiscopatuexemplumseprebuitbonorumoper.en: In the episcopate he showed himself a pattern of good works, and feeding the flock committed to him by admonitions, counsels, learning, word and example, he so pursued evil, that he restored the depraved morals of the peoples and fallen piety to their former state. He was a distinguished propagator of the Catholic faith, and a most zealous defender of the jurisdiction of the Church. He was renowned for excellent prudence, charity, meekness, and mercy toward the poor; the zeal of the house of God had so eaten him up, that, providing earnestly for the repair and for the fitting revenues of the churches, he endowed them not only from the incomes of the episcopal table, but also from his hereditary patrimony. An excellent proof of his devotion was when he gave a notable sum, that in the cathedral church of Cracow a lamp might be kept ever burning before the Sacrament of the altar.
inepiscopatuexemplumseprebuitbonorumoper.la: In Episcopátu exémplum se præbuit bonórum óperum, et commíssum sibi gregem pascens mónitis, consíliis, sciéntia, verbo et exémplo ita insectátus est, ut pravos populórum mores, et collápsam pietátem in pristínum restitúerit. Cathólicae fídei insígnis Propagátor, et Ecclesiásticae jurisdictiónis vindex acérrimus. Exímia incláruit prudéntia, charitáte, mansuetúdine, et misericórdia in páuperes; zelus Domus Dei ita illum coméderat, ut reparatióni, et opportúnis Ecclesiárum provéntibus impénse cónsulens, nedum ex mensæ Episcopális reddítibus, sed et de hæreditário património illas dotáverit. Exímium vero ejus religiónis arguméntum fuit, dum insígne erogávit pecúlium; ut in Templo Cathedrális Cracoviénsis lampas accénsa coram Altáris Sacraménto perpétuo asservarétur.

ibieamsanctitatislaudemadeptusestuteiusf.en: There he gained such praise for holiness that, his fame being carried to Diocletian, the Emperor himself summoned him, that he might deliver his daughter, who was troubled by a devil. And when she had been delivered, and the ungrateful Emperor could not persuade him with most ample rewards to worship the gods, he sent him bound with chains into prison, together with Modestus and Crescentia.
ibieamsanctitatislaudemadeptusestuteiusf.la: Ibi eam Sanctitátis laudem adéptus est, ut ejus fama ad Diocletiánum perláta, ipsum Imperátor accérseret, ut fíliam suam a dæmone vexátam liberáret. Qua liberáta cum ei amplíssimis præmiis ingrátus Imperátor, ut Deos venerarétur, persuadére non potuísset, una cum Modésto et Crescéntia vínculis constríctum mittit in cárcerem.

quosubiconstantioresessereperitdemittiiu.en: And when he found them yet more steadfast, he commanded them to be let down into a huge vessel full of molten lead, boiling resin and pitch; in which, when they sang divine hymns after the manner of the three Hebrew children, they were taken out thence and cast to a lion, which, prostrating itself, licked their feet. Wherefore the Emperor, inflamed with anger, because he saw that the multitude was moved by the miracle, commanded them to be stretched upon the rack, and thus their limbs to be beaten and their bones torn asunder.
quosubiconstantioresessereperitdemittiiu.la: Quos ubi constantióres esse réperit, demítti jubet in ingens vas liquáto plumbo, fervénti resína ac pice plenum : in quo cum trium puerórum hebræórum more divínos hymnos cánerent ; inde erépti leóni objiciúntur, qui se prostérnens, eórum pedes lambébat. Quare ira inflammátus Imperátor, quod multitúdinem vidébat miráculo commovéri, eos in catásta sterni jubet, et ita cædi eórum membra et ossa divélli.

pergitdeindeeodempreceptorumetintelligen.en: He then goeth on in the same course of precepts and understanding. For after he had commanded that all things which are dearest in the world be left, he added: He that taketh not up his cross, and followeth me, is not worthy of me; because they that are Christ's have crucified the flesh with the vices and concupiscences. And he is unworthy of Christ who, not taking up his cross, wherein we suffer with him, die with him, are buried with him, and rise again with him, would be secure of the Lord, who in this sacrament of faith is to live in newness of spirit.
pergitdeindeeodempreceptorumetintelligen.la: Pergit deínde eódem præceptórum et intelligéntiæ decúrsu. Nam, posteáquam relinquénda ómnia, quæ in sæculo charíssima sunt, imperáverat, adjécit: Qui non áccipit crucem suam, et séquitur me, non est me dignus; quia Qui Christi sunt, crucifixérunt corpus cum vítiis et concupiscéntia. Et indígnus est Christo, qui non crucem suam, in qua compátimur, commórimur, consepelímur, conresúrgimus, accípiens, Dóminum sit secútus, in hoc sacraménto fídei, spíritus novitáte victúrus.

fuerittuncdiscipulorumexcusabilispavorne.en: Granted that the fear of the disciples was then excusable, and that the grief of the Apostles fell not into the fault of distrust: when, the Jews and the princes of the Jews concurring in one crime, the proud swelling of fat bulls and the wanton petulance of calves was raging; when, under the eyes of the sheep, the madness of roaring beasts sought the blood of the just Shepherd; when, lastly, even he himself who had come to suffer said, of the sharing of our nature: My soul is sorrowful even unto death.
fuerittuncdiscipulorumexcusabilispavorne.la: Fúerit tunc discipulórum excusábilis pavor, nec in diffidéntiæ culpam Apostólicus mæror incíderit: quando, concurréntibus ad unum scelus Judæis Judæorumque principibus, superbus taurorum pinguium tumor et proterva vitulorum petulántia sæviébat; quando sub oculis ovium, Pastóris justi sanguínem freméntium bestiárum rabies expetébat; quando dénique etiam ipse, qui pati venerat, de nostra naturæ communicatione dicebat: Tristis est anima mea usque ad mortem.

cumdiscubuissetindomosimonisdominusiesus.en: When the Lord Jesus, the glory of the world, had sat down at table in the house of Simon, a woman that was in the city, a sinner, brought fragrant ointment of spikenard.
cumdiscubuissetindomosimonisdominusiesus.la: Cum discubuisset in domo Simónis Dóminus Jesus, mundi glória, múlier, quæ erat in civitáte peccátrix, nardi odorífera exhibuit unguénta. Ps. 8

leteturomneseculuminsolemnitatesanctemar.en: Let all the world rejoice on the solemnity of St. Mary Magdalen,
leteturomneseculuminsolemnitatesanctemar.la: Lætétur omne sæculum in solemnitate sanctæ Mariæ Magdalænæ,

letiscanamusvocibus.en: Let us sing with joyful voices,

munditriumphatprincipem.en: He triumpheth over the prince of the world.

deusquibeatumhyacinthumconfessoremtuumin.en: O God, who didst make blessed Hyacinth thy Confessor conspicuous among the peoples of divers nations by the holiness of his works and the glory of his miracles: grant us that by his examples we may be reformed for the better, and in adversities be protected by his help.
deusquibeatumhyacinthumconfessoremtuumin.la: Deus, qui beátum Hyacínthum, Confessórem tuum, in divérsis nationum pópulis óperum sanctitáte et miraculórum glória fecisti conspicuum: da nobis ut ejus in mélius reformémur exémplis, et in advérsis protegámur auxiliis.

predicatorumordinisflospulcherrimehyacin.en: O most fair flower of the Order of Preachers, Hyacinth, imbue us who sing thy merits with the fragrance of thine odour.
predicatorumordinisflospulcherrimehyacin.la: Prædicatórum órdinis flos pulchérrime, Hyacínthe, tua canéntes mérita tui nos ímbue odóris fragrántia.

celietterraletentur.en: Let the heavens and the earth rejoice.

dominesuscipemeutcumfratribusmeissimcumq.en: O Lord, receive me, that I may be with my brethren, with whom thou didst invite me when thou camest: open unto me the gate of life, and lead me to the banquet of thy feast: for thou art Christ, the Son of the living God, who by the command of the Father didst save the world: to thee we give thanks through the endless ages of ages.
dominesuscipemeutcumfratribusmeissimcumq.la: Dómine, súscipe me, ut cum frátribus meis sim, cum quibus véniens invitásti me: áperi mihi jánuam vitæ et perduc me ad convivium epulárum tuárum: tu enim es Christus Filius Dei vivi, qui præcépto Patris mundum salvásti: tibi grátias reférimus per infiníta sæculórum sæcula. Ps. 98
