hocautemquodposteriusdiximagishaberevide.en: But this which I said last seemeth rather to have the sense of the Gospel; for it followeth: And he that hateth his life in this world, keepeth it unto life eternal. Therefore in what is said above, He that loveth, there is understood, in this world; he keepeth it unto life eternal. A great and wonderful saying, how there may be in man a love for his own life that it perish, a hatred that it perish not. If thou lovest amiss, then thou hast hated; if thou hatest aright, then thou hast loved.
hocautemquodposteriusdiximagishaberevide.la: Hoc autem, quod postérius dixi, magis habére vidétur evangélicus sensus; séquitur enim: Et qui odit ánimam suam in hoc mundo, in vitam ætérnam custódit eam. Ergo, quod supra dictum est, Qui amat, subintellégitur in hoc mundo, ipse útique perdet; qui autem odit, útique in hoc mundo, in vitam ætérnam ipse custódit eam. Magna et mira senténtia, quemádmodum sit hóminis in ánimam suam amor ut péreat, ódium ne péreat. Si male amáveris, tunc odísti; si bene óderis, tunc amásti.

verborumcelestiumnullimagisquamnosprelio.en: Of the heavenly words none are more witnesses than we, whom the end of the world hath found. For how many wars and what rumours do we hear! The Huns have risen up against the Alans, the Alans against the Goths, and the Goths against the Taifali and the Sarmatians. The like banishments of the Goths have made these also exiles in Illyricum: and the end is not yet. What famine over all, a plague alike of oxen and of men and of the other cattle! so that pestilence hath made even us, who have not suffered war, yet equal to the conquered.
verborumcelestiumnullimagisquamnosprelio.la: Verbórum cæléstium nulli magis quam nos prœliórum! testes sumus, quos mundi finis invénit. Quanta enim prælia et quas opiniónes accépimus prœliórum! Hunni in Alános, Aláni in Gothos, et Gothi in Taífalos et Sármatas insurrexérunt. Hos quoque in Illyrico éxsules pária Gothórum exsília fecérunt: et nondum est finis. Quæ ómnium fames, lues páriter boum atque hóminum, ceterique pécoris! ut étiam nos, qui bellum non pertúlimus, debellátis tamen pares fécerit pestiléntia.

scapulissuisobumbravittibidominusetsubpe.en: The Lord will overshadow thee with his shoulders, and under his wings thou shalt trust:
scapulissuisobumbravittibidominusetsubpe.la: Scápulis suis obumbrávit tibi Dóminus, et sub pennis ejus sperábis:

sedquiddeeiussupereminentialoquarcuienim.en: But what shall I say of her pre-eminence? For to which of the Angels hath it been said at any time: The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the most High shall overshadow thee: and therefore also the Holy which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God? In short, Truth is sprung out of the earth, not from the Angelic creature: nor doth he take hold of the Angels, but of the seed of Abraham. It is a great thing for an Angel to be a minister of the Lord; but Mary merited something higher, to be his Mother. The fruitfulness of the Virgin therefore is a surpassing glory, and she is made by a singular gift so much more excellent than the Angels, as she hath received the name of Mother, more different than that of ministers. She, already full of grace, found this grace, that being fervent in charity, unimpaired in virginity, devout in humility, she should nevertheless become with child without knowing man, and bring forth without the pain of women. That is little: That which is born of her is called Holy, and is the Son of God.
sedquiddeeiussupereminentialoquarcuienim.la: Sed quid de ejus supereminéntia loquar? Cui enim Angelórum aliquándo dictum est: Spíritus sanctus supervéniet in te, et virtus Altíssimi obumbrávit tibi: ideóque et quod nascétur ex te Sanctum vocábitur Fílius Dei? Dénique Véritas de terra orta est, non de Angélica creatúra: nec Angelos, sed semen Abrahæ apprehéndit. Magnum est Angelo ut miníster sit Dómini; sed Maria sublímius quiddam méruit, ut sit Mater. Fœcúnditas ítaque Vírginis superéminens glória est, tantóque excelléntior Angelis facta múnere singulári quanto differéntius præ minístris nomen Matris accépit. Hanc invénit grátiam plena jam grátia, ut charitáte férvida, virginitáte íntegra, humilitáte devóta, fíeret nihilóminus sine viri cognitióne grávida‚ sine muliébri dolóre puérpera; Parum est: Quod ex ea natum est, Sanctum vocátur, et est Fílius Dei.

quomodofietistudangeledeiquiaviruminconc.en: How shall this be, O Angel of God, since I have not known man in conceiving? Hear, O Mary, Virgin of Christ: the Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Most High shall overshadow thee.
quomodofietistudangeledeiquiaviruminconc.la: Quómodo fiet istud, Angele Dei, quia virum in concipiéndo non pértuli? Audi, María, Virgo Christi: Spíritus Sanctus supervéniet in te, et virtus Altíssimi obumbrávit tibi.

spiritussanctussupervenietinteetvirtusal.en: The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the most High shall overshadow thee.
spiritussanctussupervenietinteetvirtusal.la: Spiritus Sanctus supervéniet in te, et virtus Altíssimi obumbrávit tibi.

spiritussanctussupervenietinteetvirtusal.en: The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the most High hath overshadowed thee: for the Holy which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God.
spiritussanctussupervenietinteetvirtusal.la: Spíritus Sanctus supervéniet in te, et virtus Altíssimi obumbrávit tibi: quod enim ex te nascétur Sanctum, vocábitur Fílius Dei.

verborumcelestiumnullimagisquamnostestes.en: Of the heavenly words none are more witnesses than we, whom the end of the world hath found. For how many wars and what rumours of wars have we heard! The Huns have risen up against the Alans, the Alans against the Goths, and the Goths against the Taifali and the Sarmatians. The like banishments of the Goths have made these also exiles in Illyricum: and the end is not yet. What famine over all, a plague alike of oxen and of men and of the other cattle! so that pestilence hath made even us, who have not suffered war, yet equal to the conquered.
verborumcelestiumnullimagisquamnostestes.la: Verbórum cæléstium nulli magis quam nos testes sumus, quos mundi finis invénit. Quanta enim prælia et quas opiniónes accépimus prœliórum! Hunni in Alános, Aláni in Gothos, et Gothi in Taífalos et Sármatas insurrexérunt. Hos quoque in Illyrico éxsules pária Gothórum exsília fecérunt: et nondum est finis. Quæ ómnium fames, lues páriter boum atque hóminum, ceterique pécoris! ut étiam nos, qui bellum non pertúlimus, debellátis tamen pares fécerit pestiléntia.

evigilabuntinvitameternam.en: They shall awake unto life everlasting.
